AC1, AC3, AC5 and AC6 are the legacy criteria owned by this story and are copied word for word from RWB-E2-001 with the origin tag on the scenario line; the two legacy Background lines and the feature line are unchanged. AC2, AC4, AC7 and AC8 stay with the app stories of this key and are not restated. AC9 to AC12 are the four seams this harness adds under D-RCV-60, and each one uses only legacy values.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A case enters at 90 days past due | DL16; parameter case.entry.dpd_threshold |
| BR2 | One case per customer per product group; a further account of the same customer and product group is linked to the open case | DL17; REQ-CHO-005 |
| BR3 | The hand-over set is read from v_ace_account for the ACE business date; the Workbench loads no source file | D-RCV-35 U1; ADR-010; REQ-DRI-013 |
| BR4 | No case is created from a business date whose ACE batch is not COMPLETE | JOB-02; CTL-02; FEAT-CHO-05 |
| BR5 | The EFS contact and promise history of the collection period is read from v_ace_efs_action and appended to the interaction ledger with source system EFS, one entry per efs_record_key | DL29; LOV-SOURCE; REQ-CHO-001; R-UNI-40 |
| BR6 | A repeat hand-over for the same account and business date is ignored and counted | R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | A decision that cannot be written to the decision log does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06 |
| BR8 | An account whose person_key has no row in v_ace_customer is held on the REC-05 business-key break and tried with the next run | REC-05; DQ-040; D-RCV-35 U2 |
| BR9 | One owning schema per table and no cross-schema read: each of the 19 services writes its own `rwb_*` schema and holds another service's IDs, never its rows | DP-01, DP-11; ADR-014, ADR-020; Arch v5 slides 29, 45 and 46 |
| BR10 | The decision record is written locally in the same transaction as the state change and published once on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; a redelivery is deduped by the inbox | DP-03, DP-09; ADR-015, ADR-022; Temporal and Drools design slides 11 and 16 |
| BR11 | The hand-over is an event-started Temporal step started by `AceDataReady`, not a Quartz job; no shared Quartz table is read or written | DP-10; ADR-016; Arch v5 slide 44 |

BR1 to BR8 are copied word for word from the legacy story with their sources. BR9 to BR11 are the realignment rules this harness proves. The harness asserts all eleven against the owning services and the published contracts; it does not re-implement them, and no BR row is changed by this story.

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status and no case state; the harness drives the hand-over and reads records only, and it adds no transition of its own. The facts below are caused by the owning services and are observed and asserted by the harness.

| Observed fact | Caused by | Asserted as |
|---|---|---|
| `AceDataReady` published for ALS at business date 2026-12-14 | rwb-source-data (P1) | One event on `rwb.source-data.events.v1` with the business date (TC-E2-001-01-ITG, TC-ITG-E2001-01) |
| DP01 and DP05 stamps read, the step started or held | rwb-source-data (P1) and the step in rwb-integration (P2) | A fresh answer and one run, or a stale answer and no case (TC-ITG-E2001-01, TC-ITG-E2001-02) |
| One case with status "NEW", entry date 2026-12-15 and 90 days past due at entry | rwb-case (P3) | One case on the case list and the case read (TC-E2-001-01-ITG, TC-ITG-E2001-01) |
| 16 EFS entries with source system "EFS" and their action codes | rwb-source-data (P1) | 16 entries in `interaction` read through the P1 contract (TC-E2-001-01-ITG, TC-ITG-E2001-01, TC-ITG-E2001-03) |

| Cases with entry date 2026-12-17 and the gap date 2026-12-15 | rwb-case (P3) and the run summary of rwb-source-data (P1) | The two entry dates and the gap date in the run summary (TC-E2-001-06-ITG, TC-ITG-E2001-02) |

##### 12. Contract

This is an integration story: it publishes nothing and consumes the real contracts.

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; the 2 s timeout and the breaker per downstream of DP-11 apply to every row.

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | The DP01 and DP05 stamps at the business date, fresh or stale (AC9, AC10) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/{productCode}/records` | P1 rwb-source-data | The published product records and the hand-over run summary: the entry date and the gap date (AC9, AC10) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/data-quality/exceptions` | P1 rwb-source-data | The REC-05 business-key break that lists "A-0003" (AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` | P1 rwb-source-data | The 16 entries with source system "EFS" and the action code of each row (AC1, AC9, AC11) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` | P1 rwb-source-data | The EFS append the hand-over step calls; re-driven with the same `efs_record_key` for the repeat of AC11 |
| POST | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` | P1 rwb-source-data | The administrative rerun request, refused for a role without the right (TC-E2-001-09-ITG); the step itself is started by `AceDataReady` (DP-10) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/scheduled-jobs` | P2 rwb-integration | The recorded run of the hand-over step: run or held, and the waiting count (AC9, AC10, AC11) |

| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case facts: product group, status, entry date and days past due at entry (AC1, AC9) |

The two interaction operations are P1's under the ruling recorded in the Ownership Map: the interaction ledger is `rwb-source-data`'s (DP-18) and rwb-case reads it through the P1 contract. The case list and the case timeline a screen consumes are read through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19, owned by RWB-PLT-N001-CON; its path and merge order are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0388; ASM-0563).

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; it replays a captured `AceDataReady` envelope as a test producer into the owner's topic, on the owner's contract.

The harness consumes these topics as a test consumer with its own group and asserts the records through the owners' reads; it holds no inbox table of its own, gets no production record, and publishes nothing.

None. The harness owns no table and no schema (DP-01). ##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The platform H dependencies those patterns add (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are delivered by the service and platform stories and are not repeated in the metadata H column, which stays None; DP-01, DP-05, DP-11 and DP-18 add no dependency at all, and the C rows on DP-06 and DP-07 are build-against-the-contract only. The story's real gate is the six I stories: they replace the fakes with the real behaviour, and they gate the done state, not the Day-1 start.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| EfsHandoverJourneyRunner | Test harness | Runs the fourteen `-ITG` cases of §16 in one run per business date, in fake or real mode per service, and stops at the first failed assertion with the trace |
| HandoverClient | Harness adapter | Calls the twelve consumed operations of §12.2 through one hop and records the answer and the elapsed time |
| HandoverEventReplayer | Harness adapter | Replays the captured `AceDataReady` envelope with event ID "EVT-SYN-2614-01", including the duplicate of AC11, and reads `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` |
| FakePack | WireMock project | Serves rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-integration and rwb-decision of §12.8 from the published OpenAPI documents |
| HandoverSeedLoader | Service | Seeds the accounts "A-0001" to "A-0004", the 14 contact and 2 promise rows, the open case "RW-2026-000210", the ACE batch rows of the four business dates and the parameter and outcome rows through the owner's contract or the fake |
| CaseAsserter | Assertion | Asserts the one case, its status "NEW", its product group, its entry date, its days past due at entry and the account link |
| LedgerAsserter | Assertion | Asserts the 16 entries, their source system "EFS", their action code and their `efs_record_key`, and that the set does not grow on a repeat |
| SummaryAsserter | Assertion | Asserts the run summary: the counts, the waiting count of a held run and the gap date 2026-12-15 |
| DecisionRecordAsserter | Assertion | Asserts one local record written with the state change and one central ledger entry, and that the entry holds business date 2026-12-14 in its inputs snapshot |
| RefusalAsserter | Assertion | Asserts MSG-P1-001, MSG-P2-007, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P7-003 by id and rendered text |
| SchemaBoundaryCheck | Assertion | Fails the run on any cross-schema reference, any FOREIGN KEY between two schemas, any second reader of `recovery.v_ace_*` and any call deeper than one hop |
| RunLock | Service | One run at a time in the harness environment |
| EvidenceReportPublisher | Reporter | Writes the per-run evidence report keyed by story id and business date and attaches it to the release record |
| JourneyGate | Assertion | Passes the run only when every owned criterion passes; fails and names the criterion, the seam and the observed value otherwise |

**Database.** None. The harness owns no schema, runs no Flyway migration and holds no table; seeds and assertions go through the contracts (DP-01).

**Environment and test data.** SIT for the run of record and UAT for the acceptance run, with `rwb.integration.efs-handover` on in both. The data are the synthetic seeds of the legacy story: "A-0001" for customer "C-0001", product group "MORTGAGE", 90 days past due in `v_ace_account` at business date 2026-12-14, with 14 contact rows and 2 promise rows in `v_ace_efs_action`; "A-0002" of customer "C-0002", product group "SSME", with open case "RW-2026-000210"; "A-0003" with no row in `v_ace_customer`; "A-0004" of the decision-log failure case; the ACE batch rows of 2026-12-14 COMPLETED at 05:20, 2026-12-15 not COMPLETE by 09:00 on 2026-12-16, 2026-12-16 COMPLETED at 05:15 on 2026-12-17; parameter `case.entry.dpd_threshold` = 90 and `handover.hold_until` = 09:00; the `efs_ledger_outcome` rows of the copied action codes. Each run starts from the seeded state, so a repeated run is deterministic. The harness repository, its SIT and UAT environments, its seeding, its evidence format and retention and its pass/fail gate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0388; ASM-0563).

**Build steps**

1. Build EfsHandoverJourneyRunner and HandoverClient against the published OpenAPI documents of the six services and the gateway-bff routes.
2. Publish FakePack for rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-integration and rwb-decision from the same documents, and prove the harness runs green from Day 1 on the fakes.
3. Write HandoverSeedLoader and the seed files for "A-0001" to "A-0004" and the four business dates, with the run lock and the fake or real mode per service.
4. Write HandoverEventReplayer for the ready batch, the duplicate event ID of AC11 and the two consumed events, with a unit test on the captured envelopes.
5. Write CaseAsserter, LedgerAsserter, DecisionRecordAsserter and SummaryAsserter for AC1, AC9 and AC11, with a unit test on fixtures for every asserted field.
6. Write RefusalAsserter for the held run of AC3 and AC10, the break of AC5 and the refusal of TC-E2-001-09-ITG.
7. Write SchemaBoundaryCheck and prove it fails on a planted cross-schema key, a planted cross-schema select and a second `recovery.v_ace_*` reader.
8. Replace each fake with the real service as its I story lands, in the order rwb-source-data, rwb-integration, rwb-case, rwb-decision, and rerun in UAT.
9. Write JourneyGate and EvidenceReportPublisher, and attach the report to the release record for the build under test.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.integration.efs-handover`, the legacy switch of this story: on in SIT and UAT. The harness asserts the off state on the fakes — no case is created, no entry is appended and the step does not start — and asserts that the case table and the ledger are unchanged in that state.

**Done when.** The fourteen `-ITG` test cases of section 16 pass in SIT and UAT with the six I stories in place and not only against the fakes; the evidence report for the run is attached to the release record with the eight owned criteria green; the boundary check passes with no exception; and the held run, the gap date, the break and the duplicate are green with the messages of section 14.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | Data product stale after an incomplete ACE batch | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P2-007 | Case creation held for an incomplete ACE batch | Case creation for {date} is held until a load passes its checks. {count} accounts are waiting. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P2-006 | Rerun while JOB-02 runs | {job} is already running. Wait until it ends before you run it again. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right reruns JOB-02 | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The harness asserts the message id and the rendered text of each row and never rewrites it. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the threshold, the hold time, the product map and the copied action codes are rows held by their owners; the harness reads them and never holds a copy.
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs, logs, traces or reports: the seeds are synthetic keys, events carry IDs and facts, and the evidence report holds IDs, action codes, dates, counts and results only.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `recovery.v_ace_*` read by rwb-source-data (DP-05); the harness never reads a view and never names an ACE table.
- No cross-schema read and no FOREIGN KEY between two schemas: every read goes through the owner's contract, and SchemaBoundaryCheck fails the run on a violation (DP-01, DP-11).
- No production data and no outside system: the harness calls only the six services and their fakes, never a production endpoint and never WIN, ALS or any other outside system.
- One hop only: the harness fails a run when the trace shows a call chain deeper than the gateway and one owner, and every call carries the 2 s timeout.
- The harness owns no table, no endpoint, no screen, no workflow and no schedule (DP-01, DP-10, DP-18); it is test and evidence only.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-002 for rwb-integration. This document fixes the plan-status contract baseline: the resource, the operation, the error envelope, the ACE common module interface stub, the consumed shapes of rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision, the configuration section and the fakes. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the rwb-integration side of the ACE plan status fixed as a contract: the `GET /cases/{caseId}/plan-status` resource with its fields, rights, errors and read-only rule; the published `RestructurePlanQuery` interface with its batch and timeout budget; the consumed shapes of rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision; the fakes for those three services and the ACE stub; and the statement of what the case side owns**, so that **the app story and the operations story of this key, the plan-status step of `RWB-P3-E2002-APP` and the integration harness build on Day 1 against one agreed, testable shape**.

The legacy story put the plan read, the stored status, the rule evaluation, the route move, the task, the timer and the decision log entry in one module, and it published `GET` on `/cases/{caseId}/plan-status` with `RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor(List<String> accountNos)` beside `CasePlanStatus.update` and `CaseEvents.raise`. Under D-RCV-60 the journey is cut in two: rwb-case holds the case of record, the stored status, the rules, the route state, the task, the timer and the record; rwb-integration holds the call to the ACE common module and the live answer. This document fixes the seam.

Three facts make the seam worth a contract of its own. The ACE common module is a published module interface and not a view, so the call has to be bounded by a batch size and a timeout that both sides can name (INT-34; ADR-010; DP-05). The resource has two providers in the target — the live answer here and the stored answer of rwb-case — so the flag that separates them and the message that says the value is old have to be fixed once (DP-19). And the daily step is rwb-case's, which means the batching, the answer and the refusal classes are the only things this service owes the caller (DP-10, DP-11).

The Ownership Map keeps `GET /cases/{caseId}/plan-status` with P2 and TSD P2 v3 keeps it at API-P2-010, so this document re-bases it on `/api/recovery/integration/v1` under DP-13 and records the reconciliation rather than leaving it to the app story.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST, one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling rule (DP-11, ADR-020), and a plan status is read on a screen, in a nightly step and in an integration harness. All three work only if the resource, its flag, its refusals and its budget are written down once. The contract is also where the two-provider rule is made safe: a caller must be able to tell a value read from ACE now from a value the case holds from an earlier date, or the measure of the legacy story — no case with a live plan is treated as if it had none — cannot be evidenced at the seam.

The contract fixes four things no single source fixes together. The resource shape and the meaning of `live` and `messageCode`, because the API Specification carries the fields and the legacy story carries the rule, and neither says who fills the message when the live read fails. The ACE interface call and its budget, because the legacy story publishes the signature and assumes the batching and the timeout while the technical specification reads a view instead. The error classes, because the case side must know which refusal means "keep the stored value" and which means "this caller may not see the case". And the fakes, because four teams build before the other services exist.

The contract states what it does not own as plainly as what it does: the stored status, the compare, the route move, the decision record, the task and the timer are rwb-case's; the rights and the scope data are rwb-access's; the rule package, its version and the catalog rows are rwb-decision's; the ACE plan itself is ACE's under DL14. This service names them and calls them, and writes none of them.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the task queue and the topic names follow the platform rule (DP-13, DP-14).
- The CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the RFC 9457 problem-details body and the platform message catalogue are the platform baseline; this document narrows them where it must and says so.
- The integration base of RWB-P2-E1007-APP and RWB-P2-E2001-APP is available, with its controller conventions, its problem-response mapping, its contract-client and breaker handling and its health surface.
- The embedded Drools kit contract (RWB-PLT-E1072-CON), the decision-record library contract (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON), the workflow kit (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), the parameter and reference-data client libraries (RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON), the outbox and inbox library (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON), the migration conventions (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON) and the gateway-bff composite route (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are available. This document consumes them and defines none of them.
- The rwb-case contract baseline publishes the case read by reference with its account numbers, the reference-data read of RWB-P3-E1043-CON and the parameters read of RWB-P3-E1042-CON; the rwb-access contract publishes the authorise call. Where a contract is not yet published, this document's shape and its fake stand in.
- The ACE common module publishes `RestructurePlanQuery` in SIT and UAT (INT-34; DL14).
- The plan status list LOV-PLAN-STATUS holds CREATED, APPROVED, BOOKED and BROKEN (RW-COE), and the two settings `rwb.ace.plan.batch-size` = 500 and `rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms` = 2000 are the assumed values of the key (DL11).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the provided operation: `GET /cases/{caseId}/plan-status` on `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, with its path, right, answer, errors, read-only rule and the meaning of `live` and `messageCode`.
2. Publish the consumed shapes: the case read by reference, the reference-data read of LOV-PLAN-STATUS, the parameters read of the two settings and the authorise call, each with the 2 s client budget.
3. Publish the ACE interface contract: the `RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor` signature, the batch size, the per-call timeout, the breaker, the retry and the mapping of a plan to an account.
4. State the split between the live answer here and the stored answer, the compare, the route move and the record of rwb-case, and reconcile the ownership and specification conflicts.
5. Publish the status validation contract: the list, its version, the known-code answer and the unknown-code answer.
6. Publish the configuration section: LOV-PLAN-STATUS, the two settings, the flag and the fact that no table is added.
7. Publish the error mapping of the seven messages over the operation.
8. Build the fakes: rwb-case, its reference data and its parameters; rwb-access; rwb-decision; the ACE common module stub; and the composite route stub.
9. Add the contract tests: the operation shape, the consumed shapes, the interface contract, the split note, the configuration section and the drift test between each fake and this document; tag the baseline and hand it to the app and operations stories.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The operation, a consumed shape or a field contradicts this document | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC1, AC2, AC3 |
| X2 | A fake drifts from this document, or answers a shape this document does not declare | The drift test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC5 |
| X3 | A document declares the stored plan status, the route move, the rule evaluation or the record as this service's | The review refuses the document, because those are rwb-case's and rwb-decision's | None | AC6 |
| X4 | The operation is declared with a write, an event, a Schedule or a second provider of the stored answer | The review refuses it: a read writes nothing, publishes nothing and creates no Schedule, and the stored answer is rwb-case's | None | AC1, AC6 |
| X5 | The ACE plan is declared as a view read or a table read, or `rwb_integration` is given a grant on `recovery` | The review refuses it: the plan comes through the published interface (INT-34), and only rwb-source-data reads the views | None | AC2 |
| X6 | A field-level detail of a consumed shape or of the interface answer is missing from the source material | The element is marked with the placeholder, one gap row and one assumption row are carried, and the fake is written to the assumed shape | None | AC2, AC5 |
| X7 | The caller holds no Case record R, or the case is outside the scope | The refusal is fixed with its status and its message before any ACE call is declared | MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 | AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the ACE interface and the published rwb-case and rwb-access shapes, and fakes them |
| Negotiable | The field-level detail of the consumed reads is settled with their owners; the resource, the flag rule, the batch and the timeout are fixed by this realignment |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app story, the operations story, the plan-status step of RWB-P3-E2002-APP and the integration harness of the key |
| Estimable | One operation, four consumed reads, one outside interface, five fakes and one configuration section |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against an artefact — the schema, the fake, the table section — and never against a business outcome |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The plan status is read from the ACE common module through its published interface, never from ACE tables and never from a `recovery.v_ace_*` view | INT-34; DL14; ADR-010; DP-05 |
| BR2 | The account number is the join between the case and the ACE plan | DL21 |
| BR3 | Plan status values are the rows of LOV-PLAN-STATUS with the version in force; any other code is held as an exception and never interpreted | LOV-PLAN-STATUS; DP-07 |
| BR4 | `live` is true on every 200 answer that read ACE, because such an answer means ACE answered; the flag-off answer is 200 with `live` false and no plan, and `live` false with MSG-P2-008 is the stored answer of rwb-case | Legacy plan-status resource; RWB-P3-E2002-APP |
| BR5 | A read writes nothing: no row, no outbox entry, no decision record, no cached answer | Legacy guardrail; DP-01 |
| BR6 | One base, one queue and one topic per service: this contract declares `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, `rwb-integration` and `rwb.integration.events.v1`, consumes the other bases and never declares another service's path as provided | DP-13; DP-14; Arch v5 slide 41 |
| BR7 | The ACE interface is bounded: batches of 500 account numbers, 2000 ms per call, a breaker per downstream and one retry of a read with jitter | Legacy section 13 (assumed; DL11); DP-11 |
| BR8 | The batch size and the timeout are data, read through the rwb-case parameters contract, and never code | DP-06; FSD P2 Integration v3 BR-P2-007 |
| BR9 | The Case record R right and the case scope are checked before any ACE call, and a refusal returns no data and writes nothing | Legacy AC8; DP-11 |
| BR10 | No table, no column and no index is added by this key, so no migration is added; the library objects exist from the service baseline | DP-15; Ownership Map |
| BR11 | The response shape keeps the legacy PlanStatus names and adds `accountNo`, because the ACE answer carries the account and the case side joins on it | Legacy API-P2-010; API Specification v4 PlanStatus |
| BR12 | A consumed field, path or error that no source fixes is written with the placeholder and carried in one gap row plus its assumption rows, never invented | Template and Rules §R9 |
| BR13 | No personal data appears in an answer, an example or a fake: the case reference, the plan reference, the status code, the flag and the counters only | Arch v5 slide 42; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR14 | The legacy values of the key are carried unchanged: the plan reference "TDR-SYN-0310", the account "A-0310", the statuses CREATED, APPROVED, BOOKED and BROKEN, the code "SUSPENDED" as the negative case, and the two settings 500 and 2000 | Legacy section 7 and section 13 |

##### 9. State transitions

##### 11. Data

The contract declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |

The field-level detail of the case read, the reference read, the parameter read, the authorise answer and the remaining interface elements — property types, lengths, required flags, query parameters and null rules — is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0655; ASM-1106); this document fixes the element names above and leaves the types to the review with each owner. The values of the status list and of the two settings are the legacy values of this key and are carried unchanged (BR14).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/integration/v1`; owner rwb-integration (P2).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/plan-status` | Answer planRef, accountNo, status, statusDate, live (true when the answer read ACE, false on the flag-off answer) and messageCode (empty); 401 (MSG-P4-001), 403 (MSG-P4-002), 404 (MSG-P4-003), 503 (MSG-GEN-006) | Case record R, scope applied | Read only: the same ACE state answers the same values, and nothing is written |

The operation is the one the Ownership Map keeps with P2 and the one TSD P2 v3 publishes as API-P2-010, re-based on the integration base under DP-13. Its JSON field names are the legacy PlanStatus names; `accountNo` is added because the ACE answer carries the account and the case side joins on it, and the Technical Specification and the API Specification differ on whether the field is present (GAP-0655; ASM-1106).

`live` and `messageCode` are the two fields with a rule rather than a type. `live` is true when the value was read from ACE now, which is every 200 answer that read ACE, and false on the flag-off answer, which read nothing and carries no plan; `live` false with MSG-P2-008 and the stored date is the answer of rwb-case on its own base, and the composite route chooses between them (DP-19). `messageCode` is therefore empty on every answer of this service: this service holds no stored value to date and has no older date to name (GAP-0655; ASM-1107).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11).

| Method | Path or operation | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | the case read of the rwb-case contract, by case reference | P3 rwb-case | The account numbers of the case, the owner, the queue and the scope facts |
| GET | the reference-data read of RWB-P3-E1043-CON | P3 rwb-case | LOV-PLAN-STATUS with the version in force |
| GET | the parameters read of RWB-P3-E1042-CON | P3 rwb-case | `rwb.ace.plan.batch-size` and `rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms` with the version in force |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The Case record right and the case scope, cached per session |
| Call | `RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor(List<String> accountNos)` | ACE team, the ACE common module | The plans of the account numbers, in batches of 500 within a 2000 ms budget per call |

The reference-data and parameters reads are named by DP-07 and DP-06 and their paths are taken from the P3 contract baseline when it is published; the case read and the authorise call are the case baseline and the access guard. The paths and element names of the case read, of the authorise answer and of the two reference answers are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0655; ASM-1106).

The ACE interface is a published module interface: it is not on a `/api/recovery/...` base, it is not reached through gateway-bff, and `rwb_integration` holds no grant on `recovery`. The Technical Specification's `v_ace_plan` read with a fallback to the case columns is the conflict this contract records and does not follow (GAP-0655; ASM-1108).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This contract declares no event type and publishes on no topic of its own. `rwb.integration.events.v1` carries FileDelivered and FileFailed, which belong to the outbound-file stories of this service, and `rwb.decision-record.v1` carries DecisionRecorded from the services that take a decision — here, rwb-case on each route move (DP-03, DP-09). A read has no outbox row.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. Every call of this story is call-driven: the operation is called by rwb-case's plan-status activity and by the composite route, and the service subscribes to no topic for this key, holds no inbox row and keeps no projection.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. This contract declares no workflow and no activity: the daily `PlanStatusStep` and its `readPlanStatus` activity are rwb-case's, on its own task queue, and this service answers a synchronous read on the request path with the batching and the budget inside the request. The integration harness lists a plan-status step on `rwb-integration`; that row conflicts with the sibling story and with the job map and is carried in the gap row (GAP-0655; ASM-1108).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Schedule is declared by this contract or created by this key: the legacy plan-status step of JOB-02 runs inside the event-started DailyCaseRun of rwb-case, and a second daily run over the same cases fails the review (Arch v5 slide 44; DP-10).

**Build steps**

1. Write the OpenAPI document of the operation, with its answer, the meaning of `live` and `messageCode`, its errors and its read-only rule; AC1, AC3.
2. Write the consumed document: the four reads with owner, use and the 2 s budget, and the placeholder where no source fixes a path; AC2, AC4.
3. Write the ACE interface contract: the signature, the batch of 500, the 2000 ms budget, the breaker, the retry and the plan-to-account mapping; AC2.
4. Write the split note: the live answer here, the stored answer, the compare, the route move, the task, the timer and the record there, and the two reconciliations; AC6.
5. Write the configuration section: the status list, the two settings, the flag and the no-table statement; AC6.
6. Write the validation table of the seven messages and the operation that carries each; AC3.
7. Build the five fake sets, the ACE stub and the composite route stub, with the fixtures of the legacy criteria.
8. Add the contract tests, including the drift test between each fake and this document, the batch boundary over 500 accounts and the check that the monolith base appears nowhere.
9. Tag the baseline and collect the sign-off of the app story, the operations story, the case plan-status step and the harness.

**Done when.** The five contract files validate in the pipeline, the contract tests pass, each fake answers every declared shape, and the app story, the operations story, RWB-P3-E2002-APP and RWB-ITG-E2002-ITG have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-006 | The ACE common module or a consumed read did not answer inside the budget | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-001 | No session, or the person holds no Workbench role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Case record right calls the operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the caller's scope, or unknown | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P2-008 | A stored plan status is shown because the live answer is not available | The ACE plan status is from {date}. Today's status was not returned. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record of a route move could not be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No RESTRUCTURE version is in force on the business date | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |

This contract returns MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 and no other message. MSG-P2-008, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P3-027 are the case side's and are declared here only so that the caller knows which message comes from which provider; the contract adds no wording. For MSG-GEN-006, {system} names the source that did not answer. The seven texts are the agreed texts of the legacy story and of the platform catalogue.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the status list, the two settings, the flag and the breaker thresholds are rows, parameters and values of their owners.
- No personal data and no account number in an answer, an example or a fake: the case reference, the plan reference, the status code, the flag and counters only; the fixtures use the synthetic account "A-0310" of the legacy story.
- The contract names only this service's operation as provided; the case, the reference data, the parameters and the authorise answer are consumed and never restated as this service's (DP-01, DP-13).
- One base, one queue and one topic: a document that names another service's base as provided, or a topic outside `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- The plan is read only through the published module interface; a document that declares a `v_ace_*` read, a table read or a grant on `recovery` fails the review (DP-05, ADR-010).
- A read writes nothing and publishes nothing; a document that declares a write, an event, a Schedule or a cached answer on this operation fails the review (BR5).
- The stored plan status and its date are not declared here; a document that gives this service the stored answer or the route move fails the review (BR4, AC6).
- Every example and fixture is synthetic; no production payload, case number, account number or plan reference is copied into a schema or a fake.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-002 for rwb-integration. The stored plan status, its date, the compare, the route move, the rule evaluation, the task, the durable timer, the local decision record and the plan status panel stay with rwb-case (RWB-P3-E2002-APP); this story keeps the call to the ACE common module, the live plan-status answer on `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, the status validation, the access check and the rule that a read writes nothing. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **the restructure plan status of my case read live from the ACE common module through one integration operation that answers the plan reference, the account, the status, the status date and a flag that says it was read now**, so that **the case side can show a live status or fall back to the status the case holds, and a case with a live plan is never treated as if it had none**.

The operation is `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/cases/{caseId}/plan-status`, served by `PlanStatusController` and `PlanStatusService` and backed by `AcePlanClient`, which wraps the ACE common module's published `RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor` in batches of 500 account numbers with a 2,000 ms budget per call (INT-34; DL14). The answer is `planRef`, `accountNo`, `status`, `statusDate`, `live` and `messageCode`. The status is validated against the plan status list LOV-PLAN-STATUS read through the rwb-case reference-data contract, the caller's Case record right and scope are checked through the rwb-access authorise contract, and the read writes nothing anywhere.

The legacy story held the plan read, the stored plan status, the broken plan rules, the route move, the task, the timer and the decision log entry in one module. Under D-RCV-60 that journey is cut across services and this story is the integration half of it:

- **Here.** The call to the ACE common module, the batching and the 2,000 ms budget, the mapping of a plan to a case by account number, the status validation, the access check, the live answer and the read-only rule.
- **In RWB-P3-E2002-APP.** The case of record: `plan_ref`, `plan_status` and `plan_status_as_of` in `rwb_case`, the compare, package RESTRUCTURE evaluated by the embedded Drools kit, the route state, the task, the durable timer, the decision record and the plan status panel. Its daily `readPlanStatus` activity calls this operation inside the plan-status step of JOB-02.
- **In RWB-P4-E2002-APP and RWB-P7-E2002-APP.** The role and scope data, and the rule package registry with the evaluation and the central ledger.
- **In RWB-ITG-E2002-ITG.** The cross-service proof of the nine legacy criteria as one journey.

##### 2. Business rationale

Restructure plans are calculated and held in ACE (DL14). Without the plan status on the case, a recovery officer can start litigation on a customer who is paying a plan, or miss a plan that broke. The legacy story read the status from the ACE common module each morning and on each case view, kept the last known status with its date when ACE returned none, and raised a broken plan to the restructure rules R-RES-29, R-RES-30, R-RES-31 and R-LIT-02 of package RESTRUCTURE.

Only one service may speak to an outside system, and in the target that service is rwb-integration: the ACE common module publishes `RestructurePlanQuery` (INT-34), and the plan status leaves the bank's plan engine through that interface and no other path. Making the read a service of its own does three things the monolith could not. It bounds the outside call: 500 account numbers per call, 2,000 ms per call, a breaker per downstream and a versioned status list, so a slow ACE cannot hold a case record screen or a nightly run. It makes the answer honest: the `live` flag says whether the value was read now, so the stored answer of the case and the live answer cannot be confused. And it keeps the read side-effect free, so a screen refresh or a rerun can never write a plan status.

**What the split changes, and why it changes here.**

- **DP-01.** `rwb_integration` holds no case row, no account row and no plan row, and no foreign key crosses a schema. The case is reached by its reference through the rwb-case contract; the plan is reached through the ACE interface.
- **DP-03.** No decision record is written by this story: a read takes no decision, and the record of a route move belongs to the service that moves the case. The decision-record library is a dependency of the service build, not of this operation.
- **DP-04.** No rule package is evaluated here. Package RESTRUCTURE, its version, the embedded Drools kit and the catalog rows stay with rwb-case and rwb-decision (RWB-P3-E2002-APP, RWB-P7-E2002-APP); this slice carries the kit dependency because the service ships it, and evaluates nothing.
- **DP-05.** The plan is read through the ACE common module's published interface (INT-34), not through a `recovery.v_ace_*` view and not through a table: the interface is a module interface, not a view, so the direct call of the legacy story stays where the legacy story has it, bounded by the 2,000 ms budget and the batching. Only rwb-source-data reads the thirty views (ADR-010; Arch v5 slides 8, 9, 13, 29, 37 and 45), and `rwb_integration` holds no grant on `recovery`. The TSD path that reads `v_ace_plan` and falls back to the case columns is recorded as a conflict, not followed.
- **DP-06.** The batch size and the timeout are data: `rwb.ace.plan.batch-size` = 500 and `rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms` = 2000 are read through the rwb-case parameters contract, never written in code.
- **DP-07.** The plan status list LOV-PLAN-STATUS is reference data of rwb-case, read through its contract with the version in force; no status code is written in code.
- **DP-09.** No event is published or consumed by this story. The outbox, inbox and idempotency objects exist in `rwb_integration` for the service's file stories; a read writes no outbox row.
- **DP-10.** No Temporal Schedule and no workflow is created here. The daily plan-status step is a step of JOB-02 owned by rwb-case, which calls this operation inside its own activity; this operation answers synchronously on the request path.
- **DP-11.** The in-process calls of the legacy module become REST contracts with fakes: the case read, the reference-data read, the parameter read and the authorise call, plus the ACE interface call, each one hop with a 2,000 ms budget and a breaker.
- **DP-13.** The legacy operation moves from the monolith base to `/api/recovery/integration/v1` (Ownership Map; TSD P2 v3 API-P2-010).
- **DP-15.** One Flyway sequence in `rwb_integration`; this story adds no table and no column, so it adds no migration.
- **DP-19.** The case record reads the plan section through the gateway-bff composite route, which calls this operation and the rwb-case stored answer in parallel and merges them; the browser calls neither service directly.

It meets REQ-DRI-013 (the plan status is read from the ACE common module) and REQ-CHO-002 (a change to a plan status in ACE is visible on the case through the ACE common module), and it carries the legacy measure in its own half: the live answer exists, is bounded, is validated and writes nothing, so a case with a live plan can never be treated as if it had none for want of a read.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P2-E2002-CON is published: the resource shape (`planRef`, `accountNo`, `status`, `statusDate`, `live`, `messageCode`), the operation, the error envelope, the ACE interface stub and the fakes of rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision. This story builds against that baseline.
- RWB-P2-E1007-APP and RWB-P2-E2001-APP are delivered: the integration base with its controller conventions, its problem-response mapping, its contract-client, breaker and idempotency handling, and its worker and health surface.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON are published: the decision-record library, the embedded Drools kit, the parameter and reference-data client libraries, the outbox and inbox library, the workflow kit, the migration conventions and the gateway-bff composite route.
- RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are published: the parameters contract and the reference-data contract of rwb-case, which carry `rwb.ace.plan.batch-size`, `rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms` and LOV-PLAN-STATUS with the version in force.
- RWB-P3-E2042-CON is published: the rule catalog and package read of rwb-decision, so a case that moves can name its rule and its package version. This story consumes none of it and holds no catalog row.
- The rwb-case case read and the rwb-access authorise contract are published, or are faked to the shapes of RWB-P2-E2002-CON: the case with its account numbers and its owner and queue, and the Case record R right with the scope.
- The ACE common module publishes `RestructurePlanQuery` in SIT and UAT (INT-34; DL14), and the stub of that interface answers in SIT before the real ACE endpoint is reached.
- LOV-PLAN-STATUS holds CREATED, APPROVED, BOOKED and BROKEN in the rwb-case reference data (RW-COE), and "SUSPENDED" is the code the negative tests drive.
- The parameter rows `rwb.ace.plan.batch-size` = 500 and `rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms` = 2000 are in force (assumed; DL11), as parameter rows and not as code.
- The feature flag `rwb.integration.ace-plan-status` is registered in the platform flag library; on, the operation answers live; off, it answers the stored-only refusal without calling ACE.
- The login is the rwb-integration login (DP-02): Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0654; ASM-1099).

##### 4. Flow

1. Caller: rwb-case's `readPlanStatus` activity inside the plan-status step of DailyCaseRun, or gateway-bff on behalf of the case record, calls `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/cases/{caseId}/plan-status` with the case ID only (one hop, 2 s client budget, DP-11).
2. rwb-integration: reads the case through the rwb-case contract, by case reference only: the account numbers used for the join, the owner and the queue, and the scope facts the authorise answer is checked against (DP-01).
3. rwb-integration: checks the Case record R right and the case scope through the rwb-access authorise contract, cached per session; a refusal ends the request before any ACE call and before any read of the cache (MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003).
4. rwb-integration: reads `rwb.ace.plan.batch-size` and `rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms` through the parameters contract of rwb-case with the version in force, cached for the life of the process and refreshed on a version change (DP-06).
5. rwb-integration: reads LOV-PLAN-STATUS with the version in force through the reference-data contract of rwb-case, cached with its version (DP-07).
6. rwb-integration: checks the feature flag `rwb.integration.ace-plan-status` from the platform flag library; off ends the request with the stored-only answer and no ACE call.
7. rwb-integration: `AcePlanClient` calls `RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor` with the account numbers of the case in batches of 500, each batch bounded by the 2,000 ms budget, with a breaker per downstream and one retry of a read with jitter.
8. rwb-integration: maps each returned plan to its account number and takes the plan of the case: `planRef`, `accountNo`, `status`, `statusDate`. An account absent from the answer is an account with no plan, not an error.
9. rwb-integration: validates the status code against LOV-PLAN-STATUS. A code in the list is answered unchanged. A code not in the list is answered unchanged as well: it is never mapped, labelled, coerced or defaulted to a known value, it is counted as an unknown status for the dashboard and the alert of RWB-P2-E2002-OPS, and the case side, which reads the same list through the same contract, is what refuses to store it (MSG none; legacy X3).
10. rwb-integration: answers 200 with `planRef`, `accountNo`, `status`, `statusDate`, `live` true and `messageCode` empty, and writes nothing: no table row, no outbox row, no cache entry of the answer itself (DP-09, BR12).
11. rwb-integration: where no plan is returned for the case, answers 200 with `live` true and the plan fields absent, because ACE answered and the answer is that there is no plan; the substitution of the stored status, its date and MSG-P2-008 is rwb-case's (RWB-P3-E2002-APP).
12. rwb-integration: where ACE does not answer inside the budget, or the breaker is open, answers 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming "ACE common module"; the caller keeps every stored status and retries in its next run.
13. gateway-bff: for the case record, calls this operation and the rwb-case stored answer in parallel, one hop each, and merges them: the live answer wins when `live` is true, the stored answer of rwb-case with MSG-P2-008 and its date is shown when this operation answers 503 or the flag is off (DP-19).
14. rwb-integration: records on every answer the case reference, the plan reference, the status code, the `live` flag, the batch count and the duration, never an account number and never a personal value (BR16).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | ACE returns no status for a plan the case holds | This operation answers `live` true with no plan; the case keeps its last known status and date through rwb-case; a break with product "DP04" lists the plan for the ACE team | MSG-P2-008 (shown by rwb-case) | AC3 |
| X2 | The ACE common module is unavailable or does not answer in 2 seconds | The answer is 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming "ACE common module"; the case side keeps every stored status and retries in its next run; the screen shows the stored status | MSG-GEN-006 | AC4 |
| X3 | ACE returns a status code not in the plan status list | The code is answered unchanged and never interpreted; it is counted and alerted; the case side refuses to store it and writes the break with check "Lists of values" | None | AC5 |
| X4 | The daily step runs twice for the same day | This operation is stateless and answers the same values; no status is written twice and no event is raised twice, because neither the write nor the event is here | None | AC6 |
| X5 | The decision log write fails during the broken plan move | Nothing changes here: this operation writes no record and takes no decision; the move, the rollback and the incident are rwb-case's | MSG-P7-003 (raised by rwb-case) | AC7 |
| X6 | A user calls the operation for a case outside their scope | Refused with 404 before any ACE call; nothing is returned and nothing is written | MSG-P4-003 | AC8 |
| X7 | A role without the Case record R right calls the operation | Refused with 403 before any ACE call; nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-002-10 |
| X8 | No RESTRUCTURE version is IN_FORCE on the business date | Nothing changes here, because the read never evaluates a package; the refusal, the exception queue and MSG-P3-027 are the case side's | MSG-P3-027 (raised by rwb-case) | AC9 |
| X9 | The case reference is unknown, or the case exists but holds no account | Refused with 404 for an unknown case; a case with no account answers 200 with `live` false, the plan fields absent and no ACE call, because there is nothing to ask ACE about | MSG-P4-003 (unknown case only) | AC1, AC3 |
| X10 | The reference-data, parameter or authorise call does not answer inside the budget | The answer is 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming the source; no ACE call is made, because a status that cannot be validated is not read | MSG-GEN-006 | AC1 |
| X11 | The flag `rwb.integration.ace-plan-status` is off | The answer is 200 with `live` false and no ACE call, so the caller uses the stored value; nothing is read from ACE and nothing is written | None | AC1 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the contract baseline of RWB-P2-E2002-CON and the integration base of RWB-P2-E2001-APP; the case, reference-data, parameter, authorise and ACE answers come from their fakes |
| Negotiable | The batch size, the timeout, the status list, the flag and the breaker thresholds are rows, parameters and values; the story fixes only the behaviour |
| Valuable | A live plan status is available to the case side within a bounded budget, and a read can never write a plan status |
| Estimable | One operation, one service class, one ACE client, three contract clients, one access check and one status validation |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each of the nine legacy criteria is one automated test at the level this slice can prove it; every cross-service answer is stubbed |

The nine criteria are copied unchanged from the legacy story, values included, with the cross-service answers replaced by a contract-mock Given. Each line of the legacy background and of each criterion is kept; no value is changed and no line is dropped.

**What is proved here, and what is proved at the other owners.** The split puts one journey across five services, so each criterion is proved at the level the owning service can prove it, and this story runs the nine against its own operation with the contract fakes:

- **AC1 is proved here at Component level for the read half**: the case's accounts are resolved, ACE is called in batches of 500 with the 2,000 ms budget, "APPROVED" is validated against LOV-PLAN-STATUS, the answer is `planRef` "TDR-SYN-0310", `accountNo` "A-0310", `status` "APPROVED", `statusDate` 2026-12-10 and `live` true, and nothing is written. The panel value and the evaluation with its version are proved in RWB-P3-E2002-APP and RWB-P7-E2002-APP.
- **AC2 is proved here only for the answer that starts the move**: "BROKEN" with status date 2026-12-14 is answered live with its plan reference. The stored status, the two route moves, the queue, the task, the timer, the decision entries and the retry are rwb-case's and are proved in RWB-P3-E2002-APP, and the package version is rwb-decision's.
- **AC3 is proved here for the no-plan answer**: with the ACE stub returning no status, the answer is `live` true with no plan and no error, because ACE answered and the answer is that there is no plan. The stored "BOOKED" with 2026-12-01, MSG-P2-008 and the product "DP04" break are rwb-case's and are proved there; this story guarantees only that it never invents a plan, never returns a stale value and never errors on an absent one.
- **AC4 is proved here in full at Component level**: a 3-second ACE answer is cut at 2,000 ms, the answer is 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming "ACE common module", no case answer changes and no write is attempted; the retry of the next run is the caller's.
- **AC5 is proved here for the validation half**: "SUSPENDED" is answered unchanged, is never mapped to a known status and is counted as unknown; the refusal to store it, the unchanged stored value and the "Lists of values" break are rwb-case's and are proved there.
- **AC6 and AC7 are proved here as the absence of a second effect**: the operation is stateless and idempotent by its input, so a repeat answers the same values and writes nothing, and a decision-record failure cannot leave a partial write here because there is no write. The stored-value idempotency and the decision record are rwb-case's.
- **AC8 and TC-E2-002-10 are proved here at Component level on this operation**: 404 with MSG-P4-003 for a case outside the scope and 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a role without Case record R, both before any ACE call. The role and scope data are rwb-access's (RWB-P4-E2002-APP).
- **AC9 is proved here as the absence of a package dependency**: the operation answers the plan whether or not a package version is in force, because a read never evaluates a package. The refusal, the exception queue and the message are rwb-case's and rwb-decision's.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The plan status is read from the ACE common module through its published interface `RestructurePlanQuery`, never from ACE tables and never from a `recovery.v_ace_*` view | INT-34; DL14; ADR-010; DP-05 |
| BR2 | The account number is the join between the case and the ACE plan | DL21 |
| BR3 | Plan status values: CREATED, APPROVED, BOOKED, BROKEN, read from LOV-PLAN-STATUS with the version in force; any other code is held as an exception and never interpreted | LOV-PLAN-STATUS (TSD P3 v3 T3.2); legacy BR3; DP-07 |
| BR4 | A plan marked broken while the case is in the cure period marks the plan broken and records the break | R-RES-29, R-RES-30 |
| BR5 | A second break bars a further restructure | R-RES-31; parameter restructure.max_breaks |
| BR6 | A case on the litigation route with a broken plan returns to the legal route | R-LIT-02 |
| BR7 | When ACE returns no status, the last known status and its date stay on the case | FEAT-CHO-02; VR-P2-001-1 |
| BR8 | A decision that cannot be written to the decision log does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR9 | A repeat of the same status and date raises no event | R-UNI-40 |
| BR10 | R-RES-29, R-RES-30, R-RES-31 and R-LIT-02 are rows of package RESTRUCTURE, evaluated by the case side with the version in force; this service neither evaluates nor names them | D-RCV-36 T5, T6, T7; DP-04 |
| BR11 | No RESTRUCTURE version in force is a refusal (`NoPackageInForce`), never a default move | R-UNI-41; D-RCV-36 T7 |
| BR12 | The read writes nothing: no table row, no outbox row, no decision record, no cache of the answer; a screen refresh and a rerun have no effect on any stored value | Legacy guardrail "a read of the plan status writes nothing"; DP-01 |
| BR13 | `rwb_integration` holds no grant on `recovery` and no foreign key into any other schema; the case is reached by reference through its owner and the plan through the ACE interface | ADR-010; DP-01; Arch v5 slide 41 |
| BR14 | One base and one queue: the operation is served on `/api/recovery/integration/v1` and the service runs on the task queue of `rwb-integration`; no Schedule and no workflow is created for this key | DP-13; DP-10; Arch v5 slides 41 and 44 |
| BR15 | No business value in code: the status list, the batch size, the timeout, the flag and the breaker thresholds are rows, parameters and values, read through their owners | FSD P2 Integration v3 BR-P2-007; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR16 | No personal data and no account number in an event, an activity input, a log line or a test report: the case reference, the plan reference, the status code, the flag and the counters only | Arch v5 slide 42; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR17 | The status answer is either live from ACE now or absent; this service never answers a stored value and never reports `live` true for a value it did not read | Legacy plan-status resource; RWB-P3-E2002-APP |
| BR18 | The case record reads the plan section only through the gateway-bff composite route, never by the browser calling this service directly | DP-19 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Live answered | ACE answers a plan in LOV-PLAN-STATUS | The account of the case has a plan | Live answered (no change; nothing written) |
| Live answered | ACE answers an unknown code | The code is not in LOV-PLAN-STATUS | Live answered, unknown code, counted and never interpreted |
| Live answered | ACE answers no plan | The account of the case has no plan | No plan (200, `live` true, plan fields absent) |
| Any | The case holds no account | There is nothing to ask ACE about | No plan (200, `live` false, plan fields absent, no ACE call) |
| Live answered | ACE does not answer inside the budget | Timeout, connection error or open breaker | Unavailable (503, MSG-GEN-006) |
| Unavailable | The next call | ACE answers inside the budget | Live answered |
| Any | The caller holds no Case record R | The authorise contract refuses | Refused (403, MSG-P4-002) |
| Any | The case is outside the caller's scope, or unknown | The scope check or the case read refuses | Refused (404, MSG-P4-003) |
| Any | The flag is off | `rwb.integration.ace-plan-status` is off | Stored only (200, `live` false, no ACE call) |

These are answer states of one operation, not case states: the case status stays "In progress" and the route state does not move here. The route states of the legacy story — `PLAN_CURE_PERIOD` to `PLAN_BROKEN` to `BACK_TO_ROUTE_DECISION`, and `LIT_ROUTE_APPROVED` to `NOTICE_GENERATED` — are `recovery_case.route_state` writes of rwb-case, caused by the evaluation of package RESTRUCTURE and proved in RWB-P3-E2002-APP.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-integration service identity (the rwb-integration login, DP-02) | Calls the ACE common module; reads the case, the reference data and the parameters; checks the right and the scope; answers the plan status; writes nothing |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the plan status of cases in scope (Case record R) |
| RW-RESTRUCT, restructuring officer | Reads the plan status of cases in scope (Case record R) |
| RW-REFADM | Holds no Case record right; refused on the read operation with MSG-P4-002 |
| rwb-case, through its contract | Answers the case and its account numbers, and owns the stored plan status, the route state, the task and the timer |
| rwb-access, through its contract | Answers the Case record right and the scope |
| rwb-case reference data and parameters, through their contracts | Answer LOV-PLAN-STATUS and the two settings, with their versions in force |
| The ACE common module | Answers `statusFor` for the account numbers asked, within the 2,000 ms budget |
| gateway-bff | Composes the case record plan section from this operation and the rwb-case stored answer |

The service runs as the rwb-integration login (DP-02). The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0654; ASM-1099).

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-CAS-001 | recovery_case, through the rwb-case contract | id (the path reference) | Read |
| DF-CAS-026 | case_account, through the rwb-case contract | account_key (the join key of DL21) | Read |
| DF-CAS-009, DF-CAS-010 | recovery_case, through the rwb-case contract | owner_user_id, queue_id (the scope facts of the authorise answer) | Read |
| DF-REF-159 to DF-REF-184 | reference_row, through the rwb-case reference-data contract | LOV-PLAN-STATUS with its version in force | Read |
| DF-REF-132 to DF-REF-158 | parameter_catalog, parameter_value, through the rwb-case parameters contract | `rwb.ace.plan.batch-size`, `rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms` and their versions in force | Read |
| No field ID | The ACE common module interface | planRef, accountNo, status, statusDate of the plan of the case | Read, from `RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor`; not a table and not a view |
| None | Any table of `rwb_integration` | No field | Write none |

The plan fields `planRef`, `status`, `statusDate` and the flag `live` are read from the ACE common module interface and are not read from any table; the account number used for the join is `case_account.account_key` read through the rwb-case contract. The plan fields of the case record (DF-CAS-046 `plan_ref`, DF-CAS-047 `plan_status`, DF-CAS-048 `plan_status_as_of`) are written only by rwb-case in RWB-P3-E2002-APP and are not written, cached or copied here. No ACE row is copied into `rwb_integration`, and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01).

The plan reference, the status and the status date come from the ACE interface and carry no field ID in the Logical Data Model, because the interface is a module interface and not a view (INT-34; ADR-010). The element names of the interface answer are the ones the legacy story publishes: planRef, accountNo, status, statusDate. The types, lengths and null rules of the remaining interface elements are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0654; ASM-1102).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/integration/v1`; owner rwb-integration (P2).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/plan-status` | The live ACE restructure plan status of the case: `planRef`, `accountNo`, `status`, `statusDate`, `live` (true when read from ACE now) and `messageCode` | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable: the call writes nothing and answers the same values for the same ACE state |

Response: the legacy PlanStatus shape with `accountNo` added, because the ACE answer carries the account and the case side joins on it. Errors: 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Case record R (MSG-P4-002); 404 unknown case or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 503 the ACE common module, the reference data, the parameters or the authorise contract did not answer inside the budget (MSG-GEN-006). `live` is true on every 200 answer that read ACE, because such an answer means ACE answered, and false on the flag-off answer, which carries no plan because no call was made; `live` false with MSG-P2-008 is otherwise the stored answer of rwb-case and reaches the merged screen from there. `messageCode` is empty on every answer of this service, because this service holds no stored value to date; MSG-P2-008 is set by rwb-case on its stored answer (GAP-0654; ASM-1101).

The operation name, path and base are the ones the Ownership Map and TSD P2 v3 API-P2-010 fix, moved to the integration base under DP-13. The JSON field names are the legacy PlanStatus names; the `accountNo` field and the `messageCode` rule are the two places where this story fixes a shape the API Specification leaves open (GAP-0654; ASM-1101).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11).

| Method | Path or operation | Owner | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | the case read of the rwb-case contract, by case reference | P3 rwb-case | The account numbers of the case, the owner and the queue, and the scope facts |
| GET | the reference-data read of the rwb-case contract (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | P3 rwb-case | LOV-PLAN-STATUS with the version in force |
| GET | the parameters read of the rwb-case contract (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) | P3 rwb-case | `rwb.ace.plan.batch-size` and `rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms` with the version in force |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The Case record right and the case scope, cached per session |
| Call | `RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor(List<String> accountNos)` of the ACE common module (INT-34) | ACE team, the ACE common module | The plans of the account numbers, in batches of 500 within a 2,000 ms budget |

The three rwb-case reads and the authorise call are the published contracts of the case and access services, and this story builds against their fakes; RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are the two of the contract-dependency row this story uses, and RWB-P3-E2042-CON is the third of that row and is consumed by the case side, not here. The case read and the authorise call are the case baseline and the platform guard. The paths of the case read and of the authorise call, and the element names of the reference-data and parameter answers, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0654; ASM-1103): the case read is taken from the case contract baseline, the authorise path from the access contract, and the two reference shapes from the P3 contract baseline when it is published.

The ACE interface is a published module interface and not a view: it is not on a `/api/recovery/...` base, it is not reached through gateway-bff, and `rwb_integration` holds no grant on `recovery` (INT-34; ADR-010; DP-05).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This story publishes no event type and writes no outbox row: a read takes no decision and changes no state. `rwb.integration.events.v1` carries FileDelivered and FileFailed, which belong to the outbound-file stories of this service, and `rwb.decision-record.v1` carries DecisionRecorded from the services that take the decision — here, rwb-case on each route move (DP-03, DP-09).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The operation is called on the request path by rwb-case's activity and by gateway-bff; the service subscribes to no topic for this story, keeps no projection and holds no inbox row.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None owned by this story. The daily step is `PlanStatusStep` of DailyCaseRun in rwb-case, and its `readPlanStatus` activity is the caller of this operation on the task queue `rwb-case` (RWB-P3-E2002-APP). This service registers no workflow and no activity for this key: the batching, the 2,000 ms budget and the breaker run inside the request on the service's own worker, which RWB-P2-E2002-OPS deploys. The integration harness lists a "plan-status step" on `rwb-integration`; that row conflicts with the sibling story and with the job map, where JOB-02 is rwb-case's, and the conflict is carried in the gap row rather than resolved by creating a second step (GAP-0654).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Schedule is created by this story or by this key: the legacy plan-status step of JOB-02 is a step of the event-started DailyCaseRun in rwb-case (DP-10), and this service answers a synchronous read. A Schedule here would be a second daily run over the same cases, which the job map does not allow (Arch v5 slide 44).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| interface_config | rwb_integration | P2 (Ownership Map; Arch v5 slide 41) | Not used: the ACE endpoint is configuration of the deployment, not an interface row |
| outbound_item | rwb_integration | P2 (Ownership Map; Arch v5 slide 41) | Not used: this story builds and sends no file |
| job_catalog | rwb_integration | P2 (Ownership Map; TSD P2 v3 T3.1) | Not used: no job is catalogued for this key, because no P2 Schedule exists |
| outbox_event, processed_event, outbox_delivery, idempotency_key | rwb_integration | PLT library, created in `rwb_integration` (DP-09) | Present from the service baseline and unused: a read writes no outbox row and consumes no event |

This story writes no table and adds no column; it adds no migration (DP-15). `rwb_integration` reads no table of another service, holds no foreign key across services and holds no grant on `recovery` (DP-01, BR13).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case WireMock | The P3 case contract | Case "RW-2026-000310" with account "A-0310" in PLAN_CURE_PERIOD with break count 0, the case of AC8 owned by another person, an unknown case (404) and a case with no account |
| rwb-case reference-data WireMock | The P3 reference-data contract | LOV-PLAN-STATUS with CREATED, APPROVED, BOOKED and BROKEN and its version, a version without "SUSPENDED" for AC5, and one answer beyond 2 s |
| rwb-case parameters WireMock | The P3 parameters contract | `rwb.ace.plan.batch-size` 500 and `rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms` 2000 with their versions, and one answer beyond 2 s |
| rwb-access WireMock | The P4 contract | Case record R granted in scope, refused for RW-REFADM, and a case outside an Own scope (404) |
| ACE common module stub behind this service | `RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor` | "APPROVED" with 2026-12-10, "BROKEN" with 2026-12-14, no plan for "A-0310", a 3-second answer, "SUSPENDED", and an answer for more than 500 accounts that forces two batches |
| rwb-case and rwb-decision WireMock | The P3 and P7 contracts | The evaluation answer of AC1 and the move answers of AC2, so the criteria that end in the case can be driven against the fakes; the parts that are not this slice's are asserted as calls, not as writes |

Every fake is generated from the owning service's published OpenAPI document where one exists, and the drift test fails when a fake answers a shape or an error this story does not declare.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 provided, 4 consumed | The plan-status read provided; the case read, the reference-data read, the parameters read and the authorise call consumed; one hop, 2 s timeout each, GET retried once with jitter |
| Kafka | None published, none consumed | A read publishes no event and subscribes to none (DP-09) |
