The eight criteria above are new and test only this deliverable: the resolved permission view, the authorise decision for the plan-status read and the access entry per decision. The legacy criteria of RWB-E2-002 are owned elsewhere: AC1 to AC9 are carried by rwb-integration (RWB-P2-E2002-APP), the stored status, the route moves and the rules by rwb-case (RWB-P3-E2002-APP) and the package by rwb-decision (RWB-P7-E2002-APP). The legacy exception X6 (a case outside the scope, MSG-P4-003) is answered here by AC4, and the legacy exception X7 (a role without the Case record right, MSG-P4-002) by AC3 and AC5; legacy test case TC-E2-002-10 is answered here.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The right comes from the permission matrix version in force, unioned across the roles the caller holds; a caller whose roles hold no Case record R is refused with MSG-P4-002 and no case data | FSD P4 A2.4 VR-P4-004-1; TSD P4 T6.1; DP-08 |
| BR2 | A case is in scope when the attributes the request carries satisfy the caller's `default_scope` in force — OWN, TEAM, REGION or ALL — read through the reference-data contract; no scope value is written in code | FSD P4 A2.14 VR-P4-014-1; TSD P4 T3.2 LOV-SCOPE; DP-07 |
| BR3 | A case that is absent, or outside the caller's scope, is answered 404 with MSG-P4-003 and no case data, no plan reference, no plan status and no status date, so the answer never confirms that a case or a plan exists | FSD P4 A2.14 AC-EXC-P4-014-01; legacy AC8 |
| BR4 | Every decision, granted or refused, writes one access entry with decision code `AC-READ` or `AC-DENY`, the actor, the case ID when the decision is on a case, the area, the right, the field IDs and the time, before the answer is returned | FSD P4 A2.7 AC-P4-007-01; FEAT-ACA-07 |
| BR5 | The access entry is a decision-record entry written through the local library and relayed on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; it is never a new Kafka event and never a new topic | FSD P4 A2.8; DP-03; Architecture v5 slide 20 |
| BR6 | A read that cannot be recorded returns nothing: 503 MSG-P7-003 and no case data, and an incident is raised | FSD P4 A2.7 AC-EXC-P4-007-03; R-UNI-39 |
| BR7 | An answer is cached only under the matrix version it was decided on; a change of version drops the entry in the transaction that writes the new version, with no restart and no clock | Architecture v5 slides 14 and 43; DP-11 |
| BR8 | The case attributes for the scope test arrive in the request and a missing attribute never decides an allow; no table of `rwb_case`, no rwb-case operation and no `v_ace_*` view is read, and nothing is copied into `rwb_access` | DP-01, DP-05, DP-11; ownership map (case to P3, ACE views to P1) |
| BR9 | No masking row applies to the plan-status panel: the field IDs `DF-CAS-046`, `DF-CAS-047` and `DF-CAS-048` name the plan reference, the status and the status date, none is a personal field, and no mask answer is produced or owed | FSD P4 A2.5; TSD P4 T3.1 `masking_rule`; NFR-040 |
| BR10 | The entry names IDs and field IDs only: no plan reference, no plan status, no status date, no amount, no account number and no personal value is written on it | FSD P4 A2.7; DF-DEC-002, DF-DEC-014; NFR-039 |
| BR11 | Roles, capability areas, letters, scope values, the matrix version and the field IDs are data rows and list values; no role code, area, letter or scope value is written in Java | FSD P4 BR-P4-004; TSD P4 T3.1 and T3.2; principle 1 |
| BR12 | The plan read, the stored status and its date, the route moves and the rules R-RES-29, R-RES-30, R-RES-31 and R-LIT-02 are not decided here: this story grants or refuses the read and records it | Architecture v5 slides 41 and 44; DP-01 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-access`:

- BR1 is a read of `permission` for the caller's roles at the `matrix_version` in force, with the letters held as the five-character field of TSD P4 T3.1 and the answer naming the version it used.
- BR2 is the scope rule of `ScopeRule`, comparing the attributes of the request with the `default_scope` value read through DP-07; the scope names are list values, never Java constants, and the attribute names of a request are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0908; ASM-1628).
- BR3 is the only refusal that hides a case, and it is deliberate: MSG-P4-003 echoes no case fact and the entry still names the case ID, so the audit can see the attempt.
- BR4 and BR6 are one `RecordAndApply` transaction: the record is written first, the answer is returned after it commits, and a failure answers 503 and changes nothing (X4).
- BR7 is a cache keyed on `matrix_version`; the cache size is a parameter of DP-06, and no lifetime in seconds is used, so no answer survives a version change.
- BR8 is the reason there is no repository for a case: the service holds `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, the decision record and the outbox, and nothing else.
- BR9 and BR10 are visible in the code review and in the entry itself: the three field IDs appear as identifiers, and no value of them appears anywhere in the service.

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status, no plan status and no route state: the case and its stored plan status are P3's, the live plan read is P2's, and the rules that move a case on a broken plan are rwb-decision's package and rwb-case's move (TSD P4 T4: no case state machine of its own). This story runs no workflow, owns no Schedule and starts no timer.

The only states this story has are the states of its answer and of its record, which it does not persist beyond the record:

| Answer state | When | What the caller gets | Record written |
|---|---|---|---|
| Granted | The caller holds Case record R and the case is in scope | The decision code, the scope it used, the matrix version and the entry reference; no mask answer, because none is owed | `AC-READ` |
| Refused, no right | No role of the caller holds Case record R | 403 MSG-P4-002, no case data | `AC-DENY` |
| Not found | The caller holds the right and the case is absent or outside the scope, or an attribute is missing | 404 MSG-P4-003, no case data | `AC-DENY` |
| Not answered | The record cannot be written, or the policy cannot be read | 503, no case data | None; the failure is raised as an incident |

A matrix version moves from LOADED to APPROVED to IN_FORCE to SUPERSEDED or ROLLED_BACK in the load path (TSD P4 T3.2 LOV-VERSION-STATUS); this story only reads the version in force, answers from it and drops its cached answer when it changes. The plan status values CREATED, APPROVED, BOOKED and BROKEN are rwb-integration's and rwb-case's and are never interpreted here: this story carries the field ID `DF-CAS-047`, never the value.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-access service identity (the rwb-access login, DP-02) | Resolves the letters and the scope, decides, writes the access entry and the outbox row |
| Decision-record library identity | Writes the local entry with its hash link and relays it on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (Decision log C, DP-03) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Case record R with default scope OWN: reads the plan status of a case it owns |
| RW-RESTRUCT, restructuring officer | Case record R with the role default scope: reads the plan status of a case in that scope |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Case record R with default scope ALL: reads any case's plan status, including the entries of this capability through the access-log search of RWB-P4-E1039-APP |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | No CASE_RECORD row: the plan-status read is refused with MSG-P4-002 |
| RW-SECADM, security administrator | Puts a matrix version in force through the load path stories; this story reads the version in force and answers from it |
| SY-CASEWF and the other service identities | Ask the same question for their own service; the roles of a service identity are checked as a person's are |

Reading is the whole of this story: it grants or refuses a read and writes the record of it. It changes no case, no plan, no route state and no policy row; a policy row changes only through the load path of RWB-P4-AD002-APP. The roles, areas and letters above are rows of the pack and are not fixed in code; no role in this story may grant itself a letter.

The per-service login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0909; ASM-1629); the story refers to "the rwb-access login (DP-02)" until the platform DB story fixes it.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Table in rwb_access | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039 | `role` | id, role_code, role_name, role_class, default_scope, entra_group | Read |
| DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044 | `permission` | id, role_id, capability_area, letters, matrix_version | Read |
| DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204 | `masking_rule` | role_code, field_id, unmasked, masking_version, valid_from, valid_to | Read; no row covers `DF-CAS-046`, `DF-CAS-047` or `DF-CAS-048`, and none is needed |
| DF-REF-027 to DF-REF-033 | `lov_value` | LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-SCOPE values, read through the reference-data contract of DP-07 | Read through the contract; the table is P3's |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | access entry (local decision record, DP-03) | the `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entries: decision code, actor, case ID, actions, decided at, hash chain, idempotency key | Write |
| DF-DEC-002 | access entry (local decision record) | case_id | Write |
| DF-DEC-014 | access entry (local decision record) | actions (area, right, field IDs, result) | Write |
| (outbox) | outbox library table in `rwb_access` | the `DecisionRecorded` row | Write |
| (inbox) | `processed_event` | event_id, consumer, processed_at | Write |
| DF-CAS-046, DF-CAS-047, DF-CAS-048 | case (named in the authorise request and in the entry, owned by rwb-case) | plan_ref, plan_status, plan_status_as_of | Not read and not written; carried as field IDs on the entry |
| DF-CAS-001, DF-CAS-009, DF-CAS-010 | case attributes in the authorise request (owned by rwb-case) | case ID, owner, queue and team for the scope test | Read from the request; nothing copied |

No case row, no plan row and no ACE row is copied into `rwb_access`: the case attributes for the scope test arrive with the authorise request on each decision, and the plan reference and the plan status stay with rwb-integration and rwb-case. No plan reference, plan status, status date, amount, account number or personal value is written on the access entry; the entry holds IDs and field IDs only. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None new. The decisions are served through the operations of RWB-P4-E1037-CON on base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, owner rwb-access (P4), unchanged in path and error shape. This slice adds no path, no query parameter and no response field, and decides the following behind them:

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | Decide the plan-status read for a case and a field list, with the scope test on the request attributes and the access entry | Any authenticated caller with a Workbench role | Idempotent by identity, area, right, case reference and field list within the matrix version in force |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions` | The caller's resolved roles, the CASE_RECORD letters in force, the scope and the matrix version | Authenticated caller, own record only | Not applicable |

Request for `/authorise`: the caller identity from the session, the capability area `CASE_RECORD`, the right `R`, the case reference, the plan reference, the field IDs and the case attributes for the scope test (owner, queue, team). Answer: the decision code (`AC-READ` or `AC-DENY`), the matrix version, the scope result and the access-entry reference. The field names of the request and of the answer are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0908; ASM-1628). Errors: 401 no Workbench role (MSG-P4-001), 403 no letter for the area or right (MSG-P4-002), 404 case absent or out of scope (MSG-P4-003), 503 decision record unwritable (MSG-P7-003).

The same service surface carries `GET /me/session` (TSD P4 API-P4-012, the resolved session), `GET /admin/roles` (TSD P4 API-P4-007, the role list with permissions and scope), `/masking-policies`, `GET /doa-limits` and `GET /admin/access-log`; those belong to other P4 stories (RWB-P4-E1037-APP, RWB-P4-E1022-APP, RWB-P4-E1039-APP, RWB-P4-E2013-APP) and this story changes none of them. The TSD appendix names the resolved view as `GET /me/session` and has no `/me/permissions` entry, so the resolved view is answered behind `/me/permissions` under R-PREC and the session read keeps its own story and its own shape (GAP-0908; ASM-1628).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The case attributes and the plan reference for the decision arrive in the authorise request, built by the caller from its own rows; rwb-access calls no service at run time, and the one hop and the 2 s budget of DP-11 apply to the inbound call.

The rwb-integration contract (RWB-P2-E2002-CON) is consumed as a fixture only: the plan-status envelope names case `RW-2026-000310`, plan reference `TDR-SYN-0310`, status `APPROVED` and status date `2026-12-10`, and its plan reference is what the caller passes in the authorise request. rwb-access calls no rwb-integration operation, reads no ACE view and reads no `rwb_case` row: the reference-data values reach it through the client library of rwb-case (DP-07).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 | caseId, or the actor for an entry with no case | decision code, area, right, field IDs, matrix version, record reference, business date |

The event is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the answer and relayed with the CloudEvents envelope; no personal data is carried (DP-09). The access log is never published as its own event: it is the decision-record entry of this service (DP-03). `AccessPolicyChanged` on `rwb.access.events.v1` belongs to the story that puts a matrix version in force — the load path of RWB-P4-AD002-APP — and is not republished here; `DoaLimitChanged` belongs to the delegation slice of RWB-P4-E2013-APP.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. This slice consumes no topic: the decision is served from the matrix version in force on each call, and a change of the version drops the cached answer in the transaction that writes the new version. `AccessPolicyChanged` is published for the other services' caches and for gateway-bff; this service does not consume its own outbox.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The decision is a synchronous REST call in the caller's thread, and this story runs no workflow and registers no activity on `rwb-access` (Temporal and Drools design slide 11: each service has a worker, and this capability needs none). The Drools kit is applied only as a read of the evaluated policy rows: the letters of a capability area are rows, not a decision table, and the RESTRUCTURE rows R-RES-29, R-RES-30, R-RES-31 and R-LIT-02 are evaluated in rwb-case and rwb-decision, never here (DP-04).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The daily plan-status step is JOB-02 Case creation's, owned by rwb-case (Architecture v5 slide 44) with the plan-status read carried by RWB-P2-E2002-APP, and the six-monthly access review list (JOB-18) belongs to RWB-P4-AD008-APP. This story holds no Schedule of its own.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Recovery roles as data, with role class and default scope |
| `permission` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Capability area, letters and matrix version per role |
| `masking_rule` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Read only; no row covers the three plan-status field IDs, because none is a personal field |
| access entry (local decision record) | P4 rows in `rwb_access`, written through the P7 decision-record library | The access log of this capability as `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entries (DP-03) |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_access` | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects (DP-09) |

`role_conflict` is the same service's table and is read by the sign-in path, not by this story; `delegation_limit` is served by RWB-P4-E2013-APP and is not read here. rwb-access reads no table of another service and holds no foreign key across services (DP-01); the central ledger copy of the entries is written in `rwb_decision` from the topic by RWB-P7-E1027-CON.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-integration fixture (RWB-P2-E2002-CON) | The P2 contract of this legacy key | The plan-status envelope for case `RW-2026-000310` with plan reference `TDR-SYN-0310`, status `APPROVED` and status date `2026-12-10`; replayed for the granted and the refused cases |
| RWB-P4-E1037-CON fake | The P4 authorise, resolved-view and masking contract | `/authorise` and `/me/permissions`, with a granted case, a refused case and an out-of-scope case |
| decision-record library stub | DP-03 | A healthy chain and outbox, and a stopped chain for the 503 path (TC-E2-002-11) |
| reference-data fake | DP-07 | LOV-CAPABILITY with `CASE_RECORD` and LOV-SCOPE with OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL, with the version in force |

The exact request and answer shapes of `/authorise` and `/me/permissions` are stubbed from the published fixture of RWB-P4-E1037-CON; their field list is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0908; ASM-1628).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 new provided (2 existing operations implemented), 0 consumed | The decisions are served on `/authorise` and `/me/permissions` of RWB-P4-E1037-CON on `/api/recovery/access/v1`; the case attributes arrive in the request, one hop within 2 s |
| Kafka | 1 published, 0 consumed | `rwb.decision-record.v1` published; no topic consumed and no access event on `rwb.access.events.v1` from this story |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, no activity and no Schedule on `rwb-access` |
| File | None | This story reads and writes no file |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`, module `caserecord`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.caserecord`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

This is a secondary slice: it adds no new build dependency of its own (metadata "Depends on (build)" = None, "Contract dependencies" = RWB-P2-E2002-CON), and it builds against the rwb-access baseline and its contract fake, with the platform contract libraries and the P4 contract stories already delivered by the baseline. DP-05 applies as a prohibition — no ACE view is read here, and the plan reference arrives in the authorise request from the caller. DP-04 applies as a statement that the letters of a capability area are rows, not a decision table, and that the RESTRUCTURE rows are evaluated in rwb-case and rwb-decision. DP-06 carries the feature switch and the cache size as parameters, so no value is a Java constant. DP-10 applies as a statement that the daily plan-status step and the plan timer are not this service's: JOB-02 is rwb-case's with its plan-status read in RWB-P2-E2002-APP, and the only Schedule on this service is JOB-18 of RWB-P4-AD008-APP. DP-19 is the route that renders the answer on SCR-03.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AuthoriseController | Controller | `POST /authorise` with validation and the problem mapping for 401, 403, 404 and 503 |
| PermissionController | Controller | `GET /me/permissions` for the caller's own record only |
| PermissionViewService | Service | Resolves the roles, the CASE_RECORD letters at the matrix version in force and the scope into the one answer the panel reads |
| AccessDecisionService | Service | Right, then scope, for one request; one answer and one record in that order |
| ScopeRule | Service | Compares the case attributes of the request with the `default_scope` value in force; refuses an allow when an attribute is missing |
| PolicyRepository | Repository | Reads `role`, `permission` and `masking_rule` at the version in force in `rwb_access`; reads no other schema |
| AccessRecordWriter | Service | Writes the `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entries through the decision-record library, first in the transaction, and the outbox row |
| PolicyCache | Cache | Holds an answer under the matrix version it was decided on and drops it on a version change |
| ReferenceCatalog | Service | Reads LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-SCOPE through the reference-data contract; no area or scope value in Java |

**Database and migrations**

- Reads `role`, `permission` and `masking_rule` in schema `rwb_access`; writes the access entry of the decision-record library and the outbox row.
- Migration in this story: `V2002_1__plan_status_access.sql` adds the index on `permission (capability_area, matrix_version, role_id)` used by the letter read and the index on the access entry `(actor, decided_at)` used by the access-log search of RWB-P4-E1039-APP. The tables arrive with the `rwb_access` baseline; no column is added for case, plan or customer data.
- No row of `role`, `permission` or `masking_rule` is written by this story: the matrix version is put in force by the load path of RWB-P4-AD002-APP.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The policy pack slice in force at matrix version `PM-2026.12`: CASE_RECORD R for `RW-CASEOWN`, `RW-RESTRUCT` and `RW-AUDIT`; no CASE_RECORD row for `RW-REFADM`; default scope OWN for `RW-CASEOWN`, OWN for `RW-RESTRUCT` and ALL for `RW-AUDIT`. The slice is read as data, and the TSD matrix has no Case record column, so the letters are confirmed with the matrix owner (GAP-0907; ASM-1630).
- No masking row for `DF-CAS-046`, `DF-CAS-047` or `DF-CAS-048`: none of the three is a personal field.
- LOV-CAPABILITY (the 14 capability areas, including `CASE_RECORD`) and LOV-SCOPE (OWN, TEAM, REGION, ALL) through the reference-data contract of DP-07.
- The cache size is a parameter of the parameters contract (DP-06); no cache lifetime in seconds is used, because the cache is keyed on the matrix version.
- The feature switch is `rwb.access.plan-status-authorise`, read as a parameter through the parameters contract: off means the decision is refused closed and the caller is told the capability is not open, never allowed by default.
- The login is the rwb-access login (DP-02): Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0909; ASM-1629).

**Build steps**

1. `PolicyRepository` and `PermissionViewService` over the matrix version in force, with a test per letter set and a test that the resolved view names roles, letters, scope and version in one answer; no role, area or letter in code.
2. `AccessDecisionService` with the letter union and the default-deny path; tests for AC3.
3. `ScopeRule` over the request attributes, with the not-found, the missing-attribute and the no-partial-allow tests; tests for AC4 and AC8.
4. The no-masking statement in the answer and the entry: a test that the three field IDs produce no mask marker and read no masking row; test for AC7.
5. `AccessRecordWriter` with the entry before the answer, the `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` codes, IDs and field IDs only, and the 503 when the record cannot be written; tests for AC2, AC5 and TC-E2-002-11.
6. `PolicyCache` with the version-keyed answer and the drop on a version change; tests for AC6.
7. The outbox relay for `DecisionRecorded`, with the topic name and the payload carrying no plan value and no personal value; test the envelope with the contract fake.
8. The contract-fake run of the whole capability against RWB-P2-E2002-CON and the decision-record fake, so the story builds before the other slices of the key exist in the environment.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.access.plan-status-authorise`, read as a parameter; off refuses closed, allows nothing and changes no schema, so a rollback is one value.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P2-E2002-CON and RWB-P4-E1037-CON stay green, and a SIT week shows every plan-status read decided with one entry, every refusal answered with MSG-P4-002 or MSG-P4-003 and no case data, no access entry carrying a plan reference, a plan status, a status date or a personal value, and a matrix version change taking effect with no restart.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | The token carries no Workbench role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. | The access check before this story's answer (X6) |
| MSG-P4-002 | No role of the caller holds the right in the capability area | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, on the refusal of BR1 (AC3) |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is absent or outside the caller's scope, or an attribute is missing | This case is not in your scope. | This story, on the refusal of BR2 (AC4, AC8) |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on every answer (X4) |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A list the answer needs is not available | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. | This story, on a reference-list failure (X5) |
| MSG-P2-008 | The plan status shown is the stored value, on the screen this decision guards | The ACE plan status is from {date}. Today's status was not returned. | rwb-integration and rwb-case, on the panel answer; copied here unchanged because the screen this decision guards shows it |

For MSG-P4-002 the {action} value is the action the caller attempted, for example "read the plan status"; for MSG-P4-003 no case fact, no plan reference and no plan status is echoed, because the message must not confirm that a case or a plan exists. Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId`, the text with its placeholders filled and the instance of the request; the Thai text follows DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

This story builds no screen. SCR-03 Case record and its plan status panel are served by the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 (RWB-PLT-N001-CON), which calls rwb-case for the case and the stored plan status, rwb-integration for the live plan status and rwb-access for the resolved view and the decision — one hop each, in parallel, then merges the answers into the screen model; the panel itself, the plan read and the stored fallback are RWB-P3-E2002-APP's and RWB-P2-E2002-APP's.

What this story decides for SCR-03 is whether the panel may be assembled at all, and what each state shows:

| Screen | State | What the answer decides |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-03 Case record, plan status panel | Read only, granted | The panel is assembled with the plan reference, the status and the status date; the fields this story names are rendered as they arrive, and no masking marker is applied because none is owed |
| SCR-03 Case record, plan status panel | Status from the stored value | The same grant applies; MSG-P2-008 with its date is rwb-integration's and rwb-case's message, and the grant is unchanged |
| SCR-03 Case record, plan status panel | A role without Case record R | The panel is not assembled; the page shows MSG-P4-002 and no case fact, and one `AC-DENY` entry exists |
| SCR-03 Case record, plan status panel | Case outside the scope | The page shows MSG-P4-003, the same page a case that does not exist shows, and no case fact, plan reference or plan status |
| SCR-03 Case record, plan status panel | Not available | The page shows MSG-P7-003 where the record could not be written, or MSG-GEN-006 where a list could not be read, and no case fact |

The panel shows the plan reference, the status and the status date only; no personal field is on it for this capability, so nothing is masked and no masking row is read. The screen field list of the composite route, its merge order, its field-level masking and its route specification are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0909; ASM-1631).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: roles, capability areas, letters, scope values, field IDs and the matrix version are data rows and list values read with the version in force. No role code, area, letter or scope value appears in Java.
- No personal data in events, logs, workflow inputs or tests. This story writes case IDs, role codes and field IDs only; the access entry never carries a plan reference, a plan status, a status date, a name, an address, an identity number, an account number or an amount. Test data uses synthetic keys (`RW-2026-000310`, `TDR-SYN-0310`, `A-0310`).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the owner's `v_ace_*` views, and this service reads neither: the plan reference and the case attributes for the scope test arrive in the authorise request from the caller, and rwb-access holds no ACE grant and queries no view.
- No cross-schema read (DP-01): `recovery_case`, `case_account`, `timer`, `task`, `rule_row`, `decision_log_entry` and the `v_ace_*` views are never queried; the case facts arrive in the request and the policy is the service's own.
- One writer for the policy: only the load path stories of this service write a role, a permission or a masking row; this story reads the version in force and answers from it.
- One evaluator per concern: the letters of an area are versioned rows, not a decision table, and the RESTRUCTURE rows R-RES-29, R-RES-30, R-RES-31 and R-LIT-02 stay in rwb-decision's package and rwb-case's move. rwb-access holds no route table, no DRL source and no workbook (DP-04).
- The record is written before the answer: a failure answers 503 with no case data and raises an incident, so no plan-status read is unlogged (BR4, BR6).
- The answer is idempotent for a matrix version: the same question under the same version returns the same answer, and the cache is dropped on the version change rather than on a timer.
- The feature switch refuses closed and changes no schema, and it never widens a scope or a letter.

##### 19. Out of scope

- The plan read itself, `RestructurePlanQuery`, the 2-second timeout, the batches and the live answer: rwb-integration (RWB-P2-E2002-APP), with its contract in RWB-P2-E2002-CON.
- The stored plan status, the `plan_ref`, `plan_status` and `plan_status_as_of` columns, the daily compare, the route moves, the queues and the timers of the broken plan: rwb-case (RWB-P3-E2002-APP).
- The RESTRUCTURE rows R-RES-29, R-RES-30, R-RES-31 and R-LIT-02, the package version and the central ledger entries they produce: rwb-decision (RWB-P7-E2002-APP) and RWB-P3-E2042-APP.
- The end-to-end proof of these values across the four services: RWB-ITG-E2002-ITG.
- The plan read path of the monolith, `GET /cases/{caseId}/plan-status`, which belongs to rwb-integration and rwb-case and is not served here.
- The composite route itself, the SCR-03 layout, the plan status panel and its states: RWB-P3-E2002-APP and RWB-PLT-N001-CON.
- Loading, approving and rolling back a matrix version, and publishing `AccessPolicyChanged`: RWB-P4-AD002-APP and the load path of this service.

- Break-glass access and its review, the six-monthly access review list (JOB-18, RWB-P4-AD008-APP), and every other job, workflow and Schedule of this service.
- The Helm chart, the Kafka subscription values, the metrics, the alerts and the runbook of this capability (an OPS story of this legacy key).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the rwb-decision slice of RWB-E2-002, answering which version of package `RESTRUCTURE` is in force for a business date with its state, checksum and rows `R-RES-29`, `R-RES-30`, `R-RES-31` and `R-LIT-02`, and collecting the route moves a broken plan causes into one hash-chained ledger entry per case, business date and rule identity, carrying the rule, the version `RES-2026.12`, the ACE plan status and its date, the final call, the actions and the actor, read back with `chainVerified`. The plan read, the stored status, the route move, the task, the timer, the rights and the scope check stay outside this service. Secondary slice: it owns no legacy criterion. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN), a team manager (RW-TEAMMGR) and an internal auditor (RW-AUDIT)**, I want **the RESTRUCTURE version that was in force on a business date, with its checksum and the rows that decide a plan, and one hash-chained record of every route move a broken plan caused, with the rule, the version, the ACE plan status and its date**, so that **a plan that broke and the route the case took can be explained from one read the next morning, and no service can evaluate a rule version this service never promoted**.

Inside `rwb-decision`, schema `rwb_decision`, base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, topic `rwb.decision.events.v1`, queue `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`:

- The registry: `rule_package`, `rule_package_version` and `rule_row` hold package `RESTRUCTURE`, version `RES-2026.12` in force with its checksum and rows `R-RES-29`, `R-RES-30`, `R-RES-31` and `R-LIT-02`. The version answer names only a version in force; the evaluation runs in the service that owns the package (DP-04, ADR-017), so no rule, working memory or agenda lives here.
- The records: `rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1` on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, key `caseId`, carries the moves `CURE_PERIOD_EXPIRED` by `R-RES-29` and `R-RES-30` and `TREATMENT_BROKEN` by `R-LIT-02`, and is consumed idempotently into `decision_log_entry`, append only and hash-chained.
- The read: `GET /decision-log` answers the moves of a case with `chainVerified` on every entry; an entry whose link does not hold is named and never hidden. JOB-14 at 02:00 checks the chain of the business date, so a `chainVerified` value is the result of a run.

The legacy facts are unchanged: case `RW-2026-000310`, synthetic account `A-0310`, plan `TDR-SYN-0310`; version `RES-2026.12`; plan statuses `CREATED`, `APPROVED`, `BOOKED`, `BROKEN` with `SUSPENDED` the unknown code; route states `PLAN_CURE_PERIOD`, `PLAN_BROKEN`, `BACK_TO_ROUTE_DECISION`, `RESTRUCTURE_BARRED`, `LIT_ROUTE_APPROVED`, `NOTICE_GENERATED`; the 5 working days of `timer_spec`; the 2 second timeout and the batch of 500; `restructure.max_breaks` = 2. None of them is a column of this schema: the plan facts travel inside the record and the entry.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story promised that a case with a live plan is never treated as if it had none, that a broken plan returns to its owner the next morning, and that the rule and the version behind the move are on the record. In the target those promises sit in four services: rwb-integration reads the plan, rwb-case stores the status, evaluates the package and moves the route state with its task and timer, rwb-access holds the rights, and this service holds the authority and the proof.

Both mechanisms here fail silently when they are wrong. Rule governance is central and evaluation local (ADR-017, DP-04): a version never promoted, or an artifact whose bytes no longer match its checksum, would still be evaluated and the case would still look decided by a rule. The record is no longer one table and one writer: each service writes a local record in its transaction and announces it on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (ADR-022, DP-03), and this service collects it. A move can complete with no entry and no error, and an auditor would find a plan that broke with nothing to explain it.

This story closes both gaps: only a version in force is answered, with the checksum the caller verifies before it evaluates, and a broken plan leaves one chained entry with the rule, the version, the plan status and its date, the final call, the actions and the actor. It meets REQ-DRI-013 and REQ-CHO-002 on the rule-version and record side and serves NFR-033 and NFR-035. It is this service's part only: the plan read is rwb-integration's (RWB-P2-E2002-APP, RWB-P2-E2002-CON), the stored status, the route move, the task and the timer are rwb-case's (RWB-P3-E2002-APP), the rights and the scope check are rwb-access's, and authoring, approval and promotion are RWB-P3-E2042-APP's and RWB-P7-E1073-APP's.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P2-E2002-CON is published: `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/cases/{caseId}/plan-status` with `planRef`, `accountNo`, `status`, `statusDate`, `live` and `messageCode`, its refusals and its fake (DP-11, DP-13). This story calls it at display time and holds no copy of the plan.
- The `rwb_decision` baseline exists from the service template: schema, tables, outbox and inbox objects of DP-09, base, topic, queue and chart.
- `decision_log_entry` carries `chain_seq`, `prev_hash`, `entry_hash` and `corrects_entry_id`, the chain lock, the canonical form and the append-only trigger, and the service login holds INSERT and SELECT only (RWB-P7-E1008-APP). Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2469; ASM-4099).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the record shape, the `rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1` envelope on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the idempotency key and the transaction rule, with its fake.
- Version `RES-2026.12` is loaded, tested and approved with its checksum, its valid-from date and an approver who is not its author, and its four rows each carry `action_text`, `owner_role` and `timer_spec` (RWB-P3-E2042-APP, RWB-P7-E1073-APP). This story reads and answers that version and loads none of it.
- The version-state list and LOV-DECISION are in force and read as reference data (DP-07); no list value is written in code.
- The workflow kit and namespace `rwb-recovery` are provisioned, so the 02:00 check runs as a Schedule on queue `rwb-decision` (DP-10, RWB-P7-E1008-APP).
- The synthetic facts exist: plan `APPROVED` dated 2026-12-10, then `BROKEN` dated 2026-12-14, then no status, then `SUSPENDED`; business dates 2026-12-10 to 2026-12-16; `restructure.max_breaks` = 2. Readers hold Decision log R (TSD P7 T6.1); DP-08 is not in this slice's pattern set, so the story adds no guard.
- No build dependency: it builds against the published contract fake and the registry rows of RWB-P7-E1073-APP and starts on Day 1 in its lane (§R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Version `RES-2026.12` is in force from 2026-12-01 with its checksum in `rule_package_version` and rows `R-RES-29`, `R-RES-30`, `R-RES-31` and `R-LIT-02`.
2. On 2026-12-15 the plan-status step of rwb-case finds plan `TDR-SYN-0310` broken with date 2026-12-14, evaluates the version it fetched from this registry and moves the route state through `PLAN_BROKEN` to `BACK_TO_ROUTE_DECISION` in one transaction with its local record and outbox row (RWB-P3-E2002-APP).
3. A caller asks `GET /admin/rule-packages/RESTRUCTURE/versions`; the answer names `RES-2026.12` as the one version in force with its state, valid-from date, checksum and row count, and names no other as in force.
4. rwb-case publishes `rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1` with decision code, final call `CURE_PERIOD_EXPIRED`, rule ID `R-RES-29`, rule version `RES-2026.12`, inputs reference, actions with `R-RES-30` and the state reached, and the actor.
5. `PlanStatusRecordIngest` consumes it through the inbox, deduplicating on the event identifier and again on the case, business date and rule identity.
6. `PlanStatusRecordMapper` checks the required fields and maps the record to the field groups of the ledger.
7. `MoveRecordAppender` appends one `decision_log_entry` with the rule, the version, the inputs snapshot holding `BROKEN` dated 2026-12-14, the actions holding `R-RES-30`, `PLAN_BROKEN` and `BACK_TO_ROUTE_DECISION`, the actor, the decided time and the chain columns. The status, the route state and the task stay in `rwb_case`.
8. The litigation move `TREATMENT_BROKEN` from `LIT_ROUTE_APPROVED` to `NOTICE_GENERATED` gets its own entry on its own date. A repeat appends nothing and answers the first id; a move that never happened, because the status did not change, the read timed out or no version was in force, leaves none.
9. `PlanStatusDecisionReader` answers `GET /decision-log` in `chain_seq` order with `chainVerified`, may show today's plan status beside an entry from the rwb-integration contract within 2 s, and never rewrites the entry.
10. At 02:00 JOB-14 verifies the chain of the business date, names the first break and answers `chainVerified` false from that entry on.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A version that is not in force is asked for | Refused; no rows; the answer names the package, the version and its state | None | AC2 |
| X2 | The artifact no longer matches its checksum | Refused; no rows; one incident; the state is unchanged | None | AC2 |
| X3 | The ledger cannot take the append | The append is refused and the read answers no partial page; the record waits in the producer's outbox and the ingest catches up | MSG-P7-003 | AC4, AC5 |
| X4 | The same record or the same step arrives twice | One entry for the case, date and rule identity; the first id is answered and the repeat counted | None | AC4 |
| X5 | A rule ID without a version, or an unknown decision code | Refused with the field named, nothing appended, dead-lettered after the last retry | MSG-P7-009 | AC4 |
| X6 | The chain does not hold for an entry on the page | `chainVerified` false, the page carries the warning, one incident to Compliance; the entry is never hidden | MSG-P7-012 | AC5, AC6 |
| X7 | No version in force on the business date | The owning service stops with `NoPackageInForce`; nothing is answered as in force and nothing is appended | MSG-P3-027 | AC2, AC4 |
| X8 | A role without Decision log R, or a case outside scope | Refused; nothing returned and nothing written | MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 | AC5 |

A version that is not in force is never a default. The plan-side exceptions of the legacy story, the status ACE cannot give, the unknown code, the timeout and the batch of 500, belong to rwb-integration and rwb-case and are proved by RWB-P2-E2002-APP and RWB-P3-E2002-APP.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the rwb-integration contract fake, the envelope of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, the `rwb_decision` baseline and the registry rows of RWB-P7-E1073-APP; the other platform rows are the ones the patterns add (§13) |
| Negotiable | Nothing business is fixed: package codes, rule IDs, version labels, route states and maximum breaks are rows of the package or values of rwb-case |
| Valuable | One read explains every move a broken plan caused, and no caller can evaluate a version that was not promoted or whose checksum does not match |
| Estimable | One consumer, one mapper, one appender, one reader, one version answer |
| Small | One sprint with its tests, as a secondary slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Every criterion in section 7 is one automated test on the record and registry fixtures |

These six criteria are new and test only this deliverable. They own no legacy criterion: the nine of RWB-E2-002 stay with the primary slices, the ACE read and the stored status with RWB-P2-E2002-APP, the status on the case, the route move, the task and the timer with RWB-P3-E2002-APP, the rights with RWB-P4-E2002-APP, and the cross-service proof with RWB-ITG-E2002-ITG.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Only a version in force for the business date is answered, with its state, valid-from date, checksum and rows; no older, superseded or unchecked version fills a gap | DP-04; ADR-017; NFR-034 |
| BR2 | The move a broken plan causes is recorded once, one entry per case, business date and rule identity, with the rule and the package version the owning service evaluated | REQ-DRI-013; REQ-CHO-002; legacy AC2, BR10 |
| BR3 | The entry carries `rule_id`, `rule_version`, the inputs snapshot with the ACE plan status and its date, the final call, the actions with the second rule and the state reached, and the actor | FSD P7 A2.2, A2.3; TSD P7 T3.1 |
| BR4 | An entry is append only and hash-chained; a correction is a new entry naming the one it corrects | FSD P7 AC-P7-001-01; RWB-P7-E1008-APP |
| BR5 | A decision whose record cannot be written does not proceed: the local record and the move are one transaction in the owning service, and an unavailable ledger answers no partial page | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; legacy BR8 |
| BR6 | A repeat appends nothing and is counted; a move that never happened leaves no entry | R-UNI-40; legacy BR9, BR11 |
| BR7 | A version not in force, or an artifact whose checksum does not recompute, is refused with the state named and no rows; a missing version is `NoPackageInForce` in the owning service, never a default move | R-UNI-41; legacy BR11; MSG-P3-027 |
| BR8 | The read names the rule and its version for every move, and a break in the chain is shown with `chainVerified` false and named, never hidden | NFR-033, NFR-035; MSG-P7-012 |
| BR9 | The chain of a business date is checked at 02:00, which is the only reason a `chainVerified` value is trusted for that date | NFR-035; RWB-P7-E1008-APP |
| BR10 | The plan status, its date, the route state, the queue, the task, the timer and the rights are other services' values; this service holds the version, the checksum and the record | DP-01; DP-03; legacy AC7, AC8 |

BR1 runs in the version answer. BR2, BR3, BR6 and BR10 run in the ingest, the mapper and the appender, where the dedupe key decides whether an entry is appended and the plan facts are copied as they arrive. BR4 and BR5 run in the schema and the append: the trigger refuses an UPDATE and a DELETE, and the append is one transaction with the chain lock. BR7 runs at the boundary, before any row is read. BR8 and BR9 run in the reader and the 02:00 check.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | a record for a case, date and rule identity | No entry exists | One `decision_log_entry` at the next `chain_seq` |
| Appended | the same record or move again | The idempotency key repeats | No change; the first id is answered and the repeat counted |
| Appended | the same case and date, a different move | The rule identity differs | A further entry for that date |
| APPROVED | the 00:01 promotion on the valid-from date (RWB-P7-E1073-APP) | The load checks passed and approver is not author | `IN_FORCE`; the version before it becomes `SUPERSEDED` |
| LOADED, APPROVED, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK, REFUSED | a version answer | The version is not in force | Refused, state named, no rows |
| IN_FORCE | a version answer | The checksum recomputes to the recorded one | Answered; anything else refuses and raises one incident |
| Chained | the 02:00 check | A link does not hold | That entry and every later one answer `chainVerified` false, one incident, no seal |

The case state machine is not this service's (TSD P7 T4): rwb-case owns the case status, the route state, the plan status, the queue, the task and the timer. This story records the move that reaches a route state and sets none: `PLAN_CURE_PERIOD` while the cure period runs, `PLAN_BROKEN` and `BACK_TO_ROUTE_DECISION` by `R-RES-29` and `R-RES-30`, `RESTRUCTURE_BARRED` at the second break under `restructure.max_breaks` = 2, `NOTICE_GENERATED` from `LIT_ROUTE_APPROVED` by `R-LIT-02`.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-decision service identity, schema `rwb_decision`, own login (DP-02) | Appends the entry, answers the version and serves the read; the login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2469; ASM-4099) |
| SY-DECLOG, decision log writer and the record library of DP-03 | Publishes the record from the owning service; holds no grant on `rwb_decision` |
| SY-RULES, rules component | Evaluates the package in its own service on the version answered here; never on its behalf here |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-RESTRUCT | Read the moves and plan facts of cases in scope (Decision log R, scope applied) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY | Read the ledger with its chain state for a team, an audit or a review (Decision log R) |
| RW-RISK, RW-COE | Approve and author the versions through RWB-P7-E1073-APP and RWB-P3-E2042-APP; this story answers the version and records the move |
| RW-PLATADM | Operates the Schedule and reads the incidents of a refused version and of a chain break |
| rwb-integration (P2), rwb-case (P3), rwb-access (P4) | Own the plan read, the case, the move and the rights; this service calls the plan read at display time and reads no table of theirs |

The authorisation decision is the cached permission decision the template holds from rwb-access; DP-08 is not in this slice's set, so the story adds no guard and holds no role row. Refusals are 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 with MSG-P4-003 and 503 with MSG-P7-003.

| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2469; ASM-4099) | rule_package_version | the artifact reference answered with the checksum | Read |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | objects of DP-09 | all fields | Write |

Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and TSD P7 T3.1. `decision_log_entry.case_id` is the only case value here: no plan reference, status, route-state, product-group or amount column exists and no foreign key points into another schema (DP-01). The plan facts travel inside the inputs snapshot and the actions payload; the physical shape of that snapshot is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2469; ASM-4099). `recovery_case`, `case_account`, `task` and `timer` are rwb-case's and `treatment` is rwb-treatment's.

##### 12. Contract

Base `/api/recovery/decision/v1` (DP-13), topic `rwb.decision.events.v1` (DP-14), queue `rwb-decision`, schema `rwb_decision`, Java package as §1.

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Method | Path | Purpose | Authorization |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` | The versions of `RESTRUCTURE` for a business date: the one in force with its state, valid-from date, checksum and row count, and any other version with its state only; no rows of a version not in force | Decision log R; a model-owner service identity for the checksum |
| GET | `/decision-log` | The moves of a case or a date range: query `caseId`, `from`, `to`, `page`, `size`; each item carries `rule_id`, `rule_version`, `final_call`, `decided_at`, the actions and `chainVerified`, and the page carries MSG-P7-012 on a broken link | Decision log, right R, scope applied |

The first is the registry read the Ownership Map attributes to this service; API-P7-006 of TSD appendix T-A is the decision-log query, and the entry read and the audit export are RWB-P7-E2005-APP's. Field names beyond those named, the page size (50 by default) and the artifact field are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2469; ASM-4099, ASM-4100).

The answer carries `planRef`, `accountNo`, `status`, `statusDate`, `live` and `messageCode`; a stored value answers `live` false with MSG-P2-008 and its date, and an unavailable ACE answers 503 with MSG-GEN-006. Both are rwb-integration's and are shown as they arrive.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, modules `planstatusrecord` and `restructureversion`.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| PlanStatusRecordIngest | Consumer | Consumes the record through the inbox; deduplicates on the event and on the case, date and rule identity |
| PlanStatusRecordMapper | Service | Required fields, the two refusals, and the mapping to the field groups of the entry |
| MoveRecordAppender | Service | Appends one entry with `chain_seq`, `prev_hash` and `entry_hash` in one transaction; answers the first id on a repeat |
| PlanStatusDecisionReader | Service | The read by case or date range, `chainVerified`, MSG-P7-012, and today's status from the rwb-integration contract at display |
| RestructureVersionAnswer | Service | The one version in force for the date with state, valid-from, checksum and row count; any other with its state only; no evaluation |

**Database and migrations.** Writes `decision_log_entry` only and reads `rule_package`, `rule_package_version` and `rule_row`. Index `(case_id, decided_at)`, a unique key on the idempotency key of case, date and rule identity, and a unique key on `rule_package_version (package_id, version_label)`. Per-service Flyway of DP-15: `V2002_1__plan_status_record.sql` adds the indexes and no case, plan or route column; no row is seeded.

**Configuration.** No business value: package codes, rule IDs, version labels, route states and maximum breaks are rows of the package or values of rwb-case, and the version-state list and LOV-DECISION are read as reference data (DP-07). Two settings only, the page size and the ingest retry count, neither fixed by a source in the read set (GAP-2469; ASM-4100).

**Build steps.** (1) The version answer with the state check and the checksum, tests AC1 and AC2. (2) The ingest and mapper against the fixture, AC3 and AC4. (3) The appender with the chain columns and the repeat path, AC3 and AC4. (4) The reader with the filters, `chainVerified` and the refusals, AC5. (5) The JOB-14 coverage assertion over a seeded chain, and the schema assertion that `rwb_decision` holds no case, plan or route column, AC6.

| DP | Pattern applied | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | Own schema `rwb_decision`; no other service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | Local record in the owning service and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | Embedded Drools per service; package and versions from this registry, evaluation in the owner | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |

| DP-07 | Reference data and lists through the rwb-case contract | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |

This slice adds no build dependency of its own (metadata "Depends on (build)" = None) and builds against the baseline, the RWB-P2-E2002-CON fake and the registry rows of RWB-P7-E1073-APP. The platform H rows and C rows above are the ones the patterns add; they are held by the platform, contract and registry stories and are not repeated in the metadata rows, which name the one contract dependency of the key (GAP-2470; ASM-4103). DP-04 is the point of the slice: the registry is central, the evaluation local, and the working memory and budget stay in the owning service. DP-05, DP-06 and DP-07 are prohibitions: no ACE view, no parameter and no list value in code. DP-19 is the composite route behind the screen.

**Done when.** The tests in §16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P2-E2002-CON and RWB-PLT-E1027-CON stay green, and a SIT week shows the move of 2026-12-15 recorded once with `R-RES-29` and `RES-2026.12`, the litigation move of 2026-12-16 recorded once with `R-LIT-02`, a repeat adding no entry, a page that names a broken link and hides no entry, and the version answer naming only the version in force with its checksum.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | The ledger cannot take the append or answer the read | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P7-009 | A record is refused for a missing or invalid field | The decision record was refused: {field} is missing or not valid. |
| MSG-P7-012 | An entry on the page does not match the chain | Entry {entryId} does not match the decision log chain. Do not rely on it until Compliance has reviewed it. |
| MSG-P7-008 | The 02:00 check of a date finds a break | The decision log check for {date} found a break at entry {entryId}. Entries from that entry on cannot be relied on until Compliance reviews them. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No version in force on the business date | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the Decision log right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | A case outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |

MSG-P7-009 goes to the log and the incident, never to a customer; its {field} is `ruleVersion` or `decisionCode`. For MSG-P3-027 the {check} is "no package in force" and the {detail} names the package code "RESTRUCTURE" and the business date only, never a case fact. Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response; the reads answer 401, 403, 404 and 503 with MSG-P7-003. A refused version answer names the package, the version and its state, carries no rows and has no message identifier of its own (GAP-2469; ASM-4101). MSG-P2-008 and MSG-GEN-006 are rwb-integration's and shown as they arrive.

##### 15. Screens and states

No new screen. The plan-status section of SCR-38 Decision log query shows, for a case or a date range, the entries in chain order with the rule and its version, the final call, the plan reference, the plan status and its date, the state reached, the decided time and `chainVerified`. States are Loading, Results, Empty ("No decisions match this search.") and Error with MSG-P7-003; a broken link puts MSG-P7-012 at the top and leaves every entry in place; a reader without Decision log R sees the refusal. The header beside the entries, the SCR-03 plan-status panel and the SCR-14 broken state are rwb-case's. The screen is one gateway answer through the composite route (DP-19), which calls this service for the entries and rwb-case for the header; its path and merge order are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2469; ASM-4102). No screen of this story writes.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: package codes, rule IDs, version labels, status codes, route states, the event map and the maximum breaks are rows of the package, values of rwb-case or reference data. No rule form, label, status code or route state appears in this service's Java.
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs, logs or tests: an entry carries a case identifier, a rule identity, the plan reference and actor identifiers, never a name, address, identity number or account number. Test data is synthetic.
- No cross-schema read (DP-01): no `rwb_case`, `rwb_treatment` or other service's table is read and no foreign key points into one.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: the plan comes from the rwb-integration operation; no `v_ace_*` view and no ACE table is read.
- No rule engine here: no KieBase, no working memory and no evaluation on queue `rwb-decision`.
- A version is answered only while in force and only with a matching checksum; no older, superseded or unchecked version fills a gap.
- An entry is never corrected in place: a correction is a new entry naming the one it corrects, and the trigger refuses an UPDATE and a DELETE.
- No topic or event name is typed in code (DP-09).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-002 for rwb-integration. This document deploys the plan-status operation of this key: the chart and its values, the Flyway statement, the ACE endpoint and the two settings, the trigger wiring, the flag, five dashboard series, the alert set of the key and the runbook. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **the plan-status operation of rwb-integration deployed on the service's own worker and task queue, with the ACE common module endpoint, the batch size and the timeout as environment values, behind the platform flag, with five dashboard series, the alert set of the key and a runbook**, so that **a caller always gets either a live status inside a bounded budget or a bounded refusal it can fall back from, and a rota can see and act on the three conditions that stop it**.

The legacy story assumed a nightly step and a screen that read ACE inside the monolith, and nobody had to know where the plan came from. In the target the plan read is one operation of this service, called by rwb-case's plan-status step and by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-11, DP-19), and the daily step is rwb-case's. So the deployment is where the boundary becomes real: the ACE endpoint per environment, the batch of 500, the 2,000 ms budget, the breaker, the flag and the honest observation of a read that is not allowed to fail silently.

This story deploys and proves the deployment only. It builds no controller, no validator and no client: those are RWB-P2-E2002-APP, against the baseline of RWB-P2-E2002-CON. It writes no case row and stores no plan: the stored status is rwb-case's. What it owns is the release: the chart and its values, the schema statement, the ACE connectivity, the two settings, the flag, the five series, the alert set and the runbook.

##### 2. Business rationale

A plan status is read on three paths at once: the case record screen through the composite route, the nightly step of rwb-case, and the integration harness. Each of them fails in a different way if the deployment is wrong. A wrong ACE endpoint fails every read and every nightly step keeps every stored value, which looks like a quiet day. A timeout that is longer than the caller's budget makes the caller time out while this service is still waiting, so the answer is a 504 from the edge instead of a 503 with a message. A batch size that is larger than ACE accepts turns one read into one error for the whole case. And a flag left off in an environment serves stored values that nobody labels as stored.

The deployment therefore carries the state of the read as data. Five series answer what a rota asks: how many answers were live, how many had no plan, how many carried a code outside the list, how many were refused or unavailable and with which class, and how long a call took against the budget. Four alerts are wired, each with one runbook entry: three carry a message ID (MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003) and one carries the unknown status code and its count, because the legacy story gives no message for an unknown code. The fifth condition of the key — no RESTRUCTURE version in force — is named in the mapping with its owners, because this service never evaluates a package and cannot see it (ADR-023).

The release also fixes the two settings where they belong. The batch size and the timeout are read at run time through the rwb-case parameters contract (DP-06), so a change needs no rebuild and no release; the endpoint, the breaker and the thresholds are values files of the environment. Nothing is hard-coded, and nothing in this key adds a table: the schema statement exists to prove that the read writes nothing (DP-01, DP-15).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The integration base of RWB-P2-E1007-APP and RWB-P2-E2001-APP is deployed in the environment: the worker on the task queue of the service, the namespace `rwb-recovery`, the payload codec, the health surface and the base `/api/recovery/integration/v1` behind gateway-bff.
- The Temporal workflow kit, the namespace `rwb-recovery` and the build ID provider exist (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON). This key creates no Schedule of its own.
- The platform flag library is available and the flag `rwb.integration.ace-plan-status` is registered for this service (RWB-PLT-E1047-CON; R-PREC default ruling on feature flags).
- The `rwb_integration` schema and its Flyway sequence exist, with the outbox, inbox, delivery and idempotency objects created by the service baseline and the DB story of the service (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON).
- The plan-status operation of RWB-P2-E2002-CON is published, with its answer, its refusals and its read-only rule, and its fakes answer every consumed read.
- The ACE common module publishes `RestructurePlanQuery` in SIT and UAT (INT-34; DL14), and the environment either reaches that endpoint or, where ACE SIT is not yet published, the stub of the contract baseline.
- The parameter rows `rwb.ace.plan.batch-size` = 500 and `rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms` = 2000 are in force in the rwb-case parameters (assumed; DL11), and LOV-PLAN-STATUS with CREATED, APPROVED, BOOKED and BROKEN is loaded (RW-COE).
- The platform error envelope and the message catalogue are in force, so an alert can carry a message ID.
- The environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist; the wave 2 release deploys to DEV, SIT and UAT, and the production values are a later promotion of the same artefacts.
- The topics of this service already exist: `rwb.integration.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, and the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1` (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON). This release adds no topic and registers no consumer group.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds the service image and the contract jar, runs the unit, component and contract tests of RWB-P2-E2002-CON and RWB-P2-E2002-APP, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes one chart version.
2. The chart deploys the service worker with its own login, the namespace `rwb-recovery`, the task queue of the service, the payload codec and the build ID of the release.
3. The API step confirms that `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/cases/{caseId}/plan-status` answers through gateway-bff in the environment, with the authorise contract of rwb-access reachable and the case, reference-data and parameter contracts of rwb-case replaced by the real services where they are deployed.
4. The ACE connectivity step confirms the endpoint of the environment, the certificate and the network path, and records whether the environment answers from ACE or from the contract stub.
5. The setting step confirms that `rwb.ace.plan.batch-size` and `rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms` are read from the rwb-case parameters with the version in force, that the values in force are 500 and 2000, and that a change of the version is picked up without a redeploy.
6. The schema step confirms that the release applies no migration of its own, that the library objects exist in `rwb_integration` and that the service login holds no grant on `recovery`.
7. The trigger step confirms the calling paths: rwb-case's plan-status activity reaches the operation on the task queue of rwb-case, and gateway-bff reaches it for the case record; no P2 Schedule exists, and none is created by the release.
8. The flag step sets `rwb.integration.ace-plan-status` from the values of the environment and confirms that the answer, and the ACE call, follow it.
9. The dashboards are published with the five series and the environment, the release and the build ID as dimensions.
10. The alert set is wired: four rules — three carrying MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 and one carrying the unknown status code and its count — each with its runbook entry, and the fifth row of the mapping is published with its owners and its route.
11. A smoke step reads one synthetic case in DEV and checks that the answer carries a plan reference, a status from the list, its date and `live` true, that a second call answers the same values and writes nothing, and that the stored fallback on the screen comes from rwb-case.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The chart render, the image pull or a migration job fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic to the new version | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The release would apply a migration that adds a table, a column or an index | The schema step fails the release: this key adds none, and a migration that does is refused | None | AC2 |
| X3 | The service login holds a grant on `recovery`, or on another `rwb_*` schema | The schema step fails the release and names the grant | None | AC2 |
| X4 | The ACE endpoint is wrong or unreachable in an environment | Every read answers 503 with MSG-GEN-006, the unavailable series rises and the alert pages; no value is invented | MSG-GEN-006 | AC3, AC5 |
| X5 | The timeout in force is longer than the caller's budget | The budget check fails the release, because a caller must receive a 503 and not an edge timeout | MSG-GEN-006 | AC3 |
| X6 | The batch size in force is larger than ACE accepts | The read fails for the whole case; the setting is a parameter row, so it is corrected without a release, and the failure series names the batch class | MSG-GEN-006 | AC3, AC5 |
| X7 | The flag is off in an environment and the operation still calls ACE | The flag step fails the release, because off means no outside call | None | AC4 |
| X8 | A P2 Schedule for the plan status is created by the release, or by an operator | The trigger step fails the release; the daily step is rwb-case's and a second run over the same cases is not allowed | None | AC4 |
| X9 | The worker stops while a request is in flight | The caller receives its own timeout and retries; the read writes nothing, so no repair is needed | MSG-GEN-006 | AC6 |
| X10 | A read answers a code outside LOV-PLAN-STATUS | The unknown-status series rises and the alert fires; the code is answered unchanged and never stored here | None | AC5, AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the workflow kit, the flag library and the published contract; no application code is built here |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, thresholds, the endpoint, the breaker values and the retention are environment values |
| Valuable | Makes the read observable and bounded before the release, so a failing ACE read cannot look like a quiet day |
| Estimable | One chart, one API step, one connectivity step, one setting step, one schema step, one trigger step, one flag step, five series, five mapping rows and four runbook entries |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the schema is unchanged, the settings are read as data, the paths are wired, the alerts fire on a synthetic metric, the runbook entry is followed |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One service, one task queue, one login: the worker polls the task queue of `rwb-integration` in the namespace `rwb-recovery` and carries the rwb-integration login only | Arch v5 slides 24 and 41; DP-02; DP-10 |
| BR2 | Every worker carries the build ID of its release and worker versioning is enabled, so a new build takes new requests while the old build drains | Temporal and Drools design slide 27; RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| BR3 | This release creates no Schedule and no workflow: the daily plan-status step and its activity are rwb-case's, and a second daily run over the same cases is not allowed | Arch v5 slide 44; DP-10; RWB-P3-E2002-APP |
| BR4 | The release writes `rwb_integration` only, adds no table and no column, and holds no grant on `recovery` | DP-01; DP-15; ADR-010 |
| BR5 | The ACE endpoint, the certificate, the breaker and the thresholds are values files; the batch size and the timeout are parameter rows read through their owner; none is a constant | DP-06; FSD P2 Integration v3 BR-P2-007 |
| BR6 | The flag is the platform flag library's; off means no ACE call and a live false answer, and the switch is never a service table | R-PREC default ruling; Ownership Map `feature_flag` |
| BR7 | Every alert carries a message ID and the agreed text and links one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR8 | No environment value is hard-coded: replicas, resources, thresholds, the endpoint, the breaker and the flag come from values files and the flag library | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR9 | Dashboard series, alert payloads and the runbook carry counts, case references, plan references, status codes, message IDs and build IDs only, never an account number, a name or a decoded payload | Arch v5 slide 42 (PDPA) |
| BR10 | A failing release never replaces a working one; a rollback keeps one build serving and the flag paused while the two builds change over | Temporal and Drools design slide 27; DP-10 |
| BR11 | The read is bounded by the same budget in every environment: a timeout longer than the caller's budget is a defect of the release, not a tuning value | Legacy 2 s budget; DP-11 |
| BR12 | A condition this service cannot observe is named with its owner rather than given a false alert | AC5; the split of RWB-P2-E2002-APP |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the contract tests pass | Deploying |
| Deploying | Worker registered and probes healthy | The worker polls its queue only and the authorise call succeeds | Ready |
| Ready | API step passed | The operation answers through gateway-bff and the contracts are reachable | Serving |
| Serving | Flag off | `rwb.integration.ace-plan-status` is off in the environment | Stored only |
| Stored only | Flag on | The flag is on and ACE is reachable | Serving |
| Serving | ACE unavailable | The endpoint, the certificate or the network fails | Serving (degraded) |
| Serving (degraded) | ACE reachable | The next call answers inside the budget | Serving |
| Serving | Release superseded | A new chart version passes the tests | Rolling |
| Rolling | All workers on the new build | The old build drains its open requests | Serving |
| Any | A failing release or a failed step | The previous release stays in force and the pipeline stops | Previous state |

These are states of the release, not of a case: no case status and no route state moves in this story.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
