**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract baseline of RWB-E2-008 for rwb-payment — the two REST operations on `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, the three event schemas on `rwb.payment.events.v1`, the consumed-contract declarations and their fakes, the error model, the message map and the `rwb_payment` schema baseline — is published as one frozen baseline so that RWB-P8-E2008-APP and RWB-P8-E2008-OPS start on Day 1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **contract owner of the payment service (TechX)**, I want **one published baseline for rwb-payment payment matching — the shapes of the two operations, the three event schemas, the consumed contracts with their fakes, the error model and the `rwb_payment` schema with its versioning rule — so that** the application story, the deployment story and every consumer build on Day 1 against a fake and no shape is decided twice.

The baseline fixes, and nothing else:

- the two operations of the service's ownership rows — `GET /proceeds` and `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` — on base `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, with their access rights and idempotency (DP-13, R4);
- three event schemas on `rwb.payment.events.v1` with `.retry` and `.dlt`: `rwb.payment.TreatmentBooked.v1` (EV-11), `rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1` (EV-12) and `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` (EV-25), in a CloudEvents 1.0 envelope keyed on `caseId` (DP-09);
- the declarations of the nine operations the service consumes — three ACE reads on rwb-source-data, two rwb-case reads, two treatment-record calls, the parameters and lists reads and the package read — with the element names of the review baseline and a fake per declaration (DP-05, DP-06, DP-07, DP-11);
- the `rwb_payment` baseline: `proceeds` with the field set of TSD P8 T3.1, the standard record columns, the keys, the library tables and the per-service Flyway rule (DP-01, DP-15);
- the error model and the message map of the legacy messages, so a consumer reads one envelope (DP-11);
- the event and operation contracts the gateway-bff composite route of SCR-28 consumes (DP-19).

This story writes no business logic. The behaviour of the match, the record, the events and the read is RWB-P8-E2008-APP; the deployment of the build is RWB-P8-E2008-OPS. Where a legacy shape has no target counterpart, the baseline states the placeholder and the gap, and no value is invented (GAP-2504; ASM-4143).

##### 2. Business rationale

A split story is only as good as the contract it builds against. RWB-E2-008 was written as one service call to six in-process interfaces and to two ACE views, so nothing in the legacy story can be built by a team that does not own the neighbour. Under D-RCV-60 each of those calls becomes one hop with a 2 s timeout and a fake, and the shapes have to be frozen before the application and the deployment stories open — otherwise the four services this key touches would each freeze a different shape of the same payment.

- **one baseline, four consumers.** RWB-P8-E2008-APP, RWB-P8-E2008-OPS, RWB-P8-E2027 and the Epic 4 stories of the service all read these shapes; freezing them once is what makes the lane CG-W2 work.
- **the contract is testable without a neighbour.** Every declaration carries a fake with a documented answer, so a contract test proves the shape on Day 1 and SIT only replaces the fake with the owner.
- **nothing of the business is frozen here.** The window, the tolerance, the grace days and the match types stay rows of package `PAYMENT_MATCH`; the baseline carries their shape, never their value.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The Ownership Map rows for this service are taken as authoritative: table `proceeds` (P8), operations `GET /proceeds` and `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` (P8), events EV-11, EV-12 and EV-25 (P8), jobs JOB-07 and JOB-08 (P8), no workflow name (P8). The context pack is the only source used for them.
- The API Specification, the Event and Messaging document and the Physical Schema are at their next versions and read as the parents of this baseline; the baseline restates only what this key touches.
- The platform contracts the patterns name — RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON — are published at their baseline versions; this story freezes the shapes against them and does not restate them.
- The four P3 contracts the plan names — RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON, RWB-P3-E2004-CON and RWB-P3-E2042-CON — are readable as drafts, so their response elements are declared from the published documents and the fakes are built from those declarations.
- Status is Draft (realignment v1): no approval is required to publish a baseline, and a consumer builds against the tagged version (GAP-2504; ASM-4144).
- The legacy message IDs and their texts stand in the message map; no new message text is written here.

##### 4. Flow

1. Take the two operations of the service's ownership rows, place them on base `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, and write the request, the response, the errors, the access right and the idempotency of each into 12.1.
2. Take the three events of the service's ownership rows, name them `rwb.payment.<Event>.v1`, place them on `rwb.payment.events.v1` with `.retry` and `.dlt`, fix the key and the CloudEvents envelope, and write the payload element names into 12.3.
3. Take the nine consumed operations, declare each with its base, its owner, its request and its response elements, and record the placeholder where no published document fixes an element (12.2).
4. Take the `proceeds` field set of TSD P8 T3.1, add the standard record columns of T3.0, and fix the business key, the indexes, the retention and the no-cross-schema-key rule in 12.7.
5. Add the library tables the patterns create in `rwb_payment` — `decision_record`, `inbox_event`, `outbox_event`, `idempotency_key` — as inherited shapes, not as new design.
6. Fix the error model: the platform problem shape, the codes for the legacy messages of section 14, and the rule that a refused right answers MSG-P4-002 and changes nothing.
7. Publish one fake per declaration and per provider, each with the documented answer of 12.8, so the contract tests run without a neighbour.
8. Freeze the baseline as version `v1`, tag it, and hand the tag to RWB-P8-E2008-APP and RWB-P8-E2008-OPS; any later shape change is a new version and is recorded in the Change Register.
9. Run the contract tests of section 16 against the OpenAPI document, the three event schemas and the fakes, and publish the result with the tag.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A consumer sends a shape the baseline does not declare | The request is refused with the problem envelope and no business change | MSG-P4-002 or the field code of section 14 | AC5 |
| X2 | A declared operation has no published document behind it and the owner has not confirmed the element names | The declaration carries the placeholder and the fake answers the baseline shape; the review row is open | None | AC3, GAP-2504 |
| X3 | A breaking change is proposed after the tag | The change opens a new version of the baseline; the tagged version stays buildable | None | AC7 |
| X4 | A fake returns an answer the baseline does not document | The contract test fails and the baseline is not tagged | None | AC6 |
| X5 | A schema statement of the baseline names another `rwb_*` schema or a foreign key out of `rwb_payment` | The schema lint fails and the baseline is not tagged | None (lint log) | AC4, section 17 |
| X6 | A request carries no `Idempotency-Key` on the manual match, or replays one | The operation answers the stored result or refuses the replay as declared; no second row | None | AC1 |

X2 is the only path that ends in an open review row; the rest are gates of the tag. No path invents a business value: the values behind the shapes are package rows or reference data of their owners.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs no running neighbour: every declaration has a fake and every shape comes from a published document or the Ownership Map |
| Negotiable | The element names of an unpublished consumed operation are the review baseline and may be corrected by the owner without a behaviour change |
| Valuable | Four stories and every consumer of the payment contract build on Day 1 against one tag |
| Estimable | Two operations, three event schemas, nine consumed declarations, one schema baseline, nine fakes and one message map |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion runs as a contract test at Level Contract against the documents and the fakes |

The seven criteria test the baseline only. They carry no payment, plan, case, amount or date of the legacy story except the operation, event and field names the Ownership Map and TSD P8 fix; the values behind the shapes stay rows of package `PAYMENT_MATCH` and of the reference-data contract (ASM-4144).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The baseline is one tagged version; a consumer builds against the tag and never against a draft element | R8.2; R5.7 rule 1 |
| BR2 | The operation set is the ownership rows of the service and nothing else; an operation the Ownership Map does not carry is not published | Ownership Map; GAP-2504 |
| BR3 | One base per service, `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, and no operation outside it | DP-13, R4 |
| BR4 | Event names follow `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1` on `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, with a retry and a dead-letter topic | DP-09, DP-14 |
| BR5 | One schema and one login per service; no foreign key and no statement may leave `rwb_payment` | DP-01, DP-02 |
| BR6 | Every consumed operation is declared with a fake; a declaration without a fake is not publishable | DP-11 |
| BR7 | No business value is frozen: window, tolerance, grace days, partial floor, match types and the LOV values are read from their owners | Principle 1; D-RCV-36 T10 |
| BR8 | No personal data in a schema, an event, a fake or a test fixture | Section 17 |
| BR9 | The error envelope is the platform problem shape and every legacy message ID maps to one status and one code | R7.2 s14; section 14 |
| BR10 | A breaking change is a new version and a Change Register row; a correction of an element name by its owner is a patch to the same version | R8.2; AC7 |

##### 9. State transitions

None of business data: this story changes no record. The states it owns are the states of the baseline itself.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not existing | The baseline is written and its tests pass | The tag gate of section 16 is green | `v1` Draft, tagged and handed to the consumers |
| `v1` Draft | The owner confirms or corrects an element name of a consumed operation | The change is not breaking | `v1` patched, the review row closed |
| `v1` | A published element changes shape | A consumer cannot build against the old shape | `v2` opened; `v1` stays readable and buildable |
| `v1` | A consumer asks for an operation the Ownership Map does not carry | The row is absent | No change; the request answers the gap row |

The version states are `Draft`, `Tagged` and `Superseded`, and only a tagged version is citable by an APP or OPS story.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The contract owner of rwb-payment (TechX) | Writes, tags and versions the baseline; owns the fakes and the contract tests; refuses a declaration without a published document |
| The owner of rwb-source-data (P1) | Confirms or corrects the three declarations and their fakes; owns the ACE read boundary |
| The owner of rwb-case (P3) | Confirms or corrects the open-case, plans, parameters, lists and package declarations and their fakes |
| The owner of rwb-treatment (S2) | Confirms the treatment entity behind RWB-P3-E2004-CON and its two declarations |
| The owner of rwb-decision (P7) | Confirms the package declaration and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` |
| The platform contract owners (PLT) | Own the library shapes the baseline inherits: the record, the outbox and inbox, the workflow kit, the Flyway gate and the composite route |
| RW-CREDITAD, RW-CASEOWN, SY-AGENT, RW-COE | Read the baseline as consumers; hold no write right on it |

The right of each published operation is the row of TSD P8 T6.1; the baseline declares it and grants nothing.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-payment (P8); base `/api/recovery/payment/v1` (DP-13); document `openapi/rwb-payment-v1.yaml`.

| Method | Path | Request | Response | Errors | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/proceeds` | query `matched` (boolean), `from`, `to`, `page`, `size` | 200 `ProceedsPage` with `items` of `Proceeds`, `page`, `size`, `total` | 401, 403 (MSG-P4-002), 503 | Write-off and posting, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` | path `proceedsId`; body `MatchRequest` with the case and the account to match | 200 `Proceeds` | 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 | Write-off and posting, right U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header, replayed answer on a repeat |

`Proceeds` carries DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009, and `MatchRequest` carries the case and account reference of a manual match. Architecture v5 lists `GET /cases/{id}/payments` among the IN operations of this service and the Ownership Map has no row for it: the operation is not published, the case payment list is answered through `GET /proceeds` with the case scope applied, and the absence is recorded (GAP-2504; ASM-4143).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Base | Owner | Request | Response elements |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Payments of a business date (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2504; ASM-4143)) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | source, businessDate | payment_code, account_key, payment_date, payment_amount, data_as_of |
| Next installment date of an account (name as above) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | accountKey, businessDate | next_installment_date |
| Batch status of a source (name as above) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | source, businessDate | source_system, business_date, status |
| Open case of an account (name as above) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | accountKey | caseId, absent where the account is on no open case |
| Running plans of a case (name as above) | RWB-P3-E2004-CON | P3 as the plan scopes it; the entity is S2's | caseId | treatmentId, treatment_type, installments, installment_amount, installments_paid, nextDueDate |
| Record an installment paid (name as above) | RWB-P3-E2004-CON | as above | treatmentId, proceedsId, dueDate, amount | the updated installment position |
| Run parameters (name as above) | RWB-P3-E1042-CON | P3 rwb-case | key, businessDate | value, version |
| Lists of the run (name as above) | RWB-P3-E1043-CON | P3 rwb-case | listCode, businessDate | the active values of LOV-MATCH and LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC |
| Rule package in force (name as above) | RWB-P3-E2042-CON | P3 as the plan scopes it; the package is P7's | packageCode, onDate | package code, version, rows, checksum |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a single GET retry with jitter and a breaker per downstream (DP-11, ADR-020). The element names are the review baseline: each owner confirms or corrects them at review, and a correction is a patch to the same version.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Key | Payload elements | Producer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.payment.TreatmentBooked.v1` (EV-11) | `rwb.payment.events.v1` | `caseId` | treatmentId, caseId, bookingRef, businessDate | rwb-payment, booking story (JOB-08) |
| `rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1` (EV-12) | `rwb.payment.events.v1` | `caseId` | treatmentId, dueDate, amountDue | rwb-payment, this key |
| `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` (EV-25) | `rwb.payment.events.v1` | `caseId` | proceedsId, caseId, amount | rwb-payment, this key |

Each schema is CloudEvents 1.0 with `id`, `source`, `type`, `subject`, `time` and `datacontenttype`, is registered on the topic with its subject and version, and carries no personal data. The retry topic `rwb.payment.events.v1.retry` and the dead-letter topic `rwb.payment.events.v1.dlt` are declared once for all three. `DecisionRecorded` is published by the local library on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, whose owner is rwb-decision (DP-03), and its schema is inherited and not restated. The element lists beyond the legacy ones — the matched treatment and the business date of a match, and the case id of a missed payment — are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2504; ASM-4143).

The seven rows are the service's subscriptions: EV-26 and EV-30 serve this key, and the other five serve the booking and Epic 4 stories. ###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `matchPayments` (JOB-07; name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2504; ASM-4143)) | Workflow, event-started | `rwb-payment`, namespace `rwb-recovery` | input source, businessDate, eventId; execution id derived from source and date |

The baseline fixes the registration contract — the queue, the namespace, the workflow type name, the input schema and the retry policy of the kit — and not the activity names a story chooses. `postProceeds`, the debt-sale saga step, is registered by that journey and not here.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No job of this key is a Temporal Schedule: JOB-07 and JOB-08 are event-started, and the daily cadence is the bank's Airflow edge. The baseline therefore declares no cron, no overlap policy and no catch-up window, and no Schedule row is created for this service.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Key and indexes | Columns | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `proceeds` | P8 (`rwb_payment`) | `id` primary key; business key on the payment reference where the environment grants it; index on (`matched_to`, `received_date`) | DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009 plus the standard record columns of TSD P8 T3.0 | the receipt of a case and what it was matched to |
| `decision_record` | PLT library, created in `rwb_payment` | hash chain per record kind | inherited | DP-03 |
| `inbox_event` | PLT library, created in `rwb_payment` | (`consumer_group`, `event_id`) | inherited | DP-09 |
| `outbox_event` | PLT library, created in `rwb_payment` | (`status`, `created_at`) and the relay cursor | inherited | DP-09 |
| `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_payment` | (`scope`, `key`) | inherited | DP-09 |

The baseline declares no foreign key out of `rwb_payment`, no grant on another schema and no read of another owner's table; `case_id`, `treatment_id` and `account_payment_id` are identifiers (DP-01). The migration rule is one Flyway sequence per service, numbered in `rwb_payment` and gated by the lint and drift gate of RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (DP-15); the monolith's `V2_008__payment_matching.sql` is not reused and its target name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2504; ASM-4143). `payment_missed_event_key` is not created: the key is the idempotency row.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Provider | Documented answer | Consumers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Payment OpenAPI fake | rwb-payment | a page of matched and unmatched receipts; a manual match accepted, refused with MSG-P4-002 and refused on a replayed key | APP, OPS, gateway-bff |
| Event schema fakes | rwb-payment | one valid `TreatmentBooked`, one `PaymentMissed` and one `ProceedsMatched` sample per schema, and one schema-invalid sample | APP, OPS, the three consumers |
| rwb-source-data fake | P1 | the payments, the next installment date and a COMPLETE, a FAILED and an absent batch status for the synthetic business dates | APP, OPS |
| rwb-case fake | P3 | the open case, the running plans and the absence of a case for a synthetic account | APP |
| Treatment-record fake | S2 as the plan scopes it | the running plan position and the answer of a recorded installment | APP |
| rwb-decision package fake | P7 | `PAYMENT_MATCH` with one version in force, a second version and no version in force | APP |
| Parameters and lists fake | P3 | one key with its version and the two LOV sets | APP |
| Library fakes | PLT | the record chain healthy and stopped, the outbox and inbox writers, the workflow kit with a deterministic clock | APP, OPS |
| gateway-bff route fake | PLT edge | the merged SCR-28 answer with the payment read once | APP, OPS |

Each fake is generated from its document under `contracts/fakes/`, is versioned with the baseline and is replaced by the owner in SIT without a change to a consumer.

| REST | 2 provided, 9 consumed | the two operations on `/api/recovery/payment/v1`; three rwb-source-data reads, two rwb-case reads, two treatment-record calls, the parameters and lists reads and the package read; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 3 published, 7 subscribed | three schemas on `rwb.payment.events.v1` with retry and DLT; EV-26 and EV-30 for this key, EV-10, EV-22, EV-23, EV-24 and `AssetSold` for the other stories |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.payment`, module `contract`; artefacts under `contracts/rwb-payment/`: `openapi-v1.yaml`, `events/*.avsc`, `fakes/*.json`, `schema/rwb_payment.sql`, `messages.yaml`.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `openapi-v1.yaml` | Document | the two operations, their parameters, their bodies, their errors and their examples |
| `events/*.avsc` | Document | the three event schemas and their envelope rules |
| `consumed.yaml` | Document | the nine declarations with their owners and their review state |
| `schema/rwb_payment.sql` | Document | the baseline of 12.7 with its keys, its retention and its no-cross-schema rule |
| `messages.yaml` | Document | the message map of section 14 |
| `fakes/` | Generator | one fake per declaration, generated from the document and versioned with it |
| `ContractTag` | Build step | tags the baseline and publishes the tag to the two consumer stories |

**Build steps.** (1) Write the OpenAPI document and lint it; test AC1 and AC5. (2) Write the three event schemas and validate the samples; test AC2. (3) Write the nine declarations and generate the fakes; test AC3. (4) Write the schema baseline and pass the schema lint; test AC4. (5) Run the nine contract tests, tag `v1` and publish the tag; test AC6 and AC7.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` | owner's schema `rwb_payment`; no foreign key leaves it | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter | local record library and `rwb.decision-record.v1`, inherited shape | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | embedded kit; the package read from its owner | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Status and code |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P8-001 | A run summary carries unmatched payments | 200 with the summary text; no error code |
| MSG-P8-002 | No `PAYMENT_MATCH` version is in force | 409 on a manual match; the run alert text for the workflow |
| MSG-P3-027 | The rule version is refused | 422 with the detail of the refused package and date only |
| MSG-P1-001 | The ACE batch is late or not complete | 503 on a read of stale data; the text carries the product and the date |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the right | 403 on both operations; nothing changes |

The envelope of every error is the platform problem shape — `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`, `instance` and `traceId` — and carries no personal data. The five texts are the legacy texts of RWB-E2-008 section 14 and are copied into the message map unchanged.

SCR-28 Proceeds matching is the only screen this key serves. The baseline declares the read that fills it — `GET /proceeds` filtered by matched or unmatched — and the composite route the screen calls through the gateway-bff (DP-19). SCR-14, SCR-04 and SCR-44 are served by other services and read this service only through the same operations.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a document, a schema, a fake or a test: the window, the tolerance, the grace days, the partial floor, the match types and the LOV values are rows of their owners and appear here only as element names.
- No personal data in a schema, an event, a fixture or a log: a payment is identified by its payment reference and its account key, and an account number is never an element.
- No statement leaves `rwb_payment`: no foreign key, no cross-schema `select` and no name of another service's table in the baseline.
- No declaration without a fake, no fake without a documented answer, and no tag without the contract tests.
- The five message texts are copied, never reworded; a new text needs its owner.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the application slice of RWB-E2-008 for rwb-payment — payment matching against the running plans with the package `PAYMENT_MATCH` in force, the proceeds row in `rwb_payment`, the local decision record, and `ProceedsMatched` (EV-25) and `PaymentMissed` (EV-12) on `rwb.payment.events.v1` — is split from the published shapes (RWB-P8-E2008-CON) and from the deployment of the build (RWB-P8-E2008-OPS). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **payments posted in ALS and read from v_ace_payment matched to the running plans each day, with a missed payment event when a due installment has not arrived by the time the ACE batch completes**, so that **a broken plan is known the day after it breaks**.

Inside rwb-payment this is the matching half of RWB-E2-008:

- service `rwb-payment`, schema `rwb_payment`, REST base `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, topic `rwb.payment.events.v1` with event names `rwb.payment.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-payment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.payment` (R4, DP-13);
- JOB-07 as the event-started workflow `matchPayments` started by `AceDataReady` (EV-26) for the ALS source and a business date, with no Schedule and no Quartz row (DP-10);
- the evaluation of package `PAYMENT_MATCH` on the embedded Drools kit, with the version in force supplied by rwb-decision (DP-04);
- the proceeds row in `rwb_payment.proceeds`, written on the service's own Flyway sequence (DP-01, DP-15);
- one local decision record per match and per missed payment, hash-linked and written before the row changes, published on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03);
- the `ProceedsMatched` and `PaymentMissed` outbox rows written in the same transaction as the proceeds row and relayed with a CloudEvents envelope (DP-09);
- the ACE facts — payments, next installment date and batch status — read on the rwb-source-data contract or on the read-only `v_ace_*` views granted to this login (DP-05);
- `GET /proceeds` on the per-service base behind the gateway-bff composite route that serves SCR-28 (DP-19).

Not here: the published shapes and the fakes (RWB-P8-E2008-CON); the deployment, topics and runbook (RWB-P8-E2008-OPS); booking confirmation JOB-08 and `TreatmentBooked` (EV-11), which are the other story of this service; the manual and settlement matching of Epic 4; the reference-data story RWB-E2-027 (RWB-P8-E2027); the plan states `PLAN_RUNNING` and `PLAN_CURE_PERIOD` and R-RES-27, which are rwb-case (P3); and the package, its authoring and its approval, which are rwb-decision (P7).

##### 2. Business rationale

Payments are matched to plans by hand today, and a missed installment is found weeks later, after the cure period has gone. ACE ingests the ALS payments and the Workbench reads them through v_ace_payment, keyed by payment_code and account_key. This story matches each payment to the plan installment it pays, keeps anything unmatched on the exception list, and raises PaymentMissed the morning after a due date passes with no payment in a completed ACE batch, which R-RES-27 and the transfer rules act on. It serves REQ-CHO-007 and REQ-CHO-009, control CTL-41 and the FSD P8 measure "receipts matched the same day" (FSD P8 A2.1).

Payment matching is package PAYMENT_MATCH under ADR-012, fixed by D-RCV-36 T10 on 16 November 2026; the EXACT, PARTIAL and WINDOW rows carry match type, amount tolerance, window, grace and partial floor as decision-table columns, and the decision log names rule R-RES-26 with the package version. Under D-RCV-60 four things move:

- **the money stays here.** `proceeds` is P8's table in `rwb_payment` and this story is its only writer (DP-01).
- **the scheduler is gone.** JOB-07 is no longer a Quartz row or a Spring Batch job: it is an event-started workflow on queue `rwb-payment`, started by `AceDataReady`, and the daily cadence comes from the bank's Airflow edge (DP-10).
- **the record is written here, first.** DP-03 replaces the central DecisionLogWriter with the local decision-record library, so the record and the proceeds row commit together or not at all — which is what legacy AC9 asks (DP-03).
- **the call graph is one hop.** The legacy in-process interfaces become REST contracts with a fake, one hop and a 2 s budget, so the story is buildable on Day 1 against the rwb-source-data, rwb-case and treatment fakes (DP-11, ADR-020).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P8-E2008-CON is published: both operations on `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, the schemas `rwb.payment.TreatmentBooked.v1`, `rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1` and `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1`, the consumed-contract fakes, the error model and the `rwb_payment` baseline.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published with its writer fake: the library writes in the caller's transaction and stops the action when the record cannot be written (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-E1072-CON is published: the embedded kit loads a package, evaluates a decision table and returns the row, the outputs and the package version (DP-04).
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and their client library are published, and the four P3 contracts the plan names are readable for their fakes. The plan scopes the legacy treatment record of RWB-E2-004 as RWB-P3-E2004-CON and the package surface of RWB-E2-042 as RWB-P3-E2042-CON, while the treatment entity is published by S2 rwb-treatment and the package by P7 rwb-decision: where the two readings part, the operation names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2503; ASM-4140).
- RWB-PLT-TE006-CON (outbox, inbox, relay, dedupe key), RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (event-started workflow, retry policy, visibility query), RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (Flyway sequence and drift gate) and RWB-PLT-N001-CON (gateway-bff composite route) are published.
- `proceeds` exists in `rwb_payment` with the field set of TSD P8 T3.1 (DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009) and the standard record columns of TSD P8 T3.0. The legacy story's `payment_code` and its `payment_missed_event_key` are not in that field set, which carries `account_payment_id` instead; the value and the home of the payment code are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2503; ASM-4141).
- The service runs as login `rwb_payment` on schema `rwb_payment`, holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema, and reads `v_ace_payment`, `v_ace_account` and `v_ace_batch_status` only where the environment grants those read-only views to this login, the alternative being the rwb-source-data contract (DP-05).
- `AceDataReady` (EV-26) is published by rwb-source-data on `rwb.source-data.events.v1` with the source, the business date and the batch status.
- Package `PAYMENT_MATCH` is in force with an EXACT row: amount tolerance 0 percent, window 10 days before the due date and 0 days after, grace 0 days (assumed in the legacy story, DL25). The values are rows of the package and never constants of this build.
- `rwb.payments.matching` is the feature flag of the platform library; off means the workflow writes its inbox row and holds the business date, writes no proceeds row and publishes no event.

##### 4. Flow

1. `AceDataReady` (EV-26) arrives for the ALS source with business date D; the inbox writes its row in consumer group `rwb-payment.ace-data-ready.v1` and dedupes on the event id (DP-09).
2. The event starts `matchPayments` on queue `rwb-payment` with the source, the business date and the event id as input; the execution id is derived from the source and the date, so a rerun joins the same execution (DP-10).
3. `readFacts` checks the batch status of the ALS source for D. A status other than COMPLETE ends the run with MSG-P1-001 and writes nothing, so no missed payment is raised from stale data.
4. `readFacts` reads the payments of business date D — payment_code, account_key, payment_date, payment_amount, data_as_of — from `v_ace_payment` on the owner's contract or the granted view, and the next installment date per account from `v_ace_account` (DP-05).
5. For each payment the workflow asks rwb-case for the open case of the `account_key`; a payment on an account with no open case is listed on the REC-05 business-key break and gets no proceeds row.
6. The workflow reads the running plans of the case — installment amount, installments, installments paid, treatment type and next due date — on the treatment record contract the plan scopes as RWB-P3-E2004-CON.
7. `evaluateMatch` builds the facts of one payment against one running plan and evaluates `PAYMENT_MATCH` on the embedded kit: a payment on the plan account for the installment amount, dated inside the window before the next due date, matches that installment through the EXACT row (DP-04).
8. `recordAndApply` writes one decision record — decision code D5, rule R-RES-26, the package version of the result, the inputs reference and the answer — and only after that write succeeds writes the proceeds row, calls the treatment contract to record the installment paid and writes the `ProceedsMatched` outbox row, all in one transaction (DP-03, DP-09). A failed record write rolls the step back and the run shows MSG-P7-003.
9. A payment that matches no plan installment is written with `matched_to` UNMATCHED and appears on the exception list for the reconciliation agent (R-UNI-03).
10. After the payments, `raiseMissedPayment` walks the running plans: where the next due date plus the grace days is before the business date of the completed batch and no matched payment exists for that due date, it writes the record and the `PaymentMissed` outbox row once per plan and due date.
11. The relay publishes `ProceedsMatched` and `PaymentMissed` to `rwb.payment.events.v1`, with `rwb.payment.events.v1.retry` and `rwb.payment.events.v1.dlt` behind it, keyed on the case id and wrapped in a CloudEvents 1.0 envelope with no personal data (DP-09).
12. rwb-case consumes `PaymentMissed`, applies R-RES-27 and records the case movement for reason "payment missed". This service moves no case state and writes no case row.
13. The run closes with its summary — payments read, matched, unmatched, missed events — visible on the workflow run view to Credit Administration, on the visibility query of the kit.
14. `GET /proceeds` answers the matched and unmatched receipts on `/api/recovery/payment/v1` through the gateway-bff composite route, one hop with a 2 s budget (DP-13, DP-19).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A payment matches no plan installment | The proceeds row is written with `matched_to` UNMATCHED and appears on the exception list | MSG-P8-001 | AC7, BR3 |
| X2 | A payment is on an account with no open case | It is listed on the REC-05 business-key break; no proceeds row is written | None | BR4 |
| X3 | The ACE batch for ALS is not COMPLETE for the business date | The workflow ends before matching; no missed payment is raised from stale data | MSG-P1-001 | BR5 |
| X4 | The workflow is started twice for one business date | The second start joins the existing execution; the proceeds key and the idempotency row stop a second row and a second event | None | AC6 |
| X5 | A payment arrives on the last day of the window, or one day before it opens | The first matches the installment; the second is held UNMATCHED | MSG-P8-001 | AC7 |
| X6 | No `PAYMENT_MATCH` version is in force on the business date | The evaluation refuses with NoPackageInForce (never retried), the run stops before matching, and no proceeds row and no event are written | MSG-P3-027, MSG-P8-002 | AC8 |
| X7 | The local decision record cannot be written | The transaction writes nothing: no proceeds row, no treatment update, no outbox row | MSG-P7-003 | AC9, BR12 |
| X8 | A consumed contract does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | The activity retries on the workflow policy (1 s initial, back-off 2, 10 attempts); nothing is written until an answer arrives | None | BR9 |
| X9 | A component, a statement or a test reaches another service's schema or a view this login does not hold | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | Section 17 |

X1 to X6 are the exception paths of RWB-E2-008 carried onto the split; AC1, AC3, AC4 and AC5 of the legacy story are owned by no story of this split and their paths are traced in section 18 and not restated here. X7 is the transaction rule of DP-03, X8 the retry policy of the workflow kit, and X9 the DP-01 and DP-05 boundary. The window, the tolerance and the grace days are values of the package in force, so none of them is a constant of this story.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against RWB-P8-E2008-CON, the platform contracts and the rwb-source-data, rwb-case and treatment fakes, on its own schema, with no live neighbour |
| Negotiable | The workflow, activity and consumer-group names and the run-summary shape are this story's choice; the rules, messages, package, events and proceeds field set are fixed |
| Valuable | A missed installment is known the morning after the due date, and the match is decided by a versioned package and recorded before the money row moves |
| Estimable | One workflow, four activities, one record writer, one row, two events, five consumed contracts and one read |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against synthetic rows in the data-product fake or the ACE view and synthetic plans in the case and treatment fakes |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Payment matching with the missed payment event

  Background:
    Given package "PAYMENT_MATCH" version "PM-2026.12" is in force with row "EXACT": amount tolerance 0 percent, window 10 days before the due date and 0 days after, grace 0 days
    Given case "RC-2026-000555" has account "A-0555" and running restructure plan "T-0701" with installment amount 12,500.00 THB, installments 24 and installments paid 3
    Given account "A-0555" has next installment date 2026-12-15

  Scenario: AC2 Missed payment (legacy RWB-E2-008 AC2)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns PLAN_CURE_PERIOD for "T-0701"
    Given no payment on account "A-0555" appears in v_ace_payment between 2026-12-05 and 2026-12-15
    When JOB-07 runs on 2026-12-16 for business date 2026-12-15
    Then the system writes paymentMissed to the outbox with treatment "T-0701", due date 2026-12-15 and amount due 12,500.00
    Then P3 moves plan "T-0701" from "PLAN_RUNNING" to "PLAN_CURE_PERIOD" under rule R-RES-27
    Then the transfer rule records the case movement for reason "payment missed"

  Scenario: AC6 Repeated run (legacy RWB-E2-008 AC6)
    Given JOB-07 completed for business date 2026-12-14 with 1 matched and 1 unmatched payment
    When JOB-07 is rerun for business date 2026-12-14 from SCR-44
    Then the proceeds table still has 2 rows for business date 2026-12-14
    Then no second ProceedsMatched or PaymentMissed is written

  Scenario: AC7 Window boundary (legacy RWB-E2-008 AC7)
    Given plan "T-0702" on account "A-0666" of case "RC-2026-000566" has installment amount 12,500.00 THB and next installment date 2026-12-16
    Given v_ace_payment holds payment "PAY-90004" of 12,500.00 THB on account "A-0555" dated 2026-12-05
    Given v_ace_payment holds payment "PAY-90005" of 12,500.00 THB on account "A-0666" dated 2026-12-05
    When JOB-07 runs on 2026-12-06
    Then "PAY-90004", 10 days before its due date, is matched to "INSTALLMENT" for "T-0701" by the EXACT row
    Then "PAY-90005", 11 days before its due date, is matched to "UNMATCHED"

  Scenario: AC8 No PAYMENT_MATCH version in force (legacy RWB-E2-008 AC8)
    Given no PAYMENT_MATCH version is IN_FORCE on 2026-12-15
    When JOB-07 starts for business date 2026-12-15
    Then the evaluation refuses with NoPackageInForce and MSG-P3-027 for package "PAYMENT_MATCH"
    Then it stops before matching with MSG-P8-002
    Then no proceeds row and no event is written
    Then the job monitor shows JOB-07 as failed with an alert to Credit Administration

  Scenario: AC9 Decision log names the rule and the package version (legacy RWB-E2-008 AC9)
    Given payment "PAY-90001" matches the installment of "T-0701" on 2026-12-15
    When JOB-07 writes the match
    Then the decision log entry holds decision code "D5", rule "R-RES-26" and rule version "PM-2026.12"
    Then the proceeds row is written only after the decision log entry succeeds
    Then the run summary counts the match under version "PM-2026.12"
```

The five criteria are those of RWB-E2-008 that this slice owns, copied word for word with the origin tag added to the `Scenario` line: the repeated `Then`, the legacy reference to JOB-07, the legacy names "decision log entry" and "job monitor" all stand. AC2 carries one added line because its last two steps are rwb-case's: `Given the rwb-case contract mock returns PLAN_CURE_PERIOD for "T-0701"`. The facts of the `Background` and of AC7 come from the rwb-case, treatment and rwb-source-data fakes or from the service's own granted views. Where the legacy text says the decision log entry, this build writes the local decision record of DP-03; where it says the job monitor, this build shows the run on the workflow visibility view. AC1, AC3, AC4 and AC5 of the legacy story belong to no story of this split (GAP-2503; ASM-4142).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A payment on the plan account for the installment amount, dated inside the window before the next due date, matches that installment | R-RES-26; row EXACT of package PAYMENT_MATCH |
| BR2 | A due date that passes, plus the grace days, with no matched payment raises PaymentMissed once | R-RES-27; REQ-CHO-007 |
| BR3 | A payment that matches no plan, sale or lot is held on the exception list for the reconciliation agent | R-UNI-03; CTL-41 |
| BR4 | A payment on an account with no open case is listed on the REC-05 business-key break and gets no proceeds row | REC-05; DQ-012 |
| BR5 | Matching runs only on a COMPLETE ACE batch; no missed payment is raised from stale data | JOB-07; CTL-02 |
| BR6 | One proceeds row per payment; one PaymentMissed per plan and due date | R-UNI-40; idempotency row of DP-09 |
| BR7 | Window, tolerance, grace days, partial floor and match types are columns of the package rows with a version | Principle 1; D-RCV-36 T10 |
| BR8 | Payments in `v_ace_payment` reconcile to proceeds by count and amount daily | REC-04 |
| BR9 | The match is decided by package PAYMENT_MATCH on the embedded kit; the result names R-RES-26 and the package version, and the local record holds both before the row changes | D-RCV-36 T5, T7; ADR-012; ADR-017; DP-03, DP-04 |
| BR10 | No PAYMENT_MATCH version in force is a refusal, never a default match | R-UNI-41; D-RCV-36 T7 |
| BR11 | The proceeds row is written in `rwb_payment` only; `recovery_case`, the route state and the assignment are rwb-case's and are answered, never written | DP-01; Ownership Map (`proceeds` P8, `recovery_case` P3) |
| BR12 | The proceeds row, the treatment update, the record and the outbox row commit together or not at all; a failed record write changes nothing and answers MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; legacy AC9 |
| BR13 | The same business date twice writes once and publishes once; the execution id, the proceeds key and the idempotency row carry the rule | Legacy AC6; DP-09, DP-10 |

##### 9. State transitions

None of the case. The legacy story says so, and this slice keeps it: the states here are the match state of the proceeds row and the execution state of the workflow. `PLAN_RUNNING` and `PLAN_CURE_PERIOD` belong to rwb-case and are named only as the answer `PaymentMissed` produces under R-RES-27.

| From (`proceeds.matched_to`) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not existing | `PAYMENT_MATCHED` | The EXACT row fires on the plan account inside the window | INSTALLMENT, with the treatment update and the `ProceedsMatched` outbox row |
| Not existing | `PAYMENT_HELD` | No package row fires, or the amount or date falls outside the window | UNMATCHED, with the exception-list entry |
| Not existing | `PAYMENT_NO_CASE` | The `account_key` has no open case | No row; the REC-05 break lists the payment |
| Any | The same business date again | AC6, X4 | Unchanged; the repeat is counted |

The `matched_to` values are those of LOV-MATCH in TSD P8 T3.2 (INSTALLMENT, SETTLEMENT, FEE, SALE_PROCEEDS, UNMATCHED); this story writes INSTALLMENT and UNMATCHED only, and the other three belong to the Epic 4 stories of this service.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The recovery service identity of rwb-payment (`rwb_payment`) | Runs the workflow and its activities, evaluates the package, reads the ACE facts on the contract or the granted views, writes the proceeds row, the record and the outbox, and calls the neighbours; holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema |
| SY-RULES, the embedded Drools kit | Evaluates package PAYMENT_MATCH for each payment and returns the row, the outputs and the package version (DP-04) |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Consumes PaymentMissed and ProceedsMatched and applies R-RES-27 and the transfer rule on the case of record |
| The local decision-record library (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON) | Writes the match and the missed-payment record in the caller's transaction and publishes `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03) |
| SY-AGENT, agent platform | Reads the exception list as the reconciliation agent, right R in Write-off and posting |
| RW-CREDITAD, Credit Administration officer | Reads matched and unmatched receipts on SCR-28 and the failed runs of JOB-07, right CRUA in Write-off and posting |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the plan position on SCR-14, right R in Treatment and offer |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Owns package PAYMENT_MATCH and loads a new version through the authoring route of rwb-decision; this story only evaluates the package in force |

The rights are the rows of TSD P8 T6.1 and of the legacy authority table, and nothing wider. The run is unattended: no officer task sits on the happy path, and the step runs under the service identity of the service.

Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and of TSD P8 T3.1. DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 were the `payment_match_rule` fields and are retired by D-RCV-36 (T10); they are not in Physical Schema v6 and no story reads or writes them.

No personal data is written: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates and a rule version only, and no name, address, contact value or identity number enters the schema, the record, an event, a workflow input or a log.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-payment (P8), base `/api/recovery/payment/v1` (DP-13). The published shape, the error model and the fakes are RWB-P8-E2008-CON; this story supplies the behaviour.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/proceeds` | API-P8-001: a page of receipts with their match status, filtered by `matched`, `from`, `to`, `page` and `size` | Write-off and posting, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` | API-P8-002: a manual match of a receipt to a case and account, body `MatchRequest`, response `Proceeds` | Write-off and posting, right U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |

`GET /proceeds` is the read this story's criteria use; the manual match is declared by the CON baseline and built by the Epic 4 stories of this service, and neither operation is redeclared here. Architecture v5 lists `GET /cases/{id}/payments` among the IN operations of rwb-payment and the Ownership Map carries no row for it: the case payment list is answered through `GET /proceeds` with the case scope applied, and the extra operation is not published by this story (GAP-2503; ASM-4140).

| The open case of an account (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2503; ASM-4140)) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | the case id of an `account_key`, absent where the account is on no open case; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020, DP-11).

`TreatmentBooked` (EV-11) is the third event of this topic and belongs to the booking story of this service; this story publishes no `TreatmentBooked`. `DecisionRecorded` is written by the local library to this service's outbox on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, whose owner is rwb-decision (DP-03). The other subscriptions of the service — `TreatmentApproved` (EV-10), `LotAwarded` (EV-23), `AssetTakenOn` (EV-22), `AssetSold`, `WriteOffApproved` (EV-24) and `RulePackageInForce` (EV-30) — serve the booking and Epic 4 stories of the service and are registered by the CON and OPS stories. This story's workflow consumes `AceDataReady` only.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `matchPayments` (JOB-07; name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2503; ASM-4139)) | Workflow, one execution per source and business date, event-started by `AceDataReady` | `rwb-payment`, namespace `rwb-recovery` | input: source, business date, event id; the execution id is derived so a rerun joins it |
| `readFacts` (name as above) | Activity | `rwb-payment` | the batch check, the payments, the next installment dates and the running plans in; the facts and the freshness stamp out |
| `evaluateMatch` (name as above) | Activity | `rwb-payment` | the facts in; the row, the outputs and the package version out, or `NoPackageInForce` (not retried) |
| `recordAndApply` (name as above) | Activity | `rwb-payment` | the record, the proceeds row, the treatment update, the outbox row and the inbox row in one transaction |
| `raiseMissedPayment` (name as above) | Activity | `rwb-payment` | the plans and the business date in; the record and the `PaymentMissed` outbox row out, once per plan and due date |

`confirmBookings` (JOB-08) and `postProceeds` (the debt-sale saga step) are the other activities the architecture lists for this queue; they belong to the booking story and to RWB-P8-E4044 and the debt-sale journey, and neither is built here. The five names are a design choice of this story: the sources name JOB-07 and the queue, and no source names the workflow or its activities (GAP-2503; ASM-4139).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-07 is an event-started workflow and not a Temporal Schedule; the daily cadence is delivered by the bank's Airflow edge, which runs the ACE ingestion and signals `AceDataReady`. This service owns no cron, no overlap policy and no catch-up window for it. The outbox relay runs as a library component in every service and is not a Schedule of this one.

No foreign key leaves the schema: `case_id`, `treatment_id` and `account_payment_id` are identifiers, not cross-schema keys (DP-01, DP-05).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.payment`, module `matching`; front end `src/modules/recovery/payment/ProceedsMatching.tsx`, the fragment SCR-28 embeds, read only.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>`, recovery schema | Owner's schema `rwb_payment`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/payment/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-06 and DP-07 are the parameters and the two LOV sets the story reads, and no value of the package ever becomes a constant, because the window, the tolerance and the grace days live in the rows of DP-04. DP-15 is the service's own Flyway sequence: the migration takes the next number of `rwb_payment` and is not the monolith's `V2_008__payment_matching.sql`, whose name is Not specified for this service (GAP-2503; ASM-4141). DP-04 adds the C row RWB-P7-E1073-CON that the plan's C column does not carry; the story builds against the published package document and its fake.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `matchPayments` | Workflow | JOB-07: waits for the business date, loads the package in force, runs the steps and reports the run summary |
| `readFacts` | Activity | the batch check, the payment read, the next installment dates and the running plans, with the freshness stamp |
| `PaymentMatchFacts` | Fact builder | installment amount, next due date, payment date, payment amount and treatment type, in the shape the package expects |
| `evaluateMatch` | Activity | one payment against one running plan on the embedded kit (DP-04) |
| `recordAndApply` | Activity | the one transaction: record, proceeds row, treatment update, outbox row and inbox row (DP-03, DP-09) |
| `raiseMissedPayment` | Activity | BR2 at the grace boundary, one record and one `PaymentMissed` per plan and due date |
| `ProceedsController` | Controller | `GET /proceeds` on the per-service base (DP-13) |

**Build steps.** (1) Take the CON baseline and the migration; test the keys. (2) Confirm the PAYMENT_MATCH version and its EXACT row in SIT through the fakes. (3) Build `PaymentMatchFacts` and `evaluateMatch`; test AC7 and AC9. (4) Build `raiseMissedPayment`; test AC2 and the grace boundary. (5) Build the workflow with the REC-05 path, the no-package path and the run summary; test AC6 and AC8. (6) Build `ProceedsController` for the SCR-28 skeleton and the access test. **Done when** the tests of section 16 pass and a synthetic month shows every payment in `v_ace_payment` as a proceeds row or a held exception, with R-RES-26 and the package version on every match record.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P8-001 | Run summary with unmatched payments | {count} payments for {date} matched no plan and are on the exception list. |
| MSG-P8-002 | No PAYMENT_MATCH version in force | Payment matching for {date} did not run: no matching rule is in force. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No PAYMENT_MATCH version is in force | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The ACE batch is late or not complete | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks Write-off and posting R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

For MSG-P3-027 in this story, {check} is "no package in force" and {detail} names the package code "PAYMENT_MATCH" and the business date only, never a payment or an account fact.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-28 Proceeds matching (skeleton in E2; states Loading, matched, unmatched) lists receipts from `GET /proceeds` for the Credit Administration officer, filtered by matched or unmatched, and reaches the service through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The case owner sees the plan position on SCR-14 Treatment record and the missed payment on SCR-04 Case timeline; SCR-44 shows the JOB-07 run summary from the workflow visibility query. No screen is built here beyond the fragment the CON baseline publishes.

Integration copies of these IDs end in `-ITG` and belong to RWB-ITG-E2008-ITG.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the window, the tolerance, the grace days, the partial floor and the match types are columns of the rows of package PAYMENT_MATCH; the LOV values are reference data of RWB-P3-E1043-CON.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or prompts: payments are identified by payment_code and account_key, and account numbers are never logged.
- No read of another service's tables: ACE data only on the rwb-source-data contract or through the granted `v_ace_*` views, and case, treatment and package facts only on their owners' contracts.
- Amounts use BigDecimal with scale 2 and are compared exactly; no float, no rounding rule of this story.
- Nothing of the package is read from a workbook or a `drl_source`: the package is evaluated in force, and the version on the record is the one the kit returned.

| REQ-CHO-007 | Plan timers run from the treatment; a missed payment raises an event | Business Requirements Epic 2, sections 3.8 and 4 | FEAT-OCC-11 | 7.3 Negotiate settlement or deed in lieu | R-RES-27 | TC-E2-008-02, TC-E2-008-06 |
| REQ-CHO-009 | Payments matched to the plan; unmatched to an exception list | Business Requirements Epic 2, sections 3.8 and 4 | FEAT-OCC-10, FEAT-PAY-01, FEAT-PAY-02 | 7.3 Negotiate settlement or deed in lieu | R-RES-26, R-UNI-03, R-UNI-40 | TC-E2-008-07, TC-E2-008-08, TC-E2-008-09 |

The legacy story and this file are linked one way: the legacy key is carried in the metadata and in every `Scenario` tag.

##### 19. Out of scope

- Partial payments and late payments inside a window after the due date (RWB-E2-027, RWB-P8-E2027).
- Settlement, auction and enforcement proceeds (FEAT-PAY-03, FEAT-PAY-04; Epic 4).
- Manual matching of an unmatched receipt (`POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match`, Epic 4).
- The cure period and the broken-plan rules R-RES-28 to R-RES-31 (rwb-treatment and rwb-case).
- Booking confirmation JOB-08, `TreatmentBooked` (EV-11) and the posting file — the other stories of this service and the debt-sale journey.
- Authoring, approval and rollback of package PAYMENT_MATCH (rwb-decision), the published contract shapes and the fakes (RWB-P8-E2008-CON), and the deployment of the build (RWB-P8-E2008-OPS).


### RWB-S2-E2008-APP Payment matching with the missed payment event

SCB Collections and Recovery. Henka Group, 22 November 2026.
(C) Siam Commercial Bank and Henka Pte Ltd

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the S2 rwb-treatment slice of legacy RWB-E2-008 is split out of the payment key. The matching engine, the `proceeds` row, the exception list, the `PAYMENT_MATCH` evaluation, JOB-07 and the two events stay with rwb-payment (P8) in `RWB-P8-E2008-APP` and its contract `RWB-P8-E2008-CON`; the `v_ace_payment` and `v_ace_account` reads stay with rwb-source-data (P1). This story delivers only the treatment side of a match and of a miss: the running plan of `rwb_treatment` advanced by the matched installment, the missed installment held on the plan position, the local decision record, the reads of the parameters and lists of rwb-case at their version, the plan-position read on `/api/recovery/treatment/v1` and SCR-14 through the gateway-bff composite route. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **the installment a payment matched recorded on the running plan and above all the missed installment held on the treatment record the same morning the match runs**, so that **the plan position on the case is true — the customer is a payment further ahead, or a payment behind and visible — without a person matching receipts to a schedule by hand**. That is the plan half of the legacy intent, "so that a broken plan is known the day after it breaks".

This is the secondary slice of legacy RWB-E2-008. The legacy story owns the matching of payments to plans, the exception list, the missed-payment event and JOB-07, and every one of its ten acceptance criteria is owned by `RWB-P8-E2008-APP` and by the contract `RWB-P8-E2008-CON`, not here. This story owns no legacy criterion and invents none of its values: it tests only what a match and a miss do to the plan, and it takes the plan, the account, the case, the payment codes, the amounts, the dates, the counts, the rule IDs and the package version it uses from the legacy story character for character. Its criteria are therefore new under D-RCV-60 (ASM-4451).

What this story owns:

- the treatment side of the match: `installments_paid` (DF-TRT-032) advanced by one for the installment the event reports, and the plan position — the next due date and the missed installment of the earliest unpaid due date — read from `first_due_date` (DF-TRT-029), `installments` (DF-TRT-009), `installment_amount` (DF-TRT-031) and `installments_paid` (DF-TRT-032) on the `treatment` row of `rwb_treatment` (DP-01, DP-15);
- the subscription to `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` (EV-25) and `rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1` (EV-12) on `rwb.payment.events.v1` through this service's own consumer groups and inbox, so a redelivery acts once (DP-09);
- `TreatmentWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, started by the consumed event and not by a Quartz row or a polled table, with its `applyProceedsMatched`, `holdMissedInstallment` and `RecordAndApply` activities (DP-10);
- the local decision record of the plan change, written through the RWB-PLT-E1027-CON library in the same `rwb_treatment` transaction (DP-03);
- the evaluation of the plan-position rule with the embedded Drools kit, naming rule R-RES-26 on a match and R-RES-27 on a miss with the package version the result returns (DP-04);
- the reads of the parameters and the reference data of rwb-case at their version (DP-06, DP-07), one hop with a 2 s budget against a fake (DP-11);
- the plan-position read on base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1` (DP-13) and on SCR-14 through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

Not here: the match, the exception list, the `proceeds` table, JOB-07 and the production of the two events (P8, `RWB-P8-E2008-APP` and `RWB-P8-E2008-CON`); the ACE reads that feed the match (P1); the packages and their approval (P7); the shortfall, the break count and the closure of a broken plan (`RWB-S2-E2027-APP`, `RWB-S2-E3011-APP`); the treatment record, offer, approval and booking (`RWB-S2-E3001-APP` to `RWB-S2-E3010-APP`); the case status, `CaseWorkflow`, the assignment and the tasks (P3).

##### 2. Business rationale

Payments are matched to plans by hand today, and a missed installment is found weeks later, after the cure period has gone. That gap was measured in the legacy story and it has not moved: the Workbench measures receipts matched the same day (FSD P8 measure, CTL-41) and the restructure turnaround (FSD S2 A2.10), and neither can be measured while the plan on the case is stale. REQ-CHO-007 and REQ-CHO-009 name the two halves of the answer, and this story answers them where the plan lives.

What D-RCV-60 changes is who owns which half. The payment facts, the matching decision, the proceeds row and the missed-payment event are a payment capability and stay with rwb-payment (Architecture v5 slides 3, 17 and 41). The plan is a treatment: `installments`, `first_due_date`, `installment_amount` and `installments_paid` are columns of `treatment` in `rwb_treatment`, and the plan states are the RESTRUCTURE states of TSD S2 T4 (`R-RES-25` sets `PLAN_RUNNING`). Nothing else in the target holds a plan, so nothing else can advance it or show it behind.

Three design consequences follow, and each is designed rather than left to discipline.

- **The plan is written once, by its owner.** rwb-payment reports a match; rwb-treatment applies it to its own row, and no service reads a plan out of a payment or a case table (DP-01).
- **The event is the contract, not a call chain.** The match and the miss arrive on `rwb.payment.events.v1` through the inbox, as the design shows the missed payment reaching `TreatmentWorkflow`; one delivery acts once (DP-09; Temporal and Drools Design slide 9).
- **Every change carries its record and its version.** The plan change, the record naming R-RES-26 or R-RES-27 with the package version, and the inbox row are one transaction, and nothing is polled or scheduled here (DP-03, DP-04, DP-10).

It serves REQ-CHO-007 ("plan timers run from the treatment; a missed payment raises an event") and REQ-CHO-009 ("payments matched to the plan") on the treatment side. No business value is invented or moved: the plan, the amounts, the dates, the counts, the package version and the rule IDs are the ones the legacy story and the design already carry.

##### 3. Preconditions

- `RWB-P8-E2008-CON` is published: the `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1`, `rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1` and `rwb.payment.TreatmentBooked.v1` schemas of `rwb.payment.events.v1`, their CloudEvents envelope, and the fakes of the consumed contract, all one hop and no call chain (DP-11). This story builds against the contract and its fake on Day 1 and never against a `proceeds` row.
- `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` (EV-25) and `rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1` (EV-12) carry the case ID, the treatment ID, the payment code, the amount, the due date and the business date, and no personal data; the topics carry `.retry` and `.dlt` behind them (Architecture v5 slide 42).
- `rwb_treatment` and its login exist from the platform database story, and this service's Flyway sequence is at the version that carries the library tables; this story adds its write key and its index on the same sequence and never edits an applied migration (DP-15).
- `treatment` exists in `rwb_treatment` with the columns of TSD S2 T3.1 (DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033) and the standard record columns of T3.0, including `state` and the list LOV-TRT-OUTCOME; the record and its plan terms arrive with `RWB-S2-E3001-APP` and `RWB-S2-E3004-APP`.
- A restructure plan is in force for the case, booked, with `installments` 24, `installment_amount` 12,500.00 THB, `first_due_date` 2026-12-15 and `installments_paid` 3 — the values the legacy story carries.
- The workflow kit is in place on task queue `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and the parent `CaseWorkflow` of rwb-case routes the match and the miss to this stage (Temporal and Drools Design slide 9).
- The local decision-record library `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` is published: it writes in the caller's transaction and refuses with MSG-P7-003 when the record cannot be written (DP-03).
- The parameters and reference-data client libraries of rwb-case are published (`RWB-P3-E1042-CON`, `RWB-P3-E1043-CON`): the plan-check values and the list values are read at their version and no member of a list is written in code (DP-06, DP-07).
- The package version in force is announced on `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` (EV-30); the packages, their rows and their approval are rwb-decision's, and the embedded Drools runtime is the service template's (DP-04).
- The amounts are BigDecimal with scale 2 and are compared exactly (legacy guardrail); no amount, date or count is a constant of this build.
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline: a CON dependency never blocks, and this story starts on Day 1 with only `RWB-P8-E2008-CON` as a contract dependency (ASM-4456).

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-payment matches the payments of business date D to the running plans and, in one transaction, writes the `proceeds` row and the `ProceedsMatched` outbox row, or — for a due date that passed with no matched payment — the `PaymentMissed` outbox row; its relay publishes to `rwb.payment.events.v1` with the case ID as the key (Architecture v5 slide 42; Temporal and Drools Design slide 9).
2. This service's consumer group reads the event, the inbox records the cloud event ID in its consumer group, and a redelivery is dropped before any work is done (DP-09). A signal carries the case ID, the treatment ID, the payment code, the amount, the due date and the business date to the running `TreatmentWorkflow`.
3. `TreatmentWorkflow` resolves the treatment of the event from its own row and checks that it is a treatment with a plan — `installment_amount` and `first_due_date` non-null. A settlement, a deed in lieu or any treatment without a schedule ends the step and writes nothing, because there is no installment to advance or to miss.
4. On `ProceedsMatched`, `applyProceedsMatched` builds the plan facts — the due date of the event, the installment amount, `installments_paid` and the schedule position — and asks the embedded Drools kit for the plan-position rule of the RESTRUCTURE package version in force on the business date (DP-04).
5. The result names the plan-position rule R-RES-26 and the package version, which agree with the rule ID and the version the event carries; the step then advances `installments_paid` by one for that due date and moves the plan position to the next unpaid due date.
6. On `PaymentMissed`, `holdMissedInstallment` does the same evaluation for a miss: the result names rule R-RES-27, and the step holds the missed installment on the plan position — the earliest unpaid due date and the amount due of the event — without changing `installments_paid` and without moving the plan state.
7. `RecordAndApply` writes, in one `rwb_treatment` transaction, the `treatment` row, the local decision record with the rule ID, the package version, the payment code and the due date, and the inbox completion (DP-03); a failed record write rolls the step back with MSG-P7-003 and nothing changes.
8. The activity returns the stage outcome to the parent `CaseWorkflow` — the rule ID, the package version, the plan position and the treatment ID. The parent moves the case status and, on a miss, applies its own cure-period rule; this service writes no case row (DP-01).
9. A repeated delivery of the same cloud event ID, or a second payment code against a due date already advanced, writes no second change and no second record: the inbox row and the write key carry the rule (X4, AC3).
10. SCR-14 Treatment record reads the plan position through the gateway-bff composite route, which composes the case read of rwb-case with this service's treatment read, one hop each; the browser calls no owner service directly and the screen writes nothing (DP-19).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The event names a treatment with no plan — a settlement or a deed in lieu | The step ends and writes nothing; there is no installment to advance or to miss | None | AC4 |
| X2 | The inbox sees a cloud event ID it has already processed | The delivery is dropped before any activity runs; one change and one record exist | None | AC3 |
| X3 | The local decision record cannot be written | The transaction writes nothing: no plan change, no record, no inbox completion; the event is redelivered under the same ID | MSG-P7-003 | AC5 |
| X4 | A plan advance would be written twice — a redelivery, or the same due date twice | The write key refuses the second write and changes nothing | None | AC3 |
| X5 | The parameters or the reference-data read does not answer inside the budget, or its breaker is open | Nothing is written; the activity retries on the workflow policy of 1 s initial interval, back-off 2, 10 attempts | MSG-GEN-006 | BR6 |
| X6 | A component, a statement or a test reaches a payment, proceeds, rule, case or timer table | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | Section 17 |

X1 to X4 are the paths this slice adds to the legacy story's own; X5 is the retry policy of the workflow kit on the two reads of rwb-case, and X6 the DP-01 and DP-05 boundary. The legacy exception paths X1 to X6 of RWB-E2-008 (unmatched payment, no open case, incomplete batch, repeated run, window boundary, no package in force) are rwb-payment's and are traced, not restated, in section 18.
