| Negotiable | The activity names, the consumer-group names, the write key and the flag name are this story's choice; the rules, the plan states, the list values, the messages and the package version are fixed |
| Valuable | The plan on the case is true the same morning: a payment further ahead, or a missed installment visible before the cure period runs out |
| Estimable | One stage branch, two activities, two consumers with an inbox, one repository, one migration, one library adapter and one read |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests, as a secondary slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Each of the seven criteria of section 7 is one automated test; the payment service, the package and the parent are stubbed |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Payment matching with the missed payment event — the plan position on the treatment record

  Background:
    Given package "PAYMENT_MATCH" version "PM-2026.12" is in force with row "EXACT": amount tolerance 0 percent, window 10 days before the due date and 0 days after, grace 0 days
    Given case "RC-2026-000555" has account "A-0555" and running restructure plan "T-0701" with installment amount 12,500.00 THB, installments 24 and installments paid 3
    Given account "A-0555" has next installment date 2026-12-15

  Scenario: AC1 The matched installment advances the plan (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-payment contract mock returns proceedsMatched for case "RC-2026-000555", treatment "T-0701", payment code "PAY-90001", amount 12,500.00, due date 2026-12-15, rule "R-RES-26" and package version "PM-2026.12"
    When TreatmentWorkflow consumes rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1 for business date 2026-12-14
    Then treatment "T-0701" holds installments_paid 4 and its next due date is 2027-01-15
    Then the local decision record names rule "R-RES-26", package version "PM-2026.12" and payment code "PAY-90001", and it is written in the same transaction as the treatment row
    Then the plan state stays PLAN_RUNNING and this service publishes no business event of its own

  Scenario: AC2 The missed installment is held on the plan position (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-payment contract mock returns paymentMissed for case "RC-2026-000555", treatment "T-0701", due date 2026-12-15 and amount due 12,500.00
    Given no payment on account "A-0555" appears in v_ace_payment between 2026-12-05 and 2026-12-15
    When TreatmentWorkflow consumes rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1 for business date 2026-12-15 on 2026-12-16
    Then treatment "T-0701" shows the missed installment for due date 2026-12-15 with amount due 12,500.00 and installments_paid stays 3
    Then the case owner sees the missed payment on the treatment record the same morning
    Then the local decision record names rule "R-RES-27" and the package version the evaluation returned
    Then this service writes no case status and moves no plan state

  Scenario: AC3 A repeated event writes the plan once (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-payment contract mock returns the proceedsMatched of AC1 for case "RC-2026-000555"
    When rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1 with the same cloud event ID is delivered twice in a row
    Then the inbox holds one processed event for the cloud event ID and the second delivery drops before any activity runs
    Then treatment "T-0701" still holds installments_paid 4 and exactly one decision record exists for "PAY-90001"
    Then a second payment code naming the due date already advanced writes no further advance

  Scenario: AC4 A treatment without a plan writes nothing (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-payment contract mock returns proceedsMatched for a treatment of case "RC-2026-000566" whose treatment_type is "SETTLEMENT" and whose installments is null
    When TreatmentWorkflow consumes rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1 for that case
    Then no column of the treatment row changes and no decision record of a plan advance is written
    Then the inbox records the event as processed and no retry is scheduled

  Scenario: AC5 A plan advance that cannot be recorded changes nothing (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the local decision-record mock refuses the write with MSG-P7-003
    When TreatmentWorkflow consumes the proceedsMatched of AC1
    Then no column of treatment "T-0701" changes and no inbox row is completed
    Then the step answers MSG-P7-003 and the event is redelivered under the same cloud event ID
    Then the second attempt, with the record store healthy, advances the plan once

  Scenario: AC6 The plan position shows on SCR-14 through the composite route (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given treatment "T-0701" holds installments_paid 3 and the missed installment for due date 2026-12-15 with amount due 12,500.00
    Given the gateway-bff composite route serves SCR-14 Treatment record from the case read of rwb-case and the treatment read of this service, one hop each
    When an officer holding Treatment and offer R opens SCR-14 for case "RC-2026-000555"
    Then SCR-14 shows the plan terms, installments_paid 3, the next due date 2026-12-15 and the missed installment for 2026-12-15 with 12,500.00
    Then the browser calls no owner service directly and the screen writes nothing

  Scenario: AC7 No personal data in the row, the record, the event or the logs (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a proceedsMatched arrives for case "RC-2026-000555" carrying the case ID, the treatment ID, payment code "PAY-90001", the amount 12,500.00 and due date 2026-12-15
    When TreatmentWorkflow applies the plan advance
    Then the treatment row, the local decision record, the workflow history, the log lines and the span attributes carry IDs, codes, amounts, dates and a rule version only
    Then no name, address, telephone number, national identity number or account holder name is written, logged or put on a message
```

The seven criteria are new under D-RCV-60 and test only the S2 deliverable of this story: the plan advanced by the matched installment, the missed installment held on the plan position, the inbox dedupe and the write key, the treatment without a plan, the failed record which changes nothing, the SCR-14 read and the no-PII rule. The ten legacy criteria AC1 to AC10 of RWB-E2-008 and the legacy test cases TC-E2-008-01 to TC-E2-008-10 belong to `RWB-P8-E2008-APP`, where the matching, the window, the exception list, the repeated run and the no-version-in-force rules are written word for word with their origin tags; they are not restated here and no criterion of this story claims them. Every value is the legacy story's own: plan "T-0701", account "A-0555", case "RC-2026-000555", 12,500.00 THB, 24 installments, 3 paid, due dates 2026-12-15 and 2027-01-15, payment "PAY-90001" dated 2026-12-14, package version "PM-2026.12", rules R-RES-26 and R-RES-27.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A payment the match reports for the plan's due date advances `installments_paid` by one and moves the plan position to the next unpaid due date | legacy BR1; R-RES-26; REQ-CHO-009 |
| BR2 | A due date that passes with no matched payment is held on the plan position as the missed installment, with its due date and its amount due, and `installments_paid` does not move | legacy BR2; R-RES-27; REQ-CHO-007 |
| BR3 | One advance per payment code and due date; one missed installment per plan and due date; the inbox and the write key carry the rule | legacy BR6; R-UNI-40; DP-09 |
| BR4 | The plan is this service's own row: the proceeds row, the rule rows, the case status and the timers are answers of their owners and are never read as tables | DP-01; Ownership Map (`treatment` S2) |
| BR5 | Every plan change is written with its local decision record naming R-RES-26 or R-RES-27 and the package version, in one transaction | legacy BR9; DP-03, DP-04 |
| BR6 | A parameters or list read that fails changes nothing, and the step retries on the workflow policy | DP-06, DP-07; TSD S2 T7 |
| BR7 | Window, tolerance, grace days and match types are columns of the package rows with a version, never code of this service | legacy BR7; D-RCV-36 T10 |
| BR8 | The plan position is derived from `first_due_date`, `installments`, `installment_amount` and `installments_paid`; no frequency, no amount and no date is a constant of this build | TSD S2 T3.1; legacy section 11 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1 and BR2 are `applyProceedsMatched` and `holdMissedInstallment` with the evaluated plan-position rule. BR3 is the inbox row and the write key of `RecordAndApply`. BR4 is the schema boundary of section 11. BR5 is the record library and the one transaction. BR6 is the retry policy of section 12.5. BR7 is the package read, so no threshold is a constant here. BR8 is the derivable plan position of section 11, recorded as ASM-4453.

##### 9. State transitions

None of the case. The case status is rwb-case's and is moved by the parent `CaseWorkflow` from the stage outcome this service reports (DP-01). The rows below are the plan position on this service's own `treatment` row; the plan states are the RESTRUCTURE states of TSD S2 T4, and this story moves none of them.

| From (plan position) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| `installments_paid` n, earliest unpaid due date D | PAYMENT_MATCHED | The match reports the installment of D | `installments_paid` n+1, next due date D+1 period, plan state unchanged (R-RES-26) |
| `installments_paid` n, earliest unpaid due date D | PAYMENT_MISSED | No matched payment for D and the due date has passed | Unchanged `installments_paid`; the missed installment D and its amount due held on the plan position (R-RES-27) |
| A treatment without a plan | PAYMENT_MATCHED or PAYMENT_MISSED | `installments` or `first_due_date` is null | No change; the step ends (X1) |
| Any | A repeated delivery or the same due date again | The inbox or the write key refuses | No change; the repeat is counted (X2, X4) |

The plan state `PLAN_RUNNING`, the cure period of R-RES-27, the break count and the closure of a broken plan are `RWB-S2-E2027-APP` and `RWB-S2-E3011-APP` and are named here only as the context the plan position is read in. The stage execution itself is RUNNING, COMPLETED or FAILED in the workflow history, and a failed execution is retried on the platform policy with the record failure of X3 redelivered under the same cloud event ID (ASM-4455).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The rwb-treatment service identity (login `rwb_treatment`) | Consumes the two events, evaluates the plan-position rule, writes `treatment`, the record and the inbox row, and calls the parameters and list reads; holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema |
| SY-RULES, the embedded Drools kit | Evaluates the RESTRUCTURE package version in force for the plan position and returns the rule ID and the version (DP-04) |
| The local decision-record library (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON) | Writes the plan change record in the caller's transaction and publishes `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the plan position and the missed payment on the cases in scope (Treatment and offer CRU) |
| RW-RESTRUCT, restructuring officer (FCR) | Reads the plan position and the missed payment on the cases in scope (Treatment and offer CRUA) |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module; SY-AGENT, agent platform | Read the treatment record across the contract with right R, as TSD S2 T6.1 lists them; the case status and the exception list are theirs |
| RW-CREDITAD, Credit Administration officer | Reads the matched and unmatched receipts on SCR-28 as rwb-payment serves them (Write-off and posting CRUA); no write here |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit; RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Read the plan position, the record and the version it was taken under (R) |
| No delegation of authority level applies | The story applies a match and holds a miss; it approves nothing |

The rights are the rows of TSD S2 T6.1 and nothing wider. The step is unattended: no officer task sits on the happy path, and it runs under the service identity of the service.

| DF-TRT-013, DF-TRT-014 | treatment (S2, `rwb_treatment`) | outcome, outcome_at | Not written: the outcome of a plan is `RWB-S2-E2027-APP`'s |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_record (local, `rwb_treatment`) | all fields, through `DecisionRecordWriter.record` | Write, in the same transaction (DP-03) |
| DF-FIN-002, DF-FIN-003, DF-FIN-004, DF-FIN-006, DF-FIN-008 | proceeds (P8, `rwb_payment`) | case_id, treatment_id, payment_code, amount, matched_to | Not read as a table: they arrive on the event of `RWB-P8-E2008-CON` (DP-01) |
| DF-ACE-028, DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-046, DF-ACE-054, DF-ACE-178, DF-ACE-179, DF-ACE-182 | `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_payment`, `v_ace_batch_status` (P1 views) | next_installment_date, the payment fields, the batch fields | Not read here and no view is granted: rwb-source-data serves them to rwb-payment (DP-05) |
| DF-REF-002, DF-REF-003, DF-REF-296, DF-REF-297, DF-REF-298 | `rule_row` (P7, `rwb_decision`) | rule_id, rule_version, package_version_id, drools_rule_name, outputs | Not read as a table: the evaluated result returns them (DP-04) |
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 | recovery_case, timer, assignment (P3, `rwb_case`) | the case, its status, its timers | Not read and not written: the status is the parent's and the plan clock is not this story's |
| Standard column | treatment (S2, `rwb_treatment`) | state, version, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by | Read `state`; write the audit columns as TSD S2 T3.0 defines them |
| processed_event, outbox_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_treatment` | the inbox row and the write key of the step | Write through the library, in the step's transaction (DP-09) |

`treatment` is the only table this story writes, and it writes one column of it — `installments_paid` — plus the audit columns and its `decision_log_id`. The plan position is not a stored column set: `first_due_date`, `installments`, `installment_amount` and `installments_paid` already carry it, and the earliest unpaid due date and its amount due are derived from them; the payment frequency of a plan is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2693; ASM-4453). The legacy rows of `proceeds`, of the ACE views and of the rule rows are their owners' and are not read here (DP-01, DP-05). No foreign key leaves `rwb_treatment`, and `case_id` and `decision_log_id` are identifiers, not keys across schemas. Field identifiers are those of TSD S2 T3.1 and the Logical Data Model.

**No new table and no new column of another schema.** This story's Flyway version adds the write key that makes one advance per due date and one miss per due date — a unique key on the treatment and the due date the record names, plus the index the plan-position read uses — on `rwb_treatment`, and it adds no business column (DP-15). No personal data is written: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates and a rule version only.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-treatment (S2); base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1` (DP-13). The two operations are the ones TSD S2 T-A.1 lists and RWB-S2-E3001-CON publishes; this story supplies the plan-position behaviour and adds no path.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/treatments/{treatmentId}` (API-S2-002) | `Treatment` out, including the plan terms DF-TRT-009, DF-TRT-029 and DF-TRT-031 and `installments_paid` DF-TRT-032, plus the plan-position elements of the read | Treatment and offer R, scope applied, through the guard library | Not applicable |
| PATCH | `/treatments/{treatmentId}` (API-S2-003) | `TreatmentUpdate` in, `Treatment` out; the installment-paid write of the legacy `TreatmentApi.recordInstallmentPaid` where the contract freeze chooses the REST route for the match | Treatment and offer U, scope applied | The write key on the treatment and the due date |

The errors of both are 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409, 422 and 503 with MSG-GEN-006, in the RFC 9457 problem body. The operation names, their payload elements and the element names of the plan position are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2693; ASM-4452), and this story reads the plan position on the GET as it stands.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Base / contract | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The plan-check values in force (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2693; ASM-4452)) | RWB-P3-E1042-CON | P3 rwb-case | The parameters the plan-position step reads at their version, cached; no period, threshold or amount in code (DP-06) |
| The list values of the plan and the miss reasons (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2693; ASM-4452)) | RWB-P3-E1043-CON | P3 rwb-case | LOV-TREATMENT and LOV-TRT-OUTCOME at their version; no member is written in code (DP-07) |

Two reads, one hop each with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020, DP-11). No payment, proceeds or rule read is made: those facts arrive on the contract's events (DP-01).

###### 12.3 Events published

None of this service's business events. `TreatmentApproved` (EV-10) is the event of this service's approval story and is not produced here. The local decision-record library writes its own `DecisionRecorded` row on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` inside the transaction of the change (DP-03), and the outbox relay of the service template publishes it.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Consumer group | Payload used | When |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` (EV-25) | `rwb.payment.events.v1`, owner P8 | `rwb-treatment.payment-proceeds-matched.v1` | the case ID, the treatment ID, the payment code, the amount, the due date and the business date; starts the plan advance | on the relay of rwb-payment, deduped in the inbox |
| `rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1` (EV-12) | `rwb.payment.events.v1`, owner P8 | `rwb-treatment.payment-missed.v1` | the same payload; holds the missed installment on the plan position | on the relay of rwb-payment, deduped in the inbox |
| `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` (EV-30) | `rwb.decision.events.v1`, owner P7 | `rwb-treatment.rule-package-in-force.v1` | announces the RESTRUCTURE package version in force; the stage swaps it in and stamps it on the record | once per published version |

The envelope is CloudEvents 1.0 keyed `caseId`, and the payload carries IDs, codes, amounts and dates only. A replayed workflow reuses the recorded result of the activity, so no second evaluation and no second write happens on replay (DP-04, DP-09).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TreatmentWorkflow` | Workflow, the stage child of `CaseWorkflow`, one execution per case and stage, with the four steps receive, evaluate, record and apply | `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: case ID, treatment ID, payment code, amount, due date, business date and the event ID; output: the stage outcome of section 9 |
| `applyProceedsMatched` (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2693; ASM-4452)) | Activity | `rwb-treatment` | The plan facts and the event in; the rule ID, the package version and the advanced plan position out |
| `holdMissedInstallment` (name as above) | Activity | `rwb-treatment` | The plan facts and the event in; the rule ID, the package version and the missed installment out |
| `RecordAndApply` (the design's activity) | Activity | `rwb-treatment` | One transaction: the treatment column, the decision record, the inbox completion and the outbox row of the record library |

The plan-position rule is evaluated inside the activity with the embedded Drools kit and never from workflow code (DP-04). The two activity names beyond the design's `RecordAndApply` are this story's design choice and are fixed by no source document (ASM-4452). `TreatmentWorkflow` is the one workflow the S2 ownership row carries.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The step is started by the consumed event through the workflow kit and is not a Temporal Schedule: this service owns no cron, no overlap policy and no catch-up window for the match (DP-10). The daily cadence belongs to the bank's Airflow edge that runs the ACE ingestion, and the plan clock of a running plan is `RWB-S2-E3010-APP`'s durable timer, not a task of this story. The outbox relay runs as a library component in every service and is not a Schedule of this one.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `treatment` | `rwb_treatment` | S2 | Writes `installments_paid`, the audit columns and `decision_log_id`; the table arrives with RWB-S2-E3001-APP and this story's Flyway version adds the write key and the index (DP-15) |
| `decision_record` | `rwb_treatment` | PLT library applied in this schema | Written through `DecisionRecordWriter.record` in the caller's transaction; the central `decision_log_entry` is P7's and is never touched (DP-03) |
| `processed_event`, `outbox_event`, `idempotency_key` | `rwb_treatment` | PLT library applied in this schema | The inbox row of the two consumed events, the record library's outbox row and the write key of the step (DP-09) |

Not owned and never read as a table: `proceeds` (P8, `rwb_payment`), `rule_row`, `rule_package`, `rule_package_version` and `decision_log_entry` (P7, `rwb_decision`), `recovery_case`, `timer`, `assignment` and `task` (P3, `rwb_case`), and every `v_ace_*` view (P1). No foreign key leaves the schema and no cross-schema join exists (DP-01, DP-05).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.treatment`, module `planposition`; front end `src/modules/recovery/treatment/PlanPosition.tsx`, the fragment SCR-14 embeds, read only.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_treatment`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/treatment/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 is the schema rule of section 11 and BR4. DP-03 is the transaction the story is built on: the record is a local row written with the change or not at all. DP-04 is the evaluation of the plan-position rule with the package version in force, inside the activity, so a replay reuses the recorded answer. DP-05 is a prohibition here: the payment and installment facts arrive on the P8 contract, so this module reads no `v_ace_*` view. DP-06 and DP-07 are the two reads of 12.2, cached. DP-09 is the inbox of the two consumed events, the write key and the record library's outbox row. DP-10 is the event-started stage on queue `rwb-treatment`, with no Quartz row and nothing polled. DP-11 is the contract-with-a-fake rule: the legacy in-process `TreatmentApi` calls become one-hop contracts with mocks, so this story builds on Day 1 with no payment table; where the match is delivered as a REST write instead of the event, it is served by `PATCH /treatments/{treatmentId}` (ASM-4452). DP-13 puts the read on the service base, DP-15 is the service's own Flyway version, and DP-19 reaches SCR-14 through the gateway-bff composite route.

**Dependencies the table adds and the build list does not hold.** The table adds eight H rows and three C rows (`RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`, `RWB-PLT-E1072-CON`, `RWB-PLT-E1042-CON`, `RWB-PLT-E1043-CON`, `RWB-PLT-TE006-CON`, `RWB-PLT-E1071-CON`, `RWB-PLT-E1044-CON`, `RWB-PLT-N001-CON`; `RWB-P7-E1073-CON`, `RWB-P3-E1042-CON`, `RWB-P3-E1043-CON`). Every one is a platform library or a contract of wave 0 and of the rule programme that the service template already carries, so the metadata keeps the plan's lists — `Depends on (build)` None, contract dependency `RWB-P8-E2008-CON` — and the story builds against the fakes until they publish (ASM-4454).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `TreatmentWorkflow` (plan-position branch) | Workflow | The four steps of the stage, the branch on the two events and the outcome report to the parent |
| `PaymentEventConsumer` | Consumer | Reads the two P8 events through the inbox, resolves the treatment and signals the child; a redelivery is dropped |
| `applyProceedsMatched` | Activity | The plan facts, the evaluated plan-position rule and the advance of `installments_paid` (DP-04) |
| `holdMissedInstallment` | Activity | The plan facts, the evaluated miss rule and the missed installment on the plan position |
| `PlanPositionGuard` | Service | Refuses a treatment without a plan, a second advance for the same due date and a change on a refused record |
| `RecordAndApply` | Activity | One transaction: the treatment column, the decision record, the inbox completion and the record library's outbox row |
| `TreatmentPlanRepository` | Repository | Reads and writes the plan columns of `treatment` in `rwb_treatment` only |
| `DecisionRecordAdapter` | Library adapter | Calls `DecisionRecordWriter.record` with the rule ID and the package version (DP-03) |
| `ParametersClient`, `ReferenceDataClient` | Clients | The two rwb-case reads, one hop, 2 s, a breaker (DP-06, DP-07, DP-11) |
| `Migrations` | Migration | The write key and the index on the service's own Flyway sequence (DP-15) |

**Build steps.** (1) The Flyway version with the write key and the index, and the migration test against the TSD types. (2) `PaymentEventConsumer` and the inbox path, with the doubled event and the dropped redelivery; test AC3 and X2. (3) `applyProceedsMatched` with the plan facts and the package fixture; test AC1, AC4 and the write key. (4) `holdMissedInstallment`; test AC2. (5) `PlanPositionGuard`, `RecordAndApply` and the rollback path; test AC5 and X3. (6) The plan position on the GET through the composite route fake; test AC6. (7) The boundary and no-PII tests; test AC7 and BR4. **Done when** the tests of section 16 pass, a synthetic month of matches advances each plan once per due date, every miss is held once with its due date and amount, every change has a record naming R-RES-26 or R-RES-27 and the package version, and SCR-14 shows both through the composite route in SIT.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | The local decision record cannot be written (X3) | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The identity has no right on the treatment read or write (section 12.1) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A parameters or list read did not answer inside the budget (X5) | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P4-002 are the texts the FSD S2 exception flows and the legacy story carry; MSG-GEN-006 is the platform text of the error standard for an unavailable dependency, where {system} is "Reference data" or "Parameters". Each error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId`, `detail` and `instance`; the status mapping is 403 for MSG-P4-002, 422 for a refused record check and 503 for MSG-GEN-006. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10. The two messages of the match itself, MSG-P8-001 and MSG-P8-002, are rwb-payment's run summary and are not produced here.

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | State | What the user sees or does |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-14 Treatment record | Loading | The placeholder while the composite route answers |
| SCR-14 Treatment record | Plan running | The plan terms, `installments_paid` and the next due date, read only |
| SCR-14 Treatment record | Installment missed | The missed installment with its due date and amount due, and the next due date, read only |
| SCR-14 Treatment record | Refused | A role without Treatment and offer R reads MSG-P4-002 and nothing changes |
| SCR-14 Treatment record | Plan not yet available | The treatment without a plan shows its terms and no plan position |

SCR-14 Treatment record is first in E2 for the treatment record (FSD S2 screens table) and is served by the gateway-bff composite route, which composes the case read of rwb-case with the treatment read of this service, one hop each, read only (DP-19); the browser calls no owner service directly and the screen writes nothing. SCR-28 Proceeds matching, its exception list and the JOB-07 run summary on SCR-44 are rwb-payment's and are not built or read here, beyond the running balance the Credit Administration officer already reads there. The screen field list, the route specification and the layout belong to the platform edge story and the screen owners; this story fixes the service side of the answer only.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the window, the tolerance, the grace days, the match types and the plan-check values are rows of the packages and of the parameters read at their version; a build check fails on any of them in the Java source or the module configuration (BR7, BR8).
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow inputs, events or records: the row, the record, the workflow history, the log lines and the span attributes carry the case ID, the treatment ID, the payment code, the rule ID, the package version, amounts and dates only, and no account number is logged.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views: this story reads no ACE view and holds no grant on one, and the payment and installment facts arrive on the P8 contract (DP-05, DP-01).
- No read of another service's tables and no cross-schema join: `proceeds` (P8), `rule_row` and `rule_package` (P7), `recovery_case`, `timer` and `assignment` (P3) are reached only through their owners' contracts, and the boundary test fails the build on any statement outside `rwb_treatment`.
- Amounts use BigDecimal with scale 2 and are compared exactly; no float and no rounding rule of this story.
- The decision record is written in the same transaction as the plan change, and a failed write rolls the whole step back with MSG-P7-003 (X3, AC5).
- One advance per due date and one miss per due date: the write key and the inbox carry the rule, and a redelivery writes nothing (BR3, AC3).
- Nothing is polled and no timer row is read: the step is event-started and the plan clock is not this story's (DP-10).
- The case status and the plan state are not written here; the parent moves the case and the plan states are the other stories' (DP-01, section 9).
- An applied migration is never edited: the write key and the index are a new version on the service's own Flyway sequence (DP-15).

| ADR-013, ADR-014, ADR-015, ADR-016, ADR-017, ADR-020, ADR-022 | 19 services inside ACE, a schema and a login per service, Kafka with outbox and inbox, the reusable Temporal layer, embedded Drools per service, contract-first REST with one hop, and the local decision record |

##### 19. Out of scope

- The payment and proceeds matching, the row order, the window, the tolerance, the grace, the exception list, the `proceeds` table, JOB-07 and the production of the two events: `RWB-P8-E2008-APP` and `RWB-P8-E2008-CON`.
- The ACE payment, installment-date and batch-status reads and the data-product freshness: `RWB-P1-E2008-APP` and rwb-source-data.
- The packages, their rows, their versions, their load and their approval: rwb-decision (P7).
- The plan states, the cure period (R-RES-27 to R-RES-31), the shortfall and the closure of a broken plan: `RWB-S2-E2027-APP`, `RWB-S2-E3011-APP` and rwb-case (P3).
- The treatment record, the offer, the approval, the plan offer, the booking and the schedule: `RWB-S2-E3001-APP` to `RWB-S2-E3010-APP`.
- The case status, `CaseWorkflow`, the assignment, the officer tasks and the queues: rwb-case (P3).
- The rights, the roles, the scope data and the guard library: rwb-access (P4) and the platform library stories.
- SCR-28 Proceeds matching, its exception list, the manual match and the SCR-44 run summary: rwb-payment (P8) and Epic 4.
- The gateway-bff composite route, the SCR-14 field list and the layout: `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` and the screen owners (DP-19).
- Partial and late payments inside a window (RWB-E2-027), settlement, auction and enforcement proceeds, the posting file and the application of proceeds to the case balance (Epic 4).
- The real cross-service proof against live rwb-payment, rwb-case and rwb-decision (the wave 2 integration harness, RWB-ITG-E2008-ITG), and the deployment of this build.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-008 for rwb-source-data. The legacy matcher (JOB-07) read the payments of the business date, the next installment date of each plan account and the ALS batch status in-process from the monolith's views, then matched each payment to a plan installment through package `PAYMENT_MATCH`, wrote the proceeds row and raised `PaymentMissed` when a due installment had not arrived. Under D-RCV-60 that data is answered by this service over base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`: the payments of one business date over `v_ace_payment` and the installment facts of one account over `v_ace_account`, both behind the batch and freshness gate that this service already owns (DP-05, DP-11, DP-13). The matcher, the proceeds row, the rule package, the decision record and both events stay with rwb-payment, rwb-decision and rwb-treatment (DP-03, DP-04, DP-10); this story answers two reads and one gate, stores nothing, evaluates no rule and publishes no event (DP-01, DP-09, DP-15). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **recovery developer (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **the payments of one business date and the next installment date of one account to be reads of rwb-source-data over its own ACE views, refused while the ALS batch of the business date is not COMPLETE or DP01 is STALE, each payment answered once under its `payment_code` with the exact amount and the batch status it was read under**, so that **the payment matching run matches against one copy of the ACE payment rows, a held business date is answered as a hold and never as an empty day, and no payment, installment date or batch fact is copied out of ACE into a Workbench table**.

This is the rwb-source-data slice of legacy RWB-E2-008. The legacy story ran one job that read the payments, read the next installment date of each plan account, read the ALS batch status, evaluated package `PAYMENT_MATCH`, wrote the proceeds row, called the treatment record, published `ProceedsMatched` and `PaymentMissed`, and wrote the run summary. Under D-RCV-60 that job is four owners and a contract, and this story delivers only the ACE facts it consumes and the gate they pass through:

- **the payments read** on base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`: `GET /payments?businessDate=` over `v_ace_payment`, answering one row per `payment_code` with `paymentCode`, `accountKey`, `paymentDate`, `paymentAmount` and `dataAsOf`, ordered by `paymentCode`, with `rowCount`, the status of the ALS batch row of that business date, and the data-product status the rows were read under;
- **the installment-facts read**: `GET /accounts/{accountKey}/installment-facts?businessDate=`, answering `nextInstallmentDate` from `v_ace_account` at that business date, together with `accountKey`, `productKey`, `daysPastDue` and `dataAsOf`, which are the account facts the matcher needs to build its facts for the rule package;
- **the batch and freshness gate**: a read whose ALS batch for the business date is not COMPLETE, or whose DP01 is STALE, answers 409 with MSG-P1-001 naming the product and the date of the load in use and MSG-P2-007 for the held run, and answers no row of any kind. The gate reads this service's own `data_product_load` rows and `v_ace_batch_status`, so it cannot disagree with the freshness stamp of RWB-P1-E1015-APP;
- **no proceeds row, no case lookup, no rule evaluation, no event**: this story writes no `proceeds` row, resolves no case, evaluates no package row, and publishes neither `PaymentMissed` nor `ProceedsMatched`. The `proceeds` table is rwb-payment's (ownership map: `proceeds` → P8), the plan and its installment amount are rwb-treatment's (`treatment` → S2), and the decision record of a match is rwb-decision's (`decision_log_entry` → P7).

It owns no legacy acceptance criterion of RWB-E2-008, which is why its criteria are new and tagged D-RCV-60. **AC1** (a payment matched to the installment, and the treatment record that records it) belongs to **RWB-P8-E2008-APP**, **RWB-S2-E2008-APP** and **RWB-P7-E2008-APP** for the rule result and the decision log. **AC2** (a missed payment) belongs to **RWB-P8-E2008-APP**, and P3 applies the plan state it raises. **AC3** (the exception list of an unmatched payment) belongs to **RWB-P8-E2008-APP**. **AC4** (a payment on an account with no open case, and the REC-05 break row) belongs to **RWB-P8-E2008-APP**, and **RWB-P1-E1011-APP** writes the break row. **AC5** (the ACE batch is not complete) is proved here on the read side only: this story answers the hold, and the run's refusal for the business date is **RWB-P8-E2008-APP**'s. **AC6** (a repeated run) belongs to **RWB-P8-E2008-APP**. **AC7** (the window boundary) belongs to **RWB-P8-E2008-APP** and **RWB-P7-E2008-APP**. **AC8** (no package in force) belongs to **RWB-P7-E2008-APP** and **RWB-P8-E2008-APP**. **AC9** (the decision log naming the rule and the package version) belongs to **RWB-P7-E2008-APP**. The cross-service proof is **RWB-ITG-E2008-ITG**.

The shapes of the two operations as the matching run consumes them are declared by RWB-P8-E2008-CON, which lists the rwb-source-data elements of the payment-matching step and their answers; this story implements them and publishes its OpenAPI fragment with the service baseline. The resource names, the query parameters, the response entities, the ordering, the row cap and the error status set are a target choice and not a legacy value, because the legacy read was an in-process Java interface with no path and no status code (GAP-0599; ASM-0841; GAP-0601; ASM-0843).

##### 2. Business rationale

Payments are matched to plans by hand today, and a missed installment is found weeks later, after the cure period has gone (legacy RWB-E2-008 §2). ACE ingests the ALS payments (INT-02, daily end of day) and the Workbench reads them through `v_ace_payment` (TSD P1 T5.1; REQ-RDF-002), so the facts the matcher needs are already in ACE, current to the previous working day, and the only question is who answers them. Under D-RCV-60 the answer is rwb-source-data: it owns the ACE view contract and the freshness stamp (Architecture v5 slides 15 and 41; ADR-010), and no other service reads the views (Architecture v5 slides 11 and 12). Reading the same rows from a second copy would give the matcher a different payment set from the one the reconciliation of the same day counts.

The split matters because the matcher is not the reader. The matcher belongs to rwb-payment, which owns payment and proceeds matching, and it runs as JOB-07, an event-triggered workflow started by `AceDataReady` (Architecture v5 slide 44 row JOB-07; slide 17, rwb-payment "Source data: payments for business date"; Temporal and Drools design slide 9). This service owns the row facts and the gate, and it must answer them in the shape the matcher consumes: one row per `payment_code` with the exact amount, the next installment date of the account as of the same business date, and the batch status the rows were read under. Everything else the legacy job did — the EXACT row of package `PAYMENT_MATCH`, rule `R-RES-26`, the proceeds row, `ProceedsMatched`, `PaymentMissed` and the run summary — is proved in the slices that own it.

**What D-RCV-60 changes.** Not the rationale and not one value: the case, the account, the plan, the installment amount, the next installment date, the business date, the three payments and the batch date keep their meaning and their values. What changes is where the row is read, who owns it and how it is reached — this service's own views and two reads over `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, one hop with a 2 s budget, instead of an in-process call into the monolith (DP-05, DP-11, DP-13).

**Two reads, no copy.** No table of this service holds a payment row or an installment date. Both answers are derived from the views on every request, and a second read of the same business date reads the views again; that is the whole of the no-copy rule of D-RCV-35 U1 and of FSD P1 A2.1 BR-P1-001-2 (BR4). The only thing this story adds to an ACE row is its place in one ordered answer, and that is derived and stored nowhere.

##### 3. Preconditions

Nothing in this list is a build dependency: this story is Day 1 and builds against the published baseline, the published view contract and the RWB-P8-E2008-CON fake, which is why its build dependency list is empty.

- The service baseline of rwb-source-data is published: schema `rwb_source_data`, the per-service Flyway sequence at its baseline version, `data_product` with DP01 to DP14 and `data_product_load` with its unique key on `(product_code, business_date)` (DP-01; the baseline of RWB-P1-E1001-APP and RWB-P1-E1015-APP, adopted as published artefacts and not as build dependencies).
- RWB-P1-E1069-APP's view contract is published and the three views this story reads are readable through the `rwb_source_data` login, which holds SELECT on the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views and no privilege on `public`: `v_ace_payment`, `v_ace_account` and `v_ace_batch_status` (DP-02, DP-05; TSD P1 T3.3 and T6.3; ADR-010).
- `v_ace_batch_status` is a Section B view and `v_ace_payment` and `v_ace_account` are Section A views (TSD P1 T3.3 rows 1, 2 and 17; T3.2). Until RWB-ACE-001 lands, every source-fed product shows STALE with no business date and no data job starts (TSD P1 T3.7), so the gate of this story refuses every business date and answers no row rather than an empty day (BR3).
- RWB-P1-E1015-APP is done: `data_product_load` carries a LOADED or STALE row per product and business date, written from `v_ace_batch_status` only, and MSG-P1-001 and MSG-P2-007 exist with their texts (DP-05; FSD P1 A2.14).
- RWB-P8-E2008-CON is published with its fake: the rwb-source-data elements the payment-matching step consumes, their answers, the error classes and the WireMock mappings of the run. This story builds against that contract and against its fake, and against no second draft of it (C).
- The ALS batch for the business date is COMPLETE before any row is answered: `v_ace_batch_status` carries one row per source system and business date, and `is_complete` is true only for a COMPLETED batch (TSD P1 T3.4; BR-P1-014-4).
- The reference values this story names in an answer — the data product code `DP01` and the source system `ALS` — are reference data, reached through the reference-data client library of DP-07; the Work Package lists no reference-data contract for this story, so they are a library read with a fixture until that contract is published (GAP-0604; ASM-0846).
- The caller is the payment-matching run of rwb-payment, a service caller with a workload identity token; the data steward reads a refusal with Platform administration R, and the platform administrator reads it with the same right (TSD P1 T6.2; the SY-DATALOAD actor is retired and no source names its replacement for the run of JOB-07 — GAP-0603; ASM-0845).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; RWB-P8-E2008-CON tags its baseline when its tests pass. This story starts on Day 1 and waits for nothing it builds.
- The ordering of the payment answer, the row cap of one call, the answer for an account key with no view row and the HTTP answer of a held read are not stated by any source and are fixed as below (GAP-0599; ASM-0841; GAP-0601; ASM-0843).

##### 4. Flow

1. The payment-matching run of rwb-payment is started by `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` for the ALS source and business date D (Architecture v5 slide 43 row 26; slide 44 row JOB-07; the run is RWB-P8-E2008-APP's; DP-09, DP-10).
2. `FreshnessHoldGate` reads `data_product_load` for DP01 at D and `v_ace_batch_status` for the ALS row of D before any other read of this story runs; a product that is not LOADED or a batch that is not COMPLETE ends the call at step 8 with no row (AC5, X1, X2; §12.1).
3. The run calls `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/payments?businessDate=D` once, one hop and 2 s, and receives `PaymentsAnswer`: the business date, the source system ALS, the batch status, `rowCount`, the DP01 stamp and the payment rows (DP-11; C RWB-P8-E2008-CON).
4. `PaymentFactReadService` reads `v_ace_payment` for the rows whose `payment_date` is D, folds them to one row per `payment_code`, orders them by `paymentCode` and answers the five ACE values of each row unchanged: `paymentCode`, `accountKey`, `paymentDate`, `paymentAmount` and `dataAsOf` (AC1, AC6).
5. A payment whose account is on no open case is answered like every other payment of the date: this read resolves no case, filters nothing out and attaches the row to nothing (AC3; the case lookup and the REC-05 break are RWB-P8-E2008-APP's and RWB-P1-E1011-APP's).
6. For each account the run is about to match, it calls `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/accounts/{accountKey}/installment-facts?businessDate=D`; `InstallmentFactReadService` reads `v_ace_account` for that `account_key` and answers `nextInstallmentDate` with `accountKey`, `productKey`, `daysPastDue` and `dataAsOf` (AC2).
7. Neither read answers a plan, an installment amount, a rule, a package version or a case: the plan position of account A-0555 and the installment amount of plan T-0701 are rwb-treatment's, the rule result is rwb-payment's under package `PAYMENT_MATCH`, and the decision record is rwb-decision's (DP-03, DP-04; AC2, AC4).
8. A product not LOADED for D or an ALS batch not COMPLETE for D answers 409 with a problem body that names MSG-P1-001 for the product and the date of the load in use, and carries MSG-P2-007 for the held run and no payment row and no installment fact; the run reports the hold to the data steward (AC5; MSG-P1-001, MSG-P2-007).
9. The run builds its facts, evaluates package `PAYMENT_MATCH`, writes the proceeds row, calls the treatment record, publishes `ProceedsMatched` and `PaymentMissed` and writes the run summary; this story takes no part in any of it and writes no row anywhere (RWB-P8-E2008-APP, RWB-P7-E2008-APP, RWB-S2-E2008-APP).
10. A second call for the same business date answers the same rows from the views again, counts nothing and writes nothing (AC6, BR8; DP-05).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | DP01 is STALE for the business date | 409; no payment row and no installment fact; the problem body names the product and the date of the load in use | MSG-P1-001 | AC5 |
| X2 | The ALS batch for the business date is not COMPLETE, or absent, or FAILED | 409; no row of any kind is read from the views; the hold is named for the run | MSG-P1-001, MSG-P2-007 | AC5 |
| X3 | The business date carries no payment row at all | 200 with `rowCount` 0 and the batch status COMPLETED for that date, so an empty day is distinguishable from a held one | None | AC1 |
| X4 | The same `payment_code` appears twice in a read | One row is answered and the second is folded into it; the answer still holds one row per `payment_code` | None | AC6 |
| X5 | The `account_key` of the installment read has no row in `v_ace_account` | 404 with a problem body naming the account key and the check REC-05; no installment date is invented | None | Section 12.1 |
| X6 | `businessDate` or `accountKey` is missing or malformed | 400 with a problem body naming the field; nothing is read | MSG-GEN-001 | Section 12.1 |
| X7 | A view does not answer inside 5 s, or answers an error | 503 with a problem body naming the ACE database as the unavailable system; nothing is guessed from a cache | MSG-GEN-006 | Section 12.1 |
| X8 | A caller without the right calls either read | 403, and the refusal is logged without a key value | MSG-P4-002 | Section 10 |

X1, X2, X3, X4 and X5 are the read-side paths of the legacy exception rows X3 (the batch is not complete) and X5 (a payment on the edge of the window) carried onto the split; the matcher, the exception list, the package refusal and the run summary of the legacy rows X1, X2, X4 and X6 belong to RWB-P8-E2008-APP and RWB-P7-E2008-APP. X6, X7 and X8 are the paths of every read of this service.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P8-E2008-CON and its fake, on the published baseline, the view contract of RWB-P1-E1069-APP and the freshness rows of RWB-P1-E1015-APP; needs no live rwb-payment, rwb-treatment, rwb-decision or ACE database to start |
| Negotiable | The entity names, the ordering, the row cap and the held answer are the squad's choice behind the contract; the view set, the field list, the key of a row and the values are fixed |
| Valuable | The matcher matches against one copy of the ACE payment rows of the business date, and a held date is a hold rather than an empty day |
| Estimable | Two read operations, one service, one repository over three views, one freshness gate and one problem body |
| Small | Finished inside one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is one call against the contract fake, the view fixture and the freshness fixture, with no write and no second service |
| Day 1 | The story has no build dependency; it is reachable on the first day of wave 2 and its tests run against the published baseline and the fake |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin

    Given case "RC-2026-000555" has account "A-0555" and running restructure plan "T-0701" with installment amount 12,500.00 THB, installments 24 and installments paid 3

    Given package "PAYMENT_MATCH" version "PM-2026.12" is in force on 2026-12-14 and is evaluated by rwb-payment, not by this story
```

**Target reading.** Every assertion above is new, because this story owns no legacy criterion; each one tests only the two reads and the gate around them. What the legacy story asserted of the match, the proceeds row, the treatment record, the exception list, the missed event, the package refusal and the decision log is proved in RWB-P8-E2008-APP, RWB-S2-E2008-APP and RWB-P7-E2008-APP and in RWB-ITG-E2008-ITG, and the legacy values are kept here: case RC-2026-000555, account A-0555, plan T-0701, installment amount 12,500.00 THB, next installment date 2026-12-15, business date 2026-12-14, payments PAY-90001 and PAY-90002, PAY-90003 on A-0999, package PAYMENT_MATCH version PM-2026.12 and rule R-RES-26; the tolerance, the window and the grace days of the package rows are not restated, because this story evaluates no row of them (DP-04, DP-06). AC1 and AC6 fix the two facts the matcher depends on and no source states: one row per `payment_code`, ordered by `paymentCode`, so a repeated call answers the same set, and a row cap per call so one business date cannot answer an unbounded page (GAP-0599; ASM-0841; GAP-0601; ASM-0843). AC1 also names the product the rows were read under: DP01 accounts for `v_ace_payment` in FSD P1 A2.2 and is fed by ALS in TSD P1 T3.7, and the slice note names DP05, which reads no payment, so the gate is held on DP01 and the answer carries the ALS batch row beside it (GAP-0600; ASM-0842). AC2 answers `nextInstallmentDate` here although Architecture v5 slide 15 also names a `GET /accounts/{id}` of this service that TSD P1 T-A.1 does not carry and no Work Package gives an owner, so the field may move to that operation when it is published (GAP-0602; ASM-0844). AC3 keeps a payment whose account is on no open case in the answer instead of dropping it or inventing a case, so the caller can list it on the break; the break row itself is RWB-P1-E1011-APP's and the exception list is RWB-P8-E2008-APP's. AC4 is the no-copy assertion of BR4 and the no-event assertion of DP-09. AC5 replaces the legacy freshness hold with the two rows it reads — `data_product_load` for DP01 and `v_ace_batch_status` for the ALS batch, both in this service — so the hold needs no call to the freshness story and cannot disagree with it, and it fixes the 409 answer that no source names (DP-05; GAP-0600; ASM-0842). Who answers that hold — this read or the run that is started by `AceDataReady` after the same condition — is not settled by any source, which is why the read-side assertion is here and the run's refusal is named as RWB-P8-E2008-APP's (GAP-0600; ASM-0842).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The payments of one business date are read from `v_ace_payment` over the `payment_code` key, one row per `payment_code`, ordered by `paymentCode`, each with its account key, its payment date, its exact amount and its `data_as_of` | REQ-RDF-002; TSD P1 T3.4; R-UNI-40; legacy BR6 |
| BR2 | The next installment date of an account is read from `v_ace_account.next_installment_date` at the same business date, with the account key, the product key, the days past due and `data_as_of` | Legacy §3 and §11; TSD P1 T3.4 (DF-ACE-028); TSD P1 T3.7 (one business date per read) |
| BR3 | No payment row and no installment fact is answered for a business date whose ALS batch is not COMPLETE, or whose DP01 is STALE; the refusal names the product and the date of the load in use and carries no row | BR-P1-014-4; CTL-02; legacy BR5; FSD P1 A2.14 |
| BR4 | Both answers are derived from the views at request time and never stored; a repeated read reads the views again | D-RCV-35 U1; ADR-010; BR-P1-001-2; legacy BR3 |
| BR5 | This read resolves no case: a payment whose account is on no open case is answered like every other payment, and no exception list row, break row or proceeds row is written here | Legacy AC4 and BR4; REC-05; R-UNI-03 |
| BR6 | The match type, the amount tolerance, the window and the grace days are rows of package `PAYMENT_MATCH` with a version, and this story reads none of them | Principle 1; D-RCV-36 T10; legacy BR7 |
| BR7 | The match is decided by package `PAYMENT_MATCH` through the embedded Drools kit of rwb-payment, and the record of that decision is rwb-decision's; this story evaluates no rule and writes no decision record | D-RCV-36 T5 and T7; ADR-012; DP-04; legacy BR9 |
| BR8 | A repeat of the same read for the same business date answers the same rows, and one row per `payment_code` is what makes the repeat visible rather than a second row | R-UNI-40; legacy BR6 |
| BR9 | Amounts are read as ACE holds them, at scale 2, and are passed on unchanged; this story computes no total, no difference and no tolerance | Legacy §17; TSD P1 T3.4 (numeric(19,2)) |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1 and BR2 are the two reads of steps 3 to 6: the view rows of one business date and the account row of one key, with no join across a schema and no stored copy (DP-01, DP-05). BR3 is `FreshnessHoldGate`, which reads this service's own `data_product_load` row for DP01 and the ALS row of `v_ace_batch_status`, so the gate is local and cannot disagree with the freshness stamp of RWB-P1-E1015-APP. BR4 is the absence of any payment or account table in `rwb_source_data`: a second read reads the view again (AC4). BR5 is why `PAY-90003` on `A-0999` stays in the answer: the case lookup, the exception list and the break row are three other owners, and dropping the row here would hide it from all three (AC3). BR6 is why no tolerance, window or grace value appears in this story: they are columns of the package rows, and the package is evaluated by rwb-payment through the embedded Drools kit (DP-04, DP-06). BR7 is a statement here: this story writes no decision record (DP-03). BR8 is the fold to one row per `payment_code` and the ordering that makes a repeat comparable. BR9 keeps the amount as `BigDecimal` at scale 2 and forbids a conversion to baht units, a rounding or a currency string in code.

##### 9. State transitions

None in the case model and none in the plan. This story changes no case status, creates no case, changes no plan state and writes no match state: the legacy plan transitions of `PLAN_RUNNING` to `PLAN_RUNNING` on `PAYMENT_RECEIVED` and to `PLAN_CURE_PERIOD` on `PAYMENT_MISSED` are raised by rwb-payment and applied by P3 and rwb-treatment (legacy §9; R-RES-26, R-RES-27; RWB-P8-E2008-APP, RWB-S2-E2008-APP). The only states this story observes are the freshness status of a data product and the status of the ALS batch row.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP01 LOADED for the business date and the ALS batch COMPLETED | a payments read or an installment read | The gate passes | The answer carries the rows of the business date and the stamps it read under |
| DP01 STALE, or the ALS batch not COMPLETED, absent or FAILED | either read | The gate refuses | No row is answered; the refusal names MSG-P1-001 for the product and the date of the load in use and MSG-P2-007 for the held run |
| The ALS batch of the business date FAILED | either read | The row is read as it stands | The refusal names the last COMPLETED business date as the date of the load in use; the FAILED row is never answered as a complete one |
| The business date carries no payment row | a payments read | The gate passes | `rowCount` 0 with the batch status COMPLETED, which is an empty day and not a hold |
| An account key with no `v_ace_account` row | an installment read | The key does not resolve | 404 with the key and the check REC-05; no installment date is invented |

The freshness states LOADED and STALE are written by RWB-P1-E1015-APP and read here; this story writes neither, and it never writes `v_ace_batch_status`, which is ACE's.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The payment-matching run of rwb-payment, with a workload identity token | Reads the payments of one business date and the installment facts of one account; writes nothing |
| The rwb-source-data service identity (`rwb_source_data` login) | Reads the three ACE views and `data_product_load`; holds no privilege outside its schema and the views |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward and data product owner | Reads a refused read and its problem body (Platform administration R), and sees the stale product on the data quality route |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Reads the refused read and its problem body for the business date, and reads the run's hold on the job monitor of rwb-payment |
| The ACE team | Fixes a missing or failed ACE batch row in ACE; reads the stale and late alerts of RWB-P1-E1015-APP |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Owns package `PAYMENT_MATCH` and its rows through RWB-P7-E2008-APP and the rule package registry; this story reads no row of it |
| RW-CREDITAD, Credit Administration officer | Reads matched and unmatched receipts on SCR-28 of rwb-payment, which this story does not serve |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the plan position on SCR-14 of rwb-treatment, which this story does not serve |
| rwb-source-data (P1) | Owns the two reads, the ordering, the fold and the gate; owns no case, no plan, no proceeds row and no decision record |

No credential and no personal value appears in an answer, a log line or a test: the answers carry account keys, payment codes, dates, amounts and status codes only. Roles and their rights are held as data in rwb-access and reached through its authorise contract, never by a table read (DP-01; TSD P1 T6.2).

No field of `proceeds`, `treatment`, `recovery_case`, `case_account` or `decision_log_entry` is read or written: those rows belong to P8, S2, P3 and P7 and are reached through their contracts by the run, not by this story. ##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-source-data (P1); base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` (DP-13). Two read operations of the payment-matching step; the C dependency RWB-P8-E2008-CON declares the shapes the run consumes and this story implements them.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/payments` | The payments of one business date, read from `v_ace_payment`, one row per `payment_code`, ordered by `paymentCode`, with `rowCount`, the ALS batch status and the DP01 stamp the rows were read under | The payment-matching run of rwb-payment (workload identity); Platform administration R for a refusal | Idempotent: the answer is derived from the views on every call and holds no stored state |
| GET | `/accounts/{accountKey}/installment-facts` | The next installment date of one account at one business date, read from `v_ace_account`, with the account key, the product key, the days past due and `data_as_of` | The payment-matching run of rwb-payment (workload identity); Platform administration R for a refusal | Idempotent: the answer is derived from the view on every call |

The payments answer is `PaymentsAnswer`: `businessDate`, `sourceSystem` (always `ALS`), `rowCount`, `batchStatus` of `BatchStatusStamp` with `sourceSystem`, `businessDate`, `status`, `isComplete` and `completedAt`, `productStatus` of `ProductStamp` with `productCode` (`DP01`), `businessDate`, `status` and `loadedAt`, and `rows` of `PaymentFact` with `paymentCode`, `accountKey`, `paymentDate`, `paymentAmount` and `dataAsOf`. The installment answer is `InstallmentFacts`: `accountKey`, `businessDate`, `nextInstallmentDate`, `productKey`, `daysPastDue`, `dataAsOf`, `batchStatus` and `productStatus`. Property names are a target choice and follow the naming of the P1 API appendix; the field list is fixed by section 11.

Errors are the RFC 9457 problem body: 400 for a missing or malformed `businessDate` or `accountKey` with MSG-GEN-001 naming the field, 401 without a token with MSG-P4-001, 403 without the right with MSG-P4-002, 404 for an `accountKey` with no row in `v_ace_account` naming the key and the check REC-05, 409 when the gate refuses with MSG-P1-001 naming the product and the date of the load in use and MSG-P2-007 for the held run, and 503 when a view does not answer inside 5 s or answers an error, with MSG-GEN-006 naming the ACE database.

Four things about the shape are stated by no source and are fixed here. (1) The resource names, the two query parameters and the element names of the two answers: the legacy read was an in-process Java interface with a business date argument and no path, and no source document carries a payments or installment-facts path (GAP-0599; ASM-0841). (2) The ordering and the fold: one row per `payment_code` ordered by `paymentCode`, which makes a repeat answer comparable and a duplicate visible. (3) The row cap of one call: both reads answer one business date or one account in one call and are unpaged, with the cap as configuration, because no source states the volume of payments per business date (GAP-0601; ASM-0843). (4) The answers of a held read (409 with no row) and of an account key with no view row (404 with the key and REC-05), so a hold, an empty day and an unresolvable key are three distinguishable answers. These four are recorded for the contract owner and belong in the next version of the API specification.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. This story calls no operation of another service at run time. The gate reads this service's own `data_product_load` rows and `v_ace_batch_status` instead of calling the freshness story; the reference values it names in an answer are reached through the reference-data client library of DP-07 and not through a run-time call; and the case, the plan, the rule and the decision record are the run's calls and not this story's. The reference-data contract that supplies those values is not in this Work Package's contract list, so the values are a library read with a fixture until that contract is published (GAP-0604; ASM-0846; DP-07). The bindings of C from the legacy dependency are the run's contract RWB-P8-E2008-CON, which declares what this service answers and is faked for this story's tests.

###### 12.3 Events published

None of its own. The topic of the service is `rwb.source-data.events.v1` with event names `rwb.source-data.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and its two events `AceDataReady` and `AceDataLate` belong to RWB-P1-E1015-APP (Architecture v5 slides 15 and 43). This story publishes no event, writes no outbox row and adds no message schema; `PaymentMissed` and `ProceedsMatched` are rwb-payment's two events on its own topic, raised by RWB-P8-E2008-APP after the match (Architecture v5 slides 17, 42 and 43).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The payment-matching run consumes `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` and holds it (Architecture v5 slide 43 row 26; rwb-payment is one of its four consumers); this story is reached over REST by that run after the event and subscribes to nothing. Consuming `AceDataReady` here would create a second reader of the event and a second start path for the same business date, and the run's contract fixes the single consumer (DP-09).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. Both reads are synchronous REST steps that answer in one call with a 2 s budget, and this story starts no workflow and no activity. JOB-07 is P8's event-triggered Temporal workflow on queue `rwb-payment` of the owning service (Architecture v5 slide 44 row JOB-07; slide 17, rwb-payment "Act: matchPayments"); the task queue of this service is `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and it belongs to the other P1 stories (DP-10).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Temporal Schedule and no Quartz job sits in this story: both reads are called by the run when `AceDataReady` arrives and at no fixed time (DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. This story creates no table and no column, adds no migration to the per-service sequence and writes no row.

| Object | Schema | Owner | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v_ace_payment`, `v_ace_account`, `v_ace_batch_status` | `recovery` | ACE, read through the view contract of RWB-P1-E1069-APP | SELECT only, read-only login, never copied (DP-05; ADR-010). Views are not tables and this story creates none |
| `data_product_load` | `rwb_source_data` | P1, written by RWB-P1-E1015-APP | Read for the gate and for the stamp; no row is written here |
| `processed_event`, `idempotency_key`, `outbox_event` | `rwb_source_data` | PLT library objects, created in this service's schema | Not used: this story publishes no event and stores no response (DP-09) |

No table of another service is read and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01). `proceeds` stays in `rwb_payment` and `treatment` in `rwb_treatment`, and `recovery_case`, `case_account` and `decision_log_entry` stay with their owners; none of them is named in this story's code or tests except as the objects it must not touch.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata`, module `payments`, with the published types in `...sourcedata.api`. Service base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, schema `rwb_source_data`, topic `rwb.source-data.events.v1` (not published here), task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (not used here). The build starts on Day 1 against three published artefacts and no build dependency: the service baseline, the view contract of RWB-P1-E1069-APP and the fake of RWB-P8-E2008-CON.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**One sentence per pattern.** DP-01 is the shape of this story: the payment rows and the account row are read from the views and answered over the contract, and no column of ACE is copied into `rwb_source_data`. DP-03 is a statement here: the decision record of a match names rule `R-RES-26` and the package version, and it is written by rwb-payment in its own schema through the local decision-record library and collected into the central ledger of rwb-decision; this story writes no entry and reads none (RWB-P7-E2008-APP). DP-04 is a statement here: package `PAYMENT_MATCH` version `PM-2026.12` is evaluated by rwb-payment through its own embedded Drools kit under its platform contract, this story reads no row of the package and no `drl_source`, and the tolerance, the window and the grace days are columns of those rows and never values of this service. DP-05 is the read path itself: `v_ace_payment` for the payments of one business date, `v_ace_account` for the next installment date of one account and `v_ace_batch_status` for the batch row, SELECT only through the `rwb_source_data` login (ADR-010). DP-06 is a statement: this story reads no parameter, and the window and the grace days of the match are package rows of rwb-payment and not parameters of the read. DP-07 is the data product code and the source system label the answers name, read as reference data through the client library and never as a constant in code; the Work Package lists no reference-data contract for this story, so the values come from the library with a fixture until that contract is published (GAP-0604; ASM-0846). DP-09 is a statement: both reads publish no event and write no outbox row, and no inbox row is written here because the run consumes `AceDataReady` and not this story. DP-10 is a statement: JOB-07 is P8's event-triggered workflow on queue `rwb-payment`, and this story starts no workflow, no activity and no Schedule (Architecture v5 slide 44). DP-11 is the hop: the run calls the two reads over REST, one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker, against the shapes of RWB-P8-E2008-CON and its fake; the architecture also names the P8 to P1 call as a Temporal activity, which is recorded as open because the Work Package fixes REST (GAP-0603; ASM-0845). DP-13 is the base: `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` instead of the monolith's `/api/recovery/v1`. DP-15 is not claimed: this story stores nothing, so it adds no version to the per-service sequence and reads the baseline objects the sequence already created. DP-19 is a statement: this story renders no screen; the Credit Administration officer reads SCR-28 of rwb-payment, the case owner reads SCR-14 of rwb-treatment and the data steward reads the stale product on the data quality route of gateway-bff.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `PaymentFactController` | Controller | The two operations of 12.1 on `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`; RFC 9457 problem details; the 409 hold, the 404 key and the 400 field |
| `PaymentFactReadService` | Service | The `v_ace_payment` read of one business date, the fold to one row per `payment_code`, the ordering and the `rowCount` |
| `InstallmentFactReadService` | Service | The `v_ace_account` read of one account key at one business date and the five facts it answers |
| `PaymentViewRepository`, `AccountViewRepository` | Repository | SELECT over `recovery.v_ace_payment` and `recovery.v_ace_account`; no write method exists |
| `BatchStatusReader` | Repository | SELECT over `recovery.v_ace_batch_status` for the ALS row of the business date, and the last COMPLETED date for the refusal |
| `ProductStampReader` | Repository | Reads this service's own `data_product_load` row for DP01 at the business date (DP-05) |
| `FreshnessHoldGate` | Gate | Decides pass or hold from the DP01 stamp and the ALS batch row before any other read runs, and builds the refusal body |
| `ProductCodeReferenceClient` | Client library use | The data product code and the source system label as reference data; no code in code (DP-07) |
| `PaymentsAnswer`, `PaymentFact`, `InstallmentFacts`, `BatchStatusStamp`, `ProductStamp` | Published types | The records of 12.1 in `...sourcedata.api`; no case field, no plan field and no copy of an ACE column |

**Migration (DP-15).** None. This story adds no table, no column, no index and no version to the per-service Flyway sequence, because it stores nothing. The baseline objects it reads are created by RWB-P1-E1001-APP, the views it reads are created by RWB-P1-E1069-APP and its database story under the migrations of TSD P1 T3.2, and an applied version is never edited by anyone, including this story.

**Database.** No object of `rwb_source_data` is created or written. `v_ace_payment` and `v_ace_account` are Section A views and `v_ace_batch_status` a Section B view, all ACE's, read through this service's login with SELECT only (TSD P1 T3.3; T6.3); `data_product_load` is read for the gate and the stamp and written by RWB-P1-E1015-APP. This story has no table of its own: a second read of the same business date reads the views again (BR4).

**Configuration and reference data**

- The data product code `DP01` and the source system label `ALS` are reference values read through the client library, with a fixture until the reference-data contract is published (GAP-0604; ASM-0846; DP-07).
- The row cap per call, the 2 s client budget and the 5 s statement timeout are configuration of the reads and of the view session (Architecture v5 slide 11; TSD P1 T6.3).
- The ordering `paymentCode` ascending, the fold to one row per `payment_code` and the answers of a held read and of an unresolvable key are configuration of the contract and not values a business person changes (GAP-0599; ASM-0841).
- The gate reads the product stamp and the batch row and holds nothing in a cache: a held business date is refused on every call until the batch of that date completes (BR3).
- The flag `rwb.source-data.payment-facts` gates both reads at deployment; with it off the run receives 503 and starts no matching for the business date.

**Build steps**

1. The five published types and the OpenAPI fragment of 12.1, taken from RWB-P8-E2008-CON and published with the service baseline (C).
2. `ProductStampReader` and `BatchStatusReader` over `data_product_load` and `v_ace_batch_status`, and `FreshnessHoldGate` with the 409 problem body of MSG-P1-001 and MSG-P2-007 and the last COMPLETED date in the refusal (AC5, X1, X2).
3. `PaymentViewRepository` and `PaymentFactReadService`: the `v_ace_payment` read of one business date, the fold to one row per `payment_code`, the ordering by `paymentCode` and the `rowCount` (AC1, AC6, X3, X4).
4. `InstallmentFactReadService` and `AccountViewRepository`: `nextInstallmentDate` with the four account facts, and the 404 with the key and REC-05 for an account key with no row (AC2, X5).
5. The error paths: 400 with MSG-GEN-001 naming the field, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 503 with MSG-GEN-006 for a view that does not answer inside 5 s, and the `ProductCodeReferenceClient` fixture for the product code and the source system (X6, X7, X8).
6. An architecture test that no class of the `payments` module writes a row, names `proceeds`, `treatment`, `recovery_case`, `case_account` or `decision_log_entry`, or references a case, plan, rule or event type (AC3, AC4, DP-01, DP-03).
7. A test that a second read of the same business date reads the views again and answers the same rows, so the no-copy rule is asserted and not assumed (AC4, AC6).
8. Tests for AC1 to AC6 against the four fakes of 12.8, plus the regression rows of section 16 where the fixture of the owning slice is available.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the payments of 2026-12-14 answer three ordered rows with one row per `payment_code` and the exact amounts, the installment facts of A-0555 answer the next installment date 2026-12-15, both reads refuse with 409 and MSG-P1-001 while DP01 is STALE or the ALS batch is not COMPLETE and carry MSG-P2-007, a payment whose account is on no open case stays in the answer, and no row is written anywhere.

MSG-P1-001 and MSG-P2-007 are published by the freshness story and raised here in the refusal body with the date of the load in use and the product name the answer carries, "DP01 Account and arrears" in the legacy fixture; the rendering of MSG-P2-007 for a payment-matching run rather than a case-creation run is not stated by any source and follows the P1 wording with the run named (GAP-0599; ASM-0841). MSG-GEN-006 names the ACE database as the failed system, and MSG-P4-002 names the action the caller tried and never a key value. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10. No message carries a person name, an identity number, a phone number, an address or a payment amount.
