**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the deployment slice of RWB-E2-008 for rwb-payment — the api and worker deployments of the matching build, its login and secrets, the migration and the library tables, the workflow registration on queue `rwb-payment`, the topics, the consumer group, the alerts, the run view, the flag, the backfill and the rollback — is split from the contract baseline (RWB-P8-E2008-CON) and from the application work (RWB-P8-E2008-APP). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As the **DevOps team of the recovery platform**, I want **the rwb-payment matching build deployed as one api and one worker behind the recovery edge, on its own login and schema, with its workflow registered, its topics and consumer group provisioned, an alert for every failure path carrying a message ID and an owned runbook entry, and a rollback that drains a running workflow — so that** the build runs unattended every business morning and an operator can tell a late batch from a failed run without reading a log.

The release carries, and nothing else:

- two deployments of one image — `api` serving `GET /proceeds` and `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` on `/api/recovery/payment/v1` through the gateway-bff, and `worker` polling the task queue `rwb-payment` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (DP-13, DP-19);
- the login `rwb_payment` on schema `rwb_payment`, its connection pool and its secret references, and no grant on another schema or on `recovery` (DP-01, DP-02);
- the migration of `proceeds` and of the library tables in `rwb_payment`, gated by lint and drift (DP-15);
- the workflow `matchPayments` registered on the queue with its build ID and its worker versioning, started by `AceDataReady` (EV-26) and by no Schedule (DP-10);
- the topics `rwb.payment.events.v1` with `.retry` and `.dlt`, the consumer group `rwb-payment.ace-data-ready.v1`, and the relay of the outbox (DP-09);
- the five alerts, the four dashboard series, the run view of JOB-07 and the runbook entries that go with them;
- the flag `rwb.payments.matching`, the backfill of a business date and the rollback of a build.

The behaviour of the match is RWB-P8-E2008-APP and the shapes are RWB-P8-E2008-CON; this story ships neither. Where a deployment value has no source, it is a value of the environment and the default stands as an assumption (GAP-2505; ASM-4145).

##### 2. Business rationale

A service that no one operates is not delivered. The legacy story assumed a Quartz job inside one deployed monolith, a shared recovery login and a shared job monitor; under D-RCV-60 the matching run is a workflow on its own queue, in its own namespace, under its own login, with its own topic and its own alerts. Each of those is a deployment object that has to exist before the first business morning, and each has a failure mode an operator must recognise: a batch that never arrives, a run that starts and stops on a missing package, a contract that does not answer, a record that cannot be written, and a topic that falls behind.

- **the morning is the deadline.** The run follows the ALS batch, so a late batch or an unstarted worker is a business problem by 07:00, not an infrastructure one.
- **the failures are distinguishable.** The five alerts separate a stale batch, a missing package, a paused flag, a stopped record chain and a lagging outbox, and each names its message ID.
- **a rerun is safe.** The run is idempotent per business date, so the fix for most mornings is a backfill of one date and not a repair script.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P8-E2008-CON is tagged `v1` and the image of RWB-P8-E2008-APP is built and pushed under the release build ID.
- The platform objects exist: the gateway-bff route for `/api/recovery/payment/*`, the secret store, the Kafka cluster with the event platform's topic template, the Temporal namespace `rwb-recovery`, the OpenTelemetry collector and the workload identity of the namespace (DP-19).
- The login `rwb_payment` is allocated with its secret reference; the schema `rwb_payment` exists; the connection pool size, the replica counts and the resource requests are values of the environment and stand as assumptions (GAP-2505; ASM-4145).
- rwb-source-data publishes `AceDataReady` (EV-26) for the ALS source, and the environment grants either the three `v_ace_*` views to this login or the rwb-source-data contract (DP-05).
- The five message IDs of section 14 are registered in the platform message catalogue; no text is written by this story.
- Status is Draft (realignment v1): no approval and no production change are required to prepare the release, and the first environment is non-production (GAP-2505; ASM-4146).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds one image and two deployments from it, with the release build ID of the commit and the image digest pinned; no `latest` tag is deployed.
2. The migration job runs the Flyway sequence of `rwb_payment` before the worker starts, and the drift gate compares the applied state with the baseline of RWB-P8-E2008-CON; a drift fails the release.
3. The api deployment starts behind the gateway-bff route, with its readiness probe on the health endpoint and its authorise dependency checked once, and declares no route of its own.
4. The worker deployment starts and registers the workflow `matchPayments` and its four activities on the task queue `rwb-payment`, with worker versioning on the build ID.
5. The event platform creates the topic `rwb.payment.events.v1` with its `.retry` and `.dlt`, and the service registers the consumer group `rwb-payment.ace-data-ready.v1` on `rwb.source-data.events.v1`; the group is created before the first business date.
6. The outbox relay of the library starts inside the worker, with its poll interval and its batch size as values of the environment, and publishes to the service's topic with the CloudEvents envelope of the baseline.
7. `AceDataReady` for the ALS source with business date D starts one execution of `matchPayments`; the execution id derived from the source and the date means a redelivery joins the run instead of opening a second one.
8. The flag `rwb.payments.matching` is read at the start of the run: off means the inbox row is written, the date is held and nothing else happens, and no proceeds row and no event are written.
9. The run writes its summary to the visibility view and to the outcome records; the four dashboard series and the run view of JOB-07 read them.
10. A failed run raises its alert with a message ID and a runbook link; the operator either fixes the cause — a package, a flag, a contract — or backfills the business date, which replays the same execution and writes nothing twice.
11. A rollback redeploys the previous chart and build ID; a running execution finishes on the build that started it, and a new business date starts on the previous build until the fix ships again.
12. The alert on the outbox checks the relay lag and the dead-letter topic; a message in `.dlt` is the operator's to replay after the cause is fixed, and the run is not marked complete until the outbox is empty.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The ALS batch for the business date is late or not complete | The run is skipped before matching and the plan view shows the stale product and its date | MSG-P1-001 | AC5, BR6 |
| X2 | The worker is not polling, or the event did not arrive | The business date has no execution by the run window; the alert names the missing event for the source and the date | MSG-P1-001 (runbook entry 1) | AC3, AC5 |
| X3 | No `PAYMENT_MATCH` version is in force | The execution fails before matching, the flag is not the cause and the package owner is paged | MSG-P3-027, MSG-P8-002 | AC5, BR7 |
| X4 | The record chain is stopped or the store is unavailable | The transaction writes nothing; the incident is raised and the date is backfilled once the store is back | MSG-P7-003 | AC5, AC6 |
| X5 | A consumed contract does not answer inside 2 s or its breaker is open | The activity retries on the workflow policy; after the last attempt the run is failed and the downstream owner is paged | None | AC5, BR8 |
| X6 | The outbox relay lags, or a message lands in the dead-letter topic | The lag series and the DLT alert fire, and the replay is the operator's step | None | AC4, AC5 |
| X7 | The flag is off in an environment that has the run | The date is held, no row and no event is written, and the run view says the flag is off | None | AC6 |
| X8 | The migration leaves the schema not matching the baseline | The drift gate fails the release and the worker is not started | None (pipeline log) | AC2 |

X1 to X5 are the failure paths of the legacy key restated as deployment objects; X6 is the event platform's, X7 the flag's and X8 the migration gate's. None of them changes a business value: the window, the tolerance and the grace days are rows of the package, and the thresholds of the alerts are values of the environment.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 from the tagged contract baseline and the image; needs no running neighbour beyond the platform objects of the namespace |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, thresholds, series windows, partition counts and retention are values of the environment and are tuned per environment |
| Valuable | The run happens every business morning and every failure is visible with a message ID and an owned runbook entry |
| Estimable | Two deployments, one migration job, one registration, one topic with two subtopics, one consumer group, five alerts, four series and five runbook entries |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with the platform team |
| Testable | Each criterion is a deployment check, a registration check or an alert check at Level NFR or End to end |

The seven criteria test the deployment only. No business value, amount, date or plan of the legacy story is fixed by them; the only dates they name are the business date of the run and the values of the environment (ASM-4145).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One image, two deployments, one login and one queue per service; no deployment reaches another schema | DP-01, DP-02, R4 |
| BR2 | The migration runs before the worker and a drift fails the release | DP-15 |
| BR3 | The workflow is registered on `rwb-payment` and started by `AceDataReady`; no Schedule is created | DP-10 |
| BR4 | The topic, its retry and dead-letter topics and the consumer group exist before the first business date | DP-09 |
| BR5 | Every alert names a message ID and one owned runbook entry; no alert without a message ID is released | R7.2 s14 |
| BR6 | A run whose batch is not complete writes nothing and is not retried against stale data | Legacy BR5; CTL-02 |
| BR7 | No package in force is a failed run and never a default match | Legacy BR10; R-UNI-41 |
| BR8 | A consumed contract is called with one hop and a 2 s timeout, and a breaker per downstream protects the run | DP-11; ADR-020 |
| BR9 | A backfill is safe to repeat and writes nothing twice; the key is the business date and the payment | DP-09; legacy AC6 |
| BR10 | A rollback drains in-flight runs and never kills an execution; a new date starts on the rollback build | R8.2; AC7 |

##### 9. State transitions

None of business data: this story changes no record and no case state. The states it owns are the deployment and the run.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | The chart is applied and the migration passes | The drift gate is green | Deployed, the worker registered |
| Deployed | The flag is off | X7 | Deployed, the date held |
| Deployed | `AceDataReady` for a new date | The batch is COMPLETE and a package is in force | Running, then completed with its summary |
| Running | A failure path fires | X1 to X5 | Failed with its alert; the date is backfillable |
| Deployed | A rollback is applied | AC7 | The previous build serves new dates; the running execution finishes |
| Deployed | The outbox has a message in `.dlt` | X6 | The run is not complete until the replay |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None new. The two operations of the service — `GET /proceeds` and `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` on `/api/recovery/payment/v1` — are deployed by this story as they are tagged in RWB-P8-E2008-CON, behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). This story changes no path, no body and no error, and publishes no health or admin route of its own beyond the platform probe.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Base | Owner | Deployment note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Payments, next installment date and batch status of the ALS source | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | the client is configured with a 2 s timeout, one GET retry with jitter and a breaker; the granted `v_ace_*` views are the alternative |
| Open case and running plans of a case | `/api/recovery/case/v1` and RWB-P3-E2004-CON | P3 rwb-case | same policy; the plan is read before the match of a payment |
| Parameters, lists and the package in force | RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON, RWB-P3-E2042-CON | P3 and P7 | read once per run and cached for the run, with the version of each |

The operation names are those of the baseline and carry the placeholder where no published document fixes them (GAP-2505; ASM-4145).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Provisioning |
|---|---|---|
| `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` (EV-25) | `rwb.payment.events.v1` | the topic and its `.retry` and `.dlt` are created with the values of the environment; the outbox relay publishes |
| `rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1` (EV-12) | `rwb.payment.events.v1` | as above; the alert on the DLT covers a failed publish |
| `rwb.payment.TreatmentBooked.v1` (EV-11) | `rwb.payment.events.v1` | the topic is shared with the booking story; this release creates it and publishes nothing of it |
| `DecisionRecorded` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | written by the library; the topic belongs to rwb-decision and is not created here |

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Consumer group | Provisioning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AceDataReady` (EV-26) | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | `rwb-payment.ace-data-ready.v1` | the group is registered before the first business date and its offset policy is the environment's |
| `RulePackageInForce` (EV-30) | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | `rwb-payment.rule-package.v1` | registered with the booking story; this release creates the group only |

The other five subscriptions of the service belong to the booking and Epic 4 stories and are not registered here.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Registration |
|---|---|---|
| `matchPayments` (JOB-07) | Workflow | registered on queue `rwb-payment`; the build ID pins the worker version; the execution id derives from the source and the business date |
| `readFacts`, `evaluateMatch`, `recordAndApply`, `raiseMissedPayment` | Activities | registered with the workflow; the retry policy is the kit's, `NoPackageInForce` is non-retryable |
| `confirmBookings` (JOB-08) and `postProceeds` | Workflow and activity | registered by the booking story and the debt-sale journey; this release does not register them |

The registration check asserts the queue, the workflow type, the input schema and the absence of a Schedule. The build ID and the versioning policy are values of the release and are recorded with it (GAP-2505; ASM-4146).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Schedule, cron, overlap policy or catch-up window is created for this service. The run follows `AceDataReady` from the bank's Airflow edge; the outbox relay is a library component inside the worker and not a Schedule.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| `decision_record`, `inbox_event`, `outbox_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT libraries in `rwb_payment` | the library migration of the same job |

The job creates no table of another schema, requests no grant beyond `rwb_payment`, and reads the three `v_ace_*` views only where the environment grants them to this login. No migration of the monolith is reused.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Chart.** `deploy/rwb-payment/`: one image, two deployments (`api`, `worker`), the migration job, the route fragment, the alert rules, the dashboard, the runbook links and the values files per environment.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `api` deployment | Deployment | serves the two operations behind the gateway-bff, with its readiness and liveness probes |
| `worker` deployment | Deployment | polls `rwb-payment`, registers the workflow and its activities, runs the outbox relay |
| `migrate` job | Job | runs the Flyway sequence and the library migration before the worker; the drift gate reads its result |
| `topics` manifest | Manifest | the service topic, its `.retry` and `.dlt`, and the two consumer groups |
| `alerts` rules | Rules | five alerts, each with a message ID, a label set and a runbook link |
| `dashboard` | Chart | four series: runs by outcome, payments read and matched, unmatched receipts, outbox lag |
| `runbook` | Document | five entries: event not received or worker not polling; stale batch; no package; record chain stopped; outbox lag or DLT |

| Runbook entry | Trigger | First step | Owner role |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | No execution by the run window | check the relay of rwb-source-data and the worker registration | DevOps team |
| 2 | MSG-P1-001 on the plan view or the run | check the batch status of the source and the business date; do not force the run | DevOps team with the data owner |
| 3 | MSG-P3-027 and MSG-P8-002 | confirm no version is in force and page the package owner; do not load a version here | RW-COE |
| 4 | MSG-P7-003 and a stopped chain | check the record store, then backfill the date | DevOps team with the platform record owner |
| 5 | The lag series or a `.dlt` message | find the cause, replay the message, confirm the run completes | DevOps team with the event platform owner |

**Build steps.** (1) Write the chart, the probes and the migration job; test AC1 and AC2. (2) Register the workflow and the versioning policy; test AC3. (3) Create the topics and the consumer groups; test AC4. (4) Write the five alerts, the four series and the five runbook entries; test AC5. (5) Wire the flag, the backfill and the rollback; test AC6 and AC7.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Alert and text |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | The ACE batch is late or not complete | the run is skipped; the text names the product and its date |
| MSG-P8-001 | The run summary carries unmatched payments | the summary text only; no alert of its own |
| MSG-P8-002 | No `PAYMENT_MATCH` version is in force | the failed-run alert carries the text and the business date |
| MSG-P3-027 | The rule version is refused | the failed-run alert carries the refusal detail, the package code and the date only |
| MSG-P7-003 | The record cannot be written | the incident alert carries the text and the business date; the date is backfillable |

The texts are the legacy texts of RWB-E2-008 section 14, unchanged. MSG-P4-002 is the API's 403 and needs no alert. An alert never carries an account, a payment reference or a customer value.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built here. The operator reads the run on the workflow visibility view and on the run view of JOB-07 (SCR-44), and the officer reads the receipts on SCR-28; both are served by the base and the composite route the release deploys. The four dashboard series are the operator's view of the same run.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No secret in a chart value, a pipeline log or a prompt: the login, the client credentials and the payload keys are secret references only.
- No personal data in an alert, a series, a log or a run input: an alert names the service, the source, the business date and the message ID, and never an account, a payment or a customer.
- No business value in a chart, an alert threshold or a runbook: the package values belong to their owner and the thresholds are values of the environment.
- No deployment reaches another schema, another queue or another topic than the ones named here, and no operator edits a row of `rwb_payment` to fix a run.
- No rollout without the drift gate, the registration check and the five runbook entries in place.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-008 for the wave 2 integration harness. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **member of the integration and QA team**, I want **a repeatable cross-service journey harness for payment matching and the missed payment event across rwb-payment, rwb-source-data, rwb-decision, rwb-treatment, rwb-case and rwb-access**, so that **the PAYMENT_MATCH journey is proven end to end, with evidence, before the wave 2 release is accepted**.

This story builds the harness and the evidence only. It builds no production endpoint, no screen, no table, no migration, no workflow and no schedule. It serves no operation, it owns no table and it starts no workflow of its own. The real behaviour is owned by the eight I stories RWB-P8-E2008-APP (JOB-07 as an event-started workflow in rwb-payment, the proceeds match, the missed payment event and the REC-04 result), RWB-P1-E2008-APP (the ACE payment, account and batch-status reads and the data-quality exception list), RWB-S2-E2008-APP (the treatment plan position and the installment update), RWB-P3-E2042-APP (the PAYMENT_MATCH package in force), RWB-P7-E2008-APP (the decision record and the central ledger), RWB-P4-E2008-APP (the role, scope and right check), RWB-P3-E2004-APP (the case, the account and the running plans of the case) and RWB-P1-E1069-APP (the ACE view grants behind the reads), and those eight stories block the ITG run.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy RWB-E2-008 journey is one business day of the payments module: the ALS payments posted in ACE for business date D are matched to the installments of the running plans, an installment that is still unpaid when the ACE batch completes raises a missed payment, and anything that matches no plan is held for a person. Today the match is done by hand and a missed installment is found weeks later, after the cure period has gone. The split gives each service its own app story and leaves one integration story — this one — that proves the whole journey across the service boundaries on synthetic data, on one business date, with a report that can be re-run for any build.

The harness proves, in one run and one evidence pack: that JOB-07 starts on `AceDataReady` and runs for the business date the ACE batch actually completed; that package PAYMENT_MATCH fires row EXACT under rule R-RES-26 with package version PM-2026.12 on every match; that the D5 decision record is written before the proceeds row and names the rule and the version; that the proceeds row and `ProceedsMatched` leave the service together; that `recordInstallmentPaid` moves the plan to installments paid 4 with next due date 2027-01-15; that an unpaid due date raises `PaymentMissed` and P3 moves the plan PLAN_RUNNING to PLAN_CURE_PERIOD under R-RES-27; that an unmatched receipt sits on the exception list with MSG-P8-001 and is readable unmatched; that a payment on an account with no open case leaves no proceeds row and lands on the REC-05 business-key break; that an incomplete ALS batch stops the run with MSG-P1-001 instead of raising a missed payment from stale data; that the rerun of one business date adds no second row and no second event; and that the ledger, the proceeds and the plan all agree on one business date.

It evidences REQ-CHO-007 and REQ-CHO-009 at the integration level, with the match measure REC-04 and the REC-05 break, and it leaves every business rule, every message and every screen behaviour where the owning stories put them.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The eight I stories are published and deployed in the SIT environment, or the contract fakes of §12.8 stand in for each of them: RWB-P3-E2004-APP (case, account and running plans), RWB-P1-E1069-APP (ACE view grants and the payment, next-installment and batch-status reads), RWB-P3-E2042-APP (PAYMENT_MATCH package in force), RWB-P8-E2008-APP (JOB-07, the proceeds match and the missed payment event), RWB-S2-E2008-APP (treatment plan position and the installment update), RWB-P1-E2008-APP (freshness, the data-quality exception list and the job rerun), RWB-P7-E2008-APP (decision record and ledger) and RWB-P4-E2008-APP (authorise).
- Package PAYMENT_MATCH version "PM-2026.12" is in force, with exactly one EXACT row: amount tolerance 0 percent, window 10 days before the due date and 0 days after, grace 0 days. The version is loaded and approved through the rwb-decision rule-package operations by RWB-P3-E2042-APP; the harness only reads it and asserts it.
- The ACE batch for ALS with business date 2026-12-14 is COMPLETE, so JOB-07 has a batch to run on. The batch is read through the P1 contract, never from the ACE view.
- The ALS payment fixture for business date 2026-12-14 is loaded through the P1 test profile, and `AceDataReady` for that business date opens the JOB-07 window.
- Case "RC-2026-000555" has account "A-0555" and running restructure plan "T-0701" with installment amount 12,500.00 THB, installments 24 and installments paid 3, account "A-0555" has next installment date 2026-12-15, and plan "T-0702" on account "A-0666" of case "RC-2026-000566" has installment amount 12,500.00 THB with next installment date 2026-12-16 (legacy section 7 Background).
- gateway-bff is deployed with the composite proceeds and exception route available to the screens that consume it. The composite route path and its merge order: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0393; ASM-0568).
- The harness environment, its repository, its test-data seeding (including the ALS payment fixture format), its evidence format and retention and its pass or fail gate: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0393; ASM-0568).

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: takes the run lock for the environment, records the build ID, the business date and the versions of the six contracts it is about to exercise, then seeds the case, the account, the plan, the payments and the PAYMENT_MATCH version through the owning contracts or the published fakes and reads each item back to assert the seeded state.
2. Harness: publishes or replays `AceDataReady` for business date 2026-12-14 on `rwb.source-data.events.v1`, then starts JOB-07 through the workflow it starts on queue `rwb-payment` and records its workflow ID, the business date and the run outcome.
3. Harness: asserts the EXACT row of PAYMENT_MATCH (tolerance 0 percent, window 10 days before and 0 days after, grace 0 days), the R-RES-26 decision record with decision code D5, and package version PM-2026.12 on the entry, and fails the run when any of the three disagrees.
4. Harness: reads the proceeds of the business date through the P8 contract and asserts, for "PAY-90001", treatment "T-0701", source "CUSTOMER", amount 12,500.00 and matched to "INSTALLMENT", one `ProceedsMatched` event and one outbox row; then asserts `recordInstallmentPaid` for "T-0701" with due date 2026-12-15 and, after the ALS batch of 2026-12-15, installments paid 4 and next due date 2027-01-15 through the S2 and P3 contracts.
5. Harness: for the plan with no matched payment for its due date, asserts `PaymentMissed` on `rwb.payment.events.v1` with treatment "T-0701", due date 2026-12-15 and amount due 12,500.00, and asserts on the case timeline and the plan position that the plan moved PLAN_RUNNING to PLAN_CURE_PERIOD under R-RES-27.
6. Harness: reads the unmatched side of the P8 proceeds operation and asserts the "PAY-90002" row with matched to "UNMATCHED", no treatment, and the run summary carrying MSG-P8-001 with one unmatched payment for 2026-12-14.
7. Harness: asserts the REC-05 business-key break: no proceeds row exists for "PAY-90003" on account "A-0999", and "PAY-90003" is on the P1 data-quality exception list with check "References" for the data steward.
8. Harness: withholds the COMPLETE batch for business date 2026-12-15, lets the scheduled JOB-07 time of 2026-12-16 pass, and asserts that no run happens for that business date, that no `PaymentMissed` exists for due date 2026-12-15, and that the freshness read carries MSG-P1-001 naming "DP01 Account and arrears" and 2026-12-14.
9. Harness: reruns JOB-07 for business date 2026-12-14 through the P1 rerun operation and asserts that the proceeds still hold two rows for that business date and that no second `ProceedsMatched` and no second `PaymentMissed` exist, so the idempotency keys of payment_code and of treatment plus due date hold.
10. Harness: forces the decision-log write to fail through the P7 fake or the service's fault profile, runs the match again, and asserts that no proceeds row is written, that the run summary carries MSG-P7-003, and that the run is reported failed at that assertion rather than green.
11. Harness: writes one run report per business date, keyed by story key and business date, with the request, the response, the proceeds row, the decision entry, the plan position, the events and each assertion result; the report format and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0393; ASM-0568).

| X2 | A payment sits on an account with no open case ("PAY-90003" on "A-0999") | No proceeds row for "PAY-90003"; the REC-05 business-key break carries "PAY-90003" for the data steward | None | TC-E2-008-04-ITG |
| X3 | The ACE batch for ALS is not COMPLETE for the business date (2026-12-15 ended "FAILED") | JOB-07 does not run for 2026-12-15; no `PaymentMissed` for due date 2026-12-15; the freshness answer names "DP01 Account and arrears" and 2026-12-14 | MSG-P1-001 | TC-E2-008-05-ITG |
| X4 | JOB-07 is rerun for business date 2026-12-14 | Still two proceeds rows for that date; no second `ProceedsMatched`; no second `PaymentMissed` | None | TC-E2-008-06-ITG |
| X5 | A payment lands on the last day of the window and another one day before it opens ("PAY-90004" at 10 days, "PAY-90005" at 11 days) | "PAY-90004" matched to "INSTALLMENT" for "T-0701"; "PAY-90005" matched to "UNMATCHED" and held | MSG-P8-001 | TC-E2-008-07-ITG |
| X6 | No PAYMENT_MATCH version is in force on the business date | The run stops before matching with NoPackageInForce and MSG-P3-027 naming package "PAYMENT_MATCH", then MSG-P8-002; no proceeds row and no event; the job monitor shows JOB-07 failed | MSG-P3-027, MSG-P8-002 | TC-E2-008-08-ITG |
| X7 | The decision log write fails for a match that would otherwise succeed | No proceeds row for the payment; the run summary carries MSG-P7-003; the record is absent while the state change is absent too, so the pair never disagrees | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E2-008-09-ITG |
| X8 | The caller holds RW-CASEOWN (Write-off and posting R absent) and calls the proceeds read | 403 with MSG-P4-002 on the direct call; the composite answer hides the unmatched action; no data is returned | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-008-10-ITG |
| X9 | The seed pack cannot be loaded | The run refuses to start and names the missing seed item; no scenario is reported as passed | None | All |
| X10 | Another run holds the environment lock | The run refuses to start and names the lock holder; the lock is never taken over | None | All |
| X11 | The evidence pack cannot be written or attached to the run record | The run is marked failed and the local evidence file is kept for rerun; no scenario is reported as passed | None | All |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs on its own once the eight I stories or their contracts are available; the fixture, the package version and the batch status are preconditions, not build dependencies |
| Negotiable | The seeded payments, the expected rule ID and the expected package version are data files, never code; the harness fixes no threshold of its own |
| Valuable | The journey is proven once across six services, and the match, the record, the proceeds and the plan position are shown to agree on one business date |
| Estimable | One harness project, one journey specification, one fake pack, one payment fixture per business date, one evidence collector and one gate |
| Small | Fits in one iteration with the owning stories' contract tests |
| Testable | Each criterion and each exception row has a fixed Given, When and Then and a machine-checked result in the run report |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Payment matching with the missed payment event

  Background:
    Given package "PAYMENT_MATCH" version "PM-2026.12" is in force with row "EXACT": amount tolerance 0 percent, window 10 days before the due date and 0 days after, grace 0 days
    Given case "RC-2026-000555" has account "A-0555" and running restructure plan "T-0701" with installment amount 12,500.00 THB, installments 24 and installments paid 3
    Given account "A-0555" has next installment date 2026-12-15

  Scenario: AC1 Payment matched (legacy RWB-E2-008 AC1)
    Given the ACE batch for ALS with business date 2026-12-14 is COMPLETED
    Given v_ace_payment holds payment "PAY-90001" of 12,500.00 THB on account "A-0555" dated 2026-12-14
    When JOB-07 runs on 2026-12-15
    Then the EXACT row of package "PAYMENT_MATCH" version "PM-2026.12" matches "PAY-90001" to the installment
    Then the decision log entry names rule "R-RES-26" and rule version "PM-2026.12"
    Then a proceeds row exists for case "RC-2026-000555" with treatment "T-0701", payment code "PAY-90001", source "CUSTOMER", amount 12,500.00 and matched to "INSTALLMENT"
    Then the system calls treatmentApi.recordInstallmentPaid for "T-0701" with due date 2026-12-15
    Then the system writes proceedsMatched to the outbox

    When JOB-07 runs on 2026-12-15
```

These four criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-E2-008 run across the six contracts, the ALS payment fixture and the JOB-07 window; the harness adds no mock Given and rewrites no Given, When or Then. AC2, AC6, AC7, AC8 and AC9 are owned by the app stories of this legacy key and are cited only through their test cases TC-E2-008-02, TC-E2-008-06, TC-E2-008-07, TC-E2-008-08 and TC-E2-008-09.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A payment on the plan account for the installment amount, dated inside the window before the next due date, matches that installment | R-RES-26; row EXACT of package PAYMENT_MATCH |
| BR2 | A due date that passes, plus the grace days, with no matched payment raises PaymentMissed once | R-RES-27; REQ-CHO-007 |
| BR3 | A payment that matches no plan, sale or lot is held on the exception list for the reconciliation agent | R-UNI-03; CTL-41 |
| BR4 | A payment on an account with no open case is listed on the REC-05 business-key break and gets no proceeds row | REC-05; DQ-012 |
| BR5 | Matching runs only on a COMPLETE ACE batch; no missed payment is raised from stale data | JOB-07; CTL-02 |
| BR6 | One proceeds row per payment_code; one PaymentMissed per plan and due date | R-UNI-40; ux_proceeds_payment_code |
| BR7 | Window, tolerance, grace days, partial floor and match types are columns of the package rows with a version | Principle 1; D-RCV-36 T10 |
| BR8 | Payments in v_ace_payment reconcile to proceeds by count and amount daily | REC-04 |
| BR9 | The match is decided by package PAYMENT_MATCH through RuleEvaluator; the result names rule R-RES-26 and the package version, and the decision log records both | D-RCV-36 T5, T7; ADR-012 |
| BR10 | No PAYMENT_MATCH version in force is a refusal (NoPackageInForce), never a default match | R-UNI-41; D-RCV-36 T7 |

The ten rules are unchanged by the split. The harness asserts them across the service boundaries and re-implements none of them: it reads the fired row and the version from the decision entry and never restates a window, a tolerance or a grace day in its own code.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case. This story changes no case status. The harness writes no state; the table is what it observes on the plan after a call to the owning service.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLAN_RUNNING | PAYMENT_RECEIVED | payment matched to the installment | PLAN_RUNNING (next due date advanced, R-RES-26) |
| PLAN_RUNNING | PAYMENT_MISSED | due_date passed and no payment matched | PLAN_CURE_PERIOD (R-RES-27) |

The proceeds row carries its own match state, which the harness reads and asserts: matched_to "INSTALLMENT" on a match, matched_to "UNMATCHED" with no treatment on a held receipt.

The harness adds a run state of its own only: Not started, Seeding, Running, Passed, Failed, with the latest run for a build deciding the gate. A failed run never overwrites a passed report for the same build and business date.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-RULES, Drools evaluator | Supplies the fired rule R-RES-26 and package version PM-2026.12 that the harness asserts; it is asked by rwb-payment, never by the harness |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Consumes `ProceedsMatched` and `PaymentMissed` and moves the plan route state; the harness asserts the result on the case and treatment contracts |
| SY-DECLOG, decision log writer | Writes the D5 entry the harness reads back through rwb-decision (Decision log C) |
| SY-AGENT, agent platform | Reads the exception list as the reconciliation agent would; the harness reads the same list, not the agent run |
| RW-CREDITAD, Credit Administration officer | Reads matched and unmatched receipts on SCR-28 (Write-off and posting CRUA); the synthetic user the access case refuses and allows |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the plan position on SCR-14 (Treatment and offer R); the role of the access refusal of TC-E2-008-10-ITG |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Owns package PAYMENT_MATCH and loads a new version (Rules and parameters CRUD); the harness seeds none of it in production and reads the version in force |
| Integration and QA team | Runs the harness, keeps the fake mappings, the payment fixture and the evidence, and owns the pass or fail gate |

No approval level from the delegation of authority applies: a match moves money inside the plan, and the harness takes no business decision. Authorisation is answered by rwb-access through the authorise operation of §12.2.

##### 11. Data

The harness owns no table. It reads and asserts the fields below through the owning services' contracts; the field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-ACE-043 | v_ace_payment | payment_code | Read through the P8 proceeds operation |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test asset in the integration pipeline and serves no operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; the 2 s timeout and the circuit breaker per downstream of DP-11 apply to every row.

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/payment/v1/proceeds` | P8 rwb-payment | Reads the matched and unmatched proceeds of the business date with payment code, treatment, source, amount and matched-to value (AC1, AC3, AC5) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/payment/v1/proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` | P8 rwb-payment | Drives the manual match path as a negative access control only; the automatic journey never calls it (TC-E2-008-10-ITG) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | Reads the case, the account and the running plan position after the events |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline` | P3 rwb-case | Reads the timeline entry of the plan movement and the missed payment |
| GET | `/api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}` | S2 rwb-treatment | Reads installment amount, installments, installments paid, treatment type and the next due date of the plan |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | P7 rwb-decision | Asserts the D5 entry with rule R-RES-26 and package version PM-2026.12, and its order before the proceeds row (AC1) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | Reads the freshness and batch state of "DP01 Account and arrears" and the MSG-P1-001 answer (AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/data-quality/exceptions` | P1 rwb-source-data | Reads the REC-05 business-key break of "PAY-90003" for the data steward (AC4) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` | P1 rwb-source-data | Reruns the job of one business date for the idempotency case (AC6, cited through TC-E2-008-06-ITG) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Role, scope and Write-off and posting right used by the proceeds read and by the access refusal (Architecture v5: rwb-access IN POST /authorise) |

The composite screen route itself is gateway-bff (DP-19), owned by the platform edge story RWB-PLT-N001-CON. Its path and merge order are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0393; ASM-0568).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event of its own; the ALS payment fixture is replayed through the rwb-source-data test profile so `AceDataReady` opens the JOB-07 window.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | What the harness asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1 | rwb.source-data.events.v1 | P1 rwb-source-data | Opens the JOB-07 window for business date 2026-12-14 and starts the event-started workflow on queue rwb-payment (DP-10) |
| rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1 | rwb.payment.events.v1 | P8 rwb-payment | One event per match with case, proceeds and amount, and one outbox row written in the same transaction as the proceeds row and the decision record (AC1) |
| rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1 | rwb.payment.events.v1 | P8 rwb-payment | One event per plan and due date that passed unpaid, with treatment "T-0701", due date 2026-12-15 and amount due 12,500.00; exactly one on a rerun (AC2, cited through TC-E2-008-02-ITG) |
| rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1 | rwb.case.events.v1 | P3 rwb-case | The plan moved PLAN_RUNNING to PLAN_CURE_PERIOD under R-RES-27 on the missed payment, and the state is visible on the case timeline |
| rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 | rwb.decision-record.v1 | P7 rwb-decision (ledger); every service publishes its own record | The D5 record of each match reaches the ledger inside the run window and names rule R-RES-26 and package version PM-2026.12 (DP-03) |
| rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1 | rwb.decision.events.v1 | P7 rwb-decision | The seeded version PM-2026.12 is the version in force on the business date, and the one rwb-payment swapped in |

The harness consumes with its own consumer group and never asserts a producer's outbox row directly; consumers dedupe through their own inbox.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

Observed, not built. JOB-07 Payment matching is an event-started workflow on queue `rwb-payment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, started by `AceDataReady` for the business date, with activity `matchPayments` in rwb-payment (Architecture v5 job map; DP-10). The harness records its workflow ID, its business date and its outcome, and asserts the proceeds, the decision entry and the plan afterwards.

JOB-11 Outbox sender is observed: the harness waits for the relay window and reads the events of §12.4 off the topics; it asserts neither the relay schedule nor its state.

No workflow is built, no activity is added and no schedule is created by this story. JOB-07 belongs to RWB-P8-E2008-APP.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The harness adds no Schedule and no cron; it starts a run from the test pipeline and, where a version must be promoted, waits for the JOB-20 Rule promote window at 00:01 in rwb-decision and asserts `RulePackageInForce`.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no table in any schema (DP-01); it reads and writes through the operations of §12.2 only.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

How the harness applies each pattern: DP-01, it owns no table and reads no schema, every read is an operation of §12.2; DP-03, it reads the D5 entry through rwb-decision and the record on the shared topic; DP-04, it reads the fired row R-RES-26 and version PM-2026.12, never the workbook or the DRL; DP-05, it asserts payments, next installment date and batch state only through the P1 and P8 contracts; DP-06 and DP-07, any parameter or LOV the journey needs is seeded through the P3 contract as data; DP-09, it subscribes to the owner's topics and the shared topic and publishes nothing; DP-10, JOB-07 is started by `AceDataReady` and observed on queue `rwb-payment`; DP-11, every call is one hop with the 2 s timeout; DP-13, every path uses the owner's base; DP-15, it runs no migration and seeds through operations; DP-19, the journey runs through the gateway route the screens use.

The platform H dependencies named by this table are delivered by the platform wave and are not repeated in the metadata H list. The blocking dependencies of this story are the eight I stories, which replace the fakes one at a time.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Test harness | Runs one journey per business date with the run lock, the build ID and the contract versions, and stops at the first failed assertion with the trace |
| FakePack | WireMock project | Serves rwb-payment, rwb-source-data, rwb-decision, rwb-treatment, rwb-case and rwb-access from the published OpenAPI documents of §12.8 |
| PaymentFixturePack | Data | The ALS payment fixture per business date, with the payment codes, dates and amounts of the legacy section 7 scenarios, replayed through the P1 test profile |
| PackageFixture | Data | The PAYMENT_MATCH EXACT row of version PM-2026.12 as read through rwb-decision, and the empty-version state of AC8; it holds values, never a threshold in code |
| MatchAssertion | Assertion | Reads the proceeds through P8 and compares payment code, amount, source, treatment and matched-to value against the expected row |
| DecisionOrderCheck | Assertion | Reads the D5 entry and the proceeds row and fails the run when the entry does not precede the row, when the rule ID is not R-RES-26, or when the version is not PM-2026.12 |
| MissedPaymentAssertion | Assertion | Reads `PaymentMissed`, the case timeline and the plan position and fails the run when the event, the state movement under R-RES-27 or the amounts disagree |
| RunReportWriter | Reporter | Writes one run report keyed by story key and business date with the trace and the per-assertion result; format and retention Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0393; ASM-0568) |

**Environment and test data**

- Environment: SIT, one namespace, the six services deployed from their wave 2 builds or replaced by the §12.8 fakes, with the Kafka topics of the six services, the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` and the Temporal namespace `rwb-recovery`. Harness repository, environment and seeding: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0393; ASM-0568).
- Data: synthetic case "RC-2026-000555", account "A-0555", plan "T-0701" (12,500.00 THB, 24 installments, 3 paid, next due 2026-12-15), case "RC-2026-000566", account "A-0666", plan "T-0702" (12,500.00 THB, next due 2026-12-16), account "A-0999" with no open case, payments "PAY-90001" to "PAY-90005", business dates 2026-12-05, 2026-12-14 and 2026-12-15, and PAYMENT_MATCH version PM-2026.12. No production record is copied.
- Reset: each run starts from the seeded state and the fixture of one business date, so a repeated run is deterministic and produces the same report.
- Business dates: the run uses 2026-12-14 as the matched and unmatched day, 2026-12-15 as the missed payment day and the boundary day of AC7, and 2026-12-16 for the withheld batch.

**Build steps**

1. Build JourneyRunner and the contract clients against the published OpenAPI documents of the six services, with the run lock and the build ID.
2. Publish FakePack for the six services from the same documents and prove the run green from Day 1 on the fakes.
3. Write PaymentFixturePack and PackageFixture and assert that `AceDataReady` starts the workflow on queue `rwb-payment` and that the EXACT row and version PM-2026.12 are the ones in force.
4. Add AC1 with MatchAssertion and DecisionOrderCheck: the record, then the proceeds row, then `ProceedsMatched`, then the plan at installments paid 4 with next due date 2027-01-15.
5. Add the missed payment of AC2 through MissedPaymentAssertion, including the plan state under R-RES-27, and the exception path of AC3 with the unmatched read and MSG-P8-001.
6. Add AC4 with the REC-05 break read and AC5 with the withheld batch, the freshness answer and MSG-P1-001.
7. Add the rerun of AC6, the window boundary of AC7, the no-version refusal of AC8 and the access refusal, then the forced decision-log failure of X7.
8. Write RunReportWriter, attach the report to the wave 2 run record, replace each fake with the real service as its I story lands, and apply the pass or fail gate; the gate definition: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0393; ASM-0568).

**Feature switch:** the harness has no production feature flag and runs in the test environment only. The production switch it exercises is `rwb.payments.matching` from the legacy solution plan: with the flag off, JOB-07 does not match and the harness asserts the disabled state before it asserts the enabled one. The flag is read and set through the platform feature-flag operation, never held in the harness.

**Done when:** the journey runs green against the eight deployed I stories in SIT, the run report for the business date holds every assertion of §7 and §16 with its trace, every match decision entry names R-RES-26 and PM-2026.12 before its proceeds row, every payment of the fixture is either a proceeds row or a held exception, and the pass or fail gate agreed with QA is met for one full business date.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P8-001 | Run summary with unmatched payments | {count} payments for {date} matched no plan and are on the exception list. |
| MSG-P8-002 | No PAYMENT_MATCH version in force | Payment matching for {date} did not run: no matching rule is in force. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No PAYMENT_MATCH version is in force | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The ACE batch is late or not complete | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks Write-off and posting R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values and owns no message text. For MSG-P3-027 in this journey {check} is "no package in force" and {detail} names the package code "PAYMENT_MATCH" and the business date only, never a payment or an account fact. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the tolerance 0 percent, the window of 10 days before and 0 days after, the grace of 0 days and the match types are columns of the PAYMENT_MATCH rows; the harness reads them from the fired row and holds no copy.
- No personal data in logs, events, tests, traces or reports: payments are identified by payment_code and account_key, account numbers are never logged, and the fixture and every seeded case are synthetic.
- No read of another service's schema and no direct ACE read: ACE payment, account and batch data come only through the rwb-source-data contract or the owning service's own views (DP-05), and every read of §12.2 goes through the owner's contract.
- The decision record is written before the proceeds row; DecisionOrderCheck fails the run when a proceeds row exists without its D5 entry, or when the entry names a rule or a version the package did not fire.
- One hop only: the harness fails a run when the trace shows a call chain deeper than the gateway and one owner, and it holds the 2 s budget per call.
- No second rule engine: the harness reads the rule ID and the package version through the rwb-decision contract, and no caller reads the workbook, the `drl_source` or a `rule_row` row.
- Each fake is replaced by the real service as its I story lands; a fake that outlives its service is a defect, not a configuration. The harness never runs against UAT or production, and an exception is never added to a scenario.

##### 19. Out of scope

- The eight owning I stories RWB-P8-E2008-APP, RWB-P1-E2008-APP, RWB-S2-E2008-APP, RWB-P3-E2042-APP, RWB-P7-E2008-APP, RWB-P4-E2008-APP, RWB-P3-E2004-APP and RWB-P1-E1069-APP, and every screen, endpoint, table, migration, rule and workflow they build.
- Production code in any service: the harness is test and evidence only.
- The CON stories of rwb-payment, rwb-source-data, rwb-decision, rwb-treatment, rwb-case and rwb-access, and the OPS and INF stories of the wave.
- Platform deployment, the gateway-bff composite proceeds and exception route (RWB-PLT-N001-CON), and the platform configuration of Kafka, Temporal and the observability stack.
- The ALS system itself, its ingestion DAG and its batch record: the harness consumes what rwb-source-data publishes.
- Partial payments, late payments inside a window after the due date and the settlement, auction and enforcement proceeds (RWB-E2-027, FEAT-PAY-03, FEAT-PAY-04, Epic 4).
- Manual matching of an unmatched receipt and the reconciliation agent that works the exception list (Epic 4).
- The cure period and the broken plan rule (R-RES-28 to R-RES-31, FEAT-TRT-11, Epic 3), and the authoring, approval and rollback of package PAYMENT_MATCH (RWB-E2-042 and RWB-E1-073).
- The other legacy journeys of Epic 2 and their harness stories.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract baseline of RWB-E2-009 for rwb-reporting — the `GET /reports/measures` shape with the dimension and baseline fields, the `measure_publish` schema, the consumed declarations and their fakes, the event subscriptions with their consumer groups, the workflow registration contract of JOB-15, the error model and the message map — is published as one frozen baseline so that RWB-P9-E2009-APP and RWB-P9-E2009-OPS start on Day 1. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **contract owner of the reporting service (TechX)**, I want **one published baseline for the steering dashboard data set — the shape of `GET /reports/measures`, the `measure_publish` schema, the consumed contracts with their fakes, the event subscriptions, the registration contract of JOB-15 and the message map — so that** the application story, the deployment story and the Power BI consumer build on Day 1 against a fake and no shape is decided twice.

The baseline fixes, and nothing else:

- the delta on the parent operation `GET /reports/measures` as tagged by RWB-P9-E1013-CON: `baselineValue`, the fixing of `dimension` as code and value, and the `X-Data-As-Of` freshness header, on base `/api/recovery/reporting/v1` (DP-13, R4);
- the two fields that RWB-E2-009 section 12 asks for — `dimension` (code and value) and `baselineValue` — both absent from the API Specification that the parent document inherited;
- the increments on `measure_publish` and `measure_snapshot` that the steering key needs — the unique key of one row per business date and the index by measure, date and product — with the field sets of DF-RPT-041 to DF-RPT-058 inherited from the parent and not restated (DP-01, DP-15);
- the declarations of the four consumed operations — the case facts of P3, the agent runs of RWB-P10-E1063-CON, the data-product freshness of P1 and the lists of RWB-P3-E1043-CON — and of the extract hand-over on the rwb-integration queue, each with a fake (DP-07, DP-11, DP-17);
- the subscriptions of the service — EV-01, EV-02, EV-05, EV-08, EV-10, EV-14, EV-15 and EV-28 — with their consumer groups and envelope rules, and no published event of the service's own;
- the registration contract of JOB-15 on queue `rwb-reporting` with its Schedule, so the deployment story registers one name and not two (DP-10);
- the error model and the message map, so a consumer reads one envelope.

This story writes no behaviour. The calculators, the reconciliation and the read are RWB-P9-E2009-APP; the deployment of the build is RWB-P9-E2009-OPS. Where a legacy shape has no target counterpart, the baseline states the placeholder and the gap, and no value is invented (GAP-2577; ASM-4248).

##### 2. Business rationale

A split story is only as good as the contract it builds against. RWB-E2-009 was written as one screen reading six in-process interfaces and one data-lake extract; nothing in it can be built by a team that does not own the neighbour. Under D-RCV-60 the facts arrive as events and on narrow contracts with a fake each, and those shapes have to be frozen before the application and the deployment stories open — otherwise the screen, the Power BI report and the run each freeze a different shape of the same measure.

- **one baseline, three consumers.** RWB-P9-E2009-APP, RWB-P9-E2009-OPS and the Power BI report of the Reporting and BI analyst read these shapes; RWB-P9-E1013-CON stays the parent of the measure set and is not restated here.
- **the contract is testable without a neighbour.** Every declaration and every subscription carries a fake with a documented answer, so the contract tests run on Day 1 and SIT only replaces the fake with the owner.
- **nothing of the business is frozen here.** The seven measure codes, their formulas, the tolerance of DL25 and the age bands stay rows of `measure_definition`; the baseline carries their shape, never their value.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The ownership rows of the service are taken as authoritative from the context pack: tables `measure_definition`, `measure_publish` and `measure_snapshot` (P9); operations `GET /reports/measures` (P9); events, none (P9); jobs JOB-15 (P9); workflows, none (P9).
- RWB-P9-E1013-CON is published as the parent baseline of the measure set: `measure_definition`, `measure_snapshot`, the `Measure` shape and the `GET /reports/measures` operation. This baseline publishes the delta of the steering key on top of it and does not restate the parent.
- The API Specification, the Event and Messaging Design, the Physical Schema and the LOV set of TSD P9 T3.2 are at their next versions and are the parents of this baseline.
- The platform contracts the patterns name — RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON — are published at their baseline versions.
- RWB-P3-E1043-CON and RWB-P10-E1063-CON are readable as drafts, so their response elements are declared from the published documents and the fakes are built from those declarations.
- Status is Draft (realignment v1): no approval is required to publish a baseline, and a consumer builds against the tagged version (GAP-2577; ASM-4248).
- The legacy message IDs and their texts stand in the message map; no new business message text is written here.

##### 4. Flow

1. Take the one operation of the ownership row, place it on `/api/recovery/reporting/v1`, and write its filters, its response shape, its errors, its right and its freshness header into 12.1.
2. Add the two fields RWB-E2-009 section 12 asks for — `dimension` and `baselineValue` — to the `Measure` schema as a versioned delta on the parent document, and state where each value comes from.
3. Take the `measure_publish` and `measure_snapshot` field sets of TSD P9 T3.1 as the parent tag fixes them, add the steering key's unique key on the business date and its snapshot index, and state the no-cross-schema-key rule in 12.7.
4. Declare the four consumed operations and the extract hand-over activity with their base, their owner and their request and response elements, and record the placeholder where no published document fixes an element (12.2).
5. Declare the eight subscriptions with their topic, their consumer group and their envelope rule, and state once that the service publishes no domain event of its own (12.3, 12.4).
6. Fix the registration contract of JOB-15 — queue, namespace, workflow type, input schema, Schedule cadence, overlap policy — so the deployment story registers one name (12.5, 12.6).
7. Fix the error model: the platform problem shape, the status of each legacy message of section 14 and the rule that a refused right answers MSG-P4-002 and changes nothing.
8. Publish one fake per declaration and per subscription, each with the documented answer of 12.8, so the contract tests run without a neighbour.
9. Freeze the baseline as version `v1`, tag it and hand the tag to RWB-P9-E2009-APP and RWB-P9-E2009-OPS; any later shape change is a new version and a Change Register row.
10. Run the contract tests of section 16 against the OpenAPI document, the subscription declarations, the schema statement and the fakes, and publish the result with the tag.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A consumer sends a shape the baseline does not declare, or a period whose `from` is after `to` | The request is refused with the problem envelope and no business change | MSG-GEN-003, MSG-P4-002 | AC1, AC5 |
| X2 | A declared operation or activity has no published document behind it and the owner has not confirmed the element names | The declaration carries the placeholder and the fake answers the baseline shape; the review row stays open | None | AC3, GAP-2577 |
| X3 | A breaking change is proposed after the tag | The change opens a new version of the baseline; the tagged version stays buildable | None | AC7 |
| X4 | A fake returns an answer the baseline does not document | The contract test fails and the baseline is not tagged | None | AC6 |
| X5 | A statement of the baseline names another `rwb_*` schema, a `v_ace_*` view or a data-lake object | The schema lint fails and the baseline is not tagged | None (lint log) | AC4, section 17 |
| X6 | A consumer asks for the data lake, INT-19 or an event of this service | No such element is published; the request answers the gap row and the hand-over of 12.2 is the replacement | None | AC2, GAP-2577 |
| X7 | A subscription declaration has no consumer group or no envelope rule | The declaration is not publishable and the tag is refused | None | AC3 |

X2 and X6 are the only paths that end in an open review row; the rest are gates of the tag. No path invents a business value: the values behind the shapes are `measure_definition` rows and reference data of their owners.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs no running neighbour: every declaration and every subscription has a fake, and every shape comes from a published document or the context pack |
| Negotiable | The element names of an unpublished consumed operation and the activity names are the review baseline and may be corrected by the owner without a behaviour change |
| Valuable | The application story, the deployment story and the Power BI report build on Day 1 against one tag |
| Estimable | One operation, one shape delta, two schema increments, four consumed declarations, one activity, eight subscriptions, one registration and eleven fakes |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion runs as a contract test at Level Contract against the documents and the fakes |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

The seven criteria test the baseline only. They carry no measure value, count, rate, agent name or business date of the legacy story except the field, list and event names that the context pack and TSD P9 fix; the values behind the shapes stay `measure_definition` rows and reference data (ASM-4248).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The baseline is one tagged version; a consumer builds against the tag and never against a draft element | R8.2; R5.7 rule 1 |
| BR2 | The operation set is the ownership row of the service and nothing else; an operation the context pack does not carry is not published | Context pack; GAP-2577 |
| BR3 | One base per service, `/api/recovery/reporting/v1`, and no operation outside it | DP-13, R4 |
| BR4 | The service publishes no domain event of this key; its only published event is the library's `DecisionRecorded` on the shared topic | DP-03; context pack events row |
| BR5 | One schema and one login per service; no foreign key and no statement may leave `rwb_reporting` | DP-01, DP-02 |
| BR6 | Every consumed operation and every owner-queue activity is declared with a fake; a declaration without a fake is not publishable | DP-11 |
| BR7 | No business value is frozen: measure codes, formulas, units, age bands, the tolerance of DL25 and the LOV values are read from their owners | Principle 1; DP-07 |
| BR8 | No personal data in a schema, an event fixture, a fake or a test | Section 17 |
| BR9 | No element of the data lake, INT-19 or INT-20 is declared; the published day's extract is handed to rwb-integration | DP-17 |
| BR10 | The error envelope is the platform problem shape and every legacy message ID maps to one status and one code | R7.2 s14; section 14 |
| BR11 | A breaking change is a new version and a Change Register row; a correction of an element name by its owner is a patch to the same version | R8.2; AC7 |

##### 9. State transitions

None of business data: this story changes no record and no publish state. The states it owns are the states of the baseline itself.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not existing | The baseline is written and its tests pass | The tag gate of section 16 is green | `v1` Draft, tagged and handed to the consumers |
| `v1` Draft | The owner confirms or corrects an element name of a consumed declaration | The change is not breaking | `v1` patched, the review row closed |
| `v1` | A published element changes shape | A consumer cannot build against the old shape | `v2` opened; `v1` stays readable and buildable |
| `v1` | A consumer asks for an element the baseline does not declare | The row is absent, for example the data lake of INT-19 | No change; the request answers the gap row |

The version states are `Draft`, `Tagged` and `Superseded`, and only a tagged version is citable by an APP or OPS story.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The contract owner of rwb-reporting (TechX) | Writes, tags and versions the baseline; owns the fakes and the contract tests; refuses a declaration without a published document |
| The owner of rwb-case (P3) | Confirms or corrects the case-list declaration, the reference-data lists and their fakes |
| The owner of rwb-agent (P10) | Confirms or corrects the agent-run declaration behind RWB-P10-E1063-CON and its fake |
| The owner of rwb-source-data (P1) | Confirms the freshness declaration and its fake |
| The owner of rwb-integration (P2) | Confirms the extract hand-over declaration, its queue and the file shape |
| The owner of rwb-decision (P7) | Confirms the eight subscription declarations and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` |
| The platform contract owners (PLT) | Own the shapes the baseline inherits: the record, the workflow kit, the reference-data client, the Flyway gate and the composite route |
| RW-BIANAL, RW-TRIBE, RW-PRODHEAD, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-DATASTEW | Read the baseline as consumers; hold no write right on it |

The right of the published operation is the row of TSD P9 T6.1; the baseline declares it and grants nothing.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity (owner) | Field | Declared as |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-RPT-031 to DF-RPT-040 | `measure_definition` (P9) | id, measure_code, name, formula, data_product, unit, definition_version, approved_by, approved_at, valid_from | inherited from RWB-P9-E1013-CON; read by the operation |
| DF-RPT-041 to DF-RPT-052 | `measure_snapshot` (P9) | id, measure_code, definition_version, business_date, product_group, dimension_code, dimension_value, value, case_count, is_baseline, frozen, published_at | inherited; `dimension_code` and `dimension_value` are the source of the `dimension` field of AC2 |
| DF-RPT-053 | `measure_publish` (P9) | id | required, uuid |
| DF-RPT-054 | `measure_publish` (P9) | business_date | required, unique across the table |
| DF-RPT-055 | `measure_publish` (P9) | status | required, from LOV-MEASURE-PUBLISH |
| DF-RPT-056 | `measure_publish` (P9) | case_list_count | required |
| DF-RPT-057 | `measure_publish` (P9) | dashboard_count | required |
| DF-RPT-058 | `measure_publish` (P9) | held_reason | optional, the reason a day was held |
| DF-CAS-001, DF-CAS-003, DF-CAS-006, DF-CAS-008, DF-CAS-010, DF-CAS-013 | `recovery_case` (P3) | case id, product group, stage, route, queue and entry date | response elements of the case-list declaration; never a table read |
| DF-DEC-007, DF-DEC-012, DF-DEC-013 | `decision_log_entry` (P7) | agent_version, final_call, override_reason | envelope elements of EV-08 and EV-28 |

The field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and of TSD P9 T3.1. The column sets of the three tables are those of the parent tag RWB-P9-E1013-CON; this baseline declares only the uniqueness of `business_date`, the two indexes and the shape delta, and adds no column. The legacy story asks for a `baselineValue` on the `Measure` schema; no column carries it, so it is derived from the frozen baseline rows of 2026-11-27 and the derivation is part of the declared shape, not a new column (GAP-2577; ASM-4248). No element of a payload is invented beyond the legacy lists and the envelope fields.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-reporting (P9); base `/api/recovery/reporting/v1` (DP-13); document `openapi/rwb-reporting-v1.yaml`, an increment on the document tagged by RWB-P9-E1013-CON. The operation, its filters and its access row belong to the parent; this baseline publishes the delta of the steering key and restates nothing else.

| Method | Path | Request | Response | Errors | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/reports/measures` | query `measure`, `product`, `route`, `from`, `to` (dates, `from` on or before `to`) | 200 `Measure[]`: measure, product, route, period, value, dimension (code and value), baselineValue; header `X-Data-As-Of` | 401, 403 (MSG-P4-002), 422 (MSG-GEN-003), 503 (MSG-GEN-006) | Reporting, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

The delta is `baselineValue`; `dimension` is declared here as a code and a value of LOV-MEASURE-DIM, which the parent already carries as two properties, and the `X-Data-As-Of` header stays as the parent declares it (RWB-E2-009 section 12). The legacy path `monolith-base/reports/measures` moves to the per-service base and keeps its operation path. No second operation is published: a rerun of a business date is a workflow-level action of RWB-PLT-E1071-CON and not an operation of this service (GAP-2577; ASM-4248).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Base | Owner | Request | Response elements |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The case facts of a business date (the read RWB-P3-E1013-APP declares) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | asOf, page | one row per case with product group, route, stage, queue, entry date, status and closed date, with the as-of time and the row count |
| The runs of an agent and version for a business date (name as above) | RWB-P10-E1063-CON | P10 rwb-agent | businessDate, agent, version | run count, accepted, overridden, latency, cost, version |
| The lists of the measures (name as above) | RWB-P3-E1043-CON | P3 rwb-case | listCode, businessDate | the active values of LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-MEASURE-UNIT, LOV-MEASURE-DIM, LOV-DATA-PRODUCT and LOV-MEASURE-PUBLISH |
| The freshness of the data products of a business date (the read RWB-P1-E1013-APP declares) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | asOf, product | the product, its business date and its freshness stamp |
| The extract hand-over of a published day (name and file shape as above) | activity on the queue `rwb-integration` | P2 rwb-integration | businessDate, row set, freshness stamp | accepted, delivery reference |

Every REST row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a single GET retry with jitter and a breaker per downstream (DP-11, ADR-020). The hand-over replaces INT-19, the data lake load area, which no longer exists; the file shape Power BI reads is fixed by no source and is the review row of AC3 (DP-17).

###### 12.3 Events published

None of the service's own. The ownership row of the service carries no event, so no schema is published on `rwb.reporting.events.v1`; the topic, its `.retry` and its `.dlt` are provisioned for the service's own lifecycle messages and carry nothing for this key. The one event this service writes is the local library's `DecisionRecorded` (EV-08) on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, whose owner is rwb-decision and whose schema is inherited and not restated (DP-03).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Consumer group | Envelope rule | Declaration |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` (EV-01) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.case.v1` | dedupe on the event id; order per case by the outbox sequence | caseId, caseNo, productGroup, accounts, businessDate |
| `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1` (EV-02) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.case.v1` | as above | caseId, queueId, ownerId, ruleId, ruleVersion |
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` (EV-05) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.case.v1` | as above | caseId, fromState, toState, ruleId, decisionLogEntryId |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | `rwb-reporting.decision.v1` | dedupe on the entry id | entryId, caseId, decisionCode, approver |
| `rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1` (EV-10) | `rwb.treatment.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.treatment.v1` | dedupe on the event id | treatmentId, caseId, terms |
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` (EV-14) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.notice.v1` | dedupe on the notice id and the dispatch | noticeId, barcode, sentDate |
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` (EV-15) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.notice.v1` | dedupe on the notice id and the delivery | noticeId, deliveredAt, status |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.reporting`, module `contract`; artefacts under `contracts/rwb-reporting/`: `openapi-v1.yaml`, `consumed.yaml`, `subscriptions.yaml`, `schema/rwb_reporting_steering.sql`, `messages.yaml`, `fakes/*.json`.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `openapi-v1.yaml` | Document | the operation, its parameters, its `Measure` delta, its header, its errors and its examples |
| `consumed.yaml` | Document | the three declarations and the two owner-queue activities, with their owners and their review state |
| `subscriptions.yaml` | Document | the eight subscriptions, their consumer groups and their envelope rules |
| `schema/rwb_reporting_steering.sql` | Document | the `measure_publish` baseline and the snapshot index, with their keys and their no-cross-schema rule |
| `messages.yaml` | Document | the message map of section 14 |
| `fakes/` | Generator | one fake per declaration and per subscription, generated from the documents and versioned with them |
| `ContractTag` | Build step | tags the baseline and publishes the tag to the two consumer stories |

**Build steps.** (1) Write the OpenAPI increment and lint it; test AC1 and AC2. (2) Write the four declarations and the hand-over contract, and generate the fakes; test AC3. (3) Write the schema statement and pass the schema lint; test AC4. (4) Write the eight subscriptions and the message map; test AC5. (5) Run the contract tests, tag `v1` and publish the tag; test AC6 and AC7.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Status and code |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P9-002 | The dashboard count differs from the case list | 409 on a replayed publish; the run and screen text names both counts and the date |
| MSG-P1-001 | A source is stale | 503 on a read of stale data; the text carries the product and the date |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Dates in the wrong order | 422 with the two field names and no value |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks Reporting R | 403 on the operation; nothing changes |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A named system is unavailable | 503 with the system name only |
| MSG-P7-003 | The local record cannot be written | 500 on the operation; the run text says nothing was changed |

The envelope of every error is the platform problem shape — `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`, `instance` and `traceId` — and carries no personal data. The texts are the legacy texts of RWB-E2-009 section 14 and of the platform, and are copied into the message map unchanged.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a document, a schema, a fake or a test: the measure codes, formulas, units, age bands, the tolerance of DL25 and the LOV values are rows of their owners and appear here only as element names.
- No personal data in a schema, an event fixture or a log: a measure carries counts, rates, amounts and codes; an agent run carries an agent, a version and an outcome.
- No statement leaves `rwb_reporting`, no element of the data lake is declared, and no `v_ace_*` view is named.
- No declaration without a fake, no subscription without a consumer group and an envelope rule, no tag without the contract tests.
- The six message texts are copied, never reworded; a new text needs its owner.
