**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the application slice of RWB-E2-009 for rwb-reporting — the seven steering calculators over the event-derived read model, the case-list reconciliation that holds a publish, `measure_publish` in `rwb_reporting`, the local record of each publish decision, the scheduled run JOB-15 and `GET /reports/measures` behind SCR-37 — is split from the published shapes (RWB-P9-E2009-CON) and from the deployment of the build (RWB-P9-E2009-OPS). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As the **Tribe lead (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **a data set for the steering dashboard with cases by stage, queue and age, decisions logged, treatments, letters sent and agent acceptance, published each morning and reconciled to the case list**, so that **the steering committee reads the same numbers the teams work with**.

Inside rwb-reporting this is the steering half of RWB-E2-009:

- service `rwb-reporting`, schema `rwb_reporting`, REST base `/api/recovery/reporting/v1`, topic `rwb.reporting.events.v1` with event names `rwb.reporting.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-reporting` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.reporting` (R4, DP-13);
- JOB-15 as the Temporal Schedule `reportingMeasuresDaily` at 01:30 on queue `rwb-reporting`, with no Quartz row and no Spring Batch descriptor (DP-10);
- the read model built from events — `CaseCreated` (EV-01), `CaseAllocated` (EV-02), `CaseStateChanged` (EV-05), `DecisionRecorded` (EV-08), `TreatmentApproved` (EV-10), `NoticeDispatched` (EV-14), `AgentRunCompleted` (EV-28) — plus the agent contract RWB-P10-E1063-CON for acceptance and override, and no data lake anywhere (DP-17);
- the publish or hold of the business date, recorded on `measure_publish` — the table RWB-P9-E1013-APP creates — through the same publish recorder, in the service's own schema (DP-01, DP-15);
- one local decision record per business date — published or held — written before the snapshot rows and relayed on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03);
- the case facts of the business date and the count of open cases at the cut-off, read on the rwb-case contract that RWB-P3-E1013-APP declares with the same run (DP-11);
- the lists of the measures — LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-MEASURE-UNIT, LOV-MEASURE-DIM, LOV-DATA-PRODUCT and LOV-MEASURE-PUBLISH — on the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-07);
- `GET /reports/measures` on the per-service base, served to SCR-37 through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

Not here: the published shapes and the fakes (RWB-P9-E2009-CON); the deployment, the topics, the alerts and the runbook (RWB-P9-E2009-OPS); the measure set and JOB-15's first build of RWB-E1-013 (RWB-P9-E1013-APP); the queue and service-level measures of RWB-E1-030 and RWB-E2-011; the agent monitoring dashboard with latency and cost of RWB-E2-031; benefit realisation of FEAT-RPT-06; regulatory returns of FEAT-RPT-07.

##### 2. Business rationale

The steering committee receives numbers counted by hand that differ from the numbers the teams see in their queues. RWB-E2-009 adds the steering measures to the nightly measure set, holds the publish when the dashboard case count differs from the case list, and serves the values to SCR-37. It serves REQ-WKM-009 and REQ-WKM-006, NFR-065, NFR-066 and the zero tolerance of DL25.

The legacy story reaches its facts through six in-process interfaces and puts its extract in a data lake. Under D-RCV-60 four things move:

- **the facts become events.** rwb-reporting builds its read model from the events of P3, S2, P6, P7 and P10 instead of calling their Java interfaces, and the agent rates come from the agent contract RWB-P10-E1063-CON (DP-17, DP-11).
- **the lake is gone.** INT-19 and INT-20 are removed; the same snapshot rows that serve SCR-37 feed the Power BI refresh through the extract hand-over, so the screen and the report cannot disagree (DP-17).
- **the scheduler is gone.** JOB-15 is a Temporal Schedule on this service's queue, and a rerun is a workflow-level action, not a second job (DP-10).
- **the row is written here, first.** The publish or hold decision is a local decision record committed in the same transaction as `measure_publish` (DP-03), which is what legacy AC9 and BR5 ask for.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P9-E2009-CON is tagged `v1` as the delta of this key on the parent baseline of RWB-P9-E1013-CON: `baselineValue` on `Measure`, the fixing of `dimension`, the four consumed declarations and the extract hand-over activity, the eight subscriptions, the registration contract of JOB-15, the message map and the fakes.
- RWB-P9-E1013-APP is done: `measure_definition`, `measure_snapshot` and `measure_publish` exist, the measure set runs at 01:30, the publish recorder and the frozen baseline of 2026-11-27 stand, and the steering calculators extend the same measure set.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (local record), RWB-PLT-E1043-CON (reference-data client), RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (Schedule and workflow kit), RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (Flyway sequence and drift gate) and RWB-PLT-N001-CON (gateway-bff composite route) are published.
- RWB-P3-E1043-CON serves LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-MEASURE-UNIT, LOV-MEASURE-DIM, LOV-DATA-PRODUCT and LOV-MEASURE-PUBLISH, and RWB-P10-E1063-CON serves the runs of an agent and version for a business date.
- Definition version "MD-2026.12" is loaded and approved by the Tribe lead: the seven steering measures of the legacy `Background`, with the reconciliation tolerance of zero (DL25). The version is a data row; no measure code is a constant.
- The legacy story's five fact interfaces (`CaseReportingApi`, `DecisionLogApi`, `TreatmentApi`, `NoticeApi`, `AgentMonitorApi`) have no target operation names and no published payloads; each fact arrives on an event or on a contract named here, with the placeholder where the field list is not fixed (GAP-2576; ASM-4243).
- The service runs as login `rwb_reporting` on schema `rwb_reporting`, holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema, and reads no `v_ace_*` view: reporting data arrives on events and contracts only (DP-01, DP-17).
- `rwb.reporting.steering` is the feature flag of the platform library; off means the run writes its record, holds the business date and publishes nothing.

##### 4. Flow

1. The Schedule `reportingMeasuresDaily` opens one workflow execution per business date D at 01:30, with the execution id derived from D so a rerun joins the run (DP-10).
2. `checkFreshness` reuses the freshness gate of RWB-P9-E1013-APP and asks rwb-source-data for the data products of D; a source that is not fresh leaves the freshness stamp at its own date and raises MSG-P1-001 (DP-17).
3. `loadReadModel` replays the events of D from `rwb.case.events.v1`, `rwb.treatment.events.v1`, `rwb.comms.events.v1`, `rwb.decision-record.v1` and `rwb.agent.events.v1` into the run-scoped fact view of the workflow, deduplicated on the event id and ordered per case by the sequence of the outbox (DP-17).
4. `loadAgentFacts` reads the runs of every agent and version for D on RWB-P10-E1063-CON: recommendations, accepted, overridden with a reason, and the version of each run (DP-11).
5. `computeMeasures` runs the seven calculators — CASES_BY_STAGE, CASES_BY_QUEUE_AGE, DECISIONS_LOGGED, TREATMENTS, LETTERS_SENT, AGENT_ACCEPTANCE, AGENT_OVERRIDE — over the fact view and writes one candidate row set per measure, product, dimension and value, with the definition version in force.
6. `reconcileCounts` sums CASES_BY_STAGE at the cut-off of D, reads the case facts of D on `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/facts` — the read RWB-P3-E1013-APP declares — and counts the open cases of the same cut-off, with the product filter optional (DP-11).
7. Where the two counts are equal, the transaction writes one local decision record with the outcome PUBLISHED, writes the snapshot rows with their `published_at`, writes the publish row of the business date as PUBLISHED with the two counts and no held reason through the recorder of RWB-P9-E1013-APP, and hands the extract over (DP-03, DP-01).
8. Where they differ, the transaction writes the record with the outcome HELD, writes the publish row as HELD with both counts and the held reason, writes no snapshot row and publishes no extract, and raises MSG-P9-002 to the Reporting and BI analyst and the data steward (BR2).
9. `handOverExtract` hands the published day's extract to rwb-integration as an activity on its queue, with the business date as its freshness stamp; INT-19, the data lake load area, is not used (DP-17).
10. `GET /reports/measures` answers the published rows on `/api/recovery/reporting/v1`: filtered by measure, product, route and period, with the scope of the role applied, the business date and freshness stamp in `X-Data-As-Of`, and each value beside its baseline value of 2026-11-27 (DP-13).
11. A rate whose denominator is zero — an agent and version with no run in D — writes no AGENT_ACCEPTANCE row; the screen shows "No runs" for that pair (BR6).
12. The run closes with its summary — measures written, the two counts, the publish status, the extract hand-over — and the visibility view of the workflow kit shows it to the Reporting and BI analyst; the rerun of the same business date replays the same execution and writes the same values (AC9).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Dashboard case count differs from the case list | The record and `measure_publish` are written as HELD, the previous day stays the latest published, and both counts are named | MSG-P9-002 | AC4, BR2 |
| X2 | A source load for the business date is stale | The measure is written from the last complete day, with that date as its freshness stamp | MSG-P1-001 | AC5, BR4 |
| X3 | A query with `from` after `to` | Refused before any read, with the two field names | MSG-GEN-003 | AC6 |
| X4 | An agent and version has no run in the day | No rate row is written and the screen shows "No runs" for that pair | None | AC7, BR6 |
| X5 | JOB-15 is rerun for a published business date | The rows are replaced with the same values, the frozen baseline of 2026-11-27 is untouched, and one record is added | None | AC9, BR13 |
| X6 | The role lacks Reporting R | The read is refused and nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-009-10, BR7 |
| X7 | The local decision record cannot be written | The transaction writes nothing: no snapshot row, no `measure_publish`, no extract | MSG-P7-003 | BR12 |
| X8 | The case-facts contract does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | `reconcileCounts` retries on the workflow policy; the day stays unpublished rather than published unverified | None | BR9 |
| X9 | The extract hand-over to rwb-integration fails | The snapshot rows stand as published, the extract is retried from the run, and the reporting analyst is alerted | MSG-GEN-006 | BR10 |
| X10 | A component, a statement or a test reaches another service's schema, a `v_ace_*` view or the data lake | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | Section 17 |

X1 to X5 are the exception paths of RWB-E2-009 carried onto the split; X6 to X10 are the paths the microservice adds. The tolerance is zero (DL25), so no path publishes a day whose counts differ; no path writes a measure code, a formula, an age band or a tolerance as a constant.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts after RWB-P9-E1013-APP against RWB-P9-E2009-CON, the platform contracts and the rwb-case, rwb-reports and agent contract fakes, on its own schema, with no live neighbour |
| Negotiable | The workflow, activity and consumer-group names, the run-fact view and the run summary are this story's choice; the measures, messages, statuses and field sets are fixed |
| Valuable | One set of numbers for the committee and the teams, and a day that cannot be published while the counts disagree |
| Estimable | One Schedule, one workflow, six activities, seven calculators, one reconciliation check, one row, one read and four consumed contracts |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against a synthetic day built from event fixtures and contract fakes with known answers |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Steering dashboard v1 data set

  Background:
    Given definition version "MD-2026.12" is in force with measures "CASES_BY_STAGE", "CASES_BY_QUEUE_AGE", "DECISIONS_LOGGED", "TREATMENTS", "LETTERS_SENT", "AGENT_ACCEPTANCE" and "AGENT_OVERRIDE"
    Given the synthetic day 2026-12-15 holds 240 open cases, 1,412 decision log entries, 38 treatments and 95 notices sent

  Scenario: AC1 Refresh (legacy RWB-E2-009 AC1)
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns the loads of business date 2026-12-15 with their checks passed
    Given the loads of business date 2026-12-15 passed their checks
    When JOB-15 runs at 01:30 on 2026-12-16
    Then GET /reports/measures?from=2026-12-15&to=2026-12-15 returns a value for each of the 7 measures with period "2026-12-15"
    Then the INT-19 extract for 2026-12-15 has freshness stamp 2026-12-15 for the 07:30 Power BI refresh

  Scenario: AC2 Reconciles (legacy RWB-E2-009 AC2)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns 240 open cases at the 2026-12-15 cut-off
    Given the case list shows 240 open cases at the 2026-12-15 cut-off
    When JOB-15 runs at 01:30 on 2026-12-16
    Then the sum of "CASES_BY_STAGE" for 2026-12-15 is 240
    Then "DECISIONS_LOGGED" for 2026-12-15 is 1,412, the count of decision log entries decided that day

  Scenario: AC3 Agent measures (legacy RWB-E2-009 AC3)
    Given the rwb-agent contract mock returns 200 recommendations, 170 accepted and 30 overridden for "case-intake" "1.2.0" on 2026-12-15
    Given agent "case-intake" version "1.2.0" made 200 recommendations on 2026-12-15, of which 170 were accepted and 30 overridden with a reason
    When JOB-15 runs at 01:30 on 2026-12-16
    Then "AGENT_ACCEPTANCE" for "case-intake" "1.2.0" on 2026-12-15 is 85.0 percent
    Then "AGENT_OVERRIDE" for "case-intake" "1.2.0" on 2026-12-15 is 15.0 percent
    Then SCR-37 shows both rates by agent

  Scenario: AC4 Counts do not match (legacy RWB-E2-009 AC4)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns 240 open cases at the 2026-12-15 cut-off
    Given the case facts read for the dashboard total 239
    Given the case list shows 240 open cases at the 2026-12-15 cut-off
    When JOB-15 runs at 01:30 on 2026-12-16
    Then no snapshot rows and no extract are published for 2026-12-15
    Then SCR-37 shows 2026-12-14 as the latest day with MSG-P9-002 naming 239, 240 and 2026-12-15
    Then an alert goes to the Reporting and BI analyst and the data steward

  Scenario: AC5 Stale source (legacy RWB-E2-009 AC5)
    Given the rwb-comms event mock returns the notice data product of 2026-12-14 for business date 2026-12-15
    Given the notice data product is from 2026-12-14 because the 2026-12-15 load has not arrived
    When a product head opens SCR-37 on 2026-12-16
    Then "LETTERS_SENT" shows the value for 2026-12-14
    Then SCR-37 shows MSG-P1-001 naming "DP07 Legal" and 2026-12-14

  Scenario: AC6 Dates in the wrong order (legacy RWB-E2-009 AC6)
    Given a team manager holds RW-TEAMMGR with Reporting R
    When a team manager sends GET /reports/measures?from=2026-12-15&to=2026-12-01
    Then the response is status 422 with MSG-GEN-003 naming "from" and "to"

  Scenario: AC7 Agent with no runs (legacy RWB-E2-009 AC7)
    Given the rwb-agent contract mock returns no recommendations for "deviation-screen" "0.9.0" on 2026-12-15
    Given agent "deviation-screen" version "0.9.0" made no recommendations on 2026-12-15
    When JOB-15 runs at 01:30 on 2026-12-16
    Then the system writes no "AGENT_ACCEPTANCE" value for "deviation-screen" on 2026-12-15
    Then SCR-37 shows "No runs" for "deviation-screen" on 2026-12-15

  Scenario: AC8 Filter by product (legacy RWB-E2-009 AC8)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns 140 open Mortgage cases at the 2026-12-15 cut-off
    Given the measures for 2026-12-15 are published and the case list shows 140 open Mortgage cases at the cut-off
    When a product head sends GET /reports/measures?measure=CASES_BY_STAGE&product=MORTGAGE&from=2026-12-15&to=2026-12-15
    Then the response holds only rows with product "MORTGAGE"
    Then their sum is 140

  Scenario: AC9 Rerun of a published day (legacy RWB-E2-009 AC9)
    Given the measures for 2026-12-15 are published
    When JOB-15 is rerun for business date 2026-12-15 from SCR-44
    Then the rows for 2026-12-15 hold the same values
    Then the frozen baseline rows of 2026-11-27 are unchanged
```

The nine criteria are those of RWB-E2-009, copied word for word with the origin tag added to the `Scenario` line: the repeated `Then`, the legacy names "JOB-15", "case list", "data product" and "the INT-19 extract" all stand. Seven carry one added line because the fact behind the `Given` comes from another service: the rwb-source-data freshness of AC1, the rwb-case case list of AC2, AC4 and AC8, the rwb-agent runs of AC3 and AC7, and the rwb-comms notice data product of AC5. Where the legacy text says the decision log entry, this build writes the local decision record of DP-03; where it says the data lake or INT-19, this build hands the extract to rwb-integration and keeps the freshness stamp (GAP-2576; ASM-4245); where it says SCR-37, the screen reaches the service through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The test cases of section 16 are the ten legacy ones.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Steering measures are computed from Workbench records and the decision log, never from a separate count | NFR-065; REQ-WKM-009 |
| BR2 | The dashboard case count equals the case list count at the same cut-off, or the publish is held | REQ-WKM-006; DL25 (tolerance zero) |
| BR3 | Agent acceptance is accepted recommendations over all recommendations, and override is overridden over all, per agent and version | NFR-066; DF-DEC-007, DF-DEC-013 |
| BR4 | A measure is shown with its business date and freshness stamp; stale data shows its date | MSG-P1-001 rule; FEAT-RPT-08 |
| BR5 | Each value is shown beside the frozen baseline of 2026-11-27 | REQ-WKM-009; RWB-E1-013 BR2 |
| BR6 | A rate with no runs in the denominator is not computed | NFR-066 |
| BR7 | Every query applies the role's scope | CTL-09 |
| BR8 | The facts of a measure arrive on events; no measure reads another service's table and none reads an ACE view | DP-01, DP-17 |
| BR9 | The comparison is made against the case facts of the same cut-off read on the P3 contract; an unanswered read is never treated as a match | DP-11; legacy BR2 |
| BR10 | The published day's snapshot rows are the single source of both SCR-37 and the Power BI extract | Legacy guardrail 4; DP-17 |
| BR11 | Measure code, formula, unit, age band, data product and the publish status are data rows with a version, never constants | Principle 1; DP-07 |
| BR12 | The record, the snapshot rows and `measure_publish` commit together or not at all; a failed record write changes nothing and answers MSG-P7-003 | DP-03; legacy AC9 |
| BR13 | The same business date twice writes the same values once and publishes once; the execution id and the business-date key carry the rule | Legacy AC9; DP-10 |

##### 9. State transitions

None of a case: RWB-E2-009 says so and this slice keeps it. The states here are the publish state of a business date and the execution state of the run.

| From (`measure_publish.status`) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not existing | The run completes and the two counts are equal | BR2 holds for the cut-off | PUBLISHED, with the snapshot rows and the extract hand-over |
| Not existing | The run completes and the two counts differ | BR2 fails by any amount | HELD, with both counts and the held reason; no snapshot row |
| HELD | A later run of the same date | The counts now agree | PUBLISHED; the HELD row is replaced and the record is kept |
| PUBLISHED | A rerun of the same date | AC9, X5 | Unchanged values; `published_at` refreshed by the run |

The values of `measure_publish.status` are LOV-MEASURE-PUBLISH (PUBLISHED, HELD) of TSD P9 T3.2; this story writes both and nothing else. The run states are those of the workflow kit: Running, Completed, Failed.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The recovery service identity of rwb-reporting (`rwb_reporting`) | Opens the Schedule run, loads the facts, computes the measures, reconciles, writes the record, the snapshots and `measure_publish`, and hands the extract over; holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema |
| The local decision-record library (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON) | Writes the publish or held record in the caller's transaction and publishes `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03) |
| The reference-data client (RWB-PLT-E1043-CON) | Serves the five lists of the measures from RWB-P3-E1043-CON with their version (DP-07) |
| RW-TRIBE, Tribe lead and squad members | Reads SCR-37 and the measures (Reporting R); approves the steering definitions |
| RW-PRODHEAD, product head | Reads SCR-37 (Reporting R) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads SCR-37 for teams in scope (Reporting R) |
| RW-BIANAL, Reporting and BI analyst | Builds the Power BI report, receives the hold and extract alerts, and reruns a business date from the visibility view (Reporting CRUD) |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Receives the hold alert and reads the reconciliation (Reporting CRU) |
| RW-FINANCE, Finance and CFO delegate | Reads SCR-37 (Reporting R) |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads the steering definitions (Reference data C) |

The rights are the rows of TSD P9 T6.1 and of the legacy authority table, and nothing wider. No person is named: every duty is a role.

Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and of TSD P9 T3.1. The three tables are the parent baseline of RWB-P9-E1013-CON (DF-RPT-031 to DF-RPT-058); this key adds no column and no table, only the steering reconciliation of the publish row and the index of the snapshot by measure, date and product. `decision_record` is a library object created in `rwb_reporting` by the library's own migration (DP-03, DP-15); no other table is added, and no fact table is created for the read model, which lives for the duration of the run (GAP-2576; ASM-4243). No migration of the monolith is reused (GAP-2576; ASM-4247). No personal data is written: identifiers, codes, counts, rates, amounts, dates and a definition version only.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-reporting (P9), base `/api/recovery/reporting/v1` (DP-13). The published shape, the error model and the fakes are RWB-P9-E2009-CON; this story supplies the behaviour.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/reports/measures` | API-P9-001: a list of `Measure` — measure, product, route, period, value, dimension, baselineValue — filtered by `measure`, `product`, `route`, `from` and `to`, with `X-Data-As-Of` | Reporting, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

The ownership row of the service carries this one operation and this story publishes none other. The legacy path `monolith-base/reports/measures` moves to the per-service base and keeps its operation path (DP-13).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Base / contract | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| The case facts of a business date (API-P3-001 as RWB-P3-E1013-APP declares it) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | `GET /cases/facts` with the as-of time and the row count; the open cases at the cut-off give the case-list count of BR2 for AC2, AC4 and AC8; faked |
| The runs of an agent and version for a business date (name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2576; ASM-4244)) | RWB-P10-E1063-CON | P10 rwb-agent | recommendations, accepted, overridden, latency and version for AGENT_ACCEPTANCE and AGENT_OVERRIDE; faked (GAP-2576; ASM-4246) |
| The freshness of the data products of a business date (the read RWB-P1-E1013-APP declares) | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | `GET /data-products/freshness` with the product and its date; reused from the gate of RWB-P9-E1013-APP; faked |
| LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-MEASURE-UNIT, LOV-MEASURE-DIM, LOV-DATA-PRODUCT, LOV-MEASURE-PUBLISH | RWB-P3-E1043-CON | P3 rwb-case | the lists of the measures and of the publish status, with their version; faked |
| The extract hand-over of a published day (name and file shape Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2576; ASM-4245)) | activity on the rwb-integration queue, P2 | P2 rwb-integration | the INT-19 replacement for the 07:30 Power BI refresh; faked |

Every REST row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a single GET retry with jitter and a breaker per downstream (DP-11, ADR-020). The case-facts and freshness reads are the ones the parent slice already calls, and neither sits in this story's C column, which carries the reference-data and agent contracts only: the row is declared from those stories and the same gap is recorded in RWB-P9-E1013-APP (GAP-2576; ASM-4243). The activity row runs on the owner's queue and returns its answer to the workflow.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Trigger | Payload used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DecisionRecorded` (EV-08), the local record of a publish or hold | `rwb.decision-record.v1`, owned by rwb-decision | The publish transaction commits | the record id, the business date, the decision code and the outcome; no measure value |

The ownership rows of the service carry no event of its own, so `rwb.reporting.events.v1` exists with its `.retry` and `.dlt` topics and this story publishes nothing of it. `DecisionRecorded` is written by the local library to this service's outbox on the shared topic (DP-03).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Consumer group | Payload used | When |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CaseCreated` (EV-01), `CaseStateChanged` (EV-05) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.case.v1` | the case id, product group, stage, route, queue and business date; CASES_BY_STAGE and CASES_BY_QUEUE_AGE | replayed for the business date of the run |
| `CaseAllocated` (EV-02) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.case.v1` | the queue and the owner of a case; CASES_BY_QUEUE_AGE | as above |
| `DecisionRecorded` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | `rwb-reporting.decision.v1` | the decision code, the agent version, the final call, the override reason and the time; DECISIONS_LOGGED, AGENT_OVERRIDE | as above |
| `TreatmentApproved` (EV-10) | `rwb.treatment.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.treatment.v1` | the treatment id, case and terms; TREATMENTS | as above |
| `NoticeDispatched` (EV-14), `NoticeDelivered` (EV-15) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.notice.v1` | the notice id, case, type and sent date; LETTERS_SENT | as above |
| `AgentRunCompleted` (EV-28) | `rwb.agent.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.agent.v1` | the run id, agent, case, outcome and fallback; the agent rates, with RWB-P10-E1063-CON as the contract of record | as above |

The consumer groups are declared once by RWB-P9-E2009-CON and registered by RWB-P9-E2009-OPS. The run replays a bounded window — the business date and the look-back the age bands need — rather than consuming continuously, so no read-model table is needed; a repeat is deduplicated on the event id (GAP-2576; ASM-4243).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reportingMeasuresDaily` (JOB-15; name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2576; ASM-4244)) | Workflow, one execution per business date, started by the Schedule | `rwb-reporting`, namespace `rwb-recovery` | input: the business date; the execution id is derived from the date, so a rerun joins the run |
| `checkFreshness` | Activity | `rwb-reporting` | the freshness gate of RWB-P9-E1013-APP for the data products of the day; the stamps out, or MSG-P1-001 |
| `loadReadModel` | Activity | `rwb-reporting` | the events of the day in; the run-scoped fact view out, deduplicated on the event id |

| `computeMeasures` | Activity | `rwb-reporting` | the seven candidate row sets with the definition version in force |
| `reconcileCounts` | Activity | `rwb-reporting` | the dashboard sum and the case-list count of the same cut-off in; the outcome and the two counts out |
| `publishDay` | Activity | `rwb-reporting` | the one transaction: the record, the snapshot rows, `measure_publish` and the extract hand-over |

The names are this story's design choice: the sources name JOB-15 at 01:30 and no source names the workflow or its activities (GAP-2576; ASM-4244).

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Workflow | Queue | Cadence | Overlap and catch-up |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reportingMeasuresDaily` (JOB-15) | `reportingMeasuresDaily` for the previous business date | `rwb-reporting` | 01:30 on each business day, replacing the Quartz row (DP-10) | one execution per business date; a late start catches up the missed dates one by one; a rerun joins the existing execution (values as environment values) |

The bank's Airflow edge runs the ACE ingestion and may trigger the same workflow by its start signal; it calls no schema and no operator edits a row to force a publish. No other Schedule belongs to this story.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.reporting`, module `steering`; front end `src/modules/recovery/reporting/SteeringDashboard.tsx`, the fragment SCR-37 embeds.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>`, recovery schema | Owner's schema `rwb_reporting`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/reporting/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed; reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none; the extract of AC1 is a gap and is handed to rwb-integration |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-17 is the largest change of this key: the legacy INT-19 extract has no lake to land in, so the published rows are the single source of the screen and the Power BI refresh, and the hand-over goes through rwb-integration. The agent facts of DP-04, DP-05 and DP-09 do not apply here: no package is evaluated, no ACE view is read and no domain event is published.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `reportingMeasuresDaily` | Workflow | JOB-15: the run of one business date, its steps, its summary and its rerun |
| `SteeringCalculators` | Service | one calculator per steering measure code, driven by the definition rows |
| `CountReconciliation` | Service | BR2 before publish; writes the outcome into `measure_publish` and the record |
| `MeasureController` | Controller | `GET /reports/measures` with the filters, the scope and `X-Data-As-Of` |
| `MeasureQueryRepository` | Repository | reads the published `measure_snapshot` rows by filter |
| `ExtractHandover` | Client | the P2 activity that hands the published day's extract over |
| `SteeringDashboard` | React component | SCR-37: filters by product, route and date; value beside baseline; agent rates; freshness and hold messages |

**Build steps.** (1) Take the CON delta on the parent baseline and the snapshot index of the key; test the keys and the `baselineValue` field. (2) Build the event fixtures and `loadReadModel`; test the counts of AC1 and AC2. (3) Build `SteeringCalculators` and `loadAgentFacts`; test the values of AC3, the percentage rule of BR3 and the no-run case of AC7. (4) Build `CountReconciliation` and `publishDay`; test AC4, AC9 and the record of BR12. (5) Build `MeasureController` with the date check, the scope and the header; test AC6 and AC8. (6) Build the SCR-37 fragment and the stale and hold messages; test AC5 in the browser. (7) Wire `checkFreshness` and `ExtractHandover`; test X2 and X9. **Done when** the tests of section 16 pass and the Power BI report and SCR-37 show the same values for one SIT day.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P9-002 | The dashboard count differs from the case list | The case count on the dashboard ({count}) does not match the case list ({listCount}) for {date}. The publish is held. |
| MSG-P1-001 | A source is stale | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Dates in the wrong order | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks Reporting R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The local record cannot be written | The decision could not be recorded. Nothing was changed. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The system named is unavailable | {system} is not available. The action is queued and will be retried. |

The first four texts are the legacy texts of RWB-E2-009 section 14, unchanged; the last two are the platform texts the split adds. A message names a measure code, a product, a count and a date, and never a case, an account or a customer value.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-37 Steering dashboard (capability area Reporting) is served through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19):

| State | What the user sees and does |
|---|---|
| Loading | Skeleton rows while `GET /reports/measures` returns |
| Filtered | Values for the chosen product, route and dates, each beside the baseline of 2026-11-27, with the business date; agent rates by agent and version; MSG-P9-002 or MSG-P1-001 when the latest day is held or stale |
| No runs | "No runs" for an agent and version with no recommendation in the day, and no rate |
| Error | MSG-P4-002, MSG-GEN-003 or MSG-GEN-006 with its field names and no partial value |

The screen builds no number of its own: it renders the published rows and their stamps. SCR-44 shows the run summary from the workflow visibility query.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: measures, formulas, units, age bands, the tolerance and the publish status are data rows with a version; the LOV values are reference data of RWB-P3-E1043-CON.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history, events or prompts: measures carry counts, rates, amounts and codes only, and agent outputs are counted, never copied.
- No read of another service's tables and no ACE view: every fact arrives on an event or on its owner's contract (DP-01, DP-17).
- Counts on SCR-37 and in the Power BI extract come from the same `measure_snapshot` rows of a published business date.
- A day is never published on an unanswered case-list count, and an operator never edits `measure_publish` to force a publish.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-009 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As the **Tribe lead (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **the case facts that the steering dashboard counts — every open case with its product group, status, stage, route, queue and entry date, read at the 2026-12-15 cut-off from rwb_case, filterable by product group and reconcilable to the case list the teams work from, with the decision count of the day taken from the decision log and never from a copy**, so that **the steering committee reads the same numbers the teams work with**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The steering committee receives numbers counted by hand that differ from what the teams see in their queues. The dashboard measures are computed in rwb-reporting (P9) from the facts the owning services publish: cases by stage, queue and age, decisions logged, treatments, letters sent and agent acceptance. This story delivers the rwb-case half — the case fact at a cut-off, the case list count it is compared with, and the product filter — on top of the case and queue rows that rwb-case already owns, and it removes the INT-19 extract: there is no data lake, so the facts reach rwb-reporting through the case events the service already publishes (DP-17).

The reconciliation is the control: the sum of the stage facts for a business date must equal the open case count of the case list at the same cut-off, with tolerance zero, or the publish is held by the P9 measure run. The decision count is the number of decision log entries decided that day, read from the decision log and never from a separate count (NFR-065). It serves REQ-WKM-009 and REQ-WKM-006 and the controls BR2, BR3 and BR7.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03), so every case state change this story counts has its decision record on the same topic rwb-reporting projects.
- RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are published: the reference-data contract of rwb-case and its client library (DP-07). The product group, stage and queue values are read as data with the version in force; no Java enum of them exists.
- RWB-PLT-E1044-CON is published: the per-service Flyway sequence and migration conventions in schema `rwb_case` (DP-15).
- RWB-PLT-E1071-CON is published: the Temporal workflow kit in namespace `rwb-recovery` (DP-10). The kit is used by the 01:30 measure run in rwb-reporting, not by this read.
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route behind which SCR-02 Case list and SCR-37 Steering dashboard are served (DP-19). The route detail for SCR-37 is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0731; ASM-1292).
- RWB-P9-E2009-CON is published: the measure, snapshot and publish contract of rwb-reporting, with its fake. It is a contract dependency and does not block the build.
- The case CON story RWB-P3-E1018-CON published the case resource and the six `rwb.case.events.v1` event schemas. This story adds no event type and no payload field; it fixes the fact dimensions that are already on the case events.
- The synthetic day 2026-12-15 exists in `rwb_case`: 240 open cases, 1,412 decision log entries decided that day, 38 treatments and 95 notices sent. The 2026-12-15 cut-off of the case list is 06:52 (FSD P3 v4 A2.18).
- The reader holds a role with Case record R and a scope, or reads only the teams and products in their scope.
- The login is the rwb-case login: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0731; ASM-1291).

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-case: a case is created, allocated, transferred or moved to a new stage on business date 2026-12-15. In one `rwb_case` transaction the service writes the case row, the stage or queue change and the case event to its outbox (DP-01).
2. The case event carries the fact dimensions the dashboard groups by: `caseId`, `caseNo`, `productGroup`, `status`, `stageCode`, `routeCode`, `queueId` and `entryDate`. No personal data travels with it.
3. rwb-reporting (P9): consumes `rwb.case.events.v1` into its case-fact projection, keyed by `caseId`, for the measure run that follows (DP-17). There is no data lake and no INT-19 extract in the target.
4. The 2026-12-15 cut-off for the case list is 06:52. A case that changes after the cut-off belongs to the next day's facts and does not change the facts of 2026-12-15.
5. The data steward or the reconciliation step reads the open case count at the cut-off from `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` with the cut-off date 2026-12-15: 240 open cases with their fact rows.
6. gateway-bff: checks the session and calls rwb-case, one hop and 2 s timeout (DP-11, DP-13). rwb-case calls the rwb-access authorise contract (cached) for Case record R, applies the caller's scope, and returns the rows.
7. The same read with `productGroup=MORTGAGE` returns the 140 Mortgage rows of the day, and the count with them.
8. rwb-reporting: at 01:30 on 2026-12-16 the measure run computes `CASES_BY_STAGE` for 2026-12-15 from its case-fact projection; the sum of the stage rows is 240, equal to the case list count at the 06:52 cut-off.
9. The measure run reads the decision count of the day from the decision log (1,412 entries decided on 2026-12-15) and writes `DECISIONS_LOGGED`; no separate count is kept, and rwb-case holds no copy of the decision rows.
10. Where the two case totals differ (239 against 240), the reconciliation names both counts and the business date. The publish hold, the SCR-37 display and the alert are the P9 slice of this legacy key; the ITG slice proves the wired behaviour end to end.
11. The reader sees the same numbers on SCR-02 Case list (owner rwb-case) and on SCR-37 Steering dashboard (owner rwb-reporting), each with its business date.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A fact-bearing state change commits after the 2026-12-15 cut-off | The facts of 2026-12-15 do not change; the change belongs to the facts of the next business date | None | AC2 |
| X2 | The sum of the stage facts differs from the case list count at the cut-off | Both counts are returned with the business date; the publish hold, the previous day and the alert are raised by the P9 measure run | MSG-P9-002 | AC4 |
| X3 | The read asks for a business date with no open case in scope | The read returns an empty page with count 0 and the list shows the empty state; no zero is written as a measure by rwb-case | None | AC2, AC8 |
| X4 | The caller's scope excludes a product group | Rows outside the scope are absent and the count is the count in scope; nothing outside the scope is returned | None | AC8 |
| X5 | A role without Case record R reads the facts | Refused with 403 by the rwb-access authorise check behind the endpoint | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-009-10 |
| X6 | rwb-access does not answer inside the REST budget | One hop, 2 s timeout (DP-11); the read is refused and is never served unscoped | None | TC-E2-009-10 |
| X7 | A source product of the measure set is stale on 2026-12-15 | The previous day is shown with its date; carried by the P9 slice (AC5) | MSG-P1-001 | AC5 |

AC1 (refresh), AC3 and AC7 (agent rates), AC5 (stale source), AC6 (dates in the wrong order) and AC9 (rerun of a published day) are cited in the flow and this table but are not owned here: AC1, AC5, AC6 and AC9 sit in the P9 slice of this legacy key and AC3 and AC7 in the agent slice. The three criteria in section 7 are the ones this story owns.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the platform contract stories and the P9 CON. The authorise answer and the decision count come from their contract fakes |
| Negotiable | The fact fields are reference-data values with a version; the story fixes the behaviour, not the numbers |
| Valuable | One set of case facts for the committee and the teams, from the service that owns the cases |
| Estimable | One read, one product filter, one count, one index and one contract fake set |
| Small | Fits in one week with its tests |
| Testable | Every owned criterion runs against the synthetic day of 2026-12-15 with known answers; every cross-service answer is stubbed in a contract fake |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Steering dashboard v1 data set

  Background:
    Given definition version "MD-2026.12" is in force with measures "CASES_BY_STAGE", "CASES_BY_QUEUE_AGE", "DECISIONS_LOGGED", "TREATMENTS", "LETTERS_SENT", "AGENT_ACCEPTANCE" and "AGENT_OVERRIDE"
    Given the synthetic day 2026-12-15 holds 240 open cases, 1,412 decision log entries, 38 treatments and 95 notices sent

  Scenario: AC2 Reconciles (legacy RWB-E2-009 AC2)
    Given the case list shows 240 open cases at the 2026-12-15 cut-off
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns 1,412 decision log entries decided on 2026-12-15
    When JOB-15 runs at 01:30 on 2026-12-16
    Then the sum of "CASES_BY_STAGE" for 2026-12-15 is 240
    Then "DECISIONS_LOGGED" for 2026-12-15 is 1,412, the count of decision log entries decided that day

  Scenario: AC4 Counts do not match (legacy RWB-E2-009 AC4)
    Given the case list shows 240 open cases at the 2026-12-15 cut-off
    Given the case facts read for the dashboard total 239
    Given the rwb-reporting contract mock returns no published snapshot for 2026-12-15 and the latest published day 2026-12-14
    When JOB-15 runs at 01:30 on 2026-12-16
    Then no snapshot rows and no extract are published for 2026-12-15
    Then SCR-37 shows 2026-12-14 as the latest day with MSG-P9-002 naming 239, 240 and 2026-12-15
    Then an alert goes to the Reporting and BI analyst and the data steward

  Scenario: AC8 Filter by product (legacy RWB-E2-009 AC8)
    Given the measures for 2026-12-15 are published and the case list shows 140 open Mortgage cases at the cut-off
    Given the rwb-reporting contract mock returns the published measures for 2026-12-15
    When a product head sends GET /reports/measures?measure=CASES_BY_STAGE&product=MORTGAGE&from=2026-12-15&to=2026-12-15
    Then the response holds only rows with product "MORTGAGE"
    Then their sum is 140
```

In this slice AC8 is exercised through the case-fact read `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases?cutOffDate=2026-12-15&productGroup=MORTGAGE`, whose 140 rows are the ones the P9 measure rows for "MORTGAGE" are checked against; the measures endpoint, the Power BI extract and the published measure rows are the P9 slice. In AC4 this slice owns the two counts and their difference; the hold, the SCR-37 message, the extract and the alert are the P9 slice. The measure codes and `JOB-15` are written as the legacy story has them; the transport that carries the facts and the decision count to the 01:30 run is read in ASM-1294.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Steering measures are computed from Workbench records and the decision log, never from a separate count | NFR-065; REQ-WKM-009 |
| BR2 | The dashboard case count equals the case list count at the same cut-off, or the publish is held | REQ-WKM-006; DL25 (tolerance zero) |
| BR3 | Agent acceptance is accepted recommendations over all recommendations, and override is overridden over all, per agent and version | NFR-066; DF-DEC-007, DF-DEC-013 |
| BR4 | A measure is shown with its business date and freshness stamp; stale data shows its date | MSG-P1-001 rule; FEAT-RPT-08 |
| BR5 | Each value is shown beside the frozen baseline of 2026-11-27 | REQ-WKM-009; RWB-E1-013 BR2 |
| BR6 | A rate with no runs in the denominator is not computed | NFR-066 |
| BR7 | Every query applies the role's scope | CTL-09 |
| BR8 | A queue snapshot is published only when the depth of each queue equals the case list count for that queue at the same time; a difference holds the snapshot and names the check | FSD P3 v4 A2.18 AC-ALT-P3-018-02 |

BR3 and BR6 are owned by the agent slice; they are listed because the measure set of this legacy key carries them. BR8 is the queue-measure wording of the same control and is written by the queue-measure story, not by this one.

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It fixes how the case facts of a business date are read at a cut-off and how they reconcile to the case list. The publish status of a business date (published or held) is set by the P9 measure run.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/case/v1`; owner rwb-case (P3).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases` | Case list and case facts at a cut-off: one row per open case with product group, status, stage, route, queue, entry date and closed date, plus the row count; filters `cutOffDate`, `productGroup`, `stage`, `queueId`, `status` | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/queues/{queueId}/cases` | The same case facts for one queue, used for the queue dimension of the dashboard | Queue and allocation R, scope applied | Not applicable |

The case-fact response shape (field names, the ageing band and the dimension codes) and the cut-off rule are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0731; ASM-1290). Until they are agreed, the read reuses the `GET /cases` resource of the case CON story with the filters above and returns the fields already defined for the case resource: `id`, `caseNo`, `productGroup`, `status`, `stageCode`, `routeCode`, `queueId`, `entryDate`, `closedDate`, and `totalCount`. Errors: 401 no session, 403 no Case record R (MSG-P4-002), 422 a date or filter that cannot be read, 503 store down.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | rwb-access (P4) | Role, scope and Case record R check before a read (TC-E2-009-10) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |

The count of decision log entries is not read by rwb-case: it reaches the dashboard through the decision-record topic that rwb-reporting projects, and this story's tests stub it with the rwb-decision contract fake.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` (EV-01) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | caseId | caseId, caseNo, productGroup, status, entryDate, businessDate |
| `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1` (EV-02) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | caseId | caseId, queueId, ownerUserId, stageCode, businessDate |
| `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1` (EV-04) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | caseId | caseId, queueId, fromQueueId, teamCode, businessDate |
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` (EV-05) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | caseId | caseId, status, stageCode, routeCode, queueId, businessDate |

No event type is added and no payload field is renamed: the four types above are the fact carriers of the dashboard, and the story is done only when each one carries the dimensions in the table. Each is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the state change and relayed with the CloudEvents envelope; no personal data is carried.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. This story adds no consumer; the case router of rwb-case is owned by the case stories.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The case fact is a synchronous read at the cut-off; the 01:30 measure run is a Temporal Schedule in rwb-reporting (P9), not in rwb-case.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None in rwb-case. The legacy JOB-15 schedule becomes a Temporal Schedule on task queue `rwb-reporting` in the P9 slice; rwb-case adds no Schedule and no nightly job.

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| recovery_case | P3 (rwb_case) | Read at the cut-off: case number, product group, status, stage, route, queue, entry date, closed date |
| queue | P3 (rwb_case) | Read for `queue_code` and `team_code` |

No table is added and no column changes. The only database change is one read index for the cut-off query (section 13). `queue_measure` is P3's and is written by the queue-measure story of RWB-E1-030, not here. rwb-case reads no table of another service and holds no foreign key across services (DP-01).

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 1 consumed | `GET /cases` and `GET /queues/{queueId}/cases` provided; authorise consumed; one hop, 2 s timeout |
| Kafka | 4 published, 0 consumed | `rwb.case.events.v1`: CaseCreated, CaseAllocated, CaseTransferred, CaseStateChanged carry the fact dimensions |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, activity or Schedule in rwb-case for this story |
| File | None | This story reads and writes no file, and there is no data lake extract |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `casefacts`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.casefacts`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none; gap if the story needs lake data |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-10 applies to the legacy JOB-15 reference only: the schedule becomes a Temporal Schedule in rwb-reporting, and rwb-case adds none. DP-17 applies by removing the INT-19 extract — the case facts leave rwb-case on `rwb.case.events.v1` into rwb-reporting, and this story needs no lake data, so no DP-17 gap is raised. DP-19 applies to the SCR-02 and SCR-37 reads behind the gateway-bff composite route, whose SCR-37 detail is a gap (ASM-1292).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CaseFactQueryService | Service | Builds the open case set of the cut-off from `recovery_case` and `queue`; applies the product, stage, queue and status filters; returns the rows and the count |
| CaseFactRepository | Repository | Reads `recovery_case` and `queue` in schema `rwb_case` only; no join to another schema |
| CaseFactController | Controller | `GET /cases` and `GET /queues/{queueId}/cases` with the filters, the scope and the count |
| FactDimensionCatalog | Service | Reads the product group, stage and queue values and their version through the reference-data contract; no Java enum of them |
| ScopeFilter | Service | Applies the caller's scope from the rwb-access answer to every fact row and to the count |
| AccessCheckClient | Client | Calls the rwb-access authorise contract (cached) before a read |
| CaseFactEventAssembler | Service | Builds the four case events with the fact dimensions on the existing payloads; no new type and no renamed field |

**Database and migrations**

- No table and no column is added. The facts are read from `recovery_case` and `queue`.
- One migration: `V2009_1__case_fact_read_index.sql` adds the index `ix_case_fact_cutoff ON recovery_case (product_group, queue_id, stage_code, closed_date)`, so the cut-off query of 240 cases and the product filter run inside the screen budget.
- The index is created in schema `rwb_case` through the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15).

**Configuration and reference data**

- Product group, stage and queue values are read through the reference-data contract of rwb-case with the version in force (DP-07). The product filter of AC8 uses the `LOV-PRODUCT` value `MORTGAGE` as data, never as a constant.
- The 06:52 cut-off of 2026-12-15 and the 01:30 measure run belong to the measure set in rwb-reporting (P9); rwb-case takes the cut-off as a caller parameter.
- The queue-measure dimensions of `queue_measure` (DF-RPT-020 to DF-RPT-030) are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0731; ASM-1293) and are not written by this story.

**Build steps**

1. CaseFactRepository and CaseFactQueryService over `recovery_case` and `queue`, with the open case set of the cut-off; tests for AC2 at 240 and for the empty set.
2. The product, stage, queue and status filters, with the count returned beside the rows; tests for AC8 at 140 MORTGAGE rows.
3. FactDimensionCatalog over the reference-data contract, so the filter values are data with a version; test the refusal when no version is in force.
4. CaseFactController with the access check, the scope filter and the two paths; test TC-E2-009-10 for the refusal with MSG-P4-002.
5. The `V2009_1` read index and the migration check (DP-15); re-run the cut-off query on the SIT volume.
6. CaseFactEventAssembler over the four existing case events, with a contract test that each carries productGroup, status, stageCode, routeCode, queueId and entryDate and no personal field.
7. Contract-fake run of every cross-service answer (authorise, decision count, published measures) so the story builds before the other services exist.

**Feature switch.** None on the read: a fact row exists when the case row exists, and the endpoint is behind the gateway-bff route and the access check. The legacy switch `rwb.reporting.steering` is the P9 slice's and is not reused here.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the two counts agree at 240 on the synthetic day, the MORTGAGE filter returns 140, the four case events carry the fact dimensions, and the contract tests of RWB-P9-E2009-CON stay green.

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks Case record R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P9-002 | The case fact total differs from the case list count at the cut-off | The case count on the dashboard ({count}) does not match the case list ({listCount}) for {date}. The publish is held. |
| MSG-P1-001 | A source of the measure set is stale | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |

MSG-P9-002 and MSG-P1-001 are raised in the P9 slice; this story returns the counts and the business date that they name.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-02 Case list (module P3, owner rwb-case) carries the case facts this story serves: case number, product, status, stage, queue, entry date and age, with the queue filter.

| State | What the user sees and does |
|---|---|
| Loading | Skeleton rows while `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` returns |
| List | One row per open case at the cut-off, with the count of the filtered list above it |
| Filtered | Rows for the chosen product group, stage, queue and status; the count follows the filter, for example 140 Mortgage cases |
| Empty | The empty state with a zero count; no row is invented |

SCR-37 Steering dashboard is the P9 slice's screen. The gateway-bff composite route serves both screens, one hop each, and merges the answers into the screen model; its SCR-37 detail and the field-level masking of any personal field are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0731; ASM-1292).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the product group, stage, queue and status values are reference data with a version; the cut-off and the measure codes are the measure set's, not this service's.
- No personal data in the case facts, events or logs: the facts carry case number, product group, status, stage, route, queue and dates only. No name, address, contact point or identity number is read, logged or published.
- No read of another service's tables and no ACE view: the facts come from `rwb_case` only, the authorise answer from rwb-access, and the decision count from the decision log's owner. The `rwb_case` schema holds no foreign key into another schema.
- Every case event is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the state change and carries IDs and facts only.
- SCR-02 and SCR-37 show the same facts: nothing is counted by hand and no separate count is kept.
- A fact of a business date is never rewritten after its cut-off; a later change belongs to the next business date.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the steering data set of RWB-E2-009 is realigned onto rwb-deviation (S8, service wave 2, business wave 2), as the secondary serving of the dashboard the split plan gives this service. The seven measure calculators, the count reconciliation, the agent rates and the SCR-37 read keep their legacy values; the facts behind them arrive on the owners' published contracts instead of the six in-process interfaces and the Workbench tables (DP-11), the definitions, the frozen baseline of 2026-11-27 and the publication rules are consumed on RWB-P9-E2009-CON, the read moves onto `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` (DP-13), JOB-15 becomes a Temporal Schedule through the workflow kit (DP-10), the INT-19 extract to Power BI is removed with the data lake (DP-17), and the schema, decision-record, reference-data, Flyway and route rules of the service apply (DP-01, DP-03, DP-07, DP-15, DP-19). The legacy module is P9 Reporting and the plan gives this slice no build row although six DP rows add a platform prerequisite, and the connection matrix carries no S8-to-P9 call and no P9 subscription to S8 (GAP-3087 to GAP-3090; ASM-5270 to ASM-5279). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As the **Tribe lead (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **a data set for the steering dashboard with cases by stage, queue and age, decisions logged, treatments, letters sent and agent acceptance, published each morning and reconciled to the case list**, so that **the steering committee reads the same numbers the teams work with**.

This story owns:

- the **measure answer** of the deviation serving on `/api/recovery/deviation/v1`: the seven measures of definition version "MD-2026.12" for a business-date range, each value beside the frozen baseline of 2026-11-27, with the business date, the definition version, the dimension and the freshness stamp (legacy section 12; DP-13);
- the **seven calculators**, one per measure code, and the **dimension** of each row (`product:`, `route:`, `agent:` and `deviation:`, for example `agent:case-intake:1.2.0`);
- the **deviation column** of the answer: the deviation codes X1 to X7 open on the counted cases at the cut-off, read from `deviation` in `rwb_deviation` (REQ-DVH-006; TSD S8 T3.1 and T3.2);
- the **count reconciliation** before a day is published: the sum of "CASES_BY_STAGE" against the count of the case list at the same cut-off, tolerance zero (legacy BR2; DL25);
- the **morning refresh**: Temporal Schedule `steering-measures` at 01:30 and `SteeringMeasureRefreshWorkflow` on queue `rwb-deviation`, which replaces JOB-15 in this service (DP-10);
- the **two agent rates** per agent and version, and the "No runs" answer for an agent with no recommendations;
- the **provenance record**: one decision-record entry per refresh run and per measure read, holding the definition version, the business date, the two counts and the verdict (DP-03).

It does not own: the canonical measure build, the `measure_definition`, `measure_snapshot` and `measure_publish` tables, the frozen baseline rows and the Power BI read model (RWB-P9-E2009-CON; rwb-reporting, P9); the case, treatment, decision, notice and agent facts (P3, P3, P7, P6 and P10); the deviation write path and its timers (`DeviationWorkflow`, the write stories of this service); the contract surface and its fakes; and the schema, migration, deployment and observability of this service (the DB, INF and OPS stories of this key).

##### 2. Business rationale

The steering committee receives numbers counted by hand that differ from what the teams see in their queues (legacy section 2). The target keeps one measure set and one reconciliation rule, and makes the serving reproducible:

- **The facts are the owners' answers**, one hop each and with a fake on Day 1: the case facts and the case-list count from rwb-case, the decision facts from rwb-decision, the treatment facts from rwb-case, the notice facts from rwb-comms and the agent run facts from rwb-agent (DP-11). No service reads another service's tables and no Workbench copy of a fact is kept (DP-01).
- **The definitions are read, never coded**: the measure codes, formulas, data products, the definition version "MD-2026.12" and the baseline of 2026-11-27 are the reporting owner's rows, consumed on RWB-P9-E2009-CON; the lists the filters use are reference data of rwb-case at their version (DP-07).
- **A published day is a claim that can be checked**: the reconciliation of the dashboard total against the case list runs before the day is published, and a mismatch of one case holds the day (legacy BR2, DL25).
- **The deviation column is why this slice sits in S8**: `deviation` is this service's one table, and the codes open at the cut-off are read here rather than copied from a case column (DP-01, REQ-DVH-006; ASM-5271).
- **The morning run is a durable schedule**, not a Quartz row: the schedule survives a restart, catches up a missed night and can be rerun for one business date with the same values (DP-10).
- **No data lake**: the INT-19 extract and the Power BI data set of the legacy story are removed with the lake, and the reporting read model is built from events by rwb-reporting (DP-17; GAP-3088).

No business value moves into code: measures, formulas, tolerance, age bands, the schedule time and the labels are data.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P9-E2009-CON is published and tagged: the measure definition read, the published measure and baseline read, the publication calendar and the error set are baselined, with their fakes, and handed to this story (DP-11; GAP-3087).
- The five platform contract stories the DP rows add are published: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (decision record), RWB-PLT-E1043-CON (reference data), RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (workflow kit), RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (Flyway) and RWB-PLT-N001-CON (gateway-bff route); the plan's build row is empty and they are declared here as prerequisites (ASM-5272).
- The case, treatment, decision, notice and agent contracts answer with a business date per answer and a freshness answer for the latest business date; their operation names are not published (GAP-3087; ASM-5274).
- `deviation` exists in `rwb_deviation` from the DB story of this service with its columns and the standard record columns of TSD S8 T3.0; this story reads it and adds no table, no column and no migration.
- The service runs as its own login on `rwb_deviation`, holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant, so a statement on `rwb_reporting` or on a `recovery.v_ace_*` view is refused by the database and fails the boundary test (DP-01, DP-02).
- The role of the reader carries Reporting R and a scope; the lists of products, routes and measures are readable at their version (legacy sections 3 and 10; DP-07).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the status of the source documents is taken as an assumption and the story stays in Draft (ASM-5270).

##### 4. Flow

1. Temporal Schedule `steering-measures` fires at 01:30 Asia/Bangkok on task queue `rwb-deviation` and starts `SteeringMeasureRefreshWorkflow` with the business date it closes (DP-10).
2. `ReadMeasureDefinitions` reads the definitions in force on RWB-P9-E2009-CON, including the seven steering measures of "MD-2026.12" and the frozen baseline rows of 2026-11-27 (DP-11).
3. `ReadFacts` reads the case facts, the case-list count at the cut-off, the treatment facts, the decision facts, the notice facts and the agent run facts of the business date, each on its owner's contract and each with its business date and freshness answer (DP-11).
4. `ComputeMeasures` runs one calculator per measure code and fills each row's dimension, value and `baselineValue`; `AgentRates` computes acceptance and override per agent and version, and writes no rate where the denominator is zero (legacy BR3, BR6).
5. `ReconcileCounts` compares the sum of "CASES_BY_STAGE" with the case-list count at the same cut-off; equal, the day is published; different, the day is held and `RaiseHoldAlert` sends MSG-P9-002 to the Reporting and BI analyst and the data steward (legacy BR2, DL25; DP-11).
6. `ReadDeviationColumn` reads the `deviation` rows open at the cut-off for the counted cases: code, raised-at, paused state and handler; a case with two codes shows both (TSD S8 T3.1; REQ-DVH-006).
7. `RecordProvenance` appends one decision-record entry through the local library with the definition version, the business date, the two counts and the verdict (DP-03).
8. A reader opens SCR-37 through the gateway-bff composite route; the screen calls `GET /reports/measures` with measure, product, route and date filters; the answer carries the published values with their business date and freshness stamp, the baseline beside each value and the header `X-Data-As-Of` (DP-19).
9. The screen shows the deviation codes of each counted row; an agent with no runs shows "No runs"; the latest published day is 2026-12-14 while 2026-12-15 is held (legacy AC4, AC7).
10. Nothing else is written: the story moves no case status, starts no workflow of another service and writes no measure table (DP-01).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The dashboard case count differs from the case-list count at the cut-off | The day is held; the previous day stays the latest published; the alert is sent | MSG-P9-002 | AC4 |
| X2 | A source answer behind a measure is stale for the business date | The value of the stale product shows with its own date | MSG-P1-001 | AC5 |
| X3 | A query with from after to | Refused before any read | MSG-GEN-003 | AC6 |
| X4 | An agent has no runs on the day | No rate is computed; "No runs" shows | None | AC7 |
| X5 | A refresh is rerun for a business date already published | The same values are answered and a second provenance entry is written; the baseline rows of 2026-11-27 are unchanged | None | AC9 |
| X6 | The role lacks Reporting R | 403 before any fact is read | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-009-10 |
| X7 | The reporting contract or the service's own schema does not answer | 503 with the platform envelope; nothing partial shows | MSG-GEN-006 | AC1, BR8 |

X1 to X5 are the paths of RWB-E2-009; X6 and X7 are the target's access and availability paths.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against RWB-P9-E2009-CON and six fakes (case, treatment, decision, notice, agent, notification), on its own schema, and needs no live P3, P6, P7, P9 or P10 |
| Negotiable | The calculator shape, the workflow activities and the dimension format are this story's choice; the measure codes, the values, the tolerance and the messages are fixed |
| Valuable | One set of numbers for the committee and the teams, with the deviation codes of the counted cases beside them |
| Estimable | Seven calculators, one reconciliation, one workflow with five activities, one schedule, one endpoint and one screen |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on the synthetic day of 2026-12-15 through the fakes, plus the access refusal and the boundary test |

```gherkin
    Then the system writes no "AGENT_ACCEPTANCE" value for "deviation-screen" on 2026-12-15
    Then SCR-37 shows "No runs" for "deviation-screen" on 2026-12-15

  Scenario: AC8 Filter by product (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the measures for 2026-12-15 are published and the case list shows 140 open Mortgage cases at the cut-off
    When a product head sends GET /reports/measures?measure=CASES_BY_STAGE&product=MORTGAGE&from=2026-12-15&to=2026-12-15
    Then the response holds only rows with product "MORTGAGE"
    Then their sum is 140

  Scenario: AC9 Rerun of a published day (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the measures for 2026-12-15 are published
    When the refresh is rerun for business date 2026-12-15 with that business date as its input
    Then the rows for 2026-12-15 hold the same values
    Then the frozen baseline rows of 2026-11-27 are unchanged
    Then a second provenance entry for the run is recorded with the same counts and verdict
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Steering measures are computed from the owners' published facts and the decision record, never from a separate count | NFR-065; REQ-WKM-009 |
| BR2 | The dashboard case count equals the case-list count at the same cut-off, or the day is held; the tolerance is zero | REQ-WKM-006; DL25 |
| BR3 | Agent acceptance is accepted recommendations over all recommendations, and override is overridden over all, per agent and version | NFR-066; DF-DEC-007, DF-DEC-013 |
| BR4 | A measure is shown with its business date and freshness stamp; stale data shows its own date | MSG-P1-001 rule; FEAT-RPT-08 |
| BR5 | Each value is shown beside the frozen baseline of 2026-11-27, read on the reporting contract and never copied or updated here | REQ-WKM-009; baseline of 2026-11-27 |
| BR6 | A rate with no runs in the denominator is not computed, and the screen shows "No runs" | NFR-066 |
| BR7 | Every query applies the role's scope and the Reporting right | CTL-09 |
| BR8 | A day is answered only when every measure of the definition version in force has a value with a business date; a missing or failed source holds the day and answers 503 rather than a partial set | Legacy section 5; AC1, X7 |
| BR9 | The deviation column names the codes X1 to X7 open on the counted cases at the cut-off, read from `deviation` in `rwb_deviation`; a code is never copied into a measure row or taken from a case column | REQ-DVH-006; TSD S8 T3.1 and T3.2; DP-01 |
| BR10 | No data lake: no INT-19 extract is written and no file is delivered; the answer serves SCR-37 and the Power BI read model is built by rwb-reporting from events | DP-17; GAP-3088 |
| BR11 | One provenance entry per refresh run and per measure read, holding the definition version, the business date, the two counts and the verdict, and no measure value and no personal data | DP-03; legacy section 11 |

##### 9. State transitions

The story changes no case status and no deviation state (legacy section 9). It sets the publish status of a business date, which is derived from the reconciliation of that date, and it records the run of the refresh.

| From | Event | To | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| No status for the date | The refresh runs and the counts are equal | Published for the business date | The answer is returned for that date and the provenance entry names published |
| No status for the date | The refresh runs and the counts differ by any amount | Held for the business date | No answer for that date, the previous day stays the latest, MSG-P9-002 and the alert |
| Published for the business date | The refresh is rerun for the same date with the same inputs | Published for the business date | The same values, a second provenance entry, the baseline rows unchanged |
| Held for the business date | A later run whose counts match | Published for the business date | The first run whose counts match publishes the day (legacy section 12) |
