The product groups, routes and measure codes the filters offer are reference data of rwb-case read at their version (DP-07; ASM-5278). Age bands and the tolerance of zero are data, not constants (legacy sections 2 and 13).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-deviation (S8); base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` (DP-13). The legacy path `GET monolith-base/reports/measures` is kept with the base moved; the operation is a read and writes only the provenance entry (DP-03).

| Method | Path | Shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/reports/measures` | `Measure[]`: measure, product, route, period, value, dimension (code and value, for example `agent:case-intake:1.2.0` or `deviation:X3`), baselineValue, definitionVersion and the deviation codes open on the counted cases; query measure, product, route, from, to; header `X-Data-As-Of` carries the business date of the latest published day | Reporting R, scope applied | Not applicable; a read, safe to repeat |

Errors: 401 with MSG-P4-001, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 422 with MSG-GEN-003 when from is after to, 503 with MSG-GEN-006 when the reporting contract or the service's schema does not answer. The `dimension` and `baselineValue` fields are the two additions the legacy story records as missing from the Measure schema in `api.yaml` (ASM-5277).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| The measure definition and published measure read, with the baseline rows of 2026-11-27; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3087; ASM-5274) | P9 rwb-reporting, on RWB-P9-E2009-CON | The seven measures in force, the definition version, the published values of a day and the frozen baseline |
| The case fact and case-list count read; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3087; ASM-5274) | P3 rwb-case | The case facts behind "CASES_BY_STAGE" and "CASES_BY_QUEUE_AGE", and the count at the cut-off for BR2 |
| The treatment fact read; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3087; ASM-5274) | P3 rwb-case | The treatment facts behind "TREATMENTS" |
| The decision fact read on the decision-record surface; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3087; ASM-5274) | P7 rwb-decision | The entries behind "DECISIONS_LOGGED" and the two agent rates, with their agent version and override reason |
| The notice fact read; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3087; ASM-5274) | P6 rwb-comms | The notice facts behind "LETTERS_SENT", with the product of the answer and its freshness |
| The agent run fact read; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3087; ASM-5274) | P10 rwb-agent | The recommendations, acceptances and overrides per agent and version |
| The notification send; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3087; ASM-5279) | P6 rwb-comms | The hold alert of MSG-P9-002 to the Reporting and BI analyst and the data steward |

Every call is one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker, and none retries inside a measure. The reporting contract is the one C row of this slice; the other six reads are consumed contracts with fakes and no C row (GAP-3087; ASM-5274).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. A refresh and a read publish no business event: the provenance entry is written locally through the library of DP-03 and relayed on the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and this service's own topic `rwb.deviation.events.v1` carries the two deviation events of its write stories (DP-14 applied as naming only; ASM-5273).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. Every measure is computed from the owners' read answers at refresh time and answered with the business date of each answer, so a stale source is shown with its own date and MSG-P1-001 rather than kept fresh by a subscription (BR4).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Item | Queue | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `SteeringMeasureRefreshWorkflow` | `rwb-deviation` | One run per business date: read the definitions, read the facts, compute the measures and the rates, reconcile the counts, read the deviation column, record the provenance |
| `ReadMeasureDefinitions` activity | `rwb-deviation` | The definitions in force and the baseline rows on RWB-P9-E2009-CON |
| `ReadFacts` activity | `rwb-deviation` | The six fact reads on their owners' contracts, each with its business date and freshness answer |
| `ComputeMeasures` activity | `rwb-deviation` | One calculator per measure code, the dimension and the two agent rates |
| `ReconcileCounts` activity | `rwb-deviation` | BR2 at tolerance zero; returns published or held with the two counts |
| `RecordProvenance` activity | `rwb-deviation` | One decision-record entry per run (DP-03) |

The workflow has no timer and no signal; it ends when the day is published or held, and its history stays far below the Continue-As-New threshold because each run is one business date.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Queue | When | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| `steering-measures` | `rwb-deviation` | Daily at 01:30 Asia/Bangkok, business date = the day it closes | Replaces JOB-15 in this service (DP-10); catches up one missed night, refuses a duplicate run for a date already published unless it is rerun with that business date as its input, and takes the business date as an input for a rerun (legacy AC9) |

`measure_definition`, `measure_snapshot`, `measure_publish`, `recovery_case`, `queue`, `treatment`, `notice`, `decision_log_entry` and every `v_ace_*` view are other owners' and are named only; this story adds no table and no column, and no foreign key leaves `rwb_deviation` (DP-01, DP-15).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The measure answer on the target base, the seven calculators, `AgentRates`, `CountReconciliation`, `DeviationColumnReader`, `ProvenanceWriter`, `SteeringMeasureRefreshWorkflow` with its five activities and the `steering-measures` Schedule, and the SCR-37 components with their held, stale and "No runs" states.

**Pattern application** (§R5.5)

| DP | Legacy marker | Pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>`, "recovery schema" | Own schema `rwb_deviation`; `measure_snapshot` and `measure_publish` are read on the reporting contract, never as tables | None |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the decision facts are consumed on the decision-record surface | H `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` (not in the empty build row, ASM-5272) |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case for the product, route and measure lists of the filters | H `RWB-PLT-E1043-CON`; C `RWB-P3-E1043-CON` |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule `steering-measures` and `SteeringMeasureRefreshWorkflow` through the workflow kit | H `RWB-PLT-E1071-CON` |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | One REST read per owner fact with a fake, one hop, 2 s, no retry inside a measure | C from the legacy dependency (`RWB-P9-E2009-CON`) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` | None |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway in `rwb_deviation`; this story adds no table and no column | H `RWB-PLT-E1044-CON` |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed: no lake and no extract; the freshness stamp serves SCR-37 and the Power BI read model belongs to rwb-reporting | None (the lake need is a gap, GAP-3088) |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route for SCR-37 | H `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` |

**Build steps.** (1) Read the definitions and the baseline on RWB-P9-E2009-CON and the six fact families on their owners' contracts, with their business dates and freshness answers. (2) Build the seven calculators and the two agent rates against the fakes with the synthetic day; prove AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC7. (3) Build `CountReconciliation` and the held answer; prove AC4 and AC9. (4) Build the endpoint with the filters, the date check, the scope and `X-Data-As-Of`; prove AC6 and AC8. (5) Add the deviation column from `deviation`; prove AC2's last step and the boundary test. (6) Add the schedule and the workflow, the provenance writer and the alert; prove AC5 and AC4's alert. (7) Build the SCR-37 components with the held, stale, "No runs" and error states.

**Done when.** AC1 to AC9 pass at component and contract level on the fakes, the boundary test shows no statement on `rwb_reporting`, `rwb_case` or a `v_ace_*` view, a held day answers no value with MSG-P9-002, and one SIT day answers the same values from the refresh and from a rerun.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P9-002 | The dashboard count differs from the case list (X1) | The case count on the dashboard ({count}) does not match the case list ({listCount}) for {date}. The publish is held. |
| MSG-P1-001 | A source is stale (X2) | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Dates in the wrong order (X3) | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks Reporting R (X6) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The reporting contract or the schema does not answer (X7) | {service} is not available now. Try again in a few minutes. |

The wording is the legacy wording, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and none is added. The legacy MSG-P4-001 and MSG-GEN-003 rows stay with the platform error envelope.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the seven measures, their formulas, the tolerance, the age bands, the schedule time and the labels are data rows read at their version (DP-07).
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs, the provenance entry, logs or prompts; measures carry counts, rates, amounts and codes only, and agent outputs are counted, never copied.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: no `v_ace_*` view, no ACE table and no other service's schema is read, and a statement that tries is refused by the grant and fails the boundary test (DP-01, DP-02).
- No measure table, no report copy and no extract file in this service: the answer is computed from the owners' answers and the one table it reads is its own `deviation` (DP-01, DP-17).
- The reconciliation runs before any value is answered, and a held day answers nothing (BR2, BR8).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; this story adds no second base and no new topic (DP-13, DP-14).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the deployment slice of RWB-E2-009 for rwb-reporting — the api and worker deployments of the steering build, its login and secrets, the migration and the record table, the Schedule registration on queue `rwb-reporting`, the consumer groups of the eight subscriptions, the extract hand-over, the alerts, the run view, the flag, the backfill and the rollback — is split from the contract baseline (RWB-P9-E2009-CON) and from the application work (RWB-P9-E2009-APP). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As the **DevOps team of the recovery platform**, I want **the rwb-reporting steering build deployed as one api and one worker behind the recovery edge, on its own login and schema, with its Schedule registered, its eight consumer groups provisioned, an alert for every failure path carrying a message ID and an owned runbook entry, and a rollback that drains a running workflow — so that** the steering data set is published every business morning and an operator can tell a late source from a held day without reading a log.

The release carries, and nothing else:

- two deployments of one image — `api` serving `GET /reports/measures` on `/api/recovery/reporting/v1` through the gateway-bff, and `worker` polling the task queue `rwb-reporting` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (DP-13, DP-19);
- the login `rwb_reporting` on schema `rwb_reporting`, its connection pool and its secret references, and no grant on another schema, on `recovery` or on a `v_ace_*` view (DP-01, DP-02, DP-17);
- the migration increment of the key — the unique key on the business date, the two indexes and the library record table in `rwb_reporting` — gated by lint and drift (DP-15);
- the Schedule `reportingMeasuresDaily` (JOB-15) at 01:30 registered with the build ID of the release, and its workflow with the six activities (DP-10);
- the eight consumer groups of the subscriptions declared by RWB-P9-E2009-CON, and no topic of this service's own (DP-17);
- the extract hand-over to rwb-integration on its queue, with the freshness stamp of the published day;
- the six alerts, the four dashboard series, the run view of JOB-15 and the six runbook entries that go with them;
- the flag `rwb.reporting.steering`, the backfill of a business date and the rollback of a build.

The behaviour of the measures is RWB-P9-E2009-APP and the shapes are RWB-P9-E2009-CON; this story ships neither. Where a deployment value has no source, it is a value of the environment and the default stands as an assumption (GAP-2578; ASM-4249).

##### 2. Business rationale

A service that no one operates is not delivered. The legacy story assumed a Quartz job inside one deployed monolith, a shared recovery login, a shared job monitor and a data-lake load area; under D-RCV-60 the run is a Scheduled workflow on its own queue under its own login, its facts arrive on eight subscriptions, its extract leaves through rwb-integration, and its publish can be held by design. Each of those is a deployment object that has to exist before the first business morning, and each has a failure mode an operator must recognise: a source that never arrives, a worker that is not polling, a Schedule that did not fire, a contract that does not answer, a record that cannot be written, and a handed-over extract that never landed.

- **the morning is the deadline.** The 07:30 Power BI refresh follows the 01:30 run, so a stale source or an unstarted worker is a business problem by 07:00, not an infrastructure one.
- **a held day is a successful run.** The most common non-zero outcome is a day held on a count mismatch; the run view and the alert tell that apart from a failed run.
- **a rerun is safe.** The run is idempotent per business date, so the fix for most mornings is a backfill of one date and not a repair script.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P9-E2009-CON is tagged `v1` and the image of RWB-P9-E2009-APP is built and pushed under the release build ID.
- RWB-P9-E1013-APP is deployed: `measure_definition` and `measure_snapshot` exist and the baseline of 2026-11-27 is frozen.
- The platform objects exist: the gateway-bff route for `/api/recovery/reporting/*`, the secret store, the Temporal namespace `rwb-recovery`, the OpenTelemetry collector and the workload identity of the namespace (DP-19).
- The login `rwb_reporting` is allocated with its secret reference; the schema `rwb_reporting` exists; the connection pool size, the replica counts and the resource requests are values of the environment and stand as assumptions (GAP-2578; ASM-4249).
- The producers of the eight subscriptions — rwb-case, rwb-decision, rwb-treatment, rwb-comms and rwb-agent — publish their topics, and rwb-integration accepts the extract hand-over on its queue.
- The six message IDs of section 14 are registered in the platform message catalogue; no business text is written by this story.
- Status is Draft (realignment v1): no approval and no production change are required to prepare the release, and the first environment is non-production (GAP-2578; ASM-4250).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds one image and two deployments from it, with the release build ID of the commit and the image digest pinned; no `latest` tag is deployed.
2. The migration job runs the Flyway sequence of `rwb_reporting` before the worker starts, and the drift gate compares the applied state with the baseline of RWB-P9-E2009-CON; a drift fails the release.
3. The api deployment starts behind the gateway-bff route, with its readiness probe on the health endpoint, and declares no route of its own.
4. The worker deployment starts and registers the workflow `reportingMeasuresDaily` and its six activities on the task queue `rwb-reporting`, with worker versioning on the build ID.
5. The Schedule `reportingMeasuresDaily` is created at 01:30 with overlap skipped and catch-up enabled; the Schedule carries the build ID of the release, so a rollback re-registers it against the previous build.
6. The eight consumer groups of section 12.4 are registered on the producers' topics before the first business date; the offsets start at the run window of the first business date and not at the end of the log.
7. The flag `rwb.reporting.steering` is read at the start of the run: off means the execution ends with the run alert, the business date is held and nothing is written.
8. `checkFreshness` reads the data-product freshness of the day on the read RWB-P1-E1013-APP declares; a stale product leaves the run to write its measure from the last complete day with that date as the freshness stamp and to raise MSG-P1-001.
9. `publishDay` commits the record, the snapshot rows and `measure_publish` in one transaction, and `handOverExtract` passes the published day's extract to rwb-integration on its queue.
10. The run writes its summary to the visibility view; the four dashboard series and the run view of JOB-15 read them, and a held day shows both counts and the held reason.
11. A failed run raises its alert with a message ID and a runbook link; the operator fixes the cause — a source, a flag, a contract, the record store — or backfills the business date, which replays the same execution and writes nothing twice.
12. A rollback redeploys the previous chart and build ID; a running execution finishes on the build that started it, the Schedule is re-registered against the previous build, and a new business date starts there until the fix ships again.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A source of the day is late or not ready | The measure of that source carries the last complete day's date, and the screen shows the stale marker | MSG-P1-001 | AC5, AC6, BR6 |
| X2 | The worker is not polling, or the Schedule did not fire | The business date has no execution by the run window; the alert names the Schedule and the date | None (run alert; runbook entry 1) | AC3, AC5 |
| X3 | The case-facts contract does not answer inside 2 s or its breaker is open | The activity retries on the workflow policy; the day stays unpublished rather than published unverified | None | AC5, AC6, BR8 |
| X4 | The record chain is stopped or its store is unavailable | The transaction writes nothing; the incident is raised and the date is backfilled once the store is back | MSG-P7-003 | AC5, AC6 |
| X5 | The dashboard count differs from the case list | The run succeeds as a held day, both counts are named, and the previous day stays the latest published | MSG-P9-002 | AC5, BR7 |
| X6 | The extract hand-over to rwb-integration fails or is not accepted | The published rows stand, the hand-over is retried from the run, and the reporting analyst is alerted | MSG-GEN-006 | AC4, AC5 |
| X7 | The flag is off in an environment that has the run | The date is held, nothing is written, and the run view says the flag is off | None (run alert) | AC6 |
| X8 | The migration leaves the schema not matching the baseline | The drift gate fails the release and the worker is not started | None (pipeline log) | AC2 |
| X9 | A consumer group is missing or its offset policy is wrong at the first business date | The run sees no events of that producer, the counts differ, and the day is held rather than published | MSG-P9-002 | AC4, BR4 |

X1 to X5 are the failure paths of the legacy key restated as deployment objects; X6 is the hand-over, X7 the flag's, X8 the migration gate's and X9 the subscription's. None of them changes a business value: the measure codes, formulas, age bands and the zero tolerance of DL25 are rows of their owners, and the thresholds of the alerts are values of the environment.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 from the tagged contract baseline and the image; needs no running neighbour beyond the platform objects and the producers' topics |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, thresholds, series windows, catch-up window, partition counts and retention are values of the environment and are tuned per environment |
| Valuable | The steering data set is delivered every business morning, a held day is visible, and every failure is named by a message ID with an owned runbook entry |
| Estimable | Two deployments, one migration job, one Schedule, eight consumer groups, six alerts, four series and six runbook entries |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with the platform team |
| Testable | Each criterion is a deployment check, a registration check or an alert check at Level NFR or End to end |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: The deployment of the rwb-reporting steering dashboard build

  Background:
    Given the contract baseline of the service is tagged "v1" and the image of the release is built under its build ID
    Given the namespace "rwb-recovery", the task queue "rwb-reporting", the schema "rwb_reporting" and the login "rwb_reporting"

  Scenario: AC1 The api and the worker are deployed on their own login and route (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the release chart of the service
    When it is applied to the environment
    Then one api deployment serves "/api/recovery/reporting/v1" through the gateway-bff route and one worker deployment polls the queue "rwb-reporting"
    Then both run under the login "rwb_reporting" with secret references and no secret value in the chart
    Then the api readiness probe passes and neither another schema nor a "v_ace_*" view is reachable from the pod
    Then the build ID and the image digest of the release are recorded

  Scenario: AC2 The migration and the record table are applied and the drift gate is green (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the migration job of the service
    When it runs before the worker starts
    Then "measure_publish" and the library record table exist in "rwb_reporting" with the key and the indexes of the baseline
    Then the snapshot index of the baseline is present on "measure_snapshot"
    Then the drift gate compares the applied state with the baseline and passes
    Then a second run of the migration changes nothing

  Scenario: AC3 The Schedule is registered and fires at the declared time (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the worker of the release
    When it starts
    Then "reportingMeasuresDaily" and its six activities are registered on the queue "rwb-reporting" in namespace "rwb-recovery"
    Then the Schedule "reportingMeasuresDaily" exists at 01:30 with overlap skipped and catch-up enabled
    Then the Schedule and the worker versioning policy name the build ID of the release
    Then one execution is opened per business date and a rerun joins the existing execution

  Scenario: AC4 The eight consumer groups are registered and the hand-over is reachable (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the producers of the eight subscriptions of the baseline
    When the release is applied
    Then the consumer groups of EV-01, EV-02, EV-05, EV-08, EV-10, EV-14, EV-15 and EV-28 exist on their topics with their offset policy
    Then this release creates no topic of the service's own and publishes no domain event
    Then the extract hand-over activity answers rwb-integration on the queue "rwb-integration" and reports an accepted delivery

  Scenario: AC5 Every alert carries its message ID or its runbook entry, and one owned entry per path (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the six alerts of the release
    When each failure path of section 5 is simulated in a non-production environment
    Then the alert fires with its message ID where a business message exists, and with its service and its business date
    Then the alert links one runbook entry with an owner role
    Then the four dashboard series and the run view of JOB-15 show the run, its summary and a held day

  Scenario: AC6 The flag governs the run and the backfill is idempotent (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the flag "rwb.reporting.steering" is off
    When the Schedule fires for a business date
    Then the date is held and no snapshot row and no publish row are written
    When the flag is on and the same date is backfilled after a failed run
    Then the execution replays and writes the same values once
    Then the backfill limit per run is a value of the environment

  Scenario: AC7 A rollback drains the build without losing a run (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a running execution on the current build
    When the previous chart and build ID are redeployed
    Then the running execution finishes on the build that started it
    Then the Schedule is re-registered against the previous build
    Then a new business date starts on the previous build
    Then the alerts and the run view keep reading both builds
```

The seven criteria test the deployment only. No measure value, count or rate of the legacy story is fixed by them; the only dates they name are the business date of the run and the values of the environment (ASM-4249).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One image, two deployments, one login and one queue per service; no deployment reaches another schema | DP-01, DP-02, R4 |
| BR2 | The migration runs before the worker and a drift fails the release | DP-15 |
| BR3 | The Schedule is registered on `rwb-reporting` and a rerun joins the execution of its business date | DP-10 |
| BR4 | The eight consumer groups exist before the first business date; this release creates no topic of its own | DP-17; legacy RWB-E2-009 section 12 |
| BR5 | Every alert names its business message ID where one exists and always one owned runbook entry; no alert without a runbook entry is released | R7.2 s14 |
| BR6 | A source that is not ready is shown with its own date and never counted as today's value | Legacy BR4; MSG-P1-001 |
| BR7 | A day whose counts differ is held and never published; the run itself is a success | Legacy BR2; DL25 |
| BR8 | A consumed contract is called with one hop and a 2 s timeout, and a breaker per downstream protects the run | DP-11; ADR-020 |
| BR9 | A backfill is safe to repeat and writes nothing twice; the key is the business date | Legacy AC9; DP-10 |
| BR10 | A rollback drains in-flight runs and re-registers the Schedule; a new date starts on the rollback build | R8.2; AC7 |

##### 9. State transitions

None of business data: this story changes no record, no case state and no publish state. The states it owns are the deployment and the run.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | The chart is applied and the migration passes | The drift gate is green | Deployed, the worker registered and the Schedule created |
| Deployed | The flag is off | X7 | Deployed, the date held |
| Deployed | The Schedule fires for a new date | The flag is on | Running, then Completed with its summary |
| Running | The counts differ | X5 | Completed as a held day, with its alert |
| Running | A failure path fires | X1 to X4, X6 | Failed with its alert; the date is backfillable |
| Deployed | A rollback is applied | AC7 | The previous build serves new dates; the running execution finishes |

| The observability owner (RWB-PLT-OBS) | Owns the collector, the dashboard template and the alert routing; the thresholds are values of the environment |

| The service owner of rwb-reporting | Approves the runbook entries and the on-call rota |

No person is named in this story: every duty is a role, and every alert routes to a role.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None new. The one operation of the service — `GET /reports/measures` on `/api/recovery/reporting/v1` — is deployed by this story as it is tagged in RWB-P9-E2009-CON, behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). This story changes no path, no parameter, no header and no error, and publishes no health or admin route of its own beyond the platform probe.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Base / contract | Owner | Deployment note |
|---|---|---|---|
| The case facts of a business date | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | the client is configured with a 2 s timeout, one GET retry with jitter and a breaker |
| The agent runs of a business date | RWB-P10-E1063-CON | P10 rwb-agent | same policy; read once per run |
| The lists of the measures | RWB-P3-E1043-CON | P3 rwb-case | read once per run and cached for the run, with the version |
| The freshness of the data products of a business date | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | same policy; read once per run before the facts |
| The extract hand-over | activity on the queue `rwb-integration` | P2 rwb-integration | the activity reports an accepted delivery; a refusal is retried by the run |

The operation and activity names are those of the baseline and carry the placeholder where no published document fixes them (GAP-2578; ASM-4249).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The ownership row of the service carries no event and this release creates no topic of its own; `rwb.reporting.events.v1`, its `.retry` and its `.dlt` are left unprovisioned for this key and the chart creates nothing on them. The library's `DecisionRecorded` (EV-08) is written to `rwb.decision-record.v1`, whose topic belongs to rwb-decision and is not created here.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Consumer group | Provisioning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CaseCreated` (EV-01), `CaseAllocated` (EV-02), `CaseStateChanged` (EV-05) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.case.v1` | registered before the first business date; offsets start at the first run window |
| `DecisionRecorded` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | `rwb-reporting.decision.v1` | as above; the topic belongs to rwb-decision |
| `TreatmentApproved` (EV-10) | `rwb.treatment.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.treatment.v1` | as above |
| `NoticeDispatched` (EV-14), `NoticeDelivered` (EV-15) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.notice.v1` | as above |
| `AgentRunCompleted` (EV-28) | `rwb.agent.events.v1` | `rwb-reporting.agent.v1` | as above |

The offset policy, the retention of the consumers' positions and the catch-up window are values of the environment (ASM-4249). A missing group is a held day and an alert (X9), never a silent empty measure.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Registration |
|---|---|---|
| `reportingMeasuresDaily` (JOB-15) | Workflow | registered on queue `rwb-reporting`; the build ID pins the worker version; the execution id derives from the business date |
| `checkFreshness`, `loadReadModel`, `loadAgentFacts`, `computeMeasures`, `reconcileCounts`, `publishDay` | Activities | registered with the workflow; the hand-over of `publishDay` runs on the rwb-integration queue |
| The Schedule `reportingMeasuresDaily` | Schedule | 01:30 daily, overlap skipped, catch-up enabled; re-registered by a rollback |

The registration check asserts the queue, the workflow type, the input schema, the Schedule and its cadence. The build ID and the versioning policy are values of the release and are recorded with it (GAP-2578; ASM-4250).

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Cadence | Overlap | Catch-up |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reportingMeasuresDaily` (JOB-15) | 01:30 on each business day, replacing the Quartz row | skipped: one execution per business date | a missed date catches up one by one, up to the window of the environment |

The time zone, the catch-up window and the backfill limit per run are values of the environment (ASM-4249). No other Schedule, cron, overlap policy or catch-up window is created for this service.

| `measure_publish` | P9 (`rwb_reporting`) | created by the parent's migration; this job adds the unique key on `business_date` and the index on `status` |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Chart.** `deploy/rwb-reporting/`: one image, two deployments (`api`, `worker`), the migration job, the route fragment, the Schedule, the alert rules, the dashboard, the runbook links and the values files per environment.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `api` deployment | Deployment | serves the one operation behind the gateway-bff, with its readiness and liveness probes |
| `worker` deployment | Deployment | polls `rwb-reporting`, registers the workflow and its activities, runs the eight consumer groups |
| `migrate` job | Job | runs the Flyway sequence and the library migration before the worker; the drift gate reads its result |
| `schedule` manifest | Manifest | the Schedule `reportingMeasuresDaily` with its cadence, overlap and catch-up values |
| `alerts` rules | Rules | six alerts, each with a message ID, a label set and a runbook link |
| `dashboard` | Chart | four series: runs by outcome, days held, measures written, hand-over failures |
| `runbook` | Document | six entries: Schedule not fired or worker not polling; stale source; count mismatch; record chain stopped; hand-over refused; consumer group missing |

| Runbook entry | Trigger | First step | Owner role |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | No execution by the run window | check the Schedule registration and the worker | DevOps team |
| 2 | MSG-P1-001 on the screen or the run | check the data-product freshness and its business date; do not force the run | DevOps team with the data owner |
| 3 | MSG-P9-002 and a held day | confirm both counts on the run view and refer the difference to the data steward; do not edit the row | RW-DATASTEW with the DevOps team |
| 4 | MSG-P7-003 and a stopped chain | check the record store, then backfill the date | DevOps team with the platform record owner |
| 5 | A refused hand-over | check rwb-integration and the freshness stamp, then replay the hand-over from the run | DevOps team with the integration owner |
| 6 | A held day on an empty measure | check the consumer group and its offsets, then backfill the date | DevOps team with the event platform owner |

**Build steps.** (1) Write the chart, the probes and the migration job; test AC1 and AC2. (2) Register the workflow, the Schedule and the versioning policy; test AC3. (3) Register the eight consumer groups and the hand-over; test AC4. (4) Write the six alerts, the four series and the six runbook entries; test AC5. (5) Wire the flag, the backfill and the rollback; test AC6 and AC7.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Alert and text |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P9-002 | The dashboard count differs from the case list | the held-day alert carries both counts and the date; the screen shows the same text |
| MSG-P1-001 | A source is stale | the stale-source alert carries the product and its date |
| None (run alert) | The flag is off, the Schedule did not fire, or the worker is not polling | the run alert names the Schedule, the business date and, for the flag, that it is off; its message ID is allocated by the catalogue owner and is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2578; ASM-4249) |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The hand-over or a named system is unavailable | the hand-over alert carries the system name and the business date |
| MSG-P7-003 | The record cannot be written | the incident alert carries the text and the business date; the date is backfillable |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks Reporting R | the API's 403; no alert |

MSG-P9-002, MSG-P1-001 and MSG-P4-002 are the legacy texts of RWB-E2-009 section 14, unchanged; MSG-GEN-006 and MSG-P7-003 are the platform texts the split adds. An alert never carries a case, an account, a payment or a customer value.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built here. The operator reads the run on the workflow visibility view and on the run view of JOB-15 (SCR-44), and the officer reads the measures on SCR-37; both are served by the base and the composite route the release deploys. The four dashboard series are the operator's view of the same run, and a held day is visible on both the run view and the screen.

The seven are new with D-RCV-60 and test the deployment only. Integration copies end in `-ITG` and belong to RWB-ITG-E2009-ITG; the ten legacy test cases stay with the criteria the APP story owns.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No secret in a chart value, a pipeline log or a prompt: the login, the client credentials and the payload keys are secret references only.
- No personal data in an alert, a series, a log or a run input: an alert names the service, the source, the measure family, the business date and the message ID.
- No business value in a chart, an alert threshold or a runbook: the measure codes, formulas, age bands and the zero tolerance of DL25 belong to their owner; thresholds are values of the environment.
- No deployment reaches another schema, another queue or a topic of this service's own, and no operator edits a row of `rwb_reporting` to force a publish.
- No rollout without the drift gate, the Schedule registration, the eight consumer groups and the six runbook entries in place.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-009 for the wave 2 integration harness. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **member of the integration and QA team**, I want **a repeatable cross-service journey harness for the steering dashboard v1 data set across rwb-reporting, rwb-case, rwb-agent and rwb-deviation**, so that **the measure set, the reconciliation gate and the dashboard read are proven end to end, with evidence, before the release is accepted**.

This story builds the harness and the evidence only. It builds no production endpoint, no screen, no table, no migration, no workflow and no schedule, it serves no operation, it owns no table and it starts no workflow. The real behaviour is owned by the four I stories RWB-P9-E2009-APP (the seven steering measures, the reconciliation gate, the publish state and GET /reports/measures in rwb-reporting), RWB-P3-E2009-APP (the case facts and the case list count of the business date), RWB-P10-E1063-APP (the agent runs, the agent metrics and the outcome counts of a run) and RWB-S8-E2009-APP (the deviation read that the dashboard's case scope depends on), and those four stories block the ITG run.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy RWB-E2-009 journey crosses more than one service. rwb-reporting holds the measure definitions in force, the measure snapshots, the publish state of a business date and the measures read; rwb-case holds the case facts and the case list count the dashboard reconciles against; rwb-agent holds the agent runs, their acceptance and override outcomes and the metrics read; rwb-deviation holds the deviation records of the cases in the measure; rwb-source-data holds the freshness of each data product and the rerun control; and rwb-access answers the role, scope and rights check behind the read. Until those services are exercised together on one business date, the program cannot show that the steering committee and the teams read the same numbers, which is the outcome REQ-WKM-009 and REQ-WKM-006 target.

The legacy story is split. The four I stories build the calculators, the reconciliation gate, the publish state, the measures read, the screen, the agent metrics and the deviation read. This story is the fifth slice: it runs the journey once per business date against the published contracts or their fakes and records the evidence. What the harness proves, in one repeatable run, is:

- JOB-15 on the synthetic day 2026-12-15, with definition version MD-2026.12 in force, produces a value for each of the seven measures: CASES_BY_STAGE, CASES_BY_QUEUE_AGE, DECISIONS_LOGGED, TREATMENTS, LETTERS_SENT, AGENT_ACCEPTANCE and AGENT_OVERRIDE.
- The case-list reconciliation is a gate and not a warning: when the dashboard count of CASES_BY_STAGE is 240 and the case list count is 239, no snapshot rows and no published extract exist for 2026-12-15, the latest published day stays 2026-12-14, MSG-P9-002 names 239, 240 and 2026-12-15, and the alert reaches the Reporting and BI analyst and the data steward.
- The freshness stamp travels with the measure read, and a stale source shows its own date: a notice data product dated 2026-12-14 makes LETTERS_SENT show 2026-12-14 and MSG-P1-001 name the data product and that date.
- The agent rates are per agent and version: case-intake 1.2.0 with 200 recommendations, 170 accepted and 30 overridden gives 85.0 percent acceptance and 15.0 percent override, and deviation-screen 0.9.0 with no runs gives no rate and the words "No runs".
- The date filter and the rerun behave: from after to is refused with 422 and MSG-GEN-003, and a rerun of a published day gives the same values with the frozen baseline of 2026-11-27 unchanged.
- REQ-WKM-009 and REQ-WKM-006 hold at the integration level, so the numbers on SCR-37 and in the Power BI report come from the same published rows.

**DP-17 applied.** The data lake and the INT-19 extract are removed (Architecture v5 slide 37; ADR-018; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-17). In the target, rwb-reporting holds the reporting read model in its own schema `rwb_reporting` and publishes `rwb.reporting.ReportPublished.v1` on `rwb.reporting.events.v1`; the event and the read model replace the extract, and Power BI reads rwb-reporting, not a lake. The harness therefore asserts the read model and the published event, never an extract file and never a lake path. A scenario that needed lake data would be a gap; this story needs none.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The four I stories have published contracts and are deployed in the SIT environment, or their contract fakes of §12.8 stand in for them: RWB-P9-E2009-APP (measures, reconciliation, publish state and the measures read in rwb-reporting), RWB-P3-E2009-APP (case facts and the case list count), RWB-P10-E1063-APP (agent runs, outcomes and metrics) and RWB-S8-E2009-APP (the deviation read).
- Definition version MD-2026.12 is in force for business date 2026-12-15, with the seven measure codes CASES_BY_STAGE, CASES_BY_QUEUE_AGE, DECISIONS_LOGGED, TREATMENTS, LETTERS_SENT, AGENT_ACCEPTANCE and AGENT_OVERRIDE loaded through the rwb-reporting contract (legacy sections 3 and 7 Background).
- The synthetic day 2026-12-15 holds 240 open cases, 1,412 decision log entries, 38 treatments and 95 notices sent, seeded through the owning contracts or the published fakes (legacy section 7 Background).
- The frozen baseline of 2026-11-27 exists and is readable through the measures read, so each value can be asserted beside it (legacy BR5).
- The test users are the roles of §10: RW-PRODHEAD and RW-TEAMMGR for the reads, RW-BIANAL and RW-DATASTEW for the hold alert, and a role without Reporting R for the refusal of §5 (legacy sections 10 and 15).
- gateway-bff is deployed with the composite steering route of DP-19 available. The gateway-bff composite steering route path and its merge order: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0391; ASM-0566).
- The harness environment, its seeding of a full measure day, its evidence format and retention, and its pass/fail gate: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0391; ASM-0566).
- No build dependency. Day 1.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: takes the run lock for the environment and records the build ID, the business date 2026-12-15, the definition version in force and the contract versions of the six services it is about to exercise.
2. Harness: seeds the synthetic day 2026-12-15 (240 open cases, 1,412 decision log entries, 38 treatments, 95 notices sent), the agent runs of case-intake 1.2.0 and deviation-screen 0.9.0, and definition version MD-2026.12 through the owning contracts or the published fakes, then reads each item back to assert the seeded state.
3. Harness: observes the JOB-15 Reporting extract run for business date 2026-12-15 and records its run state and its business date; it starts nothing and waits for the run.
4. Harness: reads the seven measures through the measures read for 2026-12-15 and asserts a value for each code, the period 2026-12-15, the freshness stamp and the baseline of 2026-11-27 beside each value (AC1).
5. Harness: asserts the case-list reconciliation, first with case list 240 against case facts 240, then with case facts 239, and asserts no snapshot rows, no published day for 2026-12-15, the latest published day 2026-12-14, MSG-P9-002 naming 239, 240 and 2026-12-15, and the alert reaching RW-BIANAL and RW-DATASTEW (AC2).
6. Harness: reads the agent measures and asserts case-intake 1.2.0 at 85.0 percent acceptance and 15.0 percent override, deviation-screen 0.9.0 with no rate and the words "No runs", and that no agent output is copied into the evidence (AC3).
7. Harness: forces the notice data product DP07 to the 2026-12-14 load, asserts LETTERS_SENT shows 2026-12-14 and MSG-P1-001 names DP07 and 2026-12-14 (AC4).
8. Harness: sends the measures read with from 2026-12-15 and to 2026-12-01 and asserts 422 with MSG-GEN-003 naming "from" and "to"; then asserts the product filter returns only the rows of the chosen product (AC4, TC-E2-009-06-ITG, TC-E2-009-08-ITG).
9. Harness: calls the authorise operation for a role without Reporting R and asserts the refusal with MSG-P4-002 and no measure rows in the answer (TC-E2-009-10-ITG).
10. Harness: reruns the published business date 2026-12-15 through the job rerun control and asserts the same values for every measure and that the frozen baseline rows of 2026-11-27 are unchanged (AC4, TC-E2-009-09-ITG).
11. Harness: asserts the Power BI read path — the rwb-reporting read model and the `ReportPublished` event of 2026-12-15 on `rwb.reporting.events.v1`, with no data lake and no extract file — and writes one run report per business date, keyed by story and business date; the report format and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0391; ASM-0566).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What the harness asserts | Message | ITG test case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The dashboard count of CASES_BY_STAGE is 239 while the case list shows 240 open cases at the 2026-12-15 cut-off | No snapshot rows and no published day for 2026-12-15; the latest published day stays 2026-12-14; the message names 239, 240 and 2026-12-15; the alert reaches RW-BIANAL and RW-DATASTEW and the publish state of 2026-12-15 is held | MSG-P9-002 | TC-E2-009-04-ITG |
| X2 | The notice data product DP07 is still the 2026-12-14 load | LETTERS_SENT shows the 2026-12-14 value with its own date; the message names DP07 and 2026-12-14; no measure is reported as if it were fresh | MSG-P1-001 | TC-E2-009-05-ITG |
| X3 | The measures read is sent with from 2026-12-15 and to 2026-12-01 | 422 on the direct call and on the composite route; the message names "from" and "to"; no rows are returned and nothing is written | MSG-GEN-003 | TC-E2-009-06-ITG |
| X4 | Agent deviation-screen 0.9.0 made no recommendations on 2026-12-15 | No AGENT_ACCEPTANCE and no AGENT_OVERRIDE value for that agent and version; the answer carries "No runs"; the run does not treat the absence as a zero | None | TC-E2-009-07-ITG |
| X5 | JOB-15 is rerun for the published business date 2026-12-15 | The rows for 2026-12-15 carry the same values; the duplicate run leaves one published day; the frozen baseline rows of 2026-11-27 are unchanged | None | TC-E2-009-09-ITG |
| X6 | A role without Reporting R calls the measures read or the composite steering route | 403 on the direct call; the composite route hides the measures; no row is returned | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-009-10-ITG |
| X7 | The seed pack cannot be loaded, another run holds the environment lock, or the evidence cannot be written | The run refuses to start and names the missing seed item or the lock holder, or is marked failed with the local evidence kept for the rerun; no scenario is reported as passed | None | All -ITG cases (the run refuses to start) |
| X8 | No definition version is in force for 2026-12-15, or MD-2026.12 is not the version the measures read names | No measure value is asserted as published for the day; the run records the missing version and fails the gate for that business date; the harness never substitutes a version of its own | None | TC-E2-009-01-ITG |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs on its own once the four I stories or their fakes are available; it builds no service feature and has no build dependency |
| Negotiable | The seed pack, the assertion set and the evidence format are agreed with QA; no business value is fixed by the harness |
| Valuable | The measure set, the reconciliation gate and the dashboard read are proven once across services, with the freshness and the baseline on the evidence |
| Estimable | One harness project, one journey specification, one fake pack, one per-run report |
| Small | Fits in one iteration with the owning stories' contract tests |
| Testable | Each scenario of §7 is one automated journey on synthetic data with a machine-checkable result |

```gherkin
    Given agent "deviation-screen" version "0.9.0" made no recommendations on 2026-12-15
```

These four criteria are new for the ITG harness and do not restate the nine legacy criteria owned by RWB-P9-E2009-APP.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Steering measures are computed from Workbench records and the decision log, never from a separate count | NFR-065; REQ-WKM-009 |
| BR2 | The dashboard case count equals the case list count at the same cut-off, or the publish is held | REQ-WKM-006; DL25 (tolerance zero) |
| BR3 | Agent acceptance is accepted recommendations over all recommendations, and override is overridden over all, per agent and version | NFR-066; DF-DEC-007, DF-DEC-013 |
| BR4 | A measure is shown with its business date and freshness stamp; stale data shows its date | MSG-P1-001 rule; FEAT-RPT-08 |
| BR5 | Each value is shown beside the frozen baseline of 2026-11-27 | REQ-WKM-009; RWB-E1-013 BR2 |
| BR6 | A rate with no runs in the denominator is not computed | NFR-066 |
| BR7 | Every query applies the role's scope | CTL-09 |

The rules are unchanged by the split. The harness asserts these seven rules against the owning services and re-implements none of them: it reads the definitions, the snapshots, the publish state and the rates through the rwb-reporting contract and never holds a formula, a tolerance or a band of its own. No BR row is changed by this story.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case. The harness changes no case status, route state, stage clock or timer. The table is what it observes on a business date and on a JOB-15 run.

| Observed object | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Business date (measure_publish) | Published | The reconciliation passed and the snapshot rows are readable for the day |
| Business date (measure_publish) | Held | The dashboard count differs from the case list count; the previous published day stays the latest |
| JOB-15 Reporting extract run | Not started, Started, Succeeded, Failed | The observed run state of the extract for the business date; the harness starts none of them |

A held day is published by the first run whose counts match, and a rerun of a published day keeps the same values; the harness asserts both and never sets a publish state itself.

The harness adds run states of its own only: Not started, Seeding, Running, Passed, Failed, with the latest run for a build deciding the gate. The gate definition is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0391; ASM-0566).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test asset in the integration pipeline and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; the 2 s timeout and the circuit breaker per downstream of DP-11 apply to every row.

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/reporting/v1/reports/measures` | P9 rwb-reporting | Reads the seven measures of the business date with period, dimension, freshness stamp and baseline value (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases` | P3 rwb-case | Reads the case list count of the cut-off and the product split used by the reconciliation and the filter (AC2, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | Reads one case fact of the seeded day, to prove the case facts behind CASES_BY_STAGE exist (AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-runs` | P10 rwb-agent | Reads the runs of case-intake 1.2.0 and deviation-screen 0.9.0 on 2026-12-15, and the no-runs answer (AC3) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-metrics` | P10 rwb-agent | Reads the recommendations, accepted and overridden counts behind the two rates (AC3) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` | P10 rwb-agent | Proves the outputs are counted and never copied into the evidence (AC3, BR3) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1/deviations` | S8 rwb-deviation | Reads the deviation records behind the case scope of the measures (AC1) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | Reads the freshness of DP07 and of every data product behind the seven measures (AC4, BR4) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` | P1 rwb-source-data | Drives the rerun control of the published day, so the same values and the unchanged baseline are asserted (AC4) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Role, scope and Reporting right check used by the composite route and by the direct call; supplies the MSG-P4-002 refusal (TC-E2-009-10-ITG) |

The composite steering route itself is gateway-bff (DP-19), owned by the platform edge story RWB-PLT-N001-CON. Its path and merge order are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0391; ASM-0566).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness produces no event; it consumes the events of §12.4 with its own consumer group.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | What the harness asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.reporting.ReportPublished.v1` | `rwb.reporting.events.v1` | P9 rwb-reporting | One event per published business date with the business date, the definition version and the measure set; no event for a held day; the event is the path Power BI reads after DP-17 |
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | The load of the business date is ready before the extract is observed, and the freshness of DP07 matches the load that arrived |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 rwb-decision (ledger); the owning service publishes its own record | The 1,412 decision log entries of the day reach the ledger and agree with DECISIONS_LOGGED, and the agent version and override reason on the records agree with the two agent rates (BR3) |
| `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` | `rwb.agent.events.v1` | P10 rwb-agent | The runs of case-intake 1.2.0 and the absence of runs of deviation-screen 0.9.0 on the day, which is the denominator the rates use (BR6) |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | The deviation records of the cases in the measure are the ones the dashboard scope reads, so a case with an open deviation is counted once (AC1) |

Consumers dedupe through their own inbox table; the harness consumes with its own group and never asserts a producer's outbox row.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

JOB-15 Reporting extract is observed, not built. Architecture v5 slide 44 makes it an Airflow-triggered extract in rwb-reporting with no data lake: it is not a Temporal workflow and not a Temporal Schedule, and the harness starts nothing. The harness waits for the run for business date 2026-12-15, records its run state and the business date, and then asserts the measures, the reconciliation outcome, the publish state and the event of §12.4.

No workflow is built, no activity is added and no Nexus operation is created by this story. The extract and its measure calculations belong to RWB-P9-E2009-APP; the Airflow edge belongs to the platform.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-15 is the Airflow edge for the extract, so the harness adds no Temporal Schedule and creates no cron. It waits for the run and asserts its outcome only.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no table in any schema (DP-01); it reads and writes through the operations of §12.2 only.

Each fake is replaced by the real service as its I story lands, contract by contract, without a change to the scenarios. The harness repository, its environment, its seeding of a full measure day, its evidence format and retention, and its pass/fail gate: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0391; ASM-0566).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Used | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | Yes | Ten consumed operations of §12.2 through gateway-bff and the owning services; one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream |
| Kafka | Yes | Consumes `rwb.reporting.ReportPublished.v1`, `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1`, `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`, `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` and `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1`; publishes nothing |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `integration/recovery-steering-dashboard` in the ACE repository, package `<ACE base package>.recovery.integration.steeringdashboard`. Not part of any deployed service, and it owns no schema, table or migration (DP-01, DP-15).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-17 | Data lake, INT-19, INT-20 | Removed (no data lake); reporting from events into rwb-reporting | none; gap if the story needs lake data |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The platform H dependencies named by this table are delivered by the platform wave and are not repeated in the metadata H list. The blocking dependencies of this story are the four I stories, which replace the fakes with real services one at a time.

**DP-17 applied.** The data lake and the INT-19 extract are removed (Architecture v5 slide 37; ADR-018). rwb-reporting holds the reporting read model in its own schema and publishes `rwb.reporting.ReportPublished.v1` on `rwb.reporting.events.v1`; the read model and the event replace the extract, and Power BI reads rwb-reporting. The harness asserts the read model and the event, holds no lake path, and fails a run that needs one. No lake row, no lake copy and no extract file is a dependency of this story.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Test harness | Runs one journey per business date, keyed by story and business date, with the run lock and the build ID; stops at the first failed assertion with the trace |
| CompositeRouteClient | Harness adapter | Calls the gateway-bff composite steering route and the ten consumed operations of §12.2, with the test user of the scenario |
| FakePack | WireMock project | Serves rwb-reporting, rwb-case, rwb-agent, rwb-deviation, rwb-source-data and rwb-access from the published OpenAPI documents of §12.8 |
| MeasureAssertion | Assertion | Reads the seven measures and fails the run on a missing code, a wrong period, a missing freshness stamp or a missing baseline value |
| ReconciliationAssertion | Assertion | Compares the CASES_BY_STAGE total with the case list count, and fails the run when a held day has snapshot rows or a published date, or when the message does not name both counts and the business date |
| AgentRateAssertion | Assertion | Computes 170 over 200 and 30 over 200, fails the run on any other rate, and fails a rate for an agent with no runs |
| RunReportWriter | Reporter | Writes one run report with the trace and the per-assertion result; format and retention Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0391; ASM-0566) |

**Environment and test data**

- Environment: SIT, one namespace, the four I stories deployed from their wave 2 builds or replaced by the §12.8 fakes, with the gateway route for `/api/recovery/*`, the topics of §12.4 and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`. Harness repository, environment and seeding: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0391; ASM-0566).
- Data: synthetic day 2026-12-15 with 240 open cases, 1,412 decision log entries, 38 treatments and 95 notices sent; definition version MD-2026.12; the frozen baseline of 2026-11-27; agents case-intake 1.2.0 (200 recommendations, 170 accepted, 30 overridden) and deviation-screen 0.9.0 (no runs); notice data product DP07 dated 2026-12-14 in the stale case and 2026-12-15 in the healthy case; case list 240 against case facts 239 in the held case; the date pair from 2026-12-15 to 2026-12-01. No production record is copied and no agent output text enters the evidence.
- Reset: each run starts from the seeded state, so a repeated run is deterministic and the same report is produced.

**Build steps**

1. Build JourneyRunner and CompositeRouteClient against the published OpenAPI documents of the six services, with the run lock and the build ID.
2. Publish FakePack for the six services from the same documents, and prove the harness runs green from Day 1 on the fakes with the healthy seed of 2026-12-15.
3. Add the composite route assertion of AC1, including the 2 s per-call budget, the single trace and the no-cross-schema check.
4. Add MeasureAssertion over the seven codes with period, freshness stamp and the 2026-11-27 baseline, and the held-day assertion of AC2 with MSG-P9-002 and the alert to the two roles.
5. Add AgentRateAssertion for case-intake 1.2.0 and the no-runs answer of deviation-screen 0.9.0, and assert that no agent output is copied (AC3).
6. Add the stale-source case of AC4 with MSG-P1-001 naming DP07 and 2026-12-14, and the date-order refusal with MSG-GEN-003 naming from and to.
7. Add the rerun of the published day with the unchanged baseline, and the access refusal with MSG-P4-002 for a role without Reporting R.
8. Add the DP-17 assertion over the rwb-reporting read model and `ReportPublished`, write RunReportWriter, replace each fake with the real service as its I story lands, attach the report to the wave 2 release record and evaluate the gate; the gate definition: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0391; ASM-0566).

**Feature switch:** `rwb.reporting.steering` is the legacy switch of RWB-E2-009 and stays with RWB-P9-E2009-APP; the harness asserts its enabled state only. The harness has no production feature flag and runs in the test environment only.

**Done when:** the journey runs green against the four deployed I stories in SIT, the run report for the business date holds every assertion of §7 and §16 with its trace, the seven measures carry the definition version and the freshness stamp, the held day leaves the latest published day at 2026-12-14 with no snapshot rows, and the Power BI read and the measures read return the same values from the rwb-reporting rows for one full business date.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P9-002 | The dashboard count differs from the case list | The case count on the dashboard ({count}) does not match the case list ({listCount}) for {date}. The publish is held. |
| MSG-P1-001 | A source is stale | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Dates in the wrong order | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks Reporting R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values; it does not own the message text. In this journey {count} is 239, {listCount} is 240 and {date} is 2026-12-15 for MSG-P9-002; {product} is "DP07 Legal" and {date} is 2026-12-14 for MSG-P1-001; {field} is "from" and {other} is "to" for MSG-GEN-003. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the measure definitions, the formulas, the reconciliation tolerance and the age bands are data held by rwb-reporting; the harness reads them and never holds a copy or a threshold.
- No personal data in logs, tests, traces or reports: the evidence holds measure codes, counts, rates, dates, roles and agent versions only; the agent outputs are counted, never copied.
- No read of another service's schema and no direct ACE read: every read goes through the owner's contract, and the harness fails a run whose trace shows a cross-schema read (DP-01).
- No data lake: DP-17 removes the lake and INT-19, the reporting read model and `ReportPublished` replace the extract, and the harness fails a run that needs a lake path or an extract file.
- Counts on SCR-37 and in Power BI come from the same rows: the harness asserts both reads on one published business date and reports a difference as a failure, not as a warning.
- One hop only: the harness fails a run when the trace shows a call chain deeper than the gateway and one owner, and every call carries the 2 s budget of DP-11.
- A fake that outlives its service is a defect, not a configuration: each fake is replaced by the real service as its I story lands, and the harness never runs against UAT or production.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-010 for rwb-source-data. The stage 2 capability had no published contract in the monolith: the DP04 rows, the join to the ACE views and the access check were in-process calls of one deployable. This baseline publishes the DP04 branch of the record read on `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` with its record shapes, its error envelope, its status and freshness rules and its fakes, so the app story and the Epic 3 consumers build in parallel from Day 1 (DP-11, DP-13; Architecture v5 slides 15 and 41). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the DP04 record of rwb-source-data: an OpenAPI 3.1 document for the DP04 branch of the record read, the `DataProductRecordPage`, `DataProductRecord` and `FieldValue` shapes with the system of record of every part, the error envelope and the message mapping, the status and freshness rules as data, the versioning rule, the nine contract tables and the fakes of the four dependencies it consumes**, so that **the app, operations and test stories of this legacy key and the Epic 3 consumers build against a fixed, testable shape from Day 1 without waiting for the service or for rwb-guarantee to be built**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST and one hop with a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). DP04 is read by the case record and by the settlement, restructure and deed-in-lieu screens of Epic 3, and its two content types come from different systems of record: the dated Workbench snapshot in this service's schema and the live ACE facts in the views (BR1-BR2 of the legacy story). If the shape of that mix is not agreed once and faked, every consumer invents its own way of joining a snapshot row to a contract number and distinguishing a Workbench fact from an ACE fact, and the guarantee claim, whose owner is only built in wave 3, blocks the whole read.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema and login `rwb_source_data`, REST base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, topic `rwb.source-data.events.v1` with event names `rwb.source-data.<Event>.v1`, task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata` (DP-02, DP-13, DP-14; Architecture v5 slides 29 and 41). The capability adds no event of its own, so the document says so explicitly and no consumer waits for one.

**What D-RCV-60 changes.** The legacy story had nothing published: the snapshot, the view join and the access check were in one process over the one `recovery` schema. Now the snapshot tables are this service's, the ACE facts are this service's views, the treatment entity is rwb-case's contract and the guarantee claim is rwb-guarantee's, and the access and freshness answers belong to two other P1 stories. The contract is what keeps that change from becoming five local agreements.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the document, topic and event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice (DP-14).
- The platform error envelope is the baseline; where this document narrows it, it does so explicitly and names the message ID per condition.
- The operations and their owners are taken from the Ownership Map v1 only; rwb-source-data never documents an operation owned by another service, and the treatment and guarantee reads are documented as consumed (DP-11).
- The record shapes reuse the components already published by RWB-P1-E1016-CON: `DataProductRecordPage`, `DataProductRecord`, `FieldValue`, `DataProductFreshness` and the error envelope; this baseline narrows the DP04 branch and adds no component owned by another service.
- `dp_treatment`, `dp_guarantee_claim`, `data_product`, `data_product_access`, `sys_objects` and `sys_fields` are P1's (Ownership Map v1), so the entity names of the record are this service's own.
- The guarantee claim contract of rwb-guarantee is a C dependency the Work Package does not list, and the field-level DP04 record schema is fixed by no source document (GAP-0512; ASM-0704).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the DP04 branch of `GET /data-products/{productCode}/records` in the OpenAPI 3.1 document, with the path parameter, the three query parameters, the owner, the 200 shape and the five error responses.
2. Fix the `DataProductRecordPage`, `DataProductRecord` and `FieldValue` shapes for DP04, with the entity of each row naming its system of record and every field carrying its field ID.
3. Agree the error envelope and map each HTTP status and refusal to its message ID, with the legacy texts copied unchanged.
4. State the status and freshness rules: LOADED and STALE from LOV-FRESHNESS, the expected-by time, and the hold on a count difference, each as a data row rather than a constant.
5. State the versioning rule: additive within major version 1, a change to the record shape is a new major version, and no event is added.
6. Publish the contract tables of section 12 and the four fakes.
7. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the shape of the record, the envelope mapping, the freshness rule, the versioning rule and the fake-to-document comparison.
8. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P1-E2010-APP, RWB-P1-E2010-OPS and the Epic 3 consumers.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | `caseId`, `page` or `size` fails schema validation | 400 with the error envelope and the failing pointer | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, AC3 |
| X2 | No valid session, or a session without the Case record right | 401 or 403 with the error envelope | MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-002 | AC1, AC3 |
| X3 | A DP04 access row is absent or not in force | 403 with MSG-P4-002; no row is returned and no field is leaked | MSG-P4-002 | AC3 |
| X4 | The case is outside the caller's scope | 404 with MSG-P4-003 | MSG-P4-003 | AC3 |
| X5 | A required property of the record has no definition in the source material | The property carries the placeholder and the gap row is carried | None | AC2 |
| X6 | A fake drifts from the document, or a property of another service's table appears in a schema | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC2, AC6 |
| X7 | A caller asks for a major version the service does not serve | 404 with the error envelope and the served major versions | None described in the sources | AC5 |

MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003, MSG-P1-001, MSG-P1-002 and MSG-GEN-006 keep their text from the legacy story and are carried unchanged in the envelope mapping; MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P4-001 are the shared envelope messages declared by RWB-P1-E1016-CON.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelope, the ownership map, the API Specification v4 and the record components of RWB-P1-E1016-CON |
| Negotiable | Field-level detail is settled with the consumers; the path, the query parameters, the record shapes and the rules are fixed |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app and operations stories of this legacy key and the Epic 3 consumers of DP04 on Day 1 |
| Estimable | One document branch, three record shapes, one envelope, two rules, nine contract tables, four fakes and six contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

```gherkin

  Background:

    Then the operation answers 400, 401, 403, 404 and 503

    Then no other service's path and no other base path is declared

  Scenario: AC2 The record shape names every fact with its system of record (new, D-RCV-60)

    Then the contract number and contract date of the primary account appear with entity "v_ace_account"
    Then the plan terms appear with entity "v_ace_plan"
    Then each row names its entity, so that dp_treatment and dp_guarantee_claim read as the Workbench snapshot and v_ace_account and v_ace_plan read as the ACE facts
    Then the record carries the business date of the snapshot and the freshness of the product
    Then no Workbench table of the document holds a property that copies an ACE column

  Scenario: AC3 One envelope and one message mapping cover every refusal (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the error envelope component of the document
    When a 400, 401, 403, 404 or 503 response is produced
    Then the body carries the code, the message, the messageId, the traceId and the field list
    Then a missing caseId answers 400 with MSG-GEN-001
    Then a caller without the Case record right or without a DP04 access row answers 403 with MSG-P4-002
    Then a case outside the caller's scope answers 404 with MSG-P4-003
    Then a failed freshness or record read answers 503 with MSG-GEN-006
    Then MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003, MSG-P1-001, MSG-P1-002 and MSG-GEN-006 carry the legacy text unchanged

  Scenario: AC4 The status and freshness rules are data, not constants (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the status and freshness section of the document
    When the DP04 rules are reviewed
    Then the freshness status is LOADED or STALE from the list LOV-FRESHNESS and the record never invents a third value
    Then the expected-by time of the product is read from data_product and is not a value of the document or the code
    Then a difference between the active treatment count written and the count answered by the treatment contract holds the stamp, so the record answers the previous business date with status STALE
    Then the rollup of a product fed by several sources takes the oldest business date, as the freshness contract of RWB-P1-E1015-CON states it
    Then no threshold, tolerance or business date is fixed in the contract

  Scenario: AC5 The versioning rule is stated and no event is added (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the document declares major version 1 in the path of /api/recovery/source-data/v1
    When a property of the DP04 record is added within the same major version
    Then the addition is accepted and a consumer that ignores it still reads the record
    When a property is removed, renamed or retyped
    Then the change requires a new major version and a caller of version 1 is answered 404 with the served major versions
    Then the document declares no event, no workflow and no Schedule for this capability, and the topic rwb.source-data.events.v1 carries only the events of RWB-P1-E1015-APP

  Scenario: AC6 The nine contract tables are complete and the fakes match them (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the contract section of this story
    When the nine sub-tables are reviewed

    Then the three fakes answer the treatment read, the guarantee claim read and the ACE account and plan fixture, and the case-existence stub answers the link check
    Then the access fake answers a granted and a refused DP04 answer
    Then the contract tests compare each fake with the document and fail on any drift
```
