##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`; a document never declares another service's path | DP-13; Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | Event names would be `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1` on `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; this capability publishes none and adds none | DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR3 | DP04 holds treatments and guarantee claims from the Workbench and contract and plan facts read from the ACE views, with one system of record for each part, and no Workbench table copies a contract, a plan or an account | REQ-RDF-014; BR1 and BR2 of the legacy story |
| BR4 | The record answers LOADED or STALE from LOV-FRESHNESS; the product is stamped only when the active count matches, with zero tolerance | DL25; TSD P1 freshness rules |
| BR5 | A role reads DP04 only through an access row in force, answered by the access contract of this service | data_product_access; REQ-RDF-010 |
| BR6 | The contract names no table of another service and no property of another service's table; the treatment and guarantee facts are consumed as contracts | DP-01; Ownership Map v1 |
| BR7 | No business value is fixed in the contract: the product code, the owner role, the expected-by time, the status list and the access rows stay data | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR8 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition; the business message texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR9 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a change to the record shape is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 11 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1, BR2 and BR9 are the shape of the document itself. BR3 is the rule the record shape carries: `dp_treatment` and `dp_guarantee_claim` name the Workbench facts and `v_ace_account` and `v_ace_plan` name the ACE facts, and no snapshot property repeats an ACE column. BR4 is stated against the freshness contract of RWB-P1-E1015-CON and the hold of the app story, and this baseline only fixes the vocabulary and the data source. BR5 is answered by RWB-P1-E1016-CON and consumed here. BR6 is the ownership check of the contract tests. BR7 is why the document contains codes and field IDs only. BR8 is section 14.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The DP04 branch, the three record shapes and the envelope are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app and operations stories and the Epic 3 consumers accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1 | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property of the record is removed, renamed or retyped | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake or an ownership breach | A contract test fails | In review |

The DP04 freshness states LOADED and STALE belong to the product and not to this baseline, which only carries their names.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-source-data | Owns the document, the record shapes and the fakes; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change and a new major version |
| Consuming teams (app, operations, and the rwb-case, rwb-guarantee and Epic 3 owners) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| Data steward | Confirms the system of record of each part of DP04 and that the record publishes no personal value |
| Platform library owner | Owns the error envelope and the naming rule this document reuses |

The identity scheme behind the document's security definition is the platform one: a user JWT from gateway-bff plus workload identity (Architecture v5 slide 11). No credential and no personal name appears in the document or in a fake.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Record page | `items` of `DataProductRecord`, `freshness` of `DataProductFreshness`, `page`, `size`, `total` |
| Snapshot row | `recordId` (the treatment or claim record ID), `entity` `dp_treatment` or `dp_guarantee_claim`, `fields` of `FieldValue` with `fieldName`, `value` and `masked` |
| ACE fact row | `recordId` (the `account_key` or the `plan_ref`), `entity` `v_ace_account` or `v_ace_plan`, `fields` of `FieldValue` |
| Field list | DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-022 for the snapshot rows, DF-TRT-034 to DF-TRT-061 for the two snapshot tables, DF-ACE-001, DF-ACE-006, DF-ACE-007, DF-ACE-160, DF-ACE-168, DF-ACE-174 and DF-ACE-175 for the ACE facts |
| Freshness | `productCode`, `productName`, `sourceSystem`, `businessDate`, `sourceExtractedAt`, `loadedAt`, `status` (LOADED or STALE), `staleSince` |
| Catalog entry of DP04 | The entry of RWB-P1-E1016-CON with `systemOfRecord` naming the Workbench for the snapshot and ACE for the plan, and the two views in `sourceViews` |

The exact field-level schema of the DP04 record — the required flags, lengths and formats per property of the snapshot and ACE rows — and the shape of the guarantee claim read of rwb-guarantee are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0512; ASM-0704); this baseline fixes the property names above from the legacy data rows and the API Specification v4 and leaves the field-level detail to the baseline review.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-source-data (P1); base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/data-products/{productCode}/records` (the DP04 branch) | API-P1-010: `DataProductRecordPage`; `productCode` DP04 required in the path; `caseId`, `page` and `size` in the query; 200 with the snapshot rows and the ACE fact rows of the case; 400, 401, 403, 404 and 503 | Case record R plus a DP04 access row in force, through the access contract of RWB-P1-E1016-CON |

The document declares the branch this legacy key supplies; the branches of the other 13 products stay with their own stories in the same service API file, and this baseline changes no path of theirs.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/treatments` and the changed-window and active-count reads of that contract | P3 rwb-case (`RWB-P3-E2004-CON`) | The treatment facts of a case; operation names are fixed by that contract; faked |
| GET | the guarantee claim read of the rwb-guarantee contract | S3 rwb-guarantee | The TCG claims of a case; faked, and not in the Work Package's C list (GAP-0512; ASM-0704) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case-existence answer of the link check; faked and test-only |
| (interface) | `AceSourceReadRepository` over `recovery.v_ace_account` and `recovery.v_ace_plan` | P1 rwb-source-data | The contract and plan facts, read at request time through this service's own ACE read contract |

No other service is called: the status list arrives as reference data through the keeper library of rwb-case (DP-07), and the ACE facts are read in this service's own views (DP-01, DP-05).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The topic of the service is `rwb.source-data.events.v1` with event names `rwb.source-data.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and its two events `AceDataReady` and `AceDataLate` belong to RWB-P1-E1015-APP. This baseline declares no event and adds none.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None in this baseline. The stage 2 build is started by this service's own `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1`, consumed by RWB-P1-E2010-APP; the contract adds no consumed event and no consumer group.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None in this baseline. `Stage2ProductWorkflow` and its activities `snapshot(page)`, `writeDp04Page`, `checkActiveCount` and `stampDp04` run on task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and are the application story's; those names are a target design choice fixed by no source document, recorded in the application slice (GAP-0510; ASM-0702). The contract fixes no workflow shape and this baseline declares none.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The capability owns no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job; the freshness cut-off Schedules belong to RWB-P1-E1015-CON and RWB-P1-E1015-APP.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| `dp_treatment`, `dp_guarantee_claim` | P1 (`rwb_source_data`) | The snapshot rows of the record, keyed by record ID and business date; no `contract_no` and no `contract_date` column |
| `data_product` | P1 (`rwb_source_data`) | The product code, owner role, refresh cycle and expected-by time behind the record and the freshness |
| `data_product_access` | P1 (`rwb_source_data`) | The DP04 access row the read is answered with |
| `sys_objects`, `sys_fields` | P1 (`rwb_source_data`) | The field IDs, entity names and data types of the record properties |
| `data_product_load` | P1 (`rwb_source_data`) | The freshness of DP04 carried by the record; written by RWB-P1-E1015-APP |

No other table is named in the contract, and no table of another service is read (DP-01, BR6).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| RWB-P3-E2004-CON treatment fake | 40 active treatments and 12 plans for the fixture case; a treatment changed at the end of the business date; a contract error | App story, contract tests |
| rwb-guarantee guarantee claim fake | 5 TCG claims for existing cases, one claim for an unknown case ID, an empty list, a contract error | App story, contract tests |
| ACE account and plan fixture | Rows of `v_ace_account` and `v_ace_plan` with `contract_no`, `contract_date`, `plan_ref`, `installments`, `recommended_installment` and `booked_at`; an account with no plan | App story, contract tests |
| RWB-P1-E1016-CON access fake | A granted DP04 answer for RW-CASEOWN, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-GUARANT, RW-CREDITAD, RW-COE and RW-AUDIT; a refused answer for RW-PHONECOL; a row not yet in force | App story, contract tests |

The case-existence answer used by the link check is the test-only stub of rwb-case's case contract and is listed with the four fakes above in the contract tests; it is recorded with GAP-0512 and ASM-0704.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 provided, 3 consumed (2 contracts and 1 case read) | The DP04 record read; the treatment and guarantee reads and the case-existence read; one hop, 2 s timeout |
| Kafka | None | No event published or consumed by this baseline |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, activity or Schedule in the contract |
| File | None | No file in this contract |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `openapi/rwb-source-data-v1.yaml` with the DP04 branch and the shared components, `contract/dp04-record.yaml` for the record shapes, `contract/error-envelope.yaml`, the status, freshness and versioning rules in the contract README, and the four fake mappings of 12.8.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-11 and DP-13 are the two patterns the baseline exists for: the in-process join becomes an operation and the monolith base becomes the service base. DP-01 and DP-05 decide what the record may name, DP-07 supplies the status list, DP-10 and DP-15 are named because the app story that consumes the baseline uses them, and DP-19 is the screen path the record is read through.

**Build steps**

1. OpenAPI 3.1 skeleton with the base path, the security definition, the error responses and the shared components; schema lint in the pipeline.
2. The DP04 branch and its three query parameters, with the field names and field IDs of section 11; the field-level detail is agreed under the recorded gap.
3. `DataProductRecordPage`, `DataProductRecord`, `FieldValue` and `DataProductFreshness` narrowed for DP04, with no property owned by another service.
4. Error envelope and the message-ID mapping, business texts copied unchanged.
5. The status, freshness and versioning rules, and the statement that no event, workflow or Schedule belongs to the baseline.
6. The four fakes and their fixtures.
7. The six contract tests; a drift between a fake and the document, or a property from another service's table, fails the build.
8. Baseline tag and the consumer sign-off note.

**Done when.** The document validates in the pipeline, the six contract tests pass, the four fakes answer every consumed path, and the app and operations stories of this legacy key and the Epic 3 consumers have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | caseId or another required query field is missing | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-001 | No valid session | Your session has ended. Sign in again. |
| MSG-P4-002 | No Case record right, or no DP04 access row | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P1-001 | DP04 is stale at its expected-by time | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P1-002 | The count check held the publish of the business date | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The freshness, the record read or a consumed contract is unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The message IDs are contract elements; the five business texts are the legacy texts carried unchanged, and MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P4-001 are the shared envelope messages of RWB-P1-E1016-CON. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

The baseline serves SCR-03 Case record (Read only; loading, refused, ready), which shows the DP04 data the role may read with the personal fields masked, through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and SCR-45 Data quality (Loading; breaks empty; breaks list), which shows the count break and the References break the app story writes. The settlement, restructure and deed-in-lieu screens of Epic 3 read the same record and are declared by their own stories. The composite route specification and the screen field list are the platform edge story's and the screen owners'; this document fixes the service side of the answer only.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the product code, the owner role, the expected-by time, the status list and the access rows stay data; the document carries codes, field IDs and enums only.
- No personal data in an example or a fake: the record carries case IDs, record IDs, field IDs, codes, dates and amounts only, and every example is synthetic.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the `recovery.v_ace_*` views: the document names `v_ace_account` and `v_ace_plan` as the ACE facts and no other service's table anywhere (DP-05, DP-01).
- No property of another service's table: the treatment and guarantee facts are consumed as contracts, and a property that copies an ACE column into a Workbench table fails the contract test.
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base or topic fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- No event, workflow or Schedule is added by the baseline: the capability is synchronous and the build is event-started by the app story (BR2).
- A fake that drifts from the document fails the build, and the error envelope and the naming rule come from the platform library, narrowed but never redefined.

| RWB-P3-E2004-CON | Contract | Consumed: the treatment facts, faked (DP-11) |
| S3 rwb-guarantee claim contract | Contract | Consumed but outside the Work Package's C list: the guarantee claim read, faked (GAP-0512; ASM-0704) |

##### 19. Out of scope

- The workflow, the four activities, the two snapshot tables and the DP04 branch implementation: RWB-P1-E2010-APP.
- The chart, the worker registration, the trigger proof, the flag, the dashboards, the alerts and the runbook: RWB-P1-E2010-OPS.
- The treatment entity and its plan timers: rwb-case, RWB-P3-E2004-APP and its contract.
- The guarantee claim record, its filing and its deadline timers: rwb-guarantee (S3, wave 3); only the consumed shape is faked here, and the filing flow is not documented by this baseline.
- The settlement, restructure and deed-in-lieu screens of Epic 3 and their composite routes: the Epic 3 screen stories and the platform edge story.
- The freshness stamp, the stale flag, the expected-by time and the `data_product_load` writer: RWB-P1-E1015-CON and RWB-P1-E1015-APP.
- The access rows, the catalog entry and the access answer: RWB-P1-E1016-CON and RWB-P1-E1016-APP.
- The ACE view SQL and the read path: RWB-P1-E1069-APP.
- The field-level completeness of the DP04 record and the shape of the guarantee claim read (GAP-0512; ASM-0704).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-010 for rwb-source-data. The stage 2 step leaves `DailyCaseRun` in rwb-case and becomes `Stage2ProductWorkflow` on this service's own task queue, started by this service's own `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` (DP-10); the dated DP04 copies of treatments and guarantee claims are written in `rwb_source_data` and the contract and plan facts stay in the `recovery.v_ace_*` views, read live and never copied (DP-01, DP-05); the treatment entity is consumed as a contract with a fake and the DP04 record read is declared by the contract story of this legacy key, while the deployment moves to RWB-P1-E2010-OPS. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **recovery developer (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **the stage 2 product build to run as `Stage2ProductWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-source-data`, started by this service's own `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1`, writing the dated DP04 copies of treatments and guarantee claims into `rwb_source_data` and reading the contract number, contract date and plan terms live from `recovery.v_ace_account` and `recovery.v_ace_plan`, with the link check, the active-count check, the freshness stamp and the DP04 record read that the Epic 3 screens use**, so that **the settlement, restructure and deed-in-lieu screens read one checked place, nothing is copied out of ACE, and the stage 2 step of the daily run belongs to the service that owns the data products**.

This is the application slice of legacy RWB-E2-010. It owns:

- all eight legacy acceptance criteria of the story, copied verbatim with their origin tag, and the business rules, messages and data rows they depend on;
- `Stage2ProductWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, its window, its case link check, its count check and its call to the freshness stamp, with the four activities `snapshot(page)`, `writeDp04Page`, `checkActiveCount` and `stampDp04` (DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 15, "Workflow: AceIngestCheck, reconciliation" and the `snapshot(page)` activity);
- the writer of `dp_treatment` and `dp_guarantee_claim` in schema `rwb_source_data`, keyed by record ID and business date, plus the `data_product_load` row of DP04 written through the freshness story (DP-01, DP-15);
- the DP04 branch of `GET /data-products/{productCode}/records` on base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, which returns the snapshot rows with the contract and plan facts read live (DP-13).

It does not own: the published shape of that operation, which is declared by RWB-P1-E2010-CON and shares the components of RWB-P1-E1016-CON; the access and catalog contract, which is RWB-P1-E1016-CON; the freshness stamp writer, which is RWB-P1-E1015-APP; the ACE view SQL and the read path, which are RWB-P1-E1069-APP; the treatment entity and its plan timers, which are rwb-case's under RWB-P3-E2004-CON; the guarantee claim record, which is rwb-guarantee's (S3); and the chart, the dashboards and the alerts, which are RWB-P1-E2010-OPS.

##### 2. Business rationale

From Epic 3 the settlement, restructure and deed-in-lieu screens need each case's treatments, plan terms, loan contracts and guarantee claims in one checked place. In the target the live treatment and guarantee records stay with S2 and S3, and the dated DP04 copies stay with P1 as the data engine, built from the live facts and read-only for reporting (Ownership Map ruling on `treatment`, `dp_treatment` and `dp_guarantee_claim`; ASM-0080). DP04 therefore still has two kinds of content: the Workbench snapshot of treatments and claims, stamped for the business date and owned by this service, and the ACE facts — contract number, contract date and plan terms — read from `recovery.v_ace_account` and `recovery.v_ace_plan` at request time. No table copies a contract, a plan or an account (DP-01, DP-05).

What D-RCV-60 changes is where the step runs and how it is started and reached. The legacy step was an in-process stage of `rwb-case`'s JOB-02 chain over the one `recovery` schema. In the target the step is a workflow of rwb-source-data, the service that owns the data products and the freshness stamp, started by the `AceDataReady` event this service already publishes (DP-10; Architecture v5 slides 15 and 44: JOB-02 starts from AceDataReady and JOB-04 reconciliation belongs to rwb-source-data). The consumers of the legacy snapshot tables become consumers of a published record read, one hop and 2 s timeout (DP-11), so the Epic 3 screens reach DP04 through gateway-bff and never through a table (DP-19).

Serves REQ-RDF-014 (stage 2 data products exist before the first treatment goes live) and REQ-RDF-010 (access per data product by role). No business value moves: the product code DP04, the owner role, the expected-by time and the access rows stay data rows held by the catalog and access stories of this service.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P1-E2010-CON is published: the DP04 branch of the record read, the record shapes `DataProductRecordPage`, `DataProductRecord` and `FieldValue`, the error envelope and the fakes are baselined and handed to this story.
- RWB-P1-E1069-APP is done: `recovery.v_ace_account` and `recovery.v_ace_plan` are readable through the `rwb_source_data` login, which holds SELECT on the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views and no privilege in `public` (DP-02, DP-05).
- RWB-P1-E1016-CON is published and RWB-P1-E1015-APP is done: the access check per data product and the freshness stamp with its `data_product_load` writer exist, so the DP04 access row and the DP04 stamp are read and written through them and not re-implemented here.
- RWB-P1-E1015-APP is done and `data_product` holds DP04 Treatment and offers with its owner role, its refresh cycle and its expected-by time; the expected-by time of DP04 is 08:00 as the legacy story assumed from DL11 (GAP-0511; ASM-0703), because no source document states the DP04 value.
- RWB-P3-E2004-CON is published with its fake: `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/treatments` and the changed-window and active-count reads of the treatment entity of rwb-case, one hop and 2 s timeout (DP-11).
- The guarantee claim read of rwb-guarantee (S3) is available as a published contract with its fake, and returns no claim until S3 is built in wave 3; the contract is a C dependency the Work Package does not list (GAP-0509; ASM-0701).
- RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (workflow kit), RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (per-service Flyway sequence), RWB-PLT-E1043-CON with RWB-P3-E1043-CON (reference data: the status lists) and RWB-PLT-N001-CON (gateway-bff composite route) are in place.
- The per-service Flyway sequence of rwb-source-data is at the version that carries `dp_treatment`, `dp_guarantee_claim` and `data_product_load`; this story adds the two snapshot tables on the same sequence and never edits an applied migration (DP-15).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; the contract is tagged by RWB-P1-E2010-CON when its tests pass.

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-source-data: the outbox publishes `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` for business date D once the freshness story has stamped the source products for D from a COMPLETE ACE batch (Architecture v5 slide 15; DP-09, DP-10).
2. The listener of this story starts `Stage2ProductWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-source-data` with the business date, the source system and the freshness summary; the workflow ID is derived from the business date and the source, so a redelivery starts no second run.
3. `snapshot(page)` activity: asks the treatment contract of rwb-case for the treatments created or changed in the window [start of D, start of D+1), page by page, one hop and 2 s, and asks the guarantee contract of rwb-guarantee for the claims changed in the same window.
4. `writeDp04Page` activity: resolves the case of every row to confirm it exists, holds on the break list any row whose case does not resolve, and upserts the other rows into `dp_treatment` and `dp_guarantee_claim` in schema `rwb_source_data`, keyed by record ID and business date, one transaction per page.
5. `checkActiveCount` activity: compares the count of active treatments written for D with the active count answered by the treatment contract; a difference holds the publish and lists the break for the data steward (MSG-P1-002).
6. `stampDp04` activity: on a match, calls the freshness stamp of RWB-P1-E1015-APP for DP04 and business date D, so the stamp row in `data_product_load` is written by its owner and not by this story.
7. Case owner, restructuring officer, guarantee officer or credit approver: reads DP04 for a case through the DP04 branch of `GET /data-products/{productCode}/records?caseId=`; the response joins the snapshot rows to `recovery.v_ace_account` and `recovery.v_ace_plan` for the contract number, contract date and plan terms, which are read at request time and never written.
8. Data steward: reads the DP04 catalog entry and the breaks; the catalog entry names the system of record of each part and never a copied ACE column.
9. A rerun of D replaces the snapshot rows by record ID, publishes nothing new and never duplicates a row.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A role without a DP04 access row reads the product | 403; the refusal is logged by the access check of this service | MSG-P4-002 | AC3 |
| X2 | A guarantee claim names a case that does not exist | The claim is held on the break list with check References and retried with the next build; nothing is written | None | AC4 |
| X3 | The treatment contract is unavailable | The workflow ends FAILED for system Treatment; the previous DP04 rows and stamp stay; DP04 turns stale at its expected-by time through the freshness story | MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P1-001 | AC5 |
| X4 | The workflow runs again for the same business date | Rows are replaced by record ID and business date; no duplicate row and no second event | None | AC6 |
| X5 | The active treatment counts differ | DP04 is not stamped for D and the break is listed for the data steward | MSG-P1-002 | AC7 |
| X6 | A treatment changed at the end of business date D | It is inside the window of D; a change one second after the window goes to D+1 | None | AC8 |
| X7 | The guarantee contract answers with an error or is not deployed yet | The claim part of the page is held on the break list, the treatment part is written, and the workflow ends with the guarantee break named | MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P1-002 | Section 12.2 |
| X8 | The rerun is asked while the workflow of D is running | The rerun is refused and the running execution is named | MSG-P2-006 | Section 12.5 |

X1 to X6 are the exception paths of RWB-E2-010 carried onto the split. X7 is the path the guarantee contract of S3 adds while its own service is not yet built (GAP-0509; ASM-0701), and X8 is the rerun guard of the workflow kit.

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the published DP04 record read, the treatment contract and the guarantee contract with their fakes, on the tables and views of the other P1 stories; needs no live rwb-case or rwb-guarantee to start |
| Negotiable | The activity names, the page size and the workflow ID derivation are this story's choice; the window, the link check, the count check and the stamp rule are fixed |
| Valuable | The Epic 3 settlement, restructure and deed-in-lieu screens read one checked place, owned by the service that publishes the data products |
| Estimable | One workflow, four activities, two repositories, one record-read controller branch and one count check |
| Small | Finished inside two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on synthetic treatments, claims and ACE rows through stub contracts, plus one component test of the record read |

```gherkin
  Scenario: AC8 A change at the end of the business date (legacy RWB-E2-010 AC8)
    Given treatment "TRT-SYN-0601" changed at 2026-12-14T23:59:59+07:00 and treatment "TRT-SYN-0602" changed at 2026-12-15T00:00:00+07:00

```

**Target reading.** Every assertion above keeps its legacy wording; what changes is where it runs, who produces the fact and how it is reached. The stage 2 step of JOB-02 is no longer a step of `rwb-case`'s `DailyCaseRun`: in the target it is `Stage2ProductWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, started by this service's own `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` (DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 15, "Workflow: AceIngestCheck, reconciliation" and the `snapshot(page)` activity). The workflow writes `dp_treatment` and `dp_guarantee_claim` in schema `rwb_source_data` (DP-01; ownership ruling: the dated DP04 copies are P1's, built from the live facts of S2 and S3 and read-only for reporting; ASM-0080). The contract number, contract date and plan terms of AC1 are read live from `recovery.v_ace_account` and `recovery.v_ace_plan` through this service's own ACE read contract and are never copied (DP-05). The treatment facts of AC1, AC2, AC5, AC7 and AC8 come through the treatment entity contract `RWB-P3-E2004-CON` (C), reached one hop with a 2 s timeout and faked, so `TreatmentQuery` and `TreatmentQuery.countActive()` in the legacy lines are the changed-window read and the active-count read of that contract, and `TreatmentQuery returns an error` in AC5 is the error answer of its fake. The guarantee claim facts of AC2 and AC4 come through the guarantee contract of rwb-guarantee, which the Work Package does not list as a C dependency (GAP-0509; ASM-0701); `GuaranteeClaimQuery` of the legacy lines is that contract's changed-window read, and the case-not-found check of AC4 is the case-existence answer of rwb-case's case contract, faked with the same gap and assumption. The DP04 access check of AC3 is this service's own `RWB-P1-E1016-CON` (H), and the freshness stamp of AC1 returns through RWB-P1-E1015-APP (H) as a `DataProductFreshness` record of the record read. The DP04 read of AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC4 is the DP04 branch of `GET /data-products/{productCode}/records`, whose shape is declared by `RWB-P1-E2010-CON` and which shares the components of `RWB-P1-E1016-CON`, so `GET /data-products/DP04/records?caseId=` of the legacy line is that operation on base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` with `productCode` DP04. The per-service Flyway sequence of this service carries the two snapshot tables (DP-15), reference data supplies the status lists (DP-07), and every screen reaches the read through gateway-bff (DP-19). No legacy line is dropped or reworded; the three mock Givens above are the only added lines, and each names the contract its block consumes.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | DP04 holds treatments and guarantee claims from the Workbench, and contract and plan facts read from v_ace_account and v_ace_plan, with one system of record and one owner for each part | REQ-RDF-014; data_product DP04; sys_objects |
| BR2 | No Workbench table copies a contract, a plan or an account; the views are read at request time | D-RCV-35 U1; tier map section 9 |
| BR3 | Every snapshot row links to an existing case, or it is held on the break list and retried with the next build | DQ load check "References" |
| BR4 | The product is stamped for the day only when the active count matches the owning module, with zero tolerance | DL25; RWB-E1-011 hold rule (FEAT-RDF-13) |
| BR5 | A role reads DP04 only through an access row in force | data_product_access; REQ-RDF-010 |
| BR6 | Credit approval for a restructure is recorded on the case by the officer; there is no interface to NLEADS | INT-26; DL12 |
| BR7 | Plan installments come from the ACE plan published calculation | DF-ACE-174 source ACE; INT-34 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1 and BR2 are this story's: the two snapshot tables hold the Workbench facts and no `contract_no` or `contract_date` column exists, because the contract and plan facts are read from the views at request time (DP-01, DP-05). The views themselves and the 30-view read path are RWB-P1-E1069-APP's, and this story reads them in-process and copies nothing. BR3 is the link check of `writeDp04Page`; the break list is this service's own data quality record. BR4 is the `checkActiveCount` activity and its hold; the tolerance and the expected-by time are data rows of `data_product` and decisions, never constants (DP-07). BR5 is served by the access check of RWB-P1-E1016-CON on the record read, so AC3 asserts the published answer and not a local guard. BR6 and BR7 are unchanged business facts: the approval is recorded on the case by the officer, and the installments come from the ACE plan through `recovery.v_ace_plan`.

##### 9. State transitions

No case status changes: the story changes the DP04 freshness status (LOADED or STALE) through the stamp owner, and the state of the `Stage2ProductWorkflow` execution of a business date (RUNNING, COMPLETED or FAILED).

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| no execution for D | `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` consumed | The business date is inside the freshness window | `Stage2ProductWorkflow` RUNNING for D |
| RUNNING | treatments and claims written | The link check and the count check pass | COMPLETED and DP04 stamped for D |
| RUNNING | count difference or contract error | The check fails or the contract does not answer | FAILED or HELD, DP04 not stamped, break listed |
| FAILED | rerun for D | The workflow of D is not running | RUNNING again, rows replaced by record ID |
| COMPLETED | a change after the window | The treatment changed on D+1 | A new execution for D+1; nothing is rewritten for D |

The freshness states LOADED and STALE are the stamp owner's and are read here; the rows of `dp_treatment` and `dp_guarantee_claim` have no state machine of their own.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The recovery squad (RW-TRIBE) | Writes the workflow, the four activities, the two repositories, the count check and the DP04 branch of the record read |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Owns DP04; reads the catalog entry and the breaks; confirms the system of record of each part |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-GUARANT, RW-CREDITAD | Read DP04 for cases in scope, through the access row in force |
| RW-COE, RW-AUDIT | Read DP04 for all cases |
| RW-PHONECOL and roles with no DP04 access row | May not read DP04 |
| rwb-case (P3) | Owns the treatment entity and answers the treatment contract this story consumes |
| rwb-guarantee (S3) | Owns the guarantee claim record and answers its contract; returns no claim until its own wave |
| The platform workflow owner | Owns the `rwb-source-data` task queue, the namespace and the worker registration this workflow runs on |
| No approval level from the delegation of authority applies | The story takes no business decision; it builds a data product |

No credential and no personal name appears in the workflow input, the activity payloads or the logs, which carry business dates, record IDs, codes and counts only.

treatment and guarantee_claim fields are read through the treatment contract of rwb-case and the guarantee contract of rwb-guarantee, not from their tables; the guarantee contract is outside the C dependencies of the plan (GAP-0509; ASM-0701). `recovery.v_ace_account` and `recovery.v_ace_plan` are read through this service's own ACE read contract and never copied. `data_product_load` is written by the freshness story on this story's call and not by a writer of its own (RWB-P1-E1015-APP). Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-source-data (P1); base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies the DP04 branch of one operation whose shape is declared by RWB-P1-E2010-CON and shares the components of RWB-P1-E1016-CON; the branches of the other 13 data products belong to their own stories.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/data-products/{productCode}/records` (the DP04 branch) | `DataProductRecordPage` with `items` of `DataProductRecord` (`recordId`, `entity`, `fields` of `FieldValue`), `freshness` of `DataProductFreshness`, `page`, `size`, `total`; `productCode` DP04; query `caseId`, `page`, `size` | Case record R plus a DP04 access row in force, through the access check of RWB-P1-E1016-CON | Idempotent by product, case and page |

The errors are 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 with MSG-P4-003 and 503 with MSG-GEN-006; the 400 and 401 of the shared envelope are declared by RWB-P1-E1016-CON and their texts are not restated here. The DP04 rows carry the snapshot fields of section 11 and the contract and plan facts read live from the two views; the record and page property names are those of `DataProductRecordPage`, `DataProductRecord` and `FieldValue` in the API Specification v4.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/treatments` and the changed-window and active-count reads of the contract | P3 rwb-case (`RWB-P3-E2004-CON`) | The treatments of the window, the changed-window read and the active count; operation names are fixed by that contract; faked | DP-11; one hop, 2 s timeout |
| GET | the guarantee claim read of the rwb-guarantee contract | S3 rwb-guarantee | The TCG claims changed in the window; faked; the contract is not in the Work Package's C list, so its name and shape are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0509; ASM-0701) | DP-11; one hop, 2 s timeout |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case (case contract) | The case-existence answer of the link check; faked and test-only, since the case reference arrives on each treatment row | DP-11; one hop, 2 s timeout |
| (interface) | `AceSourceReadRepository` over `recovery.v_ace_account` and `recovery.v_ace_plan` | P1 rwb-source-data (`RWB-P1-E1069-APP`) | The contract number, contract date and plan terms, read at request time and never written | DP-05; in-process in this service, published to others as the ACE read contract |

The guarantee claim read is the one consumed contract the Work Package does not list, and it is faked so the build never waits for S3 (GAP-0509; ASM-0701). The case-existence answer is reached through the case contract of rwb-case with the same gap and assumption, because the treatment contract returns the case reference but not the case itself. No other service is called: the status lists arrive as reference data through the keeper library (DP-07), and the ACE facts are read in this service's own views (DP-01, DP-05).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The topic of the service is `rwb.source-data.events.v1` with event names `rwb.source-data.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and its two events `AceDataReady` and `AceDataLate` belong to RWB-P1-E1015-APP. This story publishes no event and writes no outbox row of its own.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | Starts `Stage2ProductWorkflow` for the business date and the source; a redelivery starts no second run |

The event is this service's own and is consumed through the inbox of the outbox library, so the workflow start is idempotent by the cloud event id and the business date.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Stage2ProductWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per business date, workflow ID derived from the business date and the source | `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: business date, source system, freshness summary; started by `AceDataReady`; run record with the outcome and the break references |
| `snapshot(page)` | Activity | `rwb-source-data` | The window [start of D, start of D+1); page number and size in; the treatment and claim rows of the page out |
| `writeDp04Page` | Activity | `rwb-source-data` | The rows of one page; the link check, the break path and one transaction per page that upserts by record ID and business date |
| `checkActiveCount` | Activity | `rwb-source-data` | The active count of the contract and the count written for D; a match or a break with the check text |
| `stampDp04` | Activity | `rwb-source-data` | The business date and product DP04; a call to the freshness stamp of RWB-P1-E1015-APP on a match |

The workflow and activity names are a target design choice and are fixed by no source document (GAP-0510; ASM-0702). The retry policy is the workflow kit's, and the rerun of a business date is refused while the execution of that date is running (MSG-P2-006).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The workflow is event-started from `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` and owns no Temporal Schedule and no legacy Quartz job; the freshness cut-off Schedules belong to RWB-P1-E1015-APP (DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44, JOB-02 starts from AceDataReady).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dp_treatment` | `rwb_source_data` | P1 | Created by this story's Flyway version and written by `writeDp04Page`, keyed by record ID and business date; holds no `contract_no` and no `contract_date` column |
| `dp_guarantee_claim` | `rwb_source_data` | P1 | Created by the same version and written by `writeDp04Page`, keyed by record ID and business date |
| `data_product_load` | `rwb_source_data` | P1 | Not written directly: the DP04 row is written by the freshness stamp on this story's call (RWB-P1-E1015-APP) |
| `data_product`, `data_product_access` | `rwb_source_data` | P1 | Read for the expected-by time, the owner role and the access row; no row is written here |

No table of another service is read and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01). The treatment and guarantee tables of S2 and S3 are never named in SQL; their facts arrive through their contracts.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| RWB-P3-E2004-CON treatment fake | The changed-window read and the active count | 40 active treatments and 12 plans with 9 approvals; a contract error; an active count of 41 against 40 rows; a treatment changed at 23:59:59 and one at 00:00:00 |
| rwb-guarantee guarantee claim fake | The changed-window claim read | 5 TCG claims for existing cases; one claim for case ID "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000997"; an empty list until S3 is built; a contract error |
| RWB-P1-E1016-CON access fake | The DP04 access answer | A granted answer for the DP04 reading roles; a refused answer for RW-PHONECOL on DP04 |
| rwb-case case-existence fake | The link check of AC4 | The known cases of the fixture; no case for "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000997" |
| ACE account and plan fixture | `recovery.v_ace_account` and `recovery.v_ace_plan` | Rows for the 40 accounts of the fixture with `contract_no`, `contract_date`, `plan_ref`, `installments`, `recommended_installment` and `booked_at`; an account with no plan |

The treatment, guarantee and access fakes are the published contracts of those stories; the ACE fixture stands in for the views of RWB-P1-E1069-APP; and the case-existence fake is the test-only answer of rwb-case's case contract, recorded with GAP-0509 and ASM-0701.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 operation branch on `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` | 3 consumed reads (treatment, guarantee claim, case existence) | OpenAPI 3.1, one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream (DP-11) |
| Kafka | None | 1 event (`rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1`) | Own topic, own event, inbox dedupe by cloud event id |
| Temporal | `Stage2ProductWorkflow` and 4 activities on `rwb-source-data` | None | Namespace `rwb-recovery`; no Schedule |
| File | None | None | No file is read or written |
| SQL view | None | `recovery.v_ace_account` and `recovery.v_ace_plan` | SELECT only, in-process, never copied (DP-05) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata`, modules `stage2` and `read`, with the published types in `...sourcedata.api`. Service base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, schema `rwb_source_data`, topic `rwb.source-data.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-10 is the pattern this story is built on: the stage 2 step becomes an event-started workflow of this service. DP-01 and DP-05 are the ownership ruling and the live read of the ACE facts; DP-11 is the treatment and guarantee contracts with their fakes; DP-15 carries the two snapshot tables on the service sequence; DP-07 supplies the status lists; DP-13 and DP-19 fix the base and the screen path.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `Stage2ProductWorkflow` | Workflow | One execution per business date; the window, the page loop, the link check, the count check and the stamp call |
| `snapshot(page)` | Activity | The changed-window reads of the treatment and guarantee contracts, page by page |
| `writeDp04Page` | Activity | The link check, the break path and the upsert of `dp_treatment` and `dp_guarantee_claim` |
| `checkActiveCount` | Activity | The active-count comparison and its hold |
| `stampDp04` | Activity | The call to the freshness stamp of RWB-P1-E1015-APP |
| `DpTreatmentRepository`, `DpGuaranteeClaimRepository` | Repository | Upsert by record ID and business date, in schema `rwb_source_data` |
| `Dp04ReadService` | Service | The DP04 branch of the record read: the snapshot rows joined to the contract and plan facts, masked by the access answer |
| `Migrations` | Migration | The two snapshot tables on the per-service Flyway sequence, without a contract column |

**Database.** `dp_treatment` and `dp_guarantee_claim` hold the Workbench snapshot per business date. The legacy story dropped `dp_treatment.contract_no` and `dp_treatment.contract_date` because a contract is read from `v_ace_account` and never copied; in the target those columns are never created (BR2). No table holds a plan, a contract or an account row. The `data_product_load` row of DP04 is written through RWB-P1-E1015-APP.

**Configuration and reference data.** The DP04 row in `data_product` carries the owner role, the refresh cycle and the expected-by time of 08:00, which the legacy story assumed from DL11 and no source document fixes for DP04 (GAP-0511; ASM-0703). The DP04 access rows are the data steward's and are read through RWB-P1-E1016-CON. The status lists arrive as reference data (DP-07).

**Build steps**

1. The Flyway version with `dp_treatment` and `dp_guarantee_claim`, their keys on record ID and business date, and no contract column (DP-15).
2. `Stage2ProductWorkflow` and its input record, registered on `rwb-source-data`, with the workflow ID derived from the business date and the source (AC6).
3. `snapshot(page)` against the treatment and guarantee fakes, with the window [start of D, start of D+1) (AC1, AC2, AC8).
4. `writeDp04Page` with the link check, the References break and the upsert per page (AC4, AC6).
5. `checkActiveCount` and the hold of the stamp on a difference (AC7).
6. `stampDp04` through the freshness story, and the FAILED path of a contract error with the previous rows kept (AC5).
7. `Dp04ReadService` and the DP04 branch of the record read, with the live view read, the access answer and the freshness record (AC1, AC3).
8. Tests for AC1 to AC8 against the fakes and the ACE fixture.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.dataengine.stage2-products`.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the workflow starts from a synthetic `AceDataReady` in SIT, `dp_treatment` and `dp_guarantee_claim` hold the rows of the business date, the DP04 stamp is LOADED on a count match and absent on a difference, the DP04 read answers with the live contract and plan facts, and the DP04 catalog entry shows in `GET /admin/data-products` in SIT.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without a DP04 access row | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P1-001 | DP04 stale after a failed step | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P1-002 | Count check break held the publish | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | TreatmentQuery or GuaranteeClaimQuery unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P2-006 | Rerun while JOB-02 is running | {job} is already running. Wait for it to finish before you rerun it. |

The five texts are the legacy texts carried unchanged; MSG-P1-001 and MSG-P1-002 are raised by the freshness story and read here, MSG-GEN-006 names the system of the failed contract, and MSG-P4-002 is the access answer of RWB-P1-E1016-CON. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-45 Data quality (Epic 2): state Loading while the list arrives; state Breaks shows the DP04 References breaks and the active-count break for the data steward. The case record view SCR-03 shows the DP04 data for roles with an access row in force. The settlement, restructure and deed-in-lieu screens that read DP04 come in Epic 3. Every one of them reaches this service through the gateway-bff composite route, which calls rwb-case and rwb-source-data in parallel, one hop each (DP-19); the screen field list and the composite route specification belong to the platform edge story and the screen owners, and this story fixes the service side of the answer only.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the product code DP04, the owner role, the expected-by time and the access rows are data rows of `data_product`, `data_product_access` and the reference data, never constants (DP-07).
- No personal data in logs, events, workflow inputs or the fixture: the rows carry record IDs, case IDs, codes, dates and amounts only; test data is synthetic.
- No copy of ACE data: the contract number, contract date and plan terms are read from `recovery.v_ace_account` and `recovery.v_ace_plan` at request time, and the two snapshot tables hold no contract column (DP-01, DP-05).
- No read of another service's table: the treatment facts arrive through `RWB-P3-E2004-CON` and the claim facts through the guarantee contract, both with a fake (DP-11).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views, and only this service names the views (DP-05).
- The workflow loads no business value from a source outside the contracts: every fact of a row is either the contract's or the view's, and the job runs from the freshness event rather than a fixed clock (DP-10).
- An applied migration is never edited: a correction to a snapshot table is a new version on the service sequence (DP-15).
- No call to NLEADS or the Thai Credit Guarantee Corporation: their results arrive as facts recorded on the case and on the claim (BR6).

##### 1. Story

As a **recovery developer on the treatment service (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **the treatment side of the stage 2 data product: a changed-window read and an active-count read on `/api/recovery/treatment/v1` that hand the DP04 build of rwb-source-data exactly the treatment facts DP04 holds — the case, the treatment type, the approval level, the installments, the outcome and the plan facts — over a half-open business-date window, with every code labelled from the reference data of the day, and with no contract number, contract date, plan or account ever stored or read in this service**, so that **the stage 2 product is built from the service that owns the treatment record, the settlement, restructure and deed-in-lieu screens read one checked place, and nothing is copied out of ACE**.

This story is the secondary slice of legacy RWB-E2-010 and the treatment half of the split. It owns:

- the changed-window read `GET /treatments` and the active-count read `GET /treatments/active-count` on base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1` (DP-13), which replace the in-process `TreatmentQuery.changedBetween` and `countActive` of the legacy stage 2 step with a contract and a fake (DP-11);
- the DP04 field set the answer carries from the `treatment` row, with the reference-data version of every list (DP-01, DP-07);
- one Flyway version on this service's own sequence that adds the index the window read needs and changes no applied version (DP-15);
- the scope and right rule of the two reads, and the statement that the contract and plan facts are not this service's to serve (DP-05).

It does not own: the eight legacy acceptance criteria and the nine legacy test cases, the `dp_treatment` and `dp_guarantee_claim` copies, the link check, the count check, the DP04 freshness stamp, the break list, the catalog entry and the rerun, which are RWB-P1-E2010-APP and its contract RWB-P1-E2010-CON; the treatment entity, its write path and the plan timers, which are RWB-S2-E2004-APP; the guarantee claim facts, which are RWB-S3-E2010-APP; the contract number, contract date and plan terms, which stay in `recovery.v_ace_account` and `recovery.v_ace_plan`; the screens and their composite routes (DP-19); the deployment of the read (RWB-P1-E2010-OPS covers the build that calls it).

##### 2. Business rationale

From Epic 3 the settlement, restructure and deed-in-lieu screens need each case's treatments, plan terms, loan contracts and guarantee claims in one checked place (REQ-RDF-014), read only through a data-product access row (REQ-RDF-010). The target keeps two things apart that the legacy step held together: the live treatment record stays with S2 in `rwb_treatment`, and the dated DP04 copy stays with P1 as the data engine, built from the live facts and read-only for reporting (DP-01).

The legacy step called the treatment module in process, so the copy and the record moved together. In the target the copy is built by `Stage2ProductWorkflow` of rwb-source-data, which asks the owner over one contract for the treatments changed in the business-date window and for the number of active treatments it reconciles against (DP-10, DP-11). Nothing of ACE crosses that seam: the contract number, the contract date and the plan terms are read by rwb-source-data from the `v_ace_*` views at request time, never copied and never re-exposed here (DP-05).

What is left to S2 is a narrow read with three duties: the boundary the legacy step used (a change at 23:59:59 belongs to the day, one second later to the next), the field set DP04 holds for a treatment, and a count whose rule is data, not code (BR4). The volumes do not change: about 3,000 restructure accounts a month reach the restructure process (NFR-005), and every treatment of the day must be in the copy before the Epic 3 screens open.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P1-E2010-CON is published: it declares the DP04 record read and the page shape the DP04 build answers with, and this story builds the two reads against its fake, so the dependency never blocks (Contract dependency; DP-11).
- The two reads are published on this service's base, because the `treatment` table and its REST owner are S2's, although RWB-P1-E2010-APP names the changed window and the active count under the case contract of RWB-P3-E2004-CON; the assumption and the conflict row are ASM-4458 and GAP-2695, and the consumer adapts its fake, not its logic, if the conflict is resolved the other way.
- The `treatment` table of schema `rwb_treatment` exists with DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033 and the seven standard record columns of TSD S2 T3.0, and this service's Flyway sequence is at the version that carries the platform library tables; the Work Package lists no build dependency, so the table and the platform libraries are taken as present (ASM-4461; DP-01, DP-15).
- The reference-data read of rwb-case for LOV-TREATMENT, LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL and LOV-TRT-OUTCOME reaches the service through the client library, with a version and a fake (DP-07).
- The platform guard library that answers a role's right on a capability area is on the service template, so the two reads declare the right "Treatment and offer R" and nothing else (ASM-4461).
- The gateway-bff composite route that serves SCR-03 Case record from the case read and this service's reads is published; no screen calls this service directly (DP-19; RWB-PLT-N001-CON).
- The active-state rule of the count read is a parameter row of the parameters contract of rwb-case, with its version, and no local constant (ASM-4459; DP-07 for the lists, DP-11 for the read).
- Feature switch `rwb.treatment.stage2-read` exists; its default is off in the non-production environments until the DP04 build of rwb-source-data is wired to the operation (ASM-4461).

##### 4. Flow

1. The `snapshot(page)` activity of `Stage2ProductWorkflow` in rwb-source-data calls `GET /treatments?changedFrom=<start of D>&changedTo=<start of D+1>&page=1&size=<page size>` on base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1`, one hop, 2 s timeout (DP-10, DP-11, DP-13).
2. The controller refuses an empty or inverted window, a page below one and a size above the declared maximum before a statement runs (X1, X2).
3. The guard answers the right "Treatment and offer R" for the caller; a role without it is refused, and a service identity is authorised by its own right row (X3; rights are data).
4. The read selects from `treatment` of `rwb_treatment` only, where `updated_at` is at or after `changedFrom` and strictly before `changedTo`, ordered by `updated_at` and `id`, and cuts the requested page (DP-01, DP-15).
5. `TreatmentFactsAssembler` builds the DP04 field set: the treatment and case IDs, the type, the proposer, the proposed date, the offer and haircut amounts, the installments, the validity date, the approval level, the booked date, the outcome and its date, the first due date, the installment amount, the installments paid and the shortfall.
6. `ReferenceLabelResolver` answers each label with the version of the reference data of the day and stamps that version on the page; a missing version fails the page rather than answering a bare code (X6; DP-07).
7. The answer carries the items, the window, `page`, `size` and a `total` computed with the caller's scope applied, and the consumer asks for the next page until `total` is reached.
8. The consumer then calls `GET /treatments/active-count` and compares the number with the active rows it wrote for D; the zero-tolerance hold on a difference is its decision and is not taken here (BR6).
9. Both reads write nothing — no row, decision record, outbox row or state change — and a repeat of the same request returns the same page (BR8).
10. No ACE view and no other service is called on this path: the contract and plan facts are named by the DP04 answer of rwb-source-data, not by this service (DP-05).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | `changedFrom` or `changedTo` is missing, or the window is empty or inverted | 400; no statement runs and no partial page is returned | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X2 | `page` below one, or `size` above the declared maximum | 400 with the accepted range named | MSG-GEN-003 | AC4 |
| X3 | A role without Treatment and offer R, or a caller outside the scope of the rows | 403; the refusal is logged with the role and the operation, and no row is disclosed | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |
| X4 | A page of a multi-page scan is requested while a treatment of the window is being changed | The changed row appears once, under its later `updated_at`, and no row is repeated across pages | None | AC4 |
| X5 | The treatment store or the connection pool is unavailable | 503; the consumer's step fails on its side and the copy of the day is not stamped | MSG-GEN-006 | AC7 |
| X6 | The reference-data version of a list cannot be resolved | 503; the page is not answered with unversioned codes | MSG-GEN-006 | AC7 |
| X7 | A caller asks this service for a contract number, a contract date or a plan term | No such field exists in the answer and the request is refused as an unsupported query parameter | MSG-GEN-001 | AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Day 1: the table is in this service's schema, the reference data arrives through a fake and the DP04 contract is faked; no live rwb-source-data, rwb-case or ACE view is needed |
| Negotiable | The operation names, the page shape, the index name, the parameter name of the active rule and the flag are this story's choice; the field set, the half-open window, the rights and the messages are fixed |
| Valuable | The stage 2 product is built from the owner of the treatment record, with no copy of a contract, a plan or an account |
| Estimable | One controller, two read services, one assembler, one reference-label resolver, one index, one migration |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion of section 7 is one automated test on the window boundary, the field set, the count, the paging, the right or the absence of a foreign fact |

These seven criteria are new for the secondary slice and test only the treatment side; AC1 to AC8 of RWB-E2-010 and their nine test cases stay with RWB-P1-E2010-APP (GAP-2695).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | DP04 holds the treatments from the Workbench and the contract and plan facts from `v_ace_account` and `v_ace_plan`, with one system of record and one owner for each part; this service serves its part of the treatments only | REQ-RDF-014; legacy BR1; DP-05 |
| BR2 | No Workbench table copies a contract, a plan or an account, and this service stores no such column and reads no such view | legacy BR2; DP-01, DP-05 |
| BR3 | The window is half-open: a change at 23:59:59+07:00 of day D belongs to D and a change one second later belongs to D+1 | legacy AC8; BR2 of this story |
| BR4 | The set of states the active count includes is a parameter row with a version, never a constant in code or in the migration | legacy BR4; ASM-4459 |
| BR5 | A role reads the treatment facts only with the right in force and only inside its scope | legacy BR5; REQ-RDF-010 |
| BR6 | The active count is compared with the rows written for D with zero tolerance, and a difference holds the publish: the comparison and the hold are the consumer's, this service returns the number only | legacy BR4; DL25 |
| BR7 | Every code in the answer carries the version of the reference data it was labelled from | DP-07; FSD S2 BR-S2-001 |
| BR8 | The two reads are read-only and repeatable: no row, decision record, outbox row or state is written by them | legacy section 9; section 12.3 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status, no treatment state and no DP04 freshness status: the LOADED and STALE statuses of a data product, and the state of the stage 2 step on the run, are rwb-source-data's and are held by RWB-P1-E1015-APP's freshness stamp and by the run of `Stage2ProductWorkflow`. The treatment state vocabulary of section 9 of RWB-S2-E2004-APP is read by this story and never moved by it.

| rwb-source-data, through its service identity | Reads the changed window and the active count for the DP04 build (Treatment and offer R; ASM-4460) |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Owns the DP04 product of rwb-source-data; reads the treatment facts and the breaks of the copy |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-GUARANT, RW-CREDITAD | Read the treatment facts for cases in scope |
| RW-COE, RW-AUDIT | Read the treatment facts for all cases |
| RW-TEAMMGR | Reads the treatment facts and the exception queue of its team |
| RW-PHONECOL and every role with no Treatment and offer right | May not read either operation |

The access rows of the data product itself are not this story's: they are held by rwb-source-data and checked there (legacy section 10; REQ-RDF-010).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1`; owner rwb-treatment; both operations are additive to the two of RWB-S2-E2004-APP; right "Treatment and offer R" from TSD S2 T6.1; every operation applies scope and answers the platform error envelope.

| Operation | Purpose | Right | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET /treatments?changedFrom=&changedTo=&page=&size= | The treatments changed in the half-open window, paged | Treatment and offer R | Ordered by `updated_at`, `id`; 400 on an empty or inverted window and on a size above the maximum; 503 with MSG-GEN-006 when the store or a list version is unavailable |
| GET /treatments/active-count | The active treatments of the business date | Treatment and offer R | Answers the number, the business date and the version of the active-state rule; 40 for the fixture of AC3 |

The operation names, the page shape, the maximum size and the parameter name of the active rule are a target design choice fixed by no source document (GAP-2696; ASM-4459). A refused caller is refused with MSG-P4-002 and an out-of-scope row is never disclosed; the two operations are declared in the OpenAPI 3.1 document of this service and their fake is the one in section 12.8.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Owner | Purpose | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| the reference-data read for LOV-TREATMENT, LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL and LOV-TRT-OUTCOME | rwb-case (P3) | the members, the labels and the version of the three lists | one hop, 2 s, GET retried once, breaker (DP-07, DP-11); operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2696; ASM-4459) |

No other service is called: the contract and plan facts are not read here, and the case reference arrives on each treatment row.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This story writes no outbox row and publishes nothing on `rwb.treatment.events.v1`; the treatment announcements are RWB-S2-E2004-APP's, and the DP04 build is started by rwb-source-data's own event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The window is driven by the consumer's workflow, not by an event of this service (DP-10).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. This story runs on the API deployment of rwb-treatment only: the window is one call of the `snapshot(page)` activity of `Stage2ProductWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and `TreatmentWorkflow` on queue `rwb-treatment` belongs to RWB-S2-E2004-APP (DP-10).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The legacy JOB-02 stage 2 step leaves no Quartz job, no Spring Batch job and no Temporal Schedule in this service: the daily trigger is the event-started workflow of rwb-source-data (DP-10).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| treatment | rwb_treatment | Read only in this story; this story adds `ix_treatment_updated_at` on (`updated_at`, `id`) for the window read and changes no other object |

No table of another service is read, and `dp_treatment`, `dp_guarantee_claim` and `data_product_load` are not created, read or written here (DP-01).

| Fake | Answers | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| treatment read fake | the two operations of section 12.1, with the fixtures of section 7 and the 503 cases of X5 and X6 | the app tests of this story and the DP04 build of RWB-P1-E2010-APP |
| DP04 page-request fake | a `snapshot(page)` call for business date 2026-12-14 with a page size of 15, and a second page | AC1, AC4 |
| reference-data fake | the three lists with version "REF-2026.12", an empty list and a timeout | AC2, AC7 |
| guard fake | the right answer of RW-RESTRUCT, RW-CASEOWN and the service identity, and a refusal for RW-PHONECOL | AC5 |

| REST consumed | 1 | the reference-data read of rwb-case, one hop, 2 s (DP-07, DP-11) |
| Kafka published | None | no outbox row, no event |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.treatment`, module `stage2` beside the `record` and `plan` modules of RWB-S2-E2004-APP.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Stage2TreatmentReadController | REST | The two operations of section 12.1, the checks of X1, X2 and X7 and the problems of section 14 |
| ChangedWindowService | Service | Builds the half-open window, applies the scope, orders by `updated_at` and `id` and cuts the page |
| ActiveCountService | Service | Reads the active-state rule with its version and counts the included states in one statement |
| TreatmentFactsAssembler | Service | Builds the DP04 field set of AC2 from the row and nothing else |
| ReferenceLabelResolver | Service | Answers every label with the version of the day and fails the page when the version is missing |
| TreatmentReadRepository | Repository | Reads `treatment` of `rwb_treatment` only, never another schema |

**Database.** One Flyway version on the service sequence, `V<next>__rwb_treatment_ix_updated_at.sql`, which adds `ix_treatment_updated_at` on (`updated_at`, `id`); it changes no applied version, no column and no table, because the contract and plan facts are not held here (DP-01, DP-05, DP-15).

**Configuration and reference data.** The active-state rule is a parameter row with a version (states assumed from the outcome vocabulary of LOV-TRT-OUTCOME; ASM-4459); LOV-TREATMENT, LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL and LOV-TRT-OUTCOME are reference-data rows with a version, read through the contract (DP-07). The page size default and maximum are named chart values, not constants.

**Build steps**

1. Write the migration and prove that it adds one index, changes no column and names no other schema.
2. Build `TreatmentReadRepository` with the schema-boundary test that refuses a statement on another schema's table or on a `v_ace_*` view.
3. Build `ChangedWindowService` for the half-open window, the page cut and the stable order; build `ActiveCountService` and `TreatmentFactsAssembler`, and prove that no state and no list member is written in code.
4. Build `ReferenceLabelResolver` with the version stamp and the fail-closed answer of X6, then the controller with the scope and right rules of AC5.
5. Add the absence test of AC6, the paging test of AC4 and the tests of section 16 against the fakes of section 12.8.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.treatment.stage2-read` (ASM-4461). Off: the two operations answer 404 with MSG-P4-003 and the DP04 build is not wired.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass; a scan of 40 treatments on 2026-12-14 answers 40 distinct IDs over three pages, the count answers 40, and no statement, column or constant outside `rwb_treatment` is used.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A window parameter is missing or inverted, or an unsupported query parameter is sent | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | A page or a size is out of range | {field} is outside the accepted range {range}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The store or a reference-data version is unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-001 | The caller is not signed in | Sign in to continue. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Treatment and offer R calls either operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The feature switch is off, or a record is out of scope | The record was not found. |

For MSG-GEN-006 the {system} is "Treatment" for the store, as the legacy story used it, and the list code for a missing version; no consumer re-words a message text. The DP04 messages MSG-P1-001 and MSG-P1-002 belong to rwb-source-data and are not restated here.

No new screen. SCR-03 Case record shows the DP04 facts of a case and SCR-45 Data quality shows the DP04 breaks of the data steward, both composed by the gateway-bff route from the DP04 record read of rwb-source-data (DP-19). This service's two reads are called by the DP04 build and by no screen; SCR-14 Treatment record is unaffected and keeps the treatment entity of RWB-S2-E2004-APP.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code or in a migration: the active states, the page limits and every list member are data rows with a version (DP-07).
- No personal data in the answer, the logs or the tests beyond the treatment and case identifiers: the fixture carries amounts and codes, and no name, address, identity number or contact point.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views of rwb-source-data; this service reads no ACE table and no view, and re-exposes no contract or plan fact (DP-05).
- No read of another service's table and no foreign key across schemas; the only table of this story is `treatment` in `rwb_treatment` (DP-01).
- The reads write nothing: no state, no decision record and no outbox row on a read path.
- The reference-data version is stamped on every answer; an unversioned label fails the page instead of being served.
- The DP04 product, its access rows, its freshness stamp and its breaks stay with rwb-source-data; this service supplies the number the consumer reconciles with and takes no publish decision (BR6).

- AC1 to AC8 of RWB-E2-010, its nine test cases, the `dp_treatment` and `dp_guarantee_claim` copies, the link check, the active-count comparison, the break list, the DP04 stamp, the catalog entry and the rerun, which are RWB-P1-E2010-APP.
- The treatment entity, its write path, the plan facts and the plan timers, which are RWB-S2-E2004-APP.
- The guarantee claim facts of the stage 2 product, which are RWB-S3-E2010-APP.
- The contract number, contract date and plan terms of the ACE views, which rwb-source-data reads at request time.
- The access rows of DP04 and the data-product read of rwb-source-data (RWB-P1-E1016-CON), the freshness stamp (RWB-P1-E1015-APP) and the deployment of the DP04 build (RWB-P1-E2010-OPS).
- The screens, their composite routes and the deployment of this service (DP-19; RWB-PLT-N001-CON).
