##### 1. Story

As a **recovery developer on the guarantee service (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **the guarantee-claim side of the stage 2 data product: a changed-window read on `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` that hands the DP04 build of rwb-source-data exactly the claim facts DP04 holds for a guarantee claim — the case, the claim type, the claim deadline, the claimed amount, the filing date, the paid amount and the status — over a half-open business-date window, with both claim lists labelled from the reference data of the day, and with no contract number, contract date, plan or account ever stored or read in this service**, so that **the stage 2 product is built from the service that owns the claim record, the settlement, restructure and deed-in-lieu screens read one checked place, and nothing is copied out of ACE**.

This story is the secondary slice of legacy RWB-E2-010 and the guarantee half of the split. It owns:

- the changed-window read `GET /guarantee-claims` on base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` (DP-13), which replaces the in-process `GuaranteeClaimQuery.changedBetween` of the legacy stage 2 step with a contract and a fake (DP-11);
- the DP04 field set the answer carries from the `guarantee_claim` row, with the reference-data version of `LOV-CLAIM-TYPE` and `LOV-CLAIM-STATUS` (DP-01, DP-07);
- one Flyway version on this service's own sequence that adds the index the window read needs and changes no applied version (DP-15);
- the scope and right rule of the read, and the statement that the contract and plan facts are not this service's to serve (DP-05).

It does not own: the eight legacy acceptance criteria and the nine legacy test cases, the `dp_treatment` and `dp_guarantee_claim` copies, the case-link check, the active treatment count, the DP04 freshness stamp, the break list, the catalog entry and the rerun, which are RWB-P1-E2010-APP and its contract RWB-P1-E2010-CON; the treatment facts, which are RWB-S2-E2010-APP; the claim record itself, its preparation, its submission, its tracking, its negotiation and its close, which are the claim stories of this service (RWB-S3-E4013-APP to RWB-S3-E4019-APP); the contract number, contract date and plan terms, which stay in `recovery.v_ace_account` and `recovery.v_ace_plan`; the screens and their composite routes (DP-19); the deployment of the read, which follows the service deployment.

##### 2. Business rationale

From Epic 3 the settlement, restructure and deed-in-lieu screens need each case's treatments, plan terms, loan contracts and guarantee claims in one checked place (REQ-RDF-014), read only through a data-product access row (REQ-RDF-010). The target keeps two things apart that the legacy step held together: the live claim record stays with S3 in `rwb_guarantee`, and the dated DP04 copy stays with P1 as the data engine, built from the live facts and read-only for reporting (DP-01).

The legacy step called the guarantee module in process, so the copy and the record moved together, and the legacy story could say that "before it is built (Epic 4), the interface returns no claims" without saying who answers the call in between. In the target the copy is built by `Stage2ProductWorkflow` of rwb-source-data, which asks the owner over one contract for the claims changed in the business-date window (DP-10, DP-11). Nothing of ACE crosses that seam: the contract number, the contract date and the plan terms are read by rwb-source-data from the `v_ace_*` views at request time, never copied and never re-exposed here (DP-05).

What is left to S3 is a narrow read with three duties: the boundary the legacy step used (a change at 23:59:59 belongs to the day, one second later to the next), the field set DP04 holds for a claim, and a label with a version for every code, so that a claim type or a claim status is never served bare. The volumes are those of the claim book, not of the case book: a case carries one or a few claims, and the whole claim set of the day must be in the copy before the Epic 3 screens open.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P1-E2010-CON is published: it declares the DP04 record read, the page-request shape the DP04 build sends and the claim page it expects, and this story builds the read against its fake, so the dependency never blocks (Contract dependency; DP-11).
- The read is published on this service's base, because the `guarantee_claim` table and its REST owner are S3's: TSD S3 T-A.1 gives this service two operations, the claim create and the claim update, and no consumer read; the operation name, the path and the page parameters are fixed by no source document (GAP-2738; ASM-4550).
- The `guarantee_claim` table of schema `rwb_guarantee` exists with DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022 and the seven standard record columns of TSD S3 T3.0, and this service's Flyway sequence is at the version that carries the platform library tables; the Work Package lists no build dependency, so the table and the platform libraries are taken as present (ASM-4552; DP-01, DP-15).
- The reference-data read of rwb-case for `LOV-CLAIM-TYPE` and `LOV-CLAIM-STATUS` reaches the service through the client library, with a version and a fake (DP-07; ASM-4552).
- The platform guard library that answers a role's right on a capability area is on the service template, so the read declares the right "Treatment and offer R" of TSD S3 T6.1 and nothing else (ASM-4552).
- The gateway-bff composite route that serves SCR-03 Case record from the case read and the DP04 read of rwb-source-data is published; no screen calls this service directly (DP-19).
- The window is the half-open business-date window [start of D, start of D+1) in +07:00 over `guarantee_claim.updated_at`, and a claim changed at 23:59:59 of D belongs to D (ASM-4551).
- Feature switch `rwb.guarantee.stage2-read` exists; its default is off in the non-production environments until the DP04 build of rwb-source-data is wired to the operation (ASM-4550).
- No approval stop: the FSD S3 v3 and TSD S3 v2 documents carry status "In review" and the Epic 2 business requirements are not recorded as approved in this workspace, so the story starts on Day 1 at status Draft (realignment v1) (ASM-4556).

##### 4. Flow

1. The `snapshot(page)` activity of `Stage2ProductWorkflow` in rwb-source-data calls `GET /guarantee-claims?changedFrom=<start of D>&changedTo=<start of D+1>&page=1&size=<page size>` on base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`, one hop, 2 s timeout (DP-10, DP-11, DP-13).
2. The controller refuses an empty or inverted window, a page below one and a size above the declared maximum before a statement runs (X1, X2).
3. The guard answers the right "Treatment and offer R" for the caller; a role without it is refused, and a service identity is authorised by its own right row (X3; rights are data).
4. The read selects from `guarantee_claim` of `rwb_guarantee` only, where `updated_at` is at or after `changedFrom` and strictly before `changedTo`, ordered by `updated_at` and `id`, and cuts the requested page (DP-01, DP-15).
5. `ClaimFactsAssembler` builds the DP04 field set: the claim and case IDs, the claim type, the claim deadline, the claimed amount, the filing date, the paid amount and the status (DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022).
6. `ReferenceLabelResolver` answers the claim type and the status with the label and the version of the reference data of the day and stamps that version on the page; a missing version fails the page rather than answering a bare code (X6; DP-07).
7. The answer carries the items, the window, `page`, `size` and a `total` computed with the caller's scope applied, and the consumer asks for the next page until `total` is reached.
8. The consumer writes the rows it receives into `dp_guarantee_claim` in schema `rwb_source_data`, keyed by record ID and business date, and holds on its break list any row whose case does not resolve; both decisions are its own and are not taken here (BR6).
9. The read writes nothing — no row, decision record, outbox row or state change — and a repeat of the same request returns the same page (BR7).
10. No ACE view and no other service is called on this path: the contract and plan facts are named by the DP04 answer of rwb-source-data, not by this service (DP-05).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | `changedFrom` or `changedTo` is missing, or the window is empty or inverted | 400; no statement runs and no partial page is returned | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X2 | `page` below one, or `size` above the declared maximum | 400 with the accepted range named | MSG-GEN-003 | AC3 |
| X3 | A role without Treatment and offer R, or a caller outside the scope of the rows | 403; the refusal is logged with the role and the operation, and no row is disclosed | MSG-P4-002 | AC4 |
| X4 | A page of a multi-page scan is requested while a claim of the window is being changed | The changed row appears once, under its later `updated_at`, and no row is repeated across pages | None | AC3 |
| X5 | The claim store or the connection pool is unavailable | 503; the consumer holds the claim part of its page and does not stamp the copy of the day | MSG-GEN-006 | AC6 |
| X6 | The reference-data version of a list cannot be resolved | 503; the page is not answered with unversioned codes | MSG-GEN-006 | AC6 |
| X7 | A caller asks this service for a contract number, a contract date or a plan term | No such field exists in the answer and the request is refused as an unsupported query parameter | MSG-GEN-001 | AC5 |

X1, X2, X3 and the empty-answer path are the legacy step's own checks carried onto the read; X4 to X7 are the read's paths in the target. The stale-product path of the legacy story (MSG-P1-001) is the consumer's and is not restated here.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Day 1: the table is in this service's schema, the reference data arrives through a fake and the DP04 contract is faked; no live rwb-source-data, rwb-case or ACE view is needed |
| Negotiable | The operation name, the page shape, the index name, the maximum size and the flag are this story's choice; the field set, the half-open window, the rights and the messages are fixed |
| Valuable | The stage 2 product is built from the owner of the claim record, with no copy of a contract, a plan or an account |
| Estimable | One controller, one read service, one assembler, one reference-label resolver, one index, one migration |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion of section 7 is one automated test on the window boundary, the field set, the paging, the right or the absence of a foreign fact |

These six criteria are new for the secondary slice and test only the guarantee-claim side. AC1 to AC8 of RWB-E2-010 and their nine test cases stay with RWB-P1-E2010-APP, the primary slice: the `dp_guarantee_claim` copy, the References break of AC4, the treatment count of AC7 and the DP04 stamp of AC1 and AC5 are all that story's and are exercised there (GAP-2738; GAP-2739).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | DP04 holds the guarantee claims from the Workbench and the contract and plan facts from `v_ace_account` and `v_ace_plan`, with one system of record and one owner for each part; this service serves its part of the claims only | REQ-RDF-014; legacy BR1; DP-05 |
| BR2 | No Workbench table copies a contract, a plan or an account, and this service stores no such column, reads no such view and answers no such fact | legacy BR2; DP-01, DP-05 |
| BR3 | The window is half-open: a change at 23:59:59+07:00 of day D belongs to D and a change one second later belongs to D+1 | legacy AC8; ASM-4551 |
| BR4 | The claim facts DP04 holds are the record of the claim and never its outcome: the read answers the claim of the case as it stands and takes no decision on it | legacy BR1; FSD S3 A2.1 to A2.8 |
| BR5 | A role reads the claim facts only with the right in force and only inside its scope | legacy BR5; REQ-RDF-010 |
| BR6 | Every claim row DP04 holds links to an existing case, or it is held on the break list and retried with the next build; the link check is the consumer's, and this read answers the `case_id` of every claim in the window and resolves nothing | legacy BR3; GAP-2740; ASM-4555 |
| BR7 | The read is read-only and repeatable: no row, decision record, outbox row or state is written by it | legacy section 9; section 12.3 |
| BR8 | Every code in the answer carries the label and the version of the reference data of the day; a code is never served bare and no list member is written in code | DP-07; FSD S3 BR-S3-001 to BR-S3-008 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1 and BR2 are the two system-of-record statements of the legacy story, and they are why the claim facts are served here and the contract and plan facts are not. BR3 is the `updated_at` predicate of the statement. BR4 is why nothing of this story writes a claim status. BR5 is the scope clause and the guard. BR6 is the boundary to rwb-source-data: the answer names the case, the consumer checks it (GAP-2740). BR7 is why the read has no outbox row. BR8 is the reference-label resolver and the version stamp.

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status, no claim status and no DP04 freshness status: the LOADED and STALE statuses of a data product, and the state of the stage 2 step on the run, are rwb-source-data's and are held by the freshness stamp and by the run of `Stage2ProductWorkflow`. The claim status vocabulary of `LOV-CLAIM-STATUS` — PREPARING, FILED, DEFECT, PAID and REJECTED (TSD S3 T3.2) — is read by this story and never moved by it; the guaranteed claim's own state machine of 32 rules over 17 states (TSD S3 T4) belongs to the claim stories of this service, not to this read.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-source-data, through its service identity | Reads the changed window for the DP04 build (Treatment and offer R; ASM-4550) |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Owns the DP04 product of rwb-source-data; reads the claim facts and the breaks of the copy |
| RW-GUARANT, guarantee officer | Reads the claim facts for cases in scope (CRU in the matrix of TSD S3 T6.1) |
| RW-CASEOWN, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL, RW-CREDITAD | Read the claim facts for cases in scope |
| RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-TEAMMGR and the read-only roles of TSD S3 T6.1 | Read the claim facts for all cases or for their team |
| RW-PHONECOL and every role with no Treatment and offer right | May not read the operation |

The access rows of the data product itself are not this story's: they are held by rwb-source-data and checked there (legacy section 10; REQ-RDF-010). No credential and no personal name appears in the request or the answer, which carry claim and case identifiers, dates, amounts, codes and a version only.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1`; owner rwb-guarantee; this read is additive to the two operations of TSD S3 T-A.1 (`POST /cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims`, right C, and `PATCH /guarantee-claims/{claimId}`, right U), which are the claim stories' and are not restated here. Right "Treatment and offer R" from TSD S3 T6.1; the operation applies scope and answers the platform error envelope.

| Operation | Purpose | Right | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET /guarantee-claims?changedFrom=&changedTo=&page=&size= | The guarantee claims changed in the half-open window, paged | Treatment and offer R | Ordered by `updated_at`, `id`; 400 on an empty or inverted window and on a size above the maximum; 503 with MSG-GEN-006 when the store or a list version is unavailable; the answer carries each claim's `caseId`, so the consumer resolves the case itself |

The operation name, the path, the page shape, the maximum size and the parameter names are a target design choice fixed by no source document, and the ownership rows give this service two claim operations and no read (GAP-2738; ASM-4550). A refused caller is refused with MSG-P4-002 and an out-of-scope row is never disclosed; the operation is declared in the OpenAPI 3.1 document of this service and its fake is the one in section 12.8.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Owner | Purpose | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|
| the reference-data read for LOV-CLAIM-TYPE and LOV-CLAIM-STATUS | rwb-case (P3) | the members, the labels and the version of the two lists | one hop, 2 s, GET retried once, breaker (DP-07, DP-11); operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2738; ASM-4552) |

No other service is called: the contract and plan facts are not read here, and the case reference arrives on each claim row. The read consumes no case operation, because resolving the case is the consumer's check (BR6).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This story writes no outbox row and publishes nothing on `rwb.guarantee.events.v1`; the ownership rows give S3 zero events (TSD S3 T5.3, "None"), and the DP04 build is started by rwb-source-data's own event (ASM-4554).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The window is driven by the consumer's workflow, not by an event of this service (DP-10). The service's own inbox and rule loader are the template's and are not touched by this story.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. This story runs on the API deployment of rwb-guarantee only: the window is one call of the `snapshot(page)` activity of `Stage2ProductWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and `GuaranteeClaimWorkflow` on queue `rwb-guarantee` belongs to the claim stories of this service (DP-10). The read creates no workflow, signals none and starts none.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The legacy JOB-02 stage 2 step leaves no Quartz job, no Spring Batch job and no Temporal Schedule in this service: the daily trigger is the event-started workflow of rwb-source-data (DP-10), and the ownership rows give S3 zero jobs.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| guarantee_claim | rwb_guarantee | Read only in this story; this story adds `ix_guarantee_claim_updated_at` on (`updated_at`, `id`) for the window read and changes no other object |

No table of another service is read, and `dp_treatment`, `dp_guarantee_claim` and `data_product_load` are not created, read or written here (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Answers | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| guarantee claim read fake | the operation of section 12.1, with the fixtures of section 7 and the 503 cases of X5 and X6 | the app tests of this story and the DP04 build of RWB-P1-E2010-APP |
| DP04 page-request fake | a `snapshot(page)` call for business date 2026-12-14 with a page size of 2, and the following pages | AC1, AC3 |
| reference-data fake | LOV-CLAIM-TYPE and LOV-CLAIM-STATUS with version "REF-2026.12", an empty list and a timeout | AC2, AC6 |
| guard fake | the right answer of RW-GUARANT, RW-CASEOWN and the service identity, and a refusal for RW-PHONECOL | AC4 |

The claim read fake is the Day-1 unblocker of the consumer: RWB-P1-E2010-APP builds against it and its own C dependency never waits for this service (ASM-4550).

|---|---|---|

| REST consumed | 1 | the reference-data read of rwb-case, one hop, 2 s (DP-07, DP-11) |
| Kafka published | None | no outbox row, no event |
| Kafka consumed | None | the window is driven by the consumer's workflow |
| Temporal | None | no workflow and no activity in this service for this story |

| SQL view | None | no `v_ace_*` read: the ACE facts stay in rwb-source-data (DP-05) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.guarantee`, module `stage2` beside the `claim` and `workflow` modules of the claim stories.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_guarantee`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-11 and DP-13 are the pattern this story is built on: the in-process `GuaranteeClaimQuery` becomes one published read with a fake on this service's own base. DP-01 fixes the schema boundary and DP-05 the fact that no ACE fact is re-exposed here. DP-10 removes the job rather than moving it: the trigger is the consumer's event-started workflow and this service schedules nothing. DP-15 and DP-19 are one index and one composite route. DP-07, DP-10, DP-15 and DP-19 add four platform CON dependencies in the table; the reference-data client library, the workflow kit, the per-service Flyway baseline and the gateway route all arrive with the service template and the platform epics, the Work Package lists no build dependency, so the story is Day 1 against the published contracts and their fakes (ASM-4552; ASM-4554).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Stage2ClaimReadController | REST | The operation of section 12.1, the checks of X1, X2 and X7 and the problems of section 14 |
| ChangedWindowService | Service | Builds the half-open window, applies the scope, orders by `updated_at` and `id` and cuts the page |
| ClaimFactsAssembler | Service | Builds the DP04 field set of AC2 from the row and nothing else |
| ReferenceLabelResolver | Service | Answers the claim type and the status with the version of the day and fails the page when the version is missing |
| ClaimReadRepository | Repository | Reads `guarantee_claim` of `rwb_guarantee` only, never another schema |

**Database.** One Flyway version on the service sequence, `V<next>__rwb_guarantee_ix_updated_at.sql`, which adds `ix_guarantee_claim_updated_at` on (`updated_at`, `id`); it changes no applied version, no column and no table, because the contract and plan facts are not held here (DP-01, DP-05, DP-15).

**Configuration and reference data.** LOV-CLAIM-TYPE and LOV-CLAIM-STATUS are reference-data rows with a version, read through the contract (DP-07; ASM-4552); the page size default and maximum and the index name are named chart values, not constants (ASM-4550). The capability area "Treatment and offer" and its rights are access data of P4 read through the guard library.

**Build steps**

1. Write the migration and prove that it adds one index, changes no column and names no other schema.
2. Build `ClaimReadRepository` with the schema-boundary test that refuses a statement on another schema's table or on a `v_ace_*` view.
3. Build `ChangedWindowService` for the half-open window, the page cut and the stable order; build `ClaimFactsAssembler` and prove that no list member is written in code.
4. Build `ReferenceLabelResolver` with the version stamp and the fail-closed answer of X6, then the controller with the scope and right rules of AC4.
5. Add the absence test of AC5, the paging test of AC3 and the tests of section 16 against the fakes of section 12.8.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.guarantee.stage2-read` (ASM-4550). Off: the operation answers 404 with MSG-P4-003 and the DP04 build is not wired.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass; a scan of 5 claims on 2026-12-14 answers 5 distinct IDs over three pages, every claim type and status carries its label and the version of the day, and no statement, column or constant outside `rwb_guarantee` is used.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A window parameter is missing or inverted, or an unsupported query parameter is sent | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | A page or a size is out of range | {field} is outside the accepted range {range}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The store or a reference-data version is unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-001 | The caller is not signed in | Sign in to continue. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Treatment and offer R calls the operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The feature switch is off, or a record is out of scope | The record was not found. |

For MSG-GEN-006 the {system} is "Guarantee claim" for the store and the list code for a missing version; no consumer re-words a message text. The DP04 messages MSG-P1-001 and MSG-P1-002 belong to rwb-source-data and are not restated here. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No new screen. SCR-03 Case record shows the DP04 facts of a case and SCR-45 Data quality shows the DP04 breaks of the data steward, both composed by the gateway-bff route from the DP04 record read of rwb-source-data (DP-19). This service's read is called by the DP04 build and by no screen; SCR-17 Guarantee claim keeps the claim of the claim stories of this service and is unaffected, and its `Not due`, `due`, `submitted`, `paid` and `refused` labels are the screen's, not the read's.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code or in a migration: the page limits, the window bounds and every list member are data rows with a version (BR8; DP-07).
- No personal data in the answer, the logs or the tests beyond the claim and case identifiers: the fixture carries amounts, dates and codes, and no name, address, identity number or contact point.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views of rwb-source-data; this service reads no ACE table and no view, and re-exposes no contract or plan fact (DP-05).
- No read of another service's table and no foreign key across schemas; the only table of this story is `guarantee_claim` in `rwb_guarantee` (DP-01).
- The read writes nothing: no state, no decision record and no outbox row on a read path (BR7).
- The reference-data version is stamped on every answer; an unversioned label fails the page instead of being served (BR8).
- The DP04 product, its access rows, its freshness stamp, its breaks and the case-link check stay with rwb-source-data; this service serves the facts and takes no publish decision (BR6).
- No call to the Thai Credit Guarantee Corporation or to NLEADS: their results arrive as facts recorded on the claim and on the case (legacy guardrail 4).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-010 for rwb-source-data. The stage 2 step was a stage of the `rwb-case` JOB-02 chain inside one deployable, so its deployment was the deployment of that chain. In the target the build is `Stage2ProductWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-source-data`, started by `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` and owning no Schedule, and it writes two snapshot tables in `rwb_source_data` (DP-01, DP-10, DP-15). This story deploys that build, proves the trigger, gates the flag, publishes five series and three alerts and writes the runbook. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **the stage 2 product build of rwb-source-data deployed from one chart with a pinned digest and build ID, the worker that registers `Stage2ProductWorkflow` on `rwb-source-data`, the migration step that applies `rwb_source_data` and refuses another schema, the proof that the build starts from `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` and owns no Schedule, the flag `rwb.dataengine.stage2-products`, five dashboard series and three alerts each with its runbook entry**, so that **an operator can see a stage 2 build that did not start, a business date that was not stamped, a count break that held the publish or a run that failed, and prove that a rerun of the same date leaves no duplicate and that a failed release keeps the previous build**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy stage 2 step had no deployment of its own: it ran inside the rwb-case chain over one schema, so a stuck step showed up as a failed job run and an operator had the database in front of them. In the target the step is a workflow of its own service, started by an event, writing two tables in this service's schema, joined at read time to the ACE views, and its result is three facts an operator must be able to see: whether the build for the business date started, whether it was stamped, and whether the count check held it. Without this story the app story can pass its tests while the worker is unregistered, the event is consumed by nobody, the count break sits unread and DP04 turns stale with no alert (DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44).

Deployment is also where the split is enforced operationally. The release carries the `rwb_source_data` login only, applies the `rwb_source_data` migration only, and reads no other service's schema and no ACE table directly: the contract and plan facts come through this service's own views, and the treatment and guarantee facts come through their contracts at run time (DP-01, DP-02, DP-05). The observability follows ADR-023 per service: five series with the environment, release and build ID as dimensions, three alerts each carrying a message ID, and three runbook entries.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The rwb-source-data baseline chart and login are deployed, with the REST base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` and the relay of `rwb_source_data` (DP-02, DP-13).
- The Kafka event platform provides `rwb.source-data.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics and the ACLs of this service's principal (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON).
- The Temporal workflow kit and the `rwb-recovery` namespace exist, with worker versioning, the build ID provider and the payload codec (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON).
- The platform error envelope and the message catalogue are in force, so every alert can carry a message ID.
- The three environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist and the production namespace exists for the release date; the flag `rwb.dataengine.stage2-products` exists in the flag library.
- The chart of the app story is published with `Stage2ProductWorkflow` and its four activities, and the migration version that creates `dp_treatment` and `dp_guarantee_claim` sits on the service sequence (RWB-P1-E2010-APP; DP-15).
- The gateway-bff composite route for SCR-45 and SCR-03 is published (RWB-PLT-N001-CON, DP-19).
- The replica counts, the resource sizes, the lag and stale thresholds, the alert thresholds and the probe timings are environment values fixed by no source document (GAP-0513; ASM-0705).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds the service image and the contract jar, runs the unit, component and contract tests, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes one chart version.
2. The chart deploys the API deployment and the workflow worker with the `rwb_source_data` login reference, namespace `rwb-recovery`, task queue `rwb-source-data`, the payload codec and the build ID of the release.
3. The worker registration step confirms that `Stage2ProductWorkflow` and the activities `snapshot(page)`, `writeDp04Page`, `checkActiveCount` and `stampDp04` are registered on `rwb-source-data` and on no other queue.
4. The migration step applies the `rwb_source_data` sequence of this release, including the version that creates `dp_treatment` and `dp_guarantee_claim`, and refuses to run when the target schema is not `rwb_source_data`.
5. The trigger step confirms that the build is started by `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` and registers no Schedule for it, and publishes one synthetic event to prove the start.
6. The flag step sets `rwb.dataengine.stage2-products` from the values of the environment.
7. The dashboards are published with the five series and the environment, release and build ID as dimensions.
8. The three alerts are wired to their message identifiers and to their runbook entries: MSG-P1-002 for the count break, MSG-P1-001 for DP04 stale and MSG-GEN-006 for a workflow failure.
9. A smoke step writes DP04 for a synthetic business date in DEV, reads it back through the DP04 contract, and reruns the same date to prove that no duplicate row appears.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The chart render or the migration job fails | The deployment stays unready, the pipeline stops, and no traffic and no offset is committed | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The migration target is a schema other than `rwb_source_data` | The step refuses the target and the release stops before any table is created | Pipeline error, no message id | AC1 |
| X3 | The worker registers the workflow on another queue, or registers no worker | The registration check fails the release and names the queue and the workflow | None | AC1 |
| X4 | The flag is off in an environment | The worker is not deployed, no build starts on a new `AceDataReady` and DP04 keeps its previous rows | None | AC3 |
| X5 | A synthetic `AceDataReady` starts no execution | The trigger check fails the smoke run and the workflow-failure alert condition is demonstrated on the synthetic event | MSG-GEN-006 | AC2, AC5 |
| X6 | The active count differs from the count written | The stamp is held, the break is listed and the count-break alert fires | MSG-P1-002 | AC5 |
| X7 | DP04 is not stamped by its expected-by time | The product turns stale and the stale alert fires | MSG-P1-001 | AC5 |
| X8 | A dashboard series is missing, or an alert carries no message ID or no runbook link | The observability check fails the release | None | AC4, AC5 |
| X9 | A new build is promoted while an execution of the business date is running | The old build drains its execution and the new build takes the next start; the dashboards show both build IDs | None | AC6 |

X1 to X3 are the deployment paths of the release; X4 to X7 are the four conditions the flag and the three alerts exist for; X8 is the observability gate; X9 is the worker-versioning path of the workflow kit.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the workflow kit, the topic provisioning and the flag library; no application code is built here |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, thresholds and probe timings are environment values |
| Valuable | Makes a stage 2 build observable, provable and rerunnable before the Epic 3 screens depend on DP04 |
| Estimable | One chart, one worker registration, one migration step, one trigger step, five series, three alerts and three runbook entries |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the worker registers, the migration refuses a foreign schema, an alert fires on a synthetic condition, the smoke run leaves one row per date |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Deployment of the stage 2 product build for rwb-source-data

  Background:
    Given the service template chart and the platform pipeline are in force

    Given the target environment is SIT

  Scenario: AC1 The chart, the worker and the migration step are deployed and pinned (new, D-RCV-60)

    Then the release declares the rwb_source_data login and no other service's credential
    Then the migration step applies the rwb_source_data sequence and refuses a target schema other than rwb_source_data
    Then worker versioning is enabled and a new workflow goes to the new build while the old build drains

  Scenario: AC2 The build is event-started and owns no Schedule (new, D-RCV-60)

    Then the trigger step fails the release when the event starts no execution

  Scenario: AC3 The flag turns the build on and off (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the flag rwb.dataengine.stage2-products in the flag library

    When the flag is off in the same environment

    Then each series carries the environment, the release and the build ID as dimensions

  Scenario: AC5 The three alerts carry their message ID and one runbook entry each (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published alert rules and the runbook
    When a count break, a stale DP04 and a failed execution are simulated
    Then the count break raises its alert with MSG-P1-002
    Then the stale DP04 raises its alert with MSG-P1-001
    Then the workflow failure raises its alert with MSG-GEN-006
    Then every alert links one runbook entry with the check, the owner role and the recovery step
    Then no alert threshold and no probe timing is hard-coded, and no secret appears in a values file, a dashboard or the runbook

  Scenario: AC6 The smoke run writes, reads and reruns one business date, and rollback keeps the previous build (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the DEV environment and a synthetic business date
    When the smoke run publishes AceDataReady for that date
    Then dp_treatment and dp_guarantee_claim hold the rows of the date and the DP04 stamp is present
    Then the DP04 read through /data-products/{productCode}/records answers the rows of the date
    When the smoke run publishes the same event again for the same date
    Then the row count per table is unchanged and no duplicate record exists for the date
    When the release is rolled back
    Then the previous chart version and its build ID serve the queue and the smoke run passes on it
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One login, one task queue and one schema per service: the release carries the `rwb_source_data` login, polls `rwb-source-data` only and migrates `rwb_source_data` only | Architecture v5 slides 29 and 41; DP-02; DP-15 |
| BR2 | The stage 2 build is started by `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` and owns no Schedule; the freshness cut-off Schedules belong to RWB-P1-E1015-OPS | DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44 |
| BR3 | Every worker carries the build ID of its release and worker versioning is enabled, so a new build takes new executions while the old build drains | Temporal and Drools design slide 11; RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| BR4 | Every alert carries a message ID and links one runbook entry with the check, the owner role and the recovery step | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR5 | No environment value is hard-coded: replicas, resources, thresholds, probe paths and timings and the flag come from values files and parameters | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR6 | Dashboard series, alert payloads and the runbook carry counts, product codes, business dates, statuses and build IDs only, never a treatment amount, a claim amount or a personal value | ADR-023; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR7 | The release writes no ACE data and reads no other service's schema or table; the ACE facts are read through this service's own views and the treatment and guarantee facts through their contracts | DP-01; DP-05 |
| BR8 | A failing release never replaces a working one: the previous build stays in force until the new build passes its tests and its smoke run | DP-10 |
| BR9 | The stamp is written by the freshness story and never by this deployment; the deployment only proves that the stamp of a business date appears when the count matches | RWB-P1-E1015-APP; BR4 of the legacy story |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1 is the chart, the values and the migration step. BR2 is the trigger step and the fact that the release registers no Schedule. BR3 is the worker versioning and the build ID of the release. BR4 is the alert wiring and the runbook. BR5 is the values files. BR6 is the series definition and the alert payload. BR7 is the migration scope and the ACLs. BR8 is the rollback rule. BR9 is the smoke run, which reads the stamp rather than writing it.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the contract tests pass | Deploying |
| Deploying | Worker registered and probes healthy | The worker polls `rwb-source-data` only and the registration check passes | Ready |
| Ready | Release superseded | A new chart version passes its tests | Rolling |
| Rolling | All workers on the new build | The old build drains its open executions | Ready |
| Ready | Flag off | `rwb.dataengine.stage2-products` is turned off in the environment | Not deployed |
| Ready | Smoke run failed | The trigger, the read-back or the rerun step of the smoke run fails | Blocked |
| Blocked | Previous build restored | The previous chart version is redeployed with its build ID | Ready |

The DP04 freshness states LOADED and STALE and the workflow execution states RUNNING, COMPLETED and FAILED belong to the product and the app story; they are not states of this deployment.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the registration step, the dashboards and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the topic ACLs, the consumer quotas and the flag library |
| Platform workflow owner | Owns the task queue, the namespace, the worker registration and the versioning policy |
| Platform event owner | Owns `rwb.source-data.events.v1`, its retry and `.dlt` topics and the schema registry |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact and may block it on a failing smoke run |
| On-call operator | Runs the three runbook entries and opens an incident when a count break, a stale product or a failed execution persists |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Reads the DP04 status and the breaks the alerts point at |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the runbook, the alert history and the release record |

The worker runs as the `rwb_source_data` service identity (DP-02), carried by the chart as a secret reference and never as a literal name. No credential and no personal name appears in a values file, a dashboard, an alert payload or the runbook.

##### 11. Data

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Deployment values | Image digest, chart version, replica counts, resource requests and limits, probe paths and timings, log level, namespace, task queue, build ID, flag value |
| Task queue | `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, polled by the rwb-source-data worker only |
| Trigger | `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` on `rwb.source-data.events.v1`, consumed by this service's own inbox |
| Schema | `rwb_source_data`, migrated by its own per-service Flyway sequence; this release applies the version that creates `dp_treatment` and `dp_guarantee_claim` |
| Tables behind the series | `dp_treatment`, `dp_guarantee_claim`, `data_product_load`; the series read counts and statuses only |
| Dashboard series | Rows written per product, load status per product, count breaks, stale products, workflow failures; dimensions environment, release, build ID |
| Alerts | Three rules with one message ID and one runbook entry each: MSG-P1-002 for a count break, MSG-P1-001 for DP04 stale and MSG-GEN-006 for a workflow failure |
| Runbook entries | Count break held the publish, DP04 stale, workflow failed or did not start; each with the check, the owner role and the recovery step |
| Secrets | The `rwb_source_data` login secret, the Kafka client credential and the Temporal mTLS material, all from the platform secret store |
| Test data | One synthetic `AceDataReady` for a synthetic business date, the 40-treatment fixture of the app story and one count break; the fixture owner is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0513; ASM-0705) |

The deployment topology (cluster names, node pools, replica counts, resource sizes, zone spread, ingress class and the exact probe timings) belongs to each environment and is set by the platform team in its values file; the chart exposes every one of them as a value and this story fixes only their names and the rule that they are never hard-coded (GAP-0513; ASM-0705).

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only after the worker has polled `rwb-source-data` once and has registered the workflow and its four activities; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database, starts an execution or commits an offset, and a failing dependency is reported as not ready, never as live-and-broken. The paths and timings are values of the environment.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None from this story. The DP04 branch of `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/{productCode}/records` is declared by RWB-P1-E2010-CON and implemented by RWB-P1-E2010-APP; this deployment exposes it through the chart and its ingress and declares no path of its own. The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None from the deployment. The worker calls the treatment and guarantee contracts and reads the ACE views at run time as the app story's client; the chart carries no REST client of its own, no composite route and no outbound call at start-up beyond the Temporal frontend and the Kafka brokers.

###### 12.3 Events published

None of its own. `rwb.source-data.events.v1` carries `AceDataReady` and `AceDataLate` from RWB-P1-E1015-APP, and this slice publishes neither; the smoke run publishes one synthetic `AceDataReady` as a test message on the topic and not as a service event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event type | Topic | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | The listener and inbox of this service, starting `Stage2ProductWorkflow`; retry topic and `.dlt` routing on the topic |

The topic, its retry and `.dlt` topics and the event type are provisioned and owned by the platform event epic and by RWB-P1-E1015-APP; this deployment configures the consumption, the inbox and the trigger proof.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Stage2ProductWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per business date | `rwb-source-data` | Registered by the worker of this release, with the build ID and worker versioning; no Schedule |
| `snapshot(page)` | Activity | `rwb-source-data` | Registered by the same worker with the kit's retry policy |
| `writeDp04Page` | Activity | `rwb-source-data` | Registered with the same policy; idempotent by record ID and business date |
| `checkActiveCount` | Activity | `rwb-source-data` | Registered with the same policy |
| `stampDp04` | Activity | `rwb-source-data` | Registered with the same policy; calls the freshness stamp of RWB-P1-E1015-APP |

**Build ID and versioning.** The build ID is the one supplied by the workflow kit for the release commit; worker versioning is enabled and a new build takes new executions while the old build drains (BR3). The exact build ID format and the versioning policy are the platform's and are not restated here.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The deployment registers no Schedule: the build is started by `AceDataReady` and the freshness cut-off Schedules belong to RWB-P1-E1015-OPS and RWB-P1-E1015-APP (BR2; DP-10).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|
| `dp_treatment` | P1 (`rwb_source_data`) | Created by the migration step of this release; the row counts feed the rows-per-product and count-break series |
| `dp_guarantee_claim` | P1 (`rwb_source_data`) | Created by the same migration step; its row counts feed the same series |
| `data_product_load` | P1 (`rwb_source_data`) | Read for the load-status and stale-product series; written by RWB-P1-E1015-APP and never by this deployment |

The release applies the stage 2 migration of the app story and no other: no treatment table of another service, no guarantee table and no ACE table is created, altered or read directly (DP-01, DP-05, DP-15).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. No fake is deployed. The contract mocks of the treatment and guarantee reads and the ACE account and plan fixture are in-process test doubles of the app story and of its contract tests; the smoke run of DEV calls the service's own contracts and the DEV stand-ins of rwb-case, rwb-guarantee and the ACE views, never a fake shipped by this release.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 0 consumed by the deployment | The DP04 record read is the app story's; the probes are cluster-internal |
| Kafka | 0 published, 1 type consumed | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` with the inbox, the retry topic and the `.dlt` routing |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 4 activities, 0 Schedules | Worker on `rwb-source-data` with a pinned build ID and worker versioning |
| File | None | No file is read or written by the deployment |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | The release migrates `rwb_source_data` only and reads no other schema | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | The ACE facts are read through this service's own views at run time, never from a public table | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | The rwb-case reference-data contract is a run-time dependency of the worker, with its keeper library | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | The worker, the task queue and the namespace come from the workflow kit; no Schedule is registered | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | The release declares no REST path and no client of its own; the worker calls the contracts as the app story's client | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | The ingress serves `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` and no other base | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | The per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_source_data`; the migration step refuses another schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff serves SCR-45 and SCR-03; the deployment registers the route and no screen of its own | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-source-data/` overlay | API deployment, workflow worker, config map, secret references, probes, task queue, namespace, build ID and flag |
| `helm/rwb-source-data/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, flag value, build ID, thresholds (GAP-0513; ASM-0705) |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit and contract tests, image and dependency scan, chart publish, migration step, trigger step, smoke run, promotion |
| Registration step | `Stage2ProductWorkflow` and its four activities on `rwb-source-data`, with the build ID and worker versioning |
| Migration step | The `rwb_source_data` migration of this release; a target schema other than `rwb_source_data` is refused |
| Trigger step | Proves that `AceDataReady` starts the workflow and that no Schedule is registered |
| Dashboards | The five series of section 11 with the three dimensions |
| Alerts | Three rules, each with a message ID and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Three entries: count break held the publish, DP04 stale, workflow failed or did not start |

**Alert mapping**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-002 | The active count differs from the count written for the business date, so the stamp is held | Count-break alert naming the product, the business date, the check text and the build ID | Platform on-call and the data steward, ticket |
| MSG-P1-001 | DP04 is not stamped by its expected-by time | DP04-stale alert naming the product, the business date in use and the stale-since time | Platform on-call, page in the morning window, else ticket |
| MSG-GEN-006 | An execution of the build failed, or the event started none | Workflow-failure alert naming the workflow, the business date, the failure class and the build ID | Platform on-call, page |

**Rerun and idempotency.** A rerun of a business date is refused while an execution of that date is running (MSG-P2-006) and is otherwise started again on the same workflow ID pattern; `writeDp04Page` upserts by record ID and business date, so the rerun replaces the rows of the date and creates no duplicate. The smoke run proves that rule on one synthetic date (AC6).

**Rollback.** A release that fails the smoke run is not promoted. A release already promoted is rolled back by redeploying the previous chart version with its own build ID, which keeps the old build serving its open executions until they finish; the rows of a stamped date are left as they are and the previous build reruns the date through the same upsert, so no data repair is needed.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.dataengine.stage2-products`. On: the worker and the listener are deployed, and a new `AceDataReady` starts a build. Off: no worker, no execution, and `dp_treatment` and `dp_guarantee_claim` keep the rows of the last stamped date.

**Done when.** The chart renders for DEV, SIT and UAT with a pinned digest and the build ID, the worker registers `Stage2ProductWorkflow` and its four activities on `rwb-source-data`, the migration step refuses a foreign schema, the trigger step proves the start from `AceDataReady` and registers no Schedule, the five series and the three alerts are published with their message IDs and runbook links, the smoke run writes and reads back one synthetic business date and reruns it without a duplicate, and the three runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-002 | A count break held the stamp of the business date | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-P1-001 | DP04 is stale after a build that did not run or did not complete | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The stage 2 build failed, or the treatment or guarantee contract was unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P2-006 | A rerun is asked while the execution of the date is running | {job} is already running. Wait for it to finish before you rerun it. |

The four texts are the legacy texts carried unchanged, and each of the first three is the message ID of one alert. An alert payload names the product, the business date, the check, the failure class, counts and the build ID only, never a treatment amount, a claim amount or a personal value. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment has no screen of its own. Its operator-facing surfaces are the pipeline run view, the release view, the dashboard, SCR-45 Data quality through gateway-bff (loading, empty, list, refused) and the runbook. SCR-45 and SCR-03 are served by the app story and the composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the deployment only registers the route. SCR-44 Interface and job monitor is not used, because the deployment registers no job of its own and the build is event-started. The Temporal Web UI stays behind the platform identity provider: RW-PLATADM operates and RW-AUDIT reads, and payloads are decoded only through the codec server under break-glass.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the product code, the access roles, the expected-by time and the count tolerance are data rows and decisions, never a deployment value (DP-07).
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads, the runbook or the workflow history: counts, product codes, business dates, statuses, failure classes and build IDs only, and payloads stay encrypted.
- One login per service, one task queue per service and one schema per service: the release carries the `rwb_source_data` login, polls `rwb-source-data` and migrates `rwb_source_data` only (DP-02, DP-15).
- No ACE table is read directly and no ACE data is written: the release names this service's own views and no public table (DP-05).
- The release registers no Schedule: the build is event-started and the freshness cut-offs belong to RWB-P1-E1015-OPS (DP-10).
- No row of a stamped business date is deleted by an operation: a rerun replaces rows by record ID and business date, and no operator action writes a business row.
- The release pins the image digest, the chart version and the build ID; a rebuild between environments is not allowed, and a failing smoke run never replaces a working build.
- No secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; all secrets come from the platform secret store.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-010 for the wave 2 integration harness. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **member of the integration and QA team**, I want **a repeatable cross-service journey harness for the stage 2 data products DP04 (treatments, plans, contracts and guarantee claims) across rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-treatment and rwb-guarantee**, so that **the DP04 build, the read join and the access gate are proven end to end, with evidence, before the wave 2 release is accepted**.

This story builds the harness and the evidence only. It builds no production endpoint, no screen, no table, no migration, no workflow and no schedule; it serves no operation, it owns no table and it starts no workflow of its own. The real behaviour is owned by the four I stories RWB-P3-E2004-APP (the case, account link and scope reads of rwb-case), RWB-P1-E2010-APP (the DP04 stage 2 build, the snapshot tables, the freshness stamp, the count check, the references break and the DP04 read in rwb-source-data), RWB-S2-E2010-APP (the treatment record and the treatment contract of rwb-treatment) and RWB-S3-E2010-APP (the guarantee claim contract of rwb-guarantee), and those four stories block the ITG run.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy RWB-E2-010 journey crosses more than one service and more than one kind of data. rwb-treatment owns the treatment record, rwb-guarantee owns the guarantee claim, rwb-case owns the case and its account links, rwb-source-data owns the ACE view contract, the DP04 snapshot tables, the freshness stamp, the catalog entry and the access rows, and rwb-access answers the role check. The legacy story carried the build, the read and the access gate in one module against one recovery schema; the split puts the build in RWB-P1-E2010-APP, the treatment contract in RWB-S2-E2010-APP, the claim contract in RWB-S3-E2010-APP and the case and account links in RWB-P3-E2004-APP, and leaves this story the proof that the four parts agree on one business date.

What the harness proves, in one repeatable run per business date:

- JOB-02 stage 2 runs only after DP01 is stamped for the business date from a COMPLETE ALS batch, and the step state is Complete or Failed on the run.
- 40 active treatments and 5 TCG claims reach dp_treatment and dp_guarantee_claim for business date 2026-12-14, each row linked to its case.
- The contract number and contract date are read from v_ace_account and the plan terms from v_ace_plan at request time and are never copied into a Workbench table, so the read join is exercised on every call rather than on a snapshot.
- The DP04 freshness stamp is written for the day only when the count check agrees, and the catalog entry names Workbench for treatment and claim and the two ACE views for the contract and plan facts.
- A guarantee claim that names a case that does not exist is held on the break list with check References and is not written to dp_guarantee_claim.
- A role with no DP04 access row is refused with MSG-P4-002 and the refusal is logged, while the data steward read still answers.
- A repeat run for the same business date leaves the row count and the stamp unchanged, and the end-of-day boundary is 00:00:00 of the next day.

It meets REQ-RDF-014 (the stage 2 data products exist before the first treatment goes live) and REQ-RDF-010 (access to each data product is controlled per role, with personal data masked) at the integration level, and it leaves every business rule, every message and every screen behaviour where the owning stories put them.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The four I stories are published and deployed in the SIT environment, or their published contracts and the §12.8 fakes stand in for them: RWB-P3-E2004-APP (case, account links and scope reads), RWB-P1-E2010-APP (DP04 stage 2 build, snapshot tables, freshness, catalog, breaks and the DP04 read), RWB-S2-E2010-APP (treatment record and treatment contract) and RWB-S3-E2010-APP (guarantee claim contract).
- Business date 2026-12-14 and the ACE batch for ALS for it is COMPLETE at 06:20, with DP01 stamped for the day.
- The treatment module holds 40 active treatments, 12 of them restructure plans with installments published in v_ace_plan, and 9 of the 12 plans carry a credit approval recorded on the case by the restructuring officer.
- 5 TCG guarantee claim records exist for 5 existing cases, with claimed amounts from 180,000.00 to 1,250,000.00 baht.
- data_product_access version "DPA-2026.12" gives DP04 read to RW-CASEOWN, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-GUARANT, RW-CREDITAD, RW-COE and RW-AUDIT, and gives no DP04 access row to RW-PHONECOL.
- gateway-bff is deployed with the composite route of DP-19 available for the DP04 read.
- The harness environment, its seeding of the 40 treatments, the 12 plans and the 5 claims, its evidence format and retention, and its pass or fail gate: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0392; ASM-0567).
- No build dependency. Day 1.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: takes the run lock for the environment and records the build ID, the business date 2026-12-14 and the versions of the four contracts it is about to exercise.
2. Harness: seeds the 40 active treatments through the rwb-treatment contract — of which 12 are restructure plans with installments published in v_ace_plan and 9 carry a credit approval recorded on the case — the 5 TCG guarantee claims through the rwb-guarantee contract, the case links and primary account key of case RW-2026-000512 through the rwb-case contract, and the ACE facts through the rwb-source-data contract or its fake: the contract number and contract date on v_ace_account and the plan terms on v_ace_plan. It reads each seed back and asserts the seeded state.
3. Harness: observes the stage 2 step of JOB-02 for 2026-12-14, started by the AceDataReady event of the day, and records the step state, its start and end, and the business date it built.
4. Harness: asserts 40 dp_treatment rows for 2026-12-14 and 5 dp_guarantee_claim rows, each linked to its case, and asserts that no row was written for the claim of unknown case UUID 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000997.
5. Harness: reads DP04 for case RW-2026-000512 through the gateway-bff composite route and asserts the contract number and contract date of its primary account from v_ace_account and the plan terms from v_ace_plan at request time, with no contract or plan value held on a snapshot row.
6. Harness: asserts the DP04 freshness stamp for 2026-12-14 with status LOADED, and the catalog entry that names Workbench for treatment and guarantee claim and v_ace_account and v_ace_plan for the contract and plan facts.
7. Harness: asserts the count check — 40 built rows against 41 from the owning module — holds the stamp, keeps 2026-12-13 as the latest published day and lists a break with MSG-P1-002 naming 40 and 41, and that no snapshot for 2026-12-14 is published.
8. Harness: asserts the references break for the unknown case, then the access refusal of user u-phone-02 holding RW-PHONECOL with MSG-P4-002 and the logged refusal, alongside a data steward read that still answers.
9. Harness: repeats the step for 2026-12-14 and asserts 40 rows with no duplicate and an unchanged stamp, then asserts the end-of-day boundary with treatment TRT-SYN-0601 changed at 2026-12-14T23:59:59+07:00 and TRT-SYN-0602 changed at 2026-12-15T00:00:00+07:00.
10. Harness: forces the treatment contract to fail, asserts MSG-GEN-006 and MSG-P1-001 and that the 2026-12-13 rows and the previous published day stand, then returns the fake to its healthy answer.
11. Harness: writes one run report per business date, keyed by story and business date, and evaluates the pass or fail gate; the report format, its retention and the gate: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0392; ASM-0567).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What the harness asserts | Message | ITG test case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A role without a DP04 access row reads the product: user u-phone-02 holding RW-PHONECOL | 403 on the DP04 read; the refusal is logged with user u-phone-02 and product DP04; the data steward read still answers | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-010-03-ITG |
| X2 | A guarantee claim names case UUID 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000997, which does not exist | No row in dp_guarantee_claim for that claim; the break list holds it with product DP04 and check References; the other 5 claims are written | None | TC-E2-010-04-ITG |
| X3 | TreatmentQuery, and the treatment contract, is unavailable | The step ends FAILED with MSG-GEN-006 for system Treatment; dp_treatment keeps the 2026-12-13 rows; DP04 is stale at 08:00 with MSG-P1-001 and the date 2026-12-13 | MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P1-001 | TC-E2-010-05-ITG |
| X4 | The step runs again for the same business date 2026-12-14 | Still 40 rows for 2026-12-14 and no duplicate; the freshness stamp is unchanged | None | TC-E2-010-06-ITG |
| X5 | The active treatment count differs: 41 from the owning module against 40 built rows | No stamp for 2026-12-14; a break with check "Active treatment count 40 against 41" is listed for the data steward; 2026-12-13 stays the latest published day | MSG-P1-002 | TC-E2-010-07-ITG |
| X6 | A treatment changed at the end of business date 2026-12-14 | TRT-SYN-0601 changed at 2026-12-14T23:59:59+07:00 is in the 2026-12-14 build; TRT-SYN-0602 changed at 2026-12-15T00:00:00+07:00 is not | None | TC-E2-010-08-ITG |
| X7 | The count matches but no DP04 freshness stamp is written for the day | The run fails the freshness assertion, the report names the missing stamp for 2026-12-14, and the previous published day is unchanged | None | TC-E2-010-01-ITG |
| X8 | The seed cannot be loaded through the owning contracts or the fakes | The run refuses to start and names the missing seed item; no scenario is reported as passed | None | All |
| X9 | Another run holds the harness environment lock | The run refuses to start and names the lock holder; nothing is seeded and no evidence is produced | None | All |
| X10 | The evidence report cannot be written or attached | The run is marked failed with the local evidence kept for rerun and the gate stays closed | None | All |
| X11 | A role without the platform administration right, RW-TRIBE, reads the data quality list | 403 with MSG-P4-002 and the refusal logged; the data steward read of the same list is allowed | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-010-09-ITG |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs on its own once the four I stories are deployed; until then it runs against the §12.8 fakes, and it builds no service feature |
| Negotiable | The harness pack, the seed pack and the evidence format are agreed with QA; no business value is fixed by the harness |
| Valuable | The DP04 build, the read join to the two ACE views and the access gate are proven once across four services, with the counts and the stamp on the evidence |
| Estimable | One harness project, one journey specification, one fake pack for five services and one run report |
| Small | Fits in one iteration with the owning stories' contract tests |
| Testable | Each scenario of §7 is one automated journey on synthetic data with a machine-checkable result |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | DP04 holds treatments and guarantee claims from the Workbench, and contract and plan facts read from v_ace_account and v_ace_plan, with one system of record and one owner for each part | REQ-RDF-014; data_product DP04; sys_objects |
| BR2 | No Workbench table copies a contract, a plan or an account; the views are read at request time | D-RCV-35 U1; tier map section 9 |
| BR3 | Every snapshot row links to an existing case, or it is held on the break list and retried with the next build | DQ load check "References" |
| BR4 | The product is stamped for the day only when the active count matches the owning module, with zero tolerance | DL25; RWB-E1-011 hold rule (FEAT-RDF-13) |
| BR5 | A role reads DP04 only through an access row in force | data_product_access; REQ-RDF-010 |
| BR6 | Credit approval for a restructure is recorded on the case by the officer; there is no interface to NLEADS | INT-26; DL12 |
| BR7 | Plan installments come from the ACE plan published calculation | DF-ACE-174 source ACE; INT-34 |

The seven rules are copied unchanged from RWB-E2-010 and the split changes none of them. The harness asserts them across the service boundaries and re-implements none of them: the count, the access rows, the expected-by time and the tolerance are data held by rwb-source-data and rwb-access, and the harness holds no copy.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case. This story changes no case status. It observes the DP04 freshness status and the state of the stage 2 step of the JOB-02 run:

| Observed | After a build that matches | After a build that is refused or fails |
|---|---|---|
| DP04 freshness status | LOADED for 2026-12-14 | STALE, with 2026-12-13 as the latest published day |
| Stage 2 product step of JOB-02 | Complete | Failed |

The harness adds a run state of its own only: Not started, Seeding, Running, Passed, Failed, with the latest run for a build deciding the gate. A failed run leaves every row in rwb-source-data exactly as it was before the run.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward and data product owner | Owns DP04; reads the catalog entry and the breaks; supplies the control read of AC3 |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads DP04 for cases in scope; the harness drives this read for case RW-2026-000512 |
| RW-RESTRUCT, restructuring officer | Reads DP04 for the restructure plans in scope, including the plan terms of v_ace_plan |
| RW-GUARANT, guarantee officer | Reads DP04 for the guarantee claims of the cases in scope |
| RW-CREDITAD, Credit Administration officer | Reads DP04 for the cases in scope, including the 9 plans with a credit approval |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Reads DP04 for all cases |
| RW-AUDIT, audit | Reads DP04 for all cases |
| RW-PHONECOL | Holds no DP04 access row; refused with MSG-P4-002, and the refusal is asserted |
| The integration and QA team | Runs the harness, keeps the fake pack, the seed pack and the evidence, and reads the reports |

No approval level from the delegation of authority applies: the journey reads data products and takes no business decision. Authorisation is answered by rwb-access through the authorise operation of §12.2.
