##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test asset in the integration pipeline and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; the 2 s timeout and the circuit breaker per downstream of DP-11 apply to every row.

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP04/records` | P1 rwb-source-data | The DP04 read for a case, with the snapshot rows joined to v_ace_account and v_ace_plan at request time (AC1, AC3); `?caseId=` |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | The DP04 freshness stamp of the business date, LOADED or STALE, and the latest published day (AC2, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/data-products` | P1 rwb-source-data | The DP04 catalog entry and its systems of record (AC1) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/data-quality/exceptions` | P1 rwb-source-data | The References break and the count break of the business date (AC2, AC3, X11) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` | P1 rwb-source-data | Reruns the stage 2 step of JOB-02 for the business date (AC4, X4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case and its primary account key for case RW-2026-000512 (AC1) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/accounts` | P3 rwb-case | The account links of the case that the DP04 read resolves in v_ace_account (AC1) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}` | S2 rwb-treatment | The treatment record seeded for the 40 rows and for TRT-SYN-0601 and TRT-SYN-0602 (AC1, AC4) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/guarantee/v1/cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims` | S3 rwb-guarantee | Seeds the 5 TCG claims and the claim for unknown case UUID 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000997 (AC2, AC3); the contract may answer with no claims until RWB-S3-E2010-APP lands |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The DP04 read decision for u-phone-02 holding RW-PHONECOL, for RW-TRIBE and for the data steward (AC3, X11) |

The composite DP04 route through gateway-bff is DP-19, owned by the platform edge story RWB-PLT-N001-CON. Its path and merge order: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0392; ASM-0567).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event of its own; the AceDataReady event of the day is published by rwb-source-data and only replayed through its test profile.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | What the harness asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 rwb-source-data | The event of 2026-12-14 is published after the ALS batch is COMPLETE at 06:20 and is what starts the stage 2 step of JOB-02 (AC2) |
| `rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1` | `rwb.treatment.events.v1` | S2 rwb-treatment | The approval of a restructure plan reaches the topic inside the run window, so the 9 plans with a credit approval are the ones dp_treatment carries (AC1) |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 rwb-decision (ledger); every service publishes its own record | The record of the treatment approval reaches the shared topic and names the case and the treatment, alongside the treatment read of §12.2 (AC1) |

Consumers dedupe through their own inbox table; the harness consumes with its own group and never asserts a producer's outbox row.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

JOB-02 Case creation, stage 2 product step, is exercised and not built: an event-started step started by `AceDataReady` for the business date, running on queue `rwb-case` as part of DailyCaseRun or on the P1 stage-2 worker, per the owning story RWB-P1-E2010-APP. The harness records the workflow ID, the business date and the state of the step, and asserts the snapshot rows, the breaks and the stamp afterwards.

No workflow is built, no activity is added and no schedule is created by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The harness run is started by the test pipeline, not by a Temporal Schedule and not by Airflow; the daily step it observes is started by the event of §12.4.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no table in any schema (DP-01); it seeds and reads through the operations of §12.2 only.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubbed answers |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-source-data | data-products/DP04/records, data-products/freshness, admin/data-products, admin/data-quality/exceptions, admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun | DP04 for RW-2026-000512 with the contract number and contract date of its primary account and the plan terms, 40 dp_treatment rows for 2026-12-14 and 5 guarantee claims; freshness LOADED for 2026-12-14, STALE with 2026-12-13 after a failed step, and no stamp for the AC2 hold; the catalog entry with Workbench for treatment and claim; the References break for UUID 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000997 and the count break naming 40 and 41 with MSG-P1-002; 403 with MSG-P4-002 for RW-PHONECOL and for RW-TRIBE on the admin list; 503 with MSG-GEN-006 for the forced treatment failure; 409 with MSG-P2-006 for a rerun while the step runs |
| rwb-case | cases/{caseId}, cases/{caseId}/accounts | RW-2026-000512 with its primary account key and its account links; the 5 cases of the guarantee claims; no case for UUID 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000997 |
| rwb-treatment | treatments/{treatmentId} | The 40 active treatments, of which 12 are restructure plans and 9 carry a credit approval; TRT-SYN-0601 changed at 2026-12-14T23:59:59+07:00 and TRT-SYN-0602 at 2026-12-15T00:00:00+07:00; a forced error for the AC5 case |
| rwb-guarantee | cases/{caseId}/guarantee-claims | The 5 TCG claims of existing cases and the claim for the unknown case UUID; an empty list for every case until RWB-S3-E2010-APP lands |
| rwb-access | authorise | Allow the DP04 read for RW-CASEOWN, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-GUARANT, RW-CREDITAD, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT and RW-DATASTEW; refuse RW-PHONECOL and RW-TRIBE with MSG-P4-002 |

The fakes are replaced by the real service as each I story lands, contract by contract. The harness environment, its repository, its seeding of the 40 treatments, the 12 plans and the 5 claims, its evidence format and retention, and its pass or fail gate: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0392; ASM-0567).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Used | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | Yes | Ten consumed operations of §12.2 through gateway-bff and the owning services; one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream |
| Kafka | Yes | Consumes `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1`, `rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1`; publishes nothing |
| Temporal | Observed only | Starts no workflow and adds no activity; it observes the stage 2 step of JOB-02 through the P1 operations and records its state |
| File | No | Reads and writes no file itself; the run report is written by the pipeline reporter of §13 |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The platform H dependencies named by this table are delivered by the platform wave and are not repeated in the metadata H list; the harness has no build dependency of its own. The blocking dependencies of this story are the four I stories RWB-P3-E2004-APP, RWB-P1-E2010-APP, RWB-S2-E2010-APP and RWB-S3-E2010-APP, which replace the fakes with real services one at a time.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Test harness | Runs the eleven flow steps for the business date, keyed by story and business date, takes the environment lock, and stops at the first failed assertion with the trace |
| CompositeRouteClient | Harness adapter | Calls the gateway-bff composite DP04 route and the ten consumed operations of §12.2, one hop each with the 2 s budget |
| FakePack | WireMock project | Serves rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-treatment, rwb-guarantee and rwb-access from the published contract documents of §12.8 |
| Stage2Fixture | Data | The seeded 40 active treatments with 12 restructure plans and 9 credit approvals, the 5 TCG claims, the case links of RW-2026-000512, the ACE contract and plan facts, TRT-SYN-0601 and TRT-SYN-0602, and the claim of the unknown case UUID |
| JoinAssertion | Assertion | Fails the run when the DP04 answer does not carry the contract number and contract date from v_ace_account and the plan terms from v_ace_plan at request time, or when a snapshot row carries a contract or a plan value |
| CountAssertion | Assertion | Compares 40 built rows against the owning module count, and fails the run when the stamp is written on a difference or when a break with MSG-P1-002 is missing |
| AccessAssertion | Assertion | Fails the run when RW-PHONECOL or RW-TRIBE is not refused with MSG-P4-002, when the refusal is not logged, or when the data steward read does not answer |
| RunReportWriter | Reporter | Writes one run report with the trace, the per-assertion result and the gate outcome; format and retention Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0392; ASM-0567) |

**Environment and test data**

- Environment: SIT, one namespace, the four owning services deployed from their wave 2 builds or replaced by the §12.8 fakes. Harness repository, environment, seeding mechanism and evidence format: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0392; ASM-0567).
- Data: business date 2026-12-14 with the ALS batch COMPLETE at 06:20, 40 active treatments, 12 restructure plans with installments in v_ace_plan, 9 credit approvals, 5 TCG claims, case RW-2026-000512, user u-phone-02 holding RW-PHONECOL, TRT-SYN-0601, TRT-SYN-0602, case UUID 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000997, data_product_access version DPA-2026.12 and the prior published day 2026-12-13. No production record is copied.
- Reset: each run starts from the seeded state for 2026-12-14, so a repeated run is deterministic and the same report is produced.

**Build steps**

1. Build JourneyRunner and CompositeRouteClient against the published contract documents of rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-treatment, rwb-guarantee and rwb-access.
2. Publish FakePack for the five services from the same documents, and prove the harness runs green from Day 1 on the fakes.
3. Write Stage2Fixture with the 40 treatments, the 12 plans, the 9 approvals, the 5 claims and the case links, and test that a bad seed stops the run (X8).
4. Add the DP04 read assertion of AC1 through gateway-bff, with JoinAssertion, the catalog systems of record and the one-trace check.
5. Add the stage 2 observation and the count check of AC2 with CountAssertion, including the held stamp and the break naming 40 and 41.
6. Add the references break and the access set of AC3 with AccessAssertion, including the logged refusal and the data steward control read.
7. Add the repeat run and the end-of-day boundary of AC4, then the forced treatment failure with MSG-GEN-006 and MSG-P1-001, and the lock and evidence failures of X9 and X10.
8. Replace each fake with the real service as its I story lands, publish the run report per business date, and evaluate the pass or fail gate: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0392; ASM-0567).

**Feature switch:** the harness has no production feature flag and runs in the test environment only. The production switch it exercises is `rwb.dataengine.stage2-products` from the legacy solution plan: with it off the stage 2 step does not run, DP04 keeps the previous published day, and the harness asserts that state as the AC2 and AC5 baseline; with it on the step runs and the scenarios of §7 apply.

**Done when:** the journey runs green against the four deployed I stories in SIT, the run report for 2026-12-14 holds every assertion of §7 and §16 with its trace, the DP04 catalog entry shows in the admin data product read with Workbench and the two ACE views as systems of record, and the pass or fail gate agreed with QA is met for one full business date.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without a DP04 access row | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P1-001 | DP04 stale after a failed step | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P1-002 | Count check break held the publish | The {source} load for {date} was refused: {check}. The previous load is still in use. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | TreatmentQuery or GuaranteeClaimQuery unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P2-006 | Rerun while JOB-02 is running | {job} is already running. Wait for it to finish before you rerun it. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values; it does not own the message text. For MSG-P1-001 the {product} value is DP04 and {date} is 2026-12-13; for MSG-P1-002 the {source} value is DP04, {date} is 2026-12-14 and {check} is "Active treatment count 40 against 41"; for MSG-GEN-006 the {system} value is Treatment. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the access rows, the expected-by time, the tolerance and the counts are data held by rwb-source-data and rwb-access; the harness reads them and holds no copy.
- No personal data in logs, tests, traces or reports: the treatments, claims and cases are synthetic, and the report holds identifiers, codes, counts and timestamps only.
- No copy of ACE data: the contract number and contract date are read from v_ace_account and the plan terms from v_ace_plan at request time, and the JoinAssertion fails the run when a snapshot row carries a contract or a plan value.
- Treatments and claims go through their contracts: the harness reads rwb-treatment and rwb-guarantee and never their tables, and case links go through rwb-case.
- No call to NLEADS or the Thai Credit Guarantee Corporation: the credit approval arrives as a record on the case and the claim as a record of rwb-guarantee.
- No read of another service's schema and no direct ACE read: every read is an operation of §12.2, and the run fails on any cross-schema reference in the trace.
- One hop only: the harness fails a run when the trace shows a call chain deeper than the gateway and one owner.
- Each fake is replaced by the real service as its I story lands; a fake that outlives its service is a defect, not a configuration, and the harness never runs against UAT or production.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: moved from RWB-E2-011 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published query contract of the queue views as rwb-case serves it — `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` for My queue with its filters, sort and age, `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues` for the team queue summary with its count, oldest age, breach count and per-owner spread against the cap, and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases` for the drill down — together with the paging and page-size rules, the order that makes a page stable, the error envelope and its message codes, the right each answer requires, the 2 s one-hop budget, the nine contract tables and the contract fakes**, so that **the app, operations and test stories of this legacy key build against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1, and a field, an order or a count can never drift between rwb-case, the composite route and the case list without a failing build**.

The legacy key is moved with no business change: the operations, the filters, the sort, the counts, the page limits and the message texts are the ones RWB-E2-011 fixed. What this story adds is the contract form of them: one document owner, one shape per answer, one order per list, one error envelope and one fake per consumed answer.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The queue views are the most-consumed read surface of rwb-case: the My queue screen, the Team queues screen, the case list and its export, the review queue of the document hub and the steering dashboard all read the same two or three answers, and the composite route at the edge merges them with the answers of other services (DP-19). Three things therefore drift silently if no contract holds them: the computed row fields (`ageDays`, `serviceLevelDueAt`, `serviceLevelState`), the queue summary fields and their cap rule, and the order and paging that make two readers of the same list agree on what "page 2" is. A renamed queue count would empty a team screen without a failing build; a list whose order is not fixed would show one case twice across two pages and hide another.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_case`, REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`. It records that the counts these answers show move only through the events of `rwb.case.events.v1`, so no operation of this contract writes and no operation of this contract publishes (DP-14).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the document, topic and event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the retry and `.dlt` topic convention are the platform baseline (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The parameters contract of rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1042-CON, DP-06) and its reference-data contract (RWB-P3-E1043-CON, DP-07) are published, so the page-size limits, the caps and the list labels are declared as data and never as values in this document.
- The case list contract RWB-P3-E1031-CON and the queue contract RWB-P3-E1019-CON are published, so the Case page resource and the Queue resource this story extends have one owner document each and the added fields are an additive change to them.
- The timer contract RWB-P3-E1028-CON is published, so the meaning of `timer.status`, `timer.paused` and `timer.expires_at` behind `serviceLevelState`, `breachCount` and the sort is fixed by the story that writes them and not by this one.
- The Ownership Map gives `GET /cases`, `GET /queues` and `GET /queues/{queueId}/cases` to P3 rwb-case; this document declares no other service's operation as provided and names no operation the map does not already give P3.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the additive change to the rwb-case OpenAPI 3.1 document for the three read operations: the case row fields, the queue row fields, the paging parameters and the `X-Data-As-Of` header.
2. Fix the sort of the case list (`serviceLevelDueAt`, with the four groups of BR2 of the app story) and the tiebreaker, so two readers never sort differently.
3. Fix the paging rule: `page` and `size` with `total`, the default and maximum page size, and the stable order that makes a walk of pages complete and free of duplicates; declare no cursor token, because no source gives one.
4. State the summary rule of a queue: the count, the oldest entry date, the oldest age, the breach count and the per-owner spread against the cap, and that the count equals the case list count for the same filter (GAP-0707; GAP-0708; ASM-1254; ASM-1255).
5. Record the two consumed operations with their owner, their use and the 2 s budget, and map every failure to the error envelope and a message ID.
6. Record the event and workflow elements the answers depend on: the case events that move the counts, and the durable timer inside CaseWorkflow that writes the timer state the sort reads.
7. Publish the nine contract tables of section 12 and the contract fakes.
8. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the order, the paging walk, the error mapping, the rights, the budget, the drift between a fake and the document and the retired element.
9. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P3-E2011-APP, to the operations story of this legacy key and to the consumers of the list.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 500 with the platform error envelope | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A field is renamed, retyped or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1 |
| X3 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC9 |
| X4 | A page size outside 1 to 200 reaches the operation | 422 with MSG-GEN-002 naming the field, the minimum and the maximum | MSG-GEN-002 | AC6 |
| X5 | An age range arrives inverted | 422 with MSG-GEN-003 naming the two fields | MSG-GEN-003 | AC6 |
| X6 | A caller reads a queue outside its teams | 404 with MSG-P4-003 and not an empty page | MSG-P4-003 | AC4 |
| X7 | The freshness answer does not arrive inside the budget | The list is returned without the current business date and the header is omitted; no row is dropped and no count changes | None | AC8 |
| X8 | An operation of another service is written into this document as provided | The review fails: the document lists only rwb-case's own operations | None | AC1 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the same-service contracts it extends and the Ownership Map only |
| Negotiable | Field-level types and lengths are settled with the consumers; the three operations, the orders, the paging rule and the two consumed answers are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app and test stories of this legacy key on Day 1 and every consumer of the list and the queue rows |
| Estimable | One document, one additive change, two consumed operations, nine contract tables, three fakes and nine contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Contract baseline of the queue views

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule of the platform library is in force
    Given the rwb-case read surface is published under the base /api/recovery/case/v1
    Given the ownership map gives GET /cases, GET /queues and GET /queues/{queueId}/cases to rwb-case

  Scenario: AC1 The three read operations are declared with their owner (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-case is published with this change
    When it is validated against the OpenAPI 3.1 schema
    Then it validates with no error
    Then it declares GET /cases with the Case page resource, GET /queues with the Queue array and GET /queues/{queueId}/cases with the Case page resource, all under the base /api/recovery/case/v1 and owned by rwb-case
    Then the document names no other service's operation as provided
    Then every added property is optional in the schema, so a consumer of the previous version keeps working
    Then it declares the response header X-Data-As-Of on the two case answers

  Scenario: AC2 The case answer fixes the My queue filters, the sort and the row fields (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the GET /cases operation declared in the document
    When its parameters and its row fields are reviewed
    Then the request takes owner, stage, route, status, ageFrom, ageTo, queue, page, size and sort
    Then sort takes serviceLevelDueAt as the My queue default and the order is breached first, then running by due date earliest first, then paused, then the cases with no service level, with the case ID as the tiebreaker
    Then each row carries the existing case fields plus ageDays, serviceLevelDueAt and serviceLevelState, and serviceLevelState takes one of BREACHED, RUNNING, PAUSED and NONE
    Then the document states that ageDays is the calendar days from the entry date to the business date and that serviceLevelState is read from the timer projection and never recomputed by a consumer

  Scenario: AC3 The queue answer fixes the team summary and the spread against the cap (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the GET /queues operation declared in the document
    When its row fields are reviewed against the queue contract and the parameters contract
    Then each row carries the queue identity and the computed openCaseCount, oldestEntryDate, oldestAgeDays, breachCount and owners[]
    Then owners[] carries ownerUserId, openCaseCount and atCap, and atCap is a boolean against the cap in force
    Then the document states that openCaseCount counts the cases whose status is not Closed and equals the case list total for the same queue, that oldestAgeDays is the calendar days from oldestEntryDate to the business date, and that breachCount counts the open cases whose service level timer has status EXPIRED
    Then the cap is declared as data read from the queue row or from the member's personal capacity (GAP-0707; ASM-1254)
    Then the summary is declared either live from recovery_case and timer or from the reconciled queue_measure snapshot (GAP-0708; ASM-1255)

  Scenario: AC4 The queue-scoped answer fixes the page and the out-of-scope response (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the GET /queues/{queueId}/cases operation declared in the document
    When its path, its query and its error responses are reviewed
    Then it takes the path parameter queueId and the query page, size and sort
    Then its rows are the rows of GET /cases with the same computed fields and the same order
    Then a queue that is unknown or outside the caller's teams answers 404 with MSG-P4-003 and never an empty page
    Then it requires Queue and allocation R where GET /cases requires Case record R

  Scenario: AC5 Paging, page size and the order that stands in place of a cursor (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the paging parameters declared on the two case answers
    When the paging rule is reviewed
    Then page is zero-based and defaults to 0, size defaults to 50 and takes 1 to 200, and the answer carries page, size and total
    Then the document declares no cursor token, because no source gives one, and fixes the order and the tiebreaker so that a walk of pages is complete and free of duplicates
    Then a size outside 1 to 200 answers 422 with MSG-GEN-002 and an inverted age range answers 422 with MSG-GEN-003
    Then the default and the maximum are declared as parameter rows of parameter_catalog and not as values in the document (DP-06)

  Scenario: AC6 The error envelope and the message codes (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the error responses declared on the three operations
    When each condition is mapped to its status and its message ID
    Then 401 no session maps to MSG-P4-001, 403 a missing right to MSG-P4-002, 404 a queue out of scope to MSG-P4-003, 422 an inverted age range to MSG-GEN-003 and an out-of-range size to MSG-GEN-002, and 503 a store failure to the envelope
    Then MSG-P3-017 is declared as the empty-list state of GET /cases and not as an error
    Then MSG-P1-001 is declared as the stale-data banner with the date carried in X-Data-As-Of, and MSG-P3-004 as the paused marker of a row with serviceLevelState PAUSED
    Then every text is the legacy text unchanged and the envelope is the platform envelope, never a local one

  Scenario: AC7 The rights each answer requires and the scope rule (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the security and scope statements of the three operations
    When they are compared with the roles and the right names of the target
    Then GET /cases requires Case record R, and GET /queues and GET /queues/{queueId}/cases require Queue and allocation R
    Then every row is filtered by the caller's scope before it is counted, so a count never includes a case the caller may not read
    Then the authorisation is declared as the rwb-access authorise contract through the guard library, cached per request (DP-08)
    Then a refusal is declared as 403 and a scope miss as 404, and neither as an empty answer

  Scenario: AC8 The two consumed answers and the 2 s one-hop budget (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed operations of the document
    When they are compared with the Ownership Map
    Then POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise names P4 rwb-access as its owner and is marked faked
    Then GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness names P1 rwb-source-data as its owner and is marked faked (GAP-0709; ASM-1256)
    Then every consumed row states one hop, the 2 s timeout, the GET retry once with jitter and the breaker per downstream
    Then a freshness answer that does not arrive inside the budget omits the header and drops no row, and a failed authorise answers 403 or 503 and never an empty page
    Then the two operations the app story reads as data, the parameters and the reference data of rwb-case, are declared as in-process library reads and not as cross-service rows

  Scenario: AC9 The nine contract tables are complete and the fakes match them (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the contract section of this story
    When the nine sub-tables are reviewed
    Then each of 12.1 to 12.9 is present and names its owner from the Ownership Map or None where the element is empty
    Then 12.3 and 12.4 record None and name the case events that move the counts as published by their own stories
    Then 12.6 records None and names JOB-05 as retired
    Then the three contract fakes answer the paths and the payloads of 12.2 and the shapes of 12.1, and the contract tests compare each fake with the document and fail on any drift
```

These nine criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only; they restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P3-E2011-APP, which keeps the twelve legacy criteria with their own tags.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/case/v1`; the document never declares another service's path as provided | DP-13; Architecture v5 slide 41 notes |
| BR2 | Event names are `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1` on the topic `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, with retry and `.dlt` topics | DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR3 | A read declares no Idempotency-Key and writes nothing; a command declares it and stores its response | Architecture v5 slide 11; DP-09 |
| BR4 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition; the business message texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story | Architecture v5 platform baseline; Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR5 | A schema change is additive within a major version; a breaking change is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |
| BR6 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-case; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided | Ownership Map v1 |
| BR7 | The count of a queue is the count of the same filter through the case list, so the two answers can never disagree on the same rows | REQ-WKM-006; NFR-018 |
| BR8 | No business value is fixed in the contract: the page-size default and maximum, the caps and the labels stay parameters, queue rows or reference data | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; DP-06; DP-07 |
| BR9 | No personal data is declared in an answer: rows carry case numbers, codes, dates, counts and staff user IDs only, and the deviation code of a paused row is composed at the edge from the S8 answer | DP-19; REQ-WKM-002 |
| BR10 | The list order is part of the contract: a consumer that sorts differently from the document has a defect, not a preference | REQ-WKM-001; R-UNI-30 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The three operations, the paging rule and the orders are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app and test stories and the rwb-access and rwb-source-data owners accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A field is added within major version 1, for example a new service level state | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A field is removed, renamed or retyped, or an order changes | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | An operation of another owner appears as provided | The review of AC1 fails | In review |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-case | Owns the OpenAPI document and the fakes of the three operations; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change and a new major version |
| Consuming teams (app and test stories, the composite route, the case list, the review queue and the dashboard) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| rwb-access owner | Signs off the authorise row, the right names and the scope rule |
| rwb-source-data owner | Signs off the freshness row, the header and the stale-data rule |
| Platform library owner | Owns the error envelope, the CloudEvents envelope and the naming rule this document reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field is declared in an answer |

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Case row | The Case resource of RWB-P3-E1031-CON plus `ageDays`, `serviceLevelDueAt` and `serviceLevelState`, from `recovery_case` DF-CAS-001, DF-CAS-002, DF-CAS-003, DF-CAS-005, DF-CAS-006, DF-CAS-008, DF-CAS-009, DF-CAS-010, DF-CAS-011 and DF-CAS-013, and from the open `timer` DF-WRK-028, DF-WRK-030, DF-WRK-032, DF-WRK-034 and DF-WRK-035 |
| Case page | `items[]`, `page`, `size`, `total`, and the `X-Data-As-Of` header |
| Queue row | The Queue resource of RWB-P3-E1019-CON plus `openCaseCount`, `oldestEntryDate`, `oldestAgeDays`, `breachCount` and `owners[]` with `ownerUserId`, `openCaseCount` and `atCap` (GAP-0707; GAP-0708; ASM-1254; ASM-1255) |
| Queue identity | `id`, `queueCode`, `queueName`, `teamCode`, `roleCode` and the cap, from `queue` DF-WRK-001 to DF-WRK-007 |
| Cap | `queue.capacity_cap` or `queue_member.capacity` DF-WRK-048, whichever the queue in force uses (GAP-0707; ASM-1254) |
| Snapshot | `queue_measure` DF-RPT-021 to DF-RPT-030, read only when the reconciled snapshot is the source in force (GAP-0708; ASM-1255) |
| Parameters and labels | `queueview.page-size.default` 50 and `queueview.page-size.max` 200 as parameter rows; LOV-STAGE, LOV-ROUTE and LOV-CASE-STATUS through the reference-data contract |
| Error envelope | The platform envelope with one message ID per condition; the texts of section 14 |

The field-level types, lengths and required flags of the added properties are settled in the baseline review; this story fixes the names, the optionality rule of AC1, the orders of AC2 to AC5 and the summary rule of AC3.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-case (P3); base `/api/recovery/case/v1`.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases` | Case page: filters by owner, stage, route, status, age, queue; `page`, `size`, `sort`; rows with `ageDays`, `serviceLevelDueAt` and `serviceLevelState`; header `X-Data-As-Of` | Case record R, scope applied |
| GET | `/queues` | Queue array: the queue identity plus `openCaseCount`, `oldestEntryDate`, `oldestAgeDays`, `breachCount` and `owners[]` with `ownerUserId`, `openCaseCount` and `atCap` | Queue and allocation R, scope applied |
| GET | `/queues/{queueId}/cases` | Case page of one queue: `page`, `size`, `sort`, the same rows and header as `/cases` | Queue and allocation R, scope applied |

The three operations answer 401, 403 and 503; the two case answers also answer 422, and the queue-scoped answer also answers 404. None takes an Idempotency-Key and none writes. Paging is `page` and `size` with `total`, size 1 to 200 and default 50; the document declares no cursor token and fixes the order and the tiebreaker instead.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The role, scope and right check on the three operations, cached per request, faked with a grant and two refusals (DP-08) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | The business date of the case data, for the header and the stale banner, faked with the current date, an earlier date and a slow answer (GAP-0709; ASM-1256) |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retry once with jitter and a breaker per downstream. The parameters and reference data of rwb-case are in-process library reads of the same service, not consumed rows.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The contract publishes no event type. The counts and the order the answers show move only through the five events that their own stories publish on `rwb.case.events.v1` — CaseCreated, CaseAllocated, CaseTransferred, CaseStateChanged and TimerBreached — and this baseline declares them as depended on, not as published here.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` and `rwb.source-data.AceDataLate.v1` on `rwb.source-data.events.v1` are P1's and are consumed by the case workflow stories and by gateway-bff for the banner; `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` and `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` are consumed by RWB-P3-E1028-APP to pause and resume the timer this contract reads. This read path subscribes to none of them.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow | Workflow, parent, one per case, workflow ID = case ID | `rwb-case` | Holds the durable service level timer and writes the `timer` rows whose status, pause flag and expiry the sort and the breach count read; owned by RWB-P3-E1028-APP, and this baseline registers no activity and no child workflow |

No activity is registered by this story; the row fixes what the read path may assume about the writer.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The five-minute timer check (JOB-05) is retired with the TimerDue event (Architecture v5 slides 42 and 44), the 06:30 rebalancing Schedule (JOB-06) belongs to RWB-P3-E1030-APP, and this baseline registers no Schedule, no cron entry and no job name.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| recovery_case | P3 (rwb_case) | The case row behind every list row: number, product group, status, stage, route, owner, queue, team and entry date |
| queue | P3 (rwb_case) | The queue identity and the cap a queue row carries |
| queue_member | P3 (rwb_case) | The personal capacity of an owner, when that is the cap in force (GAP-0707; ASM-1254) |
| timer | P3 (rwb_case) | The open SERVICE_LEVEL timer of a case: due date, pause flag and status |
| queue_measure | P3 (rwb_case) | The reconciled snapshot, read only when it is the source in force (GAP-0708; ASM-1255) |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_case | The envelope of the events the counts depend on; not written by the read path |

`lov_value`, `reference_row` and `parameter_value` are read through the rwb-case contracts and never joined in SQL; no other schema is named (DP-01, DP-06, DP-07).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-access WireMock | `POST /authorise` with a granted answer for Case record R and Queue and allocation R, a refused answer for a role without the right, and a refused scope over SME-NTH for a scope Team in MTG-BKK | App story, contract tests |
| rwb-source-data WireMock | `GET /data-products/freshness` answering 2026-12-15, answering 2026-12-14 on business date 2026-12-15, and a delayed answer beyond 2 s | App story, contract tests |
| rwb-case read fake | The three operations with the resource shapes of 12.1, an empty page with `total` 0, a page of 200, a queue out of scope and a paused row | Composite route, case list, review queue, dashboard, contract tests |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 3 provided, 2 consumed | Cases, queues and queue cases provided; authorise and freshness consumed; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | None published, none consumed | The five case events are declared as depended on and are published by their own stories |
| Temporal | None added | The timer behind the status read here lives in CaseWorkflow and belongs to RWB-P3-E1028-APP |
| File | None | No file in this contract |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The additive change to `openapi/rwb-case-v1.yaml` for the three operations, the case row and queue row components shared with RWB-P3-E1031-CON and RWB-P3-E1019-CON, the contract README rows for the order, the paging rule and the stale-data rule, and the three WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_case`; the three answers read this service's tables only and name no other schema | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case: the page-size default and maximum are rows of `parameter_catalog` | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case: LOV-STAGE, LOV-ROUTE and LOV-CASE-STATUS | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library, on the three operations | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.case.events.v1`; the naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in schema `rwb_case`; this baseline names the read-side index the app story adds and owns no migration itself | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route for SCR-02 and SCR-07 | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

No pattern is claimed outside this list: the contract adds no decision record, no Drools model, no ACE view and no Quartz job.

**Build steps**

1. Add the case row fields, the queue row fields and the `X-Data-As-Of` header to the document; validate the additive rule of AC1 in the pipeline.
2. Fix the orders and the tiebreaker of AC2 to AC5 as schema constraints and README rows, including the page walk and the absence of a cursor token.
3. Write the summary rule of AC3 and the reason of its two gap rows into the document, so a consumer cannot read a count as a snapshot or a snapshot as a count.
4. Record the two consumed rows with their owner, their budget and their failure mapping; map every failure code of AC6.
5. Record the event and workflow rows of AC9 and add the absence test for the retired timer check.
6. Publish the three fakes and the nine contract tests; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build.
7. Baseline tag and the consumer sign-off note, including the rwb-access and rwb-source-data owners and the consumers of the list.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI artefact validates in the pipeline, the nine contract tests pass, the three fakes answer every path and the drift test is green, and the app story and the consumers of the list have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-002 | Page size outside 1 to 200 | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Age to is less than age from | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-P3-017 | The list has no case for the person and filters | There are no cases in this queue. |
| MSG-P4-003 | A queue outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The case data is from an earlier business date | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P3-004 | A case on hold for a deviation | This case is on hold for {deviation}. The prescription date is still {date}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right reads one of the three operations | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The message IDs are contract elements and the texts are the agreed legacy texts unchanged. MSG-P4-001 is an id of the rwb-access contract and appears here only in the mapping of the three operations; the other ids are the ones the operations and the header return, and the envelope is the platform envelope. Which value fills the `{product}` of MSG-P1-001 on a case list is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0709; ASM-1256).

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves SCR-02 Case list in its My queue view (states Loading, Empty, List, Filtered) and SCR-07 Team queues (states Loading, List), through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The route calls rwb-case for the list and the queue rows and other owners for the rest of the screen; this baseline fixes the rwb-case answers only, and the composite route specification and the screen field list belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the page-size limits, the caps, the labels and the states are parameters, queue rows, reference data or enumerations the timer story fixes, never values chosen by this document.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: case numbers, codes, dates, counts, amounts and staff user IDs only; no customer name, address, identity number or contact point is declared.
- The contract names only rwb-case's tables and only operations owned by rwb-case; the authorise and freshness operations are consumed and faked, never declared as provided (DP-01, DP-08).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- ACE data is reached only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views; this document declares no ACE view and no cross-schema join.
- No retired element is reintroduced: a build that declares a timer-check Schedule, a timer-check job or a TimerDue event fails the absence test of AC9.
- Every example in the document is synthetic; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The error envelope and the naming rule come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: moved from RWB-E2-011 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **screens for my queue and my team's queues with filters by stage, route, status and age, sorted by service level, served by rwb-case from its own `rwb_case` rows over `/api/recovery/case/v1` and through the gateway-bff composite route**, so that **every person sees their work in one place and the team manager sees the team's load**.

The three read operations behind the two screens are `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` for My queue with its filters, sort and age, `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues` for the team queue summary with its count, oldest age, breach count and per-owner spread against the cap, and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases` for the drill down from a queue row. The legacy story is moved with no business change: the behaviour, the values, the sort, the counts, the page limits and the message texts are the ones RWB-E2-011 fixed, and this story only re-homes them on the target naming of rwb-case.

In the target the monolith screen is not a screen model held by the case service: it is a composite route at the edge (DP-19). gateway-bff calls rwb-case once per answer and merges the answers into the screen model, so rwb-case returns the list and the queue rows and never composes a second service's panel. rwb-case authorises every call through the rwb-access authorise contract and its guard library (DP-08), reads its list labels and its page-size limits as data through the reference-data and parameters contracts of rwb-case (DP-07, DP-06), reads the business date of the case data from the rwb-source-data freshness answer, and reads nothing else outside schema `rwb_case` (DP-01). The read path writes no row and publishes no event; the counts it shows move only when their own stories publish CaseCreated, CaseAllocated, CaseTransferred, CaseStateChanged and TimerBreached on `rwb.case.events.v1` (DP-14).

##### 2. Business rationale

Cases are run from team spreadsheets and the team manager learns of a late case from email. With about 23,600 open cases at go-live (NFR-001), a case owner needs their own list ordered by the next service level date, and the team manager needs each queue's depth, oldest case and breaches without a report request. This story gives both views on the case list and the team queues screen. It meets REQ-WKM-001, REQ-WKM-002 and REQ-WKM-006. The measure is that the team queue counts equal the case list counts for the same team every day.

Nothing in that rationale changes in the target, which is why the legacy key is moved and not reworked. What changes is where the answers come from: the list and the queue rows are two operations of one owning service instead of two screens of one monolith, and the screen is composed at the edge inside one 2 s budget (DP-19, ADR-020). The queue view is now the only place a team manager can see load, ageing and breaches without a report request, because the reporting copy is read from events by rwb-reporting and arrives later than the working list.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P3-E1020-APP is done: every case has a queue and an owner by rule, so a queue row and an owner row are both populated.
- RWB-P3-E1031-CON is published: the case list contract (SCR-02) shows queue and owner with filters by queue, team and status, and the export; this story extends that page and does not redefine it.
- RWB-P3-E1028-APP is done: each assigned case has a SERVICE_LEVEL timer, and that story writes `timer.status`, `timer.paused` and the escalation fields this view reads.
- RWB-P3-E2011-CON is published: the OpenAPI 3.1 document of the three read operations, the page and queue resources, the error envelope, the paging and sort rules and the contract fakes, so the build starts on Day 1 against the fake (DP-11).
- RWB-P3-E1019-APP is done: queues are loaded with their team, role and caseload cap (RWB-E1-019; cap values DL23, assumed 150).
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1042-CON are published: the parameters contract of rwb-case with its client library, so the page-size default and maximum are read as data and never written in code (DP-06).
- RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are published: the reference-data contract of rwb-case with its client library, so LOV-STAGE, LOV-ROUTE and LOV-CASE-STATUS come as data with their version (DP-07).
- RWB-PLT-E1037-CON is published: the access guard library, and rwb-access answers the authorise check over its contract, cached per request (DP-08).
- The signed-in person holds RW-CASEOWN (scope Own) or RW-TEAMMGR (scope Team) with the scope set by rwb-access (RWB-E1-037 in the legacy numbering).
- The ACE batch for the business date is COMPLETE, or the freshness answer of rwb-source-data reports an earlier business date and the list shows its date as stale with MSG-P1-001 (GAP-0709; ASM-1256).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route for SCR-02 and SCR-07 (DP-19). Its path, its merge order and the screen field list belong to that contract; this story fixes only the three answers rwb-case returns.
- RWB-PLT-E1047-CON is published: the topic and event naming library (DP-14). RWB-PLT-E1044-CON is published: the per-service Flyway sequence in schema `rwb_case` (DP-15).
- The login is the rwb-case login (DP-02): one login and one connection pool for the service, with grants on schema `rwb_case` only (Architecture v5 slide 29).

##### 4. Flow

1. Case owner: opens My queue from the menu, reached through the App Gateway at `/recovery/*` and the gateway-bff session (DP-19).
2. Front end: calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` with `owner=me`, `sort=serviceLevelDueAt` and the filters kept for the session, one hop through the composite route.
3. rwb-case: authorises the read through the rwb-access contract, `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise`, right R on Case record and on Queue and allocation, scope applied, cached per request (DP-08).
4. rwb-case: applies the scope, the filters and the sort and returns one page of cases with age, status and service level state, plus the `X-Data-As-Of` header carrying the business date of the case data that the freshness answer of rwb-source-data reports (GAP-0709; ASM-1256).
5. Front end: shows the list in state List, or Empty with MSG-P3-017.
6. Case owner: sets the stage filter to Litigation; the front end keeps the filter in session storage and reloads the list in state Filtered.
7. Team manager: opens Team queues from the menu; the front end calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues`, one hop.
8. rwb-case: returns each queue in the manager's teams with the open case count, the oldest entry date, the breach count and the open cases per owner against the cap.
9. Team manager: selects a queue; the front end calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases` and shows the cases sorted by service level.
10. gateway-bff: merges the answers into the screen model and, for a paused row, takes the deviation code that the hover of MSG-P3-004 names from the rwb-deviation answer of the screen; rwb-case returns the paused state and the open flag only.
11. Nothing in this flow writes: the three operations are reads, no case, no queue and no timer changes, and the read path publishes no event and writes no outbox row.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The person has no case in scope for the filters | Empty state | MSG-P3-017 | AC4 |
| X2 | Age from is greater than age to | The request is refused; the list is not reloaded | MSG-GEN-003 | AC5 |
| X3 | Page size above 200 | The request is refused | MSG-GEN-002 | AC6 |
| X4 | A team manager opens a queue of another team | Not found | MSG-P4-003 | AC7 |
| X5 | Today's ACE batch has not arrived | The list shows with the stale banner and the date of the data | MSG-P1-001 | AC8 |
| X6 | A case's service level timer is paused by a deviation | The case shows "Paused" and sorts after running timers | MSG-P3-004 | AC9 |
| X7 | A role without Case record R or without Queue and allocation R opens either view | Refused with 403 by the rwb-access check behind the endpoint; the answer carries the refusal and not an empty list | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-011-13 |

The refusal of X7 is a refusal and never an empty page: a consumer that reads an empty page as "no work" would hide a permission problem, which is why the two answers are distinguished by status and not by body.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads the case, queue and timer rows that RWB-P3-E1020-APP, RWB-P3-E1019-APP and RWB-P3-E1028-APP already write; builds against the published contracts and their fakes, so neither rwb-access nor rwb-source-data needs to exist in the development environment |
| Negotiable | Columns and filter order can change; the sort, the counts and the page limits are fixed |
| Valuable | Each person works one ordered list; the team manager sees load and breaches |
| Estimable | Three endpoints extended, one consumed freshness answer, one reference-data and one parameters read, two screens |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | API tests on a seeded database and browser tests on both screens; the scope refusal and the stale banner are stubbed in the contract fakes and real in SIT |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Queue view screens: my queue, team queues, filters and ageing

  Background:
    Given the business date is 2026-12-15
    Given team "MTG-BKK" has queues "MTG-BKK-CO" and "MTG-BKK-LIT" with a caseload cap of 150
    Given user "U-CO-01" holds RW-CASEOWN in team "MTG-BKK" and user "U-TM-01" holds RW-TEAMMGR for team "MTG-BKK"

  Scenario: AC1 My queue (legacy RWB-E2-011 AC1)
    Given "U-CO-01" owns 40 open cases, 3 with an expired service level timer and 37 with running timers
    When "U-CO-01" opens My queue
    Then 40 cases list in one page
    Then the 3 breached cases come first, then the 37 by service level due date, earliest first
    Then each row shows the case number, product group, stage, status, age in days from the entry date and the service level due date

  Scenario: AC2 Team view (legacy RWB-E2-011 AC2)
    Given "MTG-BKK-CO" holds 412 open cases with the oldest entered on 2026-09-02 and 9 breaches
    Given "MTG-BKK-LIT" holds 38 open cases with the oldest entered on 2026-10-20 and 0 breaches
    When "U-TM-01" opens Team queues
    Then "MTG-BKK-CO" shows count 412, oldest case age 104 days and 9 breaches
    Then "MTG-BKK-LIT" shows count 38, oldest case age 56 days and 0 breaches
    Then each owner in "MTG-BKK-CO" shows their open case count against the cap of 150

  Scenario: AC3 Filter (legacy RWB-E2-011 AC3)
    Given "U-CO-01" owns 12 open cases on stage "LITIGATION" and 28 on other stages
    When the stage filter is set to "LITIGATION" and the list refreshes
    Then only the 12 litigation cases show
    Then after "U-CO-01" opens a case and returns to My queue the filter is still "LITIGATION"
    Then after sign-out and sign-in the filter is cleared

  Scenario: AC4 Empty queue (legacy RWB-E2-011 AC4)
    Given "U-CO-02" owns no open case
    When "U-CO-02" opens My queue
    Then the screen shows the empty state with MSG-P3-017

  Scenario: AC5 Age range in the wrong order (legacy RWB-E2-011 AC5)
    When "U-CO-01" sets age from 120 and age to 90
    Then the system refuses the request with MSG-GEN-003 naming "age to" and "age from"
    Then the list keeps its previous rows

  Scenario: AC6 Page size above the limit (legacy RWB-E2-011 AC6)
    When the front end requests My queue with page size 500
    Then the system refuses the request with MSG-GEN-002 naming "size", 1 and 200

  Scenario: AC7 Queue of another team (legacy RWB-E2-011 AC7)
    Given the rwb-access contract mock returns scope Team for "U-TM-01" over team "MTG-BKK" and no scope over team "SME-NTH"
    Given queue "SME-NTH-CO" belongs to team "SME-NTH"
    When "U-TM-01" requests the cases of "SME-NTH-CO"
    Then the system does not find the response with MSG-P4-003

  Scenario: AC8 Stale data (legacy RWB-E2-011 AC8)
    Given the rwb-source-data contract mock returns the latest complete ACE business date 2026-12-14
    Given the ACE batch of 2026-12-15 has not arrived and the case data is from 2026-12-14
    When "U-CO-01" opens My queue
    Then the 40 cases show with the stale banner MSG-P1-001 naming the date 2026-12-14

  Scenario: AC9 Paused service level (legacy RWB-E2-011 AC9)
    Given the rwb-deviation contract mock returns deviation "X1" open on 2 of the 40 cases
    Given 2 of the 40 cases have a deviation "X1" open and their service level timers paused
    When "U-CO-01" opens My queue
    Then the 2 cases show "Paused" with MSG-P3-004 on hover and sort after the 37 running timers

  Scenario: AC10 Age boundary (legacy RWB-E2-011 AC10)
    Given case "RW-2026-000301" entered on 2026-09-16 and case "RW-2026-000302" entered on 2026-09-17
    When "U-CO-01" sets age from 90 and age to 90
    Then only "RW-2026-000301" shows, with age 90 days

  Scenario: AC11 Counts reconcile to the case list (legacy RWB-E2-011 AC11)
    When "U-TM-01" reads the count of "MTG-BKK-CO" on Team queues and the case list filtered by queue "MTG-BKK-CO" and status not "CLOSED"
    Then both show 412

  Scenario: AC12 Load time (legacy RWB-E2-011 AC12)
    Given "U-CO-01" owns 500 open cases
    When "U-CO-01" opens My queue with page size 200
    Then the first page shows within 2 seconds at the 95th percentile over 20 runs
```

**Note.** The twelve criteria are the legacy ones word for word with their origin tag; no value, no message and no count is changed by the move. The three mock Givens stand in for the answers rwb-case and the composite route take from other services: the rwb-access scope answer of AC7, the rwb-source-data freshness answer of AC8 and the rwb-deviation answer that names the deviation of a paused row in AC9. AC12 is a response-time criterion and is levelled NFR in section 16.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | My queue shows the open cases whose owner is the signed-in person; Team queues shows only the queues of the manager's teams | roles.txt default scope (Own, Team); CTL-09 |
| BR2 | Sort order: breached service level first, then running by due date earliest first, then paused, then no service level timer | REQ-WKM-001; R-UNI-30 |
| BR3 | Age is the number of calendar days from the case entry date to the business date | DF-CAS-013; labels.txt Stage clock |
| BR4 | A breach is an open case whose SERVICE_LEVEL timer has status EXPIRED | R-UNI-30; REQ-CWC-011 |
| BR5 | The open case count of a queue is its cases with status not Closed, and equals the case list count for the same queue | REQ-WKM-006; NFR-018 |
| BR6 | An owner at or above the queue's caseload cap is shown at cap | Queue field capacity_cap; DL23 (GAP-0707; ASM-1254) |
| BR7 | A timer paused by a deviation shows as paused; the prescription date keeps running | R-DEV-01; R-UNI-43 |
| BR8 | Filters are kept for the browser session only and are not stored on the server | Principle 1 (no business value stored per user) |
| BR9 | The three operations are reads of `rwb_case` rows: they write nothing, take no lock and publish no event, so a queue count never changes because a person looked at it | DP-01; Architecture v5 slide 11 |
| BR10 | The page-size default and maximum, the caps and every label are data read through the parameters and reference-data contracts or from the queue row, never values in code | DP-06; DP-07; REQ-WKM-006 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It reads cases, queues and timers only.

| What moves the counts this view shows | Cause | What this view then shows | Owner story |
|---|---|---|---|
| The open count of a queue | CaseCreated, CaseAllocated, CaseTransferred or CaseStateChanged on `rwb.case.events.v1` | The new count, the new oldest entry date and the new per-owner spread on the next read | RWB-P3-E1018-APP; RWB-P3-E1020-APP; RWB-P3-E1021-APP |
| The breach count of a queue | The durable service level timer expires and escalates | The case moves to the first sort group and the queue counts one more breach | RWB-P3-E1028-APP |
| The service level state of a row | A deviation pauses or resumes the timer | PAUSED with the position after the running timers, then RUNNING again | RWB-P3-E1028-APP; S8 |
| The business date of the data | The ACE batch completes for a later business date | The stale banner disappears and every age is computed from the new date | rwb-source-data; RWB-P3-E1030-APP |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Opens My queue (Case record R, scope Own); reads queue rows of own queue (Queue and allocation R) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Opens Team queues and My queue (Queue and allocation R, Case record R, scope Team) |
| RW-CAPACITY, capacity and workforce planner | Opens Team queues (Queue and allocation R, scope All) |
| RW-RESTRUCT, RW-LITOFF | Open My queue for the cases they own (Case record R) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads both views (R, scope All); changes nothing |
| rwb-access | Answers the role, scope and right check through its authorise contract, cached per request; it owns the role, scope and masking policy and this story owns none of them |

Reading a queue row needs no reference-data administration right: the labels arrive already resolved through the reference-data contract, and a person who may read the list may read its labels.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/case/v1`; owner rwb-case (P3). The three operations exist in the target map; this story adds to them the fields and the checks the two screens need.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Added in this story | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases` | List the cases in the caller's scope with filters, paging, age and service level state | The `route` filter, `sort=serviceLevelDueAt` as the default order for My queue, the computed `ageDays`, `serviceLevelDueAt` and `serviceLevelState` (BREACHED, RUNNING, PAUSED, NONE), and the `X-Data-As-Of` response header carrying the business date of the case data | Case record R, scope applied |
| GET | `/queues` | List the queues of the caller's teams with their load | The computed `openCaseCount`, `oldestEntryDate`, `oldestAgeDays`, `breachCount` and `owners[]` with `ownerUserId`, `openCaseCount` and `atCap` (GAP-0707; GAP-0708; ASM-1254; ASM-1255) | Queue and allocation R, scope applied |
| GET | `/queues/{queueId}/cases` | List the cases of one queue, sorted by service level | The scope check that answers 404 for a queue outside the caller's teams, and the same computed fields and header as `/cases` | Queue and allocation R, scope applied |

Errors for the three: 401 no session (MSG-P4-001), 403 no right (MSG-P4-002), 404 queue unknown or outside scope (MSG-P4-003), 422 age range inverted (MSG-GEN-003) or page size outside its range (MSG-GEN-002), 503 store down. Idempotency is not applicable to a read.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data | The business date of the case data, for the `X-Data-As-Of` header and the stale banner (GAP-0709; ASM-1256) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The role, scope and right check on each of the three operations, cached per request (DP-08) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |

Two calls, no chain. The freshness answer is cached for the request and for the business date, so a page of rows does not ask again per row. The stage, route and status labels are read through the rwb-case reference-data contract (RWB-P3-E1043-CON, DP-07) and the page-size limits through the rwb-case parameters contract (RWB-P3-E1042-CON, DP-06) as in-process library reads of the same service, so neither is a cross-service row. The deviation code the hover of MSG-P3-004 names is composed at the edge from the rwb-deviation answer of the screen, so this story adds no deviation read to rwb-case and returns the paused state and the open flag only.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The read path publishes nothing and writes no outbox row. The counts and the sort move only when CaseCreated, CaseAllocated, CaseTransferred, CaseStateChanged and TimerBreached are published on `rwb.case.events.v1` by their own stories, and this story subscribes to none of them.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` moves the business date the freshness answer reports, and it is consumed by the case workflow stories on task queue `rwb-case`; this view reads the answer and subscribes to nothing. `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` and `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` are consumed by RWB-P3-E1028-APP to pause and resume the timer this view renders.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow | Workflow, parent, one per case, workflow ID = case ID | `rwb-case` | Holds the durable service level timer that writes the status, the pause flag and the escalation this view reads; owned by RWB-P3-E1028-APP, and this story adds no workflow and no activity to it |
| Queue summary read | Query inside the service | `rwb-case` | Groups `recovery_case` by `queue_id` and `owner_user_id`, joins the open SERVICE_LEVEL timer of each case, and orders the rows by the caller's teams |

###### 12.6 Schedules

None registered by this story. The 06:30 rebalancing Schedule (JOB-06) and the daily queue measure snapshot belong to RWB-P3-E1030-APP, and the nightly reporting copy belongs to rwb-reporting; this view registers no Schedule and reads no scheduler state.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| recovery_case | P3 (rwb_case) | The case row behind every list row: number, product group, status, stage, route, owner, queue, team, entry date and the open flag |
| queue | P3 (rwb_case) | The queue row of Team queues: code, name, team, role and cap |
| queue_member | P3 (rwb_case) | The personal capacity of an owner, when the per-owner cap in force is the personal one (GAP-0707; ASM-1254) |
| timer | P3 (rwb_case) | The open SERVICE_LEVEL timer of a case: type, due date, pause flag and status, for the sort and the breach count |
| queue_measure | P3 (rwb_case) | The reconciled snapshot of a queue, read only and only when it is in force (GAP-0708; ASM-1255) |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_case | Not written by this read path |

No other table is named. `lov_value`, `reference_row` and `parameter_value` are read through the rwb-case contracts and never joined in SQL, and no schema other than `rwb_case` is read (DP-01, DP-06, DP-07).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-access WireMock | The P4 contract | `POST /authorise` granting Case record R and Queue and allocation R, refusing a role without the right, and refusing scope over SME-NTH for a scope Team in MTG-BKK |
| rwb-source-data WireMock | The P1 contract | `GET /data-products/freshness` answering 2026-12-15, answering 2026-12-14 on business date 2026-12-15, and a delayed answer beyond 2 s |
| rwb-deviation WireMock | The S8 contract, used by the composite route and the browser test | An open X1 on the two paused cases of AC9, and an empty answer |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 3 provided, 2 consumed | Cases, queues and queue cases provided; freshness and authorise consumed; one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream |
| Kafka | None published, none consumed | The five case events that move the counts are published by their own stories; this read path carries no Kafka traffic |
| Temporal | None added | The timer that writes the status read here lives in CaseWorkflow and belongs to RWB-P3-E1028-APP |
| File | None | No file is read or written |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.queueview`, module `queueview`; front end folder `src/modules/recovery/case/queues`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_case`; the three answers read `recovery_case`, `queue`, `queue_member`, `timer` and `queue_measure` of this service only and never another service's tables | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and its client library: the page-size default 50 and maximum 200 are parameter rows, not constants | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case: LOV-STAGE, LOV-ROUTE and LOV-CASE-STATUS labels and versions | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library, cached per request, on each of the three operations | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.case.<Event>.v1` through the naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in schema `rwb_case`: one index migration in this story | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route for SCR-02 and SCR-07 | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-14 is claimed although this story publishes nothing: the topic and event names the counts depend on are resolved through the naming library, and a local topic name would leave the two screens reading a stream nobody writes. The same-service CON baselines RWB-P3-E2011-CON and RWB-P3-E1031-CON are class H dependencies and are not DP rows.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CaseQueueController | Controller | The three read operations; parameter checks; problem responses and status codes |
| CaseListQueryService | Service | Builds the scoped case query with filters, age and the service level sort; computes `ageDays` and `serviceLevelState` |
| QueueSummaryService | Service | Counts open cases, the oldest entry date, the breaches and the open cases per owner for each queue in scope |
| CaseListRepository | Repository | One SQL query joining `recovery_case` with the open SERVICE_LEVEL `timer` of each case, in `rwb_case` only |
| QueueSummaryRepository | Repository | Grouped counts by `queue_id` and `owner_user_id`, and the cap lookup |
| CapReader | Service | Resolves the cap in force for an owner from `queue.capacity_cap` or `queue_member.capacity` (GAP-0707; ASM-1254) |
| FreshnessClient | Client | Calls the rwb-source-data freshness answer once per request and for the business date; supplies `X-Data-As-Of` |
| AccessCheckClient | Client | Calls the rwb-access authorise contract, cached per request (DP-08) |
| MyQueuePage | React component | SCR-02 in the My queue view with filters, sort and states |
| TeamQueuesPage | React component | SCR-07 with the queue rows, owner spread and drill down |
| useSessionFilters | React component | Hook that keeps filters in session storage, wrapped in try and catch, cleared at sign-out |

**Database.** Reads `recovery_case`, `queue`, `queue_member`, `timer` and `queue_measure` in schema `rwb_case`, and uses `ix_case_owner_status`, `ix_case_status_queue` and `ix_timer_case_id` where they already exist. Adds one index, `ix_timer_case_type_status` on `timer (case_id, timer_type, status)`, in its own Flyway step `V<next>__rwb_e2_011_queue_view_index.sql` (DP-15). No column is added to any table.

**Configuration and reference data.** `queueview.page-size.default` = 50 and `queueview.page-size.max` = 200 are parameter rows of `parameter_catalog` read through the parameters contract (DP-06); stage, route and status labels come from LOV-STAGE, LOV-ROUTE and LOV-CASE-STATUS through the reference-data contract (DP-07); caseload caps come from the queue row, or from the member's personal capacity when that is the cap in force (DL23; GAP-0707; ASM-1254).

**Build steps**

1. Extend the OpenAPI document and the generated types for the three operations with the added fields, the header and the paging and sort rules; contract test against RWB-P3-E2011-CON.
2. Add the index migration and `CaseListRepository` with the service level join; test the four sort groups.
3. Build `CaseListQueryService` with scope, filters, age and the computed fields; add `route` and the sort to `GET /cases`.
4. Build `QueueSummaryService`, `CapReader` and the computed fields on `GET /queues`; test the counts against `GET /cases` for the same queue.
5. Add the scope check to `GET /queues/{queueId}/cases`.
6. Build `FreshnessClient` and the `X-Data-As-Of` header with its stale state; tests for AC8.
7. Build `MyQueuePage` with Loading, Empty, List and Filtered states and `useSessionFilters`; build `TeamQueuesPage` with Loading and List states and the drill down; add the paused marker and the hover of MSG-P3-004.
8. Authorisation through the rwb-access contract on the three operations; test the refusal of AC7 and the refusal of section 16.
9. Write the API, browser and load tests of section 16.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.p3.queue-views`, a service configuration value. Off: the menu items My queue and Team queues are hidden and the three operations return the Epic 1 fields only; on: the age, the service level state, the queue counts and the owner spread.

**Done when.** Every test in section 16 passes, the three contract fakes drive every cross-service answer, a page of 200 cases for an owner with 500 open cases loads inside 2 s at the 95th percentile through the composite route (NFR-009), and the contract tests of RWB-P3-E2011-CON stay green.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-017 | The list has no case for the person and filters | There are no cases in this queue. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Age to is less than age from | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | Page size outside 1 to 200 | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-P4-003 | A queue outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P1-001 | The case data is from an earlier business date | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P3-004 | A case on hold for a deviation | This case is on hold for {deviation}. The prescription date is still {date}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right opens a view | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

MSG-P3-017 is new (see Additions). Thai text follows DL10. The seven texts are the legacy texts unchanged; the move changes no wording. Which answer fills the `{product}` of MSG-P1-001 on a case list, and whether the banner takes it from the freshness answer or from the data product name of the header, is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0709; ASM-1256).

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | State | What the user does |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-02 Case list, My queue view | Loading | Sees skeleton rows |
| SCR-02 Case list, My queue view | Empty | Reads MSG-P3-017 |
| SCR-02 Case list, My queue view | List | Reads cases sorted by service level; opens a case on SCR-03 |
| SCR-02 Case list, My queue view | Filtered | Sets stage, route, status and age filters; clears them |
| SCR-07 Team queues | Loading | Sees skeleton rows |
| SCR-07 Team queues | List | Reads count, oldest age, breaches and owners against the cap; opens a queue's cases; goes to SCR-05 Transfer case (RWB-E2-012) |

The composite route that serves these states is owned by RWB-PLT-N001-CON; its path, its merge order and the screen field list are not fixed here, and this story fixes only the three answers it contributes. A stale business date shows as a banner on both screens and never blocks the list.
