**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the deviation side of RWB-E2-012 is split out onto rwb-deviation (S8). The transfer itself, its endpoint, its reason-code and cap checks, the assignment swap and the `CaseTransferred` publication stay with the primary slice in rwb-case (RWB-P3-E2012-APP); this story owns the open-deviation answer the move and the SCR-05 panel read, the deviation panel itself behind the gateway-bff composite route, the decision record written against the deviation when the case moves, and the handler rule R-DEV-02 and R-DEV-03 keep. The read is published on `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` (DP-13) and the service's two events on `rwb.deviation.events.v1` (DP-09, DP-14); `deviation` is the only table this service writes (DP-01). The plan's build list is empty although the DP table adds platform contract rows, the read operation of the P3 slice is not a row of the Ownership Map, and the fifteen legacy test case ids are carried by both slices (GAP-3091, -3, -8; ASM-5280, -3, -8). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **the transfer screen to show the open deviation of the case, with the rule that refuses the move while it is open, and the deviation to keep the handler its own rule named after the case has moved**, so that **a hand-off is one action with a record and never silently takes a case away from the owner a deviation put on it**.

Inside `rwb-deviation` this is the deviation side of the manual move:

- Service `rwb-deviation`, schema `rwb_deviation`, REST base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1`, topic `rwb.deviation.events.v1` with event names `rwb.deviation.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-deviation` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.deviation` (context pack).
- The read `GET /api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations`, one call per case: the open deviations with their code, handler, paused state, contact stop, raised-at, return point and rule ID (DP-13). It is the answer the P3 move names in its own section 12 and the answer the SCR-05 deviation panel renders (GAP-3093; ASM-5282).
- The deviation panel of SCR-05 behind the gateway-bff composite route: what is open, who holds it, why the move is refused, and what happens to the panel after the move or the clear (DP-19).
- The `CaseTransferred` (EV-04) handler on task queue `rwb-deviation`: it records the move against the deviation and keeps the handler that R-DEV-02 and R-DEV-03 named, because BR10 says an open deviation holds the case with its own owner (DP-10).
- The local decision record of DP-03 for that step, hash-chained in `rwb_deviation` and published on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; a failed write leaves the deviation and the panel as they were.
- Inbox idempotency on the event ID and the outbox relay of `DeviationRaised` and `DeviationCleared` through the library of DP-09 (DP-09, DP-14).
- The transfer reason list `LOV-TRANSFER-REASON` read on the reference-data contract of rwb-case, with its version (DP-07), so R02 Customer deceased and R05 Legal referral are data and not code.
- The per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_deviation` for this story's own need, with no shared `recovery` migration (DP-15).

It does not own: the transfer endpoint `POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer` and its reason-code, cap, team, hold, scope and version checks; the assignment swap; the `CaseTransferred` publication; and the queue and case screens beyond the deviation panel (the primary slice RWB-P3-E2012-APP in rwb-case). Nor the `recovery_case`, `queue`, `assignment` and `timer` tables (P3), the TRANSFER package rows, their authoring, approval and versions (rwb-decision, P7), the roles and rights (rwb-access, P4), or the contract surface with its OpenAPI and fakes (the CON stories of this service and of P3).

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy objective is unchanged: a case changes hands by one action, with a coded reason and a record, and a case that a deviation holds is not moved from the owner the deviation named (RWB-E2-012 §2, §8 BR10; REQ-WKM-003, REQ-WKM-007, REQ-CWC-010, REQ-CWC-016). Audit found debtors who met the criteria were not transferred to the responsible unit (CTL-03), and a refusal that shows only a rule ID is the same failure in another shape: the manager must see which deviation holds the case and who holds it.

D-RCV-60 changes who answers, not what the manager sees:

- **The refusal has two owners.** The TRANSFER row "TRF-010" refuses a move while a deviation is open, and the fact it reads is the deviation, which is this service's. rwb-case may not read `deviation` (DP-01) and names a one-hop read of this service instead, so the answer is published here and faked for the P3 build (DP-11; GAP-3093).
- **The panel is a composite, not a page.** SCR-05 was one ace-web screen; after the split gateway-bff composes it, and the deviation fragment is the part this service contributes, with its own states and messages (DP-19).
- **The owner stays with the deviation.** BR10 survives the split unchanged: an accepted move recorded against an open deviation keeps the handler R-DEV-02 or R-DEV-03 named, and the panel shows the case's new queue and owner beside it, so custody of the case and ownership of the deviation are never confused.
- **The record comes first.** The monolith writes the decision log before the case changes (TSD S8 T2); the local decision record of DP-03 keeps that order per service, and a failed write changes nothing.
- **No personal data anywhere.** The panel and the answer carry identifiers, codes and instants only: no name, address, identity number or contact value enters the read, the record, an event or a log (section 17).

Wave needs no conflict row here: business epic EP02 sits in wave 2 by the W-MAP and the service sits in wave 2 in Arch v5, so the two agree. Only the plan's empty build list and the platform rows of the DP table are recorded (GAP-3091; ASM-5280).

##### 3. Preconditions

- `RWB-P3-E2012-CON` is published and tagged: the transfer operation, the `TransferRequest` and `Assignment` schemas, the reason list reference, the refusal codes, `CaseTransferred` and the fakes, including the deviation fake this story replaces (C dependency; DP-11).
- The platform contract stories the DP table names are published with their stubs: the local decision record and `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03), the embedded Drools kit and the package reader (DP-04), the reference-data client (DP-07), the outbox, inbox and idempotency library (DP-09), the workflow kit (DP-10), the topic-naming library (DP-14), the per-service Flyway baseline (DP-15) and the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The plan carries no build dependency on this key, so the story starts on Day 1 against those baselines and the fakes; the rows are tracked, not blocking (GAP-3091; ASM-5280).
- `deviation` exists in `rwb_deviation` with DF-CAS-036 to DF-CAS-045 and the standard record columns of TSD S8 T3.0, created by the DB story of this service; this story adds no table and no column (GAP-3096; ASM-5285).
- Package TRANSFER version "TRF-2026.12" is in force on the business date, and row "TRF-010" refuses a move while a deviation is open; the rows are authored and approved in rwb-decision and never here (DP-04; legacy §3).
- `LOV-TRANSFER-REASON` is readable on the reference-data contract of rwb-case at its version, with R01 Capacity, R02 Customer deceased, R03 Skill, R04 Owner absent, R05 Legal referral and R06 Wrong queue; the values are the legacy assumed set pending DL23 (GAP-3097; ASM-5286).
- The receive routes for `CaseTransferred` (EV-04) and for the case status and legal-hold changes exist on the service inbox; the last two carry no published event name and are faked (GAP-3095; ASM-5284).
- The person holds Case record R in rwb-access (RW-TEAMMGR, RW-CAPACITY, RW-CASEOWN and the deviation handlers hold RU or R, TSD S8 T6.1), the case is in their scope, and no delegation of authority level applies: a move changes who works the case, not what is owed.
- The login is the rwb-deviation login (DP-02): one login, one pool, grants on `rwb_deviation` only; a statement on `rwb_case` fails at the grant and in the boundary test (DP-01).

##### 4. Flow

1. The team manager opens SCR-05 for one case of SCR-03, or for up to 50 cases selected on SCR-07, at business date 2026-12-15; gateway-bff composes the screen (DP-19).
2. The screen asks this service once per case: `GET /api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations`, one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker (DP-11, DP-13).
3. The operation authorises the call through the rwb-access contract, right R on Case record, scope applied, and answers 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 and 503 in the platform envelope; a refused authorisation refuses the read and never widens it.
4. The repository selects the `deviation` rows of the case with `cleared_at` empty; a cleared row is history and is not part of the answer.
5. The answer carries, per open deviation: code X1 to X7, handler, paused state, contact stop, raised-at, return point, the rule ID that put it there (R-DEV-02 to R-DEV-06) and the package version; no personal field and no free text (section 17).
6. The screen renders the deviation panel: the codes, the handler of each, the paused state and the "Contact stopped" mark, with the refusal of the move as MSG-P3-033 naming the TRANSFER rule the case read returned, or MSG-P3-027 when no TRANSFER version is in force (legacy §15; MSG text in section 14).
7. With no open deviation the panel is empty and the form carries the reason list read on `LOV-TRANSFER-REASON` with its version (DP-07); the reason codes are rendered as data and never frozen into the client.
8. The manager confirms a target queue or owner, a reason code and a note; the front end sends one `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/transfer` per case to rwb-case, which runs the move, the rule evaluation, the cap and team checks and the assignment swap (primary slice; C RWB-P3-E2012-CON).
9. On an accepted move rwb-case publishes `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1`; this service receives it on the inbox and starts the transfer branch of `DeviationWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-deviation` with the event ID as the workflow ID (DP-10).
10. `applyCaseTransfer`: the branch reads the open deviations of the case again and keeps the handler each row already holds, because R-DEV-02 and R-DEV-03 name the deviation owner and BR10 keeps the case with that owner; the panel shows the case's new queue and owner beside the unchanged handler (legacy BR10).
11. `recordDeviationMove`: in one `rwb_deviation` transaction and as the last step before commit, the decision record is written with the rule ID, the package version, the reason code, the from and to queue and owner and the event ID; the inbox row marks the event processed.
12. A repeated event ID is ignored as an idempotency hit, and the same `Idempotency-Key` on a raise or a clear answers the response it already gave (R-UNI-40). The deviation's own state, paused state, contact stop, raised-at and return point are never changed by a move.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The case has an open deviation and the TRANSFER row "TRF-010" refuses the move | The panel names rule "TRF-010" and the code that holds the case; nothing changes in this service | MSG-P3-033 | AC1, AC4 |
| X2 | No TRANSFER version is in force on the business date | The panel names the package check and no fallback decision is shown | MSG-P3-027 | AC1 |
| X3 | No open deviation on the case | The panel is empty and the form is offered with the reason list at its version | None | AC2, AC6 |
| X4 | Two deviations are open on one case | Both rows are answered and the panel names both; the move is refused while either is open | MSG-P3-033 | AC4 |
| X5 | The deviation was cleared | The row is history and not part of the open answer; the panel shows it cleared with its outcome | None | AC6 |
| X6 | The rwb-access answer refuses the read | 403 before any row is read, and nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 | AC9 |
| X7 | The same `CaseTransferred` event ID arrives twice | Second ignored and counted; one record | None | AC7 |
| X8 | The decision record cannot be written | The transaction rolls back, the inbox row stays unprocessed and the panel is unchanged | MSG-P7-003 | AC8 |
| X9 | The case read, or the reference-data read, does not answer inside 2 s | The panel shows the case side without the deviation fragment and the move is never taken on an unread deviation | None | Section 17 |
| X10 | A statement, a test or a component reaches a `rwb_case` row or a `v_ace_*` view | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | Section 17 |

X1, X3, X4, X5 and X7 restate the legacy exception rows X2 and the screen states of legacy §15 for this slice; X2 is legacy X11 and X8 is legacy X9. The legacy rows that belong to the move itself — no reason code (MSG-P3-001), the cap (MSG-P3-002), the team check R-UNI-18, the legal hold (MSG-P3-005), the parallel request (MSG-GEN-004) and the bulk summary (MSG-P3-035) — are answered by rwb-case and are not restated here.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on Day 1 against `RWB-P3-E2012-CON` and its fake, the platform stubs of DP-03, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10 and DP-19, and synthetic `deviation` rows; no live P3, P4 or P7 is needed |
| Negotiable | The shape of the deviation answer, the panel layout and the decision code per outcome are this story's choice; the codes, the handler rules, the messages and the columns are fixed |
| Valuable | A refused move shows its cause and its holder, and an accepted move never quietly reassigns a deviation |
| Estimable | One read operation, one screen fragment, one event branch, one activity pair, the record and the inbox row |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests on the fakes |
| Testable | Component and contract tests on synthetic cases, a browser test of the panel through the composite route, and the boundary test |

The nine criteria are new: this slice owns no legacy criterion, because the split gives the thirteen criteria of RWB-E2-012 to the primary slice in rwb-case (`acs` is empty on this slice), and each criterion here tests only the deliverable of the title — the deviation answer, the panel and the handler rule. Every value in the scenarios — the business date, the package version, the rule IDs, the case and queue IDs, the cap of 150, the reason codes, the deviation codes, the outcome words, the paused state and the message IDs — is copied character for character from RWB-E2-012 §7, §8, §14 and §15 and from TSD S8 T3.2, T4 and T6.1; no value is invented.

##### 8. Business rules

| Rule | Route set | Codes | From state | Event | Condition | Action | To state | Owner | Systems | Timer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R-DEV-01 | Deviations | X1 to X7 | ANY_STATE | DEVIATION_FLAGGED | deviation_code in (X1..X7) | Pause the stage clock, keep the prescription clock running, route to the named owner | DEV_FLAGGED | Workbench | Workbench | Same day |
| R-DEV-02 | Deviations | X1 | DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | deviation_code = X1 | Assign to the complaint officer | DEV_WITH_OWNER | Complaint officer | Workbench | None |
| R-DEV-03 | Deviations | X2, X3 | DEV_FLAGGED | OWNER_ASSIGNED | deviation_code in (X2,X3) | Assign to the specialist; Legal joins X3 for the estate claim | DEV_WITH_OWNER | Hardship and vulnerability specialist | Workbench | None |
| R-DEV-18 | Deviations | X1 to X7 | DEV_RESOLVED | CLOCK_RESUMED | Any | Resume the stage clock and return the case | RESUMED | Previous owner | Workbench | None |

The four rows are copied character for character from FSD S8 A2.2.3.1, A2.4.3.1 and the DEVIATION machine of TSD S8 T4. R-DEV-04 to R-DEV-06 assign X4 to X7 to their named owners; their text is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3094; ASM-5283). The owner column is a business role, not a service.

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A manual move needs a reason code from LOV-TRANSFER-REASON, read at its version from the reference data of rwb-case | Legacy BR1; REQ-WKM-003; REQ-CWC-010; DP-07 |
| BR2 | A move the TRANSFER package refuses is not made, and the refusing rule ID is shown; this service names the deviation that holds the case beside it | Legacy BR2, BR10; RWB-E2-012 AC2 |
| BR3 | A case with an open deviation stays with the owner the deviation rule named; an accepted move records the move and keeps that handler | Legacy BR10; R-DEV-02; R-DEV-03 |
| BR4 | The open-deviation answer carries the code, handler, paused state, contact stop, raised-at, return point and rule ID only; no personal field | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 s17 |
| BR5 | A cleared deviation is history and is not part of the open answer; it keeps its outcome and its return point | Legacy BR6; TSD S8 T3.1 (`cleared_at`, `outcome`); LOV-DEV-OUTCOME |
| BR6 | The deviation state, paused state, contact stop, raised-at and return point are never changed by a move | Legacy BR6; R-UNI-18; R-UNI-46 |
| BR7 | A case under a legal hold is not moved; the panel names the hold and the refusal | Legacy BR7; R-UNI-20 |
| BR8 | A step that cannot be written to the decision record changes nothing and answers MSG-P7-003 | Legacy BR8; DP-03; TSD S8 T2 |
| BR9 | A repeated `CaseTransferred` event ID is processed once, and a repeated request with the same `Idempotency-Key` answers what it already answered | Legacy BR9; R-UNI-40 |
| BR10 | Neither this service nor the screen reads another service's table: the case, queue and assignment come on the rwb-case contract, the package from rwb-decision, the right from rwb-access | DP-01, DP-04, DP-11 |
| BR11 | No person name, contact value, address or identity number enters the deviation row, the answer, a decision record, a log or an event | Template and Rules v1 §R7.2 s17 |

##### 9. State transitions

This story changes no case status and no case state; it reads the deviation and records a move against it.

| From (`deviation.state`) | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| DEV_WITH_OWNER, or no change | A `CaseTransferred` is processed for the case | The row is open | Unchanged: `handler_user_id`, `paused_state`, `contact_stop`, `raised_at` and the return point all stay as they were |
| DEV_RESOLVED or RESUMED | The clear path has run and the row holds `cleared_at` | The row is history | Unchanged; the row leaves the open answer |

| Step execution | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waiting | `CaseTransferred` arrives | The event ID is new | Applying |
| Waiting | The same event ID arrives again | Inbox hit (BR9) | Waiting, counted |
| Applying | The decision record is written | The transaction commits | Waiting for the next event |
| Applying | The record write fails (BR8) | X8 | Waiting, the inbox row unprocessed, nothing changed |

The deviation machine of TSD S8 T4 (22 rules over 9 states) is untouched by this story; R-DEV-01, R-DEV-02, R-DEV-03 and R-DEV-18 keep working as the FSD states them.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Team manager (RW-TEAMMGR) | Opens SCR-05 and reads the deviation panel of the cases in the team's scope (TSD S8 T6.1; the move itself is P3's) |
| Capacity and workforce planner (RW-CAPACITY) | Reassigns cases for capacity and reads the same panel |
| Case owner (RW-CASEOWN) | Raises and clears the deviation whose response feeds the panel; holds CRU on the case record |
| Complaint officer (RW-COMPLAIN), Hardship and vulnerability specialist (RW-SPECIAL), Fraud investigator (RW-FRAUD), Legal counsel (RW-LEGAL) | Hold the deviation the rules named and see it on the panel; hold RU or R on the case record |
| rwb-case (P3) | Owns the move, its checks and the `CaseTransferred` event; reads the open deviations here |
| rwb-decision (P7) | Owns the TRANSFER package, its rows, their order and their versions; this story evaluates nothing |
| rwb-access (P4) | Owns the roles and the Case record right checked on the read |
| Solution architect | Confirms the read operation and its shape, which the sources do not publish (GAP-3093; GAP-3095) |

No delegation of authority level applies: a transfer moves work, not money (legacy §10).

| None: library table | `decision_record` | Platform library in `rwb_deviation` | The hash-linked record of the move against the deviation (DP-03) |
| None: library table | `outbox_event`, `inbox_event` | Platform library in `rwb_deviation` | The two event rows and the processed `CaseTransferred` ID (DP-09) |
| DF-CAS-001, DF-CAS-005, DF-CAS-007, DF-CAS-009, DF-CAS-010, DF-CAS-011, DF-CAS-019, DF-CAS-020 | `recovery_case` | P3 rwb-case | The case reference, status, route state, owner, queue, team, deviation flag and legal hold; consumed on the contract, never written |
| DF-WRK-001, DF-WRK-004, DF-WRK-006, DF-WRK-007, DF-WRK-039, DF-WRK-040 | `queue`, `assignment` | P3 rwb-case | The target queue, its team, its method, its cap and the assignment with `transfer_reason_code`; named, never written |
| DF-REF-002, DF-REF-281, DF-REF-282, DF-REF-296 to DF-REF-298 | `rule_row`, `rule_package_version` | P7 rwb-decision | The TRANSFER rows and the version in force; read through the package, never written |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | `decision_log_entry` | P7 rwb-decision | The central ledger; rwb-decision copies the local record, this story does not write it |

`deviation` carries no transfer reason, no rule ID and no rule-version column (TSD S8 T3.1), so the reason code, the rule ID and the package version of a move live in the decision record only (GAP-3096; ASM-5285). The lists are reference data read at their version: `LOV-DEVIATION` and `LOV-DEV-OUTCOME` from TSD S8 T3.2, and `LOV-TRANSFER-REASON` with R01 to R06 on the rwb-case reference-data contract (DP-07; GAP-3097).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-deviation (S8); base `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` (DP-13). The read is the operation the P3 slice of this legacy key names; the two write operations are the service's and are unchanged by this story (GAP-3093; ASM-5282).

| Method | Path | Shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/deviations` | `DeviationSummary` list out: deviation reference, code, handler, paused state, contact stop, raised-at, return point, rule ID and package version; `[]` when nothing is open | Case record, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/deviations` | `DeviationRequest` in, `Deviation` out (API-S8-001) | Case record, right U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header |
| PATCH | `/deviations/{deviationId}` | `DeviationOutcome` in, `Deviation` out (API-S8-002) | Case record, right U, scope applied | Not applicable |

All three answer 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409, 422 and 503 in the platform error envelope; the exact shapes, the error list and the fakes are the CON story's of this service. The GET is the only operation this story builds.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| The transfer of the case and the assignment it answers (C `RWB-P3-E2012-CON`); operation `POST /cases/{caseId}/transfer` under `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case | The move the screen performs; the accepted or refused answer the panel reflects |
| The case record read; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3092; ASM-5281) | P3 rwb-case | Queue, owner, team, status, route state, deviation flag and legal hold shown beside the deviation |
| The reference-data read of `LOV-TRANSFER-REASON` (DP-07); operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3092; ASM-5281) | P3 rwb-case | The six reason codes R01 to R06 with their version |
| The package and rule-in-force read (DP-04); operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3092; ASM-5281) | P7 rwb-decision | The TRANSFER version in force, so the panel can name it and answer MSG-P3-027 |
| The authorise call on Case record R; operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3092; ASM-5281) | P4 rwb-access | The right and the scope of the read |
| The case-facts read (DP-05); operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3092; ASM-5281) | P1 rwb-source-data | The case facts the panel shows, with their freshness stamp |

All six are one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker, and none retries inside the step (DP-11, ADR-020). Only the first is a row of the plan's C list, which holds `RWB-P3-E2012-CON` alone.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The deviation read on `/api/recovery/deviation/v1`, the SCR-05 deviation panel with its four states, the `CaseTransferred` branch of `DeviationWorkflow` with its three activities, the decision record and the inbox row, the two event relays, and the per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_deviation`.

**Pattern application** (§R5.5)

| DP | Legacy marker | Pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>`, "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_deviation`; no other service's table is read | None |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON` |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H `RWB-PLT-E1072-CON`; C `RWB-P7-E1073-CON` |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract | None |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H `RWB-PLT-E1043-CON`; C `RWB-P3-E1043-CON` |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox, inbox and idempotency library, owner topic, CloudEvents | H `RWB-PLT-TE006-CON` |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H `RWB-PLT-E1071-CON` |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | None (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1` | None |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` and `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` through the naming library | H `RWB-PLT-E1047-CON` |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in `rwb_deviation` | H `RWB-PLT-E1044-CON` |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` |

The eight H rows are platform contract rows; the plan's build list for this key is empty and therefore stays empty in the metadata, and the rows are tracked, not blocking (GAP-3091; ASM-5280). DP-11 keeps the one class C dependency the plan gives, `RWB-P3-E2012-CON`; DP-04 and DP-07 also add a C row each, which the metadata does not carry.

**Build steps.** (1) Build the repository query for the open rows and the `DeviationSummary` map, with the field allow-list of BR4. (2) Publish `GET /cases/{caseId}/deviations` with the authorise call and the error mapping. (3) Build the panel with its states: open, refused, cleared history, empty. (4) Wire the `CaseTransferred` consumer and the `DeviationWorkflow` branch with its three activities. (5) Keep the handler of each open row and record the move with the rule ID and the package version, in one transaction with the inbox row. (6) Relay `DeviationRaised` and `DeviationCleared` through the outbox. (7) Fold the story's schema need into the per-service Flyway sequence, with no shared `recovery` migration. (8) Prove AC1 to AC9 on the fakes and run the boundary test.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.s8.transfer-panel`. Off: the panel shows no deviation fragment and the read answers 404 to the composite route, while the two write operations keep working.

**Done when.** AC1 to AC9 pass at component and contract level on the fakes, the panel renders the open, refused, cleared and empty states through the composite route, a repeated `CaseTransferred` writes once, a failed record changes nothing, and the boundary test shows no `rwb_case` statement and no `v_ace_*` read.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-001 | A manual transfer without a reason (the primary slice's path, named for traceability) | Choose a reason for the transfer. |
| MSG-P3-002 | Target owner, or every owner of the target queue, at the cap | {owner} is at the caseload cap. Choose another owner or the team queue. |
| MSG-P3-005 | Case closed or under a legal hold | This case cannot move to {state} from {current}. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No TRANSFER package version in force | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P3-033 | A TRANSFER rule refuses the move, and the panel names the deviation beside it | Rule {rule} does not allow this transfer. |
| MSG-P3-035 | A selection with refusals | {done} of {total} cases were moved. The others show the reason on their row. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Two moves of one case at once | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision record write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-005 | Move saved | Saved. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Case record R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The text is RWB-E2-012 §14 and FSD S8 A2.1.3.1, copied unchanged; no message is reworded and none is added. For MSG-P3-027 the {check} value is "package in force" and the {detail} names the package code TRANSFER and the business date only. The {rule} value of MSG-P3-033 is the rule ID the case read returned.

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | State | What this story answers |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-05 Transfer case | Form | The deviation fragment: codes, handlers, paused state and contact stop of the open deviations; empty when nothing is open |
| SCR-05 Transfer case | Refused | The deviation fragment beside MSG-P3-033 naming the rule and the deviation that holds the case, or MSG-P3-027 |
| SCR-05 Transfer case | Saved | The deviation fragment after the move: the case's new queue and owner, and the handler the deviation rule kept |
| SCR-03 Case record | Read only; on hold | The same open-deviation answer, read for the case banner |
| SCR-07 Team queues | List | The selection of up to 50 cases the screen is opened from; this story answers per case |
| SCR-09 Exception queue | List | Not used by this story; a refused move is not queued |

SCR-05 is a gateway-bff composite route (DP-19): the route owns the path and the merge order, rwb-case contributes the form, the case read and the move, and this service contributes the deviation fragment only. The panel never renders a rule row or a deviation text of another service; it renders codes, IDs and message IDs. The fragment's own layout is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3094; ASM-5283).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the reason codes, the deviation codes, the handler rules, the cap and the rule rows are reference data or package rows, read with their version.
- No personal data in the answer, the deviation row, a decision record, an event, a workflow input, a log or a prompt: identifiers, codes, instants and a rule version only. The panel renders no free text of the case.
- ACE data and case data only through the owner's contract: no `v_ace_*` view, no `rwb_case` statement and no other service's schema (DP-01, DP-05, DP-11).
- One evaluator per service and one package registry: this story evaluates no TRANSFER row, it reads the version in force only to name it (DP-04; ADR-017). A missing version is never a default decision (R-UNI-41).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; this story adds no second topic and no Schedule (DP-13, DP-14).
- A read that does not answer inside 2 s leaves the panel without the deviation fragment and never lets a move proceed on an unread deviation; a refused authorisation refuses the read rather than widening it.
- The decision record is written before the commit and in the same transaction as the inbox row; a failure rolls both back.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-012 for rwb-decision — the transfer decision record, the central ledger read and the TRANSFER package version in force. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As an **internal audit officer (RW-AUDIT)**, I want **the decision record of every manual transfer and reassignment sealed in the `rwb-decision` ledger with its rule ID, the TRANSFER package version in force, the reason code and the from and to queue and owner, and the TRANSFER version in force on a business date readable in one call**, so that **a hand-off is provable months later and no move can cite a rule version that was not in force when it happened**.

Inside `rwb-decision` this is the decision-and-ledger half of the legacy story RWB-E2-012:

- Service `rwb-decision`, schema `rwb_decision`, REST base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, topic `rwb.decision.events.v1` with event names `rwb.decision.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` on which the record of a move arrives (DP-03, DP-14).
- One deliverable and nothing else: the TRANSFER package row with its version rows ("TRF-2026.12" in force from 2026-12-01 and "TRF-2026.11" before it), the one call that answers which version is in force on a business date and refuses to default when none is, the acceptance of a `CASE_TRANSFERRED` record from `rwb.decision-record.v1` into the append-only, hash-chained `decision_log_entry` of `rwb_decision`, and the two reads an auditor uses on it.
- The move stays with `rwb-case`: the screen SCR-05, `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/transfer`, the caps, the assignment swap and `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1` are RWB-P3-E2012-APP's. The open-deviation answer is `rwb-deviation`'s (RWB-S8-E2012-APP). The role, the right and the scope are `rwb-access`'s (P4).
- The ledger machinery — the continuous ingest of `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the single hash chain, the daily seal and the JOB-14 Schedule — is RWB-P7-E1008-APP's and is reused, not rebuilt; the TRANSFER package's authoring, four-eyes approval, promotion and rollback are RWB-P7-E1073-APP's and RWB-P7-E1021-APP's (ASM-4135, ASM-4137).
- The database login is the per-service login of DP-02 and it is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2500; ASM-4133); this story writes "the rwb-decision login (DP-02)" and never the monolith login.

The legacy behaviour is carried unchanged: the same TRANSFER package code, the same rule ID "TRF-010" that refuses a move while a deviation is open, the same package version on the record as the version that decided, the same reason codes, the same append-only and hash-chained entry with the from and to queue and owner, the same "a failed record stops the action", and the same "no version in force is a refusal, never a default".

##### 2. Business rationale

Audit found ownership changes agreed by email and debtors who met the criteria not transferred to the responsible unit (CTL-03). The legacy story ended that by giving every manual move a coded reason, a rule check, an assignment record and a decision log entry. This story is what makes the last two provable in the target: the move happens in `rwb-case`, the rule is evaluated there by the embedded Drools kit against the TRANSFER package that `rwb-decision` governs, and the record of the move is published once and sealed once, in one ledger, under one hash chain.

The realignment changes the mechanism, not the business rule:

1. The monolith's `recovery.decision_log_entry` row written through a P7 interface becomes a record published by the owning service on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and sealed by `rwb-decision` into `rwb_decision.decision_log_entry` (DP-01, DP-03, ADR-022). No caller writes this schema.
2. The rule row named on the record is still read only through the evaluated result; this story reads no workbook, no DRL source and no `rule_row` row, and it evaluates nothing (DP-04).
3. The version that decided a move is checked against the version in force on the move's business date, and a record that names a version not in force for that date is refused instead of sealed (BR2, BR5, BR11 of the legacy story; R-UNI-38).
4. The nightly copy to the data lake (JOB-13, RWB-E1-014) has no target and is gone (DP-17); the chain check becomes the JOB-14 Temporal Schedule at 02:00 on the `rwb-decision` queue, owned by RWB-P7-E1008-APP, and this story registers its entries with it (DP-10).
5. The reason list and the caps stay `rwb-case` data; the decision code and the version-state vocabulary stay reference data of `rwb-case` read with their version (DP-07). This story writes no business value in code.

This story meets REQ-WKM-003 and REQ-WKM-008 on the record side, carries REQ-CWC-016 (the rule ID and the package version on the entry), and keeps the version half of REQ-CWC-010 and of R-UNI-38: a move decided under "TRF-2026.12" keeps that version on its record even after a rollback.

##### 3. Preconditions

| Precondition | What it gives this story |
|---|---|
| RWB-P3-E2012-CON | The published rwb-case contract of the manual move: the transfer request and answer, and the element shape of the record the move publishes — decision code, final call `CASE_TRANSFERRED`, rule ID, rule version, from and to queue and owner, reason code, actor, decided time, idempotency key. Faked, one hop, 2 s where a call is made (DP-11); no case, assignment or queue row is read |
| RWB-P7-E1008-APP | The ledger it lands in: the append-only `decision_log_entry` with `chain_seq`, `prev_hash` and `entry_hash`, the continuous ingest of `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the dedupe on the platform inbox and the JOB-14 chain check. Reused; built against its published set and fake (ASM-4135) |
| RWB-P7-E1021-APP, RWB-P7-E1073-APP | The TRANSFER package and its version rows in the registry, and the authoring pipeline that loads, tests, approves, promotes and rolls back a version. This story names the versions and reads the one in force; it loads and approves none (ASM-4137) |
| RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03) |
| RWB-PLT-TE006-CON | The outbox, inbox and idempotency library (DP-09): one envelope, one dedupe key, retry and `.dlt` |
| RWB-PLT-E1047-CON | The naming library (DP-14): the topic and event names of section 12 |
| RWB-PLT-E1044-CON | The per-service Flyway sequence and migration conventions (DP-15) |
| RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The parameters, workflow, Drools, reference-data and route baselines of the DP table of section 13; this story claims no business parameter and evaluates no package (ASM-4134) |

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E2-012:

- The TRANSFER package exists with version "TRF-2026.12" in force from 2026-12-01 and "TRF-2026.11" in force before it; row "TRF-010" refuses a move while a deviation is open (legacy sections 3, 7 and 8; FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-007-05).
- The reason codes are the six of LOV-TRANSFER-REASON in force — R01 Capacity, R02 Customer deceased, R03 Skill, R04 Owner absent, R05 Legal referral, R06 Wrong queue (DL23) — held as rwb-case reference data and never frozen here.
- RW-TEAMMGR holds Decision log R and Queue and allocation U; RW-CAPACITY holds Queue and allocation RU with scope All; RW-AUDIT holds Decision log R; RW-CASEOWN holds Decision log R and cannot transfer. No approval level from the delegation of authority applies: a transfer moves work, not money (legacy section 10; ASM-4136).
- The business date of the move is the date the version in force is resolved against, and it is the date carried on the record; a move of 2026-12-15 under "TRF-2026.12" stays under it (legacy BR11).
- The rwb-decision login (DP-02) is in the platform secret store; its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2500; ASM-4133).
- Synthetic data only: cases, queues, owners, rule IDs and reason codes of the legacy story, never a real account, customer or assignment.

##### 4. Flow

1. Team manager: moves a case in `rwb-case` — one call per case, single or a selection — with the reason code, the target queue or owner and the note; `rwb-case` checks the reason, the case state, the hold and the scope, evaluates the TRANSFER package through its embedded Drools kit, swaps the assignment and writes its local decision record in the same transaction (RWB-P3-E2012-APP; legacy section 4).
2. `rwb-case`: publishes the record on `rwb.decision-record.v1` through its outbox in that transaction, in the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, keyed by the case ID and carrying the record's idempotency key (DP-09).
3. `rwb-decision` ingest (RWB-P7-E1008-APP): receives the envelope, drops it when `ce_source` is this service, dedupes on the inbox key and hands the `CASE_TRANSFERRED` record to this story's validator.
4. `TransferRecordValidator`: checks the record against the contract element of RWB-P3-E2012-CON — decision code present and a value of LOV-DECISION, final call `CASE_TRANSFERRED`, rule ID and rule version both present, reason code present, actor and decided time present, and at least one queue or owner on each side of the move. A malformed record is not sealed: it is refused with MSG-P7-009, sent to `rwb-decision.dlt`, and an incident is raised (BR3, BR6).
5. `VersionInForceService`: resolves the TRANSFER version in force on the record's business date from `rule_package_version`. A record that names a version other than the one in force for its date is refused with MSG-P7-009 naming `ruleVersion`; no default version is ever substituted (BR5, BR11).
6. The ingest chain of RWB-P7-E1008-APP: appends one `decision_log_entry` in `rwb_decision` with the next `chain_seq`, `prev_hash` set to the entry before it (64 zeros for the first), `entry_hash` as the SHA-256 of the canonical form, the decision code, the rule ID, the rule version, the case ID, the inputs reference, the actions (from and to queue and owner, reason code) and the outcome — one transaction, one entry per record.
7. The same transaction marks the inbox key done, so a redelivery of the same envelope finds the entry and writes nothing.
8. RW-AUDIT: reads the transfer records with `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` by case, decision, rule, approver or date range, and one entry with `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}`, with its inputs reference, rule ID, rule version, actor, final call, actions, outcome, decided time, previous hash and entry hash.
9. RW-AUDIT or RW-COE: reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/TRANSFER/versions` to see which version was in force on a business date and which one replaced it; on 2026-12-20 no version is in force and the answer says so with MSG-P3-027 instead of naming a default.
10. At 02:00 the JOB-14 Schedule of RWB-P7-E1008-APP verifies the chain from `chain_seq` 1 to the last entry, including the transfer entries, and reports a break to Compliance the same day (NFR-035).
11. Nothing in this story moves a case, picks an owner, checks a cap, reads a deviation or evaluates a package: the record, the ledger read and the version in force are the whole deliverable.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A record with no decision code, or one that is not a value of LOV-DECISION | Refused; no entry is written; the envelope goes to `rwb-decision.dlt` and an incident is raised | MSG-P7-009 | AC5 |
| X2 | A record with a rule ID and no rule version | Refused; no entry is written; the refusal names `ruleVersion` | MSG-P7-009 | AC5 |
| X3 | A record whose rule version was not in force on its business date | Refused; no entry is written; the entry of the version in force is untouched | MSG-P7-009 | AC6 |
| X4 | The same envelope is delivered twice | One entry; the second delivery finds the inbox key and writes nothing | None | AC2 |
| X5 | The ledger write fails inside the transaction (chain, unique key, database) | Nothing is committed, the envelope is retried and then sent to the `.dlt` with an incident; no partial entry and no gap in `chain_seq` | MSG-P7-003 | AC2, TC-E2-012-14 |
| X6 | A read from a role without Decision log R, or a case outside the caller's scope | 403 with MSG-P4-002; nothing is read | MSG-P4-002 | AC9, TC-E2-012-13 |
| X7 | No session, or no Recovery Workbench role | 401 with MSG-P4-001; nothing is read | MSG-P4-001 | AC9 |
| X8 | No TRANSFER version is in force on the requested business date | The version list answers that none is in force for that date with MSG-P3-027; no version is named as a default | MSG-P3-027 | AC6, TC-E2-012-15 |
| X9 | A chain break is found by the JOB-14 run | The run ends failed naming the first broken `chain_seq` and the break is reported to Compliance the same day; no entry is edited or removed | None | AC8 |

The move itself never waits on `rwb-decision`: the local record of `rwb-case` is written in the move's transaction, so a refusal here leaves the case, its assignment and its event exactly as the move left them (legacy BR8, kept at the owning service). The legacy criteria of the write failure stay with RWB-P3-E2012-APP for the move and with this story for the ledger copy.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P3-E2012-CON, the ledger of RWB-P7-E1008-APP, the TRANSFER versions of the registry and the platform contracts of its DP table; it moves no case and evaluates no package |
| Negotiable | Version labels, reason codes, decision codes and the page size are registry and reference data; the story fixes only the checks, the sealing and the read |
| Valuable | Every manual move is provable in one ledger with the rule and the version that decided it, and no record can name a version that was not in force |
| Estimable | One consumer, one validator, one version resolver, one repository and two read operations |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is a consumed envelope, a refused record, a read or a version lookup, with a fixed Given, When and Then |

The legacy criteria of RWB-E2-012 stay with the other slices of the key — the screen, the endpoint and the caps with RWB-P3-E2012-APP, the deviation with RWB-S8-E2012-APP, the rights with the P4 stories — and the cross-service journey with RWB-ITG-E2012-ITG.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The ledger is `rwb-decision`'s and no other service reads or writes `decision_log_entry`; a move's record arrives as an event and never as a call that writes the schema | DP-01; DP-03; ADR-022 |
| BR2 | The record of a move names the decision code, the final call `CASE_TRANSFERRED`, the rule ID, the rule version, the from and to queue and owner, the reason code, the actor and the decided time | legacy section 12 and AC1; FSD P7 AC-ALT-P7-002-01 |
| BR3 | A record missing the decision code, the rule version, the reason code, the actor or the decided time is refused and not sealed; a rule ID with no rule version is refused naming `ruleVersion` | FSD P7 AC-ALT-P7-002-01, AC-EXC-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-05 |
| BR4 | An entry is append only and hash chained: `chain_seq` without a gap, `prev_hash` equal to the entry before it and 64 zeros at the start, `entry_hash` the SHA-256 of the canonical form | FSD P7 AC-P7-001-01 and AC-ALT-P7-001-01; TSD P7 DF-DEC-017, DF-DEC-018, DF-DEC-028 |
| BR5 | The TRANSFER version in force on the business date decides the move and is the version on the record; a record naming another version is refused and a missing version is never defaulted | legacy BR11 and BR12; D-RCV-36 T3, T5, T7; R-UNI-38 |
| BR6 | One record, one entry: a redelivery of the same envelope finds its inbox key and writes nothing | legacy BR9; DP-09 |
| BR7 | A ledger write that fails commits nothing and never leaves a gap in the chain; the envelope is retried and then quarantined on `rwb-decision.dlt` with an incident | legacy BR8; FSD P7 AC-EXC-P7-002-07 |
| BR8 | The daily chain check covers every entry, reports a break to Compliance the same day, and never edits or removes an entry | FSD P7 AC-BG-P7-007-01; NFR-035; DP-10 |
| BR9 | The decision code is a value of LOV-DECISION and the version states are the vocabulary of the registry, read as reference data with the version in force and never written in code | legacy section 11; DP-07; TSD P7 T3.1 |
| BR10 | A move is read, never re-decided: this story changes no case status, no queue, no owner and no assignment, and it evaluates no rule package | legacy section 9; DP-04 |
| BR11 | The read needs Decision log R and applies the caller's scope; no approval level of the delegation of authority applies to a transfer | legacy section 10; TSD P7 T6.1 |

##### 9. State transitions

This story changes no case status and no assignment. It owns the state of a consumed record and of a decision entry.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | A record arrives | Every field is present, the version is in force on its date and the decision code is in the list | A new `decision_log_entry` with the next `chain_seq`; the inbox key is done |
| (none) | A record arrives | A field is missing, the decision code is unknown, or the version is not the one in force | No entry; the envelope is on `rwb-decision.dlt` with an incident |
| Sealed | The same envelope is delivered again | The inbox key is already done | Unchanged, no second entry |
| Sealed | The ledger write fails mid-transaction | The entry is not committed | Unchanged; retried, then quarantined |
| Sealed | The JOB-14 run | The chain verifies | Unchanged, the run records the last `chain_seq` and `entry_hash` |
| Sealed | The JOB-14 run | A canonical form was altered | Unchanged; the run fails and a break is reported to Compliance |

The case and assignment transitions of RWB-E2-012 — the ended assignment, the new assignment and the case's queue, owner and team — are `rwb-case`'s in the same transaction as its local record, and this story neither raises nor observes them.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the transfer records and one entry with its hashes (Decision log R) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads the record of a move it made (Decision log R) |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Reads the TRANSFER versions and calls the rollback that moves the pointer; this story holds no authoring (Rules and parameters C and R) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the record of its own case (Decision log R); cannot transfer and cannot seal |
| The rwb-decision service identity | Consumes the envelope, validates, resolves the version and seals the entry |
| SY-DECLOG, decision-record writer | Supplies the record and its hash chain through DP-03 |
| SY-RULES, Drools evaluator | Evaluates the TRANSFER package in `rwb-case` (DP-04); this story only reads the version in force |
| Any role without Decision log R | Refused with MSG-P4-002 on every read of section 12.1 |

No person is named anywhere; the actors are roles and service identities. The preparer of the record is `rwb-case`'s actor and is carried unchanged on the entry.

The ledger and the registry are `rwb-decision`'s and no other service reads them (DP-01). The field IDs of `decision_log_entry` are those of TSD P7 v2 T3.1; the registry field IDs are those the P7 registry stories cite from the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. No new field is added by this story: the migration of section 13 adds two indexes and no column.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-decision` (P7); base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`. The version list is the ownership map's P7 path; the two decision-log paths are API-P7-006 and API-P7-007 of TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 on the service base. The element shape of the answer is Not specified beyond the field names TSD P7 v2 T3.1 gives (GAP-2500; ASM-4133).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` | List the versions of TRANSFER with status, valid-from and valid-to dates, so a caller names the version in force on a business date; 200, or MSG-P3-027 when none is in force for the date asked | Rules and parameters R | Not applicable, read only |
| GET | `/decision-log` | Read the decision entries by caseId, decision, ruleId, approver, from, to, page and size; 200 with the page, scope applied | Decision log R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |
| GET | `/decision-log/{entryId}` | Read one entry with its inputs reference, decision code, rule ID, rule version, actor, final call, actions, outcome, decided time, chain sequence, previous hash and entry hash; 200 | Decision log R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |

Errors: 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Decision log R or outside the scope (MSG-P4-002); 404 an unknown package code or entry; 422 or 200 with MSG-P3-027 when no version is in force on the date asked, the exact status being Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2500; ASM-4133); 503 the ledger is unavailable (MSG-P7-003). Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId`, `detail`, `instance` and `traceId`. No operation writes an entry: the record arrives on the topic of 12.4.

The record of a move makes no call into this service and this service makes no call into rwb-case for it: the record arrives on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and its element shape is fixed by RWB-P3-E2012-CON, which this story builds against and fakes (12.8). The platform contracts the DP table adds are listed in section 13 and carried in GAP-2501.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This story publishes no event of its own: it seals a record that another service already published, and the chain check of RWB-P7-E1008-APP owns the break report. `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` belongs to the registry stories and this story only reads the state it announces.

Filtered on `ce_source` so this service does not re-ingest its own records; deduped on the inbox key; retried and then quarantined on `rwb-decision.dlt` (DP-09). No payload carries a name, an e-mail address, a mobile number, a national identity number or an account number.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, module `ledger/transfer`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision.ledger.transfer`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

How each row is applied. **DP-01**: the entry and the two registry tables are `rwb_decision` rows; the case, the assignment and the queue are never read, they arrive as the record's actions. **DP-03**: the record is consumed from `rwb.decision-record.v1` and sealed with the local library, so the ledger is the second copy and never the only one. **DP-04**: the kit stays in `rwb-case` where the move is decided; this story reads only the version in force, and the C dependency RWB-P7-E1073-CON is this service's own authoring contract, built against its published set. **DP-05**: no ACE view is read; the transfer facts reach this story only as the record. **DP-07**: LOV-DECISION and the version-state list are read with their version; the decision code is never a constant (BR9). **DP-09**: the inbox key makes one record one entry, the outbox of the move is `rwb-case`'s, and the `.dlt` of this service holds the refused envelope. **DP-10**: the JOB-14 chain check is the Schedule of 12.6 and this story creates no workflow and no Schedule. **DP-11**: the two consumed operations are one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker. **DP-13**: every path of section 12 uses `/api/recovery/decision/v1`. **DP-14**: the topic is the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1` and the event is `rwb.decision.DecisionRecorded.v1`; no `rwb.p7.` or `rwb.casewf.` name survives. **DP-15**: the two indexes of this story go into the per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_decision`, after the baseline of RWB-P7-E1008-APP. **DP-19**: no screen is built; SCR-05 is composed by gateway-bff from `rwb-case` and this story serves the read behind an audit view of the case.

The platform H dependencies of the table — DP-03, DP-04, DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-14, DP-15 and DP-19 — and the C dependencies C RWB-P7-E1073-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON are not in the metadata rows, which name None and RWB-P3-E2012-CON. They are recorded in GAP-2501 and ASM-4134: all are wave 0 platform contracts or published contracts, none blocks the build, and an APP story builds against the published set and its fake.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| TransferRecordConsumer | Consumer | Reads `rwb.decision-record.v1`, filters on `ce_source` and the decision code, dedupes on the inbox key |
| TransferRecordValidator | Service | Checks the record against the element of RWB-P3-E2012-CON: decision code, final call, rule ID and version, reason code, actor, decided time, from and to side; refuses with MSG-P7-009 and quarantines |
| VersionInForceService | Service | Resolves the TRANSFER version in force on the record's business date; refuses a record naming another version and never defaults |
| TransferLedgerWriter | Service | Appends the entry through the chain of RWB-P7-E1008-APP in one transaction with the inbox key |
| RuleVersionReadController | Controller | `GET /admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` with the guard, the scope and the problem mapping |
| DecisionLogController | Controller | `GET /decision-log` and `GET /decision-log/{entryId}` with the scope and the hashes |
| DecisionLogQueryRepository | Repository | The paged read of `decision_log_entry` by case, decision, rule, approver and date range |
| RuleVersionRepository | Repository | The `rule_package` and `rule_package_version` reads of the version in force |
| SessionClient, ReferenceListClient | Clients | The two consumed operations of 12.2, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker |
| TransferRecordFakeAdapter, ChainFakeAdapter | Test adapter | The rwb-case transfer fake and the ledger fake of 12.8 |

**Database and migrations.** One migration in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15, `V2027_3__decision_transfer_ledger.sql`, adds the unique index `ux_decision_log_idempotency` on `decision_log_entry (idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL`, so a redelivery cannot write a second entry even if the inbox loses its key, and the read index `ix_decision_log_case_decided` on `(case_id, decided_at)`. It adds no column and writes no seed row. The TRANSFER package row and its two version rows are written by the registry stories; where they have not landed, this story's seed registers "TRF-2026.12" from 2026-12-01 and "TRF-2026.11" before it under the label check of ASM-4137. Append only is enforced by the trigger of RWB-P7-E1008-APP; this story adds none.

**Configuration and reference data.** No business parameter is read (DP-06 is not claimed). LOV-DECISION and the version-state list are read with their version in force. The version labels, dates and rule IDs are the legacy values: "TRF-2026.12" in force from 2026-12-01, "TRF-2026.11" before it, row "TRF-010" refusing while a deviation is open. The reason codes are `rwb-case` reference data and this story stores the code it receives without validating it against the list. `ledger.transfer.page-size-max` is a read guard for the pager and Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2500; ASM-4133).

**Build steps**

1. `TransferLedgerWriter` against the chain of RWB-P7-E1008-APP and the migration's unique index; tests AC1 and AC2.
2. `TransferRecordValidator` with the six checks and MSG-P7-009 naming the field; tests AC5 and X1, X2.
3. `VersionInForceService` over `rule_package_version` and the refusal of a version not in force on the date; tests AC6, AC7 and X3.
4. `DecisionLogQueryRepository` and the two reads with the pager, the scope and the hashes; tests AC3, AC4 and AC9.
5. The consumer with the inbox key, the `ce_source` filter, the retry policy and the `.dlt` path with its incident; tests AC2 and X5.
6. The JOB-14 assertion against the ledger fake with a clean chain and one altered canonical form; test AC8.
7. The privacy test: every entry, answer and envelope holds IDs, codes, rule IDs, version labels and dates only.
8. The contract tests of the two consumed operations against their fakes, with a 2 s budget and a breaker.

**Feature switch.** No flag of its own. The move stays behind `rwb.p3.manual-transfer`, which is `rwb-case`'s (RWB-P3-E2012-APP), and the ingest stays behind the platform ingest switch of RWB-P7-E1008-APP. With the move switched off, this story receives no record and its reads stay available.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; in SIT a move of "RW-2026-000401" appears once in the ledger with `TRF-010` and "TRF-2026.12", a redelivery writes nothing, a record naming "TRF-2026.11" on 2026-12-20 is refused and quarantined, the version list names "TRF-2026.12" as in force on 2026-12-15 and none on 2026-12-20, and the JOB-14 run verifies the chain end to end.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-009 | A record is missing the decision code, the rule version, the reason code, the actor or the decided time, or its decision code is not in the list, or its rule version was not in force on its business date | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2500; ASM-4133) | This story, on the ingest |
| MSG-P7-003 | The ledger write fails | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on the ingest and the reads |
| MSG-P3-027 | No TRANSFER version is in force on the business date asked | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. | This story, on the version list |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role holds no Decision log R, or the entry is outside the scope | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, through the session read |
| MSG-P4-001 | No session, or no Recovery Workbench role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. | This story, on every read |

For MSG-P7-009 the field named is `decisionCode`, `ruleVersion`, `reasonCode`, `actor` or `decidedAt`, and the case ID is logged with the missing field and nothing else; its text is named by FSD P7 AC-ALT-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-01 and written out in no source this story may read, so the placeholder stands. For MSG-P3-027 {check} is "package in force" and {detail} names the package code TRANSFER and the business date only. The legacy message of the move itself, MSG-P3-033 with the refusing rule ID, stays with RWB-P3-E2012-APP and is not produced here. Thai text follows DL10.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the decision code, the version states and the reason codes are reference and registry data; the version labels and dates are rows, not constants.
- No personal data in events, entries, logs, tests or prompts: the record and the entry carry case IDs, queue and team codes, user references, rule IDs, version labels and reason codes only.
- No read of another service's tables and no other service reads `rwb_decision` (DP-01): the case and assignment facts arrive as the record, and the session and the lists arrive on their operations.
- Append only, hash chained: no code path updates or deletes an entry, and the daily run reports a break instead of repairing it.
- One record, one entry: the inbox key and the unique index both refuse a second write, so a redelivery can never fork the chain.
- No second rule engine: this story evaluates no package and reads no workbook, `drl_source` or `rule_row`; the rule ID and version are read from the record.
- A version is never defaulted: no version in force is a refusal with the package code and the date, never a fallback to the latest row.
- No secret in the run material: the rwb-decision login (DP-02) and the certificate come from the platform secret store, and the test data is synthetic.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-012 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **the manual transfer path of rwb-case deployed from the service template with its Helm values and the rwb-case login, its consumer groups with retry and `.dlt` paths, its Temporal worker and the activity timeouts of the transfer decision, its readiness signal, the four capability metrics, the dashboards, the alerts and a runbook entry for each failure**, so that **an operator can see within minutes that a manual move is failing, being refused or breaching its two-second budget, and repair it without reading code or waiting for a business report**.

This story deploys an existing capability. It adds no topic, no endpoint, no table and no Schedule: the manual move is `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/transfer` over `ManualTransferWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-case`, its rule answer comes from the embedded Drools kit through `EvaluateRules`, and its evidence is the local decision record published on `rwb.decision-record.v1`.

##### 2. Business rationale

A manual move is the only write on the case that a person starts and then waits for. In the monolith a refusal was a line in a log and a bulk selection was a loop in a page; in the target the answer is a status and a message ID inside two seconds, and a refusal that nobody counts looks exactly like a quiet day. The operator therefore needs three signals that do not exist in a table: the rate of moves, the rate of refusals split by code, and the share of calls that breach the two-second budget.

The capability also depends on three other services for its correctness — rwb-access for the right, rwb-deviation for the deviation that decides the refusal of a rule, and rwb-decision for the package version — and none of them fails the screen when it is slow: the move is refused and nothing changes. That is the right behaviour for the officer and the wrong behaviour for the operator if nobody counts it, which is why the refusal rate by code and the budget breaches are dashboard series and alerts here rather than a line in a log.

Deployment is part of the capability: the chart carries the rwb-case login and no other credential (DP-02), the migration job runs the per-service Flyway sequence in schema `rwb_case` (DP-15), the two consumer groups the case service already holds are provisioned with their retry and `.dlt` paths so a deviation pause and a package version are never lost (DP-09), the worker registers the two activities with the retry policy the Temporal and Drools design fixes (DP-10), and the runbook names the four failures an operator will actually see.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The Temporal workflow kit and the `rwb-recovery` namespace are available (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), so the worker polls `rwb-case` and `ManualTransferWorkflow` runs in every environment.
- The Kafka event platform provisions topics with a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON), and `rwb.case.events.v1`, `rwb.decision-record.v1`, `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and `rwb.decision.events.v1` are provisioned by their owners.
- The observability stack of the platform is available (RWB-PLT-OBS, ADR-023): metrics, traces and logs with one trace across REST, Kafka and Temporal.
- The three environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist with their parameter scope and their Kafka and Temporal endpoints.
- RWB-P3-E2012-CON is published, so the smoke profile and the drift test run against the transfer operation and its five fakes.
- LOV-TRANSFER-REASON and the queue and member rows are loaded by their owning stories; this story reads them and holds no copy.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds one image and one chart version from the same commit, runs the unit, component and contract tests, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes the chart.
2. The chart deploys rwb-case with the rwb-case login, the pre-deploy migration job for schema `rwb_case`, the readiness and liveness probes, the api deployment that serves the transfer operation and the worker deployment that polls `rwb-case`.
3. The provisioning step declares the consumer groups the case service already holds — `rwb-case` on `rwb.deviation.events.v1` for DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared, and `rwb-case` on `rwb.decision.events.v1` for RulePackageInForce — each with its retry topic and its `.dlt` topic; it creates no topic and no consumer group for the manual path, because a manual move subscribes to nothing.
4. The provisioning step asserts that `rwb.case.events.v1` carries `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, that `rwb.decision-record.v1` is used as its owner provisions it, and that no Schedule, task queue or job is created for a manual move.
5. The worker registers `ManualTransferWorkflow`, `EvaluateRules` and `RecordAndApply` on `rwb-case`, with the retry policy of 1 s, back-off 2 and 10 attempts, `NoPackageInForce` non-retryable, and the activity timeouts of the values files.
6. The readiness probe answers healthy only when the schema is at the expected version, the outbox relay runs, the worker has polled `rwb-case` and the reference-data version of LOV-TRANSFER-REASON is readable; the liveness probe answers healthy when the process and its internal loop are up.
7. The dashboards are published: the move rate, the refusal rate by message ID, the at-cap hits, the 2 s budget breaches, the workspace of the three downstreams, the `.dlt` depth and the outbox lag.
8. The alerts are wired to the message IDs of section 14 and to the runbook entries of section 13; the thresholds are values and carry the placeholder of section 14 until they are confirmed.
9. A smoke step opens SCR-05 through gateway-bff in the SIT profile, moves one synthetic case and one selection of two, and asserts the answer inside two seconds with the record on the topic.
10. The runbook is published and reviewed with the on-call rota: a refusal that is not an incident, a downstream that does not answer, a dead-letter backlog and a worker that stopped polling.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The migration job fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic reaches the new version | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A consumer group is provisioned without its retry or `.dlt` topic | The provisioning step fails the release and the consumer refuses to start | None | AC3 |
| X3 | The worker crash-loops on the task queue | The rollout is held by the readiness gate, the previous worker keeps polling and the restart alert fires | None | AC4, AC6 |
| X4 | A manual move breaches the 2 s budget on a share of calls | The budget-breach alert fires with the downstream that spent the time and the runbook entry for a slow downstream opens | MSG-GEN-006 | AC5, AC6 |
| X5 | A downstream does not answer at all and every move is refused | The refusal-rate alert fires with the code count and the runbook entry for a downstream that is down names its owner | MSG-GEN-006 | AC5, AC6 |
| X6 | The `.dlt` topic of `rwb.case.events.v1` or of an inbound topic grows | The dead-letter alert fires on rate and depth and the runbook gives the drain and replay steps | None | AC6 |
| X7 | No TRANSFER version is in force in SIT | `NoPackageInForce` is non-retryable, the count rises under MSG-P3-027 and no page is sent | MSG-P3-027 | AC5 |
| X8 | A release declares a new topic or a Schedule for a manual move | The pipeline fails the retired-element check of AC3 | None | AC3 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the platform provisioning, the workflow kit and the observability stack; builds no application code |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, activity timeouts and alert thresholds are environment values, not story decisions |
| Valuable | Makes a write path that a person waits on observable: rate, refusals by code, cap hits, budget breaches and dead letters each have a signal and an owner |
| Estimable | One chart, one pipeline stage, one migration job, two probes, two consumer groups, eight dashboard series, five alert rules and four runbook entries |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the groups exist, the series answer, the alerts fire on a synthetic metric, the runbook entry resolves |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin

    Then no replica count, resource size, timeout, threshold or cadence is hard-coded in the template

  Scenario: AC2 The pipeline promotes one artefact and runs the contract tests (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a commit on the main line
    When the pipeline runs
    Then it builds one image and one chart version from the same commit
    Then it runs the unit, component and contract tests of RWB-P3-E2012-CON and fails the build on a drift between a fake and the document
    Then it scans the image and the dependencies and fails on a critical finding

  Scenario: AC3 The consumer groups and the dead-letter paths are provisioned (new, D-RCV-60)

    Then the consumer group rwb-case subscribes to rwb.decision.events.v1 for RulePackageInForce with the same inbox
```
