```gherkin
    Then the worker is registered on task queue rwb-case in namespace rwb-recovery with the build ID of the release
    Then the readiness probe answers healthy only when the schema version, the outbox relay, the worker poller and the reason-list version are all present, and neither probe calls another service

  Scenario: AC5 The four capability series answer on a synthetic day (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published metrics of the capability
    When a synthetic day is replayed with 40 moves, 12 refusals across five message IDs, 6 at-cap hits and 2 budget breaches
    Then the move rate answers as a count and a latency histogram per environment and business date
    Then the refusal rate answers by message ID and by rule ID, and a refusal is counted and never pages the on-call rota on its own
    Then the at-cap hits answer by queue and by owner count, and the budget breaches answer with the downstream that spent the time
    Then the .dlt depth, the outbox lag and the worker poller are on the same dashboard
    Then no series carries a customer name, an account number or a personal identifier

  Scenario: AC6 The alerts and the runbook cover the four operator failures (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the five alert rules and the published runbook
    When the move rate leaves its band, the refusal rate by code passes its value, the budget breaches pass their share and a .dlt topic grows
    Then each condition raises its alert with its message ID where one applies, its environment and its links to the case and the workflow
    Then the runbook holds one entry each for a refusal that is not an incident, a downstream that does not answer, a dead-letter backlog and a worker that stopped polling, with the check, the owner role and the recovery step
    Then every alert links exactly one runbook entry and every entry names the escalation path when the step fails
```

These six criteria are new for the deployment and test artefacts only; they restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P3-E2012-APP and no element owned by RWB-P3-E2012-CON.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One service, one schema, one login: the release uses the rwb-case login and no other service's credential | DP-02; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR2 | The migration is a per-service Flyway sequence in schema rwb_case and runs before the deployment is ready | DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| BR3 | Every subscription has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and a consumer never acknowledges an event it could not process | DP-09; Architecture v5 slide 22 |
| BR4 | A manual move creates no topic, no consumer group and no Schedule: it is a REST call that starts a workflow | DP-10, DP-14; Template and Rules §R5.5 |
| BR5 | The retry policy of the transfer decision is 1 s initial interval, back-off 2 and 10 attempts, with `NoPackageInForce` non-retryable | Temporal and Drools design slide 14 |
| BR6 | No environment value is hard-coded: replica counts, resource sizes, activity timeouts and alert thresholds come from the values files | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR7 | An alert carries a message ID where the condition maps to one, and links exactly one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR8 | A refusal is a business answer and never pages the on-call rota on its own; only a rate, a breach or a backlog pages | MSG-P3-001, MSG-P3-002, MSG-P3-005, MSG-P3-033, MSG-P3-035 |
| BR9 | The readiness signal reads the schema version, the outbox relay, the worker poller and the reference-data version in force, and calls no other service | Architecture v5 slide 28; DP-07 |
| BR10 | No dashboard series, log line or alert payload carries personal data; case IDs, workflow IDs, staff user IDs, message IDs, counts and durations only | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the migration job pass the pipeline | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration complete and probes healthy | The schema is at the expected version, the outbox relay runs and the worker polls | Ready |
| Ready | Release superseded | A new chart version is promoted | Rolling |
| Rolling | All pods on the new version | The old ReplicaSet drains and the worker build ID is the new one | Ready |
| Ready | Migration job failed | The schema is not at the expected version | Failed |
| Failed | Rollback | The previous chart version is redeployed and the migration is reversed by its own script | Ready |
| Ready | The feature switch is turned off | A change record names the switch `rwb.p3.manual-transfer` | Ready, capability inert |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the provisioning step, the dashboards, the alerts and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the topic provisioning and the visibility queries behind the stuck workflow scan |
| ACE database administrator | Owns schema rwb_case, the login and its grants, and approves the migration job |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact through the environments and the switch-on of the capability |
| On-call operator | Runs the runbook entries and opens an incident when a budget breach, a refusal rate or a dead-letter backlog persists |
| RW-PLATADM | Reads and operates the case and its queues in the running service, not in the cluster |
| Service owner of rwb-access, rwb-deviation and rwb-decision | Is paged by the refusal-rate alert when the code names its contract, and owns the repair beyond the rwb-case breaker |

The per-service login used by the chart is a secret reference resolved at deploy time; the chart references "the rwb-case login (DP-02)" and never a literal name.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

The deployment exposes one operation of RWB-P3-E2012-CON: `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/transfer`, single and per case in a selection, `Idempotency-Key` required, behind gateway-bff. Owner rwb-case (P3). The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Deployment need |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The right and scope answer before the handler; 2 s client budget and a breaker, cached per request |
| GET | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations` | S8 rwb-deviation | The open deviations that decide a refusal; 2 s client budget and a breaker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}` | P7 rwb-decision | The TRANSFER model the kit fetches and verifies; 2 s client budget and a breaker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case, own contract (RWB-P3-E1043-CON, ASM-0041) | The reason list in force; read at start-up by the readiness signal and per form load |

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Provisioning |
|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1` (event 04) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | The topic, its retry topic and its `.dlt` topic already exist for rwb-case; the deployment reuses them and creates no new topic |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (event 08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | Shared topic owned by the platform and rwb-decision; reused, not recreated |

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Provisioning |
|---|---|---|
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` (event 06) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | Consumer group `rwb-case` with the inbox of schema rwb_case; retry and `.dlt` configured in the same step |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` (event 07) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | Same consumer group, same retry and `.dlt` path |
| `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` (event 30) | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | Consumer group `rwb-case`, already provisioned for the case capability and reused here for the model swap |

The manual path itself subscribes to nothing; these three subscriptions are the case service's and are listed because the deviation flag and the package version the move depends on arrive through them.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ManualTransferWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per manual request, workflow ID carries the case ID and the idempotency key | `rwb-case` | Worker deployment with the build ID of the release; the latency the budget-break series is computed from |
| `EvaluateRules` | Activity, from the workflow kit | `rwb-case` | Registered by the same worker; the timeout and the non-retryable `NoPackageInForce` are its values |
| `RecordAndApply` | Activity, from the workflow kit | `rwb-case` | Registered by the same worker; the outbox lag and the record write share its transaction |
| `CaseWorkflow` | Workflow, parent, one per case | `rwb-case` | Not changed by this release; it keeps polling on the same queue |

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The deployment registers no Schedule and no cron entry for a manual move, because a move is started by a person through the operation. The 06:30 rebalancing Schedule and the morning allocation belong to the case service and are not registered by this release; the platform's stuck workflow scan runs as a visibility query and is not registered here either.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|
| recovery_case, assignment, queue, queue_member | P3 (rwb_case) | Created and migrated by the per-service Flyway sequence in the migration job; the app story's read-side index is the only change |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_case | Created by the same migration job; used by the outbox relay, the three consumer groups and the stored idempotent response |

`deviation` belongs to S8 and `decision_log_entry` to P7; the migration job touches schema `rwb_case` only (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Deployment use |
|---|---|
| rwb-access WireMock | Runs in the pipeline and in the SIT smoke profile, including a granted right, a refusal and the no-delegation answer |
| rwb-deviation WireMock | Same, including an open deviation, an empty answer and a delayed answer beyond 2 s |
| rwb-decision WireMock | Same, including the TRANSFER model "TRF-2026.12", a wrong checksum and the catalog answer for R-UNI-18 |
| Drools stub | Same, including the refusing row "TRF-010" and `NoPackageInForce` |
| rwb-case reference-data stub | Same, including LOV-TRANSFER-REASON with R01 to R06 |

The fakes are test-only workloads; they are not deployed into UAT or production.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 provided, 4 consumed in the deployment path | The transfer operation; authorise, deviations, the rule model and the own reference data; one hop and 2 s for the three of another owner |
| Kafka | 2 published by their owners, 3 consumed | CaseTransferred and DecisionRecorded reused; DeviationRaised, DeviationCleared and RulePackageInForce consumed with retry and `.dlt` |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 2 activities, no Schedule | `ManualTransferWorkflow` with `EvaluateRules` and `RecordAndApply` |
| File | None | The release reads no runtime file; values files are build inputs |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.case.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-case/` | Chart with api and worker deployments, service, migration job, config map, secret references and probes; no Schedule hook for this capability |
| `helm/rwb-case/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, `rwb.p3.manual-transfer`, the two client timeouts, the two activity timeouts, the alert thresholds |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit, component and contract tests, retired-element check, image and dependency scan, chart publish, promote the same artefact |
| Provisioning step | Consumer group `rwb-case` on `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and on `rwb.decision.events.v1` with retry and `.dlt`; reuse of `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`; task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery` |
| Dashboards | Eight series: move rate, move latency, refusal rate by message ID, refusal rate by rule ID, at-cap hits, 2 s budget breaches, `.dlt` depth, outbox lag and worker pollers |
| Alerts | Five rules, each with a message ID where one applies and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Four entries: a refusal that is not an incident, a downstream that does not answer, a dead-letter backlog, a worker that stopped polling |

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only when the migration is at the expected schema version, the outbox relay is running, the Temporal worker on `rwb-case` has polled and the reference-data version of LOV-TRANSFER-REASON is readable. Liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database and neither calls another service.

**Metric definitions.**

| Series | Definition | Alert value |
|---|---|---|
| Move rate | Count of 200 answers of the operation per environment and business date | Leaves its band in either direction (GAP-0713; ASM-1260) |
| Move latency | Histogram from the request to the answer, with the share above 2 s | Breach share (GAP-0713; ASM-1260) |
| Refusal rate by message ID | Count of 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 answers grouped by `messageId` | Rate per code (GAP-0713; ASM-1260) |
| Refusal rate by rule ID | Count of MSG-P3-033 answers grouped by `RuleResult.ruleId` | Reported, not paged |
| At-cap hits | Count of MSG-P3-002 answers by target queue, with one and with every owner at the cap | Rate (GAP-0713; ASM-1260) |
| Budget breaches | Count of answers or workflow executions above 2 s, with the downstream that spent the time | Share (GAP-0713; ASM-1260) |
| `.dlt` depth | Depth and rate of each dead-letter topic the capability touches | Depth or rate (GAP-0713; ASM-1260) |
| Outbox lag | Age of the oldest unpublished outbox row | Age (GAP-0713; ASM-1260) |

**Alert mapping.**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written and 503 answers rise | Record-write alert with the store state and the environment | Platform on-call, page |
| MSG-P3-027 | No TRANSFER version is in force and 422 answers rise under that code | Package-in-force alert naming the package and the business date | Platform on-call, ticket to the rwb-decision owner |
| MSG-P3-002 | At-cap hits pass their rate on one queue | Capacity alert with the queue and the owner count; never a page on a single hit | Ticket to the team manager's queue owner |
| MSG-GEN-006 | Budget breaches pass their share, or a downstream times out | Degradation alert naming the downstream and the breaker state | Platform on-call, ticket to the downstream owner |
| None | The `.dlt` depth or the outbox lag passes its value, or the worker poller count falls to zero | Pipeline alert with the topic, the lag and the build ID | Platform on-call, page |

Every alert carries its message ID where the condition maps to one, and the last condition carries the topic or the series name instead. Every threshold is a deployment value with a provisional default; the missing source is carried by the gap and the assumption of section 14 (GAP-0713; ASM-1260).

**Runbook entries.**

| Entry | When it opens | Check | Owner role | Recovery step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A refusal is not an incident | A refusal rate rises and the codes are business answers | Read the code counts and the rule IDs; compare with the queue caps and the legal holds | On-call operator | Confirm with the team manager, close without a change |
| A downstream does not answer | The budget breaches pass their share, or the authorise or deviation call times out and every move is refused | Check the breaker state, the downstream's own health and the client budget | Platform on-call, then the downstream owner | Restore the downstream; nothing is replayed, because a refused move changed nothing |
| A dead-letter backlog | A `.dlt` depth or rate passes its value | Read the topic, the failure reason and the affected case IDs | Platform on-call | Fix the cause, replay in order, verify the inbox has no duplicate |
| A worker that stopped polling | The poller count is zero or the workflow executions pile up | Read the build ID, the restart count and the task queue | Platform on-call | Roll back to the previous build ID or restart the worker; no case is left half-moved |

**Done when.** The chart renders in all three environments, the pipeline promotes one artefact and fails on a fake drift or a retired element, the two consumer groups exist with their retry and `.dlt` paths, the eight series carry the synthetic day, the five alert conditions fire on synthetic metrics, the four runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota, and one manual move and one selection of two are observed in SIT with the record on the topic.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-001 | No reason code, or a code not in the list in force | Choose a reason for the transfer. |
| MSG-P3-002 | Target owner, or every owner of the target queue, at the cap | {owner} is at the caseload cap. Choose another owner or the team queue. |
| MSG-P3-005 | Case closed or under a legal hold | This case cannot move to {state} from {current}. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No TRANSFER package version in force | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P3-033 | A TRANSFER rule refuses the move | Rule {rule} does not allow this transfer. |
| MSG-P3-035 | A selection with refusals | {done} of {total} cases were moved. The others show the reason on their row. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Two moves of one case at once | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision record write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A downstream does not answer inside the budget | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A caller without Queue and allocation U | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The message texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story and the contract; the deployment adds the routing, the threshold and the runbook link, never a new wording. For MSG-GEN-006 the {system} value is the name of the downstream that did not answer, and the message is shown on the screen only where a retry remains possible; a refused move is not queued.

The activity timeouts and the alert thresholds are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0713; ASM-1260). The provisional defaults are a start-to-close of 10 s and a schedule-to-close of 60 s for each of the two activities, a budget-breach share of 1 per cent of calls, a refusal-rate value per message ID agreed with the service owner, an at-cap rate value per queue and a `.dlt` depth of 1; each is a value in the values file and each is confirmed with the service owner before the capability is switched on in UAT.

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment serves SCR-05 Transfer case in its Form, At cap warning, Refused and Saved states behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The operator-facing surfaces of this story are the pipeline run view, the release view, the eight dashboard series and the runbook; the smoke step opens SCR-05 for a synthetic case in SIT and asserts that one move and one selection of two answer inside the two-second budget with the record on the topic.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the reason codes, the caps, the rule IDs and the package version are reference data held by their owner, never a deployment value.
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads or the runbook: case IDs, workflow IDs, staff user IDs, message IDs, counts and durations only.
- One login per service; the chart carries the rwb-case login reference and no other service's credential (DP-02).
- The service writes only schema rwb_case; the migration job never touches another schema and no dashboard query reads one (DP-01).
- Every subscription has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and the consumer dedupes through the inbox (DP-09).
- No new topic and no Schedule for a manual move: the capability reuses `rwb.case.events.v1`, `rwb.decision-record.v1`, `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and `rwb.decision.events.v1` (DP-10, DP-14).
- ACE data is read only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views; no dashboard reads an ACE view or another service's schema.
- The release pins the image digest and the chart version, and no secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook.

##### 1. Story

As a **member of the integration and QA team**, I want **a repeatable cross-service journey harness that moves a case by hand through gateway-bff and the owning services, with a reason code, a rule decision and a decision record**, so that **the wave 2 manual transfer and reassignment journey is proven end to end, with evidence, before the release is accepted**.

This story builds the harness and the evidence only. It builds no production screen, endpoint, table, workflow or schedule, it serves no operation, it owns no table and it starts no workflow. The real behaviour is owned by the I stories RWB-P3-E2012-APP (the case, queue, assignment and timeline behaviour of the move), RWB-S8-E2012-APP (the X1 deviation that blocks a move) and RWB-P7-E2012-APP (the decision record and the TRANSFER rule package in force), and those three stories block the ITG run.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy RWB-E2-012 journey crosses more than one service: rwb-case holds the case, the queue, the assignment, the timeline and the CaseTransferred event, rwb-decision holds the TRANSFER rule package and the central decision ledger, rwb-deviation holds the open X1 deviation that stops a move, and rwb-access answers the role, scope and authority check. Until the real services are exercised together through the gateway, the program cannot show that a hand-off is one action with one record, which is the outcome the program targets at 5 days from 23 days.

The harness gives one repeatable run per business date that proves the composite screen route composes the transfer form from the case and the queue, that the decision record is written before the assignment and the case update, that exactly one event and one outbox row leave the move, that the queue history is visible on the case, that a refusal or a validation answer changes nothing, and that a failure in the decision log is isolated and a repeat with the same Idempotency-Key is answered from the first result. It meets REQ-WKM-003, REQ-WKM-007, REQ-WKM-008, REQ-CWC-010 and REQ-CWC-016 at the integration level and leaves every business rule, every message and every screen behaviour where the owning stories put them.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The three I stories are published and deployed in the SIT environment: RWB-P3-E2012-APP (case, queue, assignment, timeline and CaseTransferred), RWB-S8-E2012-APP (X1 screening and the open deviation) and RWB-P7-E2012-APP (decision record, ledger and the TRANSFER package in force).
- gateway-bff is deployed with the composite route of DP-19 available. The gateway-bff composite transfer route path and its merge order: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0396; ASM-0571).
- The contract fakes of §12.8 are published from the owning services' OpenAPI documents, so the harness can run from Day 1 before the I stories land.
- LOV-TRANSFER-REASON and the queue caps are loaded by the owning stories: reason codes R01 Capacity, R02 Customer deceased, R03 Skill, R04 Owner absent, R05 Legal referral, R06 Wrong queue, and the queue cap of 150 on LIT-BKK-01.
- The harness environment, its test-data seeding, its evidence format and its retention: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0396; ASM-0571).

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: seeds the case, the two queues, the owners and the TRANSFER package version through the owning contracts or the published fakes, and reads the case back to assert the seeded state.
2. Harness: calls the gateway-bff composite transfer route for case RW-2026-000401 and asserts that the transfer form carries the case, the target queues of the team and the reason list.
3. Harness: drives POST /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/transfer through gateway-bff with a new Idempotency-Key per case, to queue LIT-BKK-01 with reason R02.
4. Harness: asserts one decision record with rule TRF-010 and package version TRF-2026.12, and asserts by timestamp order that it precedes the new assignment and the case update.
5. Harness: asserts one CaseTransferred event on rwb.case.events.v1, one outbox row on the case, the new assignment with reason code R02, and that the case status, route state and stage clock are unchanged.
6. Harness: reads GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline and asserts the queue history of the move is visible (REQ-WKM-008).
7. Harness: seeds a case with an open X1 deviation and drives a second move; asserts the TRANSFER refusal TRF-010 with MSG-P3-033 and that case, assignment and decision log are unchanged.
8. Harness: forces each failure of §5 through the fakes, asserts the message and that nothing moved, then returns the fake to its healthy answer.
9. Harness: drives a bulk move of ten cases with two refusals and asserts the per-case results with MSG-P3-035; repeats the first move with the same Idempotency-Key and asserts the first assignment is returned with no second record.
10. Harness: writes one run report per business date, keyed by story and business date; the report format and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0396; ASM-0571).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What the harness asserts | Message | ITG test case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A move is sent with no reason code | 422 from the direct call; the case, the assignment and the decision log are unchanged | MSG-P3-001 | TC-E2-012-04-ITG |
| X2 | A TRANSFER package rule refuses the move (TRF-010 on an open X1 deviation) | 409 with the refusing rule ID; no assignment, no case update and no decision log entry | MSG-P3-033 | TC-E2-012-02-ITG |
| X3 | The target owner is at the caseload cap | 422 naming the owner; the case stays with its owner | MSG-P3-002 | TC-E2-012-05-ITG |
| X4 | Every owner of the target queue is at the caseload cap | 422 naming every owner of the queue; the case stays in its queue | MSG-P3-002 | TC-E2-012-12-ITG |
| X5 | Reason R04 and the target owner is outside the case's team | 409 naming rule R-UNI-18; nothing moves | MSG-P3-033 | TC-E2-012-06-ITG |
| X6 | The case is closed or under a legal hold | 409 naming the state and the current state; nothing moves | MSG-P3-005 | TC-E2-012-07-ITG |
| X7 | Two moves of one case at the same second | Exactly one queue and one new assignment on the case; the other call gets 409 | MSG-GEN-004 | TC-E2-012-08-ITG |
| X8 | The same request is repeated with the same Idempotency-Key | The first assignment is returned; still one assignment, one decision record and one event | None | TC-E2-012-09-ITG |
| X9 | The decision log write fails | 503; the case stays in queue MTG-BKK-CO with owner U-CO-01, no new assignment, no event and no outbox row | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E2-012-10-ITG |
| X10 | Some cases in a bulk move are refused | Eight of ten move; each refused case carries its own message and the summary carries the count | MSG-P3-035 | TC-E2-012-11-ITG |
| X11 | No TRANSFER package version is in force on the business date | 422 for the package in force check; nothing changes and no decision log entry is written | MSG-P3-027 | TC-E2-012-15-ITG |
| X12 | The user holds RW-CASEOWN (Queue and allocation R only) | 403 on a direct call; the composite route hides the action | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-012-13-ITG |
| X13 | Principle 5: the decision record cannot be written | The move does not proceed; case, assignment and outbox are unchanged and the run raises the incident assertion | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E2-012-14-ITG |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs on its own once the three I stories are deployed; until then it runs against the §12.8 fakes |
| Negotiable | The harness pack, the data seeding and the evidence format are agreed with QA; no business value is fixed by the harness |
| Valuable | The hand-off is evidenced across services rather than per service, and the rule that decided it is on the evidence |
| Estimable | One harness project, one journey specification, one fake pack and one run report |
| Small | Fits in one iteration with the owning stories' contract tests |
| Testable | Each scenario of §7 is one automated journey with synthetic data and a machine-checkable result |

These four criteria are new for the ITG harness and do not restate the app criteria owned by the I stories.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A manual move needs a reason code from LOV-TRANSFER-REASON | REQ-WKM-003; REQ-CWC-010 |
| BR2 | A move the TRANSFER package refuses is not made, and the refusing rule ID returned by RuleEvaluator is shown | REQ-CWC-010; RWB-E1-021; D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR3 | A queue transfer takes its owner from the target queue's assignment method | Queue field assignment_method; RWB-E1-020 |
| BR4 | An owner at or above the queue's cap cannot receive a case | Queue field capacity_cap; DL23 |
| BR5 | A reassignment for an absent owner stays inside the case's team | R-UNI-18 |
| BR6 | A move keeps the case status, route state, stage clock and timers | R-UNI-18; R-UNI-46 |
| BR7 | A case under a legal hold or closed is not moved | R-UNI-20 |
| BR8 | A move that cannot be written to the decision log does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06 |
| BR9 | A repeated request with the same Idempotency-Key has no further effect | R-UNI-40 |
| BR10 | A case with an open deviation stays with the owner the deviation rule named | R-DEV-02; R-DEV-03 |
| BR11 | The TRANSFER version in force on the business date decides the move, and the decision log records the rule ID and that package version; a case keeps the version it was moved under | D-RCV-36 T5, T7; R-UNI-38 |
| BR12 | No TRANSFER version in force is a refusal (NoPackageInForce), never a default decision | D-RCV-36 T3; R-UNI-41 |

The harness asserts these twelve rules against the owning services and re-implements none of them, so no BR row is changed by this story.

##### 9. State transitions

None. The harness changes no case status, route state, stage clock or timer, and it writes no assignment, decision record or event itself. The table is what it observes on the case after a call to the owning service.

| Observed on the case | Before the call | After a successful move | After a refusal |
|---|---|---|---|
| queue, owner, team | MTG-BKK-CO, U-CO-01, MTG-BKK | LIT-BKK-01, U-LO-02, LIT-BKK | unchanged |
| assignment | one open assignment for U-CO-01 | that assignment ended, one new assignment with reason code R02 | unchanged |
| status, route state, stage clock start | IN_PROGRESS, WITH_FCR_OFFICER, 2026-12-01 | unchanged | unchanged |
| decision records for the move | none | one, with rule TRF-010 and package version TRF-2026.12 | none |

A failed move leaves every row exactly as it was before the call.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | The synthetic user the harness drives: transfers and reassigns cases in the team's scope (Queue and allocation CRUA) |
| RW-CAPACITY, capacity and workforce planner | Reassigns cases for capacity in scope All (Queue and allocation RU); used by the cap cases |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Writes the assignment and updates the case (Queue and allocation CRU); the harness asserts its result, it does not act for it |
| SY-RULES, Drools evaluator | Evaluates the TRANSFER package and returns the rule ID and the package version |
| SY-DECLOG, decision log writer | Writes the entry the harness reads back (Decision log C) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the result only (Queue and allocation R); cannot transfer, and the access case proves the refusal |

No approval level from the delegation of authority applies: a transfer moves work, not money. Authorisation is answered by rwb-access through the authorise operation of §12.2.

##### 11. Data

The harness owns no table. It reads the fields below through the owning services' contracts and asserts them; the field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-CAS-001 | recovery_case | id | Read |
| DF-CAS-005 | recovery_case | status | Read through rwb-case contract |

The rule row and the package version are read only through the rwb-decision contract; the harness reads no workbook, no drl_source and no rule_row row directly. Test data is synthetic. No production case, party or assignment is used, and no personal data is written to a run report.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness calls the owning services; it serves no operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; the 2 s timeout and the circuit breaker per downstream of DP-11 apply to every row.

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | Case status, route state, stage clock, owner, queue, team, legal hold and deviation flag after the move |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline` | P3 rwb-case | The queue and transfer history of the case (REQ-WKM-008) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/transfer` | P3 rwb-case | The move itself, through the composite route and directly; Idempotency-Key required |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases` | P3 rwb-case | The queue membership, the assignment method and the cap used by the form |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | P7 rwb-decision | The decision records of the move, with the rule ID and the package version |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` | P7 rwb-decision | The TRANSFER version in force on the business date and its status |
| POST | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations` | S8 rwb-deviation | The X1 deviation seeded for the refusal case; an open X1 blocks the move |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Role, scope and DoA check used by the composite route and by the direct call (Architecture v5 slide 14: rwb-access IN POST /authorise) |

The composite screen route itself is gateway-bff (DP-19), owned by the platform edge story RWB-PLT-N001-CON. Its path and merge order are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0396; ASM-0571).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness produces no event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | What the harness asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1 | rwb.case.events.v1 | P3 rwb-case | One event per successful move with caseId, fromOwner, toOwner, reasonCode and ruleId, and one outbox row written in the same transaction as the assignment and the case update |
| rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 | rwb.decision-record.v1 | P7 rwb-decision (ledger); every service publishes its own record | The record of the move reaches the ledger within 5 minutes of the call and names rule TRF-010 and package version TRF-2026.12 |
| rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1 | rwb.deviation.events.v1 | S8 rwb-deviation | The X1 deviation of the refusal case is an open deviation on the case that blocks the move under TRF-010 |

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness starts no workflow and adds no activity; it drives REST only and observes the transfer step of CaseWorkflow through the case contract.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The harness run is started by the test pipeline, not by a Temporal Schedule and not by Airflow.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubbed answers |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case | case, timeline, transfer, queues/{queueId}/cases | RW-2026-000401 in MTG-BKK-CO owned by U-CO-01, status IN_PROGRESS, route state WITH_FCR_OFFICER, stage clock 2026-12-01; LIT-BKK-01 ROUND_ROBIN cap 150 with U-LO-01 at 80 and U-LO-02 at 95; 200 with the assignment on a transfer; 409 for TRF-010, for R-UNI-18, for a legal hold and for a second move; 422 for no reason, for a cap and for no package in force; the stored response per Idempotency-Key |
| rwb-decision | decision-log, admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions | TRANSFER version TRF-2026.12 in force from 2026-12-01 with row TRF-010 refusing while a deviation is open; the record of the move with rule TRF-010 and version TRF-2026.12; no version in force on 2026-12-20; a forced write failure for the 503 case |
| rwb-deviation | cases/{caseId}/deviations | X1 open on RW-2026-000402 with the complaint officer as owner under R-DEV-02; a cleared answer for every other case |
| rwb-access | authorise | Allow RW-TEAMMGR with Queue and allocation U in team MTG-BKK; refuse RW-CASEOWN for Queue and allocation U with MSG-P4-002 |

The fakes are replaced by the real service as each I story lands, contract by contract. The harness repository and its environment: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0396; ASM-0571).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Used | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | Yes | Eight consumed operations of §12.2 through gateway-bff and the owning services; one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream |
| Kafka | Yes | Consumes rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1, rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 and rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1; publishes nothing |
| Temporal | No | Starts no workflow and adds no activity or Nexus operation; it observes the transfer step through the case contract |
| File | No | Reads and writes no file itself; the outbox row is asserted through the case contract |

The platform H dependencies named by this table are delivered by the platform wave and are not repeated in the metadata H list. The blocking dependencies of this story are the three I stories.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Test harness | Runs one journey per business date, keyed by story and business date, and stops at the first failed assertion with the trace |
| CompositeRouteClient | Harness adapter | Calls the gateway-bff composite transfer route and the eight consumed operations of §12.2, with a new Idempotency-Key per case where the operation requires one |
| FakePack | WireMock project | Serves rwb-case, rwb-decision, rwb-deviation and rwb-access from the published OpenAPI documents of §12.8 |
| SchemaBoundaryCheck | Assertion | Fails the run on any cross-schema reference found in the trace, so a service never reads another service's tables |
| DecisionOrderCheck | Assertion | Reads the decision record, the assignment and the case update and fails the run when the record does not precede the change, or when there is more than one record for one move |
| IdempotencyVerifier | Assertion | Repeats a request with the same key and fails the run on a second assignment, a second record or a second event |
| RunReportWriter | Reporter | Writes one run report with the trace and the per-assertion result; format and retention Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0396; ASM-0571) |

**Environment and test data**

- Environment: SIT, one namespace, the owning services deployed from their wave 2 builds or replaced by the §12.8 fakes. Harness repository, environment and data seeding: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0396; ASM-0571).
- Data: synthetic cases RW-2026-000401, RW-2026-000402 and RW-2026-000403, queues MTG-BKK-CO and LIT-BKK-01, owners U-CO-01, U-LO-02 and U-CO-03, reasons R02 and R04, TRANSFER version TRF-2026.12 with row TRF-010, and the key 5b0c7a1e-0000-4000-8000-000000000001. No production record is copied.
- Reset: each run starts from the seeded state, so a repeated run is deterministic and the same report is produced.

**Build steps**

1. Build JourneyRunner and CompositeRouteClient against the published OpenAPI documents of the owning services.
2. Publish FakePack for the four owning services from the same documents, and prove the harness runs green from Day 1 on the fakes.
3. Add the composite route assertion of AC1, including the 2 s per-call budget and the SchemaBoundaryCheck.
4. Add the move journey of AC2 with DecisionOrderCheck: record, then assignment and case update, then one event and one outbox row, then the timeline read.
5. Add the refusal and validation set of AC3, asserting that nothing moved for TRF-010, no reason, a cap and a legal hold.
6. Add the failure isolation of AC4 with a forced decision-log failure, then the idempotent repeat with IdempotencyVerifier.
7. Add the bulk move of X10 with the per-case results and MSG-P3-035, replace each fake with the real service as its I story lands, then publish the run report per business date and the pass/fail gate; the gate definition: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0396; ASM-0571).

**Feature switch:** the harness has no production feature flag and runs in the test environment only. The production switches it exercises are `rwb.p3.manual-transfer` and `rwb.p3.drools` from the legacy solution plan; with the manual-transfer flag off the transfer operation answers 403 for every role except SY-CASEWF, and with `rwb.p3.drools` off every move is refused with MSG-P3-027. The harness asserts the disabled and the enabled state of both.

**Done when:** the journey runs green against the three deployed I stories in SIT, the run report for the business date holds every assertion of §7 and §16 with its trace, the queue history of the move shows on the case timeline with the rule ID and the package version, and the pass/fail gate agreed with QA is met for one full business date.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-001 | No reason code | Choose a reason for the transfer. |
| MSG-P3-002 | Target owner, or every owner of the target queue, at the cap | {owner} is at the caseload cap. Choose another owner or the team queue. |
| MSG-P3-005 | Case closed or under a legal hold | This case cannot move to {state} from {current}. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No TRANSFER package version in force | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P3-033 | A TRANSFER rule refuses the move | Rule {rule} does not allow this transfer. |
| MSG-P3-035 | Bulk move with refusals | {done} of {total} cases were moved. The others show the reason on their row. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Two moves of one case at once | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-005 | Move saved | Saved. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Queue and allocation U | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values; it does not own the message text. For MSG-P3-027 in this journey {check} is "package in force" and {detail} names the package code TRANSFER and the business date only. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the reason codes, the caps, the bulk limit and the TRANSFER rows are data held by the owning services; the harness reads them and never holds a copy.
- No personal data in logs, tests, traces or reports: the note field is not logged, the events carry IDs and codes only, and the harness uses synthetic parties.
- No read of another service's schema and no direct ACE read: every read goes through the owner's contract, the SchemaBoundaryCheck fails the run on a cross-schema reference, and only rwb-source-data reads the ACE views.
- No production data and no outside system: the harness calls only the owning services and their fakes, never an outside gateway or a production endpoint.
- The decision record is written before the case changes; DecisionOrderCheck fails the run when it is not, so a move that cannot be logged does not proceed.
- No second rule engine: the harness reads rule ID and package version through the rwb-decision contract, and no caller reads the workbook, drl_source or rule_row.
- One hop only: the harness fails a run when the trace shows a call chain deeper than the gateway and one owner.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract baseline of the approval routing of RWB-E2-013 for rwb-decision, on base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, with the delegation of authority read from rwb-access through its contract. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead of rwb-decision**, I want **the published contract baseline of the five approval operations — `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/approvals`, `GET /approvals/{approvalId}`, `POST /approvals/{approvalId}/approve`, `/return` and `/refuse` on base `/api/recovery/decision/v1` — with the Approval resource and its authority element, the outcome enumerations, the escalation fields, the decision-record link, the error envelope with one message ID per condition, the two event envelopes, the nine contract tables and the six fakes**, so that **the app and OPS stories of this legacy key build against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1 and a field, a level, a status or a message code can never drift between rwb-decision, rwb-access, rwb-case, rwb-platform and the gateway without a failing build**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). Approval routing shows why the baseline has to be fixed before the build: one routing decision reads the delegation rows and the authorise answer of rwb-access, the case and the parameters and lists of rwb-case, writes a local decision record and publishes two events, and one answer carries a level, a limit version, a status, a due time and an escalation level that three screens, one workflow and rwb-case read.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_decision`, REST base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, topic `rwb.decision.events.v1` for the service's own events, event names `rwb.decision.<Event>.v1`, task queue `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`. It records that the decision record leaves on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the local library and never through the service's own topic (DP-03, DP-09), and it records that the delegation of authority table is rwb-access's and is consumed and faked here and never joined (DP-01, DP-08).

It records too what the approval answer never carries: no customer name, no account number, no document body and no limit table. The answer holds IDs, codes, amounts, levels, versions and dates; the delegation facts are read at routing time from their owner and only the row reference, the level and the version are stamped on the approval.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so schema, topic, event and path names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the retry and `.dlt` topic convention are the platform baseline (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The operations and their owners are taken from the Ownership Map only; this document never declares another service's operation as provided.
- The delegation read of rwb-access is named by the target architecture as `GET /doa-limits` under P4, and the Ownership Map API catalogue has no row for it (GAP-1252; ASM-2216); the consumed row is written with the path the architecture names and the contract story of rwb-access fixes it.
- The contract baseline of the decision log of RWB-P7-E1008-CON is published, so the decision-record link this baseline carries points at one owner document.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).
- No production data is used in any example, schema or fake; every case number, user key, delegation row and amount is synthetic.

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the rwb-decision OpenAPI 3.1 fragment of the five approval operations, the Approval resource and the ApprovalAction request.
2. Fix the status enumeration, the level enumeration, the product enumeration and the override-reason reference list as enumerated elements of the answer, each read from reference data and not written in code.
3. Fix the authority element: the approval level or route role, the delegation row reference and the limit version, with the rule that the row is read from rwb-access and never joined.
4. Fix the escalation fields: the escalation level, the due time and the escalation role, so that an escalation is a change of level with an incremented counter and not a status.
5. Map every failure to the error envelope and one message ID, one condition per row.
6. Fix the `Idempotency-Key` rule on the three calls that change an approval, and the record-version rule behind 409.
7. Record the two published events with their schema elements, their key and their envelope, and the one consumed event.
8. Record that no workflow, no Schedule and no job element is created by the contract, and that the approval clock is the durable timer the app story implements.
9. Publish the nine contract tables of section 12 and the six contract fakes.
10. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the two enumerations, the authority element, the escalation fields, the error mapping, the idempotency replay, the event payload with no personal value, the drift between a fake and the document, and the absence of a retired element and of the delegation table.
11. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P7-E2013-APP, RWB-P7-E2013-OPS, RWB-P7-E2014-APP and the harness of the wave.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body or a request body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 500 with the error envelope, and a malformed request answers 422 | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, AC5 |
| X2 | A field is renamed, removed or retyped within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X3 | A status value or a level value is added or removed | The enumeration test fails, and the change is a new major version of the answer | None | AC3 |
| X4 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC7 |
| X5 | A consumed path is not in the Ownership Map | The row carries its gap and its assumption, and the fake is derived from the owner's published document | None | AC4, AC7 |
| X6 | A retired element reappears in the document, a job or a topic | The absence test fails: no JOB-05 element, no Quartz row and no approval topic other than `rwb.decision.events.v1` | None | AC6, AC8 |
| X7 | A personal value appears in an example, a payload or a fake | The scanner fails the build and names the field and the sink | None | AC6 |
| X8 | The delegation table is declared as owned, joined or copied | The ownership test fails: `delegation_limit` is rwb-access's and the answer carries a reference only | None | AC2, AC4, AC8 |
| X9 | A field-level definition is missing from the source material | The field is marked with the placeholder and the combined gap row is carried | None | AC1, AC2, AC5 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the decision-log contract of the same service and the Ownership Map only |
| Negotiable | Field-level detail is settled with the consumers; the five operations, the ten status and level values, the message IDs and the two event names are fixed by the target architecture and the legacy story |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app and OPS stories of this legacy key and every consumer of the approval answer on Day 1 |
| Estimable | One document fragment, five operations, one resource, nine contract tables, six fakes and nine contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

These eight criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only; they restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P7-E2013-APP. The fourteen legacy criteria of RWB-E2-013 are owned by RWB-P7-E2013-APP and copied there with their legacy tag; none of them is copied here.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/decision/v1`; the document never declares another service's path as provided | DP-13; Architecture v5 slide 41 notes |
| BR2 | Event names are `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1` on the topic `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, with retry and `.dlt` topics; the decision record leaves on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | DP-03; DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR3 | Every event carries the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, is keyed by caseId, is written to the outbox in the same transaction as its state change and carries no personal data | Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43 notes; DP-09 |
| BR4 | A read declares no Idempotency-Key; a POST declares it and stores its answer | Architecture v5 slide 11; DP-09 |
| BR5 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition; the business message texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story | Architecture v5 platform baseline; Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR6 | A schema change is additive within a major version; a breaking change is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |
| BR7 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-decision; a consumed operation is described as consumed, never as provided | Ownership Map v1 |
| BR8 | The delegation of authority table is rwb-access's; the answer carries a row reference, a level and a version, never a limit value and never a copy of the table | Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; DP-01; DP-08 |
| BR9 | The status, level, product and override-reason values are reference data of rwb-case, not contract constants written in code | TSD P7 T3.2; DP-07 |
| BR10 | An escalation is a change of level or role with an incremented escalation level and a new due time; it is not a status value | Legacy RWB-E2-013 AC2 and section 9; TSD P7 T3.1 and T3.2 |
| BR11 | The decision record is written locally through the decision-record library; it is never a new event of this service | Legacy RWB-E2-013 BR10; DP-03 |
| BR12 | The approval clock is a durable timer of the workflow; no Quartz row, no JOB-05 row and no Schedule belongs to this contract | Architecture v5 slides 42 and 44; DP-10 |
| BR13 | No business value is fixed in the contract: route roles, capability areas, levels, service levels and reason codes stay data or service configuration | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR14 | An event the catalogue does not carry is not declared by this baseline, whatever a service slide names | Architecture v5 slides 14 and 42; R-PREC |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The five operations, the resource, the enumerations and the error mapping are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app and OPS stories of this legacy key and the rwb-access, rwb-case and gateway-bff owners accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A field is added within major version 1, for example a new optional escalation field | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A field is removed, renamed or retyped, or a status or level value is removed | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | Retired element reappears | The absence test of AC6 and AC8 fails | In review |

The approval state machine itself — WAITING, HELD_NO_LIMIT, APPROVED, REFUSED and RETURNED, with the escalation as a counter and a new due time — is declared by AC3 and written by RWB-P7-E2013-APP, not by this baseline.

##### 10. Authority

The letters below are taken from the rwb-decision RBAC matrix of the module specification and from no other table.

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-decision | Owns the OpenAPI and AsyncAPI fragments and the fakes; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version, and the correction of an Ownership Map row |
| Consuming teams (the app and OPS stories of this key, RWB-P7-E2014-APP, the harness, and the rwb-access, rwb-case and gateway-bff owners) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| RW-PRODHEAD, product head | Documents R on the decision log and A within the delegation table: the role the baseline names on the approve call |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Documents R: a reading role on an approval routed to the Litigation area |
| RW-HEADLIT, head of litigation | Documents R: the escalation role of a D7.x item |
| RW-RISK, risk and model risk officer | Documents R: the role that receives the no-limit incident, not an approval right |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Documents R: a reading role on the decision log that the answer's decisionLogId points at |
| Platform library owner | Owns the CloudEvents envelope, the error envelope and the naming rule this document reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field is declared in an event or an answer |

The per-service login name behind the document's security scheme is not part of this baseline; the document names the scheme "the rwb-decision login (DP-02)". The authorisation decision itself is enforced at gateway-bff under RWB-PLT-N001-CON and RWB-P4-E1037-CON and is re-checked by the service on the decisive calls; it is not declared here.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| ApprovalAction | `reason`, `resolutionReference`, `reasonCode`, `changes` and `membersPresent`, as the legacy story names them on the approve, refuse and return calls; which of them each call requires, and their types and lengths, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1255; ASM-2219) |
| Approval resource | The twenty-two properties of AC2, from approval DF-DEC-032 to DF-DEC-053; `delegationLimitId` and `limitVersion` are the authority element and are read from rwb-access, never derived from a limit table of this service |
| ApprovalDetail | The Approval resource plus the routing detail the screen reads: the decision, the regulation item, the rule and its version, the due time, the escalation level, the source type and reference, the terms and the decision-log reference |
| ApprovalPage | The Approval list with page metadata; the page shape, the default size and the maximum size are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1255; ASM-2219) |
| DecisionLogEntry | The reference returned by approve and refuse: the entry of the decision log of RWB-P7-E1008-CON, not a second resource of this service |
| Delegation read | The level, the holder, the substitute, the delegation row reference and the version, with the decision, the product and the amounts as the query; the field names behind the rwb-access contract are Not specified in the source documents beyond the architecture naming of the operation (GAP-1252; ASM-2216) |
| Event payloads | IDs, codes, levels, amounts, versions, dates and the business date only; no name, account number, document body or limit value |
| Error body | The status, the message ID and the message text of the platform envelope; no case fact and no approval fact beyond its ID |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-decision (P7); base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`.

| ID | Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-P7-002 | GET | `/approvals` | Query decision, product, page, size; answer 200 with `ApprovalPage`; errors 401, 403, 503 | Decision log A, scope applied; no `Idempotency-Key` |
| API-P7-008 | GET | `/approvals/{approvalId}` | No body; answer 200 with `ApprovalDetail`; errors 401, 403, 404, 503 | Decision log A, scope applied; no `Idempotency-Key` |
| API-P7-003 | POST | `/approvals/{approvalId}/approve` | Body `ApprovalAction`; answer 200 with `DecisionLogEntry`; errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 | Decision log A, scope applied; `Idempotency-Key` required |
| API-P7-004 | POST | `/approvals/{approvalId}/return` | Body `ApprovalAction`; answer 200 with `Approval`; errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 | Decision log A, scope applied; `Idempotency-Key` required |
| API-P7-005 | POST | `/approvals/{approvalId}/refuse` | Body `ApprovalAction`; answer 200 with `DecisionLogEntry`; errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 | Decision log A, scope applied; `Idempotency-Key` required |

The error codes of each condition and the enumerations are fixed by AC3 and AC5. Which property each `ApprovalAction` call requires, and whether a change above the caller's level is answered as 409 with the new level or as a stored `WAITING` item with a 200, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1255; ASM-2219); the legacy criterion AC7 answers MSG-P7-001 with the new level and approver, and this baseline carries that as the 409 body until the app story fixes the final shape.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Contract | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET `/api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits` | P4 rwb-access | RWB-P4-E1037-CON | The level, holder, substitute, row reference and version of the delegation table; the path is named by Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 and has no Ownership Map API row (GAP-1252; ASM-2216) |
| POST `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | RWB-P4-E1037-CON | The A letter of the capability area and the caller's level or role (DP-08) |
| GET `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | RWB-P3-E1028-CON | The case, its status and the preparer; the case-status operation is not in the Ownership Map (GAP-1255; ASM-2219) |
| GET `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | RWB-P3-E1042-CON | The route, area and service-level parameters of DP-06 |
| GET `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | RWB-P3-E1043-CON | LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL, LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-PRODUCT and LOV-OVERRIDE-REASON of DP-07 |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (AC5, DP-11, ADR-020). The delegation table is consumed and faked, never joined and never declared as provided (BR8).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Schema element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision.ApprovalRequested.v1` (event 09) | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | approvalId, caseId, decisionCode, capabilityArea, approvalLevel or routeRoleCode, amount, limitVersion, ruleId, ruleVersion, dueAt, businessDate; key caseId; written to the outbox in the same transaction as the approval row |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (event 08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | decision code, rule ID and version, limit version, approval level, final call, approval ID, concluded at, record reference; published by the local decision-record library (DP-03) |

This story declares the two envelopes because the capability depends on them; the app story publishes them. `ApprovalDecided` is named in the service contract of Architecture v5 slide 14 and has no catalogue row, no event ID and no consumer, so it is not declared (GAP-1257; ASM-2221). The data-lake copy of the decision record of FEAT-DRI-06 and RWB-E1-014 is retired with the lake under DP-17; reporting reads the event on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (GAP-1254; ASM-2218).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Consumer contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1` | `rwb.access.events.v1` | P4 rwb-access | The delegation version that came into force and its effective date, so the cache of the routing is refreshed; declared so the version in force has one owner and one event |

This baseline fixes the shape and the key (no case key: the event is reference data, so the key is the delegation version); the approval read path subscribes to no event, and the consumer is RWB-P7-E2013-APP.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The approval clock, its escalation and its restart are the durable timer of `ApprovalWorkflow`, which belongs to RWB-P7-E2013-APP; this baseline declares no workflow and no activity, and fixes only that the timer name, the task queue `rwb-decision` and the namespace `rwb-recovery` are the ones the app and OPS stories register (DP-10).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-05, the legacy approval timer job, is retired and the approval clock is a workflow timer; the service's two Schedules, JOB-14 the hash-chain check at 02:00 and JOB-20 the rule promote at 00:01, belong to the decision-log and rule-version stories and are not declared here (Architecture v5 slides 42 and 44; DP-10).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| approval | P7 (rwb_decision) | The Approval resource, the authority element, the escalation fields and the status of AC2 and AC3 |
| decision_log_entry | P7 (rwb_decision) | The `DecisionLogEntry` answer of approve and refuse and the `decisionLogId` of the approval; the entry itself is the decision-log contract of RWB-P7-E1008-CON |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_decision` | The two published events, the one consumed event and the stored `Idempotency-Key` answer of BR4 |

`delegation_limit`, `role` and `permission` are P4 rwb-access's; `recovery_case`, `task`, `timer`, `parameter_catalog`, `parameter_value`, `reference_row` and `reference_version` are P3 rwb-case's; `notice` is P6's. None of them is declared as owned here and none is read directly (DP-01, BR8).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The additive change to the rwb-decision OpenAPI 3.1 document, the Approval, ApprovalDetail, ApprovalAction, ApprovalPage and DecisionLogEntry components, the AsyncAPI fragment of `rwb.decision.events.v1` that names `ApprovalRequested`, the contract README rows for the enumerations, the authority element, the escalation rule, the error mapping and the idempotency rule, and the six WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_decision`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |

No pattern is claimed for DP-02, DP-04, DP-05, DP-12, DP-14, DP-16, DP-17, DP-18 or DP-20: this baseline declares no login value, no rule package, no ACE view, no case workflow, no renamed topic, no integration adapter, no data lake, no interaction ledger and no agent.

**Build steps**

1. Add the five operations and the five components to the OpenAPI document; validate the additive rule of AC1 in the pipeline.
2. Fix the three enumerations of AC3 as schema elements and add a test that a new status or level fails the build.
3. Write the authority element of AC2 and AC4, with the two consumed rows and the ownership test that fails a document naming `delegation_limit` as owned.
4. Write the error mapping of AC5 as one row per condition with its message ID, and assert that no condition carries two message IDs.
5. Fix the escalation fields and the rule of AC3, with a test that `ESCALATED` is not a status.
6. Record the two published and the one consumed event envelopes, with a scanner that fails on a personal value in any example or payload, and the absence test for `ApprovalDecided` and JOB-05.
7. Publish the six fakes and the nine contract tests; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build.
8. Baseline tag and the consumer sign-off note, including the app and OPS stories of this key, RWB-P7-E2014-APP, the harness and the rwb-access, rwb-case and gateway-bff owners.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI and AsyncAPI artefacts validate in the pipeline, the nine contract tests pass, the six fakes answer every consumed path and the drift test is green, no personal value appears in an example or a payload, the delegation table is named only as consumed, and the app and OPS stories of this legacy key have accepted the baseline.

| MSG-P7-003 | The local decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P7-005 | A change from the recommendation carries no coded reason | Enter the reason you are not following the recommendation. |

| MSG-GEN-001 | A required request field is missing or invalid | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The record changed under another approver | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A consumed call does not answer in time | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-001 | No Workbench role on the token | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the A letter or the level | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The approval is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: route roles, capability areas, levels, service levels, the escalation ceiling and the reason codes stay data, reference data or service configuration.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: IDs, codes, levels, amounts, versions and dates only; no name, e-mail address, account number or document body.
- The contract names only rwb-decision tables and only operations owned by rwb-decision; the delegation, the authorise answer, the case, the parameters and the lists are consumed and faked, never declared as provided (DP-01).
- The delegation of authority table is never declared as owned, joined, copied or read directly (BR8, AC4).
- One REST base, one topic and one decision-record topic: `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, `rwb.decision.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-03, DP-13).
- ACE data is reached only through the owner's contract; this document declares no ACE view and no cross-schema join.
- No retired element is reintroduced: the absence test fails a build that declares JOB-05, a Quartz row, a Schedule of this capability or an uncatalogued event.
- The error envelope, the CloudEvents envelope and the naming rule come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.
- Every example is synthetic; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
