No row of `approval`, `decision_log_entry` or `delegation_limit` is copied into `rwb_comms`: the approval is `rwb-decision`'s (P7) and the delegation table is `rwb-access`'s (P4), and their fields arrive only as facts in the approval event and in the approval read. No row of `recovery_case`, `task`, `timer` or `queue` is read or written. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8; the notice columns this story needs for the escalation kind have no field ID in TSD P6 v2 T3.1 and are written from the assumed shape of section 12.1, which is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1222; ASM-2180).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-comms` (P6); base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`. Both paths are the ones the legacy module and TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 carry (API-P6-002 and API-P6-008); this story fills the notice with the escalation kind and adds no third path. The request and response field set of the escalation notice is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1222; ASM-2180).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/notices/{noticeId}` | API-P6-002: read a notice with its message, its recipient role, its approval reference, its escalation level, its template and its sent time; 200 with the Notice | Litigation, right R, scope applied through the guard of DP-08 | Not applicable, read only |
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/messages` | API-P6-008: produce the escalation notice for the approval facts of the request and hand it to the ACE notification path; 202 with the notice reference | Case record, right C, scope applied | Idempotency-Key header, kept 24 hours |

The Notice body carries `id`, `caseId`, `caseNo`, `noticeKind` (`ESCALATION`), `approvalRef`, `decisionCode`, `capabilityArea`, `escalationLevel`, `recipientRole`, `recipientUserRef`, `templateCode`, `templateVersion`, `channel`, `messageText`, `state` and `sentAt`. The MessageRequest body carries `approvalRef`, `escalationLevel`, `recipientRole`, `recipientUserRef`, `templateCode` and `channel`.

Errors: 401 no session; 403 the role lacks the right (MSG-P4-002); 404 the notice or the case is absent or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 409 the template is withdrawn (MSG-P6-003) or the level was already notified, in which case the first notice is returned with 200; 422 a required field is missing (MSG-GEN-001); 503 the decision was not recorded (MSG-P7-003). Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set.

The notice kind `ESCALATION`, the state values and the hold reason `TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN` are values of the reference lists of DP-07 and of this service's own vocabulary, not constants of the code; the value sets are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1220; ASM-2178).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/approvals/{approvalId}` | P7 rwb-decision, on RWB-P7-E2013-CON | The approval facts the notice is rendered from: case, decision code, capability area, route role or holder, approval level, limit version, escalation level, due time and status; faked, one hop, 2 s timeout (DP-11) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access, on RWB-P4-E1037-CON | The cached role, scope and right decision behind the notice read and the message request (DP-08); faked |

The parameters contract of `rwb-case` (DP-06, RWB-P3-E1042-CON) and the reference-data contract of `rwb-case` (DP-07, RWB-P3-E1043-CON) are read in process through their client libraries and not over REST; the escalation role and the new due time arrive in the approval facts and are never resolved here. The contract dependency recorded on the story is RWB-P7-E2013-CON; the platform and published contracts the DP table adds are listed in section 13 and carried in the gap of GAP-1223.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1` (EV-13) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 | caseId | notice ID, case ID, case number, notice kind `ESCALATION`, decision code, approval reference, escalation level, template code and version, recipient role, generated at |
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` (EV-14) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 | caseId | notice ID, case ID, notice kind, approval reference, escalation level, recipient role, channel, sent at |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 ledger library, published by this service | entryId | the hash-chained record of the notice: decision code D7.1, rule R-UNI-30, approval reference, escalation level, final call ESCALATED, decided at |

All three are written to the outbox in the same transaction as the notice and relayed with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope by the outbox relay of the platform (DP-09). `NoticeGenerated` is consumed by `rwb-decision` and `NoticeDispatched` by `rwb-reporting`, as the event catalogue names them (Architecture v5 slide 42). No event carries a name, an e-mail address, a mobile number or an account number.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision.ApprovalRequested.v1` (EV-09) | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | `EscalationNoticeListener`: inbox dedupe by event ID, then `EscalationNoticeService` for the escalation level and the covering role the event names |

The escalation reaches this service as the same `ApprovalRequested` event re-published with the escalation level raised by one and the new due time, and a pass-up for want of a holder reaches it as the same event with reason `NO_HOLDER` and the covering level. No `ApprovalEscalated` event is invented and `TimerBreached` (EV-19) stays a legacy reference, because the breach is now a durable timer inside the approval workflow; this reading is the assumption of ASM-2179 and the conflict it settles is GAP-1221.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None of this story's own. The handler is a Kafka consumer with the inbox of DP-09 and not a workflow; the durable service level timer that breaches is `ApprovalWorkflow`'s on `rwb-decision` and is neither started nor signalled here; the send retry is the outbox relay's and not a workflow retry. The `Notify` and `Approval` templates of the workflow kit stay on the queue of the service that runs them, and this story registers nothing on the `rwb-comms` queue.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The escalation clock is a durable timer inside `ApprovalWorkflow` on `rwb-decision` and JOB-05 is a legacy reference only; this story starts no Schedule and polls nothing.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `notice` | P6 (`rwb_comms`) | The escalation notice, its recipient, its approval reference, its escalation level, its send state and its send time |
| `template` | P6 (`rwb_comms`) | Read only: the template of the escalation notice, its version, its channel and its state |
| `merge_field` | P6 (`rwb_comms`) | Read only: the merge catalogue the message is rendered from |
| decision record (local) | P6 rows in `rwb_comms`, written through the P7 library | The record of the notice and its final call ESCALATED (DP-03) |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_comms` | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects (DP-09) |

Not owned and never read: `approval` and `decision_log_entry` (P7), `delegation_limit`, `role` and `permission` (P4), `recovery_case`, `task`, `timer` and `parameter_value` (P3). The approval arrives on its contract, the authorise answer on the guard, and the parameters and the reference lists in process; no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms`, module `notices/escalation`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms.escalation`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The legacy in-process call this slice replaces is the monolith's telling of the new approver inside `ApprovalEscalationListener`; under DP-11 that becomes a published notice fact and a template, and the mockable boundary is the approval contract RWB-P7-E2013-CON plus the ACE notification path stub. DP-10 is where the escalation clock went: JOB-05 and its `TimerBreached` become the durable timer of `ApprovalWorkflow` on `rwb-decision`, so this story runs no Schedule and no workflow of its own and the DP-10 row is carried by the P7 slice. DP-08 is the guard the notice read inherits: the read carries the Litigation R right, the message request the Case record C right, and the cached permission decision comes from the guard library against the authorise contract. DP-19 is not built here: no screen is served by this story, because the notice reaches the approver through the ACE notification path of slide 17 and the approval queue SCR-10 is `rwb-decision`'s; the approver's work list is served by the gateway-bff composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON and this story adds no route to it (ASM-2187). DP-06 and DP-07 are read in process and never resolved into a level, a limit or a holder by this service.

The platform H dependencies of the DP table and the C dependencies of the published contracts of other services are not in the plan's H and C lists for this story, which name None and RWB-P7-E2013-CON; they are the dependencies the DP table adds and they are recorded in GAP-1223 and ASM-2181. None of them blocks the build beyond Day 1: they are platform contracts of waves 0 and 1 and the platform's published contract of `rwb-access`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| EscalationNoticeListener | Kafka consumer with the inbox | Reads `ApprovalRequested`, deduplicates by event ID, and hands the approval facts to the notice service |
| NoticeController | Controller | `GET /notices/{noticeId}` with the guard, the scope and the problem mapping for 401, 403, 404 and 503 |
| MessageController | Controller | `POST /cases/{caseId}/messages` with the Idempotency-Key, the validation and the 202 answer |
| EscalationNoticeService | Service | Decides whether a fact is a telling, orders the template read, the render, the hold, the record and the outbox in one transaction, and enforces one notice per approval and escalation level |
| TemplateCatalog | Service | Reads the template of the escalation notice, its version and its channel, and the reference lists of DP-07 with the version in force; refuses a Withdrawn template with MSG-P6-003 |
| MergeFieldResolver | Service | Renders the message from the template and the merge fields, with `{decision}` and `{caseNo}` taken from the approval facts and no other value |
| ApprovalFactClient | Adapter | The approval read of RWB-P7-E2013-CON, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker |
| AccessCheckClient | Client | The cached authorise decision of DP-08 behind the two operations |
| NotificationPathClient | Adapter | Hands the merged message to the ACE notification path for the recipient role, with the path's idempotency key, and maps the answer to accepted or unavailable |
| NoticeRepository | Repository | `notice` in `rwb_comms`, with the optimistic lock and the unique key of the notice kind, the approval reference and the escalation level |
| DecisionRecordWriter | Service | Writes the local decision record and its outbox row in the same transaction as the notice (DP-03) |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `notice`, the local decision record and the library objects, all in schema `rwb_comms`; reads `template` and `merge_field` and no other schema.
- Migration in this story, in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15: `V2013_1__comms_escalation_notice.sql` adds the notice columns of section 11 that the baseline of RWB-P6-E1046-APP and RWB-P6-E1052-APP does not hold — the approval reference, the escalation level, the recipient role and user reference, the template code and version, the message text and `sent_at` — plus the unique key `ux_notice_escalation ON notice (approval_ref, escalation_level, notice_type) WHERE notice_type = 'ESCALATION'`, so one notice per approval and level is a constraint and not only a check (BR13).
- Update the notice with `WHERE id = ? AND version = ?`; zero rows updated means the record changed (MSG-GEN-004).
- No row of `template` or `merge_field` is written here: the template catalogue and the template approval are RWB-P6-E1046-APP and RWB-P6-E1052-APP.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The template code of the escalation notice is a row of this service's `template` catalogue with the message ID MSG-P7-011, the two placeholders and the channel; the code and the channel value are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1220; ASM-2178).
- LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-NOTICE and the template and notice state lists are read through the reference-data contract of DP-07 with the version in force (RWB-P3-E1043-CON); no channel, state or notice type is a constant in code.
- The escalation roles are parameter rows of `rwb-case` (`rwb.approval.route.D7.1.role`=RW-LITOFF, `rwb.approval.route.D7.1.escalation-role`=RW-HEADLIT, `rwb.approval.route.D7.1.service-level`=1 working day, assumed; DL22), read by `rwb-decision` through DP-06 and received here in the approval facts; this story holds no default and resolves no level.
- The outbox retry policy is the platform's (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); the retry limit and the backoff are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1220; ASM-2178), and the retry behaviour this story assumes is that of ASM-2186.
- The template owner who receives the MSG-P6-003 task on a withdrawal is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1220; ASM-2178).

**Build steps**

1. `NoticeRepository` and the migration, with the unique key of the notice kind, the approval reference and the escalation level; test that a second notice for the same level is refused by the constraint.
2. `EscalationNoticeListener` with the inbox, the dedupe by event ID and the decision of what is a telling; tests for AC3 and AC4 and the not-a-telling cases of X4 and X10.
3. `TemplateCatalog`, `MergeFieldResolver` and the render of MSG-P7-011 with `{decision}` and `{caseNo}`; tests for AC1 and AC5.
4. `DecisionRecordWriter` and the fail-closed transaction: a failed record leaves no notice and no outbox row and the event is redelivered; tests for AC1 and TC-E2-013-16.
5. `NotificationPathClient` and the outbox send path: accepted sets `sent_at`, unavailable keeps the notice with `sent_at` empty and the send happens once on the retry; tests for AC6.
6. `NoticeController` and `MessageController` with the guard of DP-08, the scope, the Idempotency-Key and the error mapping; tests for AC2 and TC-E2-013-15.
7. `ApprovalFactClient` over the approval read with the 2 s timeout and the breaker, and the contract-fake run of the whole fact in isolation before the approval story is live.
8. The privacy test: the notice, the merged message, the two event payloads and the log entries carry no name, e-mail address, mobile number, national identity number or account number; test for AC7.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.comms.escalation-notice`, read as a parameter through DP-06: off means the listener consumes the fact into the inbox and writes no notice and sends nothing, while the approval, its escalation and its move keep running in `rwb-decision`; the switch never blocks the approval itself. The legacy flag `rwb.decision.approval-routing` stays a legacy reference and is the P7 slice's.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P7-E2013-CON stay green, and a SIT day shows one notice per escalated approval and escalation level, one send with `sent_at` set, no notice addressed to a level with nobody on it, a held notice with MSG-P6-003 for a withdrawn template, one send after the retry when the path was unavailable, and no personal data in any notice, event or log.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-011 | An item escalates, or a level passes it up for want of a holder | {decision} on case {caseNo} passed its service level and is now with you for approval. | This story, in the template and the merged notice |
| MSG-P6-003 | The template of the escalation notice is withdrawn | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. | This story, on the held notice |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The notification path is unavailable, or a merge value is absent | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1220; ASM-2178) | This story, on the send and the render |
| MSG-P7-003 | The local decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on the notice transaction |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role holds no right for the notice read or the message request | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, through the guard of DP-08 |
| MSG-P4-003 | The notice or the case is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. | This story, through the guard of DP-08 |

MSG-P7-011 and MSG-P6-003 are copied unchanged from the legacy story and FSD P6 v3 VR-P6-001-1; MSG-P7-003, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 are the platform messages the authorise contract and the decision-record library carry. The text of MSG-GEN-006 is named by the P6 extracts for an unavailable path and is not written out in any source this story may read, so the placeholder stands. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built in this story. The escalation notice reaches the approver through the ACE notification path of Architecture v5 slide 17 and is read through the operation of section 12.1; the approval queue SCR-10 and the decision screen SCR-11 are `rwb-decision`'s, and the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 is not extended by this story.

| Where | State | What the approver sees |
|---|---|---|
| The notification path | Sent | The merged message naming the decision and the case, in the channel the template holds |
| The notice read | Sent | The message, the recipient role, the approval reference, the escalation level, the template and the sent time |
| The notice read | Generated, `sent_at` empty | The notice is recorded and the send is pending; nothing has reached the approver yet |
| The notice read | Held, `TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN` | The hold reason and MSG-P6-003; nothing was sent, and the item is already with the new approver |
| SCR-10 Approval queue (P7) | List | The escalated item itself, with decision, case, amount, level, limit version and the new due time; this story feeds none of that screen's fields |

The screen field list, the composite route specification and the field-level masking belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and to the stories that own each screen.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the template code, the channel, the message text, the escalation roles, the levels and the due times are template rows, reference-data rows or parameters of another service; nothing of them is a constant here.
- No personal data in the notice, the template merge values, the events, the workflow inputs, the trail, the tests or the prompts: role codes, user references, the case number, the decision code, the approval reference and dates only, and the delivery address is resolved by the ACE notification path and never stored.
- No read of another service's tables (DP-01): the approval arrives on its contract, the authorise answer on the guard, the reference lists and parameters in process; no `approval`, `decision_log_entry`, `delegation_limit`, `recovery_case`, `task` or `timer` row is copied into `rwb_comms`.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views: this story reads no ACE data at all.
- One notifier and no mover: this story changes no approval, no task, no timer and no case status; the item, its case and its due time stay with `rwb-decision` and `rwb-case`, so a notice can never move a case.
- No notice without its record: the notice, its decision record and its outbox rows commit in one transaction, and a failure changes nothing and leaves the event for redelivery (R-UNI-39).
- One notice per approval and escalation level: the inbox dedupe and the unique key make a second notice and a second send impossible, and the notification path's own idempotency protects the retry.
- One base, one topic, one queue: `/api/recovery/comms/v1`, `rwb.comms.events.v1` and `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery`; no story in this key declares another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- One hop and 2 s on every call, with a breaker per downstream; a missing answer never produces a notice from a guessed level or role (DP-11).
- The switch removes the notification without a schema rollback and never blocks the approval itself.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: deployment side of RWB-E2-013 for rwb-decision: the pipeline and image, the configuration and the secrets, Flyway on start with the drift gate, the Temporal worker of the approval task queue and its Schedules, the delegation snapshot refresh, the dashboards and the alerts of pending approvals and escalation breaches, and the run book with its rollback. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **DevOps engineer of the rwb-decision service**, I want **one pipeline that builds one image and deploys the API part and the worker part of the service, the configuration and every secret reference wired per environment, Flyway running on start behind the drift gate, the Temporal worker registered on task queue `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery` with the service Schedules registered, the delegation snapshot refreshed when its version changes, the dashboards and alerts that show pending approvals and escalation breaches, and a run book with a tested rollback**, so that **the approval routing of this service can be deployed, observed, escalated and rolled back without a hand change to a schema, a secret value or a Schedule**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The routing rules of this legacy key are only as good as the deployment that runs them. Architecture v5 slide 33 deploys every service as an API part and a worker part on the same task queue, so the approval clock and its escalation exist only when the worker is registered and polling; slide 29 puts Flyway in each service's own pipeline and schema; the Temporal design puts one task queue per service in namespace `rwb-recovery`; and ADR-023 makes observability per service, with the dashboards and the alerts owned by the service that produces the numbers. This story fixes the deployment side of the approval capability: the image and its pipeline, the configuration and the secret references, the migration and the drift gate, the worker and the Schedules, the delegation snapshot and its refresh, the four alerts that matter for an approval queue, and the run book and the rollback.

It supports REQ-APD-001, REQ-APD-007 and REQ-APD-010 on the deployment side, NFR-052 for the secret references and ADR-023 for the observability of the capability. It creates no business behaviour: the routing itself is RWB-P7-E2013-APP and the contract is RWB-P7-E2013-CON, and neither is changed here.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the Helm chart deploy a service as an API deployment and a worker deployment on one task queue (RWB-PLT-TPL; Architecture v5 slide 33).
- The `rwb_decision` schema, its login, its grants and its history table are created by the ACE DB work (RWB-PLT-NF06-DB, DP-02, DP-15); the approval table and its indexes are the app story's migration.
- The migration account and the read-only drift account of the service are entries in the key store (NFR-052).
- The platform Temporal workflow kit, the namespace `rwb-recovery` and the worker registration contract are published (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, and the deployment side RWB-PLT-E1071-OPS).
- The Flyway, drift-gate and job-run conventions of the platform are published (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS) and the P1 job view operations are published with their fakes.
- The observability conventions of the platform — metric names, log fields, trace propagation and the alert routing — are published (RWB-PLT-OBS).
- No build dependency: the story has no build dependency and is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).
- No production data is used in any configuration, fixture or test: every example, user key and amount is synthetic.

##### 4. Flow

1. Pipeline: build and test the service image once; the same digest is promoted to every environment.
2. Pipeline: run the drift gate before the deployment to SIT, UAT and PROD: apply the migrations of the service to a clean container and compare the object list with the target schema of `rwb_decision` through the read-only account.
3. Pipeline: stop the deployment when the gate finds a difference; report only in DEV.
4. Deployment: on start, Flyway reads its account from the key store, applies each pending migration in the `rwb_decision` sequence once and writes the checksum to the service's own history table; the second instance waits for the lock and finds nothing pending.
5. Deployment: the API part starts on the service port behind gateway-bff and answers the health and readiness probes; no approval call is served before the schema is up to date.
6. Deployment: the worker part connects to the Temporal namespace `rwb-recovery`, registers its workflows and activities on task queue `rwb-decision`, and the worker version is recorded so that a running approval keeps its own history.
7. Deployment: the Schedules of the service are registered through the platform kit; a Schedule already registered is reconciled and not duplicated, and the approval clock itself is a durable timer of `ApprovalWorkflow` and not a Schedule.
8. Deployment: the delegation snapshot of the running service is warmed from `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits` before the readiness probe passes, and it is refreshed when `rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1` arrives without a restart.
9. Deployment: the dashboards and the four alerts of section 15 are published with the service, and the alert routing names the on-call rotation of the service rather than a person.
10. Operation: the run book is published, and the rollback is tested: the previous image digest is redeployed, the forward-only schema rule is respected, and the running approvals resume on the worker version they started on.
11. Operation: a failed run or a breach is read on SCR-44 Interface and job monitor and on the service dashboard, and the platform administrator reruns a failed job through the P1 job view after the fix is merged as a new version.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The drift gate finds an object the migrations do not produce | The deployment stops before it starts and the object is named | MSG-P3-016 | AC3 |
| X2 | An applied migration file was edited | Flyway validation fails, the pod does not become ready and the deployment stops | MSG-P3-016 | AC3 |
| X3 | The migration account cannot be read from the key store | The pod does not start; the failure is logged without the secret | None | AC2 |
| X4 | The worker cannot register on `rwb-decision` | The readiness probe fails, the pod is not put in service, and the approval timer is not served | None | AC4 |
| X5 | A Schedule is already registered and differs | The registration is reconciled to the chart value and the difference is logged; no second Schedule is created | None | AC5 |
| X6 | The delegation read does not answer during the warm-up | The readiness probe fails and no approval is routed on an empty snapshot; the reason is logged | MSG-GEN-006 | AC6 |
| X7 | A DoA version changes while approvals are open | The snapshot is refreshed, the open approvals keep the version stamped on them, and the transfer is logged | None | AC6 |
| X8 | The rollback is attempted with a pending destructive migration | The rollback is refused and the run shows the reason; PROD runs forward only and a fix is a new version | MSG-P3-016 | AC8 |
| X9 | An alert threshold cannot be met because no metric is emitted | The alert stays silent and the dashboard gap is raised as a defect of this story, not of the app | None | AC7 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the template, the chart, the per-service schema and login, the Temporal kit, the Flyway conventions, the P1 job view and the observability conventions |
| Negotiable | The alert thresholds and the Schedule window are settled with the platform team; the rules of the migration, the worker and the secret reference are fixed |
| Valuable | A deployment can never change a schema by hand, run an approval on unregistered workers or lose an escalation without an alert |
| Estimable | One pipeline stage, one chart value set, the start configuration, the worker and Schedule registration, one refresh path, four alerts, one run book and one rollback test |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs in a pipeline against containers, a two-instance environment and the Temporal namespace |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Deployment of the approval routing capability

  Background:
    Given the service is rwb-decision with schema rwb_decision, login rwb_decision and task queue rwb-decision in namespace rwb-recovery
    Given the migration account and the read-only drift account are secret references in the key store
    Given no production data is used in any configuration, fixture or test

  Scenario: AC1 One image, two parts and two instances (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the service image built by the pipeline on the release branch
    When the image is promoted to SIT
    Then the API part and the worker part are deployed from the same image digest
    Then both parts run the same version and the worker reports its version to the Temporal namespace
    Then a second instance of the API part starts and serves the approval reads with no restart of the first
    Then the image carries no configuration value and no credential

  Scenario: AC2 Configuration and secrets are references, not values (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the chart values of the service in SIT, UAT and PROD
    When the configuration is reviewed against the secret store and the parameters
    Then every account, password, certificate and token is a secret reference and never a value in the chart, the image or a pipeline file
    Then the route parameters, the capability areas and the service levels of the approval routing are read at run time from rwb-case and not copied into a chart value
    Then the feature switch rwb.decision.approval-routing is a parameter per environment with its value recorded
    Then a scan of the chart, the pipeline files, the image layers and the log output finds no credential and no personal value

  Scenario: AC3 Flyway on start and the drift gate (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the platform Flyway and drift-gate conventions of RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS
    When the service starts in SIT with two pending migrations in rwb_decision
    Then both migrate in version order, the history records their checksums, and the second start applies nothing
    When a column is added by hand to rwb_decision and the pipeline runs before SIT, UAT and PROD
    Then the gate fails with MSG-P3-016, names the object and stops the deployment
    Then PROD refuses Flyway clean and any undo file, and no object changes
    Then each run writes one job-run record to the P1 job view with type MIGRATION and status APPLIED or FAILED

  Scenario: AC4 The Temporal worker registers on rwb-decision (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the platform workflow kit of RWB-PLT-E1071-CON and its deployment contract
    When the worker part starts in SIT
    Then it registers on task queue rwb-decision in namespace rwb-recovery and polls no other queue
    Then ApprovalWorkflow and its four activities are registered and the worker version is recorded
    Then the readiness probe passes only when the worker is registered, and an approval started before a restart resumes on its recorded version
    Then no Quartz table, no shared job table and no JOB-05 row is read or written

  Scenario: AC5 The service Schedules are registered and reconciled (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the two Schedules of the service, the hash-chain check at 02:00 and the rule promote at 00:01, as their own stories define them
    When the deployment registers them through the platform kit
    Then each Schedule is created once with its cron, its overlap policy and its catch-up policy taken from the chart
    When a Schedule already exists with a different cron
    Then the registration reconciles it to the chart value and logs the difference, and no second Schedule is created
    Then the deployment creates no Schedule for the approval clock, because the approval clock is a durable timer of ApprovalWorkflow

  Scenario: AC6 The delegation snapshot is warmed and refreshed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the delegation read of rwb-access on GET /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits
    When the service starts
    Then the snapshot of the version in force is loaded before the readiness probe passes, and a failed or slow read keeps the pod out of service with MSG-GEN-006 in the log
    When rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1 arrives for a new version with its effective date
    Then the snapshot is refreshed without a restart and the next routing decision reads the new version
    Then an approval already open keeps the limit version stamped on it and the refresh is logged with both versions

  Scenario: AC7 The dashboards and the four alerts are published (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the observability conventions of ADR-023 and RWB-PLT-OBS
    When the service dashboard and the alert rules are published with the release
    Then the dashboard shows the items waiting by decision and level, the age of the oldest item, the due time distribution, escalations in the period, held items with no limit and the failures of the decision record
    Then an alert fires when an item passes its due time with no outcome, when an escalation fires and the new approver acts on none of the escalated items inside the next service level, when a commit of an approval is refused by the record library and when the delegation snapshot is older than the version in force
    Then every alert names the service, the decision, the level and the age, carries no personal value, and routes to the on-call rotation and not to a person
    Then a log line of the service names the approval ID, the case ID and the decision code only

  Scenario: AC8 The run book and the rollback are tested (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the run book of the capability and the release that carries it
    When the rollback is exercised in SIT
    Then the previous image digest is redeployed for both parts, the schema stays forward-only and no destructive migration is reversed
    Then the running approvals resume on the worker version they started on and no approval is lost or duplicated
    Then the run book names the four alerts, the four failure paths of the app story, the drift gate, the worker and Schedule checks and the escalation contacts by role
    Then a rollback with a pending destructive migration is refused with MSG-P3-016 and the run shows the reason
```

These eight criteria are new for the deployment of this capability and test only the deployment artefacts: the pipeline, the image, the chart, the secret references, the migration and the gate, the worker and the Schedules, the snapshot, the dashboards and the run book. They restate no business outcome and copy no legacy criterion.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One image per release, deployed as an API part and a worker part on one task queue; the two parts run the same version | Architecture v5 slide 33; RWB-PLT-TPL |
| BR2 | One schema and one login per service: the run and the pods use the login of rwb-decision and touch no other schema | Architecture v5 slide 29; DP-01; DP-02 |
| BR3 | Flyway runs on service start in every environment, one run per service, forward only in PROD, with the drift gate before SIT, UAT and PROD | RWB-PLT-E1044-CON; RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS; DP-15; ADR-021 |
| BR4 | The worker registers on task queue `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and polls no other queue | Temporal and Drools design slide 10 notes; DP-10; RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| BR5 | The approval clock is a durable timer of `ApprovalWorkflow`; the deployment registers no Schedule for it, and JOB-05 stays retired | Architecture v5 slides 42 and 44; DP-10 |
| BR6 | The four alert rules, the dashboard and the run book are part of the release and are reviewed with it | ADR-023; RWB-PLT-OBS |
| BR7 | Every account, certificate and token is a secret reference from the key store; no credential appears in a chart, an image, a pipeline file, a log or a prompt | NFR-052 |
| BR8 | The delegation snapshot is read from rwb-access on its contract and refreshed by `DoaLimitChanged`; the deployment never copies the table | DP-08; Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR9 | The route parameters, the areas and the service levels are read at run time from rwb-case and never copied into a chart value | DP-06; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR10 | The observability names, fields and alert routing follow the platform conventions; an alert names a role and a rotation, never a person | ADR-023; Template and Rules rule 4 |
| BR11 | The rollback redeploys the previous digest and never reverses a destructive migration; a fix is a new version | RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS BR4; ADR-021 |
| BR12 | The deployment publishes the two events and consumes the one event of the app story through the outbox and inbox library; it adds no topic and no event of its own | DP-09; RWB-P7-E2013-CON |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Pipeline starts | The drift gate passes, or the flag is off in DEV | Building |
| Building | Image built and scanned | No credential and no critical finding in the image | Migrating |
| Migrating | All pending versions applied | The history records every checksum and the P1 job view holds the run | Registering |
| Registering | The worker registers and the Schedules reconcile | The task queue is polled and the two Schedules match the chart | Warming |
| Warming | The delegation snapshot is loaded | The read answers the version in force | Ready |
| Ready | A new release is promoted | The chart and the image differ from the running release | Rolling out |
| Ready | The rollback is exercised | The previous digest is redeployed and no destructive migration is pending | Ready on the previous version |
| Ready | The drift gate fails before the next deployment | An object is not produced by the migrations | Deployment stopped |

The approval states of the capability — WAITING, HELD_NO_LIMIT, APPROVED, REFUSED and RETURNED, with the escalation as a counter — are the app story's and are not changed here; this table is the deployment state only.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Runs and reruns a deployment job through the P1 job view; reads the run and the migration record on SCR-44 |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward | Reads the runs and the schema record (Platform administration R) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the runs, the Schedule registrations and the alert history (Platform administration R) |
| DevOps engineer of rwb-decision | Owns the pipeline stage, the chart values, the start configuration, the worker and Schedule registration, the snapshot path, the alert rules and the run book |
| Pipeline migration account of the service | Applies the migrations of rwb-decision with that service's login from the key store |
| Key store administrator | Owns the secret entries and their rotation; not a Workbench role |
| Platform workflow kit owner | Owns the namespace, the worker registration contract and the Schedule convention this story reuses |

The letters are read from the platform administration area of the permission matrix; this story grants no business right and changes no approval right.

##### 11. Data

No business field is created or changed by this story. The deployment writes one job-run record per run to the P1 job view: the service, the schema, the version, the checksum, the drift result, `startedAt`, `endedAt` and a status of APPLIED or FAILED. It reads the migration account and the read-only drift account from the key store, the object list of `rwb_decision` from `information_schema`, and the delegation snapshot from rwb-access on its contract.

The approval table, its fields and its indexes are the app story's (DF-DEC-032 to DF-DEC-053) and are not restated here. The job-run record fields beyond the legacy `Job` shape, the alert thresholds and the snapshot refresh interval are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1253; ASM-2217) and (GAP-1256; ASM-2220); the legacy `Job` shape, one alert per condition with a threshold agreed at the release review, and a refresh on the event are used until the register closes the points.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The deployment provides no REST operation; the approval operations are the app story's and are declared in RWB-P7-E2013-CON.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs` | P1 rwb-source-data | Reads the deployment and migration runs of the service, with `type=MIGRATION` |
| POST | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` | P1 rwb-source-data | Reruns a failed migration job after the fix is merged as a new version |

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The deployment publishes no event; the two events of the capability are published by the application through the outbox (RWB-P7-E2013-CON 12.3).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None by the deployment itself. The service consumes `rwb.access.DoaLimitChanged.v1` for the delegation refresh, and that consumer is the app story's (RWB-P7-E2013-APP 12.4); this story only proves that the refresh reaches the running pods without a restart.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|---|
| ApprovalWorkflow | Workflow, registered by the worker part | `rwb-decision` | The worker registers it and its version; an approval started before a restart resumes on its recorded version. The workflow itself is RWB-P7-E2013-APP's |
| readDelegation, routeApproval, recordOutcome, escalateApproval | Activities, registered by the worker part | `rwb-decision` | Registered with their timeouts and retry policy from the chart; the activities are the app story's |

This story registers what the app story builds and changes neither the workflow nor an activity.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Name | Cron | Overlap policy | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|---|
| JOB-14 hash-chain check | 02:00 every day | SKIP | Registered once and reconciled to the chart; owned by RWB-P7-E1008-APP |
| JOB-20 rule promote | 00:01 every day | SKIP | Registered once and reconciled to the chart; owned by the rule-version story of this epic |

The approval clock is not in this table: it is the durable timer of `ApprovalWorkflow`, and JOB-05 is retired (DP-10, BR5). The two Schedules are registered through RWB-PLT-E1071-CON; no Quartz row and no shared job table is read.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The deployment owns no business table and creates none: `approval`, `decision_log_entry` and the library objects belong to the app and log stories of this service. Flyway writes `flyway_schema_history` inside `rwb_decision`, and that history table is not a business table.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| P1 job view fake | `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs` answering one `Job` with `type=MIGRATION`, the service, the schema, the version, the checksum, the drift result, `startedAt`, `endedAt` and status APPLIED or FAILED; `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/admin/jobs/{jobId}/rerun` answering 202 | End to end and NFR tests of this story |
| rwb-access delegation fake | `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/doa-limits` answering `DOA-2026.11` with the L6, L5 and L4 rows, and `DOA-2027.01` after the event; a delayed answer beyond 2 s and an unavailable answer | The warm-up and refresh tests of AC6 |

The fakes are the ones published by their owners; the drift test of RWB-P7-E2013-CON fails a build in which a fake and the document disagree.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 consumed | The P1 job view: read the runs and rerun a failed job |
| Kafka | None published by the deployment | The service's two published and one consumed event are the app story's |
| Temporal | 1 workflow and 4 activities registered | `ApprovalWorkflow` with `readDelegation`, `routeApproval`, `recordOutcome` and `escalateApproval` on task queue `rwb-decision` |
| File | None | No file element in the deployment; the migrations are read from the image |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The golden pipeline stage that builds one image and runs the drift gate before SIT, UAT and PROD; the chart values that set `RWB_SCHEMA=rwb_decision`, point the migration and drift accounts at their key-store references, set the Temporal namespace, the task queue and the worker version and carry the two Schedule definitions; the start configuration with `spring.flyway.clean-disabled=true`, the lock and the readiness gate; the delegation warm-up and its `DoaLimitChanged` refresh path; the dashboard and the four alert rules; the run book and the rollback test.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_decision`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The pattern set is the one of the legacy key and is applied on the deployment side: DP-10 is the worker and the Schedules, DP-15 is the start migration and the gate, DP-19 is the route the probes and the dashboard read through. No pattern is claimed for DP-02, DP-04, DP-05, DP-12, DP-14, DP-16, DP-17, DP-18 or DP-20.

**Build steps**

1. Add the drift-gate stage to the golden pipeline for SIT, UAT and PROD and wire the flag so a difference stops the deployment; prove the DEV report-only path.
2. Set the chart values: `RWB_SCHEMA=rwb_decision`, the two key-store references, the Temporal namespace and task queue, the worker version, the two Schedule definitions and the feature switch.
3. Set the start configuration: validation on start, out-of-order off, clean disabled in every profile, the lock on, and the readiness gate behind the schema version.
4. Wire the delegation warm-up before readiness and the `DoaLimitChanged` refresh path; prove the refresh without a restart.
5. Register the worker and the two Schedules; prove the reconciliation of a Schedule whose cron changed and the absence of an approval Schedule.
6. Publish the dashboard and the four alert rules with their thresholds and the role-based routing.
7. Write the run book and exercise the rollback in SIT, including the refusal of a rollback with a pending destructive migration.
8. Prove the scan: no credential in a pipeline file, the chart, the image or a log, and no personal value in a metric label or a log line.

**Done when.** The eight test cases of section 16 pass in SIT, the gate stops a drifted SIT, UAT and PROD deployment and reports it in DEV, the worker registers on `rwb-decision` and an approval survives a restart, the two Schedules reconcile, the delegation snapshot refreshes without a restart, the four alerts fire in the seeded conditions, and the rollback returns both parts to the previous digest with no approval lost.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-016 | Drift found, checksum mismatch, a refused clean or undo, or a failed migration | Schema check failed in {schema}: {object}. The deployment was stopped. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The delegation read does not answer during the warm-up | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Platform administration R reads the runs | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

MSG-P3-016 is the message of the platform migration contract, carried unchanged and shown in the pipeline log and on SCR-44, not to business users. MSG-GEN-006 is the platform message of a consumed call that does not answer in time, shown in the warm-up log. Neither message is reworded here.

##### 15. Screens and states

No new screen. SCR-44 Interface and job monitor shows one deployment and migration run per service, in state Running, Failed or Complete, with the service, the schema, the version, the checksum and the drift result, and the two Schedule registrations with their last run. The service dashboard of ADR-023 shows the approval numbers of AC7.

| Signal | What it shows | Alert |
|---|---|---|
| Items waiting | The items in WAITING and HELD_NO_LIMIT by decision and level, and the age of the oldest | An item passes its due time with no outcome |
| Escalations | The escalations in the period, their level and the time to the next outcome | An escalation fires and none of the escalated items is acted on inside the next service level |
| Record failures | The commits refused by the decision-record library | Any refusal above zero in five minutes |
| Delegation snapshot | The version loaded, its effective date and its age | The snapshot is older than the version in force |

The four rules name the service, the decision, the level and the age, carry no personal value, and route to the on-call rotation by role.

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-P7-E2013-OPS-01 | AC1, BR1 | Component | One image promoted to SIT, both parts on the same digest, a second API instance starting with no restart |
| TC-P7-E2013-OPS-02 | AC2, BR7, BR9 | NFR | Scan of the chart, the pipeline files, the image layers and the logs; no credential, no personal value; the parameters read at run time |
| TC-P7-E2013-OPS-03 | AC3, BR3, BR11 | End to end | Two pending migrations in rwb_decision; a hand-added column in SIT, UAT and PROD stops the deployment and reports in DEV; PROD refuses clean and undo; one job-run record per run |
| TC-P7-E2013-OPS-04 | AC4, BR4 | Component | Worker start in SIT; registration on rwb-decision only; an approval started before a restart resumes on its version |

| TC-P7-E2013-OPS-07 | AC7, BR6, BR10 | Component | Seeded conditions for the four alerts; the dashboard panels; a log line with an approval ID, a case ID and a decision code only |

##### 17. Guardrails

- One schema and one login per service: the run and the pods use the login of rwb-decision and touch no other schema (DP-01, DP-02).
- No credential in a chart value, an image layer, a pipeline file, a log or a prompt; every account is a secret reference from the key store (NFR-052, BR7).
- No drift-gate bypass in SIT, UAT and PROD; only DEV reports a difference instead of blocking it.
- Forward only in PROD: no clean, no undo file, no hand change; a fix is a new version through the pipeline (BR3, BR11).
- The worker polls task queue `rwb-decision` only and never another service's queue (BR4).
- No Quartz table, no shared job table and no JOB-05 row is introduced; the approval clock stays a durable timer (BR5).
- The delegation snapshot is read on the rwb-access contract and never copied into a chart, a table or an image (BR8).
- The route parameters, areas and service levels are read at run time and never copied into a chart value (BR9).
- No business value in a migration, a configuration default or an alert threshold that the business owns; thresholds are agreed at the release review and held as configuration.
- No personal data in a metric label, a log line, a trace attribute or a fixture; the alert payload carries the service, the decision, the level and the age only.
- ACE data only through the P1 or P4 contract; this deployment reads no ACE view.

##### 19. Out of scope

- The routing, the outcome checks, the escalation logic and the workflow code (RWB-P7-E2013-APP).
- The contract document, the property lists and the fakes as published artefacts (RWB-P7-E2013-CON).
- The creation of the `rwb_decision` schema, its login and its grants (RWB-PLT-NF06-DB and the per-service DB work).
- The Flyway module wiring and the platform drift gate itself (RWB-PLT-E1044-APP-2 and RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS); this story consumes them.
- The platform dashboards and alert conventions beyond the four rules of this capability (RWB-PLT-OBS).
- The two Schedules as designed (JOB-14 in RWB-P7-E1008-APP, JOB-20 in the rule-version story); this story registers and reconciles them.
- The delegation of authority table and its versions, owned by rwb-access (RWB-P4-E1037-CON).
- The approval screen SCR-10 and the decision screen SCR-11 (RWB-P7-E2013-APP, RWB-P7-E2014-APP and RWB-PLT-N001-CON).
- The data lake: there is none (DP-17, ADR-018), and the deployment declares no lake element.
- Deployment slots, release windows and the cutover plan (DL34, DL35 and the cutover work).

##### 1. Story

As a **member of the integration and QA team**, I want **a repeatable cross-service harness that routes an approval by the delegation of authority table, decides it, escalates it and holds it through gateway-bff and the owning services**, so that **the wave 2 approval journey is proven end to end, with evidence, before the release is accepted**.

This story builds the harness and the evidence only. It builds no production endpoint, table, workflow, schedule or screen. The real behaviour is owned by the I stories RWB-P4-E1038-APP (the delegation of authority table as versioned reference data), RWB-P3-E1028-APP (service levels, timers and escalation), RWB-P7-E2013-APP (the router, the approval workflow and the decision records), RWB-P3-E2013-APP (the case status, the approval task and the timer), RWB-P4-E2013-APP (the authorise answer) and RWB-P6-E2013-APP (the escalation notification), and those six stories block the ITG run.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy RWB-E2-013 journey crosses more than one service: rwb-decision holds the approval, the router and the decision records, rwb-access holds the delegation of authority table and answers the authorise check, rwb-case holds the case status, the approval task and the service level timer, and rwb-comms tells the new approver when an item escalates. Approval and authority governance is an audit finding: approvals today are given by e-mail, sometimes above the approver's limit or by the person who prepared the decision. Until the real services are exercised together through the gateway, the program cannot show that every approval follows the versioned delegation table, that nobody approves their own decision, and that no item waits unseen.

The harness gives one repeatable run per business date that proves the item is routed to the level whose row covers it or to the role named for a decision with no amount limit, that an approval inside the limit is written with its approver, level and limit version, that a breach of the service level or a level with no holder moves the item without moving the case, and that a failure in one service is isolated. It meets REQ-APD-001, REQ-APD-003, REQ-APD-004, REQ-APD-005, REQ-APD-007, REQ-APD-008, REQ-APD-009, REQ-APD-010 and REQ-APD-011 at the integration level and leaves every business rule and every screen behaviour where the owning stories put them.

- gateway-bff is deployed with the composite route of DP-19 available. The gateway-bff composite approval-queue route path and its merge order: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0397; ASM-0572).
- The contract fakes of §12.8 are published from the owning services' OpenAPI documents, so the harness runs green from Day 1 before the I stories land.
- Delegation version DOA-2026.11 with holders U-9201 at L6, U-9202 at L5, U-9203 at L4 and the L3 committee recording holder U-9204, the route parameters rwb.approval.route.D7.1.area=LITIGATION, rwb.approval.route.D7.1.role=RW-LITOFF, rwb.approval.route.D7.1.escalation-role=RW-HEADLIT and rwb.approval.route.D7.1.service-level=1 working day, the capability areas per decision code and the service levels are loaded by the owning stories.
- The harness environment, its seeding of the delegation versions, holders and service level clocks, and its evidence format and retention: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0397; ASM-0572).

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: seeds delegation version DOA-2026.11 and the L3 committee recording holder through the rwb-access contract, and the two approvals (the D7.1 demand notice and the D6.4 settlement "A-1") through the rwb-decision contract or the published fakes.
2. Harness: reads GET /approvals for the holder and asserts the decision, the amount, the level, the limit version and the age of each item.
3. Harness: approves inside the limit with one Idempotency-Key and asserts one decision record with the approver, the approval level, the limit version, the rule ID and version and final_call APPROVED, the approval status APPROVED, the case leaving Waiting approval, the P3 approval task completed and the service level timer closed.
4. Harness: drives a service level breach and asserts that the item moves one level up, or to the escalation role for a role-routed item, with MSG-P7-011 and the case still Waiting approval.
5. Harness: drives each refusal and hold of §5 — the preparer, a change above the limit, the missing reason, the override without a coded reason, the level with no holder, the committee level without a resolution reference, two approvers at once, a product with no covering limit and the decision-log failure — and asserts the status, the message and that nothing moved.
6. Harness: asserts that the DoA answer comes from POST /authorise and from the limit version on the approval, and that no service reads another service's schema.
7. Harness: writes one run report per business date, keyed by story and business date; the report format, the pass/fail gate and the retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0397; ASM-0572).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What the harness asserts | Message | ITG test case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The service level passes with no action | The item moves to the next level up, or to the escalation role; the case does not move; one escalation entry is written and the new approver is told | MSG-P7-011 | TC-E2-013-02-ITG |
| X2 | The caller prepared the decision | 409; the approval stays WAITING and no decision record is written | MSG-P7-002 | TC-E2-013-06-ITG |
| X3 | A change raises the amount above the caller's level | Not approved; the item is rerouted to the level that covers it, with the changed terms and status WAITING, and no approval at the old level is recorded | MSG-P7-001 | TC-E2-013-07-ITG |
| X4 | Refuse or return without a reason | 422 for the missing field; the approval keeps its status | MSG-GEN-001 | TC-E2-013-08-ITG |
| X5 | A change departs from the recommendation without a coded reason | 422; the recommendation and the terms are unchanged | MSG-P7-005 | TC-E2-013-10-ITG |
| X6 | The required level has no holder and no substitute | The item moves one level up at once and the routing entry records reason NO_HOLDER; the case does not move | MSG-P7-011 | TC-E2-013-11-ITG |
| X7 | A committee level is approved without a resolution reference or the members present | 422 for the missing field; the entry is written only when both are given | MSG-GEN-001 | TC-E2-013-12-ITG |
| X8 | Two approvers act on one item at once | One call succeeds and writes one entry; the other returns 409 and writes nothing | MSG-GEN-004 | TC-E2-013-13-ITG |
| X9 | No delegation row covers the decision and product | The approval is stored with status HELD_NO_LIMIT, the case stays Waiting approval and the incident is raised | MSG-P7-010 | TC-E2-013-14-ITG |
| X10 | The user holds no A letter in the decision's capability area, or is not the holder, substitute or route role | 403 on a direct call; the composite queue route hides the action | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-013-15-ITG |
| X11 | The decision record cannot be written on an approval | 503; nothing moves — no approval status change, no case status change and no decision record | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E2-013-16-ITG |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A decision with delegation rows routes to the lowest level whose row covers it on the routing date; the item keeps that delegation version | REQ-APD-001; REQ-APD-010; RWB-E1-038; Delegation of authority matrix, rule 9 |
| BR2 | A decision with no amount limit routes to the role named in its route parameters, for D7.1 notices RW-LITOFF | Parameters rwb.approval.route.*; DL22 |
| BR3 | The approver must hold the A letter in the decision's capability area and be the holder or substitute of the required level, or hold the route role | Permission matrix; Key sheet: A works within the delegation table; CTL-04 |
| BR4 | A person may not approve a decision they proposed or prepared | Admin and access model, section 6.2; CTL-05; Delegation of authority matrix, rule 10 |
| BR5 | An approval above the caller's level is refused and sent to the level that covers it, with no silent approval | REQ-APD-004; R-UNI-15 |
| BR6 | A change from the recommendation needs a coded reason; refuse and return need a reason | REQ-APD-005; R-UNI-14; CTL-07 |
| BR7 | An approval not answered inside its service level escalates one level up, or to the escalation role; the case does not move | REQ-APD-007; R-UNI-30; R-UNI-42 |
| BR8 | A level with no holder and no substitute passes the item one level up at once | REQ-APD-011 |
| BR9 | Levels L1 to L3 approve by committee resolution; the entry records the resolution reference, the date and the members present | REQ-APD-008; doa.txt, Levels sheet |
| BR10 | The limit, the rule version and the approver are written with every approval | REQ-APD-009; FEAT-DRI-04 |
| BR11 | A decision that no limit covers is held and raises an incident | Delegation of authority matrix, rule 8 |
| BR12 | An approval outcome that cannot be written to the decision log does not take effect | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |

The harness asserts these rules against the owning services; it does not re-implement them. No BR row is changed by this story.

##### 9. State transitions

The states below are the states the harness observes. The harness changes no approval status and no case status itself; every transition is caused by a call to the owning service or by the timer breach the owning service publishes.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| In progress | Recommendation routed for approval | A delegation row covers the decision, product and amount on the routing date | Waiting approval, approval WAITING |
| In progress | Recommendation routed for approval | No delegation row covers the decision and product | Waiting approval, approval HELD_NO_LIMIT |
| Waiting approval | Approver accepts | Caller within the required level, not the preparer, decision record written | In progress, approval APPROVED |
| Waiting approval | Approver changes and accepts | Changed terms within the caller's level, coded reason given, decision record written | In progress, approval APPROVED |
| Waiting approval | Approver refuses or returns | Reason given | In progress at the state the rule names, approval REFUSED or RETURNED |
| Waiting approval | TimerBreached | Service level breached | Waiting approval, with the next level or the escalation role |
| Waiting approval | A change raises the amount above the caller's level | A level covers the changed terms | Waiting approval, with the covering level |

A failed decision-record write leaves the approval and the case exactly as they were.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Holders and substitutes of levels L4 to L6 (synthetic test users at DL18) | The approvers the harness drives at their level: approve, change, refuse or return an item |
| Recording holder of levels L1 to L3 | Records the committee resolution with its reference and the members present; driven by the harness in the committee case |
| RW-RESTRUCT, RW-CREDCOMM | Treatment and offer preparers; the synthetic preparer U-9210 holds RW-RESTRUCT and may not approve what it prepared |
| RW-LITOFF Litigation officer, RW-LEGAL Legal counsel, RW-HEADLIT Head of Litigation | Approve D7.x items routed to their role, and receive the escalation of a role-routed item |
| RW-PRODHEAD Product head | Approves items of their product at their level, in Treatment and offer, Litigation, Asset and disposal, Debt sale, Write-off and posting |
| RW-SALEOFF, RW-HEADNPA, RW-HEADASL, RW-DEBTSALE | Approve Asset and disposal or Debt sale items at their level |
| RW-CREDITAD, RW-WOCOMM, RW-FINANCE | Approve Write-off and posting items at their level |
| SY-RULES, SY-CASEWF | Call the router, start and close the service level timer and publish the timer breach; driven by the harness through the owning contract |
| RW-AUDIT | Reads approvals and outcomes through the decision log |
| Approval levels | L1 Board of Directors to L6 Recovery executive, department level, per the delegation of authority table |

No approval level and no holder is created by this story; the delegation data is owned by RWB-P4-E1038-APP and the authorise answer is owned by RWB-P4-E2013-APP, through POST /authorise. No names of people appear in the harness, its data or its report.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness calls the owning services; it serves no operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; the 2 s timeout and the circuit breaker per downstream of DP-11 apply to every row.

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/approvals` | P7 rwb-decision | The approval queue of the holder: decision, amount, level, limit version and age |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/approvals/{approvalId}` | P7 rwb-decision | One approval with limit version, rule ID and version, due time and escalation level |
| POST | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/approvals/{approvalId}/approve` | P7 rwb-decision | Approve, or change and approve; Idempotency-Key required |
| POST | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/approvals/{approvalId}/return` | P7 rwb-decision | Return an item with a question; reason required |
| POST | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/approvals/{approvalId}/refuse` | P7 rwb-decision | Refuse an item with a reason |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | P7 rwb-decision | The routing, escalation and outcome records of the run |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Role, scope and DoA check behind a direct call (Architecture v5 slide 14: rwb-access IN POST /authorise) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case status, including Waiting approval |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` | P3 rwb-case | The service level timer and its state after an approval or an escalation |
| PATCH | `/api/recovery/case/v1/tasks/{taskId}` | P3 rwb-case | The approval task, asserted completed after an approval |
| POST | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/messages` | P6 rwb-comms | The escalation notification to the new approver |

The DoA answer is asserted through POST /authorise and through the limit version on the approval; the harness reads no delegation operation of its own. The composite approval-queue route itself is gateway-bff (DP-19), owned by the platform edge story RWB-PLT-N001-CON; its path and merge order are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0397; ASM-0572).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness produces no event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | What the harness asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.decision.ApprovalRequested.v1 | rwb.decision.events.v1 | P7 rwb-decision | One event per routed item, with the approval ID, case ID, level and amount, and no personal data |
| rwb.decision.ApprovalDecided.v1 | rwb.decision.events.v1 | P7 rwb-decision | One event per decided item, after the decision record |
| rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1 | rwb.case.events.v1 | P3 rwb-case | The service level breach that drives the escalation, with the approval reference |
| rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 | rwb.decision-record.v1 | P7 rwb-decision (ledger); every service publishes its own record | The routing, escalation and outcome records reach the ledger within 5 minutes of the call |

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness starts no workflow and adds no activity; it drives REST and observes the workflow that rwb-decision already owns.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The harness run is started by the test pipeline, not by a Temporal Schedule and not by Airflow; the escalation clock is driven by a fixed clock in the harness.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubbed answers |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-decision | approvals, approvals/{approvalId}, approve, return, refuse, decision-log | "A-1" at L6 with limit version DOA-2026.11; the D7.1 item at role RW-LITOFF; 409 preparer, 409 two approvers, 422 missing reason, 422 missing resolution reference, 422 missing coded reason; HELD_NO_LIMIT for HIRE_PURCHASE; a forced write failure for the 503 case |
| rwb-access | authorise, delegation data behind it | Allow the holder, substitute and route role; do not cover HIRE_PURCHASE under DOA-2026.11; an L6 SSME row with no holder and no substitute; DOA-2027.01 in force from 1 January 2027 |
| rwb-case | cases/{caseId}, cases/{caseId}/timers, tasks/{taskId} | Case status Waiting approval and In progress; the service level timer open and then closed; a timer breach at 09:00 on 15 December 2026 |
| rwb-comms | cases/{caseId}/messages | ACCEPTED for the escalation notification, with one message per escalated item |

The fakes are published from the owning services' OpenAPI documents and are replaced by the real service as each I story lands, contract by contract. The harness repository, its environment and its evidence format: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0397; ASM-0572).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |

The platform H dependencies named by this table are delivered by the platform wave and are not repeated in the metadata H list. The blocking dependencies of this story are the I stories.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Test harness | Runs one journey per business date, keyed by story and business date, and stops at the first failed assertion with the trace |
| ApprovalRouteClient | Harness adapter | Calls the eleven consumed operations of §12.2 with the Idempotency-Key header where the operation requires one |
| FakePack | WireMock project | Serves rwb-decision, rwb-access, rwb-case and rwb-comms from the published OpenAPI documents of §12.8 |
| SchemaBoundaryCheck | Assertion | Fails the run on any cross-schema reference found in the trace, so a service never reads another service's tables |
| DecisionOrderCheck | Assertion | Fails the run when an approval status changes before its decision record, or when a second record exists for one action and one Idempotency-Key |
| EscalationClock | Harness driver | Drives the fixed clock to the service level due time and starts the timer breach through the owning service, so the escalation is repeatable |
| RunReportWriter | Reporter | Writes one run report with the trace and the per-assertion result; format and retention Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0397; ASM-0572) |

**Environment and test data**

- Environment: SIT, one namespace, the owning services deployed from their wave 2 builds or replaced by the §12.8 fakes. Harness repository, environment and data seeding: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0397; ASM-0572).
- Data: delegation version DOA-2026.11 and, for the version case, DOA-2027.01 from 1 January 2027; holders U-9201 at L6, U-9202 at L5, U-9203 at L4 and the L3 committee recording holder U-9204; preparer U-9210; litigation users U-9211, U-9212 and U-9213; case RW-2026-000123 with the D7.1 demand notice under R-LIT-03 version LIT-2026.12; case RW-2026-000124 with the D6.4 MORTGAGE settlement at principal 2,400,000.00, loss 20.00 percent and loss amount 480,000.00. No production record is copied.
- Clocks: the escalation clock is a fixed clock in the harness, set to 09:00 on 14 December 2026 and advanced to the due time; the service level values themselves are read from the owning service.
- Reset: each run starts from the seeded state, so a repeated run is deterministic and the same report is produced.

**Build steps**

1. Build JourneyRunner and ApprovalRouteClient against the published OpenAPI documents of the owning services.
2. Publish FakePack for the four owning services from the same documents, and prove the harness runs green from Day 1 on the fakes.
3. Add the routing assertion of AC1, including the level, the limit version, the routing entry and the queue answer.
4. Add the approval journey of AC2, asserting the decision record before the case status, the task completion and the closed timer.
5. Add the escalation and no-holder journey of AC3 with the EscalationClock, and assert that the case does not move.
6. Add the refusal and hold answers of AC4, then the decision-log failure, keeping the same assertions.
7. Replace each fake with the real service as its I story lands, contract by contract.
8. Publish the run report per business date and add the pass/fail gate agreed with QA; the gate definition: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0397; ASM-0572).

**Feature switch:** the harness has no production feature flag and runs in the test environment only. The production switch it exercises is `rwb.decision.approval-routing` from the legacy solution plan; the harness asserts the disabled state and the enabled state of the approval endpoints.

**Done when:** the journey runs green against the six deployed I stories in SIT, the run report for the business date holds every assertion of §7 and §16 with its trace, and the pass/fail gate agreed with QA is met for one full business date.
