| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-001 | Approval above the caller's level | This needs approval at level {level}. It has been sent to {approver}. |
| MSG-P7-002 | Preparer tries to approve | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Entry cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P7-004 | Approved | Approved. The case moves to {state}. |
| MSG-P7-005 | Change from the recommendation without a coded reason | Enter the reason you are not following the recommendation. |
| MSG-P7-010 | No limit covers the decision and product | No approval limit covers {decision} for {product}. The item is held and Risk has been told. |
| MSG-P7-011 | Item escalated to a new approver (new) | {decision} on case {caseNo} passed its service level and is now with you for approval. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Reason, resolution reference or members present missing | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Item changed by another approver | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P4-002 | No A letter in the decision's area | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values; it does not own the message text. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | State | What the harness asserts |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-10 Approval queue | Loading | The composite route is called once and the answer is returned inside the 2 s budget |
| SCR-10 Approval queue | List | Each item waiting on the holder is returned with decision, case, amount, level, limit version, age and due time, and the item prepared by the caller is absent |
| SCR-10 Approval queue | Empty (common state) | An approver with nothing waiting gets an empty list, not an error |
| SCR-10 Approval queue | Refused action | A user without the A letter in the area, or not the holder, substitute or route role, is refused with MSG-P4-002 |

The harness opens no screen and renders no page; it asserts the composite route answer and the direct endpoint answers that the screen consumes. ##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: delegation versions, levels, limits, holders, route roles, capability areas, service levels and override reasons are data or parameters held by the owning services; the harness reads them and never holds a copy.
- No personal data in logs, tests, traces or reports: member references are used instead of names, the synthetic user IDs and case numbers are the only identifiers, and the run report holds IDs and assertions only.
- No read of another service's tables: the delegation is read through the rwb-access contract, the approvals and the decision records through the rwb-decision contract, the case, task and timer through the rwb-case contract and the notification through the rwb-comms contract; the SchemaBoundaryCheck fails the run on a cross-schema reference, and only rwb-source-data reads the ACE views.
- No production data and no outside system: the harness calls only the owning services and their fakes, never an outside gateway, a notification provider or a production endpoint.
- No approval without its decision record: DecisionOrderCheck fails the run when a status moves before its record, and the change is never asserted as applied.
- No item may be assigned to its preparer: the harness asserts the absence of the item in the preparer's queue and the 409 answer.
- One hop only: the harness fails a run when the trace shows a call chain deeper than the gateway and one owner.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract baseline of the approval screen for RWB-E2-014 in rwb-decision — the composite route of the screen, its panels, its field list and mask flags, the P7 operations it consumes, the screen state values, the notice summary shape, the paging and filter parameters, the error envelope, the fakes and the drift test. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the D7.1 approval screen — the composite route served by gateway-bff with its panels, its field list and its mask flags; the five rwb-decision operations on `/api/recovery/decision/v1`; the screen state values; the notice summary shape; the paging and filter parameters; the error envelope and its message IDs; the nine contract tables and the four contract fakes** so that **the app story of this key builds against a frozen, testable contract on Day 1 and a field, a mask flag, a state value, a parameter or a message code can never drift between rwb-decision, rwb-comms, rwb-source-data, rwb-case and the platform route without a failing build**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020), and a screen is the hardest place to keep it: the legacy story read the approval, the notice, its template version, the case number, the ACE balance and the contact value inside one process, in one transaction, and could change any of them without telling anybody. In the target the screen is composed at the edge and each of those facts has exactly one owner (Architecture v5 slides 14, 17, 20 and 41; DP-19).

The baseline fixes what the five parties have to agree before any of them builds. The route name, the two panels, the field list and the mask flags, because the browser renders one model and three owners produce it. The five P7 operations and their status codes, because the three decisions carry an `Idempotency-Key` and a refusal that is decided twice must not be written twice. The screen state values, because Ready, Stale input and Decided are what the officer acts on and they must mean the same thing in the route and in the service. The notice summary, because the notice body, its addressee and its account number stay in rwb-comms and only identifiers, codes and dates may cross the boundary. The paging and filter parameters, because the approval queue is read with a decision, a product and a page. The error envelope and its message IDs, because six of them are the business rules of the legacy story and their text is agreed.

It also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_decision`, REST base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, topic `rwb.decision.events.v1`, event names `rwb.decision.<Event>.v1`, the shared record topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, task queue `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`. A screen composite adds the platform's public base `/api/recovery` with no service segment and no `/v1`, which is the edge's and not this service's (DP-13, DP-19).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the schema, topic, event and path names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform route contract is published (RWB-PLT-N001-CON): the public base `/api/recovery` with no service segment and no `/v1`, the opaque session cookie with a 15-minute idle, the coarse permission, the 2 s budget per downstream and the RFC 9457 problem envelope. This document narrows that baseline for one screen and never redefines it.
- The platform envelopes — the error envelope, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the retry and `.dlt` topic convention — are the baseline (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON).
- The notice contract of RWB-P6-E1052-CON is published, because the notice summary this baseline fixes is a narrowed view of that answer.
- The decision record library and its topic are published (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON), so the `DecisionRecorded` envelope of 12.3 is the library's and not a new design.
- The operations and their owners are taken from the Ownership Map only; this document never declares another service's operation as provided.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).
- No production data is used in any example, schema or fake; every notice, case, template, user and workspace key is synthetic.

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 fragment of the screen composite: one public route, the two panels, the screen model and the field list.
2. Declare the mask flag of every field against the masking policy the route applies, and prove that no field can carry a raw personal value.
3. Declare the five P7 operations the screen consumes on base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, with their bodies, answers, access rights and error statuses.
4. Fix the screen state values and the mapping from the approval status list of LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS and the notice state of the notice answer.
5. Fix the notice summary element list as identifiers, codes and dates only, and prove that no notice body, addressee, account number or merge value is declared.
6. Fix the paging and filter parameters of the queue read.
7. Map every failure to the error envelope and one message ID, one condition per row, and keep the owner's message identifier and detail through the route.
8. Record the one published event envelope and the four fakes; publish the nine contract tables.
9. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the mask rule, the state enumeration, the notice summary scan, the parameter shapes, the error mapping, the fake drift and the absence of a monolith path.
10. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P7-E2014-APP, RWB-P7-E2014-OPS, the routing story RWB-P7-E2013-APP, the notice stories of RWB-P6-E1052-CON and the platform route story RWB-PLT-N001-APP.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response or request body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed route answers the problem envelope and a malformed request answers 422 | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1, AC7 |
| X2 | A field is renamed, removed or retyped within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1, AC3 |
| X3 | A screen state value is added or removed | The enumeration test fails, and the change is a new major version of the screen model | None | AC4 |
| X4 | A field appears without a mask flag, or a raw personal value appears in an example | The mask test fails the build and names the field | None | AC2, AC5 |
| X5 | The notice summary declares a body, an addressee, an account number or a merge value | The scan fails the build and names the element | None | AC5 |
| X6 | A contract fake drifts from the document, or a fake answers a field the document does not declare | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC8 |
| X7 | A retired element reappears: a monolith base, a data-lake extract or a second topic | The absence test fails | None | AC8 |
| X8 | A value is missing from the source material | The element carries the placeholder and one gap row | None | AC1, AC4, AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform route and envelope contracts, the notice contract of the same wave and the Ownership Map only |
| Negotiable | Field-level detail and the mask policy keys are settled with the route owner and the consumers; the operations, the state values, the message IDs and the event name are fixed by the target architecture and the legacy story |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app and deployment stories of this key and the notice and route owners on Day 1 |
| Estimable | One document fragment, one public route, five operations, nine contract tables, four fakes and eight contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

    When it is compared with the notice answer of RWB-P6-E1052-CON and with the legacy screen
    Then it carries noticeId, caseId, noticeType, noticeState, templateId, templateVersion, documentId and generatedAt, and nothing else
    Then it carries no notice body, no addressee, no account number, no merge value, no name and no postal address
    Then documentId is a reference and the PDF itself is served by rwb-document at the route and never carried in this summary
    Then the document states that the addressee role and the masked postal address the legacy screen shows are screen fields of the decision panel owned by rwb-source-data and not elements of the notice summary, because the notice answer carries no addressee (GAP-1268; ASM-2232)
    Then a scan of the summary schema and of every example finds no personal value

  Scenario: AC6 The paging and filter parameters of the queue read are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the queue read of the decision panel
    When its query parameters are compared with the module specification
    Then it declares decision, product, page and size, and decision is fixed to D7.1 for this screen
    Then page and size are integers, size carries a maximum, and a request beyond the maximum or below zero answers 422 with MSG-GEN-001 naming the parameter
    Then the answer is a page of approvals with the total count and the page parameters echoed, and no full approval body in the list
    Then the page size default and maximum are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1266; ASM-2230)
    Then the route adds no filter of its own and narrows no parameter

  Scenario: AC7 The error envelope maps one message ID per condition (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the error responses declared for the route and for the five operations
    When each condition is compared with the message catalog
    Then every error is RFC 9457 problem details with the status, the message identifier and the detail, and no second envelope is introduced
    Then 401 answers a missing or expired session, 403 answers MSG-P4-002 when the role lacks the right, and 404 answers MSG-P4-003 when the approval is absent or out of the caller's scope
    Then 409 answers MSG-P7-002 for the preparer, MSG-P7-006 for a stale input, MSG-P6-003 for a withdrawn template and MSG-GEN-004 for a decision already taken
    Then 422 answers MSG-GEN-001 for a missing reason or a bad parameter and MSG-P7-005 for a change of variant without a coded reason
    Then 503 answers MSG-P7-003 for a record that cannot be written, MSG-GEN-006 for a consumed call beyond its budget, and the route's own temporarily-unavailable problem
    Then the owner's message identifier and detail pass through the route unchanged, and no condition maps to two message IDs

  Scenario: AC8 The nine contract tables are complete, the four fakes match them and the drift test is green (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the contract section of this story
    When the nine sub-tables are reviewed and the contract tests are run
    Then each of 12.1 to 12.9 is present and names its owner from the Ownership Map, with None where the element is empty
    Then 12.1 names the public route with owner PLT and the five operations with owner P7, and 12.7 records None because this baseline owns no table
    Then the rwb-comms, rwb-source-data, rwb-case and route fakes answer the paths and payloads of 12.2 and the shapes of 12.1, each with a delayed answer beyond 2 s
    Then the drift test compares each fake with the document and fails on any drift
    Then the absence test finds no monolith base, no data-lake extract and no topic other than rwb.decision.events.v1 and rwb.decision-record.v1
    Then the document states that schema rwb_decision, REST base /api/recovery/decision/v1, topic rwb.decision.events.v1, queue rwb-decision in namespace rwb-recovery and package th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision are the names of this service, and that the public base belongs to the edge
```

These eight criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only; they restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P7-E2014-APP. The ten legacy criteria of RWB-E2-014 are owned by RWB-P7-E2014-APP and are not copied here.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/decision/v1`; a public screen path is the edge's and carries no service segment and no `/v1` | DP-13; Architecture v5 slides 10 and 41 |
| BR2 | Event names are `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1` on the topic `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, and the decision record leaves on `rwb.decision-record.v1` | DP-03, DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR3 | Every event carries the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, is keyed by caseId, is written to the outbox in the same transaction as its state change and carries no personal data | Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43 notes; DP-09 |
| BR4 | A read declares no Idempotency-Key; a POST declares it and stores its answer | Architecture v5 slide 11; DP-09 |
| BR5 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition, and the owner's identifier and detail pass through the route unchanged | Architecture v5 slides 10 and 11 |
| BR6 | A schema change is additive within a major version; a breaking change is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes |
| BR7 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-decision as provided; a consumed operation is described as consumed, never as provided | Ownership Map v1 |
| BR8 | The notice summary carries identifiers, codes and dates only: no notice body, no addressee, no account number and no merge value | RWB-P6-E1052-CON BR8; NFR-040; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR9 | Every field of the screen model declares a mask flag, and the mask is applied by the route with the policy of rwb-access; no raw personal value crosses the edge | Architecture v5 slide 35; DP-19 |
| BR10 | The screen state values and the approval status values are reference data or route baseline, never constants written in code | TSD P7 v2 T3.2; DP-07 |
| BR11 | The decision record is published by the local library on the shared topic and is never a new event of this service | DP-03; Architecture v5 slide 20 |
| BR12 | No workflow, no Schedule and no job element is declared by this baseline | DP-10; Architecture v5 slides 14 and 44 |
| BR13 | No business value is fixed in the contract: age limits, override reasons, template codes, route role codes, page sizes and timeouts stay data or service configuration | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The route, the two panels, the field list, the five operations, the states and the error mapping are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | RWB-P7-E2014-APP, RWB-P7-E2014-OPS, RWB-P7-E2013-APP, the notice owner and the route owner accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A field or an optional element is added within major version 1 | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A field, a state value or a path is removed, renamed or retyped | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | Retired element reappears | The absence test of AC8 fails | In review |

The screen state machine itself — READY, STALE_INPUT and DECIDED, and the panel states GENERATED, APPROVED and HELD — is declared by AC4 and is written by RWB-P7-E2014-APP and the route, not by this baseline.

##### 10. Authority

The letters below are taken from the rwb-decision right of TSD P7 v2 T6.1, from Appendix T-A of the same specification and from the legacy authority table, and from no other table.

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-decision | Owns the OpenAPI fragment, the fakes and the baseline tag |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version and the correction of an Ownership Map row |
| Platform route owner | Owns the public base, the session, the masking engine and the budget the fragment reuses; reviews the route and the mask flags |
| Notice owner (rwb-comms) | Reviews the notice summary and confirms that no body, addressee or merge value is carried |
| Source-data owner (rwb-source-data) | Reviews the account and contact fields and their mask flags |
| Case owner (rwb-case) | Reviews the case number field and the case-owner task row |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Approves, changes or refuses D7.1 notices they did not prepare: the role the baseline names on the five operations |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel | Holds the template approval the notice summary depends on, and decides D7.1 notices they did not prepare |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Receives the refused notice task; reads the screen of the case with Litigation R |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field is declared in the summary, the events or the examples |

The per-service login behind the operations is not part of this baseline; the document names the scheme "the rwb-decision login (DP-02)". The authorisation decision is enforced at the route and at the service under RWB-PLT-N001-CON and RWB-P4-E1037-CON and is not redeclared here.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Decision panel model | approvalId, caseId, caseNo, decisionCode, approvalStatus, routeRoleCode, dueAt, escalationLevel, preparedBy, productGroup, ruleId, ruleVersion, noticeId, noticeType, noticeState, templateId, templateVersion, documentId, inputFacts, postalAddress; the exact type and order of each field beyond the names of the legacy screen are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1266; ASM-2230) |
| Notice approval panel model | noticeId, noticeState, noticeType, templateId, templateVersion, documentId, generatedAt and the input facts the notice was built from; no body and no addressee |
| inputFacts element | inputCode, businessDate, ageDays, limitDays and stale, one element per input; the input codes are the two the parameters name, TOTAL_BALANCE and POSTAL_ADDRESS, and no other code is declared |
| Mask flags | NONE, PARTIAL and FULL with a policy key per field; the flag of every field is declared, the policy text is the route's |
| Event payload | The decision record's elements only, with identifiers, codes and dates |
| Error body | The status, the message identifier and the detail of the platform envelope; no case fact |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

The public route is the platform's; the five operations are rwb-decision's. Base `/api/recovery/decision/v1` for the operations and `/api/recovery` for the public route.

| ID | Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Route of the approval screen | GET | `/api/recovery/approvals/{approvalId}` | Composed answer with the two panels, the screen model and the states of AC4; errors 401, 403, 404, 503 | Session cookie; coarse permission at the edge; owner PLT |
| API-P7-002 | GET | `/approvals` | Query decision, product, page, size; answer a page of approvals with the total count; errors 401, 403, 503 | Decision log, right A, scope applied; no `Idempotency-Key` |
| API-P7-008 | GET | `/approvals/{approvalId}` | No body; answer the approval with its routing details; errors 401, 403, 404, 503 | Decision log, right A, scope applied; no `Idempotency-Key` |
| API-P7-003 | POST | `/approvals/{approvalId}/approve` | Body ApprovalAction; answer the decision log entry; errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 | Decision log, right A, scope applied; `Idempotency-Key` required |
| API-P7-004 | POST | `/approvals/{approvalId}/return` | Body ApprovalAction; answer the approval; errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 | Decision log, right A, scope applied; `Idempotency-Key` required |
| API-P7-005 | POST | `/approvals/{approvalId}/refuse` | Body ApprovalAction; answer the decision log entry; errors 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 | Decision log, right A, scope applied; `Idempotency-Key` required |

The public route is `GET /api/recovery/approvals/{approvalId}` as the working read of AC1, and its exact path segment is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1259; ASM-2223). The field-level types and the order of the model are Not specified either (GAP-1266; ASM-2230); the baseline carries the working read and is corrected by a new version when the register closes the point.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|
| GET `/api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}` | P6 rwb-comms, RWB-P6-E1052-CON | The notice summary of 12.1 and AC5 |
| POST `/api/recovery/decision/v1/approvals/{approvalId}/approve`, `/return`, `/refuse` | P7 rwb-decision | The three decisions of the decision panel; the baseline fixes their bodies and answers |
| GET `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/{productCode}/records` | P1 rwb-source-data, DP-05 | The total balance and the postal contact value with `data_as_of`; no C row for this contract exists in this key (GAP-1266; ASM-2230) |
| GET `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data, DP-05 | The business date behind `inputFacts`; with the same gap (GAP-1266; ASM-2230) |
| GET `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case number of the screen header, read at the route; no C row for this contract exists in this key (GAP-1266; ASM-2230) |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (AC7, DP-11, ADR-020). The baseline fixes no field name inside the owner answers beyond the elements listed in 12.1 and AC5.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Schema element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (event 08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | decision code D7.1, rule ID and version, template code and version, approver identifier, final call, inputs reference, decided at, record reference; key caseId; written to the outbox in the same transaction as the approval and the entry; published by the local decision-record library (DP-03) |

This baseline declares the envelope because the screen depends on it; the decision record is written by RWB-P7-E2014-APP through the library. `ApprovalRequested` (event 09) is published by RWB-P7-E2013-APP on routing and is not declared as an output of this screen. `ApprovalDecided` is named on the slide 14 contract line and has no row in the event catalogue of slides 42 and 43, so no envelope is declared for it here.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The routing listener of `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1` is RWB-P7-E2013-APP's, and the screen reads the current state of the approval and the notice on the two reads of 12.2.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None in this baseline. `ApprovalWorkflow` of the workflow kit is started by RWB-P7-E2013-APP and is signalled by RWB-P7-E2014-APP; the baseline declares no workflow element, no activity name and no timer, and its contract is fixed in RWB-P7-E2013-CON (DP-10).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The two Schedules of the service — the rule promote at 00:01 (JOB-20) and the hash-chain check at 02:00 (JOB-14) — belong to the rule registry story and the decision log store story, and this baseline declares no Schedule and reads no shared scheduler table (DP-10).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. This baseline owns no table: it declares the shapes of the screen and fixes the two the app story writes. `approval` and `decision_log_entry` are P7 rows in `rwb_decision` and are written by RWB-P7-E2013-APP and RWB-P7-E2014-APP; `notice`, `template` and `merge_field` are P6 rwb-comms'; `delegation_limit` is P4 rwb-access'; `parameter_catalog`, `reference_row` and `lov_value` are P3 rwb-case'; `recovery_case`, `task` and `timer` are P3 rwb-case'. None of them is declared as owned here and none is read directly (DP-01).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The additive change to the gateway-bff route document for one screen, the OpenAPI fragment of the five rwb-decision operations, the decision panel and notice approval panel components with their field list and mask flags, the contract README rows for the state values, the parameter shapes, the error mapping and the mask rule, the four WireMock mapping sets, and the drift and absence tests.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_decision`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-19 is the pattern this baseline exists for: the screen is the route, the route is the platform's, and the five operations and the notice summary behind it are the owners'. No pattern is claimed for DP-02, DP-04, DP-08, DP-12, DP-14, DP-15, DP-16, DP-17, DP-18 or DP-20: this baseline declares no login, no rule package, no authorise call, no case workflow, no renamed topic, no migration, no integration adapter, no lake extract, no ledger entry and no agent client.

**Build steps**

1. Write the route and the two panels with the field list of AC1, and the lint rule that the field list, the route table and the fake agree.
2. Add the mask flag of every field and the example scan of AC2; a field without a flag fails the build.
3. Declare the five operations with their bodies, answers, rights, `Idempotency-Key` and error statuses; test the enumeration of AC3.
4. Fix the screen states and the mapping of AC4, and the parameter shapes of AC6 with the 422 path.
5. Fix the notice summary of AC5 and add the scan that fails on a body, an addressee, an account number or a merge value.
6. Write the error mapping of AC7 as one row per condition with its message ID, and assert the pass-through of the owner's identifier and detail.
7. Publish the four fakes and the drift test of AC8; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build.
8. Add the absence test: no monolith base, no data-lake extract and no topic other than `rwb.decision.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`.
9. Baseline tag and the consumer sign-off note, including the app and deployment stories of this key, the routing story, the notice owner and the route owner.

**Done when.** The documents validate in the pipeline, the eight contract tests pass, the four fakes answer every consumed path and every example, the drift and absence tests are green, no personal value appears in an example or a payload, and the app and deployment stories of this legacy key have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-002 | The preparer opens or acts on the item | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-P7-006 | An input is past its age limit | {input} is {days} days old, past its limit. Refresh it before you decide. |
| MSG-P6-003 | The template was withdrawn and the notice is held | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-P7-005 | Change of variant without a coded reason | Enter the reason you are not following the recommendation. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field or query parameter is missing or invalid | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Another approver decided first | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-004 | Approved | Approved. The case moves to {state}. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The approval is not on the case, or the case is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P4-001 | No Workbench role on the token | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A consumed call does not answer in time | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

MSG-P7-002, MSG-P7-006, MSG-P6-003, MSG-P7-005, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-004, MSG-P7-004 and MSG-P7-003 are copied from RWB-E2-014 section 14 unchanged; MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003, MSG-P4-001 and MSG-GEN-006 are the platform message catalog's. The message IDs are contract elements and their text is the agreed text; the edge's own problem titles and details are the platform route's and are not fixed here.

##### 15. Screens and states

The baseline serves the pair SCR-11 Decision screen and SCR-18 Notice approval, reached from SCR-10 Approval queue:

| Screen | What it reads from this contract | State |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-10 Approval queue | The page of approvals of API-P7-002 with the decision, product and page parameters | The route's loading and loaded states |
| SCR-11 Decision screen | The decision panel of the route: the approval, the case number, the product group, the rule and its version, the preparer, the due time and the input facts with their ages | READY, STALE_INPUT, DECIDED |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | The notice approval panel: the notice, its type, its template code and version, its state and its document reference | GENERATED, APPROVED, HELD |

The field-level masking, the session states and the temporarily-unavailable state of the route belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and are declared as the route's in AC4; this baseline fixes the flags and the panel fields and nothing else. The route name, its path segment and the field list beyond the legacy screen are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1259; ASM-2223).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: age limits, override reasons, template codes, route role codes, product groups, page sizes and timeouts stay data, reference data or service configuration.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, codes, dates and a document reference only; no name, no address, no account number and no notice body.
- Every field of the screen model declares a mask flag, and the mask itself is the route's with the policy of rwb-access; no raw personal value crosses the edge.
- The contract names only operations owned by rwb-decision as provided and only the one public route as the edge's; every other operation is consumed and faked (DP-01, DP-07).
- One base, one topic and one queue for the service, and the public base without a service segment for the edge; a document that mixes the two fails the review (DP-13, DP-19).
- ACE data is reached only through the owner's contract; this document declares no ACE view and no cross-schema join.
- The decision record is a local record on the shared topic and never a new event of this service (DP-03).
- No retired element is reintroduced: the absence test fails a build that declares a monolith base, a data-lake extract or a third topic.
- Every example is synthetic; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-014 for rwb-decision, reworked onto the approval table and the decision-record library, with the notice served by rwb-comms and the screens served through the gateway-bff composite route. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **one screen in rwb-decision that shows the demand or recall notice generated by rwb-comms, the case facts it was built from with the business date of each, and the rule and the template version that proposed it, with approve, change or reject and a reason**, so that **the first decision in the Workbench runs with a person approving inside the service that owns approvals, and only an approved notice reaches the 16:00 dispatch run**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A demand fee notice sent to a customer incomplete is a Bank of Thailand finding, and a wrong amount or address on a notice can void the notice period and delay litigation. The legacy story checked notices on paper, in one monolith, where the notice, the case, the ACE balance and the approval could be read in one transaction and where nothing had to be agreed between owners. In the target that transaction does not exist: rwb-decision owns the approval and the central decision ledger in `rwb_decision`, rwb-comms owns the notice and its template version in `rwb_comms`, rwb-case owns the case and its routing, rwb-source-data owns the ACE account and contact facts, and gateway-bff composes the screen from the owners one hop each (Architecture v5 slides 14, 17, 20 and 41; TSD P7 v2 T1 and T5.2).

This story is the rwb-decision app slice of legacy RWB-E2-014 and it owns the ten legacy criteria that the service itself can satisfy, on the approval screen that the legacy story calls SCR-11 with the SCR-18 notice approval panel, reached through SCR-10. The notice is never read as a table: it arrives on the rwb-comms contract of RWB-P6-E1052-CON, and the template code and version on the same answer, so the screen can show the rule and the template that produced the notice without a cross-schema join (DP-01, DP-11). The two ACE facts the screen shows with their business date — the total balance and the postal address — arrive through rwb-source-data (DP-05). The screen model itself is composed at the edge under RWB-PLT-N001-CON, so the field list, the mask flags and the timeout budget of the route are the platform's and are fixed for this screen in RWB-P7-E2014-CON (DP-19).

The approval outcome is the part that has to be right: the outcome, the rule version, the template version, the approver and the business date of every input leave the service as one local decision record through the decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and are also written into `approval` and `decision_log_entry` in `rwb_decision` (DP-03). A decision that cannot be recorded does not take effect, which is principle 5 and R-UNI-39, and the notice stays Generated. Age limits, override reasons, templates, variants and role codes stay data rows read through the parameters and reference-data contracts (DP-06, DP-07), so the same screen carries a D7.1 notice of any product without a release.

It serves REQ-APD-002 (the approver sees the recommendation, the reasons, the inputs and the limit that applies on one screen) and REQ-APD-006 (demand and recall notices are approved through approval routing), and supports controls CTL-05 (the preparer cannot decide) and CTL-14 (only an approved notice is dispatched). The measure is notices sent with an approval entry: target 100 percent.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P7-E2013-APP is done: the approval of a D7.1 notice is routed to role RW-LITOFF with a 1 working day service level, escalates to RW-HEADLIT, the `approval` row carries `source_type` NOTICE, `source_ref` the notice ID, the rule and its version, and `ApprovalWorkflow` of the workflow kit is live on task queue `rwb-decision`.
- RWB-P7-E2014-CON is published: the composite route of the screen, its panels, its field list, its mask flags, the P7 operations the screen consumes, the notice summary shape, the screen state values and the fakes, so this story builds against a fixed contract on Day 1.
- The `rwb_decision` baseline is in place: `approval`, `decision_log_entry` and the library objects `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` exist, and the per-service Flyway sequence runs in `rwb_decision`.
- The decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` are live with RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (DP-03); the outbox and inbox library is live with RWB-PLT-TE006-CON (DP-09); the Temporal workflow kit and the namespace `rwb-recovery` are live with RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (DP-10).
- The rwb-comms notice contract is live (RWB-P6-E1052-CON, DP-11): notice "N-0201" is readable with its notice type, template code, template version, state and document ID, and the three NoticeApi operations the legacy story calls — approve, regenerate and hold — have an owner path on that contract or its successor (GAP-1264; ASM-2228).
- The parameters are data rows read through the parameters contract (RWB-P3-E1042-CON, DP-06): `rwb.decision.input-age-days.TOTAL_BALANCE` = 1 and `rwb.decision.input-age-days.POSTAL_ADDRESS` = 30, owner RW-COE, DL22.
- The reference data is data rows read through the reference-data contract (RWB-P3-E1043-CON, DP-07): LOV-OVERRIDE-REASON holds TEMPLATE_VARIANT and WRONG_PARTY, LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS holds WAITING, HELD_NO_LIMIT, APPROVED, REFUSED and RETURNED, LOV-PRODUCT holds MORTGAGE, HIRE_PURCHASE, SSME and UNSECURED, owner RW-COE.
- The templates DEMAND-MTG, DEMAND-MTG-B (a second Approved variant of the demand notice for Mortgage) and RECALL-MTG are Approved in language TH in rwb-comms, with the Legal approval that RWB-P6-E1046-APP owns.
- The ACE account and contact facts reach the service through the rwb-source-data data-product contract with `data_as_of` and without a `v_ace_*` read of this service: only rwb-source-data reads the ACE views (ADR-010; Architecture v5 slide 45). The data-product contract carries no C row in this key (GAP-1265; ASM-2229).
- The case number at the screen header and the case-owner task of a refusal are rwb-case facts, consumed on the rwb-case contract and faked; that contract carries no C row in this key either (GAP-1265; ASM-2229).
- The fakes of the screen are available from the first run: the rwb-comms notice fake of RWB-P6-E1052-CON, the rwb-source-data account and freshness fake, the rwb-case case-read fake behind the composite route and the route fake of RWB-PLT-N001-CON.
- Test users in SIT hold RW-LITOFF; one holds RW-LEGAL; one holds RW-CASEOWN.
- No build dependency outside rwb-decision and the platform contracts: the H rows are the contract baselines, the platform contracts and the routing app story; the C rows never block the build (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-comms generates the notice under R-LIT-03 from the current Approved template and raises `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1`. RWB-P7-E2013-APP consumes it, routes decision D7.1 to role RW-LITOFF and starts `ApprovalWorkflow`; this story does not route.
2. A litigation officer opens SCR-10 Approval queue through the gateway-bff composite route; the queue reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/approvals` with `decision` D7.1, the product filter and the page parameters of the contract.
3. The officer selects the D7.1 item; the route composes `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/approvals/{approvalId}` with the rwb-comms notice read and the rwb-case case read, one hop each, and serves SCR-11 with the SCR-18 notice approval panel.
4. The screen shows the notice as a document reference with the notice type, the template code and version, the rule ID and version, the preparer, the case number and product group, the total balance with its business date, the addressee role and the postal address masked by the route's mask flags (DP-19).
5. `InputFreshnessCheck` compares the business date of each input with its age limit parameter and reads the template's current status from the notice answer; the screen state becomes READY, STALE_INPUT or the panel state HELD.
6. The officer approves; or picks another Approved template variant of the same notice type and product, enters a coded reason and approves; or refuses with a reason.
7. For a change, the service calls the notice regenerate operation of the rwb-comms contract with the chosen template code; the new notice version replaces the proposed one on the approval and only that version is approved (GAP-1264; ASM-2228).
8. The service checks the decision rules that RWB-P7-E2013-APP fixed — the caller holds Litigation right A, the caller is not the preparer, the reason rules of section 8 — and refuses with the message of section 14 when one fails.
9. The service writes the decision record through the local decision-record library in the same transaction as the approval status, the terms and `decision_log_id`: inputs reference with each input's business date, rule and version, template code and version, approver, final call and decided at. The library relays it on `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the outbox (DP-03, DP-09).
10. On approval the service calls the notice approve operation of the rwb-comms contract so the notice state becomes Approved for the 16:00 dispatch run (JOB-10, RWB-P6-E2021-APP); on refusal it calls the hold operation with reason REFUSED_BY_APPROVER and asks rwb-case for a task in the case owner's queue with the reason.
11. The service signals `ApprovalWorkflow` with the outcome so the escalation timer stops, shows MSG-P7-004 and sets the screen state DECIDED.
12. A decision whose record cannot be written leaves the approval WAITING and the notice Generated, answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 and raises an incident under R-UNI-39.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The approver prepared the notice | Approve and refuse are not offered; a direct call is refused with 409 | MSG-P7-002 | AC4 |
| X2 | An input is past its age limit | Screen state STALE_INPUT; approve is refused until the input is refreshed | MSG-P7-006 | AC5 |
| X3 | The template was withdrawn after generation | The notice is held under R-LIT-04 and approve is refused | MSG-P6-003 | AC6 |
| X4 | Refusal without a reason | Refused with 422 | MSG-GEN-001 | AC7 |
| X5 | A change of variant without a coded reason | Refused with 422 | MSG-P7-005 | AC8 |
| X6 | Another approver decided the item first | Refused with 409; the screen reloads in state DECIDED | MSG-GEN-004 | AC9 |
| X7 | The decision record cannot be written | Nothing changes, the notice stays Generated, an incident is raised | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E2-014-12 |
| X8 | A composed read of the route exceeds its budget | The route answers 503 for that part and the screen marks it temporarily unavailable; no decision is offered on a stale panel | MSG-GEN-006 | AC10 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on the routing of RWB-P7-E2013-APP and its contract, on the screen contract RWB-P7-E2014-CON and on the published rwb-comms, rwb-source-data and rwb-case contracts and their fakes; dispatch is RWB-P6-E2021-APP |
| Negotiable | Age limits, override reasons, templates, variants and role codes are data rows; the story fixes the checks order, the state path and the record contents |
| Valuable | The first Workbench decision with a person approving, and no unapproved notice reaching dispatch |
| Estimable | One screen with two panels, five P7 operations, six consumed operations, one freshness check and one record path |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests, as the app slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Each criterion in section 7 runs as one automated test against the fakes, and the twelve cases of section 16 keep their legacy covers and data |

```

The ten criteria above are the legacy criteria of RWB-E2-014, copied line for line with the origin tag on each scenario and with one mock line added where a criterion names a fact of another owner: the notice, its template version and the three notice operations belong to rwb-comms (RWB-P6-E1052-CON), the total balance and the postal address belong to rwb-source-data, and the case number and the case-owner task belong to rwb-case. Every value of the legacy criteria is kept: the notice, the case, the template and rule versions, the preparer and the approver identifiers, the dates, the states, the two reason codes, the two message families, the limits and the two status codes. The notice PDF on AC10 is the document the notice answer references by `documentId`; the PDF body is not part of the notice summary the route may display, and the addressee role and the masked address are the route's fields and not elements of the notice answer. The paths in the criteria are the paths of the operations as the legacy story writes them; the base of this service is `/api/recovery/decision/v1` and the screen is served through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-13, DP-19).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Demand and recall notices are approved through approval routing before dispatch; only an Approved notice is dispatched | REQ-APD-006; CTL-14 |
| BR2 | The approver sees the notice, the inputs with their age, the rule and the template version on one screen | REQ-APD-002 |
| BR3 | The person who prepared the notice may not approve or refuse it | CTL-05; legacy BR3 |
| BR4 | An input past its age limit blocks the decision until the input is refreshed | VR-P7-023-3; MSG-P7-006; the parameters `rwb.decision.input-age-days.*` |
| BR5 | A notice is generated only from the current Approved template, and a withdrawn template holds the notice | R-LIT-03; R-LIT-04 |
| BR6 | A change of template variant needs a coded reason and uses only an Approved variant of the same notice type and product | R-UNI-14; CTL-07; LOV-OVERRIDE-REASON |
| BR7 | A refusal needs a reason and returns the case to the case owner's queue | legacy BR7; R-LIT-04 |
| BR8 | A decision that cannot be written to the decision log does not take effect | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR9 | The approval, the inputs reference and the decision entry are `rwb_decision` rows; the notice, the template, the case, the ACE balance and the address are reached on their owners' contracts and never by a table read or a cross-schema join (DP-01, DP-05, DP-11) | Architecture v5 slides 14, 17 and 41; DP-01 |
| BR10 | The decision outcome leaves the service as one local decision record written through the decision-record library and relayed on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, never as a new event of this service (DP-03) | Architecture v5 slides 20 and 42 notes; DP-03 |
| BR11 | The age limits, the override reasons, the approval status values, the product groups, the route role codes and the template variants are parameters and reference data read with the version in force; no such value is written in code (DP-06, DP-07) | TSD P7 v2 T3.2; FSD P7 A2.22 BR-P7-022 |
| BR12 | The screen is served through the gateway-bff composite route; the field list, the mask flags and the timeout budget are the route's and are fixed in RWB-P7-E2014-CON, and the service returns identifiers, codes and dates that the route masks (DP-19) | Architecture v5 slide 20; DP-19 |
| BR13 | Every cross-service call is one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker per downstream; a missing answer never approves a notice and never shows a stale fact as current (DP-11) | ADR-020; DP-11 |
| BR14 | The escalation of an unanswered D7.1 approval runs as a durable timer in `ApprovalWorkflow`, not as a scheduled job of this story (DP-10) | Architecture v5 slides 14 and 44; DP-10 |
| BR15 | A D7.1 notice carries no amount limit and the DoA table is not consulted for it, while REQ-APD-002 asks for the limit that applies on the screen (GAP-1260; ASM-2224) | legacy section 10; Architecture v5 slide 41 (P4 DoA table) |
| BR16 | No event, log, workflow input or test carries a name, an address, an account number or a notice body; the screen carries a masked address and identifiers only | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; NFR-040 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| In progress | Recommendation routed for approval | The notice generated under R-LIT-03 and routed by RWB-P7-E2013-APP | Waiting approval |
| Waiting approval | Approver accepts, or changes and accepts | Not the preparer; the inputs inside their limits; the template current | In progress |
| Waiting approval | Approver refuses | A reason given | In progress, with a task in the case owner's queue |
| Waiting approval | The service level passes | No decision inside the 1 working day of R-LIT-03 | Escalated to RW-HEADLIT by the durable timer of `ApprovalWorkflow` |

The notice state, which is rwb-comms' and is moved by the two calls of this story, moves Generated to Approved on approval and Generated to Held on a refusal or a withdrawn template (R-LIT-04). The approval status column of `approval` follows LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS: WAITING on routing, APPROVED on approval, REFUSED on a refusal, RETURNED on the return operation of API-P7-004, which this screen does not offer. The screen state follows RWB-P7-E2014-CON: READY, STALE_INPUT and DECIDED for SCR-11, and GENERATED, APPROVED and HELD for the SCR-18 panel; the legacy names Ready, Stale input and Decided are kept as the labels of the three shell states.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Approves, changes or refuses D7.1 notices they did not prepare (Litigation A of the legacy authority table; right A of API-P7-003 and API-P7-005 as Appendix T-A declares it) |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel | Approves, changes or refuses D7.1 notices they did not prepare (Litigation A); holds the template approval the answer depends on |
| RW-HEADLIT, Head of Litigation | Receives the escalated D7.1 approval and decides it (Litigation A) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Receives the refused notice task; may not approve (Litigation R) |
| rwb-decision service identity | Reads and writes the `approval` and `decision_log_entry` rows of `rwb_decision` and writes the outbox rows (DP-02) |
| Decision-record library identity | Writes the local decision record of every outcome and relays it on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03) |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Reads the approval of a case through the published operations; takes no decision |
| Platform route owner | Owns the composite route, its field list, its mask flags and its budget; the service answers the route |

TSD P7 v2 T6.1 declares the decision log right of each role and Appendix T-A declares right A on API-P7-003, API-P7-004 and API-P7-005; the two are read together, and the legacy authority table names the same right Litigation A. The approval level row of the legacy story is kept: a D7.1 notice carries no amount limit and delegation item 2.1.3 (delay of legal action) does not apply to issuing a notice, while the DoA table itself is P4 rwb-access' and is read through its contract by RWB-P7-E2013-APP and not here (GAP-1260; ASM-2224).

| DF-DEC-053 | approval | decision_log_id | Write |

No table is created by this story: the `approval` row is created and routed by RWB-P7-E2013-APP, and the entry is written by the decision-record library into `rwb_decision`. The write of the outcome is one transaction over `approval` (`status`, `terms`, `decision_log_id`), the entry and the outbox row, so a decision that fails to record changes nothing (BR8). No column of this service carries a name, an address, an identity number or an account number; the address is a masked value produced by the route and the notice body stays in rwb-comms and rwb-document. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-decision (P7); base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`. The shapes are those fixed in RWB-P7-E2014-CON; this story implements them and adds no path.

| ID | Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-P7-002 | GET | `/approvals` | The D7.1 queue: the items waiting for the caller's approval level, filtered by decision and product, paged | Decision log, right A, scope applied | Not applicable |
| API-P7-008 | GET | `/approvals/{approvalId}` | One approval with its routing details for the decision screen | Decision log, right A, scope applied | Not applicable |
| API-P7-003 | POST | `/approvals/{approvalId}/approve` | Approve the notice within the caller's authority; answers the decision log entry | Decision log, right A, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` required |
| API-P7-004 | POST | `/approvals/{approvalId}/return` | Return the item to the preparer with a reason; answers the approval | Decision log, right A, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` required |
| API-P7-005 | POST | `/approvals/{approvalId}/refuse` | Refuse the notice with a reason; answers the decision log entry | Decision log, right A, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` required |

The request body of the three decisions is `ApprovalAction` with `reason`, `reasonCode` and `changes.templateCode` for a change of variant, as the legacy contract fixes it. Errors: 401 no session; 403 the role lacks the right (MSG-P4-002); 404 the approval is absent or out of the caller's scope (MSG-P4-003); 409 the preparer (MSG-P7-002), a stale input (MSG-P7-006), a withdrawn template (MSG-P6-003) or a decision already taken (MSG-GEN-004); 422 a missing reason (MSG-GEN-001), a change without a coded reason (MSG-P7-005) or a missing `Idempotency-Key` (MSG-GEN-001); 503 the record was not written (MSG-P7-003) or a consumed call exceeded its budget (MSG-GEN-006). The page size default and maximum of API-P7-002 are fixed in RWB-P7-E2014-CON and are shown on the queue screen as they are declared there.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| GET `/api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}` | P6 rwb-comms, RWB-P6-E1052-CON | The notice summary: notice type, template code and version, state, document ID and case ID; the PDF is the document the summary references, not a value of this service |
| POST `/api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}/approve` | P6 rwb-comms | Moves the notice Generated to Approved on approval, with the decision entry reference. The operation is the `NoticeApi.approve` of the legacy story and is Not specified in the source documents as an operation of the Ownership Map (GAP-1264; ASM-2228) |
| POST `/api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}/regenerate` | P6 rwb-comms | Produces the new notice version from another Approved variant on a change: the `NoticeApi.regenerate` of the legacy story, with the same gap (GAP-1264; ASM-2228) |
| POST `/api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}/hold` | P6 rwb-comms | Moves the notice Generated to Held with REFUSED_BY_APPROVER on a refusal: the `NoticeApi.hold` of the legacy story, with the same gap (GAP-1264; ASM-2228) |
| GET `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/{productCode}/records` | P1 rwb-source-data, DP-05 | The total balance and the postal contact value with `data_as_of`; no C row for this contract exists in this key (GAP-1265; ASM-2229) |
| GET `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` | P1 rwb-source-data, DP-05 | The business date of the balance product, read for the age check of AC5; with the same gap (GAP-1265; ASM-2229) |
| POST the case-owner task of the rwb-case contract, on the case of the approval | P3 rwb-case | The task with the refusal reason, raised on API-P7-005; rwb-case owns the task, its queue and its SLA. The contract carries no C row in this key, and the raise path is not named as an operation of the Ownership Map (GAP-1265; ASM-2229) |
| GET `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | Read at the composite route for the case number of the screen header; this service carries `case_id` only and reads no case table, and the contract carries no C row in this key (GAP-1265; ASM-2229) |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (DP-11, ADR-020). No row reads a table and no row reads a `v_ace_*` view of this service: only rwb-source-data reads the ACE views (ADR-010).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (event 08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | caseId | decision code D7.1, rule "R-LIT-03" and its version, template code and version, approver, final call, inputs reference, decided at, record reference |

It is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the approval and the entry, and relayed with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope by the outbox relay of the platform (DP-03, DP-09). The approval itself produces no second event: the two `rwb.decision.events.v1` names the service owns are `ApprovalRequested` (event 09), published by RWB-P7-E2013-APP on routing, and `RulePackageInForce` (event 30), published by the rule registry story. `ApprovalDecided` is named on the Architecture v5 slide 14 contract line and has no row in the event catalogue of slides 42 and 43; it is therefore not published, and the decided outcome of this screen leaves as the decision record (GAP-1262; ASM-2226).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The listener that consumes `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1` and routes D7.1 to the litigation officer is RWB-P7-E2013-APP, and this story starts after the item is waiting. The story subscribes to no event of its own, and the two consumed event names of the legacy solution plan (EV-13 and EV-08) belong to the routing and to the reporting read model respectively.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| ApprovalWorkflow (workflow kit template) | Workflow, one run per routed approval, started by RWB-P7-E2013-APP | `rwb-decision` | Carries the D7.1 item, its due time and the escalation of the 1 working day service level on a durable timer; this story signals it with the outcome so the timer stops |
| recordDecision | Activity, in rwb-decision through the library | `rwb-decision` | Writes the local decision record and the outbox row; a failure fails the step and no state changes |
| applyNoticeOutcome | Activity, in rwb-decision | `rwb-decision` | Calls the approve, regenerate or hold operation of rwb-comms, in the order section 4 fixes, and returns the notice state |

The workflow input is the approval ID, the decision code, the due time and the route role code; it carries no notice body, no addressee and no personal data.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The two Schedules of the service — the rule promote at 00:01 (JOB-20) and the hash-chain check at 02:00 (JOB-14) — belong to the rule registry story and the decision log store story. The escalation of a D7.1 approval is a durable timer inside `ApprovalWorkflow` and not a Schedule (DP-10).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| approval | P7 (rwb_decision) | The approval of the D7.1 notice: status, terms and `decision_log_id` are written here; the row itself is created and routed by RWB-P7-E2013-APP |
| decision_log_entry | P7 (rwb_decision) | The entry of every outcome, written through the decision-record library |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_decision` | The decision record, the inbox of the routing and the stored `Idempotency-Key` answer of the three decisions (DP-09) |

Not owned and never read: `notice`, `template` and `merge_field` (P6 rwb-comms), `delegation_limit` (P4 rwb-access), `parameter_catalog` and `reference_row` (P3 rwb-case), `recovery_case`, `task` and `timer` (P3 rwb-case), `document` (P5 rwb-document). Each is reached through its owner's contract or, for the case number, at the composite route (DP-01).

| Fake | Serves | Documented answers used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-comms notice fake (RWB-P6-E1052-CON) | The notice read, approve, regenerate and hold | Notice `N-0201` for case `RW-2026-000123` from `DEMAND-MTG` TH version 2 in state Generated, and the same notice Approved after AC1; the variant `DEMAND-MTG-B` for AC2; the withdrawn version 2 of AC6; a refused approve for AC5; a delayed answer beyond 2 s |
| rwb-source-data account and freshness fake | The balance, the contact value and the business date | Total balance with `data_as_of` 2026-12-13 for the background; `data_as_of` 2026-12-11 for AC5; the postal address of the case, masked; a delayed answer beyond 2 s |
| rwb-case fake at the route | The case number and the case-owner task | Case `RW-2026-000123` with product group MORTGAGE; the task raise of AC3 answered; a delayed answer beyond 2 s |
| Decision-record library fake | The local record and the shared topic | A healthy chain and outbox; a stopped library for TC-E2-014-12 |
| gateway-bff route fake (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) | The composite route of the screen | The two panels and the field list of RWB-P7-E2014-CON, with the 401, 403, 404 and 503 examples |

The fakes are derived from the published contracts of RWB-P6-E1052-CON and RWB-P7-E2014-CON; the drift test of the contract story fails a build in which a fake and the document disagree.

| Call type | Count | Detail |

| REST | 5 provided, 8 consumed | API-P7-002 to API-P7-005 and API-P7-008 provided; the four rwb-comms calls, the two rwb-source-data reads, the rwb-case task raise and the route's case read consumed; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 1 published, 0 consumed | `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the library; no event of this story on `rwb.decision.events.v1` |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, module `approval`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision.approval`; front end `recovery/decision/approval` with the `DecisionScreen` shell (SCR-11) and the `NoticeApprovalPanel` (SCR-18).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_decision`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 applies here as a prohibition with one exception of direction: this service reads no `v_ace_*` view, because only rwb-source-data reads the ACE views (ADR-010; Architecture v5 slide 45), and the balance and the contact value reach it on the owner's data-product contract with `data_as_of`. That contract carries no C row in this key, which is why the two rows of 12.2 carry their gap and their fake (GAP-1265; ASM-2229).

No pattern is claimed for DP-02 (the per-service login is created by the DB story), DP-04 (this story evaluates no rule package), DP-08 (the authorise call is the platform route's and is enforced at gateway-bff), DP-12 (no case workflow is composed here), DP-14 (no topic is renamed), DP-15 (the migration belongs to the DB story), DP-16 (no integration adapter is called), DP-17 (the data lake is removed and this screen reads nothing from it, while the module specification still carries the two daily lake interfaces, GAP-1261; ASM-2225), DP-18 (no interaction ledger entry is written by an approval) or DP-20 (no agent client is called).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ApprovalController | Controller | API-P7-002, API-P7-003, API-P7-004, API-P7-005 and API-P7-008 over the D7.1 item, the `Idempotency-Key` and the problem mapping of 12.1 |
| NoticeApprovalService | Service | Orders the checks, the variant change through the notice contract, the decision call and the notice outcome, in one transaction with the record |
| InputFreshnessCheck | Service | Compares each input's business date with its age limit parameter and returns the STALE_INPUT fact with the input name, its age and its limit |
| NoticeClient | Adapter | The notice read, approve, regenerate and hold operations of rwb-comms on the published contract |
| SourceDataClient | Adapter | The balance, the contact value and the business date of the account and contact products |
| CaseTaskClient | Adapter | The task raise in the case owner's queue on a refusal, on the rwb-case contract |
| DecisionRecorder | Service | Writes the local decision record and the outbox row through the library; a failure fails the decision |
| ApprovalWorkflowImpl | Workflow | The routed item, its due time and its escalation, signalled with the outcome |
| DecisionScreen, NoticeApprovalPanel | React components | The shell and the panel of the screen, fed by the composite route and showing the states of section 9 |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `approval` (`status`, `terms`, `decision_log_id`), the local decision record, `decision_log_entry` and the library objects, all in `rwb_decision`; reads no other schema.
- No table is created here: the `approval` baseline and its indexes are RWB-P7-E2013-APP's, and the migration of this story adds no column.
- No row of `notice`, `template` or `delegation_limit` is written or read here.

**Configuration and reference data**

- `rwb.decision.input-age-days.TOTAL_BALANCE` = 1 and `rwb.decision.input-age-days.POSTAL_ADDRESS` = 30, read through the parameters contract with the version in force (DP-06).
- LOV-OVERRIDE-REASON (TEMPLATE_VARIANT, WRONG_PARTY), LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS and LOV-PRODUCT read through the reference-data contract (DP-07).
- The templates and variants are rwb-comms' rows and are read on the notice answer; no template code is written in code.
- The feature switch `rwb.decision.notice-approval`, read as a parameter: off refuses the three decisions closed with MSG-P7-005 and leaves the items WAITING.

**Build steps**

1. ApprovalController and ApprovalService over the five operations, with the `Idempotency-Key` replay and the problem mapping; tests for AC7 and AC8.
2. NoticeClient and the notice summary mapping; test the read and the three operations against the rwb-comms fake.
3. SourceDataClient and InputFreshnessCheck with the two parameters; tests for AC5 and the boundary of 1 day and 3 days.
4. NoticeApprovalService for approve, change and refuse with the notice outcome in the same transaction as the record; tests for AC1, AC2, AC3 and AC6.
5. The preparer rule and the concurrent decision through the checks of RWB-P7-E2013-APP; tests for AC4 and AC9.
6. DecisionRecorder and the fail-closed path; test TC-E2-014-12.
7. DecisionScreen and NoticeApprovalPanel against the route fake, with the masked address and the states of section 9; test AC10.
8. The SIT run: generate, approve, and confirm the approved notice in the 16:00 file of RWB-P6-E2021-APP.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P7-E2014-CON stay green, and a SIT week shows every demand and recall notice approved by a person who did not prepare it, every decision with its rule version, template version, approver and input dates, and no notice in the dispatch file without an approval entry.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-002 | The preparer opens or acts on the item | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-P7-006 | An input is past its age limit | {input} is {days} days old, past its limit. Refresh it before you decide. |
| MSG-P6-003 | The template was withdrawn | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-P7-005 | Change of variant without a coded reason | Enter the reason you are not following the recommendation. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Refusal without a reason, or a missing `Idempotency-Key` | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Another approver decided first | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-004 | Approved | Approved. The case moves to {state}. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The approval is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A consumed call does not answer in time | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

MSG-P7-002, MSG-P7-006, MSG-P6-003, MSG-P7-005, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-004, MSG-P7-004 and MSG-P7-003 are copied unchanged from RWB-E2-014 section 14. MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 and MSG-GEN-006 are the platform message catalog's. Thai text for each message follows DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

The three screens are served through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19, RWB-PLT-N001-CON); the panel names, the field list, the mask flags and the timeout budget are fixed in RWB-P7-E2014-CON, and the field-level list is Not specified in the source documents beyond the legacy screens (GAP-1258; ASM-2222). The route name and its path segment are Not specified in the same way (GAP-1259; ASM-2223).

| Screen | State | What the user does |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-10 Approval queue | List | Selects a D7.1 item; the queue reads API-P7-002 with the decision, product and page parameters |
| SCR-11 Decision screen | Ready | Reads the notice and the facts; approves, changes the variant or refuses |
| SCR-11 Decision screen | Stale input | Sees MSG-P7-006 for the input; approve is disabled |
| SCR-11 Decision screen | Decided | Sees the outcome, the approver and the time; no action is offered |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Generated | The panel inside SCR-11 shows the notice waiting for a decision |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Approved | The notice shows as approved and waiting for the dispatch run |

The notice preview inside the panel is the document reference the notice answer carries, served by rwb-document at the route; the notice body, the addressee and the account number are never in the route's own payload, and only the masked address and the codes reach the browser. The route's own loading, temporarily unavailable and session expired states are the platform route's and are declared in RWB-P7-E2014-CON.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the age limits, the override reasons, the templates, the variants, the approval status values and the route role codes are parameters and reference data read with the version in force (DP-06, DP-07).
- No personal data in events, logs, workflow inputs, tests or prompts: notice IDs, case IDs, template codes, rule versions, user identifiers and dates only, and the address on screen is masked by the route.
- No read of another service's tables and no `v_ace_*` read of this service: the notice, the template, the case, the balance and the contact value arrive on their owners' contracts (DP-01, DP-05, DP-11).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the owner's views: only rwb-source-data reads the ACE views, and this service receives the facts it shows on the data-product contract with their business date.
- The approval, the entry and the outbox row commit in one transaction, and a decision that cannot be recorded does not take effect (BR8, R-UNI-39).
- One base, one topic sequence and one queue: `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, `rwb.decision.events.v1` with `rwb.decision.<Event>.v1` names, `rwb.decision-record.v1` for the record and `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (DP-13, DP-14).
- One hop and 2 s on every call; a timeout never approves a notice, never shows a stale fact as current and never returns an uncleared screen as ready (DP-11).
- No screen field, mask flag or route path is invented here: they are the platform route's and are fixed in RWB-P7-E2014-CON.
- Every example is synthetic; no production payload is copied into a test, a fake or a message.
