**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-014 for rwb-comms; the notice side of the D7.1 approval screen — the notice answer the screen reads, the template version and state it must show, and the approve, regenerate and hold moves the decision makes — reworked onto `rwb_comms`, the decision-record library and the gateway-bff composite route. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **the demand or recall notice held in rwb-comms to be readable with the template code, version and state that produced it, and to move to Approved, to a new version from another approved variant, or to Held, only when the D7.1 approval screen of rwb-decision says so**, so that **the 16:00 dispatch run takes only a notice a person approved, a withdrawn template can never be approved, and no notice ever moves without a record of the move**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A demand fee notice sent to a customer incomplete is a Bank of Thailand finding, and a wrong amount or address on a notice can void the notice period and delay litigation. The legacy story kept the notice, its template version, the case, the ACE facts and the approval in one monolith transaction, so the screen could read all of them and the notice could be approved in the same call. In the target that transaction does not exist: rwb-decision owns the approval and the central decision ledger in `rwb_decision`, rwb-comms owns the notice, its template version and the template state in `rwb_comms`, rwb-case owns the case and its routing, rwb-source-data owns the ACE balance and contact facts, and gateway-bff composes the screen one hop per owner (Architecture v5 slides 14, 17, 20 and 41; TSD P6 v2 T1 and T5.2; P6 context pack).

This story is the rwb-comms slice of legacy RWB-E2-014. It owns the notice side of the decision and nothing else: the notice answer the SCR-18 Notice approval panel shows (notice, case, document, notice type, state, and the template code, version and state), the four operations on the notice that the decision drives — the read, the approve, the regenerate from another approved variant and the hold — and the record of each move. The approval screen itself, the routing, the preparer rule, the input-age check and the decision entry are RWB-P7-E2014-APP's, which owns the ten legacy criteria; this story carries no legacy criterion of its own and its criteria in section 7 are new, testing only the four operations and the two state rules.

The decoupling is the one the target fixes: the notice and the template are `rwb_comms` rows (DP-01); the notice move is recorded through the local decision-record library and relayed on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03); the balance and the postal address that the panel shows are rwb-source-data's facts, read at the route and never from a `v_ace_*` view of this service (DP-05); the feature switch, the notice type list, the override reasons and the template state values are parameters and reference data read with the version in force (DP-06, DP-07); the record leaves through the outbox with the CloudEvents envelope (DP-09); the 16:00 run that consumes the approved state is RWB-P6-E2021-APP's Temporal Schedule and not a Quartz row of this story (DP-10); the three former in-process `NoticeApi` calls become REST operations with a mock, one hop and a 2 s budget (DP-11); the base is `/api/recovery/comms/v1` (DP-13); and the panel reaches the answer through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). It serves REQ-APD-002 (the approver sees the recommendation, the reasons and the inputs on one screen) and REQ-APD-006 (demand and recall notices are approved through approval routing), and supports CTL-05 (the preparer cannot decide) and CTL-14 (only an approved notice is dispatched) from the notice side. The measure is the FSD P6 one: notices with an approval entry before dispatch, target 100 percent.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P6-E1052-APP is done: the notice is generated from the current Approved template with `notice_type`, `template_id`, `party_id` and `document_id` set and state Generated, and `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1` (EV-13) is published on `rwb.comms.events.v1`.
- RWB-P6-E1046-APP is done: `template` and `merge_field` hold the versions, the Legal approval (`approved_by_legal`, `approved_by`, `approved_at`, `valid_from`) and the withdrawal, so the state of a template version is a row of this service and not a value of another.
- The `rwb_comms` baseline is in place and the per-service Flyway sequence runs in `rwb_comms` (DP-15); the library objects `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` exist (DP-09).
- RWB-P7-E2014-CON is published and is the contract this story builds against on Day 1: the composite route of SCR-11 with the SCR-18 panel, the notice summary shape it consumes, the three decision operations and their answers, the `Idempotency-Key`, and the fakes. The screen contract is a C row and never blocks the build (Template and Rules §R5.7).
- The local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` are live (DP-03), and the outbox relay of the platform carries the record of every notice move (DP-09).
- The parameters contract of rwb-case is live (RWB-P3-E1042-CON, DP-06) for the switch `rwb.decision.notice-approval` as the legacy story names it, and the reference-data contract is live (RWB-P3-E1043-CON, DP-07) for LOV-NOTICE, LOV-OVERRIDE-REASON, LOV-PRODUCT and the template state values DRAFT, APPROVED and WITHDRAWN of TSD P6 T-A.2.
- The templates DEMAND-MTG, DEMAND-MTG-B (a second Approved variant of the demand notice for Mortgage) and RECALL-MTG are Approved in language TH, with the Legal approval that RWB-P6-E1046-APP records.
- Notice "N-0201" for case "RW-2026-000123" exists in state Generated from template "DEMAND-MTG" "TH" version 2 under rule "R-LIT-03" version "LIT-2026.12", prepared by "U-9211", and its approval "A-0201" is WAITING for role RW-LITOFF in rwb-decision.
- Test users in SIT hold RW-LITOFF; one holds RW-LEGAL; one holds RW-CASEOWN. The SIT fixtures are synthetic and carry no name, no address and no account number.
- No build dependency: this story has no H row. The platform contracts the patterns name (DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-19) are held by the notice contract baseline RWB-P6-E1052-CON and reached through the published libraries, and the plan records none as a build row for this slice (GAP-2389; ASM-3965).

##### 4. Flow

1. A litigation officer opens SCR-10 Approval queue and selects the D7.1 item; the queue and the screen are composed by the gateway-bff composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON on the contract RWB-P7-E2014-CON (DP-19).
2. The route calls this story's read: `GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}` with the `noticeId` of the approval's `source_ref`. The answer carries the notice `id`, `caseId`, `documentId`, `noticeType`, `state`, and the `templateCode`, `templateVersion` and `templateState` of the template version that produced it.
3. The panel shows the notice as the document reference the answer carries, together with the notice type, the template code and version, the template state and the case; the notice body and the addressee are not part of the answer and are served by rwb-document and rwb-source-data at the route.
4. rwb-decision runs its checks — the caller holds Litigation right A, the caller is not the preparer, the reason rules, the input-age limits — and on a decision calls one of the three operations of this story with an `Idempotency-Key`. The approval answer and the `decisionLogEntryId` it passes are, with the notice ID, the whole input of this service (DP-11).
5. On approve: `POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve` with the decision entry reference moves the notice Generated to Approved, stores the reference and the approval time, and the notice becomes eligible for the 16:00 dispatch run of RWB-P6-E2021-APP (JOB-10). The answer is the notice in state Approved, 200.
6. On a change of variant: `POST /notices/{noticeId}/regenerate` with `templateCode` of the chosen variant produces the new notice version from that Approved variant of the same notice type and product group and writes it on the same notice; the approval then approves that version, and only the changed notice reaches the dispatch run. That the new version stays on the same notice row is a ruling of this story (GAP-2386; ASM-3962).
7. On a refusal: `POST /notices/{noticeId}/hold` with reason `REFUSED_BY_APPROVER` and the decision entry reference moves the notice Generated to Held with `hold_reason` set, and the notice is excluded from the dispatch run. A withdrawn template is held the same way with reason `TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN` under R-LIT-04, and an approve of such a notice is refused before any move.
8. Each move writes one local decision record through the library in the same transaction as the notice row: decision code D7.1, the rule in force (R-LIT-03 on approve, R-LIT-04 on a withdrawn template), the notice and case IDs, the template code and version, the approver and the reference of the approval entry, decided at. The library relays it on `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the outbox (DP-03, DP-09); that the move writes its own record next to the entry of the approval is a ruling of this story (GAP-2390; ASM-3966).
9. A move whose record cannot be written does not happen: the notice row is unchanged, the answer is 503 with MSG-P7-003, and an incident is raised under R-UNI-39.
10. A repeat of any of the three calls with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the first answer and moves nothing a second time; a call against a notice that is no longer in state Generated answers 409 with MSG-GEN-004.
11. The dispatch Schedule of RWB-P6-E2021-APP selects the notices in state Approved for the business date and runs the conduct check; this story reads nothing of that run and is not called by it.
12. Renewed approval is not offered: an approved notice that is later withdrawn is held by the dispatch story, never re-approved here.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The live template version of the notice is WITHDRAWN | The approve is refused with 409 and the notice stays Generated; the hold with TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN moves it to Held under R-LIT-04 | MSG-P6-003 | AC3 |
| X2 | The chosen variant is not Approved, or is of another notice type or product group | The regenerate is refused with 422 and no new notice version is produced | MSG-GEN-001 | AC4 |
| X3 | The notice is not in state Generated (already Approved or Held) | The call is refused with 409 and the state is unchanged | MSG-GEN-004 | AC7 |
| X4 | The caller does not hold the Litigation right of the operation | Refused with 403; nothing changes | MSG-P4-002 | AC8 |
| X5 | The notice is absent or outside the caller's scope | Refused with 404; nothing changes | MSG-P4-003 | AC8 |
| X6 | The local decision record cannot be written | The notice row is unchanged, the answer is 503 and an incident is raised | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X7 | A repeat with the same `Idempotency-Key` | The first answer is returned; no second move and no second record | None | AC2, AC5 |
| X8 | `templateCode` missing on regenerate, or `reasonCode` missing on hold | Refused with 422 naming the field | MSG-GEN-001 | AC4, AC5 |

| Independent | One service, four operations and one record path; builds against the published notice contract RWB-P6-E1052-CON, the P7 screen contract RWB-P7-E2014-CON and the platform libraries; nothing waits on another team |
| Negotiable | The feature switch, the notice type list, the override reasons and the template state values are data rows; the story fixes only the order of the checks and the state path |
| Valuable | The notice a person approved is the only notice dispatched, and a withdrawn template cannot be approved |
| Estimable | Four operations, two state rules, one migration column, one record path |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests, as the secondary slice of a legacy key that RWB-P7-E2014-APP leads |
| Testable | Each criterion in section 7 runs as one automated test against the contract fakes and the `rwb_comms` fixtures, and the twelve legacy cases of section 16 keep their IDs and their data |

The eight criteria are new under D-RCV-60 and test only the four operations of this story and its two state rules. No legacy criterion is copied here: the ten criteria of RWB-E2-014 belong to RWB-P7-E2014-APP, which owns the approval screen, and this story answers the notice half of each of them behind that contract's fake. The values the criteria use are copied unchanged from RWB-E2-014 and the P6 extracts — the notice "N-0201", case "RW-2026-000123", template "DEMAND-MTG" version 2, variant "DEMAND-MTG-B", rule "R-LIT-03" version "LIT-2026.12", preparer "U-9211", approver "U-9212", the 09:30 withdrawal, the 10:00 decision, the 16:00 run, the reason codes `REFUSED_BY_APPROVER`, `TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN` and `TEMPLATE_VARIANT`, and the messages MSG-P6-003, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-004, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 and MSG-P7-003 — and no business value is invented. The paths are relative to the base of this service, `/api/recovery/comms/v1` (DP-13).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Only a notice in state Approved is eligible for dispatch, and the notice reaches Approved only through the D7.1 approval | REQ-APD-006; CTL-14; legacy BR1 |
| BR2 | The notice answer carries the template code, the template version and the state of that version, so the approver sees what the notice was built from | REQ-APD-002; legacy BR2 |
| BR3 | The service does not decide who approves: the preparer rule, the right and the reason rules are checked by rwb-decision, and this service refuses a move only on its own notice state and template state | CTL-05; legacy BR3; DP-11 |
| BR4 | A notice whose template version is WITHDRAWN is never approved; it is held under R-LIT-04 | R-LIT-03; R-LIT-04; legacy BR5 |
| BR5 | A change of variant regenerates from an Approved variant of the same notice type and the same product group, and only that version is approved | R-UNI-14; CTL-07; LOV-OVERRIDE-REASON |
| BR6 | The notice state moves Generated to Approved, or Generated to Held with a reason code; no other transition is accepted and a second move is refused | legacy section 9; TSD P6 T3.0 |
| BR7 | A move that cannot be written to the decision record does not happen, and the notice stays Generated | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; legacy BR8 |
| BR8 | Every move is one transaction over the notice row, the local decision record and the outbox row, and each move is idempotent on the `Idempotency-Key` | ADR-015; DP-03; DP-09 |
| BR9 | The notice, its template reference and its hold reason are `rwb_comms` rows; the approval, the entry and the case are reached on their owners' contracts and never by a table read (DP-01, DP-11) | Architecture v5 slides 17 and 41; DP-01 |
| BR10 | The notice carries no name, no address and no account number; the panel's masked address and total balance are rwb-source-data facts read at the route (DP-05, DP-19) | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; ADR-010 |
| BR11 | The feature switch, the notice types, the product groups, the override reasons and the template state values are parameters and reference data read with the version in force; no such value is written in code | TSD P6 T3.2; FSD P6 A2.1 BR-P6-001; DP-06, DP-07 |
| BR12 | The move is recorded in the local decision record with the rule in force — R-LIT-03 on an approval, R-LIT-04 on a withdrawn template — and relayed on the shared topic, so the central ledger and the reporting read model follow without a call made for them | DP-03; DP-09; legacy section 12 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Generated | Approve operation with a decision entry reference | The live template version is APPROVED | Approved |
| Generated | Hold operation with reason `REFUSED_BY_APPROVER` | A reason code is given | Held |
| Generated | Hold operation with reason `TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN` | The live template version is WITHDRAWN (R-LIT-04) | Held |
| Generated | Regenerate operation with a template code | The variant is APPROVED, of the same notice type and product group | Generated, carrying the new template and a new document reference |
| Approved | Approve or hold operation | None: the notice has left Generated | Refused with 409, state unchanged |
| Held | Approve or hold or regenerate operation | None: the notice has left Generated | Refused with 409, state unchanged |

The template state that gates the first row is `template.state` and moves DRAFT to APPROVED on the approve operation of the template catalogue and APPROVED to WITHDRAWN on its withdraw operation, both of RWB-P6-E1046-APP; this story reads it and never writes it. Sent, Delivered and Unserved are the dispatch states of RWB-P6-E2021-APP and are not reached here: this story hands over an Approved notice and reads nothing of the run. A held notice stays held until its template is approved again and the notice is regenerated and approved anew, which is a new decision and not a re-approval of the old row.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Litigation CRUA in TSD P6 T6.1: reads the notice answer (right R) and, through the approval of rwb-decision, causes the approve, regenerate and hold moves (right A) |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel | Litigation RA in TSD P6 T6.1: reads the notice and holds the template approval that the approve gates on; its own approvals are checked by rwb-decision and not here |
| RW-HEADLIT, Head of Litigation | Litigation RA in TSD P6 T6.1: the escalated approval of rwb-decision reaches the same three moves |
| rwb-decision service identity | Calls the three decision operations with the approver's decision entry reference, one hop, under the right declared in 12.1 |
| rwb-comms service identity | Reads its own `notice` and `template` rows, writes the state, the `hold_reason` and the decision entry reference, and writes the outbox rows (DP-02) |
| Decision-record library identity | Writes the local decision record of every move and relays it on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03) |
| Platform route owner | Owns the composite route, the field list, the mask flags and the budget; this story answers the route |

The three decision operations are not declared in the appendix T-A of TSD P6, so their declared right is an assumption of this story (GAP-2388; ASM-3964); the matrix of TSD P6 T6.1 gives the Litigation rights of each role and is the only source used for the rows above. Authorisation is enforced at gateway-bff through the rwb-access contract, which is not in this key's pattern set, so no DP-08 row is claimed.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity in `rwb_comms` | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-LEG-015 | notice | id | Read (the key of every operation) |
| DF-LEG-016 | notice | case_id | Read in the answer |
| DF-LEG-017 | notice | document_id | Read in the answer; written on regenerate |
| DF-LEG-018 | notice | notice_type | Read in the answer; the check of the variant |
| DF-LEG-030 | notice | party_id | Read only, never in an event |
| DF-LEG-031 | notice | template_id | Read in the answer; written on regenerate |
| DF-LEG-032 | notice | hold_reason | Write on a hold |
| Standard column | notice | state | Write on every move, read in the answer |
| Standard column | notice | version, updated_at, updated_by | Write, for the optimistic lock of the move |
| No field ID | notice | decision_log_entry_id (added by this story) | Write on approve and hold (GAP-2385; ASM-3961) |
| DF-REF-045, DF-REF-046, DF-REF-047 | template | id, template_code, template_version | Read in the answer |
| DF-REF-049 | template | product_group | Read for the same-product rule of a change |
| DF-REF-051, DF-REF-065 | template | approved_by_legal, valid_from | Read, with `state`, for the approve gate |
| Standard column | template | state | Read: DRAFT, APPROVED or WITHDRAWN |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (local, through the library) | decision code, rule, notice, case, approver, decided at, hash chain | Write |

This story creates no table: `notice` and `template` are the baseline of RWB-P6-E1052-APP and RWB-P6-E1046-APP, and the only schema change is the nullable `decision_log_entry_id uuid` on `notice` with a unique index, in the per-service Flyway step `V2014_1__notice_decision_reference.sql` in `rwb_comms` (DP-15). The reference is nullable because a notice can be held by the dispatch story without an approval entry, and it is not the record itself: the record is the library's, in `rwb_comms`, and is mirrored to the central ledger on the shared topic. The status of the approval, its terms and its own `decision_log_id` are `rwb_decision` rows and are not read or written here. No column of this service holds a name, an address, an identity number or an account number; the masked address of the panel is produced at the route from the rwb-source-data answer. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

##### 12. Contract

Owner rwb-comms (P6); base `/api/recovery/comms/v1` (DP-13). Topic `rwb.comms.events.v1`, queue `rwb-comms`, schema `rwb_comms`. The shapes below are those fixed in RWB-P7-E2014-CON, which this story builds against, and in RWB-P6-E1052-CON, the notice contract baseline of this service.

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| ID | Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-P6-002 | GET | `/notices/{noticeId}` | Read a notice with its template code, version and state for the approval panel | Litigation, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| — | POST | `/notices/{noticeId}/approve` | Move the notice Generated to Approved with the decision entry reference; answers the notice | Litigation, right A, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` required |
| — | POST | `/notices/{noticeId}/regenerate` | Produce the notice version from another Approved variant of the same notice type and product group; answers the notice | Litigation, right A, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` required |
| — | POST | `/notices/{noticeId}/hold` | Move the notice Generated to Held with a reason code and the decision entry reference; answers the notice | Litigation, right A, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` required |

The three decision operations are the `NoticeApi.approve`, `NoticeApi.regenerate` and `NoticeApi.hold` of RWB-E2-014, which the legacy publishes only as Java methods and which neither the Ownership Map nor appendix T-A of TSD P6 lists as REST rows (GAP-2384; ASM-3960). Their declared right is an assumption in the same way (GAP-2388; ASM-3964). Requests: approve and hold carry `decisionLogEntryId` and, on hold, `reasonCode`; regenerate carries `templateCode`. Errors: 401 no session; 403 the role lacks the declared right (MSG-P4-002); 404 the notice is absent or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 409 the template version is withdrawn (MSG-P6-003), or the notice is no longer in state Generated (MSG-GEN-004); 422 a missing or barred `templateCode` or `reasonCode` (MSG-GEN-001); 503 the record was not written (MSG-P7-003). The property list of the notice answer is not given by T-A.2 and is baselined in RWB-P7-E2014-CON from TSD P6 T3.1 plus the template facts (GAP-2387; ASM-3963).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| The approval answer and the decision entry reference of RWB-P7-E2014-CON | P7 rwb-decision | The `decisionLogEntryId` and the approver of every move; this story never reads the approval table and never decides who approves (DP-11) |
| The parameters read of `rwb.decision.notice-approval`, on RWB-P3-E1042-CON | P3 rwb-case | The feature switch of the three operations, read with the version in force (DP-06, BR11) |
| The reference-data read of LOV-NOTICE, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-OVERRIDE-REASON and the template state values, on RWB-P3-E1043-CON | P3 rwb-case | The same-notice-type and same-product check of a change, the reason codes and the three template states (DP-07, BR11) |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11, ADR-020). No row reads a table and no row reads a `v_ace_*` view: only rwb-source-data reads the ACE views (ADR-010).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | caseId | decision code D7.1, rule (R-LIT-03 or R-LIT-04) and its version, notice ID, case ID, template code and version, notice state from and to, reason code where one applies, approver, decided at, reference of the approval entry |

It is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the notice row and relayed with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope by the outbox relay of the platform (DP-03, DP-09). This story publishes no event of its own topic: the three events of `rwb.comms.events.v1` are `NoticeGenerated` (EV-13), published by RWB-P6-E1052-APP when the notice is produced, and `NoticeDispatched` (EV-14) and `NoticeDelivered` (EV-15), published by RWB-P6-E2021-APP. The movement of a notice between Generated, Approved and Held is not one of the three and reaches its consumers through the decision record, which is what the legacy contract of RWB-E2-014 declares ("consumes EV-13 NoticeGenerated; publishes EV-08 DecisionRecorded").

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. EV-13 `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1` is published by the generation story of this same service, and the listener that consumes it to route D7.1 to the litigation officer is RWB-P7-E2013-APP; this story starts when the approval exists and is called on the decision. The two other subscriptions of the service (the deviation events and the case state event) belong to RWB-P6-E2021-APP.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The four operations are synchronous calls of one hop and 2 s; no workflow is started and no activity is added. `NoticeDispatchWorkflow` and the 16:00 Schedule of JOB-10 are RWB-P6-E2021-APP's, and this story only makes a notice eligible for that run by moving it to Approved (DP-10 as a boundary, not as work of this slice).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Quartz row and no Schedule is added. The 16:00 dispatch run that consumes the Approved state is the Schedule of RWB-P6-E2021-APP on task queue `rwb-comms` in the namespace `rwb-recovery` (DP-10).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| notice | P6 (rwb_comms) | The notice row: `state`, `hold_reason`, `template_id`, `document_id` and the added `decision_log_entry_id` are written here |
| template | P6 (rwb_comms) | The template version, its product group, its Legal approval and its `state`; read only here, written by RWB-P6-E1046-APP |
| decision record (local) | P6 rows in `rwb_comms`, written through the P7 library | The record of every notice move (DP-03) |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_comms` | The decision record, the stored `Idempotency-Key` answer of the three operations (DP-09) |

Not owned and never read: `approval` and `decision_log_entry` (P7 rwb-decision), `document` (P5 rwb-document), `recovery_case` (P3 rwb-case), `parameter_catalog` and `reference_row` (P3 rwb-case), `outbound_item` and `interface_config` (P2 rwb-integration). `merge_field` is P6's and is not touched by this story. No foreign key crosses a service boundary (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Documented answers used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-decision approval fake (RWB-P7-E2014-CON) | The approval answer and the `decisionLogEntryId` of the move | Approval `A-0201` for notice `N-0201` with entry `E-0201` and approver `U-9212`; the refused approval of AC5; a delayed answer beyond 2 s |
| rwb-comms notice and template fake (RWB-P6-E1052-CON) | The notice rows read by the four operations | Notice `N-0201` Generated from `DEMAND-MTG` TH version 2; `DEMAND-MTG-B` and `RECALL-MTG` Approved for MORTGAGE; `DEMAND-MTG` version 2 WITHDRAWN from 09:30 on 14 December 2026 for AC3 |
| Decision-record library fake | The local record and the shared topic | A healthy chain and outbox; a refusing library for AC6 |
| Parameters and reference-data fake | The switch and the lists | `rwb.decision.notice-approval` on and off; LOV-NOTICE, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-OVERRIDE-REASON and the three template states |

The fakes are derived from the published contracts of RWB-P7-E2014-CON and RWB-P6-E1052-CON, and the drift test of each contract story fails a build in which a fake and the document disagree.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 4 provided, 3 consumed | The notice read and the three decision operations provided; the approval answer, the parameters read and the reference-data read consumed; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 1 published, 0 consumed | `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the library; nothing of `rwb.comms.events.v1` |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, activity or Schedule; the dispatch run is RWB-P6-E2021-APP's |
| File | None | No file is read or written; the notice body is a document reference owned by rwb-document |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms`, module `notices`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms.notices`; the operations are an extension of the notice controller of RWB-P6-E1052-APP and add no new module.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_comms`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/comms/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 applies as a prohibition: this service reads no `v_ace_*` view and no ACE row, and the total balance and the postal address that the panel shows are rwb-source-data facts read at the route, so the notice answer carries identifiers and codes only. DP-10 applies as a boundary: the JOB-10 run is RWB-P6-E2021-APP's Temporal Schedule, and this story adds no job. No pattern is claimed for DP-02 (the per-service login is the DB story's), DP-04 (no rule package is evaluated here; the rule in force is read as an identifier of the approval), DP-08 (the authorise call is the platform route's), DP-12 (no case workflow is composed), DP-14 (no topic is renamed by this story), DP-15 (the migration is the baseline's plus one column), DP-16, DP-17 (the data lake is removed and nothing here reads it), DP-18 (no ledger entry is written by a notice move) or DP-20. The H rows the table names are met through the notice contract baseline RWB-P6-E1052-CON and the published libraries, and the plan carries none of them as a build row of this slice (GAP-2389; ASM-3965).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| NoticeController | Controller | `GET /notices/{noticeId}` and the three POST operations, with validation, the `Idempotency-Key` and the problem mapping of 12.1 |
| NoticeReadService | Service | Builds the notice answer with the template code, version and state, and applies the scope and the mask flags of the route |
| NoticeDecisionService | Service | Orders the checks — state Generated, template state, variant eligibility — and performs the move with its record in one transaction |
| VariantSelector | Service | Resolves the chosen template code to an Approved variant of the same notice type and product group, so a change never crosses a notice type |
| DecisionRecorder | Service | Writes the local decision record and the outbox row through the library; a failure fails the move |
| TemplateStateReader | Adapter | Reads `template.state`, the Legal approval and `valid_from` of the version that produced the notice, in `rwb_comms` |
| NoticeClient (for rwb-decision) | Adapter | The contract the approval screen consumes: the read and the three decision operations, one hop, 2 s |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `notice` (`state`, `hold_reason`, `template_id`, `document_id`, `decision_log_entry_id`), the local decision record and the library objects, all in `rwb_comms`; reads no other schema.
- One migration: `V2014_1__notice_decision_reference.sql` adds the nullable `decision_log_entry_id uuid` with a unique index and the reason-code check on `hold_reason`; no column carries a name, an address or an account number.
- No row of `template` or `merge_field` is written here, and no row of `approval` or `decision_log_entry` is read.

**Configuration and reference data**

- `rwb.decision.notice-approval`, the legacy switch name kept unchanged, read as a parameter through RWB-P3-E1042-CON (DP-06); off refuses the three operations closed with 503 MSG-P7-003 and leaves the notices as they are. The namespace of the switch for the comms half is not settled (GAP-2391; ASM-3967).
- LOV-NOTICE, LOV-PRODUCT and LOV-OVERRIDE-REASON read through RWB-P3-E1043-CON (DP-07); the template state values DRAFT, APPROVED and WITHDRAWN as TSD P6 T-A.2 uses them; the hold reason vocabulary is fixed by this story because no source holds it as a list (GAP-2391; ASM-3967).

**Build steps**

1. NoticeReadService and the answer mapping with the template facts; test AC1 against the fixture of `N-0201`.
2. NoticeDecisionService and the state gate: Generated only, 409 on any other state; tests for AC7.
3. The approve path with the decision entry reference, the record and the idempotent replay; tests for AC2 and AC5.
4. The template gate: WITHDRAWN refuses with MSG-P6-003 and the hold with TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN follows; test for AC3.
5. VariantSelector and the regenerate path with the same-type and same-product check, 422 on a barred or missing code; test for AC4.
6. DecisionRecorder and the fail-closed path; test AC6 and TC-E2-014-12.
7. The scope and right refusals at the operation, with the route's field list and mask flags; test AC8.
8. The SIT run with rwb-decision: approve, and confirm the approved notice in the 16:00 run of RWB-P6-E2021-APP, and that no held notice is in it.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P7-E2014-CON and RWB-P6-E1052-CON stay green, and a SIT week shows every demand and recall notice moved only through the three operations, every move with its decision record, no approved notice with a withdrawn template, and no notice in the dispatch run without an approval entry.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P6-003 | The template version of the notice is withdrawn | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The notice is no longer in state Generated | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is missing or barred | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the declared right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The notice is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

MSG-P6-003, MSG-GEN-004, MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-P7-003 are copied unchanged from RWB-E2-014 section 14; MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 are the platform catalog's. Thai text for each message follows DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

The SCR-18 Notice approval panel inside SCR-11 is served through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19, RWB-PLT-N001-CON); the panel names, the field list, the mask flags and the timeout budget are fixed in RWB-P7-E2014-CON. This story supplies the notice half of the panel answer and sets these states:

| Screen | State | What the user sees |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Generated | The notice, its template code and version and the template state while the decision is open; approve, change of variant and reject are offered by the route, not by this service |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Approved | The notice moved on the approval and waiting for the 16:00 dispatch run |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Held | The notice held with its reason code, and MSG-P6-003 when the reason is a withdrawn template |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Withdrawn template | MSG-P6-003 and no approve offered, because the approve is refused by this service as well as by the route |

The notice preview is the document reference the answer carries, served by rwb-document at the route; the notice body, the addressee and the account number are never in the answer, and the masked address of the panel is a rwb-source-data value read at the route. The route's own loading, temporarily unavailable and session-expired states are the platform route's and are declared in RWB-P7-E2014-CON.

No `-ITG` copy exists for this key in this story: the cross-service behaviour is proved inside the same SIT run through rwb-decision, and an ITG copy of a case, if one is added, takes the suffix `-ITG` on the ITG story and not here. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the switch, the notice types, the product groups, the override reasons, the template state values and the reason codes are parameters and reference data read with the version in force (DP-06, DP-07).
- No personal data in events, logs, tests or prompts: notice IDs, case IDs, document references, template codes and versions, reason codes and dates only. The notice body and the addressee stay in rwb-document and rwb-source-data, and the SIT fixtures are synthetic.
- No read of another service's tables and no `v_ace_*` read of this service: the approval, the case and the ACE facts arrive on their owners' contracts or at the route (DP-01, DP-05, DP-11).
- The notice row and its decision record commit in one transaction, so a move that cannot be recorded changes nothing (BR7, BR8).
- Any move is idempotent on the `Idempotency-Key`, and no notice moves twice (BR8).
- One base, one topic, one queue: `/api/recovery/comms/v1`, `rwb.comms.events.v1` and `rwb-comms` in the namespace `rwb-recovery` (DP-13, DP-14).
- One hop and 2 s on every call, and a timeout never approves, regenerates or holds a notice (DP-11).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-014 for rwb-access. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer, legal counsel and head of litigation who decides a D7.1 demand or recall notice**, I want **an access answer that says whether my role carries the Litigation right to open the notice and to approve, change, refuse or return it, which version of the permission matrix and of the masking policy that answer was taken from, and an access-log entry that names the notice and the case but never the addressee's address**, so that **the first decision in the Workbench is taken by a role that may take it and is recorded as a look at that notice, and no screen opens on a notice whose address reaches a log**.

Inside `rwb-access` this is the access slice of the approval screen of legacy RWB-E2-014:

- Service `rwb-access`, schema `rwb_access`, REST base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1` with event names `rwb.access.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`.
- The slice delivers three answers and one record: the authorise decision for capability area `LITIGATION` with right `R` on opening a notice and right `A` on deciding it, the resolved permission answer for the caller, the masking answer for the addressee postal address `DF-PTY-016` (field `value_token` of `contact_point`, over `v_ace_contact.contact_value`), and the access-log entry written as a decision-record entry of DP-03 on every allowed read (`AC-READ`) and every refusal (`AC-DENY`).
- The slice builds no screen. The approval queue SCR-10, the decision screen SCR-11 and the notice approval panel SCR-18 are `rwb-decision`'s, served through the gateway-bff composite route; the notice itself is `rwb-comms`'s; the case facts, the case state and the case-owner task are `rwb-case`'s.
- The preparer rule of legacy BR3 and CTL-05 — a person may not approve what they prepared — is executed by `rwb-decision`. `rwb-access` supplies the letter `A` for the capability area and the holder or routed-role check, and nothing else; it never learns who the preparer is, so a slip in this slice cannot let a preparer approve, and a correct answer here cannot stop one on its own.
- The policy pack is data: permission rows under matrix version `PM-2026.12`, masking rows under masking version `MASK-SIT-01`. The load path that writes those rows is `rwb-access`'s own and is out of this story (RWB-P4-AD002-APP, RWB-P4-AD004-APP).
- The masking version in force for SIT is assumed `MASK-SIT-01` (GAP-0933; ASM-1658); no mask format for a postal address is fixed by any source, so this story names the field and the version and never a rendering (GAP-0931; ASM-1657).

The rights carried from the legacy story are unchanged: `RW-LITOFF`, `RW-LEGAL` and `RW-HEADLIT` hold Litigation `A` for a D7.1 notice they did not prepare, `RW-CASEOWN` holds Litigation `R` and receives the rejected-notice task without the right to approve, and internal audit reads with scope `ALL`.

##### 2. Business rationale

A demand fee notice sent on the wrong authority is a Bank of Thailand finding, and an approval that no one can prove was authorised is the same finding one step later. The legacy story proved the decision; this slice proves the authorisation behind it. Today the right to approve a notice is spread over role documents and manual checks, and the address of the addressee is copied into working files and log lines that no one reviews. Under Architecture v5 the authorise answer and the masking answer come from `rwb-access` as data, with the matrix version and the mask version naming the policy the answer was taken from, and every look at a notice is an append-only entry in the same ledger as the decisions.

This story carries controls CTL-05 (a preparer may not decide, enforced by `rwb-decision` on the letter this slice supplies), CTL-14 (only an approved notice leaves) and the audit expectation behind NFR-042 (every read of the case store and the document store is logged). It meets REQ-APD-002 and REQ-APD-006 on the access side and supports the measure notices sent with an approval entry (target 100 percent) and the measure rule and limit changes made without a code release (target 100 percent).

The realignment changes the mechanism, not the business rule:

1. The permission rows and the masking rows of the monolith's recovery schema become `rwb-access`'s own tables in `rwb_access` (DP-01), versioned by matrix version and mask version, so a change of rights or of masking needs an approved load and no release.
2. The synchronous `RecoveryAccessGuard` call inside the monolith becomes the published authorise contract, cached, with one hop and a 2 s timeout (DP-11); the screen and the services ask `rwb-access` and hold the answer for the life of the cache entry.
3. The decision-log writer inside the monolith becomes the local decision-record library of DP-03, so an `AC-READ` or `AC-DENY` entry is hash-chained and published on `rwb.decision-record.v1` where `rwb-decision`'s ledger and the audit query already read.
4. The access event that the monolith never sent becomes `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` on `rwb.access.events.v1`, and every holder of a cached answer — this service's own cache first — refreshes on it, so a new masking version is in force at the next call with no deployment.
5. The ACE data behind the masked field stays where it is: the address value is read through `rwb-source-data`'s contract by whoever displays it, and `rwb-access` answers only that the field is masked and under which version (DP-05).

##### 3. Preconditions

| Precondition | What it gives this story |
|---|---|
| RWB-P7-E2014-CON | The published notice and approval contract this slice is tested against: the notice `N-0201` for case `RW-2026-000123` with template `DEMAND-MTG` version 2 in language `TH` under rule `R-LIT-03` version `LIT-2026.12` and preparer `U-9211`, and the approval `A-0201` in state `WAITING` for route role `RW-LITOFF`, with its contract fakes. The request and response shape of the authorise call itself is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0932; ASM-1656) |
| Permission matrix `PM-2026.12` `IN_FORCE` | The rows this slice answers from, loaded by the policy pack path (RWB-P4-AD002-APP, RWB-P4-AD004-APP): `LITIGATION` `A` for `RW-LITOFF`, `RW-LEGAL` and `RW-HEADLIT`, `LITIGATION` `R` for `RW-CASEOWN`, `REPORTING` and every area `R` for `RW-AUDIT` with scope `ALL`, and no `LITIGATION` row for `RW-PHONECOL` |
| Masking version `MASK-SIT-01` in force | The rows for `DF-PTY-016` covering `RW-LITOFF`, `RW-LEGAL`, `RW-HEADLIT` and `RW-CASEOWN` with `unmasked` false, so the addressee postal address is masked for every role that decides a D7.1 notice, and no row at all for a field outside the pack, which stays masked by default. The version label is assumed for SIT (GAP-0933; ASM-1658) |
| Test users in SIT | `U-9211` holds `RW-LEGAL` and prepared `N-0201`; `U-9212` and `U-9214` hold `RW-LITOFF`; `U-9213` holds `RW-HEADLIT`; `U-9215` holds `RW-CASEOWN`; `U-9216` holds `RW-AUDIT`; `U-9217` holds `RW-PHONECOL` |
| The decision-record library and its topic | `rwb.decision-record.v1` and the local library of DP-03, so an access entry is written, chained and published in one transaction with the answer |
| gateway-bff composite route | The route of DP-19 that carries the screen's authorise, permission and masking calls to this base path, with the 2 s timeout of DP-11 |

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E2-014:

- A D7.1 notice carries no amount limit, and delegation item 2.1.3 (delay of legal action) does not apply to issuing a notice; no `delegation_limit` row is read on this path.
- Templates `DEMAND-MTG`, `DEMAND-MTG-B` and `RECALL-MTG` are Approved in language `TH`; template status is `rwb-comms`'s and does not change the authorise answer.
- The input age limits are parameter rows read by `rwb-decision`; they do not change the authorise answer.
- Every refusal is answered with MSG-P4-002 naming the action and the capability area, and no notice content (FSD P4 v3 A2.4 VR-P4-004-1).

##### 4. Flow

1. Litigation officer: opens SCR-10 Approval queue and selects the D7.1 item for notice `N-0201` of case `RW-2026-000123`.
2. gateway-bff composite route: on the screen open, calls `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` on this service with the caller's user reference, the roles the session resolved, capability area `LITIGATION`, right `R`, the notice and case as the object reference, and the field list the screen will render, `DF-PTY-016`.
3. `AuthoriseService`: reads the caller's permission rows for `LITIGATION` from `permission` in `rwb_access` under the matrix version in force, unions the letters of every role the caller holds, and answers `allowed` with right `R`, the roles that carry it, `matrixVersion` `PM-2026.12` and `maskingVersion` `MASK-SIT-01`.
4. `MaskingPolicyService`: reads the `masking_rule` rows for `DF-PTY-016` and the caller's roles under the mask version in force and answers masked. Where no row covers the field for any of the caller's roles the answer is masked as well, so the default is refuse rather than show (FSD P4 v3 A2.5, AC-EXC-P4-004-05). No value of the address is read, echoed or cached by this service.
5. `AccessLogWriter`, in the same transaction as the answer: writes the decision-record entry of DP-03 with decision code `AC-READ`, the actor, the notice reference, the case reference, the capability area, the right, the matrix version, the mask version and the field markers, with `DF-PTY-016` marked masked and no value; publishes `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the outbox.
6. The screen draws the notice, the case facts and the rule and template versions it received from `rwb-decision`, `rwb-case` and `rwb-comms`, with the address field rendered masked; the screen itself is not this story's.
7. Litigation officer: approves, or changes the template variant and approves, or refuses with a reason. The `rwb-decision` approve or refuse call runs its own checks first and asks this service for right `A` on area `LITIGATION` for the same object and the routed role.
8. `AuthoriseService`, right `A`: answers `allowed` when a permission row of one of the caller's roles holds the letter `A` for `LITIGATION` under the matrix version in force and the role the approval routes to is one of the caller's roles; otherwise it refuses with 403 and MSG-P4-002 for the named action and area.
9. `AccessLogWriter`, on that refusal: writes `AC-DENY` with the actor, the capability area, the right, the approval reference, the matrix version and the reason code, and with no notice field, no template code, no rule version and no value; `rwb-decision` then keeps its own approval and decision entries.
10. The preparer check: `rwb-decision` compares the preparer it holds on the approval with the caller and returns 409 with MSG-P7-002. This service is not called again and records nothing, because the approval was never authorised as a decision by anyone.
11. A policy pack load by the service's own administration path commits new `permission` or `masking_rule` rows and writes the outbox row for `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` with the new matrix or masking version; the load itself is RWB-P4-AD002-APP and RWB-P4-AD004-APP.
12. The cache-refresh listener of this service reads that event from `rwb.access.events.v1` and replaces the cached answer for the affected roles; the next authorise call answers with the new version and a new mask answer, with no deployment and no restart, and the answer never mixes a matrix version with a mask version from a different policy load.
13. Internal audit (`RW-AUDIT`, scope `ALL`): reads the entries through `rwb-decision`'s decision-log query, where `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entries sit beside the approval entries of the same notice.

Every answer and its access-log entry commit in one transaction (DP-03, R-UNI-39), so a call that cannot be logged is refused rather than answered (FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-007-03), and a repeated call with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the first answer without a second entry.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The caller holds no LITIGATION row at all | Refused with 403; one `AC-DENY` entry with area `LITIGATION` and the right asked; nothing shown | MSG-P4-002 | AC7 |
| X2 | The caller holds `LITIGATION` `R` and asks for right `A` | Refused with 403 for the named action; one `AC-DENY` entry with right `A`; the approval is unchanged | MSG-P4-002 | AC3 |
| X3 | The routed role of the approval is not one of the caller's roles | Refused with 403; one `AC-DENY` entry naming the right and the approval reference; no approval change | MSG-P4-002 | AC3 |
| X4 | No masking row covers the field for any of the caller's roles | The field is answered masked under the mask version in force; the entry marks it masked; no value is read | None | AC5 |
| X5 | The decision record of the access entry cannot be written | The call returns 503, no answer and no data; the reason is logged; the cache is unchanged | MSG-P7-003 | BR7 |
| X6 | A second call arrives with the same `Idempotency-Key` | The first answer and its entry are returned; no second entry is written | None | BR7 |
| X7 | A matrix version and a mask version arrive from two different policy loads | The cache refuses the mixed pair, keeps the versions it already holds and raises the mismatch; the caller gets the older consistent pair | None | AC6 |
| X8 | The policy event arrives before the cache is warm | The first call reads the rows directly, writes its entry and warms the cache from the same rows | None | AC6 |

An answer is never served without its entry and never without naming both policy versions; a call whose entry fails is an error, not a silent success.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the published approval and notice contract RWB-P7-E2014-CON and its fake; the notice content, the case facts and the rule version arrive in the request or in the screen, never as a table read |
| Negotiable | Letters, roles, areas, masking rows, mask formats and versions are data; the story fixes the answer shape and the entry only |
| Valuable | The screen cannot open or decide a notice without a current authorise answer, and the address never leaves the owning service or enters a log |
| Estimable | Three endpoints, one cache, one masking answer, one entry writer, one index migration |
| Small | Fits one week with its tests, because the screen, the approval and the notice are other stories' |
| Testable | Every criterion below is one test case in section 16; the approval and notice facts are returned by the contract fake |

The eight criteria above are the ones this story owns; the legacy AC1 to AC10 and the legacy test cases are carried by `rwb-decision` (RWB-P7-E2014-APP) and `rwb-comms` (RWB-P6-E2014-APP), and the legacy test set is kept here in section 16 against this slice's assertions.

The authorise request and response shape used above — actor, roles, area, right, object reference, route role and field list in, and allowed, roles, area, right, matrix version, masking version, field markers and messageId out — is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0932; ASM-1656); no field of it is a business value and it is renamed at the contract review if the published contract differs.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A right is taken from the permission rows of the matrix version in force, per role and capability area, with letters C, R, U, D and A; no letter, role or area is written in code | FSD P4 v3 A2.4; BR-P4-004; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 |
| BR2 | Opening a D7.1 demand or recall notice for approval needs `LITIGATION` R; approving, changing, refusing or returning it needs `LITIGATION` A | Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 10; FSD P4 v3 A2.4; TSD P4 v3 T3.2 LOV-CAPABILITY |
| BR3 | A role with no `LITIGATION` row is denied; the authorise path refuses by default and never falls back to a broader role or to a default letter | FSD P4 v3 A2.4 AC-EXC-P4-004-06; Architecture v5 zero trust, deny by default |
| BR4 | A person may not approve what they prepared: the preparer rule is executed by `rwb-decision`, and `rwb-access` supplies the letter `A` and the holder or routed-role check only | Legacy RWB-E2-014 BR3; CTL-05; Admin and access model, section 6.2 |
| BR5 | A personal field is shown masked unless a masking row for the role and the field says unmasked, and a field with no covering row stays masked | FSD P4 v3 A2.5 AC-EXC-P4-004-05; BR-P4-005 |
| BR6 | The authorise answer depends on the rights and the policy versions only: the age of an input, the template status and the presence of a reason are `rwb-decision`'s checks and never change the access answer | FSD P4 v3 A2.4 VR-P4-004-1; legacy RWB-E2-014 BR4, BR5, BR6 |
| BR7 | Every allowed read of a notice for approval writes one `AC-READ` entry and every refusal one `AC-DENY` entry, in one transaction with the answer; a call that cannot be logged is refused | FSD P4 v3 A2.7 AC-P4-007-01, AC-EXC-P4-007-03 and AC-EXC-P4-007-04; DP-03; R-UNI-39 |
| BR8 | An answer names the matrix version and the masking version it was decided under, and a policy change reaches the cached answer through `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` with no deployment | FSD P4 v3 A2.4 AC-P4-004-01; Architecture v5 slide 42 cache refresh |
| BR9 | No personal data in the entry: the access-log entry carries the field ID and a masked marker, never a value, and the address value never leaves the owning service | Legacy RWB-E2-014 section 17; NFR-042; TSD P4 v3 T7 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-access`:

- BR1 is a read of `permission` in `rwb_access` under the matrix version in force; the capability areas are the LOV-CAPABILITY values read through the reference-data contract of DP-07, and the Java code holds no enum of areas, roles or letters.
- BR2 and BR3 are one check on the letter of the requested right in the area `LITIGATION`, with the routed role compared against the caller's roles; a missing row is a refusal, never a default.
- BR4 is deliberately absent here: the approval carries the preparer and `rwb-decision` compares it before it calls this service for right `A`. This service never receives a preparer reference, so it cannot be the place where the rule is lost.
- BR5 is the `masking_rule` read plus the default; the mask format is the library's, because no source fixes a rendering for a postal address (GAP-0931; ASM-1657).
- BR6 is the absence of any notice field in the authorise request except the object reference: no input age, no template status and no reason code is sent, so no check here can disagree with `rwb-decision`.
- BR7 is one `RecordAndApply` transaction on the answer and the entry, with the idempotency key of DP-09.
- BR8 is the version pair in the answer and the cache refresh on the service's own `AccessPolicyChanged`.
- BR9 is a check on the entry writer: the field list it writes is the field ID and the masked flag, and a test asserts the entry text holds no digit of the address.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| No cached answer | Authorise call | The policy rows are in force | Allowed or denied, with the matrix and masking versions |
| Allowed | The answer is served | The `AC-READ` entry commits | Served, with the field markers |
| Denied | The refusal is served | The `AC-DENY` entry commits | Refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002 |
| Cached under version `PM-2026.12` / `MASK-SIT-01` | `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` | A later policy load is in force | Cached under the new versions, served from the next call |
| Cached, mixed versions | Refresh | The event names a matrix version and a masking version from different loads | Unchanged, with the mismatch raised |

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LOADED` | The policy pack load is approved | The approver is not the loader | `APPROVED` |
| `APPROVED` | The valid-from date is reached | None | `IN_FORCE`, and `AccessPolicyChanged` is published |
| `IN_FORCE` | The next version is approved | None | `SUPERSEDED` |

The second table is the lifecycle of the rows this story reads, owned by RWB-P4-AD002-APP and RWB-P4-AD004-APP; this story reads the version in force and publishes nothing on that path itself.

Access-log entries have no lifecycle of their own: they are append-only and are read by `rwb-decision`'s decision-log query.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-LITOFF Litigation officer | Opens a D7.1 notice for approval (`LITIGATION` R) and approves, changes, refuses or returns one they did not prepare (`LITIGATION` A) |
| RW-LEGAL Legal counsel | The same rights as RW-LITOFF on the same notice, from the same rows |
| RW-HEADLIT Head of Litigation | The same rights, on the item escalated to the route role RW-HEADLIT |
| RW-CASEOWN Case owner | Opens the case and the rejected-notice task (`LITIGATION` R); may not approve (`LITIGATION` A is refused) |
| RW-AUDIT Internal audit | Reads the access and decision entries with scope `ALL`, and the policy versions they were decided under |
| RW-PHONECOL and every role with no `LITIGATION` row | Refused by default, with an `AC-DENY` entry |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-DECLOG | Service identities: the case workflow's read of the case authorise answer and the decision-record library's write of the entry |

The preparer rule is not in this table: `rwb-decision` executes it before it asks this service for right `A`, and this service does not receive the preparer. The delegation of authority is not consulted either, because a D7.1 notice carries no amount limit; the holder check of a limit-based approval is another story's use of `delegation_limit`.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Table in `rwb_access` | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039 | `role` | role_code, role_name, role_class, default_scope | Read |
| DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044 | `permission` | role_id, capability_area, letters, matrix_version | Read |
| DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204 | `masking_rule` | role_code, field_id, unmasked, masking_version, valid_from, valid_to | Read |
| DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211 | `role_conflict` | role_code, conflicts_with, conflict_version | Read, only to report a conflicting pair to the session that asks for permissions |
| DF-PTY-016 | `contact_point` (owned by P1, read through the owner's contract of DP-05) | value_token, the addressee postal address over `v_ace_contact.contact_value` | Not read as a value: the answer names the field and the masked marker only |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (local library, DP-03) | the `AC-READ` or `AC-DENY` entry: decision code, actor, object reference, area, right, versions, field markers, time | Write |
| (inbox) | `processed_event` | event_id, consumer, processed_at | Write |
| (outbox) | outbox library table in `rwb_access` | the `AccessPolicyChanged` row and the record row | Write |
| (idempotency) | `idempotency_key` | the stored answer of an authorise call with its key | Write |

No `delegation_limit` row is read on this path: a D7.1 notice carries no amount limit and the route role, not a holder, is the check. The masked rendering of the postal address is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0931; ASM-1657); this story names the field ID, the role and the mask version and leaves the format to the one masking library every screen uses. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None new. The decision is served through the operations of RWB-P4-E1037-CON on base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, owner P4 `rwb-access`; this slice adds no path, no query parameter and no response field, and decides the following behind them:

| Method | Path | Purpose | Authorization | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | The role, scope and right decision for one capability area and right, with the routed role where the action is an approval, and the field markers | The caller's own session; the answer is the decision | 401; 403 MSG-P4-002; 422; 503 MSG-P7-003 |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/permissions` | The caller's resolved roles, letters per capability area, scope, matrix version and masking version | None beyond the session | 401; 503 |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies` | The masking answer for a field and a role, with the mask version | None beyond the session | 401; 503 |

Architecture v5 slide 14 names `POST /authorise`, `GET /me/permissions` and `/masking-policies`; TSD P4 v3 names `GET /me/session` (API-P4-012) for the same resolved view, so the resolved view is answered behind `GET /me/permissions` under R-PREC and the session read keeps its own story and its own shape. The request and response shape of `POST /authorise` is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0932; ASM-1656).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The notice, the approval and the case facts are sent in the authorise request by the composite route and by `rwb-decision`; this service calls no other service on this path, so the call stays one hop with the 2 s timeout of DP-11 and a circuit breaker.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` | `rwb.access.events.v1` | P4 `rwb-access` | matrix or mask version | the policy kind, the old and new version, validFrom, the affected capability areas or fields, the load reference |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library; consumed by P7 | the entry ID | the hash-chained `AC-READ` or `AC-DENY` entry of DP-03 |

CloudEvents 1.0 envelope; neither payload carries personal data. The `AccessPolicyChanged` event is written by the policy load path of this service (RWB-P4-AD002-APP, RWB-P4-AD004-APP) in the same transaction as the rows, and this story's part is the refresh it triggers; `DoaLimitChanged` belongs to the delegation path and is not published by this story.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None from another service. The cache refresh reads this service's own `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` from `rwb.access.events.v1` through an internal listener, which is not a cross-service subscription; no `rwb.decision.*`, `rwb.case.*` or `rwb.comms.*` event is read. The refresh fails closed: a policy event that does not parse leaves the cache on the versions it already holds (X7).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. This story starts no workflow and registers no activity; the approval itself is `ApprovalWorkflow` in `rwb-decision`, and the case is `CaseWorkflow` in `rwb-case`.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None for this story. The six-monthly access review list (JOB-18) is a Temporal Schedule of this service and belongs to its own story; the authorise path has no clock.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | The roles the caller holds and their class and default scope |
| `permission` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | The letters per capability area under the matrix version in force |
| `masking_rule` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | The unmasked flag per role and field under the mask version in force |
| `role_conflict` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | The conflicting pair reported to a session that asks for permissions |
| `delegation_limit` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | Not read here; a D7.1 notice carries no amount limit |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_access` | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects (DP-09) |

`contact_point`, `notice`, `approval`, `recovery_case` and `decision_log_entry` are other services' and are not read: the field is named, the value stays with `rwb-source-data`, and the ledger entry is written through the library (DP-01).

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-decision notice and approval WireMock | RWB-P7-E2014-CON | Notice `N-0201` for case `RW-2026-000123` with template `DEMAND-MTG` version 2 in `TH`, rule `R-LIT-03` version `LIT-2026.12` and preparer `U-9211`; approval `A-0201` `WAITING` for `RW-LITOFF`, and the escalated repeat for `RW-HEADLIT` with escalation level 1 |
| decision-record fake | RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The entry write and the publish on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, including a forced failure for X5 |
| gateway-bff route fake | RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The composite route that carries the authorise, permission and masking calls, so the screen's own calls can be asserted |
| policy pack fixture | this story's own test data | The `PM-2026.12` permission rows, the `MASK-SIT-01` masking rows and a later masking version for AC6 |

| Call type | Count in this story | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | Provided 0 new (3 existing operations used), consumed 0 | The decisions are served on `/authorise`, `/me/permissions` and `/masking-policies` of RWB-P4-E1037-CON on `/api/recovery/access/v1` |
| Kafka | Published 2, consumed 0 from other services | `rwb.access.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` published; the cache refresh reads this service's own topic |
| Temporal | 0 | No workflow, no activity, no task queue use |
| File | None | No file input or output |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`, module `access/authorise`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.authorise`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

Which patterns have an instance in this slice: DP-01 is the read of `permission` and `masking_rule` in `rwb_access`; DP-03 is the `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entry; DP-07 is the LOV-CAPABILITY area list; DP-09 is the outbox, the inbox and the idempotency key; DP-11 is the authorise contract with its mock and its 2 s timeout; DP-13 is the base path; DP-19 is the composite route. DP-05 has an instance only as an absence — this service reads no `v_ace_*` view and names the field, and the value stays with `rwb-source-data`. DP-06 and DP-10 have no instance here: no parameter row and no workflow or Schedule is this story's, and the policy rows with their versions are the data. This secondary slice adds no new build dependency of its own (metadata H = None): the platform contracts the table names are pulled by the service's baseline and by the policy pack load path (RWB-P4-AD002-APP, RWB-P4-AD004-APP), so the story is Day 1 and builds against the published contract RWB-P7-E2014-CON.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AuthoriseController | REST controller | The three operations of 12.1, the problem responses with their message IDs, and the idempotency key |
| AuthoriseService | Service | Resolution of the caller's letters for one area and right, the routed-role check, the version pair in the answer |
| AuthoriseCache | Cache | The cached answer per user, area, right and object, with the matrix and mask versions; refresh on `AccessPolicyChanged`; fail closed on a mixed pair |
| MaskingPolicyService | Service | The `masking_rule` read per role and field, the masked default, and the mask version in the answer |
| PolicyVersionResolver | Service | The matrix version and the mask version in force, read once per refresh and held together |
| RouteRoleCheck | Service | The letter `A` plus the routed role or the holder the approval names; the preparer rule is not here |
| AccessLogWriter | Service | The `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entry of DP-03, with the masked field markers and no value, in the same transaction as the answer |
| PolicyChangeListener | Kafka consumer with the inbox | The service's own `AccessPolicyChanged`, deduplicated by event ID, refreshing the cache |

**Database and migrations**

- Reads `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule` and `role_conflict` in `rwb_access`; writes the decision-record entry through the library, and the inbox, outbox and idempotency rows.
- Index `ix_permission_role_area_version ON permission (role_id, capability_area, matrix_version)`, so the authorise read is one index scan in the cache-miss path.
- Index `ix_masking_field_version ON masking_rule (field_id, masking_version, role_code)`, so the mask answer for a field and a set of roles is one scan.
- No new table and no new column: the policy tables are the policy pack path's, and the access log is the decision-record entry (DP-03).
- Migration in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15: `V2014_1__access_authorise_indexes.sql`.

**Configuration and reference data**

- LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-ROLE and LOV-SCOPE through the reference-data contract of DP-07 (RWB-P3-E1043-CON); the area `LITIGATION` is a value of that list, never a constant.
- The matrix version `PM-2026.12` and the masking version `MASK-SIT-01` in force are read from the rows, not configured; the SIT label is assumed (GAP-0933; ASM-1658).
- The access entry's decision codes `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` follow the decision-code list of the ledger, and the field markers come from the request.
- No switch of this slice's own: a screen that cannot get an authorise answer must not open, so the authorise path has no off state. The legacy flag `rwb.decision.notice-approval` stays `rwb-decision`'s and is a legacy reference here.

**Build steps**

1. `AuthoriseController` and the problem responses, with the three operations and the idempotency key; tests for 401, 403 and 503 shapes.
2. `PolicyVersionResolver` and the two index reads; test that a new matrix version is served as data with no code change.
3. `AuthoriseService` for right `R` and right `A` on `LITIGATION`, with the routed-role check; tests for AC1, AC2, AC4 and AC7.
4. `MaskingPolicyService` with the masked default and the mask version in the answer; tests for AC1, AC4 and AC5.
5. `AccessLogWriter` in the same transaction as the answer, with the masked markers and the no-value assertion; tests for AC1, AC3, AC7 and AC8, and the forced failure for X5.
6. `AuthoriseCache` and `PolicyChangeListener` with the version pair and the mixed-pair refusal; test for AC6 with a fixed clock.
7. The contract-fake run against RWB-P7-E2014-CON and the gateway-bff route fake, so the story builds before `rwb-decision` and the screen exist in the environment.
8. The denial test for a role with no `LITIGATION` row through the composite route, and the audit read of the entries through `rwb-decision`.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; every open of a D7.1 notice for approval writes exactly one `AC-READ` entry naming the notice, the case, the actor and `DF-PTY-016` as masked, with no value of the address anywhere in the entry; every refusal writes one `AC-DENY` entry with its area and right; every answer names the matrix version and the masking version it was decided under; and a masking policy change is served by the cache after `AccessPolicyChanged` with no deployment.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller's role does not carry the right in the area | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, on the authorise path |
| MSG-P4-003 | The object is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. | This story, when the scope check fails |
| MSG-P7-003 | The access entry cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on the entry writer |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The cached policy was replaced while the call was in flight | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. | This story, on the version check |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of the authorise request is missing | Enter {field}. | This story, on the request validation |
| MSG-P7-002 | A preparer tries to approve | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. | `rwb-decision`, never this story |

The {action} value in MSG-P4-002 names the action and nothing else — for a D7.1 notice, "approve a D7.1 notice", "change a D7.1 notice", "refuse a D7.1 notice" or "open a D7.1 notice" — and the problem response carries the capability area in its `detail` beside the message ID, so a refusal is diagnosable without any notice content. Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set and `instance` naming the request.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built here. The screens are `rwb-decision`'s and reach this service through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 (RWB-PLT-N001-CON):

| Screen | State | What this story supplies |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-10 Approval queue | List | The `LITIGATION` R answer per item, so the queue shows only items the caller may open, and one `AC-READ` entry per item opened |
| SCR-11 Decision screen | Ready | The `LITIGATION` A answer behind the approve, change and refuse buttons, and the field markers that keep `DF-PTY-016` masked |
| SCR-11 Decision screen | Decided | No answer of this story; the decided state is `rwb-decision`'s |
| SCR-18 Notice approval panel | Generated | The masked marker for the addressee postal address and the mask version the panel shows beside the field |
| SCR-11 Decision screen | Denied | The problem response of MSG-P4-002 with the action and the area, and the `AC-DENY` entry behind it |

The panel layout, the masked rendering and the composite route's field list are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0931; ASM-1657); the screen stories are RWB-P7-E2014-APP and the notice API stories in `rwb-comms`, and this story changes no screen behaviour.
