The legacy level System maps to End to end, Access to Component and Resilience to NFR, and each case asserts only this slice's answer and entry. No case ID with the `-ITG` suffix is used here: the integration copy of the set is RWB-ITG-E2014-ITG, which proves the same facts across `rwb-access`, `rwb-decision`, `rwb-comms` and `rwb-case` with real services, and its `TC-E2-014-01-ITG` to `TC-E2-014-12-ITG` belong to that story. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the letters C, R, U, D and A, the capability areas, the roles, the scopes, the masking rows and the matrix and mask versions are data rows; the Java code holds no letter, area, role or version literal (BR-P4-004, BR-P4-005).
- No personal data in logs, events, tests, workflow history or prompts: the access entry carries the actor reference, the notice and case references, the field ID and a masked marker. Workflow history is not used because this story starts no workflow.
- The addressee address never leaves the owning service: the value is read through `rwb-source-data`'s contract by whoever displays it, and this service answers the field ID and the masked flag only. A test scans the entry text for any part of the synthetic address.
- No read of another service's tables and no cross-schema read (DP-01): `notice`, `approval`, `recovery_case`, `contact_point` and `decision_log_entry` are never queried here.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or a `v_ace_*` view of this service; this story reads no ACE view at all.
- An answer is never served without its entry, and the answer and the entry commit in one transaction (R-UNI-39).
- The cache fails closed: an unparseable or mixed policy event leaves the versions in force, and a missing policy row is a refusal, never a default allow.
- The authorise path has no off switch, because a screen that cannot be authorised must not open; the legacy approval flag stays `rwb-decision`'s.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-014 for rwb-case, secondary slice. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer, legal counsel and head of litigation who decide a D7.1 demand or recall notice, and the case owner who must act on the outcome**, I want **rwb-case to serve the case facts behind the approval screen — case number, product group, stage, route, status, owner and entry date, the balance and arrears facts each with its as-of date and its age in days, and only for a case my role may read in my scope — and to raise one redress task on the case in the case owner's queue when a notice is refused or returned**, so that **the approver decides on facts that carry their own dates, and a refused notice becomes work somebody owes instead of a message somebody read**.

This is the secondary `rwb-case` slice of legacy RWB-E2-014. It owns no legacy criterion; AC1 to AC10 stay with `rwb-decision` (RWB-P7-E2014-APP) for the approval and with `rwb-access` (RWB-P4-E2014-APP) for the rights.

- Service `rwb-case`, schema `rwb_case`, REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`.
- It delivers three things: the case-facts projection of the case read behind the panel, with one `inputAsOf` element per input carrying its business date and age in days; the case-side right and scope answer taken from the `rwb-access` authorise contract before a field is rendered; and the outcome — one redress task on the case from `rwb.decision.ApprovalRefused.v1` or `rwb.decision.ApprovalReturned.v1`, assigned to the case owner with the reason or question, plus its trace on the case timeline.
- It builds no screen and moves no case status. SCR-10, SCR-11 and SCR-18 are `rwb-decision`'s and are composed by gateway-bff; the notice, its template version and the three notice operations are `rwb-comms`'s; the approval, the decision entry and the input age limits are `rwb-decision`'s; the access decision and the masking are `rwb-access`'s; the ACE balance, arrears and contact facts and the interaction ledger are `rwb-source-data`'s. The status move out of `WAITING_APPROVAL` and the resume state of the routing rule are RWB-P3-E2013-APP's.
- The two outcome event names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2216; ASM-3643): the catalogue lists `ApprovalRequested` and the decision record, so this slice names one event per outcome and confirms the names against RWB-P7-E2014-CON.
- The redress task's code, element type, assignment reason, due time and its notice and approval references are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2216; ASM-3644); the story names the task by the notice it comes from and reads every other value from reference data.

The legacy values are unchanged: case `RW-2026-000123`, product `MORTGAGE`, approval `A-0201`, notice `N-0201`, template `DEMAND-MTG` version 2, rule `R-LIT-03` version `LIT-2026.12`, prepared by `U-9211`, decided on 14 December 2026, the total balance of business date 13 December 2026 and of 11 December 2026 when it is 3 days old, and the refusal reason "Addressee is a guarantor; a guarantor notice is needed".

##### 2. Business rationale

A demand fee notice sent on a stale balance is a Bank of Thailand finding, and a refusal nobody acts on is the same finding one step later: the notice is blocked, the case sits, and the reason lives in a screen nobody reopens. The legacy story read the case, the balance, the approval and the queue in one process, so the age of a fact and the task of a refused notice were free. In the target that transaction is gone: `rwb-case` owns the case and its tasks in `rwb_case`, `rwb-source-data` owns the ACE facts with their business dates, `rwb-access` owns the right and the scope, `rwb-decision` owns the approval and the age limits, and gateway-bff composes the screen from the owners one hop each (Architecture v5 slides 10, 14 and 17).

The two things the case service alone can guarantee are therefore this slice's value: the panel tells the truth about how old each fact is, and a refused or returned notice becomes a task on the case with an owner and a reason. Neither can be lost to a service that is not built yet, and neither depends on the approval being live on the same day.

It serves REQ-APD-002 (the approver sees the inputs used, with their dates, on one screen) and REQ-APD-006 (demand and recall notices are approved through approval routing, and a refusal returns the case to its owner) on the case side, and supports CTL-14 (only an approved notice is dispatched, so the refusal must be visible) and CTL-05 (the preparer cannot decide, which `rwb-decision` enforces). The measure is notices sent with an approval entry, target 100 percent; the case-side measure this slice adds is every refused notice with a redress task on its case.

The realignment changes the mechanism and not the rule: the in-process case read and `RecoveryAccessGuard` become the published case contract on `/api/recovery/case/v1` (DP-13, DP-11) and the cached authorise answer of `rwb-access` (DP-08 as consumed); the ACE facts come from `rwb-source-data`'s reads with `data_as_of` (DP-05); and the refusal task becomes one `task` row and one `assignment` row in `rwb_case`, written in one transaction with the local decision record of DP-03 from an outcome read through the inbox of DP-09.

Carried business preconditions:

- Case `RW-2026-000123` exists with product group `MORTGAGE`, status `WAITING_APPROVAL` while `A-0201` waits, an owner, a stage, a route and an entry date.
- The total balance is an ACE fact with a business date: 13 December 2026 in the background and 11 December 2026 for the stale case, 3 days old on 14 December 2026 against the 1 day limit `rwb-decision` holds.
- The limits `rwb.decision.input-age-days.TOTAL_BALANCE` = 1 and `rwb.decision.input-age-days.POSTAL_ADDRESS` = 30 (assumed, owner RW-COE; DL22) are `rwb-decision`'s parameter rows; this story neither reads nor compares them.
- A D7.1 notice carries no amount limit, so no `delegation_limit` row is read on this path and the panel shows no limit.

##### 4. Flow

1. Litigation officer: opens SCR-10 Approval queue through the gateway-bff route and selects the D7.1 item of approval `A-0201` for notice `N-0201` on case `RW-2026-000123`.
2. gateway-bff: composes SCR-11 with the SCR-18 panel and calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` on this service, one hop, with the caller's session and a 2 s budget (DP-19, DP-11).
3. `AuthoriseCheck`: calls `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` with the caller, the area `Case record`, right `R` and the case as the object, and holds the answer for the life of the cache entry.
4. `AuthoriseCheck`: refuses with 403 MSG-P4-002 when the answer carries no right, and with 404 MSG-P4-003 when the case is outside the scope; no case fact is read or returned on a refusal.
5. `CaseFactsProjection`: reads `recovery_case` by ID and returns the case number, product group, stage code, route state, route code, status, owner reference and entry date, with days past due at entry, total outstanding at entry and exposure band.
6. `SourceDataClient`: reads the account read for the current total balance and days past due with `data_as_of`, and the customer read for the contact fact the postal address input comes from; the address value itself is never read, echoed or cached here (DP-05).
7. `InputAgeService`: for each input, computes the age in days from that input's business date to the ACE business date in force (the freshness read) and returns one `inputAsOf` element with `inputCode`, `businessDate` and `ageDays`; the only codes are `TOTAL_BALANCE` and `POSTAL_ADDRESS`.
8. The answer carries the case facts and `inputAsOf` only: no approval status, no notice body, no template code, no rule version and no limit, because those are other owners' facts and the route merges them from their own answers.
9. `rwb-decision`: the officer refuses `A-0201` with the legacy reason, or returns it with a question; the approval, its decision entry and the notice hold stay `rwb-decision`'s and `rwb-comms`'s.
10. `rwb-decision`: publishes the refusal or return event on `rwb.decision.events.v1` with the approval, the notice, the case, the final call, the reason or question and the record reference (GAP-2216; ASM-3643).
11. `NoticeOutcomeListener`: reads the event into the inbox of DP-09, deduplicates by event ID (R-UNI-40) and calls `signalWithStart` on `CaseWorkflow` with workflow ID equal to the case ID, on task queue `rwb-case`.
12. `raiseRedressTask`, one `RecordAndApply` transaction in `rwb_case`: reads the element type, task status and role values through DP-07; writes the `task` row with the task code for a notice redress, the notice and approval references, status OPEN, `owner_role` and the due time of the reference row; writes one `assignment` row naming `recovery_case.owner_user_id`; writes the local decision record of DP-03 with the approval, the notice, the final call and the reason code; writes the outbox row (GAP-2216; ASM-3644).
13. The case status is not written here: RWB-P3-E2013-APP moves the case and writes the resume state of its routing rule from the same outcome.
14. Case owner (`U-9215`): sees the redress task in the work list with the reason or question and the notice reference; the task carries no notice body and no address.
15. Any caller with Case record R in scope: opens SCR-04 and sees the outcome as the decision item of `rwb-decision`'s ledger read and the task item of `task`, newest first, with the final call, the reason code and the time and no notice content.
16. A repeat of the same event is dropped by the inbox; a closed case records the event and raises no task; a transaction that cannot write the record changes nothing and the event stays on the topic for redelivery.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The caller holds no Case record right | 403 before any fact is read; the answer names the action and the area and carries no case fact | MSG-P4-002 | AC3 |
| X2 | The case is outside the caller's scope | 404; no case number, product, balance or owner is returned and the case is not read | MSG-P4-003 | AC3 |
| X3 | The account or customer read does not answer inside 2 s | The panel serves the case facts it has and marks that input's date and age as unavailable; no fact is shown as current | MSG-GEN-006 | AC2 |
| X4 | The data product answers with an older business date | The as-of date and the age in days are returned as they are; the refusal of the approval is `rwb-decision`'s | MSG-P7-006 (P7) | AC2 |
| X5 | The refusal or return event arrives twice | One task; the second delivery is recorded in the inbox and raises nothing | None | AC6 |
| X6 | The event arrives for a closed case | No task and no status change; the mismatch is recorded on the activity with the case and event IDs | None | AC8 |
| X7 | The local decision record cannot be written | Nothing changes: no task, no assignment, no outbox row; the event is redelivered | MSG-P7-003 | AC8 |
| X8 | A stale case version at commit | MSG-GEN-004 and a retry; no second task is raised | MSG-GEN-004 | AC6 |
| X9 | The authorise contract does not answer | The read is refused as unavailable and no fact is returned from an unanswered check | MSG-GEN-006 | AC3 |
| X10 | The notice reference is missing from the event | The task is raised without a notice reference, the gap is recorded, and no reason is dropped | None | AC4 |
| X11 | The readiness of a fact is unknown because its business date is absent | The input is answered as unavailable, never as current | None | AC2 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on Day 1 against the published RWB-P7-E2014-CON and the case, access, source-data and decision contracts with their fakes; the approval and the notice are facts of the event, never a table read |
| Negotiable | The task code, element type, role, assignment reason and due time are data; the story fixes only the facts projection, the age rule and the one-task rule |
| Valuable | The approver sees how old every fact is, and every refused notice becomes a task with an owner and a reason |
| Estimable | One projection with an input-age list, one authorise call, one listener, one activity, one task and assignment write, one index migration |
| Small | Fits one week with its tests, because the screen, the approval, the notice and the access decision belong to other stories |
| Testable | Each criterion is one test case in section 16; the approval, notice and access facts come from the contract mocks |

These eight criteria are the ones this slice owns; it owns no legacy AC, and legacy AC1 to AC10 are carried by `rwb-decision` (RWB-P7-E2014-APP) and `rwb-access` (RWB-P4-E2014-APP). Every value above is a legacy value of RWB-E2-014: the case, product, notice and approval, the balance of 13 December 2026 and of 11 December 2026 for the stale case, 14 December 2026 as the decision date, the refusal reason, the return question and the roles. The ages 1 day and 3 days are counted in calendar days from the input's business date to the ACE business date in force.

The projection field list, the `inputAsOf` element and the way the task is named are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2216; ASM-3645) and (GAP-2216; ASM-3644); none of them is a business value and they are renamed at the contract review if the published contract differs.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The facts the D7.1 panel shows are `rwb_case` facts of this service and the balance and arrears facts of `rwb-source-data`'s contract; the notice, the approval, the rule version and the template version are other owners' facts and are never read or repeated here | REQ-APD-002; legacy s11; DP-01, DP-05 |
| BR2 | Every fact the panel shows carries the date it is true for, and every input carries its business date and its age in days counted from that date to the ACE business date in force; no fact of an older date is shown as current | REQ-APD-002; FSD P3 v4 A2.45; legacy AC5 ages |
| BR3 | Opening the case facts of a notice for approval needs Case record right R and the case in the caller's scope, answered by the `rwb-access` authorise contract; no right is 403 MSG-P4-002 and out of scope is 404 MSG-P4-003 before any fact is read | Legacy s10; FSD P3 v4 A2.45 AC-EXC-P3-045-03; TSD P3 v3 T6.1; DP-08 |
| BR4 | A refused demand or recall notice raises one task on its case, owned by the case owner, holding the reason and the notice reference, so the refusal becomes work and not a message | Legacy BR7 and AC3; REQ-APD-006; FEAT-APD-04 |
| BR5 | A returned notice raises the same task with the approver's question, and neither a refusal nor a return moves the case status in this story | Legacy AC9; RWB-P3-E2013-APP owns the status move |
| BR6 | One outcome raises one task: the event is deduplicated by event ID in the inbox, and a repeated delivery raises nothing | R-UNI-40; TSD P3 v3 T2.4 |
| BR7 | The outcome appears on the case timeline as the decision item of `rwb-decision`'s ledger read and the task item of `task`, newest first, and neither item carries a notice body, template content, an addressee or an address value | REQ-OCC-008; legacy AC3 and s17; NFR-040 |
| BR8 | A task raise that cannot be recorded does not take effect: task, assignment, local record and outbox row commit in one transaction, and a failure leaves the case unchanged and the event on the topic | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; DP-03 |
| BR9 | No business value is written in code: the task code, element type, task status, owner role, assignment reason and due time are reference data read with the version in force | FSD P3 v4 A2.45; DP-07; Template and Rules R7.2 s17 |
| BR10 | No personal data leaves this service: the panel, the task, the record and the timeline item carry the case number, codes, amounts and dates; the postal address is named as a field and never read as a value | Legacy s17; NFR-040 |
| BR11 | A closed case takes no redress task, and an outcome for a case that cannot take work is recorded as a mismatch rather than dropped in silence | FSD P3 v4 A2.3 VR-P3-003-1; R-UNI-20 |

How the rules hold in `rwb-case`:

- BR1 and BR2 are a read of `recovery_case` plus one call to the account and customer reads of `rwb-source-data` with `data_as_of`; the answer carries no field of `notice`, `approval`, `template` or `decision_log_entry`, and `InputAgeService` returns the business date as the read gives it with the difference in calendar days to the business date in force, and no limit and no stale flag.
- BR3 is one call to the authorise contract with a refusal by default: an unanswered or unparseable answer is a refusal, never an allow.
- BR4 and BR5 are one `task` row with `owner_role` and one `assignment` row naming `recovery_case.owner_user_id`; a case with no owner falls back to the case owner role, so a task is never invisible to everybody.
- BR6 is the inbox of DP-09 keyed by event ID plus a partial unique index that makes a second open task for one notice impossible.
- BR7 is the timeline read of API-P3-003, composing decision items from `rwb-decision`'s ledger read and task items from `task`; this story writes no ledger row, because the ledger is `rwb-source-data`'s under DP-18 (GAP-2216; ASM-3647).
- BR8, BR9, BR10 and BR11 are one `RecordAndApply` transaction with the record written last, the DP-07 read with the version in the record and no Java enum of task codes or statuses, a check on the answer and the record that the address is named `POSTAL_ADDRESS` and never valued, and a status check against LOV-CASE-STATUS read through DP-07.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| No task | The refusal or return event | The case is open and the event ID is new | One task OPEN, assigned to the case owner |
| Task OPEN | The case owner opens the task | None | Task IN_PROGRESS |
| Task IN_PROGRESS | The case owner completes it with an outcome | The outcome is a reference outcome | Task DONE with `completed_at` and `outcome_code` |
| Task OPEN or IN_PROGRESS | The case closes before the task is done | The case reaches a closed status | Task CANCELED with the reason |
| Task OPEN | The same event arrives again | The event ID is in the inbox | Unchanged; no second task |
| Any | The record cannot be written | None | Unchanged; MSG-P7-003; redelivery |

The task statuses are the LOV-TASK-STATUS values `OPEN`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `DONE` and `CANCELED`, read with the version in force through DP-07.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CaseWorkflow` running | The outcome arrives through the case router | The event ID is new | `raiseRedressTask` scheduled |
| `raiseRedressTask` committed | Task, assignment, record and outbox written | None | Waiting on the next signal or stage |
| Waiting | Stage ends or 28 days pass | None | Continue-As-New with the same workflow ID |

The case status is in neither table: the move out of `WAITING_APPROVAL` and the resume state of the routing rule are RWB-P3-E2013-APP's.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-LITOFF Litigation officer | Reads the case facts panel of a D7.1 notice for approval (Case record R, in scope); decides nothing here, because the approval is `rwb-decision`'s |
| RW-LEGAL Legal counsel | The same case read on the same notice, from the same answer |
| RW-HEADLIT Head of Litigation | The same case read on an item escalated to RW-HEADLIT |
| RW-CASEOWN Case owner | Reads the case facts (Case record R in scope) and receives the redress task of a refused or returned notice with its reason or question |
| RW-AUDIT Internal audit | Reads the case facts and the timeline with scope `ALL`, and the approval and ledger through `rwb-decision` |
| RW-PHONECOL and any role without Case record R | Refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002; no case fact is returned |
| SY-CASEWF, the `rwb-case` service identity | Consumes the outcome events, raises the task and the assignment, writes the local record and the outbox row |
| SY-DECLOG, the decision-record library identity | Writes the local record of the task raise and publishes it on `rwb.decision-record.v1` |

The access decision is `rwb-access`'s and is consumed on its authorise contract as the cached answer of DP-08; this story holds no permission, masking or delegation row. The preparer rule is not here: `rwb-decision` refuses the preparer with 409 and MSG-P7-002 before any outcome event exists, so a refused preparer raises no task in this service.

The task's own naming is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2216; ASM-3644). Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None new. The facts projection is served through the existing case operations of owner P3 `rwb-case` on base `/api/recovery/case/v1`; this story adds no path, no query parameter and no error code.

| ID | Method | Path | Purpose in this story | Authorization | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-P3-002 | GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | One case with the facts projection and `inputAsOf[]`: `caseNo`, `productGroup`, `stageCode`, `routeState`, `routeCode`, `status`, `ownerRef`, `entryDate`, `dpdAtEntry`, `totalOutstandingAtEntry`, `exposureBand`, `prescriptionDate`, `inputAsOf[]` | Case record R, scope applied through the authorise contract | 401; 403 MSG-P4-002; 404 MSG-P4-003; 503 MSG-GEN-006 |
| API-P3-003 | GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline` | The outcome as a decision item and a task item, newest first, with type, actor, time and reference | Case record R, scope applied | 401; 403 MSG-P4-002; 404 MSG-P4-003; 503 MSG-GEN-006 |

Each `inputAsOf` element is `inputCode`, `businessDate` and `ageDays`, one element per input, with the two codes `TOTAL_BALANCE` and `POSTAL_ADDRESS` and no other. The route's `inputFacts` element takes `businessDate` and `ageDays` from this answer and `limitDays` and `stale` from `rwb-decision`'s answer, so no limit is computed twice. The field-level type and order of the projection are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2216; ASM-3645). The work list of a case owner is served by the existing `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/me/tasks` operation and the queue views by RWB-P3-E2011-APP.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| POST `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 `rwb-access`, RWB-P4-E1037-CON | The Case record right and the scope of the caller for the case, before any fact is read; the contract carries no C row in this key and its shape is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2216; ASM-3648) |
| GET `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/accounts/{accountId}` | P1 `rwb-source-data`, DP-05 | The current total balance and days past due of the primary account with `data_as_of`, one hop, 2 s |
| GET `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/customers/{customerId}` | P1 `rwb-source-data`, DP-05 | The contact fact the postal address input comes from: its business date only. Which field carries that date is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2216; ASM-3646) |
| GET `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` | P1 `rwb-source-data`, RWB-P1-E1015-CON | The ACE business date in force, against which each input's age is counted |
| GET `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | P7 `rwb-decision` | The decision items of the case for the timeline read: final call, reason code, approver reference, time. No approval, notice or template content is read |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (DP-11, ADR-020). No row reads a table of another service, and this story adds no `v_ace_*` read of its own (GAP-2216; ASM-3646).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library; consumed by P7 | caseId | the hash-chained record of the task raise: decision code, actor, case, notice and approval references, final call, reason code, time |

CloudEvents 1.0 envelope with identifiers, codes and dates and no personal data and no notice content; written to the outbox in the same transaction as the task and the assignment and relayed by the library (DP-03, DP-09). This slice publishes nothing on `rwb.case.events.v1`: the status move that would publish `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` is RWB-P3-E2013-APP's.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision.ApprovalRefused.v1` | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | P7 | Case router, inbox dedupe by event ID, `signalWithStart` of `CaseWorkflow`, then `raiseRedressTask` |
| `rwb.decision.ApprovalReturned.v1` | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | P7 | The same path, with the approver's question on the task |

Both names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2216; ASM-3643): one event per outcome keeps a refusal and a return apart; a rename is a contract change of RWB-P7-E2014-CON and changes nothing in this story's behaviour. `ApprovalRequested` is RWB-P3-E2013-APP's and is not consumed here.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Kind | Queue | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CaseWorkflow` | Parent workflow, one per case, workflow ID = case ID | `rwb-case` | The case service's existing workflow; this story registers one activity on it and starts no workflow of its own |
| `raiseRedressTask` | Activity | `rwb-case` | Status and reference checks, task and assignment write, the local record and the outbox in one transaction |
| `RecordAndApply` | Activity, from the kit | `rwb-case` | Writes the record and the outbox rows with the task write in one transaction |

The activity input is the case reference, the notice reference, the approval reference, the final call and the reason or question; it carries no notice body, no addressee and no personal data.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. This story adds no Schedule and reads no scheduler table: the task due time comes from the reference row of its task code, and the case clocks are this service's own `timer` rows read by `GET /cases/{caseId}/timers` (DP-10).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `recovery_case` | P3 (`rwb_case`) | The case facts, the owner reference and the optimistic lock version; read only, no status write |
| `task` | P3 (`rwb_case`) | The redress task of a refused or returned notice |
| `assignment` | P3 (`rwb_case`) | The one assignee row naming the case owner for that task |
| `lov_value`, `reference_row`, `reference_version` | P3 (`rwb_case`) | Element type, task status, role and assignment reason lists, read through DP-07 |
| `parameter_catalog`, `parameter_value` | P3 (`rwb_case`) | The case-side switch, read through DP-06 |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library, in `rwb_case` | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects (DP-09) |

`notice`, `template` and `merge_field` are P6's, `approval` and `decision_log_entry` are P7's, `permission`, `masking_rule` and `delegation_limit` are P4's, `interaction` is P1's and `document` is P5's; none is read and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01). The task holds the notice and approval references as values.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `case/noticefacts`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.noticefacts`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

Instances in this slice: DP-01 is the read of `recovery_case` and the writes to `task` and `assignment`; DP-03 is the local record of the task raise; DP-05 is the balance, arrears and contact business dates read on the `rwb-source-data` contract and never from a `v_ace_*` view; DP-06 is the case-side switch; DP-07 is the LOV-ELEMENT, LOV-TASK-STATUS, LOV-ROLE and LOV-ASSIGN-REASON read; DP-09 is the inbox, the outbox and the idempotency key; DP-10 is the existing `CaseWorkflow` that receives the outcome, with no Schedule; DP-11 is the authorise call and the three source-data calls with mocks and the 2 s budget; DP-13 is the base path; DP-19 is the composite route.

DP-08 is relied on without being declared: the authorise answer is consumed on the `rwb-access` contract as one hop (DP-11) and this story adds no guard library and no permission row (GAP-2216; ASM-3648). The metadata H row is None because the platform contracts the DP rows name — the decision-record, parameters, reference-data, outbox and inbox, workflow-kit and composite-route contracts — are pulled by the `rwb-case` baseline stories this slice builds on; the slice is therefore Day 1 and builds against RWB-P7-E2014-CON and its fakes.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CaseFactsController | REST controller | The facts projection and `inputAsOf[]` on API-P3-002 and the problem responses with their message IDs |
| CaseFactsProjection | Service | The case facts and arrears facts of `recovery_case`, the owner reference and the version lock |
| InputAgeService | Service | One `inputAsOf` element per input: business date from the read and age in calendar days to the business date in force; no limit and no stale flag |
| SourceDataClient | Adapter | The account and customer reads and the freshness read, one hop, 2 s, breaker, GET retried once with jitter |
| AuthoriseCheck | Client | The Case record right and the scope answer of `rwb-access`, cached, refusing closed |
| NoticeOutcomeListener | Kafka consumer with the inbox | The refusal and return events, deduplicated by event ID, `signalWithStart` on `CaseWorkflow` |
| RaiseRedressTaskActivity | Temporal activity | Status and reference checks, task and assignment write, local record and outbox in one transaction |
| RedressTaskService | Service | The task code and due time from reference data, the one open task per notice, the assignee taken from the case owner |
| TimelineOutcomeAssembler | Service | The decision item of `rwb-decision`'s ledger read and the task item of `task` on API-P3-003, newest first, with no notice content |

**Database and migrations.** Reads `recovery_case`; writes `task`, `assignment`, the local record, the inbox and the outbox. No case update. Constraint: partial unique index `ux_task_open_notice_redress ON task (case_id, notice_ref) WHERE notice_ref IS NOT NULL AND status IN ('OPEN','IN_PROGRESS')` (BR6). Column: `task.notice_ref`, because TSD P3 v3 T3.1 gives `task` no column for the notice, and its name and type are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2216; ASM-3644). Index `ix_task_case_status ON task (case_id, status)` for the work list and the timeline. Migration `V2014_1__case_notice_redress_task.sql` in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15).

**Configuration and reference data.** LOV-ELEMENT, LOV-TASK-STATUS, LOV-ROLE and LOV-ASSIGN-REASON through DP-07 (RWB-P3-E1043-CON), so no task code, element type, role or due time is a constant (GAP-2216; ASM-3644). The case-side switch is a parameter row through DP-06 (RWB-P3-E1042-CON): off means the listener does not subscribe, no task is raised, and the panel still answers. The age limits stay `rwb-decision`'s rows; this story reads none and compares none. The legacy flag `rwb.decision.notice-approval` is not read here.

**Build steps.**

1. `CaseFactsProjection` and `CaseFactsController` with the facts and arrears projection under API-P3-002, and the absence of approval, notice and rule fields; AC1.
2. `SourceDataClient` and `InputAgeService` with the two input codes, the business date and the age in calendar days; AC2 with 13 and 11 December 2026, and the unanswered read (X3, X11).
3. `AuthoriseCheck` with the right, the scope, the refusal by default and the cache; AC3 with `RW-PHONECOL` and an out-of-scope case, and the unanswered call (X9).
4. `NoticeOutcomeListener` with the inbox, the dedupe and `signalWithStart`; AC6 and the repeat.
5. `RaiseRedressTaskActivity` and `RedressTaskService` for a refusal and a return, with the assignment to the case owner; AC4, AC5 and the closed case of AC8.
6. The decision-record failure path, with the record written last; AC8.
7. `TimelineOutcomeAssembler` against the decision-log fake with the no-notice-content assertion; AC7.
8. The contract-fake run of both events in isolation and the drift test against RWB-P7-E2014-CON, so the slice builds before the approval story is live.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; every fact is answered with its as-of date and every input with its business date and age in days and nothing else; a caller without Case record R is refused before a fact is read; every refused or returned notice has exactly one open redress task on its case, assigned to the case owner, with the reason or question and its local record; the outcome shows on the timeline with no notice content; and a repeated event raises nothing.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller's role does not carry Case record right R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, on the case read behind the authorise answer |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. | This story, on the case read |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A consumed call does not answer in time | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. | This story, on the source-data and ledger calls |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The case changed while the outcome was applied | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. | This story, on the version check |
| MSG-P7-003 | The local decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on the record writer |
| MSG-P7-006 | An input is past its age limit | {input} is {days} days old, past its limit. Refresh it before you decide. | `rwb-decision`, never this story |
| MSG-P7-002 | A preparer tries to decide | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. | `rwb-decision`, never this story |

The {action} value names the action and nothing else — here "open the case facts of a D7.1 notice" — and the problem response carries the capability area in its `detail` beside the message ID, so a refusal is diagnosable without a case fact. Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set and `instance` naming the request; the event path answers no caller and records the error on the activity, letting the retry policy act. Thai text for each message follows DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built here. The screens are `rwb-decision`'s and the platform route's, and reach this service through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 (RWB-PLT-N001-CON).

| Screen | State | What this story supplies |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-11 Decision screen | Ready | The case facts with their as-of dates, the arrears facts, the owner, the entry date and the two input ages in days |
| SCR-11 Decision screen | Stale input | The as-of date and the age in days of the stale input; the state and the limit come from `rwb-decision` |
| SCR-11 Decision screen | Decided | No field of this story changes; the decided state is `rwb-decision`'s |
| SCR-18 Notice approval | Generated | The case number behind the panel header, and nothing of the notice |
| SCR-04 Case timeline | Loaded | The outcome as the decision item of `rwb-decision`'s ledger and the task item of `task`, newest first |
| SCR-01 My work and the case owner's queue view | Loaded | The redress task of a refused or returned notice, with the reason or question and the notice reference |

The panel layout, the masked rendering of the postal address and the composite route's field list are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2216; ASM-3645); the panel and the queue screens are RWB-P7-E2014-APP and RWB-P3-E2011-APP, and this story changes no screen behaviour, field order or mask.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the task code, element type, task status, owner role, assignment reason, due time and the two input codes are data rows read with the version in force; the Java code holds no task code, element type, status or role literal (BR9).
- No personal data in logs, events, records, workflow history, tests or prompts: the panel, the task, the record and the timeline item carry the case number, codes, amounts and dates; the postal address is named `POSTAL_ADDRESS` and only its business date and age are returned, and a test scans the task text and the record for any part of the synthetic address (BR10).
- No read of another service's tables and no cross-schema read (DP-01): `notice`, `template`, `approval`, `decision_log_entry`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `delegation_limit`, `interaction` and `document` are never queried here.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract (DP-05, ADR-010): the balance, arrears and contact facts arrive on `rwb-source-data`'s reads with `data_as_of`, and this story adds no `v_ace_*` read (GAP-2216; ASM-3646).
- A fact is never shown as current without its date: an input whose business date is unknown is answered as unavailable and the panel marks it (BR2).
- The authorise answer is required before any fact is read and fails closed: a missing, unparseable or unanswered answer is a refusal, never an allow (BR3).
- The task, the assignment, the local record and the outbox row commit in one transaction, and a task that cannot be recorded does not exist (BR8, R-UNI-39).
- One hop and 2 s on every call; a timeout never shows a stale fact as current and never raises a task twice (DP-11).
- The case status and the resume state of the routing rule are not written here, so this slice cannot put a case in a state its rules did not name.
- Every example is synthetic; no production payload is copied into a test, a fake or a message.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: deployment side of RWB-E2-014 for rwb-decision — the pipeline and image, the configuration and secrets, the migration run and the drift gate, the gateway-bff route registration and its budget, the cache warm-up, the dashboards and alerts, the run book and the rollback. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **DevOps engineer of the service**, I want **the D7.1 approval screen of rwb-decision deployed as one pipeline and one image behind the gateway-bff composite route, with its schema, its secrets, its reference-data warm-up, its route registration and timeout budget, its dashboards and alerts, and a run book with a rollback**, so that **the screen is served in SIT, UAT and PROD with the same configuration every time, an empty approval queue or a failing approval call is seen the same hour, and a bad release can be undone without a hand on a database**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The screen is the first place a person approves a decision in the Workbench, so the deployment is the first place a failure becomes a business failure: an approval screen that answers but cannot write a decision record creates no record, an empty queue that nobody notices stops the litigation pipeline, and a route registered with a budget shorter than its composed reads shows an officer a panel that never loads. This story fixes the deployment of that capability: the pipeline and the image, the configuration and the secrets, the migration run and its drift gate, the route registration and its budget, the warm-up of the lists the screen needs, the dashboards and alerts, the run book and the rollback (Architecture v5 slides 20, 29, 33 and 44; ADR-021; ADR-023).

The legacy key had no deployment story of its own: the screen shipped with the monolith, its configuration was a property file and its job set carried a daily decision-log copy to the data lake. In the target there is no lake, the copy is continuous Kafka ingest in the owning service (DP-17, ADR-018), and the deployment owns no lake extract, no data-lake credential and no lake job in the run book (GAP-1261; ASM-2225).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the Helm chart and the golden pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL), and they deploy a service as an API deployment and a worker deployment on the same task queue (Architecture v5 slide 33).
- The `rwb_decision` schema and its login exist and are owned by the ACE DB story of this service (RWB-PLT-NF06-DB and the DB story of this key), so the deployment applies the migrations of its own schema only (ADR-014, ADR-021).
- The per-service Flyway sequence, the drift gate and the forward-only PROD rule are the platform deployment of RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS; this story supplies the rwb-decision values and proves the run.
- The key store holds the service's database login, its Kafka client credentials and its Temporal codec key as secret references (NFR-052).
- The gateway-bff route baseline is published (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) and its route registry accepts a route with its downstream, its method, its budget and its breaker.
- The parameters and reference-data contracts of rwb-case are live for the warm-up reads (RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON).
- The decision-record library and the outbox relay are part of the image and read their topic from configuration (DP-03, DP-09).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Pipeline: build the image of rwb-decision from the template, run the unit and contract tests of RWB-P7-E2014-CON, and publish the image with its digest.
2. Pipeline: run the drift gate of the platform against the `rwb_decision` target schema before the deployment to SIT, UAT and PROD, and stop on a difference.
3. Deployment: on start, Flyway applies each pending script of the rwb-decision sequence once, in version order, and writes the checksum to `flyway_schema_history` in `rwb_decision`.
4. Deployment: the pod reads its database login, its Kafka credentials and its codec key from the key store, and its base path, its topic, its queue and its schema name from the chart values of the environment.
5. Deployment: the service warms its reference lists — LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, LOV-OVERRIDE-REASON and LOV-PRODUCT — and its age-limit parameters from the two rwb-case contracts before it reports ready.
6. Deployment: the gateway-bff route registration is applied with the downstream, the method, the 2 s budget and the breaker of the route, and the route health check passes through the edge.
7. Deployment: the smoke job reads the D7.1 queue through the route and the operation, and the deployment reports success only when both answer.
8. Operations: the dashboards show the approval-screen error rate, the latency of the route and of the three decisions, the age of the oldest waiting item and the size of the queue; the alerts fire on the conditions of section 14.
9. Operations: the run book names the checks, the rollback and the owner of each alert; a failed release is rolled back to the previous image digest and the previous route version.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The drift gate finds an object the migrations do not produce | The deployment stops before it starts and the object is named | MSG-P3-016 | AC3 |
| X2 | A secret cannot be read from the key store | The pod does not start and the failure is logged without the secret | None | AC2 |
| X3 | A warm-up read of the lists or the parameters fails | The pod stays not ready and retries; the screen is not registered as available | MSG-GEN-006 | AC5 |
| X4 | The route registration is refused by the route registry | The deployment fails and the previous route version stays | None | AC4 |
| X5 | The route answers beyond its budget under load | The alert fires and the route marks the panel temporarily unavailable | MSG-GEN-006 | AC4, AC6 |
| X6 | The D7.1 queue is empty for longer than the threshold | The empty-queue alert fires | None | AC6 |
| X7 | A release fails after the route registration | The rollback restores the previous image digest and the previous route version | None | AC7 |
| X8 | A lake extract, a lake credential or a lake job appears in the run book or the chart | The configuration test fails the pipeline | None | AC1, AC7 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the template, the chart, the schema and login, the key store, the route registry and the two rwb-case contracts |
| Negotiable | The alert thresholds, the dashboard names and the smoke schedule are settled with the platform observability team; the rules are fixed |
| Valuable | The capability can be released, observed and undone without a hand on a database, and a silent empty queue cannot happen |
| Estimable | One pipeline, one chart, one route registration, one warm-up step, one dashboard set and one run book |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs in a pipeline or an environment against the route and the service |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Deployment of the D7.1 approval screen

  Background:
    Given the service is deployed as an API deployment and a worker deployment on the queue rwb-decision
    Given its schema is rwb_decision and its own login reads and writes that schema only

  Scenario: AC1 The pipeline builds one image and deploys the capability with no lake element (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the golden pipeline of the platform template
    When the pipeline runs for this story
    Then it builds one image, runs the unit and contract tests of RWB-P7-E2014-CON and publishes the image with its digest
    Then the chart deploys the API deployment and the worker deployment on queue rwb-decision in namespace rwb-recovery
    Then the chart and the run book carry no data-lake extract, no data-lake credential and no lake job, because the lake is removed and the decision log ingest is continuous Kafka (GAP-1261; ASM-2225)
    Then the configuration test fails the pipeline when a lake element reappears

  Scenario: AC2 The configuration and the secrets are read from the environment and the key store (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the chart values of SIT, UAT and PROD
    When the pod starts
    Then it reads the database login, the Kafka client credentials and the Temporal codec key as secret references from the key store
    Then it reads the schema name rwb_decision, the base path /api/recovery/decision/v1, the topic rwb.decision.events.v1, the record topic rwb.decision-record.v1 and the queue rwb-decision from the chart values of the environment
    Then the parameter and reference-data endpoints of rwb-case are configuration values and not code
    Then a scan of the image, the chart, the pipeline files and the logs finds no credential and no secret value

  Scenario: AC3 The migrations run on start and the drift gate stops a drifted schema (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-decision Flyway sequence and the rwb_decision target schema
    When the service starts with pending scripts
    Then each script applies once in version order and flyway_schema_history records it with its checksum inside rwb_decision
    When a column has been added to rwb_decision by hand
    Then the drift gate of the platform stops the deployment before it starts and names the object with MSG-P3-016
    Then the deployment applies no script of another service and runs no clean in any profile

  Scenario: AC4 The gateway-bff route is registered with its downstream and its budget (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the route of the approval screen and the route registry of the edge
    When the deployment registers the route
    Then the registration names the public route, the downstream host of rwb-decision, the method, the 2 s budget and the breaker per downstream
    Then the route is registered only after the service reports ready and the warm-up of AC5 has finished
    Then the smoke job calls the route and the queue operation and the deployment fails when either answers outside its budget
    Then the budget of this screen is recorded, and the exact budget of a screen that composes three reads is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1270; ASM-2234)

  Scenario: AC5 The reference lists and the parameters are warm before the route is opened (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a cold start of the service
    When it becomes ready
    Then LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, LOV-OVERRIDE-REASON and LOV-PRODUCT are loaded from the reference-data contract and the two age-limit parameters from the parameters contract, each with its version
    Then a failed warm-up read keeps the pod not ready and retries, and the route is not opened to a pod without the lists
    Then the loaded versions are visible on the dashboard and the screen never shows a list version older than the one the service reports

  Scenario: AC6 The dashboards and the alerts cover the screen and its queue (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the observability of the service under ADR-023
    When the dashboard and the alert rules are reviewed
    Then the dashboard shows the error rate and the p95 latency of the route and of the three decisions, the age of the oldest waiting D7.1 item and the size of the queue
    Then an alert fires on a 5xx rate above the threshold, on a route latency above the budget, on a decision record that cannot be written and on an empty D7.1 queue for longer than the threshold
    Then the alert names the service, the route and the owner role, and carries no case fact and no personal data
    Then the thresholds and the empty-queue window are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1271; ASM-2235)

  Scenario: AC7 The run book and the rollback are proved (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the run book of the capability
    When a release is rolled back in SIT
    Then the run book names the checks of a failed approval call, a failed record write, an empty queue and a refused route registration, each with its message ID and its owner
    Then the rollback restores the previous image digest and the previous route version, and the schema is not rolled back because PROD is forward only
    Then no run book step asks for a hand change on rwb_decision, a lake extract or a credential in a file
    Then the rollback is proved in SIT inside the release window of the environment
```

These seven criteria are new, test only the deployment of the capability and repeat no legacy criterion.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One pipeline, one image and one chart per service; the same image is promoted through SIT, UAT and PROD with different values only | Architecture v5 slides 29 and 33; ADR-021 |
| BR2 | The service reads and writes `rwb_decision` only, with its own login, and applies no script of another service | ADR-014; DP-01 |
| BR3 | Every credential is a secret reference from the key store; no credential appears in a chart value, an image layer, a pipeline file, a log or a prompt | NFR-052 |
| BR4 | Migrations run on start and the drift gate stops a drifted schema before SIT, UAT and PROD; PROD is forward only | RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS BR3, BR4 |
| BR5 | The route is registered with its downstream, its budget and its breaker, and only after the service is ready and warm | Architecture v5 slides 10, 20 and 35; DP-19 |
| BR6 | Every cross-service call behind the screen is one hop with a 2 s budget; the route is never registered with a shorter budget than its composed reads need | ADR-020; DP-11 |
| BR7 | The lists and the parameters the screen needs are warmed with their version and the pod is not ready without them | DP-06, DP-07 |
| BR8 | Every service has its own dashboards and alerts (ADR-023), and an alert carries identifiers, codes and facts only | ADR-023; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR9 | An empty approval queue is a defect and is alerted, because an unapproved notice stops the dispatch run | REQ-APD-006; CTL-14 |
| BR10 | No data lake: the deployment carries no lake extract, no lake credential and no lake job, and JOB-13 is continuous Kafka ingest in the owning service | DP-17; ADR-018 |
| BR11 | A rollback restores the image and the route version and never rolls a schema back | RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS BR4; ADR-021 |
| BR12 | No business value in the chart or in a run book step: age limits, thresholds and route role codes stay parameters and reference data | DP-06, DP-07 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Pipeline starts | The contract tests pass and the drift gate passes | Building |
| Building | Image published | The digest is recorded | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migrations applied and the warm-up finished | The lists and the parameters carry a version | Registering |
| Registering | Route registered and the smoke job passes | The route and the queue operation answer inside the budget | Serving |
| Serving | A release fails or an alert is accepted | The run book step is taken | Rolled back |
| Rolled back | Previous image and route version restored | The schema is unchanged | Serving |

The approval and screen states themselves — READY, STALE_INPUT, DECIDED and the panel states — are the app story's and are declared in RWB-P7-E2014-CON; this story deploys them and observes them.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| DevOps engineer of the service | Owns the pipeline, the chart, the route registration, the dashboard and the run book |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Reads the deployment, the route and the alert state; runs the run book steps that are platform-side |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the deployment history and the alert history (Platform administration R) |
| Key store administrator | Owns the secret entries and their rotation; not a Workbench role |
| Platform route owner | Owns the route registry and approves a route registration and its budget |
| Platform observability owner | Owns the dashboard and alert platform and the threshold review |
| Service owner of rwb-decision | Accepts the release and the rollback |

No deployment step names a person; the run book names roles and on-call rotations, never individuals.

##### 11. Data

No business field is written by this story. The deployment writes the migration history inside `rwb_decision` and the deployment and alert records of the platform, and it reads the two contracts of rwb-case for the warm-up. The deployment record carries the service, the environment, the image digest, the migration versions applied, the drift result, the route version, `startedAt`, `endedAt` and a status.

The dashboard names, the alert thresholds and the empty-queue window are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1271; ASM-2235), and the budget of a screen that composes three reads is Not specified in the same way (GAP-1270; ASM-2234). The working values of this story are a 2 s route budget inherited from the platform, an alert on any 5xx in five minutes, and a 24-hour empty-queue window that follows the 1 working day service level of D7.1.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The deployment provides no REST operation; it registers the route of the screen, which is the edge's, and consumes the service's own operations to prove the release.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method and path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|
| GET `/api/recovery/approvals/{approvalId}` | PLT gateway-bff, RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The smoke probe of the registered route after the deployment and on every release |
| GET `/api/recovery/decision/v1/approvals` | P7 rwb-decision, RWB-P7-E2014-CON | The readiness probe of the queue read, with `decision=D7.1` and a page of one |

###### 12.3 Events published

None. A deployment publishes no event; the `DecisionRecorded` event of the screen is published by the service at run time and not by the deployment.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. A deployment consumes no event. The consumer groups of the service are created by its deployment from the topic configuration and are not event-schema elements of this story.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. `ApprovalWorkflow` is started at run time by RWB-P7-E2013-APP; the deployment starts no workflow and registers no activity, and it verifies only that the worker deployment polls the queue `rwb-decision`.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The two Schedules of the service — the rule promote at 00:01 (JOB-20) and the hash-chain check at 02:00 (JOB-14) — belong to the rule registry story and the decision log store story, and this deployment neither creates nor owns a Schedule.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The deployment owns no business table; Flyway writes `flyway_schema_history` inside `rwb_decision`, and `approval`, `decision_log_entry` and the library objects are the service's rows written at run time.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| gateway-bff route fake | The registered route answering the two panels with the 200, the 401, the 403, the 404 and the 503 examples, and a delayed answer beyond the budget | Smoke job, rollback test, NFR cases |
| rwb-decision readiness fake | The queue read answering a page with one D7.1 approval and an empty page for the empty-queue alert test | Smoke job, alert test |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 consumed | The route smoke probe and the queue readiness probe |
| Kafka | None | The deployment publishes and consumes no event |
| Temporal | None | The deployment starts no workflow; it verifies the worker polls `rwb-decision` |
| File | None | The image carries the migration scripts; no file crosses the deployment |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The pipeline stage that runs the contract tests and the drift gate for rwb-decision, the chart values per environment with the secret references, the warm-up step for the lists and the parameters, the route registration with its budget and breaker, the dashboard and the four alert rules, the smoke job and the run book with its rollback.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_decision`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-15 is not claimed as a pattern of this story: the per-service Flyway sequence, its drift gate and the forward-only PROD rule are the platform deployment of RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS, and this story supplies the rwb-decision values and proves the run (AC3). No pattern is claimed for DP-02, DP-04, DP-08, DP-12, DP-14, DP-16, DP-17, DP-18 or DP-20 either: this story declares no login, no rule package, no authorise call, no case workflow, no renamed topic, no integration adapter, no lake element, no ledger entry and no agent client. DP-17 is the removal this deployment must honour: the run book and the chart carry no lake extract, no lake credential and no lake job (GAP-1261; ASM-2225).

**Build steps**

1. Add the pipeline stage: build, the contract tests of RWB-P7-E2014-CON, the image digest and the drift gate.
2. Set the chart values per environment: `rwb_decision`, the base path, the topic, the record topic, the queue and the two rwb-case endpoints, with the secrets as key-store references.
3. Add the warm-up step of the lists and the parameters and make readiness depend on it.
4. Register the route with its downstream, its budget and its breaker after readiness, and add the smoke job.
5. Build the dashboard and the four alert rules of AC6, with role-based routing and no case fact in the alert payload.
6. Write the run book with the four checks, the rollback and the owner role of each alert.
7. Prove the rollback in SIT and prove the configuration test that fails on a lake element.

**Done when.** The seven cases of section 16 pass in SIT, the drift gate stops a drifted `rwb_decision`, the route is registered with its budget and the smoke job is green, the dashboard and the four alerts are live with a tested firing, and the rollback is proved inside the release window.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-016 | Drift found, checksum mismatch or a refused clean | Schema check failed in {schema}: {object}. The deployment was stopped. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A consumed call, the warm-up or the smoke probe does not answer in time | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The record write fails on a deployed release probe | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Platform administration R reads the deployment or the alerts | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

MSG-P3-016 is the migration message of RWB-PLT-E1044-OPS, carried unchanged; MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P4-002 are the platform catalog's and the decision record's. They are shown in the pipeline log, on the dashboard and in the run book, not to business users.

No new screen. SCR-44 Interface and job monitor shows the deployment, the migration run and the route registration of the service, with the image digest, the schema, the versions applied, the drift result and the route version. The approval screens themselves — SCR-10, SCR-11 and SCR-18 — are served through the composite route and are deployed here and built in RWB-P7-E2014-APP; their states belong to RWB-P7-E2014-CON.

##### 17. Guardrails

- One schema and one login per service: the deployment uses the login of rwb-decision and touches no other schema (DP-01, DP-02).
- No credential in a chart value, an image layer, a pipeline file, a log or a prompt; every account is a key-store reference.
- No drift gate bypass in SIT, UAT and PROD, and no clean and no undo in PROD; a fix is a new version through the pipeline.
- No business value in the chart or the run book: the age limits, the thresholds and the route role codes stay parameters and reference data.
- No personal data in a dashboard, an alert, a deployment record or a log: identifiers, codes and facts only.
- No data lake: no lake extract, no lake credential and no lake job in the chart, the pipeline or the run book (DP-17).
- One hop and a 2 s budget on every call behind the screen, and the route is registered with that budget and a breaker per downstream (DP-11, DP-19).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract; the deployment declares no ACE view and no SQL of its own.
- The rollback restores the image and the route version and never a schema; the forward-only rule stands (ADR-021).

##### 1. Story

As a **member of the integration and QA team**, I want **a repeatable cross-service journey harness that takes a generated D7.1 demand notice through the composite decision screen, an approval, a change of variant and a rejection, and through the refusals that protect the decision**, so that **the first decision in the Workbench with a person approving is proven end to end, with evidence, before the release is accepted**.

This story builds the harness and the evidence only. It builds no production screen, endpoint, table, workflow or schedule, it serves no production operation, it owns no table and it starts no workflow. The real behaviour is owned by the I stories RWB-P6-E1052-APP (notice generation from the current Approved template and its version), RWB-P7-E2014-APP (the D7.1 approval, the decision record and the approve and refuse checks), RWB-P6-E2014-APP (notice approve, regenerate and hold), RWB-P4-E2014-APP (authorise, role and scope) and RWB-P3-E2014-APP (case facts, case state and the case-owner task), and those stories block the ITG run.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy RWB-E2-014 journey crosses more than one service: rwb-comms holds the notice, its template and its version, rwb-decision holds the approval and the decision record, rwb-access answers the authorisation check, and rwb-case holds the case, the case facts with their business date, the case state and the queue that receives a rejected notice. A demand fee notice sent with a wrong amount or a wrong address can void the notice period and delay litigation, and today notices are checked on paper with no record of who approved what. Until the services are exercised together through the gateway, the program cannot show that the notice seen by the approver is the notice that is approved, that the inputs behind it are inside their age limits, and that only an approved version reaches the 16:00 dispatch run.

The harness gives one repeatable run per business date that proves the composite decision route composes the item one hop at a time inside the 2 s budget, that the decision record is written before the notice changes state, that a change of variant and a rejection both route through the notice contract, and that a failure in one service leaves the notice and the approval unchanged. It meets REQ-APD-002 and REQ-APD-006 at the integration level and leaves every business rule, every screen behaviour and every message where the owning stories put them. The measure it supports is unchanged: notices sent with an approval entry, target 100 percent.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The five I stories are published and deployed in the SIT environment: RWB-P6-E1052-APP (notice generation from the current Approved template, with its version and rule), RWB-P7-E2014-APP (D7.1 approval routing, approve and refuse, the decision record), RWB-P6-E2014-APP (approve, regenerate and hold on the notice), RWB-P4-E2014-APP (authorise for role RW-LITOFF and the Litigation rights) and RWB-P3-E2014-APP (case facts with business dates, case state and the case-owner task).
- gateway-bff is deployed with the composite route of DP-19 available for the decision screen. The gateway-bff composite decision-screen route path and its merge order: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0398; ASM-0573).
- The contract fakes of §12.8 are published from the owning services' OpenAPI documents, so the harness runs green from Day 1 before the I stories land.
- Templates DEMAND-MTG (TH version 2), the variant DEMAND-MTG-B and RECALL-MTG are Approved, and the input age parameters `rwb.decision.input-age-days.TOTAL_BALANCE` = 1 day and `rwb.decision.input-age-days.POSTAL_ADDRESS` = 30 days, and the reference data LOV-OVERRIDE-REASON with the values TEMPLATE_VARIANT and WRONG_PARTY, are loaded by the owning stories and read by the harness through their contracts (DP-06, DP-07).
- The harness environment, its synthetic seeding, its evidence format and its retention: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0398; ASM-0573).

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: seeds case RW-2026-000123 with product group MORTGAGE and the ACE-sourced case facts of business date 13 December 2026, the demand notice N-0201 generated at 08:10 on 14 December 2026 from template DEMAND-MTG TH version 2 under rule R-LIT-03 version LIT-2026.12 by preparer U-9211, and the approval A-0201 in state WAITING for role RW-LITOFF, all through the owning contracts or the §12.8 fakes.
2. Harness: opens the composite decision item for A-0201 through gateway-bff as approver U-9212 at 10:00 on 14 December 2026.
3. Harness: asserts the item carries the notice content of N-0201, the case facts with the business date of each input, the postal address masked per the masking rules, rule R-LIT-03 and its version, template DEMAND-MTG and version 2, preparer U-9211, and state Ready.
4. Harness: approves, then asserts the decision record with the inputs reference, rule version, template version, approver and time, the notice in state Approved, the case out of Waiting approval, the eligibility of the notice for the 16:00 dispatch run, and MSG-P7-004.
5. Harness: repeats the item on a second seeded approval and changes the variant to DEMAND-MTG-B with the coded reason TEMPLATE_VARIANT, then asserts the new notice version is the one approved, final call APPROVED_CHANGED, and that only the approved version is eligible for the 16:00 run.
6. Harness: repeats the item on a third seeded approval and rejects it with a reason, then asserts the notice in state Held with reason REFUSED_BY_APPROVER, one task with the reason in the case owner's queue, and final call REFUSED.
7. Harness: forces each failure of §5 through the fakes, asserts the status, the message and that the notice and the approval did not move, then returns the fake to its healthy answer and repeats the answer.
8. Harness: asserts the 16:00 eligibility from the notice state and the approval only; it does not call rwb-integration and does not prove delivery.
9. Harness: writes one run report per business date, keyed by story and business date; the report format and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0398; ASM-0573).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What the harness asserts | Message | ITG test case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The approver prepared the notice | A direct approve or refuse by preparer U-9211 returns 409 and the approval stays WAITING | MSG-P7-002 | TC-E2-014-04-ITG |
| X2 | An input is past its age limit | The item is state Stale input; a direct approve returns 409 and the notice stays Generated | MSG-P7-006 | TC-E2-014-05-ITG |
| X3 | The template was withdrawn after generation | 409; the notice is held under R-LIT-04 and nothing is approved | MSG-P6-003 | TC-E2-014-06-ITG |
| X4 | Reject without a reason | 422 for field reason; the notice stays Generated and no task is raised | MSG-GEN-001 | TC-E2-014-07-ITG |
| X5 | A change of variant without a coded reason | 422; no new notice version exists and nothing is approved | MSG-P7-005 | TC-E2-014-08-ITG |
| X6 | Another approver decided the item first | 409; the item reloads in state Decided showing approver U-9214 | MSG-GEN-004 | TC-E2-014-09-ITG |
| X7 | The user holds no Litigation right for the decision | 403 on a direct call; the composite route hides the approve and reject actions | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-014-11-ITG |
| X8 | The decision record cannot be written | 503; the notice stays Generated, the approval stays WAITING and the retry after the fake recovers decides once | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E2-014-12-ITG |
