| Testable | Each scenario of §7 is one automated journey with synthetic data and a machine-checkable result |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Approval screen for D7.1 demand and recall notices - wave 2 integration harness

  Background:
    Given the environment is SIT
    Given demand notice "N-0201" for case "RW-2026-000123" was generated at 08:10 on 14 December 2026 from template "DEMAND-MTG" "TH" version 2 under rule "R-LIT-03" version "LIT-2026.12", prepared by "U-9211"
    Given its approval "A-0201" is WAITING for role RW-LITOFF
    Given the case facts carry the total balance from the ACE account data of business date 13 December 2026 and the postal address of the addressee
    Given the input age limits are 1 day for "TOTAL_BALANCE" and 30 days for "POSTAL_ADDRESS"

  Scenario: AC1 The composite decision item through gateway-bff (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the harness calls the composite decision screen route at "Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0398; ASM-0573)" for approval "A-0201"
    When gateway-bff composes the answer from rwb-decision, rwb-comms, rwb-case and rwb-access
    Then the route returns the notice content of "N-0201", the case facts with each input's business date, the postal address masked, rule "R-LIT-03" version "LIT-2026.12", template "DEMAND-MTG" version 2, preparer "U-9211" and state "Ready"
    And every call in the composition is one hop with the 2 s budget
    And no service reads another service's schema
    And the run report holds one trace spanning the gateway and each owning service

  Scenario: AC2 Approve, the record first and the notice in the 16:00 run (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given approver "U-9212" holds RW-LITOFF and did not prepare "N-0201"
    When "U-9212" approves "A-0201" at 10:00 on 14 December 2026
    Then one decision record exists with the inputs reference and each input's business date, rule "R-LIT-03" version "LIT-2026.12", template "DEMAND-MTG" version 2, approver "U-9212" and decided at 10:00
    And notice "N-0201" is in state "Approved"
    And case "RW-2026-000123" leaves "Waiting approval"
    And the notice is eligible for the 16:00 dispatch run and the run report shows it
    And the answer carries MSG-P7-004

  Scenario: AC3 A change of variant and a rejection both route through the notice contract (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given "U-9212" opens "A-0201" at 10:00 on 14 December 2026
    When "U-9212" picks template variant "DEMAND-MTG-B" with coded reason "TEMPLATE_VARIANT" and approves
    Then rwb-comms returns a new notice version from "DEMAND-MTG-B" and that version is the one approved
    And one decision record exists with final call "APPROVED_CHANGED", the proposed template "DEMAND-MTG", the chosen "DEMAND-MTG-B" and the reason code "TEMPLATE_VARIANT"
    And only the approved version is eligible for the 16:00 dispatch run
    When "U-9212" rejects "A-0201" with reason "Addressee is a guarantor; a guarantor notice is needed"
    Then the notice is held with reason "REFUSED_BY_APPROVER" and one task with the reason is in the case owner's queue
    And the decision record shows final call "REFUSED" with the reason

  Scenario: AC4 Failure isolation and the refusals (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the total balance on a second notice comes from business date 11 December 2026, above the 1 day limit
    When the harness approves that stale-input approval through the approval contract
    Then the response is 409 with MSG-P7-006 and the notice stays "Generated"
    When template "DEMAND-MTG" version 2 is withdrawn at 09:30 on 14 December 2026 and the item is opened
    Then the response is 409 with MSG-P6-003 and the notice is held under R-LIT-04
    When preparer "U-9211" calls approve directly
    Then the response is 409 with MSG-P7-002 and the approval stays "WAITING"
    When "U-9212" rejects with an empty reason
    Then the response is 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for field "reason" and no task is raised
    When "U-9212" approves with variant "DEMAND-MTG-B" and no reason code
    Then the response is 422 with MSG-P7-005 and no new notice version exists
    When another approver "U-9214" approved "A-0201" at 10:01 and "U-9212" approves at 10:02 from a screen loaded at 10:00
    Then the response is 409 with MSG-GEN-004 and the item reloads in state "Decided" showing "U-9214"
    When the decision log write is forced to fail
    Then the response is 503 with MSG-P7-003 and the notice stays "Generated"
    When every fake returns its healthy answer and the same approve is repeated
    Then one decision record exists and the notice is in state "Approved"
```

These four criteria are new for the ITG harness and do not restate the app criteria owned by the I stories. The dispatch itself is out of scope: the harness asserts eligibility for the 16:00 window and never calls rwb-integration.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Demand and recall notices are approved through approval routing before dispatch; only an Approved notice is dispatched | REQ-APD-006; CTL-14 |
| BR2 | The approver sees the notice, the inputs with their age, the rule and the template version on one screen | REQ-APD-002 |
| BR3 | The person who prepared the notice may not approve or reject it | CTL-05; Admin and access model, section 6.2 |
| BR4 | An input past its age limit blocks the decision until refreshed | VR-P7-023-3; MSG-P7-006; parameters rwb.decision.input-age-days.* |
| BR5 | A notice is generated only from the current Approved template; a withdrawn template holds the notice | R-LIT-03; R-LIT-04 |
| BR6 | A change of template variant needs a coded reason and uses only an Approved variant of the same notice type and product | R-UNI-14; CTL-07; LOV-OVERRIDE-REASON |
| BR7 | A rejection needs a reason and returns the case to the case owner's queue | FEAT-APD-04 |
| BR8 | A decision that cannot be written to the decision log does not take effect | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |

The harness asserts these rules against the owning services; it re-implements none of them. No BR row is changed by this story.

##### 9. State transitions

The states below are the states the harness observes. The harness changes no case status, no approval state and no notice state itself; every transition is caused by a call to the owning service.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Case In progress | Recommendation routed for approval | Notice generated under R-LIT-03 | Waiting approval |
| Case Waiting approval | Approver accepts, or changes and accepts | Not the preparer; inputs inside their limits; template current; decision record written | In progress |
| Case Waiting approval | Approver rejects | Reason given; decision record written | In progress, with a task in the case owner's queue |
| Approval WAITING | Approve, change and approve, or refuse | The checks of §5 pass | DECIDED, with final call APPROVED, APPROVED_CHANGED or REFUSED |
| Notice Generated | Notice approved | Decision record written | Approved |
| Notice Generated | Notice refused | Decision record written | Held, reason REFUSED_BY_APPROVER |
| Notice Generated | Template withdrawn | R-LIT-04 | Held |

A refused or failed call leaves the approval in WAITING and the notice where it was.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-LITOFF Litigation officer | The role the harness drives: approves, changes the variant or rejects D7.1 notices they did not prepare (Litigation A) |
| RW-LEGAL Legal counsel | Also holds Litigation A for D7.1; used by the preparer case, where the preparer holds it and still may not decide |
| RW-HEADLIT Head of Litigation | Receives escalated D7.1 notices and decides them (Litigation A) |
| RW-CASEOWN Case owner | Receives the task of a rejected notice; may not approve (Litigation R) |
| SY-CASEWF | The case workflow that causes the router to be called when the notice is generated |

No approval level from the delegation of authority applies in this story: a D7.1 notice carries no amount limit, and delegation item 2.1.3 (delay of legal action) does not apply to issuing a notice. Authorisation is answered by rwb-access through POST /authorise.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness calls the owning services; it serves no operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; the 2 s timeout and the circuit breaker per downstream of DP-11 apply to every row.

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/approvals/{approvalId}` | P7 rwb-decision | The approval, its state, the rule and its version, and the source reference to the notice |
| POST | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/approvals/{approvalId}/approve` | P7 rwb-decision | Approve, or change the variant and approve; returns the decision record |
| POST | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/approvals/{approvalId}/refuse` | P7 rwb-decision | Refuse with a reason; returns the decision record |
| GET | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}` | P6 rwb-comms | The notice, its state, its type, its template version and its document reference |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case, the case state and the case facts with the business date of each input |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Role, scope and Litigation right check used by the composite route and by the direct calls |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | P7 rwb-decision | The decision records of the approval, the change and the refusal |

The composite decision screen route itself is gateway-bff (DP-19), owned by the platform edge story RWB-PLT-N001-CON. Its path and merge order are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0398; ASM-0573). The notice is approved and held through the rwb-decision approval operations, which call the notice owner; the harness does not call a notice approval path of its own.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness produces no event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | What the harness asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1 | rwb.comms.events.v1 | P6 rwb-comms | The generated notice and its template version are announced within 5 minutes of the seed call, so the approval is seen to follow a real generation |
| rwb.decision.ApprovalRequested.v1 | rwb.decision.events.v1 | P7 rwb-decision | One approval request exists for A-0201 and reaches the officer inbox path through gateway-bff |
| rwb.decision.ApprovalDecided.v1 | rwb.decision.events.v1 | P7 rwb-decision | One decision is announced per approval, with the final call, and none is announced for a refused call |
| rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 | rwb.decision-record.v1 | P7 rwb-decision (ledger); every service publishes its own record | The decision record of the approval, the change and the refusal reaches the ledger within 5 minutes of the call |

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness starts no workflow and adds no activity. The ApprovalWorkflow of the workflow kit and the notice dispatch workflow are started by the owning stories; the harness observes their effect through state, events and the decision record only.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The harness run is started by the test pipeline, not by a Temporal Schedule and not by Airflow. The 16:00 dispatch run (JOB-10) is the owning stories' schedule and is not started by the harness.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None.

| Fake | Serves | Stubbed answers |

| rwb-comms | GET /notices/{noticeId}, NoticeGenerated | Notice N-0201 in state Generated, DEMAND-MTG TH version 2, document reference present; a new version from DEMAND-MTG-B on regenerate; Held REFUSED_BY_APPROVER on hold; withdrawn template returning MSG-P6-003 |
| rwb-decision | GET /approvals/{approvalId}, approve, refuse, GET /decision-log, ApprovalRequested, ApprovalDecided | Approval A-0201 WAITING for RW-LITOFF with rule R-LIT-03 version LIT-2026.12; a decision record with final call APPROVED, APPROVED_CHANGED or REFUSED; 409 for the preparer, a stale input and a decided item; 422 for an empty reason and an uncoded change; a forced write failure for the 503 case |
| rwb-access | POST /authorise | Allow RW-LITOFF and RW-LEGAL for Litigation A on D7.1; refuse a role without the right with MSG-P4-002 |

The fakes are replaced by the real service as each I story lands, contract by contract. The harness environment, its synthetic seeding and the evidence format and retention: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0398; ASM-0573).

| Temporal | No | Starts no workflow and adds no activity or Nexus operation |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The platform H dependencies named by this table are delivered by the platform wave and are not repeated in the metadata H list. The blocking dependencies of this story are the five I stories.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Test harness | Runs one journey per business date, keyed by story and business date, and stops at the first failed assertion with the trace |
| DecisionScreenClient | Harness adapter | Calls the gateway-bff composite decision route and the seven consumed operations of §12.2 with the Idempotency-Key header where the operation requires one |
| FakePack | WireMock project | Serves rwb-comms, rwb-decision, rwb-access and rwb-case from the published OpenAPI documents and AsyncAPI documents of §12.8 |
| SchemaBoundaryCheck | Assertion | Fails the run on any cross-schema reference in the trace, so a service never reads another service's tables |
| InputAgeCheck | Assertion | Reads the age limit of each input and asserts the business date on the item, including the stale total balance of 11 December 2026 against the 1 day limit |
| DecisionOrderCheck | Assertion | Asserts the decision record exists before the notice changes state, and that the record carries the inputs reference, rule version, template version, approver, time and final call |
| RunReportWriter | Reporter | Writes one run report with the trace and the per-assertion result; format and retention Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0398; ASM-0573) |

**Environment and test data**

- Environment: SIT, one namespace, the owning services deployed from their wave 2 builds or replaced by the §12.8 fakes. Harness repository, environment, seeding and evidence: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0398; ASM-0573).
- Data: synthetic case RW-2026-000123, demand notice N-0201 generated at 08:10 on 14 December 2026, approval A-0201 WAITING for RW-LITOFF, the sequence approvals of the change and the refusal, preparer U-9211, approvers U-9212 and U-9214, the total balance of business date 13 December 2026 with the stale 11 December 2026 copy, the address masked, reason codes TEMPLATE_VARIANT and WRONG_PARTY, and the 16:00 window. No production record is copied.
- Reset: each run starts from the seeded state, so a repeated run is deterministic and the same report is produced.

**Build steps**

1. Build JourneyRunner and DecisionScreenClient against the published OpenAPI documents of the owning services and the gateway-bff route contract.
2. Publish FakePack for the four owning services from the same documents and prove the harness runs green from Day 1 on the fakes.
3. Add the composite decision item assertion of AC1, including the 2 s per-call budget, the masked address and the SchemaBoundaryCheck.
4. Add the approve journey of AC2 with DecisionOrderCheck, asserting the decision record before the notice state moves and the 16:00 eligibility.
5. Add the change and the refusal journeys of AC3, then the InputAgeCheck and the refusals of AC4 with the stale 11 December 2026 input.
6. Add the concurrent decision and the decision-log failure of AC4, then the repeat after the fake recovers, and prove nothing moved in each case.
7. Replace each fake with the real service as its I story lands, contract by contract, keeping the same assertions.
8. Publish the run report per business date and add the pass/fail gate agreed with QA; the gate definition: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0398; ASM-0573).

**Feature switch:** the harness has no production feature flag and runs in the test environment only. The production switch it exercises is `rwb.decision.notice-approval` from the legacy solution plan: with the switch off the composite route offers no approve or reject action and no notice becomes Approved, and with it on the journey of §7 runs to its end.

**Done when:** the journey runs green against the five deployed I stories in SIT, the run report for the business date holds every assertion of §7 and §16 with its trace, and the pass/fail gate agreed with QA is met for one full business date.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-002 | The preparer opens or acts on the item | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-P7-006 | An input is past its age limit | {input} is {days} days old, past its limit. Refresh it before you decide. |
| MSG-P6-003 | The template was withdrawn | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-P7-005 | Change of variant without a coded reason | Enter the reason you are not following the recommendation. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Reject without a reason | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Another approver decided first | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-004 | Approved | Approved. The case moves to {state}. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Entry cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the Litigation right for D7.1 | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values; it does not own the message text. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the input age limits, the override reasons, the templates and their variants, the route role and the 16:00 window are data held by the owning services; the harness reads them and never holds a copy.
- No personal data in logs, tests, traces or reports: the postal address is masked in every answer the harness reads, the reason text is not logged, and the harness uses synthetic parties and stores IDs, business dates and assertions only.
- No read of another service's schema: every read goes through the owner's contract, the SchemaBoundaryCheck fails the run on a cross-schema reference, and only rwb-source-data reads the ACE views.
- No production data and no outside system: the harness calls only the owning services and their fakes, never a production endpoint and never WIN; it does not dispatch, and it proves no delivery.
- The harness changes nothing: it approves, changes and refuses only through the owning contracts, and it never writes a notice state, an approval state or a decision record itself.
- Only an approved notice version is eligible for dispatch: the harness asserts eligibility from the notice state and the approval, and fails the run when a changed version other than the approved one is eligible.
- One hop only: the harness fails a run when the trace shows a call chain deeper than the gateway and one owner.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-015 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the two read operations that put the clocks and the deviation flag on the case record view — `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` with its `deviations[]` and `deviationsAvailable`, and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` with its owner-role, escalation and warning fields — together with the consumed S8, P7 and P4 contracts, the event and workflow elements the capability depends on, the nine contract tables and three contract fakes**, so that **the app, operations and test stories of this legacy key build against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1 and a deviation answer, an approver answer or a timer field can never drift between rwb-case, rwb-deviation and rwb-decision without a failing build**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The capability of RWB-E2-015 shows three sources on one screen: rwb-case for the case and its timers, rwb-deviation for the deviations, rwb-decision for the approver of each deviation, and rwb-access for the authorisation check. Two of those answers are composed inside rwb-case, so their field names, their empty and degraded shapes and their timeouts are the parts most likely to drift silently: an approver field renamed in the S8 or P7 contract would empty a panel at run time, and a `deviations[]` that disappears when the deviation service is slow would hide the on-hold banner instead of degrading one section.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_case`, REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1`, event names `rwb.case.<Event>.v1`, task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`. It records that TimerBreached is event #19 of the catalogue and stays on `rwb.case.events.v1` while JOB-05 Timer check and the TimerDue event are retired (Architecture v5 slides 42 and 44), so no contract in this story declares a timer-check job, a timer-check topic or a timer-check Schedule.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the document, topic and event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the retry and `.dlt` topic convention are the platform baseline (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The case record view contract RWB-P3-E1035-CON is published, so the Case resource this story extends has one owner document and the added fields are an additive change to it.
- The timer contract RWB-P3-E1028-CON is published, so the meaning of `warn_at`, `expires_at`, `inWarning`, `escalated_to_role`, `escalated_at` and `nextEscalationRole` is fixed by the story that writes them and not by this one.
- The operations and their owners are taken from the Ownership Map only; this document never declares another service's operation as provided.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the additive change to the rwb-case OpenAPI 3.1 document: the deviation object, `deviations[]` and `deviationsAvailable` on the Case resource, and the five added fields on the Timer resource.
2. Fix the ordering rule of the timers answer and the ordering rule of `deviations[]`, so two consumers never sort differently.
3. State the degraded shapes: the case answer with `deviationsAvailable` false and the empty list, the timers answer unchanged, and the timer answer never degraded by a deviation failure.
4. Record the three consumed operations with their owner, their use and the 2 s budget, and map every failure to the error envelope and a message ID.
5. Record the event elements: TimerBreached as event #19 of `rwb.case.events.v1` published by the timer story, DecisionRecorded on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and the three events the timer story consumes.
6. Record the workflow element: the durable timer inside CaseWorkflow and the projection it writes, with no timer-check Schedule anywhere.
7. Publish the nine contract tables of section 12 and the three contract fakes.
8. Add the contract tests: schema validation, ordering, the degraded shape, the 2 s budget, the error mapping, the drift between a fake and the document, and the absence of a retired element.
9. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P3-E2015-APP, RWB-P3-E2015-OPS and the wave 2 harness RWB-ITG-E2015-ITG.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 500 with the error envelope | MSG-P3-030 | AC1 |
| X2 | A consumer cannot deserialise a TimerBreached event | The registry validation fails the build; the event is not published | None | AC5 |
| X3 | A field is renamed or removed within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1 |
| X4 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC6 |
| X5 | The consumed S8 read path is not in the Ownership Map | The row carries the gap and the assumption, and the fake is derived from the S8 published document | None | AC4 |
| X6 | A retired element reappears in the document, a job or a topic | The absence test fails: no timer-check Schedule, no TimerDue event, no timer-check topic | None | AC5 |
| X7 | A field-level definition is missing from the source material | The field is marked with the placeholder and one gap row is carried | None | AC2 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the two same-service contracts it extends and the Ownership Map only |
| Negotiable | Field-level detail is settled with the consumers; the two operations, the nine tables and the retired elements are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app, operations and test stories of this legacy key on Day 1 and every consumer of the clocks and the deviation flag |
| Estimable | Two documents, one additive change, three consumed operations, nine contract tables, three fakes and seven contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Contract baseline of the clocks and the deviation flag on the case record view

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule of the platform library is in force
    Given the rwb-case event types are CaseCreated, CaseAllocated, CaseAllocationFailed, CaseTransferred, CaseStateChanged and TimerBreached
    Given the case record view contract RWB-P3-E1035-CON is published with the Case resource

  Scenario: AC1 The OpenAPI document declares the two read operations with the added fields (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-case is published with this change
    When it is validated against the OpenAPI 3.1 schema
    Then it validates with no error
    Then it declares GET /cases/{caseId} with the Case resource and GET /cases/{caseId}/timers with the Timer array, both under the base /api/recovery/case/v1 and owned by rwb-case
    Then the Case resource carries deviations[] and deviationsAvailable beside prescriptionDate, stageClockStart, deviationOpen and legalHold
    Then the Timer resource carries nextStepOwnerRole, escalatedToRole, escalatedAt, nextEscalationRole and inWarning beside timerType, startedAt, expiresAt, warnAt, paused, status and escalationLevel
    Then both operations name their security right, their 2 s budget and their error responses 401, 403, 404 and 503
    Then every added property is optional in the schema, so a consumer of the previous version keeps working

  Scenario: AC2 The composed deviation object and its availability flag (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the deviation object declared in the document
    When it is compared with the fields the S8 contract returns
    Then it carries deviationCode, raisedAt, handlerUserId, approverUserId, pausedState, contactStop, clearedAt and outcome, with approverUserId optional
    Then deviations[] is ordered by raisedAt ascending and holds the open deviations before the cleared ones of the same date
    Then deviationsAvailable is a boolean and is the only signal a consumer uses to distinguish "no deviations" from "the deviations could not be read"
    Then the document states that a false value leaves prescriptionDate, stageClockStart, deviationOpen and legalHold in place, carries an empty deviations[] and one MSG-GEN-006 entry in the section error list

  Scenario: AC3 The timer resource fixes the ordering and the five added fields (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the Timer array declared in the document
    When its ordering and its fields are reviewed
    Then the array is ordered by expiresAt ascending and a timer without expiresAt is last
    Then nextStepOwnerRole and nextEscalationRole are role codes and not display names
    Then escalatedToRole and escalatedAt may be empty and inWarning is a boolean derived from warnAt and the business date
    Then the document states that inWarning is read from the projection and never recomputed by a consumer, and that warnAt is computed where the timer is written

  Scenario: AC4 The three consumed contracts carry their owner and the 2 s budget (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed operations of the document
    When they are compared with the Ownership Map
    Then GET /api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations names S8 rwb-deviation as its owner
    Then GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId} names P7 rwb-decision as its owner
    Then POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise names P4 rwb-access as its owner
    Then every consumed row states one hop, the 2 s timeout, the GET retry once with jitter and the breaker per downstream
    Then the S8 read path carries the ownership gap in the document until the map is corrected
    Then every failure of a consumed call maps to 401, 403, 404, 503 or the degraded shape of AC2 and never to an empty timer answer

  Scenario: AC5 The event and workflow elements are recorded, and the retired ones absent (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the event section of the document
    When it is reviewed against the event catalogue
    Then TimerBreached is declared as event 19 on rwb.case.events.v1 with caseId as the key and no personal data field
    Then DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1, DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared on rwb.deviation.events.v1 and RulePackageInForce on rwb.decision.events.v1 are declared as consumed or depended on by the capability, each with its owner
    Then the workflow element states that the durable timer runs inside CaseWorkflow on task queue rwb-case in namespace rwb-recovery and writes the timer projection
    Then the document declares no timer-check Schedule, no timer-check job and no TimerDue event

  Scenario: AC6 The nine contract tables are complete and the fakes match them (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the contract section of this story
    When the nine sub-tables are reviewed
    Then each of 12.1 to 12.9 is present and names its owner from the Ownership Map, with None where the element is empty
    Then 12.6 records None and names JOB-05 as retired
    Then the three contract fakes answer the paths and payloads of 12.2 and the deviation and approver shapes of 12.1
    Then the contract tests compare each fake with the document and fail on any drift
```

These six criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only; they restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P3-E2015-APP. The wave 2 harness RWB-ITG-E2015-ITG consumes this baseline and copies none of these criteria.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/case/v1`; the document never declares another service's path as provided | DP-13; Architecture v5 slide 41 notes |
| BR2 | Event names are `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1` on the topic `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, with retry and `.dlt` topics | DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR3 | Every event carries the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, is keyed by caseId and carries no personal data | Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43 notes; DP-09 |
| BR4 | A read declares no Idempotency-Key; a POST declares it and stores its response | Architecture v5 slide 11; DP-09 |
| BR5 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition; the business message texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story | Architecture v5 platform baseline; Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR6 | A schema change is additive within a major version; a breaking change is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |
| BR7 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-case; a consumed operation is described as consumed, never as provided | Ownership Map v1 |
| BR8 | The timer projection is read as data: `inWarning` and the escalation fields are never recomputed by a consumer, and `warn_at` belongs to the timer story | Ownership Map ruling ASM-0078; RWB-P3-E1028-CON |
| BR9 | No timer-check Schedule, no timer-check job and no TimerDue event is declared: the clock is a durable Temporal timer inside CaseWorkflow | DP-10; Architecture v5 slides 42 and 44 |
| BR10 | No business value is fixed in the contract: the warning days, the escalation roles and the timeouts stay data or service configuration | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-case (P3); base `/api/recovery/case/v1`.

| GET | `/cases/{caseId}` | Case with `prescriptionDate`, `stageClockStart`, `deviationOpen`, `legalHold`, `deviations[]` and `deviationsAvailable` | Case record R |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/timers` | Timer[] ordered by `expiresAt`, with the five added fields of AC3 | Case record R |

Both operations answer 401, 403, 404 and 503 with the error envelope; neither takes an Idempotency-Key.

| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The role, scope and Case record right check, faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retry once with jitter and a breaker per downstream.

**Deliverables.** The additive change to `openapi/rwb-case-v1.yaml`, the deviation object as a shared component, the AsyncAPI fragment of `rwb.case.events.v1` that names TimerBreached, the contract README rows for the ordering, the degraded shape and the retired elements, and the three WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |

| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |

No pattern is claimed for the parameters contract (DP-06): this capability reads no parameter and re-applies no warning day.

**Build steps**

1. Add the deviation object and the two added properties to the Case resource; validate the additive rule of AC1 in the pipeline.
2. Add the five properties to the Timer resource and the ordering rule of AC3.
3. Write the degraded-shape rule of AC2 as a schema constraint and a README row, so a consumer cannot read an empty list as "no deviations".
4. Record the three consumed rows with their owner, their budget and the gap row of the S8 path; map every failure code.
5. Record the five event rows and the workflow row, and add the absence test for the retired job, topic and event of AC5.
6. Publish the three fakes and the seven contract tests; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build.
7. Baseline tag and the consumer sign-off note, including the S8, P7 and P4 owners and the wave 2 harness.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI and AsyncAPI artefacts validate in the pipeline, the seven contract tests pass, the three fakes answer every consumed path and the drift test is green, and the app, operations and test stories have accepted the baseline.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the warning days, the escalation roles, the deviation codes and the timeouts stay data, reference data or service configuration.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: IDs, codes, dates and amounts only; `handlerUserId` and `approverUserId` are staff identifiers and no customer field is declared.
- The contract names only rwb-case tables and only operations owned by rwb-case; the S8, P7 and P4 operations are consumed and faked, never declared as provided (DP-01).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- ACE data is reached only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views; this document declares no ACE view and no cross-schema join.
- No retired element is reintroduced: the absence test of AC5 fails a build that declares a timer-check Schedule, a timer-check job or a TimerDue event.
- Every example in the document is synthetic; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The error envelope, the CloudEvents envelope and the naming rule come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-015 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **the case record view to show every timer of the case with its due date, status, warning state and escalation path, the prescription date, and any deviation flag with its handler, its approver and its return point, served by rwb-case from its own timer and case rows, the rwb-deviation contract and the rwb-decision decision log**, so that **the next deadline and the reason a case left its path are visible on the case without reading another team's list**.

The two read operations of this story are `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}`, which now carries `deviations[]` and `deviationsAvailable`, and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers`, which now carries `nextStepOwnerRole`, `escalatedToRole`, `escalatedAt`, `nextEscalationRole` and `inWarning`. The clock itself is no longer a five-minute job: it is a durable Temporal timer inside CaseWorkflow on task queue `rwb-case`, owned by RWB-P3-E1028-APP, and this story renders what that timer and the deviation service record.

##### 2. Business rationale

Deadlines are agreed by email today, and litigation was not filed for debtors who met the criteria because nobody saw the prescription date in time (control CTL-18). A deviation pauses the stage clock but never the prescription clock (REQ-DVH-002), so the case owner must see both, with who holds the deviation, who approved it and where the case returns. This story puts every timer, the escalation state and the deviation flag on the case record view and meets REQ-WKM-004, REQ-WKM-005, REQ-DVH-002 and REQ-DRI-001. The measure is that every open case's record view shows its next due date and its prescription date, and that the escalation state of a breached service level is readable without the case moving.

In the target the monolith's single screen model is split into one composite route at the edge and two answer sources behind it (DP-19). gateway-bff calls rwb-case twice, for the case and for the timers, in parallel with rwb-source-data for the account and customer facts, and merges the three answers into the screen model (Architecture v5 slide 10). rwb-case itself does not chain: it reads its own `recovery_case`, `timer` and `task` rows, then calls rwb-deviation once for the deviations of the case and rwb-decision once for the approvers on their decision log entries (Architecture v5 slide 13, P3 row: R to P4, R to P7, T and E to S8). A deviation that cannot be read inside the two-second budget degrades the deviation section only, and the on-hold banner still shows from `recovery_case.deviation_open`, so a slow deviation service never hides the next deadline.

The legacy `timer` row keeps its place: it stays an rwb_case projection behind the timers operation, while the clock that fires is a durable Temporal timer inside CaseWorkflow (DP-10). JOB-05 Timer check and the TimerDue event are retired (Architecture v5 slides 42 and 44); TimerBreached stays the nineteenth event of the catalogue on `rwb.case.events.v1`. The two escalation fields the legacy escalation step wrote, `timer.escalated_to_role` and `timer.escalated_at`, are written by the timer story RWB-P3-E1028-APP in the same schema, so this story is a reader with no write path of its own.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P3-E2015-CON is published: the OpenAPI 3.1 document of the two read operations with the added response fields, the composed deviation object, the error envelope and the three contract fakes.
- RWB-P3-E1035-CON is published: the case record view contract that fixes the shape of the case resource this story extends, so the added fields sit on one agreed resource and not on a second copy of it.
- RWB-P3-E1028-CON is published: the timer story's contract, which fixes the meaning of `warn_at`, `expires_at`, `escalated_to_role`, `escalated_at`, `nextEscalationRole` and `inWarning`, and the projection the durable timer writes.
- RWB-PLT-E1071-CON is published: the Temporal workflow kit in namespace `rwb-recovery`, so the durable timer that drives the projection runs on task queue `rwb-case` (DP-10).
- RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are published: the reference-data contract of rwb-case with its client library, so LOV-TIMER, LOV-DEVIATION and the SERVICE_LEVEL escalation roles are read as data with their version (DP-07).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03), so the approver a deviation displays is the approver of the decision record and never a value copied into rwb_case.
- RWB-PLT-E1047-CON is published: the topic and event naming library (DP-14). RWB-PLT-E1044-CON is published: the per-service Flyway sequence in schema `rwb_case` (DP-15).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route that serves SCR-03 (DP-19). Its path and merge order are owned by that platform contract; this story fixes only the two answers rwb-case returns.
- The `timer` and `task` rows exist for the case, written by RWB-P3-E1028-APP and RWB-P3-E1018-APP; the columns `timer.escalated_to_role` (DF-WRK-043) and `timer.escalated_at` (DF-WRK-044) exist with that story's migration, and this story adds no column.
- SERVICE_LEVEL rows carry the escalation role and the next escalation role for each product group and status, held in the rwb-case reference tables with their version (DP-07).
- `prescription.warning-days` is in force and is applied where `timer.warn_at` is computed (RWB-P3-E1028-APP); this story only reads `inWarning` from that warning point and never recomputes it.
- The person holds a role with Case record R and the case is in the caller's scope; rwb-access answers the authorisation check through its contract, cached per request.
- The login is the rwb-case login (DP-02): one login and one connection pool for the service, with grants on schema `rwb_case` only (Architecture v5 slide 29).

##### 4. Flow

1. Case owner: opens SCR-03 Case record for a case at the fixed business date 2026-12-15, reached through the App Gateway at `/recovery/*` and the gateway-bff session (DP-19).
2. gateway-bff: checks the session in Redis and the coarse permission, then calls three owners in parallel, one hop each: rwb-case `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}`, rwb-case `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers`, and rwb-source-data for the account and customer facts of the case. No service calls another service inside a business step.
3. rwb-case: authorises the read through the rwb-access contract, `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise`, right R on Case record, scope applied, cached for the request.
4. rwb-case, case answer: reads `recovery_case` for `id`, `case_no`, `product_group`, `status`, `prescription_date`, `stage_clock_start`, `deviation_open` and `legal_hold`.
5. rwb-case, case answer: calls rwb-deviation once, `GET /api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations`, one hop, 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11), and receives the open and the cleared deviations of the case with code, raised date, handler, paused state, contact stop, cleared date and outcome (GAP-0714; ASM-1261).
6. rwb-case, case answer: calls rwb-decision once, `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}`, one hop, 2 s timeout, and takes for each deviation the approver on the decision log entry whose decision code matches the deviation code and whose decision time is the raise of that deviation; the answer carries the approver user ID only, never the entry.
7. rwb-case, case answer: merges the deviation rows with their approvers into `deviations[]`, orders them by raised date, and sets `deviationsAvailable` true. When the S8 call times out or fails, it returns the case with `deviationsAvailable` false, an empty `deviations[]` and MSG-GEN-006 in the section, and the banner is still built from `deviation_open`.
8. rwb-case, timer answer: reads the `timer` rows of the case and, for each timer with a task, the `task.owner_role` of that task; it reads no rule row and computes no deadline.
9. rwb-case, timer answer: for each row returns `timerType`, `startedAt`, `expiresAt`, `warnAt`, `paused`, `status`, `escalationLevel`, `nextStepOwnerRole`, the escalated role and time written by the timer story, and `nextEscalationRole` from the SERVICE_LEVEL row for the product group and status in force (DP-07).
10. rwb-case, timer answer: sets `inWarning` true when the business date is on or after `warn_at` and the timer is RUNNING or PAUSED, and false otherwise; it orders the list by `expires_at` ascending.
11. gateway-bff: merges the two rwb-case answers and the rwb-source-data answer into the screen model and returns the screen inside the 2 s budget (Architecture v5 slide 10: about 1.2 s at the 95th percentile).
12. Screen: renders the timers ordered by due date, each with type, due date, status, warning state, escalation level, escalated-to role, escalated time, next escalation point and the owner role of the next step; renders the prescription date with its warning; renders the deviation rows and the On hold banner with MSG-P3-004.
13. Nothing in this flow writes: the two operations are reads, the view changes no timer, no deviation and no case, and the read path publishes no event.
14. The clock itself runs outside this story: the durable timer inside CaseWorkflow fires at `expires_at`, raises the escalation and publishes `rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1` (event #19) on `rwb.case.events.v1`, and the projection this story reads shows the result (RWB-P3-E1028-APP).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The case has no running, paused or expired timer | The timers answer is an empty list and the timers section shows the empty sentence; the prescription date and the deviations are still returned | MSG-P3-018 | AC8 |
| X2 | The case is outside the person's scope | The operation answers 404; nothing is returned and nothing is written | MSG-P4-003 | AC9 |
| X3 | The deviation service does not answer inside the timeout | The timers and the prescription date are returned; the deviation section shows that it could not be read; the on-hold banner still shows from `recovery_case.deviation_open` | MSG-GEN-006 | AC10 |
| X4 | Two deviations are open on one case | Both show with their own handler and approver; the case stays on hold until both clear | MSG-P3-004 | AC5 |
| X5 | The prescription date is 91 days away with a 90 day warning | No warning; the date is returned without MSG-P3-003 | None | AC3 |
| X6 | The deviation read passes 2 s on the first attempt | One retry with jitter, then the breaker opens for that downstream; the answer degrades as in X3 and the timer answer is untouched | MSG-GEN-006 | AC10 |
| X7 | The decision log read passes 2 s or answers an error | The deviations are returned with their handler, paused state and contact stop; `approverUserId` is omitted and the deviation section carries MSG-GEN-006 naming the decision center; the timers and the prescription date are untouched | MSG-GEN-006 | AC2 |
| X8 | A role without Case record R calls either operation | Refused with 403 by the rwb-access check behind the endpoint; the answer carries the refusal and not an empty list | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-015-11 |
| X9 | The case ID is unknown, or belongs to another service's case space | 404 with MSG-P4-003; no partial case is composed | MSG-P4-003 | AC9 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads what RWB-P3-E1028-APP, S8 and P7 already write; builds against the published contracts and their fakes, so neither the deviation nor the decision service needs to exist in the development environment |
| Negotiable | The layout, the column order and the wording of the panels are negotiable; the content is fixed by REQ-WKM-005 and the warning point by the timer story |
| Valuable | The next deadline, the escalation and the deviation are on one screen, composed inside one 2 s budget |
| Estimable | Two read operations extended, two consumed contracts, one reference-data read, one merge and two screen panels |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Every owned criterion has a test case in section 16; the S8 and P7 answers are stubbed in the contract fakes and real in SIT |

**Note.** The `timer` row stays an rwb_case projection behind `GET /cases/{caseId}/timers`, and the clock that fires is now a durable Temporal timer inside CaseWorkflow on task queue `rwb-case`, so JOB-05 Timer check and the TimerDue event are retired and TimerBreached stays event #19 on `rwb.case.events.v1` (Architecture v5 slides 42 and 44; Ownership Map ruling ASM-0078). `timer.escalated_to_role` (DF-WRK-043) and `timer.escalated_at` (DF-WRK-044) are written by the timer story RWB-P3-E1028-APP; this story only reads them and displays the escalation level, the escalated-to role, the escalated time, the next escalation role and `inWarning` from `warn_at`. The deviation rows come from S8 through the read path of the S8 contract and the approvers from P7 through the decision log, both called by rwb-case, which is what the mock Givens above stand in for; `prescription.warning-days` is applied where `timer.warn_at` is computed by RWB-P3-E1028-APP and is never re-applied here. The ten criteria above are owned by this story, and the wave 2 harness RWB-ITG-E2015-ITG copies each one with the `-ITG` suffix.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every timer of the case with status Running, Paused or Expired shows with type, due date, status and the owner role of its task | REQ-WKM-005; LOV-TIMER; DF-WRK-023 |
| BR2 | A breached service level shows the role it was escalated to, when, and the next escalation point. The case does not move | R-UNI-30; REQ-WKM-004 |
| BR3 | A deviation pauses the stage clock and keeps the prescription clock running | R-DEV-01; REQ-DVH-002 |
| BR4 | A case with a deviation open shows as on hold with the deviation and the prescription date | Case status On hold; R-UNI-04; R-UNI-05; DF-CAS-019 |
| BR5 | X1, X2 and X3 show the contact stop | R-UNI-04; R-UNI-05; R-UNI-06; CTL-16 |
| BR6 | The case leaves on hold only when every open deviation is cleared | R-UNI-43; FEAT-DVH-09 |
| BR7 | The prescription date shows a warning from the warning point `timer.warn_at` that the timer story computes from `prescription.warning-days` (assumed 90; DL22); this view never recomputes it | R-UNI-31; CTL-18; DF-WRK-033 |
| BR8 | The return point of a deviation is the routing state the case was in when it paused | DF-CAS-041; R-DEV-08 |
| BR9 | The approver of a deviation is the approver on its decision log entry, read through the rwb-decision contract; rwb_case holds no copy of it | REQ-DRI-001; DP-03; DF-DEC-010 |
| BR10 | The two operations are reads of a projection: they write no timer, no deviation and no case, and the escalation fields are written by the durable timer in RWB-P3-E1028-APP | Ownership Map ruling ASM-0078; DP-01 |
| BR11 | A role without Case record R is refused with 403 and a case outside the caller's scope is not found with 404; a refusal never returns an empty list | REQ-WKM-005; the rwb-access contract |
| BR12 | Each downstream is called once, one hop, with the 2 s timeout and a breaker; a timeout degrades the section it belongs to and never empties the timers or the prescription date | DP-11; NFR-008; Architecture v5 slide 11 |

##### 9. State transitions

None on the case. This story changes no case status, no timer status and no deviation state; it reads and displays them. The facts below are caused by other stories and are what this view shows.

| Timer state change | Cause | What this view shows | Owner story |
|---|---|---|---|
| RUNNING to EXPIRED | The durable timer inside CaseWorkflow reaches `expires_at`, raises the escalation and publishes TimerBreached (event #19) | Status Expired, escalation level 1, escalated-to role and time, next escalation role; the case queue and status unchanged | RWB-P3-E1028-APP |
| RUNNING to PAUSED | DeviationRaised consumed by rwb-case into the case workflow | Status Paused with the pause date; the prescription timer keeps running with the same date | RWB-P3-E1028-APP; S8 |
| PAUSED to RUNNING | DeviationCleared consumed by rwb-case after the last open deviation clears | Status Running with `expires_at` moved by the paused working days and `inWarning` recomputed from `warn_at` | RWB-P3-E1028-APP |
| Any status to STOPPED | The stage ends or the case closes | The timer leaves the timers section | RWB-P3-E1028-APP |
| PRESCRIPTION never changes state for a deviation | The prescription clock is never paused | The same prescription date and the same warning while a deviation is open | RWB-P3-E1028-APP |

The two escalation fields this view reads are not added by this story: `timer.escalated_to_role` and `timer.escalated_at` arrive with the migration of RWB-P3-E1028-APP, which also sets `recovery_case.deviation_open` that the on-hold banner is built from.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the case record view with its timers, prescription date and deviations (Case record R, scope Own) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads the same, including the escalation the case was raised to (Case record R, scope Team) |
| RW-SPECIAL, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-LEGAL | Read the case and its deviations (Case record R) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads (Case record R, scope All); changes nothing |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow identity | Writes the escalation fields and raises TimerBreached inside the durable timer, in RWB-P3-E1028-APP; this story only reads the projection |
| rwb-access | Answers the role, scope and Case record right check through its authorise contract, cached per request |
| rwb-deviation | Answers the deviation read; owns `deviation` |
| rwb-decision | Answers the decision log read that names the approver; owns `decision_log_entry` |

Reading the approver needs no Decision log right: the case service returns the approver's user ID only, not the decision log entry.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/case/v1`; owner rwb-case (P3). The two operations are the ones this story extends; the rest of the rwb-case surface is unchanged.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Added in this story | Access |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}` | Read one case with its clocks, its flags and its deviations | `deviations[]` (`deviationCode`, `raisedAt`, `handlerUserId`, `approverUserId`, `pausedState`, `contactStop`, `clearedAt`, `outcome`) and `deviationsAvailable` (boolean) on the Case resource that already carries `prescriptionDate`, `stageClockStart`, `deviationOpen` and `legalHold` | Case record R, scope applied |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/timers` | Read the clocks on a case: stage, service level, prescription, notice | `nextStepOwnerRole`, `escalatedToRole`, `escalatedAt`, `nextEscalationRole`, `inWarning` on each `Timer`, beside `timerType`, `startedAt`, `expiresAt`, `warnAt`, `paused`, `status` and `escalationLevel` | Case record R, scope applied |

The timers answer is ordered by `expiresAt` ascending. Errors for both: 401 no session (MSG-P4-001), 403 no Case record R (MSG-P4-002), 404 unknown or out of scope (MSG-P4-003), 503 store down. Idempotency is not applicable to a read.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations` | S8 rwb-deviation | The open and cleared deviations of the case with code, raised date, handler, paused state, contact stop, cleared date and outcome (GAP-0714; ASM-1261) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | P7 rwb-decision | The approver on the decision log entry of each deviation decision | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The role, scope and Case record right check, cached per request | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |

Three calls, no chain. The deviation call and the decision call are made by rwb-case inside the case answer, so gateway-bff still sees one hop per owner.

###### 12.3 Events published

None in this story. When the durable timer inside CaseWorkflow fires, RWB-P3-E1028-APP publishes `rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1` (event #19) on `rwb.case.events.v1` with `caseId`, `caseNo`, `timerId`, `timerType` and `expiresAt`, keyed by `caseId`; this read path publishes nothing and writes no outbox row.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None in this story. `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1`, `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` and `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` are consumed by the timer story RWB-P3-E1028-APP into `rwb_case`, where they set the pause, the resume and the rule version; this view reads the result and subscribes to nothing.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow | Workflow, parent, one per case, workflow ID = case ID | `rwb-case` | Holds the durable stage timer, the warning point and the escalation, and publishes TimerBreached when it fires; owned by RWB-P3-E1028-APP, and this story adds no workflow and no activity to it |
| Timers projection read | Query inside the service | `rwb-case` | Orders the timer rows by `expires_at`, joins `task.owner_role`, and resolves `nextEscalationRole` from the SERVICE_LEVEL reference row in force |

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. There is no timer-check Schedule and no timer-check job: the five-minute check is replaced by the durable timer inside CaseWorkflow (DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44, JOB-05 retired). This story registers no Schedule and reads no scheduler state.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| timer | P3 (rwb_case) | The projection row: type, start, expiry, warning point, paused flag, status, escalation level, escalated role and time |
| recovery_case | P3 (rwb_case) | Prescription date, stage clock start, deviation flag and legal hold |
| task | P3 (rwb_case) | The owner role of the next step on the timer |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_case | Not written by this read path; the timer story uses them for TimerBreached |

`deviation` is owned by S8 and `decision_log_entry` by P7; neither is read directly, and `rwb_case` holds no foreign key into another schema (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-deviation WireMock | The S8 contract | `GET /cases/{caseId}/deviations` with X3 on RW-2026-000502, X1 and X3 on RW-2026-000504, X1 cleared on RW-2026-000505, the empty answer of RW-2026-000501 and a delayed answer beyond 2 s |
| rwb-decision WireMock | The P7 contract | `GET /decision-log?caseId=` with entry DLE-9101 and approver U-LG-01 for X3, the approvers of the X1 entries, and a delayed answer beyond 2 s |
| rwb-access WireMock | The P4 contract | `POST /authorise` granting Case record R, refusing RW-REFADM, and refusing scope over SME-NTH for a scope Own in MTG-BKK |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 3 consumed | Case and timers provided; deviations, decision log and authorise consumed; one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream |
| Kafka | None published, none consumed | TimerBreached is published by RWB-P3-E1028-APP and consumed by gateway-bff; this read path carries no Kafka traffic |
| Temporal | None added | The durable timer lives in CaseWorkflow and belongs to RWB-P3-E1028-APP |
| File | None | No file is read or written |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.caseview`, module `caseview`; front end folder `src/modules/recovery/case/caserecord`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | The monolith base path of the legacy API (Template and Rules §R5.5, DP-13) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.case.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The same-service CON baselines RWB-P3-E2015-CON, RWB-P3-E1028-CON and RWB-P3-E1035-CON are class H dependencies of this story and are not DP rows; no pattern moves, and DP-06 is not claimed because this story reads no parameter and re-applies no warning day.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CaseClocksController | Controller | The two read operations with the added fields; maps a refusal to 403 and an unknown case to 404 |
| CaseViewService | Service | Builds the case answer: the case row, the deviation read, the approver read, the merge and `deviationsAvailable` |
| TimerViewService | Service | Builds the timers answer: ordering, the task owner role, the escalation fields, the next escalation role and `inWarning` |
| TimerProjectionRepository | Repository | Reads `timer` and `task` of the case from schema `rwb_case` only; no write path |
| DeviationClient | Client | Calls the S8 read with the 2 s timeout and the breaker; never reads `deviation` |
| ApproverClient | Client | Calls the P7 decision log once per case with the 2 s timeout; matches an entry to a deviation by decision code and raise time |
| EscalationRoleReader | Service | Resolves the next escalation role from the SERVICE_LEVEL reference row in force, through the reference-data contract (DP-07) |
| AccessCheckClient | Client | Calls the rwb-access authorise contract, cached per request |
| CaseClocksPanel | React component | The timers, the prescription date, the warnings and the escalation state on SCR-03 |
| DeviationPanel | React component | The deviations with handler, approver, contact stop and return point, and the On hold banner |

**Database.** No migration adds a column in this story. The projection columns `timer.escalated_to_role` (DF-WRK-043) and `timer.escalated_at` (DF-WRK-044) arrive with the migration of RWB-P3-E1028-APP, and this story's migration is limited to the read-side index it needs, `ix_timer_case_expiry ON timer (case_id, expires_at)`, added in its own Flyway step in schema `rwb_case`. Reads use `ix_timer_case_id` and `ix_task_case_id` where they already exist. No column of `recovery_case` and no column of `task` is added.

**Configuration and reference data.** `caseview.deviation-timeout-ms` = 2000 and `caseview.approver-timeout-ms` = 2000 are service configuration values fixed by the 2 s budget of DP-11, held in the service configuration and never in code. LOV-TIMER, LOV-TIMER-STATUS, LOV-DEVIATION and the SERVICE_LEVEL escalation roles are read through the reference-data contract with their version in force; the timer and deviation labels come from LOV-TIMER and LOV-DEVIATION. `prescription.warning-days` is not read here: it is applied where `timer.warn_at` is computed (RWB-P3-E1028-APP).

**Build steps**

1. Extend the OpenAPI document and the generated types for the two operations with the added fields; contract test against RWB-P3-E2015-CON.
2. TimerProjectionRepository and TimerViewService over schema `rwb_case`: ordering, owner role, escalation level, escalated role and time, next escalation role, `inWarning`; tests for AC1, AC4, AC6, AC7 and AC8.
3. DeviationClient with the 2 s timeout, the single retry on GET, the breaker and the degradation flag; tests for AC2, AC5 and AC10.
4. ApproverClient with the case-scoped query and the match by decision code and raise time; tests for AC2 and the approver timeout of section 5.
5. CaseViewService merge: `deviations[]` ordered by raised date, `deviationsAvailable`, and the banner from `deviation_open`; tests for AC2, AC5, AC7 and AC10.
6. Prescription warning from `warn_at` and the on-hold banner; tests for AC3 and AC6.
7. Authorisation through the rwb-access contract with the scope check; tests for AC9 and the refusal of section 16.
8. CaseClocksPanel and DeviationPanel against the merged screen model returned by the composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON; browser test of SCR-03 for AC1 to AC10.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.p3.case-clocks`, a service configuration value. Off: SCR-03 shows the Epic 1 read-only fields and the two operations return the case and the timers without the added deviation block; on: the timers with the escalation state, the prescription warning and the deviation flag.

**Done when.** Every test in section 16 passes, the two contract fakes drive every cross-service answer, a case with 6 timers and 50 documents loads inside 2 s through the composite route (NFR-009), and the contract tests of RWB-P3-E2015-CON stay green.

| MSG-P3-004 | The case is on hold for a deviation | This case is on hold for {deviation}. The prescription date is still {date}. |

For MSG-GEN-006 the {system} value is "Deviation handling" on the deviation read and "Decision center" on the approver read. MSG-P3-018 is new (see Additions). Thai text follows DL10.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the warning point, the escalation roles, the next escalation role, the timeouts and the timer and deviation labels are data read through the parameters and reference-data contracts of rwb-case or written by the timer story.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or events: the panels show staff user IDs resolved to display names by the ACE common module, no customer data is read into an answer, and test data is synthetic.
- No read of another service's table and no ACE view: deviations come only through the rwb-deviation contract, approvers only through the rwb-decision contract, and authorisation only through the rwb-access contract (DP-01, DP-11).
- ACE data is read only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views of rwb-source-data; this story reads no ACE view at all.
- No cross-schema read: `rwb_case` holds no foreign key and no join into `rwb_deviation` or `rwb_decision`.
- The view never writes: no timer, no deviation and no case is changed by either operation, and the read path writes no outbox row.
- One hop only: rwb-case calls S8 and P7 once each and returns; it never calls a service that calls another.
- Every answer carries IDs, codes, dates and amounts only; no name, address, identity number or contact point appears in a response or in a log line.
