##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`, module `access/authorise`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.authorise`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 is the reason the service answers from the attributes it is given: `recovery_case`, `timer`, `task` and `deviation` are P3's and S8's, and the `v_ace_*` customer fields are P1's, so the answer is built from identifiers and never from a joined query. DP-03 is the access log: an `AC-READ` and an `AC-DENY` are decision records on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, so an access question and a decision question are answered from one log. DP-07 supplies LOV-SCOPE and LOV-CAPABILITY with the version in force, because `lov_value` stays with P3 under the ownership map; no scope name is a Java constant. DP-10 is recorded because the legacy key carries JOB-05 and JOB-18: in the target no job of this key runs from a shared Quartz table, the service level clock is a durable timer of the workflow that owns the case, and JOB-18 (access review) is RWB-P4-AD008-APP — so this story adds no job. DP-11 is the caller-facing boundary: one hop, 2 s timeout, cached, and the answer must hold inside it. DP-13, DP-14 and DP-15 are the naming and migration conventions of the service. DP-19 is the route that renders the answer: the screen, its panels and its states are RWB-P3-E2015-APP/CON, and this story supplies only the grant and the markers.

The platform contracts the DP rows name are preconditions of the service lane already in place behind RWB-P4-E1037-CON in wave 1; this secondary slice adds no new build dependency of its own (metadata H = None; ASM-1664), and JOB-18 (access review) is RWB-P4-AD008-APP.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AuthoriseController | Controller | The three operations of the existing contract on `/api/recovery/access/v1`; validation and problem responses |
| AccessDecisionService | Service | Right, scope, escalation grant and masking profile for one request, in that order; one answer, one record |
| PermissionResolver | Service | Reads `permission` for the caller's roles and the `matrix_version` in force; resolves the five letters |
| ScopeRule | Service | Compares the object attributes of the request with the `default_scope` value in force |
| EscalationScopeService | Service | The grant of BR3 from `escalatedToRole` and `escalatedAt`; no stored state |
| MaskingProfileService | Service | The masked markers per field ID for the caller's roles and the masking version in force; default masked |
| AccessRecordWriter | Service | The `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entries through the library of DP-03, and the `AccessPolicyChanged` outbox row |
| PolicyCache | Service | The cached answer per policy version, dropped on the policy change |
| PolicyChangeListener | Service | Applies a new policy version and publishes `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` in the same transaction |
| AccessRepository | Repository | `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict`, inbox and outbox in `rwb_access`; no foreign table |

**Database and migrations**

- No new table: `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule` and `role_conflict` exist from the wave-1 stories of this service behind RWB-P4-E1037-CON, and the policy rows are loaded by the load path stories.
- One migration in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15: `V2015_1__access_decision_read_path.sql` adds `ix_masking_rule_role_field` on `masking_rule (role_code, field_id, masking_version)` and `ix_permission_role_area` on `permission (role_id, capability_area, matrix_version)`, so the two reads of an answer are index reads inside the 2 s budget of DP-11.
- The policy rows are versioned by `matrix_version`, `masking_version` and the roles' `valid_from` and `valid_to`; this story writes none of them, and a version is never edited in place (a new version is loaded, approved and published).

**Configuration and reference data**

- The matrix version and the masking version in force are data: the latest `valid_from` on or before the business date, read from `permission.matrix_version` and `masking_rule.masking_version`. The masking version of SIT is assumed to be MASK-SIT-01 (GAP-0936; ASM-1662).
- LOV-SCOPE (OWN, TEAM, REGION, ALL) and LOV-CAPABILITY (the 14 capability areas) through the reference-data contract of DP-07 (RWB-P3-E1043-CON).
- No parameter row, no timeout constant and no role code in code: the 2 s is the platform standard of RWB-PLT-E1037-CON's client, and the cache lives for the policy version in force (BR7).
- The database login is the rwb-access login (DP-02): Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0934; ASM-1660).

**Build steps**

1. `PermissionResolver` and `ScopeRule` over `permission`, `role` and the reference lists, with the matrix version named in the answer; tests for AC2, AC3 and AC6, and a test that a new scope value is accepted as data.
2. `EscalationScopeService` with the attributes of the timer, the grant and its end; tests for AC4 with the escalation open and closed.
3. `MaskingProfileService` with the covering-row lookup and the default; tests for AC1, AC5 and AC6.
4. `AccessRecordWriter` with the `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entries written before the answer, and the forced failure of X5; test TC-E2-015-08.
5. The denial path with the refusal shape and no case data; test TC-E2-015-11 and AC8.
6. `PolicyCache` and `PolicyChangeListener` with the publish and the drop; test AC9 against the PM-2026.13 fixture.
7. The migration of the two indexes, and a timing test that one answer stays inside the 2 s budget on a policy pack of the loaded size.
8. The contract-fake run of the whole capability against RWB-P3-E2015-CON and the decision-record fake, so the story builds before the case side exists in the environment.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.p4.escalation-scope`, read from the platform feature-flag library under the R-PREC default ruling. Off: the escalation grant of BR3 is not applied and the answer is the matrix-and-scope answer alone, while the masking profile and the access log are unchanged — so a case escalated to a role that does not hold it in scope stays refused, and nothing else in the service changes. The switch needs no schema rollback and blocks no case read that the policy allows.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; a case owned by the caller is answered granted with its fields marked, a case outside the scope is answered 404 with no case data, a case escalated to a role is answered granted to that role and refused again once the escalation closes, a field with no masking row comes back masked, a role without Case record R is refused with no case data, every granted and every refused read leaves its record, and an approved policy version changes the answer with no deployment.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | The token carries no Recovery role, or no second factor | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. | The access check before this story's answer (X6, X8) |
| MSG-P4-002 | No role of the caller holds the right in the capability area | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, on the refusal of BR1 |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. | This story, on the refusal of BR2 and on an ended grant (BR3) |
| MSG-P4-006 | Two roles of the caller conflict | {role} may not be held together with {role}. | The access check, from this service's `role_conflict` rows (X7) |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on every answer (X5) |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A list the answer needs is not available | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. | This story, on a reference-list failure (X9) |

For MSG-P4-002 the {action} value is the action the caller attempted, for example "read the timers"; for MSG-P4-003 no case fact is echoed, because the message must not confirm that a case exists. Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId`, the text with its placeholders filled and the instance of the request; the Thai text follows DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

This story builds no screen. SCR-03 Case record, its clocks and deviation panels, its history and its route are RWB-P3-E2015-APP/CON through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 (RWB-PLT-N001-CON); the page SCR-04 for a case outside the scope is the case service's, and the refusal text it shows is the one this story produces.

What this story decides for SCR-03 is what each state may show:

| Screen | State | What the answer decides |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-03 Case record | Read only, granted | The case, its timers and its deviation flag are rendered; the fields this story marks masked are rendered masked, and the screens hold no rule of their own |
| SCR-03 Case record | On hold for a deviation | The same grant applies; the on-hold banner and the deviation panel are P3's and S8's, and the personal fields stay masked |
| SCR-03 Case record | Escalated | The reader is the role the escalation names and sees the case although it is in neither queue nor own scope; the escalation line itself is P3's |
| SCR-03 Case record | Refused | The page shows MSG-P4-002 and no case fact, and one AC-DENY entry exists |
| SCR-03 Case record | Not found | The page shows MSG-P4-003 and no case fact, and one AC-DENY entry exists |
| SCR-03 Case record | Not available | The page shows MSG-P7-003 where the record could not be written, and no case fact |

A screen that renders a field clear because a client cached it is a defect of the screen, not of the answer: the answer always names the masking version it used, and a field is clear only where a row of that version says so.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: role codes, scope values, capability areas, field IDs, the matrix version and the masking version are data rows in `rwb_access` and list values read through DP-07; the switch is a platform flag (BR8).
- No personal data in logs, events, the record or the tests. The answer carries markers, the `AC-READ` entry carries field IDs, the `AC-DENY` entry carries the area and the right, and the event carries version labels; test data is synthetic and staff appear as user references.
- ACE customer fields only through the owner's contract and masked by role: this service stores no customer value and answers with markers, and the field IDs DF-PTY-007, DF-PTY-008 and DF-PTY-016 name fields of P1's contract without copying their values (NFR-039, NFR-040).
- No cross-schema read (DP-01): `recovery_case`, `timer`, `task`, `deviation`, `decision_log_entry` and the `v_ace_*` views are never queried; the case facts arrive in the request and the policy is the service's own.
- One writer for the policy: only the load path stories of this service write a role, a permission or a masking row; this story reads them and publishes the change, so an answer and the policy it names cannot disagree.
- The record is written before the answer: a failure answers 503 with no case data and raises an incident, so no case read is unlogged (BR5, BR6).
- The answer is idempotent for a policy version: the same question under the same versions returns the same answer, and the cache is dropped on the policy event rather than on a timer.
- The feature switch changes one rule and no schema, and it never widens a scope: off removes the escalation grant and leaves every other decision as it was.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-015 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **the clocks-and-deviation capability of rwb-case deployed from the service template with its Helm values and its own login, its two consumer groups for DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared, its timer-projection lag measure, the dashboards for timers, escalation, prescription warnings and degraded reads, the alerts on TimerBreached volume, the MSG-GEN-006 rate and stuck workflows, and a runbook for a stuck timer, a deviation read that is down and an escalation that was not applied**, so that **an operator can see within minutes that a deadline will not fire or that a deviation section is degrading, and repair it without reading code or waiting for a business report**.

This story deploys an existing capability. It adds no topic, registers no timer-check Schedule and builds no endpoint, table or workflow: the clock is a durable Temporal timer inside CaseWorkflow on task queue `rwb-case`, and the deviation flag is fed by the two S8 events on `rwb.deviation.events.v1`.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy capability leaned on a five-minute Quartz job whose only failure signal was a job exception, so a timer that never fired and a deviation that was never read looked the same as a quiet night. In the target the clock is a durable timer inside the workflow (DP-10): there is no scheduler row to be late and no job record to inspect, so the operational signal has to move from "did the job run" to "is the projection moving, is the workflow stuck and is the deviation section degrading" (Architecture v5 slides 44 and 28; JOB-05 retired, JOB-21 stuck workflow scan kept).

The capability is also the one part of the case record that depends on another service for its correctness at read time: a slow or refused S8 read does not fail the screen, it silently turns the deviation section into MSG-GEN-006 while the banner still shows. That is the right behaviour for the officer and the wrong behaviour for the operator if nobody counts it, which is why the degradation rate is a dashboard series and an alert here rather than a line in a log.

Deployment is therefore part of the capability: the chart carries the rwb-case login and no other credential (DP-02), the migration job runs the per-service Flyway sequence in schema `rwb_case` (DP-15), the two S8 consumer groups are provisioned with retry and `.dlt` paths so a deviation pause is never lost (DP-09), and the runbook names the three failures an operator will actually see.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The Temporal workflow kit and the `rwb-recovery` namespace are available (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), so CaseWorkflow polls `rwb-case` and the durable timer runs in every environment.
- The Kafka event platform provisions topics with a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON), and `rwb.deviation.events.v1` is provisioned by its owner S8.
- The observability stack of the platform is available (RWB-PLT-OBS, ADR-023): metrics, traces and logs with one trace across REST, Kafka and Temporal.
- The three environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist with their parameter scope and their Kafka and Temporal endpoints.
- RWB-P3-E2015-CON is published, so the smoke profile and the drift test run against the two read operations and the three fakes of that baseline.
- The reference data LOV-TIMER, LOV-TIMER-STATUS, LOV-DEVIATION and the SERVICE_LEVEL escalation roles are loaded by the owning stories; this story reads them and holds no copy.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds one image and one chart version from the same commit, runs the unit, component and contract tests, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes the chart.
2. The chart deploys rwb-case with the rwb-case login, the pre-deploy migration job for schema `rwb_case`, the readiness and liveness probes and the worker deployment that polls `rwb-case`.
3. The provisioning step declares the two consumer groups of this capability, `rwb-case` for `rwb.deviation.events.v1` with the topics DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared, each with its retry topic and its `.dlt` topic; it reuses `rwb.case.events.v1` for TimerBreached and creates no new topic.
4. The provisioning step asserts that no timer-check Schedule, task queue or job exists for this capability, and that `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` are consumed or produced as their owners provisioned them.
5. The dashboards are published: timers by status, overdue timers, escalated timers, prescription warnings in force, the timer projection lag, the S8 read timeouts and breaches, the MSG-GEN-006 rate, refused and out-of-scope reads, TimerBreached volume and workflow health.
6. The alerts are wired to the message IDs of section 14 and to the runbook entries of section 13; the thresholds are values and carry the placeholder of section 14 until they are confirmed.
7. A smoke step opens the case record of a synthetic case through gateway-bff in the SIT profile, so the composite route, the two rwb-case answers and the three fakes are exercised together.
8. The runbook is published and reviewed with the on-call rota: a stuck timer, a deviation read that is down, an escalation that was not applied, a projection that stopped moving, a refused read that is not an incident.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The migration job fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic reaches the new version | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A consumer group is provisioned without its retry or `.dlt` topic | The provisioning step fails the release and the consumer refuses to start | None | AC3 |
| X3 | The timer projection lag passes its value | The projection-lag alert fires and the runbook entry for a projection that stopped moving is opened | MSG-GEN-006 | AC4, AC6 |
| X4 | The S8 read times out on a share of reads | The MSG-GEN-006 rate alert fires; the deviation read-down runbook entry names the S8 owner and the breaker state | MSG-GEN-006 | AC6 |
| X5 | A workflow stops on a non-retryable failure | The stuck workflow scan of JOB-21 raises the case and the stuck-timer runbook entry starts from the workflow history | None | AC6 |
| X6 | TimerBreached volume leaves its band | The volume alert fires and the escalation-not-applied runbook entry checks the projection and the record | None | AC6 |
| X7 | A role without Case record R is refused | The refused-read count rises on the dashboard and no page is sent | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |
| X8 | A case is outside the caller's scope | The out-of-scope count rises on the dashboard and no page is sent | MSG-P4-003 | AC5 |
| X9 | A release declares a timer-check Schedule or a new topic | The pipeline fails the release on the retired-element check of AC4 | None | AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the platform topic provisioning, the workflow kit and the observability stack; builds no application code |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, alert thresholds and retention are environment values, not story decisions |
| Valuable | Makes a capability with no scheduler row observable: the projection, the workflow and the degraded section each have a signal and an owner |
| Estimable | One chart, one pipeline stage, one migration job, two probes, two consumer groups, eight dashboard panels, five alert rules and five runbook entries |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the groups exist, the panels carry data, the alerts fire on a synthetic metric, the runbook entry resolves |

These six criteria are new for the deployment and test artefacts only; they restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P3-E2015-APP.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One service, one schema, one login: the release uses the rwb-case login and no other service's credential | DP-02; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR2 | The migration is a per-service Flyway sequence in schema rwb_case and runs before the deployment is ready | DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| BR3 | Every subscription has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and a consumer never acknowledges an event it could not process | DP-09; Architecture v5 slide 22 notes |
| BR4 | No timer-check Schedule and no timer-check job exists: the clock is a durable timer inside CaseWorkflow (JOB-05 retired) | DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44 |
| BR5 | No new topic is created for this capability; `rwb.case.events.v1` carries TimerBreached and `rwb.deviation.events.v1` carries the two deviation events | DP-14; Architecture v5 slide 42 |
| BR6 | No environment value is hard-coded: replica counts, resource sizes, timeouts and alert thresholds come from values files | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR7 | An alert carries a message ID and the agreed text, and links one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR8 | A refused read and an out-of-scope read are counted on the dashboard and never page the on-call rota | MSG-P4-002; MSG-P4-003 |
| BR9 | The stuck workflow scan is the platform's (JOB-21, a visibility query every five minutes) and is reused, not rebuilt | Architecture v5 slide 44 |
| BR10 | No dashboard series, log line or alert payload carries personal data; case and workflow identifiers only | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the migration job pass the pipeline | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration complete and probes healthy | The schema is at the expected version, the outbox relay runs and the worker polls | Ready |
| Ready | Release superseded | A new chart version is promoted | Rolling |
| Rolling | All pods on the new version | The old ReplicaSet drains and the worker build ID is the new one | Ready |
| Ready | Migration job failed | The schema is not at the expected version | Failed |
| Failed | Rollback | The previous chart version is redeployed and the migration is reversed by its own script | Ready |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the provisioning step, the dashboards, the alerts and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the topic provisioning and the visibility queries behind JOB-21 |
| ACE database administrator | Owns schema rwb_case, the login and its grants, and approves the migration job |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact through the environments |
| On-call operator | Runs the runbook entries and opens an incident when a stuck workflow or an escalation-not-applied case persists |
| RW-PLATADM | Reads and operates the case record and its clocks in the running service, not in the cluster |
| Service owner of S8 rwb-deviation | Is paged by the deviation read-down alert and owns the repair beyond the rwb-case breaker |

The per-service login name used by the chart is a secret reference resolved at deploy time; the chart references "the rwb-case login (DP-02)" and never a literal name.

The alert values are deployment values; the provisional values and their confirmation are carried by the gap and the assumption of section 14 (GAP-0715; ASM-1262). The exact cluster topology, node pools, replica counts and probe timings are deployment values of the platform chart and are not fixed here.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

The deployment exposes the two read operations of RWB-P3-E2015-CON behind gateway-bff: `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` with `deviations[]` and `deviationsAvailable`, and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` with the escalation and warning fields. Owner rwb-case (P3). The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Deployment need |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations` | S8 rwb-deviation | The deviation rows of the case answer; 2 s client budget and a breaker (GAP-0714; ASM-1261) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | P7 rwb-decision | The approver on each deviation decision; 2 s client budget and a breaker |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The authorisation check before either read; cached per request |

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Provisioning |
|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1` (event 19) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | The topic, its retry topic and its `.dlt` topic already exist for rwb-case; the deployment reuses them and creates no new topic |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (event 08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | Shared topic owned by the platform and rwb-decision; reused, not recreated |

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Provisioning |
|---|---|---|
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` (event 06) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | Consumer group `rwb-case` with the inbox of schema rwb_case; retry and `.dlt` configured in the same step |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` (event 07) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | Same consumer group, same retry and `.dlt` path |
| `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` (event 30) | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | Consumer group `rwb-case`, already provisioned for the case capability and reused here |

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow | Workflow, parent, one per case, workflow ID = case ID | `rwb-case` | Worker deployment with the build ID of the release; holds the durable timer and the escalation |
| Timer projection write | Activity inside the workflow | `rwb-case` | Registered by the same worker; the series the projection lag is computed from |
| Timers projection read | Query inside the service | `rwb-case` | Served by the api deployment; not a Temporal element |

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The deployment registers no timer-check Schedule and no cron entry for this capability, because the five-minute check is replaced by the durable timer inside CaseWorkflow (DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44, JOB-05 retired). The platform's stuck workflow scan (JOB-21) runs every five minutes as a visibility query and is not registered by this release.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|
| recovery_case, timer, task | P3 (rwb_case) | Created and migrated by the per-service Flyway sequence in the migration job |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_case | Created by the same migration job; used by the two consumer groups and the outbox relay |

`deviation` belongs to S8 and `decision_log_entry` to P7; the migration job touches schema `rwb_case` only (DP-01).

| rwb-access WireMock | Same, including a granted read and a refused read |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | The monolith base path of the legacy API (Template and Rules §R5.5, DP-13) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

No pattern is claimed for the parameters contract (DP-06): the capability reads no parameter, and the warning days are applied where `warn_at` is computed.

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-case/` | Chart with api and worker deployments, service, migration job, config map, secret references, probes and the Schedule hook that registers nothing for this capability |
| `helm/rwb-case/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, `rwb.p3.case-clocks`, the two client timeouts, the alert thresholds |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit, component and contract tests, retired-element check, image and dependency scan, chart publish, promote the same artefact |
| Provisioning step | Consumer group `rwb-case` on `rwb.deviation.events.v1` for the two deviation events with retry and `.dlt`; reuse of `rwb.case.events.v1`, `rwb.decision-record.v1` and `rwb.decision.events.v1`; task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery` |
| Dashboards | Eight panels: timers by status; overdue timers; escalated timers; prescription warnings in force; timer projection lag; S8 read timeouts and breaches; MSG-GEN-006 rate; refused and out-of-scope reads |
| Alerts | Five rules, each with a message ID and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Five entries: stuck timer, deviation read down, escalation not applied, projection stopped, refused read is not an incident |

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only when the migration is at the expected schema version, the outbox relay is running and the Temporal worker on `rwb-case` has polled; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database and neither calls another service.

**Projection lag.** The series is the difference between the durable timer's fire time, which the workflow exposes as its history, and the first read of the timer row with the new status; it is exposed as a histogram and read on the dashboard and by the projection alert. It is not a job-lateness measure, because there is no job.

**Alert mapping.**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-006 | The S8 deviation read times out or breaches on a share of case-record reads | Degradation-rate alert with the S8 owner, the breaker state and the environment | Platform on-call, ticket to the S8 owner |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The timer projection lag passes its value | Projection-lag alert with the lag and the oldest affected case | Platform on-call, page |
| MSG-P4-002 | A read without Case record R is refused | Refused-read count on the dashboard | No page |
| MSG-P4-003 | A case outside the caller's scope is requested | Out-of-scope count on the dashboard | No page |
| None | TimerBreached volume leaves its band in either direction | Volume alert with the count, the band and the change against the trailing hour | Platform on-call, page when the band is exceeded upward, ticket downward |
| None | JOB-21 raises a stuck workflow on `rwb-case` | Stuck-workflow alert with the workflow ID, the stage and the last event | Platform on-call, page |

Every alert carries its message ID where the condition maps to one, and the two conditions without a message ID carry the workflow or the series name instead. The alert thresholds are deployment values with provisional defaults; the missing source for them is carried by the gap and the assumption of section 14 (GAP-0715; ASM-1262).

**Done when.** The chart renders in all three environments, the pipeline promotes one artefact and fails on a fake drift or a retired element, the two consumer groups exist with their retry and `.dlt` paths, the eight panels carry the synthetic day, the six alert conditions fire on synthetic metrics, and the five runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-006 | The deviation read times out or the projection stops moving | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P3-003 | A timer or the prescription date is inside its warning period | {timer} ends on {date}. |
| MSG-P3-004 | The case is on hold for a deviation | This case is on hold for {deviation}. The prescription date is still {date}. |
| MSG-P3-018 | The case has no running, paused or expired timer | There are no running timers on this case. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A read without Case record R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the person's scope | This case is not in your scope. |

The alert values are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0715; ASM-1262): the message texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story and the deployment adds the routing, the threshold and the runbook link, never a new wording.

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment serves SCR-03 Case record in its Loading, Read only, Editable, On hold and Degraded states behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The operator-facing surfaces of this story are the pipeline run view, the release view, the eight dashboard panels and the runbook; the smoke step opens the case record of a synthetic case in SIT and asserts that the timers, the prescription date and the deviation section answer inside the 2 s budget.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the warning days, the escalation roles, the deviation codes and the timer and deviation labels are reference data held by their owner, never a deployment value.
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads or the runbook: case IDs, workflow IDs, user IDs of staff, counts and durations only.
- One login per service; the chart carries the rwb-case login reference and no other service's credential (DP-02).
- The service writes only schema rwb_case; the migration job never touches another schema and no dashboard query reads one (DP-01).
- Every subscription has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and the consumer dedupes through the inbox (DP-09).
- No new topic and no timer-check Schedule: the capability reuses `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.deviation.events.v1`, and the clock is the durable timer inside CaseWorkflow (DP-10, DP-14).
- ACE data is read only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views; no dashboard reads an ACE view or another service's schema.
- The release pins the image digest and the chart version, and no secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-015 for the wave 2 integration harness. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **member of the integration and QA team**, I want **a repeatable cross-service journey harness that runs the timers, the escalation state, the prescription date and the deviation flag of a case through gateway-bff and the owning services**, so that **the wave 2 clocks and deviation journey is proven end to end, with evidence, before the release is accepted**.

This story builds the harness and the evidence only. It builds no production screen, endpoint, table, workflow or schedule, and it owns no table. The real behaviour is owned by the three I stories RWB-P3-E2015-APP (the two read operations, the timer ordering, the escalation fields, the prescription warning and the merge in rwb-case), RWB-S8-E2015-APP (the deviation query, the pause and the clear of the stage clock, the contact stop and the return point) and RWB-P4-E2015-APP (the role, scope and Case record right check), and those three stories block the ITG run.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy RWB-E2-015 journey crosses more than one service: rwb-case holds the case, its timers, the tasks and their owner roles and the deviation flag; rwb-deviation holds the deviations, the pause of the stage clock and the clear; rwb-decision holds the decision log entry that names the approver of a deviation; and rwb-access answers the authorisation check. Until the real services are exercised together through the gateway, the program cannot show that the next deadline, the escalation and the reason a case left its path are visible on one case, which is the outcome the program targets at 5 days from 23 days.

The harness gives one repeatable run per business date that proves the composite route composes the case record from one hop per source inside the 2 s budget, that the timers come back ordered by due date with their type, status, warning state, next step owner role and escalation fields, that the prescription date warns inside the 90 day window and stays silent at 91 days, that a case with a deviation open shows as on hold with the deviation, its handler, its approver, the contact stop and the return point while the prescription clock keeps its date, that a case stays on hold until every open deviation clears, and that one slow source degrades one section of the answer instead of the whole screen. It meets REQ-WKM-004, REQ-WKM-005, REQ-DVH-002 and REQ-DRI-001 at the integration level and leaves every business rule and every screen behaviour where the owning stories put them.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The three I stories are published and deployed in the SIT environment: RWB-P3-E2015-APP (the case and timer read operations, the timer ordering, the escalation fields, the prescription warning and the merge), RWB-S8-E2015-APP (the deviation query, the pause and the clear of the stage clock, the contact stop and the return point) and RWB-P4-E2015-APP (the authorise check).
- gateway-bff is deployed with the composite route of DP-19 available. The gateway-bff composite case-record route path and its merge order: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0399; ASM-0574).
- The contract fakes of §12.8 are published from the owning services' OpenAPI documents, so the harness can run green from Day 1 before the I stories land.
- The SERVICE_LEVEL rows that name the escalation role and the next escalation role for a product group and status, and the reference data LOV-TIMER and LOV-DEVIATION, are loaded by the owning stories through their contracts; the harness reads them and holds no copy.
- The harness environment, its test-data seeding and its evidence format and retention: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0399; ASM-0574).

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: seeds the synthetic cases, their product group, status and queue, the NOTICE_PERIOD, SERVICE_LEVEL and PRESCRIPTION rows, the tasks and their owner roles, the deviations with their handlers, the decision log entries that name the approvers, and the users with their scopes through the owning contracts or the published fakes, at the fixed business date 2026-12-15.
2. Harness: calls the case record composite route through gateway-bff for RW-2026-000501 and asserts the timers ordered by due date, each with type, status, due date, warning state, the owner role of the next step, escalation level, escalated to and next escalation point.
3. Harness: asserts the prescription date 2027-02-13 with the warning MSG-P3-003 at 60 days from the business date, and that case RW-2026-000503 at 2027-03-16, 91 days away, carries no warning.
4. Harness: asserts the expired SERVICE_LEVEL timer of 2026-12-12 at escalation level 1, escalated to RW-TEAMMGR at 2026-12-12 09:05 with the next escalation point RW-PRODHEAD taken from the SERVICE_LEVEL row, and that the case queue and status are unchanged.
5. Harness: calls the composite route for RW-2026-000502 and asserts the on hold banner with MSG-P3-004 naming the deviation and keeping the prescription date, and the deviation with code, handler, approver from decision log entry DLE-9101, raised date, contact stop and return point.
6. Harness: raises deviation X1 on 2026-12-05 and X3 on 2026-12-08 on RW-2026-000504, asserts both with their own handler and approver, clears X1 on 2026-12-14 and asserts that the case stays on hold with only X3 open.
7. Harness: asserts RW-2026-000505 is not on hold, that its cleared X1 carries outcome "Returned" and that the service level timer is running again with due date 2026-12-22, and that RW-2026-000506 returns the empty timers sentence MSG-P3-018.
8. Harness: forces each failure of §5 through the fakes (the empty timers, the out-of-scope case, the deviation query that does not answer inside 2 s, the role without Case record R), asserts the message, the partial answer and that nothing was written, then returns every fake to its healthy answer and completes the journey.
9. Harness: writes one run report per business date, keyed by story and business date; the report format and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0399; ASM-0574).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What the harness asserts | Message | ITG test case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The case has no running, paused or expired timer (RW-2026-000506) | The timers section is returned empty with the empty sentence; the prescription date and the deviations are still returned | MSG-P3-018 | TC-E2-015-08-ITG |
| X2 | The case is outside the caller's scope (RW-2026-000507 in SME-NTH read with a scope Own in MTG-BKK) | 404 from the composite route; nothing is returned and nothing is written | MSG-P4-003 | TC-E2-015-09-ITG |
| X3 | The deviation query does not answer within 2 s | The timers and the prescription date are returned; the deviation section carries the message and the on hold banner still shows from the case's deviation flag | MSG-GEN-006 | TC-E2-015-10-ITG |
| X4 | Two deviations are open on one case | Both show with their own handler and approver; after one clears the case stays on hold with the other open | MSG-P3-004 | TC-E2-015-05-ITG |
| X5 | The prescription date is 91 days away with a 90 day warning | No warning; the prescription date is returned without MSG-P3-003 | None | TC-E2-015-03-ITG |
| X6 | A role without Case record R calls the timers operation | 403 on the direct call and on the composite route; the answer carries the refusal, not an empty timers list | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-015-11-ITG |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs on its own once the three I stories are deployed; until then it runs against the §12.8 fakes |
| Negotiable | The harness pack, the data seeding, the fixed clock and the evidence format are agreed with QA; no business value is fixed by the harness |
| Valuable | The clocks, the escalation and the deviation flag are evidenced across services rather than per service |
| Estimable | One harness project, one journey specification, one fake pack, one fixed clock fixture and one run report |
| Small | Fits in one iteration with the owning stories' contract tests |
| Testable | Each scenario of §7 is one automated journey with synthetic data and a machine-checkable result |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every timer of the case with status Running, Paused or Expired shows with type, due date, status and the owner role of its task | REQ-WKM-005; LOV-TIMER |
| BR2 | A breached service level shows the role it was escalated to, when, and the next escalation point. The case does not move | R-UNI-30; REQ-WKM-004 |
| BR3 | A deviation pauses the stage clock and keeps the prescription clock running | R-DEV-01; REQ-DVH-002 |
| BR4 | A case with a deviation open shows as on hold with the deviation and the prescription date | casemodel.txt Case status (On hold); R-UNI-04; R-UNI-05 |
| BR5 | X1, X2 and X3 show the contact stop | R-UNI-04; R-UNI-05; R-UNI-06; CTL-16 |
| BR6 | The case leaves on hold only when every open deviation is cleared | R-UNI-43; FEAT-DVH-09 |
| BR7 | The prescription date shows a warning from `prescription.warning-days` before it (assumed 90; DL22) | R-UNI-31; CTL-18 |
| BR8 | The return point of a deviation is the routing state the case was in when it paused | DF-CAS-041; R-DEV-08 |
| BR9 | The approver of a deviation is the approver on its decision log entry | REQ-DRI-001 |

The harness asserts these nine rules against the owning services and the published contracts; it re-implements none of them. No BR row is changed by this story.

##### 9. State transitions

None. The harness changes no case status, no timer status and no deviation state; it reads records only. The facts below are caused by the owning services and are observed and asserted by the harness.

| Observed fact | Caused by | Asserted as |
|---|---|---|
| Timer expired and escalated to a role | the durable timer inside CaseWorkflow, run by the app story | An expired timer with its escalated role, time and next escalation point (TC-E2-015-04-ITG) |
| Prescription warning raised | the prescription clock, which is never paused | MSG-P3-003 at 60 days and no warning at 91 days (TC-E2-015-03-ITG) |
| Deviation raised | rwb-deviation | The on hold banner and the deviation row (TC-E2-015-02-ITG) |
| Stage clock paused and prescription running | DeviationWorkflow and CaseWorkflow | A paused service level timer and a running prescription (TC-E2-015-06-ITG) |
| Second deviation open | rwb-deviation | Both deviations with the case still on hold (TC-E2-015-05-ITG) |
| Deviation cleared | rwb-deviation | The cleared deviation with outcome Returned and the resumed timer (TC-E2-015-07-ITG) |
| No timer of any status | the timer rows of the case | The empty timers sentence (TC-E2-015-08-ITG) |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | The synthetic user the harness drives: reads the case record view with its timers, prescription date and deviations in scope (Case record R, scope Own) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads the case and its timers, including the escalation it was raised to (Case record R, scope Team) |
| RW-SPECIAL, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-LEGAL | Read the case and its deviations (Case record R) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the case and its deviations (Case record R, scope All); changes nothing |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Writes the escalation fields when a timer escalates, inside the app story; the harness only reads them |

Reading the approver needs no Decision log right: the answer carries the approver user ID only, not the decision log entry. Authorisation is answered by rwb-access through POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise on every call, and the harness asserts the refusal of a role without Case record R.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness calls the owning services; it serves no operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; the 2 s timeout and the circuit breaker per downstream of DP-11 apply to every row.

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case facts, the product group, the status, the prescription date and the deviation flag the banner is built from |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` | P3 rwb-case | The timers with their type, status, due date, warning state, next step owner role and escalation fields |
| POST | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations` | S8 rwb-deviation | Seeds the X1 and X3 deviations of the journey with their handler and contact stop |
| PATCH | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1/deviations/{deviationId}` | S8 rwb-deviation | Clears X1 on 2026-12-14 and asserts the resumed stage clock |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}` | P7 rwb-decision | The approver on decision log entry DLE-9101 (Architecture v5 slide 14: central decision ledger) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The role, scope and Case record right check used by the composite route and by the direct calls (Architecture v5 slide 14 and slide 41: rwb-access IN POST /authorise) |

The composite screen route itself is gateway-bff (DP-19), owned by the platform edge story RWB-PLT-N001-CON. Its path and merge order are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0399; ASM-0574). The deviation data reaches the composite answer through the S8 contract that RWB-S8-E2015-APP publishes; the harness reads no deviation list path, because the ownership map gives none.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness produces no event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | What the harness asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1 | rwb.case.events.v1 | P3 rwb-case | The event is raised when the durable timer inside CaseWorkflow fires, carries the case ID and the timer type, and the escalated role, the escalated time and the next escalation point appear on the timer row the harness reads |
| rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1 | rwb.deviation.events.v1 | S8 rwb-deviation | One event per deviation raised on RW-2026-000502 and RW-2026-000504, carrying the case ID and the deviation code, is present within 5 minutes of the seeding call, and the case then answers as on hold |
| rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1 | rwb.deviation.events.v1 | S8 rwb-deviation | The clear of X1 on RW-2026-000504 and on RW-2026-000505 is announced within 5 minutes, and the answer then carries the cleared deviation and the resumed timer |

The events are consumed for assertion only; order per case is guaranteed by the case key on both topics, and the harness reads timers and deviations through the owning contracts rather than from a topic.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness starts no workflow and adds no activity; it drives REST only. The durable timers belong to CaseWorkflow in rwb-case and the pause and the clear to DeviationWorkflow in rwb-deviation, both owned and started by the app stories; the five minute timer check is retired and the harness replaces it with a fixed clock and seeded timer rows.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The harness run is started by the test pipeline, not by a Temporal Schedule and not by Airflow, and it seeds its timer rows rather than waiting for a scheduler.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubbed answers |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case | cases/{caseId}, cases/{caseId}/timers | RW-2026-000501 with the NOTICE_PERIOD, SERVICE_LEVEL and PRESCRIPTION rows, the expired service level at level 1 escalated to RW-TEAMMGR at 2026-12-12 09:05 with next role RW-PRODHEAD, and the prescription date 2027-02-13; RW-2026-000503 with 2027-03-16; RW-2026-000506 with an empty timers answer; RW-2026-000507 in SME-NTH; the deviation flag on RW-2026-000502 |
| rwb-deviation | cases/{caseId}/deviations, deviations/{deviationId} | X3 on RW-2026-000502 with handler U-SP-01, paused state WITH_FCR_OFFICER, contact stop true and approver U-LG-01; X1 and X3 on RW-2026-000504, X1 cleared on 2026-12-14; X1 cleared on RW-2026-000505 with outcome Returned; a slow answer beyond 2 s for the timeout case |
| rwb-decision | decision-log/{entryId} | Decision log entry DLE-9101 with approver U-LG-01 and decision code X3; the approver of the X1 entries of RW-2026-000504 |
| rwb-access | authorise | Allow RW-CASEOWN in scope; allow the read roles of §10; refuse a role without Case record R with MSG-P4-002; refuse SME-NTH for a scope Own in MTG-BKK with MSG-P4-003 |

The fakes are published from the owning services' OpenAPI documents and are replaced by the real service as each I story lands, contract by contract. The harness repository and its environment: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0399; ASM-0574).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Used | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | Yes | Six consumed operations of §12.2 through gateway-bff and the owning services; one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream |
| Kafka | Yes | Consumes rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1 on rwb.case.events.v1 and rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1 and rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1 on rwb.deviation.events.v1 for the assertions; publishes nothing |
| Temporal | No | Starts no workflow and adds no activity; the durable timers belong to CaseWorkflow and the app story |
| File | No | Reads no file; the run report is a harness artefact, not a service file exchange |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The platform H dependencies named by this table are delivered by the platform wave and are not repeated in the metadata H list. The blocking dependencies of this story are the three I stories.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Test harness | Runs one journey per business date, keyed by story and business date, and stops at the first failed assertion with the trace |
| CaseRecordClient | Harness adapter | Calls the composite case-record route and the six consumed operations of §12.2 with the Idempotency-Key header where the operation requires one |
| FakePack | WireMock project | Serves rwb-case, rwb-deviation, rwb-decision and rwb-access from the published OpenAPI documents of §12.8 |
| SchemaBoundaryCheck | Assertion | Fails the run on any cross-schema reference found in the trace, so a service never reads another service's tables |
| TimerClockFixture | Fixture | Holds the business date at 2026-12-15 and seeds the NOTICE_PERIOD, SERVICE_LEVEL and PRESCRIPTION rows, so the same timer state is produced on every run without waiting for a scheduler |
| PartialAnswerCheck | Assertion | Fails the run when a slow deviation query empties the timers or the prescription section, when the on hold banner is lost, or when a refusal returns an empty list instead of the message |
| RunReportWriter | Reporter | Writes one run report with the trace and the per-assertion result; format and retention Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0399; ASM-0574) |

**Environment and test data**

- Environment: SIT, one namespace, the three I stories deployed from their wave 2 builds or replaced by the §12.8 fakes, with the clock of TimerClockFixture fixed at the business date 2026-12-15. Harness repository, environment and data seeding: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0399; ASM-0574).
- Data: synthetic cases RW-2026-000501 with the three timers and the escalated service level, RW-2026-000502 on hold for X3, RW-2026-000503 at 91 days, RW-2026-000504 with X1 and X3 open, RW-2026-000505 with X1 cleared and the timer resumed, RW-2026-000506 with no timer and RW-2026-000507 in SME-NTH; the users U-CO-01 with RW-CASEOWN, U-SP-01 as the handler and U-LG-01 as the approver; the decision log entry DLE-9101. No production record is copied.
- Reset: each run starts from the seeded state at the fixed business date, so a repeated run is deterministic and the same report is produced.

**Build steps**

1. Build JourneyRunner and CaseRecordClient against the published OpenAPI documents of the owning services.
2. Publish FakePack for the four services from the same documents, and prove the harness runs green from Day 1 on the fakes.
3. Build TimerClockFixture with the business date 2026-12-15 and the seeded timer rows, and prove a run is repeatable without a live scheduler.
4. Add the composite route assertion of AC1, including the one-hop check, the 2 s per-call budget, the single trace and the SchemaBoundaryCheck.
5. Add the escalation and prescription assertions of AC2, the deviation and on hold assertions of AC3 with the clear of X1, and the partial answer of AC4 with PartialAnswerCheck.
6. Replace each fake with the real service as its I story lands, contract by contract, and confirm the same assertions hold against the real services.
7. Publish the run report per business date and add the pass/fail gate agreed with QA; the gate definition: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0399; ASM-0574).

**Feature switch:** the harness has no production feature flag and runs in the test environment only. The production switch it exercises is `rwb.p3.case-clocks` from the legacy solution plan; the harness asserts the disabled state, where SCR-03 shows the Epic 1 read only fields, and the enabled state, where the timers, the escalation and the deviation flag are returned.

**Done when:** the journey runs green against the three deployed I stories in SIT, the run report for the business date holds every assertion of §7 and §16 with its trace, every message of §14 carries its substituted values, and the pass/fail gate agreed with QA is met for one full business date.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-003 | A timer or the prescription date is inside its warning period | {timer} ends on {date}. |
| MSG-P3-004 | The case is on hold for a deviation | This case is on hold for {deviation}. The prescription date is still {date}. |
| MSG-P3-018 | The case has no running, paused or expired timer | There are no running timers on this case. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The deviation module does not answer in time | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Case record R opens the view | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the person's scope | This case is not in your scope. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values, including "Deceased customer" in MSG-P3-004 and "Deviation handling" in MSG-GEN-006; it does not own the message text. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | State | What the harness asserts |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-03 Case record | Loading | The composite route answers at once with the case, the timers and the prescription date; the harness reads the answer the skeleton rows consume |
| SCR-03 Case record | Read only | The timers ordered by due date with type, status, warning state, next step owner role, escalation level, escalated to and next escalation point; the prescription date with its warning |
| SCR-03 Case record | Editable | The same clocks and deviation panels are returned; the edits elsewhere on the record are not exercised by the harness |
| SCR-03 Case record | On hold | The banner with MSG-P3-004 and the prescription date, each open deviation with code, handler, approver, raised date, contact stop and return point, and the cleared deviation with its outcome and the resumed timer |

The harness opens no screen and renders no page; it asserts the composite route answer that the screen consumes. Screen-level behaviour remains with the owning APP stories. The harness environment and evidence detail: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0399; ASM-0574).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the warning days, the escalation roles, the next escalation role, the timeout and the timer and deviation labels are data held by the owning services; the harness reads them and never holds a copy.
- No personal data in logs, tests, traces or reports: only staff user IDs are asserted, customer data is never read into a report, and the harness uses synthetic cases and stores IDs and assertions only.
- No read of another service's schema: every read goes through the owner's contract, the SchemaBoundaryCheck fails the run on a cross-schema reference, and only rwb-source-data reads the ACE views.
- No production data and no outside system: the harness calls only the owning services and their fakes, never an outside gateway or a production endpoint.
- The view never changes a timer, a deviation or the case: the harness asserts that a read, a refusal and the timeout case leave every source unchanged.
- One hop only: the harness fails a run when the trace shows a call chain deeper than the gateway and one owner.

- The contract baselines of rwb-case, rwb-deviation, rwb-decision and rwb-access, which their CON stories own.

- Starting, pausing and resuming timers and the escalation itself (RWB-E1-028).
- The history timeline on the case (RWB-E2-016).
- The next action panel (RWB-E2-035).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-016 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead of rwb-case**, I want **the published contract baseline for the case timeline: an OpenAPI 3.1 document for `GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline` with its query, its page and item shapes, its seven type values, its paging bounds and its error mapping, the consumed-operation list of the P7, P5, P6, P1 and P4 contracts with the one-hop 2-second rule, the event facts a timeline item reflects, the nine contract tables and the five contract fakes**, so that **the app story RWB-P3-E2016-APP, the deployment story and the wave 2 integration harness build on Day 1 against one fixed, testable contract instead of waiting for each other**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The timeline is the widest read in the workbench: it merges the records of five owners and it is the screen a new case owner opens first. If the item shape, the type list, the paging bounds and the partial-answer rule are agreed once and faked, the app story builds in parallel with rwb-decision, rwb-document, rwb-comms, rwb-source-data and rwb-access, and a change in any of those contracts is caught in a contract test rather than in an integration window.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_case`, REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1` (DP-13), task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`. No topic is declared, because the timeline publishes nothing (DP-14 applies only as a prohibition here). The baseline states one operation and one named view of it, because queue history is the same operation filtered to ASSIGNMENT and TRANSFER, so a consumer cannot drift into a second path for the same answer.

Two points of the consumed surface are open and are carried as register rows rather than guessed: the owner-side read path of the case's interaction-ledger entries, which the two Ownership Map rulings place with different owners (GAP-0716; ASM-1263), and the Ownership Map row of the case-scoped notice list that Architecture v5 slide 17 gives rwb-comms (GAP-0717; ASM-1264). Until they close, the fakes serve the shapes the document fixes and the app and harness stories build against them.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the schema, the queue and the Java package follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the RFC 9457 problem details and the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope are the platform baseline; where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The parameters contract and the reference-data contract of rwb-case are published (RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON), because the source timeout, the page size bounds and the type and reason labels are contracted as rows and not as constants.
- The operations and their owners come from the Ownership Map only; the document never declares another service's operation as provided by rwb-case.
- The legacy contract of RWB-E2-016 is read for the item fields, the error codes and the message texts; no business value is changed by this baseline.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document for the timeline operation, with the shared components that the other rwb-case reads reuse.
2. Fix the `TimelinePage` and `TimelineItem` components, the seven type values, the twelve item fields and the `unavailableSources[]` entry, with an example for each type.
3. Fix the query: `type`, `from`, `to`, `page` and `size`, with the default and the bounds read from the parameters contract, and document queue history as the same operation with a fixed type filter.
4. State the rights rule per item type, the silent omission rule and the three refusals, and map each HTTP status to its message ID.
5. Publish the consumed-operation list of 12.2 with the one-hop, 2 s and breaker rule, and name the two open points with their register rows.
6. Declare the event facts a timeline item reflects, and state that the timeline publishes no event and holds no projection.
7. Publish the nine contract tables of section 12 and the five contract fakes with their fixtures.
8. Add the contract tests: schema validation, paging bounds, type validation, error mapping, the rights filter and fake drift.
9. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P3-E2016-APP, to RWB-P3-E2016-OPS and to RWB-ITG-E2016-ITG.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A query value is outside its bounds: `size` outside 1 to 200, `page` negative, `type` outside the seven | 422 with the error envelope naming the field and its bounds; no source is called | MSG-GEN-002 | AC2 |
| X2 | `to` is before `from` | 422 with the error envelope naming both fields; no source is called | MSG-GEN-003 | AC2 |
| X3 | The caller holds no Case record R | 403 with the error envelope; the answer is a refusal, never an empty page | MSG-P4-002 | AC3 |
| X4 | The case is unknown or outside the caller's scope | 404 with the error envelope; the two conditions are deliberately one answer | MSG-P4-003 | AC3 |
| X5 | A consumed operation has no agreed path | The document carries the placeholder and the register row; the fake serves the shape only, and the field-level path is settled with the owner before the app story's Done | None | AC5 |
| X6 | A fake drifts from the document | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC5 |
| X7 | A field-level definition is missing from the source material | The field is marked with the placeholder and one gap row is carried, and no value is invented | None | AC1 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the Ownership Map and the legacy contract only |
| Negotiable | Item wording in the examples, the filter layout and the summary text are settled with the consumers; the operation, the item fields, the type list, the bounds and the rules are fixed by the target |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app story, the deployment story and the wave 2 harness on Day 1, and gives the five upstream owners one document to build their fakes from |
| Estimable | One document, one component set, one operation with a named view, nine contract tables, five fakes and six contract tests |
| Small | Fits one iteration with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact and the fakes, not against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Case timeline contract baseline for rwb-case

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule of the platform library is in force
    Given the base of rwb-case is /api/recovery/case/v1 and its login is its own (DP-02)

  Scenario: AC1 The document describes the timeline operation and its shapes (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-case is published
    When it is validated against the OpenAPI 3.1 schema
    Then it validates with no error
    Then it declares GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline on the base /api/recovery/case/v1 with the owner rwb-case
    Then the TimelinePage component declares items, page, size, total and unavailableSources
    Then the TimelineItem component declares at, type, summary, by, reference, reasonCode, fromQueueCode, toQueueCode and ruleId
    Then the document states that queue history is the same operation with type ASSIGNMENT and TRANSFER and declares no second path for it

  Scenario: AC2 The query, the type list and the bounds are in the contract (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the document declares the query type, from, to, page and size
    When a consumer reads the parameter definitions
    Then type lists exactly DECISION, ASSIGNMENT, TRANSFER, INTERACTION, NOTICE, DOCUMENT and TIMER
    Then page defaults to 0 and size defaults to 50 with a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 200, and both defaults are named as parameter rows of the parameters contract
    Then a size outside 1 to 200, a negative page or an unknown type is refused with 422 and MSG-GEN-002
    Then a to date before the from date is refused with 422 and MSG-GEN-003
    Then no rule of the document fixes a page size or a timeout as a literal

  Scenario: AC3 The rights rule per item type and the refusals are stated (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the document declares the operation under Case record R with the scope applied
    When a consumer reads the access section
    Then a decision item requires Decision log R, a document item requires Documents R and a notice item requires Litigation R
    Then an item type the caller may not read is left out of the answer with no error and no gap in the other items
    Then a caller without Case record R is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002, and an unknown or out-of-scope case is 404 with MSG-P4-003
    Then the 401, 403, 404, 422 and 503 responses are declared for the operation

  Scenario: AC4 A slow or missing source is part of the answer, not an error (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the document declares unavailableSources as a list of entries with system and messageId
    When a consumed source does not answer inside the 2 s budget or its breaker is open
    Then the operation still answers 200 with the remaining items and one entry per missing source carrying MSG-GEN-006
    Then the document states one hop, a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream for every consumed operation
    Then the document states that the timeline writes nothing, publishes nothing and holds no projection

  Scenario: AC5 The consumed operations and the five fakes match the document (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the contract section of this story
    When the consumed operations of 12.2 are reviewed against the Ownership Map
    Then every consumed operation names its owner from the map and its one-hop 2 s budget
    Then the two operations without an agreed path carry their register rows and a fake that serves the shape only
    Then the five fakes answer the paths and payloads of 12.2 and the contract tests fail on any drift
    Then no operation of another service is declared as provided by rwb-case

  Scenario: AC6 The nine contract tables and the event facts are complete (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the contract section of this story
    When the nine sub-tables are reviewed
    Then each of 12.1 to 12.9 is present and names its owner from the Ownership Map
    Then 12.3 is None and no topic is declared for the timeline
    Then 12.4 names DecisionRecorded, DeviationRaised, DeviationCleared, PaymentMissed and TreatmentBooked as the facts that create timeline items
    Then 12.7 names recovery_case, assignment, queue and timer and never the interaction table
    Then the document states that a contact summary is masked by role before it is returned
```

These six criteria test the artefact only. They restate no legacy criterion of RWB-E2-016: the eleven legacy criteria belong to RWB-P3-E2016-APP and their cross-service copies to RWB-ITG-E2016-ITG.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/case/v1`; the document never declares another service's base | DP-13; Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | The timeline publishes nothing, so no topic and no event name is declared for it; a legacy `rwb.p3.` or `rwb.casewf.` name never appears | DP-14; Architecture v5 slide 42 |
| BR3 | One operation serves the timeline and the queue history; the queue history is a named view with a fixed type filter, not a second path | Legacy contract; REQ-WKM-008 |
| BR4 | The item fields are fixed at twelve: `at`, `type`, `summary`, `by`, `reference`, `reasonCode`, `fromQueueCode`, `toQueueCode`, `ruleId`, and with `page`, `size` and `total` on the page | Legacy contract; RWB-P3-E2016-APP §12.1 |
| BR5 | The seven type values are a list value of the reference data with a version in force; they are never a Java enum and never a literal in the document | DP-07; LOV types |
| BR6 | `page` starts at 0, `size` starts at 50 and is limited to 1 to 200; the three numbers are parameter rows read through the parameters contract | DP-06; legacy contract |
| BR7 | The rights rule is per item type: Decision log R for a decision item, Documents R for a document item, Litigation R for a notice item, and Case record R for the operation itself | CTL-09; roles.txt Permissions |
| BR8 | An item type the caller may not read is omitted silently; the document states the omission so a consumer never reads an empty list as a failure | BR7; legacy AC5 |
| BR9 | A source that does not answer is an `unavailableSources[]` entry with MSG-GEN-006 on a 200 answer, never a 5xx of the timeline | NFR-008; MSG-GEN-006 |
| BR10 | Every consumed operation is one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream; a chain deeper than one is a contract defect | DP-11; ADR-020 |
| BR11 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition; the business texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story | Architecture v5 platform baseline; Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR12 | The contract names only rwb-case tables; `interaction` is another service's table and is documented as consumed, never as owned | DP-01; DP-18; ASM-0067 |
| BR13 | The document fixes shapes and no business value: no threshold, no label text, no reason code and no timeout is written as a literal | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| Tech lead of rwb-case | Owns the document, the component set and the five fakes; tags the baseline |
