The per-service login name behind the security scheme is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0675; ASM-1222); the document names it "the rwb-case login (DP-02)".

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| TimelinePage | `items[]` of TimelineItem, `page` (integer), `size` (integer), `total` (integer), `unavailableSources[]` of `system` and `messageId` |
| TimelineItem | `at` (date-time), `type` (one of the seven list values), `summary` (built from codes and labels, masked for a contact), `by` (the actor reference), `reference` (the ID of the source item), `reasonCode`, `fromQueueCode`, `toQueueCode`, `ruleId` |
| Queue-history view | The same item with `type` in ASSIGNMENT and TRANSFER, carrying from and to queue, from and to owner, `reasonCode` and `ruleId` |
| Case sources | `recovery_case` (DF-CAS-001, DF-CAS-011), `assignment` (DF-WRK-010, DF-WRK-012 to DF-WRK-016, DF-WRK-039, DF-WRK-040), `queue` (DF-WRK-002), `timer` (DF-WRK-030, DF-WRK-031, DF-WRK-035) |
| Consumed sources | `decision_log_entry` (DF-DEC-001, DF-DEC-003, DF-DEC-004, DF-DEC-012, DF-DEC-016) through P7; `document` (DF-DOC-001, DF-DOC-004, DF-DOC-005) through P5; `notice` (DF-LEG-015, DF-LEG-018, DF-LEG-019, DF-LEG-022) through P6; `interaction` (DF-INT-002, DF-INT-004 to DF-INT-011) through P1 |
| No personal data | No name, address, identity number or contact point is a property of an item; a contact summary is masked by role before it is returned (CTL-11, DL26) |

The field names above are fixed by this baseline. The physical types and lengths of a `TimelineItem` property and the summary template per type are settled with the consumers at the baseline review; this story fixes no value and invents none.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-case (P3); base `/api/recovery/case/v1`.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/timeline` | `TimelinePage`; query `type` (comma separated, the seven values), `from` (date), `to` (date), `page` (integer, default 0), `size` (integer, default 50, 1 to 200) | Case record R, scope applied; item types filtered by Decision log R, Documents R and Litigation R |

The queue history is documented as the same operation with `type=ASSIGNMENT,TRANSFER`; the document gives it a section of its own and no second path (BR3).

The interaction operations that TSD P3 v3 records as API-P3-014 and API-P3-015 are not documented as provided here: the Ownership Map gives them to rwb-source-data (P1) under ASM-0038, while the table ruling keeps the timeline and interaction API with rwb-case under ASM-0067. The baseline therefore documents the case-scoped interaction read it consumes and leaves the owner-side path open with its register row (GAP-0716; ASM-1263).

The interaction read the timeline consumes has the shape TSD P3 v3 gives API-P3-014: the query `from`, `to`, `page` and `size`, and per entry `occurredAt`, `channel`, `direction`, `contactResult` and `summary`, with the summary masked by role. That shape is declared as consumed in 12.2 with its budget, and it is superseded by the P1 contract wherever the two differ, because the ledger is P1's.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Documented use | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | P7 rwb-decision | The ledger entries of a case in the date range | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}` | P7 rwb-decision | One ledger entry, the reference a decision item carries | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` | P5 rwb-document | The document metadata of a case in the date range | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices` | P6 rwb-comms | The case-scoped notice list; Architecture v5 slide 17 names it and the Ownership Map has no row for it (GAP-0717; ASM-1264) | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}` | P6 rwb-comms | One notice by ID | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0716; ASM-1263) | P1 rwb-source-data | The case's interaction-ledger entries, for the contact items | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Case record R, the scope and the item-type rights, cached | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies` | P4 rwb-access | The masking policy of the caller's role; the mask is applied by the ACE common masking path | One hop, 2 s, cached |

The masking path is the operation Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access (`/masking-policies`); the Ownership Map API section has no row for it, so the document takes the path from that slide and confirms it in the rwb-access contract baseline (RWB-P4-E1037-CON).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The timeline writes no row and raises no event, so the contract declares no topic, no event type and no outbox row for it. A consumer must not expect a `rwb.case.*` type for a read of the history, and the six rwb-case event types of the service contract are unchanged by this baseline.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | What it declares |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7; every service writes its own record | The ledger link a decision item carries: the record reference, the rule ID, the rule version, the final call and the decided time |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` (EV-06) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 | A pause fact that becomes a timer item and a decision item on the case |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` (EV-07) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 | The end of the pause, which becomes a later timer item |
| `rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1` (EV-12) | `rwb.payment.events.v1` | P8 | A missed payment that becomes an interaction item, a timer item and a decision item |
| `rwb.payment.TreatmentBooked.v1` (EV-11) | `rwb.payment.events.v1` | P8 | A booking that becomes an interaction item and a decision item |

These five types are the facts that create a timeline item; they reach rwb-case through the case router of the stories that move the case, and the timeline itself consumes none of them, because it reads the resulting state instead of a projection. The last four are declared here so that the harness and a consumer know which facts must appear as items; the first is the ledger link of every decision item.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow | Workflow, parent, one per case, workflow ID = case ID (reference only) | `rwb-case` | No input or output schema is added by this baseline: the workflow writes the `assignment` and `timer` rows the timeline reads through its own activities, and the timeline starts no workflow and adds no activity |

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The timeline is answered inside the request, and the legacy five-minute timer check (JOB-05) is retired in favour of durable timers inside the workflow (Architecture v5 slide 44), so the contract declares no Schedule and no Quartz row.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| recovery_case | P3 (rwb_case) | Case ID and team of the answer |
| assignment | P3 (rwb_case) | The assignment and transfer items with queue, reason, reason code and rule ID |
| queue | P3 (rwb_case) | The queue code of a move |
| timer | P3 (rwb_case) | The timer items with type, start and status |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_case | The library objects of the schema; the timeline writes none of them |

`interaction` is never named as a table of this contract: it is owned by rwb-source-data under ASM-0067 and DP-18 and is read through the P1 contract (BR12). No other table is named and no foreign key crosses a schema.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-source-data WireMock | The case interaction-ledger entries with channel, direction, contact result and a summary that must come back masked; an empty answer; a delay beyond 2 s; the shape served without an agreed path | App story, harness, contract tests |
| rwb-document WireMock | The case document list with type and source; an empty answer; a delay beyond 2 s | App story, harness, contract tests |
| rwb-comms WireMock | The case notice list and the notice by ID, with type, sent date and delivery status; an empty answer | App story, harness, contract tests |
| rwb-decision WireMock | The ledger by case with entry IDs and decided times; one entry by ID; an empty answer | App story, harness, contract tests |
| rwb-access WireMock | `POST /authorise` with a granted answer for all four rights, a granted answer without Decision log R and without Litigation R, a refusal without Case record R, a refusal outside the scope; the masking policy of a role | App story, harness, contract tests |

Each fake is published from the same document and replaced by the real service as it lands, contract by contract; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 provided, 8 consumed | The timeline operation provided with the queue-history view; the P7 ledger by case and by entry, the P5 document list, the P6 notice list and notice, the P1 ledger read and the P4 authorise and masking policy consumed; one hop, 2 s, breaker |
| Kafka | None published, five types declared as the facts of an item | `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` for the ledger link and the four facts that create items; the timeline itself consumes none |
| Temporal | One workflow referenced, none added | CaseWorkflow writes the assignment and timer rows; the timeline starts nothing |
| File | None | No document content is part of the contract; the P5 metadata is the only document fact |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `openapi/rwb-case-v1-timeline.yaml` (the operation and components, merged into the service document), the queue-history section of the same file, the `contract/timeline-examples/` set with one example per type, the five WireMock mapping sets and the contract README with the paging, rights and partial-answer rules.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the item's reference is the record reference | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library; no topic for a read | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The platform dependencies of this table are held by the platform CON stories and are not repeated in the metadata rows, which are all None by the Day-1 rule.

**Build steps**

1. OpenAPI skeleton with the base, the security scheme, the error responses and the shared components; schema lint in the pipeline.
2. `TimelinePage`, `TimelineItem` and the `unavailableSources[]` entry, with an example for each of the seven types and a masked contact example.
3. The query definitions, the default and bounds from the parameter rows, and the queue-history section.
4. The access section: the four rights, the silent omission rule, the 401, 403, 404, 422 and 503 mapping and the message IDs.
5. The consumed-operation list with the budget, the two register rows and the note on the masking path.
6. The five fakes and their fixtures, including the delayed and the empty answers.
7. The six contract tests, including a drift test that compares each fake with the document and a bounds test that reads the parameter defaults.
8. Baseline tag, the sign-off note of the app, deployment and harness stories, and the handover of the two open points to the P1 and P6 owners.

**Done when.** The document validates in the pipeline, the six contract tests pass, the five fakes answer every consumed path or its placeholder, and the app, deployment and harness stories have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-019 | No item matches the filter (the screen text of an empty page with total 0) | Nothing on this case matches the filter. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A source module does not answer in time | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Date to is before date from | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | Page size outside 1 to 200, a negative page, or an unknown type | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Case record R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the caller's scope or unknown | This case is not in your scope. |

The message IDs are contract elements; the text is the agreed text taken from the legacy story where the message already existed, and no new business message is invented by this baseline. For MSG-GEN-006 the {system} value is documented per source so a consumer can map it, and Thai text follows DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves SCR-04 Case timeline in its Loading, Filtered and Empty states and the queue-history tab on the same screen, and it supplies the timeline section of SCR-03 Case record. All of them are served by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), owned by RWB-PLT-N001-CON, which calls rwb-case and the other owners in parallel and merges the answers; the document fixes the case side of that merge and no screen field list.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the document: the type list, the labels, the reason codes, the timeout and the page size bounds are rows and parameters, and an example never fixes one.
- No personal data in a component, an example or a fake: IDs, codes, dates and amounts only, and a contact summary appears only in its masked form.
- The contract names only rwb-case tables and only operations owned by rwb-case; another service's operation is documented as consumed, never as provided (DP-01).
- One base per service and no topic for a read: a document that names another base, or a `rwb.p3.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic, fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- Every example is synthetic; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The error envelope, the problem-details shape and the naming rule come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.
- An open point is written as a register row and a placeholder, never guessed into a path.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-016 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **the case record view to show every action, decision, transfer, letter, document, contact and timer event of my case on one timeline with type and date filters and a paged answer, and the queue history with the reason for each move, read from rwb-case and from the decision log, document, notice and interaction-ledger contracts**, so that **I read the whole case in one place, inside the 2-second wait, with no service reading another service's schema and no item that my role may not see**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A case lives for months or years and passes through several teams, partners and courts. Today a new owner reads email threads and spreadsheets to learn what happened. This story puts the decision log entries, assignments and transfers, contacts, notices, documents and timer events of a case on one timeline, filtered by type and date, with a queue history that shows every queue and owner and the reason for each move. It meets REQ-WKM-008 and REQ-OCC-008. The measure is that a case history with 30 events reads in under 2 seconds (NFR-009) and stays under 2 seconds at the 2031 data size (NFR-070).

In the target the same journey is cut across services and the read is composed from owners rather than from one schema. rwb-case holds the case, its `assignment`, `queue`, `timer` and `recovery_case` rows (DP-01). The decision items come from the central decision ledger of rwb-decision (P7), the document items from the metadata of rwb-document (P5), the notice items from rwb-comms (P6), the contact items from the interaction ledger owned by rwb-source-data (P1) under the default ruling and DP-18, and the rights and the mask from rwb-access (P4). The legacy in-process calls `DecisionLogQuery.forCase`, `DocumentQuery.forCase` and `NoticeQuery.forCase` become REST calls on the owners' bases, one hop, with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11), built against the contract fakes on Day 1.

Retiring the monolith surface is the realignment work. The legacy endpoint `GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline` on the shared base moves to `/api/recovery/case/v1` (DP-13), the page size limits and the per-source timeout become parameter rows read through the parameters contract instead of configuration in code (DP-06), the type and reason labels come from the reference-data contract with their version in force (DP-07), and the case screen is composed at the edge by gateway-bff, which calls rwb-case and the other owners in parallel and merges the answers (DP-19). No topic is published by this read; the event naming rule of DP-14 is respected in that the story declares no topic of its own.

Two values of the target are not settled by the sources and are carried as register rows: the owner-side read path of the case's interaction-ledger entries, because the interaction API is claimed by both P3 and P1 in the Ownership Map (GAP-0716; ASM-1263), and the Ownership Map row of the case-scoped notice list that Architecture v5 slide 17 gives rwb-comms (GAP-0717; ASM-1264). The story builds against the P1, P5, P6, P7 and P4 contract fakes and is proven end to end by RWB-ITG-E2016-ITG.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P3-E2016-CON is published: the operation shape of `GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline`, the `TimelinePage` and `TimelineItem` components with the seven type values, the error mapping, the nine contract tables and the fakes of P1, P4, P5, P6 and P7.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the local decision-record library, the record reference shape and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03). The decision item carries the ledger entry ID as its reference; this story writes no record.
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1042-CON are published: the parameters contract and its client library, so the source timeout and the page size limits are rows and not constants (DP-06).
- RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are published: the reference-data contract, with LOV-ASSIGN-REASON and LOV-TRANSFER-REASON and the type labels loaded and versioned (DP-07).
- RWB-PLT-E1047-CON is published: the naming library, so no topic or base is chosen locally (DP-14).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route that serves the case screen and composes the timeline answer with the case answer (DP-19).
- RWB-P3-E2015-APP is done: the clocks and deviations panels on SCR-03, whose timer rows this story reads on the same screen.
- RWB-P3-E2012-APP is done: every new assignment carries its queue and its transfer reason code, so a queue-history item can show from queue, to queue, reason code and rule ID.
- RWB-P3-E1035-CON is published: the case record view v1.1 contract, whose timeline answer this story extends with the paging, the queue history, the four extra item fields and `unavailableSources[]`, so no field of v1.1 is removed and a v1.1 consumer keeps working.
- The decision log, document, notice and interaction-ledger contracts are consumed and faked; the case-scoped interaction read is built against the P1 fake while its path is settled (GAP-0716; ASM-1263), and the case-scoped notice list is read under the P6 contract against the P6 fake (GAP-0717; ASM-1264).
- The roles of section 10 hold Case record R with the case in scope, and Decision log R, Documents R and Litigation R for the item types they may read, all answered by rwb-access.
- The login is the rwb-case login (DP-02): Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0675; ASM-1222).

##### 4. Flow

1. Case owner: opens SCR-04 Case timeline from SCR-03 Case record. The browser calls the gateway-bff composite route and never an owner service directly (DP-19).
2. gateway-bff: calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline` on rwb-case, one hop each, and merges the two answers into the screen model.
3. rwb-case: applies the access check through rwb-access (`POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise`), which returns Case record R, the scope and the item-type rights Decision log R, Documents R and Litigation R; a missing Case record R is a 403 and a case outside the scope is a 404.
4. rwb-case: reads the case's own records from `rwb_case` — `assignment` with `queue_code`, `recovery_case` and `timer` — for the date range, using the case indexes only.
5. rwb-case: in parallel, and only for the item types the caller may read, calls the owners' operations of section 12.2: the ledgers of P7 by case, P5 by case, P6 by case, and P1 for the interaction ledger; each call runs in an activity-free request thread with one hop, a 2 s timeout taken from the parameter `timeline.source-timeout-ms`, and a breaker per downstream.
6. rwb-case: maps every record to a `TimelineItem` with `at`, `type`, `summary`, `by`, `reference`, and, for an assignment or a transfer, `reasonCode`, `fromQueueCode`, `toQueueCode` and `ruleId`; the summary is built from codes and labels, never from free text of another service.
7. rwb-case: drops the item types the caller may not read without an error (decision items without Decision log R, document items without Documents R, notice items without Litigation R), masks each contact summary by role through the ACE common masking path with the masking policy read from rwb-access, merges the remaining items newest first with the source sequence kept on a tie, and returns one page with `page`, `size`, `total` and `unavailableSources[]`.
8. rwb-case: on a source that times out or has its breaker open, adds one entry to `unavailableSources[]` with MSG-GEN-006 for that source and returns the other items; the call itself does not fail.
9. Case owner: filters by type and by date; the front end repeats the call with `type`, `from` and `to` and shows the answer in state Filtered. A page beyond the last returns an empty `items[]` with the same `total`.
10. Case owner: opens Queue history; the front end calls the same operation with `type=ASSIGNMENT,TRANSFER` and shows from queue, to queue, from owner, to owner, reason code and rule ID for each move, with the allocation as the oldest entry.
11. Case owner: opens a decision item; the front end opens the entry through `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}` on the P7 contract, which is the reference the item already carries.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A source module does not answer within 2 seconds, or its breaker is open | The other items show; one entry per missing source names it in `unavailableSources[]`; the call returns 200 | MSG-GEN-006 | AC6 |
| X2 | The caller lacks Decision log R, Documents R or Litigation R | Those item types are left out without an error and without a gap in the other items | None | AC5 |
| X3 | Date from is after date to | Refused before any source is called; nothing is read and nothing is written | MSG-GEN-003 | AC7 |
| X4 | No item matches the filter | An empty page with total 0 and the empty sentence on the screen | MSG-P3-019 | AC8 |
| X5 | An assignment written before RWB-E2-012 has no queue | The move shows with "Queue not recorded" and its reason, and the run continues | None | AC9 |
| X6 | The case is outside the caller's scope | Not found; nothing is returned and nothing is written | MSG-P4-003 | AC10 |
| X7 | Page size is outside 1 to 200, or not an integer | Refused before any source is called, with the field and its bounds | MSG-GEN-002 | AC7, AC11 |
| X8 | The item count of a case exceeds one page | The first page returns with `total` and `page` and the caller pages; the order is stable across the pages of one query | None | AC11 |
| X9 | The caller holds no Case record R | Refused with 403 on the service call and on the composite route; the answer carries the refusal, not an empty timeline | MSG-P4-002 | AC5 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads what other stories write; builds on Day 1 against the case contract and the P1, P4, P5, P6 and P7 contract fakes. The queue on the assignment comes from RWB-P3-E2012-APP and the timer projection from RWB-P3-E1035-CON |
| Negotiable | Item wording, the filter layout and the summary text can change; the sources, the rights and the ordering are fixed |
| Valuable | A new owner reads the case without asking the previous one, and no team waits for another team's release to see the history |
| Estimable | One endpoint, one merge service, one rights filter, five consumed contracts, one screen with two states and a queue-history tab |
| Small | Fits one iteration with its tests |
| Testable | API tests with seeded `rwb_case` rows and stubbed contracts; one load test at 4,000 items; no test reaches another schema |


Four mechanism moves sit behind these criteria and change no value of them. First, the contact items are built in rwb-case from the interaction ledger, which the Ownership Map gives to rwb-source-data (ASM-0067, DP-18), so the ledger is read one hop away through the P1 contract and never from an `interaction` table in `rwb_case`; the owner-side path and the base are contested by the two rulings of the map (GAP-0716; ASM-1263). Second, the decision, document and notice items come from the P7, P5 and P6 contracts in place of the legacy in-process queries, each with one hop, the 2 s timeout of the parameter and a breaker, which is why each cross-service Given above is paired with its contract mock. Third, the case-scoped notice list is given by Architecture v5 slide 17 to rwb-comms and has no row in the Ownership Map API section (GAP-0717; ASM-1264). Fourth, queue history is the same operation with `type=ASSIGNMENT,TRANSFER`, so AC3 opens no second endpoint and no second contract. Nothing is projected: the items are merged on the read, so a source that is down removes its own items and nothing else.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The timeline holds every assignment, transfer, contact, decision log entry, notice, document and timer event of the case | REQ-WKM-008; casemodel.txt Case file |
| BR2 | Items are ordered newest first; items at the same time keep the order of their sources' sequence | events.txt Rules (ordering) |
| BR3 | A decision item shows only to a role with Decision log R, a document item only with Documents R, a notice item only with Litigation R | roles.txt Permissions; CTL-09 |
| BR4 | Queue history shows each assignment with its from and to queue, from and to owner, reason, reason code and rule ID | REQ-WKM-008; REQ-CWC-016 |
| BR5 | A decision item links to its decision log entry, which is never changed; a correction shows as a further entry | R-UNI-24; REQ-DRI-002 |
| BR6 | Personal data in a contact summary is masked by role | CTL-11; DL26 |
| BR7 | A source that does not answer in time does not stop the timeline | NFR-008 |
| BR8 | Paging is part of the operation: `page` starts at 0, `size` starts at 50 and is limited to 1 to 200; a value outside the bounds is refused with MSG-GEN-002 before any source is called | Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-06; legacy contract |
| BR9 | The same query repeated returns the same page, and two items at the same instant keep the source sequence, so a caller may page a long history without a lost or a doubled item | events.txt Rules (ordering); BR2 |
| BR10 | `unavailableSources[]` carries one entry with MSG-GEN-006 for each source that timed out or whose breaker is open, and the remaining items still return with 200 | NFR-008; MSG-GEN-006 |
| BR11 | The timeline reads `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `queue` and `timer` in `rwb_case` and the owners' contracts; it never reads another service's table, and `interaction` is not a table of this service | DP-01; DP-18; ASM-0067; ADR-010 |
| BR12 | The role mask of a contact summary is applied through the ACE common masking path with the policy read from rwb-access; the unmasked summary is never returned and never logged | CTL-11; DL26 |
| BR13 | The call writes nothing: no row, no decision record, no event and no workflow state, and a refusal writes nothing either | Legacy solution plan; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR14 | The source timeout and the page size bounds are parameter rows read through the parameters contract, and the type and reason labels come from the reference data with the version in force | DP-06; DP-07; legacy solution plan |
| BR15 | A type value outside the seven of the contract is refused with MSG-GEN-002 and is never ignored, so a filter that is meant to narrow the answer can never widen it | Legacy contract; BR8 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status and does not move a case. It reads records only, writes no row, raises no event and starts no workflow.

| Observed fact | Written by | Appears as |
|---|---|---|
| Case allocated to a queue | rwb-case allocation (RWB-P3-E1020-APP) | The oldest queue-history entry with reason ALLOCATION |
| Case transferred with a reason code | rwb-case transfer (RWB-P3-E1021-APP) | A later queue-history entry with from and to queue, from and to owner, reason code and rule ID |
| Decision recorded | rwb-decision ledger through the local decision-record library | A decision item with the ledger entry ID as its reference |
| Document attached | rwb-document metadata | A document item, left out without Documents R |
| Notice sent | rwb-comms notice | A notice item, left out without Litigation R |
| Timer started or breached | rwb-case timer projection | A timer item with its type, start and status |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the timeline and queue history (Case record R; Decision log R; Documents R; Litigation R) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads the timeline and queue history (Case record R; Decision log R) |
| RW-PHONECOL, phone collector | Reads the timeline without decisions and notices (Case record R; Documents R) |
| RW-CONDUCT, conduct and QA officer | Reads every item (R in all areas) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads every item (R in all areas); changes nothing |
| rwb-case service identity (the rwb-case login, DP-02) | Applies the access check, reads the `rwb_case` rows and calls the P1, P5, P6 and P7 contracts one hop away; writes nothing |
| gateway-bff (the platform edge) | Calls the case and timeline operations and merges the two answers for the screen; holds no copy of the items |
| RW-REFADM and every role without Case record R | Refused on the operation with MSG-P4-002 |

The per-service login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0675; ASM-1222); the story names it "the rwb-case login (DP-02)" until it is agreed.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/case/v1`; owner rwb-case (P3).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/timeline` | One page of the case timeline: `items[]` newest first, `page`, `size`, `total`, `unavailableSources[]`; query `type` (comma separated DECISION, ASSIGNMENT, TRANSFER, INTERACTION, NOTICE, DOCUMENT, TIMER), `from` (date), `to` (date), `page` (integer, default 0), `size` (integer, default 50, 1 to 200) | Case record R, scope applied; item types filtered by Decision log R, Documents R and Litigation R | Not applicable: the call writes nothing |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/timeline` with `type=ASSIGNMENT,TRANSFER` | Queue history: the same operation with the type filter fixed, so each item carries from queue, to queue, from owner, to owner, `reasonCode` and `ruleId`; no second path is published | As above | Not applicable |

`TimelinePage` fields: `items[]` of `TimelineItem`, `page`, `size`, `total`, `unavailableSources[]`. `TimelineItem` fields: `at`, `type`, `summary`, `by`, `reference`, `reasonCode`, `fromQueueCode`, `toQueueCode`, `ruleId`; `reference` is the decision log entry ID, the document ID, the notice ID, the assignment ID or the timer ID of its source. `unavailableSources[]` entries carry `system` and `messageId` (MSG-GEN-006) per missing source.

Errors: 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Case record R (MSG-P4-002); 404 unknown or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 422 `to` before `from` (MSG-GEN-003), a `size` outside 1 to 200 or a `type` outside the seven (MSG-GEN-002); 503 the case store is down. A downstream that is down is not a 5xx of this operation: it is an `unavailableSources[]` entry with 200 (BR10).

The interaction operation that TSD P3 v3 records as API-P3-014 is owned by rwb-source-data under the Ownership Map (`GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions`, owner P1; ASM-0038), while the table ruling keeps the case timeline and interaction API with rwb-case (ASM-0067). This story therefore serves the timeline, which carries the contact items, and reads the ledger one hop away as consumed in 12.2; the owner-side path is the open point (GAP-0716; ASM-1263).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; the 2 s timeout of `timeline.source-timeout-ms` and a breaker per downstream apply to every row.

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}` | rwb-decision (P7) | The ledger entries of the case in the date range, for the decision items: `id`, `decisionCode`, `ruleId`, `finalCall`, `decidedAt` | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}` | rwb-decision (P7) | One ledger entry when the case owner opens a decision item | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` | rwb-document (P5) | The document metadata of the case in the date range, for the document items: `id`, `documentType`, `source` | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices` | rwb-comms (P6) | The case-scoped notice list, for the notice items: `id`, `noticeType`, `sentDate`, `deliveryStatus`; the path is Architecture v5 slide 17 and has no Ownership Map row (GAP-0717; ASM-1264) | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}` | rwb-comms (P6) | One notice when a notice item is opened | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0716; ASM-1263) | rwb-source-data (P1) | The case's interaction-ledger entries for the contact items: `occurredAt`, `channel`, `direction`, `contactResult`, `summary` | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | rwb-access (P4) | Case record R, the scope and the item-type rights Decision log R, Documents R and Litigation R, cached by the guard library | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies` | rwb-access (P4) | The masking policy the ACE common masking path applies to a contact summary by role (CTL-11, DL26) | One hop, 2 s, cached |

The masking path is the operation Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access (`/masking-policies`); the Ownership Map API section has no row for it, so its path is taken from that slide and confirmed in the rwb-access contract baseline (RWB-P4-E1037-CON). No other service is called, and the timeline never calls a downstream of a downstream.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The timeline is a read: it writes no row and raises no event, so it has no outbox row and no topic of its own. The decision-record reference it shows is written by the local decision-record library of the story that took the decision (DP-03), and the record itself is sealed in the central ledger by rwb-decision.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The facts that become a timeline item arrive in rwb-case through the case router of the stories that move the case; the timeline holds no projection and no inbox, so it consumes nothing and its answer is always the current state of its sources. A stale item is therefore impossible, and a missing source is visible in `unavailableSources[]` rather than frozen into a table.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The timeline is served inside the request; it starts no workflow, adds no activity and holds no timer. The assignment and timer rows it reads are written by the activities of CaseWorkflow and of the allocation and transfer stories, which own them.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The legacy five-minute timer check (JOB-05) is retired and the clocks are durable timers inside the workflow (Architecture v5 slide 44); this story creates no Schedule and no Quartz row, and a read needs none.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| recovery_case | P3 (rwb_case) | Case facts of the timeline: case ID and team |
| assignment | P3 (rwb_case) | The assignment and transfer items, with queue, reason, reason code and rule ID |
| queue | P3 (rwb_case) | The queue code of a move |
| timer | P3 (rwb_case) | The timer items: type, start and status |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_case | Present in the schema; this story writes none of them |

`interaction` is not a table of this contract: it is owned by rwb-source-data (ASM-0067, DP-18) and is read through the P1 contract. No table of another service is named and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `timeline`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.timeline`; front end folder `src/modules/recovery/case/timeline` with `CaseTimelinePage.tsx` and `QueueHistoryTab.tsx`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; here the decision item carries the record reference and the story writes no record | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-14 applies as a prohibition as well as a rule: the story publishes no topic, and no legacy `rwb.casewf.` or `rwb.p3.` topic name appears in it. The H and C dependencies of this table are held by the platform and service contract stories and are not repeated in the metadata rows, which carry the in-lane stories and the contract story of this key.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| TimelineService | Service | Applies the rights filter, calls the sources in parallel, merges, sorts, pages and builds `unavailableSources[]` |
| TimelineItemMapper | Service | Maps an assignment, a transfer, a timer, a contact, a decision, a document and a notice to `TimelineItem`, with summaries built from codes and labels |
| ItemRightsFilter | Service | Drops the item types the caller may not read, silently and without a gap in the other items (BR3) |
| AssignmentHistoryRepository | Repository | Reads `assignment` with its `queue_code` for a case and a date range, using the case index |
| TimerHistoryRepository | Repository | Reads `timer` for a case and a date range, using the case index |
| CaseFactsRepository | Repository | Reads the case ID and team from `recovery_case` for the access check and the answer |
| LedgerClient | Client | Calls the P1 interaction-ledger read and returns the contact facts, or a timeout |
| DecisionLogClient | Client | Calls the P7 ledger by case and by entry ID |
| DocumentClient | Client | Calls the P5 case document list |
| NoticeClient | Client | Calls the P6 case notice list and the notice by ID |
| AccessCheckClient | Client | Calls the P4 authorise operation and the masking policy, both cached by the guard library |
| MaskingAdapter | Library adapter | Applies the role mask to a contact summary through the ACE common masking path (CTL-11, DL26) |
| SourceCallGuard | Component | Wraps each downstream call with the parameter timeout, a breaker and bulkhead, and turns a failure into an `unavailableSources[]` entry |
| CaseTimelineController | Controller | The timeline operation, the query and page validation, and the error mapping |
| CaseTimelinePage | React component | SCR-04 with the Loading, Filtered and Empty states, the type and date filters and the source notice |
| QueueHistoryTab | React component | The queue-history view on SCR-04, calling the same operation with the fixed type filter |

**Database and migrations**

- Reads `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `queue` and `timer` in schema `rwb_case`. No new table and no new column: the timeline is a read.
- Migration `V2016_1__timeline_indexes.sql` adds `ix_assignment_case_assigned_at ON assignment (case_id, assigned_at DESC)` and `ix_timer_case_started_at ON timer (case_id, started_at DESC)`, so a page of the newest items is read without a sort of the whole case.
- The migration runs in the rwb-case Flyway sequence of the service's own schema (DP-15, held by the rwb_case DB story); no other schema is touched and no index is created on another service's table.

**Configuration and reference data**

- Parameter `timeline.source-timeout-ms` = 2000, `timeline.page-size-default` = 50 and `timeline.page-size-max` = 200, through the parameters contract (DP-06). The breaker and bulkhead settings are the resilience library's platform defaults and are not business values, so no number for them is fixed here.
- LOV-ASSIGN-REASON, LOV-TRANSFER-REASON and the seven type labels, through the reference-data contract with the version in force (DP-07). The type list is a list value, not a Java enum.
- The masking policy of a role, read from rwb-access; the mask itself is applied by the ACE common masking path.

**Build steps**

1. `AssignmentHistoryRepository`, `TimerHistoryRepository` and `CaseFactsRepository` with the two indexes; unit tests for each item type and for the "Queue not recorded" case of AC9.
2. `TimelineItemMapper` with codes and labels, and the ordering with the source sequence on a tie; tests for AC1 and AC3.
3. `SourceCallGuard` and the five clients, each against its contract fake, with the parameter timeout, a breaker and the `unavailableSources[]` entry; tests for AC6 and AC3.
4. `ItemRightsFilter` and `MaskingAdapter`; tests for AC5 and for the mask of a contact summary.
5. Paging, the type and date filters and the validation of `to` before `from`, of `size` and of `type`; tests for AC4, AC7, AC8 and AC11.
6. `CaseTimelineController` with the error mapping and the access check; test for AC10 and the 403 of X9.
7. `CaseTimelinePage` with the three states and `QueueHistoryTab` on the same operation; the composite-route contract test with gateway-bff.
8. The 4,000-item load test at page size 50 over 20 runs, and the query plan check that the page uses the two case indexes only.
9. Contract-fake run of every consumed answer in isolation, so the story builds before P1, P5, P6, P7 and P4 land.

**Feature switch.** The legacy flag name `rwb.p3.full-timeline` is kept as the legacy reference. In the target the switch is a parameter read through the parameters contract: off means SCR-03 shows the timeline of RWB-E1-035 and the operation answers the same earlier view.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P3-E2016-CON stay green, the 4,000-item case returns its first 50 items inside 2 s at the 95th percentile over 20 runs, and no item of a type the caller may not read appears in any answer.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-019 | No item matches the filter | Nothing on this case matches the filter. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A source module does not answer in time | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Date to is before date from | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | Page size outside 1 to 200, or a type outside the seven | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Case record R opens the timeline | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

For MSG-GEN-006 in this story, {system} is the display name of the missing source as the screen shows it, "Document hub" for rwb-document, "Decision log" for rwb-decision, "Notice hub" for rwb-comms and "Interaction ledger" for rwb-source-data. For MSG-GEN-003 the fields are "to" and "from"; for MSG-GEN-002 the field is "size" or "type". MSG-P3-019 is new in the legacy story and keeps its text. Thai text follows DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | State | What the user does |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-04 Case timeline | Loading | Sees skeleton rows while the composite route answers |
| SCR-04 Case timeline | Filtered | Filters by type and date; pages through a long history; opens a decision, a document or a notice; reads the queue history |
| SCR-04 Case timeline | Empty | Reads MSG-P3-019 when nothing matches, with the filters still shown |
| SCR-03 Case record | Read only | Opens the timeline from the record |

Both screens are served by the gateway-bff composite route, which calls rwb-case and the other owners in parallel, one hop each, and merges the answers into the screen model (DP-19). The browser calls one composite route and no owner service directly. The route path, the screen field list, the field-level masking of the screen model and the merge order are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0674; ASM-1221); the route itself is owned by RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the full read-only case view with its other sections remains with RWB-P3-E1023-APP.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the type list, the labels, the reason codes, the timeout and the page size bounds are rows and parameters (BR14).
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts. Summaries are built from codes; a contact summary is masked by role, never logged and never returned unmasked; test data is synthetic and no production case, party, notice or document is copied.
- No read of another service's tables: decisions, documents, notices and contacts come only through the P7, P5, P6 and P1 contracts, and `interaction` is not a table of `rwb_case` (BR11, DP-01, DP-18).
- No ACE view is read: the timeline needs no ACE data, and only rwb-source-data reads the `recovery.v_ace_*` views (ADR-010).
- One hop, no chaining: the timeline never calls a downstream of a downstream, and the breaker and bulkhead are per downstream (DP-11).
- The timeline never writes: it does not copy another service's records into `rwb_case`, does not project the history and raises no event (BR13).
- A role without a right sees fewer items, never an error and never another role's items (BR3, BR12).
- The case number and the case ID on the screen come from the case contract, never from a copy.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-016 for rwb-document. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **the documents of my case, with their stored date, type, actor and version history, to appear on the case timeline and in the documents section of the record view**, so that **I read what was attached, when and by whom without leaving the case**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A case lives for months or years and passes through several teams, partners and courts. The record view is the place where a new owner learns what happened, and the documents are the part of it that proves the facts: the court notice, the appraisal report, the title deed, the settlement agreement. The legacy story puts every action, decision, transfer, letter and document of a case on one timeline with type and date filters, and its measure is that a case history with 30 events reads in under 2 seconds (NFR-009) and stays under 2 seconds at the 2031 data size (NFR-070).

This story is the rwb-document part of legacy key RWB-E2-016. The timeline endpoint, the merge, the ordering, the paging, the queue history and all twelve legacy criteria are rwb-case's, in RWB-P3-E2016-APP and its contract RWB-P3-E2016-CON; the notice items are rwb-comms' and the decision items are rwb-decision's. What this slice owns is the document item source: for a case and a date window, rwb-document returns the document items with their timestamp, their type label, a summary built from codes, the actor and the document reference, plus the version count and the version history of each document, inside the 2 second budget the gateway gives it, masked by role and filtered by scope, and it opens the document detail behind an item. The document store itself — the file, the container, the version chain and the write path — is RWB-P5-E1024-APP; this story reads it and adds no write.

In the monolith the case timeline called `DocumentQuery.forCase(...)` inside the case module. In the target that in-process call is a REST call on the owner's base (DP-11): `rwb.document` under `/api/recovery/document/v1` (DP-13) instead of the shared base, one hop from rwb-case, a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream, and one GET retry with jitter as slide 11 of Architecture v5 fixes for every call. Architecture v5 slide 10 is explicit that the Documents tab loads on click from rwb-document, one hop, inside the 2 s target, that screens never chain calls, and that the gateway asks each owner directly and only for what is on screen; the case timeline therefore reads the document items directly from this service and never through a second service. The page size and the item cap are parameters instead of configuration in code (DP-06), the type labels are data rows with a version in force (DP-07), and the screen is composed at the edge by gateway-bff (DP-19). The service owns the topic `rwb.document.events.v1` and publishes nothing to it in this story (DP-14): the timeline is pulled, not pushed.

Three values of this slice are not settled by the sources and are carried as register rows, because the sources give the document read for the Documents tab and not yet for the timeline shape: the contract shape rwb-case and rwb-document share for the case timeline, which is the operation name, the window parameters and the item field names (GAP-1059; ASM-2007); whether the version count travels on the item or only on the document detail (GAP-1060; ASM-2008); the summary wording of a document item (GAP-1061; ASM-2009); and which table supplies the type label the item shows, because the document type table is rwb-document's own reference data while DP-07 sends lists through rwb-case (GAP-1062; ASM-2010). The story builds on Day 1 against the RWB-P3-E2016-CON fake and is proven end to end by RWB-ITG-E2016-ITG.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P3-E2016-CON is published: the timeline operation of rwb-case, the `TimelinePage` and `TimelineItem` components with `at`, `type`, `summary`, `by`, `reference` and the seven type values including DOCUMENT, the error mapping and the fakes of the consumed contracts, so this story knows the shape its items must fit. The operation name that rwb-case calls on rwb-document, the names of the window parameters and the field names of the answer are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1059; ASM-2007).
- The `rwb_document` baseline is in place: `document`, `document_field`, `document_custody`, `document_type`, `case_document_check`, `document_hub_parameter`, `document_intake`, `document_text` and `retention_action` exist at the platform migration version (TSD P5 T3.1), and the local decision-record table is created by the decision-record library (DP-03).
- The documents of the case exist and are `STORED`: they are written by RWB-P5-E1024-APP (the store, the version chain and the metadata) and by the intake stories of the same service; a document whose state is `COPY_PENDING` is a document whose content read answers 503 while its metadata already lists (FSD P5 AC-EXC-P5-002-03).
- The `document_type` table version in force is the one the stored documents were typed against, so a type code always resolves to a label; the label row a document of an older type table version shows is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1062; ASM-2010).
- The parameters exist as rows: the page size, its bounds and the item cap of the document item list, read through the parameters contract of rwb-case and its client library (DP-06), and the same row held in `document_hub_parameter` where TSD P5 places it (DF-REF-244 to DF-REF-251).
- The role of the caller is resolved by rwb-access: the authorise answer carries the scope over the case and the letters of the capability area DOCUMENTS, cached by the guard library (DP-08), and a refusal is MSG-P4-002 or MSG-P4-003 and never an empty list.
- The case facts needed for the scope test come one hop from rwb-case through the case read of RWB-P3-E2016-CON; this service holds no copy of a `rwb_case` row (DP-01).
- The login is the rwb-document login (DP-02), one per service, and the schema is `rwb_document`.
- The browser never calls this service directly: every call arrives from rwb-case or through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

##### 4. Flow

1. The case owner opens SCR-04 Case timeline from SCR-03 Case record. The browser calls the gateway-bff composite route and never an owner service directly (DP-19).
2. rwb-case decides the item types the caller may read and calls the case-scoped document read of this service once, with the case ID, the date window of the filter and the page parameters; the call is one hop, with the 2 s timeout of the case contract, a breaker per downstream and one GET retry with jitter (DP-11).
3. rwb-document receives the call on base `/api/recovery/document/v1` (DP-13) and validates the request before any row is read: `to` not before `from` (422, MSG-GEN-003), a page size outside the bounds (422, MSG-GEN-002), a case ID that is not a UUID (422).
4. ScopeGuard asks the guard library for the caller's rights: Documents R over the case, and the scope of the caller's roles. The guard library answers from the cached authorise data of rwb-access; a missing Documents R is a 403 with MSG-P4-002 and a case outside the scope is a 404 with MSG-P4-003.
5. For the scope test the scope facts of the case are read one hop from rwb-case through the case read of RWB-P3-E2016-CON; no `rwb_case` column is read and no scope copy is kept in `rwb_document`.
6. DocumentItemReader reads `document` for the case and the window — the stored date from the standard record column `created_at`, the type code, the actor, the document ID and `doc_version` — newest first, with the source sequence kept on a tie, within the page size and the item cap of the parameters.
7. DocumentItemMapper maps each row to one document item of the timeline: `at` (the stored date), `type` "DOCUMENT", `summary` (built from the type label and the version count, never from a free text), `by` (the actor of the document) and `reference` (the document ID), and attaches the version count of the document.
8. DocumentVersionReader walks the version chain of each document in the page by `previous_version_id` and returns, per version, the version number, the stored date, the actor and `content_sha256`; a document with one version returns one entry and a document with three versions returns three, the current version last.
9. The masking path applies the role mask to every field that carries a personal value before the answer leaves the service; no personal value, no storage reference and no document text is part of a document item.
10. The answer returns 200 with the page of items, `page`, `size` and `total`; on a document store that does not answer inside the budget the answer is a 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming "Document hub", which rwb-case turns into the partial timeline of the legacy exception path X1 and never into a failed case read.
11. The case owner opens a document item; the front end follows the item `reference` to `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` and reads the document detail: the metadata, the current `doc_version`, the version history with the hash of each version and the extracted fields, masked by role; the owner then downloads the content through `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/content`.
12. The documents section of SCR-03 asks the same case-scoped read with the date window of the section and shows the same items; a filter by type or date reloads it in state Filtered, and no read of this story writes a row, a decision record or an event.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | rwb-document does not answer inside the 2 second budget, or its breaker at rwb-case is open | The case timeline shows the 25 items of the other sources and names the missing source; the case read itself does not fail | MSG-GEN-006 | AC5 |
| X2 | The caller's role holds no Documents R | The service answers 403 and rwb-case leaves the document items out without an error; the other item types are unaffected | MSG-P4-002 | AC4 |
| X3 | The case is unknown, or outside the caller's scope | The service answers 404 before any document row is read; nothing is returned and nothing is written | MSG-P4-003 | AC6 |
| X4 | `to` is before `from` | Refused before any row is read, with both field names | MSG-GEN-003 | AC7 |
| X5 | The page size is outside the API bounds, or not an integer | Refused before any row is read, with the field and its bounds | MSG-GEN-002 | AC7 |
| X6 | The document store does not answer, or its read times out | 503 with the display name of this service, so the caller shows the partial timeline; the retry is one GET with jitter | MSG-GEN-006 | AC5 |
| X7 | A document of the page is in state `COPY_PENDING` | The item still shows with its metadata and its stored date; the content read of that document answers 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming "Document storage" | MSG-GEN-006 | AC1 |
| X8 | A document row of the case carries a type code with no label row in the version in force | The item shows with the type code itself and the case read continues; no item is dropped and no row is guessed | None | AC1 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on Day 1 against the RWB-P3-E2016-CON fake; the documents it reads are written by RWB-P5-E1024-APP and the rights come from the published rwb-access contract, so no team waits for another team's release |
| Negotiable | The summary wording, the window parameter names and the position of the version count can change; the items, the ordering, the budget and the rights are fixed |
| Valuable | The part of the case history that proves the facts reads from one owner, inside the 2 second wait, with no schema read across services |
| Estimable | One case-scoped read, one item mapper, one version reader, one scope guard, one controller and one screen component |
| Small | Fits one iteration with its tests, as a secondary slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Component tests over seeded `rwb_document` rows, contract tests against the RWB-P3-E2016-CON fake and one timed run at the 95th percentile over 20 runs |

The seven criteria above are new and test only this slice: the document items of the case, their stored date, their type label, their summary, their actor and their reference, their version count and version history, the inclusive window, the role and scope filter, the 2 second budget and the partial answer, and the parameter validation. The twelve legacy criteria of RWB-E2-016 are rwb-case's and are carried by RWB-P3-E2016-APP; no legacy criterion text is copied into this section, and only the source values of the legacy story are reused: case "RW-2026-000601", its 5 documents among 30 events, user "U-CO-01" holding RW-CASEOWN, user "U-PC-01" holding RW-PHONECOL, the window 2026-12-05 to 2026-12-08, the wrong order 2026-12-10 to 2026-12-01, case "RW-2026-000603" of team "SME-NTH", the 4,000 item case "RW-2026-000604" at page size 50 and the 2 second budget.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The timeline holds every document of the case (legacy BR1, the document part): a document stored on the case appears as one document item in its window, and a superseded version appears inside that item's history, never as a second item | REQ-WKM-008; casemodel.txt Case file; legacy BR1 |
| BR2 | Items are returned newest first from the stored date; two documents stored at the same instant keep the order of their source sequence, so the same query returns the same page | events.txt Rules (ordering); legacy BR2 |
| BR3 | A document item shows only to a role with Documents R; the list is filtered by the role's letters and by its scope, and masking by role applies to every field that carries a personal value (CTL-11, DL26) | roles.txt Permissions; CTL-09; CTL-11; DL26; legacy BR3 |
| BR6 | Personal data in a summary is masked by role, and a document item never carries a person name, an account number, an identity number, a storage reference or document text | CTL-11; DL26; legacy BR6 |
| BR7 | A source that does not answer in time does not stop the timeline: this service answers a 503 with MSG-GEN-006 and the caller shows the other items | NFR-008; legacy BR7 |
| BR8 | Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream, and a GET is retried once with jitter; no call chains and no call reads a downstream of a downstream | Architecture v5 slides 10 and 11; DP-11 |
| BR9 | The service reads only `rwb_document` and its own ACE attachments; no `rwb_case` column is read, and the case facts arrive one hop through the rwb-case contract | Architecture v5 slide 13; DP-01 |
| BR10 | The page size, its bounds and the item cap are parameters, and the number of items one answer may carry is the parameter value, never a constant | Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-06 |
| BR11 | The document type label and the list values are data rows with a version in force; no type code, label or list value is written in code | TSD P5 T3.1, T3.2; DP-07 |
| BR12 | The read writes nothing: no document row, no field row, no version, no custody row, no decision record, no access-log row of this service and no event | Legacy solution plan; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR13 | A document that is not visible in the caller's scope is absent from the answer, never a redacted item and never a count that reveals it | CTL-11; Architecture v5 slide 10 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no document state and no case state; it reads records only, writes no row, raises no event and starts no workflow. The document states below are read-only facts that an item or its detail may show.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| — | — | — | None: this story performs no transition |

| State it may show | Written by | Appears as |
|---|---|---|
| `COPY_PENDING` | RWB-P5-E1024-APP, when the storage copy of a stored document has not completed | A document item with its metadata and stored date, and a content read that answers 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming "Document storage" |
| `STORED` | RWB-P5-E1024-APP, once the file is in its container | A document item whose content read returns the file, and a version entry in the history |
| `SUPERSEDED` | RWB-P5-E1024-APP, when a further version of the same document is stored | A version entry in the history of the item; the superseded version is still readable and never replaces the current one |

The states above are the values of `state` on `document` as TSD P5 T3.0 and the store story define them; this story reads them and never sets one. A review status (`LOV-REVIEW`) and a retention class are shown on the detail, not on the item.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the timeline and queue history (Case record R; Decision log R; Documents R; Litigation R), so every document item of the case shows |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads the timeline and queue history (Case record R; Decision log R); document items show only if the role also holds Documents R |
| RW-PHONECOL, phone collector | Reads the timeline without decisions and notices (Case record R; Documents R), so the document items show |
| RW-CONDUCT, conduct and QA officer | Reads every item (R in all areas), so the document items show |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads every item (R in all areas); changes nothing |
| rwb-document service identity (the rwb-document login, DP-02) | Serves the case-scoped document read, the document detail and the content, applies the role filter and the mask, and writes nothing |
| rwb-case (the caller) | Asks for the document items of one case and one window, one hop, and merges them with its own items; it holds no copy of a document row |
| gateway-bff (the platform edge) | Calls each owner directly for what is on screen and merges the answers; the browser never calls rwb-document (DP-19) |

A decision item needs Decision log R, a document item needs Documents R and a notice item needs Litigation R (legacy BR3). rwb-access decides every one of those letters and the scope (DP-08) and answers a refusal with MSG-P4-002 for a missing letter and MSG-P4-003 for a case outside the scope; this service holds no role, letter, scope or masking rule of its own and grants nothing.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity in `rwb_document` | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-DOC-001 | document | id — the item reference | Read |
| DF-DOC-002 | document | case_id — the filter of the read | Read |
| DF-DOC-004 | document | document_type — the code the summary label resolves from | Read |
| DF-DOC-005 | document | source — shown on the detail and used for the summary where the type label is absent | Read |
| DF-DOC-009 | document | retention_class — shown on the detail, never on the item | Read |
| DF-DOC-011 | document | doc_version — the version count of the item | Read |
| DF-DOC-025 | document | previous_version_id — the chain the version history walks | Read |
| DF-DOC-026 | document | content_sha256 — the hash of each version in the history | Read |
| DF-DOC-027 | document | captured_at — the capture time, shown on the detail and not used as the item date | Read |
| DF-REF-219 | document_type | doc_type_code — the code a stored document carries | Read |
| DF-REF-220 | document_type | label_en — the English label the summary is built from | Read |
| DF-REF-221 | document_type | label_th — the Thai label of the same row | Read |
| DF-CAS-001 | case (owner rwb-case) | id — the case of the request and of the scope answer | Read only through the rwb-case contract, one hop |
| DF-CAS-011 | case (owner rwb-case) | team_code — the team the scope test compares | Read only through the rwb-case contract, one hop |
| DF-REF-244 to DF-REF-251 | document_hub_parameter | `param_code`, `param_value`, `table_version`, `valid_from`, `valid_to` — the page size, its bounds and the item cap | Read |
| Standard record columns | document | created_at (the stored date of the item), created_by (the actor), state | Read |

No `rwb_case` column is read by this story: `DF-CAS-001` and `DF-CAS-011` arrive in the answer of the rwb-case case read, and the two columns are named here only to say which fact the scope test needs. No `document_text` row, no `document_intake` row and no `document_custody` row is read by the item list; the content of API-P5-004 is streamed from the Blob container of the store story and is never loaded into a table by this service. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 and TSD P5 T3.1.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/document/v1`; owner rwb-document (P5). This slice adds no path: it serves the read operations of TSD P5 appendix T-A behind the case timeline and the documents section, and the write side (upload, store, new version, field review, custody, generation) stays with RWB-P5-E1024-APP and the other P5 stories.

| API | Method | Path | Request | Response | Errors | Authorization | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-P5-002 | GET | `/cases/{caseId}/documents` | Path `caseId`; query `type`, `page`, `size` (TSD P5 T-A.2) and the date window `from`, `to` of the timeline; the window parameter names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1059; ASM-2007) | 200 `DocumentPage`: the documents of the case in the window, newest first, each with `at`, `type` "DOCUMENT", `summary`, `by`, `reference` and `doc_version`, plus `page`, `size` and `total`; the item field names and the summary template are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1059, GAP-1060, GAP-1061; ASM-2007, ASM-2008, ASM-2009) | 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Documents R (MSG-P4-002); 404 unknown or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 422 `to` before `from` (MSG-GEN-003) or a page size outside the bounds (MSG-GEN-002); 503 the document store is down (MSG-GEN-006) | Documents, right R, scope applied; each service authorises the object itself (Architecture v5 slide 10) | Not applicable: the call writes nothing |
| API-P5-003 | GET | `/documents/{documentId}` | Path `documentId` | 200 `Document`: the metadata, the current `doc_version`, the version history (version, stored date, actor, `content_sha256` per version) and the extracted fields of `document_field`, masked by role | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Documents R (MSG-P4-002); 404 unknown or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 503 the store is down (MSG-GEN-006) | Documents, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| API-P5-004 | GET | `/documents/{documentId}/content` | Path `documentId` | 200 the file of the version as `application/octet-stream`; 503 while the state is `COPY_PENDING` (FSD P5 AC-EXC-P5-002-03) | 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Documents R (MSG-P4-002); 404 unknown or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 503 (MSG-GEN-006 naming "Document storage") | Documents, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

The operation that rwb-case calls for the timeline is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1059; ASM-2007): no source names a case-timeline operation of this service, and TSD P5 T-A.2 gives API-P5-002 the query `type`, `page` and `size` with no date window, while RWB-P3-E2016-CON consumes "the document metadata of a case in the date range". This story therefore serves the case-scoped document read on API-P5-002, carries the window as two date parameters, and builds the case timeline use against the RWB-P3-E2016-CON fake until the baseline review fixes the names on both sides. No path is invented and no response field of TSD P5 T-A.2 is removed.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | rwb-case (P3) | The case exists, its team and its scope answer, for the 404 test of AC6; one hop, no copy kept. The answer field names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1059; ASM-2007) | One hop, 2 s, breaker, one GET retry with jitter |
| — | RWB-P3-E2016-CON, the timeline contract of rwb-case | rwb-case (P3) | The shape of the document item this service returns and the operation name rwb-case calls; both sides fake it on Day 1; the name and the field names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1059; ASM-2007) | One hop, 2 s, breaker |

The access check is not a contract dependency of this story: it is the cached authorise call of the guard library that every service makes (DP-08), answered by the published contract of rwb-access, and it caches for the request. No other service is called: this story never calls rwb-decision, rwb-comms, rwb-source-data or the gateway, and it never calls a downstream of a downstream (DP-11).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The timeline is pulled, not pushed: this read writes no row, so it has no outbox row and publishes nothing. The service owns `rwb.document.events.v1` (DP-14) and publishes `DocumentStored` and `DocumentFieldsExtracted` on it from the store and extraction stories; this story adds no event, and the two events are consumed by rwb-case and rwb-agent for their own projections (Architecture v5 slide 42), never by this read.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. This service is the producer of the document events, not a consumer of them: it answers from its own `rwb_document` rows at the moment of the request, so an item is never a projection and never stale. `DocumentFieldsExtracted` is used inside the service by the extraction path, not by this story, and no consumer group is created here.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The case-scoped read, the detail and the content are synchronous REST calls inside the request and inside the 2 second budget; this story starts no workflow, adds no activity and holds no timer. The `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` of the store and extraction stories owns the writes, and this story reads what those activities have already committed.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The retention Schedule of this service belongs to the retention story, and the document intake Schedule to the intake story (TSD P5 T5.3, Architecture v5 slide 44); a read needs no Schedule.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| document | P5 (`rwb_document`) | The document item: ID, case, type, source, version, hash, capture time and the standard record columns |
| document_type | P5 (`rwb_document`) | The type code and the labels a summary is built from, at the version in force |
| document_field | P5 (`rwb_document`) | The extracted fields of a document, shown on the detail only |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_document` | Present in the schema; this story writes none of them |
| document_custody, case_document_check, document_intake, document_text, retention_action, document_hub_parameter | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Same service; this story reads `document_hub_parameter` only, and the other tables belong to their own stories |

`recovery_case`, `assignment`, `queue` and `timer` are rwb-case's tables and are read only through its contract (DP-01). No table of another service is named in a query of this story and no foreign key crosses a schema; `document.case_id` and `document.previous_version_id` are references by value, as TSD P5 T3.3 records them.

| RWB-P3-E2016-CON fake | The timeline shape and the operation rwb-case calls | A page of `TimelineItem` with the seven type values, the item fields and the DOCUMENT type name; an empty page; a window parameter pair; the merged answer that must show 25 items when this service is late |
| rwb-case case read fake | The scope test of AC6 | Case "RW-2026-000601" of team "MTG-BKK" in scope; case "RW-2026-000603" of team "SME-NTH" out of scope with MSG-P4-003 |
| rwb-access authorise fake (guard library) | The rights and the mask of the caller | Documents R for RW-CASEOWN and for RW-PHONECOL; no Documents R for the refused caller with MSG-P4-002; the masking policy of the caller's role |
| Seeded `rwb_document` fixture | The item, the detail and the history | The 5 documents of case "RW-2026-000601" with their stored dates, document "DOC-0601" with 3 versions, the 30 documents of the timed run, the 4,000 timeline items of case "RW-2026-000604", of which the document items are one page and one document in state `COPY_PENDING` |
| gateway-bff composite route fake | The screen path (DP-19) | The composite answer of SCR-03 and SCR-04 with the documents section filled from this service, and the partial answer when this service is late |

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 3 provided, 1 consumed, 1 cached | Three read operations of base `/api/recovery/document/v1`; the rwb-case case read consumed for the scope test; the authorise answer of rwb-access through the guard library, cached; one hop, 2 s, breaker, one GET retry with jitter |
| Kafka | None | The service owns `rwb.document.events.v1`; this story publishes nothing to it and consumes nothing (12.3, 12.4) |
| Temporal | None | No workflow and no activity; the writes this story reads are committed by the intake workflow of the store stories |
