These eight criteria are new for the deployment and test artefacts only; they restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P6-E2018-APP.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A customer signs electronically only where the template's signature basis allows it, and by wet ink where Legal requires it; the deployment seeds no basis | REQ-OCC-009; DF-REF-068 |
| BR2 | No signature request leaves while a contact stop or a legal hold applies; the deployment holds no copy of either | CTL-16; R-SET-12; R-UNI-20 |
| BR3 | A system that is unavailable queues the send and retries; after the retry limit of 5 the send moves to the exception queue and the attempt-limit alert fires | R-UNI-33, R-UNI-34 |
| BR4 | The same result twice has one effect; a resend after a lost reference uses a new Idempotency-Key only when the first is confirmed lost | R-UNI-40 |
| BR5 | The signed copy is write-once on the case and is stored only through the P5 contract; the deployment stores no signed PDF | CTL-12; DT06; DP-01 |
| BR6 | One service, one schema, one login: the release uses the rwb-comms login and no other service's credential | DP-02; Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR7 | The migration is a per-service Flyway sequence in schema rwb_comms and runs before the deployment is ready; it creates no signature table | DP-15; GAP-1181 |
| BR8 | Every subscription has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and a consumer never acknowledges an event it could not process | DP-09; Architecture v5 slide 22 notes |
| BR9 | No Schedule and no new topic is created for this capability: the retry is the platform relay JOB-11 and the topics belong to their owners | DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44 |
| BR10 | No literal endpoint, certificate or secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; the chart carries references only | NFR-052; TSD P6 T7 |
| BR11 | No environment value is hard-coded: replica counts, resource sizes, timeouts, thresholds and the retry limit are values or service configuration | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR12 | An alert carries a message ID where the condition maps to one, and links one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR13 | No dashboard series, log line, alert payload or runbook entry carries a signed PDF byte, a party identity, an account number or a document body; references and counts only | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; legacy section 17 |
| BR14 | No comms event is created by this release: the signature result is read from the rwb-document contract and the decision record goes on the shared topic | DP-09; GAP-1185 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart, the migration job and the egress check pass the pipeline | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration complete and probes healthy | The schema is at the expected version and the consumer is subscribed | Ready |
| Ready | Release superseded | A new chart version is promoted | Rolling |
| Rolling | All pods on the new version | The old ReplicaSet drains | Ready |
| Ready | Egress check failed | The route or the certificate reference is missing | Failed |
| Failed | Rollback | The previous chart version is redeployed and the migration is reversed by its own script | Ready |

The request lifecycle - QUEUED, SENT, SIGNED, DECLINED, EXPIRED - is the capability's own and is described in RWB-P6-E2018-APP; the request row itself is P5 rwb-document's. This story observes it and changes no state of it.

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the egress step, the provisioning step, the dashboards, the alerts and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the topic provisioning and the platform relay window |
| Platform security team | Owns the client certificate and the secret material of the egress, and approves the reference the chart carries |
| ACE database administrator | Owns schema rwb_comms, the login and its grants, and approves the migration job |

| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Reads the exception queue in the running service, not in the cluster |

The per-service login name and the egress certificate and secret names used by the chart are secret references resolved at deploy time; the chart references "the rwb-comms login (DP-02)" and the egress material by reference, never by literal value.

##### 11. Data

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Deployment values | Image digest, chart version, replica counts, resource requests and limits, probe paths and timings, log level, the feature switch `rwb.comms.esign`, the client and egress timeouts, the alert thresholds |
| Schema | rwb_comms, migrated by the per-service Flyway sequence; the tables template, merge_field and notice with the library objects outbox_event, processed_event and idempotency_key, and no signature table |
| Topics | `rwb.case.events.v1` subscribes CaseStateChanged; `rwb.deviation.events.v1` subscribes DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared; `rwb.treatment.events.v1` subscribes TreatmentApproved; `rwb.decision-record.v1` is produced to as its owner provisions it; `rwb.comms.events.v1` is not created or extended by this capability |
| Egress | One outbound route to the ACE common module e-signature path (INT-34), with the client certificate, the trust material and the endpoint as secret references |
| Dashboard series | requests by status, queued sends and queue depth, time to an accepted reference, result latency, expiry count, exception count, attempt distribution up to 5, egress error rate, MSG-GEN-006 rate, refused counts, consumer lag |
| Runbook entries | stuck send, egress down, result never arrives, unknown reference, exception queue grows |
| Secrets | The rwb-comms login secret, the Kafka client credential, the egress client certificate and the endpoint, all from the platform secret store |

The egress endpoint, the certificate issuer and the secret names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1187; ASM-2134), and the signed PDF object store is P5's and is Not specified here (GAP-1186; ASM-2133). The exact cluster topology, node pools, replica counts and probe timings are deployment values of the platform chart and are not fixed here. The retry limit of 5 and the exception-queue rule are service configuration of rwb-comms, not chart values.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None new. The deployment exposes the three operations of the app story behind gateway-bff: `POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}/signature-requests`, `GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}/signature-requests` and `POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/signature-requests/{requestId}/result`, owner rwb-comms (P6), API-P6-009, API-P6-010 and API-P6-011, with the `SignatureRequest` answer and the Idempotency-Key header. The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None by the deployment. The outbound call of the capability is not a REST operation of a service in this workspace: it is the ACE common module e-signature path (INT-34), whose request and result shapes, endpoint and certificate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1187; ASM-2134). Its endpoint and certificate are the secret references of AC2, and the deployment adds no consumer of the P5 document contract, the rwb-treatment contract or the reference-data contract: those are the app story's and are faked for the smoke profile.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This capability publishes no comms event - Architecture v5 slide 42 names only `NoticeGenerated`, `NoticeDispatched` and `NoticeDelivered` on `rwb.comms.events.v1` and a signature is not a notice (GAP-1185; ASM-2132) - and its one relayed element is `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, written by the local library and provisioned by its owner, a library that the plan build list does not carry (GAP-1196; ASM-2143). This deployment creates no topic and publishes no comms event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Group |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` (event 05) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | rwb-comms |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` (event 06) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | rwb-comms |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` (event 07) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | rwb-comms |
| `rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1` (event 10) | `rwb.treatment.events.v1` | S2 rwb-treatment | rwb-comms |

The four events on three topics are consumed by one group `rwb-comms` with the inbox of schema `rwb_comms`, each with its retry topic and its `.dlt` topic (DP-09).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The retry worker of this capability is not a Temporal workflow: it is the platform relay window of JOB-11 calling the rwb-comms sender, plus the result handling in the service. No worker deployment polls a task queue for this capability, and no activity is registered on `rwb-comms`.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-11 Outbox sender is the platform's outbox relay, every minute, with every service as its owner (Architecture v5 slide 44); this release registers no Schedule and no cron entry, and the retry limit of 5 is applied inside the send attempt rather than by a scheduler (DP-10).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None new. The migration job creates and migrates the tables of `rwb_comms` - template, merge_field, notice, outbox_event, processed_event and idempotency_key - and touches no other schema (DP-01). `signature_request` and `document` stay with P5, `treatment` with S2, `recovery_case` with P3, `deviation` with S8 and `decision_log_entry` with P7; no dashboard query reads any of them and no signature table is created (GAP-1181).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Deployment use |
|---|---|
| rwb-document WireMock | Runs in the pipeline and in the SIT smoke profile: the created request, the read by external reference for `EA-30001` and for `EA-99999`, the update, and the version add answering version 2 of `D-0601` with write_once true |
| rwb-treatment WireMock | Same profile: treatment `T-0501` with offer validity 2026-12-20 and state OFFER_WITH_CUSTOMER_SET, and the signature record answering accepted for signed true and signed false |
| rwb-deviation WireMock | Same profile: the open deviation `X2` with contact stop on and an empty answer |
| rwb-case WireMock | Same profile: legal hold false and true, and a delayed answer beyond 2 s |
| ACE common module e-signature path stub (INT-34) | An accepted reference, a `SIGNED` result with a synthetic signed PDF, a `DECLINED` result and an `unavailable` answer for six attempts |

The fakes are test-only workloads; they are not deployed into UAT or production, and each is replaced by the real owner as its story lands. The concrete path shape, endpoint and certificate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1187; ASM-2134).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 3 provided, 1 consumed outside the workspace | The three signature-request operations provided; the outbound call to the ACE common module e-signature path (INT-34); one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 1 produced to a shared topic, 4 consumed | `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` reused; `CaseStateChanged`, `DeviationRaised`, `DeviationCleared` and `TreatmentApproved` consumed with retry and `.dlt` |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, no activity and no Schedule; the retry is the platform relay JOB-11 |
| File | None | The release reads no runtime file; values files and chart templates are build inputs |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_comms`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/comms/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-10 is claimed only for the relay dependency: no Schedule is registered by this release. DP-05 applies as a prohibition: no dashboard and no smoke step reads an ACE view. DP-13 adds nothing to the deployment beyond the base the chart exposes.

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-comms/` | Chart with the api deployment, service, migration job, config map, secret references and probes |
| `helm/rwb-comms/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, `rwb.comms.esign`, the client and egress timeouts, the alert thresholds |
| Egress step | One outbound route to the ACE common module e-signature path (INT-34), the client certificate and endpoint references, and the check that fails the release when either is missing |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit, component and contract tests, retired-element check, egress check, image and dependency scan, chart publish, promote the same artefact |
| Provisioning step | Consumer group `rwb-comms` on `rwb.case.events.v1`, `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and `rwb.treatment.events.v1` with retry and `.dlt`; reuse of `rwb.decision-record.v1`; confirmation that the relay window of JOB-11 drains `rwb_comms` |
| Dashboards | Eight panels: requests by status; queued sends and queue depth; time to an accepted reference; result latency; expiry count; exception count; attempt distribution up to 5; egress error rate, MSG-GEN-006 rate and refused counts |
| Alerts | Five rules, each with a message ID where one applies and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Five entries: stuck send, egress down, result never arrives, unknown reference, exception queue grows |

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only when the migration is at the expected schema version and the consumer group is subscribed; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database, calls another service or calls the ACE common module path.

**Alert mapping.**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | The attempt count of a send reaches 5 and the row moves to the exception state | Attempt-limit alert with the operation, the attempt count, the external reference and the age of the oldest affected row | Platform on-call, ticket to the ACE common module path owner |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The egress answers 503 or the path is unavailable on a share of sends | Egress error-rate alert with the breaker state and the environment | Platform on-call, page, ACE common module path owner |
| None | An accepted reference has no result inside the result window | Result-latency alert with the reference and the oldest affected request | Platform on-call, ticket |
| None | The exception count passes its value | Exception-queue alert with the count and its change against the trailing hour | Platform on-call, page |
| MSG-P4-002, MSG-P6-009 and MSG-P6-001 | A send is refused for want of a right, a wet ink basis or a contact stop | Refused count on the dashboard | No page |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The feature switch is off and the send is refused closed | Switch-off count on the dashboard | No page |

Every alert carries its message ID where the condition maps to one, and the conditions without a message ID carry the series name instead. The threshold, the result window and the evaluation window of every alert are set in the values file by the release manager and recorded in the runbook; no source document fixes them.

**Done when.** The chart renders in all three environments, the pipeline promotes one artefact and fails on a fake drift, a missing retry topic, a missing egress reference or a retired element, the three subscriptions exist with their retry and `.dlt` paths, the eight panels carry the synthetic day, the five alert conditions fire on synthetic metrics, the smoke profile passes against the fakes with no personal data or signed PDF content in a log line or a metric label, and the five runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P6-009 | E-signature asked for a document that needs wet ink | Legal requires a wet ink signature for {document}. Use the branch or paper path. |
| MSG-P6-001 | A contact stop is in force | Contact with this customer is stopped for {reason}. |
| MSG-P3-004 | A legal hold is on the case | This case is on hold for {deviation}. The prescription date is still {date}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The ACE path to EasyApp is unavailable, the egress is down, or the switch is off | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A branch or paper result has no scan | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P3-005 | The request is not open, or the treatment is not with the customer | This case cannot move to {state} from {current}. |

The message texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story and the deployment adds the routing, the threshold and the runbook link, never a new wording. The {system} of MSG-GEN-006 is the name of the system that failed - `EasyApp` or the name of the consumed service.

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment serves SCR-14 Treatment record with the Send for signature action, the method choice and the request list with its status, SCR-30 Case documents with the signed copy linked to the generated agreement, and SCR-09 Exception queue with the held results and the sends in the exception state, all through gateway-bff composite routes (DP-19). The operator-facing surfaces of this story are the pipeline run view, the release view, the egress check result, the eight dashboard panels and the runbook; the smoke step runs one signature journey for a synthetic case in SIT and asserts the create, the relay window, the signed version, the decline, the unknown reference and the exception state at attempt 5.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the signature basis per template, the method and status lists and the retry limit of 5 are data or service configuration held by their owner, never a deployment value.
- No personal data and no signed PDF content in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads, the smoke output or the runbook: references, counts, statuses, durations and staff user IDs only.
- One login per service; the chart carries the rwb-comms login reference and no other service's credential (DP-02).
- The service writes only schema rwb_comms; the migration job never touches another schema, creates no signature table, and no dashboard query reads one (DP-01, DP-15).
- Every subscription has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and the consumer dedupes through the inbox (DP-09).
- No new topic and no Schedule for the retry: the capability reuses the three owner topics, produces to `rwb.decision-record.v1` as its owner provisions it, and relies on the platform relay JOB-11 (DP-10).
- No literal endpoint, certificate or secret in a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; the chart carries references resolved at deploy time (NFR-052).
- ACE data is read only through the owner's contract; no dashboard and no smoke step reads an ACE view or another service's schema (DP-05).
- The release pins the image digest and the chart version, and the rollback is rehearsed once in SIT before the wave 2 release.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-018 for the wave 2 integration harness. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As an **integration engineer (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **a repeatable cross-service journey harness for the e-signature flow that runs the signed, branch and paper, decline, expiry, duplicate-result and unavailable-path journeys against the owning services' contracts, the contract fakes and the ACE common module test path, and records the evidence of every run**, so that **the signed copy on the case and the signature result on the treatment are proven end to end across rwb-comms, rwb-document, rwb-treatment, rwb-access and rwb-decision before the wave 2 release**.

This story builds the harness and its evidence only. It builds no production screen, endpoint or table, and it changes no service code.

##### 2. Business rationale

A settlement completes without paper only where Legal permits it, and the case waits for the signed copy before booking can start (REQ-OCC-009; legacy RWB-E2-018 business rationale). The legacy story delivers that inside one module, where the document hub, the treatment record, the conduct check and the decision log are all in one process. In the target architecture the same journey crosses four services and the ACE common module: rwb-comms creates the request and receives the result, rwb-document stores the signed copy as a new write-once version, rwb-treatment records signed or not signed, rwb-access authorises each call, and rwb-decision holds the record (Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 16, 17 and 18).

Each of those behaviours is owned by a service story in this wave, and each of those stories tests its own part against a contract fake. Nothing in the wave proves the whole journey: that a SIGNED result from EasyApp becomes version 2 of D-0601 on the case within 60 seconds (legacy RWB-E2-018 §12 target), that the branch scan D-0602 is linked and BRANCH is recorded, that the paper deed in lieu reaches rwb-case with CUSTOMER_ACCEPTED and signature basis WET_INK, that a decline records not signed, that an expired request refuses a later result without touching rwb-treatment, and that the same EA-30001 result twice stores one version and records the signature once (R-UNI-40).

The harness does that. It calls each owner on its own base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` (DP-13), one hop with a 2-second timeout (DP-11), through the gateway-bff composite route where a screen is in the journey (DP-19), and it reads the topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` to check that the journey is recorded (DP-09). It is the evidence the wave 2 exit needs, and it is repeatable, so the same journeys are re-run when an owning service changes its contract.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The four integration dependencies are in build or published as contracts: RWB-P6-E2018-APP (requests and results), RWB-P5-E2018-APP (signed copy as a version), RWB-P5-E2017-APP (generated agreement and its signature basis), RWB-S2-E2018-APP (signature status on the treatment). This story does not wait for them: from Day 1 it runs against their contracts and the fakes of §12.8.
- Each owning service publishes its OpenAPI contract before code, and a contract fake exists for every operation of §12.2 (Architecture v5 slide 11).
- The e-signature request and result paths sit on the rwb-comms base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`; the signed copy on the rwb-document base `/api/recovery/document/v1`; the treatment record on the rwb-treatment base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1`; the authorise check on the rwb-access base `/api/recovery/access/v1`; the decision log on the rwb-decision base `/api/recovery/decision/v1` (DP-13; Architecture v5 slide 41).
- EasyApp is reached only through the ACE common module e-signature path (INT-34). The EasyApp test tenant and the route to it through the ACE common module are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0402; ASM-0577).
- The signature basis per template is available as data on the generated agreement (E_SIGNATURE_ALLOWED or WET_INK_REQUIRED); the method list is E_SIGNATURE, BRANCH, PAPER and the request status list is QUEUED, SENT, SIGNED, DECLINED, EXPIRED (legacy RWB-E2-018 §13).
- The harness runs in SIT. The harness environment, the data seeding, the signed PDF fixture, the evidence format and the evidence retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0402; ASM-0577).
- No build dependency. Day 1.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: reads the journey file and the run settings (base per service, 2-second timeout, the 60-second signed-copy target, the retry limit of 5).
2. Harness: seeds the case facts for the journey: case RC-2026-000888, settlement T-0501 with offer validity 2026-12-20 and state OFFER_WITH_CUSTOMER_SET, agreement D-0601 generated from template SET-AGREE TH with signature basis E_SIGNATURE_ALLOWED, borrower party P-0088 with no contact stop.
3. Harness: calls `POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}/signature-requests` with the document, the party and the method, and keeps the returned request id as RS-0301.
4. Harness: calls `GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}/signature-requests` to read the request state after each step of the journey.
5. Harness: drives the EasyApp result through the ACE common module test path, or posts the same result on `POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/signature-requests/{requestId}/result` where the journey is a branch or paper result, and records the signed document and the signed date it sends.
6. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` on D-0601 and checks that version 2 exists, that write_once is true and that the stored version is the signed copy, within the 60-second target.
7. Harness: calls `PATCH /api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}` to record the signature and reads `GET /api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}` to check signed true or false and the method (E_SIGNATURE, BRANCH or PAPER) on S2.
8. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` for the case and checks that the journey is recorded, and consumes `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` to check the event of the journey.
9. Harness: exercises `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` for the acting role on every call of the journey, so an operation refused by authority is seen as a refusal and not as an error.
10. Harness: exercises JOB-11 Outbox sender on the unavailable path: the send stays in the outbox, the relay retries every minute, and the journey stops at the retry limit of 5 (Architecture v5 slide 44; legacy RWB-E2-018 AC8).
11. Harness: writes one run report keyed by story key and business date, with the journey, the requests, the observed results, the pass or fail of each step and the evidence references, and attaches it to the wave 2 run record.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | An owning service answers 404 or a 5xx on its base | The journey stops at that step; the report names the step, the service and the operation, and the run fails | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The signed copy is not version 2 or not write_once within 60 seconds | The report names the document, the observed version and the elapsed seconds, and the run fails | None | AC1 |
| X3 | The treatment record is not updated with signed and method | The report names the treatment and the values it read, and the run fails | None | AC1 |
| X4 | EasyApp is not reachable at the test route | The request returns 201 QUEUED with MSG-GEN-006 naming EasyApp and the outbox path is exercised to the retry limit of 5 | MSG-GEN-006 | AC5 |
| X5 | An expired request receives a later SIGNED result | The result is held on the exception queue, S2 is not called and the report shows the held result | None | AC3 |
| X6 | A service answers a refusal the journey expects (MSG-P4-002, MSG-P6-009 or MSG-P6-001) | The refusal is recorded as the expected result of that step, not as an error | MSG-P4-002, MSG-P6-009, MSG-P6-001 | AC2 |
| X7 | The authorise check refuses the acting role | The step is recorded as refused and the journey continues only where the journey file marks a refusal as expected | MSG-P4-002 | AC2 |

The report text is for the integration and QA teams and is not part of the message standard. Business messages are those of section 14 and are copied from legacy RWB-E2-018 §14.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs on the four contracts and the fakes of §12.8 from Day 1; no build dependency, and each fake is replaced by the real service as its I story lands |
| Negotiable | The journey file, the run settings, the seeded facts and the evidence envelope are data and configuration, never code |
| Valuable | The wave 2 exit is decided on one repeatable run of every e-signature journey instead of four separate component tests |
| Estimable | One journey runner, one contract-fake set, one evidence writer, one gate |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each journey ends in an asserted state, and every failure names the step, the service and the observed value |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: E-signature flow for customers and the bank, run as one cross-service journey

  Background:
    Given the harness runs in SIT on the per-service bases /api/recovery/<short>/v1 through gateway-bff
    Given every call is one hop with a 2-second timeout
    Given case "RC-2026-000888" has settlement treatment "T-0501" with offer validity 2026-12-20 and state "OFFER_WITH_CUSTOMER_SET"
    Given agreement document "D-0601" on the case was generated from template "SET-AGREE" "TH" with signature basis "E_SIGNATURE_ALLOWED"
    Given the borrower is party "P-0088" with no contact stop

  Scenario: AC1 The signed copy reaches the case and S2 records the signature (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given "RS-0301" sent "D-0601" for e-signature to party "P-0088" on 2026-12-10
    When EasyApp returns signing result "SIGNED" with the bank signature applied at 2026-12-11 10:15:00
    Then within 60 seconds version 2 of "D-0601" holding the signed PDF is stored on case "RC-2026-000888" with write_once true
    Then the signature request has status "SIGNED"
    Then the harness reads signed true and method "E_SIGNATURE" on "T-0501" through GET /api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}
    Then the decision log read on GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log holds the journey for case "RC-2026-000888"

  Scenario: AC2 The branch scan and the paper deed in lieu finish the same journey (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given "RS-0301" created a signature request for "D-0601" with method "BRANCH"
    Given the branch scan "D-0602" of the signed agreement arrived through document intake on 2026-12-12
    When "RS-0301" records result "SIGNED" with signed document "D-0602" and signed date 2026-12-12
    Then the signature request has status "SIGNED" and method "BRANCH"
    Then the harness reads "D-0602" linked to case "RC-2026-000888" as the signed agreement
    Given case "RC-2026-000889" has deed in lieu treatment "T-0502" for product "MORTGAGE"
    Given its contract document "D-0701" was generated from template "DIL-CONTRACT-MTG" with signature basis "WET_INK_REQUIRED"
    Given "RS-0301" created a signature request for "D-0701" with method "PAPER"
    When "RS-0301" records result "SIGNED" with scan "D-0702" and signed date 2026-12-14
    Then the signature request has status "SIGNED" and method "PAPER"
    Then the harness reads signed true and method "PAPER" on "T-0502"
    Then P3 receives event CUSTOMER_ACCEPTED with signature basis "WET_INK" and moves the case to "WITH_FIELD_INSPECTION" under R-DIL-18

  Scenario: AC3 The decline and the expired request do not sign the treatment (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given "D-0601" was sent for e-signature on 2026-12-10
    When EasyApp returns signing result "DECLINED" on 2026-12-11
    Then the signature request has status "DECLINED"
    Then the harness reads signed false on "T-0501"
    Given "D-0601" was sent for e-signature on 2026-12-10 and has status "SENT"
    Given P3 raised OFFER_EXPIRED for "T-0501" on 2026-12-21 and called SignatureApi.cancel
    When EasyApp returns signing result "SIGNED" for that request on 2026-12-21
    Then the signature request keeps status "EXPIRED"
    Then the harness holds the result on the exception queue
    Then the harness reads no signature call on "T-0501" for that result

  Scenario: AC4 The same signing result twice stores one version and records the signature once (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the signing result "SIGNED" for request reference "EA-30001" was applied
    When the same result for "EA-30001" arrives again
    Then the harness reads no second version of "D-0601"
    Then the harness reads one signature call on "T-0501"
    Then the harness counts the repeat under rule R-UNI-40

  Scenario: AC5 The EasyApp path unavailable queues the send and retries to the limit (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the ACE path to EasyApp returns "unavailable"
    When "RS-0301" sends "D-0601" for e-signature
    Then the response is status 201 with status "QUEUED" and MSG-GEN-006 naming "EasyApp"
    Then JOB-11 retries the send until it is accepted or the retry limit of 5 is reached
    Then the harness reads the attempt count of 5 in its report
```

These five criteria are new for the ITG harness and do not restate the app criteria owned by the I stories.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A customer signs electronically only where the template's signature basis allows it, and by wet ink where Legal requires it | REQ-OCC-009; template signature basis approved by Legal |
| BR2 | A signed offer routes to operations for booking | R-RES-16, R-SET-10 |
| BR3 | A mortgage deed in lieu with a wet ink signature goes to the collateral inspection before the Land Office transfer | R-DIL-18, R-DIL-27 |
| BR4 | A decline returns the case under the route set's decline rule | R-RES-17 |
| BR5 | No signature by the end of the offer validity ends the offer | R-RES-18, R-SET-11 |
| BR6 | A signature request to the customer is an outbound contact and passes the conduct check | CTL-16; R-SET-12 |
| BR7 | The signed document is write-once on the case | CTL-12; DT06 |
| BR8 | The same result twice has one effect | R-UNI-40 |
| BR9 | A system that is unavailable queues the send and retries | R-UNI-33 |

The rules are the legacy rules of RWB-E2-018. This story asserts them across services; it owns none of them, and the rule text and the rule package stay with rwb-decision and the owning service.

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Waiting customer | Customer responds, or the validity timer expires | Signature recorded, decline recorded, or OFFER_EXPIRED | In progress |

P3 makes the case status change on the treatment update this story sends. This story sets the signature request status: Queued, Sent, Signed, Declined, Expired.

The harness changes no state itself: it reads the state the owning services hold through their contracts, and it changes a case, a document, a request or a treatment only by calling the owner's operation of §12.2.

The authority inside the journey is that of legacy RWB-E2-018 §10 and is enforced by rwb-access and by the owning services. This story adds no authority.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test capability and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}/signature-requests` | P6 rwb-comms | Create the request: documentId, partyId, method (E_SIGNATURE, BRANCH, PAPER) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}/signature-requests` | P6 rwb-comms | Read the request state and method after each step |
| POST | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/signature-requests/{requestId}/result` | P6 rwb-comms | Record a branch or paper result: result, signedDocumentId, signedAt |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` | P5 rwb-document | Read the document version, write_once and storage reference of the signed copy |
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/versions` | P5 rwb-document | Add the signed copy as version 2, write-once, as the EasyApp path does |
| PATCH | `/api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}` | S2 rwb-treatment | The treatment contract that records signature_status, which the legacy TreatmentApi.recordSignature writes |
| GET | `/api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}` | S2 rwb-treatment | Read back the recorded signature_status and method for the journey assertion |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The authorise check on every acting role (Architecture v5 slide 41 first API path `/authorise`; slide 14 `POST /authorise`) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | P7 rwb-decision | Read the decision log for the case, and the record of the journey |

Every call is one hop from the harness to the owner on the owner's base (DP-11, DP-13), with a 2-second timeout and an Idempotency-Key on every POST (Architecture v5 slide 11). Where a screen is in the journey the call is made through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The request and response schemas are those of the owning service's published OpenAPI; this story introduces none.

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; its evidence goes to the wave 2 run record.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. JOB-11 Outbox sender is exercised: the unavailable path of AC5 watches the outbox relay retry every minute to the retry limit of 5 (Architecture v5 slide 44). The harness starts no workflow and no activity, and the service workflows of the journey stay with their owning stories.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-11 is the outbox relay of every service and needs no Schedule from this story; the harness creates no Temporal Schedule (DP-10 resolves to "exercise the relay, add no job").

None. The harness owns no table, creates no schema and reads no service's tables (DP-01).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `integration/recovery/esign` in the ACE repository, package `<ACE base package>.recovery.integration.esign`. Not part of a deployed service.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyFile | Rule table | One row per journey: steps, acting role, method, seeded facts, expected result |
| RunSettings | Rule table | Base per service, 2-second timeout, 60-second signed-copy target, retry limit 5 |
| SeedFixture | Service | Seeds the case, treatment, documents and party facts of the journey in SIT |
| JourneyRunner | Service | Calls each owner on its base, one hop, and records the observed result of every step |
| EasyAppDriver | Service | Drives the EasyApp send and result through the ACE common module test path and the result operation |
| DuplicateReplay | Service | Replays the same EA-30001 result and counts the repeat under R-UNI-40 |
| OutboxProbe | Service | Watches the JOB-11 relay on the unavailable path and counts the attempts to the limit of 5 |
| EvidenceWriter | Service | Writes the run report keyed by story key and business date, with the fake set and the gate result |
| HarnessGate | Service | Passes or fails the run against the pass criteria of the journey file |

**Database.** None. The harness owns no schema and uses the API only (DP-01; DP-15 applies to the owning services, not here).

**Environment and test data.** SIT, against the owning services' published contracts and the contract fakes of §12.8, with the EasyApp test path of the ACE common module. The harness environment, the data seeding and the evidence format and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0402; ASM-0577). The journey uses the legacy facts: case RC-2026-000888, settlement T-0501, agreement D-0601, party P-0088, request RS-0301, branch scan D-0602, deed in lieu contract D-0701 with scan D-0702, case RC-2026-000889 and treatment T-0502, and the result references EA-30001 and EA-99999.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |

The platform H rows of this table (DP-07, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15, DP-19) are delivered by platform wave 0 stories and are not repeated in the metadata H column, which stays empty for this story. The harness reads reference data and party facts through the owner's contract rather than through a table (DP-05), and every event it sees is read from the owner's topic (DP-09). The dependencies that block the journey's Done are the I stories of the metadata: the real services replace the fakes.

**Build steps**

1. Write the journey file and the run settings, with the facts and the pass criteria of section 16.
2. Stand up the five WireMock fakes and the ACE common module path stub of §12.8, and wire the journey to them.
3. Write SeedFixture and JourneyRunner; run AC1 end to end against the fakes.
4. Add the branch and paper journeys and the scan link; run AC2.
5. Add the decline and the OFFER_EXPIRED cancel path with the held result; run AC3.
6. Add DuplicateReplay and the R-UNI-40 count; run AC4.
7. Add OutboxProbe and the retry limit of 5; run AC5.
8. Write EvidenceWriter and HarnessGate, attach one run to the wave 2 run record, then replace each fake with its real service as the I story lands and re-run.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.integration.esign.journey`, switched on for the SIT run and off in production. The harness runs in SIT only.

**Done when.** The twelve test cases of section 16 pass against the fakes on Day 1, and the same twelve pass with every fake replaced by the real service when RWB-P6-E2018-APP, RWB-P5-E2018-APP, RWB-P5-E2017-APP and RWB-S2-E2018-APP are done, with the signed-copy evidence signed off by the integration and QA leads.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead of rwb-access with the external gateway owner**, I want **the published contract baseline of the partner identity resolution: an OpenAPI 3.1 document for one POST on the rwb-access base, the claim set the gateway supplies, the answer that carries the roles, a `PLACED` scope, the matrix version, the masking policy version and an expiry, one refusal vocabulary with its statuses and message ids, the statement that rwb-access holds no partner table and no token, the consumed parameters and reference-data reads, the absent events, and the contract fakes**, so that **the app story, the external gateway and the end-to-end proof of the key can build against one fixed, testable contract on Day 1 without waiting for `rwb-access`, `rwb-partner` or `rwb-case` to be built**.

This contract carries no legacy acceptance criterion: AC6 and AC9 of RWB-E2-019 belong to RWB-P4-E2019-APP, the seven other criteria of the key belong to RWB-ITG-E2019-ITG, and the six criteria of section 7 test the document, the claim set, the answer, the refusal vocabulary, the absence of a partner table and a token, and the fakes. It is one of the three stories of the rwb-access slice of the key, and like them it copies no part of a legacy criterion.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The legacy story resolved a partner identity inside one process, where the token issuer, the partner role, the binding, the firm status and the scope were whatever the resolver happened to read. In the target the partner identity is authenticated at the external gateway, and rwb-access is asked one question: which Recovery roles, which scope and which policy versions does this partner identity get. The answer has to be a document before three teams can build against it — the rwb-access resolver, the DMZ gateway that calls it, and the end-to-end proof of the key.

**The division is fixed and is the same in all three stories of this legacy key.** **RWB-P4-E2019-APP**, **RWB-P4-E2019-CON** and **RWB-P4-E2019-INF** are the rwb-access slice: the resolution and its answer, this contract, and the DMZ plumbing that carries the call. **RWB-S9-E2019-APP** owns the firm, the partner user, the binding and the instruction, because `partner`, `partner_user` and `partner_instruction` are S9's under the Ownership Map ruling ASM-0072. **RWB-P7-E2019-APP** owns the central ledger entries a partner sign-in and refusal leave behind. **RWB-ITG-E2019-ITG** is the end-to-end proof and carries legacy AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC7 and AC8. Because the binding moved to S9, the gateway resolves the partner user and the partner role before it calls rwb-access, and it supplies them as claims; this contract therefore fixes the claim set as the boundary and says so explicitly, instead of naming a table rwb-access may not read.

Fixing that boundary once, with faked consumers, buys three things. The rwb-access resolver can be built before rwb-partner is finished, because the only partner facts it needs are claims in a faked request. The gateway can be built and its mTLS hop tested before the resolver exists, because the answer shape is fixed. And the end-to-end proof has one place to look for what was proved and what was not: the token, the firm and the instruction are proved there, and the roles, the scope, the versions and the refusals are proved here.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_access`, REST base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1` (declared and deliberately unused), the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` for the record of a resolution, task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`. The operation path, the claim names, the answer schema and the expiry rule are named by no source, so the baseline fixes them as a stated default and carries the open point as Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0785; ASM-1432) and (GAP-0785; ASM-1438).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the topic and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published for the staff view of the same records, and RWB-P4-E2019-INF is the DMZ slice that will carry the partner-side call; neither is a build dependency of this document.
- The partner gateway platform and its FAPI 2.0 profile are RWB-PLT-N007-INF's; this baseline assumes a sender-constrained token whose lifetime is 5 minutes, as that story fixes, and carries the expiry rule of section 11 accordingly.
- RWB-P4-E2019-APP is the owner of the resolver that implements this document; the document describes shapes built from the `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule` and `role_conflict` tables as TSD P4 v3 T3.1 publishes them and adds no column.
- The ownership of the tables and paths comes from the Ownership Map only: `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule` and `role_conflict` are P4's, `partner`, `partner_user` and `partner_instruction` are S9's, `decision_log_entry` is P7's and `lov_value` is P3's. No table of another service is named as this service's (DP-01).
- The parameter and reference-data operations this document consumes are P3's, and their shapes are taken from the P3 contracts rather than restated here (DP-06, DP-07).
- The platform error envelope, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the OpenAPI 3.1 conventions are the platform baseline; where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).
- The operation path, the claim names, the answer schema and the refusal vocabulary are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0785; ASM-1432) and (GAP-0785; ASM-1439); this baseline fixes them and the contract review confirms them before they are frozen.

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document with the base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, the security scheme, the problem responses and the shared components of the service.
2. Fix the one operation, `POST /partner-identities/resolve`, with its purpose, its access rule and its `Idempotency-Key` requirement.
3. Fix the request schema of the claim set: the partner identity reference, the partner id, the partner role code or codes, the firm state and contract end, `amr`, the route and the token expiry, each mapped to the DF field it mirrors.
4. Fix the answer schema: the roles with their class and their `PARTNER_PORTAL` letters, the scope descriptor of type `PLACED` with the partner id and the instruction types, the matrix version, the masking policy version and the expiry.
5. Fix the refusal vocabulary: the status, the message id and the reason of each refusal, drawn from the legacy messages and reasons and from the P4 message catalogue.
6. State the negative boundary in the document itself: rwb-access holds no partner table, no session, no password and no token, and the firm, the binding and the instruction remain rwb-partner's.
7. Declare the consumed parameters and reference-data reads as consumed, each with its owner, one hop and the 2 s client budget; declare the instruction read of the owner as not provided here.
8. Declare that the resolution publishes no event and consumes none, and that the record of a resolution leaves through the DP-03 library on `rwb.decision-record.v1`.
9. Publish the nine tables of section 12 and the contract fakes of section 12.8.
10. Add the contract tests: schema validation, the claim and answer field names, the refusal vocabulary, the boundary statement, the consumed declarations, the absent events and the drift between a fake and the document.
11. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P4-E2019-APP, RWB-P4-E2019-INF and RWB-ITG-E2019-ITG.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The document fails OpenAPI 3.1 validation | The pipeline fails and no baseline is tagged | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A declared operation names another service's base, path or owner, or declares an S9 partner path | The review refuses the document; the partner portal paths stay rwb-partner's | None | AC1, AC5 |
| X3 | A field of the claim set or of the answer has no DF field behind it, or a required field is optional | The contract test fails | None | AC2 |
| X4 | A refusal is declared without a status, a message id or a reason, or a status falls outside the vocabulary | The contract test fails | None | AC3 |
| X5 | The document, an example or a fake names `partner`, `partner_user`, `partner_instruction`, a session store or a token | The review refuses the document | None | AC4 |
| X6 | A consumed operation is declared without an owner, without the one-hop rule or without the 2 s budget | The contract test fails | None | AC5 |
| X7 | An event is declared as published or consumed by the resolution | The review refuses the document | None | AC5 |
| X8 | A fake answers a path, a status or a payload the document does not declare | The drift test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC6 |
| X9 | An example carries a personal field, a token or a credential | The contract test fails and the example is refused | None | AC6 |
| X10 | The expiry rule of the answer is left open in the document | The review refuses the document; the rule of section 11 is stated | None | AC2 |

| Independent | No build dependency; reads the Ownership Map, the platform envelopes, the TSD field names, the P4 message texts and the P3 contract names only |

| Valuable | Unblocks the resolver, the DMZ slice and the end-to-end proof on Day 1, and keeps the partner table and the token out of rwb-access |

```gherkin

  Background:

  Scenario: AC3 The refusal vocabulary is fixed with its statuses, messages and reasons (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the refusal component of the document

    Then no partner role, an unknown role or a role of class "BANK_USER" answers 401 with MSG-P4-001
    Then no active binding answers 401 with MSG-P4-001 and reason "NO_PARTNER_BINDING"
    Then no second factor in amr answers 401 with MSG-P4-005
    Then two partner roles, or a partner role with a bank role, answers 403 with MSG-P4-006 and reason "ROLE_CONFLICT"

    Then a claim set of the wrong shape answers 400 with the field named and no message id
    Then a record that cannot be written answers 503 with MSG-P7-003

    Then no event is declared as consumed by the resolution
```

These six criteria test the artefact only. No criterion restates a legacy acceptance criterion: AC6 and AC9 of RWB-E2-019 belong to RWB-P4-E2019-APP, and AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC7 and AC8 belong to RWB-ITG-E2019-ITG.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/access/v1`; a document never declares another service's path, and the partner portal paths stay rwb-partner's | DP-13; Architecture v5 slides 17 and 41 |
| BR2 | A consumed operation is described as consumed, never as provided; its owner comes from the Ownership Map | DP-11; Ownership Map v1 |
| BR3 | Error responses use one RFC 9457 envelope and one message id per condition; the business texts of the legacy messages are kept unchanged | Architecture v5 slide 11; legacy RWB-E2-019 section 14 |
| BR4 | The schemas carry the TSD P4 v3 T3.1 field names and the claim names this baseline fixes, and add no field of another service | TSD P4 v3 T3.1, T3.2; DP-01 |
| BR5 | The partner facts in the claim set mirror the fields rwb-partner owns and are claims, not rows: rwb-access reads no S9 table | Ownership Map ruling ASM-0072; DP-01 |
| BR6 | The answer carries roles, a `PLACED` scope, the matrix version, the masking policy version and an expiry, and nothing else | Architecture v5 slide 14; legacy RWB-E2-019 AC1 and AC2 |
| BR7 | The refusal vocabulary is 400, 401, 403 and 503 with MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-005, MSG-P4-006, MSG-P4-008 and MSG-P7-003 and the four reasons of the legacy story | legacy RWB-E2-019 sections 5 and 14; FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-001-03 |
| BR8 | The expiry of an answer is an instant never later than the token expiry the gateway supplies, and no answer outlives it | Architecture v5 slide 35; RWB-PLT-N007-INF token lifetime |
| BR9 | The resolution publishes no event and consumes none; the policy events of the service belong to other stories | Architecture v5 slide 14; TSD P4 v3 T5.3 |
| BR10 | A schema change is additive within major version 1; a removed, renamed or retyped field is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 |
| BR11 | A POST requires an `Idempotency-Key`; a replay answers the first answer and writes no second record | Architecture v5 slide 11; DP-09 |
| BR12 | The contract declares no workflow, no activity and no Schedule for the capability | Architecture v5 slide 14; TSD P4 v3 T5.3 |
| BR13 | No example, fake or event payload carries a personal field, a token or a credential | NFR-040; NFR-052; ADR-010 |

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| `PartnerIdentityClaim` | `partnerIdentityRef` (DF-REF-213 identity_ref), `partnerId` (DF-REF-214 partner_id), `partnerRoleCodes` (DF-REF-215 role_code), `firmPanelStatus` (DF-PRT-005), `firmContractEnd` (DF-PRT-006), `amr`, `route`, `tokenExpiry` |
| `PartnerIdentityAnswer` | `roles` with `roleCode` DF-REF-035, `roleClass` DF-REF-037 and `letters` DF-REF-043, `scope` with `type` "PLACED" and `partnerId` DF-REF-214 and `instructionTypes`, `matrixVersion` DF-REF-044, `maskingVersion` DF-REF-202, `expiry`, `decision` |
| Refusal | `status` 400, 401, 403 or 503; `messageId` MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-005, MSG-P4-006, MSG-P4-008 or MSG-P7-003; `reason` `BANK_IDENTITY_ON_PARTNER_ROUTE`, `NO_PARTNER_BINDING`, `ROLE_CONFLICT` or `PARTNER_NOT_ACTIVE` |
| Scope type | `PLACED`, the legacy scope name, with the partner id and the instruction types; it is a descriptor of a partner session and is not added to `LOV-SCOPE` of TSD P4 v3 T3.2, which holds OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL |
| Record event | `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` with the `AC-SIGN` or `AC-DENY` entry of a resolution, from the DP-03 library |
| Named and not owned | `partner`, `partner_user` and `partner_instruction` (S9), `decision_log_entry` (P7), `lov_value` (P3) — named in the boundary statement only |

The operation path, the claim names, the answer field names and the refusal vocabulary are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0785; ASM-1432): TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021, API Specification v4 declares no `x-module: P4` partner path, and Architecture v5 slide 14 names `/authorise`, `/me/permissions`, `/doa-limits` and `/masking-policies` only. The expiry rule is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0785; ASM-1438): the only lifetime the sources fix is the gateway token lifetime of RWB-PLT-N007-INF. The mapping of a refusal to a status is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0785; ASM-1439) and is fixed by AC3. The absence of an event is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0785; ASM-1440) and is fixed by BR9 and AC5.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-access (P4); base `/api/recovery/access/v1`.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/partner-identities/resolve` | `PartnerIdentityClaim` in, `PartnerIdentityAnswer` out, or one problem detail of the refusal vocabulary; `decision` is `RESOLVED` on the answer | PARTNER_PORTAL right R of the gateway workload identity; `Idempotency-Key` required |

Errors: 400 a claim set of the wrong shape with the field named and no message id, 401 MSG-P4-001 for a bank identity on the partner route, no partner role and no binding, 401 MSG-P4-005 for no second factor, 403 MSG-P4-006 for two roles or a partner role with a bank role, 403 MSG-P4-008 for a firm that is not active, 503 MSG-P7-003 where the record cannot be written. Major version 1 sits in the base; an additive field within version 1 is a compatible change, and a removed, renamed or retyped field is a new major version (BR10). A replay of the same `Idempotency-Key` answers the first answer and writes no second record (BR11).

The path is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0785; ASM-1432). It follows the base rule of DP-13, it duplicates no path of rwb-partner, and the contract review confirms it before it is frozen.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11).

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | The instruction types of a partner role and the approval role of the binding, at the version in force (DP-06) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | `LOV-ROLE-CLASS`, `LOV-CAPABILITY` and `LOV-SCOPE` at the version in force (DP-07) |

Neither is declared as provided by rwb-access, and no operation of rwb-partner, rwb-decision or rwb-case appears in the document as provided.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The resolution publishes no event of its own; rwb-access publishes `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` and `rwb.access.DoALimitChanged.v1` from other stories only (BR9). The record of a resolution leaves through the DP-03 library as `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, which is the platform library's event and is declared here only to say where the record goes.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The document declares no inbox, no consumer group and no subscription: the versions in force are read at resolution time through the P4 tables and the P3 contracts, and the policy events that refresh a cache elsewhere are not this capability's (BR9, ASM-1440).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. No workflow, no activity and no signal is part of this contract: the resolution is synchronous, and the `rwb-access` queue carries only the access review Schedule of RWB-P4-AD008-APP (BR12).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The resolution is request-driven, and no effective date, refresh or review is a Schedule of this document.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | P4 (rwb_access) | The partner role rows of class `PARTNER_USER` behind `roles` |
| `permission` | P4 (rwb_access) | The `PARTNER_PORTAL` letters and the matrix version behind `letters` and `matrixVersion` |
| `masking_rule` | P4 (rwb_access) | The masking version behind `maskingVersion` |
| `role_conflict` | P4 (rwb_access) | The pairs behind the `ROLE_CONFLICT` refusal |
| the local decision-record table of the DP-03 library | P4, in `rwb_access` | The `AC-SIGN` and `AC-DENY` entry of a resolution |

**No partner table and no token are declared, owned or read.** `partner`, `partner_user` and `partner_instruction` are S9 rwb-partner's (Ownership Map ruling ASM-0072), `decision_log_entry` and `approval` are P7 rwb-decision's, and `lov_value` is P3 rwb-case's. The contract states that rwb-access resolves a partner identity to P4 roles and scopes from the partner-supplied claims and its own `role`, `permission` and `masking_rule` data, and reads no S9 table (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Claim fake | The claim set of AC6 and AC9 plus the refusal cases | The resolver, the contract tests, the end-to-end proof |
| Answer fake | A resolved answer for `P-5101` with `PT-LAWFIRM`, scope `PLACED` and `LF-0012`, matrix version `PM-2026.11`, masking version `MASK-SIT-01` and a five-minute expiry | The DMZ slice, the resolver, the end-to-end proof |
| Parameters fake (P3) | `GET /admin/parameters` with the instruction types `FILE_SUIT,ENFORCE`, `APPRAISE` and `COLLECT` at version PAR-2026.11 | The resolver, the contract tests |
| Reference-data fake (P3) | `GET /admin/lists/{listCode}` with the three lists at their versions | The resolver, the contract tests |
| rwb-partner contract fake (S9) | Instruction `INS-2027-000431` of `LF-0019` and the firm states of `LF-0012`, `LF-0019` and `VL-0004`, as the end-to-end proof of AC6 needs them | The end-to-end proof, the resolver's AC6 test |
| Decision-record fake (DP-03) | The append of `AC-SIGN` and `AC-DENY`, the reason, and a forced failure | The resolver, the contract tests |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 provided, 2 consumed | The resolution provided; the parameters and reference-data reads consumed; one hop, 2 s timeout with a breaker |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | No topic is declared for the resolution; the record leaves through the DP-03 library |
| Temporal | 0 workflows, 0 activities | None in this contract |
| File | None | No file input and no file output |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `openapi/rwb-access-partner-identity-v1.yaml` (OpenAPI 3.1) with the one operation and the shared components, the `PartnerIdentityClaim` and `PartnerIdentityAnswer` schemas with their examples, the refusal component, the boundary statement in the contract README, the versioning rules, and the six WireMock mapping sets of section 12.8.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables. The document names the four P4 tables and the S9 tables as not read | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the record of a resolution leaves through it | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views. No ACE view appears in this document | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library, declared as consumed | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case, declared as consumed | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library; the answer feeds the guard, which is declared as the same service's | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout, declared on both consumed reads | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`; the resolution sits on the P4 base and duplicates no S9 path | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in `rwb_access`; the document adds no migration and no column | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route for the staff view of the same records; a partner never uses it | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The dependency-added column records the build dependency of the owning story; this story is Day 1 by rule and carries no H and no C of its own.

**Build steps**

1. OpenAPI 3.1 skeleton with the base path, the security scheme, the problem responses and the shared components; schema lint in the pipeline (AC1).
2. The one operation with its access rule, its `Idempotency-Key` and its four error responses (AC1).
3. The two schemas with the field names of section 11 and their DF mapping (AC2).
4. The refusal component with the statuses, the message ids and the four reasons (AC3).
5. The boundary statement of AC4 in the document and in the README: no partner table, no session, no token.
6. The consumed reads with their owners, the one-hop rule and the 2 s budget, and the absent events of AC5.
7. The six fakes and the fixtures of section 12.8, including the resolved answer and the refusal cases (AC6).
8. The six contract tests; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build.
9. Baseline tag and the consumer sign-off note of the resolver, the DMZ slice and the end-to-end proof.

**Feature switch.** The operation is switched by the parameter `rwb.access.partner-signin` of RWB-P4-E2019-APP, not by a flag of this document; the document declares no 404 branch of its own and adds no parameter.

**Consumer sign-off**

| Consumer | What it accepts |
|---|---|
| RWB-P4-E2019-APP | The operation, the claim and answer schemas, the refusal vocabulary, the expiry rule and the six fakes |
| RWB-P4-E2019-INF | The operation path, the claim transport and the 5-minute expiry the token lifetime gives |
| RWB-ITG-E2019-ITG | The answer shape, the reasons and the record event as the evidence it records for the end-to-end key |

**Done when.** The document validates in the pipeline, the six contract tests pass, the six fakes answer every declared path, the boundary statement is in the document and the README, and the resolver, the DMZ slice and the end-to-end proof have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | No partner role, no active binding, a bank identity on the partner route, or an expired answer | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | An action outside the partner role's letters, refused by the guard or by the owner of the action | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | An instruction of another firm, refused by the owner of the instruction against the `PLACED` descriptor | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P4-005 | `amr` holds no second factor | Sign in again with your second factor. The Workbench needs multi-factor authentication. |
| MSG-P4-006 | Two partner roles, or a partner role and a bank role | Your roles {role} and {otherRole} cannot be held together. Access is refused and the security administrator has been told. |
| MSG-P4-008 | The firm is suspended, exited or past its contract end | Your firm's access to the Recovery Workbench has ended. Contact your SCB partner manager. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The record or the outbox row cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The message ids are contract elements; the texts are the legacy texts unchanged and their Thai text follows DL10. MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 are declared because the guard and the owner of the instruction answer them, and neither is produced by this operation itself.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the role codes, the instruction types, the versions, the reasons and the statuses stay rows, parameters or values behind the document.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: the partner identity reference, the partner id, the role codes and the versions only.
- No token, refresh token, secret or private key is declared, and the document states that rwb-access holds none (ADR-010).
- One REST base, one topic and one event-name pattern per service; a document that names another service's base or topic fails the review (DP-13).
- The partner table, the binding and the instruction stay out of this document: they are S9's, and a path or a table of theirs declared here fails the review (ASM-0072).
- The partner portal paths of rwb-partner are never re-declared as this service's.
- Every example is synthetic; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The error envelope and the CloudEvents envelope come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.
