These eight criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only; they restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P6-E2021-APP and they copy no criterion of the legacy story. The wave 2 harness `RWB-ITG-E2021-ITG` consumes this baseline and copies none of these criteria.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/comms/v1`; the document never declares another service's path as provided | DP-13; Architecture v5 slide 41 notes |
| BR2 | Event names are `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1` on the topic `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, with retry and `.dlt` topics | DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR3 | Every event carries the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, is keyed by caseId and carries no personal data | Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43 notes; DP-09 |
| BR4 | A read declares no Idempotency-Key; a POST declares it and stores its answer | Architecture v5 slide 11; DP-09 |
| BR5 | Error responses use one envelope and one message ID per condition; the business message texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story | Architecture v5 platform baseline; Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR6 | A schema change is additive within a major version; a breaking change is a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |
| BR7 | The document lists only operations owned by rwb-comms; a consumed operation is described as consumed, never as provided | Ownership Map v1 |
| BR8 | The dispatch facts of a notice are its own rows; the file, the acknowledgement and the proof results are rwb-integration's and WIN's and are named as consumed | DP-01; DP-16; Architecture v5 slide 17 |
| BR9 | The 16:00 run is a Temporal Schedule and a workflow; no Quartz row, no shared job table and no batch table is declared | DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44 |
| BR10 | No business value is fixed in the contract: the proof window, the statutory notice type list, the eligible states and the result code map stay data or reference data | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR11 | The decision record is the local library's entry on the shared topic, never a new event of this service | DP-03; Architecture v5 slide 42 (event 08) |
| BR12 | The letter body and the addressee are not part of this contract: the file carries a document reference and a barcode | Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43 notes; TSD P6 T3.1 |
| BR13 | The daily reconciliation REC-05 and its owner are not fixed here; the legacy story names the check and no source names the owner | Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 13; GAP-1090 |
| BR14 | ACE data is reached only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views of the owner; this document declares no view of its own | DP-05; DP-18 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The two operations, the file contract, the vocabulary and the event rows are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app, operations and test stories and the rwb-integration, rwb-decision, rwb-case, rwb-deviation and rwb-source-data owners accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A field is added within major version 1, for example a new proof result code | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A field is removed, renamed or retyped, or a hold reason value changes | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | Retired element reappears | The absence test of AC8 fails | In review |

The notice state machine that the document describes is the app story's; this baseline fixes its vocabulary and its guards and moves no notice.

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| Tech lead of rwb-comms | Owns the OpenAPI and AsyncAPI documents and the fakes; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version, and the correction of the Ownership Map rows the baseline consumes |

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Notice resource | The RWB-P6-E1052-CON Notice plus `holdReason`, `dispatchFileId` and `dispatchAttempts`; the existing properties are unchanged |
| Dispatch fields | `sent_date` DF-LEG-019, `barcode` DF-LEG-020, `sent_type` DF-LEG-023, `dispatch_file_id` DF-LEG-033 and `dispatch_attempts` DF-LEG-034, all on `notice` |
| Proof fields | `callback_date` DF-LEG-021 and `delivery_status` DF-LEG-022, set only from the proof result record |
| Hold reason | `hold_reason` DF-LEG-032 with the closed vocabulary of AC4 |
| File records | The dispatch record, the acknowledgement record and the proof result record of AC2; the field list beyond the IDs and dates named there is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1089; ASM-2037) |
| Event payloads | IDs, codes, dates and amounts only; no name, address, identity number or contact point |

The field-level types, lengths and required flags of the added properties are settled in the baseline review; this story fixes the names, the optionality rule of AC1 and the vocabulary of AC4.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-comms (P6); base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`.

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/notices` | NoticeRequest in, Notice of status 201 out, with the dispatch and proof fields of AC1 | Litigation, right C, scope applied | Idempotency-Key header, answer stored for 24 hours |
| GET | `/notices/{noticeId}` | Notice of status 200 out, with its dispatch and its proof | Litigation, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

Both operations answer 401, 403, 404, 503 and the POST also answers 409 and 422, each with the error envelope and one message ID of section 14.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | the reference-data read of RWB-P3-E1043-CON | P3 rwb-case | LOV-NOTICE, LOV-DELIVERY, LOV-SENT-TYPE, the statutory notice type list and the proof window, faked (DP-07) |
| POST | the D7.1 demand and recall approval of RWB-P7-E2014-CON | P7 rwb-decision | The approval answer that moves a notice to Approved, faked |
| GET | the case read with legal hold, owner and queue | P3 rwb-case | The conduct check and the scope test, faked. The scope source and the shape of the read are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1092; ASM-2040) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1/deviations?caseId={caseId}` | S8 rwb-deviation | The open X1 and X2 contact stops of the case, faked |
| POST | the interaction ledger write | P1 rwb-source-data | The ledger entry with channel, summary and conduct check, faked (DP-18) |
| POST | the dispatch file, the acknowledgement read and the proof result read of the rwb-integration contract | P2 rwb-integration | INT-14 out and the INT-15 results, faked (DP-16). The operation names and the file shapes are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1089; ASM-2037) |
| POST | the case facts DELIVERY_FAILED, PROOF_WINDOW_EXPIRED and the queue transfer with NOTICE_UNSERVED | P3 rwb-case | The case move and the NOTICE_PERIOD timer, faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream. The `deviations` read path carries the Ownership Map gap of the S8 rows; the ledger and the ACE facts carry the P1 ruling of DP-18 and DP-05.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Schema element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` (event 14) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 rwb-comms | noticeId, caseId, noticeType, businessDate, dispatchFileId, barcode, sentDate, sentType, conductCheck; published by the app story when the acknowledgement lands |
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` (event 15) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 rwb-comms | noticeId, caseId, barcode, result of DELIVERED, REFUSED or UNDELIVERABLE, deliveryStatus, callbackDate; published by the app story for every outcome |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (event 08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | decision record reference, decision code, ruleId, ruleVersion, finalCall, decidedAt; the local decision-record library publishes it (DP-03) |

This story declares the three elements and publishes none itself.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Consumer contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` (event 06) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | caseId, deviationCode, contactStop, raisedAt; consumed to hold the notices of the case at the next run |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` (event 07) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | caseId, deviationCode, clearedAt, outcome; consumed to make a held notice eligible again |
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` (event 05) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | caseId, fromState, toState, changedAt; consumed so a closed case is skipped by the run |

The three rows are consumed inside rwb-comms by RWB-P6-E2021-APP; this baseline fixes their shape and their key (caseId).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| NoticeDispatchWorkflow | Workflow, one run per business date | `rwb-comms` | The proof-window step, the eligible selection, the conduct check, the file handoff and the durable proof timer |
| conductCheck | Activity | `rwb-comms` | Passed or blocked with the reason and the rule ID |
| generateLetter | Activity, owner rwb-document | `rwb-document` | The letter from the approved template version |
| decisionApproval | Child workflow, owner rwb-decision | `rwb-decision` | The D7.1 approval answer |
| deliverFile | Activity, owner rwb-integration | `rwb-integration` | The WIN dispatch file and its acknowledgement |
| recordDecision | Activity through the library | `rwb-comms` | The local decision record and its outbox row |

No activity is registered by this story; the six rows fix what the app story may assume about the writer and what the operations story must deploy.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Name | Cron | Overlap policy | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| The JOB-10 notice dispatch run | 16:00 on every business day | SKIP with the catch-up window of the workflow kit | Starts NoticeDispatchWorkflow on task queue `rwb-comms` with the business date |

The handoff from the bank Airflow WIN file window to this Schedule is one row of the document and its mechanism is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1095; ASM-2043). No Quartz row, no shared job table and no batch table is declared (JOB-05 and TE-007 are retired). The outbox relay JOB-11 belongs to the platform and is not registered here. The daily reconciliation REC-05 has no owner in this baseline (GAP-1090; ASM-2038).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| notice | P6 (rwb_comms) | The notice, its dispatch fields and its proof dates; the table the two operations and the run read and write |
| template | P6 (rwb_comms) | The template version the conduct check reads |
| merge_field | P6 (rwb_comms) | The merge catalogue of the letter; read only by the loop |
| decision record (local) | P6 rows in `rwb_comms`, written through the P7 library | The held and unserved entries (DP-03) |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_comms` | The envelope of the three event rows, the inbox of the three consumed rows and the POST idempotency |

`recovery_case`, `task` and `timer` are P3's, `deviation` is S8's, `decision_log_entry` is P7's, `document` is P5's, `interaction` is P1's, and `outbound_item` and `interface_config` are P2's; the contract names them only as consumed answers (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 provided, 7 consumed | The notice request and read provided; reference data, approval, case read, contact stops, case facts, ledger write and the WIN file consumed; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 3 declared as published by their owners, 3 declared as consumed | NoticeDispatched, NoticeDelivered and DecisionRecorded; DeviationRaised, DeviationCleared and CaseStateChanged |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The additive change to `openapi/rwb-comms-v1.yaml` for this loop, the dispatch file and acknowledgement schema as a shared component, the AsyncAPI fragment of `rwb.comms.events.v1` naming events 14 and 15, the contract README rows for the vocabulary, the file shapes and the Schedule, and the six WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/comms/v1` | none |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-16 is applied through the rwb-integration contract row of 12.2: the WIN file is never called by this service directly, and the file work of the loop lives in rwb-integration. DP-08 is not in the pattern set of this key: the capability area and the right are declared per operation and enforced at gateway-bff, and the scope read of AC1 carries the gap of GAP-1092.

**Build steps**

1. Add the dispatch and proof properties to the Notice resource and validate the additive rule of AC1 in the pipeline.
2. Write the dispatch file, acknowledgement and proof result schema of AC2 with the placeholder on the fields the sources do not give.
3. Record the five dispatch columns and the three indexes of AC3 in the physical schema note and the Flyway naming.
4. Close the hold reason and outcome vocabulary of AC4 and map each value to its rule and to LOV-DELIVERY.
5. Record the six event rows of AC5 and validate the AsyncAPI fragment against the registry.
6. Record the workflow and Schedule rows of AC6, the Airflow handoff row and the absence test for the retired job, table and second topic.
7. Publish the six fakes and the eight contract tests; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build.
8. Baseline tag and the consumer sign-off note, including the rwb-integration, WIN, rwb-decision, rwb-case, rwb-deviation and rwb-source-data owners and the wave 2 harness.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI and AsyncAPI artefacts validate in the pipeline, the eight contract tests pass, the six fakes answer every consumed path and the drift test is green, and the app, operations and test stories have accepted the baseline.

The contract serves SCR-18 Notice approval in its Generated, Approved, Sent, Delivered, Unserved and Held states, SCR-04 Case timeline for the ledger entry of each dispatch outcome, and SCR-44 Batch and job monitor for the 16:00 run, its file and its rerun, all through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). ##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the proof window, the statutory notice type list, the eligible states and the result code map stay data, reference data or service configuration.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: IDs, codes, barcodes, dates and amounts only; the dispatch file carries a document reference and never an addressee.
- The contract names only rwb-comms tables and only operations owned by rwb-comms; the approval, the case read, the contact stops, the ledger and the file are consumed and faked, never declared as provided (DP-01, DP-07, DP-16, DP-18).
- One base, one topic and one queue per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- ACE data is reached only through the owner's contract or the owner's `v_ace_*` views; this document declares no ACE view and no cross-schema join (DP-05).
- No retired element is reintroduced: the absence test of AC8 fails a build that declares a Quartz row, a shared job table, a batch table or a second topic.
- Every example in the document is synthetic; no production payload and no production file is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The error envelope, the CloudEvents envelope and the naming rule come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-021 for rwb-comms. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **every approved notice of rwb-comms checked against the conduct rules, written to the WIN dispatch file through the integration service, served from the proof of delivery returned for its barcode, and readable on the rwb-comms contract with its dispatch and its proof**, so that **the notice period is counted from proof of delivery and not from printing, and a letter is never written to a WIN file while a contact stop or a legal hold is in force**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A notice period counted from the print date can be challenged, and a letter sent to a customer under a contact stop is a conduct breach. In the target that loop is not one monolith transaction: rwb-comms owns the notice and its dispatch facts in `rwb_comms`, rwb-case owns the legal hold, the case scope, the queue transfer and the NOTICE_PERIOD timer, rwb-deviation owns the contact stop of X1 and X2, rwb-decision owns the approval and the central decision ledger, rwb-source-data owns the interaction ledger, rwb-document owns the letter body, and rwb-integration owns the WIN file window and the file runs (Architecture v5 slides 17, 41 and 44; TSD P6 v2 T1 and T5.1). The conduct check therefore reads facts from four owners on their contracts and writes its result through the local decision-record library, and the dispatch and delivery facts are published so that the case, the reporting read model and the ledger follow without a table read.

This story is the rwb-comms app slice of legacy RWB-E2-021 and it owns the eight legacy criteria that the service itself can satisfy: AC3 undelivered, AC6 proof window expires, AC7 legal hold, AC8 template withdrawn, AC9 decision log write fails, AC10 repeated request, AC11 notice outside the caller's scope and AC12 notice type missing. Legacy AC1 (dispatch), AC2 (proof back), AC4 (contact stop blocks the letter) and AC5 (consent withdrawn does not stop a statutory notice) are end-to-end journeys across five services and belong to `RWB-ITG-E2021-ITG`; they are named in section 19 and are not copied here.

The decoupling is the one the target fixes: the notice, the dispatch file reference and the proof dates are `rwb_comms` rows (DP-01); the decision record goes through the local library and the shared topic (DP-03); the proof facts of ACE reach this service through the owner's contract and never through a `v_ace_*` read of our own (DP-05); the statutory notice type list, the delivery-result codes and the eligible states are reference data of rwb-case (DP-07); the dispatch and delivery facts are published to the outbox in the same transaction (DP-09); the 16:00 run is a Temporal Schedule and a workflow, not a Quartz row (DP-10); every cross-service call is one hop with a 2 s budget (DP-11); the base is `/api/recovery/comms/v1` (DP-13); the ledger entry is rwb-source-data's and is written through its contract (DP-18); and the screens reach the answer through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). It serves REQ-OCC-003, REQ-OCC-005, REQ-OCC-006 and REQ-ILG-010, carries CTL-15 and CTL-16, and gives the FSD P6 measure "notices with proof of delivery, 100 percent" its service-side evidence.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P6-E1052-APP is done: the notice is generated from an approved template, the `notice` row exists with `notice_type`, `template_id`, `party_id` and `document_id`, and NoticeGenerated is published on `rwb.comms.events.v1`.
- RWB-P6-E1055-APP is done: the proof-of-delivery capture design is settled — the barcode, the result code vocabulary of LOV-DELIVERY and the mapping of the WIN result codes are agreed with the WIN owner through rwb-integration.
- RWB-P6-E2021-CON is published: the two operations on base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`, the dispatch file contract with rwb-integration, the dispatch fields on `notice`, the hold reasons, the two event envelopes and the fakes, so this story builds against a fixed contract on Day 1.
- The `rwb_comms` baseline is in place from RWB-P6-E1046-APP and RWB-P6-E1052-APP: `notice`, `template`, `merge_field` and the library objects `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` exist, and the per-service Flyway sequence runs (DP-15).
- The decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` are live, with the RWB-PLT-E1027-CON contract (DP-03); the outbox and inbox library is live with RWB-PLT-TE006-CON (DP-09); the Temporal workflow kit and the `rwb-recovery` namespace are live with RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (DP-10).
- The reference-data contract of rwb-case is live (RWB-P3-E1043-CON, DP-07) for LOV-NOTICE, LOV-DELIVERY, LOV-SENT-TYPE, the statutory notice type list and the proof window, and the parameters of the service are read as data.
- The D7.1 demand and recall approval contract of rwb-decision is live (RWB-P7-E2014-CON): a notice reaches state Approved only through that approval, and this story reads the answer and never approves.
- The dispatch-eligible notice states are set to Approved (`rwb.comms.dispatch.eligible-states` = APPROVED) and the proof window is the 7 days of R-LIT-08, both as data and not as code. The arithmetic of the 7-day window on the sent date is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1091; ASM-2039).
- The WIN dispatch file (INT-14) and the proof results of INT-15 have a layout, an acknowledgement and an owning operation that this story can call. The layout, the acknowledgement fields and the delivery-result read path are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1089; ASM-2037).
- The cross-service answers this story needs are available as contract fakes from the first run: the approval answer of rwb-decision (RWB-P7-E2014-CON), the case read with legal hold, queue and scope of rwb-case, the contact-stop answers of rwb-deviation, the ACE facts of rwb-source-data and the WIN file answer of rwb-integration.
- The letter body and the addressee are not read here at all: they stay in rwb-document and rwb-source-data, and the dispatch file carries a document reference and the barcode, never a name or an address.
- No build dependency outside rwb-comms and the platform contracts: the H rows in the metadata table are the contract baseline, the two prior app stories and the platform contracts; the C rows never block the build (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. A litigation officer requests a notice with `POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices` and an Idempotency-Key; the generation of RWB-P6-E1052-APP runs and the answer is the Notice in state Generated (but API-P6-001 keeps its purpose of generating the notice from the approved template).
2. The approver approves the notice on SCR-18 through the D7.1 approval of rwb-decision (RWB-P7-E2014-CON) and the notice reaches state Approved.
3. At 16:00 on the business date the Temporal Schedule of this service starts `NoticeDispatchWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-comms` for the JOB-10 run, with the business date as the workflow input and no personal data in it.
4. The workflow runs its first step, the proof-window step: every notice in state Sent whose sent date is past the 7-day proof window of R-LIT-08 becomes Unserved with delivery status PENDING, one decision record is written for each, and no NOTICE_PERIOD timer is asked of rwb-case.
5. The workflow selects the notices in an eligible state (`rwb.comms.dispatch.eligible-states` = APPROVED) for the business date, one page at a time, and for each one runs the conduct check in this order: legal hold of the case, open contact stop of X1 or X2, state of the template version, and consent of the postal channel with the statutory rule.
6. A notice that fails the check is held: the hold reason is written on the `notice` row (`CONTACT_STOP_X1`, `LEGAL_HOLD`, `TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN`), the notice is not written to the dispatch file, the decision record is written through the library with the rule (R-LIT-04, R-LIT-05, R-UNI-20), the ledger entry of rwb-source-data carries conduct check BLOCKED, and rwb-case receives the routing or the task with the message of section 14.
7. A notice that passes is written to the dispatch file of the business date through the file contract of rwb-integration (INT-14), with conduct check PASSED on the ledger entry and the statutory-consent note when consent is withdrawn and the notice type is statutory (R-UNI-10).
8. The WIN acknowledgement for the file returns the barcode and the sent date for each notice; the workflow writes `barcode`, `sent_date`, `sent_type` and `dispatch_file_id` on the notice, moves it to Sent, writes the ledger entry naming the barcode and publishes `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` on `rwb.comms.events.v1`.
9. The proof result for a barcode arrives as a delivery-result fact of INT-15 through the integration service; a DELIVERED result sets `callback_date` and `delivery_status` DELIVERED, moves the notice to Delivered, writes the ledger entry and publishes `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1`, and rwb-case starts the NOTICE_PERIOD timer from the call-back date under R-LIT-07.
10. A REFUSED or UNDELIVERABLE result sets Unserved with that delivery status, writes the decision record under R-LIT-09, writes the ledger entry, publishes `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` with the result, and asks rwb-case for the transfer of the case to its owner's queue with reason NOTICE_UNSERVED and for MSG-P6-008.
11. A notice whose decision record cannot be written does not proceed: the state is unchanged, the notice is not written to the file, the run record shows MSG-P7-003 and an incident is raised under R-UNI-39.
12. A litigation officer reads the notice with `GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}`, and SCR-18 shows the state, the sent date, the barcode, the call-back date and the proof result; the ledger timeline on SCR-04 shows each entry with its conduct check result.
13. A repeat of the POST with the same Idempotency-Key returns the first notice with status 201, and a GET for a notice outside the caller's scope answers 404 with MSG-P4-003.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | WIN returns Refused or Undeliverable | Notice Unserved; case to the owner's queue with the reason | MSG-P6-008 | AC3 |
| X2 | An open X1 or X2 deviation has the contact stop on | Notice held; case to the deviation owner | MSG-P6-001 | legacy AC4 (RWB-ITG-E2021-ITG) |
| X3 | Consent for the postal channel is withdrawn | A statutory notice is still sent | None | legacy AC5 (RWB-ITG-E2021-ITG) |
| X4 | No proof 7 days after sending | Notice Unserved; notice period not started | MSG-P6-008 | AC6 |
| X5 | A legal hold is on the case | Notice held; nothing sent | MSG-P3-004 | AC7 |
| X6 | The template of an approved notice is withdrawn before dispatch | Notice held | MSG-P6-003 | AC8 |
| X7 | The decision log write fails for a held or unserved notice | Notice unchanged; retried on the next run; incident raised | MSG-P7-003 | AC9 |
| X8 | POST repeated with the same Idempotency-Key | The first notice is returned | None | AC10 |
| X9 | GET for a notice outside the caller's scope | Refused | MSG-P4-003 | AC11 |
| X10 | POST with no notice type | Refused | MSG-GEN-001 | AC12 |

X2 and X3 remain exception paths of the legacy key; their criteria are end-to-end and are owned by `RWB-ITG-E2021-ITG`. This story still raises the two outcomes in its own code, because the conduct check that produces them is the one built here (see AC9 for the X2 fact reaching the check).

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P6-E2021-CON, the two prior rwb-comms app stories and the platform contract libraries. The approval, the case read, the contact stop, the ACE facts and the WIN file are contract fakes from the first run |
| Negotiable | The proof window, the statutory notice type list, the eligible states, the delivery-result codes and the hold reasons are data rows and parameters; the story fixes the conduct order and the state path |
| Valuable | Every letter carries a conduct result, the notice state follows the proof and not the print, and the notice period starts only from a call-back date |
| Estimable | Two endpoints, one conduct-check service, one workflow with three activities and a proof-window step, one Schedule and one outbox path |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests, as the app slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Each criterion in section 7 runs as one automated test against the contract fakes, and the end-to-end path is proven by `RWB-ITG-E2021-ITG` |

The eight criteria above are the legacy criteria of RWB-E2-021 that the rwb-comms service itself satisfies, copied line for line with the origin tag on each scenario and one mock line added where the criterion names a fact of another owner. Legacy AC1 (dispatch), AC2 (proof back), AC4 (contact stop blocks the letter) and AC5 (consent withdrawn does not stop a statutory notice) are not copied: they are end-to-end journeys and belong to `RWB-ITG-E2021-ITG`, which also carries their wording, including the phrase "does not writ notice" of legacy AC4 exactly as the legacy story writes it. The paths in the criteria are the paths of the operations as the legacy names them; the base of this service is `/api/recovery/comms/v1` (DP-13).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every letter is checked before it is written to the WIN file, and the result is on the ledger entry | REQ-OCC-005; FEAT-OCC-05 |
| BR2 | A contact stop from X1 or X2 holds the notice and routes the case to the deviation owner | R-LIT-05; CTL-16 |
| BR3 | A legal hold stops every outbound action | R-UNI-20 |
| BR4 | Withdrawn consent removes the channel from the contact plan, and statutory notices continue | R-UNI-10; REQ-OCC-006; CTL-16 |
| BR5 | The notice period starts from the delivery date on the proof | R-LIT-07; CTL-15 |
| BR6 | A refused, returned or undeliverable letter records the result and queues an alternate service method | R-LIT-09 |
| BR7 | No proof inside the proof window marks the notice unserved, and the notice period does not start | R-LIT-08 |
| BR8 | A withdrawn template holds the notice | R-LIT-04 |
| BR9 | A held or unserved result that cannot be written to the decision log does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR10 | Which notice types are statutory is a list held as reference data | Principle 1; LOV-NOTICE |
| BR11 | The notice, its dispatch file reference and its proof dates are `rwb_comms` rows; no other service reads them and this service reads no other service's table (DP-01) | Architecture v5 slide 17; DP-01 |
| BR12 | The dispatch and delivery facts are written to the outbox in the same transaction as the state change and relayed with the CloudEvents envelope; the case, the reporting read model and the ledger follow from the events and not from a call made for them (DP-09) | Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43 notes; DP-09 |
| BR13 | The 16:00 run and the proof-window step are a Temporal Schedule and a workflow in this service; no Quartz row, no shared job table and no batch table is read (DP-10) | Architecture v5 slide 44 (JOB-10, JOB-11); DP-10 |
| BR14 | Every cross-service call is one hop with a 2 s budget, and a missing answer never decides an allow or a pass of the conduct check (DP-11) | ADR-020; DP-11 |
| BR15 | The eligible states, the proof window, the statutory notice types and the delivery-result codes are reference data of rwb-case read with the version in force; no value is written in code (DP-07) | FSD P6 A2.5 BR-P6-005; TSD P6 T3.2; DP-07 |
| BR16 | The ledger entry is rwb-source-data's and is written through its contract; the decision record is written through the local library; the case status, the transfer and the NOTICE_PERIOD timer are rwb-case's, driven by the facts this story sends (DP-03, DP-18) | R-PREC default ruling; DP-03; DP-18 |
| BR17 | The case status moves of the legacy story are P3's: this story holds the notice and sends the facts; R-DEV-01 and R-UNI-20 are applied by rwb-case on the DELIVERY_FAILED and PROOF_WINDOW_EXPIRED facts | R-DEV-01; R-UNI-20; TSD P6 T4 |
| BR18 | Alternate and substituted service methods are out of scope: R-LIT-10 and R-LIT-11 are Epic 5, and this story only records the unserved outcome and the reason | R-LIT-10; R-LIT-11; legacy section 19 |
| BR19 | The letter body and the addressee stay in rwb-document and rwb-source-data; the dispatch file and every event carry a document reference, a barcode and dates, never a name, an address or an account number | Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43 notes; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Generated | The D7.1 approval of rwb-decision is granted | The approval answer names the notice and the approved template version | Approved |
| Approved | The 16:00 run reaches the notice and the conduct check passes | No legal hold, no open X1 or X2 contact stop, the template version is still Approved, and the consent gate is passed or the notice type is statutory | Sent (after the WIN acknowledgement names the barcode and the sent date) |
| Approved | The 16:00 run reaches the notice and the conduct check blocks | Hold reason CONTACT_STOP_X1, LEGAL_HOLD, TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN or the pending-proof reason | Held |
| Held | The hold is lifted and the next run passes the check | The blocking fact is cleared through its owner (rwb-case for the hold, rwb-deviation for the stop, rwb-comms for the template version) | Approved, and then Sent on the same run |
| Sent | A proof result DELIVERED arrives for the barcode | The call-back date is present | Delivered (the NOTICE_PERIOD timer is rwb-case's, started from the call-back date under R-LIT-07) |
| Sent | A proof result REFUSED or UNDELIVERABLE arrives | The result is one of the two | Unserved (delivery status set, R-LIT-09, DELIVERY_FAILED to rwb-case) |
| Sent | The 16:00 run finds no proof inside the proof window | The sent date is past the 7-day window of R-LIT-08 | Unserved with delivery status PENDING and no notice period timer |

The gates on the Approved to Sent edge are the four checks of the conduct order in section 4, step 5, applied with the reference data listed in BR15. The NOTICE_PERIOD timer, the case status and the queue transfer are not state of this service: they are rwb-case's, started or applied on the facts this story publishes and sends (BR16, BR17). A held notice keeps its Approved state in the sense of the eligible-state parameter and is excluded by its hold reason, so a rerun never writes it to a second file for the same business date.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Litigation CRUA in the matrix of TSD P6 T6.1: requests a notice (right C), reads it with its dispatch and proof (right R) |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel | Litigation RA in TSD P6 T6.1: reads the notice and approves the template version that the conduct check reads (rights R and A) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Litigation R in TSD P6 T6.1: reads the notice and the proof of the case |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Litigation R in TSD P6 T6.1: reads the notices of the team's cases |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Litigation R in TSD P6 T6.1: reads the notices and operates the run through the Schedules and the run view; the run and the rerun are deployed by RWB-P6-E2021-OPS |
| rwb-comms service identity | Runs the Schedule and the workflow, reads its own `rwb_comms` rows, writes the notice state and the dispatch fields, and writes the outbox rows (DP-02) |
| Decision-record library identity | Writes the local decision record for a held or an unserved notice and relays it on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03) |

The legacy story also names RW-ENFORCE (Litigation CRU in T6.1), RW-CONDUCT and RW-HEADLIT; their rights are read from the same matrix and are not restated here. The matrix of TSD P6 T6.1 is the only source used for the letters above.

The authorise contract of rwb-access (DP-08) is not in this story's pattern set: the capability area and the right of each operation are declared in RWB-P6-E2021-CON and enforced at gateway-bff, which asks rwb-access, so no P4 dependency is declared here. The scope test of AC11 then needs a case-scope fact inside this service, and no dependency in this story provides one: the scope source and the shape of the local guard are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1092; ASM-2040).

| Standard column | notice | version, updated_at, updated_by | Write, for the optimistic lock of the workflow step |

The dispatch file reference is `notice.dispatch_file_id` (DF-LEG-033), which points at the outbound item of rwb-integration (P2) and never at a row of `rwb_integration`; `dispatch_attempts` counts the times the notice was selected for a file. The indexes are `ix_notice_barcode` on `notice (barcode)`, `ix_notice_sent_date` on `notice (sent_date, state)` for the proof-window step and `ix_notice_case_id` on `notice (case_id)` for the case read; the legacy index `ix_notice_state_sent` is replaced by `ix_notice_sent_date`, because the window step filters on the sent date and the state together. The migration is one per-service Flyway step in `rwb_comms` (DP-15). No personal data is written to `rwb_comms`: no name, no address, no identity number and no account number is a column of `notice`, and the addressee is resolved in rwb-source-data and rwb-document at the moment the letter is produced. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-comms (P6); base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`. The shapes are those fixed in RWB-P6-E2021-CON; this story implements them and adds no path.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/notices` | API-P6-001: generate a notice from the approved template and return it, 201 with the Notice | Litigation, right C, scope applied | Idempotency-Key header, kept 24 hours |
| GET | `/notices/{noticeId}` | API-P6-002: read a notice with its dispatch and its proof of delivery, 200 with the Notice | Litigation, right R, scope applied | Not applicable |

Errors: 401 no session; 403 the role lacks the Litigation right (MSG-P4-002); 404 the case or the notice is absent or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 409 the template is not approved (MSG-P6-005) or a notice of this type is already in progress (MSG-P3-005); 422 a field fails validation (MSG-GEN-001); 503 the decision was not recorded (MSG-P7-003). The Notice body carries `id`, `caseId`, `documentId`, `noticeType`, `sentDate`, `barcode`, `callbackDate`, `deliveryStatus` and `sentType` as the legacy story names them, and the exact response field list and types are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1094; ASM-2042).

Request: NoticeRequest with `noticeType` required, `partyId` defaulting to the borrower and `language` defaulting to TH, as the legacy story states and as RWB-P6-E1052-CON fixes it.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | reference-data read of LOV-NOTICE, LOV-DELIVERY, LOV-SENT-TYPE, the statutory notice type list and the proof window | P3 rwb-case, on RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The four checks of the conduct order and the result-code mapping; read with the version in force (DP-07) |
| POST | the D7.1 demand and recall approval of RWB-P7-E2014-CON | P7 rwb-decision | The approval answer that moves the notice to Approved; this story reads the answer and never approves |
| GET | case read of RWB-P6-E2021-CON for the case facts of the conduct check and the scope test | P3 rwb-case | `legal_hold`, owner and queue for the scope test; faked. The scope source and the shape of this read are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1092; ASM-2040) |
| GET | active contact stops of RWB-P6-E2021-CON | S8 rwb-deviation | The open X1 and X2 contact stops of the case; faked |
| POST | the case facts this story sends: DELIVERY_FAILED, PROOF_WINDOW_EXPIRED and the queue transfer with NOTICE_UNSERVED | P3 rwb-case | The case move and the NOTICE_PERIOD timer, which are rwb-case's (BR17) |
| POST | the interaction ledger write of RWB-P6-E2021-CON | P1 rwb-source-data | The ledger entry with channel, summary, conduct check and barcode (DP-18) |
| POST | the dispatch file and the proof-result read of rwb-integration | P2 rwb-integration | INT-14 out and the INT-15 delivery results; faked. The operation names, the columns and the acknowledgement are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1089; ASM-2037) |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retried once with jitter and a breaker per downstream. No row reads a table and no row reads a `v_ace_*` view: the ACE proof rows and the contact points reach this service through the owner's contract (DP-05, DP-18).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` (EV-14) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 | caseId | notice ID, case ID, notice type, business date, dispatch file reference, barcode, sent date, sent type, conduct check result |
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` (EV-15) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 | caseId | notice ID, case ID, barcode, result DELIVERED, REFUSED or UNDELIVERABLE, delivery status, call-back date |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 | caseId | decision code D7.1, rule ID (R-LIT-04, R-LIT-05, R-LIT-08, R-LIT-09, R-UNI-20), notice ID, decided at, record reference, business date |

All three are written to the outbox in the same transaction as the state change and relayed with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope by the outbox relay of the platform (DP-09). `NoticeDelivered` is published for the Delivered, the Refused and the Undeliverable outcome, as the legacy story states; the consumers are rwb-case, rwb-litigation, rwb-guarantee and the reporting read model, as the event catalogue names them.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | What this story does with it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` (EV-06) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | Takes note of the case and the deviation code so the next 16:00 run holds the notices of that case when the deviation carries the contact stop; deduped through the inbox |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` (EV-07) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | Takes note that the stop is cleared so a held notice is eligible again; deduped through the inbox |
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` (EV-05) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | Takes note of a case that closes or moves so the run skips it and the held notices of a closed case are left as they are; deduped through the inbox |

None of the three is a decision input on its own: the conduct check reads the live facts of its owner at the moment it runs, and the events only keep the local picture current between runs, which is what protects the loop when an event arrives after a run has started. The consumers are not a second source of truth and no event carries personal data.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| NoticeDispatchWorkflow | Workflow, one run per business date, workflow ID from the business date and the run kind | `rwb-comms` | Runs the proof-window step, selects the eligible notices, runs the conduct check for each, hands the file to integration and waits for the acknowledgement and the proof results on a durable timer |
| generateLetter | Activity, in rwb-document | `rwb-document` | Produces the letter from the approved template version when the notice does not hold a document yet |
| decisionApproval | Child workflow, in rwb-decision | `rwb-decision` | The D7.1 approval of a notice; the workflow waits for the answer and never approves on its own |
| deliverFile | Activity, in rwb-integration | `rwb-integration` | Writes the notices of the run to the WIN dispatch file (INT-14) and returns the file reference and the acknowledgement |
| conductCheck | Activity, in rwb-comms | `rwb-comms` | The four checks of section 4, step 5, returning passed or blocked with the reason and the rule ID |
| recordDecision | Activity, in rwb-comms through the library | `rwb-comms` | Writes the local decision record and its outbox row; a failure fails the step and the notice does not proceed |

The workflow input is the business date, the run kind and the page cursor; it carries no notice body, no addressee and no personal data. The waiting for a proof result is a durable timer inside the workflow and not a Schedule.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Name | Cron | Overlap policy | Catch-up | Registers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The JOB-10 notice dispatch run | 16:00 on every business day | SKIP | The window the workflow kit fixes | Starts NoticeDispatchWorkflow on task queue `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery` with the business date |

The Schedule is a Temporal Schedule of this service through RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (DP-10); it is not a Quartz row and not a row of a shared job table. The bank Airflow opens the WIN file window and the handoff from the window to this Schedule is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1095; ASM-2043).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| notice | P6 (rwb_comms) | The notice, its dispatch fields and its proof dates; the state machine of section 9 |
| template | P6 (rwb_comms) | The template version the conduct check reads; written by RWB-P6-E1046-APP and RWB-P6-E1052-APP |
| merge_field | P6 (rwb_comms) | The merge catalogue; read only here |
| decision record (local) | P6 rows in `rwb_comms`, written through the P7 library | The held and unserved decision entries of the conduct check (DP-03) |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_comms` | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects (DP-09) |

Not owned and never read: `recovery_case`, `task` and `timer` (P3), `deviation` (S8), `decision_log_entry` (P7), `document` (P5), `interaction` (P1), `outbound_item` and `interface_config` (P2). The letter body, the addressee, the ledger, the case state and the timer are reached through the contracts of their owners, and no foreign key crosses a service boundary (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Documented answers used by this story |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms`, modules `dispatch` and `notices`, Java packages `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms.dispatch` and `...comms.notices`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/comms/v1` | none |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 applies here as a prohibition with one exception of direction: this service reads no `v_ace_*` view and no ACE row, and the proof rows that the legacy story reads from `v_ace_pod` reach it as the INT-15 delivery results through rwb-integration and the owner's contract. That is the reading of ASM-2037, and it is why RWB-P1-E1066-CON is not in the contract dependencies of this story: if the proof facts have to be read from P1 instead, one C row is added and the proof step is a P1 contract read.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| NoticeController | Controller | `POST /cases/{caseId}/notices` and `GET /notices/{noticeId}` with validation, the Idempotency-Key and the problem mapping for 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 |
| NoticeService | Service | Creates and reads the notice, orders the state moves and refuses a read outside the caller's scope |
| ConductCheckService | Service | The four checks in order — legal hold, contact stop, template state, consent with the statutory rule — returning passed or blocked with the reason and the rule ID |
| DispatchSelection | Service | Selects the eligible notices of the business date, pages them, and writes `dispatch_file_id` and `dispatch_attempts` in the same transaction |
| WinFileClient | Adapter | The file contract of rwb-integration: the dispatch file of the business date, its acknowledgement and the proof results |
| CaseFactClient | Adapter | The case read, the scope read and the case facts this story sends, on the rwb-case contract |
| DeviationClient | Adapter | The active contact stops of the case on the rwb-deviation contract |
| LedgerClient | Adapter | The interaction ledger write on the rwb-source-data contract |
| ProofWindowStep | Workflow step | The first step of the run: a Sent notice past the 7-day window becomes Unserved with delivery status PENDING under R-LIT-08 |
| DeliveryResultHandler | Service | Applies DELIVERED, REFUSED and UNDELIVERABLE: the notice state, the dates, the decision record, the ledger entry and the events |
| ReferenceCatalog | Service | Reads LOV-NOTICE, LOV-DELIVERY, LOV-SENT-TYPE, the statutory notice type list and the proof window with the version in force; no value in code |
| NoticeDispatchWorkflowImpl | Workflow | The run, its ordering, its durable timer for the proof and its compensation when a step fails |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `notice`, `template`, `merge_field`, the local decision record and the library objects, all in schema `rwb_comms`; reads no other schema.
- Migration in this story: `V2021_1__notice_dispatch.sql` adds `sent_type`, `dispatch_file_id` and `dispatch_attempts` when the baseline of RWB-P6-E1052-APP does not hold them yet, the hold reason value set as a check constraint on `hold_reason`, and the three indexes of section 11. No column carries a name, an address or an account number.
- No row of `template` or `merge_field` is written here: the template catalogue is RWB-P6-E1046-APP and the template approval is RWB-P6-E1052-APP.

**Configuration and reference data**

- `rwb.comms.dispatch.eligible-states` = APPROVED, as data.
- The proof window: 7 days under R-LIT-08, read from reference data with its version; the arithmetic on the sent date is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1091; ASM-2039).
- The statutory notice type list: DEMAND, RECALL, STATUTORY_SALE_NOTICE and GUARANTOR_NOTICE as LOV-NOTICE holds them, with the statutory flag as data owned by the business; this story reads it (BR10).
- The delivery-result code map from the WIN result codes to LOV-DELIVERY as data, not as code, with the mapping agreed under RWB-P6-E1055-APP.
- The feature switch `rwb.comms.win-dispatch-loop`, read as a parameter: off means the run starts no dispatch and holds the notices with the pending-proof reason, never writes a file.
- The hold reason vocabulary is fixed by RWB-P6-E2021-CON: CONTACT_STOP_X1, LEGAL_HOLD, TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN and the pending reason.

**Build steps**

1. NoticeController and NoticeService over the two operations, the Idempotency-Key and the scope refusal; tests for AC10, AC11 and AC12.
2. CaseFactClient, DeviationClient and ReferenceCatalog with the four reads and their fakes; the conduct order of section 4, step 5; a test per branch.
3. ConductCheckService with the four checks and the reason and rule returned; tests for AC7 and AC8 and the statutory branch of the consent gate.
4. recordDecision and the fail-closed path: a failed record leaves the notice unchanged and the run record shows MSG-P7-003; test for AC9 and TC-E2-021-14.
5. ProofWindowStep in the workflow, with the boundary of the 6-day and the 7-day notice; test for AC6.
6. WinFileClient and DispatchSelection: the file of the business date, the acknowledgement that sets the barcode and the sent date, and `dispatch_attempts`; test for the dispatch path behind the fake.
7. DeliveryResultHandler for the three results with the decision record, the ledger entry and the two events; test for AC3.
8. NoticeDispatchWorkflowImpl with the ordering, the durable proof timer and the rerun rule, and the Schedule of 16:00; the contract-fake run of the whole loop before the real services are live.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.comms.win-dispatch-loop`, read as a parameter; off refuses to dispatch closed and holds the notices.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P6-E2021-CON stay green, and a SIT week shows every notice of the 16:00 run with a conduct result, every notice of the file with a barcode and a sent date, every unserved notice with its decision entry and no NOTICE_PERIOD timer asked for it, and no letter of the file carrying a name or an address.

| MSG-P6-001 | A contact stop blocks the letter | Contact with this customer is stopped for {reason}. |
| MSG-P3-004 | A legal hold or deviation blocks the letter | This case is on hold for {deviation}. The prescription date is still {date}. |
| MSG-P6-003 | The template was withdrawn before dispatch | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-P6-004 | WIN acknowledged the notice | {notice} was sent for registered mail on {date}. |
| MSG-P6-005 | The template of the notice is not approved | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1096; ASM-2044) |
| MSG-P3-005 | A notice of this type is already in progress for the case | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1096; ASM-2044) |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the Litigation right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The notice is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Notice type missing | Enter {field}. |

MSG-P6-008, MSG-P6-001, MSG-P3-004, MSG-P6-003, MSG-P6-004, MSG-P7-003, MSG-P4-003 and MSG-GEN-001 are copied unchanged from the legacy story. MSG-P4-002 is the platform refusal message of the authorise contract. MSG-P6-005 and MSG-P3-005 are named by the legacy contract of the POST and their text is not given by the legacy story or the P6 extracts, so the placeholder stands until their owner publishes it.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the proof window, the statutory notice type list, the eligible states, the hold reason vocabulary and the delivery-result code map are data rows and parameters read with the version in force.
- No personal data in events, logs, workflow inputs, tests or prompts: notice IDs, case IDs, barcodes, dates, result codes and business dates only. The notice body and the addressee stay in rwb-document and rwb-source-data, and the dispatch file carries a document reference and a barcode.
- No read of another service's tables and no `v_ace_*` read of this service: the case hold, the contact stop, the consent, the ledger and the proof rows arrive on the owner's contract (DP-01, DP-05, DP-18).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the owner's views: the ACE proof rows of the legacy story are the INT-15 delivery results of rwb-integration here, and no SQL of this service names an ACE view.
- The conduct check runs inside the same transaction that selects the notice for the file, so a stop raised after the check reaches the next run and never a second file.
- A held or unserved result that cannot be recorded does not proceed: the state is unchanged, the file is not written and the incident is raised (R-UNI-39).
- Every outbound event and the decision record are written to the outbox in the same transaction as the state change and carry IDs and facts only (DP-09, DP-03).
- One base, one topic, one queue: `/api/recovery/comms/v1`, `rwb.comms.events.v1` and `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery`; no story in this key declares another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- One hop and 2 s on every call; a timeout never passes the conduct check and never returns a notice as clean (DP-11).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-021 for rwb-source-data. The legacy dispatch loop read the borrower's postal contact point and its consent, ran the conduct check, wrote the letter into the INT-14 file, read the INT-15 proof back and appended the outcome to the interaction ledger as one mutable entry, in one deployable and one transaction. Under D-RCV-60 that loop is rwb-comms' and rwb-case's: the notice, the template, the conduct check, the WIN file, the proof read, the notice state and the notice-period timer belong to P6, P3, P2 and P1's own proof-of-delivery story. This story answers the one fact the conduct check needs from this service — the postal contact point and its consent, as rows of data product DP02 on the record read of `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` (DP-05, DP-13) — and it owns the two ledger facts of the letter: the dispatch entry with its conduct check and its barcode, and the fold that makes one barcode read as its latest outcome, on `POST` and `GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions` of the interaction ledger this service owns (DP-01, DP-18). No WIN file, no conduct check, no notice state, no decision record, no notice-period timer, no `NoticeDispatched` or `NoticeDelivered` event and no `notice` or `template` table is delivered here. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **dispatch loop of rwb-comms (service actor)**, I want **the postal contact point of a person and its consent to come back as data-product rows of rwb-source-data that carry the contact key, the type, the consent status, the verified date and the data date and never the address, and the dispatched letter to be appended to this service's interaction ledger with its conduct check and its barcode so that the barcode reads as its latest proof outcome, in order and never rewritten**.

This is the rwb-source-data slice of legacy RWB-E2-021. The legacy story read the contact point, ran the conduct check, wrote the file, read the proof and appended the outcome in one step. Under D-RCV-60 that step has four owners, and this story delivers the fact it consumes and the ledger it owns, and nothing else:

- **the contact-and-consent branch of the record read** on base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`: `GET /data-products/DP02/records?caseId=` answers, for the case's parties, one row per contact point — `contactKey` (the token of `v_ace_contact`), `contactType`, `consentStatus` resolved from `contact_point_ext` as data (GIVEN, WITHDRAWN or UNKNOWN), `verifiedAt` and the page's `dataAsOf` (the DP02 business date). It answers no address, no name and no identity number: the contact point is a reference and is never copied;
- **the letter append** on `POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions` of the ledger this service owns, with the members the loop holds: `eventCode` `LETTER`, `channel` `POSTAL`, `conductCheck` (PASSED or BLOCKED), `deliveryStatus` from `LOV-SEND-STATUS`, `externalRef` (the barcode) and `occurredAt`, written through the writer, its `case_seq` allocator, its `Idempotency-Key` rule and its append-only trigger;
- **the case ledger read** `GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions`, which answers every entry as stored and, where an entry carries an `externalRef`, the governing status of that barcode — the `deliveryStatus` of the entry with the latest `occurredAt` for the same `sourceRef` and `externalRef` — so a caller reading the dispatch entry sees the outcome the proof entry later recorded;
- **no loop**: no WIN file, no INT-14 or INT-15 handling, no conduct check implementation, no notice state, no notice-period timer, no event, no decision record and no `notice`, `template` or `merge_field` table. The `v_ace_pod` read and the proof entry itself are RWB-P1-E1055-APP's, and the proof window, the transfer and the case timer are RWB-P6-E2021-APP's and RWB-P3-E2021-APP's.

It owns no legacy acceptance criterion. AC1 to AC12 of RWB-E2-021 are proved in RWB-P6-E2021-APP (AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC10, AC12), RWB-P3-E2021-APP (AC2, AC3, AC6, AC7), RWB-P7-E2021-APP (AC9), RWB-P4-E2021-APP (AC11) and RWB-ITG-E2021-ITG (the cross-service proof of the whole key). This story is written with new criteria tagged D-RCV-60, each one testing only the read, the append and the fold above.

The shapes the loop consumes are declared by RWB-P6-E2021-CON: it names the rwb-source-data answers of the loop — the postal contact point with its consent fact, and the interaction ledger write with its channel, its summary and its conduct check — and fakes them. This story implements them and publishes its fragment with the service baseline.

##### 2. Business rationale

A notice period counted from the print date can be challenged, and a letter sent while a contact stop or a legal hold is in force is a conduct breach. Legacy RWB-E2-021 exists to make one thing true: the day a letter is served is the day the proof says it was served, and the conduct check that allowed it is on the record (REQ-OCC-003, REQ-OCC-005; CTL-15, CTL-16).

Two facts carry that promise in the target, and both are this service's. The first is the consent of the postal contact point: the Workbench holds the decision about a contact point (`contact_point_ext`) and ACE holds the contact point itself (`v_ace_contact`), and the conduct check must read the pair without either being copied into the other (D-RCV-35 U1; ADR-010; REQ-OCC-006). The second is the ledger entry of the letter: one ordered, append-only history per case, written in the same transaction as the action it records (REQ-ILG-010; NFR-070). The letter that says "sent on 2026-12-15, barcode RR223344556TH" and the proof that says "undeliverable on 2026-12-21" are two facts about one barcode, and a history that overwrites the first with the second cannot answer the question a conduct review asks — what was known, and when.

**What D-RCV-60 changes.** Not one business value. The notice `N-0101`, the case `RC-2026-000321`, the notice type `DEMAND`, the template `DEMAND-SSME` `TH` version 1, the barcode `RR223344556TH`, the sent date 2026-12-15, the call-back date 2026-12-18, the proof window of 7 days and the rule ids R-LIT-05, R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 and R-LIT-09 keep their meaning and their values. What changes is where the fact is read and who owns it: a read of DP02 over `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, one hop and 2 s (DP-05, DP-11, DP-13), and an append to this service's own ledger instead of an in-process call into the monolith (DP-01, DP-18).

**One read, one append, no copy.** No table of this service holds the address, the name or an identity value of the borrower, and none is answered, logged or put in an event (§12.3, §17). The contact point is a token, the barcode is a reference, and the entry carries codes and dates.

##### 3. Preconditions

Nothing in this list is a build dependency: this story is Day 1 and builds against the published baseline, the published view contract, the ledger writer and the RWB-P6-E2021-CON fake, which is why its build dependency list is empty.

- The service baseline of rwb-source-data is published: schema `rwb_source_data`, the per-service Flyway sequence at its baseline version, `data_product` with DP01 to DP14 and `data_product_load` with its unique key on `(product_code, business_date)` (DP-01, DP-15; the baseline of RWB-P1-E1001-APP and RWB-P1-E1015-APP, adopted as published artefacts).
- The record read `GET /data-products/{productCode}/records` of API-P1-010 is published with its DP01 and DP04 branches (RWB-P1-E1016-APP, RWB-P1-E2010-APP), and this story adds the DP02 contact-and-consent row type to it.
- `contact_point_ext` exists at the baseline with `contact_key`, `contact_type` (PHONE, EMAIL, ADDRESS), `consent_given`, `consent_at`, `verified_at`, `failed_count`, `source` and the standard record columns (TSD P1 T3.5, DF-EXT-013 to DF-EXT-019).
- The view contract of RWB-P1-E1069-APP is published and `recovery.v_ace_contact` is readable through the `rwb_source_data` login, which holds SELECT on the 30 `recovery.v_ace_*` views and no privilege on `public` (DP-02, DP-05; TSD P1 T3.3, T3.4, T6.3; ADR-010).
- The interaction ledger of RWB-P1-E1066-APP is published: the append, the case read, the `Interaction` and `InteractionRequest` schemas, the `case_seq` allocator, the unique key on `idempotency_key`, the append-only trigger `tr_interaction_append_only`, and the four ledger columns this story writes, `conduct_check` (DF-INT-012), `delivery_status` (DF-INT-028), `external_ref` (DF-INT-029) and `source_ref` (DF-INT-017), which are already in the service schema (Physical Schema v6). No migration is needed.
- RWB-P6-E2021-CON is published with its fake: the postal contact point with its consent fact and the ledger write with its channel, its summary and its conduct check. This story builds against that contract and its fake and against no second draft of it (C).
- RWB-P1-E1055-APP records the proof entry of a pod row through the same ledger writer; this story reads that entry and folds it by barcode and writes no proof row of its own.
- The reference lists this story validates against — `LOV-LEDGER-EVENT`, `LOV-CONDUCT`, `LOV-SEND-STATUS` and the contact types — reach this service through the reference-data client library of DP-07; the Work Package lists no reference-data contract for this story, so the lists are read with a fixture until it is published (ASM-3533).
- The caller is the dispatch loop of rwb-comms with a workload identity token; officers read the outcome on SCR-18 and SCR-04 through gateway-bff and never call this service directly (DP-19).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline; RWB-P6-E2021-CON tags its baseline when its tests pass. This story starts on Day 1 and waits for nothing it builds.
- The shape of the DP02 contact row, the consent vocabulary and the two operation paths are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2181; ASM-3527; GAP-2182; ASM-3528).

##### 4. Flow

1. The dispatch loop of rwb-comms starts its 16:00 run for business date D and selects the notices whose conduct check it has still to take (the run, its Schedule and its workflow are RWB-P6-E2021-APP's; DP-10).
2. Before the check of notice `N-0101` of case `RC-2026-000321`, the loop calls `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/DP02/records?caseId=RC-2026-000321`, one hop with a 2 s budget (DP-11; C RWB-P6-E2021-CON).
3. The DP02 branch reads `recovery.v_ace_contact` for the case's persons, left joins `contact_point_ext` on `contact_key` and orders the rows by `contact_key` (DP-05).
4. `ConsentStatusResolver` resolves `consentStatus` from the extension row — `consent_given` true is GIVEN, `consent_given` false with a `consent_at` is WITHDRAWN, no row or no `consent_at` is UNKNOWN — and from no value of its own (ASM-3527).
5. `FreshnessStampReader` answers `dataAsOf` and `productStatus` from the DP02 row of `data_product_load` for D; the rows carry no contact value, no address, no name and no identity number (AC1, AC7; BR2).
6. The loop takes its four conduct-check branches on its own facts and on this answer, and decides PASSED or BLOCKED with the reason and the rule id; this story takes no part in that decision and makes no statutory decision (RWB-P6-E2021-APP; R-LIT-05, R-UNI-10).
7. For a letter it dispatches, the loop appends `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/RC-2026-000321/interactions` with `eventCode` `LETTER`, `channel` `POSTAL`, `conductCheck` `PASSED`, `deliveryStatus` `SENT`, `externalRef` `RR223344556TH`, the occurred time 2026-12-15, a summary naming notice type `DEMAND` and barcode `RR223344556TH`, and an `Idempotency-Key`; the append runs the validation, the case check, the `case_seq` allocator and the insert of the writer (AC2; DP-18).
8. A letter the check held is appended the same way with `conductCheck` `BLOCKED`, the reason `CONTACT_STOP_X1` in its summary, no `deliveryStatus` and no `externalRef` (AC3).
9. The writer answers 201 with the stored entry, so what the loop holds is what was stored (AC2).
10. When the proof of `RR223344556TH` arrives, RWB-P1-E1055-APP records the proof entry of that barcode through the same writer; this story appends nothing and rewrites none of the dispatch entry (AC4).
11. A read of the case ledger answers both entries as stored and, on each, `barcodeStatus` as the governing status of the barcode — the entry with the latest `occurredAt` for the same `externalRef` — so the pair reads as one outcome while both rows stay in the history (AC4).
12. A repeat of the same `Idempotency-Key` with the same body answers the stored entry and the same `caseSeq` with no second insert (AC5); a `LETTER` entry with no `conductCheck`, or with a `deliveryStatus` and no `externalRef`, is refused with 422 and MSG-GEN-001 naming the field, and nothing is written (AC6).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | `productCode` is not a product this service serves, or `caseId` is missing or malformed | 400 with the problem body naming the field; no row is answered | MSG-GEN-004 | §12.1 |
| X2 | A caller without the right calls the read or the append | 403, and the refusal is logged without a key value | MSG-P4-002 | §10 |
| X3 | A view, `contact_point_ext` or the stamp does not answer inside 5 s, or answers an error | 503 with a problem body naming the ACE database; no row is guessed from a cache | MSG-GEN-006 | §12.1 |
| X4 | A `LETTER` entry arrives with no `conductCheck` | 422 with the problem body naming the field; no entry is written | MSG-GEN-001 | AC6 |
| X5 | A `LETTER` entry arrives with a `deliveryStatus` and no `externalRef` | 422 with the problem body naming the field; no entry is written | MSG-GEN-001 | AC6 |
| X6 | The case of the append does not exist or is outside the caller's scope | 404 as the case check of the writer answers it, passed on unchanged; no entry is written | MSG-P4-003 | §12.1 |
| X7 | The same `Idempotency-Key` is replayed with a different body | 409 on the rule of RWB-P1-E1066-CON; the stored entry is not overwritten | MSG-GEN-004 | AC5 |
| X8 | The ledger cannot be written | The transaction rolls back, the caller receives 503, and no entry exists | MSG-P1-022 | §12.1 |
| X9 | `external_ref` is longer than the 60 characters of DF-INT-029 | 422 naming the field; the barcode is never truncated | MSG-GEN-001 | AC6 |

X1 and X3 are the read paths this story adds; X4 to X6 and X9 are the validation of the append; X7 and X8 are the refusals and the rollback the writer already ships and this story inherits unchanged. The conduct check, the contact stop, the legal hold, the withdrawn template, the proof window, the transfer and the decision record are the exception paths of RWB-P6-E2021-APP, RWB-P3-E2021-APP and RWB-P7-E2021-APP and are not carried here.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P6-E2021-CON and its fake, on the published baseline, the view contract of RWB-P1-E1069-APP, the record read of RWB-P1-E1016-APP and the writer of RWB-P1-E1066-APP; needs no live rwb-comms, rwb-case or WIN to start |
| Negotiable | The class split, the fold rule and the summary wording are the squad's choice behind the contract; the contact token, the consent vocabulary, the two operation paths and the barcode are fixed |
| Valuable | The conduct check runs on a consent fact that is read and not copied, and the letter and its proof are two facts in one ordered history that no later write can rewrite |
| Estimable | One row type on an existing read, one extended append with its read-back, one resolver and one fold |
| Small | Finished inside one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is one call against the contract fake, the ACE contact fixture, the extension fixture and the ledger fixture, with no second service and no file |
| Day 1 | The story has no build dependency; it is reachable on the first day of wave 2 and its tests run against the published baseline and the fake |
