##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the letters C, R, U, D and A, the capability areas, the roles, the scopes, the notice types, the masking rows and the matrix and mask versions are data rows; the Java code holds no letter, area, role, notice type or version literal (BR-P4-004, BR-P4-005).
- No personal data in logs, events, tests, workflow history or prompts: the access entry carries the actor reference, the notice and case references, the field IDs and a masked marker. Workflow history is not used because this story starts no workflow.
- No addressee name or address in an entry, an event or a log: the value is read through `rwb-source-data`'s contract by whoever displays it, this service answers the field ID and the masked flag only, and a test scans the entry text for any part of the synthetic address.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or a `v_ace_*` view of this service; this story reads no ACE view at all, and the notice reaches it only through RWB-P6-E2021-CON.
- No business rule executed here: the conduct check, the contact stop, the legal hold, the template state, the consent rule, the proof window and the notice state are `rwb-comms`'s; this story answers the right, the scope and the mask, and a change of any business rule changes no line of it.
- No read of another service's tables and no cross-schema read (DP-01): `notice`, `template`, `recovery_case`, `contact_point`, `interaction` and `decision_log_entry` are never queried here.
- An answer is never served without its entry, and the answer and the entry commit in one transaction (R-UNI-39).
- The cache fails closed: an unparseable or mixed policy event leaves the versions in force, and a missing policy row is a refusal, never a default allow.
- The authorise path has no off switch, because a notice that cannot be authorised must not be requested or read; the legacy dispatch flag stays `rwb-comms`'s.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-021 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN), a litigation officer (RW-LITOFF) and an enforcement owner (RW-ENFORCE)**, I want **the legal hold placed on the case and lifted again with a reason and returned as a flag on the case read, every dispatch and every proof of delivery written as a ledger entry and shown on the case timeline from the facts `rwb-comms` publishes, and one `NOTICE_UNSERVED` task raised to the case owner when a letter is refused, undeliverable or unproven inside its window**, so that **no letter leaves a case that is on hold, the case itself shows what was posted and what came back, and an undelivered letter always has an owner and an action**.

This is the case slice of legacy RWB-E2-021 (`Split (rework)`, secondary; it owns no legacy criterion — GAP-2217; ASM-3649):

- Service `rwb-case`, schema `rwb_case`, REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1` with event names `rwb.case.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`.
- It builds three things only: the hold switch that `rwb-comms` reads before writing a letter (`POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold`, `legalHold` on `GET /cases/{caseId}`); the letter facts on the case timeline (`GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline`, fed from the interaction ledger through the `rwb-source-data` contract, DP-18); and the one `NOTICE_UNSERVED` task and queue transfer that follow an unserved letter.
- It builds no notice, no template, no merge field, no conduct-check rule, no WIN file, no proof capture and no notice-period timer. The notice, its states and the conduct check are `rwb-comms`'s (RWB-P6-E2021-APP, built against RWB-P6-E2021-CON and its fake); the notice-period clock from the delivery date is RWB-P3-E5002-APP; the deviation contact stop is `rwb-deviation`'s; the ledger record is `rwb-source-data`'s; the central decision ledger is `rwb-decision`'s.

##### 2. Business rationale

A notice period counted from a print date can be challenged, and a letter that leaves a case on legal hold is a conduct breach. In the split, one service must own the two facts the rest of the loop depends on — whether a letter may leave this case at all, and what happened to it afterwards on the case record. Keeping them in `rwb-case` means `rwb-comms` needs one published read and no table, and it means the officer sees the dispatch and the proof on the same timeline as every other case event, without a cross-service join. It serves REQ-OCC-005 (a conduct result on every outbound contact), REQ-ILG-010 (dispatch results in the ledger) and the FSD P6 measure "notices with proof of delivery, 100 percent".

##### 3. Preconditions

- The case exists in `rwb_case` with its owner, queue and status; the ACE business keys (`account_key`, `person_key`) are on the case and are read as keys only, never as a foreign key.
- RWB-P6-E2021-CON is published; this story is built against that contract and its fake, never against a live `rwb-comms` (DP-11, DP-09).
- The `rwb-source-data` ledger contract is published and its fake is available; the case holds no `interaction` table (DP-18; GAP-2221; ASM-3653).
- The platform decision-record library (DP-03), the outbox and inbox library (DP-09), the workflow kit (DP-10) and the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) are in place from wave 0 (ASM-3655).
- The requester holds a role with Case record U to place or lift a hold and Case record R to read the case and its timeline (TSD P3 T6.1). Scope is applied to every read.
- The hold reason list, the `SERVICE_LEVEL` row for the task due date and the LOV values used here are in force as reference data of `rwb-case` (DP-07; GAP-2218 and GAP-2222).

##### 4. Flow

1. Litigation officer opens the case: `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` returns the case with `legalHold`, `status`, `status_before_hold`, the owner, the queue and the next action; the gateway composes it with the other tabs over the DP-19 route.
2. Case owner or litigation officer places a legal hold: `POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold`. The service writes one decision record (R-UNI-20), keeps the status it held in `status_before_hold`, moves the case to `ON_HOLD`, and inserts `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` in the outbox of the same transaction.
3. `rwb-comms` reads the case through the published case contract before each letter; the `legalHold` flag is the case-side input of its conduct check. This story provides the flag only; the check, its held reason and the file are P6's.
4. `rwb-comms` publishes `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` with the notice, the barcode and its conduct result. The rwb-case inbox applies it: one ledger entry through the `rwb-source-data` contract (channel `LETTER`, conduct check `PASSED`, barcode in the summary). The case status does not move.
5. `rwb-comms` publishes `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` with `DELIVERED` and the call-back date. The inbox writes the delivery ledger entry dated on the call-back date; the notice period from that date is started by RWB-P3-E5002-APP, not here.
6. The same event with `REFUSED`, `UNDELIVERABLE` or `PENDING` (an unproven letter): the inbox writes the ledger entry, one decision record (decision code `D7.1`, rule R-LIT-09), places the case in its owner's queue with the reason `NOTICE_UNSERVED`, raises one `OPEN` task `NOTICE_UNSERVED` to the case owner, sets the next action and inserts `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1` in the outbox.
7. The officer reads the letter facts on SCR-04: `GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline` merges the case's own events with the ledger entries of the case, in time order. Lifting the hold on the case returns it to the status in `status_before_hold` (R-UNI-21) and publishes `CaseStateChanged`.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The decision-record or ledger write fails for a dispatch, proof or unserved fact | Nothing is applied; the event stays unacknowledged and is retried; an incident is raised under R-UNI-39 | MSG-P7-003 | AC8 |
| X2 | The same P6 event is delivered twice (relay retry, replay) | The inbox deduplicates on event ID and business date; one ledger entry, one task, one decision record, one event | None | AC6 |
| X3 | The case is outside the caller's scope | Refused; no ledger entry is returned | MSG-P4-003 | AC9 |
| X4 | A hold is placed on a case already `ON_HOLD`, or lifted where there is none | Refused; nothing changes | MSG-P3-005 | AC2 |
| X5 | The `rwb-source-data` ledger contract is down or answers beyond 2 s | The fact is not applied and the event is retried by the inbox; no task is raised before its ledger entry exists | MSG-P7-003 | AC8 |
| X6 | The P6 read that the case record composes times out or the breaker is open | The case answer still returns `legalHold` and the case facts; the notice panel shows a retry state and no fact is fabricated | None | AC3 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P6-E2021-CON and its fake; no in-lane story is waited for (Day 1) |
| Negotiable | The hold reason list, the task code, the owner role and the task due date are data, not code |
| Valuable | Two facts the loop cannot work without — may this letter leave, and what happened to it — sit on the case |
| Estimable | One operation, one flag, one timeline query, one consumer, one activity and one screen fragment |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Every criterion runs against the P6, ledger and gateway fakes with synthetic notices |

    Then the case is "IN_PROGRESS" with legalHold false

    When rwb-case consumes NoticeDispatched for "N-0101"
    Then one ledger entry exists for case "RC-2026-000321" with channel "LETTER", conduct check "PASSED" and a summary naming "RR223344556TH"
    Then GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/RC-2026-000321/timeline returns that entry with the barcode
    Then the case status stays "IN_PROGRESS"
    Then no name, address or notice text appears in the event, the ledger summary or the log line

  Scenario: AC4 A proof of delivery is on the case timeline on the call-back date (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given notice "N-0101" is "Sent" on 2026-12-15
    When the rwb-comms contract mock returns NoticeDelivered for "N-0101" with result "DELIVERED" and call-back date 2026-12-18
    Then the timeline shows a delivery entry on 2026-12-18 with delivery status "DELIVERED"
    Then the case status stays "IN_PROGRESS"
    Then rwb-case starts no timer of its own for the notice period

  Scenario: AC5 An unserved letter raises one task and one queue transfer (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given notice "N-0101" is "Sent" on 2026-12-15
    When the rwb-comms contract mock returns NoticeDelivered for "N-0101" with result "UNDELIVERABLE"
    Then exactly one task "NOTICE_UNSERVED" is "OPEN" on case "RC-2026-000321" with the case owner role
    Then the task due date is read from the SERVICE_LEVEL reference row in force
    Then the case is placed in its owner's queue with the reason "NOTICE_UNSERVED"
    Then one decision record exists with decision code "D7.1" and rule "R-LIT-09"
    Then the case next action names "NOTICE_UNSERVED" and the owner sees MSG-P6-008 for notice type "DEMAND" and result "UNDELIVERABLE"
    Then the CaseTransferred event carries the case number and the reason "NOTICE_UNSERVED"

  Scenario: AC6 A repeated result changes nothing (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the unserved result of "N-0101" for business date 2026-12-21 was applied
    When the same event is delivered again with the same event ID
    Then case "RC-2026-000321" has one "NOTICE_UNSERVED" task, one ledger entry and one decision record
    Then no second CaseTransferred event is published

  Scenario: AC7 An unproven letter is unserved and a letter inside its window is not (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given notice "N-0102" for case "RC-2026-000654" is "Sent" with sent date 2026-12-15
    And notice "N-0103" for case "RC-2026-000655" is "Sent" with sent date 2026-12-16
    When the rwb-comms contract mock returns NoticeDelivered for "N-0102" with result "PENDING" on 2026-12-22
    Then case "RC-2026-000654" has the "NOTICE_UNSERVED" task and one decision record with rule "R-LIT-08"
    Then case "RC-2026-000655" has no "NOTICE_UNSERVED" task
    Then no notice-period entry appears on either timeline

  Scenario: AC8 Nothing is applied when the decision cannot be recorded (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-source-data ledger mock is unavailable
    When NoticeDelivered for "N-0101" with result "UNDELIVERABLE" arrives
    Then case "RC-2026-000321" is unchanged: no task, no queue move and no next action
    Then the consumer record shows MSG-P7-003 and the event stays unacknowledged for retry
    Then one incident is raised under rule "R-UNI-39"

  Scenario: AC9 The timeline of a case outside the caller's scope (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RC-2026-000321" is outside the scope of "LIT-0101"
    When "LIT-0101" sends GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/RC-2026-000321/timeline
    Then the response is status 404 with MSG-P4-003
    Then no ledger entry is returned
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A legal hold on a case stops every outbound action on it and every letter for it | R-UNI-20; REQ-OCC-005 |
| BR2 | Lifting the hold returns the case to the status it held when the hold was placed, and the move is recorded | R-UNI-21 |
| BR3 | The case exposes the hold as one flag on its published read; no other service reads the case tables for it | R-PREC (Arch v5 catalogue); DP-01 |
| BR4 | Every dispatch and every proof of delivery is one ledger entry for the case, with its channel, conduct result and delivery status | REQ-ILG-010; FEAT-ILG-07 |
| BR5 | A refused, returned or undeliverable letter records the result and moves the case to its owner with an action, under R-LIT-09 | R-LIT-09; CTL-15 |
| BR6 | No notice-period clock is started from a print date or from an unserved letter; the clock is the E5002 story's and starts from the delivery date | R-LIT-07; R-LIT-08 |
| BR7 | A held or unserved result that cannot be written to the decision record does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR8 | Which hold reasons, task codes and due dates apply is data held as reference data, never code | Principle 1; LOV-ROLE; GAP-2218 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Any active status | Legal hold placed | R-UNI-20; the case is not `CLOSED` | `ON_HOLD`, with the previous status kept in `status_before_hold` |
| `ON_HOLD` | Legal hold lifted | R-UNI-21 | The status in `status_before_hold` |
| `ON_HOLD` | Legal hold placed or lifted twice | The case is already in the target state | No change; refused with MSG-P3-005 |

The notice state (`Approved`, `Sent`, `Delivered`, `Unserved`, `Held`) is `rwb-comms`'s and is never held in `rwb_case`: this story writes the case status, the task, the next action and the ledger reference only. Task status moves `OPEN` to `DONE` or `CANCELED` through the existing task operation of RWB-P3-E2035.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Places and lifts a hold (Case record U); reads the case and the timeline; works the `NOTICE_UNSERVED` task |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Places and lifts a hold (Case record U); reads the dispatch and the proof on the timeline |
| RW-ENFORCE, enforcement owner | Places and lifts a hold; reads the timeline |
| RW-TEAMMGR, RW-LEGAL, RW-HEADLIT, RW-HEADNPA | Read the case, the hold and the timeline (Case record R) |
| RW-CONDUCT, Conduct and QA officer | Reads the timeline entries with their conduct result (Case record R) |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Applies the P6 facts, the task, the queue transfer and the outbox rows |

No approval level from the delegation of authority applies in this story; approval of the notice itself is RWB-P3-E2014-APP and RWB-P6-E2021-APP.

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |

| DF-CAS-001 | recovery_case | id | Read |
| DF-CAS-002 | recovery_case | case_no | Read |
| DF-CAS-005 | recovery_case | status | Write |
| DF-CAS-010 | recovery_case | queue_id | Write |
| DF-CAS-020 | recovery_case | legal_hold | Read, write |
| DF-CAS-055 | recovery_case | status_before_hold | Write |

| DF-REF-147 to DF-REF-158 | parameter_value, reference_row | The `SERVICE_LEVEL` row and the hold reason list | Read, through the reference-data contract (DP-07) |

Personal data: none is copied into this service's letter facts. The ledger summary carries the case number, the notice type, the barcode and the result code, never a name, an address or notice text.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

All on base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, owner `rwb-case` (P3).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/legal-hold` | Place or lift the legal hold on the case: body `hold` (boolean, required), `reason` (string, required on place) | Case record U |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}` | The case read, extended with `legalHold`, `statusBeforeHold`, the next action and the case's queue | Case record R, scope applied |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/timeline` | The case timeline: the case's own events merged with the ledger entries of the case, in time order, paged | Case record R, scope applied |
| GET | `/me/tasks` | The caller's tasks, which include `NOTICE_UNSERVED` (existing operation, unchanged) | Case record R |
| PATCH | `/tasks/{taskId}` | Closes or cancels the `NOTICE_UNSERVED` task with an outcome code (existing operation, unchanged) | Case record U |

Errors: 401 no session; 403 role without Case record U (MSG-P4-002); 404 case not found or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 409 the case is already in the target state (MSG-P3-005); 422 a field fails (MSG-GEN-001); 503 the decision record cannot be written (MSG-P7-003). `POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold` is idempotent by the case ID and the target state.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2220; ASM-3652) | The interaction write and the case-read operations of the `rwb-source-data` contract | rwb-source-data (P1) | Writing the dispatch, the proof and the unserved entry; reading the case's ledger entries for the timeline (DP-18) | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2220; ASM-3652) | The keep-safe cases read of the `rwb-comms` contract, fixed by RWB-P6-E2021-CON | rwb-comms (P6) | Nothing is called for the letter facts: they arrive as events; the notice read is used only to show the notice type on the timeline, built against the contract fake (DP-11) | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2220; ASM-3652) | The decision-record write and seal operations of the `rwb-decision` contract, owned by `rwb-decision` on base `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | rwb-decision (P7) | The central seal of the decision record written locally (DP-03) | One hop, 2 s |

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` (EV-05) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | caseId | caseId, caseNo, fromState, toState, eventCode (`LEGAL_HOLD_PLACED`, `LEGAL_HOLD_LIFTED`), ruleId (R-UNI-20, R-UNI-21), packageVersion |
| `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1` (EV-04) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | caseId | caseId, caseNo, queueId, ownerRef, reasonCode (`NOTICE_UNSERVED`), ruleId (R-LIT-09), noticeRef |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 owns the type and the ledger; every service writes its own record | caseId | decision record reference, decision code (`D7.1` where a rule decided the notice outcome), ruleId, packageVersion, business date |

All three are written to the outbox in the same transaction as the change and relayed with the CloudEvents envelope (DP-09). No payload carries a name, an address, a notice text or a barcode beyond the notice reference.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` (EV-14) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 | Inbox: one ledger entry with channel `LETTER`, the conduct result, the barcode in the summary and the sent date |
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` (EV-15) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 | Inbox: the delivery entry (`DELIVERED`, with the call-back date), or the unserved entry with the task, the decision record and the queue transfer (`REFUSED`, `UNDELIVERABLE`, `PENDING`) |

Both are consumed with the inbox object and the idempotency key `noticeId` + business date, so a relay retry or a replay applies nothing twice (DP-09).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow | Workflow (parent, one per case, workflow ID `case-{caseId}`) | `rwb-case` | Receives the signal that carries one P6 letter fact and runs the apply step; holds no Quartz trigger (DP-10) |
| ApplyNoticeFact | Activity (the one activity this story adds) | `rwb-case` | Validates the fact, calls the ledger contract, and writes the case status or the task, the decision record and the outbox rows in one transaction |

No other workflow and no other activity is added. The letter fact is applied by an event-started workflow, not a schedule, and the workflow reads no clock and calls no rule engine.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The legacy behaviour sat in `JOB-10` (daily 16:00), which is `rwb-comms`'s; on the case side the fact arrives as an event and the workflow is started by it (DP-10). `rwb-case` owns no schedule for the letter loop.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| recovery_case | P3 (`rwb_case`) | Writes `status`, `status_before_hold`, `legal_hold`, `queue_id` and the next-action columns; no new column and no new table |
| task | P3 (`rwb_case`) | The `NOTICE_UNSERVED` task row: `task_code`, `status`, `owner_role`, `due_at`, `outcome_code` |
| assignment | P3 (`rwb_case`) | The queue placement of the case after an unserved letter, with its reason |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_case` | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects (DP-09) |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in `rwb_case` | The local hash-linked decision record of the change (DP-03) |

`interaction` is **not** owned here: the ledger belongs to `rwb-source-data` under DP-18 and the R-PREC default ruling, so there is no `interaction` table in `rwb_case`, no view over it and no foreign key to it (GAP-2221; ASM-3653). `notice`, `template` and `merge_field` are `rwb_comms`'s and are neither read nor written. `decision_log_entry` is `rwb-decision`'s and is reached only through its contract.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-comms WireMock and event stub | RWB-P6-E2021-CON | A dispatch for "N-0101" with barcode "RR223344556TH", sent date 2026-12-15 and conduct `PASSED`; a delivery on 2026-12-18; `UNDELIVERABLE`; `PENDING` on 2026-12-22; a duplicate delivery with the same event ID; a delayed answer beyond 2 s |
| rwb-source-data WireMock | The P1 ledger contract | A successful write with a returned reference; a case ledger with two entries; an unavailable answer for AC8 |
| rwb-decision WireMock | The P7 decision-record contract | A successful seal; an unavailable answer for AC8 |
| gateway-bff composite route (WireMock) | The DP-19 route of SCR-04 and the case record view | The merged case and timeline answers of AC1, AC3 and AC4, including the retry state of X6 |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 3 provided, 3 consumed groups | The hold operation, the case read and the timeline provided; the ledger, the notice read and the decision-record seal consumed; one hop, 2 s, breaker |
| Kafka | 3 published, 2 consumed | `rwb.case.events.v1` (two types), `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and the two `rwb.comms` facts consumed with the inbox |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 1 activity | CaseWorkflow per case; ApplyNoticeFact |
| File | None | No file is read or written by this story; the WIN file is `rwb-comms`'s |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `letterloop`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.letterloop`; front-end fragment `src/modules/recovery/case/NoticeTimeline.tsx`, embedded in SCR-04 and the case record view.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The platform edges this table adds belong to wave-0 CON stories that are already in place and are not repeated as H rows in the metadata table, which carries only the contract dependency of this legacy key (ASM-3655). DP-07 resolves to the reference-data contract of `rwb-case` built in wave 1 (RWB-P3-E1043-CON), so no new dependency is added. DP-05 resolves to one ACE read: the account number shown with the letter facts is read from `v_ace_account` by `case_account.account_key`, inside `rwb_case`, with no copy and no foreign key.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CaseHoldController | Controller | `POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold` and the `legalHold` field of the case read |
| CaseHoldService | Service | Applies R-UNI-20 and R-UNI-21, keeps `status_before_hold`, refuses a repeat with MSG-P3-005, writes the decision record |
| NoticeFactConsumer | Inbox consumer | Consumes EV-14 and EV-15, deduplicates by event ID and business date, signals CaseWorkflow |
| NoticeFactValidator | Service | Required fields of the fact (noticeRef, caseRef, result, date), builds the idempotency key, refuses an unreadable fact with MSG-GEN-001 |
| ApplyNoticeFact | Activity | The one transaction: ledger entry, decision record, task, next action, queue placement, outbox rows |
| LedgerClient | Client | The `rwb-source-data` contract with one hop, 2 s and a breaker; no retry of its own (the workflow owns retry) |
| NoticeTaskFactory | Service | The `NOTICE_UNSERVED` task row: owner role from `LOV-ROLE`, due date from the `SERVICE_LEVEL` row (DP-07) |
| CaseTimelineQuery | Query | Merges the case's own events with the ledger entries of the case for `GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline` (DP-18) |
| DecisionRecordWriter | Library adapter | Local hash-linked record with the rule ID and package version, in the same transaction (DP-03) |
| CaseEventPublisher | Outbox adapter | Inserts CaseStateChanged, CaseTransferred and DecisionRecorded in the outbox (DP-09) |
| NoticeTimeline | React component | The SCR-04 fragment: dispatch, delivery and unserved entries with their conduct result, read only |

**Database and migrations**

- No new table and no new column: `legal_hold`, `status_before_hold`, the next-action columns, `task` and `assignment` already exist in `rwb_case`.
- One index only: `ix_task_case_code ON task (case_id, task_code)` so the consumer finds an existing `NOTICE_UNSERVED` task without a scan (idempotency).
- Migration `V2021_1__notice_task_index.sql` runs in the service's own migration sequence with a parameterised schema name; no other schema is touched and no foreign key into `rwb_comms` or `rwb_source_data` is created.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The `SERVICE_LEVEL` reference row that gives the `NOTICE_UNSERVED` task its due date. The row code and its value are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2218; ASM-3650).
- The hold reason list and its codes, as a reference table of `rwb-case`; the list is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2222; ASM-3654).
- No feature flag of its own: the legacy flag `rwb.comms.win-dispatch-loop` is P6's, and a key for this slice is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2219; ASM-3651).
- The 2 s timeout and the single hop are the platform rule of DP-11, not a configurable value of this story.

**Build steps**

1. CaseHoldController and CaseHoldService with R-UNI-20 and R-UNI-21, the repeat refusal and the decision record; tests for AC1 and AC2.
2. NoticeFactConsumer with the inbox, the dedupe key and the signal; tests for AC6.
3. NoticeFactValidator and the ledger write in `ApplyNoticeFact`; tests for AC3, AC4 and AC8.
4. NoticeTaskFactory, the next action and the queue placement with reason `NOTICE_UNSERVED`; tests for AC5 and AC7.
5. CaseTimelineQuery and the `NoticeTimeline` fragment against the gateway route fake; tests for AC3, AC4 and AC9.
6. Decision-record and outbox wiring in the one transaction, with the incident on failure; tests for AC8.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the RWB-P6-E2021-CON contract tests stay green, every move and every unserved letter carries a decision record with its rule ID and package version, and no letter fact is stored in `rwb_case` outside the ledger reference.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-005 | A hold is placed on a case already `ON_HOLD`, or lifted where there is none | This case cannot move to {state} from {current}. |
| MSG-P3-004 | A legal hold or deviation blocks the letter (read by the P6 check from this flag) | This case is on hold for {deviation}. The prescription date is still {date}. |
| MSG-P6-008 | A notice is refused, undeliverable or has no proof in the window | {notice} for case {case} was not served: {reason}. The case is in your queue to choose another service method. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of the fact or the request is missing | Enter {field}. |

| Screen | What the user sees and does |

| SCR-04 Case timeline | One row per event and per ledger entry of the case, in time order: the dispatch with its conduct result and barcode, the delivery with the call-back date, the unserved result with its reason. Read only; loaded on click over the DP-19 composite route |
| Case record view | The hold banner with `legalHold`, the status `ON_HOLD`, the next action `NOTICE_UNSERVED` and its due date; the hold is placed and lifted from here with a reason |
| SCR-18 Notice approval (P6) | Unchanged; the notice states it shows are `rwb-comms`'s. This story adds the hold banner that tells the officer why a letter cannot go |

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the hold reason list, the task code, the owner role and the task due date are data rows with a version.
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs, ledger summaries or logs: the case number, the notice reference, the barcode and the result code only.
- No read of another service's tables: the ledger goes through `rwb-source-data`, the letter facts through `rwb-comms`, the decision record through its own library and seal. ACE data only through `v_ace_*` views, read only.
- The ledger write, the decision record and the outbox row commit in one transaction, so a stop or a hold raised after a fact is applied reaches the next one and no half state exists.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-021 for rwb-decision; the D7.1 decision record of the letter dispatch loop in the central decision ledger, and its two reads. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **conduct and QA officer (RW-CONDUCT), a litigation officer (RW-LITOFF) and an internal auditor (RW-AUDIT)**, I want **every decision of the letter dispatch loop that a rule decides — the conduct-check hold under R-LIT-04 or R-LIT-05, and the delivery result under R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08 or R-LIT-09 — appended once as a D7.1 entry of the central decision ledger of `rwb-decision`, carrying the notice reference, the notice type, the case reference, the rule id with its rule version, the final call HELD, DELIVERED or UNSERVED, the hold reason or the delivery status and the notice period start date where one applies, and carrying no WIN payload, no address and no customer value**, so that **a held, a served or an unserved letter can be explained years later from the rule and the version that decided it, and a record that cannot be appended stops the decision instead of disappearing from the history**.

Inside `rwb-decision` this is the decision-record slice of legacy RWB-E2-021:

- Service `rwb-decision`, schema `rwb_decision`, REST base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, topic `rwb.decision.events.v1` with event names `rwb.decision.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the decision-record path of DP-03.
- One deliverable and nothing else: the appender of the D7.1 dispatch record and the two decision-log reads. The loop's decisions are taken by the service that owns the notice; this service appends each record once, chained and append only, and serves `GET /decision-log/{entryId}` for one entry and `GET /decision-log` for the entries of a case in a date range.
- What stays with `rwb-comms` (P6, RWB-P6-E2021-CON, RWB-P6-E2021-APP and RWB-P6-E2021-OPS): the notice, its states, the conduct check of the four gates, the template check and the notice hold, the dispatch selection, the INT-14 WIN dispatch file, the INT-15 proof capture, the result-code map, the dispatch messages and the JOB-10 Schedule at 16:00. None of it is rebuilt here.
- What stays with `rwb-case` (P3): the legal hold flag of the case, the case state, the queue transfer with reason NOTICE_UNSERVED and the NOTICE_PERIOD timer started from the call-back date. What stays with `rwb-source-data` (P1, DP-18) is the interaction ledger entry, and with `rwb-integration` (P2) the WIN interface configuration, the file window and the file runs. This story writes none of them.
- The record and the decision are one pair under DP-03: the owning service writes the record through the decision-record path inside the transaction of the decision it records, and this service appends it to the ledger in one idempotent transaction of its own, so a record with no decision behind it is never appended and a decision whose record cannot be appended does not proceed (BR13).
- The service appends and exposes; it selects no notice, runs no conduct check, writes no hold reason, dispatches nothing, captures no proof, moves no case and starts no timer (BR9). The database login is the per-service login of DP-02, and the story refers to "the rwb-decision login (DP-02)".

The legacy behaviour carried into the decision service is unchanged in meaning: one entry for every decision of the loop and no exception, the rule id and the rule version on the entry, the hold reason of a held letter and the result of an unserved letter on the entry, a delivery that starts the notice period and a proof window that does not, a record that can never be altered, and no held or unserved outcome standing without its record (legacy RWB-E2-021 AC3, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9 and BR2, BR5, BR6, BR7, BR8, BR9).

Which fields of the record this service consumes, and where the notice reference, the hold reason or the delivery status and the notice period start date sit in the entry, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1276; ASM-2246). The rule version label carried by the letter rules is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1276; ASM-2247), and so is the enforcement of the right and scope behind the two reads (GAP-1276; ASM-2249).

##### 2. Business rationale

A notice period counted from the print date can be challenged, and a letter sent while a contact stop or a legal hold is in force is a conduct breach. The WIN dispatch loop proves the serving of the letter: a conduct check before the file, a barcode from the acknowledgement, a call-back date from the proof, and an unserved outcome when the proof never comes. That loop is only defensible if each decision inside it is recorded with the rule and the version that made it: which rule held the letter and why, which rule served it and from which date, which rule closed it as unserved and on which result. The monolith wrote that record with the notice row in one process and one schema, so the two could not drift apart. In the target the notice is `rwb-comms`'s and the evidence of every decision is collected in `rwb-decision` (Architecture v5 slides 14, 27, 28 and 41), so the record of the loop has to be appended there, chained, unchangeable, and readable by the officer who follows the letter and by the auditor who later asks why the case was transferred.

Under Architecture v5 the central decision ledger, the rule registry and the approvals are `rwb-decision` (slides 14 and 41); every service writes its decision record through the local library in the same transaction as the change it records and publishes `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (slide 20, "every service"; slide 42, event 08); `rwb-decision` collects the records into the ledger within 5 minutes and seals it daily in write-once storage (slide 28); and the ledger is read through the decision-log operations (slide 14). The realignment changes the mechanism, not the business rule:

1. The in-process `DecisionLogApi.write` call of the monolith becomes the decision-record path of DP-03: the record is written where the decision commits and is appended here on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, with the append-only rule and the hash chain the FSD already carries (FEAT-DRI-01, FEAT-DRI-03).
2. The entry is not a copy of the notice and not a copy of the file record: it names the notice, the notice type, the case, the rule and version, the final call, the hold reason or the delivery status and the notice period start date, and it names no address, no barcode payload, no WIN field and no customer value (BR5, BR13).
3. The final call and the five rule ids are data rows and registry rows, never literals in the code (BR8); the conduct check, the template check, the hold, the dispatch file, the proof read, the timer and the ledger entry stay with their owners, and this story reads none of their tables (DP-01, DP-18).
4. The one decision-log read of the monolith becomes two operations on the service's own base (DP-13): the entries of a case in a date range, and one entry with its rule version and its chain fields.
5. The data-lake copy of the log is retired with the data lake (DP-17); the ingest of `rwb.decision-record.v1` is continuous Kafka (JOB-13) and the daily chain check JOB-14 at 02:00 covers these entries like any other.
6. The record is append only and hash chained, so a decision that fails leaves no entry, a repeated record leaves one entry, and a break in the chain is a reportable event rather than a silent edit.

This story meets REQ-OCC-003, REQ-OCC-005, REQ-OCC-006 and REQ-ILG-010 on the record side: it proves which rule held a letter and why, that the notice period starts only from a proof, and that an unserved letter cannot reach the case without its entry. It carries control CTL-15 (the notice period starts from proof of delivery), CTL-16 (a contact stop blocks the contact) and the principle that no action proceeds unlogged (R-UNI-39).

##### 4. Flow

1. `rwb-comms` runs the JOB-10 letter loop of the business date on its own Temporal Schedule: the proof-window step first, then the conduct check of each eligible notice. The Schedule is `rwb-comms`'s and this story registers none (12.6).
2. A notice fails the check, or a proof result closes it: the owning service takes the decision with the rule that decided it, and in the same transaction writes its notice change, its outbox row and, through the decision-record path of DP-03, the D7.1 record with the final call, the rule id and version, the notice reference, the notice type, the case reference and the hold reason or the delivery status (RWB-P6-E2021-APP; Architecture v5 slide 28).
3. The record path publishes `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, keyed by the case ID, with the record reference, the decision code, the rule id, the rule version, the final call and the decision time (DP-09; slide 42, event 08).
4. `rwb-decision` `DispatchRecordListener` reads the fact into the inbox of DP-09, deduplicates by event ID and by the record reference (R-UNI-40), keeps the facts whose decision code is D7.1 and whose final call is HELD, DELIVERED or UNSERVED, and passes them to `DecisionLogAppendService`; every other decision code is the ledger baseline's general ingest.
5. `DecisionLogAppendService` checks the entry: the decision code D7.1 is a value of LOV-DECISION at the version in force; the final call is one of the three; the notice reference, the notice type and the case reference are present; the rule id carries a version, and the pair exists in the rule registry at the version in force; a held record carries a hold reason of the closed vocabulary and a delivery record carries a delivery status. A record that fails the check is refused with MSG-P7-009 naming the missing field and nothing is written (BR8, BR11).
6. `DecisionLogAppendService`, one transaction in `rwb_decision`: takes the next `chain_seq`, computes `prev_hash` from the last entry's `entry_hash` (64 zeros for the first), computes `entry_hash` as the SHA-256 of the entry's canonical form, writes the `decision_log_entry` row with `decided_at` from the record and the notice period start date where the record carries one, and writes the inbox row and the idempotency row of the record reference. A failed append changes nothing: no entry, no chain position and no inbox row (BR3, BR13).
7. A repeated fact with the same record reference returns the first entry's ID, adds one to the repeat count for R-UNI-40 and appends nothing (BR7). A held letter and its later delivery are two decisions and give two entries, chained in decision order (BR1).
8. A decision whose record cannot be appended does not proceed: the record path answers the owning service with MSG-P7-003, the notice stays Approved and is not written to the WIN file, no chain position is used and an incident is raised under R-UNI-39 (BR13).
9. A litigation officer, a conduct and QA officer or an internal audit reader reads one entry with `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}`, and the entries of a case in a date range with `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId=…&decision=D7.1&from=…&to=…`, one page at a time in `decidedAt` order with the total count of the range (BR10). A caller without the Decision log right is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002; a case outside the caller's scope is refused with 404 and MSG-P4-003, and no entry of that case is returned.
10. Nothing in this story moves a notice, a case, a timer or a record on the WIN side: the entry is written beside the decision and the readers of `rwb-comms`, `rwb-case` and the auditor's screen keep their own state (BR9). The daily chain check JOB-14 and the daily seal are the baseline's, not rebuilt here.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A held record carries a hold reason outside the closed vocabulary, or a delivery record carries no delivery status | The append is refused, nothing is written and no chain position is used | MSG-P7-009 | AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5 |
| X2 | The record carries a rule id with no rule version, or a pair absent from the registry at the version in force | The append is refused and the fact stays on the topic for redelivery | MSG-P7-009 | AC9 |
| X3 | The decision-log store is unavailable, or the chain position cannot be taken | The decision is not recorded: the record path answers MSG-P7-003, the notice stays Approved and is not written to the WIN file, no chain position is used and an incident is raised as in R-UNI-39 | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X4 | The same record is delivered again, or replayed from the topic | One entry exists; the inbox dedupe and the record reference both hold, and the repeat is counted for R-UNI-40 | None | AC7 |
| X5 | A passing dispatch arrives with no rule behind it, or a generation record with decision code D7.1 and rule R-LIT-03 | No entry is appended for the pass: this slice appends only a hold or a delivery result, and the generation entry is another story's | None | AC1 |
| X6 | The proof window expires for one notice of the run and not for the other | One entry is appended for the expired notice and no entry for the one inside its window | None | AC3 |
| X7 | The decision code is not a value of LOV-DECISION, or is not D7.1 | The fact is left to the ledger baseline's general ingest and this story appends nothing | None | AC1 |
| X8 | The caller holds no Decision log right, or asks for a case outside its scope | 403 with MSG-P4-002, or 404 with MSG-P4-003; no entry is returned | MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 | AC8 |
| X9 | The record carries an address, a WIN field or a customer value it should not carry | The append refuses the field at the schema check: the record path answers MSG-P7-003 and nothing is written, because an entry is not a copy of the file | MSG-P7-003 | AC2, AC8 |
| X10 | The reference list, the parameters or the rule registry cannot be read at the version in force | The append or the read is refused rather than assumed, and the fact is retried; no entry is written with an assumed code, final call or rule version | MSG-P7-003 | AC9 |

An entry is only ever appended beside the decision that caused it: the entry, its chain position, its inbox row and its idempotency row are written in one transaction, so a decision can never leave a half record and a record can never exist for a decision that was not taken (BR13).

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the loop contract RWB-P6-E2021-CON, the decision-record path of DP-03, the inbox library and the fakes; no conduct check, notice state, template check, file, proof read, timer or ledger entry is rebuilt here |
| Negotiable | The decision code, the final-call set, the hold reason and delivery status vocabulary, the payload field set, the parameter names and the message ids are data, registry rows or parameters of their owners; the story fixes only the entry, the append-only rule, the chain and the two reads |
| Valuable | Every held, served and unserved letter is explained by the rule and the version that decided it, and that explanation cannot be quietly changed |
| Estimable | One listener, one appender with the chain, one query controller with two operations, one index step and one fake set |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests; it is the decision-record slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Each of the nine criteria in section 7 runs as one automated test against the contract fakes, with a fixed business date and a fixed chain |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

No legacy acceptance criterion is owned verbatim by this story: `acs` is empty for RWB-E2-021, and every legacy criterion of the key acts on the notice, the WIN file or the proof — the notice state, the conduct check, the written file, the returned barcode and the case transfer — which belong to RWB-P6-E2021-APP, RWB-P6-E2021-CON, RWB-P6-E2021-OPS, `rwb-case` and RWB-ITG-E2021-ITG. The nine criteria below are new for the `rwb-decision` slice and test only the D7.1 record and its two reads; each keeps the legacy values of RWB-E2-021 and introduces no business value.

    Given the record under record reference "RR223344556TH-2026-12-21" was appended and the ledger returned its entry ID
    When the same record with the same record reference arrives again, and the topic is replayed from the first offset of the business date
    Then one entry exists for the record, the first entry ID is returned and the repeat count of R-UNI-40 is raised by one
    Then no second entry and no second chain position are written, and the chain is unchanged

  Scenario: AC8 The two reads return the entry and its chain and are scoped (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the entry of AC2 and the held entry of AC4 are stored for case "RC-2026-000321" on 2026-12-18 and 2026-12-14
    When the reader sends GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}
    Then the response is 200 with final call "DELIVERED", rule "R-LIT-07", the rule version in force, notice reference "N-0101", notice type "DEMAND", case reference "RC-2026-000321", the notice period start date 2026-12-18, decidedAt, prevHash and entryHash
    Then the response carries no notice state, no address, no customer name, no account number and no WIN payload
    When the reader sends GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId=RC-2026-000321&decision=D7.1&from=2026-12-14&to=2026-12-22&page=1
    Then the page holds the two entries in decidedAt order with a total of 2, and the delivered entry's prevHash equals the held entry's entryHash
    Given the rwb-access contract mock returns no Decision log right R for one caller and the scope of team "MTG-BKK" for the reader, against case "RC-2026-000654" in team "HP-NE"
    When each caller sends the read
    Then the responses are 403 with MSG-P4-002 and 404 with MSG-P4-003, and no entry is returned

  Scenario: AC9 A record without a rule version is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-comms contract mock returns a D7.1 record for notice "N-0101" with rule "R-LIT-09" and an empty rule version
    When the ledger consumes that record
    Then the append is refused with MSG-P7-009 naming "ruleVersion" and nothing is written
    Then no chain_seq is consumed and the fact stays on the topic for redelivery
    When the record is corrected to the rule version in force of "R-LIT-09"
    Then one entry is appended with both the rule id and the rule version
```

The nine criteria are new, and `acs` is empty for this story: no legacy criterion of RWB-E2-021 is owned verbatim here, because each of them acts on the notice, the WIN file or the proof and belongs to its own slice. The values are the legacy values — notices `N-0101`, `N-0102` and `N-0103`, cases `RC-2026-000321`, `RC-2026-000654` and `RC-2026-000655`, barcode `RR223344556TH`, call-back date `18122026` and the delivered date 2026-12-18, the business dates 2026-12-14, 2026-12-15, 2026-12-21 and 2026-12-22, decision code D7.1, rules `R-LIT-04`, `R-LIT-05`, `R-LIT-07`, `R-LIT-08`, `R-LIT-09` and `R-UNI-20`, hold reasons `CONTACT_STOP_X1`, `LEGAL_HOLD` and `TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN`, results `DELIVERED`, `UNDELIVERABLE` and `PENDING`, final calls `HELD`, `DELIVERED` and `UNSERVED`, notice type `DEMAND`, template `DEMAND-SSME`, and the messages MSG-P6-008, MSG-P6-001, MSG-P6-003, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P3-004 — and no new business value is introduced. The payload field set of the record, the placement of the notice reference and of the delivery facts, the rule version label, the message ids of this slice and a panel id for the record have no source and are carried in GAP-1276 with ASM-2246, ASM-2247 and ASM-2250. The `-ITG` copies of the test cases belong to RWB-ITG-E2021-ITG.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One entry per decision of the loop: a held letter, a delivered letter and an unserved letter each give one entry, and a held letter and its later delivery are two entries chained in decision order | Legacy RWB-E2-021 AC3, AC6, AC7, AC8; FSD P7 v3 A2.2; REQ-OCC-003 |
| BR2 | The entry carries decision code D7.1 and one of the final calls HELD, DELIVERED or UNSERVED, written through the decision-record path of DP-03; the decision code is read from LOV-DECISION at the version in force and is never a literal | Legacy RWB-E2-021 sections 4 and 18; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 and T3.2; BR-P7-002 |
| BR3 | Every entry is hash chained and append only: a `chain_seq`, a `prev_hash` equal to the previous entry's `entry_hash` (64 zeros for the first), an `entry_hash` equal to the SHA-256 of the canonical form, no UPDATE and no DELETE, and a correction as a new entry with `corrects_entry_id` | REQ-DRI-002, REQ-DRI-003; FSD P7 v3 AC-P7-001-01 and AC-ALT-P7-001-01; Architecture v5 slide 28 |
| BR4 | The entry names the notice reference, the notice type, the case reference, the rule id with its version, the final call, the hold reason or the delivery status and the notice period start date where one applies; it carries no address, no customer name, no account number, no WIN field and no file payload | Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 17; Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43 notes; §R7.2 s17 |
| BR5 | The rule id and the rule version are both on the entry and the pair exists in the rule registry at the version in force; a record with a rule id and no version is refused | FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-01 and A2.3; Drools design slide 16 (rule id and version in the record) |
| BR6 | One entry under a repeated record: the inbox dedupe and the record reference make a second entry impossible, and the repeat is counted for R-UNI-40 | FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-03; R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | The hold reason and the delivery status are validated against the closed vocabulary the loop contract fixes: `CONTACT_STOP_X1` under R-LIT-05, `LEGAL_HOLD` under R-UNI-20, `TEMPLATE_WITHDRAWN` under R-LIT-04, and `UNDELIVERABLE`, `REFUSED` and `PENDING` under R-LIT-09 and R-LIT-08; no value is written in code | RWB-P6-E2021-CON AC4; Routing Logic v4 rows R-LIT-04, R-LIT-05, R-LIT-08, R-LIT-09 |
| BR8 | The story appends and exposes; it selects no notice, runs no conduct check, writes no hold reason, dispatches no file, captures no proof, moves no case and starts no timer | Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; DP-01 |
| BR9 | The two reads declare the Decision log right R with the scope applied; a role without it is refused with MSG-P4-002 and a case outside the scope with MSG-P4-003 | TSD P7 v2 T-A.1, T6.1 and T6.2; REQ-DRI-012 |
| BR10 | A record that lacks its decision code, its final call, its notice reference or its rule version, or that carries a value outside its list, is refused with MSG-P7-009 and appends nothing; no entry is written from an assumed value | FSD P7 v3 AC-ALT-P7-002-01, AC-EXC-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-05 read on this slice |
| BR11 | A delivered record carries the notice period start date from the call-back date under R-LIT-07; the notice period, the timer and the end date stay with rwb-case and are never computed here | R-LIT-07; CTL-15; Routing Logic v4 row R-LIT-07 |
| BR12 | The entry, its chain position, its inbox row and its idempotency row commit in one transaction; a failed append leaves nothing, the fact is redelivered, and the decision that cannot be recorded does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; FSD P7 v3 A2.5; DP-03 |
| BR13 | The ingest of `rwb.decision-record.v1` is continuous Kafka and the entries reach the ledger inside the completeness target of Architecture v5 slide 28; the daily chain check and the seal are the baseline's, and the JOB-10 Schedule of the loop is rwb-comms's | Architecture v5 slides 28 and 44 (JOB-10, JOB-13, JOB-14); TSD P7 v2 T5.3; DP-10 |
| BR14 | The two reads are one hop from the gateway-bff composite route, the service reads no table of another service, and the notice, the case, the deviation, the timer and the ledger entry arrive as facts or stay with their owners | Architecture v5 slides 13 and 41; DP-01; DP-11; DP-18; DP-19 |

##### 9. State transitions

None for a notice, a case, a timer or a WIN file. The states below are the states of an entry of this story, and the entry has no state column of its own: it is appended and then immutable.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Absent | `DecisionRecorded` arrives with decision code D7.1 and final call HELD | The hold reason is in the closed vocabulary, the rule id carries a version present in the registry, and the chain head is known | Appended at the next `chain_seq` with its `prev_hash`, its `entry_hash`, its inbox row and its idempotency row in one transaction |
| Absent | `DecisionRecorded` arrives with decision code D7.1 and final call DELIVERED | The call-back date is present and the entry carries the notice period start date | Appended at the next `chain_seq`, as above |
| Absent | `DecisionRecorded` arrives with decision code D7.1 and final call UNSERVED | The delivery status is `UNDELIVERABLE`, `REFUSED` or `PENDING`, and no notice period start date is carried | Appended at the next `chain_seq`, as above |
| Absent | The record fails the check of BR10, or the store or the chain is unavailable | The record is refused, or the append cannot commit | Absent: MSG-P7-009 or MSG-P7-003, nothing written, no chain position used, the fact redelivered and the decision stopped |
| Absent | The run passes a notice with no rule fired | A pass is a conduct result and not a decision of a rule | Absent by design: no entry, and the conduct result stays on the ledger entry of rwb-source-data |
| Appended | The same record arrives again with the same record reference | The inbox or the idempotency key holds the entry | Unchanged: the first entry's ID is returned and the repeat is counted |
| Appended | A later decision of the same notice arrives | The notice is held and then delivered, or held and then unserved | A second entry is appended at the next `chain_seq`, chained to the first |
| Appended | A correction is taken | The correction names the entry it corrects | A new entry is appended with `corrects_entry_id`, and the corrected entry stays unchanged |
| Appended | An UPDATE or a DELETE is attempted, or the daily check and seal run | Any caller, including the schema owner | Unchanged: the statement is refused by the append-only rule, and the seal verifies the chain |

The notice stays in the state `rwb-comms` gives it (Approved, Held, Sent, Delivered or Unserved), the case state and the queue are `rwb-case`'s, and the NOTICE_PERIOD timer is `rwb-case`'s; this story changes none of them (BR8, BR11).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CONDUCT, conduct and QA officer | Reads the held and blocked entries of the cases in scope (Decision log R in TSD P7 v2 T6.1) and uses them for the conduct review |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer; RW-ENFORCE, enforcement owner | Reads the entries of the notices of the case in scope: the hold, the delivery and the unserved outcome with the rule and version |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel | Reads the entries that name a withdrawn template and the holds it caused |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit and RW-COMPLY, Compliance and PDPA officer | Reads one entry and the entries of a case in a date range, with the chain fields, and never a customer value (Decision log R, scope ALL) |
| Every role of TSD P7 v2 T6.1 | Holds R on the decision log and reads the entries of the cases in its scope |
| SY-DECLOG, decision record writer | Writes the D7.1 record inside the decision transaction at the producer and appends it to the ledger here; the append is the service identity's and not a person's |
| The `rwb-decision` service identity | Consumes the fact, reads its own `rwb_decision` rows, the rule registry and the reference lists, and appends the entry, its inbox row and its idempotency row (DP-02) |
| A role outside the matrix, or a case out of the caller's scope | Refused with MSG-P4-002, or 404 with MSG-P4-003 |
| No approval level from the delegation of authority applies | The approval of a notice is the D7.1 approval of another P7 story and RWB-P6-E2021-CON; this story reads no `delegation_limit` row and approves nothing |

The right and the scope behind the two reads are declared on the operations and enforced at gateway-bff (DP-19), which asks `rwb-access`; this story adds no guard of its own, holds no role, scope or delegation row, and makes no authorise call (GAP-1276; ASM-2249). The database login is per service (DP-02) and this story refers to "the rwb-decision login (DP-02)".

No row of `notice`, `recovery_case`, `deviation`, `timer`, `interaction`, `interface_config` or `parameter_value` is copied into `rwb_decision`: the notice, the case and the result arrive as facts of the record, and the address, the file payload and the customer value never arrive at all (DP-01, DP-18). The barcode `RR223344556TH`, the call-back date `18122026`, the delivered date 2026-12-18 and the business dates are named in this document as legacy values only, and none of them is a customer value. Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8; the container of the notice reference, the hold reason, the delivery status and the notice period start date inside `actions` and `outcome` is the reading of ASM-2246 and is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1276; ASM-2246).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-decision` (P7); base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`. Both paths are the ones TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 carries (API-P7-006 and API-P7-007) and the Ownership Map gives to P7. The request and response field set of a dispatch entry is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1276; ASM-2246).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | API-P7-006: the entries of a case in a date range, searched by `caseId`, `decision`, `ruleId`, `approver`, `from`, `to`, `page` and `size`; 200 with the DecisionLogPage | Decision log, right R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}` | API-P7-007: one entry with its decision code, final call, rule id and version, notice reference, notice type, hold reason or delivery status, notice period start date and chain fields; 200 with the DecisionLogEntry | Decision log, right R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |

The DecisionLogEntry body carries `entryId`, `chainSeq`, `caseId`, `decisionCode`, `ruleId`, `ruleVersion`, `inputsRef`, `finalCall`, `decidedAt`, `prevHash`, `entryHash`, `correctsEntryId` and `actorUserId`, and for a dispatch entry the notice reference, the notice type, the hold reason or the delivery status and the notice period start date; the DecisionLogPage body carries `items`, `page`, `size` and `total`. The field-level shape is the reading of ASM-2246.

Errors: 401 no session; 403 the role lacks the Decision log right (MSG-P4-002); 404 the entry or the case is absent or outside the scope (MSG-P4-003); 422 a query value is outside its list; 503 the ledger is unavailable. Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set. `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/cases/{caseId}/recommendation` (API-P7-001) and the approval operations (API-P7-002 to API-P7-005) are the decision center's and belong to the approval and recommendation stories of this service; this story declares them neither as provided nor as consumed.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Operations consumed | None. The record of the loop arrives as the `DecisionRecorded` fact of 12.4 and not over REST, and this story calls no operation of another service: the notice, the case, the deviation, the timer and the ledger entry stay with their owners and no value of them is read back |

The capability area, the right and the scope of the two reads are declared on the operations and enforced at gateway-bff through the composite route of DP-19, which asks `rwb-access`, so this story adds no `RecoveryAccessGuard` equivalent and no authorise call (GAP-1276; ASM-2249). The reference lists, the parameters and the rule registry of 12.7 are read inside the service or at the version in force carried by the record; if the reference-data contract of `rwb-case` is called directly at a later version of this story, one C row is added and the same reads move there (GAP-1277; ASM-2248).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Events published | None. This story publishes no event of its own: the record is a fact of `rwb-comms` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and the entries of the ledger are read through the operations of 12.1 |

`rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` is published by the owning service of each decision and `rwb-decision` is its consumer, as the event catalogue names it (Architecture v5 slide 42, event 08), and the ledger append needs no confirmation event because the letter loop is not a point of no return of the strict mode of slide 28. The `ApprovalRequested`, `ApprovalDecided` and `RulePackageInForce` events of `rwb.decision.events.v1` belong to the approval and rule-registry stories of this service and are not touched here.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 ledger and its shared topic; published by `rwb-comms` for the decisions of the letter loop, and by all 19 services for their own | `DispatchRecordListener`: inbox dedupe by event ID and by the record reference, then `DecisionLogAppendService` for the decision code D7.1, the final call, the rule id and version, the notice reference, the notice type, the case reference, the hold reason or the delivery status and the notice period start date |

The fact carries IDs, codes, versions, a rule reference and dates only; no address, no customer value and no WIN payload travels on the topic (BR4, BR12). Which further fields of the fact this service requires is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1276; ASM-2246). Records with any other decision code are the ledger baseline's general ingest.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Workflows and activities | None. The append is a transactional write on the consumer path and not a workflow step; the handler is a Kafka consumer with the inbox of DP-09 |

The loop's own workflow is `NoticeDispatchWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-comms`, and it is neither started nor signalled here: this story registers no workflow and no activity on the `rwb-decision` queue and adds none to the workflow kit.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Schedules | None. This story creates no Temporal Schedule and starts nothing on a clock: the JOB-10 notice dispatch run at 16:00 is `rwb-comms`'s Schedule (Architecture v5 slide 44), and the one Schedule of this service's ledger, the chain check JOB-14 at 02:00, is the decision-log baseline's |

DP-10 applies here only to the owning service's Schedule: a Schedule is registered by the service that owns the job, and the record ingest of this story is continuous Kafka and not a clock (BR13).

Not owned and never read: `notice`, `template`, `merge_field` (P6), `recovery_case`, `timer`, `task` (P3), `deviation` (S8), `interaction` (P1), `interface_config`, `outbound_item` (P2), `role`, `permission` and `delegation_limit` (P4). No foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01).
