##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, module `log/dispatch`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision.dispatch`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | none |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the record itself: the append through the decision-record path, the chain, the append-only rule and the shared topic. DP-01 is the boundary: the entry lives in `rwb_decision` and the notice, the case, the deviation, the timer and the ledger entry are never read as tables. DP-07 is the D7.1 code and the closed vocabulary of hold reasons and delivery statuses read at the version in force. DP-09 is the inbox dedupe, the record reference and the CloudEvents envelope. DP-10 is stated as a boundary and not as work: the 16:00 run is `rwb-comms`'s Schedule and this story registers none (12.6). DP-11 is the one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker behind the edge, and it is why no service call is made on the consumer path. DP-13 is the base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`; DP-19 is the gateway-bff route through which SCR-38 Decision log query reaches the two operations. DP-05 and DP-18 have an instance only as an absence: this service reads no `v_ace_*` view and no ACE table — the proof rows of the legacy story arrive only as the delivery status of a record — and it writes no interaction entry, because the ledger is `rwb-source-data`'s.

The platform H dependencies of the DP table and the published C dependencies of other services are not in the metadata rows of this story, which name None and `RWB-P6-E2021-CON`; they are the dependencies the DP table adds and they are recorded in GAP-1277 and ASM-2248, with the two baselines of 12.7. None of them blocks the build beyond Day 1.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| DispatchRecordListener | Kafka consumer with the inbox | Reads `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, deduplicates by event ID and record reference, keeps the D7.1 facts with final call HELD, DELIVERED or UNSERVED and hands them to the appender |
| DecisionLogAppendService | Service | Checks the decision code, the final call, the notice reference and type, the rule id with its version and the hold reason or delivery status, and writes the entry, its chain position, its inbox row and its idempotency row in one transaction (BR2, BR5, BR7, BR10, BR12) |
| ChainHasher | Service | The canonical form of an entry and its SHA-256, the first `prev_hash` of 64 zeros and the `prev_hash` of every later entry (BR3) |
| RuleRegistryReader | Repository | Reads `rule_row` and `rule_package_version` by rule id and version to prove the rule that decided the letter (BR5) |
| DecisionLogQueryController | Controller | The two operations of 12.1 with the declared right, the scope, the paging and the problem mapping for 401, 403, 404, 422 and 503 |
| DecisionLogQueryService | Service | The date-range search of a case and the single read, the row shape of a dispatch entry, and the total count of the page |
| DecisionLogRepository | Repository | `decision_log_entry` in `rwb_decision`, insert only, with the search indexes and the idempotency key |
| ReferenceListClient, ParameterClient | Client | LOV-DECISION, the final-call list, the closed vocabulary, the page-size bound and the completeness target at the version in force |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `decision_log_entry`, its inbox and idempotency rows in schema `rwb_decision`, and reads `rule_row` and `rule_package_version` in the same schema; reads no other schema (DP-01).
- The table, its columns of TSD P7 v2 T3.1, the append-only trigger `tr_declog_append_only`, the missing grant for UPDATE and DELETE and the unique key on the idempotency key belong to the decision-log store baseline and are not rebuilt here (GAP-1277).
- One migration step in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15): `V2021_1__decision_log_dispatch_index.sql` adds the composite index `ix_declog_dispatch_case ON decision_log_entry (case_id, decision_code, decided_at DESC)` that the date-range read uses. The index name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1276; ASM-2246).
- No row of `notice`, `recovery_case`, `deviation`, `timer`, `interaction` or `parameter_value` is written here.

**Configuration and reference data**

- LOV-DECISION which holds D7.1, the final-call list of HELD, DELIVERED and UNSERVED, and the closed vocabulary of hold reasons and delivery statuses are read at the version in force; the values are the legacy values and the list names are those of TSD P7 v2 T3.2 and RWB-P6-E2021-CON AC4.
- The page-size bound of the search and the completeness target of the ingest are parameters with no default in code; their names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1276; ASM-2251). The rule version label is read from the registry and never composed in code (GAP-1276; ASM-2247).
- The outbox retry policy and the inbox retention are the platform's (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON). No feature switch of this story's own is named by a source: the record appears wherever the loop takes a decision, and the switch of the loop is `rwb.comms.win-dispatch-loop` of RWB-P6-E2021-APP.

**Build steps**

1. `DecisionLogRepository` and the index step; test the date-range read of a case, the single read and the INSERT-only constraint (AC8).
2. `ChainHasher` and the canonical form: `chain_seq`, `prev_hash` from the previous entry, the first `prev_hash` of 64 zeros and `entry_hash` as the SHA-256 of the canonical form (AC2, AC8).
3. `DispatchRecordListener` with the inbox and the dedupe by event ID and record reference; test the replay and the repeated record of AC7, and the pass that appends nothing (AC1).
4. `DecisionLogAppendService` with the checks of BR10 and the fail-closed transaction; test the forced failure of AC6 and the chain position the refused write does not use.
5. `RuleRegistryReader` and the rule id with its version; test the record without a version of AC9 and a pair absent from the registry (X2).
6. `ReferenceListClient` and `ParameterClient` with the version in force, and the refusal rather than an assumed code, final call or rule version (BR10, X10).
7. The four record shapes: held under `R-LIT-04`, `R-LIT-05` and `R-UNI-20`, delivered under `R-LIT-07`, unserved under `R-LIT-09` and `R-LIT-08`; tests for AC2, AC3, AC4 and AC5.
8. `DecisionLogQueryController` with the declared right, the scope, the paging and the problem mapping; tests for AC8, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003.
9. The boundary test: no write to `rwb_comms`, `rwb_case`, `rwb_source_data` or `rwb_integration`, and no address, customer value or WIN payload in any entry, event payload or log line (AC2, AC8, BR4).
10. The contract-fake run of the whole slice from Day 1: the record, library, ledger, scope, reference and registry fakes green before the real services land.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the chain of a SIT day verifies from the first entry with no break, a held letter and its later delivery leave two chained entries naming their own rule and version, a refused decision leaves none and does not consume a chain position, a repeated record leaves one entry, both reads answer inside the 2 s budget of the frame, and no notice, case, timer or ledger entry was changed by this story.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | A dispatch record cannot be appended, or the store or the chain is unavailable | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | The record path, on the append; the owning service stops the decision, the notice stays Approved and is not written to the WIN file, and an incident is raised under R-UNI-39 |
| MSG-P7-009 | A record lacks its decision code, its final call, its notice reference or its rule version, or carries a value outside its list | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1276; ASM-2250) | This story, on the schema check of the append, naming the missing field |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller holds no Decision log right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | The edge, through the authorise answer of the read |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case or the entry is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. | The edge, through the authorise answer of the read |
| MSG-P6-008 | The notice was refused, undeliverable or had no proof in the window | {notice} for case {case} was not served: {reason}. The case is in your queue to choose another service method. | `rwb-comms`; asserted here and named in the outcome of the entry |
| MSG-P6-001 | A contact stop blocked the letter | Contact with this customer is stopped for {reason}. | `rwb-comms`; asserted and named in the outcome of the held entry |
| MSG-P6-003 | The template was withdrawn before dispatch | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. | `rwb-comms`; asserted and named in the outcome of the held entry |
| MSG-P3-004 | A legal hold or a deviation blocked the letter | This case is on hold for {deviation}. The prescription date is still {date}. | `rwb-case`; asserted and named in the outcome of the held entry |

MSG-P7-003, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003, MSG-P6-008, MSG-P6-001, MSG-P6-003 and MSG-P3-004 are copied unchanged from RWB-E2-021 section 14 and the FSD P7 v3 message set. MSG-P7-009 is named by FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-05 and its text is written by no source, so the placeholder stands and is carried in GAP-1276 with ASM-2250. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10. Delivery shape: every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled and `instance` naming the request, with the status mapping 401 no session, 403 MSG-P4-002, 404 MSG-P4-003, 422 a query value outside its list and 503 MSG-P7-003 on the record path.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built in this story. The two reads are consumed by SCR-38 Decision log query, which searches the log by case, rule, approver and date with export (FSD P7 v3 Screens), and by the auditor's view of the ledger; both are reached through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 and are another story's. The notice screens stay `rwb-comms`'s (SCR-18 Notice approval of RWB-E2-014) and the case timeline stays `rwb-case`'s (SCR-04), and this story feeds neither of them.

| Where | State | What the reader sees |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-38 Decision log query (P7) | List | The D7.1 entries of the case in decidedAt order, each with its rule and version, its notice reference and type, its final call and its hold reason or delivery status |
| The entry read | One entry | The same row with the notice period start date where one applies, its `decidedAt`, its `prevHash` and its `entryHash`, and a `correctsEntryId` beside the entry it corrects |
| The read | 403, or 404 | MSG-P4-002 for a caller without the right, MSG-P4-003 for a case outside the scope; no row is returned |

A panel or screen id for showing the dispatch record beside the notice on the notice screens, and the field list of SCR-38, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1276; ASM-2246). The screen field list and the composite route specification belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and to the story that owns SCR-38.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the decision code, the final-call set, the hold reason and delivery status vocabulary, the rule versions, the page-size bound, the completeness target and the message ids are reference rows, registry rows or parameters read at the version in force; nothing of them is a constant here.
- No personal data in the entry, the inputs reference, the event, the audit line, the tests or the logs: the notice reference, the notice type, the case reference, the rule id and version, the final call, the hold reason or delivery status, the dates and the hashes only. The address, the addressee name, the account number and the WIN payload stay with `rwb-source-data`, `rwb-comms` and `rwb-integration` (BR4).
- No read of another service's tables (DP-01, DP-18): the notice, the case, the deviation, the timer and the ledger entry arrive as facts of the record or are never touched.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views: this story reads no ACE data at all, and the proof rows of the legacy story arrive as the delivery status of a record through `rwb-integration` and `rwb-comms`.
- One appender and no mover: this story changes no notice, no case, no timer and no ledger entry, so a decision record can never move a case (BR8).
- No entry without its decision and no decision without its entry: the entry, its chain position, its inbox row and its idempotency row commit in one transaction, and a decision whose record cannot be appended is stopped with an incident (BR12, R-UNI-39).
- Append only and hash chained: no UPDATE and no DELETE on `decision_log_entry`, a correction is a new entry with `corrects_entry_id`, and the chain is verifiable from `chain_seq` 1 (BR3).
- One entry per decision: the inbox dedupe and the record reference make a second entry for the same decision impossible, and a later decision of the same notice is a second entry and not an edit (BR1, BR6).
- One base, one topic and one queue: `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, `rwb.decision-record.v1` for the record and `rwb.decision.events.v1` for this service's own events, with `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`; no monolith base and no other service's base or topic is declared here as this service's own (DP-13, DP-14).
- One hop and 2 s with a breaker per downstream on the reads behind the edge; an unreadable list, parameter or rule row refuses the append rather than writing an assumed value (DP-11).

##### 19. Out of scope

- The notice, its states Approved, Held, Sent, Delivered and Unserved, the conduct check of the four gates, the template check, the notice hold and the dispatch selection: RWB-P6-E2021-APP, with the contract in RWB-P6-E2021-CON. This story appends the record of a decision and changes no notice.
- The INT-14 WIN dispatch file, the INT-15 proof round trip, the proof capture, the result-code map and the acknowledgement: RWB-P6-E2021-APP, RWB-P6-E1046-APP, RWB-P6-E1055-APP and `rwb-integration` (P2, DP-16). No file layout, barcode payload or WIN field is designed or stored here.
- The NOTICE_PERIOD timer, the case transfer with reason NOTICE_UNSERVED and the case state: `rwb-case` (P3). The notice period start date is written on the entry and the period itself is never computed here.
- The legal hold flag of the case: `rwb-case` (P3, DF-CAS-020). It reaches this story only as the hold reason `LEGAL_HOLD` of a record.
- The interaction ledger entry, its conduct check column, its channel and its summary: `rwb-source-data` (P1, DP-18) and RWB-P6-E2021-APP.
- The WIN interface configuration, the file runs and the outbound items: `rwb-integration` (P2). The JOB-10 Schedule at 16:00 is `rwb-comms`'s, and this story registers no Schedule (12.6).
- The D7.1 approval of a demand and recall notice, the approval queue SCR-10, the decision screen SCR-11 and the recommendation read `GET /cases/{caseId}/recommendation`: the other P7 stories of this service. This story approves nothing and reads no `delegation_limit` row.
- The general ingest of every other decision code into the ledger, the append-only table itself, the daily chain check JOB-14 at 02:00 and the daily seal: the decision-log baseline of this service.
- The data-lake copy of the log, JOB-13 and lake retention: retired with the data lake (DP-17); the ingest of the ledger is continuous Kafka.
- SCR-38 Decision log query as a built screen, the notice panel and the composite route: the screen stories and RWB-PLT-N001-CON.
- SMS and LINE dispatch through NSS and LINE OA (RWB-E2-022), alternate service methods and substituted service (R-LIT-10, R-LIT-11, Epic 5), the breach path for a contact sent while a block is on (FEAT-DVF-10, Epic 7) and notice approval (RWB-E2-014), as the legacy story left them.
- The `-ITG` copies of the test cases and the cross-service harness: RWB-ITG-E2021-ITG. The Helm chart, the Kafka subscription values, the metrics, the alerts and the runbook of this capability: RWB-P6-E2021-OPS and an OPS story of this legacy key.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-021 for rwb-comms. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **the dispatch loop of rwb-comms deployed from the service template with its Helm values, its own login, its per-service Flyway migration and a worker on task queue `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, the 16:00 Temporal Schedule and its handoff from the Airflow WIN file window, the outbox relay and the three consumer groups with their retry and `.dlt` paths, the dashboards for a file that is missing and a proof window that has expired, the alerts for a missing file, an unacknowledged file and a proof window expiry, and a runbook for a re-run of JOB-10**, so that **an operator sees within minutes that tonight's letters were not written to WIN, or that the proof never came back, and repairs the run by business date without reading code and without writing a second file for the same date**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy capability had one signal and it was a job exception: the 16:00 run either threw or it did not, and a file the bank never received looked exactly like a quiet night (legacy sections 5 and 13). In the target the run is a Temporal Schedule and a workflow, the file is written by rwb-integration, the acknowledgement and the proof results come back through integration, and the notice facts live in `rwb_comms` (Architecture v5 slides 17, 41, 44; DP-10). There is no scheduler row to be late and no job record to inspect, so the operational question moves from "did the job run" to "was the file written, was it acknowledged, did the proof arrive inside the window, and is the decision record chain moving".

The capability is also the one whose failure is silent by design: a held notice, an unserved notice and a notice waiting for proof are all correct outcomes of a correct run, so an operator cannot tell a good night from a bad one by the notice count. That is why the dispatch file, the acknowledgement and the proof window are three dashboard series and three alerts here, each with a message ID of section 14 and one runbook entry, and why the rerun is defined by business date with the skip rule that the legacy story states: a rerun from SCR-44 skips the notices already Unserved or Held and the notices already in a file of that date.

Deployment is part of the capability for the same reason: the chart carries the rwb-comms login and no other credential (DP-02), the migration job runs the per-service Flyway sequence in `rwb_comms` (DP-15, ADR-021), the worker polls `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and polls nothing else, the Schedule is the only clock of the service, and the three consumer groups exist with retry and `.dlt` so a contact stop that arrives while the run is open is never lost (DP-09).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The Temporal workflow kit and the `rwb-recovery` namespace are available (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), so the worker polls `rwb-comms` and the Schedule runs in every environment.
- The Kafka event platform provisions topics with a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON), and `rwb.comms.events.v1`, `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and `rwb.case.events.v1` are provisioned by their owners.
- The observability stack of the platform is available (RWB-PLT-OBS, ADR-023): metrics, traces and logs with one trace across REST, Kafka and Temporal.
- The three environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist with their parameter scope and their Kafka and Temporal endpoints.
- RWB-P6-E2021-CON is published, so the smoke profile and the drift test run against the two operations, the file contract and the six fakes of that baseline.
- The bank Airflow owns the WIN file window for JOB-10 (Architecture v5 slide 44 notes) and its handoff to this Schedule is agreed. The mechanism of the handoff is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1095; ASM-2043).
- The WIN file drop and the rwb-integration file run are owned by P2 and by the WIN owner; this story deploys nothing of theirs and reads their answers.
- The worker placement, the replica counts and the deployment slots are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1093; ASM-2041), and the deployment slot decision DL35 is open in the P6 TSD.
- The owner of the daily reconciliation REC-05 that the legacy story names is not stated in the sources (GAP-1090; ASM-2038).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds one image and one chart version from the same commit, runs the unit, component and contract tests, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes the chart.
2. The chart deploys rwb-comms with the rwb-comms login, the pre-deploy migration job for schema `rwb_comms`, the readiness and liveness probes, the api deployment and the worker deployment that polls `rwb-comms`.
3. The provisioning step declares the Schedule of 16:00, the three consumer groups of the capability on `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and `rwb.case.events.v1`, and the outbox relay subscription of the service; it creates no topic and no queue of another service.
4. The provisioning step asserts that no Quartz table, no shared job table and no batch table is read or written, and that the only clock of the service is the one Schedule.
5. The dashboards are published: dispatch files written by business date, notices in a file, acknowledgements received, notices without an acknowledgement, notices held by reason, notices unserved by result, proof window expiries, notices waiting for proof, decision record write failures and workflow health.
6. The alerts are wired to the message IDs of section 14 and to the runbook entries of section 13; the thresholds are values and carry the placeholder of section 11 until they are confirmed.
7. A smoke step runs a synthetic business date in the SIT profile against the six fakes of RWB-P6-E2021-CON: the request, the run, the file, the acknowledgement and one proof result, so the loop is exercised end to end before WIN and the neighbouring services are live.
8. The runbook is published and reviewed with the on-call rota: a missing dispatch file, an unacknowledged file, a proof window that expired without proof, a held notice that should have gone out, a stopped decision record chain and a re-run of JOB-10 by business date.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The migration job fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic reaches the new version | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The worker is deployed without the `rwb-comms` queue, or on another queue | The readiness probe stays unready and the release fails its own check | None | AC1 |
| X3 | The Schedule is missing, or a second clock is registered | The provisioning check fails the release and the runbook entry for a missing file opens | None | AC2 |
| X4 | The dispatch file is not written for the business date | The missing-file alert fires and the runbook entry for a missing file starts with the file window and the integration run | MSG-P6-004 | AC5, AC6 |
| X5 | The acknowledgement never returns | The unacknowledged-file alert fires; the notices stay Sent-less and the rerun writes no second file for the date | MSG-P6-004 | AC5, AC6 |
| X6 | The proof window expires with no proof for a share of notices | The proof-window alert fires; the notices become Unserved under R-LIT-08 and the runbook entry names the WIN owner | MSG-P6-008 | AC5, AC6 |
| X7 | A consumer group is provisioned without its retry or `.dlt` topic | The provisioning step fails the release and the consumer refuses to start | None | AC4 |
| X8 | The decision record chain stops during a run | The run fails its step, the notices do not proceed and the incident rule of R-UNI-39 applies | MSG-P7-003 | AC4, AC6 |
| X9 | A release declares a new topic, a Quartz row or a second Schedule | The pipeline fails the release on the retired-element check | None | AC2, AC9 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the platform topic provisioning, the workflow kit and the observability stack; builds no application code |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, alert thresholds, retention and the deployment slots are environment values, not story decisions |
| Valuable | Makes a capability with no scheduler row observable: the file, the acknowledgement and the proof window each have a signal, an alert and an owner |
| Estimable | One chart, one pipeline stage, one migration job, two deployments, one Schedule, three consumer groups, ten dashboard series, six alert rules and six runbook entries |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the Schedule exists, the groups exist, the panels carry data, the alerts fire on a synthetic metric, the runbook entry resolves |

These nine criteria are new for the deployment and test artefacts only; they restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P6-E2021-APP.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One service, one schema, one login: the release uses the rwb-comms login and no other service's credential | DP-02; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR2 | The migration is a per-service Flyway sequence in schema rwb_comms and runs before the deployment is ready | DP-15; ADR-021; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| BR3 | Every subscription has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and a consumer never acknowledges an event it could not process | DP-09; Architecture v5 slide 22 notes |
| BR4 | The only clock of the service is the 16:00 Schedule; no Quartz row, no shared job table and no batch table exists | DP-10; Architecture v5 slide 44 |
| BR5 | No new topic is created for this capability: `rwb.comms.events.v1` carries events 14 and 15, `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and `rwb.case.events.v1` are consumed, and `rwb.decision-record.v1` is shared | DP-14; Architecture v5 slide 42 |
| BR6 | The outbox relay is JOB-11 of the platform and runs every minute; the service configures nothing of it but its own outbox | Architecture v5 slide 44; DP-09 |
| BR7 | No environment value is hard-coded: replica counts, resource sizes, timeouts, thresholds and deployment slots come from values files | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR8 | An alert carries a message ID and the agreed text, and links one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR9 | A refused read and an out-of-scope read are counted on the dashboard and never page the on-call rota | MSG-P4-002; MSG-P4-003 |
| BR10 | A re-run is idempotent on the notice ID and the business date and skips the notices already Unserved or Held and the notices already in a file of that date | Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 12 (Jobs) |
| BR11 | The service writes only schema rwb_comms and reads no other schema and no `v_ace_*` view; the proof rows are the INT-15 results of rwb-integration | DP-01; DP-05; DP-16 |
| BR12 | No dashboard series, log line or alert payload carries personal data; notice IDs, case IDs, barcodes, counts and durations only | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR13 | The stuck workflow scan is the platform's JOB-21 and is reused, not rebuilt | Architecture v5 slide 44 |
| BR14 | The daily reconciliation REC-05 and its owner are not fixed here; no source names them | Legacy RWB-E2-021 section 13; GAP-1090 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the migration job pass the pipeline | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration complete and probes healthy | The schema is at the expected version, the outbox relay runs and the worker polls rwb-comms | Ready |
| Ready | Release superseded | A new chart version is promoted | Rolling |
| Rolling | All pods on the new version | The old ReplicaSet drains and the worker build ID is the new one | Ready |
| Ready | Migration job failed | The schema is not at the expected version | Failed |
| Failed | Rollback | The previous chart version is redeployed and the migration is reversed by its own script | Ready |
| Ready | The feature switch is turned off | The parameter changes in the environment | Ready with the dispatch off; the run writes no file |

The notice states are the app story's; this story moves none of them and only turns the dispatch on and off.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the provisioning step, the Schedule registration, the dashboards, the alerts and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the Temporal cluster, the topic provisioning and the visibility queries behind JOB-21 |
| ACE database administrator | Owns schema rwb_comms, the login and its grants, and approves the migration job |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact through the environments and the rollback when a run fails |
| On-call operator | Runs the runbook entries and opens an incident when a missing file or an unacknowledged file persists past its second window |
| RW-PLATADM | Reads the notices and operates the run and the rerun from the run view, not in the cluster |
| Owner of rwb-integration (P2) and the WIN owner | Are paged by the missing-file and the unacknowledged-file alerts and own the repair beyond the rwb-comms breaker |
| Owner of rwb-decision (P7) | Is paged by the decision-record alert and owns the shared chain |

The per-service login name used by the chart is a secret reference resolved at deploy time; the chart references "the rwb-comms login (DP-02)" and never a literal name.

##### 11. Data

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Deployment values | Image digest, chart version, replica counts, resource requests and limits, probe paths and timings, log level, feature switch `rwb.comms.win-dispatch-loop`, the two client timeouts, the alert thresholds, the deployment slot |
| Schema | rwb_comms, migrated by the per-service Flyway sequence; `notice`, `template`, `merge_field` and the library objects |
| Topics | `rwb.comms.events.v1` produces events 14 and 15 with retry and `.dlt`; `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and `rwb.case.events.v1` are consumed with retry and `.dlt`; `rwb.decision-record.v1` is produced on as its owner provisions it |
| Queue | Temporal task queue `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery` |
| Schedules | One: the JOB-10 notice dispatch run at 16:00 on business days; JOB-11 and JOB-21 are the platform's |
| File | The INT-14 dispatch file of one business date and the INT-15 proof result, both written and read through rwb-integration |
| Dashboard series | Files written by business date, notices in a file, acknowledgements received, notices without an acknowledgement, notices held by reason, notices unserved by result, proof window expiries, notices waiting for proof, decision record write failures, workflow open and stuck |
| Runbook entries | Missing dispatch file, unacknowledged file, proof window expired, held notice that should have gone out, stopped decision record chain, re-run of JOB-10 |
| Secrets | The rwb-comms login secret, the Kafka client credential and the Temporal mTLS material, all from the platform secret store |

The alert values, the replica counts, the probe timings and the deployment slot are deployment values; the provisional alert values and their confirmation are carried by the gap and the assumption of this story (GAP-1093; ASM-2041). The exact cluster topology, the node pools and the slot assignment follow the open decision DL35 of the P6 TSD and are not fixed here.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The deployment exposes the two operations of RWB-P6-E2021-CON unchanged; this story adds no path, no parameter and no response field, and the probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None declared by this story. The consumed operations of the capability — the reference data of rwb-case, the approval of rwb-decision, the case read and the case facts, the contact stops of rwb-deviation, the ledger of rwb-source-data and the file of rwb-integration — are deployed as client configuration only: their endpoints, their 2 s budget, their retry and their breaker are values of the environment, and no contract is defined here. The naming of the rwb-integration file operation is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1089; ASM-2037).

###### 12.3 Events published

None declared by this story. `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1`, `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` are produced on the topics their owners provision; the deployment only configures the producer credential, the retry topic and the `.dlt` topic of `rwb.comms.events.v1` and reuses the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1` without recreating it.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None declared by this story. The three consumer groups of `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and `rwb.case.events.v1` are provisioned with retry and `.dlt` as AC4 states, and their payload shapes belong to RWB-P6-E2021-CON.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|---|
| NoticeDispatchWorkflow | Workflow, one run per business date | `rwb-comms` | Worker deployment with the build ID of the release; polls `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and no other queue |
| conductCheck | Activity, in rwb-comms | `rwb-comms` | Registered by the same worker |
| recordDecision | Activity, in rwb-comms | `rwb-comms` | Registered by the same worker; the series the decision-record alert reads |
| generateLetter | Activity, owner rwb-document | `rwb-document` | Called as a child activity of the other service; nothing deployed here |
| decisionApproval | Child workflow, owner rwb-decision | `rwb-decision` | Called by the workflow; nothing deployed here |
| deliverFile | Activity, owner rwb-integration | `rwb-integration` | Called by the workflow; the file run is rwb-integration's |

The worker is the only workload that polls a Temporal queue in this service. Its autoscaling, its replica count and its resource sizes are values, not template constants.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Name | Cron | Overlap policy | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|---|
| The JOB-10 notice dispatch run | 16:00 on business days | SKIP with the catch-up window of the workflow kit | One Temporal Schedule, created by the provisioning step of this release, with the business date as the workflow input |

The bank Airflow owns the WIN file window and hands it to this Schedule; the handoff row is part of the release and its mechanism is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1095; ASM-2043). The outbox relay JOB-11 runs every minute as a platform job and the stuck workflow scan JOB-21 is the platform's visibility query; neither is registered here. The daily reconciliation REC-05 is not registered here, because no source assigns its owner (GAP-1090; ASM-2038).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None declared by this story as a new element. The migration job creates and migrates `notice`, `template`, `merge_field`, the local decision record and the library objects in schema `rwb_comms`; `recovery_case`, `task`, `timer`, `deviation`, `decision_log_entry`, `document`, `interaction` and `outbound_item` belong to other services and the migration job never touches them (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None deployed into UAT or production. The six fakes of RWB-P6-E2021-CON run in the pipeline and in the SIT smoke profile of AC8 only, and they are test-only workloads.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | None declared | The two operations are deployed unchanged; their clients are configuration |
| Kafka | 3 topic subscriptions and 2 topic productions provisioned | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and `rwb.case.events.v1` consumed; `rwb.comms.events.v1` produced with retry and `.dlt`; `rwb.decision-record.v1` shared |
| Temporal | 1 worker, 1 workflow, 3 activities, 1 child workflow, 1 Schedule | The worker on `rwb-comms`, its activities, the approval child and the 16:00 Schedule |
| File | 2 | The INT-14 dispatch file of the business date and the INT-15 proof result, both through rwb-integration |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/comms/v1` | none |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-comms/` | Chart with api and worker deployments, service, migration job, config map, secret references, probes and the Schedule hook of this release |
| `helm/rwb-comms/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, `rwb.comms.win-dispatch-loop`, the two client timeouts, the alert thresholds, the deployment slot |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit, component and contract tests, retired-element check, image and dependency scan, chart publish, promote the same artefact |
| Provisioning step | The 16:00 Schedule; consumer group `rwb-comms` on `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and `rwb.case.events.v1` with retry and `.dlt`; reuse of `rwb.comms.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`; task queue `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery` |
| Dashboards | Ten series of section 11 |
| Alerts | Six rules, each with a message ID and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Six entries: missing dispatch file, unacknowledged file, proof window expired, held notice that should have gone out, stopped decision record chain, re-run of JOB-10 |

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only when the migration is at the expected schema version, the outbox relay dependency is reachable and the Temporal worker on `rwb-comms` has polled; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database, calls another service or opens a file window.

**Dispatch series.** The file series is the count of dispatch files written by business date and read from the run records of the workflow and the file reference of rwb-integration; the acknowledgement series is the count of notices whose barcode and sent date landed after the file; the proof series is the count of notices past the proof window with no proof. They are not job-lateness measures, because there is no job.

**Alert mapping.**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P6-004 | The dispatch file of the business date is missing | Missing-file alert with the business date, the workflow and the file reference | Platform on-call, page; ticket to the rwb-integration and WIN owners |
| MSG-P6-004 | The acknowledgement does not return inside its value | Unacknowledged-file alert after the second window with the file reference and the count of notices waiting | Platform on-call, page; ticket to the WIN owner |
| MSG-P6-008 | The proof window expires for a share of notices | Proof-window alert with the count, the oldest sent date and the barcode range | Ticket to the WIN owner, no page |
| MSG-P6-001 | A contact stop holds notices for a share of the case set | Held-by-reason series; a hold that should have gone out raises the held-notice alert | Platform on-call, ticket |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record chain stops during a run | Decision-record alert with the run, the notice and the chain position | Platform on-call, page; escalation to rwb-decision |
| None | JOB-21 raises a stuck workflow on `rwb-comms` | Stuck-workflow alert with the workflow ID, the step and the last event | Platform on-call, page |

Every alert carries its message ID where the condition maps to one, and the condition without a message ID carries the workflow name instead. The alert thresholds are deployment values with provisional defaults; the missing source for them is carried by the gap and the assumption of this story (GAP-1093; ASM-2041).

**Rollback.** The previous chart version is redeployed with its image digest, the migration is reversed by its own script in `rwb_comms`, the Schedule is restored to the previous definition, the workflow runs in flight drain on the previous build ID, and the feature switch is turned off first when a run is writing files, so no second file is written for a business date during the rollback. A rolled-back release leaves the notices in their states and writes no compensating notice.

**Done when.** The chart renders in all three environments, the pipeline promotes one artefact and fails on a fake drift or a retired element, the Schedule and the three consumer groups exist with their retry and `.dlt` paths, the ten panels carry the synthetic day, the six alerts fire on synthetic metrics, the rerun of a business date writes no second file, the rollback and the switch-off are exercised once in SIT, and the six runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |

| MSG-P6-004 | The dispatch file is missing or unacknowledged | {notice} was sent for registered mail on {date}. |
| MSG-P6-001 | A contact stop holds the letters of a case | Contact with this customer is stopped for {reason}. |

| MSG-P4-002 | A read without the Litigation right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | A notice outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A consumed call does not answer in time | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The message texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story where the message already existed; the deployment adds the routing, the threshold and the runbook link, never a new wording. The alert values and the deployment slot are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1093; ASM-2041).

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment serves SCR-18 Notice approval in its Generated, Approved, Sent, Delivered, Unserved and Held states, SCR-04 Case timeline for the ledger entry of each outcome and SCR-44 Batch and job monitor for the 16:00 run, its file, its acknowledgement and its rerun, all behind the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The operator-facing surfaces of this story are the pipeline run view, the release view, the ten dashboard panels, the six alerts and the runbook; the smoke step runs the loop of a synthetic business date in SIT and asserts that the two operations answer inside the 2 s budget and that the file and the acknowledgement are exercised against the fakes.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the proof window, the statutory notice type list, the eligible states, the hold reasons and the result code map are reference data held by their owner, never a deployment value.
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads or the runbook: notice IDs, case IDs, barcodes, user IDs of staff, counts and durations only.
- One login per service; the chart carries the rwb-comms login reference and no other service's credential (DP-02).
- The service writes only schema rwb_comms; the migration job never touches another schema and no dashboard query reads one (DP-01).
- ACE data is reached only through the owner's contract or the owner's `v_ace_*` views; no dashboard and no smoke step reads an ACE view, and the proof rows come as the INT-15 results of rwb-integration (DP-05, DP-16).
- Every subscription has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and the consumer dedupes through the inbox (DP-09).
- One clock and no new topic: the 16:00 Schedule starts the workflow, `rwb.comms.events.v1` carries the two events, and no Quartz row, shared job table or batch table exists (DP-10, DP-14).
- The release pins the image digest and the chart version, and no secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook.
- A rerun is idempotent on the notice ID and the business date, and no operator writes or edits a dispatch file by hand (BR10).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-021 for the wave 2 integration harness. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **one repeatable cross-service journey harness that runs a letter from the conduct check through the WIN file, the acknowledgment and the INT-15 proof of delivery to the notice-period timer, against the owning services' published contracts and their fakes**, so that **the notice period is proven to start from proof of delivery and not from printing, and no letter is proven to reach the WIN file while a contact stop or a legal hold is on**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A notice period counted from the print date can be challenged, and a letter sent while a contact stop is on is a conduct breach. Those two outcomes are only as good as the loop that produces them: the conduct check in rwb-comms, the WIN letters file (INT-14) sent through rwb-integration on the 16:00 window (JOB-10), the WIN acknowledgment, the INT-15 proof file that ACE ingests, the ledger entry in rwb-source-data, the decision record in rwb-decision and the NOTICE_PERIOD timer in rwb-case. That loop crosses six services and four call types, so a defect at any hop shows up as a wrong notice state or a timer that starts on the wrong date.

This story owns the harness that proves the loop, and the four legacy criteria that describe it end to end: AC1 dispatch, AC2 proof back, AC4 contact stop blocks the letter and AC5 consent withdrawn does not stop a statutory notice. It serves REQ-OCC-003, REQ-OCC-005, REQ-OCC-006 and REQ-ILG-010, and it carries CTL-15 and CTL-16 and the FSD P6 measure "notices with proof of delivery, 100 percent" into evidence.

The harness is decoupled the same way the services are. It calls each owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` and never a monolith base (DP-13, DP-01), it calls through the gateway-bff composite route where a screen would (DP-19), every call is one hop with a 2 s budget (DP-11), the ledger is read from rwb-source-data and never from a table (DP-05, DP-18), reference data such as the statutory notice type list is read from rwb-case (DP-07), the decision record is read from rwb-decision and its library and topic (DP-03), the dispatch and delivery facts are consumed as Kafka events from the owner's topic (DP-09), and the 16:00 run of JOB-10 is exercised on the Schedule in rwb-comms rather than a Quartz row (DP-10).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The harness runs in SIT, with the WIN file-drop fixture and the INT-15 proof-file fixture on the JOB-10 16:00 window: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0404; ASM-0579).
- The published contracts of rwb-comms, rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-access and rwb-decision are in the contract registry, and a WireMock stub set is generated from each one.
- The dispatch-eligible notice states are set to Approved (`rwb.comms.dispatch.eligible-states` = APPROVED), and the proof window is the 7 days of R-LIT-08, both present as data, not code.
- The statutory notice type list is readable as reference data through the rwb-case reference-data contract (DP-07); the list of statutory types is data owned by the business, and this story reads it and does not set it.
- An approver path exists so that a notice reaches state Approved before the run; notice approval itself is RWB-P7-E2014-APP.
- A SIT case, notice, deviation, contact point and consent status can be seeded through the owning services' published operations only; the seeding set and the harness environment specification are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0404; ASM-0579).
- The feature switch `rwb.comms.win-dispatch-loop` is on for the environment under test.
- No build dependency. Day 1, with the fakes in place from the first run, and each fake replaced by the real service as its I story lands.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: seeds the SIT case `RC-2026-000321`, its notice `N-0101` (type DEMAND, template DEMAND-SSME, language TH, version 1 Approved), its contact point, its consent status and, for the blocked run, the open deviation, through the owning services' published operations only.
2. Harness: requests the notice with `POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices` and reads it back with `GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}`, proving the notice is built and returned by its owner (DP-11, DP-13).
3. Harness: reads the case with `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` for legal hold and queue state, and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` for a NOTICE_PERIOD timer, before and after the run.
4. Harness: holds the JOB-10 window at 16:00 on the business date under test on the rwb-comms Schedule and triggers the file window; the window control and its fixture are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0404; ASM-0579).
5. Harness: drops the INT-14 WIN letters fixture, then reads the WIN acknowledgment fixture and asserts the barcode RR223344556TH and the sent date reach the notice as Sent.
6. Harness: subscribes to `rwb.comms.events.v1` and asserts `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` (EV-14) carries the notice for the case and no personal data.
7. Harness: drops the INT-15 proof-file fixture for the barcode with result DELIVERED and the call-back date, asserts `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` (EV-15), and asserts the notice becomes Delivered with the call-back date.
8. Harness: asserts the ledger entry through `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` with conduct check PASSED and the barcode summary, and the decision record through `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log`.
9. Harness: asserts the NOTICE_PERIOD timer on `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` is running from the delivery date and not from the sent date.
10. Harness: repeats the run with the open X1 deviation and the contact stop on, and asserts the notice is Held with hold reason CONTACT_STOP_X1, the conduct check is BLOCKED, one decision entry names R-LIT-05, and the WIN file fixture does not contain the notice.
11. Harness: repeats the run with the postal consent status WITHDRAWN on a statutory notice type, and asserts the notice is written to the WIN file and the conduct check is PASSED with the summary "Statutory notice, consent withdrawn".
12. Harness: authorises each call through `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` and records the refusal path for a caller outside the case scope.
13. Harness: publishes the per-run evidence report keyed by story and business date, with the four criteria and their assertions, and gates the wave on the result.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A fake answers a shape the published contract does not allow | The run fails at that hop; the report names the service, the operation and the contract version | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The WIN window fixture is not picked up inside the run window | The run fails and the report names the window and the fixture; the run is not marked passed | None | AC1 |
| X3 | The INT-15 proof fixture is not read back | The run fails and the report names the fixture; a notice that stays Sent is reported as an unproven delivery, not as a pass | None | AC2 |
| X4 | `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` or `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` is not consumed inside the run window | The run fails and the report names the event and the topic | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X5 | The notice is written to the WIN file while the contact stop is on | The run fails on AC4 regardless of the notice state | None | AC4 |
| X6 | A statutory notice is held because consent was withdrawn | The run fails on AC5 | None | AC5 |
| X7 | The NOTICE_PERIOD timer starts from the sent date | The run fails on AC2 and the report names the two dates | None | AC2 |
| X8 | A caller outside the case scope is authorised | The run fails on the access check and the report names the operation | None | AC4 |
| X9 | A real service is reachable but its contract version differs from the registry | The run fails before any assertion and the report names the service and both versions | None | AC1 |

The report text is for the wave entry check and is not part of the message standard. The business messages the journey produces are in section 14 and are asserted as data on the notice, the case and the ledger.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs against published contracts and fakes from Day 1; the only waits are the six I stories, one at a time |
| Negotiable | The fixtures, the window control and the report shape are configuration and agreed at the wave entry check, not business values in code |
| Valuable | The dispatch loop and the proof-based notice period are proven end to end before the wave opens |
| Estimable | One harness runner, one stub set, two file fixtures, one event probe, one report |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against its fake and again against the real owner as the I story lands |

AC3 and AC6 to AC12 are cited in the flow and exception table but are owned by the app stories of this legacy key (RWB-P6-E2021-APP, RWB-P1-E2021-APP, RWB-P3-E2021-APP, RWB-P4-E2021-APP and RWB-P7-E2021-APP); the four criteria above are the ones this ITG story owns.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every letter is checked before it is written to the WIN file, and the result is on the ledger entry | REQ-OCC-005; FEAT-OCC-05 |
| BR2 | A contact stop from X1 or X2 holds the notice and routes the case to the deviation owner | R-LIT-05; CTL-16 |
| BR3 | A legal hold stops every outbound action | R-UNI-20 |
| BR4 | Withdrawn consent removes the channel from the contact plan, and statutory notices continue | R-UNI-10; REQ-OCC-006; CTL-16 |
| BR5 | The notice period starts from the delivery date on the proof | R-LIT-07; CTL-15 |
| BR6 | A refused, returned or undeliverable letter records the result and queues an alternate service method | R-LIT-09 |
| BR7 | No proof inside the proof window marks the notice unserved, and the notice period does not start | R-LIT-08 |
| BR8 | A withdrawn template holds the notice | R-LIT-04 |
| BR9 | A held or unserved result that cannot be written to the decision log does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR10 | Which notice types are statutory is a list held as reference data | Principle 1; LOV-NOTICE |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| In progress | Offer or notice sent to the customer | WIN acknowledges the notice | Waiting customer |
| In progress | Deviation flagged or legal hold placed | Contact stop or legal hold found at the check | On hold (set by P3 under R-DEV-01 or R-UNI-20; this story holds the notice only) |

The case status moves are made by P3 on the events the dispatch loop raises. The owning services change the notice state: Approved to Sent, Approved to Held, Sent to Delivered, Sent to Unserved (DELIVERY_FAILED, PROOF_WINDOW_EXPIRED).

The harness changes no state itself. It seeds through the owning services' published operations, drives the 16:00 window and the two file fixtures, and then asserts the states the owners reached: notice Approved, Sent, Held, Delivered and Unserved, and the case status Waiting customer or On hold. A state the harness set by hand would prove nothing, so the report names the owner and the operation that made each move.

| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Reads the notice, its dispatch and its proof through the rwb-comms contract; owns the journey case for the run |
| RW-CONDUCT, Conduct and QA officer | Reads the blocked contacts on the ledger for AC4 |
| RW-HEADLIT and roles with Litigation R | Read the same journey evidence |
| QA lead | Owns the harness configuration, the fixtures, the report shape and the pass or fail gate |
| Integration lead | Owns the harness code, the stub set and the swap from a fake to the real service |
| The owning services' identities | rwb-comms, rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-access and rwb-decision make every state change the harness asserts; rwb-integration and rwb-comms run the 16:00 window |
| No approval level from the delegation of authority applies | The harness takes no business decision; notice approval is RWB-P7-E2014-APP |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test runner and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices` | P6 rwb-comms | Request the journey notice and read back its state (AC1, AC4, AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}` | P6 rwb-comms | Read the notice, its barcode, its sent date, its call-back date and its delivery status (AC1, AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | Case status and legal hold before and after the run (AC1, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` | P3 rwb-case | The NOTICE_PERIOD timer and its start date (AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` | P1 rwb-source-data | The ledger entry, its conduct check and its summary (AC1, AC4, AC5) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Role, scope and authority check for each call, including the refusal path (AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | P7 rwb-decision | The decision entry for a held notice and the rule that produced it (AC4) |

The contact point and consent read is the rwb-source-data contract operation named in RWB-P1-E2021-APP; its path is not restated here. Every operation is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with a 2 s budget and a circuit breaker per downstream (DP-11, DP-13); where a screen would compose them, the harness calls the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). No operation is invented in this story.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; it consumes the owner's events and writes its report to the wave record.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` (EV-14) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 rwb-comms | Assert the dispatch fact for AC1 |
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` (EV-15) | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 rwb-comms | Assert the delivery fact and the status DELIVERED for AC2 |

Both events carry IDs and business facts only, keyed by caseId, and the harness asserts that no personal data is present (DP-09).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness exercises the existing JOB-10 WIN notices run, a Temporal Schedule in rwb-comms that opens the Airflow file window at 16:00, and the JOB-11 Outbox sender run, the outbox relay in every service, and asserts their effects through the services' contracts and the owner's topic (DP-10). No workflow, activity or Schedule is created, changed or owned by this story.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added. JOB-10 WIN notices at 16:00, the Schedule in rwb-comms with the Airflow file window, is exercised on the business date under test only, and no cron, overlap policy or catch-up window is set by this story (DP-10).

None. The harness owns no schema and no table (DP-01); it reads and writes through the owning services' contracts, and the ledger is rwb-source-data's (DP-18).

The platform H dependencies in the table above (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are delivered by the platform waves and are not repeated in the metadata H field of this story, which stays empty. The blocking dependencies are the six I stories: RWB-P7-E2014-APP, RWB-P6-E2021-APP, RWB-P1-E2021-APP, RWB-P4-E2021-APP, RWB-P3-E2021-APP and RWB-P7-E2021-APP. Each one replaces its fake; until it is live the run uses the stub, and a stub pass is reported as a stub pass.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Job | Runs the four owned criteria in order for a business date and holds the run lock |
| StubSet | Fake | The five WireMock stubs generated from the published contracts, with the contract version pinned |
| WinFileFixture | Fixture | The INT-14 WIN letters drop and the WIN acknowledgment, keyed by barcode and business date |
| ProofFileFixture | Fixture | The INT-15 proof rows, keyed by barcode, with result DELIVERED, REFUSED or UNDELIVERABLE |
| WindowControl | Service | Moves the JOB-10 16:00 window in the environment under test and triggers the Airflow file window |
| EventProbe | Service | Consumes `rwb.comms.events.v1` and asserts EV-14 and EV-15 for the case |
| EvidenceReport | Service | Writes the per-run report keyed by story and business date, and holds the pass or fail gate |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, against the fakes from Day 1 and the real services as the I stories land, on the case `RC-2026-000321` and the notice `N-0101` of the legacy criteria plus the deviation, contact point and consent rows those criteria need. The environment, the seeding set and the evidence retention are not specified in the source documents (GAP-0404; ASM-0579). Seeding uses only the owning services' published operations, never a schema write.

**Build steps**

1. Generate the five stubs from the published contracts and pin each contract version in the run report; fail the run on a version mismatch (X1, X9).
2. Build the two file fixtures and the window control, and prove the drop and the read-back for one business date (X2, X3).
3. Build the JourneyRunner for AC1: request the notice, hold the 16:00 window, drop the WIN fixture, read the acknowledgment, assert Sent with the barcode and the ledger entry with conduct check PASSED.
4. Add the EventProbe for EV-14 and EV-15 and assert the key and the absence of personal data (X4).
5. Add AC2: drop the INT-15 DELIVERED row, assert Delivered with the call-back date, the ledger entry and the NOTICE_PERIOD timer started on the delivery date and not on the sent date (X7).
6. Add AC4: seed the open X1 deviation with the contact stop, assert Held with CONTACT_STOP_X1, BLOCKED on the ledger, one R-LIT-05 decision entry, the MSG-P6-001 route and the notice absent from the WIN fixture (X5).
7. Add AC5: seed the WITHDRAWN postal consent on the statutory type, assert the notice in the WIN file and PASSED with the statutory summary (X6).
8. Add the access path through `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise`, including the refusal for a caller outside the case scope (X8).
9. Add the EvidenceReport and the gate, then swap one stub for its real service as each I story lands and rerun the four criteria.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.comms.win-dispatch-loop`, the legacy flag of this behaviour, is on for the environment under test so the dispatch loop runs as the release will.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass for the four owned criteria; the four criteria pass against the five fakes on Day 1 and again, one at a time, against each real service as its I story lands; and the wave entry check holds a run report keyed by story and business date with the contract and fixture versions named.

The harness produces none of these messages itself; it asserts the message the owning service returns and names the message ID in the report, so a run failure points at a service and a message and not only at a date.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the proof window, the statutory notice types, the eligible states, the fixture contents and the result code mappings are data.
- No personal data in logs, fixtures, reports, tests or prompts: the ledger summaries carry codes and barcodes, and the events are asserted for the absence of personal data.
- No read of another service's tables: every read and every seed goes through the owning contract (DP-01), and the ledger is rwb-source-data's (DP-18).
- One hop and a 2 s budget per call, with a circuit breaker per downstream, so the harness fails where a screen would (DP-11).
- A stub pass is never reported as a real-service pass: the report names the contract version and whether the hop was a stub or the owner.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and it never sets a notice, case, timer or decision state by hand.
- A failing criterion is fixed in the service that owns it or reported as a gap; it is never waived in the script.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-022 for rwb-comms. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the message-dispatch operation of rwb-comms — `POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/messages` with its `MessageRequest`, its 202 `Interaction` answer, its refusal envelope, its delivery status list, its Idempotency-Key answer, its decision-record and event envelopes and its contract fakes — together with the consumed contact-point, case, reference-data and deviation shapes of their owners**, so that **the app, operations and integration stories of this legacy key build against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1, and a field rename, a status value or a message ID can never drift between rwb-comms, rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-deviation and rwb-decision without a failing build**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). The capability of RWB-E2-022 answers one request and then waits for another system to answer twice: the send is accepted with a reference, and the delivery arrives later as a result for that reference. That is the part most likely to drift silently. A renamed `conductCheck` value, a status the reader does not know, or a 409 whose message ID changes from MSG-P6-001 to MSG-P6-002 would not fail a build; it would show the wrong reason on SCR-03 and record the wrong refusal in the central decision ledger.

The baseline also fixes the naming the checks require: schema `rwb_comms`, REST base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`, topic `rwb.comms.events.v1`, queue `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms`. It records that this capability publishes no new `rwb.comms.*` event — Architecture v5 slide 17 names only `NoticeGenerated`, `NoticeDispatched` and `NoticeDelivered`, and a message is not a notice — and that its one published event is `DecisionRecorded` on the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03).

Three things stay deliberately open in this baseline and are carried as non-blocking dependencies: the shapes of the ACE notification path (INT-17, INT-18), the operation names of the P1 contact point and failed-count element, and whether the case facts arrive through the case read or the authorise answer. Each is faked, each is tagged, and each is replaced by its owner as the wave 2 stories land.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the document, topic and event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the retry and `.dlt` topic convention are the platform baseline (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The template catalog contract of rwb-comms (`RWB-P6-E1046-CON`) is published, so the template reference a message names has one owner document.
- The notice contract of rwb-comms (`RWB-P6-E1052-CON`) is published, so this document can state that a message produces no notice and adds nothing to the notice resource.
- The operations and their owners are taken from the Ownership Map only; this document never declares another service's operation as provided.
- The ACE notification path request and result shapes are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1069; ASM-2017), so the two call shapes of 12.4 are stated as placeholders and carried by the fake of 12.8.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the additive change to the rwb-comms OpenAPI 3.1 document: the `POST /cases/{caseId}/messages` operation, the `MessageRequest` schema and the `Interaction` schema.
2. Fix the one answer the operation returns and the seven refusal conditions, each with its status code and its message ID, including the two that gateway-bff answers before the call.
3. Fix the delivery status list of a message and state that it is not LOV-DELIVERY, which stays the WIN proof-of-delivery list.
4. State the Idempotency-Key rule: the key is required on the POST, the answer is stored, and a repeated key returns the first answer without a second send.
5. Record the consumed operations with their owner, their use and the 2 s budget, and map every failure of a consumed call to the envelope and a message ID or to a refusal closed.
6. Record the event elements: `DecisionRecorded` on the shared topic as the only published element, the three consumed events, and the statement that no new comms event is declared.
7. Record the absence of a workflow and of a Schedule, because the retry is the platform outbox relay JOB-11 and this capability registers neither.
8. Publish the nine contract tables of section 12 and the four contract fakes, then the contract tests: schema validation, the refusal matrix, the status list, the idempotency answer, the drift between a fake and the document, and the absence of a new comms event.
9. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P6-E2022-APP, RWB-P6-E2022-OPS and the wave 2 harness RWB-ITG-E2022-ITG.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X2 | A field is renamed, removed or retyped within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X3 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC9 |
| X4 | A delivery status outside the list arrives from the ACE notification path | The result is not applied and the document is the reference; a new value needs an additive change and the path owner's agreement | None | AC6 |
| X5 | The ACE notification path publishes no shape | The two call shapes stay placeholders, carried by the fake and by the gap; the baseline is still published | None | AC4, AC5 |
| X6 | A consumed contract names no operation for the element rwb-comms needs | The row carries the gap and the assumption and the fake is derived from the owner's published document | None | AC8 |
| X7 | The document declares a new `rwb.comms.*` event for a message | The absence test fails: the only publisher of that topic is the notice capability | None | AC8 |
| X8 | The document declares a Schedule or a workflow for the retry | The absence test fails: the retry is the platform relay JOB-11 | None | AC8 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the two same-service contracts it extends and the Ownership Map only |
| Negotiable | Field-level lengths and optionality are settled with the consumers; the operation, the seven refusal conditions, the status list and the event statement are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app, operations and integration stories of this legacy key on Day 1 and every consumer of the message and its delivery status |
| Estimable | One document, three schemas, four consumed rows, nine contract tables, four fakes and seven contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

    Then a missing channel or template answers 422 with MSG-GEN-001 naming the field
