These nine criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only; they restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P6-E2022-APP or RWB-ITG-E2022-ITG. The wave 2 harness `RWB-ITG-E2022-ITG` consumes this baseline and copies none of these criteria.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every outbound message carries a conduct check result on its ledger entry | REQ-OCC-005; FEAT-OCC-05 |
| BR2 | No message is sent while a contact stop is in force | CTL-16; R-UNI-04, R-UNI-05 |
| BR3 | Deviation codes that block SMS and LINE are a reference list; X6 blocks both until a contact point is verified | R-DEV-16; R-UNI-12; Principle 1 |
| BR4 | Messages go only to a verified contact point with consent GIVEN for that channel | CTL-17; R-UNI-10 |
| BR5 | A legal hold stops every outbound action | R-UNI-20 |
| BR6 | A system that is unavailable queues the send and retries; after the limit it goes to the exception queue | R-UNI-33, R-UNI-34, R-UNI-36 |
| BR7 | A refusal that cannot be written to the decision log is not completed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR8 | Only the current Approved template for the channel is used | R-LIT-03; CTL-14 |
| BR9 | The same request twice sends one message | R-UNI-40 |
| BR10 | A message raised by a route rule — the offer letter of R-RES-09 — is outside this contract; this operation answers only a person's request | R-RES-09; legacy section 19 |
| BR11 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/comms/v1`; the document never declares another service's path as provided | DP-13; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR12 | Event names are `rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1` on the topic `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, with retry and `.dlt` topics; the one published element of this capability is `DecisionRecorded` on the shared topic | DP-03, DP-14; Architecture v5 slides 17 and 42 |
| BR13 | A read declares no Idempotency-Key; a POST declares it and stores its response | Architecture v5 slide 11; DP-09 |
| BR14 | A schema change is additive within a major version; a breaking change is a new major version, and the delivery status list is closed unless it changes additively with the path owner's agreement | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |
| BR15 | No business value is fixed in the contract: the blocking deviation codes, the result-code maps, the attempt limit and the templates stay data | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR16 | No personal data is declared in a schema, an example or a fake: the contact point is a token, and the message body and the addressee are never in a payload | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; legacy section 17 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The operation, the three schemas, the refusal matrix and the status list are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app, operations and integration stories and the P1, P3, S8 and P7 owners accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A field is added within major version 1, for example a new template reference | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A field is removed, renamed or retyped, or a published status value changes meaning | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A new comms event or a Schedule is declared | The absence test of AC8 fails | In review |

The message lifecycle itself — QUEUED, SENT, DELIVERED, READ, FAILED, EXCEPTION — is owned by RWB-P6-E2022-APP and is described there; this baseline fixes only the status values and the answer shapes it declares.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-comms | Owns the OpenAPI and AsyncAPI documents and the fakes; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version and the resolution of the ACE notification path gap |
| Consuming teams (app, operations, integration, and the rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-deviation and rwb-decision owners) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| Platform library owner | Owns the CloudEvents envelope, the error envelope, the Idempotency-Key rule and the naming rule this document reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field is declared in an event, an answer or an example, and owns the NSS and LINE OA result-code maps |

The Case record right C the operation applies is declared by the operation itself. TSD P6 T6.1 is the only source for the letters, and DP-08 is not in the pattern set of this legacy key, so the declaration of the right sits at gateway-bff and the reconciliation is carried by GAP-1075 and ASM-2023. The per-service login name behind the document's security scheme is not part of this baseline; the document names the scheme "the rwb-comms login (DP-02)".

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| `MessageRequest` | `channel` with the values SMS and LINE and required, `templateCode` required, `language` with TH and EN and default TH, `partyId` defaulting to the borrower; the legacy names these four and no others |
| `Interaction` | `id`, `caseId`, `partyId`, `occurredAt`, `channel`, `direction`, `conductCheck`, `summary`, `sourceSystem`, `deliveryStatus`, `externalRef` |
| `conductCheck` | `PASSED` and `BLOCKED` |
| `deliveryStatus` | `SENT`, `DELIVERED`, `FAILED` and, for LINE, `READ`; explicitly not LOV-DELIVERY |
| Event payloads | IDs, codes, dates and counts only; no name, no phone number, no LINE identifier, no message body and no addressee |
| Idempotency | The key of the POST and the stored answer, in `idempotency_key` of schema `rwb_comms` |

The field-level types, lengths and required flags beyond the legacy statement are settled in the baseline review and are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1073; ASM-2021); this story fixes the names, the two closed value lists and the one allowed answer of the POST.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-comms (P6); base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`.

| Method | Path | API ID | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/messages` | API-P6-008 | `MessageRequest` → 202 `Interaction`; the seven refusal conditions of AC3 | Case record C, scope applied | Idempotency-Key header, response stored |

The document declares no read operation for a message: the API specification of this module lists API-P6-001 to API-P6-011 only, and the message and its status are read through the P1 interaction on the case timeline route (GAP-1070; ASM-2018).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Call | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|
| Contact point of a party for a channel — the operation named in RWB-P1-E1066-CON | P1 rwb-source-data | The contact type, the token, consent GIVEN and the verified flag; faked. The operation name and its fields are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1070; ASM-2018) |
| Record a failed contact — the operation named in RWB-P1-E1066-CON | P1 rwb-source-data | The failed count after a FAILED result; faked, and the element is not named in the published contract (GAP-1070) |
| `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The legal hold and the deviation flag; faked. Not in this key's Contract dependencies (GAP-1075) |
| Reference data for LOV-CHANNEL — the contract of RWB-P3-E1043-CON | P3 rwb-case | `SMS` and `LINE` as data rows (DP-07); faked |
| `GET /api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations` | S8 rwb-deviation | The open deviation with its contact stop and its code; faked only |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker, and a GET is retried once with jitter (DP-11, ADR-020). The refusal's decision record is a write through the local decision-record library (DP-03), listed in 12.3 and not in this table.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Schema element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (event 08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | decision record reference, the decision code (the deviation code on a refusal), the final call, the case ID, the decided-at time, the rule and its version where one applied; no personal data; written by the local library in the same transaction and relayed by the outbox |

New `rwb.comms.*` events for this capability: None. `rwb.comms.events.v1` carries `NoticeGenerated`, `NoticeDispatched` and `NoticeDelivered` and nothing else in this story, because a message is not a notice (Architecture v5 slide 17).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Consumer contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` (event 06) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | caseId, deviation code, raised at, contact stop flag; keeps the blocking list current when the case read degrades |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` (event 07) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | caseId, deviation code, cleared at, outcome; releases the block |
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` (event 05) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | caseId, previous and new state, changed at; the consumer group of `rwb-comms` keeps the case projection the conduct check reads |

Each subscription has its retry topic and its `.dlt` topic, and the consumer dedupes through `processed_event` in schema `rwb_comms` (DP-09).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The send is a synchronous REST request whose durability is the outbox row; this baseline registers no workflow, no activity and no child workflow on task queue `rwb-comms`.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-11 Outbox sender is the platform's outbox relay, every minute, with every service as its owner (Architecture v5 slide 44). The legacy story called the same job the sender to the ACE notification path with a retry limit of 5, and the reconciliation of the two readings is carried by GAP-1071 and ASM-2019; this baseline registers no Schedule, no cron entry and no job name.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| template | P6 (rwb_comms) | The current Approved version for a channel and a language |
| notice | P6 (rwb_comms) | Not written for a message: a message produces no notice |
| merge_field | P6 (rwb_comms) | The merge codes the template may use |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_comms | The send request, the inbox of the three consumed events and the stored answer of the POST |

`interaction` and `contact_point_ext` are P1's, `recovery_case` and `task` are P3's, `deviation` is S8's and `decision_log_entry` is P7's; the contract names them only as consumed answers (DP-01, DP-18).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-source-data WireMock | The verified `MOBILE` contact point of `P-0077` with consent `GIVEN` and failed count 0, the `MOBILE` contact point with consent `WITHDRAWN` for the 409 of MSG-P6-002, the verified `LINE` contact point, the accepted failed-count update and a delayed answer beyond 2 s | App story, operations smoke profile, contract tests |
| rwb-case WireMock | `GET /cases/{caseId}` for `RC-2026-000777` with legal hold false, then true; a case outside the scope; a delayed answer beyond 2 s | App story, operations smoke profile, contract tests |
| rwb-deviation WireMock | The open deviation `X1` with contact stop on, the open deviation `X6`, an empty answer and a delayed answer beyond 2 s | App story, contract tests |
| ACE notification path stub | An accepted reference `NSS-7781` with `DELIVERED`, a `FAILED` result, the LINE `DELIVERED` then `READ`, and `unavailable` for six attempts; the NSS and LINE OA result-code maps as data | App story, operations smoke profile, integration harness |

The exact shapes of the ACE notification path and of the P1 contact-point and failed-count elements are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1069, GAP-1070; ASM-2017, ASM-2018); every fake is derived from the owner's published document or from the legacy interface name, and is replaced by the real service as its story lands.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 provided, 5 consumed | The send operation provided; the contact point, the failed-count update, the case, the reference data and the deviation read consumed; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 1 declared as published by its owner, 3 consumed | `DecisionRecorded` on the shared topic; `DeviationRaised`, `DeviationCleared` and `CaseStateChanged`; no new comms event |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, no activity and no Schedule; JOB-11 is the platform relay |
| File | None | No file in this contract |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The additive change to `openapi/rwb-comms-v1.yaml`, the `MessageRequest` and `Interaction` schemas with the two closed value lists, the AsyncAPI fragment of `rwb.comms.events.v1` that confirms `NoticeGenerated`, `NoticeDispatched` and `NoticeDelivered` and adds nothing, the contract README rows for the refusal matrix, the Idempotency-Key rule, the status list and the absent elements, and the four WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_comms`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/comms/v1` | none |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-19 is claimed because the operation is reached through the gateway-bff route behind SCR-03 and the two refusals of the route are declared here; DP-10 only because the retry path is JOB-11 and no Schedule is registered.

**Build steps**

1. Add the operation, the `MessageRequest` schema and the two closed value lists; validate the additive rule in the pipeline.
2. Write the `Interaction` schema and the rule that the answer is the only representation of a message this module publishes.
3. Write the refusal matrix as a schema constraint and a README row, one condition to one status and one message ID, including the two answered at gateway-bff.
4. Record the Idempotency-Key rule and the stored answer.
5. Record the five consumed rows with their owner, their budget and the two gap rows.
6. Record the event rows and the absent elements, and add the absence test for a new comms event, a Schedule and a workflow.
7. Publish the four fakes and the seven contract tests; a drift between a fake and the document fails the build.
8. Baseline tag and the consumer sign-off note, including the P1, P3, S8 and P7 owners and the wave 2 harness.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI and AsyncAPI artefacts validate in the pipeline, the seven contract tests pass, the four fakes answer every consumed shape and the drift test is green, and the app, operations and integration stories have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P6-001 | A contact stop applies | Contact with this customer is stopped for {reason}. |
| MSG-P6-002 | No consent for the channel | The customer has not consented to {channel}. Use another channel. |
| MSG-P6-003 | The template is withdrawn | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-P3-004 | A legal hold is on the case | This case is on hold for {deviation}. The prescription date is still {date}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks Case record C on the route | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Channel or template missing | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | NSS or LINE OA is unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The message IDs are contract elements; the text is the agreed text taken unchanged from the legacy story, and the {system} value of MSG-GEN-006 is fixed by the consumed row that failed.

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves the Send message action of SCR-03 Case record in its editable and refused states, the message row of SCR-04 Case timeline in its Loading and filtered states, and the send row of SCR-09 Exception queue, all through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). This baseline fixes the operation's request and answer and the refusal matrix only; the screen field list, the composite route specification and the masking of the contact point belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and to RWB-P6-E1052-CON's screen stories.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the blocking deviation codes, the result-code maps, the attempt limit, the templates and the languages stay data, reference data or service configuration.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: the contact point is a token, the message body and the addressee are never in a payload, and no name, address or identity number is declared.
- The contract names only rwb-comms tables and only the one operation owned by rwb-comms; the P1, P3, S8 and P7 elements are consumed and faked, never declared as provided (DP-01).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- No new comms event is declared for a message, and no absence test is relaxed: a release that adds one fails the build.
- No Schedule and no workflow is declared: the retry is the platform relay JOB-11, and the message lifecycle is the outbox row.
- Every example in the document is synthetic; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The error envelope, the CloudEvents envelope, the Idempotency-Key rule and the naming rule come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-022 for rwb-comms in the 19-service realignment. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **messages sent from approved templates through NSS and the LINE official account, with the contact rules applied before sending and the delivery status on the case**, so that **the customer is reached on the channel they use and every contact is recorded**.

This story is the rwb-comms part of legacy RWB-E2-022. It builds one operation — `POST /cases/{caseId}/messages` on base `/api/recovery/comms/v1` — with the conduct check, the outbox row, the recording of the refusal in the local decision record, the mapping of the NSS and LINE OA results onto the delivery status, and the screen action behind SCR-03 and SCR-04. It builds no case state, no ledger table and no direct call to NSS or LINE OA.

##### 2. Business rationale

Case owners send SMS and LINE messages outside the Workbench today, so a message can reach a customer under a contact stop or without consent, and the case has no record of it. This story sends from Legal-approved templates through the ACE notification path (INT-17, INT-18), refuses a message when a contact stop, a legal hold or missing consent applies, and records every attempt and its delivery result. It serves REQ-OCC-004, REQ-OCC-005, REQ-OCC-006 and REQ-ILG-010, and controls CTL-16 and CTL-17.

The realignment changes the path, not the business. The monolith called NSS and LINE OA from one module and wrote the interaction into its own schema. In the target, rwb-comms calls only the ACE notification path (REQ-DRI-006), the contact point, its consent and its failed count belong to rwb-source-data (DP-05, DP-18), the case and its legal hold belong to rwb-case, the deviation that carries the contact stop belongs to rwb-deviation, and the decision record is written to the local library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03). This story therefore calls one contract of rwb-source-data and one read of rwb-case, publishes the decision record, and writes no other service's table.

**Where the other criteria of the legacy key are owned.** This story owns AC2, AC4, AC8, AC9 and AC11. AC1, AC3, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC10 and AC12 are owned by the wave 2 integration story `RWB-ITG-E2022-ITG`, which proves the same values across rwb-comms, rwb-source-data, rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision against the ACE notification path test profile; they are not copied here. The contract baseline of the operation is `RWB-P6-E2022-CON`, the deployment of its egress, retry and operator surfaces is `RWB-P6-E2022-OPS`, and the other criteria of the legacy key are answered in the same wave by the reads of RWB-P1-E2022-APP, RWB-P4-E2022-APP and RWB-P7-E2022-APP.

##### 3. Preconditions

- `RWB-P6-E2022-CON` is published: the request and answer shapes of `POST /cases/{caseId}/messages`, the refusal envelope, the delivery status list, the Idempotency-Key rule, the event envelopes and the fakes (DP-11).
- `RWB-P6-E1052-APP` is delivered, so notices, templates and the template catalog of `rwb_comms` exist and a current Approved template can be resolved for a channel and a language.
- `RWB-P1-E1066-CON` is published for the contact point, its consent, its verified flag and its failed count. The exact operation names for the failed-count update and for the consent and verified fields are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1070; ASM-2018).
- `RWB-P3-E1043-CON` is published for the reference data of LOV-CHANNEL (DP-07), so `SMS` and `LINE` are data rows and not values in code.
- The case facts the conduct check needs — the legal hold and the open deviation with the contact stop — arrive through the rwb-case case read, and the deviation facts also arrive as `DeviationRaised` and `DeviationCleared` (DP-09). The case read is not in this story's Contract dependencies and the area and right of the refusal are declared at gateway-bff, because DP-08 is not in the pattern set of this legacy key (GAP-1075; ASM-2023).
- The decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` are live (DP-03, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON), and the outbox and inbox library is live in schema `rwb_comms` (DP-09, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON).
- The ACE notification path to NSS and LINE OA is available in the environment (legacy DL30), and its request and result shapes are carried by the stub of section 12.8 until the path publishes them (GAP-1069; ASM-2017).
- The blocking deviation codes per channel, the NSS result-code map, the LINE OA status map and the attempt limit are reference data or service configuration; the legacy names the retry limit as 5 and rule R-UNI-34 (GAP-1071; ASM-2019).
- The sender holds RW-CASEOWN or another role with Case record C, and the case is in the sender's scope; the right is declared at gateway-bff and refused with MSG-P4-002 or MSG-P4-003.
- No secret, phone number, LINE identifier or message body is written to a log, an event or a workflow input: the number and the identifier stay tokens (legacy section 17).

##### 4. Flow

1. The case owner opens SCR-03 Case record through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) and chooses Send message, the channel (SMS or LINE), the template and the party.
2. gateway-bff declares the Case record right C, the scope and the session, and calls `POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/messages` with an Idempotency-Key; a role without the right is refused there with MSG-P4-002.
3. rwb-comms: the idempotency store of schema `rwb_comms` is read for the key; a key already answered returns the stored answer and no second send is attempted.
4. rwb-comms: the case read of rwb-case is taken once (one hop, 2 s) for the legal hold and the deviation flag, and the active deviations are taken from the `DeviationRaised` and `DeviationCleared` state of the inbox when the case read degrades; a missing case answer refuses the send closed.
5. rwb-comms: the current template for the channel and the language is resolved from `template` (a current Approved version for LOV-CHANNEL `SMS` or `LINE`); a withdrawn template with no later Approved version is refused with MSG-P6-003.
6. rwb-comms: the conduct check runs — legal hold on the case, open deviation with contact stop, open deviation in the blocking list of the channel, and consent GIVEN on a verified contact point of that channel read once through the P1 contract.
7. rwb-comms: a failed check writes the decision record through the local library, writes the refusal as a `BLOCKED` entry through the P1 ledger operation and answers 409 with MSG-P6-001, MSG-P6-002, MSG-P6-003 or MSG-P3-004; nothing is written to the outbox.
8. rwb-comms: a passed check merges the template, writes the `PASSED` interaction through the P1 ledger operation with delivery status SENT and the external reference empty, and writes the send request to `outbox_event` in the same transaction (DP-09); the answer is 202 with the interaction.
9. The platform outbox relay (JOB-11, every minute) hands the outbox row to the P6 sender, which calls the ACE notification path with the contact point token, the template reference, the language and the case reference (INT-17 for SMS, INT-18 for LINE). No Temporal Schedule is registered by this story.
10. The ACE notification path returns an accepted reference, which the sender stores on the interaction as the external reference and which moves the outbox row from queued to sent.
11. The ACE notification path reports the result for that reference — the NSS result code, or the LINE delivered and then read — and rwb-comms maps it to DELIVERED, READ or FAILED on the interaction; a FAILED result raises the failed count of the contact point by one through the P1 contract.
12. An unavailable path leaves the row queued for the next window; at the attempt limit of 5 the row moves to the exception state under R-UNI-34 and the interaction is FAILED.
13. The case owner sees the message and its status on SCR-04 Case timeline, read from the P1 interaction through the case timeline route; SCR-09 Exception queue lists the sends in the exception state.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The case has an open X6 lost contact | Refused and logged | MSG-P6-001 | AC3, owned by RWB-ITG-E2022-ITG |
| X2 | An open deviation has the contact stop on | Refused and logged | MSG-P6-001 | AC4 |
| X3 | No consent GIVEN on the channel | Refused and logged | MSG-P6-002 | AC5, owned by RWB-ITG-E2022-ITG |
| X4 | The template is withdrawn | Refused | MSG-P6-003 | AC6, owned by RWB-ITG-E2022-ITG |
| X5 | NSS or LINE OA is unavailable | Queued and retried; after the attempt limit to the exception state, then the exception queue | MSG-GEN-006 | AC7, owned by RWB-ITG-E2022-ITG |
| X6 | NSS returns a failure code | Interaction FAILED; the contact point failed count raised through the P1 contract | None | AC8 |
| X7 | The same request with the same Idempotency-Key | One message only; the first answer is returned | None | AC9 |
| X8 | The decision record cannot be written on a refusal | Nothing sent; the refusal is not completed; request refused; incident | MSG-P7-003 | AC10, owned by RWB-ITG-E2022-ITG |
| X9 | A legal hold is on the case | Refused and logged | MSG-P3-004 | AC11 |
| X10 | No channel given | Refused | MSG-GEN-001 | AC12, owned by RWB-ITG-E2022-ITG |
| X11 | The rwb-case case read does not answer inside the 2 s budget | The send is refused closed: no message leaves, no outbox row is written, and the caller is told the case could not be read; one entry records the degraded read | MSG-GEN-006 | AC11, ASM-2023 |
| X12 | The P1 contact point answer does not arrive inside the 2 s budget | The conduct check cannot answer PASSED, so the send is refused closed with MSG-GEN-006 and nothing leaves | MSG-GEN-006 | AC8, ASM-2018 |
| X13 | The P1 failed-count update fails after a FAILED result | The interaction keeps FAILED and the update is retried from the same delivery result; a duplicate is absorbed by the P1 operation and by the inbox of `rwb_comms` | None | AC8, ASM-2018 |
| X14 | The delivery result arrives for a reference rwb-comms does not know | The result is not applied and is kept for the exception count; no interaction is invented | None | AC2, GAP-1072 |
| X15 | A read of a message is asked for | There is no read operation for a message in the API specification of this module; the message and its status are read from the P1 interaction through the case timeline route | None | AC9, GAP-1070 |

The five criteria above are copied from legacy section 7 with every line, ID and value kept, each tagged with its origin. The cross-service line added inside a scenario is the mock of the owner's published contract with the same values the legacy line already fixed; no business value is added. AC1, AC3, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC10 and AC12 of the legacy key are owned by `RWB-ITG-E2022-ITG` and are not copied here.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every outbound message carries a conduct check result on its ledger entry | REQ-OCC-005; FEAT-OCC-05 |
| BR2 | No message is sent while a contact stop is in force | CTL-16; R-UNI-04, R-UNI-05 |
| BR3 | Deviation codes that block SMS and LINE are a reference list; X6 blocks both until a contact point is verified | R-DEV-16; R-UNI-12; Principle 1 |
| BR4 | Messages go only to a verified contact point with consent GIVEN for that channel | CTL-17; R-UNI-10 |
| BR5 | A legal hold stops every outbound action | R-UNI-20 |
| BR6 | A system that is unavailable queues the send and retries; after the limit it goes to the exception queue | R-UNI-33, R-UNI-34, R-UNI-36 |
| BR7 | A refusal that cannot be written to the decision log is not completed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR8 | Only the current Approved template for the channel is used | R-LIT-03; CTL-14 |
| BR9 | The same request twice sends one message | R-UNI-40 |
| BR10 | A message raised automatically by a route rule — the offer letter of R-RES-09 — is sent by the rule's owning stage in Epic 3, never by this operation; this operation sends only on a person's request | R-RES-09; legacy section 19 |
| BR11 | No direct call to NSS or LINE OA: every send and every result goes through the ACE notification path (INT-17, INT-18) | REQ-DRI-006; legacy section 17 |
| BR12 | The interaction ledger is rwb-source-data's (DP-18) and the contact point with its failed count is its `contact_point_ext`; rwb-comms reads and writes both only through the P1 contract and never touches `rwb_source_data` | DP-01, DP-05, DP-18 |
| BR13 | Every outbound message and every refusal writes one decision record through the local library in the same transaction, and a refusal that cannot be recorded is not completed | DP-03; R-UNI-39 |
| BR14 | One REST base per service — `/api/recovery/comms/v1` — one hop, a 2 s timeout and an Idempotency-Key on the POST; no business value, and no phone number, LINE identifier, message body or addressee, is carried in an event, a workflow input or a log | DP-11, DP-13; ADR-020; legacy section 17 |

##### 9. State transitions

None in the case. This story changes no case status: the case state machine is rwb-case's and the deviation state machine is rwb-deviation's. It sets the conduct check on the interaction — `PASSED` or `BLOCKED` — and the delivery status on the interaction and on the message lifecycle of the outbox row.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| no message | a send is requested on the case | the conduct check answers `PASSED` | QUEUED — the interaction and the outbox row are written in one transaction |
| no message | a send is requested on the case | the conduct check answers `BLOCKED` | REFUSED — 409 with MSG-P6-001, MSG-P6-002, MSG-P6-003 or MSG-P3-004, no outbox row, one decision record |
| QUEUED | the platform relay hands the row to the sender | the ACE notification path accepts the request | SENT — the accepted reference is stored as the external reference |
| SENT | a result arrives for the reference | `DELIVERED` on SMS, or `DELIVERED` on LINE | DELIVERED |
| SENT | a result arrives for the reference | `READ` on LINE | READ |
| SENT | a result arrives for the reference | `FAILED` on either channel | FAILED — the contact point failed count rises by one through P1 |
| QUEUED | the retry window finds the path unavailable | the attempt count is below 5 | QUEUED — the next window retries |
| QUEUED | the retry window finds the attempt count at 5 | R-UNI-34 | EXCEPTION — the row is in the exception state and SCR-09 lists it, and the interaction is FAILED |

`SENT`, `DELIVERED`, `READ` and `FAILED` are the message values of this story. They are not LOV-DELIVERY, which keeps the WIN proof-of-delivery values (GAP-1076; ASM-2024).

##### 10. Authority

The rights below are the Case record rights this story applies. The Case record area and right C are declared by the operation itself (API-P6-008, Case record C, scope applied); TSD P6 T6.1 is the only source used for the letters, and it declares two areas, Documents and Litigation, so the letter for each role is taken from its T6.1 row and the reconciliation of the Case record area is carried by GAP-1075.

| Who | Case record right used by this story | TSD P6 T6.1 row |
|---|---|---|
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | C — sends a message on a case in scope | Documents CRU; Litigation R |
| RW-PHONECOL, phone collector | R only — the send is refused with MSG-P4-002 | Documents R; Litigation none |
| RW-FIELDCOL, field collector | C | Documents CR |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | C (its T6.1 letters are CRUA) | Documents CRU; Litigation CRUA |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | R only — the send is refused with MSG-P4-002 | Documents R; Litigation none |
| SY-DECLOG, decision record writer | Writes the refusal and the pass record through the local library; no case right, a service identity | T6.2 service identities |

DP-08 is not in the pattern set of this legacy key, so the declaration of the right sits at gateway-bff on the composite route to SCR-03 and no rwb-access guard library is wired here; this story keeps a local guard on the refusal path that refuses closed when the right or the case answer is missing (GAP-1075; ASM-2023). No role in this story may grant itself a right.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Owner | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DF-REF-046, DF-REF-047, DF-REF-048, DF-REF-066, DF-REF-051 | template | template_code, template_version, language, channel, approved_by_legal | P6 (rwb_comms) | Read |
| DF-LEG-015, DF-LEG-016, DF-LEG-018 | notice | id, case_id, notice_type | P6 (rwb_comms) | Not read and not written by this story: a message produces no notice |
| DF-EXT-015 | contact_point_ext | consent_given | P1 (rwb_source_data) | Read through the P1 contract |
| DF-EXT-017 | contact_point_ext | verified_at | P1 (rwb_source_data) | Read through the P1 contract |
| DF-EXT-018 | contact_point_ext | failed_count | P1 (rwb_source_data) | Written through the P1 contract, never directly |
| DF-ACE-075, DF-ACE-077, DF-ACE-078 | contact point behind the P1 contract | contact_type, person_key, contact_value | P1 (rwb_source_data) | Read through the P1 contract as a token; the value never enters `rwb_comms` |
| DF-CAS-001, DF-CAS-020 | recovery_case | id, legal_hold | P3 (rwb_case) | Read through the P3 case read |
| DF-CAS-038, DF-CAS-043, DF-CAS-044 | deviation | deviation_code, contact_stop, cleared_at | S8 (rwb_deviation) | Read through the case read and the two deviation events |
| DF-INT-002 to DF-INT-006, DF-INT-011 to DF-INT-013, DF-INT-028, DF-INT-029 | interaction | case_id, person_key, occurred_at, channel, direction, summary, conduct_check, source_system, delivery_status, external_ref | P1 (rwb_source_data) | Written and read through the P1 contract only |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_log_entry | the refusal and the pass record | P7 (rwb_decision) | Written through the local decision-record library (DP-03) |

`rwb_comms` holds no message table. The message, its template reference and its addressee are not persisted in `rwb_comms`: the interaction is rwb-source-data's and the content leaves the service inside the call to the ACE notification path. The one row this capability could write in its own schema is a `notice` row, and it writes none, because a message is not a notice. The record of a message for the case timeline is therefore the P1 interaction, which carries no template field (GAP-1077; ASM-2025). Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-comms (P6); base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`.

| Method | Path | API ID | Request | Answer | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/messages` | API-P6-008 | `MessageRequest`: channel (SMS or LINE), template, language, party; field-level detail Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1073; ASM-2021) | 202 `Interaction`: interaction id, channel, direction, conduct check, delivery status, reference, plus the case and party identifiers | Case record C, scope applied | Idempotency-Key header, response stored |

Errors: 401 no session; 403 the role lacks Case record C (MSG-P4-002); 404 the case is outside the scope (MSG-P4-003); 409 a contact stop (MSG-P6-001), no consent (MSG-P6-002), a withdrawn template (MSG-P6-003) or a legal hold (MSG-P3-004); 422 a field is missing (MSG-GEN-001); 503 the decision record could not be written (MSG-P7-003).

There is no read operation for a message in the API specification of this module (T-A.1 lists API-P6-001 to API-P6-011 only). The message and its status are read through the P1 interaction on the case timeline route, and SCR-09 is fed by the exception state of the outbox rows (GAP-1078; ASM-2026).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Call | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` contact points of a party for a channel — the P1 contract operation named in RWB-P1-E1066-CON | P1 rwb-source-data | The contact type, the token, consent GIVEN and the verified flag for the conduct check; faked. The operation name and the field names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1070; ASM-2018) |
| `POST` record a failed contact — the P1 contract operation named in RWB-P1-E1066-CON | P1 rwb-source-data | Raises the failed count by one after a FAILED result; faked. The operation is not named in the published contract (GAP-1070) |
| `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The legal hold and the deviation flag of the case; faked. Not in this story's Contract dependencies, so the fake is derived from the published P3 document (GAP-1075) |
| `GET` reference data for LOV-CHANNEL — the P3 reference-data contract of RWB-P3-E1043-CON | P3 rwb-case | `SMS` and `LINE` as data rows, never as values in code (DP-07); faked |
| `GET /api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations` | S8 rwb-deviation | The open deviation with its contact stop and its code, for the conduct check and for the refusal text; faked only, because the runtime path is the case read and the two deviation events (GAP-1075) |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker, and a GET is retried once with jitter (DP-11, ADR-020). The refusal's decision record is a write, not a read: it goes through the local decision-record library of the platform (DP-03, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, owner P7 rwb-decision) in the same transaction as the refusal and is relayed as `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` — see 12.3. This story reads no `rwb_source_data`, `rwb_case`, `rwb_deviation` or `rwb_decision` table (DP-01).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (event 08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | decision record reference, the decision code (the deviation code on a refusal), the final call, the rule and its version where one applied, the case ID and the decided-at time; written by the local library in the same transaction and relayed by the outbox |

New `rwb.comms.*` events for this capability: None. Architecture v5 slide 17 names only `NoticeGenerated`, `NoticeDispatched` and `NoticeDelivered` on `rwb.comms.events.v1`, and a message is not a notice, so this story publishes no new comms event and adds none to the AsyncAPI document of the topic. The delivery status is carried to the timeline through the P1 interaction, not through a comms event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Element used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` (event 06) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | case ID, deviation code, raised at, the contact stop flag; keeps the blocking list of the case current when the case read degrades |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` (event 07) | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | case ID, deviation code, cleared at, outcome; releases the block |
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` (event 05) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | case ID, previous and new state, the changed-at time; the consumer group of `rwb-comms` keeps the case projection the conduct check reads |

The three are consumed into the inbox of schema `rwb_comms` (`processed_event`), deduplicated by event ID, and each has its retry topic and its `.dlt` topic (DP-09). Their arrival is what lets the conduct check answer while the case read is degraded.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The send is a synchronous REST request whose durability is the outbox row, and the retry is the platform relay's window; this story registers no workflow, no activity and no child workflow on task queue `rwb-comms`. The refusal is a transaction, not a workflow step.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-11 Outbox sender is the platform's outbox relay, every minute, one owner for every service (Architecture v5 slide 44), and this story registers no Temporal Schedule, no cron entry and no job name. DP-10 is claimed because the legacy key's retry path is JOB-11 and the workflow kit is in the build dependency list; the send attempt itself is the P6 sender's code, called by the relay window. The legacy five-attempt limit and its exception-queue rule R-UNI-34 are applied inside that call (GAP-1071; ASM-2019).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| template | P6 (rwb_comms) | The current Approved version for a channel and a language |
| notice | P6 (rwb_comms) | Not written by this story: a message produces no notice |
| merge_field | P6 (rwb_comms) | The merge codes the template may use |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_comms | The send request, the inbox of the three consumed events and the stored answer of the POST |

Not owned and never written: `interaction` and `contact_point_ext` are P1's, `recovery_case` and `task` are P3's, `deviation` is S8's and `decision_log_entry` is P7's. rwb-comms holds no foreign key across services and no copy of a contact point, a case or a ledger entry (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-source-data WireMock | A verified `MOBILE` contact point for `P-0077` with consent `GIVEN` and failed count 0 → 202; a `MOBILE` contact point with consent `WITHDRAWN` → the 409 path of MSG-P6-002; a verified `LINE` contact point with consent `GIVEN`; the failed-count update answering accepted, and a delayed answer beyond 2 s | AC2, AC4, AC8, AC9, AC11; the operations smoke profile |
| rwb-case WireMock | `GET /cases/{caseId}` for `RC-2026-000777` with legal hold false, then legal hold true; a case outside the scope; an answer delayed beyond 2 s | AC11 and the refusal-closed path of X11 |
| rwb-deviation WireMock | The open deviation `X1` with contact stop on for `RC-2026-000777`; the open deviation `X6`; an empty answer; a delayed answer beyond 2 s | AC4; the contract tests of RWB-P6-E2022-CON |
| decision-record library stub | A healthy chain and outbox, and a stopped chain for the 503 path of MSG-P7-003 | X8, and the contract tests |
| ACE notification path stub, NSS | An accepted reference `NSS-7781` with result `DELIVERED`, then a `FAILED` result; an `unavailable` answer for six attempts | AC8 and the exception state of section 9 |
| ACE notification path stub, LINE OA | An accepted reference, then delivered and then read (`DELIVERED`, `READ`) | AC2 |

The exact shapes of the ACE notification path and of the P1 contact-point operation are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1069, GAP-1070; ASM-2017, ASM-2018); the stubs are derived from the legacy interface names and from the published P1 document, and each stub is replaced by its real owner as the wave 2 stories land.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 provided, 5 consumed | The send operation provided; the contact point, the failed-count update, the case read, the reference data and the deviation read consumed; one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 1 published, 3 consumed | `DecisionRecorded` published on the shared topic; `DeviationRaised`, `DeviationCleared` and `CaseStateChanged` consumed with retry and `.dlt` |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, no activity and no Schedule in this story; JOB-11 is the platform relay |
| File | None | Nothing is written to a file; the send is a REST call to the ACE notification path |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms`, module `messaging`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms.messaging`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_comms`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/comms/v1` | none |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 applies as a prohibition as well as a permission: this story reads no ACE view and no ACE table, because the contact point arrives through the P1 contract as a token. DP-10 is claimed for the relay dependency only; no Schedule is registered here.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| MessageController | Controller | `POST /cases/{caseId}/messages`, validation and the problem mapping for 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 |
| MessageService | Service | Template resolution, conduct check, merge, the interaction write and the outbox write in one transaction |
| ConductCheckService | Service | The legal hold, the contact stop, the channel blocking list and the consent check; shared with the letter capability of RWB-P6-E2021-APP |
| TemplateResolver | Service | The current Approved template for the channel and the language from `template`, with the withdrawn case answered MSG-P6-003 |
| MessageSender | Service | The send attempt the relay window calls: the call to the ACE notification path, the accepted reference and the attempt counter |
| MessageResultMapper | Service | Maps the NSS result code and the LINE OA status onto DELIVERED, READ or FAILED and raises the failed count through P1 |
| IdempotencyStore | Repository | The stored answer of the POST under its key, in `idempotency_key` |
| ContactPointReader | Service | The P1 contract read of the contact point, its consent, its verified flag and its failed count |
| CaseFactsReader | Service | The P3 case read of the legal hold and the deviation flag, with the degraded answer refused closed |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` in schema `rwb_comms`; reads `template` and `merge_field`.
- Migration in this story: `V2022_1__message_dispatch.sql` adds the index on `idempotency_key (key, created_at)` used by the stored-answer read and the index on `outbox_event (state, next_attempt_at)` used by the relay window. No table is created for a message.
- No row of `notice`, `interaction`, `contact_point_ext`, `recovery_case`, `deviation` or `decision_log_entry` is written by this story's migration, and none is written by its code except through the owners' contracts.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The blocking deviation codes per channel: X1, X2 and X3 when the contact stop is on, and X6 — data rows owned by the Conduct and QA officer, never values in code.
- The NSS result-code map to SENT, DELIVERED and FAILED, and the LINE OA status map to DELIVERED and READ — data rows owned by the data steward.
- The attempt limit of 5 and the exception-queue rule R-UNI-34 — service configuration read as data (GAP-1071; ASM-2019).
- The feature switch `rwb.comms.sms-line`, default off in DEV and on in SIT: off refuses the send closed with MSG-GEN-006 and sends nothing, and never allows a send by default.
- The login is the rwb-comms login (DP-02).

**Build steps**

1. MessageController and MessageService over the `RWB-P6-E2022-CON` document, with the idempotency store first; test AC9.
2. ConductCheckService with the legal hold, the contact stop, the blocking list and the consent check against the P1, P3 and deviation fakes; test AC4, AC11 and the refusal-closed paths of X11 and X12.
3. TemplateResolver with the current Approved rule and the withdrawn case; test the MSG-P6-003 path.
4. The refusal transaction: the decision record through the local library and the `BLOCKED` interaction through P1, ordered before the answer; test the MSG-P7-003 path.
5. MessageSender with the accepted reference, the attempt counter and the exception state at attempt 5; test the `unavailable` path against the path stub.
6. MessageResultMapper with the two maps as data and the failed-count call through P1; test AC2 and AC8.
7. The gateway-bff route behind SCR-03 and the timeline read of SCR-04 against the P1 fake; browser test of a send and of a refusal.
8. Contract-fake run of every cross-service answer in isolation, so the story builds before rwb-source-data, rwb-case and rwb-deviation are live in SIT.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.comms.sms-line`, read as service configuration; off refuses closed and allows nothing.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of `RWB-P6-E2022-CON` stay green, and a SIT week with the ACE notification path test profile shows one SMS and one LINE message to test numbers with their delivery status, every refusal message written once in the central decision ledger, and no phone number, LINE identifier or message body in a log, an event or a workflow input.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P6-001 | A contact stop applies | Contact with this customer is stopped for {reason}. |
| MSG-P6-002 | No consent for the channel | The customer has not consented to {channel}. Use another channel. |
| MSG-P6-003 | The template is withdrawn | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-P3-004 | A legal hold is on the case | This case is on hold for {deviation}. The prescription date is still {date}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks Case record C on the route | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Channel or template missing | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | NSS or LINE OA is unavailable, or a consumed read does not answer in time | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story; the {reason} of MSG-P6-001 is the deviation code and its name as the reference data holds them, and the {system} of MSG-GEN-006 is the name of the system that failed — `NSS`, `LINE OA` or the name of the consumed service.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-03 Case record, state editable: the Send message action for roles with Case record C, with the channel, the template and the party, and the refusal message shown in place. SCR-04 Case timeline, states Loading and filtered: each message with its channel, its conduct check and its delivery status, read from the P1 interaction. SCR-09 Exception queue: the sends that failed after the attempt limit of 5.

All three are gateway-bff composite routes (DP-19); this story provides the operation and the answer behind them and builds no screen of its own. No screen shows a phone number or a LINE identifier: the contact point is shown as its masked token. The template of a message is not stored anywhere in the target, so the timeline shows the channel, the conduct check and the delivery status and reads no template from a stored message (GAP-1077; ASM-2025).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the blocking deviation codes, the result-code maps, the LINE status map, the attempt limit, the templates and the languages are data rows, reference data or service configuration read with their version.
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs, logs, tests or prompts. The mobile number, the LINE identifier, the message body and the addressee never appear in an event, a workflow input or a log: the contact point travels as a token, the ACE notification path detokenises it, and test data uses synthetic tokens and test numbers only.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the owner's `v_ace_*` views; this story reads no ACE table and no ACE view, because the contact point arrives through the P1 contract (DP-05).
- No cross-schema read and no cross-service write: the interaction ledger and the contact point with its failed count are P1's, the case is P3's, the deviation is S8's and the decision record is P7's; rwb-comms reaches each through its contract and holds no copy (DP-01, DP-05, DP-18).
- No direct call to NSS or LINE OA: every send and every result goes through the ACE notification path (REQ-DRI-006), and the stubs stand behind that path, never in front of it.
- The refusal and the pass record are written through the local decision-record library in the same transaction as the answer, and a refusal that cannot be recorded is not completed (R-UNI-39, DP-03).
- One REST base, one hop and a 2 s timeout: the operation is `/api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/messages`, the consumed calls carry the budget and a breaker, and no consumer is called twice for one decision (DP-11, DP-13, ADR-020).
- Only the current Approved template is used, and a withdrawn template with no later Approved version refuses the send; no template body is copied into code or into a test.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-022 for rwb-source-data. The legacy story read the contact points and consent, ran the conduct check, merged the template, wrote the ledger entry, sent through the ACE notification path and took the result, all in one deployable. The send, the conduct check, the template, JOB-11 and the result listener move to rwb-comms (P6), the refusal record to rwb-decision (P7) and the access right to rwb-access (P4). This story keeps the two facts those slices stand on and the ledger they append to: the contact-point read over the service's own `v_ace_contact` and `contact_point_ext`, the failed count, and the message append with its delivery result on the ledger of RWB-P1-E1066-APP, folded on `external_ref` because that ledger is append-only (DP-05, DP-13, DP-18). No NSS or LINE OA call, no template read, no conduct check, no outbox sender and no decision-log write is built here. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **the contact points of a party with their consent, verification and failed count to be answered by rwb-source-data, the count of a contact point to rise by one per failed message and to answer the same count on a repeat, and every outbound SMS and LINE message with its delivery result to be entries of this service's ledger folded on their external reference**, so that **the conduct check decides from facts it does not own, a failed attempt is counted once, and the delivery state of a message is a ledger fact rather than an update of a row**.

This is the rwb-source-data slice of legacy RWB-E2-022. It delivers four things:

- **the contact-point read**: `GET /contact-points?personKey=&channel=` on base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` (DP-13), with `channel` `MOBILE` or `LINE`, one row per contact point with `contactKey` (a token, never the number and never the LINE identifier), `contactType`, `consentStatus`, `verifiedAt`, `failedCount` and `dataAsOf`;
- **the failed-count operation**: `POST /contact-points/{contactPointKey}/failed-contacts` with an `Idempotency-Key`, which raises `contact_point_ext.failed_count` once per (contact point, reference) and answers the new count;
- **the message append and its result**: `POST /interactions`, the message as a `CONTACT` entry with `channel` `SMS` or `LINE`, `direction` `OUTBOUND`, `conductCheck`, `deliveryStatus` and `externalRef` (for example `NSS-7781`), and the later result as a second append with the same `externalRef`, because the ledger has no update path;
- **the read-back and the migration**: `GET /interactions?externalRef=&caseId=` folds the appends of one reference to the latest status, its time and the count; the migration adds the channel index and the count check on `contact_point_ext` and the two delivery columns with their index on `interaction`.

It owns none of the twelve legacy criteria: the send and its refusals are RWB-P6-E2022-APP's, the record RWB-P7-E2022-APP's, the right RWB-P4-E2022-APP's and the cross-service proof RWB-ITG-E2022-ITG's; its own criteria are new (GAP-2183; ASM-3534). That no contact-point read and no failed-count operation exist in the P1 inventory of TSD P1 T-A.1 is a Work Package ruling, not a source statement (GAP-2183; ASM-3535).

##### 2. Business rationale

Collections reaches a customer on the channel the customer uses, and the consent that allows it and the quality of the contact point are Workbench decisions, not ACE facts. ACE holds the phone, e-mail and address records (INT-04, `v_ace_contact`); the Workbench holds consent and verification in `contact_point_ext` (FSD P1 A2.1.3.2; TSD P1 T3.5). Today the legacy message path reads that row, sends, counts and updates in one deployable, so a contact point that keeps failing is visible to nobody but the message code. Under D-RCV-60 rwb-comms decides and sends, and this service answers the consent, the verification and the count and keeps the ledger the outcome is written to (DP-01, DP-05, DP-18).

A count is useful only if it counts one thing once. The legacy step added one when NSS answered a failure; over REST the same result can be redelivered or replayed, and a count that rises on every redelivery never resets. The operation therefore raises the count once per (contact point, reference), so the count is the number of messages that failed and not the number of callers (R-UNI-40). The same reasoning decides the delivery state: the legacy code updated the entry, the target ledger is append-only, so the result is a second append and the state is the latest append folded on `external_ref` (DP-18).

**What D-RCV-60 changes.** No business value: the channels, the consent rule, the contact stop, the retry limit, the references and the count keep their meaning. What changes is ownership and reach - this service's own tables and views and its own REST base, one hop with a 2 s budget, instead of an in-process call into the monolith (DP-11, DP-13). A contact point stays an ACE record; this service adds only its decision about it and never copies the number or the LINE identifier (BR-P1-001-5; legacy guardrail 2).

##### 3. Preconditions

Nothing here is a build dependency: the story is Day 1 and builds against published artefacts and one contract fake.

- RWB-P1-E1001-APP has published the baseline: schema `rwb_source_data`, the per-service Flyway sequence, and `contact_point_ext` with its seven business fields and the standard record columns (DP-01).
- RWB-P1-E1066-APP is done: `POST /interactions` answers, the `Idempotency-Key` handling is in place, the case check answers 404 for a case out of scope, and `tr_interaction_append_only` refuses any change to an entry. This story extends that resource; it builds no writer.
- RWB-P1-E1069-APP's view contract is published and `recovery.v_ace_contact` is readable through the `rwb_source_data` login, which holds SELECT on the views and no privilege on `public` (DP-02, DP-05; ADR-010).
- RWB-P1-E1015-APP writes `data_product_load`; the DP02 stamp of the person's business date is readable for `dataAsOf`.
- RWB-P6-E2022-CON is published with its fake: the elements the message path consumes, their answers and error classes (C).
- `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` and `outbox_event` exist in `rwb_source_data` as platform library objects; the stored response of `idempotency_key` is what a repeat answers (DP-09).
- The channel values `MOBILE`, `LINE`, `SMS` and the delivery values `SENT`, `DELIVERED`, `READ`, `FAILED` are read through the reference-data client library of DP-07 with a fixture; TSD P1 T3.8 no longer lists LOV-CHANNEL for P1 (GAP-2183; ASM-3540).
- The caller is the rwb-comms service identity of the message slice with a workload identity token; the data steward reads the count with Platform administration R (TSD P1 T6.2).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline.

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-comms decides to send on case "RC-2026-000777" for party "P-0077" and asks for the party's contact points on the channel, one hop with a 2 s budget (DP-11; the decision is RWB-P6-E2022-APP's).
2. `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/contact-points?personKey=P-0077&channel=MOBILE` reads the party's `recovery.v_ace_contact` rows and joins `contact_point_ext` on `contact_key`; a row with no extension row answers `UNKNOWN`, an empty `verifiedAt` and count 0, and is never dropped (AC1).
3. `ConsentRenderService` renders `consent_given` true as `GIVEN`, false with a `consent_at` as `WITHDRAWN`, and no row as `UNKNOWN`; `dataAsOf` is the DP02 business date (AC1).
4. rwb-comms runs its conduct check and sends through the ACE notification path; NSS accepts with reference "NSS-7781" and returns "DELIVERED" (the send is RWB-P6-E2022-APP's; REQ-DRI-006 forbids a direct NSS call here).
5. rwb-comms posts the message as a `CONTACT` entry with channel "SMS", direction "OUTBOUND", conduct check "PASSED", status "DELIVERED", reference "NSS-7781" and a key; the append answers 201 (AC2; DP-18).
6. When the result changes - LINE reported delivered and then read - rwb-comms appends the later status with the same `externalRef` and a new key; the repository has no update method (AC3).
7. `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/interactions?externalRef=NSS-7781&caseId=RC-2026-000777` answers the latest status, the time of the append that carried it and the count of appends (AC3).
8. On a failure rwb-comms posts the reference to `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/contact-points/{contactPointKey}/failed-contacts`; the count rises once for that (contact point, reference) and a repeat of the key answers the stored count (AC4, AC5).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | `channel` missing, or `personKey` empty or malformed | 422; nothing answered and nothing written; the field is named | MSG-GEN-001 | AC5 |
| X2 | The contact point has no row in `contact_point_ext` and none in `v_ace_contact` | 404; nothing written, and no count invented or created on the fly | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2183; ASM-3535) | AC5 |
| X3 | A repeat of the same `Idempotency-Key` with the same body | The stored answer; the count unchanged and no second row | None | AC4 |
| X4 | The same `Idempotency-Key` with a different body | 409; nothing written | None | Section 12.1 |
| X5 | A second append of a result for one `externalRef` | A new entry; the earlier one unchanged and the read folds both | None | AC3 |
| X6 | `v_ace_contact` does not answer inside 5 s or errors | 503 naming the ACE database; nothing guessed from a cache | MSG-GEN-006 | Section 12.1 |
| X7 | The delivery columns are missing because the letter slice of this key has not migrated | The append is refused with 503; no entry with a null reference | MSG-GEN-006 | Section 13 |
| X8 | A caller without the right | 403, logged without a token or a reference value | MSG-P4-002 | Section 10 |

X1 to X5 are legacy X6, X7 and X10 carried onto the split; the contact stop, consent, template and legal-hold refusals of legacy X1 to X4, X8 and X9 are raised by rwb-comms and rwb-decision and never reach this service (GAP-2183; ASM-3535).

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P6-E2022-CON and its fake, the baseline, the view contract and the ledger writer; needs no live rwb-comms, rwb-deviation, rwb-decision or ACE database to start |
| Negotiable | The class split, the token format and the fold are the squad's choice behind the contract; the channels, the field list, the count rule and the append-only rule are fixed |
| Valuable | rwb-comms decides from facts it does not own, a failure is counted once, and the delivery state is history instead of an overwrite |
| Estimable | Four operations, one repository over one view and two tables, one migration and one fold |
| Small | Finishes inside one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is one call against the contract fake and two fixtures, with no second service and no live NSS or LINE OA |
| Day 1 | No build dependency; reachable on the first day of wave 2 and tested against the baseline and the fake |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: SMS and LINE dispatch through NSS and LINE OA

  Background:
    Given case "RC-2026-000777" is owned by "CO-0201" with borrower party "P-0077"
    Given the rwb-comms contract mock returns NSS reference "NSS-7781" with result "DELIVERED" for the message of case "RC-2026-000777"
    Given the rwb-comms contract mock returns the LINE result "DELIVERED" then "READ" for the message of case "RC-2026-000777"
    Given template "SMS-REMIND" "TH" version 1 with channel "SMS" and template "LINE-REMIND" "TH" version 1 with channel "LINE" are Approved and current in rwb-comms

  Scenario: AC1 The MOBILE contact point of P-0077 answers consent "WITHDRAWN" and failed count 0 (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given party "P-0077" has a verified "MOBILE" contact point with consent "WITHDRAWN" and failed count 0
    When rwb-comms calls GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/contact-points?personKey=P-0077&channel=MOBILE
    Then the answer holds one row with contactType "MOBILE", consentStatus "WITHDRAWN", a verifiedAt time and failedCount 0
    Then the row carries the token of the contact point as its contactKey and no mobile number
    Then the answer carries a dataAsOf date and neither a case number nor a party name

  Scenario: AC2 The outbound SMS is appended as a CONTACT entry with conduct check "PASSED" and reference "NSS-7781" (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given party "P-0077" has a verified "MOBILE" contact point with consent "GIVEN"
    When rwb-comms posts the message of case "RC-2026-000777" with channel "SMS", direction "OUTBOUND", conduct check "PASSED", status "DELIVERED" and reference "NSS-7781" with Idempotency-Key "c0ffee00-0001"
    Then the answer is 201 with one interaction of event code "CONTACT", channel "SMS" and direction "OUTBOUND"
    Then it carries conduct check "PASSED", delivery status "DELIVERED" and external reference "NSS-7781"
    Then the entry is written once and no operation updates it afterwards

  Scenario: AC3 The LINE message reaches "READ" through a second append folded on "NSS-7781" (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the CONTACT entry of case "RC-2026-000777" for reference "NSS-7781" carries channel "LINE", conduct check "PASSED" and status "DELIVERED"
    When rwb-comms appends the result of "NSS-7781" with status "READ" and Idempotency-Key "c0ffee00-0002"
    And rwb-comms reads it back with GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/interactions?externalRef=NSS-7781&caseId=RC-2026-000777
    Then the read answers status "READ" with the time of the second append and two appends folded on "NSS-7781"
    Then the first entry still carries "DELIVERED" and was not changed

  Scenario: AC4 The failed count rises to 1 once and a repeat of the same key answers 1 (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given party "P-0077" has a verified "MOBILE" contact point with consent "GIVEN" and failed count 0
    And the rwb-comms contract mock returns result "FAILED" for reference "NSS-7781" after the retry limit of 5
    When rwb-comms posts the failure of "NSS-7781" for that contact point with Idempotency-Key "c0ffee00-0001"
    Then the answer is 201 with the contactKey and failedCount 1
    When the same request is sent again with Idempotency-Key "c0ffee00-0001"
    Then the answer is the first answer with failedCount 1 and the stored row still holds 1
    Then a third call with a new key and the same reference increments nothing

  Scenario: AC5 A missing channel and an unknown contact point are refused with nothing written (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given party "P-0077" has one verified "MOBILE" contact point with consent "GIVEN" and failed count 0
    When rwb-comms calls GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/contact-points?personKey=P-0077 with no channel
    Then the answer is 422 with MSG-GEN-001 naming "channel"
    When rwb-comms posts a failure for contact point "PHONE:NO-SUCH-9988" with Idempotency-Key "c0ffee00-0003"
    Then the answer is 404 and the count of every contact point of "P-0077" stays 0
    Then no interaction entry and no failed-contact row exists for "PHONE:NO-SUCH-9988"

  Scenario: AC6 No mobile number and no LINE identifier is stored or returned (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the v_ace_contact fixture holds a mobile number and the LINE identifier of party "P-0077"
    When rwb-comms reads the contact points of "P-0077" for channel "MOBILE" and for channel "LINE"
    And rwb-comms appends the message of "NSS-7781" for case "RC-2026-000777"
    Then neither answer carries the number or the identifier, and each row carries its token only
    Then the ledger entry carries the token, the reference "NSS-7781" and no number
    Then no column of contact_point_ext and none of this story's migration holds a number or a LINE identifier
```

**Target reading.** Every assertion is new, because this story owns no legacy criterion, and each tests only the read, the count and the ledger; the legacy values are kept (case RC-2026-000777, owner CO-0201, party P-0077, templates SMS-REMIND and LINE-REMIND TH version 1, reference NSS-7781, consent GIVEN and WITHDRAWN, count 0 to 1, retry limit 5, key c0ffee00-0001, channels MOBILE, LINE and SMS, conduct check PASSED). AC1 answers the consent fact of legacy AC5 without refusing anything, which is rwb-comms' decision (REQ-OCC-006; CTL-17); the three rendered values are the reading of TSD P1 T3.5 (GAP-2183; ASM-3536). AC2 fixes the entry as `CONTACT` with the two delivery columns (GAP-2183; ASM-3538). AC3 replaces the legacy update with an append and a fold (GAP-2183; ASM-3538). AC4 counts one failed message once (R-UNI-40); its relation to the "consecutive" wording of the FSD is not settled by a source (GAP-2183; ASM-3539). AC5 fixes the refusal set of the two writes, which no source states (GAP-2183; ASM-3535). AC6 asserts the legacy guardrail instead of assuming it.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every outbound message carries a conduct check result on its ledger entry | REQ-OCC-005; FEAT-OCC-05 |
| BR2 | No message is sent while a contact stop is in force | CTL-16; R-UNI-04, R-UNI-05 |
| BR3 | Deviation codes that block SMS and LINE are a reference list; X6 blocks both until a contact point is verified | R-DEV-16; R-UNI-12 |
| BR4 | Messages go only to a verified contact point with consent GIVEN for that channel | CTL-17; R-UNI-10 |
| BR5 | A legal hold stops every outbound action | R-UNI-20 |
| BR6 | A system that is unavailable queues the send and retries; after the limit it goes to the exception queue | R-UNI-33, R-UNI-34, R-UNI-36 |
| BR7 | A refusal that cannot be written to the decision log is not completed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR8 | Only the current Approved template for the channel is used | R-LIT-03; CTL-14 |
| BR9 | The same request twice sends one message; here, one failure of one reference raises the count by one | R-UNI-40 |

**Where each rule lives.** BR1 is a field of the append: rwb-comms sends the result it computed and this story stores it; no conduct check runs here (DP-18). BR2, BR3, BR5, BR7 and BR8 belong to rwb-comms, rwb-deviation, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-comms' template table. BR4 is split: this story answers `consentStatus` and `verifiedAt` as facts and the decision to send is rwb-comms' (DP-05). BR6 is the caller's retry: the limit of 5 sits on JOB-11 of rwb-comms and this story counts only the failure it is told about (GAP-2183; ASM-3539). BR9 is the `Idempotency-Key` of both writes, answered from the stored response and never from a second write (DP-09).

##### 9. State transitions

None in the case model: this story changes no case status, creates no case and reads no case. It changes one counter and adds ledger entries; the delivery state of a message is derived from its appends and never stored as a mutable state.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| a contact point at count n | a failed-contact call | The contact point resolves and the key is new | At n+1 and the answer carries n+1 |
| a contact point at count n | a repeat of the key, or a second call for the same reference | The reference is already counted | At n and the answer carries n |
| a contact point at count n | a failed-contact call | The contact point does not resolve | Nothing written; 404 |
| a message with no entry | the first append | The case check answers and the body validates | One `CONTACT` entry with the status given |
| a message at DELIVERED | a second append with the later status | A new key and the same `externalRef` | A second entry at READ or FAILED; the first unchanged |
| a message with two entries | the read-back | The reference is folded | The latest status and the time of its append |

The four delivery values are reference data through the client library and never written in code (DP-07; legacy section 9).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The rwb-comms service identity, with a workload identity token | Reads the contact points, posts a failed contact, appends a message and its result, and reads the fold |
| The rwb-source-data service identity | Reads `v_ace_contact` and the DP02 stamp; writes `contact_point_ext` and `interaction` in its own schema; no privilege outside it |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward and data product owner | Reads the count answer of a contact point (Platform administration R) |
| RW-CONDUCT, Conduct and QA officer | Reads blocked-contact evidence through the rwb-comms read, not through this story |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Reads a refused call and its problem body |

No credential and no personal value appears in an answer, a log line or a test. Roles and rights are data in rwb-access (DP-01; TSD P1 T6.2).
