| RWB-P6-E2022-CON | The published dispatch contract of `rwb-comms`: `POST /cases/{caseId}/messages` with channel `SMS` or `LINE`, template code, language, party, the 202 interaction answer, the 409 refusals with MSG-P6-001, MSG-P6-002, MSG-P6-003 and MSG-P3-004, and the declaration of the decision record on `rwb.decision-record.v1`. Which fields of that record this service consumes is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1274; ASM-2252) |
| RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The decision-record path and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03): the append, the chain position, the `prev_hash`, the `entry_hash`, the append-only rule, the idempotency key of a record and the local write inside the producer's transaction |
| RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The reference-data client library and the `rwb-case` reference-data contract (DP-07): LOV-DECISION, which holds "X6", the final-call list, which holds "contact refused", the reason-code list and LOV-CHANNEL with `SMS` and `LINE`, each at the version in force. The final-call list and the reason-code list have no name in the sources (GAP-1274; ASM-2253) |
| RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The outbox and inbox library with CloudEvents (DP-09) for the inbox dedupe of the consumed records and the idempotency row of an append, and the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) through which the case owner, the conduct officer and the auditor reach the two reads |
| The decision-log store baseline | `decision_log_entry` with the columns of TSD P7 v2 T3.1, the append-only trigger `tr_declog_append_only`, the missing grant for UPDATE and DELETE, the unique key on the idempotency key and the chain check JOB-14 at 02:00. The baseline is the service's own earlier work and is in no H row of this story (GAP-1274; ASM-2255) |
| The authorise answer of `rwb-access` (P4) | `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` (Architecture v5 slide 14) for the Decision log right R and the caller's scope behind the two reads; consumed, faked and in no C row of this story. DP-08 is not in the pattern set of this legacy key, so the right is declared at gateway-bff and this story keeps a local guard that refuses closed (GAP-1274; ASM-2255) |

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E2-022:

- Templates `SMS-REMIND` `TH` version 1 (channel `SMS`) and `LINE-REMIND` `TH` version 1 (channel `LINE`) are Approved and current; template status is `rwb-comms`'s and never changes the record of a decision already taken.
- Case `RC-2026-000777` is owned by `CO-0201` with borrower party `P-0077`, and it has no legal hold and no open deviation at the moment of the send. Party `P-0077` has a verified `MOBILE` contact point and a verified `LINE` contact point, each with consent `GIVEN`; the withdrawals and the stops named in the criteria are the legacy values (consent `WITHDRAWN`, deviation `X6` lost contact, deviation `X1` with contact stop on, legal hold true).
- The phone number and the LINE identifier stay tokens in the Workbench and the ACE notification path detokenizes them; no test, fixture, log line or entry of this story holds a number or an identifier (legacy section 17). No build dependency: the story builds against RWB-P6-E2022-CON and its fakes, and every platform contract of the DP table is a wave 0 or wave 1 contract.

##### 4. Flow
1. `rwb-comms` (P6): receives `POST /cases/{caseId}/messages` on its own base for case `RC-2026-000777`, channel `SMS` or `LINE`, template `SMS-REMIND` or `LINE-REMIND`, language `TH` and party `P-0077`, and runs the contact check inside its own transaction (RWB-P6-E2022-APP).
2. `rwb-comms` evaluates the contact rules embedded in its own activity (DP-04) and takes one answer with the rule id and the rule version that fired: R-UNI-04 for a contact stop, R-UNI-10 for no consent on the channel, R-UNI-20 for a legal hold and R-LIT-03 for a withdrawn template.
3. `rwb-comms`, on a refusal, answers 409 with MSG-P6-001 naming the reason, MSG-P6-002 naming the channel, MSG-P6-003 naming the template or MSG-P3-004 for the legal hold, and writes in that same transaction the record with decision code "X6", final call "contact refused", the rule id and version, the channel, the reason code, the case reference and the requesting role `RW-CASEOWN`.
4. `rwb-comms`, on a send that passed the check, writes its interaction, its outbox row and in the same transaction the record of the send with decision code "X6", the channel, the case and the requesting role; the final call of that record is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1274; ASM-2253).
5. The record path publishes `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, keyed by the case ID, with the entry ID, the record's idempotency key and the facts of the decision (DP-09; Architecture v5 slide 42, event 08).
6. `rwb-decision` `ContactRecordListener`: reads the fact into the inbox of DP-09, deduplicates it by event ID and by the record's idempotency key (R-UNI-40), keeps the facts whose decision code is "X6", and passes them to `ContactRecordAppendService`. Every other decision code is the decision-log baseline's general ingest and not this story's.
7. `ContactRecordAppendService`: reads LOV-DECISION, the final-call list, the reason-code list and LOV-CHANNEL through the reference-data contract of DP-07 at the version in force, requires the decision code, a final call from the list, the rule id, the rule version, the channel, the case reference and the requesting role, and refuses a record that lacks any of them with MSG-P7-003 naming the missing field; nothing is written (BR8, BR11). A repeated fact with the same idempotency key returns the first entry's ID, raises the repeat count for R-UNI-40 and appends nothing (BR7); a second append for the same refusal of the same case, channel and rule at the same decided time is refused with 409 and MSG-GEN-004 (BR6).
8. `ContactRecordAppendService`, one transaction in `rwb_decision`: takes the next `chain_seq`, computes `prev_hash` from the last entry's `entry_hash` (64 zeros for the first), computes `entry_hash` as the SHA-256 of the entry's canonical form, writes the `decision_log_entry` row with `inputs_ref` pointing at the inputs reference of the record, and writes the inbox row of the fact and the idempotency row of the key. A failed append changes nothing (BR3, BR13).
9. A case owner, a conduct officer or an auditor reads the entries of a case in a date range with `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` by `caseId`, `decision`, `ruleId`, `approver`, `from`, `to`, `page` and `size`, and one entry with `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}`; each row holds `entryId`, `chainSeq`, the case, the decision code, the final call, the rule id and version, the channel, the reason code, the requesting role, the inputs reference, `decidedAt`, `prevHash` and `entryHash` and never a message body or a contact value. A caller without the right is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002 and a case outside its scope with 404 and MSG-P4-003 (BR10).
10. Nothing in this story sends a message, moves a case, clears a deviation or changes a contact point: the refusal is `rwb-comms`'s, the case is `rwb-case`'s and the consent is `rwb-source-data`'s (BR9). Every entry commits with its chain position, its inbox row and its idempotency row in one transaction (BR13), and the ingest of the shared topic is continuous Kafka with no Schedule (12.6).

##### 5. Exception paths
| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The record names no decision code, no final call, no rule id, no rule version, no channel, no case or no requesting role | The append is refused, nothing is written and no chain position is used | MSG-P7-003 | AC1, AC12 |
| X2 | The decision code is not a value of LOV-DECISION, or the final call is not in the final-call list at the version in force | The append is refused and the fact stays on the topic for redelivery; nothing is written from an assumed value | MSG-P7-003 | AC3, AC4 |
| X3 | The decision log store is unavailable, or the chain position cannot be taken | The refusal is not completed: `rwb-comms` answers 503, nothing is sent to NSS or to LINE OA, and an incident is raised as in R-UNI-39 | MSG-P7-003 | AC7 |
| X4 | The same record is delivered again, or replayed from the topic | One entry exists; the inbox dedupe and the idempotency key both hold, and the repeat is counted for R-UNI-40 | None | AC9 |
| X5 | A second append arrives for the same refusal of the same case, channel and rule at the same decided time | The second append is refused and the first entry stands | MSG-GEN-004 | AC9 |
| X6 | A delivery result of NSS or LINE OA arrives for a reference the ledger already holds (`FAILED`, `DELIVERED` or `READ`) | No entry is appended and no chain position is used: a delivery result is not a decision of this service and the delivery status is `rwb-comms`'s | None | AC6, AC9 |
| X7 | A correction of an entry is needed, or an UPDATE or a DELETE is attempted | A correction is a new entry with `corrects_entry_id` and the corrected entry stays unchanged; an UPDATE or a DELETE is refused by the missing grant and by `tr_declog_append_only`, and the attempt is audited | None | AC8 |
| X8 | The caller holds no Decision log right, or asks for a case outside its scope | 403 with MSG-P4-002, or 404 with MSG-P4-003; no entry is returned | MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 | AC10, AC11 |
| X9 | The authorise answer or a reference list does not arrive inside the 2 s budget | The read or the append is refused closed rather than assumed, and the fact is retried; the answer is never widened to cover the failure | MSG-GEN-006, MSG-P7-003 | AC10, AC1 |
| X10 | A refusal was blocked by the contact check but its local record was not written in the producer's transaction | Nothing is sent, the send answers MSG-P7-003, and no fact reaches this service, so no entry and no chain position exist for it | MSG-P7-003 | AC7 |
| X11 | An entry carries a message body, a phone number, a LINE identifier or a customer value, in a fixture or in a payload | The boundary test fails the build: the record carries references, codes and the reason only | None | AC12 |

An entry is only ever appended beside the decision that caused it, so nothing of this story can send a message, and no message can leave with a decision that has no record (BR13).

##### 6. INVEST check
| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P6-E2022-CON and its fakes, the decision-record path of DP-03, the reference-data contract and the decision-log store baseline; no conduct check, template check, outbox, retry, dispatch, delivery status or ledger entry is rebuilt here |
| Negotiable | The decision code, the final-call list, the reason-code list, the channel list and the message ids are data or parameters of their owners; the story fixes only the entry, the append-only rule, the chain and the two reads |
| Valuable | Every refused contact and every contact that was allowed can be traced to the rule and the version that decided it, and that explanation cannot be quietly changed |
| Estimable | One listener, one appender with the chain, one query controller with two operations, one boundary test and one fake set |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests; it is the decision-record slice of a legacy key split five ways |
| Testable | Each of the twelve criteria in section 7 runs as one automated test against the contract fakes, on a fixed business date and a fixed chain |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria
`acs` is empty for this story: no legacy acceptance criterion of RWB-E2-022 is owned verbatim here, because every criterion of the key sends a message, refuses a send, maps a delivery result or reads an interaction, and those belong to RWB-P6-E2022-APP, RWB-P1-E2022-APP, RWB-P4-E2022-APP and RWB-ITG-E2022-ITG. The twelve criteria below are new for the `rwb-decision` slice and test only the record, its chain and its two reads. They add no business value: they keep the legacy values — decision code "X6" and final call "contact refused" exactly as the legacy story writes them, the channel values `SMS` and `LINE`, the templates `SMS-REMIND` and `LINE-REMIND` in `TH` at version 1, the case `RC-2026-000777` owned by `CO-0201` with borrower party `P-0077`, the deviations `X6` lost contact and `X1` dispute or complaint with the contact stop, the consent values `GIVEN` and `WITHDRAWN`, the contact types `MOBILE` and `LINE`, the hold and refusal reasons of the legacy story, legal hold true, the retry limit of 5 with rule R-UNI-34, the exception queue, the delivery status `FAILED`, the conduct checks `PASSED` and `BLOCKED`, the delivery statuses `DELIVERED` and `READ`, the message ids expected, the external reference "NSS-7781", the Idempotency-Key "c0ffee00-0001", the inputs reference "inputs/2026-12-03/7f3a", the rule version "UNI-2026.11" and the roles of the legacy story.

The twelve criteria are new and `acs` is empty for this story. Every value inside them is a legacy value of RWB-E2-022 or of the P7 baseline, and no new business value is introduced. The payload field set of the record, the request and answer shape of the two reads, the final call of a passed check, the reason-code list, the rule version label of R-LIT-03, the parameter names and the per-service login name have no source and are carried in GAP-1274 and GAP-1275 with ASM-2252 to ASM-2255. The `-ITG` copies of the test cases belong to RWB-ITG-E2022-ITG.

##### 8. Business rules
| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every refusal of the contact check writes exactly one decision entry, and every send that passed the check writes exactly one: a refusal and a send each leave one entry and no more | Legacy RWB-E2-022 AC3, AC10, BR1, BR7; FSD P7 v3 A2.2; REQ-OCC-005 |
| BR2 | The entry of a refusal carries decision code "X6" and final call "contact refused" | Legacy RWB-E2-022 AC3; BR-P7-002; DP-07 |
| BR3 | Every entry is hash chained — a `chain_seq`, a `prev_hash` equal to the previous entry's `entry_hash` (64 zeros for the first) and an `entry_hash` equal to the SHA-256 of the entry's canonical form — and the ingest of the shared topic is continuous Kafka inside the completeness target of slide 28, with JOB-14 at 02:00 and the daily seal the baseline's | REQ-DRI-003; FSD P7 v3 AC-ALT-P7-001-01; Architecture v5 slides 28 and 44 |
| BR4 | The log is append only: an entry is never changed and never deleted, and a correction is a new entry naming the one it corrects in `corrects_entry_id` | REQ-DRI-002; FSD P7 v3 AC-P7-001-01 and A2.1 |
| BR5 | The entry names the case reference, the channel, the rule id and rule version, the reason code, the requesting role and the inputs reference; it never carries the message body, the phone number, the LINE identifier, a contact value, a template body or a party identifier | Legacy RWB-E2-022 section 17; DF-ACE-078; CTL-11; §R7.2 s17 |
| BR6 | A refusal is recorded whole or not at all: a refused append leaves no entry, a second append for the same refusal is refused, and one entry exists under a repeated record because the inbox dedupe and the idempotency key hold and the repeat is counted | Legacy RWB-E2-022 BR7, BR9; FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-03; R-UNI-39, R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | The decision code, the final call, the reason code and the channel are data rows read at the version in force; none of them is a literal in code | BR-P7-002; TSD P7 v2 T3.2; DP-07; GAP-1274 with ASM-2253 |
| BR8 | The story records and exposes; it sends no message, runs no contact check, merges no template, writes no outbox row, maps no delivery result, and changes no case, deviation, contact point or interaction | Architecture v5 slides 14, 41 and 44; DP-01; DP-18 |
| BR9 | The two reads declare the Decision log right R with the scope applied, are one hop from the gateway-bff composite route and read no table of another service; a role without the right is refused with MSG-P4-002 and a case outside the scope with MSG-P4-003 | TSD P7 v2 T-A.1, T6.1 and T6.2; REQ-ILG-010; DP-11; DP-19 |
| BR10 | A record that lacks its decision code, its final call, its rule id, its rule version, its channel, its case reference or its requesting role is refused with MSG-P7-003 and appends nothing; no entry is written from an assumed value | FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-05 read on this slice; REQ-OCC-005 |
| BR11 | No personal data in the entry, the inputs reference, the event, the audit line, the tests or the logs; the contact point is a token and this service never holds a contact value | Architecture v5 slide 11; legacy RWB-E2-022 section 17; REQ-DRI-001 |
| BR12 | The entry, its chain position, its inbox row and its idempotency row commit in one transaction; a failed append leaves nothing and the fact is redelivered, and a refusal that cannot be recorded does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; FSD P7 v3 A2.5; DP-03 |
| BR13 | The rule evaluation stays embedded in the owning service (DP-04) and this service records the rule id and version it is given; the rule packages stay in the registry of this service and no rule is evaluated and no workflow, activity or Schedule is registered on this path | Architecture v5 slides 27 and 44; Template and Rules §R5.5 DP-04, DP-10 |

##### 9. State transitions
None for a case, a message, a deviation or a contact point. The states below are the states of an entry of this story, and the entry has no state column of its own: it is appended and then immutable.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Absent | `DecisionRecorded` arrives with decision code "X6" and final call "contact refused" | The code is in LOV-DECISION, the final call is in the list, the rule id and version, the channel, the case and the requesting role are present, and the chain head is known | Appended at the next `chain_seq`, with its `prev_hash`, its `entry_hash`, its inbox row and its idempotency row in one transaction |
| Absent | `DecisionRecorded` arrives with a code or a final call outside its list, or with a value missing, or the store or the chain is unavailable | The record fails the check of BR10, or the append cannot commit | Absent: refused with MSG-P7-003, no chain position used, the fact redelivered, the refusal not completed and an incident raised under R-UNI-39 |
| Appended | The same record arrives again with the same idempotency key | The inbox or the idempotency key holds the entry | Unchanged: the first entry's ID is returned and the repeat is counted |
| Appended | A duplicate append for the same refusal arrives | The first entry of that refusal stands | Unchanged: the second append is refused with MSG-GEN-004 |
| Appended | A delivery result arrives for the reference of the send | A delivery result is not a decision of this service | Unchanged: no entry is appended and no chain position is used |
| Appended | A correction is taken, or an UPDATE or a DELETE is attempted | The correction names the entry it corrects; any caller, including the schema owner, may not change an entry | Appended: a new entry with `corrects_entry_id`; otherwise unchanged, the statement refused by the append-only rule |
| Appended | The daily chain check and the daily seal run | JOB-14 at 02:00 and the seal of the baseline | Sealed: the entry is unchanged and the chain is verified |

The message keeps its own lifecycle and delivery status in `rwb-comms`, the deviation keeps its state in `rwb-deviation`, the consent keeps its state in `rwb-source-data` and the case keeps its state in `rwb-case`; this story changes none of them (BR8).

##### 10. Authority
The rights below are the Decision log rights this story applies; TSD P7 v2 T6.1 declares R on the decision log for every role and T6.2 declares the service identities. DP-08 is not in the pattern set of this legacy key, so the declaration sits at gateway-bff on the composite route and this story keeps a local guard that refuses closed when the answer is missing (GAP-1274; ASM-2255).

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Sends the message that produces the record on a case in scope (Case record C) and reads the entries of that case (Decision log R) |
| RW-CONDUCT, Conduct and QA officer | Reads blocked contacts and their entries, one entry and the entries of a case in a date range (Decision log R) |
| RW-COMPLAIN and RW-TEAMMGR | Read the entries of a disputed case and of team cases, including the contact stop from `X1` (Decision log R) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit; RW-COMPLY, Compliance and PDPA officer | Read the ledger by case and by date range and one entry with its rule version and its chain fields, and never a contact value, which the entry never carries (Decision log R, scope ALL for audit) |
| SY-DECLOG, decision record writer | Writes the record inside the refusal or the send transaction at the producer and appends it to the ledger here; the append is a service identity's and not a person's. A role outside the matrix, or a case out of the caller's scope, is refused with MSG-P4-002, or 404 with MSG-P4-003 |
| The `rwb-decision` service identity | Consumes the fact, reads its own `rwb_decision` rows, and appends the entry, its inbox row and its idempotency row (DP-02) |
| `rwb-comms` | Owns the contact check, the send, the template check, the outbox, the retry limit of 5 with R-UNI-34, the exception queue, the dispatch, the delivery status and the failed count; this story holds no authority over any of them |
| `rwb-source-data`, `rwb-case`, `rwb-deviation`, `rwb-integration`, `rwb-access` | Own the interaction ledger and the consent, the case and its legal hold, the deviation and its contact stop, the NSS and LINE interface configuration, and the session, role and scope; this story writes none of them, and no approval level from the delegation of authority applies, because a contact decision is not an approval |

The database login is per service (DP-02) and its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1274; ASM-2255); the story refers to "the rwb-decision login (DP-02)" and never to the shared legacy login.

| DF-INT-002 to DF-INT-006, DF-INT-012, DF-INT-028, DF-INT-029 | `interaction` (P1) | case_id, channel, conduct_check, delivery_status, external_ref | Never read and never written: the interaction is `rwb-source-data`'s and the delivery status is `rwb-comms`'s |
| (reference lists), (inbox, idempotency) | reference data (P3); `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | LOV-DECISION, the final-call list, the reason-code list, LOV-CHANNEL; event_id, consumer, processed_at, the record's key and the first entry ID | The lists through the reference-data contract of DP-07, never a table; the inbox and idempotency rows written |

No row of `recovery_case`, `deviation`, `template`, `contact_point_ext` or `interaction` is copied into `rwb_decision`: the case, the deviation, the consent and the template arrive as facts of the record and the contact value never arrives at all (DP-01, DP-18). The phone number, the LINE identifier, the message body and the party `P-0077` are named in this document as legacy values only and are written in no entry of this story (BR5, BR11). Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8; the container of the channel, the reason code and the requesting role inside `actions` is the reading of ASM-2252 and is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1274; ASM-2252).

##### 12. Contract
###### 12.1 REST operations provided
Owner `rwb-decision` (P7); base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`. Both paths are the ones TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 carries (API-P7-006 and API-P7-007) and the Ownership Map gives to P7. The request and response field set of a contact entry is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1274; ASM-2252).

| Method | Path | API ID | Request | Answer | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/decision-log` | API-P7-006 | Query: `caseId`, `decision`, `ruleId`, `approver`, `from`, `to`, `page`, `size`; a case with a date range is `caseId` with `from` and `to` | 200 `DecisionLogPage`: `items`, `page`, `size`, `total` | Decision log R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |
| GET | `/decision-log/{entryId}` | API-P7-007 | None | 200 `DecisionLogEntry`: `entryId`, `chainSeq`, `caseId`, `decisionCode`, `finalCall`, `ruleId`, `ruleVersion`, `inputsRef`, the channel, the reason code, the requesting role, `decidedAt`, `prevHash`, `entryHash`, `correctsEntryId`, `actorUserId` | Decision log R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |

Errors: 401 no session; 403 the role lacks the Decision log right (MSG-P4-002); 404 the entry or the case is absent or outside the scope (MSG-P4-003); 422 a query value is outside its list; 503 the ledger is unavailable or the authorise answer did not arrive inside the 2 s budget. Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set. `GET /cases/{caseId}/recommendation` (API-P7-001) and the approval operations API-P7-002 to API-P7-005 and API-P7-008 are P7 operations of the decision center and belong to the other P7 stories of this service; this story declares none of them.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed
| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access (Architecture v5 slide 14) | The cached role, scope and Decision log right R decision behind the two reads; consumed, faked, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker (DP-11), and in no C row of this story (GAP-1274; ASM-2255) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-DECISION with "X6", the final-call list with "contact refused", the reason-code list and LOV-CHANNEL with `SMS` and `LINE`, at the version in force (DP-07); faked |

The five fakes of this slice stand behind those rows and behind the record under test: the **rwb-comms dispatch contract fake** (RWB-P6-E2022-CON) poses the five refusals and the send, the **decision-record library fake** (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON) supplies the append, the chain and the append-only refusal, the **rwb-access fake** answers the authorise call, the **rwb-case reference-data fake** supplies the four lists, and the **central ledger fake** supplies the ledger reference, the completeness reading, the replay of the same fact and the chain head. The record itself arrives on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and not over REST.

###### 12.3 Events published
None. This story publishes no event of its own: the record of a contact decision is a fact of `rwb-comms` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and the entries are read through the operations of 12.1. `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` is published by the owning service of each decision and `rwb-decision` is its consumer, as the event catalogue names it (Architecture v5 slide 42, event 08). The `ApprovalRequested`, `ApprovalDecided` and `RulePackageInForce` events of `rwb.decision.events.v1` belong to the approval and rule-registry stories of this service and are not touched here; no new event is added to that topic and no new topic is created.

###### 12.4 Events consumed
| Event | Topic | Owner | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 ledger and its shared topic; published by `rwb-comms` for the contact decisions of the SMS and LINE loop | `ContactRecordListener`: inbox dedupe by event ID and by the record's idempotency key, then `ContactRecordAppendService` for the decision code, the final call, the rule id and version, the channel, the reason code, the case reference, the requesting role and the inputs reference |

The fact carries IDs, codes, versions and a reference only; no message body, no phone number, no LINE identifier and no customer value travels on the topic (BR5, BR11). Which fields of the fact this service requires is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1274; ASM-2252); the reading this story applies is that of ASM-2252. Each consumed fact has its retry topic and its `.dlt` topic on the platform convention (DP-09).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities
None. The append is a transactional write on the consumer path and not a workflow step; the handler is a Kafka consumer with the inbox of DP-09; the contact check and its evaluation (DP-04) run inside the activity of `rwb-comms` and are neither started nor signalled here. This story registers no workflow and no activity on the `rwb-decision` queue and adds none to the workflow kit.

###### 12.6 Schedules
None, and this story creates no Schedule of its own. The legacy JOB-13 decision-log copy at 01:00 is retired: the ingest of `rwb.decision-record.v1` here is continuous Kafka, as Architecture v5 slide 44 states. The daily chain check JOB-14 at 02:00 and the daily seal of the ledger to write-once storage are the decision-log baseline's and cover these entries like any other. No cron entry, no job name and no Temporal Schedule is registered by this story.

###### 12.7 Tables owned
| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `decision_log_entry` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | The contact entry, its decision code, final call, rule id and version, channel, reason code, requesting role, inputs reference and chain position; append only |
| `approval` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | Not read and not written: a contact decision is not an approval |
| `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row`, `rule_test_case` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | The registry stays here, but nothing of it is read on this path: the evaluation is embedded in the owning service (DP-04) |
| decision record (local library), `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | P7 rows in the producer's schema through the decision-record path; PLT library created in `rwb_decision` | The local write of DP-03 inside the refusal or the send transaction with its hash chain, and the inbox and idempotency rows of an append (DP-09) |

Not owned and never read: `interaction` and `contact_point_ext` (P1), `recovery_case` and the reference lists (P3), `deviation` (S8), `template` and `merge_field` (P6), `interface_config` (P2), `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule` and `delegation_limit` (P4). No foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01).

##### 13. Solution plan
**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, module `log/contact`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision.contact`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_decision`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | The monolith base path | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | none |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

Which pattern has an instance here: DP-03 is the record itself — the append through the decision-record path, the `prev_hash` and `entry_hash` chain, the append-only rule and the shared topic, with its H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON. DP-01 is the boundary — the entry lives in `rwb_decision` and the interaction, the contact point, the case, the deviation and the template are never read as tables. DP-07 is the four lists read with the version in force; DP-09 is the inbox dedupe and the idempotency row of an append; DP-11 is the one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker on the authorise call and the reference-data read; DP-19 is the gateway-bff route of the two reads. DP-05, DP-10 and DP-18 have an instance only as an absence: no ACE view and no ACE table is read and the phone number and the LINE identifier never enter; the legacy JOB-13 copy becomes continuous Kafka with no Schedule (12.6); the interaction ledger is `rwb-source-data`'s and this story holds no ledger entry. The platform H dependencies of the DP table — H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON and H RWB-PLT-N001-CON — and the C dependencies of the published contracts of other services — C RWB-P3-E1043-CON and the authorise contract of P4 — are not in the metadata rows of this story, which name None and RWB-P6-E2022-CON; they are the dependencies the DP table adds and are recorded in GAP-1274 and ASM-2255. None blocks the build beyond Day 1: they are platform contracts of waves 0 and 1 and published contracts of `rwb-case` and `rwb-access`, built against their fakes.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ContactRecordListener | Kafka consumer with the inbox | Reads `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, deduplicates by event ID and by the record's idempotency key, keeps the "X6" contact facts and hands them to the appender |
| ContactRecordAppendService | Service | Checks the decision code, the final call, the rule id and version, the channel, the case reference and the requesting role, and writes the entry, its chain position, its inbox row and its idempotency row in one transaction (BR2, BR10, BR12) |
| ChainHasher | Service | The canonical form of an entry and its SHA-256, the first `prev_hash` of 64 zeros and the `prev_hash` of every later entry (BR3) |
| DecisionLogQueryController, DecisionLogQueryService, DecisionLogRepository | Controller, service, repository | The two operations of 12.1 with the declared right, the scope and the paging; the row shape of a contact entry; `decision_log_entry` insert only with its search indexes and idempotency key |
| ReferenceListClient | Client | LOV-DECISION, the final-call list, the reason-code list and LOV-CHANNEL through DP-07 with the version in force |
| AuthoriseClient | Client | The cached authorise answer of `rwb-access` behind the two reads, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker (DP-11) |

**Database, configuration and reference data**

- Writes `decision_log_entry`, its inbox and idempotency rows, all in schema `rwb_decision`; reads no other schema (DP-01). The table, its columns of TSD P7 v2 T3.1, the trigger `tr_declog_append_only`, the missing grant and the unique key on the idempotency key belong to the decision-log store baseline and are not rebuilt here (GAP-1274). One migration step in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15, through RWB-PLT-E1044-CON): `V2022_1__decision_log_contact_index.sql` adds `ix_declog_contact_case ON decision_log_entry (case_id, decision_code, decided_at DESC)` for the case-and-date search; the index name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1274; ASM-2252).
- LOV-DECISION with "X6", the final-call list with "contact refused", the reason-code list and LOV-CHANNEL with `SMS` and `LINE` are reference data read through DP-07 with the version in force (BR7). The rule version labels are the ones the owning service returns; "UNI-2026.11" is the legacy value of the P7 baseline for a universal rule and the label of R-LIT-03 is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1274; ASM-2254). The page-size bound and the 5-minute completeness target are parameters of their owners whose names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1274; ASM-2255), and no feature switch of this story's own is named by a source; the send switch is `rwb.comms.sms-line` of RWB-P6-E2022-APP.

**Build steps**

1. `DecisionLogRepository` and the index step; test the search by case and date range and the single read, and that an INSERT outside a transaction is refused (AC11). Then `ChainHasher` and the canonical form: `chain_seq`, `prev_hash` from the previous entry, the first `prev_hash` of 64 zeros and `entry_hash` as the SHA-256 of the canonical form (AC1, AC8).
2. `ContactRecordListener` with the inbox and the dedupe by event ID and idempotency key, and `ContactRecordAppendService` with the checks of BR10 and the fail-closed transaction; test the replay of the same fact (AC9) and the forced failure of AC7 with the chain position the refused write does not use.
3. The append-only rule with the trigger and the grant, the four statements of AC8 refused and the audit line written. Then `ReferenceListClient` with the version in force, and the refusal rather than an assumed code, final call, reason code or channel (BR7, X9).
4. `DecisionLogQueryController` and `AuthoriseClient` against their fakes; tests for AC10, AC11, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 (TC-E2-022-13), then the contract-fake run of the whole slice from Day 1 and the boundary test: no write to `rwb_comms`, `rwb_source_data`, `rwb_case` or `rwb_deviation`, and no message body, phone number, LINE identifier, contact value or template body in any entry, event payload or log line (AC5, AC12).

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the chain of a SIT day verifies from the first entry with no break, each of the five refusals leaves one entry naming its rule and version, a send leaves one entry beside it, a refusal whose record cannot be written leaves none and does not consume a chain position, a repeated record leaves one entry, both reads answer inside the 2 s budget of the frame, and no message, case, deviation or contact point was changed by this story.

##### 14. Validation and messages
| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | A contact record cannot be appended, or the record lacks a value the entry requires | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | The record path, on the append; the send answers 503 and nothing leaves |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A second append arrives for the same refusal | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. | This story, on the duplicate append of AC9 |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller holds no Decision log right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, through the authorise answer of the read |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case or the entry is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. | This story, through the authorise answer of the read |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The authorise answer or a reference list does not arrive inside the 2 s budget | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. | This story, on the read path and on the append path |
| MSG-P6-001 | A contact stop applies | Contact with this customer is stopped for {reason}. | `rwb-comms` on the refusal; this story asserts it and never rewrites it |
| MSG-P6-002 | No consent for the channel | The customer has not consented to {channel}. Use another channel. | `rwb-comms` on the refusal; this story asserts it and never rewrites it |
| MSG-P6-003 | The template is withdrawn | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. | `rwb-comms` on the refusal; this story asserts it and never rewrites it |
| MSG-P3-004 | A legal hold is on the case | This case is on hold for {deviation}. The prescription date is still {date}. | `rwb-case` through the refusal of `rwb-comms`; this story asserts it and never rewrites it |

MSG-P6-001, MSG-P6-002, MSG-P6-003, MSG-P3-004 and MSG-P7-003 are copied unchanged from RWB-E2-022 section 14, and MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 and MSG-GEN-006 from the P7 baseline. The message id set of this slice beyond these nine has no source and is carried in GAP-1274 with ASM-2255. The {reason} of MSG-P6-001 is the reason code as the data holds it ("X6 Lost contact", "X1 Dispute or complaint").

Delivery shape: every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set to the ID above, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled, and `instance` naming the request. The status mapping is the legacy one: 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 with MSG-P4-003, 409 with MSG-GEN-004, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 of the send, and 503 with MSG-P7-003 on the record path.

##### 15. Screens and states
No screen is built in this story. The two reads are consumed by SCR-38 Decision log query, which searches the log by case, rule, approver and date with export, and by the auditor's view of the ledger; both are reached through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 and are another story's. SCR-03 Case record and SCR-04 Case timeline stay `rwb-comms`'s, and this story feeds neither of them.

| Where | State | What the reader sees |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-38 Decision log query (P7) | List | The "X6" entries of the case in decidedAt order, each with its final call, its rule id and version, its channel, its reason code and its requesting role |
| The entry read | One entry | The same row with its inputs reference, its `decidedAt`, its `prevHash` and its `entryHash`, and a correction beside the entry it corrects |
| The read | 403, or 404 | MSG-P4-002 for a caller without the right, MSG-P4-003 for a case outside the scope; no row is returned |

No screen shows a phone number or a LINE identifier: the record carries neither. A panel or screen id for showing a contact entry beside the message on SCR-04, and the field list of SCR-38, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1274; ASM-2252); the field list and the composite route specification belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and to the story that owns SCR-38.

##### 17. Guardrails
- No business value in code: the decision code, the final-call list, the reason-code list, the channel list, the page-size bound, the completeness target and the message ids are reference or parameter rows, and the rule ids and versions are facts of the owning service; nothing of them is a constant here.
- No personal data in the entry, the inputs reference, the event, the audit line, the tests or the logs: the case reference, the channel, the reason code, the rule id and version, the requesting role, the hashes and the dates only. The message body, the phone number, the LINE identifier and the contact value stay in `rwb_comms`, `rwb_source_data` and the ACE notification path (BR5, BR11).
- No cross-schema read and no cross-service write: the interaction and the consent are P1's, the case is P3's, the deviation is S8's, the template is P6's, the interface configuration is P2's and the role and scope are P4's; each is reached through its contract and none is copied (DP-01, DP-18). ACE data only through the owner's contract or the owner's `v_ace_*` views, and this story reads no ACE table and no ACE view, because the contact point never enters it (DP-05).
- One appender and no mover: this story changes no message, case, deviation, contact point or interaction, so a decision record can never send a message or clear a stop (BR8).
- No entry without its record and no record without its decision: the entry, its chain position, its inbox row and its idempotency row commit in one transaction, and a refusal whose record cannot be written is not completed, with incident under R-UNI-39 (BR12).
- Append only and hash chained: no UPDATE and no DELETE on `decision_log_entry`, a correction is a new entry with `corrects_entry_id`, and the chain is verifiable from `chain_seq` 1; the inbox dedupe, the idempotency key and the refusal of a duplicate append make a second entry impossible (BR3, BR4, BR6).
- One base and one topic: `/api/recovery/decision/v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` with `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`; no monolith base and no other service's base or topic is declared here as this service's own.
- One hop and 2 s with a breaker per downstream on the authorise call and the reference-data read; an unreadable list refuses the append rather than writing an assumed value (DP-11).
- The rule evaluation stays embedded in the owning service and this story loads no rule model and calls no Drools runtime on any path (DP-04, BR13).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-022 for rwb-comms. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **the SMS and LINE dispatch capability of rwb-comms deployed from the service template with its Helm values and its own login, its egress path to NSS and LINE OA through the ACE notification path with its credential and certificate references, the retry worker around the platform relay JOB-11, the alert on the five-attempt limit, the dashboards for the FAILED and exception-queue counts, a runbook for a stuck send, a smoke profile against the fakes, the feature switch and the rollback**, so that **an operator can see within minutes that a message is not leaving, that a channel's results have stopped arriving, or that sends are piling up in the exception queue, and repair it without reading code or waiting for a business report**.

This story deploys an existing capability. It builds no endpoint, no table, no topic and no workflow: the send is the operation of `RWB-P6-E2022-CON`, the message lifecycle is the outbox row in schema `rwb_comms`, and the every-minute retry is the platform outbox relay JOB-11.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy capability leaned on one Quartz job and one exception log for two very different failures. A message that the ACE notification path never accepted and a message whose result never came back looked the same from operations: nothing on the job record, nothing on the case, and a customer who was never reached. In the target the retry is the platform relay (Architecture v5 slide 44, JOB-11, every minute, every service), so the operational signal has to move from "did the job run" to "is a send leaving, is a result coming back, and is the exception queue growing".

There is a second operational fact that only deployment can carry: this is the one capability of rwb-comms whose failure reaches a customer outside the bank. NSS and LINE OA are reached only through the ACE notification path (REQ-DRI-006, INT-17 and INT-18), and that egress needs a certificate, an endpoint and a secret that the platform secret store holds and the chart only references. An operator who cannot see whether the egress is up will read the exception queue as a business problem.

Deployment is therefore part of the capability: the chart carries the rwb-comms login and no other credential (DP-02), the migration job runs the per-service Flyway sequence in schema `rwb_comms` (DP-15), the three consumer groups are provisioned with retry and `.dlt` paths so a contact stop is never missed (DP-09), and the runbook names the four failures an operator will actually see.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The Kafka event platform provisions topics with a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON), and `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and `rwb.case.events.v1` are provisioned by their owners.
- The observability stack of the platform is available (RWB-PLT-OBS, ADR-023): metrics, traces and logs with one trace across REST, Kafka and the outbound call.
- The three environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist with their parameter scope, their Kafka and Temporal endpoints and their egress rules to the ACE notification path.
- `RWB-P6-E2022-CON` is published, so the smoke profile and the drift test run against the operation and the four fakes of that baseline.
- `RWB-P6-E2022-APP` is delivered, so the send attempt, the result mapping and the exception state exist to be deployed and observed.
- The ACE notification path's endpoint, its client certificate and the secret names that hold them are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1074; ASM-2022); the chart references them as secret references until the path owner and the platform security team fix the names.
- The attempt limit of 5 and the exception-queue rule R-UNI-34 are service configuration of rwb-comms, not deployment values of the chart (GAP-1071; ASM-2019).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds one image and one chart version from the same commit, runs the unit, component and contract tests, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes the chart.
2. The chart deploys rwb-comms with the rwb-comms login, the pre-deploy migration job for schema `rwb_comms`, the readiness and liveness probes and the api deployment that serves the operation.
3. The egress step declares the outbound route to the ACE notification path for the two channels, the client certificate reference and the endpoint from the secret store; no chart value carries a literal endpoint, certificate or secret.
4. The provisioning step declares the consumer groups of `rwb-comms` on `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and `rwb.case.events.v1`, each with its retry topic and its `.dlt` topic, and confirms that the relay window of JOB-11 picks up the outbox rows of `rwb_comms` without a new Schedule.
5. The dashboards are published: sends by channel, sends by delivery status including FAILED, queue depth and exception count, accepted-reference latency, result latency, the attempt distribution up to the limit, the egress error rate, the MSG-GEN-006 rate and the refused counts.
6. The alerts are wired to the message IDs of section 14 and to the runbook entries of section 13; the thresholds are values and carry the placeholder of section 14 until they are confirmed.
7. A smoke step sends one SMS and one LINE message for a synthetic case against the fakes and the SIT profile, so the operation, the outbox row, the retry window, the result mapping and the fake of the notification path are exercised together.
8. The runbook is published and reviewed with the on-call rota: a stuck send, an egress that is down, a result that never arrives, an exception queue that grows, and a refused send that is not an incident.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The migration job fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic reaches the new version | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The egress route or the certificate reference is missing | The release fails the egress check and the send answers 503 on its first attempt; the runbook entry for an egress that is down starts | MSG-GEN-006 | AC2 |
| X3 | A consumer group is provisioned without its retry or `.dlt` topic | The provisioning step fails the release and the consumer refuses to start | None | AC3 |
| X4 | The attempt count of a send reaches the limit of 5 | The send moves to the exception state and the attempt-limit alert fires | None | AC4 |
| X5 | The result of an accepted send never arrives | The result-latency alert fires and the runbook entry for a result that never arrives names the reference and the channel | None | AC5, AC6 |
| X6 | The FAILED count or the exception count passes its value | The dashboard panel and its alert fire with the channel and the environment | None | AC5 |
| X7 | The feature switch is off in an environment | The send is refused closed with MSG-GEN-006 and nothing leaves; the refusal is counted, not paged | MSG-GEN-006 | AC8 |
| X8 | A rollback is ordered | The previous chart version is redeployed and the migration is reversed by its own script; the outbox rows are left for the earlier version to drain | None | AC8 |
| X9 | A refused send is counted as a failure | The refused count is a separate series and never opens a release incident | MSG-P4-002, MSG-P6-001 | AC5 |
| X10 | A release declares a new topic or a Schedule for the retry | The pipeline fails the release on the retired-element check of AC3 | None | AC3 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the platform topic provisioning, the secret store and the observability stack; builds no application code |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, alert thresholds and retention are environment values, not story decisions |
| Valuable | Makes an outbound capability observable: a send that does not leave, a result that does not return and a queue that grows each have a signal and an owner |
| Estimable | One chart, one pipeline stage, one migration job, two probes, three consumer groups, the egress step, eight dashboard panels, five alert rules and five runbook entries |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the egress check passes, the groups exist, the panels carry data, the alerts fire on a synthetic metric, the runbook entry resolves |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Deployment of SMS and LINE dispatch through NSS and LINE OA

  Background:
    Given the service template chart and the platform pipeline are in force
    Given the target environment is SIT

  Scenario: AC1 The Helm chart and values deploy rwb-comms with its own login (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-comms Helm chart and its values-dev.yaml, values-sit.yaml and values-uat.yaml
    When the chart is rendered for DEV, SIT and UAT
    Then each render succeeds with the chart version and the image digest pinned
    Then the release declares the rwb-comms login reference and no other service's credential
    Then the migration job runs the per-service Flyway sequence in schema rwb_comms before the deployment is marked ready, creating template, notice, merge_field and the outbox, inbox and idempotency objects
    Then the readiness probe answers healthy only when the schema is at the expected version and the consumer groups are subscribed
    Then no replica count, resource size, timeout, threshold or cadence is hard-coded in the template

  Scenario: AC2 The egress to NSS and LINE OA runs through the ACE notification path with referenced credentials (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the egress step of the release for the two channels
    When it is rendered for each environment
    Then the release declares one outbound route to the ACE notification path (INT-17, INT-18) and no route to NSS or LINE OA directly
    Then the client certificate, the trust material and the endpoint are secret references resolved at deploy time, and no values file, chart template or runbook holds a literal endpoint, certificate or secret
    Then the egress check fails the release when the route or the certificate reference is missing, and the send answers 503 with MSG-GEN-006 on its first attempt
    Then the concrete endpoint, the certificate issuer and the secret names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1074; ASM-2022)

  Scenario: AC3 The retry worker and JOB-11 are deployed without a new Schedule or topic (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the outbox rows of schema rwb_comms and the platform relay of JOB-11
    When the release is deployed and the provisioning step runs
    Then the send request is picked up by the every-minute relay window and executed by the rwb-comms send attempt, and no Temporal Schedule, cron entry or job row is registered by this release
    Then a consumer group rwb-comms subscribes to rwb.deviation.events.v1 for DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared and to rwb.case.events.v1 for CaseStateChanged, each with its retry topic and its .dlt topic, and the consumer never acknowledges an event it could not process
    Then rwb.decision-record.v1 is produced to as its owner provisions it and is not recreated, and no new topic is created for this capability
    Then the provisioning step fails the release when a retry or .dlt topic is missing, and the retired-element check fails a release that declares a Schedule for the retry

  Scenario: AC4 The five-attempt limit raises its alert (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a send whose attempts are counted from 1 to 5 in schema rwb_comms
    When the attempt count of one send reaches 5 and the row moves to the exception state under rule R-UNI-34
    Then one alert fires with the channel, the environment, the attempt count, the send reference and the age of the oldest affected row
    Then the alert links the exception-queue runbook entry and names the ACE notification path owner as the second-line contact
    Then the alert does not fire on a first or second attempt, and it fires once per send and not once per window
    Then the alert threshold and its evaluation window are deployment values with provisional defaults

  Scenario: AC5 The dashboards carry the delivery and exception series (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published dashboard
    When a synthetic day is replayed with delivered, read, failed and queued sends on both channels, one unavailable window and five sends that reached the limit
    Then the panels show sends by channel, sends by delivery status including FAILED, queue depth, the exception count, accepted-reference latency, result latency and the attempt distribution up to 5
    Then every panel names its service, its environment and its business date
    Then a refused send is counted on its own series and never opens a release incident
    Then no panel carries a phone number, a LINE identifier, a message body, an addressee or an account number, only references and counts

  Scenario: AC6 The runbook covers a stuck send, a down egress, a missing result and a growing exception queue (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published runbook and the five alert rules
    When a send sits in the queued state beyond its window, the egress answers 503, an accepted reference has no result, or the exception count passes its value
    Then each condition has one runbook entry with the check, the owner role and the recovery step
    Then the stuck-send entry names the outbox row, the attempt count, the last error and the send reference, and the step that is safe to repeat
    Then the missing-result entry names the external reference and the channel and states that a resend uses a new Idempotency-Key only after the first reference is confirmed lost
    Then every alert links exactly one runbook entry and every entry names the escalation path when the step fails

  Scenario: AC7 The smoke profile runs against the fakes before a real send (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the SIT smoke profile with the four fakes of RWB-P6-E2022-CON
    When the smoke step runs on the release build
    Then it sends one SMS and one LINE message for case "RC-2026-000777" and party "P-0077" with synthetic tokens and test numbers only
    Then it asserts the 202 answer, the outbox row, the retry window, the DELIVERED and READ statuses and one refusal with MSG-P6-002
    Then it exercises the MSG-GEN-006 path with the notification path fake answering unavailable and asserts the exception state at attempt 5
    Then it asserts that no phone number, LINE identifier or message body appears in a log line or a metric label

  Scenario: AC8 The feature switch and the rollback are safe (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the feature switch rwb.comms.sms-line and the two channel switches in the values files
    When the switch is off in an environment and a send is requested
    Then the send is refused closed with MSG-GEN-006, nothing leaves for the ACE notification path and the refusal is counted on its own series
    When a rollback is ordered
    Then the previous chart version and its image digest are redeployed, the migration is reversed by its own script, and the outbox rows are left for the earlier version to drain without a duplicate send
    Then the rollback is rehearsed once in SIT and the rehearsal is recorded in the runbook
```

These eight criteria are new for the deployment and test artefacts only; they restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P6-E2022-APP.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every outbound message carries a conduct check result on its ledger entry | REQ-OCC-005; FEAT-OCC-05 |
| BR2 | No message is sent while a contact stop is in force | CTL-16; R-UNI-04, R-UNI-05 |
| BR3 | Deviation codes that block SMS and LINE are a reference list, loaded as data by their owner | R-DEV-16; R-UNI-12 |
| BR4 | Messages go only to a verified contact point with consent GIVEN for that channel; the deployment holds no copy of a contact point | CTL-17; R-UNI-10 |
| BR5 | A legal hold stops every outbound action | R-UNI-20 |
| BR6 | A system that is unavailable queues the send and retries; after the limit of 5 it goes to the exception queue and the attempt-limit alert fires | R-UNI-33, R-UNI-34, R-UNI-36 |
| BR7 | A refusal that cannot be written to the decision record is not completed, and the 503 is counted as an incident path, not as a business refusal | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR8 | Only the current Approved template for the channel is used; the deployment seeds no template | R-LIT-03; CTL-14 |
| BR9 | The same request twice sends one message; a resend after a lost reference uses a new key only when the first is confirmed lost | R-UNI-40 |
| BR10 | A message raised by a route rule — the offer letter of R-RES-09 — is not part of this deployment's traffic | R-RES-09; legacy section 19 |
| BR11 | One service, one schema, one login: the release uses the rwb-comms login and no other service's credential | DP-02; Architecture v5 slide 29 |
| BR12 | The migration is a per-service Flyway sequence in schema rwb_comms and runs before the deployment is ready | DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| BR13 | Every subscription has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and a consumer never acknowledges an event it could not process | DP-09; Architecture v5 slide 22 notes |
| BR14 | No Schedule and no new topic is created for this capability: the retry is the platform relay JOB-11 and the topics belong to their owners | DP-10, DP-14; Architecture v5 slide 44 |
| BR15 | No environment value is hard-coded: replica counts, resource sizes, timeouts, thresholds and the attempt limit are values or service configuration | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR16 | An alert carries a message ID where the condition maps to one, and links one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR17 | No dashboard series, log line, alert payload or runbook entry carries a phone number, a LINE identifier, a message body or an addressee; references and counts only | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; legacy section 17 |
| BR18 | No literal endpoint, certificate or secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; the chart carries references only | NFR-052; TSD P6 T7 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart, the migration job and the egress check pass the pipeline | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration complete and probes healthy | The schema is at the expected version and the consumers are subscribed | Ready |
| Ready | Release superseded | A new chart version is promoted | Rolling |
| Rolling | All pods on the new version | The old ReplicaSet drains | Ready |
| Ready | Egress check failed | The route or the certificate reference is missing | Failed |
| Failed | Rollback | The previous chart version is redeployed and the migration is reversed by its own script | Ready |

The message lifecycle — QUEUED, SENT, DELIVERED, READ, FAILED, EXCEPTION — is the capability's own and is described in RWB-P6-E2022-APP; this story observes it and changes no state of it.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the egress step, the provisioning step, the dashboards, the alerts and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the topic provisioning and the platform relay window |
| Platform security team | Owns the client certificate and the secret material of the egress, and approves the reference the chart carries |
| ACE database administrator | Owns schema rwb_comms, the login and its grants, and approves the migration job |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact through the environments and the rollback rehearsal |
| On-call operator | Runs the runbook entries and opens an incident when a send is stuck or the exception queue grows beyond its value |
| ACE notification path owner | Is paged by the egress-down and missing-result alerts and owns the repair beyond the rwb-comms breaker |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Reads the exception queue in the running service, not in the cluster |

The per-service login name, the certificate and the secret names used by the chart are secret references resolved at deploy time; the chart references "the rwb-comms login (DP-02)" and the egress material by reference, never by literal value.

##### 11. Data

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Deployment values | Image digest, chart version, replica counts, resource requests and limits, probe paths and timings, log level, the feature switch `rwb.comms.sms-line` and the two channel switches, the client timeouts, the edge and the egress timeouts, the alert thresholds |
| Schema | rwb_comms, migrated by the per-service Flyway sequence; the tables template, notice and merge_field with the library objects outbox_event, processed_event and idempotency_key |
| Topics | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` subscribes DeviationRaised and DeviationCleared; `rwb.case.events.v1` subscribes CaseStateChanged; `rwb.decision-record.v1` is produced to as its owner provisions it; `rwb.comms.events.v1` is not created or extended by this capability |
| Egress | One outbound route to the ACE notification path for SMS and LINE, with the client certificate, the trust material and the endpoint as secret references |
| Dashboard series | sends by channel, sends by delivery status, queue depth, exception count, accepted-reference latency, result latency, attempt distribution, egress error rate, MSG-GEN-006 rate, refused counts, consumer lag |
| Runbook entries | stuck send, egress down, result never arrives, exception queue grows, refused send is not an incident |
| Secrets | The rwb-comms login secret, the Kafka client credential, the egress client certificate and the endpoint, all from the platform secret store |

The alert values, the egress endpoint, the certificate issuer and the secret names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1074; ASM-2022). The exact cluster topology, node pools, replica counts and probe timings are deployment values of the platform chart and are not fixed here. The attempt limit of 5 and the exception-queue rule are service configuration of rwb-comms, not chart values (GAP-1071; ASM-2019).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None new. The deployment exposes the one operation of `RWB-P6-E2022-CON` behind gateway-bff: `POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/messages`, owner rwb-comms (P6), API-P6-008, with the 202 `Interaction` answer, the seven refusal conditions and the Idempotency-Key header. The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None by the deployment. The outbound call of the capability is not a REST operation of a service in this workspace: it is the ACE notification path (INT-17, INT-18), an ACE common module interface whose request and result shapes are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1069; ASM-2017). Its endpoint and certificate are secret references of AC2, and the deployment adds no consumer of the P1, P3, S8 or P7 contracts: those are the app story's and are faked for the smoke profile.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The capability's one published element is `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, written by the local decision-record library and relayed by the platform relay; the shared topic is provisioned by its owner and is reused, not recreated (DP-03, DP-09). This deployment creates no topic and publishes no comms event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None provisioned by this story as a new group for the capability's own logic beyond the three subscriptions of AC3: `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` and `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` on `rwb.deviation.events.v1`, and `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1`. All three are consumed by one group `rwb-comms` with the inbox of schema `rwb_comms`, each with its retry topic and its `.dlt` topic.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The retry worker of this capability is not a Temporal workflow: it is the platform relay window of JOB-11 calling the rwb-comms send attempt, plus the result handling in the service. No worker deployment polls a task queue for this capability, and no activity is registered on `rwb-comms`.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-11 Outbox sender is the platform's outbox relay, every minute, with every service as its owner (Architecture v5 slide 44); this release registers no Schedule and no cron entry, and the five-attempt limit is applied inside the send attempt rather than by a scheduler (GAP-1071; ASM-2019).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None new. The migration job creates and migrates the tables of `rwb_comms` — template, notice, merge_field, outbox_event, processed_event and idempotency_key — and touches no other schema (DP-01). `interaction` and `contact_point_ext` stay with P1, `recovery_case` and `task` with P3, `deviation` with S8 and `decision_log_entry` with P7; no dashboard query reads any of them.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Deployment use |
|---|---|
| ACE notification path stub | Runs in the pipeline and in the SIT smoke profile: an accepted reference with DELIVERED, the LINE delivered then read, a FAILED result and an `unavailable` answer for six attempts |
| rwb-source-data WireMock | Same profile: the consent GIVEN and WITHDRAWN answers and the failed-count update |
| rwb-case WireMock | Same profile: legal hold false and true, and a delayed answer beyond 2 s |
| rwb-deviation WireMock | Same profile: the open deviation X1 with contact stop on and an empty answer |

The fakes are test-only workloads; they are not deployed into UAT or production, and each is replaced by the real owner as its story lands.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 1 provided, 1 consumed outside the workspace | The send operation provided; the outbound call to the ACE notification path (INT-17, INT-18); one hop, 2 s |
| Kafka | 1 produced to a shared topic, 3 consumed | `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` reused; `DeviationRaised`, `DeviationCleared` and `CaseStateChanged` consumed with retry and `.dlt` |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, no activity and no Schedule; the retry is the platform relay JOB-11 |
| File | None | The release reads no runtime file; values files and chart templates are build inputs |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_comms`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/comms/v1` | none |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-10 is claimed only for the relay dependency: no Schedule is registered by this release. DP-05 applies as a prohibition: no dashboard and no smoke step reads an ACE view.

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-comms/` | Chart with the api deployment, service, migration job, config map, secret references, probes, the egress configuration and the Schedule hook that registers nothing for this capability |
| `helm/rwb-comms/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, `rwb.comms.sms-line` and the two channel switches, the client and egress timeouts, the alert thresholds |
| Egress step | One outbound route to the ACE notification path, the client certificate and endpoint references, and the check that fails the release when either is missing |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit, component and contract tests, retired-element check, egress check, image and dependency scan, chart publish, promote the same artefact |
| Provisioning step | Consumer group `rwb-comms` on `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and `rwb.case.events.v1` with retry and `.dlt`; reuse of `rwb.decision-record.v1`; confirmation that the relay window of JOB-11 drains `rwb_comms` |
| Dashboards | Eight panels: sends by channel; sends by delivery status; queue depth; exception count; accepted-reference latency; result latency; attempt distribution up to 5; egress error rate, MSG-GEN-006 rate and refused counts |
| Alerts | Five rules, each with a message ID where one applies and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Five entries: stuck send, egress down, result never arrives, exception queue grows, refused send is not an incident |

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only when the migration is at the expected schema version and the consumer groups are subscribed; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database, calls another service or calls the ACE notification path.

**Alert mapping.**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | The attempt count of a send reaches 5 and the row moves to the exception state | Attempt-limit alert with the channel, the attempt count, the send reference and the age of the oldest affected row | Platform on-call, ticket to the ACE notification path owner |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The egress answers 503 or the notification path is unavailable on a share of sends | Egress error-rate alert with the breaker state and the environment | Platform on-call, page, ACE notification path owner |
| None | An accepted reference has no result inside the result window | Result-latency alert with the reference, the channel and the oldest affected send | Platform on-call, ticket |
| None | The exception count passes its value | Exception-queue alert with the count and its change against the trailing hour | Platform on-call, page |
| MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P6-001 | A send is refused for want of a right or for a contact stop | Refused count on the dashboard | No page |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The feature switch is off and the send is refused closed | Switch-off count on the dashboard | No page |

Every alert carries its message ID where the condition maps to one, and the three conditions without a message ID carry the series name instead. The alert thresholds, the result window and the pending values are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1074; ASM-2022); the values are provisional defaults until they are confirmed.

**Done when.** The chart renders in all three environments, the pipeline promotes one artefact and fails on a fake drift, a missing retry topic, a missing egress reference or a retired element, the three consumer groups exist with their retry and `.dlt` paths, the eight panels carry the synthetic day, the five alert conditions fire on synthetic metrics, the smoke profile passes against the fakes with no personal data in a log line or a metric label, and the five runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P6-001 | A contact stop applies | Contact with this customer is stopped for {reason}. |
| MSG-P6-002 | No consent for the channel | The customer has not consented to {channel}. Use another channel. |
| MSG-P6-003 | The template is withdrawn | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-P3-004 | A legal hold is on the case | This case is on hold for {deviation}. The prescription date is still {date}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks Case record C | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Channel or template missing | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | NSS or LINE OA is unavailable, the egress is down, or the switch is off | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The alert values, the egress endpoint and the secret names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1074; ASM-2022); the message texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story and the deployment adds the routing, the threshold and the runbook link, never a new wording.

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment serves SCR-03 Case record with the Send message action in its editable and refused states, SCR-04 Case timeline with the message row in its Loading and filtered states, and SCR-09 Exception queue, all through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The operator-facing surfaces of this story are the pipeline run view, the release view, the egress check result, the eight dashboard panels and the runbook; the smoke step sends one SMS and one LINE message for a synthetic case in SIT and asserts the 202 answer, the outbox row, the retry window, the two channel statuses and one refusal inside the 2 s budget.
