**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the case-side slice of RWB-E2-024 is written for `rwb-case` on schema `rwb_case`, REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1`, queue `rwb-case`, against the contract baseline RWB-P5-E2024-CON. Status Draft because no approval of the realigned story is recorded (GAP-2223; ASM-3660). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **field collector who syncs a visit and the case owner who chases what the visit did not deliver**, I want **the case a capture is checked against — its number, its status, its entry date, its stage and its route — the answer that the case is mine because I hold a task or an assignment on it, and one task on the case when a required document is still missing after a sync**, so that **an inspection is accepted only against its own case with that case's own entry date, and nothing the visit was supposed to produce is lost because a document did not arrive**.

Inside `rwb-case` this is the case-side slice of legacy RWB-E2-024: the case context and the one record the field-capture path of the document hub stands on.

- Service `rwb-case`, schema `rwb_case`, REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1` with event names `rwb.case.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`.
- The slice delivers four answers and one record. The answers are the `Case` resource of `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` — case number, status, entry date `DF-CAS-013`, stage code `DF-CAS-006`, route code `DF-CAS-008` and the caller's task and assignment; the case-scope answer taken from the `rwb-access` authorise contract; the stage and route keys the checklist is read by; and the `DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST` version in force as reference data. The record is the task raised when a required document is still missing after a sync.
- The capture is not here: the upload, the manifest, the limits, the scan, the OCR, the extraction, the bill threshold and SCR-30 are `rwb-document`'s (RWB-P5-E2024-APP), the rights and the scope policy are `rwb-access`'s (RWB-P4-E2024-APP), and the field app is the field app's.
- The entry date is answered once as the comparison date of the capture-time-before-entry-date check (legacy BR3); the age limit is measured by the hub from the receipt time, so this service answers a date and never a limit.
- The task and the assignment that make a case `OWN` are this service's rows, so the scope evidence is resolved here while the scope policy stays `rwb-access`'s. The checklist items are the hub's; this service holds only the checklist *version* as a `reference_version` row and the stage and route that select the items.
- The service writes the task as one `task` row and one DP-03 entry in one transaction, and publishes no event of its own: `rwb.case.events.v1` stays the case baseline's.

##### 2. Business rationale

Inspection photos and utility bills are sent today by chat or carried back to the office, the date and place of a visit cannot be shown when it is questioned, and a checklist meant to be completed during the visit is found to be incomplete only when someone asks the borrower again. The legacy story put the capture into the intake path of the document hub. This slice supplies the three things that path cannot invent for itself — the case a capture belongs to, the entry date the capture time is compared with, and the answer that the collector is entitled to the case at all — and closes the loop the legacy story left open: when a sync leaves a required document missing, the case gets one task and one timeline entry, so the missing deed is chased on the case instead of in a chat.

The story carries controls CTL-11 (position and photos of a home are personal data) and the evidence expectation of R-DIL-22 (`checklist, photographs and bills captured` before the asset unlock decision), L3 process 13 Manage documents and correspondence, and feature FEAT-DCM-21. It meets REQ-DCM-013 on the case side.

The realignment changes the mechanism, not the rule: DP-01 and DP-11 turn `CaseDirectory.findById` into the published case operation of this service in `rwb_case` (one hop, 2 s timeout, a fake, no copied case row); DP-11 turns the ACE common access check into the `rwb-access` authorise contract as data while the task and the assignment stay `rwb_case` rows; DP-07 answers the checklist version as reference data and leaves the items to the hub; DP-06, DP-07 and DP-03 make the task a `task` row whose code, owner role and due date are data, recorded through the local decision-record library in the same transaction and published on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; DP-09 consumes `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` through the inbox, deduplicated by event ID; DP-15 and DP-19 give one migration in this service's Flyway sequence and the composite route to the screens.

That resource is published with twelve fields and does not name the stage code or the route code, although the field range it cites (DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023) covers both: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2223; ASM-3657) |

The story that publishes that baseline is not named in the sources (GAP-2223; ASM-3658) |

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E2-024:

- The collector holds a task on the case, so the case is in `OWN` scope; a case with no task and no assignment for the caller is outside the scope and is answered 404 with MSG-P4-003 (FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-004-01).
- The case in the tests is the legacy deed in lieu case at stage `DEED_IN_LIEU` with entry date `2026-10-02`, so the checklist of R-DIL-22 (`WITH_FIELD_INSPECTION`) is the one read here.
- The checklist version label `CHK-2026.11` is a test value only: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2223; ASM-3659).
- Every refusal names the case and the action only, never a customer field, a document, a position or a file name (legacy section 17; CTL-11).

##### 4. Flow

1. Field collector: opens the case in the field app and starts a capture batch; the app asks the Workbench for the case context.
2. `CaseContextController`, through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19): serves `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` — case number, status, entry date `DF-CAS-013`, stage code `DF-CAS-006`, route code `DF-CAS-008` and the caller's open task and current assignment.
3. `CaseScopeResolver`: for area `DOCUMENTS` and right `C`, calls `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` on `rwb-access` with the caller, the case, the area, the right and the case activity that makes it `OWN` (DP-11, one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker). `rwb-access` answers allowed or refused: 403 MSG-P4-002 for a right the role does not carry, 404 MSG-P4-003 for a case outside the scope, and this service adds no second policy check.
4. The field app: sends the batch to the document hub with the case in the path; the comparison date of the capture-time-before-entry-date check is the entry date of step 2, `2026-10-02`, and the age limit is measured by the hub from the receipt time.
5. `ChecklistVersionReader`: answers the `DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST` version in force through the reference-data contract (DP-07) — label, state and valid-from — so the hub resolves the required item of the case's stage and route against one version.
6. The document hub: stores the accepted captures through its own store, satisfies the item of each stored type, and publishes `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` once per accepted item.
7. `DocumentStoredListener`, through the inbox of DP-09: records the event ID once, ignores a repeat, and reads the case checklist through API-P5-008 — one hop, 2 s timeout.
8. `ChecklistTaskRaiser`: when the answer still lists a required type, raises one `task` — element type `HUMAN_TASK`, discretion `REQUIRED`, status `OPEN`, the task code read from reference data naming the missing type and the checklist version, the owner role read from reference data, and the due date from the parameter in force (DP-06, DP-07).
9. `DecisionRecordWriter`, in the same transaction as the task: writes the DP-03 entry with the case, the rule reference, the missing type, the checklist version and the task reference, and publishes on `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the outbox.
10. Case owner: opens `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline` and sees the task as a `TASK` item with actor `SY-CASEWF`, source system `WORKBENCH` and its time, beside the document items the hub composes; once the document is on the case, the owner completes the task through the task API with the outcome code read from reference data.

A task that cannot be recorded is not raised (step 9, R-UNI-39); a checklist answer that does not arrive leaves the case unchanged with the reason in the log, rather than a task without evidence (step 7).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The case does not exist | 404; no task, no record, no data | MSG-P4-003 | AC4 |
| X2 | The case exists but the caller holds no task and no assignment on it | The scope answer is refused and the case read returns 404; nothing is raised | MSG-P4-003 | AC4 |
| X3 | The role does not carry Documents `C` | 403 from the authorise answer, naming the action and the area; the batch is not accepted | MSG-P4-002 | AC3 |
| X4 | The authorise call does not answer within 2 s or meets an open breaker | The case context is not served; the app may retry the same request; nothing is raised | MSG-GEN-006 | AC3 |
| X5 | The checklist answer does not answer within 2 s | No task is raised, nothing changes, and the reason is in the log; the event stays in the inbox | MSG-GEN-006 | AC6 |
| X6 | The checklist lists no required type for the stage and route | The answer is empty and no task is raised; the case is unchanged | None | AC5, AC6 |
| X7 | A required type is still missing after the sync | One `OPEN` task with the missing type in its code, and one decision-record entry | None | AC6, AC7 |
| X8 | The same `DocumentStored` event is redelivered, or the sync is resent | The inbox ignores the repeat; the open task is unchanged and no second task is raised | None | AC8 |
| X9 | The decision record cannot be written | The task is not raised, nothing changes, and an incident is raised | MSG-P7-003 | AC6, TC-E2-024-17 |
| X10 | The earlier task is completed and a later sync still leaves the type missing | One new task is raised for that type, because the earlier one is closed | None | AC8 |

A refusal, a timeout and a failed record all leave the case, its tasks and its decision record as they were; only a checklist answer that names a required type and a committed record produce a task.

| Independent | Builds against the case baseline RWB-P3-E1018-CON, the reference-data and parameters contracts of this service, the `rwb-access` authorise contract and RWB-P5-E2024-CON, each with a fake; no other Epic 2 story is needed |
| Negotiable | The task code, owner role, discretion, due date and checklist version are data rows; the story fixes the answers and the one task |
| Valuable | A capture is accepted only against its own case and entry date, and a document the visit did not produce becomes a task on the case before anyone asks the borrower again |
| Estimable | Two read operations used, one authorise call, one checklist read, one task raise with its record, one index migration |
| Small | Fits one week with its tests, because the upload, the scan, the OCR, the checklist items and the screens are other stories' |
| Testable | Every criterion in section 7 is one test case in section 16; the case, the task, the checklist and the document event come from contract fakes |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Case context, case scope and the missing-document task for field app captures

  Background:
    Given the environment is SIT
    Given case "RW-2026-000501" with entry date 2026-10-02, status "IN_PROGRESS" and stage "DEED_IN_LIEU", and a field inspection task for field collector "FC-01" with role RW-FIELDCOL
    Given the rwb-access contract mock returns allowed for "FC-01" on area "DOCUMENTS", right "C" and scope "OWN" for case "RW-2026-000501"
    Given the rwb-document contract mock returns the document checklist of case "RW-2026-000501" with checklist version "CHK-2026.11", "INSPECTION_PHOTO" present and "SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT" required and missing
    Given the rwb-document contract mock returns document "DOC-0501-01" of type "INSPECTION_PHOTO" for case "RW-2026-000501", stored at 2026-12-15 14:20
    Given the reference-data contract returns LOV-TASK-STATUS with "OPEN", LOV-ELEMENT with "HUMAN_TASK", LOV-DISCRETION with "REQUIRED" and LOV-SOURCE with "WORKBENCH"
    Given the parameters contract returns the checklist task due-date parameter in force

  Scenario: AC1 The case context of a capture (new, D-RCV-60)
    When "FC-01" reads GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} for case "RW-2026-000501" before the batch is sent
    Then the answer is 200 with case number "RW-2026-000501", status "IN_PROGRESS", entry date 2026-10-02, stage code "DEED_IN_LIEU" and the route code of the case
    Then the answer carries the field inspection task of "FC-01" with status "OPEN" and element type "HUMAN_TASK"
    Then the answer carries no customer field, no document, no file and no position

  Scenario: AC2 The case entry date is the comparison date of a capture (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-document contract mock refuses the item captured at 2026-10-01 09:00 with MSG-GEN-003 naming "Capture time" and "Case entry date"
    When the refusal is resolved against the case answer of this service
    Then the case answer carries entry date 2026-10-02 and no other date is offered for the comparison
    Then the refusal names 2026-10-02 as the case entry date
    Then no case row, no task and no document is changed by the refusal

  Scenario: AC3 A collector with a task holds the case in scope (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given "FC-01" holds the field inspection task on case "RW-2026-000501" and an assignment from 2026-10-02 with reason "ALLOCATION"
    When the case context is resolved for area "DOCUMENTS", right "C" and case "RW-2026-000501"
    Then the answer is allowed with scope "OWN" and the case in scope
    Then the activity that makes the case "OWN" is the open task and the open assignment of "FC-01", and no other case is returned
    Then the call to POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise carries the case, the area and the right and no customer field

  Scenario: AC4 A case with no task and no assignment is refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RW-2026-000502" where "FC-01" holds no task and no assignment
    When "FC-01" reads GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId} for case "RW-2026-000502"
    Then the response is 404 with message MSG-P4-003
    Then the authorise answer for that case is refused and no case data is returned
    Then no task is raised and no decision record is written for "RW-2026-000502"

  Scenario: AC5 The checklist keys and the checklist version (new, D-RCV-60)
    When the case answer of "RW-2026-000501" is read by the document hub
    Then the answer carries stage code "DEED_IN_LIEU" and the route code of the case, the two keys the checklist is read by
    Then the reference-data answer carries the DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST version "CHK-2026.11" in force with its state and its valid-from date
    Then no checklist item row is written in rwb_case: the items stay in the document hub's document_checklist_item

  Scenario: AC6 A required document still missing raises one case task (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the sync of 2026-12-15 14:20 stored ten documents and rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 is consumed for document "DOC-0501-01"
    When the checklist answer of the case still lists "SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT" as required and missing
    Then one task exists on case "RW-2026-000501" with element type "HUMAN_TASK", discretion "REQUIRED", status "OPEN" and the owner role read from reference data
    Then the task code names the missing type "SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT" and the checklist version "CHK-2026.11", read from reference data
    Then the task due date is the value of the parameter in force and no due date is written in code
    Then one decision-record entry is written in the same transaction as the task

  Scenario: AC7 The task appears on the case timeline (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the case timeline of "RW-2026-000501" is read through GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline
    When the task of AC6 is "OPEN"
    Then one item of type "TASK" shows the task with actor "SY-CASEWF", source system "WORKBENCH" and its created time
    Then the document items of the timeline are the document hub's and the ledger's, and this service writes no document item

  Scenario: AC8 A repeated sync or a repeated event raises no second task (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the task of AC6 is "OPEN" on case "RW-2026-000501" for the type "SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT"
    When the same rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 event is delivered again and the officer resends the same ten client file IDs
    Then no second task exists and the first task is unchanged
    Then the inbox holds the event ID once and the duplicate is ignored
```

These eight criteria are the ones this slice owns and all are new under D-RCV-60, because a secondary slice owns no legacy criterion: legacy AC1 to AC15 of RWB-E2-024 are carried by `rwb-document` (RWB-P5-E2024-APP) against RWB-P5-E2024-CON and the legacy access answer by `rwb-access` (RWB-P4-E2024-APP). The legacy test cases are kept here in section 16 against this slice's assertions, so nothing the legacy story proves is lost. The shared values are the legacy ones unchanged: case `RW-2026-000501` with entry date `2026-10-02`, collector `FC-01` with role `RW-FIELDCOL`, the ten-file inspection of `2026-12-15 14:20` at `13.7563` and `100.5018`, the offline capture at `2026-12-14 10:05`, the entry-date refusal of `2026-10-01 09:00` against `2026-10-02`, and case `RW-2026-000502` with no task for `FC-01`. The authorise request and response shape, the stage and route fields of the case answer, the checklist version label and the task data are not in the sources: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2223; ASM-3657), (GAP-2223; ASM-3658), (GAP-2223; ASM-3659).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A capture belongs to the case named in the request: the case number, status, entry date and stage and route are read from the case row of `rwb_case`, and no case is matched, created or changed on this path | Legacy RWB-E2-024 BR6; FEAT-DCM-21 |
| BR2 | A capture is accepted only for a case the collector is entitled to: the scope answer comes from `rwb-access` on the caller's task or open assignment, and a case with neither is answered 404 with MSG-P4-003 | Legacy AC12 and X7; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-004-01; TSD P3 v3 T6.1 |
| BR3 | The case entry date `DF-CAS-013` is the comparison date of the capture-time-before-entry-date check; the age limit is measured by the document hub from the receipt time and is not answered here | Legacy BR3; DF-CAS-013; CAPTURE_MAX_AGE_DAYS |
| BR4 | The document checklist is read by the case's stage code and route code, and the checklist version in force is a `reference_version` row answered through the reference-data contract | REQ-DCM-011; DF-REF-243; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 |
| BR5 | The required document types and their present counts are the document hub's `document_checklist_item` and `case_document_check`; no checklist item row is written or copied in `rwb_case` | TSD P5 v2 T3.1; Ownership Map (P5) |
| BR6 | A required document still missing after a sync raises one `OPEN` task, only one per case and missing type: a redelivered event or a resent sync raises nothing, and a new task comes only after the earlier one is closed | Legacy X1 and AC4; R-UNI-40 |
| BR7 | The task and its decision-record entry commit in one transaction, so a task that cannot be recorded is not raised | Legacy BR10 and X12; Principle 5; R-UNI-39; DP-03 |
| BR8 | The task is visible on the case timeline as a `TASK` item with its actor, source system and time, and the timeline shows the documents the hub stored without this service copying them | REQ-OCC-008; FEAT-WKM-08; TSD P3 v3 API-P3-003 |
| BR9 | No personal data on this path: the case context carries the case and not the customer, and a position, a file name, a bill value and a photo never enter the task, the record or a log line | Legacy BR9; CTL-11; DL26 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-case`:

- BR1 is one read of `recovery_case` by `id`, keyed by the case in the path; the case number is the value the case was created with (RWB-P3-E1018-APP). BR2 is one call on the authorise contract with the case and the caller's activity; the letters and the policy are rows of `rwb_access`, and a missing row is a refusal, never a default allow.
- BR3 is the presence of `entryDate` in the answer and nothing else: with no age limit and no clock here, the check cannot be duplicated with a different value. BR4 is the `reference_version` read for table code `DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST` under the valid-from rule, with the status list `LOV-VERSION-STATUS`.
- BR5 is an absence: a test asserts that no `document_checklist_item` and no `case_document_check` row is created in `rwb_case`. BR6 is the partial unique index `ux_task_case_code_open ON task (case_id, task_code) WHERE status = 'OPEN'` plus inbox deduplication, so it holds against both a redelivered event and a resent sync.
- BR7 is one transaction of the `task` row and the DP-03 entry, with the DP-09 idempotency key on the internal raise. BR8 is the task read of the timeline: the document items are composed from the hub's read, so this service writes no document item.
- BR9 is a check on the writer: it writes the case, the missing type code, the checklist version and the task reference, and a test scans the text for any part of a position, a file name or a bill value.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case. This story changes no case status, stage or route: the case context is read and the task is the only row written.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | The checklist answer names a required type and the record commits | No `OPEN` task exists for the case and that type | `OPEN`, with the owner role and due date of the data |
| `OPEN` | The document of the missing type is stored on the case | The case owner completes the task through the task API | `DONE`, with the outcome code of the reference data |
| `OPEN` | The case owner starts the chase | None | `IN_PROGRESS` |
| `OPEN` or `IN_PROGRESS` | The case closes | The closure reason is recorded by the case | `CANCELED` |
| `DONE` or `CANCELED` | A later sync leaves the same type missing again | No `OPEN` task exists for the case and that type | `OPEN`, a new task row |

The task states are the `LOV-TASK-STATUS` values read as reference data. The case state machine is the case baseline's (R-UNI-01 to R-UNI-50) and this story moves nothing in it.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| `RW-FIELDCOL` Field collector | Reads the case context of a case they hold a task or an assignment on (Case record `R`) and sends its captures through the document hub (Documents `C`) |
| `RW-CASEOWN` Case owner | Reads the context and the timeline (`CRU`) and receives and completes the missing-document task (`CRU`) |
| `RW-RESTRUCT` Restructuring officer (FCR) | Reads the context and the captured documents on deed in lieu cases (`RU`) |
| `RW-PHONECOL` Phone collector | Reads only (`R`); holds no Documents `C` and cannot send a capture |
| `RW-TEAMMGR` Team manager | Reads the case record and the timeline (`R`) and reassigns the task (queue and allocation `CRUA`) |
| `SY-CASEWF` Case workflow module | Service identity: writes the task and its record, and reads the case and the checklist answer |
| `SY-OCR` OCR and extraction pipeline | Reads the case context of a case it extracts for (`R`) |

The rights and the scope policy are `rwb-access`'s and are not restated here. The owner role of the task is read from reference data and is not fixed by this story: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2223; ASM-3659).

The `Case` resource of RWB-P3-E1018-CON does not name `stageCode` and `routeCode` although its field range covers them: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2223; ASM-3657). ##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None new. The case context and the case timeline are served through operations of the case baseline RWB-P3-E1018-CON on base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, owner P3 `rwb-case`; this slice adds no path, no query parameter and no response field, and decides the following behind them:

| Method | Path | API ID | Purpose in this story | Authorization | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | API-P3-002 | The case context of a capture: case number, status, entry date, stage code, route code and the caller's task and assignment | Case record `R`, scope applied through the authorise contract | 401; 403 MSG-P4-002; 404 MSG-P4-003; 503 MSG-GEN-006 |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline` | API-P3-003 | The `TASK` item of the missing-document task, composed with the other sources of the timeline | Case record `R`, scope applied | 401; 403 MSG-P4-002; 404 MSG-P4-003; 503 MSG-GEN-006 |

The `Case` resource and the `TimelinePage` shape are the baseline's (RWB-P3-E1018-CON, RWB-P3-E1023-CON); the stage code `DF-CAS-006` and the route code `DF-CAS-008` this slice needs are Not specified in the source documents as named fields of that resource (GAP-2223; ASM-3657). The field app uses this operation and no second one: an app-specific path would be a second contract for one resource.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Story | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 `rwb-access` | RWB-P4-E1037-CON | The case-scope answer for area `DOCUMENTS`, right `C` and the case as the object reference, with the caller's open task or assignment as the `OWN` activity; one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker. The request and response shape is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2223; ASM-3657) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/document-checklist` | P5 `rwb-document` | API-P5-008; the story that publishes this baseline is not named in the sources (GAP-2223; ASM-3658) | The required document types of the case with their present counts, read once per consumed `DocumentStored` event; one hop, 2 s timeout, and a failed read raises no task |

The reference-data read of DP-07 and the parameters read of DP-06 are this service's own contracts (RWB-P3-E1043-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON) and are served inside the service without a hop; this slice is their consumer for the five lists and one parameter it names, and no list value and no number is typed in code.

###### 12.3 Events published

None for this slice. The task is read from the task API and from the case timeline, and this service publishes no event when it raises a task, so the six event types of `rwb.case.events.v1` — `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseAllocationFailed.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` and `rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1` — stay exactly the set the case baseline publishes. The decision-record entry is published by the DP-03 library on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and is not an event of this service's topic.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` (the legacy DocumentStored, EV-16) | `rwb.document.events.v1`, through the inbox of DP-09 | P5 `rwb-document` | One per accepted capture: the trigger of the checklist read of step 8. Deduplicated by event ID; the payload carries no position, no file name and no bill value and none of them is copied into the task or the record |

No other event is consumed: the sync itself is a request on the document hub, and the task is raised from the checklist answer of the hub, not from a case event.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. This story starts no workflow, registers no activity and signals none. `CaseWorkflow` (workflow ID `case-{caseId}`, task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`) is Epic 3 work (ADR-011) and is not used here; the task raise is a synchronous transaction of the service.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None for this story. No Temporal Schedule, no `JOB-nn` and no clock belongs to this path: the only time value here is the due date of the task, which is a parameter row.

| `recovery_case` | P3 (`rwb_case`) | The case context: id, case_no, status, stage_code, route_code, entry_date — read only |

| `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_case` | The inbox row of the document event and the idempotency key of the raise (DP-09) |

`document`, `document_checklist_item`, `case_document_check`, `document_intake` (P5), `interaction` (P1), `role`, `permission` and `masking_rule` (P4) are other services' and are never queried here (DP-01); the checklist and the documents arrive through the owners' operations and the scope answer through the authorise contract.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `case/context`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.context`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

Every pattern in the metadata has an instance here: DP-01 is the read of `recovery_case`, `assignment`, `task`, `reference_version` and the parameter rows in `rwb_case`; DP-03 the entry of the task raise; DP-06 the due-date parameter; DP-07 the five lists and the checklist version; DP-09 the inbox and the idempotency key (no outbox row, because this slice publishes no event); DP-11 the authorise call and the checklist read with their fakes; DP-15 the one index migration; DP-19 the composite route.

This secondary slice adds no build dependency of its own (metadata H = None): the platform contracts the DP rows name are pulled by the rwb-case baseline stories RWB-P3-E1018-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON and the service's platform work, so the story is Day 1 and builds against RWB-P3-E1018-CON and RWB-P5-E2024-CON with their fakes.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CaseContextController | REST controller | The two operations of 12.1, RFC 9457 problem responses with their message IDs, and the scope application of every read |
| CaseContextService | Service | The case context of a capture: the case row, the caller's task and assignment, the stage and route keys and the entry date |
| CaseScopeResolver | Client | The authorise call of 12.2 with area `DOCUMENTS`, right `C` and the `OWN` activity; one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker, and a refusal never cached as an allow |
| ChecklistVersionReader | Client | The `DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST` version in force through the reference-data contract, and the five lists this slice names |
| DocumentStoredListener | Kafka consumer with the inbox | The document event, deduplicated by event ID, reading the case checklist once per event |
| ChecklistTaskRaiser | Service | The one `task` of a missing required type: code, owner role, discretion and due date from data, and the unique open-task rule |
| DecisionRecordWriter | Service | The DP-03 entry of the task raise, in the same transaction, with the case, missing type, checklist version and task reference |
| CaseTimelineComposer | Service | The `TASK` item on the timeline, with actor `SY-CASEWF` and source system `WORKBENCH` |

**Database and migrations**

- One migration in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15): `V2024_1__checklist_task.sql`.
- Constraint `ux_task_case_code_open ON task (case_id, task_code) WHERE status = 'OPEN'`, so a redelivered event or a resent sync cannot open a second task for one missing type (BR6).
- Index `ix_task_case_status ON task (case_id, status)` for the timeline read and the activity lookup, and `ix_assignment_case_assignee ON assignment (case_id, assignee_user_id)` for the scope evidence.
- No new table and no new column beyond those two indexes and the constraint: `task`, `assignment` and `recovery_case` exist in the case baseline.
- The checklist version and the parameter are read through the contracts; no local copy is created.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The `DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST` version in force is read from `reference_version`, never configured; the label `CHK-2026.11` in the tests is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2223; ASM-3659).
- The task code, the owner role and the discretion of the task are data rows: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2223; ASM-3659).
- The due date is the parameter value in force through DP-06; the parameter key and its value are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2223; ASM-3659).
- The decision code of the raise is read from the decision-code list of the ledger: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2223; ASM-3659).
- No feature flag of this slice's own: a case that cannot be read or authorised must not accept a capture, so the case context has no off state. The legacy flag `rwb.dochub.field-capture` stays the document hub's.

**Build steps**

1. `CaseContextController` and the problem responses on the two operations, with the 401, 403, 404 and 503 shapes; unit test the 404 of MSG-P4-003 for a case outside the scope.
2. `CaseContextService` over the `Case` resource with the entry date, stage code, route code and the caller's task and assignment; contract test AC1, AC2 and AC5 against the case baseline fake.
3. `CaseScopeResolver` against the authorise fake, including the timeout and the open breaker; component test AC3, AC4 and the access case TC-E2-024-16.
4. `ChecklistVersionReader` over the reference-data fixture and the due-date parameter over the parameters fixture; test that a new checklist version is served as data with no code change.
5. `DocumentStoredListener` with the inbox and the checklist read, then `ChecklistTaskRaiser` with the unique open-task rule: component test the redelivery of AC8, the timeout of X5, one task per missing type, no task for a stage with no checklist, and a new task after the earlier one closes (X10).
6. `DecisionRecordWriter` in the same transaction as the task, and the forced failure of TC-E2-024-17: no task, no entry, MSG-P7-003 and an incident.
7. `CaseTimelineComposer` with the `TASK` item, and the contract-fake run of the whole path against RWB-P5-E2024-CON and the case baseline, so the story builds before the hub and `rwb-access` are in the environment.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; a capture for case `RW-2026-000501` is answered with entry date `2026-10-02` and the case in `OWN` scope, a capture for `RW-2026-000502` is answered 404 MSG-P4-003 with nothing raised, a sync that leaves `SETTLEMENT_AGREEMENT` missing raises exactly one `OPEN` task with its decision-record entry, the task shows on the timeline as a `TASK` item, and no position, file name or bill value appears in the task, the record or a log line.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-003 | The case does not exist, or the caller holds no task and no assignment on it | This case is not in your scope. | This story, on the case read and the scope application |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller's role does not carry Documents `C` | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | `rwb-access`, carried unchanged |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The authorise call or the checklist read does not answer | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. | This story, on the two client calls |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record of the task raise cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on the record writer |
| MSG-GEN-002 | A required value of the case read is missing from the request | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. | This story, on the path and query validation |

Every request-level error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId`, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled and the capability area where one applies, and `instance` naming the request. A refusal names the case and the action only: no customer field, no document, no position and no file name is in any message. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10. The message IDs and their text are the legacy ones, carried unchanged from RWB-E2-024 section 14.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the case status, stage and route values, the task code, the owner role, the discretion, the task status, the source system, the checklist version and the due date are data rows read through DP-06 and DP-07; the Java code holds none of them.
- No personal data in logs, events, tests, workflow history or prompts: the context carries the case and not the customer, and the task and record carry the case, the missing type, the checklist version and the task reference; a test scans both for any part of a position, a file name or a bill value.
- The position, the photo and the file stay with the document hub: this service receives no coordinate, no file name and no bill value, and holds no copy of a document.
- No read of another service's tables and no cross-schema read (DP-01): `document`, `document_checklist_item`, `case_document_check`, `document_intake`, `interaction`, `role`, `permission` and `masking_rule` are never queried here.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or a `v_ace_*` view of this service; this story reads no ACE view at all, because the case row it reads is its own.
- A task is never raised without its decision record, and the two commit in one transaction (R-UNI-39, BR7).
- A missing answer from `rwb-access` or from the hub is a refusal or a no-op, never a default allow and never a task without evidence; the authorise answer is not cached as an allow across a case.
- Idempotency twice over: the inbox deduplicates the document event by event ID, and `ux_task_case_code_open` keeps one open task per case and missing type.
- The case context has no off switch, because a capture that cannot be tied to its case must not be accepted; the legacy capture flag stays the document hub's.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-024 for rwb-decision; the decision record of a field capture and its two reads. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN) and the internal auditor (RW-AUDIT) who has to show what happened to an inspection**, I want **one decision record for every field capture the document hub stores on a case and one for every item it refuses, in the central decision ledger of `rwb-decision`, carrying the rule and its version, the inputs reference, the document and the client file ID, the capture kind and the final call, append only, hash chained and readable by case through `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log`**, so that **an inspection is proved the day it is made — what was stored, what was refused and why — and no photo or bill on a case is a document nobody can explain**.

Inside `rwb-decision` this is the decision-record slice of the legacy story RWB-E2-024:

- Service `rwb-decision`, schema `rwb_decision`, REST base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, topic `rwb.decision.events.v1` with event names `rwb.decision.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the decision-record library of DP-03.
- One deliverable and nothing else: the field-capture decision record. For every document stored from a field capture and for every item the store refuses, the service appends one entry to `decision_log_entry` through the decision-record path of DP-03, carrying the case, the decision code, the rule id and rule version, the inputs reference, the object reference (the document ID of a stored capture, the client file ID of a refused item), the document type and capture kind, the final call and the message id of a refusal, with its hash-chain position; and it serves the two decision-log reads so the entries of a case can be read and one entry can be read with its inputs and versions.
- The decision code the entry carries is `DOCATT`, the attach entry the document store writes for a stored document (legacy section 4 step 6, section 11 and decision D-RCV-31). The legacy story's `Decision` field `D6.5` stays the routing-decision tag it is carried from and is not read as the code of this entry; which of the two the entry carries is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1283; ASM-2275).
- One entry per stored document and one per item the store refuses; a `DUPLICATE` item resolves to the entry of the item received first and writes no second entry. Whether a refused item leaves an entry is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1284; ASM-2276).
- What stays with `rwb-document` (P5, RWB-P5-E2024-APP with RWB-P5-E2024-CON): the field-capture endpoint, the manifest and file matching, the duplicate check on `client_file_id`, the file type and size checks, the clock skew and the age limit, the malware scan and the quarantine, the store, the capture columns and the partial unique index, the `DocumentStored` event, the OCR intake, the `UTILITY_BILL` extraction and the review queue, the SCR-30 panel and the switch `rwb.dochub.field-capture`. This story consumes those facts and decides none of them.
- What stays with `rwb-access` (P4, RWB-P4-E2024-APP): the authorise answer for capability area `DOCUMENTS` with rights `C`, `R` and `U`, the scope answer with the task on the case as the `OWN` test, the masking of `captured_at`, `capture_latitude`, `capture_longitude`, `capture_kind` and the review state, and the `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entries. This story consumes the answer for its reads and writes no access entry.
- What stays with `rwb-case` (P3, RWB-P3-E2024-APP): the case, its entry date, the field inspection task and its state, and the reference lists and parameters behind DP-06 and DP-07. This story reads none of them as a table.
- What stays with `rwb-agent` (P10): the agent policies, prompts and runs, and the agent version an entry may name in DF-DEC-007. No agent runs on the field-capture path, so this story writes no `agent_version`.
- The service records and exposes the decision; it changes no document, no capture row, no review item, no task and no case status (BR10).
- The database login used by the capability is the per-service login of DP-02. Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1281; ASM-2272); this story uses the phrase "the rwb-decision login (DP-02)" and never the shared login of the legacy module.

The values carried from the legacy story are unchanged: case `RW-2026-000501` with entry date `2026-10-02` and a field inspection task for field collector `FC-01` with role `RW-FIELDCOL`, an inspection of ten synthetic files (eight `INSPECTION_PHOTO` and two `UTILITY_BILL`) synced at `2026-12-15 14:20` at latitude `13.7563` and longitude `100.5018`, a capture made with no signal at `2026-12-14 10:05` synced at `2026-12-15 08:30`, a utility bill showing amount `1,284.50` and due date `28/12/2569` read as `1284.50` and `2026-12-28`, the clock skew of 5 minutes and the age limit of 30 days, and case `RW-2026-000502` where `FC-01` has no task.

##### 2. Business rationale

An inspection that reached the document hub without a record of it is evidence with no chain of custody, and a capture that was silently dropped is a visit the bank paid for and cannot show. The legacy story proved the capture; this slice proves the record of it. Today the decision is written inside the same monolith transaction as the document, so the two cannot be told apart in an audit, and an item the store refused leaves no trace at all. Under Architecture v5 the store is `rwb-document`'s and the ledger is `rwb-decision`'s, so the explanation has to live in the one place every service's record is collected and read: the central decision ledger of `rwb-decision`, through `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log`.

This story carries the record half of REQ-DCM-013 and the measure `Decisions within the delegation of authority` at 100 percent for the field-capture path. It carries CTL-11 (the GPS position and the photos of a home are personal data, masked by role and never logged) on the record side, NFR-033 (every decision reproducible from the log, with the versions and the inputs), NFR-035 (the chain is checked daily) and the principle that no action stands without its record (legacy BR10, R-UNI-39, R-UNI-40).

The realignment changes the mechanism, not the business rule:

1. The in-process decision-log write of the monolith becomes the decision record of the owning service: `rwb-document` writes its local record in the same transaction as the document, publishes `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and this service appends the entry to the central ledger through the library of DP-03, with the append-only rule and the hash chain that FEAT-DRI-01 and FEAT-DRI-03 already carry (Architecture v5 slide 28).
2. The refusal is recorded rather than discarded: an item the store refuses is a decision the service declined to take, so it leaves one entry with its message id and no document reference, and an auditor can count refusals per case instead of inferring them from an absence.
3. The entry never becomes a copy of the capture: the position, the file, the photo and the bill value stay in `rwb_document`, and the entry names the field, the type and the version that decided it (legacy BR9; CTL-11; DL26).
4. The decision code and the final calls are reference data of `rwb-case` read through DP-07, and the ledger's completeness target and chain-check time are parameters read through DP-06, so none of them is a constant of this service (legacy BR1 to BR10 as data; principle 1).
5. The one decision-log read of the monolith becomes two operations on the service's own base (DP-13 through the base of section 12.1), reached through the gateway-bff composite route the screens already use (DP-19); the nightly copy of the log to the data lake is retired with the data lake (DP-17), and the ingest of `rwb.decision-record.v1` is continuous Kafka as JOB-13 states.

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E2-024:

- Case `RW-2026-000501` exists with entry date `2026-10-02` and a field inspection task for field collector `FC-01` with role `RW-FIELDCOL`, so the case is in that collector's `OWN` scope (legacy section 7 Background). The case and the task are `rwb-case`'s and reach this service as facts.
- The document type rows `INSPECTION_PHOTO` with no fields, `INSPECTION_CHECKLIST` with no fields and `UTILITY_BILL` with `bill_amount`, `due_date` and `account_ref` are in force as reference data (legacy section 3). The types are the store's and are named on the entry; this story classifies nothing.

They are the store's checks; this story records their outcome and holds no default of its own.

##### 4. Flow

1. Field collector: `FC-01` captures eight photos and two bills in the field app, ten synthetic files in the test data, and the app syncs them at `2026-12-15 14:20`; the capture, the scan and the store are `rwb-document`'s and are not rebuilt here.
2. `rwb-document` (P5): runs the manifest, duplicate, type, size, time and position checks and the malware scan, stores each accepted item, sets the capture columns, and for each stored item and each item it refuses writes its local decision record in the same transaction as the change (legacy section 4 steps 4 to 8; BR1).
3. `rwb-document` publishes `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` for each of those records, keyed by the case ID, in the same transaction as its outbox row (DP-03, DP-09; Architecture v5 slide 28).
4. `rwb-decision` `FieldCaptureDecisionListener`: reads the fact into the inbox of DP-09, deduplicates by event ID and by the idempotency key the fact carries (R-UNI-40), and passes the decision facts to `FieldCaptureDecisionRecorder`: the case, the decision code, the object reference (document ID or client file ID), the document type and capture kind, the final call, the message id of a refusal, the rule id and rule version, the actor reference, the capture time and the inputs reference.
5. `FieldCaptureDecisionRecorder`: reads the decision code list and the document type codes through the reference-data contract of DP-07 and the ledger parameters through the parameters contract of DP-06, at the version in force on the business date, and composes the entry. It decides nothing about the capture: it applies no threshold, no clock skew and no age limit, and it holds no copy of the store's rules (BR2, BR11).
6. `DecisionLogAppender`, one transaction in `rwb_decision`: takes the next `chain_seq`, computes `prev_hash` from the last entry's `entry_hash`, computes `entry_hash` as the SHA-256 of the entry's canonical form, writes the `decision_log_entry` row with its `inputs_ref`, and writes the outbox row of the append. A failed append changes nothing: no entry, no chain position and no outbox row (DP-03; R-UNI-39; BR13).
7. `DecisionLogAppender`: a repeated fact with the same idempotency key returns the first entry's ID, adds one to the repeat count for R-UNI-40, and appends nothing (BR14).
8. When the append cannot be made, the decision-record library raises `DecisionLogUnavailableException` to its caller inside the store's transaction, and the caller answers MSG-P7-003: the item is refused, nothing is stored for it, and an incident is raised (legacy X12; BR4).
9. `FieldCaptureCompletenessChecker`, on the ingest window of the ledger: reads `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` for the case and compares the documents the case holds with the DOCATT entries of the case, and reports a document with no entry as a gap, which is the missing-record alert of Architecture v5 slide 28 (BR12, X8).
10. An auditor or a case owner reads the entries with `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` by `caseId`, `decision`, `ruleId`, `approver`, `from`, `to`, `page` and `size`, and one entry with `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}`, each guarded by the authorise answer of DP-11 and refused with MSG-P4-002 or MSG-P4-003 as section 14 states (BR15).
11. Nothing in this story moves a document, a capture row, a review item, a task or a case: the entry is appended beside them, and the readers of the screens keep reading the capture facts through `rwb-document`'s contract (BR10).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The store refuses an item for its type, its size, its capture time or its position | The refusal leaves one entry with `finalCall` `REFUSED`, the message id of the refusal and the client file ID, and no document reference; the other items are unaffected | MSG-P5-001, MSG-P5-016, MSG-P5-017, MSG-GEN-002, MSG-GEN-003 (produced by `rwb-document`) | AC2, TC-E2-024-07 to TC-E2-024-11 |
| X2 | The same client file ID is sent again, and the store answers `DUPLICATE` | No second entry is written; the entry of the item received first stands, and the chain of the case is unchanged | None | AC3, TC-E2-024-04, TC-E2-024-05 |
| X3 | The same `DecisionRecorded` fact is delivered again or replayed from the topic | One entry exists; the inbox dedupe and the idempotency key both hold, and the repeat is counted for R-UNI-40 | None | AC3, TC-E2-024-04 |
| X4 | The record cannot be written, because the library is unavailable or the chain cannot be taken | Nothing is written: no entry, no chain position, no outbox row; the item is refused and nothing is stored for it, and an incident is raised | MSG-P7-003 | AC5, TC-E2-024-17 |
| X5 | An entry names a rule id with no rule version, or a decision code outside the list in force | The append is refused with MSG-P7-009 naming `ruleVersion` or `decisionCode`, and nothing is written | MSG-P7-009 | AC1 |
| X6 | A caller attempts to change or delete an entry | The statement is refused, by the missing grant for the service login and by the append-only rule of the table; a correction is a new entry naming the one it corrects in `corrects_entry_id` | None | AC4 |
| X7 | The fact carries no object reference, or names a case the document contract does not confirm | The append is refused for that fact and the incident names the fact ID; no entry is written on a guessed document or a guessed client file ID | MSG-GEN-006 | AC1 |
| X8 | The documents of a case and the DOCATT entries of the case do not agree inside the ingest window | The checker reports the document with no entry as a gap and raises the missing-record alert; no entry is invented for it | MSG-GEN-006 | AC1 |
| X9 | The decision code list or the parameters cannot be read at the version in force | The append is refused and the fact is retried; no entry is written with an assumed code or an assumed version | MSG-GEN-006 | AC1 |
| X10 | The caller holds no right in the `DECISION_LOG` area, or asks for a case out of scope | 403 with MSG-P4-002, or 404 with MSG-P4-003; nothing is returned | MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 | TC-E2-024-16 |
| X11 | A request never reached the store: a manifest and file mismatch, too many files, or a case outside the collector's scope | No `DOCATT` entry exists for it, because no decision was taken; the refusal is the store's or the access answer's and is recorded there | MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002, MSG-P4-003 (produced by `rwb-document` and `rwb-access`) | TC-E2-024-12, TC-E2-024-14, TC-E2-024-15 |

An entry is only ever appended beside the fact that caused it: the entry, its chain position and its outbox row commit in one transaction, so a fact can never leave a half record and a record can never exist for a capture that was not decided (BR13).

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the field-capture contract of RWB-P5-E2024-CON, the platform contract libraries of its DP table and the fakes; no capture, scan, store, intake, extraction, review, case or access behaviour is rebuilt here |
| Negotiable | The decision code, the final call set, the parameter names, the document types and the message ids are data or parameters of their owners; the story fixes only the record, the append-only rule, the chain, the fail-closed refusal and the two reads |
| Valuable | Every capture on a case, stored or refused, can be explained, counted and shown unchanged to an auditor |
| Estimable | One listener, one recorder, one appender with the chain, one query controller with two operations, one completeness checker, one migration, one fake set |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests; it is the decision-record slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Each of the seven criteria in section 7 runs as one automated test against the contract fakes with a fixed business date and a fixed chain |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Field app photos and bills into the document hub — the rwb-decision field-capture decision record

  Background:
    Given the environment is SIT
    Given the rwb-case reference-data contract mock returns the document types INSPECTION_PHOTO, INSPECTION_CHECKLIST and UTILITY_BILL in force, with no fields for INSPECTION_PHOTO and INSPECTION_CHECKLIST and with bill_amount, due_date and account_ref for UTILITY_BILL
    Given the rwb-case parameters contract mock returns the clock skew of 5 minutes, the age limit of 30 days and the file limit of 50 in force

  Scenario: AC1 Ten DOCATT records for one inspection, chained and readable (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-document contract mock returns case "RW-2026-000501" with entry date 2026-10-02 and ten documents stored from the sync at 2026-12-15 14:20, eight "INSPECTION_PHOTO" and two "UTILITY_BILL", each with source "UPLOAD", its client file ID, capture time 2026-12-15 14:20, latitude 13.7563 and longitude 100.5018
    Given the rwb-case reference-data contract mock returns the decision code list in force and the rwb-case parameters contract mock returns the ledger parameters in force
    When the ten DOCATT records of that sync reach rwb.decision-record.v1 as DecisionRecorded facts
    Then ten decision_log_entry rows exist in rwb_decision for case "RW-2026-000501" with decision code "DOCATT", one per stored document, each keyed by its document ID and its client file ID
    Then each entry carries the ruleId and ruleVersion in force, the inputsRef, the document type ("INSPECTION_PHOTO" or "UTILITY_BILL"), the capture kind, the actor reference "FC-01" and finalCall "ACCEPTED"
    Then each entry carries chain_seq, prevHash and entryHash, every prevHash equals the entryHash of the entry before it, and the first prevHash is 64 zeros
    Then GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log for case "RW-2026-000501" returns the ten entries in chain order, and GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId} returns one with its rule, its version, its inputsRef, its document reference and its decidedAt

  Scenario: AC2 An item the store refuses is recorded too (new, D-RCV-60)

    When the ten DOCATT records of that sync reach rwb.decision-record.v1 as DecisionRecorded facts

    Then the entry of the refused item is readable with GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId} and names no document, no file name and no position

    When an UPDATE setting final_call and a DELETE of that entry are attempted through the rwb-decision login (DP-02) and again through the schema owner role
    Then all four statements are refused, the first two by the missing grant for the service login and the last two by the append-only rule of the table
    Then the entry is unchanged and its entryHash still equals the SHA-256 of its canonical form
    Then the refused attempts are written to the ACE audit log with the table, the operation and the entry ID

  Scenario: AC5 A record that cannot be written refuses the item (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-document contract mock returns three items of case "RW-2026-000501"

    When the two DOCATT records reach rwb.decision-record.v1 as DecisionRecorded facts
    Then each entry carries the capture time 2026-12-14 10:05 as recorded at capture and the decidedAt 2026-12-15 08:30

```

These seven criteria are new for the `rwb-decision` slice of RWB-E2-024 and are the record and read criteria of the key. `acs` is empty for this story: no legacy criterion is owned verbatim here, because every legacy criterion of the key stores, scans, extracts or refuses a capture, and those changes belong to RWB-P5-E2024-APP, RWB-P4-E2024-APP and RWB-P3-E2024-APP. The values are the legacy values of RWB-E2-024 — case `RW-2026-000501` with entry date `2026-10-02`, field collector `FC-01` with role `RW-FIELDCOL`, the ten items (eight `INSPECTION_PHOTO`, two `UTILITY_BILL`), the three document types, the syncs at `2026-12-15 14:20` and `2026-12-15 08:30`, the capture at `2026-12-14 10:05`, latitude `13.7563` and longitude `100.5018`, the bill amount `1,284.50`, the clock skew of 5 minutes and the age limit of 30 days, and the messages MSG-P5-001, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P7-009 — and no new business value is introduced.

The decision code `DOCATT` and the final call set `ACCEPTED`, `REFUSED` and `QUARANTINED` are the reading of ASM-2275 and ASM-2276 and are carried in GAP-1283 and GAP-1284; the payload field set of the entry, the read shape, the message id set, the panel id, the parameter names and the login name have no source and are carried in GAP-1281 with ASM-2271, ASM-2272 and ASM-2273.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every document stored from a field capture and every item the store refuses leaves exactly one decision record; no capture is stored and no refusal is returned without it, and the record and the change are written in the same transaction | Legacy BR10; R-UNI-39; FSD P7 v3 A2.2; FEAT-DRI-02 |
| BR2 | The record is written on the decision-record path of DP-03: it is appended to the chain, it names the rule and the rule version in force, and the entry, its chain position and its outbox row commit together or not at all | FSD P7 v3 A2.1 and A2.3; TSD P7 v2 T5.3; DP-03 |
| BR3 | The entry names the case, the decision code, the object reference, the document type, the capture kind, the final call, the rule id and version, the inputs reference, the actor reference, the capture time and the decided time | TSD P7 v2 T3.1; legacy section 11; ASM-2271 |
| BR4 | A record that cannot be written refuses the item: the library raises `DecisionLogUnavailableException`, the store's transaction rolls back, the answer is MSG-P7-003 and an incident is raised; no item stands unlogged | Legacy X12 and TC-E2-024-17; FSD P7 v3 VR-P7-001-2 and AC-EXC-P7-002-02; principle 5 |
| BR5 | The entry is append only and hash chained: an UPDATE and a DELETE are refused, a correction is a new entry naming the one it corrects in `corrects_entry_id`, and every `entry_hash` is the SHA-256 of the entry's canonical form | FEAT-DRI-01; FSD P7 v3 AC-P7-001-01 and AC-ALT-P7-001-01; NFR-035 |
| BR6 | One entry per stored document and one per refused item, keyed on the object reference; a `DUPLICATE` item resolves to the entry of the item received first and writes none, and a repeated fact writes none | Legacy BR4; R-UNI-40; ASM-2276 |
| BR7 | The capture time is the device time recorded at capture, stored as sent; the server never replaces it, and the decided time is the server's | Legacy BR2 and section 17; FEAT-DCM-21 |
| BR8 | The decision code and the final call values are reference data of the `rwb-case` reference-data contract, not constants: an unknown code is refused with MSG-P7-009 naming `decisionCode`, and a rule id with no version with MSG-P7-009 naming `ruleVersion` | FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-01 and AC-EXC-P7-002-05; BR-P7-001; DP-07 |
| BR9 | No personal data in the entry, the fact, the outbox or the logs: the position, the file name, the photo and the bill value stay in `rwb_document`, and the entry carries references, codes, the capture kind and dates only | Legacy BR9 and section 17; CTL-11; DL26; NFR-033 |
| BR10 | The story records and exposes; it writes no document, no capture row, no intake item, no review item, no task and no case status, and it reads no table of another service | Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; DP-01 |
| BR11 | The service applies no capture rule: the type, the size, the clock skew, the age limit, the duplicate check and the malware result are `rwb-document`'s, and the entry copies their outcome | Legacy BR1, BR3, BR4; FSD P4 v3 A2.4 VR-P4-004-1 |
| BR12 | The ledger is reconciled: the documents of a case are compared with the DOCATT entries of the case inside the ingest window, and a document with no entry is reported as a gap and alerted; no entry is invented for it | Architecture v5 slide 28; NFR-035; ASM-2273 |
| BR13 | The entry, its chain position and its outbox row are written in one transaction; a failed append leaves nothing and the fact is redelivered | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; DP-03 |
| BR14 | One entry per fact under a repeated delivery: the inbox dedupe and the idempotency key make a second entry impossible, and the repeat is counted | FSD P7 v3 AC-EXC-P7-002-03; R-UNI-40 |
| BR15 | The two reads declare the `DECISION_LOG` capability area and the right `R` with the scope applied; a role outside the matrix is refused with MSG-P4-002 and a case out of scope with MSG-P4-003 | TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 and T6.1; legacy section 10 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb_decision`:

- BR1 and BR2 are one append on the `DecisionRecorded` fact of the owning service, through the library of DP-03; the store's transaction is `rwb-document`'s and this story supplies the path, its fail-closed contract and its exception.
- BR3 is the entry composition: the columns of TSD P7 v2 T3.1 plus the object reference and the capture facts of the assumed shape of ASM-2271.
- BR4 is the exception mapping: `DecisionLogUnavailableException` from the library becomes MSG-P7-003 for the item and an incident for the platform administrator queue.
- BR5 is the table's append-only trigger `tr_declog_append_only` and the missing `UPDATE` and `DELETE` grant on the service login, both inherited from the decision-log baseline.
- BR6 is the partial unique key on the object reference and the inbox dedupe by event ID and idempotency key.
- BR8 is a read of the reference-data contract of DP-07 at the version in force; the Java code holds no decision code and no final call value.
- BR9 is a check on the entry writer: the entry's canonical form is built from references and codes, and a test scans the entry, the fact and the log line for any digit of `13.7563` and `100.5018` and for `1,284.50`.
- BR12 is the completeness checker of flow step 9: one read of the document contract per case per window, one comparison, one gap alert.
- BR15 is the guard on the two reads, inherited from the decision-log baseline's authorise path.

##### 9. State transitions

None for a document, a capture row, a review item, a task or a case. The states below are the states of an entry of this story, and the entry has no state column of its own: it is appended and then immutable.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Absent | A `DecisionRecorded` field-capture fact arrives | The decision code, the rule version and the object reference are readable at the version in force | Appended, with the next `chain_seq`, its `prev_hash` and its `entry_hash`, in one transaction with its outbox row |
| Absent | A `DecisionRecorded` field-capture fact arrives | The decision code is unknown, or the rule id has no version, or the object reference is absent | Absent: refused with MSG-P7-009 or MSG-GEN-006, and nothing is written |
| Absent | A `DecisionRecorded` field-capture fact arrives | The library is unavailable or the chain cannot be taken | Absent: MSG-P7-003 for the item, nothing stored, and the fact stays for redelivery |
| Appended | The same fact arrives again with the same idempotency key | The inbox or the idempotency key holds the entry | Unchanged: the first entry's ID is returned and the repeat is counted |
| Appended | A correction of the decision is taken | The correction names the entry it corrects | A new entry is appended with `corrects_entry_id`, and the corrected entry stays unchanged |
| Appended | An UPDATE or a DELETE is attempted | Any caller, including the schema owner | Unchanged: the statement is refused by the append-only rule |

The capture itself moves through `rwb-document`'s states — received, scanned, stored, intake item, extracted, in review — and the case stays in its stage; this story changes none of them (BR10, BR11).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the DOCATT entries of a case and one entry with its inputs reference, its versions and its chain position (`DECISION_LOG` R), with scope `ALL` |
| RW-COMPLY, Compliance and PDPA officer | Reads the same, without a position, a file name or a bill value, which the entry never carries (`DECISION_LOG` R) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the entries of the cases in own scope and shows the inspection beside the documents on the case (`DECISION_LOG` R) |
| RW-RESTRUCT, restructuring officer (FCR) | Reads the entries of a deed in lieu case in scope (`DECISION_LOG` R) |
| RW-FIELDCOL, field collector | Named on the entry as its actor reference; sends the capture through `rwb-document` and reads the entry only where its scope and the matrix allow |
| Every role of TSD P7 v2 T6.1 | Holds `R` on the decision log and reads the entries of the cases in its scope |
| A role outside the matrix, or a case out of the caller's scope | Refused with MSG-P4-002, or 404 with MSG-P4-003 |
| The `rwb-decision` service identity | Consumes the fact, reads its own `rwb_decision` rows, and appends the entry and its outbox row (DP-02) |
| The decision-record library identity | Provides the chain position, the `prev_hash`, the `entry_hash` and the fail-closed exception of the append (DP-03) |
| `rwb-document` | Owns the capture, the scan, the store, the capture columns, the intake, the extraction, the review queue and the SCR-30 panel; this story holds no authority over any of them |
| `rwb-access` | Owns the authorise, scope and masking answers and the access entries; this story consumes the answer for its reads and writes no entry |
| `rwb-agent` | Owns the agent version an entry may name; no agent runs on this path |
| No approval level from the delegation of authority applies | The field-capture decision is a system decision and carries no approver; the approval path of this service is another story's |

The authorisation decision behind the two reads is `rwb-access`'s role, scope and right data, taken through the authorise contract of DP-11 and the guard the service's decision-log baseline already carries; this story adds no guard of its own and holds no role, scope or delegation row (ASM-2274). The database login is per service (DP-02) and its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1281; ASM-2272); the story refers to "the rwb-decision login (DP-02)".

| (inbox) | `processed_event` | event_id, consumer, processed_at | Write |
| (outbox) | outbox library table in `rwb_decision` | the append row | Write |

No row of `document`, `document_intake`, `document_field`, `document_type`, `document_hub_parameter`, `recovery_case`, `task`, `role`, `permission` or `masking_rule` is copied into `rwb_decision`: the capture facts arrive on the document contract and on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and the other services' tables are never queried. Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8; the object reference, the capture facts and the message id of a refusal have no field ID in TSD P7 v2 T3.1 and are written from the assumed shape of section 12.1, which is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1281; ASM-2271).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-decision` (P7); base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`. Both paths are the ones TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 carries (API-P7-006 and API-P7-007); this story fills them with the DOCATT entries of a field capture and adds no third path. The request and response field set of a field-capture entry is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1281; ASM-2271).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/decision-log` | API-P7-006: search the decision log by `caseId`, `decision`, `ruleId`, `approver`, `from`, `to`, `page` and `size`, and by the object reference of a field-capture entry; 200 with the DecisionLogPage | `DECISION_LOG`, right `R`, scope applied through the authorise contract | Not applicable, read only |
| GET | `/decision-log/{entryId}` | API-P7-007: read one entry with its inputs reference, its rule and version, its object reference, its capture facts, its final call and its hash chain; 200 with the DecisionLogEntry | `DECISION_LOG`, right `R`, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |

The DecisionLogEntry body this story reads and writes carries `entryId`, `chainSeq`, `caseId`, `decisionCode`, `ruleId`, `ruleVersion`, `inputsRef`, `recommendation` with the document type, the capture kind and the item result, `finalCall`, `objectRef`, `clientFileId`, `docTypeCode`, `captureKind`, `captureTime`, `messageId`, `decidedAt`, `prevHash`, `entryHash`, `correctsEntryId` and `actorUserId`. The DecisionLogPage body carries `items`, `page`, `size` and `total`. The object-reference filter of the search, the field names of the entry and the final call set are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1281; ASM-2271).

Errors: 401 no session; 403 the role lacks the right (MSG-P4-002); 404 the entry or the case is absent or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 422 a query value is outside its list (MSG-GEN-001); 503 the log is unavailable (MSG-GEN-006) or the append could not be made (MSG-P7-003). Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` | P5 rwb-document, on RWB-P5-E2024-CON | The documents the case holds, with their type, source, capture time and review state, for the completeness check of the ledger (BR12, X8); faked, one hop, 2 s timeout (DP-11) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access, on RWB-P4-E1037-CON | The cached role, scope and right decision behind the two reads: area `DECISION_LOG`, right `R` (BR15); faked. The contract is added by the DP table and is not in the metadata rows (GAP-1282; ASM-2274) |

The reference lists of `rwb-case` (DP-07, RWB-P3-E1043-CON) and the parameters of `rwb-case` (DP-06, RWB-P3-E1042-CON) are read in process through their client libraries, with their contract fakes, and are not cross-service REST rows; the capture facts arrive on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and not over REST. The contract dependency recorded on the story is RWB-P5-E2024-CON; the platform and published contracts the DP table adds are listed in section 13 and carried in the gap of GAP-1282.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This story publishes no event of its own: the field-capture decision is a fact of `rwb-document` and the entries of the central ledger are read through the operations of 12.1. `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` is published by the owning service of each decision, and `rwb-decision` is its consumer, as the event catalogue names it (Architecture v5 slide 42). The `ApprovalRequested`, `ApprovalDecided` and `RulePackageInForce` events of `rwb.decision.events.v1` belong to the approval and rule-registry stories of this service and are not touched here.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 ledger library, published by `rwb-document` for these decisions | `FieldCaptureDecisionListener`: inbox dedupe by event ID, then `FieldCaptureDecisionRecorder` and `DecisionLogAppender` for the object reference, the document type, the capture kind, the final call, the message id, the rule and version and the capture time |

The fact carries IDs, codes, versions, a message id and a time only; no file, no photo, no position and no bill value travels on the topic (BR9). Which fields of the fact this service requires, and whether the document reference travels on the fact or is read through the document contract, is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1281; ASM-2271); the reading this story applies is that of ASM-2271 and the document read of 12.2 covers the gap.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None of this story's own. The append is a transactional write on the consumer path and not a workflow step; the handler is a Kafka consumer with the inbox of DP-09; the store's transaction is `rwb-document`'s and this story neither starts nor signals it. The `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` on queue `rwb-document` is `rwb-document`'s and is observed through the document contract, not built here. This story registers no workflow and no activity on the `rwb-decision` queue and adds none to the workflow kit.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The ingest of `rwb.decision-record.v1` is continuous Kafka, as JOB-13 states (Architecture v5 slide 44); the daily hash-chain check JOB-14 at 02:00 and the rule promote JOB-20 at 00:01 are `rwb-decision`'s decision-log and rule-governance baselines, and they cover the entries of this story like any other without being rebuilt or scheduled here. This story creates no Temporal Schedule and starts nothing on a clock.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `decision_log_entry` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | The field-capture entry, its object reference, its chain position, its hashes, its inputs reference and its final call; append only |
| decision record (local library) | P7 rows in `rwb_decision`, written through the decision-record library | The append of DP-03 and its hash chain |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_decision` | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects (DP-09) |

Not owned and never read: `document`, `document_intake`, `document_field`, `document_type` and `document_hub_parameter` (P5), `recovery_case`, `task`, `timer` and `parameter_value` (P3), and `role`, `permission` and `masking_rule` (P4). The other P7 tables — `approval`, `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` — are not touched by this story. No foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01).
