###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count in this story | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | Provided 2, consumed 2 | `GET /decision-log` and `GET /decision-log/{entryId}` provided; the document list and the authorise decision consumed, one hop and 2 s with a breaker per downstream |
| Kafka | Published 0, consumed 1 | `rwb.decision-record.v1` consumed; no event published and no new topic |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, no activity and no Schedule; the store's transaction and the intake workflow are `rwb-document`'s |
| File | None | No file input and no file output; a photo and a bill never leave `rwb-document` |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, module `log/fieldcapture`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision.fieldcapture`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

Which patterns have an instance in this slice: DP-01 is the boundary — the entry lives in `rwb_decision` and the capture facts arrive on the document contract and on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, never as a read of `rwb_document`; DP-03 is the append path of the central ledger with its chain, its append-only rule and its fail-closed exception; DP-06 is the ingest target and the chain-check time read as parameters; DP-07 is `LOV-DECISION` and the document type codes read as reference data; DP-09 is the outbox, the inbox and the idempotency key; DP-11 is the document read of the completeness checker and the authorise decision behind the reads, each with a mock and a 2 s timeout; DP-15 is the one migration of the slice; DP-19 is the composite route the reads are reached through, not built here.

The platform H dependencies in the table — H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and H RWB-PLT-N001-CON — and the C dependencies of the published contracts of other services — C RWB-P3-E1042-CON, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON and the authorise contract RWB-P4-E1037-CON that DP-11 consumes — are not in the metadata rows of this story, which name `Depends on (build)` = None and `Contract dependencies` = RWB-P5-E2024-CON. They are the dependencies the DP table adds and they are recorded in GAP-1282 and ASM-2274. None of them blocks the build beyond Day 1: they are platform contracts of waves 0 and 1 and published contracts of `rwb-case` and `rwb-access`, built against their fakes.

The work of the legacy key that sits with other slices: the field-capture endpoint `POST /cases/{caseId}/field-captures`, the manifest parsing and file matching, the duplicate check on `client_file_id`, the type, size, time and position checks, the malware scan and the quarantine, the store, the capture columns `captured_at`, `capture_latitude`, `capture_longitude`, `client_file_id` and `capture_kind`, the migration `V2_5_024__field_capture.sql` and its partial unique index, the `DocumentStored` event, the OCR intake, the `UTILITY_BILL` extraction, the review queue and the SCR-30 panel are `rwb-document`'s (RWB-P5-E2024-APP, with the contract RWB-P5-E2024-CON). The scope and masking answer is `rwb-access`'s (RWB-P4-E2024-APP) and the case, its entry date and the task are `rwb-case`'s (RWB-P3-E2024-APP). This story builds the record of the decision and nothing beside it.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| FieldCaptureDecisionListener | Kafka consumer with the inbox | Reads `DecisionRecorded` for the field capture, deduplicates by event ID and idempotency key, and hands the decision facts to the recorder |
| FieldCaptureDecisionRecorder | Service | Composes the entry from the decision facts, reads the decision code list, the document type codes and the ledger parameters at the version in force, and decides nothing about the capture (BR3, BR8, BR11) |
| DecisionLogAppender | Service | Takes the next `chain_seq`, computes `prev_hash` and `entry_hash`, and writes the entry and its outbox row in one transaction (DP-03, BR13, BR5) |
| DecisionRecordFailClosedHandler | Service | Maps the library's `DecisionLogUnavailableException` to MSG-P7-003 for the item and to an incident for the platform administrator queue, so the store's transaction rolls back and nothing is stored (BR4) |
| FieldCaptureCompletenessChecker | Service | Compares the documents of a case from the document contract with the DOCATT entries of the case inside the ingest window and reports a document with no entry as a gap (BR12) |
| DecisionLogQueryController | Controller | `GET /decision-log` and `GET /decision-log/{entryId}` with the declared area and right, the scope, the paging and the problem mapping for 401, 403, 404, 422 and 503 |
| DecisionLogRepository | Repository | `decision_log_entry` in `rwb_decision`, with the append-only rule, the chain columns, the object reference and the idempotency key |
| DocumentFactClient | Adapter | The document list of RWB-P5-E2024-CON for the completeness check, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker |
| AccessCheckClient | Client | The cached authorise decision behind the two reads (DP-11) |
| ReferenceAndParameterClient | Client | `LOV-DECISION`, the document type codes and the ledger parameters at the version in force (DP-06, DP-07) |
| InputsSnapshotResolver | Service | Resolves the `inputs_ref` of the entry and the freshness stamp of each input the decision read |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `decision_log_entry`, the local decision record of the append and the library objects, all in schema `rwb_decision`; reads no other schema (DP-01).
- Migration in this story, in the per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_decision`: `V2024_1__decision_field_capture_entry.sql` adds the field-capture columns of section 11 that the decision-log store baseline does not hold — the object reference, the client file ID, the document type code, the capture kind, the capture time and the message id of a refusal — plus the partial unique key `ux_declog_capture ON decision_log_entry (case_id, object_ref, decision_code) WHERE decision_code = 'DOCATT' AND object_ref IS NOT NULL`, so one entry per stored document and one per refused item is a constraint and not only a check (BR6), and the search index for the case-and-decision read of 12.1. The column names and types are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1281; ASM-2271).
- The append-only rule is the table's, with the trigger `tr_declog_append_only` that refuses an UPDATE and a DELETE from the schema owner and the missing grant for the service login, as FSD P7 v3 AC-P7-001-01 fixes it.
- No row of `document`, `document_intake`, `document_field` or `parameter_value` is written here: the document hub's tables and the case's parameters are their owners'.

**Configuration and reference data**

- `LOV-DECISION` and the document type codes are reference data of `rwb-case` read through DP-07 at the version in force; the value `DOCATT` and the final call set are the reading of ASM-2275 and ASM-2276 and are held as reference rows, not as constants (GAP-1283; GAP-1284).
- The ledger ingest target of 5 minutes and the daily chain-check time of 02:00 are parameter rows of `rwb-case` read through DP-06 with the version in force; the parameter names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1281; ASM-2273), and the story holds no default.
- The capture parameters `CAPTURE_CLOCK_SKEW_MINUTES` 5, `CAPTURE_MAX_AGE_DAYS` 30, `CAPTURE_MAX_FILES` 50 and `INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB` 25 are the store's rows; this story reads them only as facts of a refusal it records, and applies none of them (BR11).
- The outbox retry policy, the inbox retention and the chain-check alert route are the platform's (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON).

**Build steps**

1. `DecisionLogRepository` and the migration, with the partial unique key on the object reference and the append-only trigger; test that a second entry for the same document and an UPDATE are both refused (AC4, AC3).
2. `FieldCaptureDecisionListener` with the inbox, the dedupe by event ID and idempotency key, and the not-a-decision cases of X11; test the replay of the same fact (AC3).
3. `FieldCaptureDecisionRecorder` and `ReferenceAndParameterClient`: the entry composed from the decision facts and the versions in force, with the refusal of an unknown decision code and of a rule id with no version (X5; AC1).
4. `DecisionLogAppender` and the chain: `chain_seq`, `prev_hash`, `entry_hash` over the canonical form, the first `prev_hash` of 64 zeros, and the one-transaction append (AC1, AC4).
5. `DecisionRecordFailClosedHandler`: the `DecisionLogUnavailableException` path to MSG-P7-003 with the store's rollback and the incident; the test of the three items of AC5 with the library fake forced to fail (AC5, TC-E2-024-17).
6. `InputsSnapshotResolver` and the `inputs_ref` with the freshness of each input, including the capture time of the offline capture (AC7).
7. `DecisionLogQueryController` with the two operations, the declared area and right, the scope, the paging and the problem mapping; tests for AC1 and the refusals of TC-E2-024-16.
8. `FieldCaptureCompletenessChecker` over the document list of a case, with the gap report of X8 and the ledger ingest window of DP-06.
9. The contract-fake run of the whole slice: the document fake, the access fake, the reference-data and parameters fakes, the decision-record fake and the outbox fake, green from Day 1 (AC1 to AC7).
10. The boundary test: no write to `rwb_document`, `rwb_case` or `rwb_access`, and no position, file name or bill value in any entry, fact, outbox row or log line (AC6, BR9).

**Feature switch.** None of its own is named by a source, and the record path must have no off state: a capture that cannot be recorded must not be stored, so a switch that silenced the record would break BR4 and the principle that no action stands unlogged. The legacy flag `rwb.dochub.field-capture` stays `rwb-document`'s and is a legacy reference here; with it off no capture reaches the store and no DOCATT record arrives (GAP-1281; ASM-2271).

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P5-E2024-CON stay green, and a SIT day shows one DOCATT entry per stored document and one per refused item of a field capture, each with its rule and version, its inputs reference, its object reference and its final call; a chain with no break and no entry changed or deleted; a refused record that refuses the item with MSG-P7-003 and stores nothing; both reads answering by case and by entry; and not one document, capture row, review item, task or case status changed by this story.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-003 | The record of the item cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on the fail-closed handler; the legacy message text is copied unchanged |
| MSG-P7-009 | An entry has a rule id with no version, or a decision code outside the list in force | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1281; ASM-2271) | This story, on the append, naming `ruleVersion` or `decisionCode` |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role holds no right in the `DECISION_LOG` area | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, through the authorise answer of the read |
| MSG-P4-003 | The entry or the case is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. | This story, through the authorise answer of the read |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A query value is outside its list, or a required field of the entry is absent | Enter {field}. | This story, on the read and on the append |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The log, the reference list or the parameters are unavailable | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1281; ASM-2271) | This story, on the read and on the retried fact |
| MSG-P5-001, MSG-P5-016, MSG-P5-017, MSG-GEN-002, MSG-GEN-003, MSG-P5-003, MSG-P5-015 | An item is refused for its type, its malware, its size, its time or its position, or a bill field needs checking | The legacy texts of section 14 of RWB-E2-024 | `rwb-document`, on the item; this story only records the message id on the entry of a refusal |

MSG-P7-003, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 are copied unchanged from the FSD P7 v3 message set and the platform messages the authorise contract carries; MSG-P5-001, MSG-P5-003, MSG-P5-015, MSG-P5-016, MSG-P5-017, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002 and MSG-GEN-003 are the legacy texts and are produced by `rwb-document`, not here. The text of MSG-P7-009 is named by the FSD P7 v3 exception flows but is not written out in any source this story may read, and no source writes the text of MSG-GEN-006, so both placeholders stand; the message id set of this story beyond these six has no source and is carried in GAP-1281. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built in this story. The two reads are consumed by the decision-log view of a case and by the decision screen SCR-11 of this service, which are served through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 and are another story's; SCR-30 Case documents and SCR-31 Document review queue stay `rwb-document`'s and this story feeds neither of them. A panel id for showing the DOCATT entries beside the captures on SCR-30 is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1281; ASM-2271).

| Where | State | What the reader sees |
|---|---|---|
| The decision-log read (P7) | List | The DOCATT entries of the case in chain order, with the document or the client file ID, the document type, the capture kind, the capture time, the rule and version, the final call and the message id of a refusal |
| The entry read | One entry | The same row with its inputs reference, its freshness stamps, its `decidedAt`, its `prevHash` and its `entryHash` |
| The entry read | An entry of a refused item | `finalCall` `REFUSED` or `QUARANTINED`, the message id and no document reference |
| The entry read | An entry with `correctsEntryId` | The correction beside the entry it corrects, and the corrected entry unchanged |
| The read | 403, or 404 | MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right, MSG-P4-003 for a case out of scope; no row is returned |

The screen field list, the composite route specification and the masking of each field belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and to the story that owns each screen.

| TC-E2-024-11 | AC2, BR9 | NFR | An EICAR test file quarantined with MSG-P5-016; one entry with `finalCall` `QUARANTINED` and no document, and no file or position in it |

The legacy level System maps to Contract or Component as the row shows, Access to Component and Resilience to NFR. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID. Every case is asserted on the record side of this story: the entry, its object reference, its capture facts, its versions, its final call, its message id, its chain and its two reads; the capture, the scan, the store, the intake and the extraction are the document contract fake's. The `-ITG` copies of these cases belong to RWB-ITG-E2024-ITG and are not written here.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the decision code, the final call set, the document types, the ledger parameters and the message ids are reference rows, parameter rows or facts of another service; nothing of them is a constant here.
- No personal data in the entry, the fact, the outbox, the tests or the logs: the case reference, the document reference, the client file ID, the document type, the capture kind, the capture time, the rule and version, the inputs reference, the actor reference, the final call and dates only. The position, the file name, the photo and the bill value stay in `rwb_document`, and a test scans the entry, the fact and the log line for any digit of `13.7563` and `100.5018` and for `1,284.50`.
- No read of another service's tables (DP-01): the capture facts arrive on the document contract and on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the authorise answer on its contract, the reference lists and parameters in process; no `document`, `document_intake`, `document_field`, `recovery_case`, `task`, `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule` or `parameter_value` row is copied into `rwb_decision`.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views: this story reads no ACE data at all.
- One recorder and no mover: this story changes no document, no capture row, no review item, no task and no case status, so a decision record can never move a case (BR10).
- No entry without its change and no change without its entry: the entry, its chain position and its outbox row commit in one transaction, and a store transaction that cannot record its decision rolls back and refuses the item (BR4, BR13, R-UNI-39).
- Append only and hash chained: no UPDATE and no DELETE on `decision_log_entry`, and the chain is verifiable from `chain_seq` 1 (BR5).
- One entry per stored document and one per refused item: the partial unique key on the object reference and the inbox dedupe make a second entry impossible (BR6, BR14).
- One base, one topic, one queue: `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, `rwb.decision.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` with `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`; no story in this key declares another service's base or topic as its own.
- One hop and 2 s on every call, with a breaker per downstream; a missing document fact, a missing reference list or a missing parameter never produces an entry from a guessed type, code or version (DP-11).
- The record path has no off switch, because a capture that cannot be recorded must not be stored.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-024 for the wave 2 integration harness. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **a repeatable cross-service journey harness for field captures that carries an inspection of photos and bills into the document hub with its capture time, position and bill fields, and shows the result on the case, in the review queue and in the decision log**, so that **the field capture journey is proven end to end across rwb-document, rwb-access, rwb-case and rwb-decision before the app stories of RWB-E2-024 are signed off**.

This story builds the harness, its contract fakes, its seed pack, its evidence pack and its pass or fail gate. It builds no production endpoint, screen, table or migration.

##### 2. Business rationale

RWB-E2-024 splits into four app stories and this integration story. The app stories build their own part inside their own service: the field capture endpoint and the capture columns on the document in RWB-P5-E2024-APP, the scope and role check in RWB-P4-E2024-APP, the case and task facts the journey starts from in RWB-P3-E2024-APP, and the decision record behind the store in RWB-P7-E2024-APP. None of them can prove on its own that a photo taken with no signal on 14 December arrives on 15 December with its own capture time, that the same sync sent twice still leaves ten documents on the case, that a bill photographed in the field is read into `bill_amount` and `due_date` without a chat message or a paper envelope, or that a low-confidence amount stops in the review queue instead of passing as a fact. That proof is this story.

The journey is the one the business asks for: an inspection is on the case the same day it is made, with the date, the place and the bill values that can be shown when the inspection is questioned (REQ-DCM-013). The harness runs it against the published contracts of the four services on one business date and produces evidence that can be re-run for any build.

The architecture changes the path, not the business. The monolith wrote one `recovery.document` table and one `recovery.document_hub_parameter` row set from one module, called the case interface in process, and logged the decision in the same transaction as the state change. In the target, rwb-document owns `rwb_document` for metadata, custody, OCR text and fields, and the harness never reads it (DP-01); the case entry date and the task come from rwb-case by one hop with a 2 s timeout and never from a case table (DP-11); the type, field and parameter values are reference data and parameters owned by rwb-case and read through its contract (DP-06, DP-07); the DOCATT decision record goes to the local library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03); Flyway in `rwb_document` carries the capture columns (DP-15); the store writes its outbox and `DocumentStored` travels on `rwb.document.events.v1` (DP-09); and the whole journey runs on the gateway route the real screens use, on the owners' own bases (DP-19). The harness is the place where those boundaries are exercised together, so a capture that is lost, duplicated or misread is found in SIT and not by a case owner who cannot show the inspection.

The legacy exception table gives the measure: eleven triggers, each with a named message and each returned on the item rather than failing the request. The harness asserts that shape too, because a batch that fails whole on one bad file is as wrong as a batch that accepts it.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The wave 2 harness environment (SIT) is available with the gateway route for `/api/recovery/*`, the topics `rwb.document.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and the intake profile of rwb-document. The harness environment, its seed pack and its evidence format: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0406; ASM-0581).
- The four integration dependencies have published their contracts, or their contract fakes stand in for them: RWB-P5-E2024-APP (rwb-document), RWB-P4-E2024-APP (rwb-access), RWB-P3-E2024-APP (rwb-case) and RWB-P7-E2024-APP (rwb-decision).
- Case `RW-2026-000501` exists in the seeded data with entry date 2026-10-02 and a field inspection task for the collector `FC-01` with role RW-FIELDCOL, so the case is in that collector's Own scope (legacy section 7 Background).
- The document type rows INSPECTION_PHOTO with no fields, INSPECTION_CHECKLIST with no fields and UTILITY_BILL with `bill_amount`, `due_date` and `account_ref` are loaded as reference data, through the P3 contract only.
- The parameters CAPTURE_CLOCK_SKEW_MINUTES 5, CAPTURE_MAX_AGE_DAYS 30, CAPTURE_MAX_FILES 50 and INTAKE_MAX_FILE_MB 25 are in force through the P3 parameter contract; 5, 30, 50 and 25 are the legacy values (legacy section 3, section 13) and are read, never coded.
- The clock skew of 5 minutes and the age limit of 30 days are asserted as the values in force, so the boundary conditions of AC1 and AC5 are fixed by data and not by the build.
- The test user of role RW-FIELDCOL (`FC-01` in the legacy data) holds Documents right C on the case in scope; the P4 session operation is the only place that right is confirmed.
- Synthetic files only: synthetic photos with no person and no real address, synthetic utility bills, one HEIC file and one EICAR test file. No real customer data, phone number or position enters the harness or its evidence.
- The feature switch `rwb.dochub.field-capture` is on in the harness profile; off, the operation answers 404 and the run stops at step 5 with X1.
- No build dependency and no contract dependency. Day 1: the whole story runs against the four fakes from the first day.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: takes the run lock for the environment and records the build ID, the business date 2026-12-15 and the four contract versions it is about to exercise.
2. Harness: seeds the case `RW-2026-000501` with entry date 2026-10-02, the field inspection task for `FC-01`, the three document types and the four parameters, and, per scenario, the extra case and task state the scenario names; a missing seed item stops the run (X7).
3. Harness: calls `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` for `FC-01` and records the role, the scope and the Documents right it will exercise.
4. Harness: calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` and records the case state, the entry date and the task the journey starts from.
5. Harness: calls `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/field-captures` with the manifest of `clientFileId`, kind PHOTO, BILL or CHECKLIST, capture time with offset, latitude and longitude, and one file part per item, with an Idempotency-Key per scenario; records the status and the item results.
6. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` and records the count, the type, the source, the capture time, the position and the review state of each document.
7. Harness: reads one document through `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` and records its `captured_at`, `capture_latitude`, `capture_longitude`, `client_file_id` and, for a bill, its extracted fields with their confidence.
8. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/review-items` and records whether the low-confidence bill field appears there (AC8).
9. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` and records whether the DOCATT entry exists for each stored document and for each item the store refused (AC1, AC6).
10. Harness: subscribes to `rwb.document.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` for the run window and records `DocumentStored`, `DocumentFieldsExtracted` and `DecisionRecorded` for the case, and asserts that no event names a file, a position or a bill value.
11. Harness: waits for the JOB-12 Document intake window and records the intake item per bill and per checklist, and the state the review queue holds after extraction (AC1, AC8).
12. Harness: writes the per-scenario evidence into one run report keyed by story key and business date, evaluates the gate and attaches the report to the wave 2 release record; then releases the run lock and restores the seeded data.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A contract fake or a real service answers an unexpected status for the journey | The scenario is marked failed and the report names the operation, the expected status and the answer | None | AC1, AC6 |
| X2 | A document that the response named as ACCEPTED is not readable through the document operation within the run window | The scenario is marked failed; the report names the case, the document ID and the missing entry | None | AC1, AC2, AC3 |
| X3 | The batch is answered 413 or 422 instead of a per-item result | The scenario is marked failed unless the scenario is the batch-shape one, and the report carries the problem detail | MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002 | AC6 |
| X4 | An item carrying the EICAR signature is accepted and a document is written | The scenario is marked failed; a quarantine that leaves a document is a defect, not a warning | MSG-P5-016 | AC6 |
| X5 | A capture is sent for a case with no task for the collector and is accepted | The scenario is marked failed; the report names the case and the absent task | MSG-P4-003 | AC7 |
| X6 | The decision log answers 503 on the journey read | The scenario is marked failed and the report keeps the last good ledger read for rerun | None | AC1, AC6 |
| X7 | The seeded data cannot be loaded (case, task, type, field or parameter missing) | The run refuses to start and names the missing seed item; no scenario is reported | None | All |
| X8 | Another run holds the environment lock | The run refuses to start and names the holder and the start time | None | All |
| X9 | The evidence pack cannot be attached to the release record | The run is marked failed; the local evidence file is kept for rerun | None | All |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the four published contracts or their fakes and the intake profile; it builds no service feature and has no build dependency |
| Negotiable | The scenarios, the seeded values, the file fixtures and the item results are data files, never code |
| Valuable | The capture journey is proven once across four services, before the app stories claim Done |
| Estimable | One journey runner, one fake set, one capture pack, two assertions, one evidence collector, one gate |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each owned criterion has a scenario with a fixed Given, When and Then and a recorded result |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria


##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Every field capture goes through the same type, size and malware checks as any other document, before storage | REQ-DCM-013; RWB-E1-041; RWB-E1-024 |
| BR2 | The capture time is the device time recorded at capture; the receipt time is the server time, and the server never replaces the device time | FEAT-DCM-21 |
| BR3 | A capture time later than receipt plus the clock skew, before the case entry date, or older than the age limit is refused on the item | CAPTURE_CLOCK_SKEW_MINUTES (5), CAPTURE_MAX_AGE_DAYS (30); DF-CAS-013 |
| BR4 | The client file ID is unique per case; a repeat returns the earlier result and stores nothing | R-UNI-40 |
| BR5 | The item kind sets the document type: photo to INSPECTION_PHOTO, bill to UTILITY_BILL, checklist to INSPECTION_CHECKLIST; no classification runs | Document types reference data; DL19 |
| BR6 | A capture is attached to the case named in the request; no case matching runs | FEAT-DCM-12 is not needed when the case is known |
| BR7 | Bills are extracted with the UTILITY_BILL field list, and a field below the confidence threshold goes to review | RWB-E1-053 BR2; RWB-E1-054 |
| BR8 | GPS position and photos of a home are personal data: masked by role and never logged | CTL-11; DL26 |
| BR9 | A capture that cannot be written to the decision log through the store is not stored | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |

BR1 to BR9 are the legacy rules BR1 to BR10 of RWB-E2-024, with legacy BR6 folded into BR5 and legacy BR8 into BR2. The split changes none of them; the harness asserts them across the service boundaries and restates none of them in code.

##### 9. State transitions

None on the case. This story does not change a case status. The document `review_status` it observes is NOT_NEEDED on an accepted capture, PENDING after extraction of a bill, and REVIEW on a bill field below the threshold (AC8); the intake item it observes is created by JOB-12 and then resolved by extraction. The inspection task and the R-DIL-22 move to ASSET_UNLOCK_DECISION stay in Epic 3.

The harness adds a run state of its own only: Not started, Running, Passed, Failed, with the latest run for a build deciding the gate.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test asset in the integration pipeline and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/field-captures` | P5 rwb-document | The capture request under test (AC1, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7), with an Idempotency-Key per scenario |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` | P5 rwb-document | Reads the document list with type, source, capture time, position and review state (AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` | P5 rwb-document | Reads one document, its capture columns and, for a bill, its extracted fields with confidence (AC2, AC3, AC8) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/review-items` | P5 rwb-document | Asserts the bill with a low-confidence field in the review queue (AC8) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | Reads the case state, the entry date and the task the journey starts from (AC1, AC7) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | Confirms the role, the scope and the Documents right the sync runs under (AC1, AC7) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | P7 rwb-decision | Asserts the DOCATT entry per stored document and the absent entry per refused item (AC1, AC6) |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with the 2 s timeout and the breaker of DP-11, and the POST carries an Idempotency-Key (BR4). The scope check that rwb-document makes inside its own process is not a separate path in the Ownership Map, so the harness confirms the right through the P4 session operation instead. The reference-data and parameter reads named in section 11 are rwb-case contract operations called by rwb-document, not by the harness, and their paths are not restated here.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; the evidence goes to the release record through its pipeline integration.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` | `rwb.document.events.v1` | P5 rwb-document | Asserts one event per accepted document, ten for AC1, six for AC5, none for a refused or quarantined item (AC1, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7) |
| `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` | `rwb.document.events.v1` | P5 rwb-document | Asserts the extracted bill fields of AC3 and the review state of AC8 without reading a table |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | Asserts that the DOCATT record of each stored document reached the shared topic inside the run window (DP-03, DP-09), alongside the ledger read of 12.2 |

The harness subscribes with its own consumer group and asserts the event, never the producer's table. Key is `caseId`; the payload carries IDs and facts only.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

JOB-12 Document intake (`DocumentIntakeWorkflow` on queue `rwb-document`) is exercised, not built: the harness waits for its window after the sync, records the intake item per bill and per checklist, and asserts the state extraction leaves behind (AC1, AC3, AC8). JOB-11 Outbox sender is observed on its every-minute window for `DocumentStored` and `DocumentFieldsExtracted`.

Legacy section 12 has the store and the listener create the intake item inside the monolith; Architecture v5 slide 16 gives rwb-document `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` with OCR, classify and extract, and slide 44 gives JOB-12 the every-15-minute window with KEDA workers. The harness follows the higher source, so it asserts the item and the fields after the window rather than a call inside the request.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The harness adds no workflow and no schedule; JOB-12's window and JOB-11's minute timer are the platform's and are only observed.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no table in any schema (DP-01); it reads and writes through the operations of 12.2 only.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Contract | What it answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| WireMock rwb-document, field captures | `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/field-captures` | OpenAPI of P5 | 200 with one result per item, status ACCEPTED, DUPLICATE, REFUSED or QUARANTINED, with the message code of AC6; 404 with MSG-P4-003 for AC7; keeps the request journal for the idempotency assertions of AC4 and AC5 |
| WireMock rwb-document, reads | `GET .../documents`, `GET /documents/{documentId}`, `GET /review-items` | OpenAPI of P5 | The ten documents of AC1 with type, source, capture time and position, the bill fields of AC3, the single review item of AC8 |
| WireMock rwb-document, intake profile | JOB-12 `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` outcome | The P5 intake contract | The intake item per bill and the extracted fields with confidence 0.5500 on the amount for AC8 |
| WireMock rwb-case | `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | OpenAPI of P3 | The case state, entry date 2026-10-02 and the task for `FC-01` of AC1; no task for `RW-2026-000502` in AC7 |
| WireMock rwb-access | `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | OpenAPI of P4 | Role RW-FIELDCOL, the Own scope and Documents right C; the refusal of MSG-P4-003 for AC7 |
| WireMock rwb-decision | `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | OpenAPI of P7 | The DOCATT entry per stored document and the absent entry per refused item; 503 for X6 |
| Malware-scan and intake profile | The scan and store step rwb-document makes before storage | The rwb-document profile, not a service contract | Clean for the ten files of AC1, a threat for the EICAR file of AC6, a size refusal for MSG-P5-017 when the profile is switched to 1 MB |

Each fake is replaced by the real service as its I story lands, without a change to the scenarios. The concrete fake mappings, the intake profile and the evidence format: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0406; ASM-0581).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 7 consumed, one hop on the owner's base with the 2 s timeout of DP-11; Idempotency-Key on the POST |
| Kafka | 3 events consumed on `rwb.document.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`; none published |
| Temporal | Observed only: JOB-12 Document intake on queue `rwb-document` and JOB-11 Outbox sender; no workflow, activity or schedule added |
| File | None. The synthetic files travel in the multipart request body and are never written to a shared share or a fixture folder by the harness |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `integration/recovery-document-capture` in the ACE repository, package `<ACE base package>.recovery.integration.documentcapture`. Not part of any deployed service, and it ships no Flyway script and no schema of its own (DP-15 applies to rwb-document, which owns the capture columns).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added | How this harness applies it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none | The harness owns no table and reads no schema; every document, case, session and ledger read is an operation of 12.2 |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The DOCATT entry is read through rwb-decision and the `DecisionRecorded` event on the shared topic, per stored document |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON | The clock skew 5, the age limit 30 and the file limit 50 are read as parameters, so a boundary scenario needs a parameter change and no code change |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The three document types and the UTILITY_BILL field list are seeded reference data, never values in the harness code |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON | The harness subscribes with its own consumer group and counts the events per accepted item; it never reads an outbox table |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) | Each consumed operation is called once from the harness with a 2 s timeout and an Idempotency-Key on the POST; no chain is built |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON | The capture columns are rwb-document's own Flyway change; the harness asserts the columns through the contract and runs no migration |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The journey runs through the gateway route the real case screens use, on the owners' own bases, so a route fault is found in SIT |

The platform H dependencies in the table (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, H RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are delivered by the platform waves and are not repeated in the metadata: the harness converges on them and has no build dependency of its own. The blocking dependencies of this story are the four I stories, which replace the fakes with real services one at a time.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Job | Runs the twelve flow steps for one scenario and one business date, and owns the run lock |
| FakeRegistry | Configuration | WireMock mappings for the four services and the intake profile, one set per contract version |
| CapturePack | Data | The synthetic files and manifests of each scenario: eight photos and two bills, a HEIC file, an EICAR file, a bill image with the amount and due date of AC3, and the parameter boundary sets |
| DocumentAssertion | Service | Reads the document list and one document through rwb-document and compares count, type, source, capture time, position, review state and extracted fields |
| DecisionAssertion | Service | Reads the decision log and the shared topic and compares the DOCATT record per stored document, with none for a refused item |
| EvidenceCollector | Service | Writes one report keyed by story key and business date, with request, response, item results, document reads, review items and decision entries |
| GateEvaluator | Service | Passes the run when every owned scenario passes and the evidence pack is attached |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, the wave 2 harness profile, business date 2026-12-15, synthetic files only. The seeded values are the legacy section 7 Background and the state each scenario names; no other value is added, and no file shows a person or a real address. The environment, the seed pack and the evidence format: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0406; ASM-0581).

**Build steps**

1. Write the CapturePack for the Background and the eight scenarios, including the parameter boundary sets; test that a bad seed stops the run (X7).
2. Write the FakeRegistry with the four WireMock mapping sets and the intake profile, and pin each contract version in the run report; fail the run on a version mismatch (X1).
3. Write the JourneyRunner for AC1: the session and case reads, the sync of ten files, the ten document reads and the ten events.
4. Add the DocumentAssertion for the capture time, the position and the stored date, which carries AC2 and the offline replay.
5. Add AC3 and AC8 with the JOB-12 window, the extracted fields of the bill, the confidence 0.5500 and the review queue read.
6. Add AC4 and AC5 with the request journal and the two Idempotency-Keys, and the duplicate count of ten and six.
7. Add AC6 and AC7: the per-item refusals of MSG-GEN-002, MSG-P5-001 and MSG-P5-016 with the batch answering 200, then the 404 of MSG-P4-003 with no document and no event.
8. Write the EvidenceCollector and the GateEvaluator, attach the report to the wave 2 release record, and rerun the eight scenarios on the release build.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.dochub.field-capture` is on in the harness profile, as the legacy story sets it; the harness itself is a pipeline stage selected by the run profile, not by a business flag.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the run report is attached to the wave 2 release record with all eight owned scenarios, and each fake has been replaced by the real service where its I story has landed in SIT. The intake profile and the evidence sign-off wait for the values of GAP-0406.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-015 | Captures accepted with no GPS position | {count} files have no location. They are on the case without a position. |
| MSG-P5-001 | File type not allowed | This file type cannot be stored. Use PDF, JPG or PNG. |
| MSG-P5-003 | A bill field needs checking | Some fields need checking. The document is in the review queue. |
| MSG-P5-016 | A capture with malware | This file was not stored because the malware scan found a threat. It is held in quarantine. |
| MSG-P5-017 | A capture above the size limit | This file is larger than {size} MB and cannot be stored. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed for an item | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | Manifest and files do not match | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | Capture time in the future; too many files | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Capture time before the case entry date or the age limit | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without Documents C | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the collector's scope | This case is not in your scope. |

The harness produces none of these messages itself; it asserts the message the owning service returns and names the message ID in the report, so a run failure points at a service and a message and not only at a date. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the three document types, the UTILITY_BILL field list, the clock skew, the age limit, the file limit and the confidence threshold are parameters and reference data.
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs, logs, evidence or prompts. The harness evidence carries document identifiers, statuses, message codes and timestamps only, never a file, a position or a bill value.
- No read of another service's tables and no schema of the harness's own: every read and write goes through the operations of 12.2 (DP-01).
- GPS position and photos of a home are personal data (BR8): the synthetic files show no person and no real address, and a position appears only as the value a contract returns, once, in the report.
- Each fake is replaced by the real service as its I story lands; a fake that outlives its service is a defect, not a configuration.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and an exception is never added to a scenario; a value that must change changes in the seed pack or the parameters through a reviewed change.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract baseline of the stage 2 and 3 extraction extension of `rwb-document` is split out of legacy RWB-E2-025 and published on base `/api/recovery/document/v1` with the topic `rwb.document.events.v1`, the checked-fields read, the checked-field shapes, the eleven-type field code fixture, the state filter and masking rule, the error envelope, the event declaration and the fakes with their drift test. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the stage 2 and 3 extraction extension of `rwb-document` — the checked-fields read on base `/api/recovery/document/v1` with the `CheckedField` and `CheckedFieldSet` shapes, the state filter and masking rule, the eleven-type field code fixture with the five new types and the extended hearing-notice list, the error envelope with every message ID and its status, the `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` declaration with no field value, and the fakes with their drift test —**, so that **the app story of this legacy key, the S4 litigation reader, the S2 treatment reader, the review queue of `rwb-document` and the wave 2 integration harness build against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1, and a renamed checked field, a different state filter, an extra payload property or a personal value in an event can never drift between two services without a failing test**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). Legacy RWB-E2-025 hands the litigation and treatment modules a Java interface inside the same process — `DocumentFieldReader.checkedFields(UUID caseId, String documentType)` returning `CheckedField` — together with an in-process `ExtractStep`, an in-process `DocumentTypeCatalog` and a document read on the monolith base. Under the target architecture S4 and S2 are separate services that cannot link a Java interface of `rwb-document`, the extraction is an activity of a workflow on the owner's own task queue, and the parts most likely to drift silently are exactly the ones this baseline fixes:

- a checked field renamed or dropped, so the litigation pack renders a judgment amount it cannot attribute to a field or a document version;
- a state filter widened to REVIEW, so an unchecked value reaches the pack and the treatment record with no person having seen it;
- a personal value such as `party_names` returned without its flag or without masking, so a contract's parties reach a role that may not see them;
- an extraction event carrying a field value, so a contract amount leaves the service in a Kafka payload;
- an error answered with the wrong status or without a `messageId`, so a reader cannot tell a document outside its scope from a type that is not in force;
- a field code set read from a different place by the extraction and by the reader, so the same judgment yields two different field lists on the same date.

The baseline fixes the names the checks require: schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`. It makes the C dependencies of the app story explicit — the P3 parameters contract `RWB-P3-E1042-CON` and the P3 reference-data contract `RWB-P3-E1043-CON` — and it records that the `rwb-case` case read is consumed and faked although the plan lists it in no C row of this key (`ASM-1906`).

It also records what the sources leave open. No TSD P5 T-A.1 row and no Architecture v5 slide names a REST operation or a path for reading checked fields, so the operation, the path and the field-level names of `CheckedField` and `CheckedFieldSet` are the baseline's own choice and are Not specified in the source documents (`ASM-1904`). The extraction operations themselves are not this key's: they are published by RWB-P5-E1053-CON and this baseline consumes and references them without declaring a second copy (`ASM-1905`). Nothing else is guessed: the five new types, their fields, the pattern of `red_case_no`, the pass mark 0.90, the field threshold 0.80 and the message IDs are copied character for character from RWB-E2-025, FSD P5 A2.22 and TSD P5 T3.1.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the operation, topic, event and queue names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the retry and `.dlt` topic convention are the platform baseline (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- TSD P5 T3.1 is in force for `document`, `document_field`, `document_intake`, `document_text`, `document_type` and `document_hub_parameter`, and TSD P5 T3.2 is in force for LOV-DOC-TYPE, LOV-EXTRACT-STATUS and LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW.
- The extraction baseline RWB-P5-E1053-CON is published with the extract operation, the extract-state read, the fields read, the `FieldSet` shape, the field set fixture of DOCTYPE-2026.11 and the agent route it consumes, so this baseline extends a contract that exists and declares no second extraction operation (`ASM-1905`).
- The classification baseline RWB-P5-E1050-CON and the review baseline RWB-P5-E1054-CON are published, so `predicted_type`, `classification_confidence`, `review_reason` and the states CONFIRMED and CORRECTED have one owner document each (`ASM-1910`).
- The Ownership Map is the only source of owners: `document`, `document_field`, `document_intake`, `document_text`, `document_type` and `document_hub_parameter` are P5's in `rwb_document`; `recovery_case`, `lov_value`, `parameter_catalog` and `reference_row` are P3's; the `agent_*` tables and the model route are P10's.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7), so its four H, C, I and X columns are empty and every dependant builds against the published baseline and its fakes.
- The release date 31 December 2026 is the legacy one and is tentative (`ASM-1908`), and the story carries Status Draft (realignment v1) because no approval of the realigned story is recorded (`ASM-1909`).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document of `rwb-document` with the checked-fields read, the two resources of section 11 and the error responses of section 14, on the single base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, beside the operations RWB-P5-E1053-CON and RWB-P5-E1024-APP already declare.
2. Fix the read: the case path parameter, the required `documentType` query, the optional `documentVersion`, the declared Documents right R, the scope rule and the access log on every read.
3. Fix `CheckedField` and `CheckedFieldSet` field by field, with the required set, the confidence precision, the `state` values OK, CONFIRMED and CORRECTED and the `personal` flag.
4. Publish the field code fixture of the eleven types from the type table version DOCTYPE-2026.12: the 26 codes of the six Epic 1 types and the 20 codes of the five new types, with `party_names` marked personal.
5. Fix the state filter and the masking rule: only OK, CONFIRMED or CORRECTED rows are returned; a REVIEW row is never returned; a personal value is returned only when the caller's masking rule allows it.
6. Map every failure to the error envelope and a message ID, status by status, and record the absent operation name and the absent C row as a gap and its assumptions.
7. Declare the event position: the one extraction event `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` on `rwb.document.events.v1`, with the new type codes in `documentType`, no field value and no personal value; no third event of this key.
8. Publish the fakes, the drift test and the absence test, then hand the baseline to RWB-P5-E2025-APP, the S4 and S2 readers, the review queue and RWB-ITG-E2025-ITG.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X2 | A field is renamed, removed or retyped within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a corrected document or a new major version | None | AC2, AC3 |
| X3 | The state filter returns a REVIEW field, or a fourth state appears | The contract test fails: the answer carries OK, CONFIRMED and CORRECTED only | None | AC4 |
| X4 | A personal value is returned without its flag or without masking | The contract test and the no-personal-data test fail | None | AC4 |
| X5 | A field code set is read from a different place by the extraction and by the reader | The contract test fails against the published fixture of the version in force | None | AC3, AC7 |
| X6 | An error returns a wrong status or no `messageId` | The contract test fails on the error envelope and the message table | MSG-P4-001 | AC5 |
| X7 | A field value or a personal value appears in the event payload, or a fourth event is declared | The AsyncAPI schema test, the no-personal-data test and the absence test fail | None | AC6, AC8 |
| X8 | A fake drifts from the document, or a second extraction operation is declared | The drift test or the absence test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC7, AC8 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Criterion | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Independent | Pass | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, TSD P5 T3, the Ownership Map and the two same-service baselines it extends |
| Negotiable | Pass | The field-level names are settled with S4, S2 and the review queue; the operation set, the state filter, the fixture, the error mapping, the event declaration and the absence rule are fixed by the target architecture and the legacy section 12 |
| Valuable | Pass | Unblocks RWB-P5-E2025-APP, the S4 and S2 readers and the wave 2 harness on Day 1 |
| Estimable | Pass | One document, one operation, two resources, one fixture, nine contract tables and seven fakes |
| Small | Pass | Fits one sprint with its contract tests |
| Testable | Pass | Every criterion in section 7 is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

The eight criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only; they restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P5-E2025-APP. The legacy AC1 to AC11 of RWB-E2-025 are owned by RWB-P5-E2025-APP, and the wave 2 harness RWB-ITG-E2025-ITG consumes this baseline and copies none of these criteria.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/document/v1` on every declared operation | DP-01; Template and Rules §R4; Architecture v5 slide 41 notes |
| BR2 | One topic per service: `rwb.document.events.v1`, with the retry and `.dlt` topics of the platform convention | DP-09; Architecture v5 slides 16 and 42 |
| BR3 | A change inside major version 1 is additive; a removed, renamed or retyped property and a narrowed required set are a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |
| BR4 | The document declares only tables of `rwb_document` and only operations owned by `rwb-document`; an operation of the same service that another baseline owns is described as consumed and referenced, never re-declared | Ownership Map; DP-01; `ASM-1905` |
| BR5 | The service has exactly two events, `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` and `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1`; this key declares the second and adds no type, topic or payload property | TSD P5 T5.3; Architecture v5 slide 42; `ASM-1907` |
| BR6 | No business value is fixed in the contract: the types, the field codes, the patterns, the threshold, the pass mark, the extraction methods and the review-only flags stay rows of the type table and the parameter table | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; RWB-E2-025 section 17 |
| BR7 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, codes, versions, dates, confidences and states only, and no party name, customer name, account number or title-doc number in clear | Architecture v5 slide 11; RWB-E2-025 BR7 and section 17 |
| BR8 | No field value and no document text in the event or a log: the payload carries field names, confidences and states, and the read carries a value only behind masking and the access log | DP-09; RWB-E2-025 section 12 |
| BR9 | Every consumed row states one hop, a 2 s timeout, a GET retry once with jitter and a breaker per downstream, and a failed read maps to MSG-GEN-006 naming the system that failed | DP-11, ADR-020; Architecture v5 slide 11 |
| BR10 | Every error uses one envelope and one message ID per condition; the message texts are copied unchanged from RWB-E2-025 section 14 | Architecture v5 platform baseline; Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR11 | The checked-field read is a GET: it declares no `Idempotency-Key`, writes nothing and has no side effect; the extraction operation that may follow keeps the `Idempotency-Key` of its own baseline | Architecture v5 slide 11; DP-09; `ASM-1905` |
| BR12 | The contract declares no case state and no extraction state machine beyond the values the fields may take; a transition belongs to the app story that performs it, and CONFIRMED and CORRECTED belong to RWB-P5-E1054-APP | RWB-E2-025 section 9; `ASM-1910` |

##### 9. State transitions

| Baseline state | Event | Condition | Next state |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The read, the two resources, the fixture, the four consumed rows and the event declaration are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | RWB-P5-E2025-APP, the S4 and S2 readers, the review queue and the wave 2 harness accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1, for example an optional `extractorVersion` on `CheckedField` | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, or a required set is narrowed | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake or in the fixture | A contract test fails | In review |

This baseline declares no case state machine and no extraction state machine of its own. The values below are the values the fields may carry; the writing of them is the extraction's, and the move out of REVIEW belongs to RWB-P5-E1054-APP.

| Field value in the baseline | Meaning declared by this document |
|---|---|
| `state` = "OK" | A field whose confidence is at or above the threshold and whose value converted and matched its pattern |
| `state` = "REVIEW" | A field below the threshold, a `review_only` field, a value that could not be converted or a value that failed its pattern; declared and never returned by the read |
| `state` = "CONFIRMED" | A field a person accepted in the review queue of RWB-P5-E1054-APP |
| `state` = "CORRECTED" | A field a person corrected in the review queue of RWB-P5-E1054-APP, with the stored value the corrected one |
| `extractStatus` = "PENDING", "DONE", "FAILED" | The LOV-EXTRACT-STATUS values of TSD P5 T3.2, carried by the extraction baseline this key consumes |
| `personal` = true | A value masked for a role without the right; `party_names` is the one code this baseline asserts it for |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-document | Owns the OpenAPI document, the AsyncAPI fragment, the fixture and the seven fakes; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version and the operation name of the single gap this baseline records |
| Consuming teams (RWB-P5-E2025-APP, the S4 litigation reader, the S2 treatment reader, the review queue and the wave 2 harness) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer; RW-RESTRUCT, restructuring officer (FCR) | Confirm that the read carries what the pack and the treatment record need (Documents CRU on the case in scope) |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads the type table version the fixture is built from (Reference data CRUD) |
| Platform library owner | Owns the CloudEvents envelope, the error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the naming rule this document reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field is declared in an answer, an example or a fake |

The per-service login behind the document's security scheme is not part of this baseline; the document names the scheme "the rwb-document login (DP-02)" and the name is Not specified in the source documents (`ASM-1904`). The declared area and right are enforced at gateway-bff (DP-19); no `rwb-access` contract is declared here. The model route is not this service's secret: the provider, the model and the key belong to `rwb-agent` and are consumed through RWB-P5-E1053-CON.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| CheckedField | documentId (uuid, required), docVersion (integer, required), fieldName (string, required), value (string), state (OK, CONFIRMED or CORRECTED, required), confidence (numeric(5,4)), dataType, personal, extractorVersion, tableVersion, from the `document_field` fields DF-DOC-012 to DF-DOC-017, DF-DOC-034 and DF-DOC-035 |
| CheckedFieldSet | caseId, documentType, documentVersion, tableVersion, fieldCount, fields (array of CheckedField); ordered by documentId and fieldName |
| Field code fixture | The 46 codes of version DOCTYPE-2026.12: the 26 codes of the six Epic 1 types of DOCTYPE-2026.11 and the 20 codes of CONTRACT, CREDIT_APPROVAL, MORTGAGE_DOCUMENT, COURT_FILING and JUDGMENT of section 13 of the app story; `party_names` carries personal true |
| Field code source | `document_type.field_definitions` (DF-REF-224) in the version in force by `valid_from` and `valid_to`, with name, data_type, personal, extraction_method, review_only and the optional pattern; the fixture declares the codes and never the values of the table |
| Read semantics | Only OK, CONFIRMED and CORRECTED; the version in force on the extraction date; masking by role; the access log on every read |
| Event payload | `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1`: intakeId, documentId, documentType, tableVersion, extractorVersion, extractedAt, fieldCount, fields [fieldName, confidence, state] |
| Error envelope | RFC 9457 problem details with `messageId`, `detail`, `instance` and the status of section 14 |

Every example in the document is synthetic and uses the legacy values: case "RW-2026-000601", documents "DOC-0602" and "DOC-0605", the types "CONTRACT", "JUDGMENT" and "COURT_NOTICE", the confidence 0.7100 and 0.9200, the field threshold 0.80, the pass mark 0.90, the type table versions "DOCTYPE-2026.11" and "DOCTYPE-2026.12" and the extractor versions of the Epic 1 baseline. No example carries a customer value: the party names of the legacy AC2 are declared as the field code `party_names` with no value, and the field values of the legacy examples are examples only. The field-level names of `CheckedField` and `CheckedFieldSet` beyond the legacy interface comment are Not specified in the source documents (`ASM-1904`).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-document (P5); base `/api/recovery/document/v1`.

| Method | Path | API ID | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/checked-fields` | no TSD row; the baseline's own path (`ASM-1904`) | Query `documentType` required and `documentVersion` optional; answer 200 `CheckedFieldSet` | Documents R with scope applied; each read to the access log | Not applicable |

The read is the target shape of the legacy Java interface `DocumentFieldReader.checkedFields(UUID caseId, String documentType)`. The path is the baseline's own choice because no TSD P5 T-A.1 row and no Architecture v5 slide names a checked-field read, and the choice is recorded with its assumption.

The extract operation, the extract-state read and the fields read are declared by RWB-P5-E1053-CON with their own paths, rights and `Idempotency-Key` rule; the document read and the content read are RWB-P5-E1024-APP's. This baseline references them, consumes them as rows of 12.2 and re-declares none of them.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case, its queue and its team behind the scope filter of the read; one hop, 2 s, faked, and in no C row of the plan (`ASM-1906`) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters/{paramCode}` | P3 rwb-case | `EXTRACT_FIELD_THRESHOLD`, `EXTRACT_ACCURACY_PASS`, `EXTRACT_PRECISION_PASS`, `EXTRACT_RECALL_PASS`, `EXTRACT_MAX_ATTEMPTS`, `EXTRACT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` and `BE_YEAR_OFFSET` (C `RWB-P3-E1042-CON`) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-DOC-TYPE with the eleven types, LOV-EXTRACT-STATUS and LOV-INTAKE-REVIEW (C `RWB-P3-E1043-CON`) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/extract` | P5 rwb-document, same service | The extraction of an item of a new type, consumed from RWB-P5-E1053-CON and never re-declared (`ASM-1905`) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/intake-items/{intakeItemId}/extraction` | P5 rwb-document, same service | The extract state and the field set of an item, consumed from RWB-P5-E1053-CON |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/fields` | P5 rwb-document, same service | The active fields of a document at the document level, consumed from RWB-P5-E1053-CON |

Every cross-service row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retry once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (DP-11, ADR-020). A failed case read maps to 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming "Case service" and a failed list read to 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming "Reference data", and a refusal never returns a partial field set. The case read is consumed and faked and is named in no C row of the plan, so it carries `ASM-1906` and no row is added to the metadata C list.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Declared schema |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` | `rwb.document.events.v1` with the retry topics at 1 min, 10 min and 1 h and the `.dlt` topic | P5 rwb-document | Key documentId, or intakeId when the item has no document; payload intakeId, documentId, documentType (with the codes of the new types), tableVersion, extractorVersion, extractedAt, fieldCount and fields [fieldName, confidence, state]; CloudEvents 1.0 binary mode; no field value, no personal value and no document text |

This baseline declares the event schema because the service owns the topic, and it declares no new property, no new type and no new topic for the new document types: the type codes travel in `documentType` (`ASM-1907`). The row itself is written by the extraction of RWB-P5-E1053-CON inside its own transaction, and this key publishes nothing at run time. The service's other event, `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1`, is declared by the store baseline RWB-P5-E1024-APP; no third event exists for `rwb-document`.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The OpenAPI 3.1 document `openapi/rwb-document-v1.yaml` with the checked-fields read and the two resources; the AsyncAPI 3.0 fragment for `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` with the eleven type codes; the field code fixture `contract/field-set-DOCTYPE-2026.12.json` with the 46 codes and the personal flag of `party_names`; the contract README rows for the state filter, the version rule, the masking rule, the error mapping and the event count; and the seven WireMock mapping sets of section 12.8.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The H, C, I and X lists of the metadata table are empty: this baseline adds no build dependency of its own (it is Day 1 by rule), and the platform and service contracts it names are the ones the app story declares. DP-01 is why the document declares six tables of `rwb_document` and no table of another service: the field rows, the type table and the parameter rows are this schema's and the case is a consumed answer. DP-06 and DP-07 are the two C rows: the seven parameters and the three lists are read through the `rwb-case` contracts and never typed into the document. DP-09 fixes the topic, the envelope and the one-event rule, so the new type codes travel in an existing payload property and no new schema is invented. DP-10 names the two activity contracts the extraction runs in and declares no timer. DP-11 is the whole point of this baseline: the Java interface `DocumentFieldReader` becomes one hop with a published shape, a fake and a 2 s timeout, so S4 and S2 build on Day 1 and the case scope arrives through a second consumed row rather than a cross-schema join. DP-13 gives the read the service base and removes the monolith base from the contract. DP-19 records that the checked fields reach SCR-30 and SCR-31 through the gateway-bff composite route; this baseline fixes the answer shape only and no route specification.

**Build steps**

1. Write the read with its path, parameters, resource and error responses; validate the document in the pipeline.
2. Fix the required and optional sets of AC2 and the four-decimal confidence as schema constraints and README rows.
3. Publish the field code fixture of AC3 from the type table version in force, with the 46 codes and the single personal flag, and compare it with the fixture of RWB-P5-E1053-CON.
4. Record the state filter, the version rule and the masking rule of AC4 as schema constraints and README rows.
5. Map every status and message ID of AC5 and record the RFC 9457 envelope.
6. Declare the event of AC6 with the absence test for a third event and the no-personal-value test.
7. Publish the seven fakes and the eight contract tests, including the drift and absence tests; tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off of RWB-P5-E2025-APP, the S4 and S2 readers and RWB-ITG-E2025-ITG.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI artefact and the AsyncAPI fragment validate in the pipeline, the eight contract tests pass, the seven fakes answer every operation and read of sections 12.1 and 12.2, the fixture carries the 46 codes, the drift and absence tests are green, and RWB-P5-E2025-APP and RWB-ITG-E2025-ITG have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | HTTP status |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-003 | A document has a field in review (a label, not an error) | Some fields need checking. The document is in the review queue. | 200 |
| MSG-P4-001 | No authenticated caller | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. | 401 |
| MSG-P4-002 | Caller lacks Documents R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | 403 |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case or document outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. | 404 |
| MSG-P5-006 | documentType is not in the version in force | {value} is not a document type in force. Choose a type from the list. | 422 |
| MSG-GEN-001 | An absent or empty documentType, or a body that fails validation | Enter {field}. | 422 |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The case read or the list read fails | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. | 503 |

The message IDs and the wording are contract elements copied unchanged from RWB-E2-025 section 14 and the service messages of `rwb-document`; Thai text for each follows decision DL10.

Delivery shape: every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set to the ID above, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled, and `instance` naming the request. The status mapping fixed by AC5 is: 401 with MSG-P4-001, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 with MSG-P4-003, 422 with MSG-P5-006 or MSG-GEN-001, and 503 with MSG-GEN-006. For MSG-GEN-006 the {system} value is fixed by the consumed row that failed: "Case service" for the case read and "Reference data" for a list read. MSG-P5-003 is not an error response: it is the review label the screens show for a document with a field in REVIEW.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-30 Case documents and SCR-31 Document review queue read the answers this baseline fixes, through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which calls the owner once and merges the answer into the screen model; the screens, their forms and their actions are RWB-P5-E1026-APP and RWB-P5-E1054-APP. This baseline fixes the answer shapes only and declares no screen field list and no route specification.

| Screen state implied by the contract | What the answer carries |
|---|---|
| Case with checked fields of a stage 2 or 3 type | A `CheckedFieldSet` with the OK, CONFIRMED and CORRECTED fields of each document of the requested type |
| Document with a field in review | No REVIEW entry in the set, and the review label of MSG-P5-003 on the document |
| Personal field | An entry with `personal` true, and its value present only when the caller's masking rule allows it |
| Document of a type not in force | No entry, and the 422 of MSG-P5-006 when the requested type is not in the version in force |
| Document outside the caller's scope | No entry, and the 404 of MSG-P4-003 |

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the types, the 46 field codes, the patterns, the threshold, the pass mark, the extraction methods and the review-only flags stay rows of the type table and the parameter table.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, codes, versions, dates, confidences and states only; `party_names` is declared as a code with no value, and no customer name, account number or title-doc number is declared in clear.
- No field value and no document text in an event, an example or a log: the payload carries field names, confidences and states; the read carries a value only behind masking and the access log.
- The extraction operations are consumed from RWB-P5-E1053-CON and never re-declared; a second extract operation fails the absence test.
- Only the two events of `rwb-document` exist; the new type codes travel in `documentType` and no fourth event or payload property is added.
- ACE data is reached only through the owner's contract or a `v_ace_*` view; this document declares no ACE view and no cross-schema join.
- The contract names only `rwb_document` tables and only operations owned by `rwb-document`; every other read is consumed and faked, never declared as provided (DP-01, DP-11).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review.
- Every example in the document is synthetic and the legacy values are examples only; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The contract declares no case state and no extraction state machine; a transition belongs to the app story that performs it.
