##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, module `log/extraction`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision.extraction`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the pattern the record itself travels on — the local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` — and it is applied here as the append path of the central ledger, with its H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; it is not in the story's metadata list of patterns, and its dependency is carried in the gap of GAP-1286 beside the other DP-added dependencies. DP-01 is the boundary: the extraction entry lives in `rwb_decision` and the document facts arrive on the document contract, never as a read of `rwb_document`. DP-11 is the mockable boundary for the document read, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker. DP-13 is the base: every path of 12.1 and 12.2 is on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1`, and the monolith base appears nowhere. DP-19 is not built here: SCR-38 Decision log query and the auditor's screen are reached through the gateway-bff composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and this story adds no route to it.

DP-10 is the JOB-12 intake window, and the clock stays with `rwb-document`: under RWB-P5-E2025-APP the intake is the event-started `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` on queue `rwb-document`, so this story declares no Schedule (12.6) and registers no workflow or activity (12.5). No Schedule and no workflow is invented for the extract-and-record path, because the record is appended where the fact arrives.

The platform H dependencies of the DP table — H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON and H RWB-PLT-N001-CON — and the C dependencies of the published contracts of other services — C RWB-P3-E1042-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON — are not in the metadata rows of this story, which name None and RWB-P5-E2025-CON; they are the dependencies the DP table adds and they are recorded in GAP-1286 and ASM-2278. None of them blocks the build beyond Day 1: they are platform contracts of waves 0 and 1 and two published contracts of `rwb-case`, built against their fakes.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ExtractionDecisionListener | Kafka consumer with the inbox | Reads `DecisionRecorded` for the stage 2 and 3 extraction, deduplicates by event ID and idempotency key, and hands the decision facts to the recorder |
| ExtractionDecisionRecorder | Service | Reads the document facts and the parameter and reference versions in force, composes the entry, and decides nothing about the extraction itself (BR2, BR3, BR11) |
| DecisionLogAppender | Service | Takes the next `chain_seq`, computes `prev_hash` and `entry_hash`, and writes the entry and its outbox row in one transaction (DP-03, BR13, BR15) |
| ChainVerifier | Service | Recomputes the chain from a start position and reports count, last `chain_seq` and last `entry_hash`, and the break if any |
| DecisionLogQueryController | Controller | `GET /decision-log` and `GET /decision-log/{entryId}` with the declared area and right, the scope, the paging and the problem mapping for 401, 403, 404, 422 and 503 |
| DecisionLogRepository | Repository | `decision_log_entry` in `rwb_decision`, with the append-only rule, the chain columns, the idempotency key and the search of 12.1 |
| DocumentFactClient | Adapter | The document read of RWB-P5-E2025-CON, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker |
| ParameterVersionClient | Client | The threshold and the pass mark of DP-06 and the decision code list of DP-07, with the version in force on the business date |
| InputsSnapshotResolver | Service | Resolves the `inputs_ref` of the entry and the freshness stamp of each input the decision read |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `decision_log_entry`, the local decision record of the append and the library objects, all in schema `rwb_decision`; reads no other schema (DP-01).
- Migration in this story, in the per-service Flyway sequence of the service: `V2025_1__decision_extraction_entry.sql` adds the extraction columns of section 11 that the decision-log store baseline does not hold — the document reference and version, the document type code, the field name, the parameter version, the confidence, the threshold and the threshold reading — and the unique key `ux_declog_idempotency ON decision_log_entry (idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL`, so one entry per decision is a constraint and not only a check (BR14). The column names and types are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1285; ASM-2277).
- The append-only rule is the table's, with the trigger `tr_declog_append_only` that refuses an UPDATE and a DELETE from the schema owner and the missing grant for the service role, as FSD P7 v3 AC-P7-001-01 fixes it.
- No row of `document`, `document_field` or `parameter_value` is written here: the document hub's tables and the case's parameters are their owners'.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The field threshold 0.80 and the accuracy pass mark 0.90 are parameter rows of `rwb-case` read through DP-06 with the version in force; the parameter names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1285; ASM-2277), and the story holds no default.
- The decision code list and the approval level list are reference data of `rwb-case` read through DP-07; the value an extraction decision carries is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1285; ASM-2277), because LOV-DECISION names D5.1 to D9.3 and the access events only.
- The final call values `accepted` and `sent to the review queue` are the reading of ASM-2277 and are held as data, not as constants: a change is a reference row and not a release.
- The outbox retry policy and the inbox retention are the platform's (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON).
- The feature switch of this capability, if one is wanted, is a parameter of DP-06 and is not named here, because no source names it (GAP-1285; ASM-2277).

**Build steps**

1. `DecisionLogRepository` and the migration, with the unique key on the idempotency key and the append-only trigger; test that a second entry for the same decision and an UPDATE are both refused (AC4, AC5).
2. `ExtractionDecisionListener` with the inbox, the dedupe by event ID and idempotency key, and the not-a-decision cases of X6; test the replay of the same fact (AC5).
3. `ExtractionDecisionRecorder` and `ParameterVersionClient`: the entry composed from the document facts and the versions in force, with the refusal of an unknown decision code and of a rule or pattern with no version (X3, X4; AC1).
4. `DecisionLogAppender` and the chain: `chain_seq`, `prev_hash`, `entry_hash` over the canonical form, the first `prev_hash` of 64 zeros, and the fail-closed transaction (AC4, X5).
5. `InputsSnapshotResolver` and the `inputs_ref` with the freshness stamp of each input (AC1, AC6).
6. `DecisionLogQueryController` with the two operations, the declared area and right, the scope, the paging and the problem mapping; tests for AC6 and the refusals of AC8 (TC-E2-025-12).
7. `ChainVerifier` over 100 entries, with the count, the last `chain_seq` and the last `entry_hash` reported (AC4).
8. The contract-fake run of the whole slice: the document fake, the parameters and reference-data fakes, the decision-record fake and the outbox fake, green from Day 1 (AC1 to AC8).
9. The boundary test: no write to `rwb_document`, `rwb_case`, `rwb_litigation` or `rwb_treatment`, and no extracted value in any entry, outbox row or log line (AC7, BR7).

**Feature switch.** None of its own is named by a source. The capability is selected by the reference row that enables the stage 2 and 3 types in `rwb-document`, which is RWB-P5-E2025-APP's switch `rwb.dochub.extraction-stage23`; with that switch off no extraction decision of a new type arrives, and this story appends nothing for a type it never receives. This story adds no second switch (GAP-1285; ASM-2277).

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P5-E2025-CON stay green, and a SIT day shows one entry per document and per extracted field with its pattern or rule version, its parameter version, its confidence, its threshold reading and its final call; a chain of 100 entries verified with no break and no entry changed or deleted; one entry under a repeated fact; both reads answering by case and by document; and not one document, field, case, legal action, hearing, judgment or treatment changed by this story.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the decision code, the final call set, the threshold and its version, the pass mark, the pattern identifiers and the message ids are reference rows, parameter rows or facts of another service; nothing of them is a constant here.
- No personal data in the entry, the inputs reference, the event, the outbox, the tests or the logs: the case ID, the document reference and version, the document type code, the field name, the pattern and parameter versions, the confidence, the threshold reading, the final call and dates only; the extracted value, the party names and the amounts stay in `rwb_document`.
- No read of another service's tables (DP-01): the document arrives on its contract, the extraction decision on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the parameters and the reference lists in process; no `document`, `document_field`, `recovery_case`, `parameter_value`, `legal_action`, `hearing` or `treatment` row is copied into `rwb_decision`.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views: this story reads no ACE data at all.
- One recorder and no mover: this story changes no document, no field, no case, no legal action, no hearing, no judgment and no treatment, so a decision record can never move a case (BR10).
- No entry without its record, and no record without its entry: the append, its chain position and its outbox row commit in one transaction, and a failure leaves nothing and redelivers the fact (BR13, R-UNI-39).
- Append only and hash chained: no UPDATE and no DELETE on `decision_log_entry`, a correction is a new entry with `corrects_entry_id`, and the chain is verifiable from `chain_seq` 1 (BR15).
- One entry per decision: the inbox dedupe and the unique key on the idempotency key make a second entry impossible (BR14).
- One base, one topic, one queue: `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, `rwb.decision.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` with `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`; no story in this key declares another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13, DP-14).
- One hop and 2 s on every call, with a breaker per downstream; a missing document fact or a missing parameter version never produces an entry from a guessed type, threshold or code (DP-11).

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF)**, I want **the confirmed fields that rwb-document extracted from the stage 2 and 3 document types — contracts, credit approvals, mortgage documents, court filings, hearing notices and judgments — applied to the legal action and to its hearing in rwb-litigation, through the published checked-field contract RWB-P5-E2025-CON and without opening a document, a field row, a type row or a parameter table myself**, so that **the legal action carries the court name, the black and red case numbers, the claim and the judgment amounts and the filing, judgment and hearing dates from the paper the officer already holds, and a value that no person has checked and no rule has passed never reaches the case**.

This document is the S4 litigation slice of legacy RWB-E2-025. It owns no legacy criterion: the eleven criteria AC1 to AC11 of the story master are the document hub's and are owned by `RWB-P5-E2025-APP`, which keeps the classification, the extraction, the evaluation runner, the review queue and the write-once rule word for word; the shapes, the path, the state filter, the masking rule and the fakes of the reader are owned by the contract `RWB-P5-E2025-CON`. What this story owns is the S4 deliverable of the title: the application of the checked fields to its own rows, the withholding of a field in review, the version and parameter reads, the idempotent write, the refusals it passes through and the read model of the litigation screen. Its criteria are therefore new under D-RCV-60 and test only that deliverable.

The legacy story says what this slice is in its flow step 9: "S4 and S2 modules: read confirmed field values through DocumentFieldReader to fill the pack and the treatment record (from Epic 3 and Epic 5)". Its out-of-scope list says the complementary half just as plainly: "Writing extracted values into legal_action, hearing or treatment (S4 in Epic 5, S2 in Epic 3)". That write into `legal_action` and `hearing` is this story, and it is the only business write it makes.

Four facts shape the slice.

1. **The reader is a contract, not a table.** Legacy `DocumentFieldReader.checkedFields(UUID caseId, String documentType)` returned `List<CheckedField>` in process. In the target, rwb-document publishes that read as `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/checked-fields` with `CheckedFieldSet` and `CheckedField` (`documentId, docVersion, fieldName, value, state (OK, CONFIRMED, CORRECTED), confidence`), and this service consumes it one hop, with a 2 s timeout, a breaker and a GET retry once with jitter (DP-11; RWB-P5-E2025-CON).
2. **S4 holds no document.** rwb-litigation reads no `document`, `document_field`, `document_type` or `document_hub_parameter` row and no `v_ace_*` view: those tables are rwb-document's in `rwb_document` and the thirty `recovery.v_ace_*` views are read by rwb-source-data alone (DP-01, DP-05). The `rwb_litigation` login holds no grant on `rwb_document` and no `v_ace_*` grant, so the boundary is enforced by the database and not only by review.
3. **Only checked values move.** A field in state `REVIEW`, a field of a type that is not in the version in force and a value whose extraction confidence is below the pass mark are never promoted here. The column keeps the value it already holds, the fact set that needs the withheld field stays reported open with its review reason, and the officer is sent to the review queue of the hub.
4. **The values are data with a version.** The type codes, the field codes, the field threshold and the accuracy pass mark are read at their version: the type-table version arrives as `tableVersion` on the reader's answer, the threshold and the pass mark come from the parameters contract of rwb-case, and the type list from its reference-data contract (DP-06, DP-07). Nothing of them is a constant of this module.

##### 2. Business rationale

A judgment is a date and an amount, and a court filing is a court, a black case number, a filing date and a claim. Today the litigation officer reads them from paper and types them onto the legal action, and the litigation pack of `R-LIT-16` is assembled from the same paper by hand. The legacy key measured the cost: litigation takes 21 days to file, packs are incomplete and law firm progress is not tracked (FSD S4 A1.3, A2.4 and A2.16).

The document hub now extracts those values. Legacy RWB-E2-025 extended classification and extraction to five new types — `CONTRACT`, `CREDIT_APPROVAL`, `MORTGAGE_DOCUMENT`, `COURT_FILING`, `JUDGMENT` — and kept hearing notices under the Epic 1 type `COURT_NOTICE`, in the type table version `DOCTYPE-2026.12` valid from `2026-12-31`, with a field threshold of `0.80` and an accuracy pass mark of `0.90`. That half is `RWB-P5-E2025-APP` and is not restated here.

What the hub cannot do is write the litigation record. The legal action, its hearing, its court numbers and its judgment are rwb-litigation's: the service owns legal actions, hearings, judgments, enforcement and the LED auction ladder in schema `rwb_litigation`, on tables `legal_action` and `hearing` (TSD S4 T3.1; context pack S4). So a value leaves the hub once, on a published read, and lands on the row of the service that owns the fact. The moment rwb-litigation reads `document_field` for itself, two services own one extraction and the state filter of the reader can be bypassed by a query.

Three consequences follow, and each is designed rather than left to discipline.

- **The litigation rows fill themselves where the names meet.** Of the six types, three carry codes whose names are the names of S4 columns: `COURT_FILING` gives `court_name`, `black_case_no`, `filing_date` and `claim_amount`; `JUDGMENT` gives `court_name`, `red_case_no`, `judgment_date` and `judgment_amount`; `COURT_NOTICE` gives `court_name`, `black_case_no` and `hearing_date`. They fill `legal_action` DF-LEG-006 to DF-LEG-012 and `hearing` DF-LEG-026. Three types do not: `contract_no`, `party_names`, `contract_amount`, `contract_date`, `approval_no`, `approved_amount`, `approval_date`, `approval_level`, `title_doc_no`, `mortgage_amount`, `registration_date` and `land_office` name no litigation column, and `filing_date` meets `filed_date` only by word. Where the names do not meet, nothing is mapped, and the difference is counted and recorded (GAP-2835; ASM-4689).
- **A withheld value keeps its item open.** The reader returns no `REVIEW` field, so the legal action keeps its empty or previous column and the pack item that needs the value stays open with the review reason the hub reports — `LOW_CONFIDENCE` for a field below the threshold and `UNKNOWN_TYPE` for a document that arrived before the type version took effect. The officer is sent to the review queue of the hub, which is where a person may accept or correct the value; this service has no review screen and no override.
- **The write is a write of facts, not a case move.** Applying a judgment amount does not set a LOV-LEGAL-STATUS value and does not move the case: `R-LIT-44` records the judgment, `R-LIT-16` verifies the pack, and the litigation states of `R-LIT-01` to `R-LIT-79` are the stage stories' (FSD S4 A2.4, A2.16; TSD S4 T4). This story supplies the facts those rules read.

It serves REQ-DCM-006 on the litigation side and REQ-DCM-005 as the consumer of its outcome: the record that receives the value is the legal action, and the review path is the hub's. It puts CTL-08 in place on the reading side — a proposal below the pass mark takes effect only when it is loaded, so no value is promoted from a package that is not in force — and CTL-11 and CTL-12 by construction: a personal value is never stored and a write-once document is never touched, because no document is written at all. It carries R-UNI-38: a value is applied under the version in force on the date it is read. Wave 2 is the W-MAP wave of EP02, earlier than the service's Architecture v5 wave 3, and R5.6 keeps it.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P5-E2025-CON is published: the checked-fields read on base `/api/recovery/document/v1` as `GET /cases/{caseId}/checked-fields` with the `documentType` query, the `CheckedFieldSet` and `CheckedField` shapes, the state filter (OK, CONFIRMED and CORRECTED only), the masking rule, the error envelope with its message IDs and statuses, and the contract fake. This story builds against the contract and its fake on Day 1 and never against a document table.
- `legal_action` and `hearing` exist in `rwb_litigation` from the S4 baseline stories, with the columns of TSD S4 T3.1 — `legal_action` DF-LEG-001 to DF-LEG-014 and `hearing` DF-LEG-024 to DF-LEG-029 — the standard record columns of T3.0 and the lists of T3.2: LOV-LEGAL-TYPE (`NOTICE`, `CIVIL_CASE`, `APPEAL`, `ENFORCEMENT`, `BANKRUPTCY_PETITION`, `LED_AUCTION`), LOV-LEGAL-STATUS (`OPEN`, `FILED`, `JUDGMENT`, `ENFORCING`, `CLOSED`, `WITHDRAWN`), LOV-HEARING (`FIRST_HEARING`, `WITNESS`, `JUDGMENT_READING`, `MEDIATION`) and LOV-HEARING-OUTCOME (`HELD`, `ADJOURNED`, `SETTLED`, `JUDGMENT`). This story creates no table of its own and adds only the source-stamp columns of section 11.
- A legal action of the case exists, or the caller creates it in the same request (API-S4-002). A hearing is created or updated only from a `hearing_date` the reader returns, and the `hearing_type` of such a row is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2836; ASM-4695).
- The field threshold and the accuracy pass mark are read at their version through the parameters contract of rwb-case (DP-06, C `RWB-P3-E1042-CON`), and the type list LOV-DOC-TYPE with the eleven types through its reference-data contract (DP-07, C `RWB-P3-E1043-CON`).
- The platform outbox and inbox library (H `RWB-PLT-TE006-CON`), the workflow kit (H `RWB-PLT-E1071-CON`), the parameter and reference-data client libraries (H `RWB-PLT-E1042-CON`, H `RWB-PLT-E1043-CON`) and the gateway-bff composite route (H `RWB-PLT-N001-CON`) are named by the pattern table and stand in no build row of this story's plan; the story builds against their fakes until they publish (ASM-4692). The outbox library and the workflow kit are not used by this slice at all (ASM-4694).
- The service runs as login `rwb_litigation` on schema `rwb_litigation`, topic `rwb.litigation.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-litigation` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.litigation`; it holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant (DP-02, DP-01).
- The caller holds a Workbench role with the Litigation right of TSD S4 T6.1 — RW-LITOFF holds CRUA, RW-ENFORCE CRU, RW-LEGAL RA, RW-HEADLIT and RW-PRODHEAD RA — and the read is refused on the document side for a role without Documents R; this story adds no right of its own.
- The gateway-bff composite route serves SCR-19 Litigation workspace, which the FSD lists first in E5, later than this story's wave 2, so the read model is built and proved against the route fake (ASM-4693).
- The release date 31 December 2026 is the legacy one and is tentative, and the status is Draft (realignment v1) because no approval of the realigned story is recorded (ASM-4696).

##### 4. Flow

1. The litigation officer opens SCR-19 Litigation workspace for a case through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) and selects a legal action and the document type whose extracted facts the action needs — `COURT_FILING`, `JUDGMENT` or `COURT_NOTICE` for the mappings of this story.
2. `LitigationAndEnforcementController` accepts `POST /api/recovery/litigation/v1/cases/{caseId}/legal-actions` (API-S4-002) with an `Idempotency-Key`, or `PATCH /api/recovery/litigation/v1/legal-actions/{legalActionId}` (API-S4-004) when the action exists, and validates the case, the action type, the scope and the declared right before anything is read.
3. `CheckedFieldsClient` calls `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/checked-fields?documentType={type}`, one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker, GET retry once with jitter (DP-11).
4. `LegalActionFieldMapper` maps only a field code that names a column of `legal_action` or `hearing`, and counts every code that does not (section 11). It ignores `state` other than OK, CONFIRMED and CORRECTED — which the contract already filters — and rejects a field whose confidence is below the pass mark.
5. `LegalActionRepository` and `HearingRepository` write the mapped values, the source `document_id`, `doc_version` and `table_version` and the idempotency row in one transaction with the local decision record the service writes before any change; no column outside the mapped set changes.
6. `HearingRepository` creates one hearing row for a `hearing_date` of the action that has none for that date, or updates the `next_date` of the open hearing of the action to it; the `hearing_type` policy is the one of ASM-4695.
7. The officer sees the values on SCR-19 with the document and version each came from; the hub's SCR-30 and SCR-31 remain the only place a `REVIEW` field is checked or corrected, and the withheld fact set is shown open with its review reason.
8. The pack of `R-LIT-16` and the treatment record of `RWB-S2-E2025-APP` read the same facts from their owners — the pack from this service, the treatment row from rwb-treatment — and no caller is offered a second copy of the reader.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A field is in state REVIEW or below the pass mark | Not mapped; the column keeps its value; the fact set is reported open | MSG-P5-003 on the document in the hub | AC3 |
| X2 | The type is not in the version in force, or the item is in review with any reason | No checked field returned, so nothing is mapped and the item stays open | None | AC3 |
| X3 | A field code names no litigation column | Counted as unmapped, never stored, never logged with its value | None | AC7 |
| X4 | The reader refreshes inside the 2 s window and then refuses | 503 with MSG-GEN-006, nothing written, one GET retry with jitter | MSG-GEN-006 | AC6 |
| X5 | The caller lacks Documents R on the document side | 403 from the reader, passed through unchanged, nothing written | MSG-P4-002 | AC6 |
| X6 | The document is outside the caller's scope | 404 from the reader, passed through unchanged, nothing written | MSG-P4-003 | AC6 |
| X7 | The same document version and type-table version is applied twice | The second apply is the first result and no column changes | None | AC5 |
| X8 | A role without Litigation right calls the action endpoint | 403 from this service before any read | MSG-P4-002 | Access test |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Consumes one published contract and its fake; adds no table, no event, no Schedule and no workflow of its own |
| Negotiable | Type codes, field codes, threshold, pass mark and the mapping table are data and contract, not code |
| Valuable | The court numbers, amounts and dates reach the legal action without retyping, and only after a person or a rule has passed them |
| Estimable | One client, one mapper, two repositories, one idempotency key and eight criteria |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its contract, component and end-to-end tests |
| Testable | Every criterion runs against the P5 contract fake and the two rwb-case fakes with the legacy fixture values |

The eight criteria are new under D-RCV-60 and test only the S4 deliverable of this story. The eleven legacy criteria AC1 to AC11 of RWB-E2-025 — the court notice, the contract, the low confidence, the pass-mark proposal, the classification, the document before the version, the Buddhist Era date, the pattern mismatch, the reader filter, the write-once file and the scope refusal — belong to `RWB-P5-E2025-APP`, are written there word for word with their origin tags, and are not restated here. The shapes, the path, the state filter and the fakes this story consumes are `RWB-P5-E2025-CON`'s. The cross-service journey of the same values across rwb-document, rwb-litigation and rwb-case is the wave 2 integration harness's, and no criterion of this story claims it.

Two readings of the sources are stated here rather than hidden in the code. The columns that carry a fact, the source-stamp columns and the mapping rule are this story's design and are named by no source (GAP-2835; ASM-4689). The creation of a `hearing` row from an extracted `hearing_date` and the `hearing_type` it carries are named by no source either (GAP-2836; ASM-4695). The values of the examples are the legacy ones — case "RW-2026-000601", documents "DOC-0602", "DOC-0603" and "DOC-0605", the confidence 0.7100, the threshold 0.80, the pass mark 0.90, the amounts 2400000.00 — and the dates 2026-11-01 and 2027-03-05 are synthetic test data of the same fixture, not business values of any source.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The stage 2 and 3 types and their fields are those of the document type table version in force on the read date; the version is the one the reader reports and this service reads no type table of its own | Legacy RWB-E2-025 BR1; R-UNI-38; TSD S4 T3.1 (ASM-4689) |
| BR2 | A field in state REVIEW in the hub is never applied here; the column keeps its value and the fact set that needs it stays reported open with its review reason | Legacy BR2; RWB-P5-E2025-CON state filter; MSG-P5-003 |
| BR3 | A value below the accuracy pass mark is never promoted whatever state an upstream answer carries, and a review-only proposal takes effect only when its version is loaded | Legacy BR3 and AC4; CTL-08; DL11 |
| BR4 | Only a field code that names a column of `legal_action` or `hearing` is mapped; a code that names none is counted and recorded, and no amount or date is translated from one name into another | Legacy BR4; modified for the service boundary (GAP-2835; ASM-4689) |
| BR5 | The write is a write of facts: it sets no LOV-LEGAL-STATUS value, moves no case status and satisfies no litigation rule by itself | FSD S4 A2.4, A2.16; TSD S4 T4 (`R-LIT-16`, `R-LIT-44`) |
| BR6 | The apply is idempotent on the legal action, the document ID, the doc_version and the type-table version, in one transaction with the source stamps | Legacy section 12 idempotency; TSD S4 T3.0 |
| BR7 | No personal value is written, logged or put on a payload: `party_names` is never mapped, and masking is the hub's rule applied on its own answer | Legacy BR7; DF-DOC-015; CTL-11; DL26 (ASM-4691) |
| BR8 | No table of another service and no ACE table or view is read: the case, the parameters, the lists, the document fields and the decision log are reached only through their owners' contracts | DP-01, DP-05, DP-06, DP-07 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status and sets no LOV-LEGAL-STATUS value: `legal_action.status` stays where the legal-action stories put it, and the litigation transitions `R-LIT-01` to `R-LIT-79` remain the stage stories'. What this story writes is the fact columns of `legal_action` and, for a `hearing_date`, a `hearing` row that is active; `hearing.outcome` and `legal_action.lit_status` are untouched.

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Reads and applies the checked fields of a legal action in scope (Litigation CRUA) |
| RW-ENFORCE, enforcement owner | Reads the applied facts of an action after judgment (Litigation CRU) |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel and RW-HEADLIT, head of litigation | Read and approve on the action (Litigation RA) |
| RW-NPAMGR, NPA and asset manager | Reads the applied facts (Litigation R) |
| RW-CONDUCT, conduct and QA officer | Reads the applied facts and the unmapped count (Litigation R) |

**Mapping and non-mapping.** `COURT_FILING` → `court_name`, `black_case_no`, `filed_date`, `claim_amount`; `JUDGMENT` → `court_name`, `red_case_no`, `judgment_date`, `judgment_amount`; `COURT_NOTICE` → `court_name`, `black_case_no`, `hearing.hearing_date`. Not mapped, counted as the difference: `contract_no`, `party_names`, `contract_amount`, `contract_date`, `approval_no`, `approved_amount`, `approval_date`, `approval_level`, `title_doc_no`, `mortgage_amount`, `registration_date`, `land_office`. No parameter table, no type row and no field row is read: the type list and the two parameter values arrive through the rwb-case contracts (DP-06, DP-07), and `legal_action` and `hearing` are the only tables of `rwb_litigation` this story writes beyond the idempotency row.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

DP-09 and DP-10 are carried as prohibitions: the slice publishes no event and registers no Schedule, and the library and kit stand in no build row (ASM-4692, ASM-4694). DP-11 is the whole point of the story: the legacy in-process `DocumentFieldReader` becomes one hop with a published shape, a fake and a 2 s timeout, so this slice builds on Day 1 against RWB-P5-E2025-CON.

**Build steps**

1. Build `CheckedFieldsClient` against the P5 fake and the drift test of 12.8; no statement may name `rwb_document`.
2. Build `LegalActionFieldMapper` with the mapping table as one data row set and a unit test per mapped code and per unmapped code.
3. Add the source-stamp and idempotency columns on the service's own Flyway sequence, owned by the S4 baseline stories, with the apply key of BR6.
4. Write the apply in one transaction with the local decision record and the repeat count; prove AC3 and AC5.
5. Prove AC4 with the parameters and reference-data fakes and a build check that fails on a code, a threshold, a pass mark or a version in the source.
6. Prove AC6 with the 404, 403 and timeout fakes, and AC8 with the composite route fake.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.litigation.extract-stage23`. Off: the apply offers no type, nothing is read from rwb-document and no column is written.

**Done when** the tests in section 16 pass and the applied-fact report of the 60-document sample runs against the P5 fake with the unmapped count attached.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: type codes, field codes, the table version, the threshold, the pass mark and the two lists are rows read at their version; a build check fails on a type code, a field code, an amount, a date, a threshold, a pass mark or a valid-from date in the Java source or the module configuration.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow inputs, events or `rwb_litigation`: `party_names` is never mapped, stored, logged or put on a message, and a property test places a synthetic party name in the reader's answer and asserts that it appears in no row, no log line and no span attribute (ASM-4691).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: no component reads an ACE table or a `recovery.v_ace_*` view, and the `rwb_litigation` login holds no `v_ace_*` grant (DP-01, DP-05).
- No read of another service's tables and no cross-schema join: `document`, `document_field`, `document_type` and `document_hub_parameter` (P5), `recovery_case`, `parameter_catalog`, `reference_row` and `lov_value` (P3) and `decision_log_entry` (P7) are reached only through their owners' contracts, and the boundary test fails the build on any statement outside `rwb_litigation`.
- Only checked values move: a `REVIEW` field, a value below the pass mark, a type not in force and an item with reason `UNKNOWN_TYPE` are withheld, and no code path promotes them.
- One hop and a 2 s budget on every consumed read, with a breaker and no call chain; a repeat is the same apply key and never a silent second write.
- No event, no topic producer, no outbox row and no Schedule in this slice (DP-09 and DP-10 as prohibitions), and no case status and no LOV-LEGAL-STATUS value is written.
- The screens are read only for the hub's fields: SCR-19 shows what this service wrote, and no screen writes a checked field.

##### 1. Story

As a **restructuring officer (RW-RESTRUCT)**, I want **the confirmed fields that rwb-document extracted from the stage 2 and 3 document types — the contract, the credit approval and the mortgage document — applied by `TreatmentWorkflow` to the treatment record of the case in rwb-treatment, through the published checked-field contract RWB-P5-E2025-CON and without opening a document, a field row, a type row or a parameter table myself**, so that **the treatment record carries the contract amount, the contract date and the mortgage registration facts from the paper the officer already holds, so that the value a case is worked on is not retyped and never one that no person has checked and no rule has passed**.

This document is the S2 treatment slice of legacy RWB-E2-025. It owns no legacy criterion: the eleven criteria AC1 to AC11 of the story master are the document hub's and are owned by `RWB-P5-E2025-APP`, which keeps the classification, the extraction, the evaluation runner, the review queue and the write-once rule word for word, and the shapes, the path, the state filter, the masking rule and the fakes of the reader are owned by the contract `RWB-P5-E2025-CON`. The cross-service journey of the same values across rwb-document, rwb-treatment and rwb-case is the integration harness's. What this story owns is the S2 deliverable of the title: the application of the checked fields to its own row, the withholding of a field in review, the type and parameter reads at their version, the idempotent write, the refusal it passes through, the masking it never breaks and the read model of the two treatment screens. Its criteria are therefore new under D-RCV-60 and test only that deliverable.

The legacy story says what this slice is in its flow step 9: "S4 and S2 modules: read confirmed field values through DocumentFieldReader to fill the pack and the treatment record (from Epic 3 and Epic 5)". Its out-of-scope list says the complementary half just as plainly: "Writing extracted values into legal_action, hearing or treatment (S4 in Epic 5, S2 in Epic 3)". That write is this story, and it is the only business write it makes.

Four facts shape the slice.

1. **The reader is a contract, not a table.** Legacy `DocumentFieldReader.checkedFields(UUID caseId, String documentType)` returned `List<CheckedField>` in process, inside one module. In the target, rwb-document publishes that read on its own service base and this service consumes it, one hop, with a 2 s timeout and a breaker (DP-11; ADR-020). The `CheckedField` shape is `documentId, docVersion, fieldName, value, state (OK, CONFIRMED, CORRECTED), confidence`, and the read returns only fields in those three states. The operation, its path under `/api/recovery/document/v1` and its field-level element names are the baseline's and are recorded as named by no source (GAP-2702; ASM-4478).
2. **S2 holds no document.** rwb-treatment reads no `document`, `document_field`, `document_type` or `document_hub_parameter` row and no `v_ace_*` view: those tables are rwb-document's in `rwb_document` and the thirty `recovery.v_ace_*` views are read by rwb-source-data alone (DP-01, DP-05; Architecture v5 slide 8). The `rwb_treatment` login holds no grant on `rwb_document` and no `v_ace_*` grant (Architecture v5 slide 8), so the boundary is enforced by the database and not only by review.
3. **Only checked values move.** A field in state `REVIEW`, a field of a type that is not in the version in force and a value whose extraction confidence is below the pass mark are never promoted here. The treatment row keeps the value it already holds, the fact set it needs stays reported open with its review reason, and the officer is sent to the review queue of the hub.
4. **The values are data with a version.** The type and field codes, the field threshold and the accuracy pass mark are rows read at their version: the type version arrives as `tableVersion` on the reader's answer, the threshold and the pass mark come from the parameters contract of rwb-case, and the type list from its reference-data contract (DP-06, DP-07). Nothing of them is a constant of this module.

Two patterns in the metadata list apply here as prohibitions and are stated as such in section 13. DP-09 is the outbox and inbox library, and this story publishes and consumes no event: the extraction event of the hub is rwb-document's and this story carries no integration dependency on it, while the one event of this service, `TreatmentApproved`, belongs to the approval story (TSD S2 T5.3; EV-10 in the context pack). DP-10 is a Temporal Schedule or an event-started workflow, and this story registers no Schedule: the document intake job JOB-12 (legacy RWB-E2-025 section 4) and the monthly retention run JOB-17 are rwb-document's. Both rows are in the pattern list and neither has an application in this slice; no event and no Schedule is invented to fill them.

It does not own: the classification, the extraction, the review queue, the document type table and its version, the extractor versions and every `rwb_document` row, which are `RWB-P5-E2025-APP`'s and `RWB-P5-E2025-CON`'s; the treatment create, offer, approval, plan and affordability stories, which are `RWB-S2-E3001-APP` to `RWB-S2-E3005-APP`; the case status and the `CaseWorkflow` parent, which are rwb-case's (P3); the RESTRUCTURE, SETTLEMENT and DEEDINLIEU packages and their rows, which are rwb-decision's (P7); the roles, rights and scope data, which are rwb-access's (P4); the gateway-bff composite route and the screen field list, which are the platform edge story's and the screen owners'.

##### 2. Business rationale

A treatment record is the row the whole restructure, settlement and deed-in-lieu stage is worked on: the offer is built against it, the approval level is looked up from it and the plan is booked from it. Today the officer types its baseline facts from paper — the contract amount and the day it was signed, and the mortgage document that secures it — and two people reading the same contract produce two different amounts. The legacy story measured the gap on the document side and on the treatment side at once: the litigation pack and the treatment record need the contract amount and the mortgage registration, and officers read them from paper and type them in (legacy RWB-E2-025 section 2).

The document hub now extracts those values. Legacy RWB-E2-025 extended classification and extraction to five new types — `CONTRACT`, `CREDIT_APPROVAL`, `MORTGAGE_DOCUMENT`, `COURT_FILING` and `JUDGMENT` — with `contract_no`, `party_names`, `contract_amount`, `contract_date`, `approval_no`, `approved_amount`, `approval_date`, `approval_level`, `title_doc_no`, `mortgage_amount`, `registration_date` and `land_office` among the fields of the three types this slice consumes, in the type table version `DOCTYPE-2026.12` valid from `2026-12-31`, with a field threshold of `0.80` and an accuracy pass mark of `0.90`. That half is `RWB-P5-E2025-APP`, and this story does not repeat it, restate it or test it.

What the hub cannot do is write the treatment. The treatment, its contract amounts and its mortgage facts are rwb-treatment's: the service owns treatments, contracts, settlement and deed-in-lieu agreements and plan timers, in schema `rwb_treatment` (Architecture v5 slide 4 places TDR, settlement and DIL with S2; `treatment` is the one table of the service in the context pack and the Ownership Map). So the value leaves the hub once, on a published read, and lands on the row of the service that owns the fact. That is the whole of this slice, and it is why the story is a consumer and never a reader: the moment rwb-treatment reads `document_field` for itself, two services own one extraction and the state filter of the reader can be bypassed by a query.

Three consequences follow, and each is designed rather than left to discipline.

- **The stage, not the screen, applies the facts.** The legacy reader was called by the module that needed the values. In the target the caller is `applyDocumentFacts`, an activity of `TreatmentWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-treatment`, started by the case signal the parent `CaseWorkflow` forwards (Architecture v5 slide 13, row P3 Case with T and E into S2 Treatment; Temporal and Drools Design slides 9 and 11). The activity runs inside the stage, so a replay reuses the recorded result and a retry repeats nothing that completed.
- **A withheld value keeps the row as it is.** The reader returns no `REVIEW` field, and this service additionally drops any entry the reader returns in another state and any value below the pass mark. The treatment row therefore keeps the amount it already holds, the fact set is reported open with the review reason the hub gives — `LOW_CONFIDENCE` for a field below the threshold and `UNKNOWN_TYPE` for a document that arrived before the type version took effect — and the officer is sent to the review queue of the hub, which is where a person may accept or correct the value. This service has no review screen and no override of its own, and it never clears a column because one read came back short.
- **The write is a write of facts, not a case move.** Applying a contract amount does not move the case to `PROPOSED_IN_COLLINS` and does not open, send or approve an offer: R-RES-01, R-RES-10 and the offer and approval rows are the stage stories' of this epic, and the case status is moved by the parent `CaseWorkflow` alone (FSD S2 A2.1.3.1; TSD S2 T4). This story supplies the facts those rows read.

It serves REQ-DCM-006 ("fields are extracted into the index for the agreed document types, in Thai and in English") on the treatment side and REQ-DCM-005 ("classified with a confidence; below the threshold to the review queue") as the consumer of its outcome: the record that receives the value is the treatment, and the review path is the hub's. It puts control CTL-08 in place on the reading side — a proposal below the pass mark takes effect only when it is loaded, so no value is promoted here from a package that is not in force — and CTL-11 and CTL-12 by construction: a personal value is never stored and a write-once document is never touched, because no document is written at all. It carries R-UNI-38: a value is applied under the version in force on the date it is read.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P5-E2025-CON is published: the checked-fields read on base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, the `CheckedField` and `CheckedFieldSet` shapes, the state filter (OK, CONFIRMED and CORRECTED only), the masking rule, the error envelope with its message IDs and statuses, and the contract fake. The operation, its path and its field-level names are the baseline's own and are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2702; ASM-4478); this story builds against the contract and its fake on Day 1 and never against a document table.
- `treatment` exists in `rwb_treatment` from `RWB-S2-E3001-APP`, with the columns of TSD S2 T3.1 — DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033 — the standard record columns of T3.0 and the lists of T3.2 (LOV-TREATMENT, LOV-PROPOSER, LOV-TRT-OUTCOME, LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL, LOV-CREDIT-RESULT, LOV-TRT-SIGNATURE). This story adds the fact columns of section 11 to that table on the service's own Flyway sequence and creates no other table.
- A treatment row of the case exists, or the stage has just opened it through `RWB-S2-E3001-APP`; the apply writes the row of the case and never opens a second treatment for the same case and stage.
- The field threshold and the accuracy pass mark are read at their version through the parameters contract of rwb-case (DP-06, C `RWB-P3-E1042-CON`); the parameter codes are the hub's own (`EXTRACT_ACCURACY_PASS` and the field threshold of the extraction contract) and the operation names this story reads are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2702; ASM-4478).
- The type list LOV-DOC-TYPE with the eleven types is read at its version through the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-07, C `RWB-P3-E1043-CON`); the type codes themselves arrive on the reader's answer and the list is used only to name the three types this slice consumes.
- The platform parameter and reference-data libraries (H `RWB-PLT-E1042-CON`, H `RWB-PLT-E1043-CON`), the outbox and inbox library (H `RWB-PLT-TE006-CON`), the workflow kit (H `RWB-PLT-E1071-CON`) and the gateway-bff composite route (H `RWB-PLT-N001-CON`) are named by the pattern table and stand in no build row of this story's plan; the service template carries them and the story builds against their fakes until they publish (ASM-4481). The outbox producer and the workflow kit's Schedule are not used at all by this slice (ASM-4482).
- The service runs as login `rwb_treatment` on schema `rwb_treatment`, topic `rwb.treatment.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.treatment`; it holds no grant on another `rwb_*` schema and no `v_ace_*` grant (Architecture v5 slide 8, one login and connection pool per service; DP-02).
- The caller holds a Workbench role with the Treatment and offer right of TSD S2 T6.1 — RW-RESTRUCT holds CRUA and RW-CASEOWN, RW-SPECIAL and RW-GUARANT hold CRU — and the reader is called with a role that carries Documents R on the document side; the refusal and the masking of the read are the P5 contract's and this story adds no right of its own (AC6, AC7).
- The gateway-bff composite route serves SCR-14 Treatment record and SCR-15 Settlement offer, both listed with the treatment stage of this epic; the read model is built and proved against the route fake until the route publishes (ASM-3076).
- The release date 31 December 2026 is the legacy one and is tentative, and the story stands Draft (realignment v1) until the realignment is approved; no approval is a precondition of the build.

##### 4. Flow

1. The case reaches the treatment stage: the route decision of rwb-valuation ends with the case in `ROUTE_APPROVED_RESTRUCTURE`, `ROUTE_APPROVED_SETTLEMENT` or `ROUTE_APPROVED_DIL`, the case router of rwb-case signals `CaseWorkflow`, and the parent starts `TreatmentWorkflow` as a child on task queue `rwb-treatment` (Architecture v5 slides 3 and 13; Temporal and Drools Design slide 9).
2. The stage opens or reads the treatment row of the case through `RWB-S2-E3001-APP`'s `openTreatment` activity, and the case signal it holds names the case and the business date.
3. `TreatmentWorkflow` calls `applyDocumentFacts` for the types of this slice — `CONTRACT`, `CREDIT_APPROVAL` and `MORTGAGE_DOCUMENT` — with the case ID, the treatment ID and the identity of the caller the stage is working for.
4. `CheckedFieldClient` calls the checked-fields read of `RWB-P5-E2025-CON` once per type, one hop, with a 2 s timeout and a breaker, with no retry chain and no second downstream call; the operation name and path are the contract's (GAP-2702; ASM-4478).
5. `CheckedFieldFilter` keeps only the entries in state `OK`, `CONFIRMED` or `CORRECTED` and drops every other entry and every value below the accuracy pass mark, so a value in `REVIEW` cannot be applied even if a future contract version returned it.
6. `Stage23TreatmentMapper` maps each kept field code onto the treatment column of the same name in this service's own set: `contract_amount`, `contract_date`, `mortgage_amount`, `registration_date`, `land_office` and `title_doc_no`. A code with no column of the same name is not mapped and the difference is recorded (GAP-2702; ASM-4478).
7. `Stage23VersionGuard` checks the `tableVersion` the reader reports against the version the reference-data contract reports in force, and checks that the threshold and the pass mark it applies are the ones the parameters contract answers at their version (DP-06, DP-07).
8. `TreatmentFactWriter` writes, in one `rwb_treatment` transaction, the mapped columns of the `treatment` row, the source identifier of each contributing entry — `documentId`, `docVersion` and the type-table version — and the idempotency row of the request. The outbox row set is empty and no other service's row is touched (DP-01, DP-09).
9. `Stage23Idempotency` builds the write key from the document ID, the `doc_version` and the type-table version of each contributing entry, recognises a repeat of the same key and answers from the first result; a repeated read writes nothing at all (AC5).
10. The activity returns to the workflow the facts it applied, the version they were applied under, the entries it withheld with their review reasons and the outcome of each read; the workflow records the result in its history and waits on the next signal.
11. The officer reads the treatment through `GET /api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}` (API-S2-002): the fact columns, the document version each fact came from and the open items are answered from `rwb_treatment`, and the checked fields themselves are shown on the hub's own surfaces, read only.
12. SCR-14 Treatment record and SCR-15 Settlement offer read the treatment through the gateway-bff composite route, which composes the case read of rwb-case with the treatment read of this service, one hop each, read only (DP-19).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A field of the requested type is in state `REVIEW` in the hub | The field is not applied and the column keeps the value it holds; the fact set is reported open with its review reason and the officer is sent to the review queue of the hub | MSG-P5-003 | AC2 |
| X2 | A value arrives with an extraction confidence below the pass mark | The value is not promoted by this service, whatever state the entry carries, and the fact set is reported open | MSG-P5-003 | AC2 |
| X3 | The document arrived before the type version took effect, or the classifier could not place it, so the item carries `UNKNOWN_TYPE` | No field is applied, the treatment row is unchanged, and the item stays in review with its reason | MSG-P5-003 | AC3 |
| X4 | The checked-fields read does not answer inside 2 s, or its breaker is open | Nothing is written; the activity fails with 503 and the platform envelope, and it is retried on the platform policy of 1 s initial interval, back-off 2 and 10 attempts | MSG-GEN-006 | AC6 |
| X5 | The caller's role carries no Documents R on the document read | The reader refuses before returning a value; this service writes nothing and adds no right of its own | MSG-P4-002 | AC6, AC7 |
| X6 | The document or the case lies outside the caller's scope | The reader answers 404 and this service writes nothing; the caller cannot tell an out-of-scope document from a missing one | MSG-P4-003 | AC6 |
| X7 | The same read is repeated for the same document ID, `doc_version` and type-table version | No column changes; the repeat is answered from the first result and counted | None | AC5 |
| X8 | A field code has no treatment column of the same name — `contract_no`, `party_names`, `approval_no`, `approved_amount`, `approval_date`, `approval_level` | Nothing is written for that code; the value stays in the hub and the difference is recorded with its assumption (GAP-2702; ASM-4478) | None | AC1 |
| X9 | The treatment named by the stage does not exist, does not belong to the case, or is not in a state that accepts facts | The activity fails with 404 or 409 and nothing is read further; no partial fact set is written | None | AC5 |
| X10 | A component, a statement or a test reaches a `rwb_document` table, a `document_type` row, a `document_hub_parameter` row or a `v_ace_*` view | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build; nothing is released | None (pipeline log) | Section 8, BR9 |

X1 to X3 are the withholding paths the reader's state filter implies; X4 to X6 are the three refusals of the published read; X7 is the idempotency of the apply; X8 is the mapping difference between the extracted codes and the treatment columns; X9 is the row the stage names; X10 is the schema boundary. A refusal under X4, X5 or X6 writes nothing at all, because the filter, the guard and the mapping run before the transaction opens, and the activity is retried only under the platform policy of ADR-020 and not with a retry chain of its own.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against `RWB-P5-E2025-CON` and its fake; the parameter, reference-data, outbox and composite-route contracts are fakes until their stories publish (ASM-4481) |
| Negotiable | The type and field codes, the threshold, the pass mark and the table version are rows read at their version; the story fixes the behaviour, not the values, and the mapping is limited to names the sources share |
| Valuable | The officer stops retyping the contract amount, the contract date and the mortgage registration from paper, and a value no person checked never reaches the treatment |
| Estimable | One activity, one client, one filter, one mapper, one version guard, one writer, one idempotency guard and one read model |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests, as a secondary slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Each of the eight criteria of section 7 is one automated test; every cross-service answer is stubbed in the contract fakes |

The eight criteria are new under D-RCV-60 and test only the S2 deliverable of this story: the application of confirmed checked fields to the treatment row, the withholding of a field in review and the value the row keeps, the version and parameter reads, the idempotent write, the refusal it passes through with the retry the platform policy gives, the masking it never breaks and the read model of the two treatment screens. The eleven legacy criteria AC1 to AC11 of RWB-E2-025 — the court notice, the contract, the low confidence, the pass-mark proposal, the classification, the document before the version, the Buddhist Era date, the pattern mismatch, the reader filter, the write-once file and the scope refusal — belong to `RWB-P5-E2025-APP`, are written there word for word with their origin tags, and are not restated here. The shapes, the path, the state filter and the fakes this story consumes are `RWB-P5-E2025-CON`'s. The cross-service journey of the same values across rwb-document, rwb-treatment and rwb-case is the wave 2 integration harness's, and no criterion of this story claims it.

Three readings of the sources are stated here rather than hidden in the code. The reader's transport, operation name and field-level names are Not specified in the source documents and come from `RWB-P5-E2025-CON`; the column of `treatment` that carries a fact and the column that carries the type-table version are this story's design and are named by no source (GAP-2702; ASM-4478). The masking rule the treatment read applies is the hub's for the value it returns, and which role may see an unmasked party name on the treatment side is named by no source for this service (GAP-2702; ASM-4478). The `registration_date "2026-11-01"` of AC1 is the contract date of the same fixture used as synthetic test data, and it is not a business value of any source. The one-hop REST read of the legacy in-process interface is the pattern table's (DP-11) and the architecture's REST rule, while the connection matrix of Architecture v5 slide 13 puts the S2 call to P5 in the Temporal column; the story follows the pattern table and the work package, and the disagreement is carried as GAP-2703 with ASM-4483.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The stage 2 and 3 types and their fields are those of the document type table version in force on the extraction date; the version is the one the reader reports and this service reads no type table of its own | Legacy RWB-E2-025 BR1; R-UNI-38; TSD S2 T3.1 (GAP-2702; ASM-4478) |
| BR2 | A field below the threshold, failing its pattern or marked review-only has state REVIEW in the hub and is never applied here; the fact set that needs it stays reported open with its review reason | Legacy RWB-E2-025 BR2; RWB-P5-E2025-CON state filter; MSG-P5-003 |
| BR3 | A value whose extraction confidence is below the accuracy pass mark is never promoted by this service, whatever state an upstream answer carries; the proposal of a review-only field takes effect only when its version is loaded | Legacy RWB-E2-025 BR3 and AC4; CTL-08; DL11 |
| BR4 | Each field may carry a pattern in the hub's field definitions; the pattern is data, and this service repeats none of it and validates no extracted value against a pattern of its own | Legacy RWB-E2-025 BR4; RWB-P5-E2025-CON |
| BR5 | Only fields in state OK, CONFIRMED or CORRECTED are used; a field in any other state is withheld and never written on `treatment` | Legacy RWB-E2-025 BR5; RWB-P5-E2025-CON |
| BR6 | Extraction never changes the stored file of a write-once document. This is the hub's rule; here it is a boundary, because this story writes no document and no file at all | Legacy RWB-E2-025 BR6; CTL-12; DP-01 |
| BR7 | Party names and other personal field values are masked unless the role may see them; a personal value is never stored on `treatment`, never logged and never put on an event | Legacy RWB-E2-025 BR7; DF-DOC-015; CTL-11; DL26 (GAP-2702; ASM-4480) |
| BR8 | Dates read in Buddhist Era are stored as ISO dates; the value applied to a date column is the ISO value the reader returns, and no era conversion is repeated here | Legacy RWB-E2-025 BR8; TSD S2 T3.1 |
| BR9 | This service reads no `document`, `document_field`, `document_type` or `document_hub_parameter` row and no `v_ace_*` view; the checked values arrive only on the published read of RWB-P5-E2025-CON, and the `rwb_treatment` login holds no grant that would allow otherwise | DP-01; Architecture v5 slide 8; the ownership rows of the S2 context pack and the Ownership Map (the four tables are P5's) |
| BR10 | The write is a write of facts: it moves no case status, opens no offer, approves nothing and writes no decision record, because no rule is evaluated by this slice | FSD S2 A2.1.3.1; TSD S2 T4; legacy RWB-E2-025 section 9 |
| BR11 | A repeated read of the same document ID, `doc_version` and type-table version writes once, and a repeated read never clears a column the row already holds | R-UNI-40; legacy RWB-E2-025 section 12 (idempotency); AC5 |
| BR12 | No value a business person may change is written in code: the types, the fields, the patterns, the threshold, the pass mark and the lists are rows read at their version | BR-S2-001; FSD S2 A2.1.3.1; legacy RWB-E2-025 BR4 |
| R-UNI-38 | A new rule version applies to decisions taken from its effective date, and an open case keeps the version it was decided under. Here the version in force is the table version the reader reports and the parameter values the contracts answer | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-UNI-38) |
| CTL-08 | A proposed change takes effect only when it is loaded. This story therefore promotes no threshold, no pass mark and no review-only proposal that is not in force at its version | Legacy RWB-E2-025 BR3; CTL-08; DL11 |
| CTL-11 | Personal data is masked for a role that may not see it and is not copied outside the system that owns it; a party name is never written to `rwb_treatment` | Legacy RWB-E2-025 BR7; CTL-11; DL26 |
| CTL-12 | A write-once document is never altered. It holds here by construction: this story touches no document and no file | Legacy RWB-E2-025 BR6; CTL-12 |

The rules hold in `rwb_treatment` as follows. BR1, BR3 and BR5 are executed by `CheckedFieldFilter` and `Stage23VersionGuard` before anything is written: the filter drops every entry that is not OK, CONFIRMED or CORRECTED and every value below the pass mark, and the guard compares the reported table version with the version the reference-data contract reports in force. BR2 and BR3 are visible to the officer as an open fact set with its review reason and as MSG-P5-003 on the document, not as a value on the treatment. BR4, BR6 and BR8 are prohibitions over this module: no pattern, no file and no era conversion exists in it, and a build check fails on a date literal, an amount literal, a threshold or a pass mark in the source. BR7 is asserted by a property test that places a synthetic party name in the reader's answer and proves it appears in no row, no log line and no span attribute. BR9 is the schema grant and the boundary test. BR10 is a build check on the module: no call to a case-state operation, no offer operation and no approval envelope. BR11 is the write key of `Stage23Idempotency` and the rule that a withholding read never nulls a column. BR12 is the reference-data and parameter reads.

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status and does not move the lifecycle state of the treatment, which belongs to the stage stories.

Two things are written, and both are records rather than state machines:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| A `treatment` row with no fact column set | The `applyDocumentFacts` activity | The case, the types and the caller are valid and the reader answers with kept entries | The same row with the fact columns, the source identifiers and the stamped type-table version |
| A `treatment` row with fact columns set | The `applyDocumentFacts` activity | A kept entry of a later `doc_version` arrives | The same row with the new value and the new source identifiers |
| A `treatment` row with fact columns set | The `applyDocumentFacts` activity | Every entry of the type is in `REVIEW`, below the pass mark, or the read reports `UNKNOWN_TYPE` | Unchanged, and every fact set is reported open with its reason |
| A `treatment` row and a document set already applied | The `applyDocumentFacts` activity | The same document ID, `doc_version` and type-table version | Unchanged; the first result is answered and the repeat is counted |

The field-state values are the hub's and not this story's: `OK`, `CONFIRMED` and `CORRECTED` are applied, `REVIEW` is withheld, and the move out of `REVIEW` happens in the review queue of the hub's own story. The case states of the stage — `PROPOSED_IN_COLLINS`, `IN_FCR_QUEUE`, `WITH_FCR_OFFICER`, `OFFER_WITH_CUSTOMER`, `AWAITING_CREDIT_APPROVAL`, `WITH_OPS_BOOKING`, `BOOKED_IN_ALS_NLEADS`, `PLAN_RUNNING` and their settlement and deed-in-lieu siblings (TSD S2 T4) — are moved by the parent `CaseWorkflow` and by the stage stories of this epic, and no state of them is written here.

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| RW-RESTRUCT, restructuring officer (FCR) | Treatment and offer CRUA in the TSD S2 T6.1 matrix: works the stage, applies the checked fields of the three types on the case in scope, reads the facts and the open items |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Treatment and offer CRU: applies and reads the same facts on the cases in scope |
| RW-SPECIAL, hardship and vulnerability specialist; RW-GUARANT, guarantee officer | Treatment and offer CRU: applies and reads the same facts in scope |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | R: reads the facts and the open items of the team's cases |
| RW-CREDCOMM, credit approval committee member; RW-PRODHEAD, product head | RA: reads the credit-approval facts the stage compares its offer against; no approval is taken here |
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer; RW-LEGAL, legal counsel | R: reads the contract and mortgage facts of a case they are working; the litigation fill is the S4 slice's |
| The other reading roles of TSD S2 T6.1 — RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-CONDUCT, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-BIANAL, RW-TRIBE (R) | Read the applied facts of a case and the version they were applied under |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-AGENT (R) | Read as service identities through the same checks; a service identity carries no Documents R unless the hub's contract grants it |
| rwb-treatment service identity (login `rwb_treatment`, DP-02) | Calls the checked-fields read with the caller's own identity, filters, maps, guards the version, writes `treatment` in `rwb_treatment`, and holds no grant on `rwb_document` or on a `v_ace_*` view |
| rwb-document (P5) service identity | Owns the documents, the fields, the type table and the review queue; serves the checked fields and the masking decision and is never written by this story |
| rwb-case (P3) service identity | Owns the parameters and the reference rows this story reads at their version; called as a contract and never read as a table |

The rights above are the rows of TSD S2 T6.1 and nothing wider. Four roles named by the legacy authority table are not exercised here because their rights are on the document side and not on the treatment record: SY-OCR, the extraction pipeline, holds Documents CRU and writes the fields the hub serves; RW-REFADM, the reference data administrator, loads the type table version and the parameter values; the business lead with Legal approves the type and field list under DL19; and RW-RESTRUCT's Documents CRU is exercised in the hub's screens, not on this row. This slice passes the reader the caller's own identity, so the hub's refusal and masking apply unchanged, and no credential and no personal name appears in the request, the row, the workflow input or the logs. Where a person must be named the row carries the user identifier, never a name.
