| BR Field ID | Entity (owner) | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-TRT-001 | treatment (S2, `rwb_treatment`) | id | Read as the row the facts are written on; written only when the stage opens the row |
| DF-TRT-002 | treatment (S2, `rwb_treatment`) | case_id | Read as the key of the read and of the write |
| DF-TRT-004 | treatment (S2, `rwb_treatment`) | treatment_type | Read to place the stage; never written by this slice |
| DF-TRT-013, DF-TRT-014 | treatment (S2, `rwb_treatment`) | outcome, outcome_at | Not written: the outcome of the treatment is the stage's and the plan stories' |
| DF-TRT-003, DF-TRT-005 to DF-TRT-012, DF-TRT-023 to DF-TRT-033 | treatment (S2, `rwb_treatment`) | the proposer, the terms, the approval, the booking, the credit result, the plan and the signature fields | Not written: they belong to `RWB-S2-E3001-APP` to `RWB-S2-E3005-APP` and are left exactly as those stories set them |
| No BR Field ID | treatment (S2, `rwb_treatment`) | `contract_amount`, `contract_date`, `mortgage_amount`, `registration_date`, `land_office`, `title_doc_no` | Write, from the field code of the same name of `CONTRACT` or `MORTGAGE_DOCUMENT`; the column names and their field IDs are this story's design and are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2702; ASM-4478) |
| No BR Field ID | treatment (S2, `rwb_treatment`) | `source_document_id`, `source_doc_version`, `source_table_version` | Write, the identifiers and the type-table version of the entry each fact came from; the column names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2702; ASM-4478) |
| DF-DOC-001, DF-DOC-002, DF-DOC-004 | document (P5, `rwb_document`) | id, case_id, document_type | Read through the contract only, as the identifier and the type of each checked field; never from the table |
| DF-DOC-012 to DF-DOC-017 | document_field (P5, `rwb_document`) | id, document_id, field_name, field_value, confidence, confirmed_by | Read through the contract only, as `documentId`, `fieldName`, `value` and `confidence`; never from the table |
| DF-DOC-034, DF-DOC-035 | document_field (P5, `rwb_document`) | extracted_value, extractor_version | Read through the contract only, as the extracted value and the version of the extractor; never from the table |
| DF-DOC-015 | document_field (P5, `rwb_document`) | the personal field the party names ride on | Read through the contract only and never stored: a party name is masked or withheld and reaches no row, no log and no event |
| DF-REF-224, DF-REF-229 to DF-REF-231, DF-REF-233 | document_type (P5, `rwb_document`) | field_definitions, table_version, valid_from, valid_to, classify_threshold | Read through the contract only, as `tableVersion` on the answer; never from the table |
| DF-REF-246 and the parameter catalog | document_hub_parameter (P5) and parameter_catalog (P3) | param_value and the parameter row | Read through the parameters contract of rwb-case only, never from the table |
| Standard column | treatment (S2, `rwb_treatment`) | state, version, created_at, created_by, updated_at, updated_by | Write `updated_at`, `updated_by` and the optimistic `version` of the row; the other standard columns are the stage's |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_treatment` | the write key of the apply | Write, once per applied document set |

Field IDs are those of TSD S2 T3.1 and the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. The fact columns are the one addition this story makes: TSD S2 T3.1 gives the treatment no contract and no mortgage column, so the columns are named for the extracted codes, the amounts follow the numeric(18,2) convention TSD S2 T3.1 already uses for DF-TRT-007 and DF-TRT-008, the dates follow its date convention, and `title_doc_no` and `land_office` carry no type in any source — the whole set is recorded as GAP-2702 with ASM-4478. `document`, `document_field`, `document_type` and `document_hub_parameter` (P5), `recovery_case`, `parameter_catalog` and `reference_row` (P3) and `decision_log_entry` (P7) are not created, not written and not read as tables: no foreign key leaves `rwb_treatment`, `treatment.case_id` is an identifier and not a foreign key across schemas, and no `v_ace_*` view is reachable from the login (DP-01, BR9).

**No personal data.** The only personal value in the pipeline is `party_names`, which the hub extracts from a contract and masks for a role that may not see it. It is never mapped onto a column, never stored, never logged and never put on an event: the officer sees it on the hub's own document surfaces through the composite route, masked, and this service holds no copy of it. Amounts, dates, a title document number and a land office are business facts of the treatment and not personal data, and the fixture values of section 7 are synthetic examples only.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-treatment (S2); base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1` (DP-13). The two operations are the rows API-S2-001 and API-S2-002 of TSD S2 T-A.1, re-based on the service path; this story adds no operation of its own and changes no element of their published shape.

| ID | Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| API-S2-001 | POST | `/cases/{caseId}/treatments` | Open a treatment; when the request names a document type, apply the confirmed checked fields of that type in the same transaction | Treatment and offer C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header required; a repeated key answers the first result |
| API-S2-002 | GET | `/treatments/{treatmentId}` | Read the treatment with its terms, its state, the fact columns, the document version each fact came from and the fact sets it reports open | Treatment and offer R, scope applied | Not applicable |

The errors are 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 with the RFC 9457 problem body; 403 carries MSG-P4-002, 404 carries MSG-P4-003, 422 carries the platform field error and 503 carries MSG-GEN-006. The answer of API-S2-001 and API-S2-002 carries the applied facts with their `documentId`, `docVersion` and type-table version, and the withheld fact sets with their review reasons; those element names of the checked-field fill are this story's design and are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2702; ASM-4478). The treatment resource declares no offer operation, no approval envelope and no plan body: those belong to `RWB-S2-E3002-CON`, `RWB-S2-E3003-CON` and `RWB-S2-E3004-CON`.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| The checked-fields read, whose path and operation name are fixed by RWB-P5-E2025-CON and are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2702; ASM-4478) | `/api/recovery/document/v1` | P5 rwb-document (`RWB-P5-E2025-CON`) | The target shape of the legacy `DocumentFieldReader.checkedFields(UUID caseId, String documentType)`: the checked fields of a case and a type, each `documentId, docVersion, fieldName, value, state (OK, CONFIRMED, CORRECTED), confidence`, filtered by state and masked by role; one hop, 2 s, a breaker, no call chain (DP-11; ADR-020); built against the contract and its fake |
| The parameters read of the field threshold and the accuracy pass mark, operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2702; ASM-4478) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case (`RWB-P3-E1042-CON`) | The field threshold and `EXTRACT_ACCURACY_PASS` at their version, cached; no threshold and no pass mark in code (DP-06) |
| The reference-data read of LOV-DOC-TYPE, operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2702; ASM-4478) | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | P3 rwb-case (`RWB-P3-E1043-CON`) | The eleven type codes the stage may ask for and the version in force they are read at; the extracted codes themselves come on the reader's answer (DP-07) |

One operation is consumed at run time and two are consumed as parameters and lists; all three are one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker, and none calls another service. The two H rows of DP-06 and DP-07 and the two C rows they add stand in no build row of this story's plan (ASM-4481). A failed document read answers 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming "Document service", and a failed parameter or list read answers 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming "Reference data"; no refusal returns a partial fact set.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The topic of the service is `rwb.treatment.events.v1` with event names `rwb.treatment.<Event>.v1` (Architecture v5 slide 8; context pack), and the one event it carries, `TreatmentApproved`, belongs to the approval story of this epic (TSD S2 T5.3; EV-10 in the context pack). This slice announces no second event: applying an extracted amount is a fact about a row and not a decision or a stage move, and DP-09 is stated as a prohibition in section 13. No outbox row is written by this story.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The extraction event of the hub is rwb-document's own and this story carries no integration dependency on it (I is None in the work package), so this service subscribes to no topic for it, holds no consumer group for it and registers no listener. The stage receives its trigger as the case signal the parent `CaseWorkflow` forwards, and a replayed workflow reuses the recorded signal (Architecture v5 slide 13; Temporal and Drools Design slide 9). The inbox table of the platform event library exists in `rwb_treatment` for the events other S2 stories consume — `PaymentMissed` (EV-12) among them, which the design shows reaching the stage through the case router (Temporal and Drools Design slide 9) — and this story writes none of its rows.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TreatmentWorkflow` | Workflow, the stage child of `CaseWorkflow`, one execution per case and stage; not changed in shape by this story | `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Input: case ID, treatment ID, business date, caller identity; output: the applied and withheld fact sets of section 7 |
| `applyDocumentFacts` | Activity, new in this story | `rwb-treatment` | Input: case ID, treatment ID, the three document types, caller identity; output: the applied facts with their source identifiers and table version, the withheld fact sets with their reasons, and the outcome of each read |

The activity is called by `TreatmentWorkflow` in the stage it already runs; it opens no child workflow, starts no timer and calls no third service. The name `applyDocumentFacts` and the shape of its input and output records are this story's design and are fixed by no source (GAP-2702; ASM-4478).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No row of the job map belongs to this capability: the document intake job JOB-12 (legacy RWB-E2-025 section 4) and the monthly retention run JOB-17 are rwb-document's, and the classifier and the extraction run inside the intake workflow. DP-10 is in the pattern list and registers nothing here: no cron entry, no Temporal Schedule and no event-started workflow is created or moved by this story, and the only clock it touches is the 2 s budget of a single REST hop.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | This story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `treatment` | `rwb_treatment` | S2 | Adds the fact and source columns of section 11 on the service's Flyway sequence and writes them through `TreatmentFactWriter`; the fields DF-TRT-003 to DF-TRT-033 stay the stage stories' |
| `idempotency_key` | `rwb_treatment` | PLT library object created in this schema | Written once per applied document set, in the same transaction as the row |
| `processed_event` | `rwb_treatment` | PLT library object created in this schema | Created by the library for the consumers other S2 stories add; this story writes none of its rows |

Not owned and never read as a table: `document`, `document_field`, `document_type` and `document_hub_parameter` (P5, `rwb_document`), `recovery_case`, `parameter_catalog`, `reference_row` and `lov_value` (P3, `rwb_case`), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7, `rwb_decision`), and every `v_ace_*` view (P1). No foreign key leaves the schema and no cross-schema join exists (DP-01, BR9). The outbox, inbox and idempotency tables are the service template's and are described here only for the row this story writes (ASM-4481).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Documented answer | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-document checked-fields fake (`RWB-P5-E2025-CON`) | The checked fields of case "RW-2026-000601" for CONTRACT, CREDIT_APPROVAL and MORTGAGE_DOCUMENT with the values of section 7; a REVIEW entry at confidence 0.7100 for "DOC-0601"; an empty answer with reason UNKNOWN_TYPE for "DOC-0602"; a 404 for the document of team "LIT-NE"; a 403 for a role without Documents R; a masked party_names entry; no answer beyond 2 s | AC1, AC2, AC3, AC6, AC7, AC8 |
| rwb-case parameters fake (`RWB-P3-E1042-CON`) | The field threshold 0.80 and the accuracy pass mark 0.90 at their version, and a delayed answer beyond 2 s | AC4, AC6 |

| gateway-bff composite route fake (`RWB-PLT-N001-CON`) | The merged SCR-14 and SCR-15 answer for case "RW-2026-000601" with the treatment facts of this service and the checked fields of rwb-document read once | AC8 |
| idempotency double over the write key | One applied set per document ID, `doc_version` and type-table version; a second apply of the same key is answered by the first | AC5 |

The fakes are test-only and are replaced by the real services in SIT; a drift between a fake and the published contract is a build failure of `RWB-P5-E2025-CON` or of the platform story that owns the fake.

| Kafka | None | No event published and none consumed by this story; the topic `rwb.treatment.events.v1` carries the events of the sibling stories |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.treatment`, module `stage23facts`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.treatment.stage23facts`; front end `src/modules/recovery/treatment/Stage23Facts.tsx`, the read-only fragment SCR-14 and SCR-15 embed. Service base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1`, schema `rwb_treatment`, topic `rwb.treatment.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 keeps the write inside `rwb_treatment`: `treatment`, the fact columns and the idempotency row are this schema's, and the case, the type version, the threshold and the pass mark are answers of contracts, never rows of another schema. DP-06 and DP-07 are the two parameter and list reads of 12.2, cached, so no threshold, pass mark, type code or version is a constant of the module. DP-11 is the whole point of the slice: the legacy in-process `DocumentFieldReader` becomes one hop with a published shape, a fake and a 2 s timeout, and S2 builds on Day 1 without a document table. DP-13 puts the two operations on the service base and removes the monolith base from the paths this story serves. DP-19 records that the facts reach SCR-14 and SCR-15 through the gateway-bff composite route; the route specification and the screen field list are the edge contract's.

Two patterns are prohibitions in this slice and are stated so that no build adds what the list implies:

- **DP-09 writes no event.** The library is the service template's and this story uses it for the idempotency and inbox tables of `rwb_treatment` and for the one write key of the apply. `DocumentFieldsExtracted` is produced by rwb-document and this story registers no listener for it (I is None), and the one event of rwb-treatment belongs to the approval story, so this module declares no producer, writes no outbox row and adds no event to the topic.
- **DP-10 registers no Schedule.** No job of this capability exists to schedule: the intake Schedule and the retention Schedule are rwb-document's (JOB-12, JOB-17; the job map). This module declares no cron entry, no Temporal Schedule and no event-started workflow, and the stage clock it runs under is the parent workflow's.

**Dependencies the table adds and the plan does not hold.** The pattern table adds five H rows — `RWB-PLT-E1042-CON` and `RWB-PLT-E1043-CON` for DP-06 and DP-07, `RWB-PLT-TE006-CON` for DP-09, `RWB-PLT-E1071-CON` for DP-10 and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` for DP-19 — and two C rows, `RWB-P3-E1042-CON` and `RWB-P3-E1043-CON`, while the plan's lists for this story hold Depends on (build) `None` and Contract dependencies `RWB-P5-E2025-CON` only. The metadata table keeps the plan's lists as they are, the service template carries every one of the five, and the story builds against their fakes until those stories publish (ASM-4481).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `ApplyDocumentFactsActivity` | Activity | The `applyDocumentFacts` entry point: resolves the types, calls the client per type, filters, maps, guards the version, writes, and returns the applied and withheld sets |
| `CheckedFieldClient` | Client | The checked-fields call on `RWB-P5-E2025-CON`, one hop, 2 s, a breaker and no retry chain (GAP-2702; ASM-4478) |
| `CheckedFieldFilter` | Service | Keeps only OK, CONFIRMED and CORRECTED entries and drops every entry below the pass mark, so a withheld value cannot be promoted by a future contract version |
| `Stage23TreatmentMapper` | Mapper | Maps a field code onto the treatment column of the same name only; holds the field code names of the contract and the column names of section 11, and no amount, no date and no list value (GAP-2702; ASM-4478) |
| `Stage23VersionGuard` | Service | Compares the reported `tableVersion` with the version the reference-data contract reports in force and the parameter values with the parameters contract; refuses the apply when they disagree |
| `TreatmentFactWriter` | Repository | Writes the fact columns, the source identifiers, the stamped type-table version and the idempotency row in one `rwb_treatment` transaction; writes no other table |
| `Stage23Idempotency` | Service | Builds the write key from the document ID, the `doc_version` and the type-table version, recognises a repeat and re-runs nothing that completed |
| `TreatmentFactReader` | Service | Serves API-S2-002 with the facts, the source identifiers and the fact sets reported open |
| `Stage23FactsPanel` | React component | Shows the applied facts, the version each came from and the open fact sets on SCR-14 and SCR-15, read only, with the refusal and unavailable states |

**Database and migrations.** One Flyway version on the service's own sequence adds the fact and source columns of section 11 to `treatment`, with no cross-schema key and no index of another schema. `idempotency_key` and `processed_event` are platform library objects created in `rwb_treatment` by the library's own migration. No other table, column or index is added, and an applied migration is never edited. The column set is Not specified in the source documents and is recorded as GAP-2702 with ASM-4478.

**Configuration and reference data.**

- The field threshold and the accuracy pass mark are parameter values resolved through the parameters contract and client library of rwb-case (DP-06); the operation this story calls is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2702; ASM-4478).
- LOV-DOC-TYPE with the eleven types is read through the reference-data client library (DP-07); no list value is copied into `rwb_treatment`.
- The type and field codes and the table version are taken from the reader's answer at run time; a build check pairs the field code names held by `Stage23TreatmentMapper` with the fixture of `RWB-P5-E2025-CON`, so a code that leaves the fixture fails the build (AC4).
- The 2 s budget, the single hop and the breaker are the platform rule of ADR-020 and not a value of this story.
- The feature switch `rwb.treatment.stage23-facts`, read as a flag of the platform library: off means the stage applies no checked field and API-S2-002 answers the treatment with no applied set, while the two operations themselves are unchanged.

**Build steps**

1. `CheckedFieldClient` against the contract fake, with the 2 s budget, the breaker, the no-answer path and the two refusals; test X4, X5, X6 and AC6.
2. `CheckedFieldFilter` and `Stage23VersionGuard` over the fake's answers, with the REVIEW entry, the below-pass-mark value, the empty answer and the version disagreement; test AC2, AC3, AC4.
3. `Stage23TreatmentMapper` with the name-identical mapping and the unmapped codes; test AC1, X8 and the build check of AC4.
4. `TreatmentFactWriter` in one transaction with the idempotency row and the uniqueness of the write key; test AC1 and AC5.
5. `Stage23Idempotency` with the repeated apply, the repeated read and the new `doc_version`; test AC5.
6. `ApplyDocumentFactsActivity` registered on `rwb-treatment` and called from `TreatmentWorkflow`, with the retry policy of the platform and the no-partial-write path; test AC6.
7. `TreatmentFactReader` and `Stage23FactsPanel` through the composite route fake, with the applied set, the open fact sets and the masked party names; test AC7 and AC8.
8. The boundary test: no statement outside `rwb_treatment`, no `v_ace_*` read, no read of `rwb_document` or `rwb_case`, no event producer, no consumer and no Schedule in the module; test BR9, BR10, BR11 and the two prohibitions.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the contract tests of `RWB-P5-E2025-CON` stay green, a SIT week shows the contract and mortgage facts applied once per document version and type-table version, no value in REVIEW promoted and no column cleared by a withholding read, no read of a document table or an ACE view in the logs, no event and no Schedule registered by this module, and SCR-14 shows the facts through the composite route.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-003 | A document has a field in review, so the fact this story needs is withheld and its set is reported open (X1, X2, X3) | Some fields need checking. The document is in the review queue. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller's role lacks Documents R on the read, or the Treatment and offer right on the operation (X5, AC6, AC7) | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The document or the case lies outside the caller's scope (X6, AC6) | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The checked-fields read, the parameters read or the reference-data read did not answer inside the budget (X4) | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The four texts are copied unchanged from legacy RWB-E2-025 section 14 and are the wording of the hub and the access module; no message is reworded and no new message is added. For MSG-P4-002 the {action} value names what the caller tried — for example "apply the checked fields of this treatment" — and never a case fact, a document ID or a role name. For MSG-GEN-006 the {system} value is "Document service" on the checked-fields read and "Reference data" on the parameters and list reads. Each error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set to the ID above, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled and `instance` naming the request; the status mapping is 403 for MSG-P4-002, 404 for MSG-P4-003 and 503 for MSG-GEN-006, and MSG-P5-003 is a label of the document and of the open fact set and not an error of this service. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built in this story. Three surfaces show what it writes, all read through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), and only the first two are this service's own read model.

| Screen | State | What the user sees or does |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-14 Treatment record | Loading | The placeholder while the composite route answers |
| SCR-14 Treatment record | Draft or submitted | The contract amount, the contract date and the mortgage registration facts, with the document ID and the document version each fact came from, and the type-table version they were applied under |
| SCR-14 Treatment record | Fact set open | The contract, credit-approval or mortgage fact set that needs a withheld field, with its review reason and the review queue of the hub as the place to fix it, and MSG-P5-003 on the document |
| SCR-14 Treatment record | Refused | A role without the Treatment and offer right reads MSG-P4-002 and nothing changes |
| SCR-14 Treatment record | Out of scope | A case outside the scope reads MSG-P4-003 |
| SCR-14 Treatment record | Document service unavailable | MSG-GEN-006, and the treatment keeps the facts it already holds |
| SCR-15 Settlement offer | Draft or below floor | The contract amount as the baseline of the offer the settlement story builds, read only |
| SCR-15 Settlement offer | Approval sought, sent, accepted | The same baseline, unchanged by this story |
| SCR-30 Case documents | List, as rwb-document serves it | The stage 2 and 3 types with their checked fields and their review state, read only through the same route |
| SCR-31 Document review queue | List and reviewed, as rwb-document serves it | The marked fields of the new types, read only here; the correction is the hub's |

The route merges the answer of this service with rwb-document's; the route path, the screen-model field list and the merge order belong to `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` and the edge stories, not here (ASM-3076). SCR-14 and SCR-15 are the treatment screens of the epic, so the panel is built against the route fake and switched on with them.

##### 16. Test cases

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the type codes, the field codes, the table version, the field threshold, the accuracy pass mark and the lists are rows read at their version; a build check fails on a type code, a field code, an amount, a date, a threshold, a pass mark or a valid-from date in the Java source or the module configuration.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow inputs, events or `rwb_treatment`: `party_names` is never mapped, stored, logged or put on a message, and a property test places a synthetic party name in the reader's answer and asserts that it appears in no row, no log line and no span attribute.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: no component of this story reads an ACE view or an ACE table, and the `rwb_treatment` login holds no `v_ace_*` grant (DP-01; Architecture v5 slide 8).
- No read of another service's tables and no cross-schema join: `document`, `document_field`, `document_type` and `document_hub_parameter` (P5), `recovery_case`, `parameter_catalog` and `reference_row` (P3) and `decision_log_entry` (P7) are reached only through their owners' contracts, and the boundary test fails the build on any statement outside `rwb_treatment`.
- Only checked values move: a field in REVIEW, a value below the pass mark, a type not in force and an item with reason UNKNOWN_TYPE are withheld, and no code path promotes them; the withheld fact set is shown open with its reason.
- One hop and a 2 s budget on the single consumed read, with a breaker and no call chain; a repeat is the same write key and never a silent second write.
- No event, no topic producer, no outbox row and no Schedule: this story publishes nothing, consumes nothing and schedules nothing (DP-09 and DP-10 as prohibitions), and the facts reach the other services on the owners' own reads.
- The write is a write of facts: no case state, no treatment lifecycle state, no offer and no approval is written here, and no decision record is written because no rule is evaluated.
- The screens are read only: SCR-14 and SCR-15 show what this service wrote and what the hub serves, and no screen writes a checked field.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-025 for rwb-document. The legacy story prepared a classifier version, a type table version and a reader and expected an operator to run the extraction job from a shared scheduler. This story deploys the stage 2 and 3 extension of `rwb-document`: one chart and its values, the migration step of the extraction sequence with its reader index, the one intake Schedule on queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery` verified and never duplicated, the model route endpoint and the credential references of the service identity, the OCR provider endpoint verified and not replaced, the dashboards and alerts for extraction outcomes and field accuracy, the flag that turns the new types on and off, and the runbook with its rollback. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **the stage 2 and 3 extension of `rwb-document` deployed as one Helm release with its values files, its migration gate over the extraction sequence and the reader index, the one intake Schedule on queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery` verified with no second timer, the endpoint and credential references the extraction needs for the model route and the OCR provider, the feature flag that turns the new types on and off, the dashboards that show extraction outcomes and field accuracy, the alerts on a failed extraction and on an accuracy below the pass mark, and a runbook with its rollback**, so that **an operator can see an item that failed to extract, a field set that fell below the accuracy pass mark, a model route that stopped answering and a Schedule that stopped moving, recover from the run book alone, and prove that the six Epic 1 types were untouched and that no document was altered when the flag was switched or the release was rolled back**.

The legacy story ran the extension inside a shared scheduler and a shared schema: the type table version and the classifier version were prepared by hand, `ExtractStep` ran as a job step of JOB-12, and the reader was a Java interface nobody could see the health of. In the target that picture splits in four. JOB-12 stays one Temporal Schedule in the service that owns it, so the release verifies the Schedule rather than registering a second one (DP-10). The extraction writes tables of `rwb_document` only, so the migration gate carries the Epic 1 sequence and the reader index (DP-01). The new types are data rows of the type table, so the release ships a flag and no code per type. The reader is a published operation of this service, so the release publishes its latency and error series and the S4 and S2 callers build against the contract (DP-11, DP-13). What is left for this story is a chart, a migration gate, a Schedule check, two provider bindings, six dashboard series, five alert rules, five runbook entries and a rollback.

Deployment is also where the extension is kept reversible. The flag removes the five new types without a schema change and without a redeployment of a type table; the type table version is a data load owned by the reference data administrator and the release only reports which version each environment holds; and no release ever replaces the OCR provider or the model provider, because both are owned elsewhere and this story carries their endpoints and credential references only. The observability follows ADR-023 per service: six series, five alerts and five runbook entries, each alert carrying a message identifier and one runbook entry.

##### 2. Business rationale

The business measure of this legacy key is fields extracted without review, and the operational measure behind it is the one no unit test sees: a new type whose accuracy fell below the pass mark must be visible before an officer trusts its values in a litigation pack. A field set that fails, a model route that has expired its credential, a Schedule that stopped after a release and a type table version that was never loaded are all silent unless the release emits them and the run book says what to do.

The split changes what an operator does. In the legacy story the operator re-ran a job and checked a type table by hand. In the target the operator reads the Schedule's run history, the extraction-outcome counters of each type, the accuracy series against the 0.90 pass mark and the review backlog of the new types, and then takes one of five actions: re-run the Schedule for the business date, hold the flag, reload the type table through the reference data administrator, clear the model route credential, or roll back the chart. The runbook is written for that sequence, because the difference between a busy release week and an incident is whether the operator has to guess which of the five failed.

The story also carries the retirement explicitly. No Quartz job, no scheduler table and no second timer is deployed; the intake Schedule is the only timer and the release refuses a second one (BR3). The five new types are data, so their rollback is a flag and never a rebuild, and the six Epic 1 types keep their behaviour under every value of the flag (BR4, BR9).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The Kafka event platform provides `rwb.document.events.v1` with its three retry topics and its `.dlt` topic, and the ACLs of this service's principals (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON; DP-09).
- The Temporal workflow kit and the namespace `rwb-recovery` exist, with worker versioning, the build ID provider and the payload codec (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON; DP-10).
- The per-service Flyway sequence and the migration conventions of `rwb_document` are published (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON), and the sequence of the Epic 1 extraction is in place (RWB-P5-E1053-CON).
- The platform error envelope and the message catalogue are in force, so an alert can carry a message identifier.
- The three environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist and the production namespace exists for the release date; the feature flag library is available.
- The worker compute, the storage, the containers, the topic binding, the ACLs and the service identity exist in each environment, and the private route to the model provider is open (the infrastructure stories of this service).
- The gateway-bff composite route for SCR-30 and SCR-31 is published (RWB-PLT-N001-CON; DP-19).
- The extraction operations and the checked-fields read are declared (RWB-P5-E1053-CON, RWB-P5-E2025-CON), so the release deploys a capability that exists and not a shell.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7). The baseline it deploys is RWB-P5-E2025-APP's, the contract it gates is RWB-P5-E2025-CON's and the endpoints it injects are the platform's; none of them blocks the chart work.
- The release date 31 December 2026 is the legacy one and is tentative (ASM-1912), and the story carries Status Draft (realignment v1) because no approval of the realigned story is recorded (ASM-1913).

The model name and the model version behind the agent route, the alert thresholds, the evaluation cadence and the exact business-hours window are Not specified in the source documents (ASM-1916). The OCR provider product and its endpoint are the ones the Epic 1 intake release provisions and are verified here, not replaced (ASM-1918).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds the service image and the contract jar, runs the unit, component and contract tests, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes one chart version.
2. The chart deploys the API deployment and the worker deployment with the rwb-document login, the namespace `rwb-recovery`, the task queue `rwb-document`, the codec, the build ID of the release and the values of the platform.
3. The worker scaling step enables KEDA on the queue backlog of `rwb-document`, so the pool grows with the 15-minute run and the front stays at its fixed replica count.
4. The migration step applies the `rwb_document` sequence of the release and refuses to run when the target schema is not `rwb_document`; the index `ix_document_type_case` of the checked-fields read is one step of it, and this story adds no table and no column.
5. The type table step reports the version in force per environment (`DOCTYPE-2026.11` or `DOCTYPE-2026.12`) and fails the smoke run when the version the environment is meant to hold is not in force; the load itself stays with the reference data administrator and the type table of RWB-P5-E1025-APP (ASM-1914).
6. The Schedule step verifies the intake Schedule: workflow `DocumentIntakeWorkflow`, queue `rwb-document`, namespace `rwb-recovery`, every 15 minutes in business hours, overlap policy skip and a catch-up window of one run; it creates nothing and fails the release when the Schedule is missing, duplicated or pointed at a foreign workflow, because the Schedule belongs to RWB-P5-E1049-OPS.
7. The provider step binds the model route endpoint and the OCR provider endpoint from the values of the environment, the client credential of the service identity from the platform secret store, and fails the release when an endpoint is missing, points outside the private network or carries a literal secret (ASM-1916, ASM-1918).
8. The flag step sets `rwb.document.extract-stage23` from the values of the environment; the legacy name `rwb.dochub.extraction-stage23` is recorded as retired and is not deployed (ASM-1915).
9. The dashboards are published with the six series and the environment, release, build ID and document type as dimensions.
10. The five alerts are wired to their message identifiers and to their runbook entries: MSG-P2-004 for a failed extraction run, MSG-P5-003 for a review backlog of the new types, MSG-GEN-006 for an unavailable dependency or an expired credential, and the accuracy and read alerts whose identifiers are Not specified in the source documents (ASM-1917).
11. A smoke step in SIT loads the 60-document sample with the flag on, waits for one Schedule run, confirms fields of the five new types with one `DocumentFieldsExtracted` event, turns the flag off and confirms that the new types are no longer offered and that the six Epic 1 types still extract, then restores the environment.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The chart render or the migration job fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic, no offset and no migration is left half applied | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The migration step is pointed at a schema other than `rwb_document` | The step refuses and the release stops | None | AC1 |
| X3 | A run of the intake Schedule fails, or runs past its threshold | The run-failure alert fires with MSG-P2-004 naming the run, the time and the runbook path; the Schedule retries on its next interval | MSG-P2-004 | AC4 |
| X4 | The model route does not answer, or its credential has expired | The extraction of the item fails on every attempt, the item stays unreviewed with `extract_status` FAILED, and the dependency alert fires with MSG-GEN-006 naming the system and the runbook entry names the rotation | MSG-GEN-006 | AC3, AC4, AC5 |
| X5 | A Schedule is missing, registered twice, or points at a foreign workflow | The Schedule check fails the release: one Schedule ID, one workflow, one queue | None | AC2 |
| X6 | The type table version the environment should hold is not in force | The type table step fails the smoke run and the release is not promoted | None | AC1, AC6 |
| X7 | Field accuracy on the sample falls below the pass mark | The accuracy alert fires with the per-field series and the runbook entry names the review-only proposal route through RWB-P5-E1025-APP | Not specified in the source documents (ASM-1917) | AC4, AC5 |
| X8 | A dashboard series is missing, or an alert carries no message identifier or no runbook link | The observability check fails the release | None | AC4 |
| X9 | The feature flag is off in an environment | The five new types are not offered to classification and the checked-fields read returns nothing for them; the six Epic 1 types are unaffected; the flag is not a way to stop a run in progress | None | AC6 |
| X10 | A new build is promoted while runs are open | The open runs replay on the new build from their history; the dashboards show both build IDs | None | AC1, AC4 |
| X11 | The reader latency or error rate of the checked-fields read passes its threshold | The read alert fires and the runbook entry names the caller, the route and the partition of the case | Not specified in the source documents (ASM-1917) | AC4, AC5 |
| X12 | A reviewer or a caller reads a document outside their scope after the release | The 404 shape of MSG-P4-003 is unchanged and no field value is returned | MSG-P4-003 | AC5 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the workflow kit, the topic provisioning, the migration conventions, the flag library and the provider endpoints; no application code is built here |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, lag and error thresholds, the evaluation cadence and quotas are environment values |
| Valuable | Makes the new types observable, reversible and provable before the release date, and keeps the six Epic 1 types untouched |
| Estimable | One chart, one migration gate, one Schedule check, two provider bindings, one flag, six series, five alerts and five runbook entries |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the migration refuses a foreign schema, one Schedule exists, an alert fires on a synthetic metric, the smoke run passes |

```gherkin
    Given the published dashboards and alert rules of the deployment
    When a synthetic run produces extracted items of the five new types, one failed item, one field set below the pass mark and one handler failure on the reader
    Then the dashboards show extraction outcomes per type and status, fields in review per type, the extractor version in use, the field accuracy of the sample against the 0.90 pass mark, the checked-fields read latency and error rate, and the queue backlog and age of the task queue
    Then each series carries the environment, the release, the build ID and the document type as dimensions
    Then the run-failure alert fires with MSG-P2-004, the review-backlog alert with MSG-P5-003 and the dependency alert with MSG-GEN-006
    Then the accuracy alert and the read alert carry their identifiers, which are Not specified in the source documents (ASM-1917)
    Then each alert names the Schedule ID, the build ID, the environment and one runbook link
    Then no panel and no alert payload carries a field value, a party name, an account number or a document text

  Scenario: AC5 The runbook and the rollback are exercised (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published runbook and the rollback of the release
    When a failed extraction run, a review backlog of a new type, an unavailable model route, an accuracy below the pass mark and a failing reader are simulated
    Then each condition maps to one runbook entry with the check, the owner role and the recovery step
    Then the model route entry names the credential rotation and the dependency owner, and no entry asks an operator to edit a type row by hand
    Then the rollback redeploys the previous chart with its own build ID and the open runs finish on the old build
    Then a rollback leaves the type table version and the field rows in place, because the release writes no business row and the migration is additive
    Then the smoke run ends with the fields of the five new types, one DocumentFieldsExtracted event per extraction and no altered file, and the environment restored

  Scenario: AC6 The feature flag turns the new types on and off (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published runbook, the flag and the SIT type table holding DOCTYPE-2026.12
    When the flag rwb.document.extract-stage23 is turned off in SIT and one Schedule run is waited for
    Then the five new types are not offered to classification and the checked-fields read returns no field for them
    Then the six Epic 1 types still extract and still answer their fields with the flag off
    Then the legacy flag rwb.dochub.extraction-stage23 appears in no values file, chart or runbook
    Then turning the flag on again restores the new types on the next run with no redeployment of the type table
    Then the flag is a value of the environment and never a literal in a template
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One login, one task queue and one schema per service: the release carries the rwb-document login, polls `rwb-document` only and migrates `rwb_document` only | Arch v5 slide 41; DP-02; DP-01 |
| BR2 | The release publishes on `rwb.document.events.v1` only and subscribes to no topic of this service; the decision-record topic is not used by this path | Arch v5 slides 16 and 42; DP-09 |
| BR3 | One Schedule and one scheduler: the intake Schedule is the only timer for JOB-12, registered in Temporal on queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`; the release verifies it and registers no second one, and no Quartz job, scheduler table or cron entry exists | Arch v5 slide 44; DP-10; `ASM-1914` |
| BR4 | The five new types are reversible by one flag, `rwb.document.extract-stage23`, which replaces the legacy `rwb.dochub.extraction-stage23`, and the six Epic 1 types keep their behaviour under every value of the flag | legacy section 13; DP-07; `ASM-1915` |
| BR5 | Every alert carries a message identifier or its recorded placeholder and links one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR6 | No environment value is hard-coded: replicas, resources, thresholds, intervals, quotas, endpoints and the flag come from values files and parameters | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR7 | Dashboard series, alert payloads and the runbook carry counts, identifiers, statuses, business dates, type codes and build IDs only, never a field value, a party name or a document text | ADR-023; CTL-11; DL26 |
| BR8 | The release exposes the checked-fields read and the extraction operations through the chart and its ingress and declares no path of its own; SCR-30 and SCR-31 are reached through the gateway-bff composite route | DP-19; RWB-P5-E2025-CON 12.1 |
| BR9 | The type table version is data: the release reports it and never loads it, and a version is applied only by the approved load of RWB-P5-E1025-APP | DL19; `ASM-1914` |
| BR10 | A failing release never replaces a working one: the previous build stays in force until the new build passes its tests and its smoke run | DP-10 |
| BR11 | The release provisions no ACE grant, no view and no lake route, and carries no provider key in a value, a template or a runbook | DP-01; DP-05; D-RCV-35 U1; NFR-052 |
| BR12 | A field set below the pass mark is never promoted to a confident one by the release: the accuracy series and its alert route the proposal through the review-only load of the type table | CTL-08; `ASM-1917` |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the contract tests pass | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration applied and worker registered | The `rwb_document` sequence applied and the worker polls `rwb-document` | Ready |
| Ready | Schedule and type table verified | One Schedule with the intake release ID, and the expected type version in force | Scheduled |
| Scheduled | First run completes | The run finishes and its counters reach the dashboards | In use |
| In use | Release superseded | A new chart version passes its tests | Rolling |
| Rolling | All workers on the new build | The old build drains its open runs | In use |
| In use | Flag off | `rwb.document.extract-stage23` is turned off in the environment | Restricted |
| Restricted | Flag on | The flag is turned on again and the next run extracts the new types | In use |
| In use | Smoke run failed | The Schedule check, the provider check, the type table check or the smoke step fails | Blocked |
| Blocked | Previous build restored | The previous chart is redeployed or a later build passes the smoke run | In use |

The field states OK, REVIEW, CONFIRMED and CORRECTED and the `extract_status` values are the app story's runtime and are not states of this deployment.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the migration gate, the Schedule check, the provider bindings, the dashboards and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the Schedule, the topic ACLs, the consumer quotas, the flag library and the restart of a run |
| Platform event owner | Owns `rwb.document.events.v1`, its retry and `.dlt` topics, its schema subject and its retention |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads and reports the type table version the release checks; never the DevOps engineer |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact and may block it on a failing smoke run |
| On-call operator | Runs the five runbook entries and opens an incident when a failed extraction, an accuracy drop or a reader failure persists |
| rwb-document owner | Owns the extraction extension, the checked-fields read and the migration the release applies |
| Agent service owner | Owns the model route, the model, the prompt and the provider credential behind it |
| Data steward | Confirms that no dashboard, alert or runbook carries a field value or a personal value |

The worker runs as the rwb-document service identity (DP-02), carried by the chart as a secret reference and never as a literal. The login name is Not specified in the source documents (ASM-1916).

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Deployment values | Image digest, chart version, replica counts for the API and the worker, resource requests and limits, probe paths and timings, log level, namespace, task queue, build ID, feature switch, KEDA backlog threshold, Schedule ID, model route endpoint, OCR provider endpoint reference, alert thresholds |
| Task queue | `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, polled by the worker of this service only |
| Topic | `rwb.document.events.v1` with its partitions, replication factor, retention and key, its three retry topics and its `.dlt` topic; no subscription of this service |
| Schema | `rwb_document`, migrated by its own per-service Flyway sequence; the reader index `ix_document_type_case` is one step of it and the release adds no table and no column |
| Schedule | The intake Schedule: `DocumentIntakeWorkflow`, queue `rwb-document`, namespace `rwb-recovery`, every 15 minutes in business hours (JOB-12), overlap policy skip, catch-up window one run; verified by this release and registered by RWB-P5-E1049-OPS |
| Type table | The version in force per environment, reported and never loaded; `DOCTYPE-2026.11` before the release date and `DOCTYPE-2026.12` from 2026-12-31 |
| Flag | `rwb.document.extract-stage23`, on in DEV and SIT for the tests, from the values of each environment; the legacy `rwb.dochub.extraction-stage23` is retired |
| Provider bindings | The model route endpoint published by the agent service with the client credential of the service identity, and the OCR provider endpoint of the intake release with its secret; both as secret references |
| Dashboard series | Extraction outcomes per type and status, fields in review per type, extractor version in use, field accuracy of the sample against the pass mark, checked-fields read latency and error rate, queue backlog and age; dimensions environment, release, build ID, document type |
| Runbook entries | Failed extraction run, review backlog of a new type, unavailable model route, accuracy below the pass mark, failing checked-fields read; each with the check, the owner role and the recovery step |
| Alerts | Five rules and one runbook entry each: MSG-P2-004 for a failed run, MSG-P5-003 for the review backlog, MSG-GEN-006 for an unavailable dependency, and the accuracy and read alerts with the placeholder of ASM-1917 |
| Secrets | The rwb-document login secret, the Kafka client credential, the Temporal mTLS material, the model route client credential and the storage identity reference, all from the platform secret store |
| Test data | The 60-document sample of the app story, masked, one forced extraction failure, one field set below the pass mark and one flag-off run; synthetic identifiers only |

The deployment topology (cluster names, node pools, replica counts, resource sizes, zone spread, ingress class and probe timings) belongs to each environment and is set by the platform team in its values file; the chart exposes every one of them as a value and this story fixes only their names and the rule that they are never hard-coded.

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only after the worker has polled `rwb-document` once and the API has answered its health path; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database or commits an offset, and an unreachable model route is reported as not ready for extraction, never as live-and-broken.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | The release migrates `rwb_document` only and reads no other schema | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | The seven parameters stay rows read through the client library; no chart value carries them | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | The three lists stay reference rows and the type codes stay type table rows; no chart value carries them | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | The topic with its retry and `.dlt` topics, the inbox of the readers and the relay | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | The worker, the task queue, worker versioning and the one intake Schedule from the kit; the release verifies the Schedule and registers no Quartz job | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | The release declares no REST path and no client of its own; the private routes are the platform's | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | The ingress registers the service base `/api/recovery/document/v1` for the edge | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | The ingress serves the gateway-bff edge; no screen is deployed | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-10 is the substantive row of this story: JOB-12 stops being a Quartz job on a shared scheduler and is one Temporal Schedule on the service's own queue, so the release verifies the Schedule, the worker and the build ID and the operator restarts a run through the Schedule rather than a scheduler table. DP-01 keeps the migration inside `rwb_document` and makes the step refuse a foreign schema. DP-06 and DP-07 keep the pass mark, the threshold and the three lists out of the values files, so the only thing an environment sets is where the data lives, not what it says. DP-09 keeps the topic and the retry and `.dlt` topics under the platform owner while this release verifies the ACLs it needs. DP-11 and the two provider bindings are what the release does not own: the endpoints and the credential references are injected and checked, and no client, no model and no provider key is deployed here. DP-13 and DP-19 register the service base and the edge route and deploy no screen.

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-document/` overlay | API deployment, worker deployment, config map, secret references, probes, task queue, namespace, build ID, KEDA rule, provider bindings and flag |
| `helm/rwb-document/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, flag value, build ID, Schedule ID, KEDA threshold, model route endpoint, OCR provider reference, alert thresholds |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit and contract tests, image and dependency scan, chart publish, migration gate, type table step, Schedule check, provider step, smoke run, promotion |
| Migration step | The `rwb_document` sequence with `ix_document_type_case`; a target schema other than `rwb_document` is refused |
| Type table step | Reports the version in force and fails the smoke run when the expected version is not in force; loads nothing |
| Schedule check | One Schedule with the intake release ID, the workflow, the queue, the interval, the overlap policy and the catch-up window; a missing, duplicated or foreign Schedule fails the release |
| Provider bindings | The model route endpoint with the client credential reference, and the OCR provider endpoint reference verified as the intake release's |
| Dashboards | The six series of section 11 with the four dimensions |
| Alerts | Five rules, each with a message identifier or its placeholder and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Five entries: failed extraction run, review backlog of a new type, unavailable model route, accuracy below the pass mark, failing checked-fields read |

**Alert mapping**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P2-004 | A run of the intake Schedule failed or ran past its threshold | Run-failure alert naming the Schedule ID, the run, the time, the business date and the runbook path | Platform on-call, page in business hours, else ticket |
| MSG-P5-003 | Fields of a new type are held for a person and the backlog passes its age | Review-backlog alert naming the type, the count per state and the age of the oldest item | Reviewer lead and the data steward, ticket |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The model route, a case read or a list read is unavailable, or a credential has expired | Dependency alert naming the system and the health state | Platform on-call and the agent service owner, page |
| Not specified in the source documents (ASM-1917) | The field accuracy of the sample falls below the 0.90 pass mark | Accuracy alert naming the field, the type, the measured value, the pass mark and the evaluator version | Data steward and the rwb-document owner, page |
| Not specified in the source documents (ASM-1917) | The latency or the error rate of the checked-fields read passes its threshold | Read alert naming the operation, the caller service and the partition of the case | Platform on-call, ticket |

**Retry and offsets.** The Schedule retries a failed run on its next interval and never runs two runs at once, because the overlap policy is skip. The activity retry is the kit's policy; the release adds no retry of its own, and the agent route keeps the 60-second budget per attempt and the three attempts of the extraction baseline. The relay commits its offset after the outbox row is marked sent, so a restart republishes nothing twice.

**Rollback.** A release that fails the smoke run is not promoted. A release already promoted is rolled back by redeploying the previous chart version with its own build ID, which keeps the old build serving its open runs until they finish; the Schedule keeps its ID and points at the workflow, so a rollback changes the build under it and not the timer. A rollback leaves the type table version and the field rows in place, because the release writes no business row of its own and the migration is additive; reverting the new types is the flag and not the chart.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.document.extract-stage23`. On: the five new types are classified, extracted and read. Off: the new types are not offered to classification and the checked-fields read returns nothing for them, while the six Epic 1 types keep their behaviour. The legacy name `rwb.dochub.extraction-stage23` appears in no value, chart or runbook (ASM-1915).

**Done when.** The chart renders for DEV, SIT and UAT with a pinned digest and the build ID, the migration step refuses a foreign schema and creates the reader index, the type table step reports the expected version, the Schedule check passes with one Schedule and a second apply changes nothing, the provider bindings resolve the model route and the OCR provider without a literal secret, the flag-off run restricts the new types and leaves the six Epic 1 types extracting, the six series and the five alerts are published with their identifiers or placeholders and their runbook links, the smoke run produces fields of the five new types with one event per extraction and no altered file, and the five runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P2-004 | A run of the intake Schedule failed or ran past its threshold | {job} failed at {time} for business date {date}. Follow run book {runbook}. |
| MSG-P5-003 | Fields of a new type are held for a person | Some fields need checking. The document is in the review queue. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The model route, the case read or the list read is unavailable, or a credential has expired | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-003 | A caller reads a document outside its scope after the release | This case is not in your scope. |
| Identifier pending | The field accuracy of the sample falls below the pass mark | Not specified in the source documents (ASM-1917) |
| Identifier pending | The checked-fields read passes its latency or error threshold | Not specified in the source documents (ASM-1917) |

MSG-P5-003 is the legacy text of RWB-E2-025 section 14 and is unchanged; MSG-P4-003 is the legacy scope text of the same section. MSG-P2-004 is the job-failure text of the observability epic and MSG-GEN-006 the platform text for an unavailable system, both used with their agreed wording. The accuracy and read alerts have no identifier in the source set, so they carry the placeholder until the Error and Message Standard names them. An alert payload names counts, statuses, business dates, type codes, the Schedule ID, the build ID and group names only, never a field value, a party name or a document text.

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment has no screen of its own. Its operator-facing surfaces are the pipeline run view, the release view, the Temporal Web UI, the dashboards, SCR-30 Case documents and SCR-31 Document review queue through the gateway-bff composite route, and the runbook. The two screens are served by the app stories and the route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the deployment only registers the ingress path. The Temporal Web UI stays behind Entra ID: RW-PLATADM operates and RW-AUDIT reads, and payloads are decoded only through the codec server under break-glass. The job monitor of Epic 2 shows the same run data; this release publishes the run records the monitor reads.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the types, the field codes, the patterns, the threshold, the pass mark and the review-only flags are type table rows and parameters, never a deployment value.
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads, the runbook or the workflow history: counts, statuses, type codes, identifiers, business dates and build IDs only, and payloads stay encrypted.
- One login, one task queue and one schema per service: the release carries the rwb-document login, polls `rwb-document` and migrates `rwb_document` only (DP-02, DP-01).
- The release deploys no ACE grant, no view and no lake route (DP-05, BR11).
- One Schedule and one scheduler: the intake Schedule is verified once and no second timer, Quartz job or cron entry exists (BR3).
- The model route and the OCR provider are injected as endpoint and secret references; no provider key, model name or credential is written into a value, a template, a dashboard or the runbook (BR11, NFR-052).
- The type table version is reported and never loaded by the release; a version is applied only by the approved load of RWB-P5-E1025-APP (BR9).
- The flag restricts the five new types and never touches the six Epic 1 types, and it is never a way to stop a run in progress (BR4).
- The release pins the image digest, the chart version and the build ID; a rebuild between environments is not allowed, and a failing smoke run never replaces a working build.
- No secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; all secrets come from the platform secret store.

##### 1. Story

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **a repeatable cross-service journey harness for the extraction of the stage 2 and 3 document types, with the extraction, review and reader evidence attached to the wave 2 release**, so that **the journey of a contract, credit approval, mortgage document, court filing, hearing notice or judgment, from intake through classification and field extraction to the litigation reader and the treatment reader, is proven end to end across rwb-document, rwb-decision, rwb-litigation and rwb-treatment before the app stories of RWB-E2-025 are signed off**.

This story builds the harness, its contract fakes, its seed pack, its evidence pack and its pass or fail gate. It builds no production endpoint, screen, table or migration. The classifier, the extractor and the review queue stand behind the rwb-document contract; the harness proves that the values those steps produce arrive at the readers of the two route services with a confidence, in the right state and in the right form.

##### 2. Business rationale

RWB-E2-025 splits into four app stories and this integration story. RWB-P5-E2025-APP extends classification and extraction inside rwb-document to the new types, adds the field patterns, the review queue and the reader. RWB-S4-E2025-APP consumes the checked fields in rwb-litigation to fill legal actions, hearings and judgments. RWB-S2-E2025-APP consumes them in rwb-treatment for the contract and mortgage values of the treatment record. RWB-P7-E2025-APP records the decisions those steps take. Not one of them can prove on its own that a value read off a scanned court notice travels from intake to the litigation pack, or that a judgment amount read at low confidence is withheld from a reader until a person has checked it. That proof is this story.

The journey is the one the business cares about. A contract, a credit approval, a mortgage document, a court filing, a hearing notice or a judgment arrives; it is classified into one of the eleven types with a confidence; each field is extracted with its own confidence and checked against the pattern held in the type table; a person checks only the uncertain ones; and the checked values reach the case index, the litigation reader and the treatment reader without anyone typing an amount or a date (REQ-DCM-006, REQ-DCM-005). The harness runs that journey against the published contracts of the four services on one business date and produces evidence that can be re-run for any build. REQ-DCM-017 and REQ-DCM-018 enter only as the shape of the journey: the documents, their versions and their dates are the inputs the harness stages, and the electronic discovery answer and the court evidence attributes are not extracted fields and are not asserted here.

The architecture changes the path, not the business. The monolith wrote document_field rows and handed them to the litigation and treatment modules inside one process and one schema. In the target, rwb-document owns the metadata, the OCR text, the fields and the retention (DP-01, schema `rwb_document`); every other service reads fields through the document contract, one hop on `/api/recovery/document/v1` with a 2 s timeout (DP-11, DP-13); the case facts behind the journey come from rwb-case through its contract, including the parameters and the reference data of the type table (DP-06, DP-07); JOB-12 Document intake runs as an event-started workflow, `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` on queue `rwb-document`, so OCR, classification and extraction happen off the request path (DP-10); the document events leave through the outbox on `rwb.document.events.v1` (DP-09); and the screens the officers use are composite routes of gateway-bff, so the same bases the harness calls are the ones the screens call (DP-19). The harness is the place where those boundaries are exercised together, so a broken boundary is found in SIT and not by a litigation officer who cannot see the judgment date.

The measure is the journey evidence: for each owned criterion, one pass or fail with the intake request, the document read, the field rows and their states, the review item, the reader answer at rwb-litigation and at rwb-treatment, and the decision log entry captured in one report.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The wave 2 harness environment (SIT) is available with the gateway route for `/api/recovery/*`, the topics `rwb.document.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the task queue `rwb-document` and the Azure Blob write-once container behind rwb-document. The harness environment, its seeding and its evidence format: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0407; ASM-0582).
- The four integration dependencies have published their contracts, or their contract fakes stand in for them: RWB-P5-E2025-APP (rwb-document), RWB-P7-E2025-APP (rwb-decision), RWB-S4-E2025-APP (the rwb-litigation reader) and RWB-S2-E2025-APP (the rwb-treatment reader).
- Document type table version DOCTYPE-2026.12 is in force from 2026-12-31 with the eleven types, each with its classify_threshold and its field_definitions. Hearing notices stay under the Epic 1 type COURT_NOTICE. Types and fields: CONTRACT (contract_no, party_names, contract_amount, contract_date); CREDIT_APPROVAL (approval_no, approved_amount, approval_date, approval_level); MORTGAGE_DOCUMENT (title_doc_no, mortgage_amount, registration_date, land_office); COURT_FILING (court_name, black_case_no, filing_date, claim_amount); JUDGMENT (court_name, red_case_no, judgment_date, judgment_amount); COURT_NOTICE (court_name, black_case_no, notice_date, hearing_date). Each field carries data type, extraction method, review_only and an optional pattern (legacy section 13; DL19).
- The field threshold is 0.80 and the accuracy pass mark is 0.90 per field on the sample; document_hub_parameter row EXTRACT_ACCURACY_PASS holds 0.90 (legacy sections 3, 7 and 13; DL11).
- The masked sample of 60 documents is staged and masked: 10 each of CONTRACT, CREDIT_APPROVAL, MORTGAGE_DOCUMENT, COURT_FILING, JUDGMENT and COURT_NOTICE (legacy section 7 Background; RWB-TE-004).
- The classifier version that knows the eleven types is selected through the P10 agent runtime, so the classification run has a version to name in the evidence (legacy section 3).
- The feature switch `rwb.dochub.extraction-stage23` is on in the harness profile (legacy section 13).
- Synthetic and masked documents only: no real party name, account number or case document enters the harness or its evidence (legacy section 17).
- No build dependency. Day 1.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: takes the run lock for the environment and records the build ID, the business date and the versions of the four contracts it is about to exercise.
2. Harness: seeds the 60-document masked sample and the DOCTYPE-2026.12 rows (the eleven types, their thresholds, field definitions and patterns in force on the business date) through the seed pack.
3. Harness: records the session it runs under for each test officer (RW-LITOFF of team "LIT-BKK", RW-RESTRUCT, RW-REFADM), with the role, the scope and the Documents right it will exercise.
4. Harness: calls the P3 case operation and records the case state of "RW-2026-000601" and of the team each document belongs to, as the journey starts from it.
5. Harness: uploads each sample document through the P5 intake operation, `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents`, and records the document ID and the returned upload reference; the file itself is handed to Azure Blob through the link rwb-document returns, never by the harness writing a blob.
6. Harness: waits for the extraction window (JOB-12, `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` on queue `rwb-document`) and records the intake state, the predicted type, the classification confidence and the review reason the intake read returns.
7. Harness: reads each document through `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` and records the type, the review status, the write-once flag, the storage reference and every field with its value, confidence and state.
8. Harness: reads the review items of the run through `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/review-items` and records which fields of which document are waiting, with the message the read carries.
9. Harness: confirms or corrects one marked field through `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/review` and, where the correction changes a value, through `PATCH /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/fields/{fieldId}`, then records the state the field moves to.
10. Harness: reads the checked fields as the rwb-litigation reader does, for case "RW-2026-000601" and type "JUDGMENT", and again as the rwb-treatment reader does for the contract values, and records exactly which fields each answer holds and which it withholds.
11. Harness: reads the decision log through `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` and records whether the decision entry of the reviewed field exists with its decision code and final call.
12. Harness: writes the per-scenario evidence into one run report keyed by story key and business date, evaluates the gate, attaches the report to the wave 2 release record and releases the run lock.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A field is below the threshold of 0.80 | The field gets state REVIEW and one review item appears on the P5 review operation for the document | MSG-P5-003 | AC3 |
| X2 | A field's accuracy on the sample is below the pass mark of 0.90 | The field is proposed as review_only in the next table version; the version in force does not change until it is loaded | None | Legacy AC4 (RWB-P5-E2025-APP) |
| X3 | A value does not match the pattern of its field | The field gets state REVIEW and one review item appears | MSG-P5-003 | AC6 |
| X4 | A document arrives before the valid-from date of DOCTYPE-2026.12 | It is classified against the earlier version and goes to review with review_reason UNKNOWN_TYPE | MSG-P5-003 | Legacy AC6 (RWB-P5-E2025-APP) |
| X5 | A reader asks for fields still in REVIEW | The answer holds only fields in state OK, CONFIRMED or CORRECTED; the review field is absent, not blank | None | AC4 |
| X6 | The document is write-once | The field rows are written; the file hash, the storage_ref and write_once are unchanged | None | AC7 |
| X7 | The document is outside the caller's scope | The P5 read answers 404 and the harness records it as the expected answer, not as a run failure | MSG-P4-003 | AC8 |
| X8 | A role without Documents R reads the document | The read answers 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-025-12-ITG |
| X9 | The seeded data cannot be loaded (type table row missing, sample document absent, case not as the scenario states) | The run refuses to start and names the missing seed item; no scenario is reported | None | All |
| X10 | The evidence pack cannot be attached to the release record | The run is marked failed; the local evidence file is kept for the rerun | None | All |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the four published contracts or their fakes and the SIT harness profile; it builds no service feature and has no build dependency |
| Negotiable | The scenarios, the seeded sample values and the type table rows are data files, never code |
| Valuable | The extraction journey is proven once across four services, before the app stories claim Done |
| Estimable | One journey runner, one fake set, one sample pack, one assertion set per reader and one gate |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each owned criterion has a fixed Given, When and Then and a recorded result in the run report |

The legacy ACs of RWB-E2-025 are owned by the four app stories of this legacy key. Legacy AC4 (a field below the pass mark proposed as review-only), legacy AC5 (classification into the new types with the confusion matrix) and legacy AC6 (a document before the valid-from date) are cited in the flow and exception table because the harness stages their inputs, and they stay with RWB-P5-E2025-APP. The eight criteria above are the ones this ITG story owns, and each tests only the integration deliverable.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The stage 2 and 3 types and their fields are those of the document type table version in force on the extraction date | Document types reference table; DL19; R-UNI-38 |
| BR2 | A field below the threshold, failing its pattern, or marked review-only has state REVIEW and sends the document to the review queue | RWB-E1-053 BR2, BR3; REQ-DCM-005 |
| BR3 | A field whose accuracy on the sample is below the pass mark is proposed as review-only; the proposal takes effect only when loaded | EXTRACT_ACCURACY_PASS (0.90 assumed); DL11; CTL-08 |
| BR4 | Each field may carry a pattern in field_definitions; the pattern is data | Principle 1; RWB-E1-053 BR5 |
| BR5 | Readers in other modules receive only fields in state OK, CONFIRMED or CORRECTED | FEAT-DCM-10 |
| BR6 | Extraction never changes the stored file of a write-once document | CTL-12 |
| BR7 | Party names and other personal field values are masked unless the role may see them | DF-DOC-015; CTL-11; DL26 |
| BR8 | Dates read in Buddhist Era are stored as ISO dates | RWB-E1-053 BR6 |

The rules are unchanged by the split. The harness asserts them across the service boundaries and restates none of them in code.

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status and no service state moves because of the harness. It observes document_field.state (OK, REVIEW, CONFIRMED, CORRECTED) and document.review_status as the P5 operations set them, and it asserts the state a field is in after each read.

The harness adds a run state of its own only: Not started, Running, Passed, Failed, with the latest run for a build deciding the gate.
