##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test asset in the integration pipeline and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` | P5 rwb-document | Reads the document, its type, its review status, its write-once flag and every field with its state (AC2, AC3, AC5, AC6, AC7) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` | P5 rwb-document | Reads the document set of the case and the index the litigation reader sees (AC1, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/review-items` | P5 rwb-document | Asserts that the low-confidence field produced one review item (AC3) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/review` | P5 rwb-document | Confirms or corrects a marked field and records the state it moves to (AC4) |
| PATCH | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/fields/{fieldId}` | P5 rwb-document | Corrects the value of one field where the scenario corrects rather than confirms (AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | Reads the case state the journey starts from and the team the case belongs to (AC8) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | P7 rwb-decision | Asserts the decision entry of the reviewed field with its decision code and final call (flow step 11) |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with the 2 s timeout and the breaker of DP-11, and the two write calls carry an Idempotency-Key per scenario. The case document set read, `GET /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents`, is the index that the SCR-30 list consumes, so AC1 and AC4 assert it and not only the single-document read. The harness also reads the session of each test officer through `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` (P4 rwb-access) to record the role, the scope and the Documents right the journey runs under; that call is the harness's identity step, is not asserted as a journey outcome, and is therefore not one of the seven rows above. The intake upload of flow step 5 is `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents`, the operation named by RWB-P5-E2025-APP; the harness uses it to stage the sample and does not assert it beyond the document ID it returns.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; the evidence goes to the release record through its pipeline integration.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` | `rwb.document.events.v1` | P5 rwb-document | Confirms that the intake of each sample document reached the topic inside the run window, so the extraction window of JOB-12 can be waited on deterministically |
| `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` | `rwb.document.events.v1` | P5 rwb-document | Confirms that the field rows of each document were written and offered to the consumers, alongside the document read of 12.2 (DP-09) |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 rwb-decision (ledger); every service publishes its own record | Confirms that the reviewed field's decision reached the shared ledger topic inside the run window |

The harness subscribes with its own consumer group and asserts the event, never the producer's table. A duplicate is expected and deduplicated on the harness side, so a re-run of the same business date is deterministic.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

JOB-12 Document intake is observed, not built. The harness waits for the `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` on queue `rwb-document` to finish OCR, classification and extraction for the sample, and records the intake state and the time the window took. JOB-11 Outbox sender is observed too: the harness waits for the relay window and records that the two document events and the decision record left their outboxes.

No workflow is built, no activity is added and no schedule is created by this story. The classifier and extractor runs behind `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` belong to RWB-P5-E2025-APP; the harness records their version from the field rows it reads.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The harness run is started by the test pipeline, not by a Temporal Schedule and not by Airflow. JOB-12's own trigger is rwb-document's and is only observed.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no table in any schema (DP-01); it reads and writes through the operations of 12.2 only.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Contract | What it answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| WireMock rwb-document | The five document operations of 12.2 | OpenAPI of P5 | The document with its type, review status, write-once flag and fields at the confidences and states of the scenario; 404 with MSG-P4-003 for the out-of-scope document; 403 with MSG-P4-002 for the role without Documents R; the review item and the state after a confirm or a correction |
| WireMock rwb-case | `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | OpenAPI of P3 | Case "RW-2026-000601", its team and its state, and the team of the case that holds "DOC-0605" |
| WireMock rwb-decision | `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | OpenAPI of P7 | The decision entry of the reviewed field with its decision code and final call |
| Classifier stand-in | The classify step inside `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` | The P5 internal contract, not in this workspace | A type and a confidence per sample document, with "JUDGMENT" for "DOC-0602" and "DOC-0603" and "CONTRACT" at 0.9300 for "DOC-0601" |
| Extractor stand-in | The extract step inside `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` | The P5 internal contract, not in this workspace | The field values, confidences and states of the scenario, including judgment_amount at 0.7100, red_case_no at 0.9200 and judgment_date "2027-03-05" |
| rwb-litigation reader consumer | The reader contract RWB-S4-E2025-APP publishes | OpenAPI of S4 | The checked fields it received for case "RW-2026-000601" and type "JUDGMENT", recorded in the evidence |
| rwb-treatment reader consumer | The reader contract RWB-S2-E2025-APP publishes | OpenAPI of S2 | The checked contract fields it received for the case, recorded in the evidence |

Each fake is replaced by the real service as its integration dependency lands, without a change to the scenarios. The harness repository, its environment, the fake versions and the evidence format: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0407; ASM-0582).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 7 consumed and asserted, one hop on the owner's base with the 2 s timeout of DP-11, plus the P4 session identity step |
| Kafka | 3 events consumed, two on `rwb.document.events.v1` and one on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; none published |
| Temporal | Observed only: JOB-12 `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` and JOB-11 outbox relay on queue `rwb-document`; no workflow, activity or schedule added |
| File | No service file interface is called. The masked sample files are harness test data, uploaded through the P5 intake operation; the harness writes no blob and reads no blob |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `integration/recovery-document-extraction` in the ACE repository, package `<ACE base package>.recovery.integration.documentextraction`. Not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added | How this harness applies it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none | The harness owns no table and reads no schema; every field value in the evidence comes from a P5 operation, never from `rwb_document` |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON | The threshold and the pass mark the harness asserts are read as parameters, so a change is a parameter load and not a harness release |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The eleven types, their thresholds, field definitions and patterns are seeded reference data, never values in the harness code |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON | The harness consumes `DocumentStored`, `DocumentFieldsExtracted` and `DecisionRecorded` with its own consumer group and asserts the events, never the producer's table |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON | JOB-12 is observed as the event-started `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` on queue `rwb-document`; the harness waits for its window and adds no Schedule and no workflow |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) | Each consumed operation is called once from the harness with a 2 s timeout, so the boundary a screen would cross is the one under test |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none | Every path of 12.2 uses the owner's base, so the harness never calls a monolith base and the reader paths of S4 and S2 are the target ones |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The journey runs through the gateway route the real screens use, on the same bases, so a routing defect fails the harness before an officer sees it |

The platform H dependencies in the table (H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, H RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are delivered by the platform waves and are not repeated in the metadata: the harness converges on them and has no build dependency of its own. The blocking dependencies of this story are the four I stories, which replace the fakes with real services one at a time.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Job | Runs the twelve flow steps for one scenario and one business date, and stops at the first failed assertion with the trace |
| FakeRegistry | Configuration | WireMock mappings for rwb-document, rwb-case and rwb-decision, one set per contract version |
| SamplePack | Data | The 60 masked documents, their labels, and the type table rows of DOCTYPE-2026.12 with the patterns and the pass mark as data |
| FieldAssertion | Service | Compares the type, the value, the confidence and the state of every field of a document with the scenario |
| ReaderAssertion | Service | Compares the checked fields the rwb-litigation and rwb-treatment readers received with what they may see (BR5, BR7) |
| EvidenceCollector | Service | Writes one report keyed by story key and business date, with the intake request, the document read, the review item, the reader answers and the decision entry |
| GateEvaluator | Service | Passes the run when every owned scenario passes and the evidence pack is attached to the release record |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, the wave 2 harness profile, one business date, the 60-document masked sample and synthetic case "RW-2026-000601". The seeded values are the legacy Background and the state each scenario names; no other value is added, and no production record is copied. A run starts from the seeded state, so a repeated run is deterministic and produces the same report. The harness environment, the seeding and the evidence format: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0407; ASM-0582).

**Build steps**

1. Write SamplePack with the 60 masked documents, their labels and the DOCTYPE-2026.12 rows; test that a bad seed stops the run (X9).
2. Write FakeRegistry for the three services and the classifier and extractor stand-ins behind the P5 contract, and prove the harness runs green on the fakes alone from Day 1.
3. Write JourneyRunner for AC1 and AC2: intake, the JOB-12 window, the document read and the field assertion on value, confidence and state.
4. Add AC5 and AC6 with the Buddhist Era normalisation and the pattern check, both asserted from the field rows the P5 read returns.
5. Add AC3 and AC7: the review item and MSG-P5-003 on the low-confidence field, and the unchanged file hash, storage_ref and write_once on the write-once document.
6. Add AC4 and AC8: the confirm and correct path through the review and field operations, then the reader answers at rwb-litigation and rwb-treatment, and the out-of-scope 404.
7. Write EvidenceCollector and GateEvaluator, attach the report to the wave 2 release record, and rerun the eight scenarios on the release build; replace each fake with the real service as its I story lands.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.dochub.extraction-stage23` is on in the harness profile, as the legacy story sets it; off, the new types are not offered to classification and the reader returns nothing for them, and the harness records that state rather than failing. The harness itself is a pipeline stage selected by the run profile, not by a business flag.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the run report is attached to the wave 2 release record with all eight owned scenarios, the field accuracy of the court notices is at or above 0.90 on the sample, and each fake has been replaced by the real service where its I story has landed in SIT.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-003 | A document has a field in REVIEW | Some fields need checking. The document is in the review queue. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Caller lacks Documents R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Document outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The document store is unavailable | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

The harness asserts these messages and never rewrites them. Its own report text is for the release team and is not part of the message standard. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

No screen is built by this story. The harness drives the operations behind those screens and asserts the states above through the contracts; the screens themselves belong to RWB-P5-E2025-APP and to the review story of the document hub.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the types, the fields, the patterns, the threshold of 0.80 and the pass mark of 0.90 are data and parameters; no class per document type and no pattern in the harness source.
- No personal data in logs, events, evidence or prompts: party names, amounts and case documents never enter a log or an event, the sample is masked, and the report holds identifiers, confidences and states only.
- No read of another service's tables, and no schema of the harness's own: every read and write goes through the operations of 12.2 (DP-01). The harness writes nothing to legal_action, hearing or treatment.
- The Epic 1 results are unchanged: the RWB-E1-053 regression set runs beside the harness and the six Epic 1 types keep their results.
- Each fake is replaced by the real service as its I story lands; a fake that outlives its service is a defect, not a configuration.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and an exception is never added to a scenario; a value that must change changes in the sample pack or the type table through a reviewed change.

##### 19. Out of scope

- Writing extracted values into legal_action, hearing or treatment (S4 in Epic 5, S2 in Epic 3). The harness proves what the readers receive, not what they store.
- Litigation pack assembly and the defect list check (FEAT-LIT-04, FEAT-LIT-05, Epic 5).
- Generation of contract, credit approval and mortgage documents (RWB-E2-026).
- Electronic discovery and court evidence attributes (REQ-DCM-017, REQ-DCM-018); they enter only as journey inputs, not as extracted fields.
- The production code of any service: the classifier version, the extractor, the review queue, the reader implementations and every screen stay with their app stories.

The harness, the fakes and the evidence pack cover the items above only as a caller or a consumer would see them; building any of them is out of scope for this story.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the contract baseline of the generation API of `rwb-document` is split out of legacy RWB-E2-026 and published on base `/api/recovery/document/v1` with the topic `rwb.document.events.v1`, the provider contracts and the fakes. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of the generation API of `rwb-document` — the generate operation on base `/api/recovery/document/v1` with its `GenerateRequest`, `GenerationResult` and `Document` shapes, the four provider interfaces it consumes with their owner and their fake, the error envelope with its message IDs, the `Idempotency-Key` rule, the `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` event schema and the decision record on `rwb.decision-record.v1`**, so that **the app story of this legacy key, the screens story, the template catalog consumers and the wave 2 integration harness build against a fixed, testable contract on Day 1, and a renamed field, a differently read template version or a silent missing merge value can never drift between two services without a failing build**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020). Legacy RWB-E2-026 exposes the generation engine as an in-process `DocumentGenerator` interface inside one module, with a `TemplateCatalog`, a `TreatmentReader` and a `MergeFieldProvider` implemented by other modules, and reads the template catalog, the case facts, the treatment, the party and collateral facts and the decision log across module boundaries. Under the target architecture each of those becomes a contract of another service, and the shapes most likely to drift silently are exactly the ones this engine depends on:

- a field renamed in `GenerateRequest`, `GenerationResult` or the `Document` answer, so the screens story reads a document without its version;
- a template version read differently by two consumers, so the same case yields two different Legal-approved versions on the same date;
- a missing merge field answered 200 with an empty value, so a document reaches a customer with a blank amount;
- an event payload changed, so `rwb-case` or `rwb-agent` receives a `DocumentStored` it cannot read;
- an error returned with the wrong status or without a `messageId`, so a caller cannot tell a withdrawn template from a missing one.

The baseline fixes the names the checks require: schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`. It makes the C dependencies of the app story explicit - the P6 template catalog (C `RWB-P6-E1046-CON`), the P3 parameters and reference lists (C `RWB-P3-E1042-CON`, `RWB-P3-E1043-CON`) and the P7 central ledger (C `RWB-P7-E1027-CON`) - and it records that the P3 case contract, the S2 treatment contract and the P1 source-data contract are consumed and faked although the plan lists them in no C row (`ASM-1933`).

It also records the naming conflict the sources carry: the Ownership Map and TSD P5 API-P5-016 name `POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents`, while Architecture v5 slide 16 names `POST /documents/generate`. The baseline declares the Ownership Map name and records the loser as `GAP-1024` and `ASM-1934`. Nothing else is guessed: the field-level names this key does not settle carry the placeholder `Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1024; ASM-1930)`.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the operation, topic, event and queue names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice.
- The platform error envelope, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the retry and `.dlt` topic convention are the platform baseline (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- TSD P5 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2 are in force for API-P5-016, and TSD P5 T3.1 is in force for the `document` and `document_type` definitions the `Document` shape draws on.
- The Ownership Map is the only source of owners: `document`, `document_type`, `document_hub_parameter` and `document_field` are P5's in `rwb_document`; `template` and `merge_field` are P6's in `rwb_comms`; `recovery_case`, `lov_value`, `parameter_catalog` and `reference_row` are P3's; `treatment` is S2's; `decision_log_entry` is P7's; the ACE views and `sys_fields` are P1's.
- The `rwb-comms` template catalog baseline RWB-P6-E1046-CON is published, so the template version and the merge field list this generation API consumes have one owner document and one fake.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document of `rwb-document` with the generate operation, the three resources of section 11 and the error responses of section 14, on the single base `/api/recovery/document/v1`.
2. Fix the generate resource: the path, the `treatmentId` and `templateCodes` parameters with the 1 to 10 bound, the `language` default, the 201 answer, the `Idempotency-Key` header and the declared Documents right C.
3. Fix the `Document` shape, so the screens story reads one answer with the document identifier, the case, the type, the source, the storage reference, the retention class, the write-once flag, the document version and the template code, version and treatment.
4. Fix the four provider interfaces with their owners and their typed answers: the template catalog current version and merge field list, the treatment read, the merge field provider and the decision record.
5. Map every failure to the error envelope and a message ID, status by status, and carry the naming conflict and the missing C rows as gap rows.
6. Record the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the 24-hour window, and state the stored-answer behaviour of a repeat.
7. Declare the event position: `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` on `rwb.document.events.v1` with five payload fields and no personal data, the record on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and no third event for this key.
8. Publish the six fakes, the drift test and the baseline tag, then hand the baseline to RWB-P5-E2026-APP, RWB-P5-E2017-APP and the wave 2 harness.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A response body fails schema validation | The build fails on the schema lint; a deployed service answers 500 with the error envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X2 | A field is renamed, removed or retyped within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a corrected document or a new major version | None | AC2, AC3 |
| X3 | The template version is read on a different rule by two consumers | The contract test fails on the date, language and product group rule | None | AC4 |
| X4 | A provider answers an unknown or missing merge field with 200 | The contract test fails: the answer must name the field as missing, and the app answers 422 with MSG-P5-009 | MSG-P5-009 | AC4, AC5 |
| X5 | The event payload changes, a sixth field is added, or a personal value appears in it | The AsyncAPI schema test and the no-personal-data test fail | None | AC7 |
| X6 | A contract fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and the merge is blocked | None | AC8 |
| X7 | A third event is declared for this key | The absence test fails: only `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` and `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` exist for `rwb-document`, and this key publishes the first of them | None | AC8 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Criterion | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Independent | Pass | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, TSD P5 T-A, the Ownership Map and the P6 catalog baseline only |
| Negotiable | Pass | The field-level names are settled with the consumers; the operation shape, the provider set, the error mapping, the event schema and the idempotency rule are fixed by the target architecture and the legacy section 12 |
| Valuable | Pass | Unblocks RWB-P5-E2026-APP, RWB-P5-E2017-APP and the wave 2 harness on Day 1 |
| Estimable | Pass | One document, three resources, one operation, four provider interfaces, nine contract tables and six fakes |
| Small | Pass | Fits one sprint with its contract tests |
| Testable | Pass | Every criterion in section 7 is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

```gherkin
    When they are compared with the legacy section 12 answer and the TSD P5 T3.1 document fields
    Then GenerationResult carries decisionLogEntryId and documents as an array of Document
    Then Document carries documentId, caseId, documentType, source, storageRef, retentionClass, writeOnce, docVersion, templateCode, templateVersion, treatmentId and state
    Then documentId, caseId, documentType, source and docVersion are required and every other property is optional, so a consumer of the previous version keeps working
    Then source is one of "SCAN", "UPLOAD", "GENERATED", "PARTNER" and "EMAIL" of LOV-DOC-SOURCE and state is "DRAFT" for a generated document
    Then the example carries templateCode "DIL-CONTRACT", templateVersion 2, treatmentId "TRT-0301", documentType "CONTRACT", source "GENERATED" and docVersion 1
    Then a generated document declares writeOnce false, so the write-once switch on send belongs to RWB-P5-E2017-APP

  Scenario: AC4 The four provider interfaces carry their owner and their typed answer (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the provider interfaces declared in the document
    When they are compared with the legacy section 12 published interfaces and the Ownership Map
    Then TemplateCatalog.current(templateCode, language, productGroup, asOf) answers a TemplateVersion with the version, its Legal approval, its valid-from date and its product group, and names P6 rwb-comms as its owner
    Then TemplateCatalog.mergeFields(templateId) answers a list of MergeField with the code, the required flag and the format, and names P6 rwb-comms as its owner
    Then TreatmentReader.find(treatmentId) answers a TreatmentSummary with the type, the approval and the decision log reference, and names S2 rwb-treatment as its owner
    Then MergeFieldProvider.resolve(caseId, treatmentId, mergeFieldCodes) answers the values by code and names P3 rwb-case, S2 rwb-treatment and P1 rwb-source-data as its owners
    Then DecisionRecord writes the record with decision code "D6.4" and final call "GENERATED" and names P7 rwb-decision as the owner of the central ledger
    Then every provider answer marks a missing required field as missing and never as an empty value
    Then the case read, the treatment read, the source-data read and the ledger read are recorded in GAP-1024 because the plan lists them in no C row

  Scenario: AC5 The error envelope and the status mapping are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the error responses declared for the generate operation
    When each status is compared with the legacy section 12 errors and section 14
    Then 401 answers MSG-P4-001, 403 answers MSG-P4-002, and 404 answers MSG-P4-003 for a case or a treatment that is not found or lies outside the scope
    Then 409 answers MSG-P5-011 for a treatment that is not approved or not open, and MSG-GEN-004 for a concurrent request
    Then 422 answers MSG-P5-009 for a missing merge value, MSG-P5-010 for a template that is not approved or not found, MSG-P6-003 for a withdrawn template and MSG-GEN-001 for empty templateCodes
    Then 503 answers MSG-P7-003 for a failed decision record and MSG-GEN-006 for a failed render or a failed consumed call
    Then every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with messageId, detail and instance, and a refusal returns no partial document set and no decision record

  Scenario: AC6 The Idempotency-Key rule and the 24-hour window are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the Idempotency-Key rule of the generate operation
    When it is compared with the legacy section 12 idempotency row and the parameter GEN_IDEMPOTENCY_HOURS
    Then the header is required on the POST and a repeat with the same key inside the window answers the first stored answer with 201
    Then a repeat creates no second document, no second decision record and no second event
    Then the window is the parameter GEN_IDEMPOTENCY_HOURS, whose value is 24, read through the parameters contract and never written in code
    Then the template bound of the request is the parameter GEN_MAX_TEMPLATES, whose value is 10, read the same way
    Then the concurrent case is answered 409 with MSG-GEN-004 and never by a second stored set

  Scenario: AC7 The DocumentStored event and the decision record are declared schemas (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the AsyncAPI fragment of this baseline and the record declaration of the document
    When they are compared with the service catalogue and TSD P5 T5.3
    Then rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 is declared on the topic rwb.document.events.v1, keyed by caseId, with the five payload fields documentId, caseId, documentType, source and storedAt
    Then the envelope is CloudEvents 1.0 in binary mode and the payload carries no personal value, no merge value and no file byte
    Then the decision record is declared on rwb.decision-record.v1 with the decision code D6.4, the final call GENERATED and a reference to the merge snapshot rather than the snapshot itself
    Then the document states that the store RWB-P5-E1024-APP writes the DocumentStored row per stored document and that this key declares the schema and publishes nothing itself

  Scenario: AC8 The six fakes match the document and no third event is declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the contract section of this story
    When the nine sub-tables are reviewed and the fakes are run against the document
    Then each of 12.1 to 12.9 is present and names its owner from the Ownership Map, with None where the element is empty
    Then the six fakes of 12.8 answer the operation of 12.1 and the eight reads of 12.2 with the values of the legacy examples, including template "DIL-CONTRACT" version 2, treatment "TRT-0301" and the date 2026-12-10
    Then the drift test compares each fake with the document and fails on any mismatch of a path, a status, a field name or a required flag
    Then only rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1 and rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1 exist for rwb-document, and the absence test fails a build that declares a third event on this key
```

The eight criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only; they restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P5-E2026-APP. The legacy AC1 to AC14 of RWB-E2-026 are owned by RWB-P5-E2026-APP, and the wave 2 harness RWB-ITG-E2026-ITG consumes this baseline and copies none of these criteria.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/document/v1` on every declared operation | DP-01; Template and Rules §R4; Architecture v5 slide 41 notes |
| BR2 | One topic per service: `rwb.document.events.v1`, with the retry and `.dlt` topics of the platform convention | DP-09; Architecture v5 slides 16 and 42 |
| BR3 | A change inside major version 1 is additive; a removed, renamed or retyped property and a narrowed required set are a new major version | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility) |
| BR4 | The document declares only tables of `rwb_document` and only operations owned by `rwb-document`; a consumed operation is described as consumed and faked, never as provided | Ownership Map; DP-01 |
| BR5 | This key publishes no event of its own invention: the service has exactly `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` and `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1`, and this key declares the first | TSD P5 T5.3; Architecture v5 slides 16, 41 and 43 |
| BR6 | No business value is fixed in the contract: template codes, merge codes, type mapping, decision code, dates, the idempotency window and the template bound stay data rows or parameters of the app story | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; RWB-E2-026 section 17 |
| BR7 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, codes, versions, dates and amounts only, and no customer name, address, national ID number or title-doc number in any payload | Architecture v5 slide 11; RWB-E2-026 BR11 and section 17 |
| BR8 | No file byte, merge value or merge snapshot in any payload: the record carries the reference to the snapshot and the document carries `storageRef` only | DP-09; RWB-E2-026 section 17 |
| BR9 | Every consumed row states one hop, a 2 s timeout, a GET retry once with jitter and a breaker per downstream, and a failed read maps to MSG-GEN-006 naming the system that failed | DP-11, ADR-020; Architecture v5 slide 11 |
| BR10 | Every error uses one envelope and one message ID per condition; the message texts are copied unchanged from legacy RWB-E2-026 section 14 | Architecture v5 platform baseline; Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR11 | A POST requires `Idempotency-Key` and stores its answer, so a repeat inside the window creates nothing; a GET declares none | Architecture v5 slide 11; DP-09 |
| BR12 | The contract declares no case state and no document state machine beyond the values the fields may take; a transition belongs to the app story that performs it | RWB-E2-026 section 9; RWB-P5-E2017-APP owns send and review |

##### 9. State transitions

| Baseline state | Event | Condition | Next state |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The operation, the three resources, the four provider interfaces and the eight consumed rows are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | RWB-P5-E2026-APP, RWB-P5-E2017-APP, the P6 catalog owner and the wave 2 harness accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1, for example a new optional field on `Document` | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, or a required set is narrowed | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake, or a retired element returns | A contract test fails | In review |

This baseline declares no case state machine and no document state machine of its own. The value `DRAFT` is the value of the `state` property of a generated document; the creation of that state, the review out of it and the write-once switch on send are the app stories', and the treatment state and the template state belong to `rwb-treatment` and `rwb-comms`.

| Field value in the baseline | Meaning declared by this document |
|---|---|
| `source` = "GENERATED" | A document produced by this engine; the other values of LOV-DOC-SOURCE belong to the intake paths |
| `state` = "DRAFT" | A generated document that is not yet sent and is therefore not write-once |
| `writeOnce` = false | The value of a generated draft; the switch on send is RWB-P5-E2017-APP |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-document | Owns the OpenAPI document, the AsyncAPI fragment and the six fakes; tags the baseline |
| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change, a new major version, the naming resolution of GAP-1024 and the correction of the plan's C list for the case, S2, P1 and P7 reads |
| Consuming teams (RWB-P5-E2026-APP, RWB-P5-E2017-APP, the P6 catalog owner, the P3 and P1 owners, the P7 owner and the wave 2 harness) | Review and sign off the parts they consume |
| RW-LEGAL, Legal counsel | Confirms that the approved version of a template is a precondition of the answer and never an option of the request (Documents A on the P6 catalog) |
| Platform library owner | Owns the CloudEvents envelope, the error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the naming rule this document reuses |
| Data steward | Confirms that no personal data field is declared in an answer, an example or a fake |

The per-service login behind the document's security scheme is not part of this baseline; the document names the scheme "the rwb-document login (DP-02)" and the name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1024; ASM-1928). The declared area and right are enforced at gateway-bff (DP-19); no `rwb-access` contract is declared here.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| GenerateRequest | treatmentId (uuid, required), templateCodes (array of string, 1 to 10, required), language (TH or EN, default TH), overrides (optional, used by RWB-P5-E2017-APP) |
| GenerationResult | decisionLogEntryId, documents (array of Document) |
| Document | documentId, caseId, documentType, source, storageRef, retentionClass, writeOnce, docVersion, templateCode, templateVersion, treatmentId, state, from the `document` fields DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-011, DF-DOC-032 and DF-DOC-033 |
| TemplateVersion | version, approvedByLegal, validFrom, productGroup, language, mergeFieldCodes; read through C `RWB-P6-E1046-CON` and never copied |
| MergeField | mergeCode, required, format, sourceEntity and sourceField; read through C `RWB-P6-E1046-CON` |
| TreatmentSummary | treatmentId, treatmentType, approved, decisionLogId, outcome; read through the S2 contract |
| MergeFieldValue set | The values by merge code answered by the P3, S2 and P1 providers; never persisted by this service |
| DecisionRecord | decisionCode, finalCall, inputsRef, decidedAt and the chain fields of the library; decision code D6.4, final call GENERATED |
| Error envelope | RFC 9457 problem details with `messageId`, `detail`, `instance` and the status of section 14 |

Every example in the document is synthetic and uses the legacy values: template "DIL-CONTRACT" version 2, treatment "TRT-0301", the date 2026-12-10, the decision code "D6.4", the parameter values 24 and 10 and the identifiers of the legacy cases. No example carries a real customer value; the legacy values are examples only. The field-level names of `TemplateVersion`, `MergeField`, `TreatmentSummary` and `DecisionRecord` beyond what the legacy section 12 names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1024; ASM-1930).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-document (P5); base `/api/recovery/document/v1`.

| Method | Path | API ID | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/generated-documents` | API-P5-016 | Request `GenerateRequest`; answer 201 `GenerationResult` | Documents C, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header, 24-hour window |

Error statuses 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 are those of T-A.2 and section 14. The path is the Ownership Map and TSD P5 API-P5-016 name; the Architecture v5 slide 16 name `POST /documents/generate` is recorded as the loser of the conflict `GAP-1024` with the assumption `ASM-1934`, and it is declared nowhere in the document.

`POST /documents/{documentId}/regenerate` (API-P5-017) is this service's operation and belongs to the contract of RWB-P5-E2017-CON; this baseline references it and claims neither its shape nor its path as its own.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | the template catalog current version | P6 rwb-comms | `TemplateCatalog.current`: the version, its Legal approval, its valid-from date and its product group; the path is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1024; ASM-1921); the owner document is C `RWB-P6-E1046-CON` |
| GET | the template catalog merge field list | P6 rwb-comms | `TemplateCatalog.mergeFields`: the merge codes, their required flag and their format; same owner document |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case facts of the merge fields, faked (C `RWB-P3-E1042-CON` is the parameters contract of the app story; the case contract `RWB-P3-E1018-CON` is in no C row and is carried by `ASM-1933`) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}` | S2 rwb-treatment | The treatment type, approval and `decision_log_id`; consumed and faked, and in no C row of the plan (`ASM-1933`) |
| GET | the party and collateral read of the source data | P1 rwb-source-data | The customer name and the title-doc number, masked by policy; consumed and faked, path Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1024; ASM-1933) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters/{paramCode}` | P3 rwb-case | `GEN_IDEMPOTENCY_HOURS` and `GEN_MAX_TEMPLATES` (C `RWB-P3-E1042-CON`) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | The type mapping and language lists (C `RWB-P3-E1043-CON`) |
| POST | the central ledger sealing operation | P7 rwb-decision | The seal of the local D6.4 record (C `RWB-P7-E1027-CON`) |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retry once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (DP-11, ADR-020). A failed read maps to 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming the system that failed and never to an accepted generation. The case contract, the S2 treatment contract, the P1 source-data contract and the P7 read are consumed by the generation API; the plan's C list names the P6 catalog, the P3 parameters and lists and the P7 ledger only, so those four rows carry `ASM-1933` and no row is added to the metadata C list.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Declared schema |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` | `rwb.document.events.v1` | P5 rwb-document | Key caseId; payload documentId, caseId, documentType, source, storedAt; CloudEvents 1.0 binary mode; no personal data, no merge value, no file byte |
| decision record | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library, consumed by P7 | The hash-chained record with decision code D6.4, final call GENERATED and `inputsRef` naming the merge snapshot, never the snapshot |

This baseline declares the event schema and the record declaration because the service owns the topic; the `DocumentStored` row itself is written by the store RWB-P5-E1024-APP in its own transaction, and this key publishes nothing at run time. The service's other event, `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1`, is declared in the same topic by the extraction stories and is named here only to fix the count. No third event exists for `rwb-document`.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The generation path subscribes to no topic: the treatment, the case, the source data, the parameters, the lists and the catalog are synchronous reads, and the trigger is the HTTP request. A change of a template version reaches this engine on its next read.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Kind | Queue | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `generate` | Activity contract | `rwb-document` | One typed activity interface with `GenerationRequest` in and `GenerationResult` out, idempotent by the request key; called synchronously by the controller and by the screens story; no workflow is declared here |

No workflow is declared by this baseline. `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` of the L3 workflow kit template "Document intake" is owned by RWB-P5-E1049-APP and only its generate step is named.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. This baseline declares no Schedule, no cron entry and no job name; JOB-17 retention belongs to RWB-P5-E1017-APP.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| `document` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | The `Document` shape and the columns the answer carries, with the keys of RWB-P5-E2026-APP section 11 |
| `document_type` | P5 (`rwb_document`) | Contracted use only: the document type and the retention class behind the template-to-type mapping |
| decision-record library table | PLT library, created in `rwb_document` | The D6.4 record the operation writes |
| outbox, inbox and idempotency library tables | PLT library, created in `rwb_document` | The idempotency row behind `Idempotency-Key` and the service's event envelope objects |

`template` and `merge_field` are P6's, `recovery_case`, `lov_value`, `parameter_catalog` and `reference_row` are P3's, `treatment` is S2's, `decision_log_entry` is P7's and the ACE views, `sys_fields` and `sys_objects` are P1's; they are named as consumed answers and never declared as this service's tables (DP-01).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** The OpenAPI 3.1 document `openapi/rwb-document-v1.yaml` with the generate operation and the three resources; the AsyncAPI 3.0 fragment for `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` and the record declaration; the contract README rows for the provider ownership, the error mapping, the idempotency window and the event count; and the six WireMock mapping sets of section 12.8.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The H, C, I and X lists of the metadata table are empty: this baseline adds no build dependency of its own (it is Day 1 by rule), and the platform and service contracts it names are the ones the app story declares. DP-05 appears because the legacy `AceSourceQuery` read is replaced by the P1 contract; DP-15 and DP-19 appear because the migration step and the screen route are recorded here for the app story to use.

**Build steps**

1. Write the generate operation with its path, parameters, resources and error responses; validate the document in the pipeline.
2. Fix the required and optional sets of AC2 and AC3 and the 1 to 10 bound as schema constraints and README rows.
3. Declare the four provider interfaces with their owners, their typed answers and the missing-field rule of AC4.
4. Map every status and message ID of AC5 and record the RFC 9457 envelope.
5. Record the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the 24-hour window of AC6, and the two parameter names as parameters rather than values.
6. Declare the `DocumentStored` schema and the record of AC7, with the absence test for a third event.
7. Publish the six fakes and the eight contract tests, including the drift test; tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off of RWB-P5-E2026-APP, RWB-P5-E2017-APP and the wave 2 harness.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI artefact and the AsyncAPI fragment validate in the pipeline, the eight contract tests pass, the six fakes answer every operation and read of sections 12.1 and 12.2, the drift test is green, and RWB-P5-E2026-APP and RWB-ITG-E2026-ITG have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-009 | A required merge field has no value (new) | {template} cannot be generated. {field} has no value on the case. |
| MSG-P5-010 | No current template version approved by Legal (new) | {template} has no version approved by Legal for {product} in {language}. |
| MSG-P5-011 | The treatment is not approved or not open (new) | Documents can be generated only for an approved {treatment} that is still open. |
| MSG-P6-003 | The template is withdrawn | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | templateCodes is empty | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A concurrent request for the same treatment and template | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The renderer fails | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Caller lacks Documents C | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |

The message IDs and the wording are contract elements copied unchanged from RWB-E2-026 section 14; Thai text for each follows decision DL10.

Delivery shape: every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set to the ID above, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled, and `instance` naming the request. The status mapping is the legacy one, fixed by AC5: 401 with MSG-P4-001, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 with MSG-P4-003, 409 with MSG-P5-011 or MSG-GEN-004, 422 with MSG-P5-009, MSG-P5-010, MSG-P6-003 or MSG-GEN-001, and 503 with MSG-P7-003 or MSG-GEN-006. For MSG-GEN-006 the {system} value is fixed by the consumed row that failed.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-30 Case documents is the screen the generated drafts appear on, in state DRAFT; the generation screens, their overrides form and the review and send actions are RWB-P5-E2017-APP. The contract serves them through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which calls the owner once and merges the answers into the screen model; this baseline fixes the answer shapes only and declares no screen field list and no route specification. The screen states the baseline implies are the ones the `Document` shape carries: a generated document in DRAFT with `writeOnce` false, a version number, and the template code and version it was produced from.

The sixteen legacy test cases of RWB-E2-026 are listed in the order of the WP and the legacy story; each is answered here at contract level against the artefact and the fakes, and its business outcome is proved by RWB-P5-E2026-APP. TC-E2-026-15 keeps the legacy level Access and maps to Component, TC-E2-026-16 keeps the legacy level Resilience and maps to NFR, and the System level of the others maps to Contract because the artefact under test is the contract. The integration harness copies end in `-ITG` and belong to RWB-ITG-E2026-ITG. The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same test case ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: template codes, merge codes, the type mapping, the decision code, the dates, the idempotency window and the template bound stay data rows or parameters of the app story.
- No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, codes, versions, dates and amounts only; no customer name, address, national ID number or title-doc number is declared in any answer.
- No merge value, no merge snapshot and no file byte in a payload, an example, a fake or a log; the record carries `inputsRef` and the document carries `storageRef`.
- No template body is declared: the catalog answer names a version and a merge field list, and the body stays behind the P6 owner's claim-check reference.
- ACE data is reached only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views; this document declares no ACE view and no cross-schema join.
- The contract names only `rwb_document` tables and only operations owned by `rwb-document`; every other read is consumed and faked, never declared as provided (DP-01, DP-11).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review.
- Only the two events of `rwb-document` exist, and this key declares one of them; the absence test of AC8 fails a build that declares a third.
- Every example in the document is synthetic and the legacy values are examples only; no production payload is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The contract declares no case state and no document state machine; a transition belongs to the app story that performs it.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: the generation engine of legacy RWB-E2-026 is rebuilt inside `rwb-document` with the schema `rwb_document`, the topic `rwb.document.events.v1`, the REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, the template catalog read through the `rwb-comms` contract and the document written through RWB-P5-E1024-APP. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **restructuring officer (FCR)**, I want **the generation engine that fills the contract, credit approval and mortgage templates from the case facts with the merge field catalog and Legal-approved versions**, so that **the documents the screens generate are correct and versioned**.

Inside `rwb-document` this is the generation capability of the document service:

- Service `rwb-document`, schema `rwb_document`, REST base `/api/recovery/document/v1`, topic `rwb.document.events.v1` with event names `rwb.document.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-document` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`.
- The engine reads the template version and the merge field list through the template catalog contract of `rwb-comms` (C `RWB-P6-E1046-CON`, DP-11, one hop, 2 s timeout, faked). It never reads the `template` or `merge_field` table: both are P6's in `rwb_comms` (DP-01).
- It reads the case through the `rwb-case` case contract `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` with a fake, the parameters and the reference lists through the `rwb-case` parameters and reference-data contracts (C `RWB-P3-E1042-CON`, `RWB-P3-E1043-CON`, DP-06 and DP-07), the treatment through the `rwb-treatment` contract (S2, consumed and faked), and the party and collateral facts through the `rwb-source-data` contract (P1, consumed and faked, DP-05). Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream. The case contract, the S2 contract and the P1 contract are consumed by this story and appear in no C row of the work package (`ASM-1923`).
- It renders PDF/A-2b with the Thai fonts embedded and formats every value by its catalog format: the Thai long date in Buddhist Era, amounts with two decimals and amounts in Thai words.
- It records the decision through the local decision-record library of DP-03 (H `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`; the central ledger contract of `rwb-decision` is C `RWB-P7-E1027-CON`) in the same transaction as the document row and the outbox row, with decision code D6.4 and final call GENERATED.
- It stores each generated document through RWB-P5-E1024-APP with `source` GENERATED, state DRAFT and `write_once` false; the store, not this engine, writes the blob, sets `storage_ref` and writes the `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` row per document. The path is `{container}/{caseId}/{documentId}/v1` as in RWB-P5-E1024-APP.
- Parameters are read through the parameters contract and client library of `rwb-case` (DP-06, H `RWB-PLT-E1042-CON`), and the document-hub rows they resolve to live in `document_hub_parameter` in `rwb_document`, which the Ownership Map gives to P5. The reference lists are read through the reference-data contract (DP-07, H `RWB-PLT-E1043-CON`). No parameter value and no list value is typed in code.
- The document row carries `template_id` (DF-DOC-032), `treatment_id` (DF-DOC-033), a `template_version` integer and the template code read from the catalog. The TSD P5 T3.1 table has `template_id` and `treatment_id` and no `template_code` or `template_version` column, while the legacy section 13 adds `template_code`, `template_version` and `treatment_id` in its own migration; the two added here are the assumption `ASM-1922` and the gap `GAP-1023`. The template codes themselves are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1023; ASM-1925).
- The database login is one per service (DP-02). Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1023; ASM-1928); the story uses the phrase "the rwb-document login (DP-02)" and never a shared login.

The legacy behaviour is carried unchanged in intent and values: the same user story, rationale, preconditions, flow, exception paths, business rules, messages, authority, data fields, fourteen acceptance criteria and sixteen test cases, adapted to the target service's schema, topic, API base and contracts.

##### 2. Business rationale

Deed in lieu and restructure document sets are typed today from the case file into Word templates, and a wrong amount or an old template wording reaches the customer. This engine fills each Legal-approved template version from the case facts held in the Workbench, refuses to produce a document with a missing value or an unapproved template, and records which template version and which inputs produced each document. It meets REQ-DCM-012 and REQ-OCC-002, applies control CTL-14 to the deed in lieu and restructure documents, and supports the target of 1,000 deed in lieu cases a month in 2027 (NFR-006).

The realignment changes the mechanics, not the business rule:

1. One service, one schema, one topic and one API base: `rwb-document`, `rwb_document`, `rwb.document.events.v1` and `/api/recovery/document/v1`. The legacy `recovery.dochub.generation` package is retired and the operation is rebased below the service base (DP-13).
2. Every cross-service part becomes a published contract with a fake and a 2 s timeout: the P6 catalog (C `RWB-P6-E1046-CON`), the P3 case, parameters and lists (C `RWB-P3-E1042-CON`, `RWB-P3-E1043-CON`), the S2 treatment and the P1 source data (consumed and faked, `ASM-1923`). No module is called in process and no foreign table is read.
3. The decision log write becomes the local decision-record library of DP-03, written in the same transaction as the document rows and the outbox rows and published on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; `rwb-decision` seals it in the central ledger.
4. The template catalog moves out of the document module: `template` and `merge_field` are P6's in `rwb_comms`, and the engine reads the current version and the merge field list through the catalog contract only (`ASM-1921`).
5. Parameters and reference data leave the code: `GEN_IDEMPOTENCY_HOURS`, `GEN_MAX_TEMPLATES` and the font come through the parameters contract (DP-06) and the type mapping and template codes are data rows (DP-07, DL19, DL28).
6. The renderer is target-side work: PDF/A-2b with the Thai fonts embedded, one component, one conformance test (`ASM-1926`).
7. Every generated draft is stored through RWB-P5-E1024-APP, so the blob, the hash, the retention class and the write-once policy stay with the store and the engine never writes a file itself.
8. The migration is one step in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15) with one partial unique index for the concurrent case, and no data lake is connected and no `INT-19`/`INT-20` path is used anywhere (DP-17).

##### 3. Preconditions

| Precondition | What it gives this story |
|---|---|
| RWB-P5-E2026-CON | The published contract baseline of the generation API: the generate operation, `GenerateRequest`, `GenerationResult`, the `Document` shape, the provider interfaces, the error envelope, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the event schema |
| RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The decision-record library: `RecordAndApply` writes the D6.4 record inside the caller's transaction and publishes it on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03) |
| RWB-PLT-E1042-CON | The parameters client library, so `GEN_IDEMPOTENCY_HOURS`, `GEN_MAX_TEMPLATES` and `GEN_FONT` are read through a published shape (DP-06) |
| RWB-PLT-E1043-CON | The reference-data client library for the type mapping list and the language list (DP-07) |
| RWB-PLT-TE006-CON | The outbox, inbox and idempotency library; the `DocumentStored` row and the idempotency row are written in the generation transaction (DP-09) |
| RWB-PLT-E1044-CON | The per-service Flyway sequence that carries the two added columns and the partial unique index as one step (DP-15) |
| RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The gateway-bff composite route through which the case documents screen reaches the generated drafts (DP-19) |
| RWB-P5-E1024-APP | The store command and the `Document` shape: source, storage reference, retention class, write-once flag, version, and the `DocumentStored` row per stored document |
| RWB-P3-E1042-CON | `rwb-case`'s parameters contract, which resolves the three generation parameters (DP-06) |
| RWB-P3-E1043-CON | `rwb-case`'s reference-data contract, which resolves the type mapping and language lists (DP-07) |
| RWB-P6-E1046-CON | The `rwb-comms` template catalog contract: the current version by code, language, product group and date, and the merge field list of a version (the C dependency that replaces the legacy in-process `TemplateCatalog`) |
| RWB-P7-E1027-CON | The central decision ledger contract that collects the local D6.4 record (DP-03) |

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E2-026:

- Templates DIL-CONTRACT, DIL-CA and DIL-MORTGAGE, and RES-AGREEMENT for restructure, are loaded in Thai with `approved_by_legal = true`. The template codes are assumed (DL28); their field-level identity is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1023; ASM-1925).
- The template-to-document-type mapping is in the document type table: DIL-CONTRACT to CONTRACT, DIL-CA to CREDIT_APPROVAL, DIL-MORTGAGE to MORTGAGE_DOCUMENT, RES-AGREEMENT to CONTRACT (assumed; DL19). The mapping rows are data, never code; its field-level shape is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1023; ASM-1925).
- The case has a treatment of type DEED_IN_LIEU or RESTRUCTURE with `decision_log_id` set (approved at D6.4) and no outcome.
- The merge field providers of P3 (case), S2 (treatment) and P1 (party and collateral) are listed in the `MergeFieldResolver` configuration and are reached through their contracts, never through their tables.
- The caller holds Documents C (RW-RESTRUCT or RW-CASEOWN), or is the service identity SY-CASEWF for rule-driven generation from Epic 3.
- The feature flag `rwb.document.generation-engine` is on. The legacy flag name `rwb.dochub.generation-engine` is retired with the monolith; the new name and the 24-hour idempotency window are assumed (`ASM-1929`).

The generation operation path is the Ownership Map and TSD P5 API-P5-016 name `/cases/{caseId}/generated-documents`, while Architecture v5 slide 16 names `POST /documents/generate`; the conflict is recorded as `GAP-1023` and resolved as `ASM-1920`. The database login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1023; ASM-1928).

##### 4. Flow

1. Restructuring officer or SY-CASEWF: calls `POST /api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/generated-documents` with `GenerateRequest` (`treatmentId` required, `templateCodes` 1 to 10 required, `language` TH or EN default TH, the overrides the screens story uses) and an `Idempotency-Key` header. The controller passes it to the `generate` activity on queue `rwb-document` (12.5).
2. `DocumentGenerationService`: reads the treatment through the `rwb-treatment` contract `GET /api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}` (S2, one hop, 2 s, breaker) and checks it is approved, open and of type DEED_IN_LIEU or RESTRUCTURE (BR5). The contract is consumed and faked and is not in the C list (`ASM-1923`).
3. `TemplateSelector`: for each template code, reads the current version through the `rwb-comms` catalog contract (C `RWB-P6-E1046-CON`) for the language and product group: approved by Legal, active, highest version valid on the request date; the most specific product group match wins over a template for all products (BR1, BR2).
4. `MergeFieldResolver`: reads the merge field list of that version through the same contract and asks each owning provider for the values through its contract: `rwb-case` (`GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}`), `rwb-treatment` (the treatment read of step 2) and `rwb-source-data` (the party and collateral read, DP-05). Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream.
5. `MergeFieldResolver` and `ValueFormatter`: check that every required merge field has a value (BR3), then format each value by its catalog format: the Thai long date in Buddhist Era, amounts with two decimals and amounts in Thai words (BR4). A national ID number is filled from the token service at render time and never logged (BR11).
6. `TemplateRenderer`: renders each template body to PDF/A-2b with the Thai fonts embedded and writes the rendered file to the draft area of the quarantine container through the storage product RWB-PLT-TE012-APP that RWB-P5-E1024-APP also uses (the storage product is not a new X dependency of this story), at `{container}/{caseId}/{documentId}/v1`, keeping the merge snapshot beside it and never in a log.
7. `DocumentGenerationService`, one transaction in `rwb_document`: writes one decision record with decision code D6.4, an inputs reference to the merge snapshot and, per document, the template code and version, through the decision-record library of DP-03; stores each document through RWB-P5-E1024-APP with `source` GENERATED, state DRAFT, `write_once` false, the template code, the template version and the treatment ID; and writes one `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` outbox row per document (DP-09). A failed record aborts the whole set.
8. `GeneratedDocumentController`: returns 201 with `GenerationResult`: `decisionLogEntryId` and `documents[]` with `documentId`, `templateCode`, `templateVersion`, `documentType`. The screens story RWB-P5-E2017-APP shows the drafts for review.
9. Outbox relay: publishes `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` to `rwb.document.events.v1`, keyed by caseId, and the decision record to `rwb.decision-record.v1`; no payload carries a file byte or a personal value.

A failure at any step removes the draft file and writes nothing: no document row, no decision record and no outbox row for the set (X5, X11, AC2, AC7, AC14). The whole set is stored or none of it is (BR8).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A required merge field has no value | Generation stops; nothing stored; the field is named | MSG-P5-009 | AC2 |
| X2 | The current template version is not approved by Legal | Generation stops; nothing stored | MSG-P5-010 | AC4 |
| X3 | The template is withdrawn | Generation stops; a task goes to the restructuring officer, as R-LIT-04 does for notices | MSG-P6-003 | AC5 |
| X4 | The treatment is not approved, is closed, or is of another type | 409; nothing stored | MSG-P5-011 | AC6 |
| X5 | The decision log write fails | Nothing stored; draft files removed; incident raised | MSG-P7-003 | AC7 |
| X6 | The same request is repeated with the same Idempotency-Key | The first result is returned; nothing new is stored | None | AC8 |
| X7 | Two requests for the same treatment and template run at once | One succeeds; the other gets 409 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC9 |
| X8 | A template body cannot be rendered | 503; nothing stored; incident raised | MSG-GEN-006 | AC10 |
| X9 | No template exists for the product group or language | Generation stops and names the template | MSG-P5-010 | AC11 |
| X10 | The case is outside the caller's scope | 404 | MSG-P4-003 | AC12 |
| X11 | One template of a set fails its check | Nothing of the set is stored | MSG-P5-010 | AC14 |
| X12 | The caller lacks Documents C | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E2-026-15 |

Three target-service notes:

- X7 is enforced by the partial unique index `ux_document_draft_per_template ON document (treatment_id, template_id) WHERE state = 'DRAFT' AND is_active` plus the pre-insert read, exactly as the legacy `template_code` index did; the second request receives 409 with MSG-GEN-004 and keeps no row.
- A repeat with the same `Idempotency-Key` inside the 24-hour window returns the first answer and creates nothing, including the AC8 case where the first answer carried document DOC-0311. The window and the header rule are `ASM-1929` and are declared by RWB-P5-E2026-CON.
- A downstream contract that does not answer within 2 s, or whose breaker is open, is refused with 503 and MSG-GEN-006 naming the system that failed; no partial set is stored and the drafting area is cleaned as in X5.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the contract baseline (RWB-P5-E2026-CON), the store (RWB-P5-E1024-APP), the P6 catalog contract, the decision-record, parameters, reference-data, outbox, Flyway and gateway contracts, all earlier work |
| Negotiable | Templates, merge fields, formats, the type mapping and the fonts are data rows or parameters owned by Legal and the product owner |
| Valuable | Ends re-keying of deed in lieu and restructure documents and makes every generated set traceable to a template version |
| Estimable | One service, one renderer, one resolver, one formatter, one operation, one migration, no screen |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion in section 7 is one test case in section 16, on synthetic case data |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria
