```gherkin
    Then the response is 422 with MSG-P6-003 naming "DIL-MORTGAGE"
    Then the system raises a task to the restructuring officer who requested it

  Scenario: AC6 A treatment that is not approved is refused (legacy RWB-E2-026 AC6)
    Given treatment "TRT-0302" of type "DEED_IN_LIEU" with no decision_log_id
    When the engine runs for treatment "TRT-0302"
    Then the response is 409 with MSG-P5-011
    Then the system stores nothing

  Scenario: AC7 The decision log write fails (legacy RWB-E2-026 AC7)
    Given the decision log store does not accept writes
    When the engine runs for treatment "TRT-0301" and template "DIL-CONTRACT"
    Then the response is 503 with MSG-P7-003
    Then no document row exists for "TRT-0301" and the draft file is removed from the container
    Then the system raises an incident as in R-UNI-39

  Scenario: AC8 A repeated request (legacy RWB-E2-026 AC8)
    Given a request with Idempotency-Key "K-0301" generated document "DOC-0311"
    When the same request with Idempotency-Key "K-0301" arrives again
    Then the response is 201 with document "DOC-0311"
    Then no second document or decision log entry is written

  Scenario: AC9 Two requests at the same time (legacy RWB-E2-026 AC9)
    Given two requests for treatment "TRT-0301" and template "DIL-CONTRACT" with different keys arrive together
    When both run
    Then one returns 201 with one DRAFT document
    Then the other returns 409 with MSG-GEN-004

  Scenario: AC10 A template body that cannot be rendered (legacy RWB-E2-026 AC10)
    Given the body of "DIL-CONTRACT" version 2 is a damaged file
    When the engine runs
    Then the response is 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming "document generation"
    Then the system stores nothing and an incident is raised

  Scenario: AC11 No template for the product group (legacy RWB-E2-026 AC11)
    Given template "DIL-CONTRACT" exists only for product group "MORTGAGE"
    Given case "RW-2026-000305" has product group "HIRE_PURCHASE"
    When the engine runs for that case and "DIL-CONTRACT"
    Then the response is 422 with MSG-P5-010 naming "DIL-CONTRACT" for "HIRE_PURCHASE"

  Scenario: AC12 A case outside the caller's scope (legacy RWB-E2-026 AC12)
    Given case "RW-2026-000306" is in team "HP-NE" and the officer's scope is team "FCR-BKK"
    When the officer requests generation for that case
    Then the response is 404 with MSG-P4-003

  Scenario: AC13 A set of three documents in one request (legacy RWB-E2-026 AC13)
    Given templates "DIL-CONTRACT", "DIL-CA" and "DIL-MORTGAGE" are current and approved
    When the engine runs for treatment "TRT-0301" with the three template codes
    Then the system stores three documents with types "CONTRACT", "CREDIT_APPROVAL" and "MORTGAGE_DOCUMENT"
    Then one decision log entry names the three template codes and versions

  Scenario: AC14 A set is stored whole or not at all (legacy RWB-E2-026 AC14)
    Given templates "DIL-CONTRACT" and "DIL-MORTGAGE" are current and approved
    Given template "DIL-CA" has no version approved by Legal
    When the engine runs for treatment "TRT-0301" with the three template codes
    Then the response is 422 with MSG-P5-010 naming "DIL-CA"
    Then the system stores none of the three documents and no decision log entry is written
```

Every Given, When and Then line above is the legacy line unchanged. The cross-service parts are mocked by the five added Background Givens on the `rwb-comms` catalog, the `rwb-case` case, the `rwb-treatment` treatment, the `rwb-source-data` party and collateral facts and the `rwb-decision` central ledger. In AC1 the "PDF" is the PDF/A-2b file stored through RWB-P5-E1024-APP, and the "document" carries the template code, the template version and the treatment ID of the target `document` row. In AC7 the "decision log store" is the decision-record library and the central ledger contract of `rwb-decision`. In AC5 the task is raised through the `rwb-case` task contract; the operation is not part of this story.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A document is generated only from the current template version: approved by Legal, active and valid on the request date; the most specific product group match wins over a template for all products | DF-REF-047, DF-REF-049, DF-REF-051; CTL-14; R-LIT-03 |
| BR2 | A withdrawn template with no approved successor holds generation and raises a task | R-LIT-04; R-LIT-06 |
| BR3 | Every required merge field must have a value; otherwise nothing is generated and the field is named | Merge field catalog (RWB-E1-046); FEAT-OCC-07 |
| BR4 | Values are formatted by the catalog format: Thai long date in Buddhist Era, amounts with two decimals and in Thai words | Merge field catalog; Principle 1 |
| BR5 | Generation is allowed only for an approved, open treatment of type DEED_IN_LIEU or RESTRUCTURE | DF-TRT-003, DF-TRT-004, DF-TRT-013; R-DIL-14; R-DIL-16 |
| BR6 | A generated document carries the template code and version, the treatment and the source GENERATED; it is a DRAFT and not write-once until it is sent (RWB-E2-017) | DF-DOC-005, DF-DOC-010; CTL-12 |
| BR7 | Generation that cannot be written to the decision log does not proceed | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06 |
| BR8 | A set is generated whole or not at all | Events rule "Transactions" |
| BR9 | A repeat with the same Idempotency-Key returns the first result | R-UNI-40 |
| BR10 | A new template version applies to documents generated from its valid-from date; earlier documents keep their version | R-UNI-38 |
| BR11 | A national ID number is filled from the token service at render time; the clear value exists only inside the stored PDF | DF-PTY-007; CTL-11; DL26 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-document`:

- BR1 and BR10 are executed by `TemplateSelector` against the P6 catalog contract: the answer carries the version, its Legal approval, its valid-from date and its product group, and the engine keeps the version on the document row. The legacy in-process `TemplateCatalog` is retired; the catalog is `rwb-comms`'s table and this service holds no copy (`ASM-1921`).
- BR2 is executed by the refused generation plus the task raised through the `rwb-case` task contract; the engine writes no task row of its own (DP-01, DP-11).
- BR3, BR4 and BR11 are executed by `MergeFieldResolver` and `ValueFormatter`: the required flag comes from the catalog answer, the format comes from the catalog answer, the token service is called at render time, and no merge value, snapshot or clear ID number is ever written to a log (section 17).
- BR5 is executed by the treatment read through the `rwb-treatment` contract: the type, the approval and the `decision_log_id` arrive in one answer, and no treatment table is read (S2 owns `treatment`).
- BR6 is executed by the document row: `source` GENERATED, `state` DRAFT, `write_once` false, `template_id`, `template_version` and `treatment_id` written in one transaction, and by the store that keeps `write_once` false until the document is sent.
- BR7 and BR8 are executed by the decision-record library of DP-03 inside the generation transaction: the record, every document row and every outbox row commit together or not at all (R-UNI-39); a partial set is impossible.
- BR9 is executed twice: the `Idempotency-Key` row of the outbox and idempotency library (DP-09) returns the first answer inside 24 hours, and the partial unique index refuses a second active DRAFT for the same treatment and template.
- The parameters and reference lists arrive through DP-06 and DP-07; the migration is one step in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15); the event is in the outbox (DP-09); the engine evaluates no rule package and loads no Drools kit.

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status. It creates documents in state DRAFT.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | Generation requested | BR1, BR3 and BR5 pass and the decision log write succeeds | document state DRAFT |

Target columns written by the same transition:

| Column | Value in this story |
|---|---|
| `document.state` | DRAFT |
| `document.source` | GENERATED |
| `document.write_once` | false |
| `document.doc_version` | 1 |
| `document.template_id` | The identifier of the current catalog version (DF-DOC-032) |
| `document.template_version` | The version number read from the catalog (the added column, `ASM-1922`) |
| `document.treatment_id` | The treatment of the request (DF-DOC-033) |
| `document.is_active` | true |

No transition out of DRAFT happens in this story: review, send and the write-once switch on send belong to RWB-P5-E2017-APP (BR6). No case state, no treatment state and no template state is changed here; the template state belongs to `rwb-comms` and the treatment state to `rwb-treatment`.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-RESTRUCT, restructuring officer (FCR) | Requests generation for a treatment in scope (Documents C) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Requests generation for a treatment in scope (Documents C) |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Calls the generation operation for rule-driven generation from Epic 3 (R-DIL-14, R-DIL-16) |
| SY-DECLOG, decision record writer | Writes the D6.4 record inside the generation transaction |
| RW-LEGAL, legal counsel | Approves template versions (Documents CRUA; RWB-E1-034); approval is a precondition of this story, not part of it |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads generated documents (Documents R); cannot generate |
| the rwb-document login (DP-02) | The service identity that writes the document rows, the decision record and the outbox rows |

No approval level from the delegation of authority applies in this story. The treatment itself was approved at D6.4 before generation.

Service identities and owners: `rwb-document` owns the `document` row and the generation transaction; the decision-record library writes the local record and `rwb-decision` (P7) owns the central ledger; `rwb-comms` (P6) owns the template version, its Legal approval and the merge field catalog; `rwb-treatment` (S2) owns the treatment; `rwb-case` (P3) owns the case, the parameters and the reference lists; `rwb-source-data` (P1) owns the party and collateral facts.

The authorisation decision is `rwb-access`'s (Recovery roles as data, scope, masking and DoA in `rwb_access`) and is consumed as the cached permission decision the service holds. This story adds no guard, no role and no scope rule of its own: the refusal shapes are 403 with MSG-P4-002, 403 or 404 with MSG-P4-003, exactly as the legacy endpoints had them. Where the legacy guard is replaced by the shared guard library (DP-08) is another story's deliverable; this story inherits it.

The database login is per service (DP-02). Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1023; ASM-1928); the story refers to "the rwb-document login (DP-02)".

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary and the TSD P5 T3.1 table. The legacy section 11 lists DF-DOC-032 twice; the target table lists it once.

No `rwb_case` row and no ACE view is read by this service: the case fields arrive inside the `rwb-case` contract answer and the customer name and title-doc number arrive inside the `rwb-source-data` contract answer, masked by policy and read in one hop (DP-05, DP-01). The template fields are read through the `rwb-comms` contract and are not copied. The `template_code` and `template_version` columns are added beside `template_id` and `treatment_id` because the legacy data model carries all four and the TSD P5 T3.1 carries only two (`ASM-1922`). No personal value and no file byte enters an event payload, a workflow input, a decision record or a log.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Operation | Path | Owner | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/generated-documents` | P5 | `GenerateRequest`: `treatmentId` uuid required, `templateCodes` array of string 1 to 10 required, `language` TH or EN default TH, `overrides` for the screens story; header `Idempotency-Key` required; answer 201 `GenerationResult` with `decisionLogEntryId` and `documents[]` (`documentId`, `templateCode`, `templateVersion`, `documentType`) |

The Ownership Map and TSD P5 API-P5-016 give this path; Architecture v5 slide 16 names `POST /documents/generate`. The conflict is recorded as `GAP-1023` and resolved as `ASM-1920` in favour of the Ownership Map name. The field-level definition of `GenerateRequest` and `GenerationResult` is fixed by RWB-P5-E2026-CON and is Not specified in the source documents beyond the legacy section 12 (`ASM-1924`).

`POST /api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/regenerate` is API-P5-017 and belongs to RWB-P5-E2017-APP; this story declares it neither as provided nor as consumed.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Path | Owner | Story | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | the template catalog current version and merge field list | P6 rwb-comms | RWB-P6-E1046-CON | The current version by code, language, product group and date, and the merge field list of a version; the path is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1023; ASM-1921) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | RWB-P3-E1018-CON (consumed and faked; in no C row, `ASM-1923`) | The case facts of the merge fields, in one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}` | S2 rwb-treatment | the S2 contract, consumed and faked | The treatment type, approval and `decision_log_id` of BR5; not in the C list (`ASM-1923`) |
| GET | the party and collateral read of the source data | P1 rwb-source-data | the P1 contract, consumed and faked | `first_name`, `last_name` and `title_doc_no`, masked by policy (DP-05); the path is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1023; ASM-1923) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters/{paramCode}` | P3 rwb-case | RWB-P3-E1042-CON | `GEN_IDEMPOTENCY_HOURS`, `GEN_MAX_TEMPLATES`, `GEN_FONT` (DP-06) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The type mapping and language lists (DP-07) |
| POST | the central ledger sealing operation of `rwb-decision` | P7 rwb-decision | RWB-P7-E1027-CON | The seal of the local D6.4 record; consumed, not in the C list as a separate read (`ASM-1923`) |

The case contract `RWB-P3-E1018-CON`, the S2 treatment contract, the P1 source-data contract and the P7 read are consumed by this story and are not in its C list as the WP gives it: the gap `GAP-1023` and the assumption `ASM-1923` record that, and the C list is left exactly as the WP gives it. Every row is one hop with a 2 s timeout, a GET retry once with jitter and a breaker per downstream (DP-11, ADR-020). A failed read maps to 503 with MSG-GEN-006 naming the system that failed and never to a partial set.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` (EV-16) | `rwb.document.events.v1` | P5 | caseId | documentId, caseId, documentType, source, storedAt |
| decision record (decision code D6.4, final call GENERATED) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library, consumed by P7 | caseId | the hash-chained record with the merge snapshot reference, not the snapshot itself |

CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, binary mode. The store RWB-P5-E1024-APP writes the `DocumentStored` row per stored document in its own transaction; this engine contributes the decision record and the document rows that the store commits. Neither payload carries a personal value, a merge value or a file byte. `rwb.document.DocumentFieldsExtracted.v1` is the service's other event and is published by the extraction path, never by this story.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. This story consumes no Kafka event: the treatment, the case, the source data, the parameters and the lists are synchronous reads, and the trigger is the HTTP request.

| `generate` | Activity | `rwb-document` | Renders and stores one requested set inside the caller's request; called synchronously by `GeneratedDocumentController` and by the screens story RWB-P5-E2017-APP |
| `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` | Workflow, from the L3 workflow kit template "Document intake" | `rwb-document` | Named only: owned by RWB-P5-E1049-APP, and its generate step is the same activity; this story neither registers nor changes the workflow |

None. JOB-17 retention belongs to RWB-P5-E1017-APP; this story starts no Schedule and no timer.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.document`, module `document/generation`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| GeneratedDocumentController | Controller | The operation of 12.1; `Idempotency-Key` handling; error mapping to RFC 9457 problem responses with `messageId`; access check and scope |
| DocumentGenerator | Published interface | The generation entry point for the controller and for RWB-P5-E2017-APP, with `GenerationRequest` and `GenerationResult` |
| DocumentGenerationService | Service | Steps 2 to 8; BR1 to BR10; one transaction; removes the draft files on any failure |
| TemplateSelector | Service | Picks the current version by language, product group and date through the catalog contract (BR1, BR2, BR10) |
| MergeFieldResolver | Service | Calls each provider contract listed in its configuration and checks the required fields (BR3) |
| ValueFormatter | Service | Thai long dates in Buddhist Era, amounts with two decimals, amounts in Thai words (BR4) |
| TemplateRenderer | Service | Renders `{{merge_field_code}}` bodies to PDF/A-2b with the Thai fonts embedded |
| DocumentStoreClient | Client | Calls RWB-P5-E1024-APP with source GENERATED, state DRAFT and `write_once` false; never writes a file itself |
| DecisionRecordWriter | Service | Writes the D6.4 record and its merge snapshot reference through the decision-record library (DP-03) |
| DocumentHubRepository | Repository | Reads and writes `document` and reads `document_type` in `rwb_document` |
| IdempotencyRepository | Repository | Holds the request key and the first answer (DP-09) |

**Database.**

- Writes `document` with DF-DOC-001 to DF-DOC-011, DF-DOC-032, DF-DOC-033, the standard columns, and the two added columns `template_code` varchar(30) and `template_version` integer.
- Reads `document_type` in `rwb_document` for the document type and the retention class of each generated document.
- One migration in the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15): step `V2026_1` adds `document.template_code` varchar(30) null, `document.template_version` integer null and the partial unique index `ux_document_draft_per_template ON document (treatment_id, template_id) WHERE state = 'DRAFT' AND is_active`.
- No other table is touched; `template`, `merge_field`, `decision_log_entry` and every P3, S2, P1, P7 table stay with their owners (DP-01).

**Configuration and reference data.**

- Template codes DIL-CONTRACT, DIL-CA, DIL-MORTGAGE and RES-AGREEMENT and the template-to-document-type mapping are data rows loaded by the reference data administrator (DL19, DL28); the codes are assumed and their identity is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1023; ASM-1925).
- Parameters `GEN_IDEMPOTENCY_HOURS` 24, `GEN_MAX_TEMPLATES` 10 and `GEN_FONT` "TH Sarabun New", assumed and read through the parameters contract (DL28) (`ASM-1926`, `ASM-1929`).
- Decision code D6.4 with final call GENERATED, assumed; the LOV-DECISION list is owned by the data steward (`ASM-1927`).
- Feature flag `rwb.document.generation-engine`. Off: the operation answers 404 and `DocumentGenerator` refuses every call (`ASM-1929`).

**Build steps**

1. Add the Flyway step `V2026_1` with the two columns and the partial unique index; repository tests, including a second active DRAFT for the same treatment and template being refused.
2. Build `TemplateSelector` against a stub catalog for approved, unapproved, withdrawn, product-specific, all-product and future-version templates with a valid-from date; unit tests for BR1, BR2 and BR10.
3. Build `MergeFieldResolver` and its provider list against the three provider fakes; unit tests for a missing required field (BR3, AC2).
4. Build `ValueFormatter` with tests for the Buddhist Era long date and the amount in Thai words ("10 December 2569 BE", "1,250,000.00 baht (one million two hundred fifty thousand baht)").
5. Build `TemplateRenderer` with a sample Thai template; check PDF/A-2b conformance and the embedded fonts, and the damaged-body path of AC10.
6. Build `DocumentGenerationService`: the order of checks, the render, the draft write, the decision record, the store call per document, the outbox row and the removal of every draft on failure; integration test that a forced record failure leaves nothing (AC7, AC14, TC-E2-026-16).
7. Build `GeneratedDocumentController` with the `Idempotency-Key` handling, the concurrent case of AC9 and the status mapping of section 12 and section 14.
8. Add the contract test against RWB-P5-E2026-CON and the API tests for AC1 to AC14 and the access test TC-E2-026-15.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 removes the four cross-module reads of the legacy engine: the template catalog becomes the P6 contract, the case the P3 contract, the treatment the S2 contract and the party and collateral facts the P1 contract, each with a fake. DP-03 replaces the in-process decision-log writer with the local library inside the generation transaction. DP-05 is the legacy `AceSourceQuery` path: the customer name and the title-doc number come from the P1 contract and from no `v_ace_*` view of this service. DP-06 and DP-07 keep the three parameters and the two lists out of the code. DP-09 puts the event, the record and the idempotency row in the outbox and inbox library. DP-11 gives every consumed call one hop and a 2 s budget. DP-15 gives the service its own migration step. DP-19 puts the generated drafts on the case documents screen through the composite route.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, a sample deed in lieu set is checked by legal counsel against the approved wording, a three-document set is generated in SIT inside the 2 s budget per downstream, `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` is on the topic once per document with no personal data, and no draft file remains after a refused set.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-009 | A required merge field has no value (new) | {template} cannot be generated. {field} has no value on the case. |
| MSG-P5-010 | No current template version approved by Legal (new) | {template} has no version approved by Legal for {product} in {language}. |
| MSG-P5-011 | The treatment is not approved or not open (new) | Documents can be generated only for an approved {treatment} that is still open. |
| MSG-P6-003 | The template is withdrawn | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | templateCodes is empty | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A concurrent request for the same treatment and template | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The renderer fails | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Caller lacks Documents C | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |

Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

HTTP mapping from the legacy section 12, unchanged: 401 for an unauthenticated caller (MSG-P4-001, whose wording is outside this story), 403 for MSG-P4-002, 404 for a case or a treatment that is not found or lies outside the scope (MSG-P4-003), 409 for MSG-P5-011 and MSG-GEN-004, 422 for MSG-P5-009, MSG-P5-010, MSG-P6-003 and MSG-GEN-001, 503 for MSG-P7-003 and MSG-GEN-006.

Delivery shape: every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set to the ID above, `detail` carrying the text with its placeholders filled, and `instance` naming the request. For MSG-GEN-006 the {system} value is "document generation" for a renderer failure and the name of the contract that failed for a downstream timeout. For MSG-P5-010 the {language} value is the `language` of the request and the {product} value is the product group of the case, read from the `rwb-case` answer.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The restructuring officer reaches the engine through the screens of RWB-P5-E2017-APP, which calls the same operation and the same `generate` activity. Generated documents appear on SCR-30 Case documents in the list state with state DRAFT, through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 (RWB-PLT-N001-CON). The DRAFT label, the review action and the send action belong to RWB-P5-E2017-APP; this story fixes only the state a generated document is created in.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: template codes, merge fields, formats, the type mapping, the decision code, the parameters and the font are data rows or parameters.
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs, payloads, logs, tests or prompts: merge values and the merge snapshot are never logged; tests use synthetic parties; the clear ID number is used only at render time and exists only inside the stored PDF.
- No read of another service's tables (DP-01): the template catalog, the case, the treatment, the party and collateral facts, the parameters, the lists and the central ledger come through published contracts. ACE data is reached only through the owner's contract or a `v_ace_*` view, and this service reads no view.
- No document is produced from a template version without `approved_by_legal = true`, and no template version and no merge field is held in this service's schema.
- No clear ID number outside the rendered PDF, and no merge snapshot in a log, an event or a decision-record payload: the record carries the reference only.
- The engine writes no blob itself: every draft goes through RWB-P5-E1024-APP at `{container}/{caseId}/{documentId}/v1` and is removed when the set is refused.
- The decision record is written in the same transaction as the document rows and the outbox rows; a failure stores nothing and raises an incident (R-UNI-39, R-UNI-40).
- The engine is idempotent twice over: `Idempotency-Key` on the POST and the partial unique index on treatment, template and DRAFT state.
- One evaluator if any: this story evaluates no rule package, so no Drools kit is loaded and no rule row is read.
- The feature flag `rwb.document.generation-engine` removes the capability without a rollback of the schema.

##### 1. Story

As a **restructuring officer (FCR)**, I want **the rwb-comms generation engine that fills the contract, credit approval and mortgage templates from the case facts with the merge field catalog and the Legal-approved template versions**, so that **the documents the screens generate are correct and versioned, and no other service reads the template or merge field tables of rwb-comms**.

The engine owns templates, merge fields, selection and rendering. The document record, the stored file and the write-once copy belong to rwb-document (P5); the decision record goes to the local decision-record library and `rwb.decision-record.v1`.

##### 2. Business rationale

Deed in lieu and restructure document sets are typed today from the case file into Word templates, and a wrong amount or an old template wording reaches the customer. This engine fills each Legal-approved template version from the case facts, refuses to produce a document with a missing value or an unapproved template, and records which template version and which inputs produced each document. It meets REQ-DCM-012 and REQ-OCC-002, applies control CTL-14 to the deed in lieu and restructure documents, and supports the target of 1,000 deed in lieu cases a month in 2027 (NFR-006).

In the microservice layout the template and merge field catalog is the asset of rwb-comms, so the generation decision sits with the owner of that data; the byte store and the document lifecycle (DRAFT, REVIEWED, SENT, write-once) stay with rwb-document. The split keeps one writer per table and lets another workbench reuse the engine through one REST contract.

##### 3. Preconditions

- rwb-comms holds the template catalog and the merge field catalog as data (`rwb_comms.template`, `rwb_comms.merge_field`) with its own Flyway baseline, and the Legal approval record is a column set on the template version.
- Templates DIL-CONTRACT, DIL-CA, DIL-MORTGAGE and RES-AGREEMENT are loaded in Thai with approved_by_legal = true (template codes assumed, DL28).
- The template-to-document-type mapping is reference data of rwb-document: DIL-CONTRACT to CONTRACT, DIL-CA to CREDIT_APPROVAL, DIL-MORTGAGE to MORTGAGE_DOCUMENT, RES-AGREEMENT to CONTRACT (assumed, DL19).
- The case has a treatment of type DEED_IN_LIEU or RESTRUCTURE with decision_log_id set (approved at D6.4) and no outcome yet.
- The merge field providers of P3 (case), S2 (treatment) and P1 (party, collateral) are listed in the MergeFieldResolver configuration as contract clients.
- The caller holds Documents C (RW-RESTRUCT or RW-CASEOWN), or is the service identity SY-CASEWF for rule-driven generation from Epic 3.
- The rwb-document contract and its fake (RWB-P5-E2026-CON) are published; the story builds against them and never against rwb_document tables.

##### 4. Flow

1. Restructuring officer or SY-CASEWF: requests generation for a case, a treatment and a list of template codes on `POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/generated-documents` with an Idempotency-Key.
2. System: reads the treatment through the rwb-treatment (S2) contract and checks it is approved and open.
3. System: for each template code, reads the current version from `rwb_comms.template` for the language and product group: approved by Legal, active, highest version valid on the request date.
4. System: reads the merge codes of that version from `rwb_comms.merge_field` and asks each owning service's contract (P3, S2, P1) for the values.
5. System: checks that every required merge field has a value; formats each value by its catalog format (Thai long date in Buddhist Era, amount to two decimals, amount in Thai words).
6. System: reads the template body through the rwb-document file contract and renders it to PDF/A-2b with the Thai font named in the parameters.
7. System: calls the rwb-document contract once per document to create the DRAFT document row with template code, template version and treatment ID, and to store the file; the service counts the calls and treats the set as whole or not at all.
8. System: publishes one decision record (decision code D6.4, inputs reference to the merge snapshot, per document the template code and version) through the local library and the outbox to `rwb.decision-record.v1`.
9. System: returns the generated documents; the screens of RWB-E2-017 show them for review. If any step fails, no document is created in rwb-document and any draft file written in this request is removed.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A required merge field has no value | Generation stops; nothing stored; the field is named | MSG-P5-009 | AC2 |
| X2 | The current template version is not approved by Legal | Generation stops; nothing stored | MSG-P5-010 | AC4 |
| X3 | The template is withdrawn | Generation stops; a task goes to the restructuring officer through the rwb-case contract, as R-LIT-04 does for notices | MSG-P6-003 | AC5 |
| X4 | The treatment is not approved, is closed, or is of another type | 409; nothing stored | MSG-P5-011 | AC6 |
| X5 | The decision record cannot be published | Nothing stored; draft file removed; incident raised | MSG-P7-003 | AC7 |
| X6 | The same request is repeated with the same Idempotency-Key | The first result is returned; nothing new is stored | None | AC8 |
| X7 | Two requests for the same treatment and template run at once | One succeeds; the other gets 409 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC9 |
| X8 | A template body cannot be rendered | 503; nothing stored; incident raised | MSG-GEN-006 | AC10 |
| X9 | No template exists for the product group or language | Generation stops and names the template | MSG-P5-010 | AC11 |
| X10 | The case is outside the caller's scope | 404 | MSG-P4-003 | AC12 |
| X11 | One template of a set fails its check | Nothing of the set is stored | MSG-P5-010 | AC14 |
| X12 | The caller lacks Documents C | 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-026-15 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the rwb-document contract fake (RWB-P5-E2026-CON); the P3, S2 and P1 reads are contract clients with fakes; no build dependency in the lane (ASM-3978) |
| Negotiable | Templates, merge fields, formats, type mapping and font are data and parameters, owned by Legal and the product owner |
| Valuable | Ends re-keying of deed in lieu and restructure documents, and fixes template ownership with the service that holds the catalog |
| Estimable | One service, one renderer, one resolver, one endpoint, one decision record, no screen |
| Small | Fits in two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each AC is one contract or component test with synthetic case data and recorded contract payloads |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A document is generated only from the current template version: approved by Legal, active and valid on the request date; the most specific product group match wins over a template for all products | DF-REF-047, DF-REF-049, DF-REF-051; CTL-14; R-LIT-03 |
| BR2 | A withdrawn template with no approved successor holds generation and raises a task | R-LIT-04; R-LIT-06 |
| BR3 | Every required merge field must have a value; otherwise nothing is generated and the field is named | Merge field catalog (RWB-E1-046); FEAT-OCC-07 |
| BR4 | Values are formatted by the catalog format: Thai long date in Buddhist Era, amounts with two decimals and in Thai words | Merge field catalog; Principle 1 |
| BR5 | Generation is allowed only for an approved, open treatment of type DEED_IN_LIEU or RESTRUCTURE | DF-TRT-003, DF-TRT-004, DF-TRT-013; R-DIL-14; R-DIL-16 |
| BR6 | A generated document carries the template code, the template version, the treatment ID and the source GENERATED; rwb-document creates it as a DRAFT and it is not write-once until it is sent (RWB-E2-017) | DF-DOC-005, DF-DOC-010; CTL-12 |
| BR7 | Generation whose decision record cannot be published does not proceed; the record is written through the local library and the outbox | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06; DP-03, DP-09 |
| BR8 | A set is generated whole or not at all | Events rule "Transactions" |
| BR9 | A repeat with the same Idempotency-Key returns the first result | R-UNI-40 |
| BR10 | A new template version applies to documents generated from its valid-from date; earlier documents keep their version | R-UNI-38 |
| BR11 | A national ID number is filled from the token service at render time; the clear value exists only inside the generated PDF and never in a log, an event or a workflow input | DF-PTY-007; CTL-11; DL26 |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms.generation`.

| Component | Type | Microservice responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| GeneratedDocumentController | Controller | The 12.1 endpoint; Idempotency-Key; error mapping to problem responses |
| GenerationService | Service | Steps 2 to 8 of §4 in one unit of work; refuses the whole set on any failure; removes draft files |
| TemplateSelector | Service | Selects the version from `rwb_comms.template` by language, product group and date (BR1, BR2); never reads another schema (DP-01) |
| MergeFieldCatalog | Service | Reads the merge codes of the selected version from `rwb_comms.merge_field` (BR3) |
| MergeFieldResolver | Service | Calls the P3, S2 and P1 contract clients in parallel; checks required values |
| ValueFormatter | Service | Thai long date in Buddhist Era, amounts to two decimals, amounts in Thai words (BR4) |
| TemplateRenderer | Service | Merges `{{merge_field_code}}` tags, renders PDF/A-2b with the parameter font, reads the body through the P5 contract |
| DocumentDraftClient | Client | One create call per document to RWB-P5-E2026-CON; counts calls; compensates on failure (BR6, BR8) |
| DecisionRecordPublisher | Publisher | Local decision-record library and outbox to `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03, DP-09) |
| GenerationRepository | Repository | Template and merge field reads; request key and request lock |
| ConfigClient | Client | Parameters and reference data through the P3 contracts (DP-06, DP-07) |
| TaskClient | Client | Raises the task for a withdrawn template through the rwb-case contract |

**Database.** Per-service Flyway sequence in `rwb_comms` (DP-15): template and merge_field with the standard record columns, the unique key on (template_code, template_version), and an index on (template_code, language, product_group, valid_from). The request key and the request lock of X6 and X7 are kept in `rwb_comms`; the table for them is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2393; ASM-3976). No Flyway migration touches another schema.

**Configuration and reference data.** Parameters through the rwb-case contract (DP-06): GEN_IDEMPOTENCY_HOURS 24, GEN_MAX_TEMPLATES 10, GEN_FONT "TH Sarabun New" (values assumed). Reference data through the same owner (DP-07): language list TH and EN, product groups, and the template-to-document-type mapping held by rwb-document (DL19). Templates and merge fields stay data rows of this service, owner legal counsel (DL28).

**Build steps.**
1. Flyway baseline of `rwb_comms` with template and merge_field; repository and unique-key tests.
2. TemplateSelector against the own-schema tables: approved, unapproved, withdrawn, product-specific, all-product and valid-from cases.
3. MergeFieldCatalog and MergeFieldResolver with contract fakes; test the missing required field.
4. ValueFormatter with Buddhist Era date and Thai-words amount tests.
5. TemplateRenderer with a sample Thai template; check PDF/A-2b conformance and the embedded font.
6. GenerationService: order of checks, render, P5 create calls, decision record, compensation, all-or-nothing set.
7. Controller with Idempotency-Key, request lock and the 12.1 error mapping.
8. Contract test of the new endpoint against RWB-P5-E2026-CON and the note of the addition in the P6 API specification.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.comms.generation-engine`. Off: the endpoint returns 404.

**Done when:** the tests in section 16 pass; a sample deed in lieu set is checked by legal counsel against the approved wording; no rwb_document, rwb_case or rwb_decision table is read or written by the service.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: template codes, merge codes, formats, type mapping, language list and font are data rows or parameters.
- No PII in events, workflow inputs or logs: merge values and the merge snapshot are never logged; tests use synthetic parties; the clear national ID number is used only at render time and exists only inside the PDF.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract: case, treatment, party and collateral values come from P3, S2 and P1, never from an ACE table and never from another service's schema.
- No document is produced from a template version without approved_by_legal = true; no row of rwb_document is read or written, only its contract.

##### 1. Story

As a **restructuring officer (FCR)**, I want **the treatment stage of the case to ask the generation engine of the document service for the contract, credit approval and mortgage documents of the treatment it is working, to pin the template version that was in force on the request date, and to keep the returned document reference and that version on the treatment row in the same transaction as the decision record that says which template and which version produced it**, so that **the documents the screens show are the ones produced from the Legal-approved version, and the treatment itself carries the proof of which version it was given**.

This is the treatment-side slice of legacy RWB-E2-026. The generation engine of the legacy — the template selector, the merge-field resolver, the value formatter, the renderer, the file and the store — is RWB-P5-E2026-APP's and P5 rwb-document's, or P6 rwb-comms' for the catalogue. This story owns:

- the request and the use of the generated document: `generateContractDocument`, the activity of `TreatmentWorkflow` on queue `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, the stage child of `CaseWorkflow` of rwb-case (DP-12; Architecture v5 slide 18; Temporal and Drools Design slides 13 and 18);
- the one-hop REST call to the generation operation that RWB-P5-E2026-CON publishes, with a 2 s timeout, a breaker and a mock, built on Day 1 against the contract and never against rwb-document (DP-11, ADR-020);
- the two `treatment` columns it writes — the reference of the contract document the engine returned and the template version it pinned — added by this story's own Flyway version on the per-service sequence, with their index (DP-15);
- the local decision record of the generation, written through the RWB-PLT-E1027-CON library inside the caller's transaction with decision code D6.4, the template code and the template version (DP-03), and the outbox row of the same transaction (DP-09);
- the parameters read and the reference-data read the request is checked against, at their version (DP-06, DP-07);
- the treatment side of the base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1` (DP-13) and the read that surfaces the reference on SCR-14 and SCR-15 through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19);
- the event the generation writes, which carries identifiers, codes and versions and no personal value (DP-09).

It does not own: the templates, the merge-field definitions, the template versions and the Legal approval of a version, which are P6 rwb-comms' (`template`, `merge_field`); the generation engine, the rendering, the PDF/A-2b body, the file custody, the e-signature and the retention, which are P5 rwb-document's and P6 rwb-comms' (`document`, `document_type`, `document_hub_parameter`, `signature_request`, `retention_rule`) and the stories RWB-P5-E2026-APP and RWB-P5-E2026-CON; the offer, the settlement terms and the approval below the floor, which are RWB-S2-E3001-APP to RWB-S2-E3005-APP; the case status and the `CaseWorkflow`, which are rwb-case's (P3); the central decision ledger, which is P7 rwb-decision's; the rights, the roles and the scope data, which are rwb-access's (P4); the gateway-bff composite route and the screen field list, which are the platform edge story's and the screen owners'.

##### 2. Business rationale

Deed in lieu and restructure document sets are typed today from the case file into Word templates, and a wrong amount or an old template wording reaches the customer. The legacy engine fills each Legal-approved template version from the case facts held in the Workbench, refuses to produce a document with a missing value or an unapproved template, and records which template version and which inputs produced each document. That business objective is unchanged and is now split across two services: the engine and the files live in rwb-document (P5), the template catalogue in rwb-comms (P6), and the treatment that the documents belong to stays here.

What D-RCV-60 changes on this side is small in code and large in guarantees. In the monolith the generation was an in-process call from the treatment module into the document module: `DocumentGenerator.generate(...)` ran inside one JVM, wrote `document` rows and a `decision_log_entry` in the one `recovery` schema, and returned. In the target the call is one hop over the published contract of the document service (DP-11), the documents are rows of `rwb_document` that this service never reads, and the only durable trace on the treatment is the reference the engine returned plus the version it pinned. That trace has to be written with the decision record of the same action, in one transaction, because a treatment that carries a document reference no record explains is exactly what REQ-DCM-012 and the no-record rule forbid (DP-03; Temporal and Drools Design slide 14; R-UNI-39).

The second change is where the version rule bites. The legacy read the current version by language, product group and request date inside the engine. Here the version is read by the owner of the catalogue and reported on the answer, and this service pins the reported version on its own row: a new template version applies from its valid-from date and earlier documents keep their version (R-UNI-38). Pinning it here is what lets SCR-14 show, months later, which wording the customer was given, without this service reading a template row.

The third change is the boundary. The legacy story read `template`, `document`, `case` and the ACE views within one module. In the target this service writes two columns of its own `treatment` row and calls one operation; it holds no grant on `rwb_document`, `rwb_comms`, `rwb_case` or a `v_ace_*` view (DP-01, DP-05). The merge values it supplies are the ones its own row holds; the customer name and the title-doc number never pass through it (DP-05, CTL-11).

Serves REQ-DCM-012 and REQ-OCC-002. No business value is invented or moved: the template codes, the document types, the type mapping, the decision code D6.4, the amounts, the dates and the message IDs are the values the legacy story, the FSD S2 A2.18 and the TSD S2 already carry, read in force.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P5-E2026-CON is published: the generate operation on `/api/recovery/document/v1`, `POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents` (API-P5-016) with `GenerateRequest` (treatmentId, templateCodes, language, overrides), the 201 `GenerationResult` (`decisionLogEntryId`, `documents`), the `Document` shape with `documentId`, `documentType`, `source`, `docVersion`, `templateCode`, `templateVersion` and `treatmentId`, the error set with the RFC 9457 problem body and its message IDs, the `Idempotency-Key` rule and the fakes. The operation identifier the contract does not state is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1878; ASM-3080).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: `DecisionRecordWriter.record(DecisionRecord)` with `@Transactional(propagation = MANDATORY)`, refusing with MSG-P7-009 and failing with MSG-P7-003, and the `decision_record` DDL template applied in this service's own schema (DP-03).
- `treatment` exists in `rwb_treatment` from RWB-S2-E3001-APP with the fields DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033 of TSD S2 T3.1, holding treatment "TRT-0301" of type DEED_IN_LIEU or RESTRUCTURE with `decision_log_id` set and no outcome.
- Templates "DIL-CONTRACT", "DIL-CA" and "DIL-MORTGAGE" for a restructure and "RES-AGREEMENT" are loaded in Thai with the Legal approval recorded against the version, and the type mapping is DIL-CONTRACT to CONTRACT, DIL-CA to CREDIT_APPROVAL, DIL-MORTGAGE to MORTGAGE_DOCUMENT and RES-AGREEMENT to CONTRACT. The codes, the mapping and the approval are values in force read at their version; the catalogue and the mapping are P6 rwb-comms' and P5 rwb-document's and this story reads neither table (GAP-1879; ASM-3082).
- Package DEEDINLIEU or RESTRUCTURE is in force for the business date with the row R-DIL-16 (generate the credit approval, the contract and the mortgage documents, when `final_call = approved`), arriving from rwb-decision on `RulePackageInForce` and evaluated by the embedded Drools runtime of the service template, which adds no build dependency of its own (ASM-3082; Temporal and Drools Design slides 13 and 15; FSD S2 A2.18).
- The two columns and the index of section 13 are applied on this service's Flyway sequence by this story, after the version that carries the library tables, and no applied migration is edited (DP-15).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route that serves SCR-14 Treatment record and SCR-15 Settlement offer from the case read, the treatment read and the document read, one hop each, read only (DP-19).
- The parameters contract and the reference-data contract of rwb-case are reachable as client libraries (DP-06, DP-07), and the capability area "Treatment and offer" with its rights is rwb-access data.
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline, and a CON story is Day 1 by rule: this story starts on Day 1 with only CON build dependencies (§R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The case reaches D6.4 with an approved route, or the deed in lieu route reaches TRANSFER_PRICE_SET; `TreatmentWorkflow` on queue `rwb-treatment`, the child of `CaseWorkflow` of rwb-case, is running for the case (Architecture v5 slide 18; Temporal and Drools Design slides 13 and 18).
2. The stage asks the embedded Drools runtime for the package version in force and evaluates it with the treatment facts it holds: the treatment type, the approval, `final_call` and the transfer price against the floor.
3. R-DIL-16 fires with `final_call = approved`: its action is to generate the credit approval, the contract and the mortgage documents and to put the offer to the customer; its target state is OFFER_WITH_CUSTOMER_DIL, reported to the parent and moved there, not here (FSD S2 A2.18; ASM-3082).
4. `generateContractDocument` activity: reads the `treatment` row it owns and builds the `GenerateRequest` of the contract — `treatmentId`, the template codes of the set, `language` TH — and the S2 value set the contract's treatment provider answers for that treatment.
5. The S2 value set is exactly what the row holds: the contract amount from `offer_amount` (DF-TRT-007), the installments (DF-TRT-009), the interest rate (DF-TRT-027), the first due date (DF-TRT-029), and the case and decision-record identifiers (DF-TRT-002, DF-TRT-003). Names, the national ID number and the title-doc number are never supplied by this service; they belong to rwb-source-data and rwb-case and are masked by policy (DP-05, CTL-11).
6. The request is checked against the template-count bound read through the parameters contract at its version, and the template codes against LOV-DOC-TYPE read through the reference-data contract at its version; a code outside the list or a count above the bound is refused before the call (DP-06, DP-07).
7. The activity calls the generate operation of RWB-P5-E2026-CON once, on one hop, with a 2 s timeout and a breaker. The engine reads the template version in force by language, product group and request date, checks that every required merge field has a value, renders and stores the drafts, and answers 201 with the `documentId`, the `templateCode` and the `templateVersion` of each document (DP-11; FSD S2 A2.18; R-UNI-38).
8. The activity takes the document of type CONTRACT from the answer — the document of record of the treatment — and its `templateVersion`, and writes, in one `rwb_treatment` transaction: the two columns of the treatment row, the local `decision_record` through `DecisionRecordWriter.record` with decision code D6.4, the template code and the template version, the outbox row of the generation event, and the idempotency row of the request (DP-03, DP-09).
9. The write key is the treatment ID, the template code and the template version, so a replay of the same activity, a redelivery of the same request and a repeated `Idempotency-Key` all answer the first reference and write once (R-UNI-40; legacy AC8).
10. The stage reports the outcome to the parent `CaseWorkflow`: the document reference, the template version, the decision record and the target state the rule names. The parent moves the case; this service writes no case table.
11. A refused or failed generation writes nothing: the treatment keeps every column it had, no decision record and no outbox row is written, and the activity retries on the platform policy or fails non-retryably as the contract's status says.
12. SCR-14 shows the treatment with its document reference and template version, read from this service and merged with the document read of rwb-document by the gateway-bff composite route; SCR-15 shows the treatment the offer is built on (DP-19).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A required merge field has no value on the case | The engine refuses before storing anything and names the template and the field; the activity carries the problem body back unchanged; no reference, no version and no record is written | MSG-P5-009 | AC2 |
| X2 | The version in force is not approved by Legal, or no template exists for the product group or language | The engine refuses and names the template; the treatment row is unchanged; the stage reports the refusal to the parent | MSG-P5-010 | AC2, AC6 |
| X3 | The template is withdrawn and no later version is approved | The engine refuses and names the template; the task to the officer who requested it is raised by the screens story, not here | MSG-P6-003 | AC6 |
| X4 | The treatment is not approved, is closed, or is of another type | 409 with the problem body; nothing is stored | MSG-P5-011 | AC6 |
| X5 | The local decision record cannot be written | The whole transaction rolls back: no reference, no template version, no outbox row; the user sees MSG-P7-003 and the activity retries | MSG-P7-003 | AC5 |
| X6 | The same request is repeated with the same key, or the activity is replayed | The first answer is returned; nothing new is written | None | AC4 |
| X7 | The same treatment and template are requested twice at once | One transaction commits; the other is refused by the engine with 409 and this service writes nothing | MSG-GEN-004 | AC4 |
| X8 | A template body cannot be rendered, or the document service does not answer inside 2 s | 503 with the problem body naming the system; nothing is stored here and the activity retries on the platform policy | MSG-GEN-006 | AC6 |
| X9 | The caller holds no Documents C, or the case lies outside the caller's scope | 403 or 404 with the problem body; nothing is read further and nothing is written | MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 | AC6, AC8 |
| X10 | A component, a statement or a test reaches a `rwb_document`, `rwb_comms` or `rwb_case` table, a template row or a `v_ace_*` view | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build; nothing is released | None (pipeline log) | Section 8, BR1 |

X1 to X6 are the legacy paths of the generation carried onto the split; X7 and X8 add the concurrent and the unavailable cases of the one-hop call; X9 is the guard's answer; X10 is the boundary rule of the target. Nothing is written on any of X1 to X4 or X8 to X10, because the engine's refusal arrives before this service's transaction opens, and X5 rolls back the transaction that already holds the reference and the record.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against the RWB-P5-E2026-CON fake, the decision-record writer fake, the parameters and reference-data fakes and the composite-route fake; needs no live rwb-document, rwb-comms, rwb-decision or rwb-case |
| Negotiable | The activity name, the column names, the write key and the value-set shape are this story's design; the template codes, the document types, the decision code, the message IDs and the version rule are values in force |
| Valuable | The officer stops re-keying the contract set and the treatment carries the version it was given, so the wording behind a signed document can be shown months later |
| Estimable | One activity, one client, one value builder, one writer, two columns and one index, one event and one read model |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests, as a secondary slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Each of the eight criteria of section 7 is one automated test; every cross-service answer is stubbed in a contract fake |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Document generation engine for contract, CA and mortgage templates — the rwb-treatment request and use

  Background:
    Given case "RW-2026-000301" with product group "MORTGAGE"
    Given treatment "TRT-0301" of type "DEED_IN_LIEU" on that case with decision_log_id set and no outcome
    Given template "DIL-CONTRACT" version 2 in Thai for "MORTGAGE" with approved_by_legal true
    Given the merge fields of "DIL-CONTRACT" version 2 are case_no, borrower_name, title_doc_no, transfer_price and contract_date
    Given the template-to-document-type mapping is DIL-CONTRACT to CONTRACT, DIL-CA to CREDIT_APPROVAL and DIL-MORTGAGE to MORTGAGE_DOCUMENT
    Given a restructuring officer with role RW-RESTRUCT in scope of the case

    Given the treatment row "TRT-0301" holds offer_amount 1250000.00 and its own installments, interest rate and first due date

  Scenario: AC2 A missing merge value is refused and nothing is generated (new, D-RCV-60)

    Then the outbox row of rwb.treatment.ContractDocumentGenerated.v1 is written in the same transaction

  Scenario: AC4 A repeated request with the same key returns the first reference and writes once (new, D-RCV-60)
```

The eight criteria are new under D-RCV-60 and test only the S2 deliverable of this story: the request and its values, the pinned version, the reference in one transaction with the record, the repeat, the record failure, the refusal and the unavailable service, the screen and the personal-data boundary (ASM-3079). The fourteen legacy criteria AC1 to AC14 of RWB-E2-026 — Generate, Missing field, Version, A version not approved by Legal, A withdrawn template, A treatment that is not approved, The decision log write fails, A repeated request, Two requests at the same time, A template body that cannot be rendered, No template for the product group, A case outside the caller's scope, A set of three documents in one request and A set stored whole or not at all — belong to `RWB-P5-E2026-APP`, are written there word for word with their origin tags, and are not restated here. The paths, the request and answer shapes, the error set and the fakes this story consumes are `RWB-P5-E2026-CON`'s. The cross-service journey of the same values across rwb-treatment, rwb-document, rwb-comms and rwb-case is `RWB-ITG-E2026-ITG`'s and no criterion of this story claims it.

Three readings of the sources are stated here rather than hidden in the code. The operation identifier of the generation call and the shape of the S2 value set on the wire are Not specified in the source documents, so they come from `RWB-P5-E2026-CON` and from this story's own design over the row's fields (GAP-1878; ASM-3080). The `treatment` table of TSD S2 T3.1 has no column that holds a document reference and no column that holds a template version, so this story adds two nullable columns and records the difference (GAP-1878; ASM-3085). The template catalogue and the merge-field definitions sit with P6 rwb-comms in the target while the legacy files them under the document module's feature, and the loser is the legacy placement, which changes nothing here because this story reads neither table (GAP-1879; ASM-3082).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | This service supplies only the merge values its own `treatment` row holds; a name, a national ID number and a title-doc number are never supplied by it and reach it from no table and no view | DP-05, CTL-11, DL26; legacy RWB-E2-026 BR11; TSD S2 T3.1 |
| BR2 | The template version is the one in force on the request date — approved by Legal, active and valid on that date, the most specific product group match winning over a template for all products — read by the catalogue owner and pinned on the treatment row as reported | Legacy RWB-E2-026 BR1; DF-REF-047, DF-REF-049, DF-REF-051; CTL-14; R-UNI-38 |
| BR3 | A new template version applies to documents generated from its valid-from date; earlier documents keep the version they were generated under, and that version stays readable on the treatment row | Legacy RWB-E2-026 BR10; R-UNI-38 |
| BR4 | An approval below the floor, a withdrawn template and a treatment that is not open are refusals that arrive on the contract's problem body; this service re-words no message and stores nothing on a refusal | Legacy RWB-E2-026 BR2, BR5, BR7; MSG-P5-010, MSG-P6-003, MSG-P5-011 |
| BR5 | A document reference is written only with the decision record of the same generation, in one transaction, with the template code and the template version; a failed record write rolls the reference back too | Legacy RWB-E2-026 BR7; Principle 5; R-UNI-39; DP-03 |
| BR6 | A repeat with the same key writes once: one reference, one pin and one record; the key is the treatment ID, the template code and the template version | Legacy RWB-E2-026 BR9; R-UNI-40; AC4 |
| BR7 | A generation that the treatment records is announced once, on this service's topic, with identifiers, the document type, the template code, the template version and the decision record; no personal value and no file byte is on it | DP-09; Architecture v5 slides 18 and 42 notes; AC8 |
| BR8 | No value a business person may change is written in code: the template codes, the type mapping, the languages, the formats, the generation window and the template bound are data rows or parameters read at their version | Legacy RWB-E2-026 BR4, section 17; BR-S2-001; DP-06, DP-07 |
| BR9 | This service reads no `document`, `document_type`, `document_hub_parameter`, `template` or `merge_field` row and no `v_ace_*` view; the documents and the catalogue arrive only on the published contract, and the `rwb_treatment` login holds no grant that would allow otherwise | DP-01; Architecture v5 slides 29 and 41; Ownership Map |
| BR10 | The case status stays rwb-case's: the stage reports the generation and the target state R-DIL-16 names to the parent `CaseWorkflow`, which moves the status, and this service writes no case table | DP-01; Architecture v5 slide 18; FSD S2 A2.18 |
| BR11 | The two columns this story adds are nullable and additive: a treatment without a generated document keeps them empty, and no sibling story's write is narrowed by them | DP-15; TSD S2 T3.1; section 13 |
| BR12 | A refusal of the engine, a 503 or a record failure leaves the treatment exactly as it was; nothing is stored before the engine's 201 answer names the document and its version | AC2, AC5, AC6; R-UNI-39 |
| R-UNI-38 | A new rule version applies to decisions taken from its effective date, and an open case keeps the version it was decided under. Here it is the template version, pinned on the treatment row | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-UNI-38) |
| R-UNI-39 | The decision record, the change and the outbox rows are one transaction; a failed write moves nothing | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-UNI-39); Temporal and Drools Design slide 14 |
| R-UNI-40 | A repeated request with the same key returns the first result and writes nothing new | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-UNI-40) |
| R-DIL-16 | The credit approval, the contract and the mortgage documents are generated when `final_call = approved`, and the offer goes to the customer; the target state is OFFER_WITH_CUSTOMER_DIL | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-DIL-16); FSD S2 A2.18.3.1 |
| CTL-11 | Personal data is masked for a role that may not see it and is not copied outside the system that owns it; no name, national ID number or title-doc number is written to `rwb_treatment` | Legacy RWB-E2-026 BR11; CTL-11; DL26 |
| CTL-14 | A document is produced only from an approved template version, and the approval is recorded against the version | Legacy RWB-E2-026 BR1; CTL-14 |

The rules hold in `rwb_treatment` as follows. BR1 is the value builder: it holds the four column names of the row and the two identifiers, and a property test places a synthetic name in the contract's answer and proves it appears in no column, no log line, no event and no span attribute. BR2 and BR3 are the pin: the version is taken from the answer and never computed here, and the build check fails on a version literal. BR4 and BR12 are the ordering of the checks: nothing opens a transaction until the engine has answered 201. BR5 and BR6 are the writer's one transaction and the write key. BR7 is the outbox row and the AsyncAPI fragment. BR8 is the parameters and reference-data reads. BR9 is the schema grant and the boundary test. BR10 is the child-workflow return. BR11 is the migration review: two nullable columns, no backfill and no change to an existing column.

##### 9. State transitions

None of the rows below is a case status owned here: each is a change of this service's own record, and the case status R-DIL-16 implies is reported to the parent `CaseWorkflow` (BR10; DP-01).

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| A `treatment` row with no contract document | `generateContractDocument` and a 201 answer from the engine | R-DIL-16 with `final_call = approved`, the treatment approved and open, the engine's version approved by Legal | The same row with the document reference and the template version written, in state DRAFT of the document |
| A `treatment` row with a document reference | A repeat of the same request key | Same treatment, same template code, same template version | Unchanged; the first reference is answered |
| A `treatment` row with no contract document | A refusal of the engine | MSG-P5-009, MSG-P5-010, MSG-P6-003, MSG-P5-011 or MSG-GEN-004 | Unchanged, and the stage reports the refusal |
| A `treatment` row with no contract document | A record failure or a 503 | MSG-P7-003 or MSG-GEN-006 | Unchanged; the transaction rolls back and the activity retries |
| A `treatment` row with a document reference | A new template version in force | A new request with the new version on or after its valid-from date | The reference and the version of the new request; the earlier document keeps its own version on the document side |

The document's own lifecycle is not this story's: `source` GENERATED, state DRAFT and `write_once` false are the values of the generated draft, and the review out of DRAFT and the write-once switch on send belong to the screens story of this key (RWB-P5-E2017-APP). The treatment's `state` column is not moved here.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-RESTRUCT, restructuring officer (FCR) | Treatment and offer CRUA in the TSD S2 T6.1 matrix: runs the generation from the treatment screen and reads the reference and the version it produced |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Treatment and offer CRU: the same in scope |
| RW-SPECIAL, hardship and vulnerability specialist (CRU); RW-GUARANT, guarantee officer (CRU) | Read the treatment and its document reference on cases in scope; the request is the officer's |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager (R); RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL, RW-CONDUCT, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-BIANAL, RW-TRIBE (R) | Read the reference and the version on cases in scope; generate nothing |
| RW-CREDCOMM, credit approval committee member (RA); RW-PRODHEAD, product head (RA) | Read the reference; the approval itself is RWB-S2-E3003-APP's |
| SY-CASEWF, the case workflow module (R) | Calls the generation for rule-driven generation through the stage, with the service identity of `rwb_treatment`, as R-DIL-16 names |
| The rwb-treatment service identity (login `rwb_treatment`, DP-02) | Builds the request, calls the contract once, writes the two columns, the record and the outbox row in one transaction, and holds no grant on `rwb_document`, `rwb_comms`, `rwb_case` or a `v_ace_*` view |
| rwb-document (P5) service identity | Owns the engine, the documents, the types and the files; answers the generate operation and is never written by this story |
| rwb-comms (P6) service identity | Owns `template` and `merge_field` and the Legal approval of a version; this story reads neither table and calls no P6 operation |
| No delegation of authority level applies | The treatment was approved at D6.4 before generation; this story requests documents and records their reference |

No credential and no personal name appears in the request, the row, the record, the event or the logs. Where a person must be named the row carries a user identifier, never a name.
