##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test asset in the integration pipeline and serves no operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; the 2 s timeout and the circuit breaker per downstream of DP-11 apply to every row.

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/generated-documents` | P5 rwb-document | The generation request under test (AC1 to AC8), with the Idempotency-Key header |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` | P5 rwb-document | The generated documents and their type, source, state, template code and version (AC1, AC3, AC4, AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}` | P5 rwb-document | The document metadata, the merge snapshot reference and the rendered file the harness opens (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC7) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/admin/templates` | P6 rwb-comms | The template code, version, language, product group and approved_by_legal state the journey starts from (AC1, AC3, AC4, AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}` | S2 rwb-treatment | Treatment type, decision_log_id and outcome (AC1, AC6) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | P7 rwb-decision | The decision record with decision code "D6.4", the inputs reference and, for a set, the three codes and versions (AC1, AC4, AC5, AC7, AC8) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The role, the scope and the Documents right the generation runs under (TC-E2-026-15-ITG) |

Every POST carries an Idempotency-Key kept for the parameter row GEN_IDEMPOTENCY_HOURS of 24 (BR9). The merge field values themselves are resolved inside rwb-document through the providers owned by rwb-case, rwb-treatment and rwb-source-data; the harness never calls those providers and asserts the values only through the merge snapshot and the rendered file.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event; the evidence goes to the release record through its pipeline integration.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` | `rwb.document.events.v1` | P5 rwb-document | One event per stored document, inside the run window (AC1, AC4), and no event for a refused document (AC2, AC5, AC7) |
| `rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1` | `rwb.treatment.events.v1` | S2 rwb-treatment | Confirms the seeded treatment the generation runs on reached its approved state (AC1, AC6) |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 rwb-decision (ledger); every service publishes its own record | Asserts that the record of the generation reached the shared topic inside the run window, alongside the ledger read of section 12.2 (AC1, AC4, AC7) |

The harness subscribes with its own consumer group and asserts the events, never the producer's table.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

Observed only. JOB-12 Document intake is the workflow `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` on queue `rwb-document`, and its `generate` and `seal` activities are the ones that render and store the file the harness opens (Architecture v5 slide 16; job map slide 44). JOB-11 Outbox sender is observed on its every-minute window for the `DocumentStored` and `DecisionRecorded` events.

The harness starts no workflow, adds no activity and writes no schedule. Both jobs are owner-built by P5 and by the platform outbox library.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The harness run is started by the test pipeline, not by a Temporal Schedule and not by Airflow.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no table in any schema. rwb-document writes `rwb_document` through its own Flyway sequence (DP-01, DP-15); the harness reads the result through the operations of section 12.2 only.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Contract | What it answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| WireMock rwb-document | generated-documents, cases/{caseId}/documents, documents/{documentId} | OpenAPI of P5 | 201 with the generated document set, 422 with MSG-P5-009, MSG-P5-010 or MSG-GEN-001, 409 with MSG-P5-011 or MSG-GEN-004, 503 with MSG-P7-003 or MSG-GEN-006, per scenario; keeps the request journal for the idempotency and counter assertions |
| WireMock rwb-comms | admin/templates | OpenAPI of P6 | DIL-CONTRACT version 2 in Thai for MORTGAGE with approved_by_legal true; DIL-CONTRACT version 3 valid from 2026-12-15; DIL-CA with version 1 not approved; DIL-MORTGAGE withdrawn; the HIRE_PURCHASE refusal |
| WireMock rwb-treatment | treatments/{treatmentId} | OpenAPI of S2 | TRT-0301 of type DEED_IN_LIEU with decision_log_id set and no outcome; TRT-0302 with no decision_log_id |
| WireMock rwb-access | me/session | OpenAPI of P4 | RW-RESTRUCT and RW-CASEOWN in scope with Documents C; RW-TEAMMGR with Documents R refused with MSG-P4-002; the out-of-scope case with MSG-P4-003 |
| WireMock rwb-decision | decision-log | OpenAPI of P7 | The decision record with decision code "D6.4", the inputs reference and the three codes and versions; 503 for AC7 |
| Renderer shares of the P5 contract | The `generate` and `seal` activities of `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` | The P5 activity contract | A PDF/A-2b file with the Thai fonts embedded, and a damaged body for the render failure case |

The PDF/A-2b conformance check and the embedded Thai font check are harness assertions, not new business rules. The document container path, the seed pack and the evidence format: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0408; ASM-0583).

Each fake is replaced by the real service as its I story lands, without a change to the scenarios.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 7 consumed, one hop on the owner's base with the 2 s timeout of DP-11 |
| Kafka | 3 events consumed on three topics; none published |
| Temporal | Observed only: JOB-12 `DocumentIntakeWorkflow` on queue `rwb-document` and JOB-11 outbox relay; no workflow, activity or schedule added |
| File | The rendered file of each document is opened and asserted against the draft container; the harness writes no file of its own outside its evidence pack |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `integration/recovery-document-generation` in the ACE repository, package `<ACE base package>.recovery.integration.documentgeneration`. Not part of any deployed service and not in any service schema.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added | How this harness applies it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none | The harness owns no table and reads no schema; every document, template, treatment and decision fact comes from an operation of section 12.2 |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The generation record is read through rwb-decision and the `DecisionRecorded` event is read on the shared topic; the harness writes no ledger entry |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none | Party and collateral facts reach the file through rwb-source-data and rwb-document; the harness asserts them in the merge snapshot and the rendered file only |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON | GEN_IDEMPOTENCY_HOURS, GEN_MAX_TEMPLATES and GEN_FONT are seeded parameter rows read through the contract, never values in the harness code |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The document types and the template-to-document-type mapping are seeded reference data, asserted through the operation that returns them |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON | The harness subscribes with its own consumer group to the three topics and asserts the events, never the outbox table |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) | Each of the seven consumed operations is called once from the harness with a 2 s timeout and a breaker, and the generation POST carries the Idempotency-Key |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON | The harness runs no migration; it reads the document columns the P5 Flyway sequence added through the operation, and fails the run on any direct schema read in the trace |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The journey runs through the gateway route the real screens use, on the same owner bases, so the route is exercised and not bypassed |

The platform H dependencies in the table are delivered by the platform wave and are not repeated in the metadata; the harness converges on them and has no build dependency of its own. The blocking dependencies are the seven I stories, which replace the fakes one at a time.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Job | Runs the twelve flow steps for one scenario and one business date, and stops at the first failed assertion with the trace |
| FakeRegistry | Configuration | WireMock mapping sets for the five services and the renderer shares, one set per contract version |
| TemplateFixturePack | Data | Templates, versions, Legal approval state, merge field lists, document types and the type mapping per scenario, as data files |
| MergeSnapshotAssertion | Assertion | Compares the merge snapshot reference with the case facts and the values that reached the file |
| PdfAssertion | Assertion | Opens the rendered file and compares the formatted amount, the Thai words, the Buddhist Era date and the PDF/A-2b and font conformance |
| DecisionAssertion | Assertion | Reads the decision log and the shared topic and compares decision code "D6.4", the inputs reference and the template codes and versions |
| EvidenceCollector | Service | Writes one report keyed by story key and business date, with request, response, document metadata, file values, snapshot reference and decision record |
| GateEvaluator | Service | Passes the run when every owned scenario passes and the evidence pack is attached to the wave 2 release record |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, the wave 2 harness profile, one business date, synthetic case "RW-2026-000301" and synthetic treatment "TRT-0301" with the seeded templates and case facts of section 3. No production record is copied, and no real national ID number is seeded (BR11). The harness environment, its seed pack, its container path and its evidence format: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0408; ASM-0583). Each run starts from the seeded state, so a repeated run is deterministic and produces the same report.

**Build steps**

1. Write the TemplateFixturePack and the SeedPack from the Background and the eight scenarios, with the template codes, versions, approval states, merge fields, document types and parameter rows as data; test that a bad seed stops the run (X13).
2. Write FakeRegistry with the five WireMock sets and the renderer shares, published from the same OpenAPI documents the services publish.
3. Write JourneyRunner for AC1 and assert the document metadata, the merge snapshot, the rendered values and the decision record across the five boundaries.
4. Add the refusal paths AC2, AC5 and AC6 with the counter assertions: no document row, no file and no decision record on a refusal.
5. Add AC3 with the two versions and the document generated before the valid-from date, and assert that the earlier file still opens.
6. Add AC4 with the three-template set, then AC7 with the decision log unavailable and the draft file removed.
7. Add AC8 with the repeated key and the request journal, then X8, X9 and the access and scope failures through the fakes.
8. Write EvidenceCollector and GateEvaluator, attach the report to the wave 2 release record, and rerun the eight scenarios on the release build.

**Feature switch.** The production switch the journey exercises is `rwb.dochub.generation-engine`, owned by RWB-P5-E2026-APP: off, the operation answers 404 and nothing is generated; on, the journey runs. The harness itself is a pipeline stage selected by the run profile, not by a business flag, and has no production switch.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the run report is attached to the wave 2 release record with all eight owned scenarios and their evidence, and each fake has been replaced by the real service where its I story has landed in SIT. The container path, the seed pack and the evidence format wait for the values of GAP-0408.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P5-009 | A required merge field has no value (new) | {template} cannot be generated. {field} has no value on the case. |
| MSG-P5-010 | No current template version approved by Legal (new) | {template} has no version approved by Legal for {product} in {language}. |
| MSG-P5-011 | The treatment is not approved or not open (new) | Documents can be generated only for an approved {treatment} that is still open. |
| MSG-P6-003 | The template is withdrawn | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | templateCodes is empty | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A concurrent request for the same treatment and template | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The renderer fails | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Caller lacks Documents C | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |

Thai text for each message follows decision DL10. The harness asserts these messages and never rewrites them; its own report text is for the release team and is not part of the message standard.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: template codes, merge field names, value formats, the template-to-document-type mapping and the font are data files and parameter rows, never constants in the harness.
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs, logs, evidence or prompts. Merge values and the merge snapshot are never logged in clear; the evidence keeps identifiers, statuses and timestamps only, and the clear national ID number stays inside the stored file (BR11).
- No read of another service's tables and no schema of the harness's own: every read goes through the operations of section 12.2 (DP-01, DP-15), and a cross-schema reference found in the trace fails the run.
- No document is produced from a template version without approved_by_legal true, and no scenario may seed one to make a run pass.
- Each fake is replaced by the real service as its I story lands; a fake that outlives its service is a defect, not a configuration.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and an exception is never added to a scenario; a value that must change changes in the seed pack through a reviewed change.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract baseline of rwb-payment for the payment-matching key — the rule-evaluation result this service consumes from rwb-decision with the package code, the version in force, the rule ID, the row order and the outputs, the local decision-record envelope on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the three event schemas of `rwb.payment.events.v1`, `GET /proceeds` and `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` with their `Idempotency-Key` rule and RFC 9457 problem responses, and the rule that every match records the package version in force with no breaking change without a new version — with the fakes that answer them**, so that **RWB-P8-E2027-APP, the screen route of SCR-28, rwb-decision and the wave 2 harness build against one frozen, testable surface on Day 1 and a field, an event type, a version label or an error shape can never drift between them without a failing build**.

This story publishes the contract only. It writes no code, no migration and no table, it matches no payment, and it moves nothing.

The contract sits on the naming the service already has (Arch v5 slide 41 notes; Template and Rules §R4): schema `rwb_payment`, login per service, REST base `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, topic `rwb.payment.events.v1` with its `.retry` and `.dlt` topics, event names `rwb.payment.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-payment` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.payment`. The shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` is the platform library's.

The legacy acceptance criteria AC1 to AC10 of RWB-E2-027 are **not** copied here. AC6, AC7 and AC10 are owned word for word by RWB-P8-E2027-APP, AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5, AC8 and AC9 by RWB-P8-E2008-APP, and AC3 by RWB-P7-E2027-APP; every criterion of section 7 is new under D-RCV-60 and tests only the contract deliverable in this title.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling decision (DP-11, ADR-020), and embedded Drools per service with the rule registry in rwb-decision is its companion (ADR-017, DP-04). Both only work if two things are fixed before any code: the shape of the rule answer this service receives from another team's service, and the shape of the money answer this service gives to the rest of the platform. Without the first, rwb-payment would invent its own reading of the rule result and the package version on a record would stop being comparable across services; without the second, rwb-case, rwb-asset, rwb-debtsale, rwb-writeoff and rwb-guarantee would each parse `ProceedsMatched` in their own way.

The baseline therefore fixes four surfaces and one rule.

- **The rule answer.** `rwb-decision` publishes an evaluation result for a package code and a business date. The Temporal and Drools design names it as `RuleResult(packageCode, packageVersion, ruleId, outputs)`; this baseline adds the row order the matching key needs and reads the version field as the version in force, and marks both as the working read until rwb-decision publishes its own schema (GAP-2507; ASM-4153). The row order is what makes the first-match rule testable at the contract level without any business threshold in the document.
- **The record.** The local decision record is the platform library's (DP-03): a match writes it in the same transaction as the `proceeds` row and publishes `DecisionRecorded` on the shared topic. This baseline declares the envelope and the fields the matching record carries and declares no topic of its own for it.
- **The events.** `TreatmentBooked` (EV-11), `PaymentMissed` (EV-12) and `ProceedsMatched` (EV-25) are produced by this service on `rwb.payment.events.v1` (Arch v5 slides 42 and 43; slide 17). TSD P8 v2 T5.3 gives their names and direction and no payload, so the payload field lists are published here from the legacy facts and marked (GAP-2507; ASM-4155).
- **The two operations.** `GET /proceeds` (API-P8-001) and `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` (API-P8-002) are this service's, with the rights of TSD P8 T6.1, the `Idempotency-Key` rule of the second and the problem response of the platform.
- **One rule about change.** The package version in force is recorded on every match, and no consumer of the result may see a breaking change without a new version and a new registry row. That is what makes a match explainable a year later.

The baseline also records what it does not own. The registry, the governance of a version, the load checks, the four-eyes approval and the 00:01 promotion are rwb-decision's (RWB-P7-E2027-APP). The workbook is rwb-case's (RWB-P3-E2042-APP). The money is matched and written here, and the case, the balance, the posting and the ledger are not.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service naming rule is in force (RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the topic, the retry topic, the `.dlt` topic, the queue and the event names follow the platform rule rather than a local choice (DP-13, DP-14).
- The platform error envelope, the pagination convention and the `Idempotency-Key` rule are the platform baseline (Arch v5 slide 11; RWB-PLT-N009-CON); where this document narrows them it does so explicitly.
- The ownership of every object is taken from the Ownership Map only: `proceeds` is P8's, `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` are P7's, `treatment` is S2's, `recovery_case` is P3's and `decision_record` is a PLT library object created in each schema.
- The rule registry answers as `RWB-P7-E2027-APP` and `RWB-P7-E1073-CON` describe it; the model fetch and the checksum are named in the Temporal and Drools design (slide 15 notes) and are fixed here as consumed rows.
- The local decision-record library and the shared topic are `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`; this baseline declares the envelope as consumed and adds no second writer.
- The event catalogue is `Arch v5` slides 42 and 43: `TreatmentBooked` is row 11, `PaymentMissed` is row 12 and `ProceedsMatched` is row 25, and `DecisionRecorded` is row 08 on the shared topic whose consumers the catalogue lists as rwb-decision and rwb-reporting. The key's service conventions list `DecisionRecorded` as consumed here; the difference is recorded and read as a ledger acknowledgement of this service's own record (GAP-2507; ASM-4154).
- The rule-evaluation result has no published schema and the operation names of the version-in-force lookup and of the treatment installment-paid call are not given by any source; both carry the placeholder (GAP-2507; ASM-4153).
- No build dependency and no approval stop: a CON story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7) and is published at status Draft (realignment v1).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the OpenAPI 3.1 document of rwb-payment for this key: the two operations of 12.1 with their query, their request and answer elements and their seven error responses, under the base `/api/recovery/payment/v1`.
2. Fix the `Proceeds` element from the `proceeds` columns of DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009, with the match outcome on `matched_to`, `source`, `amount`, `received_date` and `posting_ref`, and no property added for a threshold, a rule row or a case state.
3. Fix the consumed rule-evaluation result: the package code, the version in force, the rule ID, the row order and the outputs, with the two fields the sources do not name marked with the placeholder.
4. Fix the local decision-record envelope on `rwb.decision-record.v1`: the record fields a match carries, the transaction rule and the hash chain, declared as the library's and not as this service's own event.
5. Fix the three event schemas of `rwb.payment.events.v1`: the CloudEvents attribute set, the `ce_type` of each, the key `caseId`, the payload field list and the rule that the payload carries identifiers and facts only.
6. Fix the `Idempotency-Key` rule of the manual match, the seven error responses and the rights of the two operations against TSD P8 T6.1.
7. Publish the five contract fakes of 12.8 and the drift test that compares each fake with the document.
8. Tag the baseline and hand it to RWB-P8-E2027-APP, the screen route of SCR-28 and the wave 2 harness; rwb-decision and rwb-treatment consume it as the answer they must give.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A request or answer body fails schema validation | The schema lint fails the build; a deployed service answers 400 or 500 with the problem envelope | MSG-GEN-001 | AC4, AC5 |
| X2 | A field is renamed, removed or retyped within major version 1 | The contract test fails; the change needs a new major version and a new `ce_type` for an event | None | AC6 |
| X3 | A fake drifts from the document | The drift test fails the build and blocks the merge | None | AC6 |
| X4 | A field of the rule-evaluation result, of the record envelope or of an event payload is not given by any source | The row carries the placeholder, the gap and the assumption, and the fake is derived from the published document | None | AC1, AC2, AC3 |
| X5 | A business threshold, a match type or a version label appears as an enumeration member or a default in the document | The vocabulary test fails the build; the values are rule-row data and registry rows | None | AC1, AC6 |
| X6 | The document declares another service's table as owned, adds a `v_ace_*` read it may not have, or names a second topic for the record | The boundary test fails the build | None | AC2, AC6 |
| X7 | A manual match is repeated with the same `Idempotency-Key` | The stored answer is returned and no second effect is described | None | AC5 |
| X8 | The rights of an operation are not the ones TSD P8 T-A.2 declares | The access test fails the build | MSG-P4-002 | AC4, AC5 |
| X9 | A published event body does not match the accepted schema version | The registry refuses the body in BACKWARD mode and the producing build fails | None | AC3 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the Ownership Map, the Architecture v5 catalogue and the published contracts of rwb-decision and rwb-treatment only |
| Negotiable | The element names beyond the ones the sources give, the example values and the fixture set are settled in the baseline review; the base, the topic, the queue, the two paths, the rights and the event types are fixed by the target architecture |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app story, the screen route of SCR-28, the wave 2 harness and the rwb-decision and rwb-treatment teams on Day 1 |
| Estimable | One OpenAPI document, one AsyncAPI fragment, the nine contract tables, five fakes and a drift test |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, never against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Contract baseline of rwb-payment for the payment matching key

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule of the platform library is in force
    Given the ownership of proceeds is P8, of rule_package and rule_row is P7 and of treatment is S2
    Given every consumed contract is the published contract of its owner and is answered by its fake

  Scenario: AC1 The consumed rule-evaluation result is declared with the package code, the version in force, the rule ID, the row order and the outputs (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the declaration of the rule-evaluation result in the contract document
    When it is validated against the schema lint of the pipeline
    Then it declares the result as the answer of rwb-decision (P7) with packageCode, versionInForce, ruleId, rowOrder and outputs, and with the rule ID and the row order of the fired row only
    Then the version field is declared as the version in force on the requested business date and not as a caller argument
    Then outputs is declared as the named output columns of the fired row and carries no free-form text and no payment or customer field
    Then the result declares the NoPackageInForce outcome and no default row, no default version and no fallback result
    Then no business threshold, no match type and no version label appears in the document as an enumeration member, a default or an example constant
    Then the field names the sources do not give are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2507; ASM-4153) and the document marks them so
    Then the result declares one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker and no retry of its own (DP-11)

  Scenario: AC2 The local decision-record envelope is declared on rwb.decision-record.v1 and written before the row (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the decision-record section of the baseline
    When it is compared with RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and with DP-03
    Then one record is declared per match with the entry ID, the case reference, the decision code D5, the rule ID, the rule version, the inputs reference, the final call, the decided-at time, the chain sequence, the previous hash, the entry hash and the actor reference
    Then the record is declared as written through the local library in the caller's transaction, before the proceeds row, and a failed write leaves the match unmade with MSG-P7-003
    Then the envelope is declared as CloudEvents 1.0 binary mode on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1 with the type of EV-08, and this service declares no topic of its own for the record
    Then the record carries identifiers, codes, an amount, a date and a rule version only, and no personal data
    Then the document declares no write of decision_log_entry and no read of any registry table

  Scenario: AC3 The three event schemas of rwb.payment.events.v1 are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the event section of the baseline
    When one body of each type is validated against the registry in BACKWARD mode
    Then TreatmentBooked is declared as rwb.payment.TreatmentBooked.v1 (EV-11), PaymentMissed as rwb.payment.PaymentMissed.v1 (EV-12) and ProceedsMatched as rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1 (EV-25), each on rwb.payment.events.v1
    Then each envelope declares CloudEvents 1.0 binary mode with ce_specversion 1.0, ce_id, ce_type, ce_source, ce_subject, ce_time and the trace header, keyed by caseId
    Then ProceedsMatched carries the case, the proceeds, the payment code, the treatment, the source, the amount, the matched-to, the rule ID, the rule version and the received date
    Then PaymentMissed carries the case, the treatment, the due date, the amount due and the business date, and TreatmentBooked carries the case, the treatment, the booking reference, the amount and the booking date
    Then every payload carries identifiers, codes, amounts and dates only and no name, e-mail address, mobile number, national identity number or account number
    Then the field lists the sources do not give are marked with the placeholder (GAP-2507; ASM-4155)
    Then the .retry topic and the .dlt topic are declared for the topic and the producer writes to its outbox in the same transaction as the state change

  Scenario: AC4 GET /proceeds is declared with its query, its answer and its right (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the provided operations of the baseline
    When they are compared with TSD P8 T-A.1 and T-A.2
    Then GET /api/recovery/payment/v1/proceeds is declared with the query matched, from, to, page and size and the answer ProceedsPage (API-P8-001)
    Then the Proceeds element carries the nine proceeds fields of DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009 and the rule ID and rule version of its decision record, and no case state and no balance
    Then the operation declares Write-off and posting R with the scope applied, and answers 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 409 and 503 as RFC 9457 problem responses with messageId
    Then the document declares no second list operation for the same receipts and no read of another service's table

  Scenario: AC5 POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match is declared with its Idempotency-Key rule, its errors and its right (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the manual match section of the baseline
    When it is compared with TSD P8 T-A.2 and T6.1
    Then POST /api/recovery/payment/v1/proceeds/{proceedsId}/match is declared with a MatchRequest in and a Proceeds answer out (API-P8-002)
    Then the operation requires the Idempotency-Key header, stores its answer and returns the stored answer on a repeat without a second effect
    Then it declares Write-off and posting U with the scope applied and answers 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 for an unknown proceeds, 409 for a receipt already matched, 422 with MSG-GEN-001 and 503, each as one problem response with one message ID
    Then the document names the behaviour behind the operation as the Epic 4 story of this service and declares no rule evaluation of its own for it
    Then the request element carries the case reference, the account reference and the match target only, and no personal field

  Scenario: AC6 The version in force is recorded on every match and no breaking change is made without a new version (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the versioning section of the baseline and the published fakes
    When the document and the five fakes are compared
    Then the rule-evaluation result, the record, the three event payloads and the Proceeds answer all carry the version in force, and a match without it is declared invalid
    Then an additive change within major version 1 keeps the version and is accepted by the registry in BACKWARD mode, and a breaking change raises a new major version and a new ce_type
    Then the document declares that a new rule package version needs a new registry row in rwb-decision and no redefinition of the result shape
    Then the rwb-decision registry fake answers the version list, the model fetch with its checksum, the refused schema check of "PM-2027.02" and NoPackageInForce for 2027-02-01
    Then the treatment fake answers the installment-paid call and its refusal, and the rwb-access fake answers a session with and without the right
    Then the drift test compares every fake with the document and fails the build on any difference, and a fake that adds a threshold or a match type fails the vocabulary test
```

These six criteria are new for the contract baseline and test the artefact only. They copy no criterion of RWB-E2-027 and restate no business outcome owned by RWB-P8-E2027-APP: the three legacy criteria of the matching rules stay with the app story, the ten of the exact and exception behaviour with RWB-P8-E2008-APP and RWB-P7-E2027-APP, and the end-to-end journey with the wave 2 harness.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The contract declares the two operations, the three event types, the record envelope and the consumed rule-evaluation result, and nothing else | Architecture v5 slide 17 and 41; TSD P8 v2 T-A.1; Ownership Map |
| BR2 | The rule-evaluation result is declared as consumed from rwb-decision and carries the package code, the version in force, the rule ID, the row order and the outputs; the version in force is the registry's answer and never a caller argument | DP-04; Temporal and Drools slide 16; GAP-2507 |
| BR3 | The record is the platform library's on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, written in the caller's transaction before the proceeds row; a failed write leaves the match unmade | DP-03; legacy BR8; R-UNI-39 |
| BR4 | `TreatmentBooked`, `PaymentMissed` and `ProceedsMatched` are published on `rwb.payment.events.v1` in CloudEvents 1.0 keyed by `caseId`, with the `.retry` and `.dlt` topics, and carry identifiers and facts only | DP-14; Architecture v5 slides 42 and 43; slide 17 |
| BR5 | A POST declares the `Idempotency-Key` and stores its answer; a GET declares none | Architecture v5 slide 11; TSD P8 T-A.2 |
| BR6 | The rights are those of TSD P8 T6.1: Write-off and posting R for the read and U for the manual match, each with the scope applied | TSD P8 v2 T-A.2 and T6.1; RWB-E2-027 section 10 |
| BR7 | The vocabulary is closed: LOV-MATCH, LOV-MATCH-TYPE and LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC are reference rows read through DP-07 and are never enumeration members of the document or constants of the code | TSD P8 v2 T3.2; DP-07; legacy BR10 |
| BR8 | No business value in the contract: the tolerance, the window, the grace, the partial floor and the row order are columns of the PAYMENT_MATCH rows and registry rows, never schema defaults or example constants | D-RCV-36 T10; legacy BR10; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR9 | The version in force is recorded on every match, and a breaking change to a published element raises a new major version and a new `ce_type`; a new rule package version needs a new registry row | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes (BACKWARD compatibility); ADR-017; D-RCV-36 T7 |
| BR10 | The document declares no `v_ace_*` grant it may not hold, no `proceeds` property of another owner and no registry table; every consumed read is a published operation or a view of this service | DP-01, DP-05; Architecture v5 slide 41 |
| BR11 | One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; the document never declares another service's base, topic or queue as its own | DP-13, DP-14; Template and Rules §R4 |
| BR12 | No personal data in a schema, an example or a fake: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates, a rule ID and a version label only | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

##### 9. State transitions

This document has a lifecycle, not a business state machine.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The two operations, the three event types, the record envelope and the consumed result are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | RWB-P8-E2027-APP, the SCR-28 route, the wave 2 harness and the rwb-decision and rwb-treatment owners accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A property is added within major version 1 | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A property is removed, renamed or retyped, or an event type or a required field changes | New major version drafted |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A forbidden element appears | The boundary test of AC2 and AC6 fails: a registry table, a second topic or a business constant | In review |

The `proceeds` row states this contract describes — matched to INSTALLMENT, matched to another target, or UNMATCHED with its reason — are the app story's. The package version states LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK and REFUSED are rwb-decision's and are named here only as the value the version field carries.

No person is named in the document, an example or a fake. The rwb-payment login is named "the rwb-payment login (DP-02)" and its secret is not part of this baseline.

##### 11. Data

The contract baseline declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| `Proceeds` element | The columns of DF-FIN-001 to DF-FIN-009: `id`, `case_id`, `treatment_id`, `account_payment_id`, `source`, `amount`, `received_date`, `matched_to` and `posting_ref`; plus the rule ID and the rule version read from the record of the match |
| Consumed rule-evaluation result | `packageCode`, `versionInForce`, `ruleId`, `rowOrder` and `outputs`; the two names the sources do not give are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2507; ASM-4153) |
| Decision record | DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031 through the local library, written before the row (DP-03) |
| Events | The three payloads of 12.3 with identifiers, codes, amounts and dates only |
| Registry tables | `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` are P7's and are named as reached only through the operations of 12.2; no field of them is declared here |
| ACE facts | `v_ace_payment` and `v_ace_account` are read by this service under DP-05; the document declares no foreign key, no copy and no cross-schema read |
| Not written here | `recovery_case` (P3), `treatment` (S2), `decision_log_entry` (P7) and `asset` or `debtsale` tables (S5, S6) |

No new table, no new column and no migration is declared by this story. `payment_match_rule` and DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 are retired and appear in the document only as the assertion that no shape may recreate them (D-RCV-36 T10).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-payment` (P8); base `/api/recovery/payment/v1` (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/proceeds` | Query `matched`, `from`, `to`, `page`, `size`; `ProceedsPage` of status 200 out (API-P8-001) | Write-off and posting R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |
| POST | `/proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` | `MatchRequest` in, `Proceeds` of status 200 out (API-P8-002); the behaviour is the Epic 4 story RWB-P8-E4043-APP | Write-off and posting U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header required; the answer is stored |

The `Proceeds` element carries `id`, `caseId`, `treatmentId`, `accountPaymentId`, `source`, `amount`, `receivedDate`, `matchedTo`, `postingRef`, `ruleId` and `ruleVersion`. Errors: 401 no session; 403 the role lacks the right (MSG-P4-002); 404 an unknown proceeds or an unknown case reference; 409 the receipt is already matched or the version changed at commit; 422 a required field is invalid (MSG-GEN-001); 503 a downstream or the record library does not answer (MSG-P7-003). Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set. The service's other operation `GET /cases/{caseId}/payments` is the first API path of the service on Arch v5 slide 41 and belongs to another key of this service; it is not declared here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the document |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` | P7 rwb-decision | The version in force on the business date and its checksum; the document fixes the fields it reads, not the operation |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}` | P7 rwb-decision | The model of the version in force and its checksum, fetched once per version (DP-04; Temporal and Drools slide 15 notes) |
| The version-in-force evaluation read (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2507; ASM-4153)) | `/api/recovery/decision/v1` | P7 rwb-decision | The shape of the consumed rule-evaluation result of AC1; the document declares it as the answer rwb-decision publishes |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | The parameters of the run, through the client library (DP-06) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-MATCH, LOV-MATCH-TYPE and LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC (DP-07) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The role, the scope and the Write-off and posting right behind the two operations of 12.1 |
| POST | The installment-paid operation of rwb-treatment (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2507; ASM-4153)) | S2 rwb-treatment | The installment paid and the shortfall of a PARTIAL match, declared as consumed and faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker (DP-11, ADR-020). The two rwb-decision registry operations and the evaluation result are class-C contract dependencies of DP-04 (`RWB-P7-E1073-CON`) and of the registry story, and this document's contract-dependency row is None; the absence is recorded in GAP-2507 and ASM-4152.

The document declares the workflow and activity names and their task queue because a consuming team must know which queue carries the work; it registers nothing. The Drools evaluation runs only inside an activity, so a replay reuses the recorded result and never recompiles a model; `NoPackageInForce` is non-retryable.

##### 13. Solution plan

**The CON declares shapes and moves nothing.** It publishes one OpenAPI 3.1 document, one AsyncAPI fragment, the nine contract tables, five fakes and a drift test. It writes no code, no migration and no table, and it changes no payment, no plan, no case and no rule package.

**Deliverables.** `openapi/rwb-payment-v1.yaml` (additive, for the two operations of 12.1), `asyncapi/rwb-payment-v1.yaml` (the three events and the record), the `Proceeds`, `ProceedsPage` and `MatchRequest` elements, the declared rule-evaluation result, the record envelope, the vocabulary of LOV-MATCH, LOV-MATCH-TYPE and LOV-PROCEEDS-SRC as published reference lists, the contract README rows for the seven consumed operations and the five WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | referred to; the app story carries the dependency |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | referred to; the app story carries the dependency |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | C RWB-P7-E1073-CON in fact, not in the metadata row |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | referred to; the app story carries the dependency |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | referred to; the app story carries the dependency |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | referred to; the app story carries the dependency |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | referred to; the app story carries the dependency |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | referred to; the app story carries the dependency |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | referred to; the app story carries the dependency |

DP-04 is the row this document exists for: the kit is the platform's and the packages come from rwb-decision, so the one thing every team must agree on is the shape of the answer (AC1). DP-03 is the second: the record is written by the library in the caller's transaction and this service declares no second writer or topic (AC2). DP-13 and DP-14 fix the base and the event names, and DP-11 fixes the one-hop budget the document states on every consumed row. The metadata rows of this story name None for the build and contract dependencies; the C row of DP-04 is recorded in GAP-2507 and ASM-4152 because a CON story is Day 1 and builds against the published set.

**Build steps**

1. Write the two operations of AC4 and AC5 and validate the additive rule in the pipeline.
2. Write the `Proceeds`, `ProceedsPage` and `MatchRequest` elements and the two error sets with one message ID per condition.
3. Write the declaration of the consumed rule-evaluation result of AC1 and mark the two fields the sources do not give.
4. Write the record envelope of AC2 and validate it against the library schema of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON.
5. Write the AsyncAPI fragment of AC3 and validate one body of each type against the registry fake.
6. Write the versioning and version-recording rules of AC6 and the vocabulary of the closed lists.
7. Publish the five fakes and the drift test; wire the drift test into the build of the app story, the SCR-28 route and the wave 2 harness.
8. Tag the baseline and collect the consumer sign-off.

**Done when.** The OpenAPI document and the AsyncAPI fragment validate, the six contract tests pass, the drift test is green on the build of this story and of the app story, and the app story, the SCR-28 route, the wave 2 harness, rwb-decision and rwb-treatment have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P8-001 | A run summary holds unmatched payments; the document declares the field that carries the count and not the wording | {count} payments for {date} matched no plan and are on the exception list. |
| MSG-P3-027 | A package version check fails, or no version is in force; the document declares the message ID the run summary carries | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field of a request is absent or invalid | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The record changed at commit, or a receipt was already matched | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written before the row | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks the Write-off and posting right the operation declares | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The six message IDs are legacy or catalogue identifiers and the text is the legacy and FSD wording copied unchanged; the contract adds no message ID and rewords nothing. For MSG-P3-027 the {check} value is compile, schema, scenario or package in force and {detail} names a row ID, a column or a package code only. Thai text follows DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

The contract serves SCR-28 Proceeds matching in its loading, matched and unmatched states through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The route calls `GET /proceeds` for the list and reads the rule ID and the rule version of each matched receipt from its record; it calls the manual match operation for the Epic 4 flow of the same screen. The contract fixes the rwb-payment answers only: the route specification, the field list and the screen states belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and the version list a person reads to see LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED and REFUSED is rwb-decision's, shown by SCR-39 Rules and parameters in Epic 8. The refusal states the screen shows — not recorded, refused, already matched, no version in force — read the message IDs of section 14 on the same route.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the match type, the row order, the amount tolerance, the window, the grace and the partial floor are columns of the PAYMENT_MATCH rows and rows of the registry, never enumeration members, defaults or example constants.
- No personal data in a schema, an example, a fake or a log: identifiers, codes, amounts, dates, a rule ID and a version label only; every example is synthetic.
- The money is matched here and nowhere else: the document declares no posting, no balance change and no property of `recovery_case`, `treatment` or a ledger table.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or this service's `v_ace_*` views, and no cross-schema foreign key; the boundary test fails a build that adds one (DP-01, DP-05).
- One evaluator, one result: the document declares the consumed result and no evaluation of its own, and it never reads a workbook, a `drl_source` or a `rule_row` (DP-04).
- The record is written before the row and on the shared topic only; this service declares no second writer and no second topic for it (DP-03).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; a document that names another service's base or topic as its own fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- A published version is never edited in place: a breaking change raises a new major version and a new `ce_type`, and a new rule package version needs a new registry row (BR9).
- No secret in the document, a fake or a values file: the rwb-payment login (DP-02) and the Temporal material come from the platform secret store.

##### 1. Story

As a **Credit Administration officer (RW-CREDITAD)**, I want **the matching rules for amount, date window and partial payments held as rows of the PAYMENT_MATCH rule package, the package read from rwb-decision's registry and evaluated in this service by the embedded Drools kit in row order, each match recorded as a local decision record that names the rule ID and the package version in force and then written to `proceeds` in `rwb_payment`, with the exception list for what does not match**, so that **most payments match without a person, the rest are listed, and every match can be explained by the row and the approved version that decided it**.

This story is the rwb-payment half of the legacy key RWB-E2-027. It runs inside:

- service `rwb-payment`, schema `rwb_payment`, REST base `/api/recovery/payment/v1`, topic `rwb.payment.events.v1` with its `.retry` and `.dlt` topics and the event names `rwb.payment.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-payment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.payment` (DP-01, DP-13, DP-14);
- the tables this service owns: `proceeds` only, plus the library objects `decision_record`, `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key` created in `rwb_payment` by its own Flyway sequence (DP-03, DP-15);
- the rule registry of `rwb-decision` (`rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row`, `rule_test_case`) as a **read-only source**: this service holds only a local evaluated copy of the model, verifies its checksum and swaps it in on `RulePackageInForce` (DP-04; ASM-4148).

What stays outside this story:

- the registry and the governance of a package version — the load, its checks, the four-eyes approval, the 00:01 promotion, the one-call rollback and the version states — with `rwb-decision` (P7, RWB-P7-E2027-APP);
- the PAYMENT_MATCH workbook, its Rows and Tests tabs and the authoring pipeline, with `rwb-case` (P3, RWB-P3-E2042-APP and RWB-P3-E1073-APP);
- the session, the role and the right behind every operation, with `rwb-access` (P4);
- the installment shortfall that a PARTIAL match passes to the plan, with `rwb-treatment` (S2);
- the manual match `POST /proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` and the settlement, auction and enforcement proceeds, which are the Epic 4 stories of this service (RWB-P8-E4043-APP, RWB-P8-E4044-APP).

The legacy rule behaviour is carried unchanged: the same package code PAYMENT_MATCH, the same three rows and their row order, the same condition and output columns, the same first-match-wins rule, the same dated version in force, the same refusal of an invalid version load in full, the same "no version in force is a refusal and never a default match", and the same rule that a match whose decision record cannot be written is not made.

##### 2. Business rationale

The exact rule of RWB-E2-008 leaves short and late installments on the exception list, and a person matches them by hand each morning. RWB-E2-027 adds the PARTIAL and WINDOW rows of the PAYMENT_MATCH package, applies the rows in row order, records each match with the rule ID and the package version, and lets Credit Administration change a window or a tolerance through a new approved version with no code release. The match type, the amount tolerance, the window, the grace and the partial floor are columns of the decision table, not code and not a reference table (D-RCV-36 T10): this story reads them from the evaluated model and carries no threshold of its own.

The realignment changes the mechanism, not the business rule:

1. The matching code of the monolith becomes the `matchPayments` activity of an event-started workflow on task queue `rwb-payment` (DP-10): JOB-07 starts from `AceDataReady` (EV-26) instead of a Quartz trigger on a shared table (Arch v5 slide 44).
2. `RuleEvaluator` of the monolith becomes the embedded Drools kit (DP-04): one `KieBase` per package version, held in an LRU cache of at most 20, never recompiled per call; the package arrives from rwb-decision's registry and its checksum is verified before the swap.
3. The decision log write becomes the local decision-record library on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03): the record is written in the same transaction as the `proceeds` row, chained to the record before it, and rwb-decision collects it into the central ledger.
4. `recovery.proceeds` becomes `proceeds` in `rwb_payment` (DP-01), and the ACE payment and account facts arrive through `v_ace_payment` and `v_ace_account` under the P1 contract and this service's own views (DP-05), never by a join to another module's tables.
5. `/api/recovery/v1` becomes `/api/recovery/payment/v1` (DP-13), and the payment events are published on `rwb.payment.events.v1` under the naming library (DP-14) with the outbox relay and the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope of the platform library.
6. The parameters and the reference lists that select a match type, a version label or a date boundary are read through the rwb-case contracts (DP-06, DP-07), and the screen that lists the matches and the exceptions is composed by the gateway-bff route behind SCR-28 (DP-19).
7. Every cross-module call is one hop against a published contract with a 2 s budget and a breaker (DP-11).

This story serves REQ-CHO-009 and the rule-version half of R-UNI-38 and R-UNI-41: an earlier decision keeps the version it was taken under, and no version in force is a refusal.

| Precondition | What it gives this story |
|---|---|
| RWB-P8-E2027-CON | The published contract of this service for this key: the `Proceeds` element, the two operations, the three event envelopes and the rule-evaluation result this service consumes from rwb-decision. Faked until it is published (DP-11) |
| RWB-P8-E2008-APP | JOB-07, the `proceeds` table, the exception list and the exact-match run of RWB-E2-008 are live; this story replaces the single exact row with the evaluated package |
| RWB-PLT-E1072-CON | The embedded Drools kit (DP-04): the compile of a workbook to a `KieBase`, the checksum, first-match semantics with the default row last, and the `NoPackageInForce` outcome |
| RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03): one record in the caller's transaction, hash-chained |
| RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON | The parameters and reference-data client libraries (DP-06, DP-07) |
| RWB-PLT-E1071-CON | The Temporal workflow kit in namespace `rwb-recovery` (DP-10): the event-started workflow, its retry policy and its activity registration |
| RWB-PLT-E1047-CON | The naming library (DP-14): the topic, the retry topic, the `.dlt` topic and the event names of section 12 |
| RWB-PLT-E1044-CON | The per-service Flyway sequence and migration conventions (DP-15) |
| RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The gateway-bff composite route (DP-19): SCR-28 is composed there; this story serves its data and builds no screen |
| RWB-P3-E2042-CON | The rwb-case authoring contract: the workbook and its Tests tab whose rows this service consumes as an evaluated model (C) |

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E2-027:

- RWB-E2-008 is done: JOB-07, the `proceeds` table and the exception list are live, and a PAYMENT_MATCH version with the EXACT row in force decides the exact matches.
- The PAYMENT_MATCH package holds the EXACT, WINDOW and PARTIAL rows in the Drools template with at least 50 scenarios, authored and approved (RWB-E2-042, RWB-E1-073; in the target RWB-P3-E2042-APP and RWB-P7-E2027-APP).
- The decision-record library accepts a D5 entry with a rule ID and a rule version.
- PAYMENT_MATCH version "PM-2026.12" is in force from 2026-12-01 with the EXACT, WINDOW and PARTIAL rows of section 7. It was loaded and approved in the registry (RWB-P7-E2027-APP). The label is read as the one version in force for that date; the "PMT-2026.12" label carried by RWB-P3-E2042-APP is the same package and must be reconciled to one version row before SIT (GAP-2506; ASM-4150).
- The reader holds RW-CREDITAD or another role with Write-off and posting R.
- TreatmentApi records an installment shortfall (RWB-E2-004; in the target the rwb-treatment contract).
- Synthetic data only: payment codes, account keys, case references, plan references, amounts, dates, version labels and rule IDs of the legacy story; no real customer, account or payment.

##### 4. Flow

1. `rwb-source-data` publishes `AceDataReady` (EV-26) for the business date; the workflow kit starts the JOB-07 workflow on task queue `rwb-payment`, which runs the `matchPayments` activity (Arch v5 slide 44; DP-10).
2. `PaymentMatchFactsBuilder` reads the payments of the business date through the P1 contract and this service's `v_ace_payment` view, the accounts and the next installment date through `v_ace_account`, and the running plans and their installments through the rwb-treatment contract; it builds one fact set per running plan of the case.
3. `RuleVersionResolver` asks rwb-decision's registry for the PAYMENT_MATCH version in force on the business date, fetches the model of that version, and verifies its checksum against the registry answer before it is used. The resolved version label is held for the whole run, so every match of the run names the same version (DP-04; ASM-4148).
4. The embedded Drools kit evaluates the facts against the evaluated copy of the package. The model fires one row — the first match in row order (EXACT, then WINDOW, then PARTIAL) — and the result names the rule ID, the row order, the package code and the package version (BR1).
5. `MatchDecisionWriter` builds the D5 decision record with the case, the plan, the payment code, the amount, the due date, the rule ID and the package version, and writes it through the local decision-record library in the same transaction as the `proceeds` row (DP-03; BR6, BR8).
6. In that same transaction the service writes the `proceeds` row: case, treatment, payment code, source, amount, received date and `matched_to` (DP-01).
7. For a PARTIAL match, `MatchOutcomeReader` calls the rwb-treatment contract to record the installment paid and the shortfall on the plan.
8. The service writes `ProceedsMatched` (EV-25) to its outbox in the same transaction; for a payment no row matches it writes the `proceeds` row with `matched_to` UNMATCHED, its D5 record under R-UNI-03 and the exception-list entry, and for a plan with no payment in the window it writes `PaymentMissed` (EV-12). The outbox relay publishes to `rwb.payment.events.v1` with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope.
9. Credit Administration reads matched and unmatched receipts on SCR-28 through the gateway-bff route, each matched receipt with its rule ID and package version from the local decision record.
10. The `confirmBookings` and `postProceeds` activities of the service are the booking and posting steps of this service and are not extended by this story.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A partial payment below the partial floor | Unmatched; exception list | MSG-P8-001 | AC5 (owned by RWB-P8-E2008-APP for the exact rule, by this story for the evaluated row) |
| X2 | A late payment one day past the window | Unmatched; exception list | MSG-P8-001 | AC4 (not owned by this split; the row is evaluated here) |
| X3 | A package version load with two rows of the same row order or a tolerance above 100 | The load is refused in full by the registry; "PM-2026.12" stays in force | MSG-P3-027 | AC6 |
| X4 | The decision record cannot be written for a match | No `proceeds` row is written; the payment is picked up by the next run; incident | MSG-P7-003 | AC7 |
| X5 | A payment above the installment by more than the tolerance | Unmatched; exception list | MSG-P8-001 | AC8 (not owned by this split) |
| X6 | Two rows would match | The row with the lower row order decides; one record only | None | AC9 (not owned by this split) |
| X7 | No PAYMENT_MATCH version is in force on the business date | The run stops; no payment is matched and no `proceeds` row is written; no default version is substituted | MSG-P3-027 | AC10 |
| X8 | The fetched model fails its checksum | The local cache keeps the last good model of the version in force; the mismatch is counted and alerted; no match is taken on the unverified model | None | AC10, TC-E2-027-13 |
| X9 | The `AceDataReady` event of the business date is repeated | The inbox dedupes on the event ID; the run writes no second `proceeds` row and no second event | None | TC-E2-027-01 |
| X10 | The rwb-treatment contract does not answer within 2 s | The activity retries on the kit policy; after the last attempt the payment stays unmatched with its reason and the run summary names it | MSG-P8-001 | TC-E2-027-02 |

A stale `proceeds` row at commit is a conflict and the transaction rolls back, so a payment cannot be matched twice by two runs of the same business date.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P8-E2027-CON, RWB-P8-E2008-APP and the platform contracts of its DP table; reads no registry table and writes no other schema |
| Negotiable | The thresholds, the row order, the match types, the version labels, the message texts and the alert thresholds are rule rows, parameters, reference rows or chart values; the story fixes only the evaluation, the record and the write order |
| Valuable | Short and late installments match without a person, and every match names the rule and the approved version that decided it |
| Estimable | One facts builder, one version resolver, one evaluator call, one match writer, one outcome mapper, one event writer and one migration |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is a run of JOB-07 on a fixed business date with a fixed package version and a fixed payment set |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Payment matching rules with the data team

  Background:
    Given PAYMENT_MATCH package version "PM-2026.12" is in force from 2026-12-01 with rows:
      | rule_id | row_order | match_type | amount_tolerance_pct | window_days_before | window_days_after | partial_floor_pct |
      | EXACT   | 1         | EXACT      | 0                    | 10                 | 0                 |                   |
      | WINDOW  | 2         | WINDOW     | 0                    | 10                 | 3                 |                   |
      | PARTIAL | 3         | PARTIAL    | 0                    | 10                 | 3                 | 90                |
    Given case "RC-2026-000555" has account "A-0555" and running plan "T-0701" with installment amount 12,500.00 THB and next installment date 2026-12-15

  Scenario: AC6 Invalid package version refused (legacy RWB-E2-027 AC6)
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns the refused schema check naming "PARTIAL" and the tolerance column
    Given a PAYMENT_MATCH workbook for version "PM-2027.02" where rows "WINDOW" and "PARTIAL" both have row order 2 and "PARTIAL" has tolerance 120
    When it is loaded through POST /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/PAYMENT_MATCH/versions
    Then the response is status 422 with MSG-P3-027 for the schema check naming "PARTIAL" and the tolerance column
    Then the system refuses the load in full and "PM-2026.12" stays in force

  Scenario: AC7 Decision log write fails (legacy RWB-E2-027 AC7)
    Given the decision log store is unavailable during JOB-07 on 2026-12-15
    When "PAY-91001" is matched
    Then the system writes no proceeds row for "PAY-91001"
    Then the run summary shows MSG-P7-003 for "PAY-91001"
    Then the system raises an incident under rule R-UNI-39
    Then the next run of JOB-07 for 2026-12-14 matches "PAY-91001"

  Scenario: AC10 No PAYMENT_MATCH version in force (legacy RWB-E2-027 AC10)
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns NoPackageInForce for business date 2027-02-01
    Given no PAYMENT_MATCH package version is in force on 2027-02-01
    When JOB-07 runs for business date 2027-02-01
    Then RuleEvaluator.evaluate("PAYMENT_MATCH", facts, 2027-02-01) throws NoPackageInForce
    Then the run stops with MSG-P3-027 for the package in force check
    Then no payment is matched and no proceeds row is written for 2027-02-01
```

The three criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-E2-027 AC6, AC7 and AC10 copied word for word, with one leading `Given` added to AC6 and to AC10 because the cross-service part they exercise is mocked here: the load and its checks belong to rwb-decision (P7) and the version-in-force lookup belongs to the registry contract of RWB-P8-E2027-CON. The load path in AC6 is written on the target base of its owner, `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, because DP-13 gives every service its own base and the load and its checks are rwb-decision's operation; every other word and every value of the three criteria is the legacy one, and this story builds neither the load nor its checks (GAP-2506; ASM-4148). The other seven legacy criteria of RWB-E2-027 stay with the slices that own them: AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5, AC8 and AC9 with RWB-P8-E2008-APP, AC3 with RWB-P7-E2027-APP, and the cross-service journey with the wave 2 harness.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Rows are tried in row order and the first row that matches decides (first match); the default row is always last | D-RCV-36 T5; ADR-012; legacy BR1 |
| BR2 | EXACT: plan account, amount within the tolerance, date inside the window before the due date | R-RES-26; legacy BR2 |
| BR3 | WINDOW: as EXACT with the window extended after the due date; a late match is a late payment for the plan | R-RES-28; legacy BR3 |
| BR4 | PARTIAL: amount at or above the partial floor and below the installment; the shortfall is held on the plan | R-SET-15 pattern; REQ-CHO-009; legacy BR4 |
| BR5 | A payment no row matches is held on the exception list | R-UNI-03; CTL-41; legacy BR5 |
| BR6 | Each match decision is written to the local decision record with the rule ID (EXACT, WINDOW or PARTIAL) and the package version in force on the business date; earlier matches keep their version | R-UNI-38; D-RCV-36 T5, T7; legacy BR6 |
| BR7 | A package version with any invalid row is refused in full by the registry and never reaches this service | Reference data change process step 3; CTL-08; legacy BR7 |
| BR8 | A match whose decision record cannot be written is not made: the record and the `proceeds` row commit together or not at all | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; legacy BR8; DP-03 |
| BR9 | No version in force is a refusal (`NoPackageInForce`), never a default match | D-RCV-36 T3; R-UNI-41; legacy BR9 |
| BR10 | The tolerance, window, grace and partial floor are condition and output columns of the PAYMENT_MATCH rows, not code and not a reference table | D-RCV-36 T10; REQ-CHO-009; legacy BR10 |
| BR11 | The match type, the row order and the thresholds are read from the evaluated model only; this service reads no workbook, no `drl_source` and no `rule_row` | DP-04; Temporal and Drools slide 15 |
| BR12 | The package version is resolved once per run from the business date and is named on every record of that run; the model is verified by its checksum before it is used and the last good model is kept on a failure | DP-04; Temporal and Drools slide 15 notes; AC10 |
| BR13 | `proceeds` lives in `rwb_payment` and no other service reads or writes it; the ACE facts arrive through `v_ace_*` views and the P1 contract only | DP-01, DP-05; Ownership Map row `proceeds` (owner P8); Architecture v5 slide 17 |
| BR14 | The registers of a match — the case ID, the payment code, the amount, the due date, the rule ID and the rule version — carry no personal data | Architecture v5 slide 42 notes; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

##### 9. State transitions

This story changes no case status. It owns the state of a `proceeds` row.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | `matchPayments` runs | The decision record commits with the row | MATCHED (INSTALLMENT) |
| (none) | `matchPayments` runs | No row matches | UNMATCHED, with its reason and its record |
| (none) | `matchPayments` runs | The decision record cannot be written | No row is written; the payment is retried by the next run |
| (none) | `matchPayments` runs | No version is in force for the business date | No row is written for any payment of that date; the run stops |

The plan route states the results feed stay with rwb-case (P3):

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLAN_RUNNING | PAYMENT_RECEIVED | payment matched to the installment | PLAN_RUNNING (R-RES-26) |
| PLAN_CURE_PERIOD | PAYMENT_RECEIVED_LATE | payment received inside the cure period | PLAN_RUNNING (R-RES-28) |

The package version states LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK and REFUSED are rwb-decision's and are read here only through the registry answer.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CREDITAD, Credit Administration officer | Reads matches and the exception list (Write-off and posting CRUA); owns the matching values through the package rows |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Authors the PARTIAL and WINDOW rows and loads the version (Rules and parameters C); loads nothing through this service |
| RW-RISK, risk and model risk officer | Approves the package version (Rules and parameters A); calls the rollback in rwb-decision |
| RW-FINANCE, Finance and CFO delegate | Reads matches (Write-off and posting RA) |
| The rwb-payment service identity | Runs the JOB-07 workflow and its activities, writes the records and the rows, publishes the events |
| SY-RULES, Drools evaluator | Evaluates the evaluated copy of the package inside the activity and names the rule and the version |
| SY-DECLOG, decision record writer | Supplies the hash-chained local record of DP-03 |
| SY-AGENT, agent platform | Reads the exception list as the reconciliation agent (Epic 4) |
| RW-CASEOWN and any role without the Write-off and posting right | Refused with MSG-P4-002 on the read operation of section 12.1 |

Separation of duty stays in rwb-decision: the analyst who loads a version does not approve it and RW-RISK approves. No person is named anywhere; the actors are roles and service identities.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-payment` (P8); base `/api/recovery/payment/v1` (DP-13).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/proceeds` | List receipts with their match status, the rule that matched and the package version, for the matched and unmatched lists of SCR-28; 200 with `ProceedsPage` (API-P8-001, TSD P8 v2 T-A.2) | Write-off and posting R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |
| POST | `/proceeds/{proceedsId}/match` | Match a receipt to a case and an account by hand; 200 with `Proceeds` (API-P8-002). Declared here as the operation of this service; its behaviour is the Epic 4 story RWB-P8-E4043-APP | Write-off and posting U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header required |

The two paths are the ownership map's P8 paths; the query of `GET /proceeds` is `matched`, `from`, `to`, `page` and `size`, and the errors are 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 503 with one RFC 9457 problem response and one message ID each. The request and answer shapes are fixed by RWB-P8-E2027-CON and are consumed here, not redefined.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/PAYMENT_MATCH/versions` | P7 rwb-decision | The version in force on the business date and its checksum; one hop, 2 s, faked (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}` | P7 rwb-decision | The model of the version in force, fetched once per version and verified by its checksum (DP-04; Temporal and Drools slide 15 notes) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | The parameters of the matching run, through the client library (DP-06); faked |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-MATCH, LOV-MATCH-TYPE and the version label list (DP-07); faked |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The caller's role, scope and Write-off and posting right behind `GET /proceeds`; faked |
| POST | The installment-paid operation of rwb-treatment (operation name Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2506; ASM-4148)) | S2 rwb-treatment | Records the installment paid and the shortfall of a PARTIAL match; faked |

Every row is one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker. The rwb-decision rows are the C row of DP-04 (`RWB-P7-E1073-CON`) and of the registry story (`RWB-P7-E2027-APP`); neither is in this story's contract-dependency row, which carries the three rwb-case contracts (GAP-2506; ASM-4148).

| `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` (EV-25) | `rwb.payment.events.v1` | caseId | case ID, proceeds ID, payment code, treatment ID, source, amount, matched-to, rule ID, rule version, received date |

Every event is written to the service's outbox in the same transaction as the state change and relayed with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, keyed by `caseId`, by the platform outbox relay (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON; DP-09 is the platform pattern and is not a pattern of this key's table). The topic name and the event names follow the naming library (DP-14); the `.retry` and `.dlt` topics are provisioned by RWB-P8-E2027-OPS. No event carries a name, an e-mail address, a mobile number, a national identity number or an account number.

| Event | Topic | Producer | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|

| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` (shared) | all 19 services | The ledger acknowledgement of a local record; this service registers no second writer for it (GAP-2506; ASM-4151) |
| `rwb.debtsale.LotAwarded.v1` (EV-23) | `rwb.debtsale.events.v1` | S6 rwb-debtsale | Names the lot a debt-sale receipt belongs to; consumed by the Epic 4 proceeds stories and declared here for the interface of the service |

The inbox of the service dedupes every event on its ID, so a repeated `AceDataReady` starts no second run and a repeated `RulePackageInForce` performs no second swap.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| JOB-07 payment matching | Event-started workflow, started by `AceDataReady` | `rwb-payment` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | One run per business date; the workflow that hosts the matching (DP-10; Arch v5 slide 44) |
| `matchPayments` | Activity | `rwb-payment` | Builds the facts, resolves the version, evaluates, writes the record and the row, writes the outbox events |
| `confirmBookings` | Activity | `rwb-payment` | JOB-08 booking confirmation; declared, not extended here |
| `postProceeds` | Activity | `rwb-payment` | The saga step of the settlement and sale flows; declared, not extended here |

The workflow is deterministic: the Drools evaluation runs only inside the activity, so a replay reuses the recorded result and never recompiles a model. The retry policy is the kit's (1 s initial interval, back-off 2, 10 attempts) and `NoPackageInForce` is non-retryable.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-07 and JOB-08 are event-started workflows triggered by `AceDataReady`, not Schedules (Arch v5 slide 44). The only Schedule of this key is the 00:01 rule promote of rwb-decision (JOB-20) and it is not registered, retimed or duplicated here.

| `proceeds` | P8 (`rwb_payment`) | One row per receipt and its match |
| `decision_record` | PLT library, created in `rwb_payment` | The local hash-chained decision record of each match (DP-03) |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_payment` | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects of the service |

Not owned and not read as tables: `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` (P7, reached only through the registry operations of 12.2), `treatment` (S2), `recovery_case` (P3) and `decision_log_entry` (P7). No foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01).
