##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.payment`, module `matching`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.payment.matching`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

How this story applies each row. **DP-01**: `proceeds` and the four library objects sit in `rwb_payment`; the matching facts of the plan arrive on the rwb-treatment contract and the ACE facts through this service's views, never by a join to another schema. **DP-03**: each match writes one local record in the transaction that writes the row, chained to the record before it, and publishes `DecisionRecorded` on the shared topic; a record that cannot be written stops the match (BR8). **DP-04**: the model is fetched from rwb-decision, verified by its checksum and evaluated by the embedded kit, held per version in an LRU cache of at most 20; the story reads no `rule_row` and no workbook, and the C row `RWB-P7-E1073-CON` is built against its published set and its fake. **DP-05**: `v_ace_payment` and `v_ace_account` are the SELECT-only views of this service and the payment set of the business date is read through the P1 contract. **DP-06**: the matching parameters — the run window, the batch readiness and the feature switch values — are read as parameters, never as constants. **DP-07**: LOV-MATCH, LOV-MATCH-TYPE and the version label list are reference rows with their version; the thresholds stay rule-row columns and are never reference data (BR10). **DP-10**: JOB-07 is the event-started workflow of task queue `rwb-payment` started by `AceDataReady`, and no Schedule and no shared Quartz table is registered. **DP-11**: the six consumed operations of 12.2 are one hop on the owner's base with a 2 s timeout and a breaker; the legacy in-process `TreatmentApi` and `RuleEvaluator` calls become the treatment contract and the embedded kit. **DP-13**: every path of section 12 uses `/api/recovery/payment/v1`; no monolith base appears in the code or the tests. **DP-14**: the topic is `rwb.payment.events.v1` with its `.retry` and `.dlt` topics and the events are `rwb.payment.<Event>.v1`, taken from the naming library and never hand-written. **DP-15**: one Flyway sequence in `rwb_payment` adds the evaluated-model cache metadata and the indexes of the matching read, and no other schema is touched. **DP-19**: SCR-28 is composed by the gateway-bff route and this story serves its data; no screen template and no `ace-web` page is built here.

The platform H dependencies of the table — `RWB-PLT-E1027-CON`, `RWB-PLT-E1072-CON`, `RWB-PLT-E1042-CON`, `RWB-PLT-E1043-CON`, `RWB-PLT-E1071-CON`, `RWB-PLT-E1047-CON`, `RWB-PLT-E1044-CON` and `RWB-PLT-N001-CON` — are the DP-added dependencies and are all listed in the metadata row. The C dependencies of DP-04 (`RWB-P7-E1073-CON`) and of the registry story are **not** in the metadata C row, which carries the three rwb-case contracts; the absence is recorded in GAP-2506 and ASM-4148, and none of them blocks the build because an APP story builds against the published set and its fake (Template and Rules §R5.4).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ProceedsController | Controller | `GET /proceeds` with the session read, the scope and the problem mapping; the manual match path is declared and served by the Epic 4 story |
| PaymentMatchFactsBuilder | Service | Builds the facts of the payment, the account, the installment and the business date |
| RuleVersionResolver | Service | Resolves the PAYMENT_MATCH version in force, fetches the model, verifies the checksum, keeps the last good model |
| PaymentMatcher | Service | Calls the embedded kit for PAYMENT_MATCH, applies the fired row, returns the rule ID, the row order and the version |
| MatchDecisionWriter | Service | Builds the D5 record with the rule ID, the package version and the inputs, and writes it through the library before the row |
| MatchOutcomeReader | Service | Maps the result outputs to the `proceeds` row and to the shortfall passed to rwb-treatment |
| ProceedsRepository | Repository | `proceeds` in `rwb_payment`, with the optimistic lock and the unique key on payment code and business date |
| PaymentEventWriter | Service | Writes `ProceedsMatched`, `PaymentMissed` and `TreatmentBooked` to the outbox in the same transaction |
| MatchPaymentsActivity | Activity | The JOB-07 step that orders the components and the transaction |
| ModelRefreshHandler | Consumer and workflow | Consumes `RulePackageInForce`, fetches, verifies and swaps the evaluated copy atomically |
| ParameterClient, ReferenceDataClient, SessionClient, TreatmentClient | Clients | The six consumed operations of 12.2, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `proceeds`, `decision_record`, `outbox_event`, `processed_event` and `idempotency_key`, all in schema `rwb_payment`; reads no other schema.
- One migration in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15, `V2027_2__payment_matching_rules.sql`: the unique key of a payment code within a business date on `proceeds`, the index of the matched and unmatched read, and the model-cache metadata table of the evaluated copy. It creates no table of rwb-decision and no `payment_match_rule`.
- Updates a `proceeds` row with `WHERE id = ? AND version = ?`; zero rows updated is a conflict and the run retries, never writes twice.
- The tables of RWB-P8-E2008-APP are reused and not rebuilt; this story adds no column to `proceeds` beyond the ones section 11 lists.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The PAYMENT_MATCH version labels, the valid-from dates and the rows are the legacy values: "PM-2026.12" from 2026-12-01 with EXACT 1, WINDOW 2 and PARTIAL 3; "PM-2027.01" from 2027-01-01 with WINDOW at 5 days after; "PM-2027.02" refused in full. The rows are registry data of rwb-decision and are never seeded here (GAP-2506; ASM-4150).
- The model cache bound of 20, the warm-up list of PAYMENT_MATCH and the warm-up timeout are values of the chart of RWB-P8-E2027-OPS, not constants of the code.
- The version label in force, the match types and the source and match-to lists are read through DP-07 with the version in force; no list value is a constant of the code.
- The feature switch `rwb.p8.matching-rules` is read as a parameter through DP-06. Off: JOB-07 matches on the EXACT row only, as in RWB-P8-E2008-APP, and no new version is swapped in.

**Build steps**

1. `PaymentMatchFactsBuilder` and `ProceedsRepository`, with the unique key of the migration; unit-test the facts of the legacy payments and the duplicate-run case (X9).
2. `RuleVersionResolver` with the version lookup, the checksum verification and the last-good-model rule; test the cold cache and the checksum mismatch (X8, AC10).
3. `PaymentMatcher` on the embedded kit with first-match semantics; test the fired row and the row order.
4. `MatchDecisionWriter` with the write-before-row order and the fail-closed behaviour; test AC7 and TC-E2-027-13.
5. `MatchOutcomeReader` and the treatment call, with the timeout and the retry path (X10).
6. `MatchPaymentsActivity` and the JOB-07 workflow registration on `rwb-payment`, started by `AceDataReady`; test the repeated event and the missing event.
7. `ModelRefreshHandler` for `RulePackageInForce`, with the atomic swap and the checksum check.
8. The privacy test: no record, event or log line carries a name, an e-mail address, a mobile number or an account number.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; a synthetic month of 1,000 payments runs with every record naming a rule ID and a package version; "PM-2027.02" is refused in full with MSG-P3-027; no version in force on 2027-02-01 stops the run with MSG-P3-027 and writes no row; and a forced record failure writes no `proceeds` row.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P8-001 | The run summary holds unmatched payments | {count} payments for {date} matched no plan and are on the exception list. | This story, on the run summary and the exception read |
| MSG-P3-027 | A package version check fails, or no version is in force | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. | This story on the version-in-force check; rwb-decision on the load |
| MSG-GEN-001 | An empty file is loaded | Enter {field}. | rwb-decision, named only |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The version label is already loaded | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. | rwb-decision, named only |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, through the record library |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, through the session read |

For MSG-P3-027 the {check} value is compile, schema, scenario or package in force, and {detail} names the row ID, the column or the package code only, never a payment or a person. The texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story; Thai text follows DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-28 Proceeds matching is composed by the gateway-bff route (DP-19) in its loading, matched and unmatched states, and this story serves its data through `GET /proceeds`. For each matched receipt the screen shows the rule ID and the package version from the local decision record; for each unmatched receipt it shows the reason. PAYMENT_MATCH versions show on SCR-39 Rules and parameters (Epic 8) and on rwb-decision's version list; SCR-40 holds no payment matching table, because the match types and the thresholds are rule-row columns and never reference data.

| Where | State | What the caller sees |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-28 matched | Matched | The receipt, the plan, the rule ID and the package version that decided |
| SCR-28 unmatched | Unmatched | The receipt, its amount and the reason it matched no row |
| The run summary | Stopped, no version in force | MSG-P3-027 with the package in force check and the business date |
| The run summary | Record failure | MSG-P7-003 for the payment codes whose record could not be written |

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the match type, the row order, the amount tolerance, the window, the grace and the partial floor are columns of the PAYMENT_MATCH rule rows; no threshold, no window and no floor is a constant, a default or a reference-table value.
- No personal data in logs, events, workflow inputs, test data or prompts: the records and the event payloads hold payment codes, case and plan references, amounts, dates, rule IDs and version labels only.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or this service's `v_ace_*` views: no other module's table is read and no cross-schema foreign key exists (DP-01, DP-05).
- One evaluator, no direct read: the matching engine calls the embedded kit and reads no workbook, no `drl_source` and no `rule_row`; the registry is reached only through the operations of 12.2 (DP-04).
- The record is written before the row: no match exists without its local decision record, and a failed record leaves the payment unmatched with MSG-P7-003 (BR8).
- The package version in force is chosen once per run from the business date; no match is made without a version in force and no default version is ever substituted (BR9, BR12).
- The model is verified by its checksum before it is used; a mismatch keeps the last good model and alerts (X8).
- One base, one topic, one queue and one login per service; the topic, the retry topic and the `.dlt` topic come from the naming library and never from a literal (DP-13, DP-14).
- No secret in code, a test, a values file or a log: the rwb-payment login (DP-02), the Kafka credential and the Temporal material come from the platform secret store.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: created as the rwb-access slice of legacy RWB-E2-027 — the payment-matching access profile: the rights of the four roles of the legacy story held as permission rows, the session answer, the refusal and the read entries of the matching operations. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **security administrator (RW-SECADM)**, I want **the payment-matching rights of the data-team matching slice held as permission rows of the matrix version in force and answered for every caller of the matching operations — the receipt read, the exception-list read, the rule-package load and the rule-version approve — with every refusal and every exception-list read written as one access entry naming the area, the right, the matrix version and the case**, so that **a role without the right cannot see a receipt or change a matching rule, and every person who read the unmatched list can be named afterwards**.

Inside `rwb-access` this is the authority half of the legacy story RWB-E2-027:

- Service `rwb-access`, schema `rwb_access`, REST base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access` (context pack P4).
- One deliverable: the `PaymentMatchAccessProfile` (the area and the right each matching operation needs), the `RightResolver` that answers ALLOW or DENY from the `permission` rows of the matrix version in force, the session and roles answers that carry those rows, and the AC-DENY and AC-READ entries the matching operations write, read through `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` (DP-01, DP-03).
- The match itself stays with `rwb-payment` (P8, RWB-P8-E2027-APP): JOB-07, the `RuleEvaluator` call, the fired row, the proceeds row and the exception list. This story matches nothing, writes no proceeds row and reads no ACE view.
- The package, its versions, the parsed rows and the approval stay with `rwb-decision` (P7, RWB-P7-E2027-APP); the workbook and its Rows and Tests tabs stay with `rwb-case` (P3, RWB-P3-E2042-APP); the installment shortfall stays with `rwb-treatment` (S2). This story holds only the right that gates each of those calls.
- The rights are the legacy values unchanged: RW-CREDITAD Write-off and posting CRUA, RW-FINANCE Write-off and posting RA, RW-COE Rules and parameters C, RW-RISK Rules and parameters A (legacy section 10). The capability areas are values of LOV-CAPABILITY: `WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING` and `RULES_AND_PARAMETERS` (TSD P4 T3.2).
- The database login used by the capability is the per-service login of DP-02. Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2311; ASM-3838); this story uses the phrase "the rwb-access login (DP-02)" and never the shared monolith login.
- The permission rows of the four roles are already in force in matrix version "PM-2026.11"; they are loaded and approved by the matrix stories of this service and are not rebuilt here (ASM-3836). This story serves and enforces them.

##### 2. Business rationale

RWB-E2-027 makes most receipts match without a person and lists the rest, and its authority section says who may read that list and who may change the rule behind it. A matching rule that any role can load, or an exception list that any role can read without a trace, would defeat the control the story serves: CTL-41 and REQ-CHO-009 are only met if the person who reads the unmatched receipts is named, and if the person who changes a threshold is not the person who approves it.

In the monolith the check was a hard-coded role test inside the payments module, and the access trail was a single shared log. The realignment moves the rows and the answer to the owner of access (Arch v5 slides 4 and 8) and makes every other service's guard read that answer; the entry becomes an append-only decision record in the serving service's own schema. This story is the slice that holds the four role rows of the legacy story, answers them on the session, refuses the receipt read, the exception-list read and the rule-package calls of a role that lacks the right, and records each refusal and each exception-list read with the matrix version that decided it.

It serves REQ-CHO-009 on the authority side and carries the legacy control CTL-41: every match names its rule and its package version, and every read of the unmatched list names its reader. It changes no business rule of the matching itself.

PAYMENT_MATCH version "PM-2026.12" is in force from 2026-12-01 and version "PM-2027.01" is loaded with valid from 2027-01-01 (legacy AC3, AC5, AC6).

##### 4. Flow

1. A caller of a matching operation presents the session token; the guard of the serving service resolves the caller's roles and letters from the session answer of `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` and asks `PaymentMatchAccessProfile` for the area and the right the operation needs.
2. `RightResolver`: reads the `permission` rows of the caller's roles for that area at the matrix version in force, takes the union of the letters over the roles held, and answers ALLOW when the right is present and DENY when it is absent. A role the caller does not hold contributes nothing, and a missing row is DENY, never ALLOW.
3. On ALLOW the guarded operation runs: the receipt read, the exception-list read, the package-version load or the rule-version approve. This story builds none of those four operations.
4. On DENY the guarded call stops with status 403 and MSG-P4-002 before the operation runs, and `RefusalRecorder` writes one AC-DENY entry with the area, the right, the result REFUSED and no payment, account or case data; the entry is committed before the 403 is returned.
5. RW-CREDITAD or RW-FINANCE: reads the matched and unmatched receipts of a case on SCR-28 through the gateway-bff route. The read is allowed from WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING R; `ReadRecorder` writes one AC-READ entry with the actor, the case id, the filter, the row count and the matrix version in force.
6. RW-SECADM: reads the entries of a user and a period through `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log`, with the decision code AC-READ or AC-DENY, the area, the right, the result, the case id, the row count and the matrix version of each entry.
7. RW-SECADM: reads the roles and their permission rows through `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles`; the answer names the role, the area, the letters and the matrix version, so the four rows of the legacy story are visible as data.
8. Nothing in this story matches a payment, evaluates a rule package, writes a proceeds row, approves a version or changes a case status.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A role without the Write-off and posting right reads the receipts | 403 before the read runs; no receipt data; one AC-DENY entry with area WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING and right R | MSG-P4-002 | AC2, TC-E2-027-11 |
| X2 | A role without the Rules and parameters C loads a package version | 403 before the load runs; no version is written; one AC-DENY entry with area RULES_AND_PARAMETERS and right C | MSG-P4-002 | AC3, TC-E2-027-12 |
| X3 | A role holding C but not A approves a loaded version | 403 before the approval runs; the version stays LOADED; one AC-DENY entry with right A | MSG-P4-002 | AC6 |
| X4 | No permission row exists for the role and the area of the call | DENY, not ALLOW; 403; one AC-DENY entry with the area and the right | MSG-P4-002 | AC7 |
| X5 | The session cannot be resolved, or the caller holds no Workbench role | 401 and no operation runs; one AC-DENY entry with reason NO_ROLE is written where the token identifies a user | MSG-P4-001 | TC-E2-027-11 |
| X6 | The entry of a refusal or of an exception-list read cannot be written | The refusal stands and the read returns nothing; the call answers 503; an incident is raised; no unaudited read is served | MSG-P7-003 | AC4, TC-E2-027-13 |

The entry of a refusal and the entry of a read are written before the answer leaves the service, so a read that cannot be recorded is not served (legacy BR8 and guardrail 4). A stale `permission` row at commit, matched on its `version` column, is MSG-GEN-004 and the call is retried, never applied twice.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P8-E2027-CON, the platform contracts of its DP table and the fakes; it matches no payment, evaluates no rule package and rebuilds no matrix load |
| Negotiable | The roles, the letters, the areas and the matrix versions are rows and reference data; the story fixes only the profile, the union rule, the deny-by-default rule and the entry shape |
| Valuable | A role without the right cannot read a receipt or change a matching rule, and every read of the unmatched list names its reader and its matrix version |
| Estimable | One profile, one resolver, one session assembler, one refusal recorder, one read recorder and one repository |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is a session read, a roles read, a refused call or a logged read, with a fixed Given, When and Then |

The seven criteria are new under D-RCV-60 and they test only the access profile, its answers and its entries. Every business value is the legacy story's: the four roles and their letters (legacy section 10), the case, the plan and the payment of 10,000.00 THB (legacy AC5) and the two package versions (legacy AC3 and AC6). The legacy criteria of RWB-E2-027 stay with the other slices of the key: the match with RWB-P8-E2027-APP, the registry with RWB-P7-E2027-APP, the workbook with RWB-P3-E2042-APP and the journey with RWB-ITG-E2027-ITG (GAP-2314; ASM-3837).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The right of a caller is the union of the letters of the roles the caller holds in the capability area of the operation, at the matrix version in force; a role not held contributes nothing | FSD P4 AC-ALT-P4-001-02; legacy section 10 |
| BR2 | No permission row for the role and the area is DENY, not ALLOW; the resolver never falls back to a default letter and never caches an allow across a matrix version | FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-001-05; legacy section 17 |
| BR3 | The area and the right each matching operation needs are declared in one profile: receipt read and exception-list read WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING R, package-version load RULES_AND_PARAMETERS C, rule-version approve RULES_AND_PARAMETERS A | legacy sections 10 and 12; LOV-CAPABILITY; ASM-3832 |
| BR4 | A call without the right stops with 403 and MSG-P4-002 before the operation runs, and nothing of the guarded operation is written | FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-001-05; legacy section 14 and TC-E2-027-11, TC-E2-027-12 |
| BR5 | Every refusal writes one AC-DENY entry with the area, the right and the result, and every exception-list read writes one AC-READ entry with the case id, the filter and the row count; the entry is written before the answer | FSD P4 A2.6 and AC-P4-007-01; legacy BR8 |
| BR6 | An entry names no personal data: no name, no identity number, no phone number, no account key and no payment amount; the case id, the payment-free filter and the counts are the whole record | legacy section 17; NFR-040; FSD P4 AC-ALT-P4-005-01 |
| BR7 | The matrix version that decided a call is written on the entry and is never re-resolved afterwards; a later version changes the next call, not the record of an earlier one | FSD P4 AC-P4-004-01; legacy BR6 (earlier decisions keep their version) |
| BR8 | A read that cannot be recorded is not served, and a refusal that cannot be recorded is still a refusal: the call answers 503 and an incident is raised | legacy BR8 and section 5 X4; FSD P4 AC-EXC-P4-004-04 |
| BR9 | The letters are rows of the `permission` table and are never a constant of the code; a change of a letter is a matrix version, not a release | legacy BR10 pattern; FSD P4 BR-P4-004 |
| BR10 | The separation of duty of the rule package holds at the right: the loader holds C, the approver holds A, and no role holds both for this key | legacy section 10; TSD P4 T6.1 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status and no permission letter; it reads them. The two case transitions of the legacy story — `PLAN_RUNNING` on `PAYMENT_RECEIVED` under R-RES-26 and `PLAN_CURE_PERIOD` on `PAYMENT_RECEIVED_LATE` under R-RES-28 — are rwb-case's and rwb-payment's.

The only boundary this story owns is the matrix version a call is decided under:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| (entry of a call) | The matrix version in force changes | A later read is made on or after the new valid-from date | The new entry carries the new version; the earlier entry keeps its version |
| (session answer) | The matrix version in force changes | The session is read on or after the new valid-from date | The session carries the new version and its letters |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CREDITAD, Credit Administration officer | Reads the matched and unmatched receipts and the exception list; every read is recorded (Write-off and posting CRUA) |
| RW-FINANCE, Finance and CFO delegate | Reads the matched receipts; every read is recorded (Write-off and posting RA) |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Loads a PAYMENT_MATCH package version; may not approve it (Rules and parameters C) |
| RW-RISK, risk and model risk officer | Approves a loaded package version; may not load it (Rules and parameters A) |
| RW-SECADM, security administrator | Reads the roles and the access entries, and owns the permission rows (Platform administration R; the matrix owner role of FSD P4 A2.4) |
| RW-CASEOWN and any role without the right of the call | Refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002 on every operation of the profile, with one AC-DENY entry |
| SY-AGENT, agent platform | Reads the exception list as the reconciliation agent under the same session check; its letters in WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2311; ASM-3832) |
| The rwb-access service identity | Resolves the rights, writes the AC-DENY and AC-READ entries and answers the three reads of section 12.1 |
| SY-DECLOG, decision log writer | Supplies the hash-chained write of DP-03 for every entry |

Separation of duty: the analyst who loads a version does not approve it, and this story enforces the pair of rights that makes that true (BR10). No person is named anywhere; the actors are roles and service identities.

`role`, `permission` and `decision_log_entry` are rwb-access's and no other service reads them (DP-01). The field IDs are those of TSD P4 T3.1 and of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. This story adds no table and no column: it reads the two matrix tables and writes entries into the log table of RWB-P4-E1039-APP. `delegation_limit`, `masking_rule` and `role_conflict` are P4's but are not used by this key: a match is not an approval, the receipt carries no personal field and no role pair is refused by the profile.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-access` (P4); base `/api/recovery/access/v1`. The three paths are the ownership map's P4 operations, and API-P4-012, API-P4-007 and API-P4-008 of TSD P4 T-A.1 on the service base. The payment-matching profile is not a new endpoint: it is the pair (area, right) that the session answer and the entries carry.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/me/session` | The caller's resolved session: roles, the permission rows with their letters, the matrix version, the scope, the masking version and the break-glass state; 200 | None R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |
| GET | `/admin/roles` | List the roles with their permission rows, the areas, the letters, the scope and the matrix version; 200 | Platform administration R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |
| GET | `/admin/access-log` | Search the entries of `rwb_access`: query `user`, `from`, `to`, `event`, `capabilityArea`, `page`, `size`; AccessLogPage with `at`, `user`, `event` (AC-READ or AC-DENY), `capability`, `right`, `result`, `caseId`, `rowCount`, `matrixVersion`; 200 | Platform administration R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |

The session answer holds `roles[]` with `roleCode`, `scope` and `permissions[]` of `capabilityArea` and `letters`, plus `matrixVersion`, `maskingVersion` and the break-glass state. Errors: 401 no session (MSG-P4-001 where the caller holds no role); 403 the role lacks the right of the admin read (MSG-P4-002); 503 the entry of the read could not be written (MSG-P7-003). Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set. The refused load and approve calls are not published here: they are the operations of RWB-P7-E2027-APP, stopped at their edge by the guard that reads this answer (GAP-2313; ASM-3834).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case, on RWB-P3-E1043-CON | LOV-CAPABILITY with `WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING` and `RULES_AND_PARAMETERS`, LOV-ROLE and LOV-SCOPE with the version in force, so the areas and the roles of the profile are reference data and never constants (DP-07); faked, one hop, 2 s (DP-11) |

Only one operation is consumed: the matrix tables hold the letters, so no parameter is read by this story and DP-06 adds no call (GAP-2312; ASM-3833). The rwb-payment read is not consumed: this story answers the guard that sits in front of it, and the mock of 12.8 supplies the item shape the guard protects. The platform and published contracts the DP table adds are listed in section 13 and carried in the gap of GAP-2312.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 ledger library, published by this service | entryId | the hash-chained record of a refusal or an exception-list read: decision code, the area, the right, the result, the case id, the row count, the matrix version, the actor and the decided time |

One event type, on the shared ledger topic and not on `rwb.access.events.v1`: an access entry is a decision record, not a change of access policy, and the two policy events of the service belong to RWB-P4-E1037-APP and the delegation story (ASM-3835). The row is written to the outbox in the transaction of the entry and relayed with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope; no event carries a name, an identity number, a phone number, an account key or an amount.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The two reads of the matrix are synchronous, the session and the roles answers are computed from `rwb_access`, and no subscription is needed for a right. The matching run of JOB-07 is rwb-payment's and reaches this story only as a guarded caller.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The three operations are synchronous reads; the resolver and the two recorders run in the request; and this story starts no workflow, registers no activity and adds nothing to the `rwb-access` task queue. The matching run of the legacy story is JOB-07 of rwb-payment and is not a workflow of this story. The six-monthly access review (JOB-18) is a Schedule of rwb-access but belongs to RWB-P4-AD008-APP; this story registers none.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. JOB-18, the six-monthly access review, runs on the `rwb-access` queue as a Temporal Schedule of RWB-P4-AD008-APP (DP-10); this story creates no Schedule, no timer and no trigger, and the matrix version reaches the service as data and not by a job.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | The four role rows of the legacy story and their class and default scope, read for the session and the roles answer |
| `permission` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | The letters of a role in a capability area at a matrix version; the only source of an ALLOW |
| `decision_log_entry` | P4 (`rwb_access`) | One append-only, hash-chained entry per refusal and per exception-list read |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_access` | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects the DP-03 library uses |

Not owned and not read: `proceeds` (P8), `treatment` (S2) and `v_ace_payment` (P1); `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` (P7); `lov_value`, `parameter_value` (P3). `delegation_limit`, `masking_rule` and `role_conflict` are P4's and are unused by this key. No foreign key crosses a schema and no other service reads these three tables (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

|---|---|---|

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`, module `accessrights/profile`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.accessrights.profile`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

How this story applies the rows that carry work. **DP-01, DP-13**: the three tables and every path sit in `rwb_access` and under `/api/recovery/access/v1`; no service reads them and no monolith base appears. **DP-03**: a refusal and an exception-list read each write one local entry in the transaction and publish `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; an entry that cannot be written stops the read (BR8). **DP-07, DP-11**: the one consumed call reads LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-ROLE and LOV-SCOPE once, one hop, 2 s, so the areas and the role codes are reference data; the receipt item arrives from the rwb-payment fake. **DP-15, DP-19**: no new table and no migration, and SCR-28 stays a gateway-bff composite route for which this story supplies the session fragment and the logged read. Rows that add no work: **DP-04** (nothing is evaluated — the profile holds the right that gates a load, not a rule, so no C dependency is taken), **DP-05** (no ACE view), **DP-06** (no parameter — the letters are matrix rows), **DP-10** (no job; JOB-18 is AD008's, JOB-07 is rwb-payment's), **DP-14** (no event on `rwb.access.events.v1`; the entry uses the shared ledger topic).

The platform H dependencies of the table — H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON — and the C dependencies C RWB-P3-E1043-CON are the DP-added dependencies that are **not** in the metadata rows, which name None and RWB-P8-E2027-CON. They are recorded in GAP-2312 and ASM-3833: they are platform contracts of wave 0 and the reference-data contract of rwb-case, none blocks the build, and an APP story builds against the published set and its fake.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| PaymentMatchAccessProfile | Service | Declares the area and the right each matching operation needs: receipt read and exception-list read WRITE_OFF_AND_POSTING R, package-version load RULES_AND_PARAMETERS C, rule-version approve RULES_AND_PARAMETERS A |
| RightResolver | Service | Answers ALLOW or DENY from the `permission` rows of the caller's roles at the matrix version in force; a missing row is DENY and no allow is cached across a version |
| SessionAssembler | Service | Builds the session and roles answers: roles, areas, letters, scope and matrix version |
| RefusalRecorder | Service | Writes the AC-DENY entry with the area, the right and the result, and no payment, account or amount |
| ReadRecorder | Service | Writes the AC-READ entry of an exception-list read with the case id, the filter, the row count and the matrix version, and fails the read closed |
| AccessEntryRepository | Repository | Reads and writes the entries and the matrix rows of `rwb_access` only |

**Build steps**

1. Write `PaymentMatchAccessProfile` with the four operations of BR3 and unit test the pair it returns for each.
2. Build `RightResolver` over `permission`; test the union of two roles, the missing row and the version boundary of AC5.
3. Extend `SessionAssembler` so the session and the roles answers carry the letters and the matrix version; test AC1.
4. Build `RefusalRecorder` and put it before the 403 of the guarded call; test AC2, AC3 and AC6.
5. Build `ReadRecorder` for the exception-list read and assert the entry carries no personal field; test AC4 and the fail-closed half of AC7.
6. Test the deny-by-default half of AC7 with a role that has no row in the area.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.access.payment-match.profile`. Off: the four matching operations answer DENY for every caller, so a switch-off closes the path rather than opening it; the two admin reads stay on.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; the four roles answer their legacy letters on the session; a refused read, load and approve each write one AC-DENY entry with its area and right; every exception-list read writes one AC-READ entry with the case id, the row count and the matrix version, and holds no personal data; and a read that cannot be recorded returns nothing.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller's roles do not carry the right of the operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-001 | The caller holds no Workbench role | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The entry of the read or of the refusal could not be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A matrix or entry row changed under the call | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |

`{action}` is the operation of the guarded call — "read proceeds", "read the exception list", "load a rule version", "approve a rule version" — and never a payment, a case or a person. Thai text follows DL10.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the areas, the letters and the matrix version are rows and reference data; the profile holds only the pair (area, right) each operation needs.
- No personal data in an entry, a log, an event or a payload: the case id, the filter, the row count and the matrix version are the whole record, never a name, an identity number, a phone number, an account key or an amount.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views: the receipts come through RWB-P8-E2027-CON and the plan through nothing.
- Deny by default and fail closed: a missing row is DENY, and a read that cannot be recorded is not served.
- The entry is written before the answer; no refusal and no exception-list read exists without its entry.
- One resolver: every matching operation asks `RightResolver`, and no handler tests a role code itself.

##### 1. Story

As a **Credit Administration officer (RW-CREDITAD)**, I want **the consequence of a payment match held on the plan of a treatment — the installment the match reports advanced, the shortfall of a partial payment held on the treatment row of `rwb_treatment`, the cure period of a missed installment run as a durable timer of `TreatmentWorkflow`, and the plan broken when the cure period passes unpaid — with every step naming the rule and the rule version that decided it**, so that **a plan that is being paid is kept alive and a plan that has stopped being paid is known the morning the match runs, instead of being found by a person reading an exception list**.

This is the secondary slice of legacy RWB-E2-027. The legacy story owns the matching rules themselves — the EXACT, WINDOW and PARTIAL rows of the `PAYMENT_MATCH` package, the row order, the tolerance, the window, the grace, the partial floor, the exception list and the matching job — and every one of its acceptance criteria is owned by `RWB-P8-E2027-APP` and by the contract `RWB-P8-E2027-CON`, not here. This story owns no legacy criterion: it tests only what a match does to the plan, and the values it uses are the ones the legacy story already carries (ASM-4485, ASM-4487).

What this story owns:

- the plan consequence of a match on `treatment` in `rwb_treatment`: `installments_paid` (DF-TRT-032) advanced by one, `installment_shortfall` (DF-TRT-033) held for the due date of the installment, `state` (TSD S2 T3.0), `outcome` (DF-TRT-013) and `outcome_at` (DF-TRT-014), and `decision_log_id` (DF-TRT-003), all under this service's own login and Flyway sequence (DP-01, DP-15);
- the cure period of a missed installment as a durable timer inside `TreatmentWorkflow`, the stage child of `CaseWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, with the activities `EvaluateRules` and `RecordAndApply` (DP-10; Architecture v5 slides 11 and 13 via the context pack);
- the match consequence read from `RWB-P8-E2027-CON` — the payment, the installment and its due date, the match type, the rule ID, the package code and version and the shortfall — one hop with a 2 s timeout against a mock (DP-11);
- the rule answer: `R-RES-27` (missed installment starts the cure period), `R-RES-28` (a late payment inside the cure period ends the wait), `R-RES-29` (break count incremented, plan broken), `R-RES-30` (return to the route decision with reason `broken_plan`) and `R-RES-31` (further restructure barred at `restructure.max_breaks = 2`), evaluated with the embedded Drools runtime from the package in force (DP-04);
- the local decision record of every step, written through the decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, before the treatment row changes and in the same `rwb_treatment` transaction (DP-03, DP-14);
- the parameters read (`CURE_PERIOD_DAYS`, `restructure.max_breaks`) and the reference-data read (`LOV-TRT-OUTCOME`) of rwb-case at their version (DP-06, DP-07);
- the read of the plan consequence on base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1` (DP-13) and on SCR-14 through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).

It does not own: the matching of payments to plans, the `PAYMENT_MATCH` rows and their versions, the tolerance, window and partial floor, the exception list, MSG-P8-001, the proceeds row and the matching job — those are `RWB-P8-E2027-APP` and `RWB-P8-E2027-CON` (P8); the rule registry, the package load and the approval that gives a version force — those are rwb-decision's (P7); the payment, account and batch-status reads — those are rwb-source-data's (P1); the case status, the case task of R-RES-30 and `CaseWorkflow` — those are rwb-case's (P3); the treatment record, the offer, the settlement range and the plan offer — those are `RWB-S2-E3001-APP` to `RWB-S2-E3011-APP`.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story fixed the gap plainly: the exact rule of RWB-E2-008 left short and late installments on the exception list, a person matched them by hand each morning, and a plan that had quietly stopped being paid sat in the same list. Its objective carries over unchanged — most payments match without a person, every match names its rule and its package version so it can be explained later, and the plan on the case tells the truth about where the customer stands (REQ-CHO-009; CTL-41; FSD P8 measure "receipts matched the same day").

What D-RCV-60 changes is which half of that sentence belongs to which service. A match is a payment fact: it reads the payments of the business date, applies the package rows in row order, writes the proceeds row and the exception list. A plan is a treatment fact: `installment_amount`, `installments`, `first_due_date`, `installments_paid` and `installment_shortfall` are columns of `treatment` in `rwb_treatment`, and the plan clock is named as this service's own workflow in the service catalogue (TSD S2 T3.1; context pack ownership rows).

So the value crosses one boundary and lands where the fact lives. rwb-payment decides which installment a payment matched and what is missing; rwb-treatment holds the plan, so rwb-treatment applies the consequence, starts the cure period, and breaks the plan when the cure period passes unpaid. The moment this service read a payment table or a proceeds row for itself, two services would own one match and the rule that no match exists without its record could be bypassed by a query (DP-01, DP-05; legacy guardrails).

Two consequences are designed rather than left to discipline. The rule set is data: the tolerance, the window, the grace, the partial floor, the cure period and the break limit are columns of a row or parameter values in force, read at evaluation time, so the only numbers in this module are column names and field IDs (legacy BR10; D-RCV-36 T10; DP-06). And the clock is a timer, not a scan: the legacy build discovered a plan late by polling a timer table, while the target runs the cure period as a durable timer inside the workflow, so a plan is never found late by a job and no other service's timer row is read (DP-10). Nothing moves without its record either: the record is written before the row, with the rule ID and the version in force, and an earlier step keeps the version that decided it (legacy BR6, BR8; R-UNI-38, R-UNI-39, R-UNI-41).

It serves REQ-CHO-009 on the treatment side: the plan is kept current by the match and is closed when it breaks. No business value is invented or moved.

##### 3. Preconditions

- `RWB-P8-E2027-CON` is published: the match consequence of a business date for a case and its plans, carrying the payment, the installment, the due date, the match type, the rule ID, the package code and version and the shortfall, one hop with a 2 s timeout behind a breaker (DP-11). The operation name and the payload member names are not published by any source (GAP-2705; ASM-4487). This story builds against the contract and its fake on Day 1 and never against a payment, proceeds or rule table.
- The `rwb_treatment` schema and login exist from the platform database story, and the `treatment` table exists with the columns of TSD S2 T3.1 (DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033) and the standard record columns of T3.0, including `state`, `version`, `outcome` (DF-TRT-013) and `outcome_at` (DF-TRT-014) with LOV-TRT-OUTCOME.
- A treatment of the restructure, settlement or deed in lieu route is booked for the case, with its plan terms `installments` (DF-TRT-009), `installment_amount` (DF-TRT-031), `first_due_date` (DF-TRT-029) and `installments_paid` (DF-TRT-032) written by `RWB-S2-E3010-APP`, in state `PLAN_RUNNING` with the plan states of TSD S2 T4 (ASM-4489).
- The workflow kit is in place on task queue `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and `CaseWorkflow` of rwb-case starts this stage as a child on that queue and passes the payment signal to it (DP-10; ASM-4487).
- A rule package holds the RES rule set of the route at a version in force for the business date, and the embedded Drools runtime of the service template evaluates it inside an activity (DP-04; ASM-4488).
- The parameters read of rwb-case is available through its client library: `CURE_PERIOD_DAYS` and `restructure.max_breaks` are values in force with their version, and the reference-data read serves LOV-TRT-OUTCOME (DP-06, DP-07; ASM-4488). The parameter codes and the package code are not published by any source (GAP-2706; ASM-4488).
- The decision-record library is published: it writes the row in the caller's transaction and refuses with MSG-P7-003 when it cannot (DP-03; ASM-4490).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline, and a C dependency never blocks: this story starts on Day 1 with only `RWB-P8-E2027-CON` as its contract dependency.

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-payment matches the payments of the business date against the running plans and publishes or holds the result of each installment; the row order, the tolerance, the window and the partial floor are its own (P8; not this story).
2. rwb-case signals `CaseWorkflow`, which passes the payment signal to `TreatmentWorkflow` on queue `rwb-treatment` for the treatment of the plan (ASM-4487).
3. `TreatmentWorkflow`: the `EvaluateRules` activity reads the match consequence of the plan for that business date from `RWB-P8-E2027-CON` (DP-11) and the rule version in force for the date.
4. `EvaluateRules`: the embedded Drools runtime fires the first row of the RES rule set in force; the answer names the rule ID and the package version that decided (DP-04).
5. `RecordAndApply`: the decision record is written with the rule ID, the package version and the inputs — payment code, due date, amount, shortfall — and no personal data (DP-03).
6. `RecordAndApply`: on a matched installment, `installments_paid` is advanced by one and the shortfall held for that due date is cleared; on a PARTIAL match, the difference between `installment_amount` and the matched amount is held in `installment_shortfall` for that due date (legacy AC1, AC2 values).
7. `TreatmentWorkflow`: on a missed installment the cure timer starts for `CURE_PERIOD_DAYS` of the product; a match inside the cure period cancels the timer early; when the timer fires unpaid, the break count is incremented, the plan is marked broken and the stage reports the outcome to `CaseWorkflow` (R-RES-27 to R-RES-30).
8. RW-CREDITAD: reads the plan on SCR-14 through the gateway-bff composite route, with the state, the installments paid, the shortfall and the rule and version each step named (DP-19).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A partial payment below the partial floor | rwb-payment raises no match for the installment; nothing reaches this service; the plan state and the shortfall are unchanged; the exception list and its message stay with P8 | MSG-P8-001 (P8) | AC3 |
| X2 | A late payment outside the window | No match is raised; the cure timer keeps running and fires unpaid | None | AC5 |
| X3 | No rule version in force for the business date | The step refuses with `NoPackageInForce`; no treatment row and no record is written for that date | MSG-P3-027 | AC6 |
| X4 | The decision record cannot be written | The treatment row is not changed; the step retries on the workflow policy and nothing is applied without its record | MSG-P7-003 | AC7 |
| X5 | A late payment arrives while the cure timer is firing | The answer that is committed first wins; the record names the rule that decided and the second answer finds the state already moved | None | AC4 |
| X6 | The caller holds no right on the treatment read | The read is refused; no plan consequence is returned | MSG-P4-002 | AC8 |

| Independent | Uses the match consequence read of RWB-P8-E2027-CON and this service's own `treatment` row only |
| Negotiable | The cure period and the break limit are parameter values; the story fixes the order of the record and the row and the state names |
| Valuable | A plan that is paid stays alive and a plan that has stopped being paid is known the morning the match runs |
| Estimable | One read, one rule evaluation, one record and one row write per step, plus one durable timer |
| Small | One activity pair and its tests; it fits in a wave-2 sprint |
| Testable | Each criterion runs against the contract fakes and a rule version loaded for the business date |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Payment matching rules with the data team

  Background:
    Given the rwb-payment contract mock returns the match result for business date 2026-12-15
    Given case "RC-2026-000555" has running plan "T-0701" with installment amount 12,500.00 THB, next installment date 2026-12-15 and installments_paid "3"
    Given rule package version "PM-2026.12" is in force from 2026-12-01, naming the rows "EXACT", "WINDOW" and "PARTIAL"

  Scenario: AC1 A missed installment starts the cure period as a durable timer (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-payment contract mock returns a missed installment for plan "T-0701" and due date 2026-12-15
    When TreatmentWorkflow applies the result
    Then the plan state is PLAN_CURE_PERIOD and a durable timer of 30 calendar days (CURE_PERIOD_DAYS for MORTGAGE) is running in the workflow
    Then the decision record of the step names rule "R-RES-27" and the rule version in force
    Then installments_paid and installment_shortfall are unchanged

  Scenario: AC2 A matched installment advances the plan (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-payment contract mock returns payment "PAY-91001" of 12,500.00 THB matched to "INSTALLMENT" for plan "T-0701", due date 2026-12-15, rule "EXACT" and version "PM-2026.12"
    When TreatmentWorkflow applies the result
    Then installments_paid is "4" and no shortfall is held for due date 2026-12-15
    Then the decision record names rule "EXACT" and rule version "PM-2026.12"
    Then the plan state stays PLAN_RUNNING

  Scenario: AC3 A partial payment holds the shortfall on the plan (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-payment contract mock returns payment "PAY-91002" of 11,875.00 THB matched to "INSTALLMENT" for plan "T-0701", due date 2026-12-15, rule "PARTIAL" and version "PM-2026.12"
    When TreatmentWorkflow applies the result
    Then installment_shortfall is 625.00 for due date 2026-12-15 and installments_paid is "4"
    Then the decision record names rule "PARTIAL" and rule version "PM-2026.12"
    Then a payment below the partial floor writes no shortfall and leaves the plan unchanged

  Scenario: AC4 A late payment inside the cure period ends the wait early (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given plan "T-0701" is in state PLAN_CURE_PERIOD with the cure timer running
    Given the rwb-payment contract mock returns payment "PAY-91004" of 12,500.00 THB matched 3 days after due date 2026-12-15, rule "WINDOW"
    When TreatmentWorkflow applies the result
    Then the cure timer is cancelled and the plan returns to PLAN_RUNNING under rule "R-RES-28"
    Then installments_paid is advanced by one and the decision record names rule "R-RES-28" and the version in force
    Then the first committed answer stands and the second finds the state already moved

  Scenario: AC5 A cure period that passes unpaid breaks the plan (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given plan "T-0701" is in state PLAN_CURE_PERIOD and the 30-day cure timer fires with no matched payment
    When the timer fires
    Then the break count is incremented and the plan is marked PLAN_BROKEN under rule "R-RES-29"
    Then the stage reports the case back to the route decision with reason "broken_plan" under rule "R-RES-30"
    Then where the break count reaches restructure.max_breaks = 2 a further restructure is barred under rule "R-RES-31"
    Then no case status is written by this service

  Scenario: AC6 No rule version in force is a refusal (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rule package read returns no RES rule version in force for 2027-02-01
    When TreatmentWorkflow evaluates the plan step for that date
    Then the evaluation throws NoPackageInForce and MSG-P3-027 is shown for the package in force check
    Then no treatment row and no decision record is written for 2027-02-01

  Scenario: AC7 Nothing moves without its record (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the decision-record library is unavailable during the step
    When TreatmentWorkflow applies a matched installment
    Then the treatment row is unchanged and MSG-P7-003 is shown
    Then the step is retried and no state, shortfall or installments paid is written without its record

  Scenario: AC8 The plan consequence is read under the caller's right (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-access contract mock returns no "Treatment and offer R" right for the caller
    When the caller reads GET /api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}
    Then the response is status 403 with MSG-P4-002
    Then no plan consequence is returned and nothing changes
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The match consequence is read from rwb-payment and never re-computed here: the match type, the rule ID, the package version and the shortfall are the payer's answer | Legacy story scope; DP-11 |
| BR2 | A matched installment advances `installments_paid` by one and clears the shortfall held for that due date | Legacy AC1, AC2 (recordInstallmentPaid); DF-TRT-032 |
| BR3 | A PARTIAL match holds the difference between the installment amount and the matched amount as `installment_shortfall` for that due date | Legacy BR4, AC2; DF-TRT-033 |
| BR4 | A missed installment starts the cure period; a match inside it ends the wait and returns the plan to running | R-RES-27, R-RES-28 |
| BR5 | The cure period and the break limit are parameter values in force, read at evaluation time, never code | D-RCV-36 T10; legacy BR10; DP-06 |
| BR6 | When the cure period passes unpaid the break count increments and the plan is broken; below the limit the case returns to the route decision; at `restructure.max_breaks = 2` a further restructure is barred | R-RES-29, R-RES-30, R-RES-31 |
| BR7 | Every step writes a decision record with the rule ID and the version in force; an earlier step keeps the version that decided it | Legacy BR6; R-UNI-38 |
| BR8 | A step whose record cannot be written is not applied | Legacy BR8; R-UNI-39 |
| BR9 | No version in force is a refusal, never a default | Legacy BR9; R-UNI-41 |

##### 9. State transitions

None of the case status. This story moves the plan state on its own `treatment` row (ASM-4489):

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLAN_RUNNING | missed installment applied | no match for the installment of the due date | PLAN_CURE_PERIOD (R-RES-27) |
| PLAN_CURE_PERIOD | match inside the cure period | matched amount at or above the floor of the row that fires | PLAN_RUNNING (R-RES-28) |
| PLAN_CURE_PERIOD | cure timer fires | no matched payment in the cure period | PLAN_BROKEN (R-RES-29) |
| PLAN_BROKEN | stage report | break count below `restructure.max_breaks` | case returns to the route decision (R-RES-30), by rwb-case |

The case status itself is moved by `CaseWorkflow` of rwb-case on the stage report; this service writes no case row.

| SY-DECLOG, decision record writer | Writes the record of the step |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow | Starts the stage and reads its outcome |

Separating duty: the analyst who authors a rule row does not approve it; the approval is rwb-decision's.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This story writes the `treatment` row and the decision record and raises no event of its own. The service's owned event EV-10 is `rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1` on `rwb.treatment.events.v1` (TSD S2 T5.3) and is raised by the offer and booking stories, not here.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The match reaches this service through the stage signal of `CaseWorkflow` and the match-consequence read of `RWB-P8-E2027-CON`, so this story subscribes to no topic and needs no consumer group (ASM-4487). Both inputs are supplied by contract fakes.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Queue | Role | Retry and timeout |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TreatmentWorkflow` | `rwb-treatment` | Stage child of `CaseWorkflow`; holds the plan clock and the cure timer | One execution per treatment, durable across restarts |
| `EvaluateRules` activity | `rwb-treatment` | Reads the match consequence and evaluates the RES row in force | Default policy; the read fails at 2 s and is retried |
| `RecordAndApply` activity | `rwb-treatment` | Writes the decision record, then the treatment row, in one transaction | Default policy; a record failure fails the activity |
| cure timer | `rwb-treatment` | Durable timer of `CURE_PERIOD_DAYS` for the product; cancelled by a match inside it | Cancelled on the match; fires the break step |

None. DP-10 replaces the polled timer check with a durable workflow timer, and the context pack gives S2 no job (Jobs 0). No Temporal Schedule and no batch window is created by this story.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.treatment`, module `treatment/plan-consequence`.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `MatchConsequenceReader` | Service | Reads the match consequence of the plan for the business date through `RWB-P8-E2027-CON`, one hop with a 2 s timeout |
| `PlanConsequenceRules` | Service | Evaluates the RES row in force with the embedded Drools runtime and returns the rule ID and the version |
| `PlanConsequenceApplier` | Service | Applies the answer to `installments_paid`, `installment_shortfall`, `state`, `outcome` and `outcome_at` |
| `PlanDecisionRecorder` | Service | Builds the record with the rule ID, the version and the inputs, and writes it before the row |
| `CureTimerActivities` | Activity | Starts, cancels and fires the cure timer of `TreatmentWorkflow` |
| `TreatmentPlanResource` | REST | Serves the plan-consequence elements of the treatment read |

**Patterns applied.**

| DP | How it lands here | Dependency |
|---|---|---|
| DP01 | Only `rwb_treatment` is opened; no other service's table is read | none |
| DP03 | Local decision record plus `rwb.decision-record.v1`, written in the same transaction | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP04 | Embedded Drools kit; the RES package comes from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP05 | No `v_ace_*` read; the payment comes through rwb-payment's contract | none |
| DP06 | `CURE_PERIOD_DAYS` and `restructure.max_breaks` from the parameters contract | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP07 | LOV-TRT-OUTCOME from the reference-data contract | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP10 | The cure wait is a durable workflow timer, not a Quartz job or a polled row | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP11 | The match consequence is a REST contract with a mock, one hop, 2 s | C RWB-P8-E2027-CON |
| DP13 | The read is served on `/api/recovery/treatment/v1` | none |
| DP14 | `rwb.treatment.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1` names come from the naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP15 | Columns and rows live on this service's own Flyway sequence in `rwb_treatment` | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP19 | SCR-14 is reached through the gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Database.** No new table and no new column: `installments_paid`, `installment_shortfall`, `state`, `outcome` and `outcome_at` come with the `treatment` table from `RWB-S2-E3001-APP`, and the rule ID and the version live in the decision record linked by `decision_log_id` (ASM-4490). DP-15 is applied by keeping every write on this service's own sequence and login.

**Configuration.** `CURE_PERIOD_DAYS` and `restructure.max_breaks` are parameter values in force, loaded and approved through rwb-decision and rwb-case; the design example reads 30 calendar days for MORTGAGE and `restructure.max_breaks = 2` (ASM-4488). The package code of the RES rule set is not published by any source (GAP-2706).

**Build steps.**

1. Read the match consequence through the contract fake and map it to the plan facts; test AC2 and AC3.
2. Evaluate the RES row in force and return the rule ID and the version; test AC1 and AC6.
3. Write the record before the row in one transaction and fail closed; test AC7.
4. Start and cancel the cure timer; test AC1 and AC4.
5. Fire the cure timer, increment the break count, break the plan and report the stage outcome; test AC5.
6. Serve the plan consequence on the treatment read under the caller's right; test AC8.

**Feature flag.** `rwb.treatment.plan-consequence`, this story's own. Off: no match consequence is applied and the plan is read as written by the earlier stories. The payment-side flag `rwb.payments.matching-rules` stays with P8.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, and a synthetic month of plans shows every applied step with a decision record naming a rule ID and a version in force.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-027 | No rule version is in force for the business date | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record could not be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller holds no right on the read | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P8-001 | Raised by rwb-payment, not here: unmatched payments of the run | {count} payments for {date} matched no plan and are on the exception list. |

For MSG-P3-027 the {check} value is package in force, and {detail} names the package code only, never a payment or a person. Thai text follows DL10 (legacy section 14).

SCR-14 shows the treatment with its plan consequence: the state, the installments paid, the shortfall of the current due date, and the rule ID and version of the last step from its decision record (states Loading; plan running; cure period; broken). The matched and unmatched receipt list stays SCR-28 with rwb-payment and is not re-cut here. The route is reached through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19); the rule version in force shows on the rules screen with rwb-decision.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the cure period, the break limit and every column of the rule rows are data in force, read at evaluation time.
- No personal data in events, records, workflow inputs or logs: the record holds the payment code, the due date, the amount, the shortfall, the rule ID and the version only.
- ACE data only through its owner's contract: this story opens no `recovery.v_ace_*` view and no other service's table (DP-01, DP-05).
- The decision record is written before the treatment row, and no plan change exists without it.
- One evaluator: the step calls the rule engine and reads no rule table, workbook or `drl_source`.
- The plan clock is a workflow timer: no Quartz job, no polled timer row and no scheduled scan (DP-10).
- The treatment read is served under the caller's right and scope; a refusal changes nothing.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-027 for rwb-decision, the rule registry and the PAYMENT_MATCH governance of the matching rules. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **the PAYMENT_MATCH rule package held and governed in the rwb-decision registry — the package row, its version rows, the parsed row catalogue and its test cases, with the load of a workbook version and every check on it, the four-eyes approval, the promotion at 00:01 and the one-call rollback, each written as a decision record and readable through the decision log**, so that **a matching rule changes as approved, dated data that every consuming service can name, and no version reaches a payment run without at least 50 passing test cases and a second pair of eyes**.

Inside `rwb-decision` this is the registry and governance half of the legacy story RWB-E2-027:

- Service `rwb-decision`, schema `rwb_decision`, REST base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, topic `rwb.decision.events.v1` with event names `rwb.decision.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` for the decision records every governance action writes (DP-03).
- One deliverable and nothing else: the PAYMENT_MATCH package in the rule registry and its governance — the `rule_package` row, the `rule_package_version` rows "PM-2026.12" and "PM-2027.01" and the refused "PM-2027.02", the parsed `rule_row` catalogue (EXACT at row order 1, WINDOW at 2, PARTIAL at 3), the `rule_test_case` set of at least 50 cases (58 for the package), the load with its compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row and scenario checks and its dry run, the four-eyes approval, the promotion at 00:01, the one-call rollback, and one decision record for each of those actions, read through `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log`.
- The match stays with `rwb-payment` (P8, RWB-P8-E2027-APP): JOB-07 and its event-started workflow, the `RuleEvaluator` call, the fired row, the proceeds row, the posting file, the exception list and the D5 entry a match writes. This story never matches a payment, writes no proceeds row and reads no ACE view.
- The workbook and its Rows and Tests tabs stay with `rwb-case` (P3, RWB-P3-E2042-APP and the authoring pipeline RWB-P3-E1073-APP), with the parameters and the reference data those stories publish (DP-06, DP-07); this story receives the workbook at the load operation and resolves no rule value of its own.
- The session, the role, the right and the delegation of authority stay with `rwb-access` (P4, RWB-P4-E2027-APP); the installment shortfall a PARTIAL match passes to the plan stays with `rwb-treatment` (S2, RWB-S2-E2027-APP).
- The registry is rwb-decision's under the R-PREC default ruling: `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` are P7 rows (ASM-2293), and the generic scaffold of RWB-P7-E2042-APP — the four tables, their Flyway baseline and the shared operation signatures — is reused and not rebuilt (ASM-2295). Every consuming service holds only an evaluated copy (DP-04).
- The database login used by the capability is the per-service login of DP-02. Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1290; ASM-2289); this story uses the phrase "the rwb-decision login (DP-02)" and never the shared monolith login.

The legacy rule change of RWB-E2-027 is carried into the registry unchanged: the same package code PAYMENT_MATCH, the same three rows and their row order, the same thresholds as row columns, the same "the author cannot approve" rule, the same dated version in force, and the same refusal of an invalid load in full.

##### 2. Business rationale

The matching rules of RWB-E2-027 are the reason a short or a late installment matches without a person. In the monolith they were a table read by code; the two rules that were missing, PARTIAL and WINDOW, could only arrive as a change to the matching class. D-RCV-36 T10 retires `payment_match_rule` and makes the match type, the amount tolerance, the window, the grace and the partial floor columns of a decision table, so a change of a threshold is a change of data, not code. That only works if the data is governed: tested, approved by a second pair of eyes, dated, promoted and reversible in one call.

Governance is central and evaluation is local (Arch v5 slide 27; ADR-017). rwb-decision owns the registry — the packages, their versions, the parsed rows and the test cases — and publishes `RulePackageInForce` when an approved version reaches its valid-from date. The owning service loads the model, verifies the checksum and swaps it in (DP-04). Without the registry there is no answer to the two questions an audit asks of every match: which rule fired, and under which approved version.

This story is the rwb-decision half of that split for RWB-E2-027. rwb-case writes the PAYMENT_MATCH workbook and its Tests tab, rwb-payment runs JOB-07 against the version in force, and this story holds the package, proves at load that the rows are consistent and that at least 50 test cases pass, takes the approval from a role other than the author, promotes the version at 00:01, rolls it back in one call when it must, and records every one of those actions in the decision log. It is what makes the measure of RWB-E2-027 true: every match names its rule and its package version, and no version reaches a run untested or unapproved.

The realignment changes the mechanism, not the business rule:

1. The reference rule tables of the monolith become `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` in `rwb_decision`, with no other service reading them (DP-01). The 448 route-set rows and the other packages are not this story's; PAYMENT_MATCH is.
2. The version label and the valid-from date become the identity of a version, and the version in force on a business date is a lookup and never a default (BR6, BR10).
3. The load checks of the legacy version load become the registry's own pipeline — compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row, at least 50 scenarios and the dry run — and a failure refuses the whole load (BR3).
4. The approval becomes a four-eyes operation of the service: RW-RISK approves, the author cannot, and the approval is not a credit decision of the delegation of authority (ASM-2294).
5. The nightly copy to the data lake is gone (DP-17); the announcement of a version in force is `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1`, and each governance action writes a local decision record that is published on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03).
6. The Quartz job that promoted a version becomes the JOB-20 Temporal Schedule at 00:01 on the `rwb-decision` queue (DP-10), which this story registers the package with and does not create (ASM-2296).

This story meets REQ-CHO-009 on the governance side and carries the rule-version half of R-UNI-38 and R-UNI-41: an earlier decision keeps the version it was taken under, and no version in force is a refusal and never a default match.

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E2-027:

- The package code PAYMENT_MATCH exists with owner role RW-COE, and version "PM-2026.12" is in force from 2026-12-01 with the EXACT, WINDOW and PARTIAL rows of section 7 (legacy sections 3 and 7).
- The PAYMENT_MATCH workbook holds the Rows tab (RuleSet = package code, NAME = rule ID, default row last) and the Tests tab with at least 50 test cases; the package carries 58 (RWB-P3-E2042-APP AC2; `rules.testcases.min` = 50). The 58 is the count of the Tests tab and is copied from the E2-042 package of the same code.
- Version "PM-2027.01" is authored with valid from 2027-01-01 and changes WINDOW to 5 days after the due date (legacy AC3); version "PM-2027.02" is authored with rows WINDOW and PARTIAL both at row order 2 and a PARTIAL tolerance of 120 (legacy AC6).
- RW-COE holds Rules and parameters C, RW-RISK holds Rules and parameters A and RW-AUDIT holds Rules and parameters R (legacy section 10 and section 12).
