##### 4. Flow

1. RW-COE: authors the PAYMENT_MATCH workbook in rwb-case with its Rows and Tests tabs (RWB-P3-E2042-APP), stores it write-once with its SHA-256, and calls the load operation of rwb-decision with the workbook and the valid-from date.
2. rwb-decision `RuleVersionService`: reads the parameter `rules.testcases.min` through DP-06, parses the Rows tab into `rule_row` candidates and the Tests tab into `rule_test_case` candidates, and compiles the workbook to a KieBase through the embedded Drools kit (DP-04).
3. rwb-decision `RuleCheckPipeline`: runs the compile check, the schema check on the condition and output columns, the overlap check, the unreachable row check, the default row check and the scenario check against at least `rules.testcases.min` = 50 test cases, then the dry run; any failure refuses the whole load with MSG-P3-027 and writes nothing.
4. rwb-decision `RuleVersionService`, one transaction: writes the `rule_package_version` row with status LOADED, the workbook reference, the generated DRL, the checksum, the valid-from date, the author, the test result and the dry-run counts; writes the `rule_row` rows and the `rule_test_case` rows of the version; writes the decision record of the load (DP-03); and returns 201 with the version.
5. RW-RISK: approves the version through the approve operation. The service refuses the call when the approver is the author (MSG-P7-002), and otherwise moves the version to APPROVED, records the approver and the approval time, and writes the decision record of the approval.
6. JOB-20: the rule-promote Temporal Schedule runs at 00:01 on the `rwb-decision` queue (Arch v5 slide 44; DP-10). It promotes every APPROVED version whose valid-from date has arrived to IN_FORCE, supersedes the version it replaces, writes the decision record of the promotion and publishes `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` with the package code, the version label, the checksum and the valid-from date. A version whose valid-from date has not arrived is not promoted.
7. The consuming service (rwb-payment for PAYMENT_MATCH) consumes the event, fetches the model, verifies the checksum and swaps it in; this story builds none of that (DP-04, RWB-P8-E2027-APP).
8. RW-COE: when a version in force must be withdrawn, calls the rollback operation once for the version. The service moves the pointer to the version in force before it, marks the rolled-back version ROLLED_BACK, keeps every earlier decision on the version it was taken under, and writes the decision record of the rollback. A rollback with no earlier version is refused with MSG-P3-015.
9. RW-AUDIT or any role with the decision-log read: reads the governance actions through `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` by package, date and actor, and one entry with `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}`, with its inputs reference, rule ID, rule version, actor, final call, decided time, previous hash and entry hash.
10. Nothing in this story matches a payment, writes a proceeds row, calls rwb-treatment or changes a case status: the registry and its governance are the whole deliverable.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A version is loaded with two rows of the same row order, or a tolerance above 100 | The load is refused in full with 422; no version row, no rule row and no test-case row is written; "PM-2026.12" stays in force | MSG-P3-027 | AC3, TC-E2-027-06 |
| X2 | The Tests tab holds fewer than `rules.testcases.min` cases, or a case fails | The load is refused with 422, the failing check and the failing case IDs named; no version is created | MSG-P3-027 | AC4 |
| X3 | The author of the version calls approve | The call is refused; the version stays LOADED and no approval is recorded | MSG-P7-002 | AC5 |
| X4 | The decision record of an action cannot be written | Nothing is committed: no version row, no status change, no promotion, no rollback, no event; an incident is raised and the action is retried by its caller | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E2-027-07, TC-E2-027-13 |
| X5 | A rollback is called for the only version the package has, or for a version that was never in force | The call is refused; the version in force stays in force and nothing is written | MSG-P3-015 | AC8 |
| X6 | A version label that already exists for the package is loaded again | The load is refused with 409; the version already held is untouched | MSG-GEN-004 | TC-E2-027-06 |
| X7 | An empty workbook, or a workbook without validFrom, is loaded | The load is refused with 422 and the missing field named; nothing is written | MSG-GEN-001 | TC-E2-027-06 |
| X8 | The caller holds no right for the operation, or the version is outside the caller's scope | 403 with MSG-P4-002; nothing is read, written or promoted | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-027-11, TC-E2-027-12 |
| X9 | No version has a valid-from date on or before the business date, so no version is in force for it | The registry answers that no version is in force for that date; the consuming service raises `NoPackageInForce` and reports MSG-P3-027; no default version is ever substituted | MSG-P3-027 | TC-E2-027-10 |

A stale version row at commit, matched on its `version` column, is MSG-GEN-004 and the action is retried, never applied twice. The version row, its rule rows, its test-case rows and its decision record are always written together, so a version cannot exist without its record and no promotion can announce a version that was not recorded.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P8-E2027-CON, the platform contracts of its DP table, the registry scaffold of RWB-P7-E2042-APP and the fakes; it matches no payment and rebuilds no authoring pipeline |
| Negotiable | The version labels, the valid-from dates, the row values, the test cases and the message texts are data and registry rows; the story fixes only the checks, the four-eyes rule, the promotion and the rollback semantics |
| Valuable | A matching rule changes as approved, dated data with at least 50 passing cases and two pairs of eyes, and every change is explainable from the decision log |
| Estimable | One controller pair, one check pipeline, one test-case runner, one approval, one promotion handler, one rollback, one repository and one record writer |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is a load, an approval, a promotion, a rollback or a read, with a fixed Given, When and Then and a recorded result |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The registry is rwb-decision's, and a version is never edited in place: a change is a new version, and a rollback moves a pointer | Arch v5 slides 27 and 41; ASM-2293; DP-01 |
| BR2 | Every version is loaded from the Drools XLS workbook through the load operation, and the version row holds the workbook reference, the generated DRL, the SHA-256 and the valid-from date | Temporal and Drools slide 15 and its notes |
| BR3 | The load checks are compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row, at least `rules.testcases.min` = 50 scenarios and the dry run; any failure refuses the load in full | Temporal and Drools slide 15; legacy BR7; AC-P7-007-01 |
| BR4 | First match wins, the default row is last, and the PAYMENT_MATCH row order is EXACT 1, WINDOW 2, PARTIAL 3 | legacy BR1; D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR5 | The author of a version cannot approve it; the approver is RW-RISK, and the two are distinct users holding Rules and parameters C and A | Temporal and Drools slide 15; legacy section 10; ASM-2294 |
| BR6 | A version is in force from its valid-from date; JOB-20 promotes an APPROVED version at 00:01, supersedes the version it replaces and publishes `RulePackageInForce` | Arch v5 slides 14, 27 and 44; Temporal and Drools slide 15 |
| BR7 | A rollback is one call and puts the version in force before the rolled-back one in force; a decision taken under the rolled-back version keeps that version on its record | FSD P7 AC-ALT-P7-007-02; legacy BR6 |
| BR8 | Every governance action — load, approve, promote, roll back — writes its decision record in the same transaction, and an action whose record cannot be written is not taken | FSD P7 VR-P7-001-2 and principle 5; legacy BR8; ASM-2297 |
| BR9 | The match type, row order, amount tolerance, window, grace and partial floor are columns of the rule rows, not code and not a reference table | legacy BR10; D-RCV-36 T10 |
| BR10 | No version in force on the business date is `NoPackageInForce` and MSG-P3-027, never a default version | legacy BR9; D-RCV-36 T3 |
| BR11 | The version states are LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK and REFUSED, and no other value is written | Temporal and Drools slide 15 notes; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 |
| BR12 | No user, role or code writes `rule_row` or `rule_test_case` except through a load; the parsed rows and the test cases are derived from the workbook of the version | Temporal and Drools slide 15 T4 and T6; AC-P7-007-01 |
| BR13 | The decision code, the rule ID and the rule version of a governance record are values of the LOV-DECISION list and of the package, never a constant of the code | TSD P7 v2 T3.1 `decision_log_entry`; ASM-2289 |

##### 9. State transitions

This story changes no case status and no plan state. It owns the state of a package version.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | A workbook is loaded | Every check passes and the decision record is written | LOADED |
| (none) | A workbook is loaded | A check fails, the label exists, or the record cannot be written | (no row is created); the earlier version in force keeps its state |
| LOADED | Approve | The caller is not the author and holds Rules and parameters A | APPROVED |
| LOADED | Approve | The caller is the author | LOADED (refused, MSG-P7-002) |
| APPROVED | JOB-20 at 00:01 | The valid-from date has arrived | IN_FORCE; the version it replaces becomes SUPERSEDED |
| APPROVED | JOB-20 at 00:01 | The valid-from date has not arrived | APPROVED (unchanged) |
| IN_FORCE | Rollback, one call | A version was in force before it | ROLLED_BACK; the previous version becomes IN_FORCE |
| IN_FORCE | Rollback, one call | No version was in force before it | IN_FORCE (refused, MSG-P3-015) |
| IN_FORCE | A newer version is promoted | The newer version reaches its valid-from date | SUPERSEDED |

The case and plan transitions of RWB-E2-027 — `PLAN_RUNNING` on `PAYMENT_RECEIVED` under R-RES-26 and `PLAN_CURE_PERIOD` on `PAYMENT_RECEIVED_LATE` under R-RES-28 — are rwb-case's and rwb-payment's, and this story neither raises nor observes them.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Loads a PAYMENT_MATCH workbook version, runs the dry run, calls the rollback, and reads the registry and the decision log (Rules and parameters C and R) |
| RW-RISK, risk and model risk officer | Approves a loaded version (Rules and parameters A); may not be the author of the version |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the package, the versions, the test results and the governance decision records (Rules and parameters R) |
| RW-DATASTEW, data steward and data product owner | Reads the versions and their valid-from dates (Rules and parameters R) |
| The rwb-decision service identity | Runs the checks, the dry run, the promotion handler and the rollback, and writes the decision records |
| SY-DECLOG, decision log writer | Supplies the hash-chained record write of DP-03 |
| SY-RULES, Drools evaluator | Compiles the workbook and supplies first-match semantics and the checksum through the embedded kit at load (DP-04); it evaluates nothing in this story |
| RW-CASEOWN and any role without a Rules and parameters right | Refused with MSG-P4-002 on every operation of section 12.1 |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A package version is not a credit decision; the approval is four eyes and not a DoA level |

Separation of duty: the analyst who loads a version does not approve it, and RW-RISK approves with a distinct user reference (BR5; legacy section 10). No person is named anywhere; the actors are roles and service identities.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-decision` (P7); base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`. The six rule-package and rule-version paths are the ownership map's P7 paths; the two decision-log paths are API-P7-006 and API-P7-007 of TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 on the service base. The load and version-list request and answer shapes are the legacy section 12 shapes; the rollback request body, the dry-run body beyond `testResult` and `dryRunCounts`, and the decision code of a governance entry are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1290; ASM-2289).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/rule-packages` | List the packages of the registry with their code and owner role; 200 with the package list | Rules and parameters R | Not applicable, read only |
| POST | `/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` | Load a workbook version: multipart `file` (xlsx with the Rows and Tests tabs) and `validFrom`; run the checks and the dry run; 201 with the version | Rules and parameters C | Package code and version label; a repeated label is 409 with MSG-GEN-004 |
| GET | `/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` | List the versions of a package with status, valid-from and valid-to dates, author, approver, checksum, test result and dry-run counts; 200 | Rules and parameters R | Not applicable, read only |
| GET | `/admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/dry-run` | Read the dry-run counts and the per-test-case result of a version | Rules and parameters R | Not applicable, read only |
| POST | `/admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/approve` | Approve a loaded version with four eyes; 200 with the version at APPROVED | Rules and parameters A | Idempotency-Key header; the author's call is refused with MSG-P7-002 |
| POST | `/admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/rollback` | Roll a version in force back to the version before it in one call; 200 with the two versions | Rules and parameters C | Idempotency-Key header; a second call for the same version finds it no longer in force |
| GET | `/decision-log` | Read the governance decision records by case, decision, rule, approver and date range; 200 with the page | Decision log R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |
| GET | `/decision-log/{entryId}` | Read one decision record with its inputs reference, versions, actor, final call, actions, outcome and hashes; 200 | Decision log R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |

The version body carries `versionId`, `packageCode`, `versionLabel`, `status`, `validFrom`, `validTo`, `author`, `approver`, `checksum`, `testResult` (`total`, `passed`, `failed`, `failedScenarioIds`) and `dryRunCounts`. Errors: 401 no session; 403 the role lacks the right (MSG-P4-002); 404 an unknown package code or version; 409 the version label exists (MSG-GEN-004) or the version is not in the state the call needs; 422 a check failed (MSG-P3-027 with the check, row and column in the problem detail) or a required field is missing (MSG-GEN-001); 503 the decision record could not be written (MSG-P7-003). Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set. No promote operation is published: the promotion is JOB-20's Schedule of 12.6.

The version states, the check names and the match types are values of the registry and of the reference lists of DP-07, never constants of the code; the value set of the version states is the one Temporal and Drools slide 15 gives. The four `/admin/rule-versions` paths the ownership map also gives P7 are legacy paths with no target story: this story and the P7 registry stories serve the `/admin/rule-packages` and `/admin/rule-package-versions` families only (GAP-1293; ASM-2292).

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this story |

| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case, on RWB-P3-E1043-CON | LOV-DECISION and the version-state list with the version in force (DP-07); faked |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access, on RWB-P4-E1037-CON | The caller's role, scope and Rules and parameters right behind every operation of 12.1; the guard reads this answer and the operation declares the right it needs; faked |

The parameters and the reference lists are read through their client libraries and also over these two operations; neither is resolved into a rule value here. They are served in this story by the rwb-case parameters and reference-data fake of 12.8, and the session read by the rwb-access fake; the rwb-payment contract fake, the Drools kit fake and the decision-record library fake complete the fake set of 12.8. The contract dependency recorded on the story is RWB-P8-E2027-CON: rwb-payment's contract fixes what a match entry names, and this registry is what it names. The platform and published contracts the DP table adds are listed in section 13 and carried in the gap of GAP-1291.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` (EV-30) | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | P7 | packageCode | package code, version label, package version ID, checksum, valid-from date, promoted at |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 ledger library, published by this service | entryId | the hash-chained record of a governance action: decision code, rule ID (the package code), rule version, inputs reference, actor, final call, decided at |

Both are written to the outbox in the same transaction as the action and relayed with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope by the outbox relay of the platform. `RulePackageInForce` is consumed by the owning services that hold an evaluated copy — for PAYMENT_MATCH that is rwb-payment — and by gateway-bff for its cache refresh (Arch v5 slides 20, 43 and 44). No event carries a name, an e-mail address, a mobile number or an account number.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. This story consumes no Kafka event: the workbook arrives through the load operation, the approval through its operation, and the promotion is the Schedule of 12.6. `ApprovalRequested` (EV-09) is not raised by a package-version approval, because that approval is not an item routed by the delegation of authority (BR5; ASM-2294).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None of this story's own. The load, the approve and the rollback are synchronous REST operations; the promotion is the JOB-20 Temporal Schedule of 12.6 and not a workflow; and the embedded Drools kit is called in process at load and never inside a workflow. This story registers nothing on the `rwb-decision` task queue, starts no workflow and adds no activity, and the matching window of JOB-07 is rwb-payment's and not this story's (DP-10; ASM-2296).

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | When | Mechanism | Owner and this story's part |
|---|---|---|---|
| JOB-20 Rule promote | 00:01 | A Temporal Schedule on the `rwb-decision` queue that promotes every APPROVED version whose valid-from date has arrived to IN_FORCE, supersedes the version it replaces, writes the decision record and publishes `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` (Arch v5 slide 44; Temporal and Drools slide 15) | P7 rwb-decision, shared rule-registry infrastructure. This story registers PAYMENT_MATCH with its valid-from date and asserts the promotion in AC6; it creates no Schedule and no new trigger (ASM-2296) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, module `rules/registry`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision.rules.registry`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

How this story applies each row. **DP-01**: the four registry tables and `decision_log_entry` sit in `rwb_decision`; the story reads no schema of another service and no service reads its tables — the rows travel as the model, the catalog and the event. **DP-03**: the load, the approval, the promotion and the rollback each write one local decision record in the same transaction and publish `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; a record that cannot be written stops the action (BR8). **DP-04**: the load and the promotion use the embedded kit for the compile, the checksum and first-match semantics, and the registry supplies the package to the consuming services; the C dependency RWB-P7-E1073-CON is this service's own rule-package contract story and is built against its published set, because the kit lives in the platform library and the contract story is consumed, not rebuilt. **DP-05**: no ACE view is read by this story; the payment facts reach it only through the decision entry a match wrote, and the registry never sees `v_ace_payment`. **DP-06**: `rules.testcases.min` = 50 is read as a parameter for the scenario check and is never a constant. **DP-07**: LOV-DECISION and the version-state list are read as reference data with the version in force; the match types and thresholds stay row columns and are never reference data (BR9). **DP-10**: the promotion is the JOB-20 Temporal Schedule at 00:01 and this story creates no workflow and no Schedule; the matching window of JOB-07 is rwb-payment's, so no job of the matching run appears here. **DP-11**: the three consumed operations are called once, one hop, on the owner's base with a 2 s timeout and a breaker; the legacy in-process calls to the parameter, the list and the access check become those published calls. **DP-13**: every path of section 12 uses `/api/recovery/decision/v1`; no monolith base appears. **DP-14**: the topic is `rwb.decision.events.v1`, the event is `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1`, and the shared decision-record topic keeps its platform name. **DP-15**: this story owns its migration in the `rwb_decision` Flyway sequence and touches no other schema. **DP-19**: no screen is built here; the Epic 8 screen reads these operations through the gateway-bff composite route and this story adds no route.

The platform H dependencies of the table — H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON — and the C dependencies C RWB-P7-E1073-CON, C RWB-P3-E1042-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON are the DP-added dependencies that are **not** in the metadata rows, which name None and RWB-P8-E2027-CON. They are recorded in GAP-1291 and ASM-2290: they are platform contracts of wave 0 and published contracts of rwb-case and of this service, none of them blocks the build, and an APP story builds against the published set and its fake. DP-04 also brings this service's own rule-package contract story C RWB-P7-E1073-CON, and DP-06 and DP-07 bring the parameters and reference-data contracts of rwb-case.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| RulePackageController | Controller | `GET /admin/rule-packages` and the version list, with the guard, the scope and the problem mapping |
| RuleVersionController | Controller | The multipart load, the dry run, the approve and the rollback, with the Idempotency-Key and the 201, 200, 409 and 422 answers |
| RuleVersionService | Service | Orders the load in one transaction: parse, check, dry run, version row, rule rows, test cases, decision record |
| WorkbookParser | Service | Reads the Rows tab into `rule_row` candidates (RuleSet = package code, NAME = rule ID, default row last) and the Tests tab into `rule_test_case` candidates; rejects an empty or malformed workbook with MSG-GEN-001 |
| RuleCheckPipeline | Service | Compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row and scenario checks through the embedded kit; refuses the whole load with MSG-P3-027 and names the check, the row, the column and the failing case IDs |
| TestCaseRunner | Service | Runs the Tests tab against the compiled model, counts total, passed and failed, and records the expected and actual result of every case |
| DryRunService | Service | Runs the dry run over the test cases and stores the counts and the per-case result of the version |
| ApprovalService | Service | Refuses the author with MSG-P7-002, moves LOADED to APPROVED with the approver and the time, and writes the decision record |
| PromotionService | Schedule handler | On the JOB-20 run, promotes every APPROVED version whose valid-from date has arrived, supersedes its predecessor, writes the record and publishes `RulePackageInForce` |
| RollbackService | Service | Moves the pointer to the previous version in one call, marks the rolled-back version ROLLED_BACK, refuses a version with no predecessor with MSG-P3-015, and writes the record |
| RuleRegistryRepository | Repository | The four tables in `rwb_decision`, with the optimistic lock and the unique keys of the migration |
| DecisionLogController | Controller | `GET /decision-log` and `GET /decision-log/{entryId}` with the decision-log read, the scope and the hashes |
| DecisionRecordWriter | Service | The local record and its outbox row in the same transaction as the action (DP-03) |
| ParameterClient, ReferenceDataClient, SessionClient | Clients | The three consumed operations of 12.2, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker |
| PaymentContractFakeAdapter | Test adapter | The rwb-payment contract fake of 12.8, replaced by the contract test of RWB-P8-E2027-CON when it lands |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row`, `rule_test_case`, `decision_log_entry` and the library objects, all in schema `rwb_decision`; reads no other schema.
- One migration in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15, `V2027_1__decision_payment_match_governance.sql`, adds the unique key of the version label within a package (`ux_rule_package_version_label`) and the unique key of the row order within a version (`ux_rule_row_version_row_order`), so a repeated label and a duplicate row order are refused by the database as well as by the checks; it adds no column to the four tables and writes no seed row.
- The tables and their baseline are RWB-P7-E2042-APP's; where they have not landed, this story's migration is reconciled with that baseline at the first joint environment (ASM-2295). The PAYMENT_MATCH package row is written on the first load if it is absent, with owner role RW-COE.
- Update a version with `WHERE id = ? AND version = ?`; zero rows updated is MSG-GEN-004 and the action is retried, never applied twice.

**Configuration and reference data**

- `rules.testcases.min` = 50 through the parameters contract of DP-06; the PAYMENT_MATCH Tests tab holds 58 cases, so the check passes with 8 to spare (RWB-P3-E2042-APP AC2).
- The PAYMENT_MATCH version labels, valid-from dates and rows are the legacy values: "PM-2026.12" from 2026-12-01 with EXACT 1, WINDOW 2, PARTIAL 3; "PM-2027.01" from 2027-01-01 with WINDOW at 5 days after; "PM-2027.02" refused. RWB-P3-E2042-APP and RWB-P7-E2042-APP hold the same package under the label "PMT-2026.12" from 2026-12-15 — a conflict recorded in GAP-1292 and read here as one package that must be reconciled to one version row before SIT (ASM-2291).
- LOV-DECISION and the version-state list are read through DP-07 with the version in force; no decision code and no state is a constant in code. The decision code of a governance entry is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1290; ASM-2289).
- The owner role RW-COE and the approver role RW-RISK are rows of the access model, received from the session read and the parameters; the author and the approver must be distinct user references (ASM-2294).
- The checksum and the workbook reference are stored with the version and published on `RulePackageInForce`; a version is never edited in place (BR1, BR2).

**Build steps**

1. `RuleRegistryRepository` and the migration's two unique keys; test that a repeated label and a duplicate row order are refused by the constraint.
2. `WorkbookParser` and `TestCaseRunner` over the Rows and Tests tabs; tests for AC2 and for X7.
3. `RuleCheckPipeline` with the six checks and the dry run, and the refusal in full with MSG-P3-027; tests for AC3, AC4, X1 and X2.
4. `RuleVersionService` with the single transaction and `DecisionRecordWriter`, and the fail-closed behaviour of X4; tests for AC2, TC-E2-027-07 and TC-E2-027-13.
5. `ApprovalService` with the four-eyes rule and the LOADED to APPROVED transition; tests for AC5 and X3.
6. `PromotionService` on the JOB-20 run, with effective dating, the supersede step and the `RulePackageInForce` outbox row; tests for AC6 and X9.
7. `RollbackService` with the one-call rollback, the previous-version pointer and the MSG-P3-015 refusal; tests for AC7 and AC8.
8. `DecisionLogController` and the read of the governance records, with the scope and the hashes; test for AC9.
9. The privacy test: the workbook, the rows, the test cases, the records and the two event payloads hold package codes, version labels, rule IDs, thresholds, dates, amounts and payment codes only, and no name, e-mail address, mobile number, national identity number or account number.

**Feature switch.** The legacy flag `rwb.p3.drools` is kept as the legacy reference and is read in the target as a parameter through DP-06. Off: the load, the approve and the rollback operations answer as unavailable and no version reaches IN_FORCE, while the registry and the decision log stay readable and the version already in force keeps running. The exact answer with the switch off is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1290; ASM-2289).

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; a SIT environment shows "PM-2026.12" IN_FORCE from 2026-12-01 with 58 of 58 test cases, "PM-2027.02" refused in full with MSG-P3-027, the author's approve refused with MSG-P7-002, "PM-2027.01" promoted at 00:01 with one `RulePackageInForce` event, one rollback that returns "PM-2026.12" to IN_FORCE with the earlier entry still naming "PM-2027.01", and one decision record per action, each returned by the decision-log read.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-027 | A load check fails, or no version is in force on the business date | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. | This story, on the load and the version list |
| MSG-P7-002 | The author of a version calls approve | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. | This story, on the approve |
| MSG-P3-015 | A rollback is called for a version with no predecessor | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1290; ASM-2289) | This story, on the rollback |
| MSG-GEN-001 | An empty workbook, or a missing validFrom, is loaded | Enter {field}. | This story, on the load |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The version label is already loaded, or the version changed at commit | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. | This story, on the load and the update |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record of an action cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on every governance action |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role holds no right for the operation, or the version is outside its scope | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, through the session read |

For MSG-P3-027 the {check} value is compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row, scenario or package in force, and {detail} names the row ID, the column, the test-case ID or the package code only, never a payment or a person. The six texts above are copied unchanged from the legacy story and FSD P7 v3 A2.7; the text of MSG-P3-015 is named by FSD P7 A2.7 AC-EXC-P7-007-05 and is not written out in any source this story may read, so the placeholder stands (GAP-1290; ASM-2289). Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the match type, the row order, the amount tolerance, the window, the grace and the partial floor are columns of the PAYMENT_MATCH rows, and `rules.testcases.min` is a parameter.
- No personal data in logs, events, workflow history, test cases or prompts: the rows, the test cases and the records hold package codes, version labels, rule IDs, thresholds, dates, amounts and payment codes only.
- No read of another service's tables, and no other service reads `rwb_decision` (DP-01): the parameters, the reference lists and the session arrive on their operations, and the payment facts arrive only as the decision entry a match wrote.
- The decision record is written before the action commits; no version exists, no version is approved, promoted or rolled back without its record (BR8).
- One registry, one evaluator: the registry governs and the consuming service evaluates through its embedded Drools kit; this story never evaluates a package for a business decision and never reads a workbook at runtime.
- A version is never edited in place: a change is a new version, and a rollback moves the pointer; the workbook and the DRL are stored write-once with their checksum.
- The version states are the six of BR11 and the check names are the seven of BR3; no other value is written and none is a constant of the code.
- No secret in a workbook, a test case or the run material: the rwb-decision login (DP-02) and the certificate come from the platform secret store, and the test data is synthetic.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **rwb-payment deployed for the payment-matching key with a `RulePackageInForce` consumer group on `rwb.decision.events.v1` that refreshes the evaluated copy of PAYMENT_MATCH and falls back to the version in force — never to a default match — a provisioned `rwb.payment.events.v1` with its `.retry` and `.dlt` topics and their ACLs, the consumer groups of the six consumed events, a Temporal worker pool on task queue `rwb-payment` that registers the JOB-07 workflow and its activities and no Schedule, a Flyway migration job that touches `rwb_payment` only, secrets taken from the key store by reference, four alerts on outbox lag, dead-letter depth, workflow failures and rule-cache staleness, a canary gate and a rehearsed rollback**, so that **an operator can see whether the matching run is deciding on the approved version, catch a stuck run or a lost event before a payment is affected, and return to the previous version or the previous release without a code change**.

This story deploys and operates the capability of RWB-P8-E2027-APP. It writes no business code, no rule row, no threshold and no event schema; it fixes how the service is provisioned, observed, gated and rolled back.

##### 2. Business rationale

A rule package is data and a matching run is a workflow, so almost nothing that can go wrong in this key looks like "the service is down". The evaluated copy can be a version behind, a `RulePackageInForce` event can be lost, a run can sit on a retry, an event can pile up in the `.dlt` topic, or the outbox relay can fall behind while every probe answers healthy. In the monolith the matching rules were a table read in process and the run was a Quartz trigger on a shared job table; a stale table and a stuck job were the same class of incident and the same person looked at them. In the target the model is fetched from another service, the run is a workflow on another platform and the events cross a broker, so each of those failures has its own signal and its own recovery path.

Deployment is therefore part of the capability. The rule-cache refresh is an operational behaviour, not a library detail: the event must arrive, the model must be verified, and when it cannot be, the service must keep the version in force and say so — because the alternative, a default match or an empty cache, silently breaks BR9 and every decision taken under it. The topics need their retry and dead-letter paths and their ACLs, because a mis-scoped ACL and a missing `.dlt` topic both look like "the consumer is quiet". The worker pool needs its own build ID and its own visibility, because JOB-07 is started by `AceDataReady` (EV-26) and a worker that is not polling is invisible until the morning cut-off. The migration job must be pinned to `rwb_payment`, because the registry tables are rwb-decision's and a migration that touches them would cross the boundary DP-01 draws.

The values that operators need are not specified by any source: the alert thresholds, the cache-staleness window, the outbox-lag and dead-letter limits, the worker pool size, the canary percentage and the probe timings (DL11 is open on the non-functional target values). This story therefore fixes their names and the rule that they are values of the chart, and carries the numbers as placeholders (GAP-2508; ASM-4156).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The Kafka event platform provisions a topic with a `.retry` topic and a `.dlt` topic and applies topic ACLs (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-N002-INF).
- The Temporal workflow kit and the `rwb-recovery` namespace are available (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), because the matching run is an event-started workflow on task queue `rwb-payment` (DP-10).
- The per-service Flyway sequence and the migration conventions are in force (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON), and the `rwb_payment` schema and login exist with their grants (RWB-PLT-DB).
- rwb-decision publishes `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` on `rwb.decision.events.v1` (EV-30) and owns the 00:01 promotion (JOB-20; Arch v5 slide 44).
- The platform secret store, the workload identity and the mTLS material are available; their names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2508; ASM-4157) and the chart references them by role only.
- The registry answers the version list and the model fetch (RWB-P7-E2027-APP, RWB-P7-E1073-CON), and the model carries its SHA-256.
- The message catalogue and the platform error envelope are in force, so an alert can carry a message ID where a message exists.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds the service image from the template, runs the unit, component and contract tests of the app story, scans the image and the dependencies, publishes the chart, and promotes the same image digest and chart version through DEV, SIT and UAT without a rebuild.
2. The chart deploys the service with its own login, its migration job, its probes, the consumer configuration and the values of section 11: the rule-cache bound and warm-up list, the worker pool size, the consumer concurrency, the outbox-lag and dead-letter limits, the canary percentage and the alert windows.
3. The provisioning step creates `rwb.payment.events.v1` with its `.retry` and `.dlt` topics and the producer ACL for this service, and the consumer groups of the six consumed events with their own `.retry` and `.dlt` paths.
4. The migration job runs the per-service Flyway sequence against `rwb_payment` only, and the deployment is not marked ready before it succeeds.
5. The worker pool registers task queue `rwb-payment` in namespace `rwb-recovery` with the JOB-07 workflow and the `matchPayments`, `confirmBookings` and `postProceeds` activities under the build ID of the release; no Schedule is registered.
6. The warm-up step asks the registry for the version in force of PAYMENT_MATCH, fetches the model, verifies its checksum and loads it, so the first business date of the morning does not pay the fetch.
7. The read-only smoke step publishes a synthetic `AceDataReady` for a test business date, asserts that the run starts on `rwb-payment`, that a synthetic match writes one record and one `proceeds` row in the test schema, and that one synthetic `RulePackageInForce` swaps the model.
8. The dashboards are published: version in force and its load time, run outcomes, retry and dead-letter depth, outbox lag, workflow failures and rule-cache staleness.
9. The four alerts and the canary gate are wired to the runbook entries; the canary gate holds the promotion until the canary slice is green.
10. The rollback path is rehearsed: a release rollback by chart version, and a rule rollback by the one call in rwb-decision followed by the swap on the event, with no release of this service.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A `RulePackageInForce` event fails the fetch or the checksum | The activity retries on the kit policy; after the last attempt the event goes to the `.retry` topic and then to the `.dlt` with an alert, and the version in force stays loaded | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X2 | No model can be loaded at start-up | Readiness reports the rule cache as not warm; the "rule-cache stale" alert fires after the warm-up window; no match is taken and no default version is substituted | MSG-P3-027 | AC1, AC5 |
| X3 | A topic ACL is missing or too narrow | The consumer or the producer fails to start or to write, the dead-letter depth stays at zero and the run does not appear; the provisioning test fails and the release is blocked | None | AC2 |
| X4 | The worker pool is not polling, or the workflow build ID has no compatible worker | No run starts from `AceDataReady`; the "workflow failures" and "no run started" signals fire; the previous build stays serving | None | AC3, AC5 |
| X5 | The migration job targets another schema or a registry table | The migration test fails on the schema assertion and the release is blocked; the schema of rwb-decision is never touched | None | AC4 |
| X6 | A secret is read from a values file or an environment literal instead of the key store | The pipeline secret scan fails the build and the release is blocked | None | AC5 |
| X7 | The outbox relay falls behind | The outbox-lag alert fires with the age of the oldest unsent event; events are not lost and the relay catches up | None | AC5 |
| X8 | The canary slice is red | The promotion stops and the previous chart version stays in service; a rollback of the release is one command | None | AC6 |
| X9 | A run is stuck on a retry | The workflow-failure alert names the workflow ID and the activity; the run is retried on the kit policy and then left for the runbook entry | MSG-P8-001 | AC3, AC5 |

No alert of this story raises a business message except the ones that carry MSG-P3-027 and MSG-P8-001, whose texts are the app story's.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the platform topic provisioning, the workflow kit, the secret store and the pipeline; builds no business code |
| Negotiable | The alert thresholds, the cache bound, the pool sizes, the resource sizes, the canary percentage and the probe timings are environment values, not story decisions |
| Valuable | Makes the version in force, the runs, the retry paths, the outbox and the secret hygiene visible and operable, and makes a rollback a command rather than a release |
| Estimable | One chart with its values, one provisioning step, one migration job, one worker pool, four alerts, four runbook entries, one canary gate and one rollback |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: a rendered chart, a provisioned topic, a registered queue, a migration result, a secret reference, a synthetic metric and a gate result |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Deployment and operations of the payment matching rules in rwb-payment

  Background:
    Given the service template chart and the platform pipeline are in force
    Given the target environment is SIT
    Given the package code is PAYMENT_MATCH and the version in force is "PM-2026.12" from 2026-12-01

  Scenario: AC1 The rule cache refreshes on RulePackageInForce and falls back to the version in force (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a running rwb-payment pod with version "PM-2026.12" of PAYMENT_MATCH loaded and verified
    When rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1 arrives for a newer version with its checksum
    Then the service fetches the model of that version, verifies the checksum and swaps it in one step, so a run sees either the old or the new version and never a half-loaded one
    When a later event names a version whose model fails its checksum
    Then no swap happens, the version in force stays loaded, the mismatch is counted with the package code, the version label and both checksums
    When the registry answers NoPackageInForce for a business date
    Then the run stops with MSG-P3-027 and no match is taken, and no default version and no empty model is ever substituted
    Then the warm-up list and the cache bound of 20 come from the values files and are never hard-coded

  Scenario: AC2 The topic, its retry and dead-letter topics and the ACLs are provisioned (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the provisioning step for rwb-payment
    When it runs against the environment
    Then rwb.payment.events.v1 exists with its .retry topic and its .dlt topic
    Then the producer ACL permits this service to write the topic, its retry topic and its dead-letter topic, and permits no other service to write them
    Then the consumer groups of AceDataReady, TreatmentApproved, RulePackageInForce, DecisionRecorded, LotAwarded and AssetSold exist with their retry and dead-letter paths
    Then a failed swap or a failed activity reaches the retry topic and then the .dlt topic, and the message is never acknowledged as processed
    Then the consumer dedupes through the inbox, so a repeated event starts no second run and no second swap
    Then the provisioning test fails the release when a topic, a retry path, a dead-letter path or an ACL is missing

  Scenario: AC3 The Temporal worker pool registers the JOB-07 workflow and no Schedule (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the deployment of this release
    When the worker pool starts on namespace rwb-recovery
    Then task queue rwb-payment is registered with the JOB-07 workflow and the matchPayments, confirmBookings and postProceeds activities under the build ID of the release
    Then a synthetic AceDataReady starts one run of the JOB-07 workflow on the queue
    Then the worker pool size and the maximum concurrent activities come from the values files
    Then no Schedule is registered, and the 00:01 rule promote Schedule JOB-20 remains rwb-decision's and is not retimed, duplicated or disabled here
    Then a worker that is not polling is visible as a workflow-failure and no-run signal and does not silently drop the business date

  Scenario: AC4 The migration job touches rwb_payment only (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the migration job of the chart
    When it runs against the environment
    Then it applies the per-service Flyway sequence of this release to schema rwb_payment and to no other schema
    Then it creates or updates proceeds, decision_record, outbox_event, processed_event and idempotency_key, and creates no registry table and no payment_match_rule
    Then the deployment is not marked ready before the migration reports success
    Then the schema assertion test fails the release when the job names another schema, another service's login or a registry table

  Scenario: AC5 Every secret and identity is a reference to the key store (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rendered chart and the running workload
    When the configuration is inspected
    Then the rwb-payment login, the Kafka client credential, the Temporal mTLS material, the registry certificate and the key-store reference are mounted from the platform secret store and appear in no values file, no config map and no image layer
    Then the workload runs under its own identity and holds no other service's credential
    Then the pipeline secret scan fails the build on a secret in code, a values file, a test or a log
    Then a rotation of a secret is picked up without a rebuild of the image

  Scenario: AC6 Four alerts, the canary gate and the rollback are in place (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published alerts, the canary gate and the runbook
    When the four conditions are replayed with synthetic metrics
    Then an outbox lag above its value raises its alert with the age of the oldest unsent event
    Then a dead-letter depth above its value raises its alert with the topic, the consumer group and the event type
    Then a workflow failure or a run that did not start for the business date raises its alert with the workflow ID and the activity
    Then a rule cache that is not warm or is a version behind raises its alert with the package code and the version in force
    Then each alert links exactly one runbook entry with the check, the owner role and the recovery step
    Then the canary gate holds the promotion until the canary slice is green, and a red slice stops it
    Then the release rollback returns the previous chart version and the rule rollback is one call in rwb-decision followed by the swap on the event, with no release of this service
```

The six criteria are new under D-RCV-60 and they test deployment and operations only: no legacy criterion of RWB-E2-027 is restated, no business rule is re-evaluated, and every business assertion they touch — the version in force and the stopped run — is the app story's and is named, not proved, here.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The evaluated copy of PAYMENT_MATCH is refreshed on `RulePackageInForce`: fetch, verify the checksum, swap atomically; on any failure the version in force stays loaded | DP-04; Temporal and Drools slide 15 notes; ADR-017 |
| BR2 | No version in force is a stopped run with MSG-P3-027; no default version, no empty model and no last-known-anything is substituted | legacy BR9; D-RCV-36 T3; R-UNI-41 |
| BR3 | Every topic has a `.retry` topic and a `.dlt` topic, and a consumer never acknowledges an event it could not process | DP-09 as the platform pattern; Arch v5 slide 22 notes; RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| BR4 | The JOB-07 and JOB-08 runs are event-started workflows on task queue `rwb-payment`; this release registers no Schedule and never touches JOB-20 | DP-10; Arch v5 slide 44 |
| BR5 | The migration job writes schema `rwb_payment` only, and creates no registry table and no retired table | DP-01, DP-15; D-RCV-36 T10 |
| BR6 | Readiness answers healthy only when the migration is at the expected schema version, the worker polls, the outbox relay is up and the version in force of PAYMENT_MATCH is loaded and verified | Arch v5 slide 27; Temporal and Drools slide 28 |
| BR7 | Every secret and identity is a reference to the platform secret store; no secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or a runbook | NFR-052; DP-02 |
| BR8 | Every alert carries the package code, the version label, the topic, the consumer group or the workflow ID it needs, and links exactly one runbook entry with the owner role | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR9 | A rule rollback is one call in rwb-decision and the swap back happens on the event; the service is never redeployed to change a rule | Arch v5 slide 27; Temporal and Drools slide 15 |
| BR10 | One image digest and one chart version are promoted through the environments without a rebuild, and the canary gate holds the promotion until its slice is green | Template and Rules §R5.7 rule 6; RWB-PLT-N004-OPS |
| BR11 | Nothing on a dashboard, an alert or a runbook carries a case fact or a personal datum | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR12 | The alert thresholds, the cache-staleness window, the outbox-lag and dead-letter limits, the pool sizes, the canary percentage and the probe timings are values of the chart and never constants of a template or of code | GAP-2508; ASM-4156 |

##### 9. State transitions

The deployment, and not a payment, moves through these states.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart, the tests and the scans pass | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration complete and probes healthy | The schema is at the expected version and both probes answer | Ready |
| Ready | Warm-up complete | The version in force of PAYMENT_MATCH is loaded and verified | Warm |
| Warm | `RulePackageInForce` arrives | The checksum verifies and the swap succeeds | Warm (new version) |
| Warm | Checksum mismatch or fetch failure | The version in force stays and the alert fires | Warm (unchanged; alerting) |
| Warm | Rollback called in rwb-decision | The earlier version is announced and swapped back | Warm (earlier version) |
| Warm | Release superseded | The canary slice is green and the promotion proceeds | Rolling |
| Rolling | All pods on the new version | The old ReplicaSet drains and each pod is Warm | Warm |
| Any | A red canary slice or a failed gate | The promotion stops and the previous chart version stays in service | Previous release in service |

No state of this table is a `proceeds` row state; the row states MATCHED and UNMATCHED are the app story's.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the provisioning step, the migration job, the worker pool, the dashboards, the alerts and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the topic provisioning, the ACLs and the consumer group rights |
| ACE database administrator | Owns the `rwb_payment` schema, the login and its grants, and approves the migration job |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact through the environments and holds the canary gate |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Owns the rule content and the runbook entry for a version not in force |
| RW-RISK, risk and model risk officer | Calls the rollback in rwb-decision, which is one call |
| On-call operator | Runs the runbook entries and opens an incident when an alert persists |
| Identity and access team | Owns the key-store references, the rotation of the secrets and the workload identity |

Separation of duty stays where it is: the person who promotes a release is not the person who approves a rule version, and a rule rollback is RW-RISK's call in rwb-decision. No person is named anywhere; the actors are roles and service identities.

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None provided by this story. The deployment exposes the two operations of the service through gateway-bff, and they are declared in RWB-P8-E2027-CON. The readiness and liveness probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}` | P7 rwb-decision | The model fetch of the warm-up and of the swap, verified by its checksum |

**Pattern application**

The DP rows that change a deployment artefact are DP-04 (the warm-up, the cache bound and the swap), DP-10 (the worker pool and the absence of a Schedule), DP-14 (the topic, its retry and dead-letter topics and their ACLs), DP-15 (the migration job pinned to one schema) and DP-19 (the route the probes and the smoke step do not use). DP-03 and DP-01 fix what the migration job may create. The advisory H rows are not build dependencies of an OPS story and are carried with the app story.

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-payment/` | Chart with deployment, service, migration job, config map, secret references, probes, the worker pool configuration and the rule-cache warm-up hook |
| `helm/rwb-payment/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, feature switches, the rule-cache bound and warm-up list, the pool sizes, the outbox-lag and dead-letter limits, the alert windows and the canary percentage |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit, component and contract tests, image and dependency scan, secret scan, chart publish, canary gate, promote the same artefact |
| Provisioning step | `rwb.payment.events.v1` with its `.retry` and `.dlt` topics and the producer ACL; the six consumer groups; task queue `rwb-payment` in namespace `rwb-recovery` |
| Migration job | The per-service Flyway sequence against `rwb_payment`, with the schema assertion of AC4 |
| Warm-up hook | One version-list read and one model fetch with its checksum, with the timeout from the values |
| Dashboards | Version in force and load time, run outcomes, retry and dead-letter depth, outbox lag, workflow failures, rule-cache staleness |
| Alerts | Four rules, each with its entity, its value and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Four entries: rule-cache refresh and fallback, dead-letter replay, stuck or missing run, release and rule rollback |

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only when the migration is at the expected schema version, the outbox relay is running, the Temporal worker has polled and the version in force of PAYMENT_MATCH is loaded and verified. A registry that answers `NoPackageInForce` is a degraded dependency with its count and does not fail the pod, because a failed pod would hide the business signal. Liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database and neither calls rwb-decision on every check; the warm-up is a start-up step and the refresh is the event.

**Alert mapping.**

| Condition | Alert | Payload | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outbox lag above its value | Outbox lag, with the age of the oldest unsent event and the topic | Topic, age, count | Platform on-call, ticket |
| Dead-letter depth above its value | Dead-letter depth, with the topic, the consumer group and the event type | Topic, consumer group, count, first and last occurrence | Platform on-call, page |
| A workflow failure, or no run started for the business date | Workflow failure, with the workflow ID, the activity and the attempt count | Workflow ID, activity, business date | Platform on-call, page |
| The rule cache is not warm, or is a version behind after its window | Rule-cache stale, with the package code and the version in force | Package code, version in force, loaded version, warm-up duration | Business on-call (RW-COE) and platform on-call, page |

**Rollback runbook.** Two rollbacks, and neither is a code change to a rule. The release rollback returns the previous chart version and keeps the same image digest repository. The rule rollback is one call in rwb-decision (`POST /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/rollback`, owned there); rwb-decision announces the earlier version in force and this service swaps back on the event, so no release is needed and no cache is edited by hand. The cache-purge entry exists only to rebuild the cache from scratch: it empties the cache, the warm-up runs, and the version in force is fetched and verified before readiness reports Warm.

**Canary gate.** The promotion runs a canary slice of the traffic with the previous release still serving; the gate reads the four alert conditions and the run outcome of the canary business date and holds the promotion until the slice is green. The canary percentage and the window are values, not constants (GAP-2508; ASM-4156).

**Done when.** The chart renders in the three environments with every value in its values file, the topic with its retry and dead-letter topics and the ACLs is verified by a test, the six consumer groups exist, the worker pool registers the JOB-07 workflow and no Schedule, the migration job is proven to touch `rwb_payment` only, the secret scan is green and no secret is in a values file, the four panels and the four alerts fire on synthetic metrics, the canary gate blocks a red slice, and the rollback entries are rehearsed by the on-call rota.

| ID | When | Message |

| MSG-P8-001 | A run summary holds unmatched payments and the run is reported on the dashboard | {count} payments for {date} matched no plan and are on the exception list. |

The texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story and the message catalogue; the deployment adds the alert routing and the runbook link, never a new wording. The checksum mismatch, the cache-staleness, the outbox lag and the dead-letter conditions carry identifiers, counts and durations to the alert and produce no business message. Thai text follows DL10.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the match type, the row order, the amount tolerance, the window, the grace and the partial floor are rows of the PAYMENT_MATCH package and rows of the registry. The cache bound, the warm-up list and the alert windows are configuration, not rule content.
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads, workflow history or the runbook: payment codes, case references, package codes, version labels, checksums, counts and durations only.
- One topic and one consumer group set per service; the 00:01 promotion Schedule JOB-20 is never registered, retimed, duplicated or disabled in this release (DP-10, DP-14).
- The service writes only schema `rwb_payment` and the registry is reached only through its two operations; the migration job creates no registry table (DP-01, DP-04, DP-15).
- Every topic has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic and the consumer dedupes through the inbox (DP-09 as the platform pattern; RWB-PLT-TE006-CON).
- The release pins the image digest and the chart version; a rebuild between environments is not allowed and no rule version is ever shipped in the image (BR10).
- No secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; every one is a key-store reference under the workload's own identity (BR7).
- A red canary slice or a red gate blocks the promotion, and no gate is waived for a release (BR10).
- No ACE data is copied into a dashboard, a log or a topic; the freshness signal of the source is P1's (DP-05).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-027 for the wave 2 integration harness. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **a repeatable cross-service journey harness for the PAYMENT_MATCH matching journey, with the fired rule row, the package version, the decision ledger entry and the proceeds outcome of one business date captured as evidence against the wave 2 release**, so that **the matching journey is proven end to end across rwb-payment, rwb-decision, rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-treatment before the app stories of RWB-E2-027 are signed off**.

This is the wave 2 **integration harness** for legacy RWB-E2-027. It builds no production endpoint, no screen, no table and no migration. It exercises the published operations of the five services involved: rwb-payment (P8) for the proceeds and the match, rwb-decision (P7) for the rule-package registry and the central decision ledger, rwb-case (P3) for the case, the account and the plan, through the rule-package authoring story RWB-P3-E2042-APP, rwb-access (P4) for the session and the rights, and rwb-treatment (S2) for the installment shortfall. Contract fakes stand in for each service until its I story lands. The story owns a seed pack, an evidence pack and a pass or fail gate, and nothing else.

The rule package is the unit under test. The harness loads PAYMENT_MATCH version "PM-2026.12", runs the journey against the ALS payment fixture for one business date, and asserts that one rule row, one package version and one ledger entry agree on every match across the five services.

##### 2. Business rationale

RWB-E2-027 splits into five app stories and this integration story. The app stories build the rule-package authoring operation and the registry in rwb-decision, the matching activity and the proceeds in rwb-payment, the session and rights in rwb-access, the case and plan read in rwb-case, and the installment shortfall in rwb-treatment. None of them can prove on its own that **one rule row, one package version and one ledger entry agree across five services on one business date**: rwb-payment fires row "PARTIAL" of version "PM-2026.12", writes decision code "D5" with rule "PARTIAL" and version "PM-2026.12", passes the shortfall to rwb-treatment, and the proceeds entry, the decision entry and the plan shortfall all name the same package version. That proof is this story.

The journey is the one the business cares about. A payment arrives in the ACE payment view for the business date, JOB-07 matches it against the running plan by the rule rows in force, the short and late installments match without a person, and anything that matches no row is on the exception list with a reason (REQ-CHO-009, control CTL-41). The measure is the P8 measure "receipts matched the same day": every match names its rule and its package version, and every unmatched receipt carries a reason. The harness runs that measure on synthetic data, on one business date, and produces evidence that can be re-run for any build.

The architecture changes the path, not the business. The monolith ran one matcher inside one module against one rule table. In the target:

- The rule registry, the rule rows and the rule test cases are owned by rwb-decision (P7), and the evaluator is the embedded Drools kit inside the owning service (DP-04, ADR-017). rwb-payment loads the version on `RulePackageInForce` (JOB-20), verifies the checksum and swaps it in.
- The decision record is written by rwb-payment in its own schema in the same transaction as the state change, then collected into the central ledger in rwb-decision (DP-03, ADR-022), and published on `rwb.decision-record.v1`.
- ACE payment and account data are read through rwb-source-data's contract or through rwb-payment's own ACE views (DP-05); nothing reads another service's tables (DP-01).
- Parameters and reference data come from rwb-case (DP-06, DP-07); the match type, row order, tolerance, window, grace and partial floor stay columns of the rule rows, never code and never a reference table (D-RCV-36 T10).
- JOB-07 is an event-started workflow in rwb-payment, started by `AceDataReady`, with activity `matchPayments` (DP-10, Arch v5 slide 44), not a Quartz job.
- Every call is one hop on the owner's base with a 2 s timeout (DP-11), every path is `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` (DP-13), every topic is `rwb.<short>.events.v1` (DP-14), every service keeps its own Flyway sequence (DP-15), and the screen path runs through gateway-bff (DP-19).

The harness is the place where those boundaries are exercised together, so a broken boundary is found in SIT and not by a payment that silently matches the wrong installment.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The wave 2 harness environment (SIT) is available with the gateway route for `/api/recovery/*`, the Kafka topics of the five services and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and the Temporal namespace `rwb-recovery` with queue `rwb-payment`. The harness environment, its seeding mechanism and its evidence format: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0409; ASM-0584).
- The five integration dependencies have published their contracts, or their contract fakes stand in for them: RWB-P3-E2042-APP (rwb-case, the rule-package authoring operation), RWB-P8-E2027-APP (rwb-payment), RWB-P4-E2027-APP (rwb-access), RWB-S2-E2027-APP (rwb-treatment) and RWB-P7-E2027-APP (rwb-decision).
- PAYMENT_MATCH package version "PM-2026.12" is in force from 2026-12-01 with the EXACT, WINDOW and PARTIAL rows of section 7, loaded through the rwb-decision rule-package operation and approved by RW-RISK (legacy sections 3 and 7 Background).
- Case "RC-2026-000555" has account "A-0555" and running plan "T-0701" with installment amount 12,500.00 THB and next installment date 2026-12-15 (legacy section 7 Background).
- The decision entry of every match carries decision code "D5" and names the rule ID (EXACT, WINDOW or PARTIAL) and the package version in force on the business date (legacy BR6).
- The test user holds RW-CREDITAD or another role with Write-off and posting R; the author of a package version holds RW-COE with Rules and parameters C and the approver holds RW-RISK with Rules and parameters A (legacy section 10).
- Synthetic payments only: no real account, customer or payment data enters the harness or its evidence (legacy section 17).
- No build dependency. Day 1.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: takes the run lock for the environment and records the build ID, the business date and the versions of the five contracts it is about to exercise.
2. Harness: seeds case "RC-2026-000555", account "A-0555", plan "T-0701" with installment amount 12,500.00 THB and next installment date 2026-12-15, and loads PAYMENT_MATCH version "PM-2026.12" through `POST /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/PAYMENT_MATCH/versions`, then confirms it is in force through `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/PAYMENT_MATCH/versions`.
3. Harness: calls the P4 session operation `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` for the test user and records the role, the scope and the Write-off and posting right it will exercise.
4. Harness: calls the P3 case operation `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` and records the case state, the account and the running plan the journey starts from.
5. Harness: loads the ALS payment fixture for the business date — for the exact, partial, late, below-the-floor, overpayment and two-row cases of section 7 — and records the fixture file hash and the payment codes it contains.
6. Harness: opens the JOB-07 window by publishing the `AceDataReady` event for the business date on `rwb.source-data.events.v1` and records the workflow ID of the event-started JOB-07 run it starts in rwb-payment.
7. Harness: reads the proceeds through `GET /api/recovery/payment/v1/proceeds`, matched and unmatched, and records the payment code, the amount, the matched-to value and the treatment ID of each row (AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5, AC8, AC9).
8. Harness: reads the decision log entries through `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` and records the decision code, the rule ID, the package version and the inputs reference of each entry (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC9).
9. Harness: reads the treatment shortfall through `GET /api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}` and records installment amount, due date and installment shortfall (AC2).
10. Harness: asserts the package version on each entry — the version in force on the business date, and the earlier version on an earlier match (AC3) — and marks the scenario failed when any entry names another version or none.
11. Harness: subscribes to `rwb.payment.events.v1` and to `rwb.decision-record.v1` for the run window with its own consumer group and asserts `ProceedsMatched`, `PaymentMissed` and `DecisionRecorded` for the case and the business date.
12. Harness: writes the per-scenario evidence into one run report keyed by story key and business date, evaluates the gate, attaches the report to the wave 2 release record and releases the run lock.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A partial payment below the partial floor | The payment is unmatched, carries MSG-P8-001 in the run summary and appears on the exception list | MSG-P8-001 | AC5 |
| X2 | A late payment outside the window | The payment is unmatched with a decision entry under R-UNI-03 and appears on the exception list | MSG-P8-001 | AC4 |
| X3 | A package version is loaded with two rows of the same row order or a tolerance above 100 | The load is refused in full with status 422 and "PM-2026.12" stays in force; the harness asserts the refusal and never lets the bad version into the run | MSG-P3-027 | TC-E2-027-06-ITG |
| X4 | The decision log write fails for a match | No proceeds row is written, the run summary shows MSG-P7-003, an incident is raised under R-UNI-39 and the next run matches the payment; the scenario passes only when the proceeds read confirms no row | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E2-027-07-ITG |
| X5 | A payment above the installment by more than the tolerance | The payment is unmatched and appears in the unmatched proceeds read | MSG-P8-001 | AC8 |
| X6 | Two rows would match the same payment | The row with the lower row order decides and exactly one decision entry is written | None | AC9 |
| X7 | No PAYMENT_MATCH version is in force on the business date | The run of JOB-07 stops, no payment is matched and no proceeds row is written; the harness records the refusal and fails the gate for that business date | MSG-P3-027 | TC-E2-027-10-ITG |
| X8 | The seed pack cannot be loaded, another run holds the environment lock, or the evidence pack cannot be attached to the release record | The run refuses to start and names the missing seed item or the lock holder, or is marked failed with the local evidence file kept for rerun; no scenario is reported as passed | None | All |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the five published contracts or their fakes, the ALS payment fixture and the JOB-07 window; it builds no service feature and has no build dependency |
| Negotiable | The scenarios, the seeded case, the fixture payments and the expected rule IDs are data files, never code |
| Valuable | The matching journey is proven once across five services, with the rule row and the package version agreeing on every entry |
| Estimable | One journey runner, one fake set, one seed pack, one evidence collector, one gate |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each owned criterion has a scenario with a fixed Given, When and Then and a recorded result |

AC6, AC7 and AC10 are owned by the app stories of this legacy key and are cited only through their test cases, TC-E2-027-06-ITG, TC-E2-027-07-ITG and TC-E2-027-10-ITG.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Rows are tried in row order and the first row that matches decides (first match) | D-RCV-36 T5; ADR-012 |
| BR2 | EXACT: plan account, amount within the tolerance, date inside the window before the due date | R-RES-26 |
| BR3 | WINDOW: as EXACT, with the window extended after the due date; a late match is a late payment for the plan | R-RES-28 |
| BR4 | PARTIAL: amount at or above the partial floor and below the installment; the shortfall is held on the plan | R-SET-15 pattern; REQ-CHO-009 |
| BR5 | A payment no row matches is held on the exception list | R-UNI-03; CTL-41 |
| BR6 | Each match decision is written to the decision log with the rule ID (EXACT, WINDOW or PARTIAL) and the package version in force on the business date; earlier matches keep their version | R-UNI-38; Principle 5; D-RCV-36 T5, T7 |
| BR7 | A package version with any invalid row is refused in full by the version-load check | Reference data change process, step 3; CTL-08 |
| BR8 | A match that cannot be written to the decision log is not made | Principle 5; R-UNI-39 |
| BR9 | No PAYMENT_MATCH version in force is a refusal (NoPackageInForce), never a default match | D-RCV-36 T3; R-UNI-41 |
| BR10 | The tolerance, window, grace and partial floor are condition and output columns of the PAYMENT_MATCH rows, not code and not a reference table | D-RCV-36 T10; REQ-CHO-009 |

The rules are unchanged by the split. The harness asserts them across the service boundaries and never restates a threshold in its own code; every threshold is read from the row the package fired.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case. This story does not change a case status. rwb-case changes the plan route state on the results, and the harness observes it:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| PLAN_RUNNING | PAYMENT_RECEIVED | payment matched to the installment | PLAN_RUNNING (R-RES-26) |
| PLAN_CURE_PERIOD | PAYMENT_RECEIVED_LATE | payment received inside the cure period | PLAN_RUNNING (R-RES-28) |

The package version moves LOADED to APPROVED to IN_FORCE, or to REFUSED, through the rwb-decision rule-package operations; the harness drives the first three and asserts REFUSED for the invalid version of X3.

The harness adds a run state of its own only: Not started, Seeding, Running, Passed, Failed, with the latest run for a build deciding the gate.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CREDITAD, Credit Administration officer | Reads the matched and unmatched receipts and the exception list in the evidence (Write-off and posting CRUA); owns the matching values |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Authors the PARTIAL and WINDOW rows and loads the package version the harness seeds (Rules and parameters C) |
| RW-RISK | Approves the seeded package version (Rules and parameters A) |
| RW-FINANCE, Finance and CFO delegate | Reads the matches in the evidence (Write-off and posting RA) |
| SY-RULES, Drools evaluator | Supplies the fired rule ID and the package version through the rwb-payment contract |
| SY-DECLOG, decision log writer | Supplies the D5 entries the harness asserts, through rwb-decision's contract only |
| SY-AGENT, agent platform | Reads the exception list as the reconciliation agent would, not exercised here |
| RW-TRIBE, squad members and the QA team | Run the harness, keep the fake mappings, the seed pack and the evidence, read reports |
| Integration lead | Agrees the ALS payment fixture, the JOB-07 window control and the contract versions with the five service teams |
| QA lead | Owns the seed pack, the evidence format and the pass or fail gate |
| No approval level from the delegation of authority applies | The story takes no business decision |

Separation of duty: the analyst who loads a version does not approve it; RW-RISK approves and the author cannot. The harness seeds both steps with two distinct test users and never with one.
