**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-032 for rwb-agent. The suggestion stays with the service that owns the agent rows and the model gateway: the in-process `ModelSuggestionClient.suggestOffer` becomes one published operation under `/api/recovery/agent/v1` (DP-11, DP-13), the run and the policy are rows of `rwb_agent` (DP-01), the decision log write becomes the local decision-record library plus the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03), the account, the arrears and the payments come through rwb-source-data's contract instead of the `recovery` tables (DP-05), the parameters and the lists come through the rwb-case contracts (DP-06, DP-07), the run completion is published as EV-28 through the outbox (DP-09), and the admin reads and SCR-14 are reached through the gateway-bff route (DP-19). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **restructuring officer (RW-RESTRUCT)**, I want **the TDR team's offer-suggestion model called through the model gateway by the agent service so the treatment record carries its suggestion when the model exists**, so that **one gateway serves every model the Workbench uses, every suggestion is recorded with its model version, and the officer still decides the offer in every case**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story RWB-E2-032 gave the restructuring officer one suggestion on the treatment record: the TDR team's offer-suggestion model is reached through the model gateway, its answer appears on SCR-14 with the model code and version, and one decision log entry and one agent run row hold what was suggested next to what was offered (FEAT-AGT-10; FSD P10 v3 A2.10; REQ-CHO-006, REQ-DRI-001). If the model is not in service the gateway returns no suggestion and the officer works as today, so the capability ships with the policy in mode OFF.

In the target the model, its policy and its run belong to rwb-agent. Arch v5 slide 41 gives the service the agent policies, the prompts, the runs, the guardrails and the evaluations in schema `rwb_agent`, and slide 16 gives it the Temporal workflow `AgentRunWorkflow` with a 60-second budget and then the rule result, the topic `rwb.agent.events.v1` with `AgentRunCompleted`, and the Enterprise AI private endpoint (INT-23) as its only outside call. That shape decides the story. The suggestion is no longer a Java interface inside the monolith: it is one REST operation of rwb-agent on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`, called by the treatment service with one hop and a client budget (DP-11, DP-13), so the treatment service can be built, released and tested without the agent service.

The facts the model reads are not this service's either. The account balance, the total balance, the days past due, the interest rate and the payments of the last 12 months are ACE data, read through rwb-source-data's contract and never from a `recovery` table or a `v_ace_*` view of this schema (DP-05; ADR-010). The treatment, its case and its type belong to rwb-treatment, and the case facts to rwb-case. The parameters and the list values — the reference data of LOV-AGENT, LOV-AUTONOMY and LOV-AGENT-RUN — are read through the rwb-case contracts (DP-06, DP-07). What stays inside the service is the whole of the run: the policy version in force, the mode, the timeout, the schema reference, the guardrail, the run row and the suggestion itself.

Two writes complete the target shape. The decision log entry becomes a local decision record written by the library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the same transaction as the run row, relayed from the outbox as `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` to the central ledger of rwb-decision (DP-03; ADR-022). The run completion becomes EV-28 `AgentRunCompleted` on `rwb.agent.events.v1` as a CloudEvents 1.0 message with no personal data (DP-09; Arch v5 slide 43). Both leave through the outbox, so a suggestion is never returned for a run that was not published and a record is never announced for a run that was not committed.

This story owns all eight legacy criteria of RWB-E2-032 — AC1 to AC8 — and copies them word for word in section 7, each with the origin tag of its legacy criterion. AC9 to AC15 are new and test only the microservice change of the title: the operation on the agent base, the run and the policy in `rwb_agent`, the record on the shared topic, EV-28 through the outbox, the facts through the owner contracts, the parameters and the lists, and the two waits of the call. The legacy story carries the requirement IDs REQ-CHO-006 and REQ-DRI-001, and section 18 traces both.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P10-E1058-APP is done: the agent runtime exists in `rwb_agent` with `agent_policy`, `agent_prompt`, `agent_run`, `agent_sample`, `agent_evaluation_run`, `agent_evaluation`, `agent_feedback` and `agent_alert`, and the two admin reads of TSD P10 v2 T-A answer (TSD P10 v2 T3.1; RWB-P10-E1058-APP owns the schema and the baseline migration).
- RWB-P10-E2032-CON is published: the shape of the suggestion operation, the decision-record mapping, the EV-28 payload and the fakes of section 12.8. This story builds against it and never restates it.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the local decision-record library, the record shape and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` with its CloudEvents 1.0 envelope (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is published: the outbox and retry library, the relay from the outbox to the topic and the inbox dedupe (DP-09).
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-PLT-E1043-CON are published with their client libraries: the parameter contract and the reference-data contract of rwb-case (DP-06, DP-07), consumed against RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON.
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route contract and its stub for the admin reads and SCR-14 (DP-19).
- The treatment read is available against its fake: RWB-P3-E2004-CON is the contract baseline for the treatment entity in the plan, and the runtime treatment and its type belong to rwb-treatment (S2) per Arch v5 slide 41. Which of the two answers the read at run time is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0633; ASM-0979).
- A policy row exists for agent "TDR_OFFER". Until the TDR team deploys the model it has mode "OFF" and review date 2027-02-28 (assumed; DL33). When deployed, a new version with mode "L1", the model code and version, the output schema "tdr-offer-v1" and timeout 60 seconds is loaded by RW-COE and approved by RW-RISK.
- The lists of TSD P10 v2 T3.2 are in force as reference data of rwb-case: LOV-AGENT (INTAKE, SCREENING, LEGAL_DOC, EXTRACT, TDR_OFFER), LOV-AUTONOMY (OFF, SHADOW, L1) and LOV-AGENT-RUN (ANSWERED, TIMED_OUT, GUARDRAIL_FAILED, BELOW_FLOOR, TOOL_UNAVAILABLE, MODEL_ERROR, DISABLED). The service holds no copy of a list in code (DP-07).
- The account, the arrears and the payments are reachable through rwb-source-data's contract: `principal_outstanding`, `total_balance`, `days_past_due`, `interest_rate`, `payment_date` and `payment_amount` (DF-ACC-009, DF-ACE-020, DF-ACE-018, DF-ACE-025, DF-ACE-045, DF-ACE-046). The operation and the product path are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0633; ASM-0980).
- The private endpoint of Enterprise AI (INT-23) is reachable from the pods over HTTPS: host, port and certificate are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0633; ASM-0988) and are provisioned by RWB-P10-E2032-INF.
- The login is the rwb-agent login (DP-02) on schema `rwb_agent`; its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0633; ASM-0976).
- This story is in lane L-P10-A and starts after RWB-P10-E1058-APP, the in-lane story it waits for (§R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The treatment service asks rwb-agent for a suggestion for a treatment. The request is one hop on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`, with the case ID and the treatment ID in the body and the idempotency key `TDR_OFFER:<treatmentId>` (DP-11, DP-13; legacy section 12).
2. SuggestionController validates the request and reads the treatment through the rwb-treatment contract: its type, its case and its state. A treatment whose type is not "RESTRUCTURE" ends here with no call and no suggestion (BR6; AC8).
3. TdrSuggestionService reads the policy version of agent "TDR_OFFER" in force for the business date from `agent_policy` in `rwb_agent`: `policy_version`, `model_code`, `model_version`, `output_schema_ref`, `autonomy_mode`, `timeout_seconds`, `confidence_floor` and `review_date`. A version whose `autonomy_mode` is "OFF" returns no suggestion and makes no call, and no run row and no record are written (AC2).
4. The step looks up the idempotency key on `agent_run`. A run already exists for the key: its stored suggestion and its `decision_log_id` are returned and no second model call is made (R-UNI-40; AC7).
5. TdrInputAssembler builds the masked inputs. The account facts and the 12 months of payments come through the rwb-source-data contract with one hop and a 2 s client budget; the case facts come through rwb-case; the customer name, the account number and every personal field are masked before the model call, and the masked snapshot is kept as the inputs reference (DP-05; AC12).
6. ModelGatewayClient calls the Enterprise AI private endpoint (INT-23) with the model code, the masked inputs and the output schema "tdr-offer-v1", bounded by `timeout_seconds` of the policy version in force — 60 seconds for the versions of this story (NFR-010; BR1).
7. GuardrailChecker tests the answer against "tdr-offer-v1": installments 1 to 360, monthly amount above 0, interest rate 0 to 30, confidence. An answer outside the schema ends the run in status "GUARDRAIL_FAILED" with check "SCHEMA" and no suggestion (AC5).
8. RecordAndApply runs in one `rwb_agent` transaction: it writes the `agent_run` row with the agent code, the policy and model versions, the autonomy mode, the case and subject, the idempotency key, the status, the fallback flag, the guardrail result, the output, the confidence, the latency, the cost and `run_at`; it writes the local decision record with decision "D5" and final call "SUGGESTION_RECORDED" and stores its reference in `agent_run.decision_log_id`; and it inserts the outbox rows of the two events. A failed record write rolls the whole transaction back (DP-03; R-UNI-39; AC6).
9. The outbox relay publishes `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28) on `rwb.agent.events.v1`, both as CloudEvents 1.0 messages keyed by the case ID, with no personal data (DP-09; AC11). rwb-decision seals the record into the central ledger; the run completion is read by rwb-decision, rwb-document and rwb-deviation (Arch v5 slide 43).
10. The operation answers with the eight members of the legacy `OfferSuggestion` record: `agentRunId`, `decisionLogEntryId`, `modelCode`, `modelVersion`, `installments`, `monthlyAmountThb`, `interestRate` and `confidence` (legacy section 12; AC9).
11. The restructuring officer sees the suggestion on SCR-14 with the model code and the model version, or MSG-P10-007 when there is none. The panel is served by the gateway-bff composite route, which calls the agent read and merges the answer, and the browser calls no service directly (DP-19; AC14).
12. A rerun for the same treatment hits the idempotency key, returns the stored answer and writes nothing: no second run row, no second record, no second event, and the hit is counted once (R-UNI-40).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The model is not in service (mode OFF) | No call, no run row and no decision record; the treatment shows the message | MSG-P10-007 | AC2 |
| X2 | The model does not answer within 60 seconds | The call is ended at the policy timeout; the run holds status "TIMED_OUT" with fallback true; no suggestion and no record; the treatment continues (R-UNI-32) | MSG-P10-007 | AC4, AC15 |
| X3 | The answer fails the output schema "tdr-offer-v1" | The run holds status "GUARDRAIL_FAILED" with check "SCHEMA"; no suggestion and no record | MSG-P10-007 | AC5 |
| X4 | The decision record cannot be written | The transaction rolls back; no suggestion is returned and the caller receives the refusal; the run row is not kept with a decision link (R-UNI-39) | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X5 | The same treatment asks again | The first suggestion and its decision record reference return from the run row; no second model call, no second record and no second event | None to a user | AC7, AC12 |
| X6 | The treatment type is not "RESTRUCTURE" | No call and no suggestion; nothing is written | None to a user | AC8 |
| X7 | A role without the right reads the agent runs | Refused; nothing is returned and nothing is written | MSG-P4-002 | AC14 |
| X8 | The rwb-source-data contract answers an error or facts older than the business date | No suggestion and no record; the run is kept with the reason of the read and the freshness of the facts; no value is defaulted | MSG-P10-007 | AC12 |
| X9 | The model gateway answers a 4xx or a 5xx | The run holds status "MODEL_ERROR" with fallback true; no suggestion and no record; the caller receives MSG-P10-007 | MSG-P10-007 | AC15 |
| X10 | The outbox relay is down after a committed transaction | The run row and the record stay committed and the outbox rows are relayed when the sender succeeds; no event is lost and no event is published twice (R-UNI-33, R-UNI-35) | None to a user | AC11 |
| X11 | The reference value of the mode or of a run status is outside its list | The value is refused as a configuration error, the run is not written with an invented value and the version is named | None to a user | AC13 |

X1 to X6 are the legacy exception paths of RWB-E2-032 carried onto the service; X7 is the legacy access path of TC-E2-032-09; X8 to X11 are the failures that appear when the call, the facts and the record cross a boundary. X4 keeps the legacy wording: the caller receives `DecisionNotRecordedException` and MSG-P7-003, so the treatment service needs no change.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds after RWB-P10-E1058-APP in lane L-P10-A against the published contracts RWB-P10-E2032-CON, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON and the fakes of section 12.8; the four C dependencies are built against their fakes and block nothing (§R5.4) |
| Negotiable | The request and answer field names, the record mapping, the event payload and the route are agreed in RWB-P10-E2032-CON; the policy values, the schema limits and the review date are data |
| Valuable | Puts a recorded, versioned suggestion on the treatment record through one gateway and one service, with no second integration path and no AI outside rwb-agent |
| Estimable | One operation, one service, one input assembler, one gateway client, one guardrail, one run writer, one record writer and one publisher |
| Small | Under two weeks with one developer and its tests; the legacy estimate was under one week for the in-process interface |
| Testable | Each of the fifteen criteria of section 7 is one automated test on an observable: a REST answer, a stored row, a record field, an outbox row, a topic message, a masked input or a gate |

**Target reading.** The policy "TDR_OFFER", its versions "P1" and "P2", the modes "OFF" and "L1", the model version "TDR-OFFER-1.0", the output schema "tdr-offer-v1", the 84 installments of 18,900.00 baht, the review date 2027-02-28, the 60 seconds, the 61 seconds of silence, installments -12, treatment "T-1001" on case "RW-2026-001001", treatment "T-1002" of type "SETTLEMENT", decision "D5", final call "SUGGESTION_RECORDED", check "SCHEMA", and the messages MSG-P10-007, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P4-002 are the legacy values of RWB-E2-032, copied character for character, and so are the two Background lines. The scenario lines of AC1 to AC8 keep their legacy titles and every legacy Given, When and Then, and each carries the origin tag of its legacy criterion. Four of the eight carry one inserted line as their first Given, because the legacy criterion asserts a cross-service read or write that can be mocked. AC1 and AC7 insert `Given the rwb-source-data contract mock ...` and `Given the rwb-treatment contract mock ...`: the model call reads the account facts and the payments through rwb-source-data (DP-05) and the type gate reads the treatment through rwb-treatment. AC3 inserts `Given the rwb-decision contract mock ...` because the entry it reads is the record sealed by rwb-decision from the shared topic (DP-03). AC8 inserts `Given the rwb-treatment contract mock ...` because `treatment.treatment_type` is a rwb-treatment field in the target, and the legacy read of the treatment row is a call to its owner. AC2, AC4, AC5 and AC6 need none: AC2 and AC6 assert that no call and no record exist, AC4 asserts a run status after a silent stub, and AC5 asserts a schema refusal on an answer the stub already returned, so none of the four reads or writes another service. The in-process `ModelSuggestionClient.suggestOffer` and its `OfferSuggestion` record become one operation under `/api/recovery/agent/v1` (DP-11, DP-13) whose path below the base is fixed in RWB-P10-E2032-CON and is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0633; ASM-0977). The run, the policy and the guardrail are rows and code of `rwb_agent` (DP-01). The decision log write becomes the local decision-record library plus `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03) and the run completion becomes EV-28 through the outbox (DP-09). The account, the arrears and the payments come through rwb-source-data's contract and no `v_ace_*` view is granted to this login (DP-05; ADR-010; ASM-0980). The parameters and the lists come through the rwb-case contracts (DP-06, DP-07; ASM-0981). The admin reads and SCR-14 come through the gateway-bff route (DP-19; ASM-0982). The suggestion call keeps the legacy synchronous answer and therefore carries the policy timeout of 60 seconds, while DP-11's 2 s client budget applies to every other hop; the exception is recorded as ASM-0978 because no source reconciles the two waits.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The TDR model is reached only through the model gateway on the Enterprise AI private endpoint (INT-23), with the model code, the masked inputs and the output schema "tdr-offer-v1", and never by code inside the service | Legacy BR1; DL33; TSD P10 v2 T5.1; Arch v5 slide 16 |
| BR2 | Mode "OFF" returns no suggestion, makes no call and writes no run row and no record; the review date is held on the policy row | Legacy BR2; `agent_policy.autonomy_mode`, `review_date` (DF-AGT-008, DF-AGT-016) |
| BR3 | A suggestion is returned only after its decision record is written, in the same transaction as the run row | Legacy BR3; Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06; DP-03 |
| BR4 | A timeout, a model error or a failed schema check gives no suggestion, records the fallback and lets the treatment continue | Legacy BR4; R-UNI-32; TSD P10 v2 NFR-010 |
| BR5 | One suggestion per treatment; the key is "TDR_OFFER:<treatmentId>" and a repeat returns the stored answer with no second call | Legacy BR5; R-UNI-40; DF-AGT-045 |
| BR6 | The model is called only for treatment type "RESTRUCTURE", read from the treatment's owner | Legacy BR6; `treatment.treatment_type` (DF-TRT-004) |
| BR7 | The suggestion is advice: the officer builds and submits the offer and no suggestion is written into an offer field or a treatment status | Legacy BR7; Agent catalog; R-RES-09, R-RES-10 |
| BR8 | No value a business person may change is written in code: the model code and version, the output schema, the timeout, the confidence floor, the mode and the review date are rows of the `agent_policy` version in force | BR-P10-010; FSD P10 v3 A2.10.3.1 |
| BR9 | The run writes only `rwb_agent` tables and the shared outbox; the account, the payments, the treatment and the case are read through their owners' contracts | DP-01; DP-05; ADR-010 |
| BR10 | Every event carries IDs and facts only; the masked inputs snapshot is stored as the record's inputs reference and no account number, customer name or personal field reaches a topic, a log or a workflow payload | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; Arch v5 slides 42 and 43 |
| BR11 | The lists of TSD P10 v2 T3.2 are reference data of rwb-case and no copy of a list sits in code | DP-07; TSD P10 v2 T3.2 |
| BR12 | An operation of this service answers on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`, and no path of another service is declared as its own | DP-13; Arch v5 slide 41 |
| BR13 | A run completion is published once, from the outbox, after the transaction commits, and a repeat of the relay publishes nothing | DP-09; R-UNI-33; R-UNI-40 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| REQUESTED | MODE_OFF | the policy version in force has `autonomy_mode` "OFF" | NO_SUGGESTION, with no run row |
| REQUESTED | KEY_FOUND | a run exists for "TDR_OFFER:<treatmentId>" | ANSWERED, with the stored answer returned and no second call |
| REQUESTED | CALL_ANSWERED | the model answered inside the policy timeout and the answer meets "tdr-offer-v1" | ANSWERED |
| REQUESTED | CALL_SILENT | the call reached the policy timeout | TIMED_OUT, with fallback true |
| REQUESTED | MODEL_REFUSED | the gateway answered a 4xx or a 5xx | MODEL_ERROR, with fallback true |
| CALL_ANSWERED | SCHEMA_REFUSED | the answer fails the output schema | GUARDRAIL_FAILED, with check "SCHEMA" |
| ANSWERED | RECORD_COMMITTED | the run row, the record and the outbox rows commit in one transaction | ANSWERED, with `decision_log_id` set |
| ANSWERED | RECORD_FAILED | the decision record cannot be written | ROLLED_BACK, with no run row and no record |
| ANSWERED | RELAYED | the outbox relay publishes EV-28 and the record | ANSWERED, with the two events published once |

These are the states of one attempt of the suggestion and of its run row, not a case state machine. The statuses ANSWERED, TIMED_OUT, GUARDRAIL_FAILED, BELOW_FLOOR, TOOL_UNAVAILABLE, MODEL_ERROR and DISABLED are the values of LOV-AGENT-RUN (TSD P10 v2 T3.2), and REQUESTED, NO_SUGGESTION, ROLLED_BACK and RELAYED are steps of the operation and are not written into `agent_run.status`. **This story moves no case status and no treatment status**: `recovery_case` belongs to rwb-case, the treatment belongs to rwb-treatment, and the suggestion area of SCR-14 is read-only (BR7).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-RESTRUCT | Reads the suggestion on SCR-14 (Treatment and offer R) |
| RW-CASEOWN | Reads the suggestion on SCR-14 (Treatment and offer R) |
| SY-CASEWF | Calls the suggestion operation from the treatment service over one hop |
| SY-AGENT | Reads the account, the payments and the case facts through their owners' contracts (Case record R, Treatment and offer R) |
| SY-DECLOG | Writes the local decision record and its outbox row (Decision log C) |
| RW-COE, RW-RISK | Load and approve the "TDR_OFFER" policy version (Rules and parameters C and A) |
| RW-PLATADM | Reads the agent runs of "TDR_OFFER" through the admin read (Platform administration R) |
| rwb-agent service identity | Runs the operation, writes `agent_run` and the outbox in `rwb_agent`, and calls the model gateway |

The legacy authority table is copied with its role codes. The per-service login of the service identity is the rwb-agent login (DP-02) and its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0633; ASM-0976). The migration of `SY-CASEWF` from an in-process interface to a REST caller changes no right in the matrix; the right under which the treatment service calls the operation is the service identity's right on the agent contract and is agreed with rwb-access.

| BR Field ID | Entity in rwb_agent | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-TRT-001, DF-TRT-002, DF-TRT-004 | treatment (rwb-treatment, owner S2) | id, case_id, treatment_type | Read, through the rwb-treatment contract |
| DF-ACC-009, DF-ACE-018, DF-ACE-020, DF-ACE-025 | v_ace_account (owner P1) | principal_outstanding, days_past_due, total_balance, interest_rate | Read, through rwb-source-data's contract (DP-05) |
| DF-ACE-045, DF-ACE-046 | v_ace_payment (owner P1) | payment_date, payment_amount | Read, through rwb-source-data's contract (DP-05) |
| DF-AGT-001 to DF-AGT-025 | agent_policy | policy_version, model_code, model_version, output_schema_ref, autonomy_mode, confidence_floor, timeout_seconds, review_date, valid_from, valid_to, status | Read |
| DF-AGT-026 to DF-AGT-035 | agent_prompt | prompt_version, body_hash | Read, where a prompt version is named on the run |
| DF-AGT-036 to DF-AGT-060 | agent_run | id, agent_code, agent_version, prompt_version, model_version, case_id, subject_id, autonomy_mode, trigger_event, idempotency_key, status, fallback, guardrail_result, output, confidence, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_thb, data_as_of, run_at, decision_log_id | Write |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (local library) and decision_log_entry (rwb_decision, owner P7) | all fields, written through the decision-record library and sealed by rwb-decision | Write locally |

Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. The run is the only row this story writes, and it is in `rwb_agent` (DP-01). The record is written by the library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and never into `rwb_decision` directly (DP-03). The account, the payment and the treatment facts are read through their owners' contracts and no copy is kept: the masked inputs snapshot travels inside the record as its inputs reference and holds no account number and no customer name (ASM-0983). The values of `agent_version` and `prompt_version` for agent "TDR_OFFER" are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0633; ASM-0983); the legacy decision-log mapping fixes `agent_version` null and no prompt version applies to a model called directly through the gateway.

The two admin reads this story uses — `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-runs` and `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs` — are provided by rwb-agent and baselined in RWB-P10-E1058-CON; this story reads them and declares no shape of its own (DP-13). Every path is on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1` and none is served on the legacy monolith base.

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0633; ASM-0980) | rwb-source-data (P1) | The account facts and the 12 months of payments, masked before the model call (DP-05) | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0633; ASM-0979) | rwb-treatment (S2) | The treatment, its case and its type (DF-TRT-001, DF-TRT-002, DF-TRT-004) | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0633; ASM-0979) | rwb-case (P3) | The case facts the run names, and the parameter and reference-data values in force (DP-06, DP-07) | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0633; ASM-0981) | rwb-decision (P7) | The sealed decision record of a suggestion, read back for AC3 (DP-03) | One hop, 2 s |

Every operation is one hop with a 2 s client budget (DP-11, ADR-020). The call to the Enterprise AI private endpoint is not a REST operation between services: it is the external call of 12.9.

| `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28) | `rwb.agent.events.v1` | P10 | the case ID | run ID, agent_code, agent_version, model_version, case ID, outcome, fallback, run_at |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 owns the type and the central ledger; every service writes its own record | the record reference | record reference, decision "D5", model version, agent version null, final call "SUGGESTION_RECORDED", the suggested terms, the actions `{treatmentId, agentRunId}` |

Both rows are inserted in the outbox in the same transaction as the run row and relayed with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope (DP-09; DP-03). No personal data is carried (BR10).

None. The suggestion is asked over REST and the story reads no topic; the inbox of the outbox library is used only for the relay's own dedupe.

The workflow name, the queue and the 60-second budget are those of Arch v5 slide 16; the activity names are this story's and are agreed in RWB-P10-E2032-CON.

None. The suggestion is request-driven and no Temporal Schedule is created, changed or owned by this story; the Arch v5 job map names no job for an agent suggestion (slide 44).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.agent`, module `tdr`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.agent.tdr`; the operation, its request and answer records in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.agent.tdr.api`. Front end: the suggestion area of SCR-14, read through the gateway-bff route.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; C RWB-P7-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none; C from the legacy dependency |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-11 resolves to the operation of 12.1 and to the four consumed reads, each one hop with a 2 s client budget; the suggestion call itself carries the policy timeout of 60 seconds, which is the recorded exception of ASM-0978. DP-05 resolves to the rwb-source-data contract and to no view of this service: no `v_ace_*` view is granted to the rwb-agent login (ADR-010). The treatment read is the C dependency RWB-P3-E2004-CON (the treatment entity contract baseline) against the runtime owner rwb-treatment (ASM-0979).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| SuggestionController | REST controller | Validates the request, declares the operation, maps errors to the problem response and answers with the eight members |
| TdrSuggestionService | Service | Mode check, idempotency, the gateway call, the guardrail, the record and the run |
| TdrInputAssembler | Service | Reads the account, the payment, the treatment and the case facts through their contracts and masks the personal fields |
| ModelGatewayClient | Client | Calls INT-23 with the model code, the masked inputs and "tdr-offer-v1", with the policy timeout and a breaker |
| GuardrailChecker | Service | Tests the answer against the output schema: installments 1 to 360, monthly amount above 0, interest rate 0 to 30, confidence |
| RunWriter | Repository | Reads `agent_policy` and `agent_prompt`, and writes and looks up `agent_run` in `rwb_agent` |
| DecisionRecordWriter | Library adapter | Writes the local decision record with decision "D5" in the same transaction (DP-03) |
| RunCompletedPublisher | Outbox adapter | Inserts the EV-28 row and the record row, and reads the relay result (DP-09) |
| TreatmentSuggestionPanel | React component | The suggestion area of SCR-14, fed by the gateway-bff route, with the suggestion or MSG-P10-007 |

**Database and migrations.** No new table and no new column in this story: `agent_run`, `agent_policy` and `agent_prompt` come from the agent runtime baseline migration of `rwb_agent` that RWB-P10-E1058-APP owns (TSD P10 v2 T3.1; ASM-0984). If the baseline does not carry a column this story needs, the script that adds it takes its number from the rwb-agent Flyway sequence; that number is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0633; ASM-0984). One index serves the idempotency lookup and the admin read: `agent_run (idempotency_key)` and `agent_run (agent_code, run_at)`. Index names are naming-library values and not business values.

**Configuration and reference data**

- Policy versions (RW-COE): `agent_code` "TDR_OFFER", `policy_version`, `model_code`, `model_version`, `output_schema_ref` "tdr-offer-v1", `autonomy_mode`, `timeout_seconds` 60, `confidence_floor`, `review_date` and the segment fields. The P1 version has mode "OFF" and review date 2027-02-28; the P2 version is loaded when the TDR team deploys the model.
- The lists LOV-AGENT, LOV-AUTONOMY and LOV-AGENT-RUN are reference data of rwb-case, read through the reference-data contract; the service holds no copy (DP-07; ASM-0981).
- The parameter values this story reads — the feature value that switches the suggestion and the read preferences of the clients — are rows of the rwb-case parameter contract (DP-06). Which keys the service reads is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0633; ASM-0981).
- The feature flag `rwb.agent.tdr-suggestion` is a data row of the platform feature-flag library (§R3 default ruling); off, the operation answers no suggestion with no call, as the legacy section 13 requires.

**Build steps**

1. Write the operation and its request and answer records from RWB-P10-E2032-CON, with the 2 s budget, the problem response and the idempotency key; tests for AC9.
2. Build the mode-off and the type-gate paths against the rwb-treatment fake, with no call and no write; tests for AC2 and AC8.
3. Build TdrInputAssembler against the rwb-source-data and rwb-case fakes, with the masking and the freshness rule; tests for AC1, AC12 and AC13.
4. Add the model gateway client, the schema check and the timeout and error paths against the model stub; tests for AC4, AC5 and AC15.
5. Add the record write before the answer and the run row in one transaction, with the rollback path; tests for AC6 and AC10.
6. Add the idempotent repeat: the key lookup, the stored answer and the counted hit; test for AC7.
7. Add the outbox rows and the relay, and the registry check before the relay; test for AC11.
8. Build the suggestion area of SCR-14 against the gateway-bff route stub, with the refusal path; test for AC14, and keep AC3 green through the rwb-decision fake.
9. Run the boundary scan and the two admin reads against the baseline of RWB-P10-E1058-APP; test for AC10 and AC14.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass with mode "OFF" in SIT; AC1 and AC15 pass against the model stub until the TDR model is deployed; no suggestion is returned without its record; every event is published once from the outbox; and the pipeline finds no read of another service's table and no list, threshold or schema limit in code.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P10-007 | No suggestion: the model is not in service, the call timed out, the gateway answered an error or the schema check failed | No offer suggestion is available for this treatment. The TDR model is not in service. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Platform administration reads the agent runs | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The three messages are the legacy messages of RWB-E2-032 and keep their wording character for character. MSG-GEN-001 (a required value is empty) and MSG-P10-001 (a configuration file fails a check) belong to the agent platform story and are not restated here. No message ID is added by this story.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-14 Treatment record (states draft, submitted, approved, booked, broken) keeps the suggestion area in the draft state that the legacy story describes: the suggestion shown with its terms, model code and version, or not available with MSG-P10-007. The officer edits the offer fields as before and the suggestion is never copied into them. What changes is the path: the panel is served by the gateway-bff composite route, which calls the agent read on `/api/recovery/agent/v1` and merges the answer with the other services the screen needs, so the browser calls no service directly (DP-19). The route name and path, and the field order and masking of the panel, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0633; ASM-0982) and are agreed with the route contract RWB-PLT-N001-CON.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the model code, the model version, the output schema, its limits, the timeout, the confidence floor, the mode and the review date are rows of the policy version in force (BR8; BR-P10-010).
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow payloads, prompts or events: the inputs are masked before the model call, the account number and the customer name never reach a topic or a log, and the workflow payloads pass the payload codec (BR10).
- No read of another service's tables: the account and the payments come through rwb-source-data's contract, the treatment through rwb-treatment, the case and the parameters through rwb-case, and the record is written through the P7 library; `rwb_agent` holds no foreign key into another schema (DP-01, DP-05).
- One base and one topic per service: the operation answers on `/api/recovery/agent/v1` and the events leave on `rwb.agent.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`; no other service's path or topic is declared (DP-13, DP-14).
- The suggestion is written to no offer field, no treatment status and no case status; it is advice on the run and on the record (BR7).
- A suggestion is returned only after its record is committed, and both events are published only from the outbox (BR3, BR13).
- No value is defaulted for a fact the owner contract did not return, and no run status outside LOV-AGENT-RUN is written (BR11; X11).
- Every fixture is synthetic; no production account, payment, model answer or record is copied into a fake or a test.

##### 19. Out of scope

- Building or training the TDR model, which is the TDR team's and outside the Workbench (legacy section 19).
- The settlement and restructure agent proposing plan terms, shadow from Epic 2 and live from Epic 3 per the agent catalog.
- Affordability and plan calculation (ACE restructure calculator, R-RES-06).
- The agent runtime baseline, the policy and prompt load and approve operations, and the two admin reads (RWB-P10-E1058-APP, RWB-P10-E1058-CON).
- The rest of the agent runtime: the case intake, the screening and the legal document agents, the guardrail checker as a shared capability, the evaluation harness and the monitor (RWB-P10-E1058-APP, RWB-P10-E1060-APP, RWB-P10-E1063-APP).
- The change of an autonomy level and its approval (RWB-P10-E3030-APP, RWB-P10-E8004-APP).
- The contract shapes of the suggestion operation, the record mapping, the EV-28 payload and the fakes (RWB-P10-E2032-CON).
- The network path to INT-23, the topic and its retry and `.dlt` topics, the queue, the secrets and the capacity (RWB-P10-E2032-INF).
- The treatment, the case, the account data and the reference data themselves, and the rights, the scope and the masking policy (rwb-treatment, rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-access).
- The central decision ledger, its sealing and its read (P7 rwb-decision).

##### 1. Story

As a **restructuring officer (RW-RESTRUCT)**, I want **`TreatmentWorkflow` of rwb-treatment to ask the agent-run operation of `RWB-P10-E2032-CON` for a TDR offer suggestion for the case facts it already holds, to store the answer on the treatment row as a proposal with the model, the prompt and the policy version it came from, to fall back to the rule result of the `RESTRUCTURE` package in force when the agent is slow or unavailable, and to record the suggestion and every officer override in the local decision record in the same transaction**, so that **the treatment record holds what was suggested next to what the officer offered, and every suggestion can be explained afterwards by the model and prompt version that produced it**.

This is the treatment-side slice of legacy RWB-E2-032. It owns:

- the use of the suggestion on the treatment side: the `suggestTdrOffer` activity of `TreatmentWorkflow`, the child of `CaseWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, which asks the suggestion operation for the facts of the treatment it is running and waits at most 60 s for the answer (Architecture v5 slides 16 and 18; Temporal and Drools Design slides 12 and 13);
- the proposal on the `treatment` row of `rwb_treatment`: the suggested terms, the model code and version, the prompt version, the policy version, the agent run id, the decision record id and the confidence, written as a proposal and never as an approved amount (DF-TRT-001, DF-TRT-002, DF-TRT-004, DF-TRT-007, DF-TRT-009);
- the fallback to the rule result of the `RESTRUCTURE` package in force when the answer does not arrive inside the wait, when the answer carries no suggestion, or when the agent refuses the call (R-UNI-32);
- the local decision record of every suggestion and of every officer override, written through the RWB-PLT-E1027-CON library inside the caller's transaction, with the rule ID and the package version on the fallback, hash-linked and published on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03), together with the outbox row (DP-09);
- the parameter value of the suggestion wait and the reference-data lists LOV-PROPOSER and LOV-TREATMENT read at their version (DP-06, DP-07);
- one REST operation on base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1` that returns the proposal of a treatment (DP-13), reached by SCR-15 through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19);
- the boundary: ACE facts only through the owner's contract or the `v_ace_*` views (DP-05), and no table of another service read or joined (DP-01).

It does not own: the model, the prompt, the guardrails, the run, the evaluation and the human-feedback record, which are P10 rwb-agent's (`RWB-P10-E2032-APP` and the contract `RWB-P10-E2032-CON`); the rule packages, their rows and their versions, which are P7 rwb-decision's; the settlement offer, the below-floor approval and the TDR plan, which are `RWB-S2-E3002-APP`, `RWB-S2-E3003-APP` and `RWB-S2-E3004-APP`; the case status, `CaseWorkflow` and the case table, which are rwb-case's (P3); the roles, rights and scope data, which are rwb-access's (P4); the gateway-bff composite route and the layout, which are the platform edge story's.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story put a suggestion on the treatment record through an interface inside the monolith: `ModelSuggestionClient.suggestOffer` returned an `OfferSuggestion` record, the decision log was written by the in-process `DecisionLogWriter`, the agent run was a table of the same `recovery` schema, and the P3 treatment service called all of it in one process. Its business objective is unchanged and is the one that matters here: the restructuring officer builds each restructure offer by hand from the balance, the arrears and the payment history, and a recorded suggestion next to the officer's offer lets the case be explained afterwards — what was recommended, by which model, at which policy version, and what the officer did with it (REQ-CHO-006, REQ-DRI-001).

What D-RCV-60 changes is where the answer comes from and who owns it. The suggestion is no longer produced by a component of the treatment module: it is a run of rwb-agent, reached by one REST operation on `/api/recovery/agent/v1` with one hop and a client budget (DP-11, DP-13; Architecture v5 slide 16; ADR-020), and the run, the prompt, the guardrail and the evaluation are rows of `rwb_agent` (Architecture v5 slide 41). The treatment service therefore holds a proposal and not a model: it sends the facts it owns, stores the answer it receives, and never reaches the Enterprise AI endpoint itself. That single ruling is what keeps one gateway, one prompt store and one model inventory in the platform, and it is why nothing in section 11 of this story is an `agent_run` write.

The second change is the fallback. The design gives every stage the same safety: an agent that is slow or unavailable does not stop the case, because after 60 seconds the rule result is used and the decision record says so (Architecture v5 slide 16; Temporal and Drools Design slide 27; R-UNI-32). Here the rule result is the answer of the `RESTRUCTURE` package version in force, which this stage already evaluates for its own steps, so the officer sees a proposal either way: the model's, or the rule's, and the record names which one.

The third change is the material action. The suggestion is advice, and the target keeps the officer's decision where the legacy put it: the officer builds and submits the offer, and the approval of an offer below the floor or outside the band is the approval story's (legacy BR7; FSD S2 A2.3 and A2.4). The architecture note on agent risk is explicit — a human decides every material action, and the prompts, the outputs and the model versions are logged (Architecture v5 slide 44) — so this story writes a proposal, a flag and a record, and it never writes an approved amount, an offer state or a booking.

Serves REQ-CHO-006 and REQ-DRI-001: a treatment record holds what was suggested next to what was offered, and the decision carries the model, the agent and the prompt version that produced it. No business value is invented or moved: the model code, the version, the policy version, the mode, the review date, the terms and the messages are the values the legacy story, the FSD and the design already carry, read in force.

##### 3. Preconditions

- `RWB-P10-E2032-CON` is published: the suggestion operation on base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`, whose path below the base is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0634; ASM-0977), its eight answer members `agentRunId`, `decisionLogEntryId`, `modelCode`, `modelVersion`, `installments`, `monthlyAmountThb`, `interestRate` and `confidence`, its request members case ID, treatment ID and the idempotency key `TDR_OFFER:<treatmentId>`, its refusals 200 with no suggestion and MSG-P10-007, 503 with MSG-P7-003 and 409 for a repeat that returns the stored answer, its one hop with the 2 s client budget of DP-11, and the rwb-agent fake. This story builds against that contract and its fake and never against `rwb_agent`.
- The platform libraries are in place as the wave 0 service-template capability: the decision-record writer of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON with `DecisionRecordWriter.record(DecisionRecord)` declared `@Transactional(propagation = MANDATORY)`, the outbox and inbox library of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, the parameters client of RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, the reference-data client of RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and the composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON (ASM-3098).
- The `rwb_treatment` schema and login exist from the platform database story, and this service's Flyway sequence is at the version that carries the library tables; this story adds the proposal columns of the `treatment` row on the same sequence and never edits an applied migration (DP-15).
- The workflow kit is in place on task queue `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and `CaseWorkflow` of rwb-case starts this stage as a child on that queue with parent close policy ABANDON (Temporal and Drools Design slide 13).
- The `RESTRUCTURE` package is in force for the business date, announced by rwb-decision on `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1`, and the embedded Drools runtime of the service template evaluates it; the package, its rows and its version stay rwb-decision's and this story stores no rule text (DP-04 capability of the template; ASM-3098).
- The parameter value of the suggestion wait and the lists LOV-PROPOSER with AGENT, RULE and PERSON, and LOV-TREATMENT with its eleven values, are in force and are read as data with their version; neither the 60 seconds nor any member of either list is written in code (BR-S2-001; TSD S2 T3.2).
- Treatment "T-1001" of case "RW-2026-001001" is open in state Draft, opened by `RWB-S2-E3001-APP`, and its treatment type is RESTRUCTURE (legacy sections 3 and 4).
- No approval is needed to build against a Draft contract baseline, and an APP story with only contract dependencies starts on Day 1 with the C dependency of RWB-P10-E2032-CON never blocking (§R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. `TreatmentWorkflow` is running on queue `rwb-treatment` for case "RW-2026-001001" with treatment "T-1001" open and in state Draft, having reached the offer step of the restructure route.
2. The workflow reads the `RESTRUCTURE` package version in force from the package signal and the parameter value of the suggestion wait from the parameters contract, and confirms that the treatment type of the row is RESTRUCTURE before it asks anything: on any other type the step makes no call (legacy BR6, AC8 of `RWB-P10-E2032-APP`).
3. `suggestTdrOffer` activity builds the request from the facts the stage holds: the case ID, the treatment ID, the route, the band and the plan terms as identifiers and amounts, the idempotency key `TDR_OFFER:T-1001`, the model code and the output schema `tdr-offer-v1` as the contract declares them. No name, no account number, no address and no document text leaves the service (section 17; ASM-3097).
4. The activity calls the suggestion operation of `RWB-P10-E2032-CON` once, with one hop and the 2 s client budget of DP-11 (ASM-3095).
5. The workflow waits at most 60 s for the answer and records the waiting period as a durable timer, so a worker restart does not lose the wait (R-UNI-32; Architecture v5 slide 16; ASM-3096).
6. On an answer that carries a suggestion, the activity builds the proposal from the eight members of the contract: the terms as identifiers and amounts, the model code and version, the confidence, the agent run id and the decision record id.
7. `recordSuggestion` activity writes, in one `rwb_treatment` transaction: the proposal on the `treatment` row of "T-1001" with the model version, the prompt version, the policy version and the run id it came from, the local `decision_record` row through `DecisionRecordWriter.record` with decision "D5", final call "SUGGESTION_RECORDED", the suggestion as the recommendation and the facts it was asked with as the inputs reference, the outbox row and the idempotency row of the key.
8. On a wait of 60 s without an answer, on an answer of 200 with no suggestion and MSG-P10-007, or on a refusal of 503 with MSG-P7-003, the activity takes the rule result of the `RESTRUCTURE` package version in force, records it as the proposal with the rule ID and the package version in place of the model version, sets the fallback fact on the proposal and on the decision record, and the stage continues on its next step (R-UNI-32; MSG-P10-007).
9. The activity returns the proposal and the decision record id to the stage; the stage reports the target state of the rule that its offer step takes — AWAITING_CREDIT_APPROVAL when the suggested terms fall outside the band, as R-RES-10 does — to the parent `CaseWorkflow`, which moves the case status. This service writes no case table (DP-01).
10. The officer reads the proposal on SCR-15 through the gateway-bff composite route, which composes the case read of rwb-case, the treatment read of this service and the proposal read of 12.1 in one hop each (DP-19).
11. When the officer overrides the suggestion, the override is written by the offer story of this service, and this story writes the second decision record that names the proposal it overrode — the agent run id, the model version and the suggested terms — in its inputs and marks the first proposal overridden, in one transaction with the same outbox row rule.
12. A repeated request with the same key `TDR_OFFER:T-1001` is answered with the stored suggestion or the stored proposal, writes no second proposal, no second record and no second outbox row, and makes no second model call (R-UNI-40; 409 of the contract).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The answer does not arrive inside the 60 s wait | The rule result of the `RESTRUCTURE` package in force is used, the fallback fact is recorded on the proposal and on the decision record, and the stage continues (R-UNI-32) | MSG-P10-007 | AC2 |
| X2 | The answer is 200 with no suggestion because the model is not in service | No model terms are stored; the rule result is used as X1 and SCR-15 shows the same message | MSG-P10-007 | AC2, AC6 |
| X3 | The agent refuses with 503 because the decision record could not be written on its side | No proposal is written, the treatment row and its state are unchanged, and the activity fails to the workflow, which retries it on the platform policy — 1 s initial interval, back-off 2, 10 attempts | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X4 | The 2 s client budget of the one hop is exceeded | The call is abandoned at the caller, no proposal is written from it, and the wait of X1 runs to its end and falls back to the rule result (DP-11) | MSG-P10-007 | AC2 |
| X5 | The local decision record cannot be written | The transaction rolls back: no proposal, no outbox row, no idempotency row; the user sees MSG-P7-003 and the call is retried with the same key | MSG-P7-003 | AC1, section 17 |
| X6 | The same key arrives twice | The first proposal is returned, the repeat is counted, and no second model call is made (R-UNI-40) | None | AC5 |
| X7 | The treatment type is not RESTRUCTURE | No call, no proposal and no record; the step moves on with the offer as today | None | AC1 |
| X8 | No `RESTRUCTURE` version is in force for the business date | No call is made and no proposal is written; the stage ends with the package refusal it received and the case keeps its status | MSG-P7-003 | Section 12.4 |
| X9 | A role without Treatment and offer R asks for the proposal | 403 with the guard library's answer, and the service log records the role and the operation, never a personal field | MSG-P4-002 | AC6, section 10 |
| X10 | A class, a statement or a test reaches an `rwb_agent`, `rwb_decision` or `rwb_case` table or a `v_ace_*` view directly | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build; nothing is released | None (pipeline log) | Section 17 |

X1 to X3 are the fallback and refusal paths of the legacy story carried onto the split; X4 is the client budget of DP-11, which the one hop adds; X5 and X6 are the record and repeat rules of the legacy (R-UNI-39, R-UNI-40); X7 and X8 are the type guard and the package refusal the workflow model adds; X9 is the guard's answer; X10 is the schema boundary. A refusal under X9 writes nothing at all, because the guard runs before the transaction opens.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Starts on Day 1 against the RWB-P10-E2032-CON fake, the record-writer fake, the parameters and reference-data fakes and the composite-route fake; needs no live rwb-agent, no model and no Enterprise AI endpoint |
| Negotiable | The activity and operation names of this slice, the column names of the proposal and the shape of the override record are this story's choice; the terms, the versions, the lists, the rights and the messages are fixed |
| Valuable | The officer sees a recorded suggestion next to the offer, the record says which model and prompt produced it, and a slow agent never stops the case |
| Estimable | One activity pair, one proposal on one row, one read operation, one library adapter, one migration and one panel behind a route |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests, as a secondary slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Each of the eight criteria of section 7 is one automated test; the agent, the package, the writer and the route are stubbed |

The eight criteria are new under D-RCV-60 and test only the treatment-side deliverable of this story: the proposal on the `treatment` row, the 60 s wait and its fallback to the rule result, the out-of-band flag, the override record, the write-once key, the refusal path, the personal-data boundary and the screen read. The eight legacy criteria AC1 to AC8 of RWB-E2-032 — the exposure of the model, the mode OFF path, the logged record, the timeout, the schema failure, the unrecorded decision, the repeated request and the non-restructure type — belong to `RWB-P10-E2032-APP`, are written there word for word with their origin tags, and are not restated here (ASM-3094). The shape of the operation, its eight answer members, its refusal codes and its fake are `RWB-P10-E2032-CON`'s; the cross-service proof of the suggestion across rwb-treatment and rwb-agent is the wave 2 integration harness's and no criterion of this story claims it.

Three readings of the sources are stated here rather than hidden in the code. The treatment side of the suggestion is not described by any source — the legacy story describes the agent side end to end and the TSD gives `treatment` no column for a suggestion, a model version or a prompt version — so the proposal, its columns and its values are this story's design and are carried as a gap with its assumption (GAP-1882; ASM-3094). The one hop carries the 2 s client budget of DP-11 while the agent call keeps the policy timeout of 60 seconds, and no source reconciles the two waits, so both are declared and either breach falls back to the rule result (ASM-3095, ASM-3096; GAP-0634). The band the suggested terms are tested against is a row value of the `RESTRUCTURE` package and is not restated as a number here (GAP-1882; ASM-3094). The conflict between the operation list of Architecture v5 slide 16 and the in-process client of the legacy section 12 is carried as `GAP-1883`.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The model is reached only through the agent-run operation of `RWB-P10-E2032-CON`; this service embeds no model client, calls no Enterprise AI endpoint and reads no `rwb_agent` row | Legacy RWB-E2-032 BR1; DP-11; Architecture v5 slides 16 and 41 (GAP-1883) |
| BR2 | The suggestion is asked only for a treatment whose type is RESTRUCTURE; any other type makes no call and returns no proposal | Legacy RWB-E2-032 BR6; DF-TRT-004; TSD S2 T3.2 |
| BR3 | The proposal is advice: it never writes the approved amount, the offer terms, the offer state or a booking; the officer builds and submits the offer and decides it | Legacy RWB-E2-032 BR7; Architecture v5 slide 44 agent-risk note; FSD S2 A2.3 and A2.4 |
| BR4 | A suggestion is kept only with the model code, the model version, the prompt version and the policy version that produced it; a proposal without them is not written | REQ-DRI-001; legacy RWB-E2-032 AC3 (GAP-1882; ASM-3094) |
| BR5 | A model answer that is not there inside the wait, an answer that carries no suggestion or a refusal gives the rule result of the `RESTRUCTURE` package version in force, recorded with the fallback fact, and the stage continues | Legacy RWB-E2-032 BR4; R-UNI-32; Architecture v5 slide 16; Temporal and Drools Design slide 27 |
| BR6 | The suggestion and every override are recorded before they are returned: the proposal, the local decision record and the outbox row are one transaction, and a failed record rolls the call back with MSG-P7-003 | Legacy RWB-E2-032 BR3; R-UNI-39; DP-03 |
| BR7 | One proposal per treatment per key `TDR_OFFER:<treatmentId>`: a repeat returns the stored answer and writes nothing | Legacy RWB-E2-032 BR5; R-UNI-40 |
| BR8 | The case status stays rwb-case's and the treatment state stays this service's own `state` column: the stage reports the target state of the rule it took and the parent moves the case | ASM-3062; DP-01 |
| BR9 | No value a business person may change is written in code: the band, the wait, the model code and version, the prompt version, the policy version and the lists are values in force read with their version | BR-S2-001; BR-S2-004; TSD S2 T3.2 (DP-06, DP-07) |
| BR10 | A role reads the proposal only with Treatment and offer R, and the right is declared and not re-implemented: the check is the platform guard library's | TSD S2 T6.1; DP-08 as a template capability (ASM-3098) |
| BR11 | ACE data is never read here: the facts of the request are the treatment's own and, were an ACE fact needed, it would come through the contract of rwb-source-data or a `v_ace_*` view granted to this schema | DP-05; Architecture v5 slide 41; `ownership.json` |
| R-UNI-32 | The agent or the model does not answer inside the timeout of 60 seconds: fall back to the rule result and continue, and record the fallback on the decision | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-UNI-32); Temporal and Drools Design slide 27 |
| R-UNI-39 | The decision cannot be written: block the action and raise an incident, and no action proceeds unlogged | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-UNI-39); legacy RWB-E2-032 BR3 |
| R-UNI-40 | The same event arrives twice with the same key: ignore the second and record the idempotency hit | Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-UNI-40); legacy RWB-E2-032 BR5 |
| R-RES-10 | A case in WITH_FCR_OFFICER with OFFER_PREPARED and `offer outside the range or deviation_flag = Y` routes the offer to credit approval; its target state is AWAITING_CREDIT_APPROVAL | TSD S2 T4; FSD S2 A2.4; BR3 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1 and BR2 are the `suggestTdrOffer` activity and the contract's request. BR3 is the absence of any write to DF-TRT-007, DF-TRT-009 and the treatment `state` in this story's components, asserted by a build check and by AC1. BR4 and BR5 are the proposal builder and the fallback branch of the activity. BR6 is `recordSuggestion` and the library. BR7 is the idempotency key and the inbox. BR8 is the stage outcome and the parent workflow. BR9 is the parameters and reference-data reads and the package read. BR10 is the contract's `security` section and the guard. BR11 is the schema grant and the boundary test. R-UNI-32 is the 60 s wait and the rule branch. R-UNI-39 is the rollback of X5. R-UNI-40 is the 409 path of AC5. R-RES-10 is the target state the stage reports when the proposal is outside the band.

##### 9. State transitions

None of the rows below is a case status or the `treatment.state` of this service. The case status is moved by the parent `CaseWorkflow` on rwb-case from the outcome the stage reports (ASM-3062; DP-01), and `treatment.state` stays Draft through this story, because a suggestion approves nothing and books nothing.

| From (proposal state on the treatment row) | Event | Condition | Reported target state |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | SUGGESTION_RECEIVED | The answer carries a suggestion inside the band | None reported; the offer step stays with the officer |
| none | SUGGESTION_RECEIVED | The answer carries a suggestion outside the band | AWAITING_CREDIT_APPROVAL, the target of R-RES-10 |
| none | AGENT_SLOW or AGENT_REFUSED | No answer inside the 60 s wait, no suggestion, or a refusal | RESUME_STATE, the target of R-UNI-32 |
| SUGGESTED | OFFICER_OVERRIDE | The officer enters different plan terms | None reported; the second record names the proposal it overrode |
| SUGGESTED, OVERRIDDEN | REPEAT_REQUEST | The same key `TDR_OFFER:<treatmentId>` asks again | None; the stored proposal is returned |

The proposal has its own lifecycle in the proposal columns of the `treatment` row — proposed, overridden, replaced by the rule result — and their names are this story's design, Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1882; ASM-3094). The stage execution itself is RUNNING, COMPLETED or FAILED in the workflow history, and a failed execution is retried on the platform policy, 1 s initial interval with back-off 2 and 10 attempts, with a package refusal non-retryable.

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| The rwb-treatment squad, service identity of `rwb_treatment` | Runs the activity, writes the proposal, the decision record and the outbox rows, calls the agent contract |
| RW-RESTRUCT, restructuring officer (CRUA) | Reads the proposal on SCR-15, overrides it, builds and submits the offer; the primary role of the story |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner (CRU) | Reads the proposal on SCR-15 for cases in scope |
| RW-SPECIAL, hardship and vulnerability specialist (CRU) | Reads the proposal on cases in scope |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager (R); RW-PRODHEAD, product head (RA); RW-CREDCOMM, credit approval committee member (RA) | Read the proposal; the approval of an offer outside the band is RWB-S2-E3003-APP's |
| The other reading roles of TSD S2 T6.1 — RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-LITOFF, RW-LEGAL, RW-GUARANT, RW-CONDUCT, RW-RISK, RW-COE, RW-AUDIT, RW-BIANAL, RW-TRIBE (R) | Read the treatment and its proposal on cases in scope |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, SY-AGENT (R) | Read as service identities through the same checks |
| rwb-agent (P10) | Owns the operation, the model, the prompt, the guardrail, the run, the evaluation and the human-feedback record; answers the one hop |
| rwb-decision (P7) | Owns the `RESTRUCTURE` package, its rows and its version, and publishes `RulePackageInForce` |
| rwb-access (P4) | Owns the rights, the roles and the scope data the guard library answers with |
| No delegation of authority level applies | The story proposes; it approves nothing and books nothing |

No credential and no personal name appears in the request, the row, the record, the workflow input or the logs. Where a person must be identified the row carries a user identifier, never a name, and the masking of the personal fields of the case is the platform edge's.

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-TRT-001 | treatment | id | Read: the treatment the proposal belongs to |
| DF-TRT-002 | treatment | case_id | Read: carried as the case ID of the request |
| DF-TRT-003 | treatment | decision_log_id | Not rewritten here: the record ID of the open stays, and the proposal carries its own record ID with the proposal |
| DF-TRT-004 | treatment | treatment_type | Read: the model is asked only when the value is RESTRUCTURE (BR2) |
| DF-TRT-005 | treatment | proposed_by | Not rewritten here: `RWB-S2-E3001-APP` writes it at open, and the proposer of the proposal is carried with the proposal from LOV-PROPOSER |
| DF-TRT-006 | treatment | proposed_at | Not rewritten here: the business time of the proposal is carried with the proposal |
| DF-TRT-007 | treatment | offer_amount | Read, never written here: it stays empty until `RWB-S2-E3002-APP` writes the offer |
| DF-TRT-009 | treatment | installments | Read, never written here: the suggested count is a proposal value and the plan count is `RWB-S2-E3004-APP`'s |
| DF-TRT-031 | treatment | installment_amount | Not written here: the plan story writes the count that becomes the plan |
| DF-TRT-032 | treatment | installments_paid | Not written here: the open writes zero and the plan story carries it |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_record (local, in `rwb_treatment`) | all fields through `DecisionRecordWriter.record` | Write, in the same transaction (DP-03) |
| The proposal columns of the `treatment` row | treatment | the suggested terms as identifiers and amounts, the model code, the model version, the prompt version, the policy version, the agent run id, the decision record id, the confidence, the out-of-band flag and the proposal state | Write: names and types Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1882; ASM-3094) |
| DF-AGT-004, DF-AGT-005, DF-AGT-036, DF-AGT-040, DF-AGT-049, DF-AGT-058 | agent_policy, agent_run (`rwb_agent`, owner P10) | the model code, the model version, the run ID and the record ID of the suggestion | Not read and not written here: they arrive as the eight answer members of `RWB-P10-E2032-CON` (`agentRunId`, `modelCode`, `modelVersion`, `decisionLogEntryId`) and are stored on the proposal |
| DF-ACC-009, DF-ACE-020, DF-ACE-018, DF-ACE-025, DF-ACE-045, DF-ACE-046 | v_ace_account, v_ace_payment (`rwb_source_data`, owner P1) | the balance, the arrears and the payments of the legacy inputs | Not read here: the masked inputs snapshot is assembled by P10 rwb-agent behind its own contract (DP-05), and this service sends the facts of the treatment only |
| DF-CAS-001 to DF-CAS-023 | recovery_case (`rwb_case`, owner P3) | the case and its status | Not read and not written: the status arrives as the case signal the parent forwards |

`treatment` is the only table this story touches, and it adds no table: it adds the proposal columns of section 13 to the row `RWB-S2-E3001-APP` created, and writes the `decision_record` through the library in the same schema. The eight answer members are the only P10 identifiers this story sees, they arrive on the contract's answer, and no `agent_policy`, `agent_run`, `agent_prompt` or `agent_evaluation` row is read or written (DP-01; Architecture v5 slide 41; `ownership.json`). No foreign key crosses a schema and no row of another service's table is joined.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-treatment (S2); base `/api/recovery/treatment/v1` (DP-13). This story supplies one read of the proposal; the treatment create and read of `RWB-S2-E3001-CON` and the offer operations of `RWB-S2-E3002-CON` and `RWB-S2-E3004-CON` are unchanged by it.

| Method | Path | Request and response | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | Below the base, the segment of the proposal read Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1882; ASM-3094) | `Treatment` id in the path, the proposal out: the suggested terms, the model code, the model version, the prompt version, the policy version, the agent run id, the decision record id, the confidence, the out-of-band flag and the proposal state, or the fallback fact and its rule ID and package version | Treatment and offer R, scope applied, through the guard library | Not applicable |

The errors are 401, 403, 404 and 503 with the RFC 9457 problem body; 403 carries MSG-P4-002 and 404 carries MSG-P4-003. The proposal read declares no offer body, no approval envelope and no plan body: those belong to the sibling contracts of this epic.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Operation | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | The suggestion operation of `RWB-P10-E2032-CON`, path below `/api/recovery/agent/v1` Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0634; ASM-0977) | P10 rwb-agent | One suggestion for one treatment, answered with the eight legacy members; refusals 200 with no suggestion and MSG-P10-007, 503 with MSG-P7-003, 409 for a repeat |
| GET | The parameters read of the RWB-P3-E1042-CON contract, operation Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1882; ASM-3094) | P3 rwb-case | The suggestion wait in force, whose value the design fixes at 60 seconds (R-UNI-32) |
| GET | The reference-data read of the RWB-P3-E1043-CON contract, operation Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1882; ASM-3094) | P3 rwb-case | LOV-PROPOSER and LOV-TREATMENT at their version in force |

Every call is one hop with the 2 s client budget of DP-11 (ADR-020). The agent call is the one hop of this story that may take the agent's policy timeout of 60 seconds, and the exception is recorded with its assumption (ASM-3095, ASM-3096; ASM-0978). The model itself is reached only by rwb-agent, on the Enterprise AI private endpoint, and this service holds no external call (X section 19).

###### 12.3 Events published

The topic of the service is `rwb.treatment.events.v1` with event names `rwb.treatment.<Event>.v1` (DP-14); `TreatmentApproved` and `TreatmentClosed` belong to `RWB-S2-E3003-APP` and `RWB-S2-E3004-APP`, and this story publishes neither. The only event of this story is the one the library writes inside the transaction: `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, once per proposal and once per override, with no personal data in its payload (DP-03, DP-09; Architecture v5 slides 20 and 42).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` (EV-30) | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | Announces the `RESTRUCTURE` package version in force; the stage stamps it on the fallback record and reads the band from it |
| CaseEvent (EV-29), the case signal | no topic: the case router and the parent `CaseWorkflow` of rwb-case | P3 rwb-case | Carries the route and the case facts the stage evaluates; forwarded by the parent |

`rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28) is not consumed here: its consumers are rwb-decision, rwb-document and rwb-deviation (Architecture v5 slide 43), and the suggestion answer already carries the run ID, the model version and the record ID this story stores. The package event is consumed through the inbox of the outbox library, so a redelivery starts no second swap; the case signal is a Temporal signal forwarded by the parent and is not a Kafka subscription of this service.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `TreatmentWorkflow` | Workflow, the stage child of `CaseWorkflow`, one execution per case and stage | `rwb-treatment` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | The offer step takes the suggestion as its input and reports the target state of section 9 |
| `suggestTdrOffer` | Activity | `rwb-treatment` | Input: case ID, treatment ID, the treatment type, the route, the band, the plan terms and the key `TDR_OFFER:<treatmentId>`; output: the proposal or the fallback result, with the decision record ID; one REST hop and one 60 s wait |
| `recordSuggestion` | Activity | `rwb-treatment` | One transaction: the proposal on the treatment row, the local decision record, the outbox row and the idempotency row (the `RecordAndApply` shape of the design) |

The activity names outside the design's `TreatmentWorkflow` are this story's design and are fixed by no source document (GAP-1882; ASM-3094). The package evaluation of the fallback is the embedded Drools runtime's, inside `suggestTdrOffer`, and adds no activity of its own.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The suggestion is request-driven, the stage is started by the parent `CaseWorkflow`, and the Arch v5 job map names no job for an agent suggestion (Architecture v5 slide 44). The 60 s wait is a durable timer inside the workflow execution, not a Schedule.

| Table | Schema | Owner | This story |

| `treatment` | `rwb_treatment` | S2 | Adds the proposal columns of section 13 to the row of `RWB-S2-E3001-APP` and writes them; DF-TRT-001, DF-TRT-002 and DF-TRT-004 are read |
| `decision_record` | `rwb_treatment` | PLT library object applied in this schema | Written through `DecisionRecordWriter.record` in the caller's transaction; the central `decision_log_entry` is P7's and is never touched |
| outbox, inbox, idempotency | `rwb_treatment` | PLT library objects | The service template's and not restated here (ASM-3098) |

No `agent_run`, `agent_policy`, `agent_prompt`, `agent_evaluation`, `rule_package`, `rule_row` or `recovery_case` table is created, read or joined (DP-01, `ownership.json`).
