**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-032 for the wave 2 integration harness. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **restructuring officer (RW-RESTRUCT)**, I want **a repeatable cross-service journey harness for the TDR offer-suggestion model at E3e — a restructure treatment opening, the policy in force deciding whether a suggestion is attempted, the call through the model gateway on the 60 s policy timeout, the answer checked against `tdr-offer-v1`, the D5 record written before the suggestion returns, and the suggestion read back with its model code and version, or MSG-P10-007 — with the evidence pack attached to the wave 2 release**, so that **one suggestion, one agent run and one D5 record are proven to describe the same treatment on the same model version before RWB-S2-E2032-APP, RWB-P10-E2032-APP, RWB-P7-E2032-APP and RWB-P3-E2004-APP claim Done**.

This story builds the harness, its contract fakes, its seed pack and its TDR model stub, its evidence pack and its pass or fail gate. It builds no production endpoint, no screen, no table and no migration. Nothing it writes is deployed to a service.

No single app story can prove the journey. RWB-S2-E2032-APP can prove that the treatment record exists and that a restructure treatment opens. RWB-P10-E2032-APP can prove that the policy in force is read, that the model is called through the gateway and the private endpoint, that the answer passes the `tdr-offer-v1` check and that an agent run is stored. RWB-P7-E2032-APP can prove that a D5 record is written and that the ledger read returns it. RWB-P3-E2004-APP can prove the case record and the account facts the journey reads through the case contract. The agreement between the four of them — one suggestion, one run and one D5 record describing the same treatment on the same model version, with no treatment transaction waiting on a model — is this story, and only this story.

##### 2. Business rationale

RWB-E2-032 split into four app stories and this integration story. RWB-S2-E2032-APP builds the treatment record, the open restructure treatment and the suggestion area behind the treatment read. RWB-P10-E2032-APP builds the policy in force, the gateway call, the output schema check, the guardrail, the agent run and the agent-output read. RWB-P7-E2032-APP builds the D5 mapping and the ledger read. RWB-P3-E2004-APP carries the case record and the account facts the journey starts from. What no app story can prove on its own is the chain the business relies on, and the business relies on all of it at once.

The chain is this. A restructure treatment opens on the treatment service. The policy in force decides whether a suggestion is attempted at all: mode OFF makes no call and returns nothing, mode L1 attempts it. The call goes through `ModelGatewayClient` with the 60 s timeout held on the policy row, not in code. The answer is checked against `tdr-offer-v1`. The D5 record is written before the suggestion is returned, so a suggestion a reader can see always has a ledger entry behind it. The treatment screen then shows the terms with the model code and version, or MSG-P10-007 when there is no suggestion. That is the journey this harness proves.

The journey carries two requirements. A treatment record holds every offer's type, terms, approval and outcome (REQ-CHO-006): the harness asserts that the suggestion it reads back sits on the treatment record beside the officer's own offer fields and is never copied into them. Every decision records the rule, model, agent and prompt versions (REQ-DRI-001): the harness asserts that the D5 record names model version "TDR-OFFER-1.0" and the inputs reference, so a reader of the ledger can tell which model produced the recommendation that the officer saw.

The D5 decision is the anchor. Legacy section 12 gives the mapping: case_id, decision code "D5", the model version, no agent version, the masked inputs snapshot as the inputs reference, the suggestion as the recommendation, final call "SUGGESTION_RECORDED", and the treatment ID and run ID in the actions. The harness exercises that mapping across rwb-agent and rwb-decision, so a change to the mapping on either side is caught before an officer sees a suggestion that no ledger entry supports.

Architecture v5 changes the path, not the business. In the monolith the suggestion client, the run row and the decision log sat in one deployment and one schema, called in process and waited on. In the target:

- the account and the treatment come through the owning services' contracts, and the harness reads no `recovery` schema table at any point (DP-01);
- the D5 record is a local decision record published on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` and held in the ledger by rwb-decision (DP-03);
- the account facts behind the suggestion — principal outstanding, days past due, balance, interest rate and the last 12 months of payments — come through the owning service's contract, never from an ACE view the harness reads itself (DP-05);
- the policy versions, the record modes, the output schema limits and the 60 s timeout are parameters and data, loaded and seeded, never values in the harness (DP-06);
- the autonomy modes "OFF" and "L1", the run statuses, the guardrail check name, the decision code "D5" and the final call are reference data served from files (DP-07);
- the completion and the ledger write are CloudEvents observed on the owner's topic, with an outbox on the producer and an inbox on the consumer, so a duplicate never counts twice (DP-09);
- the request is one hop on the rwb-agent contract with the 2 s REST budget, the model call itself stays inside `AgentRunWorkflow` with the 60 s policy timeout, and the stored output plus the D5 record are read back through the agents' and the ledger's contracts, so no treatment transaction waits on a model (DP-11);
- every path is on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` (DP-13);
- the treatment screen and the journey reach the services through the gateway-bff composite route, so the harness drives the same route the screens use (DP-19).

DP-11 is the pattern that changed the most, and it is stated plainly here. The monolith called `ModelSuggestionClient` in process and waited for the answer inside the treatment transaction. In the target the treatment side does not call rwb-agent that way: the request is one hop on the rwb-agent contract with the 2 s REST budget, the model call stays inside `AgentRunWorkflow` with the 60 s policy timeout, and the suggestion is read back through the stored agent output and the D5 record rather than held open in the treatment transaction. That is the assumption of section 3. The start operation itself is the one open point: Architecture v5 slide 13 gives the treatment row no call to rwb-agent, slide 16 starts agent runs only from `CaseCreated` and `DocumentStored`, and the Ownership Map has no rwb-agent operation that starts a suggestion run. It is recorded as a Conflict gap (GAP-0414) and agreed between the two owners at the wave 2 entry check. Until it is published, the harness reports this journey as blocked, never as passed.

The measure is the journey evidence: for each owned criterion, one pass or fail with the treatment, the suggestion, the run, the decision record and the fallback flag captured in one report that can be re-run for any build.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The wave 2 harness environment (SIT) is available with the gateway route for `/api/recovery/*`, the topic `rwb.agent.events.v1` and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the Temporal namespace `rwb-recovery` with the queues `rwb-agent` and `rwb-treatment`, and the private endpoint test profile that stands in for the TDR model (INT-23).
- The four integration dependencies have published their contracts, or their contract fakes stand in for them: RWB-S2-E2032-APP (rwb-treatment, the treatment record, the open restructure treatment and the suggestion area), RWB-P10-E2032-APP (rwb-agent, the policy in force, the gateway call, the output schema check and the agent run), RWB-P7-E2032-APP (rwb-decision, the D5 mapping and the ledger read) and RWB-P3-E2004-APP (rwb-case, the case record and the account facts the journey reads).
- Policy "TDR_OFFER" version "P1" is in force with mode "OFF" and review date 2027-02-28; version "P2" is in force with mode "L1", model version "TDR-OFFER-1.0", output schema "tdr-offer-v1" and timeout 60 seconds, loaded by RW-COE and approved by RW-RISK (legacy sections 3 and 7).
- Restructure treatment "T-1001" is open on case "RW-2026-001001", the account holds principal outstanding 1,250,000.00 baht and 120 days past due, and treatment "T-1002" has type "SETTLEMENT" (legacy sections 4 and 7).
- The TDR model stub answers the suggestion of 84 installments of 18,900.00 baht with model version "TDR-OFFER-1.0", stays silent for 61 seconds, and answers installments -12 — one control per scenario, never in the same run (legacy AC1, AC4, AC5). The rwb-decision fake answers unavailable for AC6 (legacy AC6).
- The feature switch `rwb.agent.tdr-suggestion` is on in the harness profile (legacy section 13).
- Synthetic cases, synthetic treatments and masking tokens only: no customer name, account number, national identifier or contact detail enters the harness, the seed pack, the events, the logs or the evidence pack (legacy section 17).
- Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0414; ASM-0589): the start operation that begins a suggestion run, the harness environment and its seeding, the TDR model stub and its 61 s and -12 controls, the OFF-policy fixture, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate.
- No build dependency. Day 1.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: takes the run lock for the environment and records the build ID, the business date and the versions of the four contracts it is about to exercise.
2. Harness: seeds case "RW-2026-001001", the account facts (principal outstanding 1,250,000.00 baht, 120 days past due), restructure treatment "T-1001", settlement treatment "T-1002", and both policy versions — "TDR_OFFER" P1 mode OFF with review date 2027-02-28, and P2 mode L1 with model version "TDR-OFFER-1.0", output schema "tdr-offer-v1" and timeout 60 seconds.
3. Harness: calls the P4 session operation against the rwb-access fake and records the role, the scope and the rights the journey runs under.
4. Harness: subscribes to `rwb.agent.events.v1` and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` with its own consumer group before the treatment is opened, so the run window starts before the call.
5. Harness: opens the restructure treatment through `POST /api/recovery/treatment/v1/cases/{caseId}/treatments`, or lets the rwb-treatment fake accept it where RWB-S2-E2032-APP has not landed, and records which of the two paths was used.
6. Harness: waits for `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` on `rwb.agent.events.v1` inside the run window, or reads the stored output through `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` when the event has not arrived inside the window, and records which of the two paths proved the run.
7. Harness: reads the run through `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-runs` and records the status, agent code, model version, autonomy mode, idempotency key, fallback flag, guardrail result and decision log id.
8. Harness: reads the treatment through `GET /api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}` and asserts the suggestion of 84 installments of 18,900.00 baht with model code "TDR_OFFER" and model version "TDR-OFFER-1.0", or MSG-P10-007 in the suggestion area, and that the offer fields are untouched.
9. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` and asserts one D5 record with the model version, the inputs reference and the suggested terms, before the decision log id on the run row is asserted against it.
10. Harness: repeats step 5 for the same treatment and asserts that the first suggestion and its decision record id return and that no second run exists for the key "TDR_OFFER:<treatmentId>".
11. Harness: runs the OFF policy, the 61 s silence, the installments -12 answer, the decision-log failure and the settlement treatment as separate scenarios against the same contracts, and records the message and the run status of each.
12. Harness: writes the per-scenario evidence into one run report keyed by story key and business date, evaluates the gate, attaches the report to the wave 2 release record, releases the lock and restores the seed.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The model is not in service (mode OFF) | No call and no decision record; the treatment read carries the message in the suggestion area | MSG-P10-007 | AC2 |
| X2 | The model does not answer within 60 seconds | The run holds status "TIMED_OUT"; no suggestion and no D5 record; the treatment continues (R-UNI-32) | MSG-P10-007 | AC4 |
| X3 | The answer fails the output schema | The run holds status "GUARDRAIL_FAILED"; no suggestion is returned | MSG-P10-007 | AC5 |
| X4 | The decision log write fails | No suggestion is returned; the run is kept without a decision link and the incident is raised under R-UNI-39 by the service, not by the harness | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X5 | The same treatment asks again | The first suggestion and its decision record id return; no second call is made (R-UNI-40) | None to a user | AC7 |
| X6 | The treatment type is not RESTRUCTURE | No call, no suggestion and no run | None to a user | AC8 |
| X7 | A role without the right reads the agent runs | The read answers 403 | MSG-P4-002 | AC9 |
| X8 | The seed pack cannot be loaded (case not seeded, policy version absent, treatment type missing, stub control off) | The run refuses to start and names the missing seed item; no scenario is reported | None | All |
| X9 | The start operation of the Conflict gap is not published | The journey is reported blocked and no scenario is reported as passed | None | AC1 |
| X10 | The evidence pack cannot be attached to the release record | The run is marked failed and the local evidence file is kept for rerun | None | All |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the four published contracts or their fakes, the policy fixtures, the TDR model stub and the private endpoint test profile; it builds no service feature and has no build dependency |
| Negotiable | The scenarios, the seeded values, the policy versions, the timeout, the schema limits and the stub controls are data files, never code |
| Valuable | The offer-suggestion journey is proven once across four services, with the D5 record and the model version in the same evidence as the suggestion |
| Estimable | One journey runner, one fake set, one fixture pack, three assertion helpers, one evidence collector, one gate |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each owned criterion has a fixed Given, When and Then and a recorded pass or fail in the report |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source | Proved by |
|---|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The TDR model is reached only through the model gateway on the private endpoint | DL33; integration INT-23 | AC1, AC5 |
| BR2 | Mode OFF returns no suggestion and makes no call; the review date is held on the policy row | agent_policy.autonomy_mode, review_date | AC2 |
| BR3 | A suggestion is returned only after its decision record is written | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06 | AC3, AC6 |
| BR4 | A timeout or a failed check gives no suggestion and the treatment continues | R-UNI-32 | AC4, AC5 |
| BR5 | One suggestion per treatment; the key is "TDR_OFFER:<treatmentId>" | R-UNI-40 | AC7 |
| BR6 | The model is called only for treatment type RESTRUCTURE | treatment.treatment_type | AC8 |
| BR7 | The suggestion is advice; the officer builds and submits the offer | Agent catalogue, settlement and restructure agent; R-RES-09, R-RES-10 | AC1, AC3 |

The rules are unchanged by the split. The harness asserts them across the service boundaries and restates none of them in code: the model code, the model version, the output schema limits, the timeout, the review date and the autonomy modes are seeded data.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case and none for the treatment. This story changes no case status and no treatment status; the harness asserts that a suggestion, a timeout, a failed check or a repeat request never moves the treatment out of its draft state and never writes the suggestion into the offer fields.

The story writes an agent run and, when a suggestion returns, one decision record. The run carries the status rwb-agent gives it, and the harness asserts only the three the legacy story names: "ANSWERED" for a completed run, "TIMED_OUT" with fallback true for a run that reached the 60 s limit, and "GUARDRAIL_FAILED" with check "SCHEMA" for an answer that fails `tdr-offer-v1`.

The harness adds run states of its own only: Not started, Running, Blocked, Passed, Failed, with the latest run for a build deciding the gate. Blocked is the state of this journey while the start operation of the Conflict gap is unpublished.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test asset in the integration pipeline and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/treatment/v1/cases/{caseId}/treatments` | S2 rwb-treatment | Opens the restructure treatment "T-1001" and the settlement treatment "T-1002"; the start point of the journey (AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}` | S2 rwb-treatment | Reads the treatment, the suggestion area with the terms, the model code and version, or MSG-P10-007 (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | Reads the case and the seeded account facts the journey starts from (AC1) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` | P10 rwb-agent | Reads the stored suggestion and the run output when the completion event has not arrived inside the run window (AC1, AC3, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-runs` | P10 rwb-agent | Reads the run: status, agent code, model version, autonomy mode, idempotency key, fallback flag, guardrail result and decision log id (AC1, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs` | P10 rwb-agent | Reads the TDR_OFFER version, mode and review date (AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | P7 rwb-decision | Asserts the D5 record, its model version, its inputs reference and the suggested terms (AC1, AC3, AC6, AC7) |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with the 2 s timeout, and the one POST carries an If-Match and a key per scenario; the key "TDR_OFFER:<treatmentId>" belongs to the service and is only asserted here. The treatment side has no rwb-agent operation to start the suggestion run in the target matrix — Architecture v5 slide 13 gives S2 no call to P10 and the Ownership Map has none — so the start operation is the one open point recorded as a Conflict gap (GAP-0414) and agreed as stated in section 3. The P4 session operation is called against the rwb-access fake only (12.8) and reads the role and rights under which the journey runs.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event on a production topic; the evidence goes to the release record through the pipeline.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` | `rwb.agent.events.v1` | P10 rwb-agent | Closes the run window and gives the run ID, the status and the fallback flag before the output and run reads (DP-09, DP-11) |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | Asserts that the D5 record reached the shared topic inside the run window, alongside the ledger read of 12.2 (DP-03, DP-09) |

The harness consumes with its own consumer group and never reads a producer's outbox, inbox or schema.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

`AgentRunWorkflow` on queue `rwb-agent` is exercised, not built: the model call sits inside the workflow with the 60 s policy timeout and then the rule result (R-UNI-32), and the harness asserts which of the two a run ended on through the status and the fallback flag (AC1, AC4). JOB-11 Outbox sender is observed on its every-minute window, so the harness knows when a produced event should have crossed the topic.

The harness starts no workflow, adds no activity and writes no schedule. The start of the run belongs to RWB-P10-E2032-APP and the treatment side to RWB-S2-E2032-APP, under the agreement recorded in section 3.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The harness adds no workflow and no schedule; the 60 s limit is inside `AgentRunWorkflow` and JOB-11's every-minute window is the platform's, both only observed.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no table in any schema and no schema of its own; it reads and writes through the operations of 12.2 only.

| Fake | Serves | Contract | What it answers |

| WireMock rwb-treatment | The two S2 operations of 12.2 | OpenAPI of S2 | The open restructure treatment "T-1001" and the settlement treatment "T-1002" of type "SETTLEMENT"; the suggestion area with model code "TDR_OFFER" and version "TDR-OFFER-1.0", or MSG-P10-007; the treatment state unchanged by the suggestion; keeps the request journal for the repeat assertion |
| WireMock rwb-agent | The three P10 operations of 12.2 | OpenAPI of P10 | The stored suggestion, the run with status "TIMED_OUT" and fallback true, the run with status "GUARDRAIL_FAILED" and check "SCHEMA", the run with no decision log id, the OFF policy in the configs read, and the empty run list for the settlement treatment |
| WireMock rwb-decision | `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | OpenAPI of P7 | The D5 record with model version "TDR-OFFER-1.0", the inputs reference and the suggested terms; 503 for AC6 |
| WireMock rwb-case | `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | OpenAPI of P3 | Case "RW-2026-001001" with the seeded account facts, principal outstanding 1,250,000.00 baht and 120 days past due |
| WireMock rwb-access | The P4 session operation | OpenAPI of P4 | The role, the scope and the Treatment and offer right of the restructuring officer, and the RW-PHONECOL test user with Case record R only (MSG-P4-002) |

Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0414; ASM-0589): the fake set, the TDR model stub and its 61 s and -12 controls, the OFF-policy fixture, the harness environment and seeding, the evidence format and retention, and the pass or fail gate.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `integration/recovery-agent-tdr` in the ACE repository, package `<ACE base package>.recovery.integration.agenttdr`. Not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added | How this harness applies it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none | The harness holds no schema and reads no table: the treatment, the case, the run and the D5 record come through the operations of 12.2 |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The D5 record is read through rwb-decision and the `DecisionRecorded` event is read on the shared topic; the harness never reads a decision table |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none | The account facts behind the suggestion — principal outstanding, days past due, balance, interest rate and payments — are seeded and read back through the case contract, never from an ACE view |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON | The policy versions, the timeout, the output schema limits and the review date are parameter data loaded from files, never values in the harness |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The autonomy modes, the run statuses, the guardrail check name, the treatment types, the decision code "D5" and the final call are seeded reference data |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON | The harness subscribes with its own consumer group and asserts the two events, never a producer's table |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) | The request is one hop on the rwb-agent contract with the 2 s budget, the model call stays inside `AgentRunWorkflow` with the 60 s policy timeout, and the suggestion is read back through the stored output and the D5 record |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none | Every path of 12.2 uses the owner's base, so the harness never calls a monolith base |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The journey runs through the gateway route the treatment screen uses, on the same bases |

The platform H dependencies in the table (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, H RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are delivered by the platform waves and are not repeated in the metadata: the harness converges on them and has no build dependency of its own. The blocking dependencies of this story are the four I stories, which replace the fakes with real services one at a time.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Job | Runs the twelve flow steps for one scenario and one business date and holds the run lock |
| FakeRegistry | Configuration | WireMock mappings for rwb-treatment, rwb-agent, rwb-decision, rwb-case and rwb-access, one set per contract version, plus the TDR model stub selection |
| TdrFixturePack | Data | The case, the account facts, the two treatments, both policy versions, the stub controls and the seeded state each scenario names |
| SuggestionAssertion | Service | Compares the suggested terms, the model code, the model version, the suggestion area and MSG-P10-007 against the fixture, and asserts that the offer fields are untouched |
| DecisionRecordAssertion | Service | Checks the D5 record, its model version, its inputs reference, its suggested terms, its final call and the run's decision log id, including the case where none exists |
| IdempotencyAssertion | Service | Repeats the open for the same treatment and checks the returned suggestion, the returned decision record id and the absence of a second run for the key "TDR_OFFER:<treatmentId>" |
| EvidenceCollector | Service | Writes one report keyed by story key and business date, with the treatment, the suggestion, the run, the decision record, the message and the fallback flag |
| GateEvaluator | Service | Passes the run when every owned scenario passes and the evidence pack is attached, and reports the journey blocked when the start operation is unpublished |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, the wave 2 harness profile, one business date, one synthetic case, two synthetic treatments and masking tokens only. The seeded values are the legacy section 7 Background, the two treatments, both policy versions and the three stub controls; no other value is added. Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0414; ASM-0589): the environment, the seed pack, the evidence format and retention.

**Build steps**

1. Write the TdrFixturePack with the Background, treatments "T-1001" and "T-1002", both policy versions and the three stub controls; test that a bad seed stops the run (X8).
2. Write the FakeRegistry with the five WireMock mapping sets and the TDR model stub selection, with the policy versions, the review date and the reference data loaded from files.
3. Write JourneyRunner for AC1: open the treatment, wait for `AgentRunCompleted` or read the stored output inside the run window, then assert the suggestion and the one run.
4. Add AC3 and AC6 with the decision-record-first ordering, the run's decision log id and the 503.
5. Add AC2 with the OFF policy and the configs read, AC7 with the idempotency key and AC8 with the settlement treatment.
6. Add AC4 and AC5 with the 61 s silence and the installments -12 answer, asserting "TIMED_OUT" with fallback true and "GUARDRAIL_FAILED" with check "SCHEMA".
7. Add AC9 with the RW-PHONECOL user, then write EvidenceCollector and GateEvaluator, attach the report to the wave 2 release record and rerun the nine scenarios on the release build.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.agent.tdr-suggestion` is on in the harness profile, as the legacy story sets it. Off, the suggestion read returns no suggestion and no call is made, and the harness reports the journey as not applicable rather than as passed. The harness itself is a pipeline stage selected by the run profile, not by a business flag.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the run report is attached to the wave 2 release record with all nine owned scenarios, and each fake has been replaced by the real service where its I story has landed in SIT. AC1 passes against the TDR model stub until the TDR model is deployed; that is the legacy done condition and it is unchanged. Until the start operation of the Conflict gap (GAP-0414) is published by both owners, this journey is reported blocked, not passed. The fixture pack and the evidence sign-off wait for the values of the rows cited in sections 3, 12.8 and 15; not specified in the source documents (GAP-0414; ASM-0589): the environment, the seed pack and the evidence format.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P10-007 | No suggestion: model not in service, timeout or failed check | No offer suggestion is available for this treatment. The TDR model is not in service. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The harness asserts these messages and never rewrites them. Its own report text is for the release team and is not part of the message standard.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-14 Treatment record, in the draft state, carries the suggestion area beside the officer's offer fields: ready (the suggested terms with model code "TDR_OFFER" and model version "TDR-OFFER-1.0" and the line "Suggested by TDR_OFFER, version TDR-OFFER-1.0"), unavailable (MSG-P10-007), and unchanged (the officer edits the offer fields as before, with the suggestion never copied into them). In the submitted, approved, booked and broken states the suggestion area shows the recorded terms and no call is made.

No screen is built by this story. The harness drives the operations behind those states and asserts all three through the contracts: the suggestion present with its model version, absent with MSG-P10-007, and the offer fields untouched. The panel and its states belong to RWB-S2-E2032-APP. Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0414; ASM-0589): the labels and the layout of the suggestion area that the harness would assert.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the model code, the model version, the output schema limits, the 60 s timeout, the review date, the autonomy modes and the decision code are data in the seed pack, never values in the harness.
- No personal data in the model request, the events, the workflow inputs, the logs or the evidence. The inputs reference is the masked snapshot, and the seed holds synthetic cases, synthetic treatments and masking tokens only.
- No read of another service's tables and no schema of the harness's own: the account and the treatment come through the owning services' contracts, and the harness runs no migration.
- The suggestion is never written into the offer fields or the treatment status: the harness asserts that the treatment record holds what was suggested beside what was offered, and that nothing moves because a suggestion returned or failed.
- The harness never calls the model endpoint directly: the model call belongs to `AgentRunWorkflow` inside rwb-agent, and the harness only drives the stub behind it as the INT-23 test profile.
- Each fake is replaced by the real service as its I story lands; a fake that outlives its service is a defect, not a configuration.

##### 19. Out of scope

- Building or training the TDR model: it belongs to the TDR team, outside the Workbench, and the harness sees it only through the stub and the private endpoint test profile.
- The settlement and restructure agent proposing plan terms: shadow from Epic 2 and live from Epic 3, per the agent catalogue.
- Affordability and plan calculation in the ACE restructure calculator (R-RES-06).
- Production code of any service in the journey: the operations of rwb-treatment, rwb-agent, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access, their schemas and their screens belong to their own stories.

The harness, the fakes and the evidence pack cover the four items above only as a caller or a consumer would see them; building any of them is out of scope for this story.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-033 for rwb-integration. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the rwb-integration side of the composed case and queue list fixed as a contract: the two read-only operations on the service base, the page shape, the filter set, the breach and clock fields, the error envelope, the read-only idempotency statement, the P3 and P4 operations it consumes and the fakes that stand in for them**, so that **the app story of this legacy key builds on Day 1 against one agreed, testable shape and no team waits for rwb-case or rwb-access to land**.

The legacy story had no contract of its own: the case list, its ageing, its breach filter, its extract and the access-log call sat in one monolith module over one schema, so the shape of a page was whatever `CaseListQueryService` returned. Under D-RCV-60 the case, the queue and the timer belong to rwb-case (Arch v5 slide 41), the rights, the scope and the access log belong to rwb-access, the parameters and the reference data belong to rwb-case (R-PREC default ruling), and the composition that stays with rwb-integration is a consumer of all of them. A composition needs its contract more than an owner does: it has to say what page it answers, which filter values it accepts, which fields it carries, what it does when a source does not answer, and what it never writes.

The contract also fixes the seam the split creates, and the seam is a duplication. The Ownership Map keeps `GET /cases` and `GET /cases/export` with P3 and ADR-020 with DP-19 serves SCR-02 from the owner through gateway-bff; the WP still splits a P2 APP slice that owns AC1 to AC11 of the legacy key. The resolution is the one RWB-P2-E2006-APP recorded for the credit approval pack: the composed read and the export exist as an additional, read-only composition on the integration base, the owner keeps the system-of-record read and its own export, and the duplication is stated in this document and in the gap and assumption rows rather than hidden (GAP-0661; ASM-1133; ASM-1134).

The third thing this document fixes is the second duplication, inside the composition. The ageing and service-level rules of the legacy story run case-side, in the P3 ageing contract, and they run again here, in `AgeingAndBreachCalculator`, so that a page can be filtered by breach and ordered consistently over one page rather than one case at a time. Both evaluations read the same owner fields; the document says which answer is the record and which is the composition, so the two can be tested against each other (ASM-1145).

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling rule (ADR-020) and it only pays off if the seam is written down once. Here the seam is wide: a page over the manager's whole scope, six filter values, twelve columns, two computed clock states, a breach flag, a paging envelope, an Excel file with a row limit and one access-log entry, over six consumed operations in two other services.

If the shape is agreed and faked on Day 1, three things move at once. The app story builds the controller, the composition, the calculator, the clock reader, the validator, the export writer and the screen support against the fakes. The test stories of RWB-E2-033 read one page shape and one column set, so the same assertion runs against the composed page and against the case-side screen. The P3 and P4 contract stories learn exactly which fields and which rights the composition needs, which is the only way the owner's contract gets published with the fields a consumer actually reads.

The contract also states what this service does not own. The case rows, the queue list, the timer projection, the parameters and the reference data are rwb-case's; the right, the scope, the default scope and the access log are rwb-access's. This document defines the consumed side of each and restates none of them as its own. Nothing is copied into `rwb_integration`, and no foreign key leaves the schema.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the REST base, the topic and the event names follow the platform rule and not a local choice (DP-13, DP-14).
- The platform error envelope and the message catalogue are the platform baseline; this document narrows them where it must and says so (ADR-020).
- The parameter and reference-data contracts of rwb-case are as published (RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON; DP-06, DP-07). This document consumes them and fakes them; it defines neither.
- The case-list, ageing and case-record contracts of rwb-case are as published (RWB-P3-E1031-CON, RWB-P3-E2011-CON, RWB-P3-E1018-CON). This document consumes them and names the fields the composition reads.
- The authorise contract and the guard library of rwb-access are as published (RWB-P4-E1037-CON; DP-08), including the access-log operation of an export.
- The gateway-bff composite route that serves SCR-02 Case list is as published (RWB-PLT-N001-CON; DP-19).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the two provided operations: method, path, purpose, right, idempotency and the response of each.
2. Fix the page shape: the row of the composed page, the paging envelope and the twelve columns of the legacy story.
3. Fix the filter set and the validation source of each value: the reference-data lists, the queue list and the parameter bounds.
4. Fix the breach and clock fields: `ageDays`, `serviceLevelDueAt`, `serviceLevelState`, `prescriptionDate` and `prescriptionClockStatus`, with the rule identifiers that produce them.
5. Fix the order and the breach filter, so that two pages of one list are stable and the export with the same filters returns the same row set.
6. Fix the error envelope: 401, 403, 422, 503 and the unavailable answer, with the message identifier of each.
7. Publish the six consumed operations with the element each read needs and the fakes that stand in for them.
8. State the read-only rule: no table, no row, no event, no workflow and no Schedule, and the one access-log entry per export asked of its owner.
9. State the duplication: the P3 case list and export remain the owner's, and this composed read and export are an additional composition with the same fields from the same contracts.
10. Publish the fakes and the drift test, then tag the baseline and hand it to the app story and the test stories of this key.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A filter value is not in the list its owner publishes, or a page size is outside the bounds the parameter contract returns | The contract names the answer as 422 with the field and the list version, so the app can refuse before any case is read | MSG-GEN-007; MSG-GEN-002 | AC3 |
| X2 | A consumed operation has no field in its owner's published contract for an element this document declares | The element carries the placeholder, one gap row and one assumption row, and the fake is written to the assumed shape | None | AC1, AC5 |
| X3 | A fake drifts from this document, or the app calls a path this document does not declare | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC5 |
| X4 | A code path reads a case, queue, timer, role, parameter or reference row of another service, or an ACE view | The architecture boundary test fails the build | None | AC6 |
| X5 | A consumed contract removes, renames or retypes an element this document declares | The contract goes back to review with that owner and the app and test stories are re-baselined | None | AC2, AC3 |
| X6 | The export is asked for above the row limit the parameter contract returns | The contract names 422 with the limit before any file is built, so no partial file can be produced | MSG-P3-021 | AC3 |
| X7 | The access-log entry of an export cannot be recorded | The contract names the answer as 503 with no file, so the app cannot produce a file that has no entry | MSG-P7-003 | AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes and the owners' published operations and declares none of theirs as its own |
| Negotiable | The JSON field names and the problem body are settled with the owners and the app story; the operation set, the columns, the filter set and the read-only rule are fixed by this realignment |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app story and the test stories of this key on Day 1 and tells the P3 and P4 contract stories which fields and rights a consumer reads |
| Estimable | Two provided operations, one page shape, six consumed operations, one error envelope and six fakes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact — the OpenAPI document, the fake, this file — and never against a business outcome |

```gherkin
  Scenario: AC2 The page shape is fixed with its row, its envelope and its columns (new, D-RCV-60)

  Scenario: AC3 The filter set, the breach and clock fields and the order are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the filter and order contract of this story
    When a list is requested with a filter set
    Then the accepted filters are product, stage, status, owner, queue, page, size, sort and breached, and the export takes the same set without page and size
    Then each value is validated against LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS, LOV-STAGE or the queue codes in force, and the page size against the bounds the parameter contract returns
    Then serviceLevelState is one of BREACHED, RUNNING, PAUSED and NONE, and prescriptionClockStatus one of RUNNING, EXPIRED and NONE
    Then the rows are ordered by breach, then age in state descending, then case number, so two pages of one list are stable
    Then an export with the same filters returns the same row set as the pages it covers, and above the row limit it answers 422 with MSG-P3-021

  Scenario: AC4 The error envelope and the read-only idempotency are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the error and idempotency contract of this story
    When each documented answer is reached in a fake
    Then the answers are 200, 401 with MSG-P4-001, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 422 with MSG-GEN-007, MSG-GEN-002 or MSG-P3-021, and 503 with MSG-GEN-006 or MSG-P7-003
    Then the problem body of every error is the platform error envelope, and no answer carries a stack trace, a payload or a personal value
    Then both operations are declared read-only, so a repeat of the same request on unchanged data returns the same rows in the same order and stores no response
    Then the export declares one access-log entry per export, asked of rwb-access, and a refused entry produces no file

  Scenario: AC5 The six fakes match this document and drift fails the build (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the fakes of 12.8
    When each fake is compared with the element it serves
    Then every consumed path and payload is answered with the shape of this document
    Then every documented answer of AC4 is reachable in a fake, including the slow answer for the 2 s budget
    Then a drift between a fake and this document fails the contract test and blocks the merge

  Scenario: AC6 No cross-schema read, no foreign key and the duplication is declared (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the code and the migrations of the app story of this key
    When the architecture boundary test runs
    Then no statement reads a table of another service or an ACE view, and the only cross-service calls are the declared paths of 12.2, one hop each with a 2 s budget
    Then rwb_integration holds no foreign key into another schema and no copy of a case, a queue, a timer, a role, a parameter or a reference row
    Then the document states that GET /cases and GET /cases/export stay with rwb-case and that this composed read and export are an additional read-only composition
    Then no event is published, no workflow is started and no Schedule is created by this slice
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: `/api/recovery/integration/v1`; a document never declares another service's path as its own | DP-13; Arch v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | One topic per service: `rwb.integration.events.v1` with the events FileDelivered and FileFailed, and this slice publishes neither and declares no event name | DP-14; Arch v5 slides 16 and 43; ASM-1143 |
| BR3 | The two provided operations are read-only: a page and an Excel file, no business table, no row, no event and no workflow | Legacy RWB-E2-033 section 9 and section 12; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR4 | The case, the queue, the timer projection, the parameters and the reference data are read only through the rwb-case contracts, and the rights, the scope and the access log only through the rwb-access contract | DP-01; DP-06; DP-07; DP-08; Arch v5 slides 13, 41 and 45 |
| BR5 | `ageDays`, `serviceLevelState`, the breach flag and `prescriptionClockStatus` are computed from the owner's timer and clock fields by the rule identifiers BR2 to BR5 of the app story, and no value is stored | Legacy BR2 to BR5; R-UNI-30; R-DEV-01 |
| BR6 | The order is breach, then age in state descending, then case number, and the export returns the same row set as the pages it covers | Legacy AC1 and AC11; legacy flow step 7 |
| BR7 | Every filter value is a row of its owner's reference data or of the queue list, and the page bounds and the export row limit are parameter rows; no limit and no list value is in the contract as a constant | Legacy BR6 and BR7; DP-06; DP-07 |
| BR8 | The export records one access-log entry, through the rwb-access contract, before the file is made; a refused entry produces no file | Legacy BR7; CTL-11; REQ-ACA-006 |
| BR9 | The page is composed twice by design: rwb-case keeps `GET /cases` and `GET /cases/export`, and this document fixes the additional read-only composition on the integration base | Ownership Map `GET /cases` and `GET /cases/export`; ADR-020; DP-19; GAP-0661; ASM-1133 |
| BR10 | The ageing and service-level rules are evaluated on both sides on the same owner fields; the case-side answer is the record and this one is the composition | Legacy BR2 to BR5; ASM-1145 |
| BR11 | No contract element names a person: the page carries the case number and the owner reference, and no customer field | Legacy guardrail 2; CTL-11 |
| BR12 | The file is produced on request and is never a data-lake file; the data lake is removed | DP-17; Arch v5 slide 37 |

##### 11. Data

The contract declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Page answer | The rows of the caller's scope, the page number, the size and the total count of the legacy page |
| Page row | `caseNo`, `product`, `queue`, `owner` (the text "Unassigned" when empty), `status`, `stage`, `ageDays`, `serviceLevelState`, `serviceLevelDueAt`, `prescriptionDate`, `prescriptionClockStatus`, `deviationOpen` |
| Filter set | `product`, `stage`, `status`, `owner`, `queue`, `page`, `size`, `sort`, `breached`; the export takes the same set without `page` and `size` |
| Validation source | LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-STAGE from the reference-data contract, the queue codes from the queue list, the page bounds and `caselist.export.maxrows` from the parameter contract, each with the version in force |
| Ageing element | `ageDays`, `stageClockStart`, `serviceLevelDueAt`, `serviceLevelState`, `prescriptionDate`, `prescriptionClockStatus` as the ageing contract publishes them for a page of case ids |
| Authorise element | The Case record right, the caller's scope and its default scope, cached per session |
| Access-log element | The user, the time, the filters and the row count of one export, written by rwb-access |
| Error element | The platform error envelope with the message identifier of each answer in AC4 |
| Export file | The Excel column set of the legacy story: case number, product, queue, owner, status, stage, age in state, service level state, service level due, prescription date, prescription clock, deviation open |

The physical names, lengths and required flags of the page, the ageing element and the access-log element are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0661; ASM-1136; ASM-1137; ASM-1140); this document fixes the element names above and leaves the physical names to the review with the rwb-case and rwb-access owners. The exact form of the two provided paths and of the column order of the file are Not specified in the same way.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/integration/v1`; owner rwb-integration (P2). Two operations, both read-only.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/case-list` | The composed case and queue list page: the rows of the caller's scope with the twelve columns of 11, the filter set, the breach filter, the stable order and the paging envelope | Case record R, scope applied, through the rwb-access authorise contract | Read only: the same request on unchanged data returns the same rows in the same order; no response is stored |
| GET | `/case-list/export` | The same filters without page and size, written as an Excel file with the legacy export column set, after one access-log entry is recorded through rwb-access | Case record R, scope applied | Read only on the data; one access-log entry per export |

The Ownership Map keeps `GET /cases` and `GET /cases/export` with P3, so these two paths are not its rows and are fixed here under the service base of DP-13; their exact form and the JSON field names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0661; ASM-1134; ASM-1136). Errors: 401 no session or no Recovery role (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Case record right (MSG-P4-002); 404 a case read that names no case; 422 a filter value outside its list (MSG-GEN-007), a page size outside the bounds (MSG-GEN-002) or an export above its row limit (MSG-P3-021); 503 a consumed contract that does not answer inside the budget (MSG-GEN-006), a database that is unavailable (E503) or an access-log entry that cannot be recorded (MSG-P7-003), which produces no file.

The two operations are the legacy contract shape, kept for the integration base, and they are an additional composition: rwb-case keeps the system-of-record read of the case list and its own export, and the two answers agree on the row, the queue, the owner, the age and the service level state because they read the same contracts (BR9, ASM-1133).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases` | P3 rwb-case | The case rows of the caller's scope with the filters and the paging of the legacy operation; the case-list contract of RWB-P3-E1031-CON |
| GET | The ageing and service-level read of the RWB-P3-E2011-CON contract, for a page of case ids | P3 rwb-case | `ageDays`, `stageClockStart`, `serviceLevelDueAt`, `serviceLevelState`, `prescriptionDate` and `prescriptionClockStatus`, batched so that one page is one hop |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case record read of RWB-P3-E1018-CON, for a field a list row does not carry |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/queues` | P3 rwb-case | The queue codes in force with their team code and role, for the queue filter and its validation |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | The page bounds and `caselist.export.maxrows` with the version in force (DP-06) |
| GET | The reference-data read of the RWB-P3-E1043-CON contract | P3 rwb-case | LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-STAGE with the version in force (DP-07) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The Case record right, the caller's scope and its default scope, cached per session by the guard library (DP-08) |
| POST | The access-log operation of the RWB-P4-E1037-CON contract | P4 rwb-access | One access-log entry per export: the user, the time, the filters and the row count |

Every operation is one hop with a 2 s client budget and no retry on a 4xx (ADR-020). The ageing read, the reference-data read and the access-log operation are named by their owner contract only; their paths, query parameters and JSON field names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0661; ASM-1137; ASM-1139; ASM-1140). The case-list, queue and parameter paths are the Ownership Map rows of P3 under the service base of DP-13, and the authorise path is the one Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access. The per-case timer projection the Ownership Map names, `GET /cases/{caseId}/timers`, is read only through the batched ageing element of this contract, so that one page is one hop.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This slice publishes no event, writes no outbox row and holds no decision record. `rwb.integration.events.v1` carries FileDelivered and FileFailed from the outbound file side of this service (Arch v5 slide 16 and slide 43; ASM-1143), and the decision-record topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` is not used here because the read takes no decision.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The page is composed per request, so this slice subscribes to no topic and holds no inbox: a case that changes is seen on the next read, not through a projection of `CaseStateChanged`, `DeviationRaised` or `TimerBreached`.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. Both operations are synchronous and served inside the request; this document declares no workflow, no activity and no timer. The stage and prescription clocks belong to the case workflow of rwb-case.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. Neither operation is scheduled: the page is read on request and the export is officer-driven. No Schedule, no Temporal timer and no batch window is declared here (Arch v5 slide 44).

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| None | — | This read declares no table of its own: nothing is copied into `rwb_integration` and no row is written (DP-01) |
| `recovery_case`, `queue`, `timer`, `parameter_value`, `reference_row` | P3 rwb-case, in `rwb_case` | Read only through the contracts of 12.2; never read directly and never copied |
| `role`, the access log | P4 rwb-access, in `rwb_access` | Read and written only through the contracts of 12.2; the access-log entry of an export is the owner's row |

The platform library objects `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `outbox_delivery` and `idempotency_key` exist in `rwb_integration` from the service baseline and this slice writes no row in any of them, because a read-only operation stores no response. `interface_config`, `outbound_item` and `job_catalog` stay the file stories' and are untouched here. No foreign key leaves the schema (DP-15 applies to the baseline only; ASM-1142).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `contract/case-list.yaml` (the OpenAPI document of the page: the operation, the filter set, the row, the paging envelope and the error answers), `contract/case-list-export.yaml` (the operation, the column set, the row limit and the file answer), `contract/case-list-consumed.yaml` (the eight consumed operations with the element each read needs), and the six WireMock mappings with their fixtures.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/integration/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library; no event and no topic is added | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence; this slice adds no migration | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Build steps**

1. Write the page document: the operation, the filter set, the twelve columns, the paging envelope and the problem body.
2. Write the export document: the same filters without page and size, the column set, the row limit and the file answer.
3. Write the consumed document for the eight operations, with the element each read needs and the placeholder where the source names no path or field.
4. State the read-only rule and the access-log rule: no table, no row, no event, no workflow, one entry per export.
5. State the duplication: the P3 read and export remain the owner's, and this composition is additional and read-only.
6. Build the six WireMock mappings and their fixtures.
7. Add the six contract tests of section 16, including the drift test between each fake and this document.
8. Tag the baseline and collect the sign-off of the app story and the test stories of this key.

**Done when.** The three contract files validate in the pipeline, the six contract tests pass, the six fakes answer every consumed path, every answer of AC4 and the slow answer, and the app story of this legacy key has accepted the baseline.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the page bounds, the export row limit, the lists and the service levels are rows of their owners' parameter and reference data, read with the version in force.
- No personal data in a page, a filter, a file or a fake: the case number, the owner reference and the codes only, and every fixture is synthetic.
- The contract names only rwb-integration's own operations as provided; the P3 and P4 operations are consumed and are never restated as this service's (DP-01, DP-13).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base as provided, or a topic outside `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- The case, the queue and the timer appear nowhere as objects of this service, and no foreign key leaves `rwb_integration` (DP-01, DP-15).
- The read is declared read-only, so a contract that lets the app write a row, publish an event or start a workflow fails this document.
- The duplication with the P3 case list and export is stated in 12.1, 12.7 and BR9, and a change that hides it fails the review.

##### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **every case in every queue in my scope on the case list with its identifier, product, queue, owner, status, age in state, stage and prescription clock states and service level breach flag, with a breach filter and an extract**, so that **I can see where work is waiting without asking anyone**.

The legacy story extended the case-list operation and the case export of the monolith, served by `CaseAndWorkflowController`, `CaseListQueryService`, `PrescriptionClockReader`, `AgeingCalculator` and `CaseExportService`, reading `recovery_case`, `queue` and `timer` in the shared recovery schema. Under D-RCV-60 the case, the queue, the timer and the task are rwb-case's (Arch v5 slide 41), the roles, the scope, the rights and the access log are rwb-access's, the parameters and the reference data are rwb-case's (R-PREC default ruling), and no service reads another service's table (DP-01). What stays with rwb-integration is the composition: a read-only case-list page and an Excel export on the integration base, `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/case-list` and `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/case-list/export`, composed per request from the P3 case-list and ageing contracts, the P4 authorise contract, the P3 parameter contract and the P3 reference-data contract, with the breach filter, the prescription clock, the deviation flag and the stable order of the legacy story applied to the composed page.

The Ownership Map keeps `GET /cases` and `GET /cases/export` with P3, and ADR-020 with DP-19 puts the screens directly on the owner services through gateway-bff. This story does not move that ownership: rwb-case keeps the system-of-record read of the case list and its own export, and the composed page and the file on the integration base are an additional, read-only composition for the integration slice of this legacy key. That the same page is now composed twice, once case-side and once integration-side, is recorded as a gap and an assumption and is not hidden (GAP-0660; ASM-1133). The precedent is the credit approval pack of RWB-P2-E2006-APP, which records the same deliberate double composition.

The slice writes no business row. It reads nothing from another schema, holds no copy of a case, a queue or a timer, publishes no event, starts no workflow and creates no Schedule, because the legacy story wrote nothing either. Its only write is the access-log entry of an export, which is the rwb-access owner's row and is asked for through the owner's contract; the file itself is produced on request and is never a data-lake file (DP-17).

##### 2. Business rationale

A team manager today learns where cases wait by asking each owner or by building a spreadsheet. The legacy story completed the case list for every queue in the manager's scope: a breach filter, the prescription clock beside the stage clock so a paused case is not read as safe, and the same columns in the extract. It meets REQ-WKM-002 (every queue in the team, filtered by status, product and ageing, with an export), REQ-DVH-006 (the deviation flag is visible in every queue view) and REQ-ACA-006 (a read of the case store is written to the access log), and the business measure is the count of cases past their service level per queue, which the manager can read every morning.

In the target the facts are in the same place but the path changes. The case rows, the queue and the timer projection are case facts of rwb-case (DP-01), so they are read through the case-list and ageing contracts and never from `recovery_case`, `queue` or `timer`. The roles, the scope and the rights are data of rwb-access (Arch v5 slide 41), so the authorise check is one call of its contract (DP-08). The page size limits and the export row limit are parameters of rwb-case (DP-06), and the lists the filter values are checked against are reference data of rwb-case (DP-07), so neither is written in code. Every call is one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker, built on Day 1 against its fake (DP-11 as it applies to the consumed contracts, ADR-020).

The composition survives a boundary that the monolith did not have. Inside one service, a page and its extract read the same rows in the same transaction; across a contract there is no shared transaction, so the story fixes the two rules that keep the two answers consistent: the page and the export are read with the same filter set and the same stable order, and the export re-reads at the moment of the request rather than reusing a page from the browser. A case that changes between two page requests is therefore ordered by case number, never by a row number, which is what AC11 asserts.

The duplication is the one deliberate cost, and it is stated. The ageing and service-level rules (BR2 to BR5) are evaluated twice: by the P3 ageing contract for the case-side screen, and by `AgeingAndBreachCalculator` here for the composed page and the export, on the same timer and clock inputs. The two answers agree because both read the same owner's fields; where they could disagree, the case-side answer is the record and this page is the composition (GAP-0660; ASM-1145).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P2-E2033-CON is published and baselined: the two provided operations, the page shape, the filter set, the breach and clock fields, the error envelope, the read-only idempotency statement and the contract fakes of this story.
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1042-CON are published: the parameter contract of rwb-case and the client library. `caselist.export.maxrows` (assumed 10,000 in the legacy story, DL11) and the case-list page bounds are rows of that contract, not code (DP-06; ASM-1138).
- RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are published: the reference-data contract of rwb-case, which carries LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-STAGE with the version in force (DP-07; ASM-1139).
- RWB-PLT-E1037-CON and RWB-P4-E1037-CON are published: the authorise contract, the guard library that caches the rights of a session, and the access-log operation of an export (DP-08).
- RWB-PLT-E1047-CON is published: the naming library, so the REST base, the topic name and the event names of this service follow the platform rule and not a local choice (DP-13, DP-14).
- RWB-PLT-E1044-CON is published: the per-service Flyway sequence and the migration conventions of `rwb_integration` (DP-15). This story adds no migration, because it stores nothing (ASM-1142).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route that serves SCR-02 Case list (DP-19).
- RWB-P3-E1031-CON is published: the case-list contract of rwb-case, which fixes the row of the composed page and the filter set this story passes through.
- RWB-P3-E2011-CON is published: the ageing and service-level contract of rwb-case, which publishes `ageDays`, `stageClockStart`, `serviceLevelDueAt`, `serviceLevelState`, `prescriptionDate` and `prescriptionClockStatus` for a case (DP-01; ASM-1137).
- RWB-P3-E1018-CON is published: the case record read of rwb-case, used when a list row does not carry a field the composition needs.
- The role to permission matrix gives RW-TEAMMGR the Case record right R with Team scope, and the caller is signed in through Entra ID with a role that holds Case record R.
- The queues of the teams are loaded in rwb-case, with their team and their role, and are read through the queue list of its contract, never from a table of this service.
- The feature switch `rwb.casewf.case-list-ageing` is carried to the platform flag library and is on; while it is off the breach filter and the clock columns are not served (ASM-1144).
- The login is the rwb-integration login (DP-02): Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0660; ASM-1135).

##### 4. Flow

1. Team manager: opens SCR-02 Case list through gateway-bff and chooses the filters (DP-19).
2. gateway-bff: calls `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/case-list` on rwb-integration, one hop, and merges the answer into the SCR-02 screen model.
3. rwb-integration: checks the Case record right and the caller's scope through the rwb-access authorise contract, cached per session by the guard library; a role without Case record R is a 403 and nothing is read (DP-08).
4. rwb-integration: validates each filter value against its list of values read through the rwb-case reference-data contract, the queue code against the queue list of the rwb-case contract, and the page size against the bounds read through the rwb-case parameter contract (DP-06, DP-07).
5. rwb-integration: reads the page of cases in the caller's scope through the rwb-case case-list contract, with the filters and the paging the legacy operation used; the contract is the only path to the rows (DP-01).
6. rwb-integration: reads the ageing and service-level fields of that page of case ids through the rwb-case ageing contract, batched so that one page is one hop: `ageDays`, `stageClockStart`, `serviceLevelDueAt`, `serviceLevelState`, `prescriptionDate` and `prescriptionClockStatus`.
7. rwb-integration: `AgeingAndBreachCalculator` applies BR2 to BR5 to those inputs, so the page carries the age in state, the service level state and the breach flag of the legacy story, and `PrescriptionClockReader` resolves the prescription clock state and its date beside the stage clock.
8. rwb-integration: applies the breach filter when `breached` is set and orders the rows by breach, then age in state descending, then case number, and returns one page with its paging envelope.
9. Front end: shows the columns of section 15 and marks each breached case with the text "Breached", never by colour alone.
10. Team manager: chooses Extract; the front end calls `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/case-list/export` with the same filters and without page and size.
11. rwb-integration: reads the parameter `caselist.export.maxrows` and refuses the export with 422 when the matching rows exceed it, before any file is built.
12. rwb-integration: records one access-log entry through the rwb-access contract, with the user, the time, the filters and the row count; a refused entry stops the export and no file is produced.
13. rwb-integration: writes the matching rows with the ageing and clock columns to an Excel file and returns it as a download; the file is produced on request and is stored nowhere (DP-17).
14. rwb-integration: answers the export with the file and with `Cache-Control: no-store`; the read is idempotent, so the same request on unchanged data returns the same rows in the same order and the access log holds one entry per export.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A filter value is not in its list of values, for example product CAR | Request refused with 422 before any case is read | MSG-GEN-007 | AC6 |
| X2 | Page size below 1 or above 200 | Request refused with 422 | MSG-GEN-002 | AC7 |
| X3 | No case matches the filters | Empty state; the extract holds the header row only | MSG-P3-020 | AC8 |
| X4 | A queue filter names a queue outside the caller's scope | Only cases in scope are returned, so the result is empty | MSG-P3-020 | AC9 |
| X5 | A case has no SERVICE_LEVEL timer yet (status New) | `serviceLevelState` NONE; `breached` false | None | AC5 |
| X6 | The service level due time equals the current time | Not breached; breached from the next minute | None | AC4 |
| X7 | The extract would hold more than 10,000 rows | Extract refused before any file is built | MSG-P3-021 | AC10 |
| X8 | A case changes between two page requests | Order is stable by case number, so no case is skipped or repeated by the order | None | AC11 |
| X9 | The caller's role does not hold Case record R | Refused with 403 before any contract is called; nothing is read and nothing is logged as an export | MSG-P4-002 | Access test TC-E2-033-12 |
| X10 | A consumed contract (rwb-case case list, ageing, queues, parameters, reference data, or rwb-access) does not answer inside the 2 s budget | One hop, 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream; no partial page and no file is returned, and a page is never answered from a stale cache | MSG-GEN-006 | AC1, AC3 |
| X11 | The access-log entry of an export cannot be recorded | No file is produced and nothing is written; the export is refused | MSG-P7-003 | AC3 |

X10 is the mechanism that replaces the legacy in-process calls: a page that cannot be composed has no answer to show, so the failure is a 503 and not a thinner page. X11 is a refusal and not a degradation: an export that cannot be recorded is not made (BR7 in the legacy story, kept here).

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on Day 1 against the published contracts: this key's contract baseline, the parameter and reference-data contracts, the authorise contract, the naming library, the migration conventions and the edge route. The rwb-case and rwb-access answers come from their contract fakes |
| Negotiable | The export columns, the filter set and the page bounds are fixed by the legacy story; the list values, the limits and the queue codes are data rows of their owners |
| Valuable | Gives the manager the whole of the team's work in one list and one file, and keeps the case facts with rwb-case |
| Estimable | Two operations, one composition service, one calculator, one clock reader, one export writer, six consumed contracts and one page of screen support |
| Small | Fits one iteration with its tests, and writes no business row |
| Testable | Each owned criterion is one automated test against the contract fakes; the access case is a component test and the boundary case is an architecture test |
