AC1 to AC11 are the criteria this story owns; every value is copied unchanged from the legacy story and the only additions are the `Given` lines that state what each contract mock returns. The rwb-case contracts answer the rows, the queues, the ageing and service-level fields, the prescription clock, the deviation flag, the list values and the two parameter limits. The rwb-access contract answers the Case record right, the scope and the access-log entry of an export. The breach decision at the boundary (AC4), the age in state (AC1, AC2), the paused clock (AC2), the absent timer (AC5) and the order (AC1, AC11) are this story's own computation on those inputs, which is why they are asserted here and not stubbed. X9 is proved by TC-E2-033-12 against this story's own operation.

The page is composed twice in the target. rwb-case keeps `GET /cases` and `GET /cases/export` and the case-side screen, and this story composes the same page on the integration base for the integration slice of this legacy key. The duplication is deliberate and recorded (GAP-0660; ASM-1133); the values the two answers share are read from the same P3 contracts, so they agree on the row, the queue, the owner, the age and the service level state.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The list holds only cases in the caller's scope: Own, Team or All, from the role's default scope, read through the rwb-access authorise contract | `role.default_scope` through the P4 contract; CTL-09; DP-08 |
| BR2 | Age in state is the whole number of calendar days from `stage_clock_start` (or `entry_date` when it is empty) to today in Asia/Bangkok | `recovery_case.stage_clock_start`, `entry_date` through the P3 ageing contract; legacy RWB-E2-011 `ageDays` |
| BR3 | A case is breached when its SERVICE_LEVEL timer has status EXPIRED, or has status RUNNING with `expires_at` earlier than now. A breach does not move the case | R-UNI-30; timer status through the P3 ageing contract |
| BR4 | A deviation pauses the stage clock and keeps the prescription clock running; the list shows both; a paused SERVICE_LEVEL timer is never breached | R-DEV-01; timer `paused` through the P3 ageing contract |
| BR5 | `prescriptionClockStatus` is RUNNING or EXPIRED from the PRESCRIPTION timer, and NONE when the case has no such timer | timer type; LOV-TIMER-STATUS; the P3 ageing contract |
| BR6 | Filter values are checked against LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-STAGE and against the queue codes in force, all read through their owners' contracts | lists of values; the P3 queue list; DP-07 |
| BR7 | The extract holds at most `caselist.export.maxrows` rows, carries no customer personal field, and is written to the access log before the file is made | legacy RWB-E1-031; CTL-11; REQ-ACA-006; DP-06 |
| BR8 | The service reads no case, queue, timer, role, parameter or reference row of another service: every fact comes through the owner's contract, one hop, and `rwb_integration` holds no copy and no foreign key into another schema | Arch v5 slides 13, 41 and 45; DP-01; ADR-010; ADR-020 |
| BR9 | The page and the export are read-only: no business row is written, no event is published, no workflow is started and no Schedule is created; the only write is the access-log entry of an export, asked for through the rwb-access contract | legacy BR and section 9; DP-17; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR10 | The page size limits and the export row limit are parameter rows of rwb-case read with the version in force; no limit is written in code | DP-06; legacy guardrail 1 |
| BR11 | The file is produced on request for the officer and is never a data-lake file; the data lake is removed | DP-17; Arch v5 slide 37; ASM-1146 |
| BR12 | The switch is the platform feature flag `rwb.casewf.case-list-ageing`; while it is off, the breached parameter is ignored and the list and export keep the columns of the case-side read | legacy solution plan; platform flag library (ASM-1144) |
| BR13 | The ageing and service-level rules are evaluated on both sides: the P3 ageing contract for the case-side screen, and `AgeingAndBreachCalculator` here for the composed page and the export, on the same owner fields; the case-side answer is the record | GAP-0660; ASM-1145 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status and does not move a case. It reads the case rows, the queue list and the timer projection through their owners' contracts and, for an export, writes one access-log entry through the rwb-access contract.

| Observed fact | Written by | Appears as |
|---|---|---|
| Case number, product, queue, owner, status, stage, entry date, stage clock start, deviation flag | rwb-case (P3) | The row of the page and of the file |
| Age in state, service level due, service level state, prescription date, prescription clock state | rwb-case (P3) ageing contract, re-applied here by BR2 to BR5 | The computed columns of the page and of the file |
| Queue code, team code and queue role | rwb-case (P3) | The queue filter values and their validation |
| Case record right, scope and default scope | rwb-access (P4) | Whether the caller sees a page, and which rows |
| Access-log entry of an export | rwb-access (P4) | One log row per export, with the user, the time, the filters and the row count |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads and extracts the list for the team's queues (Case record R, Team scope) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads and extracts the list for the cases they own (Case record R, Own scope) |
| RW-PRODHEAD, RW-AUDIT, RW-CONDUCT and other roles with Case record R | Read and extract the list in their scope |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | No Case record right; refused with MSG-P4-002 |
| rwb-integration service identity (the rwb-integration login, DP-02) | Applies the access check, calls the P3 and P4 contracts one hop away, composes the page, builds the file and writes nothing but the owner's access-log entry |
| rwb-case, through its contracts | Owns the case, the queue, the timer projection, the parameters and the reference data; is the record of the case-side list and of its own export |
| rwb-access, through its contracts | Owns the right, the scope, the masking policy and the access log; the export entry is its row |
| gateway-bff (the platform edge) | Calls the composed operation once and merges the answer into the SCR-02 screen model; holds no copy of a case |
| No approval applies | The story takes no decision |

The service runs as the rwb-integration login (DP-02). The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0660; ASM-1135).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/integration/v1`; owner rwb-integration (P2).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/case-list` | The composed case and queue list page: the rows of the caller's scope with case number, product, queue, owner, status, stage, age in state, service level state, service level due, prescription date, prescription clock state and deviation open, the filter set, the breach filter, the stable order and the paging envelope | Case record R, scope applied, through the rwb-access authorise contract | Read only: the same request on unchanged data returns the same rows in the same order; no response is stored |
| GET | `/case-list/export` | The same filters without page and size, written as an Excel file with the legacy export columns, after the access-log entry is recorded | Case record R, scope applied | Read only on the data; each export records its own access-log entry |

The Ownership Map keeps `GET /cases` and `GET /cases/export` with P3 and ADR-020 with DP-19 puts SCR-02 on the owner service through gateway-bff, so the composed page and the export on the integration base are an additional read-only composition and not a move of the owner's operation (GAP-0660; ASM-1133; ASM-1134). The two paths are not rows of the Ownership Map and are fixed here under the service base of DP-13; their exact form and the JSON field names of the page, the filter set and the problem body are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0660; ASM-1134; ASM-1136).

The query parameters are the legacy ones: `product`, `stage`, `status`, `owner`, `queue`, `page`, `size`, `sort` and `breached` (true or false), and the export takes the same set without `page` and `size`. Each row carries `caseNo`, `product`, `queue`, `owner` (with the text "Unassigned" when it is empty), `status`, `stage`, `ageDays`, `serviceLevelState` (BREACHED, RUNNING, PAUSED or NONE), `serviceLevelDueAt`, `prescriptionDate`, `prescriptionClockStatus` (RUNNING, EXPIRED or NONE) and `deviationOpen`. Errors: 401 no session or no Recovery role (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Case record right (MSG-P4-002); 422 a filter value outside its list (MSG-GEN-007), a page size outside 1 to 200 (MSG-GEN-002) or an export above its row limit (MSG-P3-021); 503 a consumed contract does not answer inside the budget (MSG-GEN-006) or a database is unavailable (E503); and 503 an access-log entry that cannot be recorded (MSG-P7-003), which produces no file.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (ADR-020). The Ownership Map and the P3, P4 contract stories name the owners; this story declares only the consumed side.

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases` | rwb-case (P3) | The case rows of the caller's scope with the filters and the paging of the legacy operation; the case-list contract of RWB-P3-E1031-CON | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | The ageing and service-level read of the RWB-P3-E2011-CON contract, for a page of case ids | rwb-case (P3) | `ageDays`, `stageClockStart`, `serviceLevelDueAt`, `serviceLevelState`, `prescriptionDate` and `prescriptionClockStatus`, batched so that one page is one hop; the per-case projection the Ownership Map names is `GET /cases/{caseId}/timers` | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/queues` | rwb-case (P3) | The queue codes in force with their team code and role, for the queue filter and its validation | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | rwb-case (P3) | The case record read of RWB-P3-E1018-CON, used when a list row does not carry a field the composition needs | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | The reference-data read of the RWB-P3-E1043-CON contract | rwb-case (P3) | LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-STAGE with the version in force (DP-07) | One hop, 2 s, cached |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | rwb-case (P3) | `caselist.export.maxrows` and the case-list page bounds, with the version in force (DP-06) | One hop, 2 s, cached |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | rwb-access (P4) | The Case record right, the caller's scope and its default scope, cached per session by the guard library (DP-08) | One hop, 2 s, cached |
| POST | The access-log operation of the RWB-P4-E1037-CON contract | rwb-access (P4) | One access-log entry per export: the user, the time, the filters and the row count; a refusal fails the export | One hop, 2 s |

The path of the ageing read, the path of the reference-data read and the path and the row shape of the access-log operation are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0660; ASM-1137; ASM-1139; ASM-1140). The case-list, queue and parameter paths are the Ownership Map rows of P3 under the service base of DP-13, and the queue codes come from that queue list and not from a queue table of this service (ASM-1147); the authorise path is the one Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The composed read and the export publish no event, write no outbox row and hold no decision record. The service's topic `rwb.integration.events.v1` carries only FileDelivered and FileFailed, which belong to the file stories of this service (Arch v5 slide 16 and slide 43), and this story declares no topic and no event name of its own (DP-14).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The page is composed per request through the owners' contracts and subscribes to no topic: a case that changes is seen on the next read, not through a projection of `CaseStateChanged`, `DeviationRaised` or `TimerBreached`, and no inbox row is written by this story.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The page and the export are served inside the request: no workflow, no activity, no signal and no timer. The stage clock and the prescription clock belong to the case workflow of rwb-case, which this story only reads through its contract.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The legacy story had no job and the target adds none: the page is read on request and the export is officer-driven, so no Schedule, no Temporal timer and no batch window is created by this story (Arch v5 slide 44).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | — | — | This story creates, reads and writes no table; nothing is copied into `rwb_integration` (DP-01, BR8) |
| `recovery_case`, `queue`, `timer`, `role`, `parameter_value`, `reference_row` | each owner's own schema | rwb-case (P3) and rwb-access (P4) | The facts behind the consumed contracts; this story never reads them |
| The access log | rwb_access | rwb-access (P4) | One entry per export, written by the owner through its contract |

The `rwb_integration` schema holds interface config, file runs and outbound items for the file stories of this service (Arch v5 slide 41), and the platform library objects `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `outbox_delivery` and `idempotency_key` exist in it from the service baseline. This story adds no table, no column and no index to any of them, writes no row in any of them, and adds no migration in the service's Flyway sequence (DP-15, ASM-1142).

| rwb-case WireMock — reference data and parameters | The P3 contracts of RWB-P3-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1042-CON | LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-STAGE with the version in force, LOV-PRODUCT without `CAR` for AC6; page size minimum 1, maximum 200 and `caselist.export.maxrows` 10,000 |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.integration`, module `caselist`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.integration.caselist`; front end support `src/modules/recovery/integration/caselist/CaseListPage.tsx`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables; here the case, the queue and the timer come from rwb-case's contracts | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/integration/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library; no event and no topic is added here | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema; this story adds no migration | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-14 applies to the names of this service and not to a new event: the topic `rwb.integration.events.v1` and the events FileDelivered and FileFailed stay the file stories', and this slice publishes nothing (12.3). DP-15 applies to the service baseline and not to this read: the story adds no table and no migration, and the H dependency is on the conventions of the sequence (ASM-1142).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CaseListController | Controller | `GET /case-list` and `GET /case-list/export`; the parameter binding, the error mapping and the `Cache-Control: no-store` header |
| CaseListCompositionService | Service | Composes the page: the access check, the filter validation, the case rows, the ageing fields, the breach filter, the order and the paging envelope |
| AgeingAndBreachCalculator | Service | Pure functions for BR2 to BR5, unit tested without a database: age in state, the service level state, the breach flag, the boundary rule and the paused rule |
| PrescriptionClockReader | Service | Resolves `prescriptionClockStatus` and `prescriptionDate` from the PRESCRIPTION timer of the ageing answer (BR5) |
| FilterValidator | Service | Checks each filter value against the reference-data lists and the queue codes in force, and the page size against the parameter bounds |
| CaseExportService | Service | Re-reads with the same filters, applies the row limit, asks for the access-log entry first, and writes the legacy columns |
| ExportWorkbookWriter | Component | Writes the Excel file of the legacy column set in the request; the file is streamed to the caller and stored nowhere |
| CaseListClient | Client | The case rows through the rwb-case case-list contract (DP-01) |
| AgeingClient | Client | The ageing and service-level fields of a page of case ids through the rwb-case contract, batched to one hop |
| QueueCatalog | Service | The queue codes, their teams and their roles through the rwb-case queue list |
| ParameterReader | Service | `caselist.export.maxrows` and the page bounds through the rwb-case parameter contract with the version in force (DP-06) |
| ReferenceCatalog | Service | LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-STAGE through the reference-data contract with the version in force (DP-07) |
| AccessCheckClient | Client | The Case record right and the scope through the rwb-access authorise contract, cached per session by the guard library (DP-08) |
| AccessLogClient | Client | One access-log entry per export through the rwb-access contract; a refusal fails the export |
| SourceCallGuard | Component | Wraps each contract call with the 2 s timeout, a breaker and a bulkhead, and turns a failure into the unavailable answer (X10) |
| CaseListPage | React component | The SCR-02 columns, the breach filter, the breach marker, the paused marker and the empty state; the screen is served through gateway-bff (DP-19) |

**Database and migrations**

- No table, no column and no index: the read copies nothing and the schema `rwb_integration` is not touched by this story (BR8, BR9).
- No migration in the rwb-integration Flyway sequence. DP-15 is satisfied by the baseline of RWB-P2-E1007-APP and by the conventions of RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (ASM-1142).
- The service connects with its own login, `rwb_integration`, holding grants on its own schema only and no grant on `recovery` or on another `rwb_*` schema (DP-02, Arch v5 slide 29). The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0660; ASM-1135).

**Configuration and reference data**

- `caselist.export.maxrows` (assumed 10,000 in the legacy story, DL11) and the case-list page bounds are rows of the rwb-case parameter contract, read with the version in force; no limit is in code (DP-06; ASM-1138).
- LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-STAGE are rows of the rwb-case reference-data contract with the version in force, and the queue codes are those of the rwb-case queue list; no code value is in code (DP-07; ASM-1139).
- The feature switch keeps the legacy name `rwb.casewf.case-list-ageing` as its reference. In the target it is a feature flag of the platform flag library (R-PREC default ruling; the Ownership Map gives `feature_flag` to PLT); off ignores the breached parameter and serves the case-side columns only (BR12; ASM-1144).

**Build steps**

1. `CaseListCompositionService` and `CaseListController` against the contract fakes, with the filter set, the paging envelope and one test per AC; AC1, AC8, AC9.
2. `CaseListClient` and `AgeingClient` over the rwb-case contracts, with the batched ageing read so that one page is one hop; AC1, AC2, AC5.
3. `AgeingAndBreachCalculator` and `PrescriptionClockReader` with unit tests for BR2 to BR5, including the boundary of AC4 and the paused clock of AC2; AC1, AC2, AC4, AC5.
4. `FilterValidator` with `ReferenceCatalog`, `QueueCatalog` and `ParameterReader`, so no list value and no limit is in code; AC6, AC7.
5. `AccessCheckClient` and the scope refusal with 403; the access case of section 16.
6. `CaseExportService` and `ExportWorkbookWriter` with the legacy column set, the row limit from the parameter contract, and the access-log entry recorded before the file is built; AC3, AC8, AC10.
7. The stable order by breach, age in state and case number, with the two-page test; AC11.
8. `SourceCallGuard` with the timeout, the breaker and the unavailable answer; X10 as a component test.
9. `CaseListPage` against the gateway-bff stub, with the list, filtered, paused, breached and empty states of section 15.
10. The contract-fake run of every consumed answer in isolation and the architecture test that no statement reaches another schema, so the story builds before rwb-case and rwb-access land.

**Feature switch.** The legacy flag name `rwb.casewf.case-list-ageing` is kept as the legacy reference for the switch. In the target the switch is a feature flag of the platform flag library (Template and Rules §R3 default ruling; Ownership Map `feature_flag` is PLT); off ignores the breached parameter and keeps the case-side columns (ASM-1144).

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, page 1 of the list over 23,600 synthetic cases returns in under 2 seconds at the 95th percentile in SIT (NFR-008 as the legacy story states it), the export of 10,000 rows completes and one access-log entry is recorded per export, the contract tests of RWB-P3-E1031-CON, RWB-P3-E2011-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON and RWB-P4-E1037-CON stay green, and no query of this story reaches the `recovery` schema or another `rwb_*` schema.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-007 | A filter value is not in its list | {value} is not a valid value for {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | Page size outside 1 to 200 | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-P3-020 | No case matches the filters | No cases match these filters. Change a filter to see more. |
| MSG-P3-021 | Extract above the row limit | The export holds at most {max} rows. Narrow the filters and try again. |
| MSG-P4-001 | No valid session | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role lacks Case record R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The export access event cannot be recorded | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A consumed contract does not answer inside the budget | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0660; ASM-1136) |

MSG-GEN-007 to MSG-P7-003 are copied unchanged from the legacy story, and no identifier is renumbered by the realignment. MSG-GEN-006 is the platform unavailable message; its text is fixed by the Error and Message Standard and not by this story, so the placeholder stands here (ASM-1136). MSG-P1-001 does not arise in this story, because the composed page carries no ACE data product and no freshness stamp. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

| Screen | State | What the user does |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-02 Case list | Loading | Sees the list placeholder while the composed operation answers |
| SCR-02 Case list | List | Reads the columns case number, product, queue, owner, status, stage, age in state, service level state, service level due, prescription date, prescription clock and deviation |
| SCR-02 Case list | Filtered | Sets filters for queue, product, status, stage, owner and breached, and reads the filtered page |
| SCR-02 Case list | Empty | Reads the empty message MSG-P3-020 when no case matches |
| SCR-02 Case list | Breached marker | Reads the text "Breached" on a breached row, never colour alone |
| SCR-02 Case list | Paused marker | Reads "Paused" on a case whose stage clock is paused, with the prescription clock beside it |
| SCR-02 Case list | Extract | Chooses Extract with the same filters and receives the Excel file, or the row-limit message MSG-P3-021 |

The screen is SCR-02 Case list and is served by the gateway-bff composite route, which calls rwb-integration once and merges the answer into the case screen model, one hop (DP-19). The route path, the screen-model field list and the merge order are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0660; ASM-1141) and belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the case-side slice RWB-P3-E2033-APP carries the screen work of the owner's own list, and this story supplies the page model, the columns and the states above for the composed page.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: page size limits, the export limit, the lists and the service levels are read from the parameter catalog and the reference tables through their owners' contracts; the story fixes only the behaviour.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or prompts; the page and the extract carry the case number, the owner reference and no customer field, and test data is synthetic.
- No read of another service's tables and no ACE view: the case, the queue and the timer come only through the rwb-case contracts, the rights and the access log only through the rwb-access contract, and the service holds no grant on the `recovery` schema or on another `rwb_*` schema (DP-01, DP-08, ADR-010).
- The breach flag is computed at read time; the story never changes a timer or a case, and a refusal writes nothing.
- One hop, no chaining: the operation never calls a downstream of a downstream, and the breaker and bulkhead are per downstream (ADR-020).
- The export carries no customer personal field, is recorded in the access log before the file is made, and is never written to a data lake (DP-17).
- The page and the export are read-only: no business row, no decision record, no event and no workflow state (BR9).
- A role without the Case record right sees a refusal, never a partial list and never another role's rows (X9).

##### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR)**, I want **the case and queue list served by rwb-case from its own `rwb_case` rows, each row carrying the case number, the product group, the queue, the owner, the status, the stage, the age in state in days, the age since entry, the service level state and due time, the prescription date and the prescription clock, with the filters checked against the lists in force, the page bounds and the extract row limit read as parameter rows, a stable order, and a drill down from a queue**, so that **every case in every queue in my scope is on one list I can trust without asking anyone, and the age I read is the age of the owner's own row**.

This is the case-list slice of legacy RWB-E2-033. Inside `rwb-case` it is served on the service's own base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, from schema `rwb_case`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1` and task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`.

- The legacy story extended the monolith's `GET monolith-base/cases`, its export and `CaseListQueryService`, `PrescriptionClockReader`, `AgeingCalculator` and `CaseExportService`, reading `recovery_case`, `queue` and `timer` in the shared recovery schema. Those tables are rwb-case's own (DP-01), so this slice is the owner's read of them with no contract between the service and its tables.
- The composed screen and the workbook on the integration base are RWB-P2-E2033-APP's and read this service through RWB-P2-E2033-CON; the rights, the scope rows and the access log are rwb-access's (DP-08); the deviation record behind the open flag is rwb-deviation's; the end-to-end journey is RWB-ITG-E2033-ITG. The list served here and the list composed there are the same facts twice, which is the stated cost of the split (GAP-2224; ASM-3661).
- The export itself — the workbook, its columns and the access-log entry that precedes it — is RWB-P3-E1031-APP, which owns that operation of this base. This slice owns the one invariant the legacy story added to it: at most `caselist.export.maxrows` rows, refused before anything is written (BR11). The queue summary counts, the cap use and the queue screens are RWB-P3-E2011-APP's, whose `ageDays` and page-size rows this slice re-uses and does not redefine.
- The rights are the legacy ones: `RW-TEAMMGR` with Team scope, `RW-CASEOWN` with Own scope, `RW-PRODHEAD`, `RW-AUDIT` and `RW-CONDUCT` in their scope, and a role with no Case record right refused with MSG-P4-002.

This secondary slice owns no legacy acceptance criterion: legacy AC1 to AC11 are carried by RWB-P2-E2033-APP, and the legacy test set TC-E2-033-01 to TC-E2-033-12 is kept here against this slice's own assertions, so the values the legacy story fixed are proved on the owner's rows as well as on the composed page.

The slice writes no business row: it reads `recovery_case`, `queue` and `timer` in `rwb_case`, computes the ages and the service level state at read time, publishes no event, starts no workflow, creates no Schedule and holds no foreign key to another service (DP-01).

##### 2. Business rationale

A team manager today learns where cases wait by asking each owner or by building a spreadsheet. The legacy story completed the case list for every queue in the manager's scope — a breach filter, the prescription clock beside the stage clock so a paused case is not read as safe, and the same columns in the extract — and met REQ-WKM-002 (every queue in the team, filtered by status, product and ageing, with an export), REQ-DVH-006 (the deviation flag in every queue view) and REQ-ACA-006 (a read of the case store is written to the access log). The business measure is the count of cases past their service level per queue, read every morning.

In the target the facts stay where they are and the read moves with them. The case, the queue and the timer are rwb-case's, so the list is served by the owner of the rows: one query, one transaction, the same filter set and the same order for the page and for the limit check that guards the extract. A reader cannot be told a different age by a service that copied the case.

With about 23,600 open cases at go-live and 26,500 at the end of 2027 (NFR-001) and about 370 staff online in the busiest hour (NFR-002), this is the largest read in the Workbench and it has to stay inside the 2 s target of NFR-008. The mechanism is unchanged: one indexed query, the open timers joined once per page, the ages computed in the service, and the bounds read as parameter rows so a limit change is a data change.

Three rules do the visible work. The age in state is what the case has waited where it stands, not the age of the case (BR2), so a case that has just moved must not read as months old. A deviation pauses the stage clock and never the prescription clock (BR4), which is the failure the legacy story was written to prevent. The order ends on the case number (BR10), so pagination can neither repeat nor skip a case.

The scope is not a filter this service owns: it is the answer of the rwb-access authorise contract, cached per request, and a role without the right is refused rather than shown an empty page (BR1).

##### 3. Preconditions

| Precondition | What it gives this story |

| RWB-P3-E1019-APP is done | Queues carry their code, team and role, so a queue filter resolves against a row in force |
| RWB-P3-E1020-APP is done | New cases carry a queue and an owner by rule, so an unassigned case is the exception it should be |
| RWB-P3-E1028-APP is done | Each assigned case carries a SERVICE_LEVEL timer with `status`, `paused` and `expires_at` and, where the legal period applies, a PRESCRIPTION timer; this slice reads those rows and writes none |
| RWB-P3-E1031-APP and RWB-P3-E1031-CON are published | The export operation of this base exists, so the row-limit check has an operation to guard and the legacy extract columns keep one owner |
| RWB-P3-E2011-APP is done for the queue views | Its `ageDays`, its service level state and its page-size parameter rows are carried unchanged; this story adds the age in state beside them and declares no second pair of bounds |
| The parameters in force hold the bounds and the row limit | The case-list page-size minimum 1 and maximum 200 served by RWB-P3-E2011-APP and `caselist.export.maxrows` 10,000 (assumed in the legacy story, DL11), as rows of `parameter_value` with the version in force (DP-06; GAP-2224; ASM-3663) |
| The reference data in force holds the lists | LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-STAGE as rows of `reference_row` with the version in force, read in process through the rwb-case reference-data contract (DP-07) |
| The role to permission matrix gives RW-TEAMMGR Case record R with Team scope | The caller signs in through Entra ID with a role holding Case record R; the right, the scope and its default are answered by rwb-access and cached per request by the guard library (DP-08) |
| The feature switch `rwb.casewf.case-list-ageing` is on | Off, the breach filter is ignored and the list keeps the columns of RWB-P3-E2011-APP and RWB-P3-E1031-APP; the switch's mechanism and owner are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2224; ASM-3666) |
| The platform contracts the DP rows name are published | RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1037-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON. They are pulled by the rwb-case baseline stories, so this slice adds no build dependency and starts on Day 1 |
| The connection is the rwb-case login (DP-02) | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2224; ASM-3666) |

##### 4. Flow

1. Team manager: opens SCR-02 Case list through the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) and chooses the filters queue, product, status, stage, owner and breached.
2. gateway-bff: calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases` on rwb-case, one hop, and merges the answer into the screen model.
3. rwb-case: `AccessCheckClient` asks the rwb-access authorise contract for Case record R and the caller's scope, cached for the request; a role without the right is a 403 and nothing is read (DP-08, BR1).
4. `FilterValidator` checks each filter value against the list in force for its field and a queue filter against the queue codes in force; a value outside its list is a 422 before any case is read (BR6).
5. `PageBoundsReader` reads the page-size minimum and maximum through the parameters contract with the version in force and refuses a size outside them with 422 (BR7).
6. `CaseListQueryService` builds one query over `rwb_case`: `recovery_case` filtered by the request and by the scope predicate, `queue` joined for the queue code and its team, and the open SERVICE_LEVEL and PRESCRIPTION `timer` rows of each case joined once for the page (BR8).
7. `AgeingCalculator` computes `ageInStateDays` from `stage_clock_start`, or from `entry_date` when it is empty, and `ageSinceEntryDays` from `entry_date`, both as whole calendar days to the reference day in Asia/Bangkok (BR2).
8. `ServiceLevelStateReader` resolves the service level state: EXPIRED, or RUNNING past `expires_at`, is BREACHED; a paused timer is PAUSED; a RUNNING timer inside its due time is RUNNING; no timer is NONE; a paused timer is never breached (BR3, BR4, BR5).
9. `PrescriptionClockReader` resolves `prescriptionDate` from the case row and `prescriptionClockStatus` from the PRESCRIPTION timer, NONE when there is none; `deviationOpen` is read from `recovery_case.deviation_open` and nothing else about the deviation is read (BR5, BR12).
10. `CaseListQueryService` orders the rows breach first, then age in state descending, then case number ascending, and returns one page with its envelope (BR10).
11. Team manager: selects a queue on the queue screen; the front end calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/cases`, which applies the same scope, row shape, order and bounds to one queue and answers 404 for a queue outside the caller's teams.
12. Team manager: chooses Extract; the front end calls the export operation of this base with the same filters and without page and size; RWB-P3-E1031-APP re-reads with those filters, and this slice's limit check refuses with 422 when the matching rows exceed `caselist.export.maxrows`, before any file or access-log entry is built (BR11).
13. Nothing in steps 1 to 12 writes a case, a queue or a timer, publishes an event, adds an outbox row or starts a workflow: the operations are reads and the limit check is a refusal (BR9).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A filter value is not in its list of values, for example product CAR | Refused with 422; nothing is read | MSG-GEN-007 | AC3 |
| X2 | Page size below 1 or above 200 as the rows in force state them | Refused with 422 | MSG-GEN-002 | AC4 |
| X3 | No case matches the filters | Empty state on the list; the extract of RWB-P3-E1031-APP holds the header row only | MSG-P3-020 | AC6 |
| X4 | A queue filter names a queue outside the caller's scope | Only cases in scope are returned, so the result is empty | MSG-P3-020 | AC7 |
| X5 | A case has no SERVICE_LEVEL timer yet (status NEW) | Service level state NONE; breached false | None | AC1 |
| X6 | The service level due time equals the current time | Not breached; breached from the next minute | None | AC5 |
| X7 | The extract would hold more than `caselist.export.maxrows` rows | The extract is refused before anything is written and no file is produced | MSG-P3-021 | AC9 |
| X8 | A case changes between two page requests | The order ends on the case number, so no case is skipped or repeated by the order | None | AC10 |
| X9 | The caller's role does not hold the Case record right | Refused with 403 before any row is read; a refusal and never an empty page | MSG-P4-002 | AC7 |
| X10 | The rwb-access authorise contract does not answer inside the 2 s budget | One hop, 2 s timeout and a breaker; 503, and no page is served from a stale right cache | MSG-GEN-006 | AC7 |
| X11 | A queue id in the drill down is unknown or outside the caller's teams | Not found; nothing is read | MSG-P4-003 | AC8 |

X9 and X11 are the two refusals this slice must not turn into an empty answer: a consumer that reads an empty page as "no work" hides a permission problem, which is why the two are distinguished by status and not by body. X10 is the platform unavailable message.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads rows that RWB-P3-E1019-APP, RWB-P3-E1020-APP and RWB-P3-E1028-APP already write, and builds against RWB-P2-E2033-CON and its fake plus the rwb-access fake, so neither rwb-access nor the edge is needed in the development environment |
| Negotiable | The row fields are the legacy columns and the layout belongs to the designer (DL31); the order, the bounds, the row limit and the refusals are fixed |
| Valuable | Puts every case of every queue in the manager's scope on the owner's own list, with the age in state beside the age since entry and the prescription clock beside the service level state |
| Estimable | Two read operations, one query, one calculator, one state reader, one validator, one bounds reader and one page of screen support |
| Small | Reads only: no business row, no outbox row, no event, no workflow and no Schedule |
| Testable | Each criterion is one automated test; the access case and the drill down are component tests, and the boundary of the service level is a unit test on the calculator |

The ten criteria are this slice's own; legacy AC1 to AC11 are carried by RWB-P2-E2033-APP, and the legacy test set is kept in section 16. Every legacy value is kept character for character: the three cases of legacy AC1 with their owners, statuses, stage clock starts and service levels, their order, the paused timer and the running prescription clock of legacy AC2, the due time of legacy AC4, product CAR of legacy AC6, page size 500 and the bounds 1 and 200 of legacy AC7, product SSME of legacy AC8, the team HP-NE case of legacy AC9, the 10,000-row limit of legacy AC10 and the 120 cases with pages of 50 of legacy AC11.

Where a criterion needs another service the `Given` names the contract mock: the rwb-access authorise answer (AC7, AC8) is the only cross-service answer this slice takes. The reference and parameter rows are this service's own data and are seeded, not stubbed (DP-06, DP-07). Two readings had to be fixed and are recorded: the legacy `ageDays` is the legacy age in state, while RWB-P3-E2011-APP publishes `ageDays` as the age since entry, so this story keeps `ageDays` as the queue views publish it and adds `ageInStateDays` for the legacy column (GAP-2224; ASM-3664); an unassigned case is answered with no owner value and shown as the text "Unassigned", as the legacy criteria read the cell (GAP-2224; ASM-3664).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The list holds only cases in the caller's scope — Own, Team or All — taken from the rwb-access authorise contract; a role without the Case record right is refused and never given an empty page | CTL-09; `role.default_scope`; DP-08 |
| BR2 | Age in state is the whole number of calendar days from `stage_clock_start`, or from `entry_date` when it is empty, to the reference day in Asia/Bangkok; age since entry is the whole number of calendar days from `entry_date` to the same day | DF-CAS-018, DF-CAS-013; legacy BR2; GAP-2224; ASM-3664 |
| BR3 | A case is breached when its SERVICE_LEVEL timer has status EXPIRED, or status RUNNING with `expires_at` earlier than now; a breach does not move the case | R-UNI-30; DF-WRK-032, DF-WRK-035 |
| BR4 | A deviation pauses the stage clock and keeps the prescription clock running; the list shows both; a paused SERVICE_LEVEL timer is never breached | R-DEV-01; DF-WRK-034, DF-WRK-035 |
| BR5 | `serviceLevelState` is BREACHED, RUNNING, PAUSED or NONE from the SERVICE_LEVEL timer; `prescriptionClockStatus` is RUNNING or EXPIRED from the PRESCRIPTION timer and NONE when the case has no such timer; `prescriptionDate` is read from the case row | LOV-TIMER; LOV-TIMER-STATUS; DF-CAS-017; legacy BR5 |
| BR6 | Each filter value is checked against the list in force for its field — LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS, LOV-STAGE — and a queue filter against the queue codes in force; a value outside its list is refused before any case is read | DP-07; `queue.queue_code`; legacy BR6 |
| BR7 | No value is written in code: the page-size bounds are the parameter rows RWB-P3-E2011-APP fixes, the extract row limit is `caselist.export.maxrows` 10,000 (assumed, DL11), and every list is a reference row read with the version in force | DP-06; DP-07; GAP-2224; ASM-3663 |
| BR8 | The read holds only `rwb_case` rows — `recovery_case`, `queue` and `timer` — and no other service's table, view or row is read, joined or copied | DP-01; ADR-010 |
| BR9 | The operations are read-only: no business row, no outbox row, no event, no workflow and no Schedule; a refusal writes nothing | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR10 | The order is breach first, then age in state descending, then case number ascending, so the order is total and a case that changes between two requests is never skipped or repeated | Legacy flow step 7; legacy AC11 |
| BR11 | The extract holds at most `caselist.export.maxrows` rows, carries no customer personal field, and a request above the limit is refused with 422 before the access-log entry and before any file is built | REQ-ACA-006; legacy BR7; FSD P3 A2.19 AC-EXC-P3-019-02; RWB-P3-E1031-APP |
| BR12 | `deviationOpen` is read from `recovery_case.deviation_open` and names only that a deviation is open; the deviation record, its code, its owner and its clearance are rwb-deviation's | REQ-DVH-006; DF-CAS-019; R-DEV-01 |

How the rules hold in `rwb-case`: BR1 is one authorise call cached for the request, applied as a predicate and not as a filter over the answer, so no page can carry a row from outside the scope. BR2 is `AgeingCalculator`, a pure function over two dates and a reference day passed in, unit tested without a database. BR3 to BR5 are one read of the two timer types per page and one resolver per row, with the paused test ahead of the breach test so the order of the two tests cannot decide a breach. BR6 and BR7 are `FilterValidator` and `PageBoundsReader`; no list value and no limit is a constant, so removing a value from the reference data removes it from the accepted filters with no release. BR8 is the repository, and an architecture test fails a statement that names another schema. BR9 is the absence of a write path. BR10 is the SQL order clause with the tie break on `case_no`, whose uniqueness is fixed at creation. BR11 is a count with the page's own filters and scope, taken before the export writer starts, so the count and the file cannot disagree. BR12 is one boolean column; this service holds no deviation table.

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story does not change a case status and does not move a case. It reads `recovery_case`, `queue` and `timer` in `rwb_case` and writes nothing: the export it guards is RWB-P3-E1031-APP's and the access-log entry is rwb-access's.

| Observed fact on the list | Written by | Appears as |
|---|---|---|
| Case number, product group, queue, owner, status, stage, entry date, prescription date and the open deviation flag | rwb-case (P3), the Epic 1 and Epic 2 stories of this service | The row of the page |
| Stage clock start and the SERVICE_LEVEL and PRESCRIPTION timers with their status, pause flag and due time | rwb-case (P3), RWB-P3-E1028-APP | `ageInStateDays`, `ageSinceEntryDays`, `serviceLevelState`, `serviceLevelDueAt`, `prescriptionClockStatus` |
| The Case record right and the caller's scope | rwb-access (P4) through the authorise contract | Whether a page is answered, and which rows |
| The queue code, its team and its role | rwb-case (P3), RWB-P3-E1019-APP | The queue filter values and the drill down |
| The page-size bounds and the extract row limit | rwb-case (P3), the parameter rows of DP-06 | Whether a request is served or refused |

A case that changes between two page requests changes the next answer and nothing else: no row is rewritten, no timer is recomputed, and the order is total by case number.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads the list and the drill down for the team's queues (Case record R, Team scope); the extract file is RWB-P3-E1031-APP's |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the list for the cases they own (Case record R, Own scope) |
| RW-PRODHEAD, RW-AUDIT, RW-CONDUCT and other roles with Case record R | Read the list in their scope |
| RW-CAPACITY, capacity and workforce planner | Reads with scope All through the queue views of RWB-P3-E2011-APP; the scope is rwb-access's answer, not this story's |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | No Case record right; refused with MSG-P4-002 |
| rwb-access, through its contract | Answers the right, the scope and its default; owns the role, permission and masking rows and the access log, none of which this story owns |
| No approval applies | The story takes no decision |

The service runs as the rwb-case login (DP-02); the name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2224; ASM-3666), and it holds grants on `rwb_case` only.

| DF-WRK-035 | timer | status | Read |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2224; ASM-3663) | parameter_catalog, parameter_value | the case-list page-size bounds and `caselist.export.maxrows`, with the version in force | Read, in process through the rwb-case parameters contract |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2224; ASM-3663) | reference_row, reference_version | LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-STAGE rows with the version in force | Read, in process through the rwb-case reference-data contract |

Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. Every row is a `rwb_case` row: the parameters and the reference rows are read through the contracts of this same service and never joined in SQL, and no other schema is named by any statement (BR8). No row is written, so no field is marked Write.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/case/v1`; owner rwb-case (P3).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases` | One page of the cases in the caller's scope with the columns of the legacy list — case number, product group, queue, owner, status, stage, age in state, service level state, service level due, prescription date, prescription clock and deviation — with the age since entry beside the age in state, the filter set, the breach filter, the stable order and the paging envelope | Case record R, scope applied through the rwb-access authorise contract | Read only: the same request on unchanged data returns the same rows in the same order |
| GET | `/queues/{queueId}/cases` | The same row shape and order for one queue, as the drill down from a queue row; 404 for a queue outside the caller's teams | Queue and allocation R and Case record R, scope applied | Read only, as above |
| GET | `/cases/export` | The export operation of RWB-P3-E1031-APP re-read with the same filters without page and size; this story adds no column and no file, only the row-limit check refused with 422 MSG-P3-021 before the access-log entry and the file | Case record R, scope applied | Read only on the data; each export records its own access-log entry, which is rwb-access's row |

The query parameters are `product`, `stage`, `status`, `owner`, `queue`, `deviation`, `ageFrom`, `ageTo`, `page`, `size`, `sort`, with `breached` added by the legacy story. The route filter and the queue default sort are RWB-P3-E2011-APP's and are served unchanged; this story adds no filter and no sort token.

Each row carries `caseNo`, `productGroup`, `queueCode`, `ownerUserId` (absent when the case has no owner and shown as the text "Unassigned"), `status`, `stageCode`, `ageInStateDays`, `ageDays` (the age since entry, published by RWB-P3-E2011-APP), `entryDate`, `prescriptionDate`, `serviceLevelDueAt`, `serviceLevelState` (BREACHED, RUNNING, PAUSED or NONE), `prescriptionClockStatus` (RUNNING, EXPIRED or NONE) and `deviationOpen`. The names `ageDays`, `serviceLevelDueAt`, `serviceLevelState` and `prescriptionClockStatus` are the ones the legacy story and RWB-E2-011 fixed; the spelling of the other elements, of the envelope, of the filter set and of the problem body is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2224; ASM-3662).

Errors: 401 no session or no Recovery role (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Case record right (MSG-P4-002); 404 queue unknown or outside the caller's teams (MSG-P4-003); 422 a filter value outside its list (MSG-GEN-007), a page size outside its bounds (MSG-GEN-002) or an extract above its row limit (MSG-P3-021); 503 the store is down or the authorise contract does not answer inside its budget (MSG-GEN-006).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop, no chaining; 2 s timeout and a breaker (ADR-020).

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | rwb-access (P4) | The Case record right, the Queue and allocation right where the drill down needs it, and the caller's scope with its default, cached per request by the guard library (DP-08) | One hop, 2 s, cached per request |

The parameter and reference rows are read in process through RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON: library reads of this same service, not cross-service calls (DP-06, DP-07). The freshness header and the account columns of the legacy screen are RWB-P3-E2011-APP's and RWB-P2-E2033-APP's, so a page here carries no second downstream.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The list and the drill down publish no event and write no outbox row. The topic `rwb.case.events.v1` with the names `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1`, `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` and `rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1` belongs to the case, allocation, transfer, state and timer stories under DP-14; this slice subscribes to none of them and adds none.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The list is read from the rows per request, so a change is seen on the next read rather than through a projection, and no inbox row is written. `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` and `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` are consumed by RWB-P3-E1028-APP to pause and resume the timer this slice renders; that is not this slice's subscription.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The page and the drill down are served inside the request: no workflow, no activity, no signal and no timer. The durable service level and prescription timers live in `CaseWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-case`, owned by RWB-P3-E1028-APP; this slice reads their projection in `timer` and adds nothing to it.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The legacy story had no job and the target adds none: the list is read on request and the extract is officer-driven. The daily rebalancing Schedule and the queue measure snapshot belong to RWB-P3-E1030-APP.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `recovery_case` | rwb_case | rwb-case (P3) | The case row behind every list row: number, product group, status, stage, owner, queue, team, entry date, prescription date, stage clock start and the open deviation flag |
| `queue` | rwb_case | rwb-case (P3) | The queue code and team of the queue column, of the queue filter values and of the drill down |
| `timer` | rwb_case | rwb-case (P3) | The open SERVICE_LEVEL and PRESCRIPTION timer of a case: type, due time, pause flag and status |
| `parameter_catalog`, `parameter_value`, `reference_row`, `reference_version` | rwb_case | rwb-case (P3) | The page-size bounds, the extract row limit and the filter lists, read through this service's contracts and never joined in SQL |
| `outbox_event`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in rwb_case | Platform library | Not written by this read path |

No other table is named. `case_list_row` is rwb-source-data's daily projection and is not read here: the API and the screen are P3's, which is the R-PREC default ruling read as the API and not as the row table. `case_account`, `case_party`, `assignment`, `queue_member` and `queue_measure` are this service's and are not read either.

| gateway-bff composite route stub | The edge route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The SCR-02 route and the merged screen model (DP-19), so the page's own calls can be asserted |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `caselist`; front end `src/modules/recovery/case/caselist/CaseListPage.tsx`.

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_case`; the page reads `recovery_case`, `queue` and `timer` of this service only | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and its client library: the page bounds and `caselist.export.maxrows` are parameter rows | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case: LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-STAGE with the version in force | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library, cached per request, on both operations and on the limit check | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/case/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.case.<Event>.v1` through the naming library; no event and no topic is added here | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in `rwb_case`: no new migration, because the timer index the legacy story asked for is the one RWB-P3-E2011-APP lands | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route for the case list and the queue drill down | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 is the read of the three tables; DP-06 the two parameter reads of AC4 and AC9; DP-07 the three lists of AC3; DP-08 the authorise answer of AC7 and AC8; DP-13 the base path; DP-19 the composite route. DP-14 has an instance as a naming rule only, since the list publishes nothing. DP-15 has an instance as the sequence convention only: the legacy `ix_timer_case_type` index is landed by RWB-P3-E2011-APP as `ix_timer_case_type_status` on `timer (case_id, timer_type, status)`, and a second index on the same leading columns would add write cost and no read (GAP-2224; ASM-3665).

Metadata H is None: the platform contracts the DP rows name are pulled by the rwb-case baseline stories and by the queue-view story of this service, and RWB-P2-E2033-CON never blocks. The story is Day 1 and builds against the published contract and its fake.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CaseListController | Controller | `GET /cases` and `GET /queues/{queueId}/cases`; parameter binding, problem responses with their message IDs, and the limit refusal on the export path |
| CaseListQueryService | Service | The scoped, filtered and ordered query for one page, the envelope, and the drill down with its queue predicate |
| CaseListRepository | Repository | One SQL query over `recovery_case`, `queue` and the open SERVICE_LEVEL and PRESCRIPTION `timer` rows, in `rwb_case` only |
| AgeingCalculator | Service | Pure functions for BR2 and BR4 on a reference day passed in |
| ServiceLevelStateReader | Service | BR3 and BR5, with the paused test ahead of the breach test |
| PrescriptionClockReader | Service | BR5: `prescriptionClockStatus` and `prescriptionDate` |
| FilterValidator | Service | BR6: each filter value against its list in force and the queue filter against the queue codes |
| PageBoundsReader | Service | BR7: the page-size bounds through the parameters contract |
| ExportLimitReader | Service | BR11: `caselist.export.maxrows` and the count with the page's own filters and scope |
| AccessCheckClient | Client | The Case record right and the scope through the authorise contract, cached per request (DP-08) |
| CaseRowMapper | Component | The row of 12.1, with the owner placeholder and the absent prescription date |
| CaseListPage | React component | The list in its List, Filtered, Empty, Breached and Paused states, the Extract refusal, and the queue drill down |

**Database and migrations.** Reads `recovery_case`, `queue` and `timer`; uses `ix_case_status_queue`, `ix_case_owner_status` and the `ix_timer_case_type_status` index RWB-P3-E2011-APP lands. No new table, column, index or migration for this story (GAP-2224; ASM-3665). The service connects with its own login (DP-02), holding grants on `rwb_case` only.

**Configuration and reference data.** The page bounds are the parameter rows RWB-P3-E2011-APP fixes, read with the version in force; this story declares no second pair, and the legacy limit of 1 to 200 is that maximum (GAP-2224; ASM-3663). `caselist.export.maxrows` is 10,000, the legacy value under DL11, read as a parameter row and never as a constant. LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS, LOV-STAGE and the queue codes are rows in force (DP-07). The feature switch keeps the legacy name `rwb.casewf.case-list-ageing`; off, the breach filter is ignored and the queue-view and export columns are served (GAP-2224; ASM-3666).

**Build steps**

1. `CaseListController` and `CaseRowMapper` against the contract fake and the rwb-access stub, with problem bodies and one test per refusal; AC1, AC3, AC4.
2. `CaseListRepository` and `CaseListQueryService` with the scope predicate, the filters, the timer join and the order of BR10; AC1, AC5, AC7.
3. `AgeingCalculator` with unit tests on the reference day, the empty stage clock, the paused clock and the 09:00 to 09:01 boundary; AC2, AC5.
4. `ServiceLevelStateReader` and `PrescriptionClockReader`, with the paused test ahead of the breach test and the absent timer; AC1, AC2.
5. `FilterValidator` with the three lists and the queue codes; AC3.
6. `PageBoundsReader` and `ExportLimitReader`, with the count taken before the export writer starts; AC4, AC9.
7. The drill down with the same row shape and the queue scope check that answers 404; AC8.
8. `AccessCheckClient` and the refusal of a role with no Case record right, as a refusal and not an empty page; AC7.
9. `CaseListPage` with the five states and the Extract refusal, asserted against the route stub; AC1, AC6, AC9.
10. The architecture test that no statement names a schema other than `rwb_case`, and the contract test of RWB-P2-E2033-CON, so the story builds before rwb-access and the edge land.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; page 1 over 23,600 synthetic cases returns in under 2 s at the 95th percentile in SIT (NFR-008); the 10,000-row limit is refused with 422 and no file; the RWB-P2-E2033-CON contract test is green; and no query of this story reaches a schema other than `rwb_case`.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-007 | A filter value is not in its list | {value} is not a valid value for {field}. | This story, in `FilterValidator` |
| MSG-GEN-002 | The page size is outside its bounds | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. | This story, in `PageBoundsReader` |
| MSG-P3-020 | No case matches the filters on the list | No cases match these filters. Change a filter to see more. | This story, on the empty state |
| MSG-P3-021 | The extract is above its row limit | The export holds at most {max} rows. Narrow the filters and try again. | This story, on the export path before the file |
| MSG-P4-001 | No valid session | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. | rwb-access, surfaced here |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role does not hold the Case record right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | rwb-access through the authorise contract, surfaced here |
| MSG-P4-003 | The queue is unknown or outside the caller's teams | This case is not in your scope. | This story, on the drill down |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The authorise contract does not answer inside its budget | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2224; ASM-3662) | This story, on the authorise guard |

The first six are copied unchanged from the legacy story and no identifier is renumbered by the realignment. MSG-P4-003 is the scope refusal of RWB-P3-E2011-APP, used here so both stories answer a queue outside scope the same way. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10. The refusal order is fixed: session, then right, then each filter value, then the page size, then the count for the limit, and only then is a row read or a file built.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the page bounds, the extract row limit, the three lists and the queue codes are parameter and reference rows read with the version in force; the code holds behaviour and no value (BR7).
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or prompts: a row carries the case number, codes, dates, whole days and a staff user reference, never a customer name, identity number, address, contact point or account number, and test data is synthetic.
- No read of another service's tables: the case, the queue and the timer are `rwb_case` rows, the rights come through the rwb-access contract, and no statement names a `recovery` or another `rwb_*` schema (DP-01, DP-08, ADR-010).
- No ACE view is read: this slice needs no account, customer, contact or collateral field, so it touches no `v_ace_*` view.
- The operations are reads: no case, queue, timer or assignment row is written, no outbox row is added and nothing is locked for the length of a page (BR9).
- One hop only: the service calls the authorise contract and returns, and never calls a service that calls another (ADR-020).
- The order is total and ends on the case number, so pagination cannot skip or repeat a case, and no page is served from a stored copy.
- A refusal is a refusal: no right, a queue outside the teams and a value outside its list are answers with a status and a message identifier, never an empty page and never a thinner row.
- The extract guards a file that is not this story's: the limit is checked before the access-log entry and before any workbook is built.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-033 and rewritten for rwb-access. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **team manager (RW-TEAMMGR), a case owner or an internal auditor who reads the case and queue list**, I want **rwb-access to answer, for that list and for its extract, which capability right my session holds, which scope predicate filters every row and every queue, which personal fields come back masked, and which filter set and row count the extract records**, so that **a manager sees every case of the team and no case of another team, the file leaves one record of who took what, and no answer tells anybody that a case outside their scope exists**.

Inside `rwb-access` this is the authority side of legacy RWB-E2-033:

- Service `rwb-access`, schema `rwb_access`, REST base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`.
- The capability is the answer behind the list and the extract, in three parts: the session answer of `GET /me/session`, extended here with the CASE_RECORD right, the scope predicate and the two policy versions in force; the per-object check for one case or one queue row, which is the CASE_RECORD branch of the authorise contract of DP-08 (`RWB-P4-E1037-CON`); and one access record per extract. No screen, no list query, no timer and no workflow is built here.
- The policy the answers come from is data in `rwb_access`: `role` with `default_scope`, `permission` with `capability_area`, `letters` and `matrix_version`, and `masking_rule` with `field_id`, `unmasked` and `masking_version`. No case, queue, timer, deviation or customer row is read (DP-01), and no parameter, list of values or queue code is copied into this schema.
- The row facts the object check needs — the case, its queue, its team, its owner and its region — arrive in the request from the caller, which holds them. The list itself, its twelve columns, the age in state, the breach flag and the two clocks stay in `rwb-case` (`RWB-P3-E2033-APP`, `RWB-P3-E2011-APP`), the composed page and the workbook stay in `rwb-integration` (`RWB-P2-E2033-APP`), and the extract writer stays in `RWB-P3-E1031-APP`.
- The legacy behaviour carried into the access service is unchanged: the same four scope values OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL, the same refusal of a role with no Case record right, the same "not in your scope" answer that never confirms a case exists, the same masking default of a field with no rule, and the same single record per extract. The legacy story fixed the scope, the refusal and the entry; it fixed no element name for the answer, so the names of section 12.1 are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2320; ASM-3849).

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story exists because a team manager learns where work waits by asking each owner or by building a spreadsheet, and RWB-E1-031 with RWB-E2-011 puts the queue, the owner, the age and the service level state on the list. What none of those stories settles is who may see the page: the monolith answered a manager, a case owner and an auditor out of one in-process guard, with the scope applied inside the same query and the masking applied by whichever screen the reader happened to be on. Under Architecture v5 each service authorises its own object against cached permission data from `rwb-access`, with a 2 s timeout (slide 10), the case service reaches the access service by REST (slide 13), and the roles, permissions, scopes and masking rules are `rwb-access` rows (slide 41).

This story supplies that answer for the case and queue list and for its extract: the CASE_RECORD right, the scope predicate that filters every row and every queue, the masking markers of the fields the row asks about, and the record the extract leaves. It meets REQ-WKM-002 on the access side (the team's queues, filtered and exportable, and nothing of another team), carries REQ-DVH-006 (a deviation flag on a case in scope is never suppressed by this answer, so the flag is visible in every queue view), and meets REQ-ACA-006 on the extract side (one record of the user, the time, the filters and the row count before the file is made); REQ-ACA-006 also named a data-lake copy, which no longer exists. The measure of success is that every list read and every extract is granted or refused by the policy in force, that no role reaches a queue outside its scope, and that every extract leaves exactly one record with its filters and its row count.

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E2-033, owned by other services where they say so:

- Matrix version `PM-2026.12` is in force and gives CASE_RECORD right R to RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-SPECIAL and RW-AUDIT, with `default_scope` OWN for RW-CASEOWN, TEAM for RW-TEAMMGR and ALL for RW-AUDIT, and no CASE_RECORD right to RW-REFADM (TSD P4 T3.1 `role.default_scope`, LOV-SCOPE; legacy section 3). That the other reading roles of the legacy authority table keep the scope their own role row carries is assumed (ASM-3851).

##### 4. Flow

1. Caller: a person opens SCR-02 Case list. gateway-bff resolves the session and calls the case list service, which asks `rwb-access` for the session answer.
2. `rwb-access`: reads the caller's roles from the session ACE Common resolved at sign-in, and the rights, scope and matrix version from `permission` and `role` for the versions in force.
3. `rwb-access`, right check: no CASE_RECORD R for any role the caller holds gives 403 with MSG-P4-002 naming the action, and an answer with no scope and no version (BR1).
4. `rwb-access`, scope predicate: the scope value comes from the `default_scope` of the caller's roles, read against LOV-SCOPE: OWN admits the cases the caller owns, TEAM the cases of `teamCode`, REGION the cases of `regionCode`, ALL any case (BR2). The answer carries the predicate and never a queue list, because the queue rows are the caller's.
5. `rwb-access`, masking: for the field IDs the caller names, the profile for the versions in force is read from `masking_rule`; a field with no covering row is marked masked (BR5). The answer marks each field `masked` or `clear` and carries no value.
6. `rwb-access`: caches the answer for the versions in force, writes nothing, and returns it inside the 2 s budget of DP-11.
7. Caller: builds the page, applies the predicate to the queue filter and to every row, and serves the twelve columns of the legacy list; a case outside the predicate is answered 404 with MSG-P4-003, never an empty row.
8. Caller, on a queue row or a case row: asks the authorise answer for that object with its team, owner and region. `rwb-access` answers from the same cached policy per object; one batch may carry at most the page size in force (BR6).
9. Team manager: chooses Extract. The caller sends the same filters, the export intent and the number of rows the scoped query returned.
10. `rwb-access`: checks the row count against `caselist.export.maxrows`, writes one access record (BR7) through the log path of `RWB-P4-E1039-APP`, and only then answers that the extract may be built; the workbook itself is `RWB-P3-E1031-APP`'s.
11. Policy change: a new matrix or masking version is loaded through the load path and is used from its `valid_from`; the next answer under the new version is computed afresh and no restart is needed (BR6).

Every answer is written before it is returned where it records a read; when the record cannot be written, the extract is refused with a 503 rather than served unrecorded (BR7).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | No Recovery role in the session | 401 before the policy is read; no scope, no version and no row | MSG-P4-001 | BR1 |
| X2 | A role with no Case record right | 403 with the action named; no scope, no version and no row read | MSG-P4-002 | AC2 |
| X3 | A case or queue outside the predicate, whatever the request asks | 404 with no owner, no team and no field marker, so the answer never confirms the case exists | MSG-P4-003 | AC3 |
| X4 | A field has no masking row | The field is marked `masked` with the default marker; the answer is otherwise granted | None | AC11 |
| X5 | A filter token outside its list of values | 422 on the field; no access record and no case read | MSG-GEN-007 | AC7 |
| X6 | One batch of object checks above the page size in force | 422 naming the bound; no object is checked | MSG-GEN-002 | AC8 |
| X7 | The extract above `caselist.export.maxrows` | 422 naming the limit; no record and no file | MSG-P3-021 | AC6 |
| X8 | The access record cannot be written | The extract is refused with 503 and no file is made, and an incident is raised to the platform queue | MSG-P7-003 | BR7 |
| X9 | The parameters or reference contract does not answer inside its budget | No answer rather than a guessed one: 503, and the refusal is recorded | MSG-GEN-006 | BR9 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds and tests against the composed-page fake of `RWB-P2-E2033-CON` and the platform contracts already in force; reads `rwb_access` only and calls no other service at run time |
| Negotiable | The policy pack — roles, matrix, scope values, masking rows and their versions — is data; the story fixes the shape of the answer and the refusal behaviour only |
| Valuable | The list shows a manager the team's queues and hides another team's, the extract leaves one record, and no answer confirms that a case outside the scope exists |
| Estimable | One extended answer, one object check, one access record, one cache and no migration |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests; no screen, no query over case rows, no timer and no workflow |
| Testable | Every criterion in section 7 has a test case in section 16, on fixed synthetic data |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The list and the extract need CASE_RECORD right R. A role without it is refused before any object is read, and the refusal carries no scope and no version | legacy BR1; CTL-09; TSD P4 T6.2 |
| BR2 | The scope value is the `default_scope` of the caller's roles, read against LOV-SCOPE: OWN, TEAM, REGION or ALL. Where a caller holds two roles the wider scope applies. The request never widens the answer | `role.default_scope`; LOV-SCOPE; legacy BR1 |
| BR3 | A case outside the predicate is answered as not in scope, 404 with no case fact, so the answer never confirms that a case exists | legacy section 5 X4; CTL-09 |
| BR4 | The answer takes no view of a timer, a breach, an escalation or a deviation: access depends on the object's team, owner and region and on the two versions in force only | legacy BR3, BR4 |
| BR5 | Masking: a field whose `masking_rule` row for the role and the version in force holds `unmasked` false is marked masked, and a field with no covering row is masked with the default marker. The answer marks fields and never carries a value | `masking_rule`; AC-EXC-P4-004-05; legacy BR7 |
| BR6 | Every answer names the matrix version and the masking version it used. A version is used from its `valid_from`, and one batch of object checks carries at most the page size in force | `matrix_version`, `masking_version`, `valid_from`; parameter row |
| BR7 | One access record per extract, with the actor, the time, the filter set, the row count and no case ID, written before the workbook is built; a refused record serves no file | legacy BR7; REQ-ACA-006; AC-ALT-P4-007-02 |
| BR8 | Only `role`, `permission` and `masking_rule` of `rwb_access` are read. No case, queue, timer, parameter, list or queue code is read here, and no other schema is named | DP-01, DP-05, DP-06, DP-07 |
| BR9 | A refusal is a refusal: 401, 403, 404, 422 or 503 with its message identifier and no data, never a thinner answer | legacy section 5 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status and no policy row. It reads `role`, `permission` and `masking_rule` and, on an extract, adds one access record through the log path of `RWB-P4-E1039-APP`, which is append only and belongs to that story. A policy version has its own load lifecycle (LOADED, VALIDATED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED), which the load stories own (RWB-P4-AD002-APP, RWB-P4-AD004-APP); this story only reads the version in force.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads and extracts under scope TEAM for the queues of the team |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads and extracts under scope OWN |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads and extracts under scope ALL, and still sees the masked fields |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | No CASE_RECORD right; refused with MSG-P4-002 |
| A break-glass grant of CASE_RECORD R with scope ALL | Honoured for the incident window; every record written in it carries the grant ID and the incident (`RWB-P4-E1039-APP`) |
| No approval applies | The story takes no decision and approves nothing |
