##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test asset in the integration pipeline and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases` | P3 rwb-case | The list with the filters, the page and the size, and the ageing, service-level and prescription columns (AC1, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9, AC11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/export` | P3 rwb-case | The Excel extract with the ageing and clock columns, and its row limit (AC3, AC8, AC10) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The single case, its age in state and its deviation flag (AC2, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` | P3 rwb-case | The SERVICE_LEVEL and PRESCRIPTION timer projection, their status and pause (AC2, AC4, AC5) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/me/session` | P4 rwb-access | The role, the Team scope and Case record R the journey runs under (AC1, AC9, TC-E2-033-12-ITG) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` | P4 rwb-access | The export entry with the user, the time, the filters and the row count (AC3) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles` | P4 rwb-access | The role's default scope check behind the scope of every row (AC1, AC9, TC-E2-033-12-ITG) |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with the 2 s timeout, and every read is idempotent on unchanged data. The scope check that rwb-case makes inside its own process is not a path in the Ownership Map, so the harness seeds it through the role, the scope and the right of the rwb-access fake (12.8) and reads the resulting answer through the P3 operations instead of calling an access path of its own.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event on a production topic; the seed of section 4 is loaded as data, and the evidence goes to the release record through the pipeline.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | Fixes the instant a status or stage change reached the topic, so the row the list returns after it describes the same case at the same instant (DP-14) |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | The raise of X1 on 9 December 2026 that pauses the stage clock of case "RW-2026-000104" and makes its row PAUSED and not BREACHED (DP-14) |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationCleared.v1` | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | Confirms that no clearance of the case happened inside the run window, so the pause the list shows is the open deviation and not a stale flag (DP-14) |

The harness consumes with its own consumer group and never reads a producer's outbox, inbox or schema.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

`CaseWorkflow` on task queue `rwb-case` is observed, not built: the durable timer inside it is the clock behind the SERVICE_LEVEL and PRESCRIPTION projection the list reads, and the harness asserts that the projection and the timer agree at 09:00 and 09:01 (AC2, AC4). `DeviationWorkflow`, the child on task queue `rwb-deviation`, is observed, not built: it is the pause of the stage clock that makes the row PAUSED (AC2).

The harness starts no workflow, adds no activity and writes no schedule. The case query, the timer projection, the export and the access-log entry belong to the app stories of the seven integration dependencies.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The harness adds no workflow and no schedule; the fixed clock at 09:00 and 09:01 is the harness's own, and the durable timer it reads belongs to `CaseWorkflow`.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no table in any schema and no schema of its own; it reads through the operations of 12.2 and writes one access-log entry through the P4 contract.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Contract | What it answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| WireMock rwb-case | The four P3 operations of 12.2 | OpenAPI of P3 | The three rows of AC1 with their ages and service-level states and the order by breach, age and case number; the four cases of AC3; the boundary reads at 09:00 and 09:01; the PAUSED case with the prescription clock and the open deviation; the empty state and the single row of AC8 and AC9; the export bytes with the header and one data row and, for AC8, the header only; the 422 refusals with MSG-GEN-007, MSG-GEN-002 and MSG-P3-021; keeps the request journal for the filter, page and ordering assertions |
| WireMock rwb-access | The three P4 operations of 12.2 | OpenAPI of P4 | The session with role RW-TEAMMGR, Team scope for "MTG-BKK" and Case record R; the role's default scope from `GET /admin/roles`; the RW-REFADM user without the right, answering 403 MSG-P4-002; the export entry with the user, the time, the 3 filters and row count 1 after the export |
| WireMock rwb-deviation | The two S8 events of 12.4 | AsyncAPI of S8 | `DeviationRaised` for X1 on 9 December 2026 and no `DeviationCleared` inside the run window for case "RW-2026-000104" |
| WireMock rwb-integration | The routed read the screen uses | OpenAPI of P2 | The routed answer the case list screen receives, so the journey runs on the same route the manager drives and not on a direct call the screen never makes |
| Fixed clock | The harness itself | None | 10 December 2026 at 09:00 and 09:01 Asia/Bangkok, the two instants the boundary and the ageing are asserted at |

Each fake is replaced by the real service as its integration dependency lands, without a change to the scenarios. Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0415; ASM-0590): the fake set, the concrete fixture values, the harness environment, the OpenXML comparison method and the evidence format.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 7 consumed, one hop on the owner's base with the 2 s timeout |
| Kafka | 3 events consumed on `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.deviation.events.v1`; none published on a production topic |
| Temporal | Observed only: `CaseWorkflow` on queue `rwb-case` and its `DeviationWorkflow` child on queue `rwb-deviation`; no workflow, activity or schedule added |
| File | One Excel export, compared cell by cell against the expected columns and the row the list returned |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `integration/recovery-case-list` in the ACE repository, package `<ACE base package>.recovery.integration.caselist`. Not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added | How this harness applies it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none | The case, the queue and the timer are read through the P3 operations and the access log through the P4 operation; the harness opens no connection to any schema |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON | The export limit of 10,000 rows (assumed; DL11), the page range of 1 to 200 and the service level values are seeded from the parameter catalog, never values in the harness |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-CASE-STATUS, LOV-STAGE, LOV-TIMER-STATUS and the queue codes are loaded from files, so product "CAR" is refused by the data and not by a rule in the harness |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON | The session, the role's default scope and the refusal of RW-REFADM are read through the P4 operations; the harness reproduces no scope rule |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none | Every path of 12.2 uses the owner's base, so the harness never calls a monolith base |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON | No legacy `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic name survives: the harness subscribes to `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and asserts the naming library's topic names for every event it consumes |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON | Each service migrates its own schema; the harness runs no migration, creates no view and reads no schema |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The journey runs through the gateway route the case list screen uses, on the same bases, composed in parallel for the composite read |

The platform H dependencies in the table (H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, H RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are delivered by the platform waves and are not repeated in the metadata: the harness converges on them and has no build dependency of its own. The blocking dependencies of this story are the seven I stories, which replace the fakes with real services one at a time.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Job | Runs the twelve flow steps for one scenario and one business date, holds the run lock and drives the fixed clock |
| FakeRegistry | Configuration | WireMock mappings for rwb-case, rwb-access, rwb-deviation and rwb-integration, one set per contract version, plus the fixed clock selection |
| CaseListFixturePack | Data | The team, the two queues, the five cases and the out-of-scope case, the timers, the deviation, the export limit, the 23,600-case pack and the role and scope fixtures, per scenario |
| RowAssertion | Service | Compares the rows, their order, the ages in state, the service-level states, the prescription clock and the deviation flag against the fixture, and the three refusals of AC6, AC7 and AC9 |
| ExtractAssertion | Service | Compares the Excel file cell by cell with the expected header and data row, and asserts the header-only file of AC8 and the no-file refusal of AC10 |
| AccessLogAssertion | Service | Reads the export entry through the P4 operation and asserts the user, the time, the three filters, the row count and the entry-before-file order |
| EvidenceCollector | Service | Writes one report keyed by story key and business date, with the rows, the timers, the export cells, the access-log entry, the messages and the NFR read |
| GateEvaluator | Service | Passes the run when every owned scenario passes and the evidence pack is attached |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, the wave 2 harness profile, one business date, the fixed clock at 09:00 and 09:01, synthetic cases and synthetic roles only. The seeded values are the legacy sections 3 and 7: team "MTG-BKK" with queues "MTG-BKK-CO" and "MTG-BKK-LIT", cases "RW-2026-000101" to "RW-2026-000105", case "RW-2026-000201", deviation X1 on 9 December 2026, the export limit of 10,000 rows, the page range of 1 to 200 and the 23,600-case pack; no other value is added. Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0415; ASM-0590): the environment, the seed pack, the comparison method and the evidence format.

**Build steps**

1. Write the CaseListFixturePack with the team, the two queues, the five cases, the out-of-scope case, the timers, the deviation, the export limit and the 23,600-case pack; test that a bad seed stops the run without reporting a scenario (X10).
2. Write the FakeRegistry with the four WireMock mapping sets and the fixed clock, with the lists of values and the queue codes loaded from files.
3. Write JourneyRunner steps 1 to 5 for AC1: the session, the subscription, page 1, the columns, the three ages, the three service-level states and the order.
4. Add AC2 and AC4 with the paused case, its two clocks and the two boundary reads at 09:00 and 09:01.
5. Add AC6, AC7, AC8, AC9 and AC10 with the three filter refusals, the empty state, the scope case and the extract limit.
6. Add AC3 with the export, the cell-by-cell comparison and the access-log entry, then AC5 and AC11 with the NEW case and the two pages of 50.
7. Add the not-authorized case of TC-E2-033-12-ITG and the 23,600-case read, write EvidenceCollector and GateEvaluator, attach the report to the wave 2 release record and rerun the eleven scenarios on the release build.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.casewf.case-list-ageing` is on in the harness profile, as the legacy story sets it. Off, the breached parameter is ignored and the list and export keep the earlier columns, so the harness reports the journey as not applicable rather than as passed. The harness itself is a pipeline stage selected by the run profile, not by a business flag.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the run report is attached to the wave 2 release record with all eleven owned scenarios, and each fake has been replaced by the real service where its I story has landed in SIT. The NFR-008 check is a read the harness measures and does not build: page 1 of the list over 23,600 synthetic cases returns in under 2 seconds at the 95th percentile in SIT. The fixture pack and the evidence sign-off wait for the values of the gap and assumption rows cited above.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-007 | A filter value is not in its list | {value} is not a valid value for {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | Page size outside 1 to 200 | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-P3-020 | No case matches the filters | No cases match these filters. Change a filter to see more. |
| MSG-P3-021 | Extract above the row limit | The export holds at most {max} rows. Narrow the filters and try again. |
| MSG-P4-001 | No valid session | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role lacks Case record R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The export access event cannot be recorded | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

The harness asserts these messages and never rewrites them. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10. Its own report text is for the release team and is not part of the message standard.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-02 Case list, states Loading, Empty, List and Filtered. The team manager sets filters for queue, product, status, stage, owner and breached; reads the columns case number, product, queue, owner, status, stage, age in state, service level state, service level due, prescription date, prescription clock and deviation; and chooses Extract. A breached row carries the text "Breached", not colour alone; a paused stage clock shows "Paused". The Empty state shows MSG-P3-020.

No screen is built by this story. The harness drives the four states and the operations behind them and asserts the same facts through the contracts: the loading page holds the row count and the order, the list state the eleven columns, the filtered state the single row and the empty state the message. The visual layout belongs to RWB-P3-E2033-APP under DL31, and the accessibility acceptance of the "Breached" and "Paused" text is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0415; ASM-0590).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the page limits, the export limit, the lists of values, the queue codes and the service level values are parameter or reference data in the seed pack, never values in the harness.
- No personal data in the export sample, the events, the workflow inputs, the logs or the evidence: the seed holds synthetic cases and synthetic roles only, and the extract carries no customer field.
- No read of another service's tables and no schema of the harness's own: the list is read through the P3 contract and the access log through the P4 contract, and the harness runs no migration.
- The breach flag is computed at read time by rwb-case; the harness never changes a timer, a case or a deviation, and asserts that neither the boundary read nor the extract moved one.
- Each fake is replaced by the real service as its I story lands; a fake that outlives its service is a defect, not a configuration.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and a value that must change changes in the seed pack through a reviewed change, never by an exception in a scenario.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-034 for rwb-integration. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the rwb-integration side of the interaction ledger fixed as a contract: the seven CloudEvents types this consumer declares on their owners' topics, the P1 append contract and the P1 EFS and contact reads, the rwb-case, rwb-comms, rwb-partner, rwb-treatment and rwb-payment fact contracts it calls, the two admin operations it provides on the new base, the delivery states, the dedupe key and the three-attempt exception rule, the decision-record element and the contract fakes**, so that **the app, operations and test stories of this legacy key build on Day 1 against one agreed, testable shape and no team waits for another service to exist**.

The legacy story had no contract of its own: the ledger, the consumer, the mapping and the screen sat in one module, so the shape of a ledger entry was whatever the module wrote. Under D-RCV-60 the ledger belongs to rwb-source-data (DP-18), the timeline to rwb-case, the masking to rwb-access and the portal to rwb-partner, and this service becomes the transport between the seven events and that ledger. A transport needs a contract more than an owner does: it has to say what it declares, what it calls, what it counts, what it parks and what it never touches, and it has to be faked so that the app story can be built and tested before rwb-source-data and rwb-case are built.

The contract also fixes the seam that the split creates. The legacy story appended "inside the delivery's transaction"; across a REST boundary there is no shared transaction, so the contract states the only rule that gives the same guarantee: the append is called before the inbox row is marked, both are idempotent on the same key, and a repeat returns the same entry reference. That single sentence is what makes TC-E2-034-05 and TC-E2-034-07 provable across two services, and it is the reason this story is Day 1 work.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST with one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling rule (DP-11, ADR-020) and the event contract is the platform rule (DP-09, DP-14). Both only pay off if the seam is written down once. Here the seam is small and load-bearing: seven types consumed on four topics owned by other services, one create-only append operation, four fact contracts, one dedupe key, one exception rule and two admin operations.

If the shape is agreed and faked on Day 1, three teams move at once. The app story builds the listener, the mapper, the delivery tracker and the two workflows against the fakes; the operations story wires the consumer groups, the retry scan, the exception queue alert and the runbook against the same document; the test stories of RWB-E2-034, RWB-E2-022 and the P1 ledger read one entry shape. Without it, each team invents its own entry, the dedupe key and the retry rule diverge between the consumer and the screen, and the one property the business asked for — that a contact is recorded once and never lost — depends on which service crashed first.

The contract also states what this service does not own. The ledger table, the append-only trigger, the EFS outcome list and the retention classes are rwb-source-data's; the timeline, the sequence order and the scope check are rwb-case's; the masking is rwb-access's; the partner portal and the instruction facts are rwb-partner's. This document defines the consumed side of each and restates none of them as its own.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the REST base, the topic and the event names follow the platform rule and not a local choice (DP-13, DP-14).
- The CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the platform error envelope and the message catalogue are the platform baseline; this document narrows them where it must and says so (DP-09).
- The outbox and inbox library contract is available (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON): `processed_event`, `outbox_delivery`, `idempotency_key`, the retry topic and the `.dlt` topic are its elements and are reused, not redefined.
- The owners' event contracts are as published: `rwb.treatment.events.v1`, `rwb.comms.events.v1`, `rwb.partner.events.v1`, `rwb.payment.events.v1` and `rwb.source-data.events.v1` (Arch v5 slides 42 and 43).
- The rwb-source-data append, EFS and contact operations are as published by the P1 stories of this legacy key (RWB-P1-E1066-CON, RWB-P1-E1067-CON). This story consumes them and fakes them; it defines none of them.
- The rwb-case, rwb-comms, rwb-partner, rwb-treatment and rwb-payment CON stories are as published (RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON, RWB-P3-E2016-CON, RWB-P4-E1037-CON, RWB-P7-E1027-CON and the owner contracts of the fact reads).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the consumed-event contract: the seven types, their topics, their owners, the envelope, the key and the dedupe key of each.
2. Publish the P1 append contract as consumed: the operation, the entry command, the answer, the repeated-key answer and the 2 s budget.
3. Publish the P1 EFS outcome read and the P1 contact read as consumed, with their stubs and their placeholders where the source names no path or field.
4. Publish the fact contracts of rwb-case, rwb-comms, rwb-partner, rwb-treatment and rwb-payment with the element each mapper needs and the degradation rule of a 404.
5. Publish the two admin operations provided, with method, path, purpose, right, idempotency and the delivery states.
6. State the dedupe key, the three-attempt rule, the move to EXCEPTION and the `RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY` task for RW-PLATADM.
7. Publish the two workflows and their activity contracts, the retry policy of each activity and the shape of the EFS read summary.
8. Publish the table ownership: the five objects of `rwb_integration` this slice writes, and the explicit statement that no ledger table, no EFS reference table and no case timeline is among them.
9. Publish the fakes and the drift test, then tag the baseline and hand it to the app, operations and test stories of this key.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A message does not carry the CloudEvents 1.0 attributes, or its type is not one of the seven | The consumer refuses it before any state change and routes it to `.dlt` with an alert; no delivery row and no append | None | AC2 |
| X2 | A message carries no business key, so no dedupe key can be built | Refused as X1; the contract names the business key of each type | None | AC2 |
| X3 | A fake drifts from this document, or the app calls a path this document does not declare | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC5 |
| X4 | A service code path reads a ledger table, an ACE view or another service's table | The architecture boundary test fails the build | None | AC6 |
| X5 | A consumed contract removes, renames or retypes an element this document declares | The contract goes back to review with the owner of that operation, and the app, operations and test stories are re-baselined | None | AC2, AC3 |
| X6 | A field-level detail of a consumed operation is missing from the source material | The element carries the placeholder, one gap row and one assumption row, and the fake is written to the assumed shape | None | AC1 |
| X7 | The exception rule is asked to park a delivery that is already DELIVERED | The operation is refused and nothing changes; the states and their legal moves are those of 12.1 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC3 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes and the owners' published operations and declares none of theirs as its own |
| Negotiable | Field-level detail of the consumed operations is settled with their owners; the dedupe key, the state list and the exception rule are fixed by this realignment |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app, operations and test stories of this key and gives the P1 ledger and the P3 timeline one entry shape to agree on |
| Estimable | Seven consumed types, one append contract, two P1 reads, five fact contracts, two admin operations, five tables and eight fakes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact — the AsyncAPI document, the OpenAPI document, the fake, this file — and never against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Channel intake contract baseline for rwb-integration

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule and the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope of the platform library are in force
    Given the outbox and inbox library contract of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is in force
    Given the ledger is owned by rwb-source-data and the timeline by rwb-case

  Scenario: AC1 The nine contract tables are complete and attributed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the contract section of this story
    When the nine sub-tables are reviewed
    Then each of 12.1 to 12.9 is present and names its owner from the Ownership Map
    Then 12.1 names the two admin operations on the base /api/recovery/integration/v1
    Then 12.2 names the P1 append, the P1 EFS read, the P1 contact read and the five fact contracts
    Then 12.3 is the decision-record element only, 12.4 is the seven consumed types, 12.6 is None and 12.8 is the fakes
    Then 12.7 names only the five objects of rwb_integration and states that no ledger table is among them
    Then a sub-table that names another service's operation as provided fails the review

  Scenario: AC2 The seven consumed types are fixed with their envelope, key and dedupe key (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the consumed-event contract of this story
    When a message of each of the seven types is validated against it
    Then each message carries the CloudEvents 1.0 attributes id, source, type, specversion, time, subject and datacontenttype
    Then each message carries the business key that builds its dedupe key as <EV-nn>:<business key>:v1, and an EFS row uses EFS:<efs_record_key>
    Then each message is keyed by its case id where a case exists and carries no personal data
    Then a message without the envelope, without a business key, or of an eighth type is refused and routed to .dlt with an alert

  Scenario: AC3 The delivery states and the three-attempt exception rule are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the delivery contract of this story
    When a delivery is followed from its first attempt to its third failure
    Then its states are PENDING, RETRYING, DELIVERED and EXCEPTION and no other state is written
    Then attempt 2 and attempt 3 follow the retry policy of the environment, and the attempt limit is three
    Then after the third failed attempt the status is EXCEPTION with the last error code and a task RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY for role RW-PLATADM
    Then a delivery in EXCEPTION may be resent to PENDING with attempt count 0, and a delivery not in EXCEPTION answers 409
    Then an unresolvable case follows the same rule and writes no entry on any attempt

  Scenario: AC4 The P1 append contract is consumed and no ledger table is owned (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the append contract of this story
    When the entry command and the answer are reviewed
    Then the command carries caseId, eventCode, channel, direction, occurredAt, sourceSystem, contactKey, fromHolderRef, toHolderRef, treatmentId, proceedsId, deliveryStatus, externalRef and idempotencyKey
    Then the append is create-only and idempotent on the key, so a repeat returns the same entry reference and writes nothing
    Then the append is called before the inbox row is marked, so a replay after a timeout writes one entry
    Then the interaction table, its append-only trigger, the EFS ledger outcome list and the retention classes are declared as rwb-source-data's and none appears in 12.7
    Then the rwb-source-data WireMock answers 201, the same reference on a repeat, 409 and 503

  Scenario: AC5 The eight fakes match this document and drift fails the build (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the eight fakes of 12.8
    When each fake is compared with the element it serves
    Then every consumed path and payload is answered with the shape of this document
    Then every error answer named in this document is reachable in a fake
    Then a drift between a fake and this document fails the contract test and blocks the merge

  Scenario: AC6 No cross-schema read and no foreign key leave this service (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the code and the migrations of the app and operations stories of this key
    When the architecture boundary test runs
    Then no statement reads a table of another service, a ledger table or an ACE view
    Then the only cross-service calls are the declared paths of 12.2, one hop each with a 2 s budget
    Then rwb_integration holds no foreign key into another schema and no copy of a ledger, case, notice, instruction, treatment or proceeds row
    Then the seven consumed topics are the only subscriptions and no topic of this service is subscribed
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base and one topic per service: this contract declares `/api/recovery/integration/v1` and consumes the owners' topics; it never declares another service's path or topic as its own | DP-13; DP-14; ownership map |
| BR2 | The seven consumed types are `rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1`, `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1`, `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1`, `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1`, `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1`, `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` and `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1`, on the owners' topics | Arch v5 slides 42 and 43; naming library (DP-14) |
| BR3 | The ledger is rwb-source-data's: the entry is created only through its append operation, and this service holds no ledger table, no ledger column and no ledger read | R-PREC default ruling; DP-18; ownership map ruling on `interaction` |
| BR4 | The append is create-only and idempotent on the key, and it is called before the inbox row is marked; a repeat returns the same entry reference and writes nothing | Legacy RWB-E2-034 BR7; R-UNI-40; REQ-ILG-007 |
| BR5 | One dedupe key per message: `<EV-nn>:<business key>:v1` for the six business events and `EFS:<efs_record_key>` for an EFS row, held in `processed_event` with a hit count | Legacy BR7; FSD P2 v3 AC-EXC-P2-007-03 and AC-EXC-P2-007-07 |
| BR6 | The delivery states are PENDING, RETRYING, DELIVERED and EXCEPTION; the attempt limit is three; the last failure raises `RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY` for role RW-PLATADM and an EXCEPTION delivery may be resent to PENDING with attempt count 0 | Legacy AC8 and AC7; FSD P2 v3 T4 and AC-EXC-P2-001-01; TSD P2 v3 LOV-OUTBOX-DELIVERY |
| BR7 | The two admin operations are the exception queue surface of this slice and are attributed to rwb-integration; the outbound-item operations are the baseline story's and are not declared here | TSD P2 v3 T-A.1 API-P2-003 and API-P2-004; ownership map |
| BR8 | The EFS read step is started by AceDataReady and is not an outbox delivery; it carries its own workflow and its own summary | Legacy section 12 (EFS contact read step); EV-26 |
| BR9 | No business value in the contract: the event codes, the channels, the directions, the retry intervals and the attempt limit are reference rows and environment values | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; FSD P2 v3 BR-P2-007 |
| BR10 | No contract element names a person: the entry carries identifiers, codes and references, and the contact point is a key | Legacy BR5; REQ-ILG-014; CTL-11 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The nine sub-tables, the seven types, the append contract and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app, operations and test stories accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A field, an error code or a fake is added without removing one | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change to a consumed operation | An owner removes, renames or retypes an element this contract declares | In review, with that owner |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake | A contract test fails | In review |
| Baselined | A new channel event is declared | The owner publishes on its own topic and this contract adds one type and one mapping | Baselined (new type) |

The delivery states of the runtime are PENDING, RETRYING, DELIVERED and EXCEPTION and are fixed in 12.1; they are not states of this document.

##### 11. Data

The contract declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Consumed event envelope | id, source, type, specversion, time, subject, datacontenttype; the payload of the event type, keyed by case id where a case exists |
| Dedupe record | consumer, idempotency key in the form above, CloudEvents id, hit count, last seen at (`processed_event`) |
| Ledger entry command | caseId, eventCode, channel, direction, occurredAt, sourceSystem, contactKey, fromHolderRef, toHolderRef, treatmentId, proceedsId, deliveryStatus, externalRef, idempotencyKey |
| Ledger entry answer | the entry reference and the event code, with the retention class resolved by the owner |
| Delivery record | event id, consumer, status, attempt count, next attempt at, last error code, delivered at, task id (`outbox_delivery`) |
| Task element | the `RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY` task for role RW-PLATADM, linked from the delivery |
| Decision-record element | decision code, final call, the action (resend or exception), the delivery reference and the freshness, written by the library on `rwb.decision-record.v1` |
| EFS read summary | businessDate, rowsRead, written, excluded, notOnCase |
| Activity input and output | the event type and payload in; the ledger entry reference and the delivery state out |

The physical names, lengths and required flags of the entry command and of the fact answers are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0665; ASM-1173); this story fixes the element names above and leaves the physical names to the review with the rwb-source-data owner. The request and response bodies of the two admin operations are likewise Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0665; ASM-1173).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/integration/v1`; owner rwb-integration (P2). Two operations.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/outbox/deliveries` | Lists the deliveries of consumer `ledger-channels` by status, consumer, event type, from and to, with the page and size parameters of the legacy appendix | Platform administration R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| POST | `/admin/outbox/deliveries/{deliveryId}/resend` | Sends a delivery in EXCEPTION again: status PENDING, attempt count 0, the workflow started again for the same event; written to the decision record with the user and the time | Platform administration U, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` header; 409 when the delivery is not in EXCEPTION |

The delivery states are PENDING, RETRYING, DELIVERED and EXCEPTION (LOV-OUTBOX-DELIVERY, TSD P2 v3 T3.2). The retry policy of a delivery is three attempts; the intervals are environment values (BR9). Errors: 401 no session, 403 no Platform administration right (MSG-P4-002), 404 unknown delivery, 409 not in EXCEPTION or a workflow already running (MSG-GEN-004), 503 dependency unavailable. These two operations are the re-based forms of API-P2-003 and API-P2-004 of TSD P2 v3 T-A.1, whose paths sat under the monolith base; the outbound-item operations `GET /admin/outbound-items` and `POST /admin/outbound-items/{itemId}/resend` remain with the rwb-integration baseline of RWB-P2-E1007-CON and are not declared here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` | P1 rwb-source-data | The `InteractionLedgerWriter` append: one entry per call, create-only, idempotent on the key; faked with 201, the same reference on a repeat, 409 and 503 |
| GET | The EFS contact-outcome read of the rwb-source-data contract, for a business date | P1 rwb-source-data | The EFS action rows of the date for accounts on open cases (legacy `EfsContactHistory.outcomesFor`); faked with listed, unlisted and not-on-a-case rows |
| GET | The contact-fact read of the rwb-source-data contract, by contact key | P1 rwb-source-data | The contact key behind an entry (legacy `ContactQuery.byKey`); faked with one hit and one 404 |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case, its holder and its status; faked with one case and one 404 for AC3 |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases` | P3 rwb-case | The open case ids of an account (legacy `CaseQuery.openCaseIdsForAccount`) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}` | P6 rwb-comms | The case, the contact key, the notice type, the barcode and the delivery status (legacy `NoticeQuery.byId`) |
| GET | The instruction-fact read of the rwb-partner contract | S9 rwb-partner | The case and the partner code of an instruction (legacy `InstructionQuery.byId`) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/treatment/v1/treatments/{treatmentId}` | S2 rwb-treatment | The treatment and its case behind an OFFER entry |
| GET | The proceeds-fact read of the rwb-payment contract | P8 rwb-payment | The proceeds and its case behind a PAYMENT entry |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The role and scope check of the two provided operations |

Every operation is one hop with a 2 s client budget and no retry on a 4xx (DP-11, ADR-020). The EFS outcome read, the contact read, the instruction read and the proceeds read are named by their legacy Java interfaces only; their paths, query parameters and JSON field names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0665; ASM-1173), and the case-list account filter is unnamed in the same way.

###### 12.3 Events published

None by this story's own topic. The shared event `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` is published by the local decision-record library of DP-03 when a resend or an exception is recorded; its schema is unchanged by this story and is the one declared in RWB-P7-E1027-CON (EV-08, Arch v5 slide 42 row 08). `rwb.integration.events.v1` carries FileDelivered and FileFailed from the outbound file side (Arch v5 slide 16) and this slice publishes neither.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event type | Topic | Owner | Consumer contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1` | `rwb.treatment.events.v1` | S2 | CloudEvents 1.0; key case id; dedupe `<EV-10>:<treatmentId>:v1`; one OFFER entry |
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 | Key case id; dedupe `<EV-14>:<noticeId>:v1`; one LETTER entry, delivery status SENT, external reference the barcode |
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 | Key case id; dedupe `<EV-15>:<noticeId>:v1`; one LETTER entry, delivery status DELIVERED, external reference the barcode |
| `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` | `rwb.partner.events.v1` | S9 | Key case id; dedupe `<EV-20>:<instructionId>:v1`; one HANDOVER entry, channel PORTAL, direction OUTBOUND |
| `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1` | `rwb.partner.events.v1` | S9 | Key case id; dedupe `<EV-21>:<instructionId>:v1`; one PARTNER_RESULT entry, channel PORTAL, direction INBOUND |
| `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` | `rwb.payment.events.v1` | P8 | Key case id; dedupe `<EV-25>:<proceedsId>:v1`; one PAYMENT entry |
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 | Key the source and the business date, for example `EV-26:ALS:2026-11-10`; starts EfsLedgerReadWorkflow for the EFS source and writes no entry by itself |

All seven are consumed with the inbox dedupe of `processed_event`, at least once, and idempotent by key. A message that fails the envelope, lacks the business key or carries an eighth type is routed to `.dlt` with an alert (DP-09). The payload of each type is the owner's; this contract declares the elements the mapper reads and does not restate the owner's schema.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| LedgerChannelIntakeWorkflow | Workflow, one execution per consumed event, workflow ID = the CloudEvents id | `rwb-integration` | Input: event type, CloudEvents id, business key, occurred time, case id, payload reference. Output: the ledger entry reference and the delivery state |
| mapChannelEvent | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: event type and payload. Output: the ledger entry command of 11; one method per type (BR2) |
| resolveChannelFacts | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: the identifier the event carries. Output: the resolved facts; a 404 leaves the link empty and is not retryable, a 5xx is retryable |
| appendLedgerEntry | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: the entry command and the key. Output: the entry reference; a repeat returns the same reference, a 409 is treated as success |
| parkDeliveryInException | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: delivery id, failure class, attempt count. Output: status EXCEPTION, the `RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY` task for RW-PLATADM, the decision record |
| EfsLedgerReadWorkflow | Workflow, started by AceDataReady for the EFS source | `rwb-integration` | Input: business date and source EFS. Output: the EFS read summary |
| readEfsOutcomes | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: business date. Output: the kept rows and the excluded count |
| appendEfsEntries | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: the kept rows. Output: the written count, one append per row under `EFS:<efs_record_key>` |
| writeEfsReadSummary | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: the counts. Output: the summary of 11 |

The retry policy of every activity is the workflow kit's: initial interval 1 s, back-off 2, maximum 3 attempts, with the 4xx answers of the append classified as non-retryable except 409 (DP-10). The workflow input and history carry identifiers, codes and counts only.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Schedule is registered for this slice. The intake is event-started from the seven consumed types and the EFS read step is started by AceDataReady, not by a timer (BR8; Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-02 and JOB-04). The outbox relay of each service runs every minute in the platform relay of DP-09 and is not a Schedule of this contract.

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |

| outbound_item | P2 (rwb_integration) | Read only, for the interface column of the exception queue; this slice writes no outbound file item |
| outbox_delivery | PLT library, created in rwb_integration | One delivery per consumed event and consumer `ledger-channels`; the status, attempt count, next attempt, last error and task of 12.1 |
| processed_event | PLT library, created in rwb_integration | The inbox: consumer, idempotency key, CloudEvents id, hit count |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_integration | The stored response of the two provided operations, kept 24 hours |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in rwb_integration | The local decision record of a resend and of an exception (DP-03) |

No other table is named. `interaction`, its append-only trigger and its indexes are rwb-source-data's; `efs_ledger_outcome` and the retention classes are rwb-source-data's; the case timeline and the sequence order are rwb-case's. None of them appears here as an object of this service (BR3, DP-01, DP-18). `outbox_event` exists in `rwb_integration` from the baseline and this slice writes no row in it, because the consumed events are produced by their owners.

**Build steps**

1. Write the AsyncAPI document: the seven types, their topics, their owners, the key and the dedupe key of each, and the `.dlt` rule.
2. Write the append contract: the entry command, the answer, the repeat answer, the 409 and the ordering rule with the inbox.
3. Write the fact contracts of the P1 EFS and contact reads and of the five owners, with the 404 and 5xx split; carry the placeholder where the source names no path or field.
4. Write the two provided operations: method, path, purpose, right, idempotency, the four states and the exception rule.
5. Write the activity contract: the two workflows, the six activities, the retry policy and the EFS read summary.
6. Write the table ownership statement and the explicit absence of the ledger, the EFS list and the timeline.
7. Build the eight WireMock mappings and their fixtures.
8. Add the six contract tests of section 16, including the drift test between each fake and this document.
9. Tag the baseline and collect the sign-off of the app, operations and test stories of this key.

**Done when.** The five contract files validate in the pipeline, the six contract tests pass, the eight fakes answer every consumed path and payload, and the app and operations stories of this legacy key have accepted the baseline.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the event codes, the channels, the directions, the retry intervals and the attempt limit stay rows of reference data and environment values.
- No personal data in an event, a command, an activity input or a fake: identifiers, codes and references only, and the contact point is a key.
- The contract names only rwb-integration's own operations as provided; the P1 append and the fact reads are consumed and are never restated as this service's (DP-01, DP-13).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base as provided, or a topic outside `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- The ledger table, its trigger, the EFS ledger outcome list and the retention classes appear nowhere as objects of this service (DP-18).
- Every example and fixture is synthetic; no production payload, contact point or event is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The envelope, the inbox, the retry topic and the `.dlt` rule come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform operator of the channel intake (RW-PLATADM on call)**, I want **each of the six ledger events that the channels publish, plus AceDataReady for EFS, turned into one ledger entry by a consumer that appends through the rwb-source-data `InteractionLedgerWriter` contract, deduplicated by its own inbox, and a delivery whose case cannot be resolved parked in the exception queue with a task after three attempts, and the EFS read step to write its read summary**, so that **a contact, letter, hand-over, offer or payment is never lost between the channel that produced it and the ledger that records it, and no delivery disappears without an owner**.

The legacy story sat in module P2 Integration and did the whole job in one place: it owned the outbox consumer "ledger-channels", the event-to-entry mapping, the holder enrichment, the retention class, the EFS read step, the ledger columns and the timeline section. Under D-RCV-60 the ledger is not a P2 object. The R-PREC default ruling puts the interaction ledger and its intake rule in rwb-source-data (P1, DP-18; ownership map ruling on `interaction` and `efs_ledger_outcome`), the case timeline and the timeline read stay in rwb-case (P3), masking stays in rwb-access (P4) and the partner portal stays in rwb-partner (S9). What is left in module P2 — the outbound and event transport of the module — is the channel intake: a consumer on the owners' topics, a mapper, an idempotent append through the P1 contract, a delivery trail with its retries and its exception queue, and the EFS read step. That is what this story builds.

The ledger table, its append-only trigger `tr_interaction_append_only` and its read are not written here (DP-01, DP-18). The six business events are consumed on their owners' topics, never on a topic of this service (DP-14). Each append is one hop to the P1 contract with a 2 s budget (DP-11, DP-13). The append-only rule survives the split because the append operation is create-only and idempotent on the entry key, and the service that owns the table refuses a second key.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contact outcomes from collections, letters sent through WIN and work held by partners are recorded in different systems today, so a case owner who picks up a case does not know which number answered or who held the case last. The legacy story answered that by bringing every channel into the one ledger built in Epic 1 and showing it as a timeline on the case. The business measure is unchanged: the share of open cases whose last right-party contact is visible on the case, which today is zero for cases that came from EFS.

The realignment keeps the measure and changes the seam. With 19 services, the ledger has one owner and it is not the integration module; if the intake also wrote the ledger there would be two writers of one append-only table, which is the failure the append-only trigger exists to prevent. The intake therefore has to be a transport: it must be allowed to fail, retry and park a delivery without the ledger knowing, and the ledger must be able to refuse a repeated key without the intake losing the event. That is what makes the channel set extensible: a seventh channel costs one mapping and one consumer group, not a change to the ledger.

The story meets REQ-ILG-009 (contact outcomes reach the ledger), REQ-ILG-010 (dispatched letters write their result, including proof of delivery), REQ-ILG-011 (a hand-over names who held the case, who holds it now and when), REQ-ILG-013 (each entry carries its retention class, resolved by the owner of the ledger), REQ-ILG-014 (the contact point is a reference and never a copy), REQ-ILG-007 (one entry per key, a repeat counted), REQ-ILG-008 (a failed write loses nothing) and REQ-ILG-006 (the timeline reads in time order, which the intake serves by carrying the occurred time unchanged). REQ-ILG-012 (the timeline is shown on the case record) is served by rwb-case and is cited here for traceability only.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P2-E2034-CON is baselined: the consumed event contracts, the P1 append contract, the two admin operations, the delivery states, the dedupe key and the three-attempt rule (this key's contract story, Day 1).
- RWB-P2-E1007-APP is done: the rwb-integration service baseline, its `rwb_integration` schema, its login, its chart and its REST base `/api/recovery/integration/v1` (DP-01, DP-13).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-PLT-E1043-CON are published: the rwb-case parameters and reference-data contracts with their client library (DP-06, DP-07). The EFS ledger outcome list and the retention classes are P1 reference rows and are read by the P1 writer, not here.
- RWB-PLT-E1037-CON is published: the rwb-access authorise contract and the guard library (DP-08).
- RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is published: the outbox and inbox library, the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the retry topic and the `.dlt` topic of each owner's topic (DP-09).
- RWB-PLT-E1071-CON is published: the workflow kit, its worker and its retry policy (DP-10).
- RWB-PLT-E1044-CON is published: the per-service Flyway sequence and the migration conventions of `rwb_integration` (DP-15).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route that serves the exception queue screen SCR-09 (DP-19).
- The six producers publish on their topics: `rwb.treatment.events.v1` (TreatmentApproved, EV-10), `rwb.comms.events.v1` (NoticeDispatched EV-14 and NoticeDelivered EV-15), `rwb.partner.events.v1` (InstructionIssued EV-20 and PartnerResultSubmitted EV-21), `rwb.payment.events.v1` (ProceedsMatched EV-25) and `rwb.source-data.events.v1` (AceDataReady EV-26).
- The P1 append contract, the P1 EFS outcome read and the P1 contact read are reachable inside the 2 s single-hop budget.
- Feature flag `rwb.integration.ledger-channels` exists in the platform flag library (legacy flag name kept), off by default in every environment.
- The service runs as the rwb-integration login (DP-02). The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0664; ASM-1168).

##### 4. Flow

1. Outbox relay: delivers one CloudEvent per message to consumer `ledger-channels` on each owner's topic, with its retry topic and its `.dlt` topic (DP-09).
2. LedgerChannelListener: validates the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the event type against the seven declared types, then reads the event's idempotency key `<EV-nn>:<business key>:v1` through the inbox of `processed_event` (DP-09). A repeat is counted in `hit_count` and acknowledged without a second append.
3. LedgerChannelIntakeWorkflow: starts one workflow execution per event, workflow ID `<eventId>` in namespace `rwb-recovery` on task queue `rwb-integration` (DP-10).
4. LedgerChannelMapper (activity `mapChannelEvent`): maps the event to exactly one ledger entry command, by BR1 to BR4: event code, channel, direction, occurred time, source system, the case id, the contact key, the holder references and the business link.
5. FactResolution (activity `resolveChannelFacts`): reads the facts it needs through their owners' contracts, one hop each with a 2 s budget and no retry on a 4xx: the case and its holder from the rwb-case contract, the notice barcode and delivery status from the rwb-comms contract, the partner code from the rwb-partner contract, the treatment from the rwb-treatment contract and the proceeds from the rwb-payment contract (DP-11).
6. LedgerAppend (activity `appendLedgerEntry`): calls the P1 append operation once with the entry command and the idempotency key, and receives the ledger entry reference. The append is create-only and idempotent on the key, so a replay after a timeout returns the same reference and writes nothing (DP-18).
7. InboxCompletion: on a 2xx answer the delivery moves to DELIVERED with its `delivered_at`, and the `processed_event` row is upserted with the key and the hit count. The append happens before the inbox mark, so a crash between the two replays the append and the P1 writer returns the same entry (BR5).
8. ExceptionPath (activity `parkDeliveryInException`): on a 5xx, a timeout or a case that cannot be resolved, the delivery stays PENDING or moves to RETRYING and its `next_attempt_at` is set by the retry policy. After the third failed attempt the delivery moves to EXCEPTION, `last_error_code` names the failure class, and a task `RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY` is raised for role RW-PLATADM and linked in `task_id` (BR6).
9. EfsContactOutcomeReader: on AceDataReady (EV-26) for the EFS source, starts EfsLedgerReadWorkflow, not an outbox delivery (BR8).
10. EfsLedgerReadWorkflow (activity `readEfsOutcomes`): reads the EFS action rows of the business date for accounts linked to open cases through the P1 EFS outcome read, and keeps only the action codes the EFS ledger outcome list holds (BR7).
11. EfsLedgerReadWorkflow (activity `appendEfsEntries`): maps each kept row to a CONTACT entry with source EFS and the idempotency key `EFS:<efs_record_key>`, and calls the same P1 append operation once per row.
12. EfsLedgerReadWorkflow (activity `writeEfsReadSummary`): closes the run with the read summary `businessDate`, `rowsRead`, `written`, `excluded`, `notOnCase`.
13. Platform administrator: opens SCR-09 through gateway-bff, filters the deliveries of consumer `ledger-channels` by status, consumer and event type, and resends a delivery in EXCEPTION (DP-19).
14. Resend: `POST /admin/outbox/deliveries/{deliveryId}/resend` sets the delivery PENDING with attempt count 0 under an `Idempotency-Key`, writes the resend to the decision record and starts the workflow again for the same event.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The same event arrives twice with the same CloudEvents id and business key | One entry exists; the repeat is counted in `hit_count` and no second append is made | None | AC8; BR5 |
| X2 | An EFS row carries an action code that the EFS ledger outcome list does not hold | No entry; the row is counted as excluded in the read summary | None | Carried by the P1 story of this legacy key (AC6) |
| X3 | An EFS row belongs to an account on no open case | No entry; the row is counted as not on a case | None | Carried by the P1 story of this legacy key (AC6) |
| X4 | The P1 append returns 5xx or times out | The delivery stays PENDING or moves to RETRYING with `next_attempt_at`; an incident is raised and no entry is discarded | None | Carried by this story as the transport half of AC7 |
| X5 | The event names a case that does not exist | No entry after each attempt; after the third failed attempt the delivery is EXCEPTION with a task for role RW-PLATADM | MSG-P2-001 | AC8 |
| X6 | A fact read answers 404 | The mapper keeps the entry and leaves the link empty; the delivery is DELIVERED and the gap is logged without personal data | None | BR4 |
| X7 | A fact read answers 5xx or times out | Retryable: the activity fails and the workflow retries inside the 2 s budget; after the third attempt the delivery is EXCEPTION | MSG-P2-001 | AC8 |
| X8 | A message fails envelope validation, or carries a type this consumer does not declare | The message is refused before any state change and routed to `.dlt` with an alert | None | BR2 |
| X9 | A role without Platform administration opens the exception queue or resends | Refused before any read or write | MSG-P4-002 | Carried by the CON story as a contract case |
| X10 | The delivery is resent while the workflow for the same event is running | Refused with 409; nothing changes and no second workflow is started | MSG-GEN-004 | BR6 |
| X11 | The P1 append refuses the key as a repeat | The answer is treated as success; the delivery is DELIVERED and the hit count rises | None | AC8; BR5 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the published contracts only: the P1 append, EFS and contact reads, the P3, P6, S9, S2 and P8 fact reads, the platform outbox and workflow kit, and the rwb-integration baseline. Every one of them is faked |
| Negotiable | Retry intervals, alert thresholds, replica counts and consumer group names are environment values; the mapping, the dedupe key and the three-attempt rule are fixed by the CON story of this key |
| Valuable | Closes the last gap between a channel that produced an interaction and the ledger that records it, without a second writer of the append-only table |
| Estimable | One listener, one mapper, two workflows, five activities, one exception path, one admin surface and one migration |
| Small | Fits two weeks with the tests of section 16 |
| Testable | Each owned criterion and each transport path has a test in section 16, and every cross-service answer is stubbed in a contract fake |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Channel intake of the interaction ledger for rwb-integration

  Background:
    Given open case "RW-2026-000301" with account "ACC-SYN-0301" and owner "U-2001"
    Given the EFS ledger outcome list holds action code "PTP" with channel CALL
    Given the retention class for every event code is "ILG-STD"

  Scenario: AC8 An event for an unknown case goes to the exception queue (legacy RWB-E2-034 AC8)
    Given event InstructionIssued names an instruction whose case does not exist
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns no case for the instruction's case
    When the outbox has retried the delivery 3 times
    Then the system writes no entry
    Then the delivery is in the exception queue with a task for role RW-PLATADM
```

AC8 is the only legacy criterion this story owns, and it is copied word for word with one Given added for the mocked cross-service part: the rwb-case contract mock returns no case for the instruction's case, because rwb-case is now another service and the case lookup is a contract call. Every value of the legacy scenario is kept: the instruction event, the nonexistent case, the three retries, the empty ledger and the task for role RW-PLATADM.

The other legacy criteria are not owned here. AC1, AC6 and AC9 (the EFS contact entry, the EFS outcome list, the late EFS row) and AC3 (the ledger is one place, read through `GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions`) belong to the rwb-source-data stories of this legacy key, which own the ledger, the EFS intake rule and the interaction read. AC2 (a hand-over is recorded) is split: the CASE_ALLOCATED and CASE_TRANSFERRED entries and the holder enrichment are rwb-case's, and only the partner hand-over and partner result entries of BR2 are produced by this intake. AC4 (letter, delivery, offer and payment are recorded) is the mapping this story transports, but the ledger assertions are the P1 story's. AC5 (nothing is written twice) is proved in three places — the inbox here in TC-E2-034-05, the append-only key in P1, and the timeline in P3. AC7 (a ledger write failure loses nothing) is the transport half carried here as exception path X4 and the ledger half carried by P1. AC10 (a case with no entry) and AC11 (a case outside the reader's scope) are the timeline and the scope rules of rwb-case, rwb-source-data and rwb-access.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Event to ledger event code: InstructionIssued to HANDOVER; PartnerResultSubmitted to PARTNER_RESULT; NoticeDispatched and NoticeDelivered to LETTER; TreatmentApproved to OFFER; ProceedsMatched to PAYMENT; an EFS action row to CONTACT. The codes are kept character for character and are sent as they are | Legacy RWB-E2-034 BR1; LOV-LEDGER-EVENT |
| BR2 | The intake consumes exactly seven types on their owners' topics and publishes none of its own: `rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1`, `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1`, `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1`, `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1`, `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1`, `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` and `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | Arch v5 slides 42 and 43; DP-14 |
| BR3 | A partner hand-over has channel PORTAL and direction OUTBOUND with the holder before and after; a partner result has channel PORTAL and direction INBOUND; a notice entry has channel LETTER and carries the delivery status and the barcode as its external reference | Legacy BR2; LOV-CHANNEL; LOV-DIRECTION |
| BR4 | The contact point travels as a reference: the entry carries `contactKey` and never a number or an address; a fact that cannot be read leaves its link empty and never blocks the entry | Legacy BR5; REQ-ILG-014; CTL-11 |
| BR5 | One entry per idempotency key. The append is called before the inbox row is marked, both are idempotent on the key, and a repeat is counted rather than rejected | Legacy BR7; R-UNI-40; REQ-ILG-007 |
| BR6 | A failed append or an unresolvable case never discards the delivery: it is retried, and after the third failed attempt it is EXCEPTION with a task `RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY` for role RW-PLATADM | Legacy BR8; FSD P2 v3 AC-EXC-P2-001-01 and T4; REQ-ILG-008 |
| BR7 | An EFS row enters the ledger only when its action code is in the EFS ledger outcome list and only for an account linked to an open case; the list and the retention classes are rows of rwb-source-data and are never copied into rwb_integration | Legacy BR3, BR6; DL29; DL26; DP-18 |
| BR8 | The EFS read step is started by AceDataReady and is not an outbox delivery; a rerun for the same business date writes only the rows not yet written, by the key `EFS:<efs_record_key>` | Legacy section 12 (EFS contact read step); EV-26 |
| BR9 | The intake writes no ledger row and reads no ledger table: the entry is created through the P1 append operation and the ledger is never queried from this service | DP-01; DP-18; ownership map ruling on `interaction` |
| BR10 | The intake publishes no business event of its own; the decision record of a resend and of an exception is written through the local library and published on `rwb.decision-record.v1` | DP-03; Arch v5 slide 42 row 08 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | Event delivered to consumer `ledger-channels` | The envelope and the type validate | PENDING |
| PENDING | appendLedgerEntry returns 2xx | The entry exists in the ledger | DELIVERED |
| PENDING | Append or fact read fails | attempt_count < 3 | RETRYING |
| RETRYING | Retry attempt returns 2xx | The entry exists in the ledger | DELIVERED |
| RETRYING | Retry attempt fails | attempt_count = 3 | EXCEPTION |
| PENDING | The case cannot be resolved | attempt_count = 3 | EXCEPTION |
| EXCEPTION | Resend by RW-PLATADM | The delivery is in EXCEPTION and no workflow runs for the event | PENDING with attempt count 0 |

The four states are the values of LOV-OUTBOX-DELIVERY: PENDING, RETRYING, DELIVERED, EXCEPTION (TSD P2 v3 T3.2 and T4). The intake changes the state of its own deliveries only; it changes no case status and no ledger row, because the ledger is append-only and owned by rwb-source-data (legacy section 9, DP-18).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-INTGR, the rwb-integration service identity | Consumes the seven types, maps each event, calls the P1 append, the P1 EFS read and the fact reads, and moves its own deliveries (service identity, no case right) |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Reads the exception queue and resends a delivery (Platform administration, RU) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the deliveries, the resend record and the run summaries (Platform administration, R) |
| rwb-source-data contract | Creates the ledger entry from the append and owns the append-only rule; it refuses a repeated key and resolves the retention class |
| rwb-case contract | Supplies the case and its holder; it owns the timeline and the scope check of the read |
| rwb-access contract | Supplies the role and scope decision of the exception queue operations |
| No approval applies | The intake takes no business decision; the resend is recorded, not approved |

The service runs as the rwb-integration login (DP-02). The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0664; ASM-1168). The `SY-CASEWF` actor and the "recovery service identity" of the legacy story are retired with the split: the EFS read step runs under the rwb-integration identity and reads EFS facts through the P1 contract, never through a view (DP-05, DP-18).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/integration/v1`; owner rwb-integration (P2). Two operations, the exception queue surface of this slice.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/admin/outbox/deliveries` | Lists the deliveries of consumer `ledger-channels` by status, consumer, event type and date window, with the attempt count, the next attempt time, the last error code and the linked task | Platform administration R | Not applicable |
| POST | `/admin/outbox/deliveries/{deliveryId}/resend` | Sends a delivery in EXCEPTION again: status PENDING, attempt count 0, the workflow started again for the same event | Platform administration U | `Idempotency-Key`; a delivery not in EXCEPTION answers 409 |

Both operations are the re-based forms of API-P2-003 and API-P2-004 of the legacy appendix (TSD P2 v3 T-A.1), whose paths sat under the monolith base. The outbound-item operations `GET /admin/outbound-items` and `POST /admin/outbound-items/{itemId}/resend` stay with the rwb-integration baseline of RWB-P2-E1007-CON and are not declared here. The request query parameters, the response fields and the error bodies of the two operations are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0664; ASM-1168).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` | rwb-source-data (P1) | The `InteractionLedgerWriter` append: one ledger entry per call, create-only and idempotent on the key (ownership map: `POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions`, owner P1) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| GET | The EFS contact-outcome read of the rwb-source-data contract, for a business date | rwb-source-data (P1) | The EFS action rows of the business date for accounts on open cases (legacy `EfsContactHistory.outcomesFor`) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| GET | The contact-fact read of the rwb-source-data contract, by contact key | rwb-source-data (P1) | The contact key behind a Workbench or notice entry (legacy `ContactQuery.byKey`) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | rwb-case (P3) | The case, its holder and its status (DP-06, DP-07 owner) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases` | rwb-case (P3) | The open case ids of an account (legacy `CaseQuery.openCaseIdsForAccount`) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |

| GET | The instruction-fact read of the rwb-partner contract | rwb-partner (S9) | The case and the partner code of an instruction (legacy `InstructionQuery.byId`) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |

The EFS outcome read, the contact read, the instruction read and the proceeds read are named by their legacy Java interfaces but have no path in the Ownership Map; their paths, query parameters and JSON field names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0664; ASM-1168). The case-list account filter is likewise unnamed and follows the same placeholder. The RWB-P1-E1066-CON and RWB-P1-E1067-CON published interfaces are the ones this story calls; the shape of the append command is the P1 contract's and is restated in RWB-P2-E2034-CON only.

###### 12.3 Events published

None by this service's topic. `rwb.integration.events.v1` carries FileDelivered and FileFailed from the outbound file side (Arch v5 slide 16) and this slice publishes neither. The decision record of a resend and of an exception is written by the local decision-record library, which publishes `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) on `rwb.decision-record.v1` in the same transaction as the delivery change (DP-03, H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event type | Topic | Owner | Consumer element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1` | `rwb.treatment.events.v1` | S2 | Inbox dedupe, then one OFFER entry |
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 | Inbox dedupe, then one LETTER entry with delivery status SENT |
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | P6 | Inbox dedupe, then one LETTER entry with delivery status DELIVERED |
| `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` | `rwb.partner.events.v1` | S9 | Inbox dedupe, then one HANDOVER entry, channel PORTAL, direction OUTBOUND |
| `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1` | `rwb.partner.events.v1` | S9 | Inbox dedupe, then one PARTNER_RESULT entry, channel PORTAL, direction INBOUND |
| `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` | `rwb.payment.events.v1` | P8 | Inbox dedupe, then one PAYMENT entry linked to the proceeds |
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | P1 | Starts EfsLedgerReadWorkflow for the EFS source; not an outbox delivery |

All seven are CloudEvents 1.0 with the envelope attributes id, source, type, specversion, time, subject, datacontenttype, keyed by the case id where a case exists. The dedupe key is the event's own business key in the form `<EV-nn>:<business key>:v1` for the six business events (`EV-10:TRT-SYN-0301:v1`, `EV-26:ALS:2026-11-10` are the documented shapes of the FSD) and `EFS:<efs_record_key>` for an EFS row. Delivery is at least once; the consumer is idempotent by key. A message without the envelope, or of a type not in this table, is routed to `.dlt` (DP-09).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| LedgerChannelIntakeWorkflow | Workflow, one execution per consumed event, workflow ID = the CloudEvents id | `rwb-integration` | Input: event type, CloudEvents id, business key, occurred time, case id, payload reference. Output: the ledger entry reference and the delivery state |
| mapChannelEvent | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: event type and payload. Output: one ledger entry command with the event code, channel, direction, occurred time, source system and links |
| resolveChannelFacts | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: the case id, notice id, instruction id, treatment id or proceeds id of the event. Output: the resolved facts; a 404 leaves a link empty, a 5xx is retryable |
| appendLedgerEntry | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: the entry command and the idempotency key. Output: the ledger entry reference; a repeat returns the same reference |
| parkDeliveryInException | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: delivery id, failure class, attempt count. Output: status EXCEPTION, task `RESOLVE_OUTBOX_DELIVERY` for RW-PLATADM, decision record |
| EfsLedgerReadWorkflow | Workflow, started by AceDataReady for the EFS source | `rwb-integration` | Input: business date, source EFS. Output: `EfsReadSummary` |
| readEfsOutcomes | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: business date. Output: the kept and the excluded EFS rows |
| appendEfsEntries | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: the kept rows. Output: the count written, one append per row with key `EFS:<efs_record_key>` |
| writeEfsReadSummary | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: the counts. Output: `EfsReadSummary(businessDate, rowsRead, written, excluded, notOnCase)` |

Every activity runs with the workflow kit's retry policy: initial interval 1 s, back-off 2, maximum 3 attempts, and a non-retryable classification for a 4xx of the append other than 409 (DP-10). The workflow history carries ids, codes and counts only, never a contact point or an amount.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Schedule is registered by this story. The intake is event-started from the seven consumed types, and the EFS read step is started by AceDataReady, not by a timer (BR8; Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-02 and JOB-04). The outbox relay itself is the platform relay of DP-09 and runs every minute in every service; it is not a Schedule of this story.

| Table | Schema | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| outbound_item | rwb_integration | P2 | Read only, for the exception queue screen and its interface column; this slice writes no outbound file item |
| outbox_delivery | rwb_integration | PLT library, created in rwb_integration | One delivery per consumed event and consumer `ledger-channels`: status, attempt count, next attempt, last error, task |

`outbox_event` exists in `rwb_integration` from the service baseline and this story writes no row in it: the consumed events are produced by their owners, and the intake records their progress on `outbox_delivery` with the CloudEvents id as `event_id`. The `interaction` table, its append-only trigger and its read are rwb-source-data's; `efs_ledger_outcome` is rwb-source-data's reference table; the timeline is rwb-case's. None of them is read or written here (DP-01, DP-18).

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.integration`, module `ledgerintake`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.integration.ledgerintake`.

| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | ACE facts read through rwb-source-data's contract; this service reads no view | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case with the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON |

| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON |

| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/integration/v1` | none |
