RWB-P2-E1007-APP is the same-service baseline story in the build dependency row: the schema, the login, the REST base and the relay of `rwb_integration` come from it.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| LedgerChannelListener | Listener | Envelope validation for the seven types, inbox dedupe, workflow start per event (BR2, BR5) |
| LedgerChannelMapper | Service | One method per event type implementing BR1, BR3 and BR4; the codes are sent, never resolved, here |
| FactResolver | Client | The P3, P6, S9, S2 and P8 fact reads behind one 2 s budget with no retry on 4xx (DP-11) |
| LedgerAppendClient | Client | The P1 append and the P1 EFS and contact reads; one hop, 2 s, idempotent on the key (DP-18) |
| DeliveryTracker | Service | The `outbox_delivery` row of a consumed event: attempt count, next attempt, status, task (BR6) |
| ChannelIntakeWorkflow | Workflow | LedgerChannelIntakeWorkflow with its four activities |
| EfsContactOutcomeReader | Workflow and activities | EfsLedgerReadWorkflow: read, append, summary (BR7, BR8) |
| ExceptionQueueController | Controller | The two admin operations, their validation and their problem responses (DP-13, DP-19) |
| DecisionRecordWriter | Library client | The record of a resend and of an exception through the local library (DP-03) |
| AccessCheckClient | Client | The role and scope check of the two admin operations (DP-08) |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `outbox_delivery`, `processed_event`, `idempotency_key` and the library table `decision_record` in schema `rwb_integration`, through the rwb-integration login (DP-02, DP-15). The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0664; ASM-1168).
- One migration in the rwb-integration sequence: `V2034_1__ledger_intake.sql` adds the partial index on `processed_event (consumer, idempotency_key)` where the inbox is read and the index on `outbox_delivery (consumer, status, next_attempt_at)` where the retry scan reads.
- No ledger column, no ledger table and no EFS reference table is created here; the six legacy columns of `interaction` and the `efs_ledger_outcome` rows are P1's migration (legacy section 13, DP-18).

**Configuration and reference data**

- Feature flag `rwb.integration.ledger-channels` in the platform flag library; off by default, on in the environments of the release. Off: the consumer acknowledges the seven types without writing, the EFS read step does not run and no delivery row moves.
- The retry intervals of a delivery and the attempt limit of three are rows of the environment configuration, not code (ASM-1170). The EFS ledger outcome list, the retention classes and the channel list are rows of rwb-source-data and are read there.
- The consumer name `ledger-channels` is kept from the legacy story as the logical consumer; its Kafka group names are deployment values of the OPS story.
- The two admin operations declare Platform administration R and U; no role name is written in code (DP-08).

**Build steps**

1. LedgerChannelListener and DeliveryTracker against the platform inbox, with one test per consumed type and the duplicate path; AC8, BR2, BR5.
2. LedgerChannelMapper, one method and one unit test per event type, with the codes of BR1 sent unchanged; BR1, BR3.
3. FactResolver over the five owner contracts and the contract fakes, with the 404 and 5xx split; BR4.
4. LedgerAppendClient over the P1 append and the two P1 reads, with the repeat answer treated as success; BR5, BR9.
5. ChannelIntakeWorkflow with its four activities and the retry policy, then the exception path and the task for RW-PLATADM; AC8, BR6.
6. EfsContactOutcomeReader as the second workflow, with the summary and the `EFS:<efs_record_key>` key; BR7, BR8.
7. ExceptionQueueController with the two admin operations, the scope check, the resend and the 409 on a running workflow; X9, X10.
8. DecisionRecordWriter on the resend and on the exception, with the rollback path; BR10.
9. The contract-fake run of every cross-service answer in isolation, so the story builds before the other services exist.
10. The migration and its indexes, then the load of the configuration rows.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.integration.ledger-channels`. On: the seven types are consumed and appended, and the EFS read step runs. Off: the deliveries are acknowledged and counted but nothing is appended and no workflow is started; the ledger of P1 is unchanged and no delivery is dated.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, a duplicate of any of the six business events writes one entry and counts one repeat, an unresolvable case ends in EXCEPTION with a task for RW-PLATADM on the third attempt, a 503 from the append loses no delivery, and the EFS read summary of a rerun is identical to the first run for the same business date.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-09 Exception queue, served by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19). The platform administrator filters the deliveries of consumer `ledger-channels` by status PENDING, RETRYING, DELIVERED and EXCEPTION, by consumer, by event type and by date window, and reads the attempt count, the next attempt time, the last error code and the task. A delivery in EXCEPTION offers the resend action; the row then shows PENDING with attempt count 0 and the resend time. The screen has the states Loading, Filtered, Empty and Action failed, and the resend confirmation names the delivery and the event type only. The screen fields, their layout and their masking are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0664; ASM-1168). No screen shows a ledger entry, a contact point or an amount: the timeline on the case is SCR-04 and belongs to rwb-case.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the event codes, the channels, the directions, the retry intervals and the attempt limit are rows of reference data and environment configuration; the mapper sends codes and resolves none.
- No personal data in logs, events, workflow inputs or histories: the entry carries `contactKey` and the identifiers of the case, the notice, the instruction, the treatment and the proceeds, never a number, an address or an amount.
- No read of another service's table and no ACE view: the ledger is reached only through the P1 append, the EFS and contact facts only through the P1 reads, and the case, notice, partner, treatment and proceeds facts only through their owners' contracts (DP-01, DP-05, DP-18).
- The intake never updates or deletes a ledger entry: the append is create-only and idempotent on the key, and the append-only trigger of the ledger stays in the owner's schema.
- One login per service and one topic per service: the release carries the rwb-integration login and consumes the owners' topics; it publishes nothing on `rwb.integration.events.v1` for this slice (DP-02, DP-14).
- A delivery is never discarded: an unresolvable case or a failed append ends in EXCEPTION with a task for RW-PLATADM after three attempts (BR6).
- Every fake and every fixture is synthetic; no production payload, contact point or event is copied into a test.

This story owns the partner half of the ledger: the ledger-facing attributes of the service's two facts, `InstructionIssued` (EV-20) and `PartnerResultSubmitted` (EV-21), published once each, keyed on the case ID, written in the same transaction as the change and its decision record, with who held the case before and after, the channel, the direction and the time, and with the contact point left as a reference. ##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **the hand-over of a case to a partner and the result the partner returns announced once, with who held the case before and after, the channel, the direction, the source and the time, and with the contact point left as a reference**, so that **the one ledger shows the partner channel beside the EFS and Workbench entries and a contact is not found and then lost again**.

This is the rwb-partner slice of legacy RWB-E2-034. The legacy story writes seven event types and one EFS read into a single ledger inside the monolith; under D-RCV-60 the ledger is rwb-source-data's (DP-18), the read and the ordered timeline are rwb-source-data's, the mapping of a fact to a ledger entry and the composed timeline are rwb-integration's in `RWB-P2-E2034-CON`, and the EFS action rows are the source-data service's. What is left, and what only this service can state, is the partner fact itself:

- the two facts of the service, `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` (EV-20) and `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1` (EV-21) on `rwb.partner.events.v1`, extended additively with the ledger attributes `eventCode`, `channel`, `direction`, `occurredAt`, `source`, `fromHolderRef` and `toHolderRef`, keyed on the case ID, in the CloudEvents envelope of the outbox library (DP-09);
- one read-only view `v_partner_ledger_fact` in `rwb_partner` over `partner_instruction` and `partner`, with its index, from which the fact is built (DP-01, DP-15);
- the transaction rule: the instruction row or the result, the local decision record and the outbox row commit together or not at all (DP-03);
- the emitter stays with the stories that first issue the instruction (RWB-S9-E6031-APP, RWB-S9-E6034-APP) and the story that takes the result (RWB-S9-E6033-APP); this story fixes the payload they write and asserts it against the contract (DP-11).

What this story does not own: the interaction table, the retention class, the ordered timeline read and the EFS read step (rwb-source-data, DP-18); the mapping and the composed timeline (rwb-integration, `RWB-P2-E2034-CON`); the letters, deliveries, offers and payments of the legacy criteria (rwb-comms and rwb-payment); the instruction operations API-S9-002 to API-S9-006 and their screens (the S9 instruction stories); and the end-to-end proof across rwb-partner, rwb-integration and rwb-source-data, which is `RWB-ITG-E2034-ITG`.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contact outcomes from collections, letters sent through WIN and work held by partners sit in different systems, so a case owner who picks up a case does not know which number answered or who held the case last; for cases that came from EFS the share of open cases with a visible last right-party contact is zero (legacy section 2). The legacy story answered that with one ledger and one timeline. The split does not change the question; it changes who can answer it truthfully. A partner is instructed by a service that holds the instruction row, and a partner returns a result to that same service, so the only place where "who held the case, since when, under which channel and with which direction" is a fact and not a copy is `rwb_partner` (context pack ownership rows: `partner`, `partner_instruction`, EV-20 and EV-21).

Three target facts shape the slice.

1. **A fact, not a ledger row.** The ledger is another service's table by the default ruling (DP-18), and one service never reads another's schema (DP-01). So the partner channel travels as an event with identifiers and codes, and the entry, its retention class and its order are written and owned downstream. Sending more than the attributes the consumer element needs would copy a ledger into an event.
2. **A hand-over has two holders.** Legacy BR2 and AC2 say a hand-over to a partner names the holder before and the partner after, with channel PORTAL and direction OUTBOUND, and a partner result is INBOUND on the same channel. Those two values are the whole reason the partner channel is legible on the timeline: without them the timeline shows that something happened to the case and not that a firm took it.
3. **No contact point leaves the service.** Legacy BR5 stores the contact point as a reference to `v_ace_contact.contact_key` and forbids copying the number or the address. `partner_instruction` holds no contact column (TSD S9 T3.1), and this service holds no ACE grant, so the fact carries no contact value at all and the ledger resolves the reference through rwb-source-data (DP-05). The rule is met by omission, which is the strongest form it can take.

The slice serves REQ-ILG-011 (a hand-over names who held the case, who holds it now and when), REQ-ILG-014 (the contact point is a reference) and REQ-ILG-007 and REQ-ILG-008 (one entry per key, and no entry lost on a failure) at the producer end; the ledger rows, the ordering and the retention class are the consumers' and are traced in their own stories.

##### 3. Preconditions

- `RWB-P2-E2034-CON` is published: the consumer element of the partner fact, its required attributes, the composed timeline element and its fake. This story builds against that fake on Day 1 and adds no operation to it (§R5.4, §R5.7).
- The platform libraries are on the service template: the local decision-record library (DP-03, RWB-PLT-E1027-CON), the outbox and inbox library with the CloudEvents envelope (DP-09, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON), the reference-data client (DP-07, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON), the parameters client (DP-06, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON), the authorise guard (DP-08, RWB-PLT-E1037-CON), the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-15, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON) and the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19, RWB-PLT-N001-CON). None of them is written into the H row of this secondary slice (GAP-3149; ASM-5532).
- `rwb_partner` and its login exist and the baseline carries `partner` (DF-PRT-001 to DF-PRT-007) and `partner_instruction` (DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016) with the standard record columns of TSD S9 T3.0.
- A sibling operation commits an instruction or a result with its `Idempotency-Key`: API-S9-002 (issue), API-S9-005 (result). Both write the decision record before the change; this story writes the fact in that same transaction (DP-03).
- The lists LOV-LEDGER-EVENT with `HANDOVER` and `PARTNER_RESULT`, LOV-CHANNEL with `PORTAL`, LOV-DIRECTION with `OUTBOUND` and `INBOUND` and LOV-SOURCE with `WORKBENCH` are read at the version in force through the reference-data contract (legacy BR1, BR2, BR4; DP-07). Their row names and keys are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3149; ASM-5533).
- The retry bound after which a fact goes to `rwb.partner.events.v1.dlt` is a parameter row; the legacy story names a retry limit of 3 and no parameter row (GAP-3149; ASM-5535).
- No approval stop: the FSD S9 is "In review" and the legacy story "Ready for build"; this story is Draft (realignment v1) (ASM-5539).

##### 4. Flow

1. A sibling operation starts the change: API-S9-002 issues an instruction, API-S9-005 takes a result, each with its `Idempotency-Key` and its decision record written in the transaction (DP-03).
2. The guard library has already resolved the caller and its right, and the cached decision carries the caller's holder reference; the fact takes `fromHolderRef` from that decision and never from the request body (DP-08; BR2).
3. `LedgerFactReader` reads the instruction and its firm from `v_partner_ledger_fact` in `rwb_partner` — the instruction reference, the case reference, the partner reference and code, the instruction type, `instructed_at`, `due_at`, the status and `result_code` (DP-01).
4. `LedgerAttributeResolver` reads the lists at the version in force and resolves the fact to its `eventCode` (`HANDOVER` for an issue, `PARTNER_RESULT` for a result), its `channel` (`PORTAL`), its `direction` (`OUTBOUND` for an issue, `INBOUND` for a result) and its `source` (`WORKBENCH`) (DP-07; BR1, BR3, BR9).
5. `LedgerFactAssembler` builds the payload: the ledger attributes of step 4, `occurredAt` from `instructed_at` or the submitted time, `fromHolderRef` from the decision, `toHolderRef` as `PARTNER:<partner_code>` for a hand-over and as the same firm reference for a result, and the identifiers of step 3. No name, no contact value, no amount (BR10).
6. `LedgerFactOutbox` writes one row of `rwb.partner.events.v1` in the open transaction, keyed on the case ID, with the schema of the fact (DP-09).
7. The transaction commits: the instruction row or the result, the decision record and the outbox row together; a refusal of any of them writes nothing (AC4, BR6).
8. The relay publishes the fact once; the consumer of `RWB-P2-E2034-CON` maps it to the ledger entry and rwb-source-data writes it with its retention class in its own schema (not built here; BR8).
9. The case timeline shows the partner entry through the gateway-bff composite route of the edge; this service serves no timeline read (DP-19; AC3).
10. A repeat under the same key returns the first answer and writes no second fact; the repeat is counted (AC5, BR5).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The outbox insert refuses | The whole transaction rolls back: no instruction change, no record, no fact | MSG-P7-003 of the sibling operation | AC4 |
| X2 | The same fact is replayed or the same `Idempotency-Key` is submitted twice | One outbox row and one event exist; the repeat is counted | None | AC5 |
| X3 | The consumer keeps refusing the fact past the retry bound | The delivery goes to `rwb.partner.events.v1.dlt` with a task for RW-PLATADM | None | AC4 |
| X4 | The list or the parameter read misses the 2 s budget, or its breaker is open | Nothing is written; one retry with jitter; no fact is built on a guessed value | MSG-GEN-006 | Section 14 |
| X5 | A caller without the Partner portal right, or a case outside its scope | Refused before a row is read; no fact is built | MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 | AC6 |
| X6 | A list member of the version in force has no row for a fact | The fact is refused; no event is built from a code that is not in force | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3149; ASM-5533) | AC3 |
| X7 | A component or a test reaches `interaction`, `recovery_case`, the ACE views or another `rwb_*` schema | The grant refuses the statement and the boundary test fails the build | None (pipeline log) | Section 17 |

X1 to X3 are the failure paths legacy BR7 and BR8 name, moved to the producer of the fact; X4 to X7 are the platform rules of the split.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on Day 1 against the `RWB-P2-E2034-CON` fake and the template libraries; it waits for no in-lane story and changes no operation |
| Negotiable | The payload element names, the view name and the activity name are this story's; the codes, channels, directions and sources are list rows read at their version |
| Valuable | The partner channel of a case becomes visible once, with its two holders, and nothing about the customer leaves the service |
| Estimable | One view, one resolver, one assembler, one outbox adapter and one contract test per fact |
| Small | Fits one sprint as a secondary slice beside the instruction and result stories it extends |
| Testable | Each criterion runs on synthetic instructions and results through the contract fakes, plus the rollback, repeat, refusal and boundary cases |

```gherkin
    When the result transaction commits

  Scenario: AC6 The holder comes from the access decision and the scope is enforced (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given identity "RW-REFADM" holds no Partner portal right and case "RW-2026-000301" is held by team "MTG-BKK"
    When "RW-REFADM" reads a partner instruction of that case

```

The six criteria are new under D-RCV-60 and test only the partner fact and its seam with the ledger contract; no legacy criterion text is copied, because AC1 to AC11 of RWB-E2-034 belong to `RWB-P2-E2034-APP`, `RWB-ITG-E2034-ITG` and the ledger owner's stories. Two legacy values are reused because the sources publish them — case `RW-2026-000301`, instruction `INS-SYN-0301`, partner `LF-SYN-01`, holders `USER:U-2002` and `PARTNER:LF-SYN-01`, the dates 17 and 18 December 2026 and the contact key `PHONE:CP-SYN-0301-M` (legacy AC2 and AC3) — and they are asserted on this service's payload, not on the ledger.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The fact maps to one ledger event code: `InstructionIssued` to `HANDOVER`, `PartnerResultSubmitted` to `PARTNER_RESULT`; no other fact of this service enters the ledger from this key | Legacy BR1; LOV-LEDGER-EVENT |
| BR2 | A hand-over to a partner has channel `PORTAL` and direction `OUTBOUND`, with the holder before from the access decision and the partner after; a partner result has channel `PORTAL` and direction `INBOUND` | Legacy BR2; LOV-CHANNEL; LOV-DIRECTION |
| BR3 | A partner fact carries source `WORKBENCH`, because it is entered on a Workbench or portal operation of this service | Legacy BR4; LOV-SOURCE |
| BR4 | The contact point is never copied: the fact carries no contact key, number or address, and the ledger resolves the reference through rwb-source-data | Legacy BR5; REQ-ILG-014; DP-05 |
| BR5 | One fact per idempotency key; a repeat writes no second row, no second event and no second entry, and is counted | Legacy BR7; REQ-ILG-007 |
| BR6 | A failed fact write rolls the change back; a consumer that keeps refusing sends the delivery to the topic's `.dlt` with a task for RW-PLATADM and no entry is lost | Legacy BR8; REQ-ILG-008; DP-09 |
| BR7 | The fact is written in the transaction that writes the instruction row and the local decision record; there is no fact without its record and no change without its fact | DP-03; FSD S9 BR-S9-005 |
| BR8 | The ledger, its retention class and the ordered read are rwb-source-data's by the default ruling; this service writes no interaction row and computes no retention class | DP-18; legacy BR6; R3 default rulings |
| BR9 | The event code, the channel, the direction, the source and the retry bound are rows read at the version in force; no code, channel or bound is a constant in the module | FSD S9 BR-S9-001; principle 1; DP-06, DP-07 |
| BR10 | A payload carries identifiers, codes, dates and document references only: no person name, contact value, amount or free text in the payload, an outbox row, a workflow input or a log | Template and Rules §R7.2 (s17); legacy guardrail 2 |

BR1 to BR3 are the payload values of AC1 and AC2; BR4 is the omission AC2 asserts; BR5 is AC5; BR6 is the rollback and the `.dlt` path of AC4; BR7 is the transaction boundary of step 7; BR8 is why 12.1 has no ledger operation; BR9 is the resolver of step 4, and a build check fails on a code in the source; BR10 is a property test on the payload, the row and the log.

##### 9. State transitions

This story changes no case status and no instruction status: the instruction states of LOV-INSTR-STATUS belong to the issue, accept, result and recall steps of this service. The only state machine it moves is the delivery state of the fact.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| — | The change commits | The instruction row or the result and the record are written | Outbox row `NEW` |
| `NEW` | The relay publishes | The broker acknowledges | `PUBLISHED` |
| `NEW`, `RETRYING` | The broker refuses | The retry bound is not reached | `RETRYING` |
| `RETRYING` | The retry bound is reached | The consumer keeps refusing | `DLT`, with a task for RW-PLATADM |
| `PUBLISHED` | The same key arrives again | The idempotency key exists | No change; the repeat is counted |

The case side — the stage, the status and the timeline's place in the case sequence — is rwb-case's and the ledger owner's, and this slice neither reads nor writes it.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner (Partner portal R) | Reads the partner instruction and result of the cases in scope; causes no fact |
| RW-AGENCYMG, partner and agency manager (CRUDA) | Issues and reads instructions and results; the fact is written for the issue it makes |
| RW-LITOFF, RW-ENFORCE, RW-SALEOFF, RW-NPAMGR, RW-DEBTSALE, RW-GUARANT (CRU) | Create and read instructions inside their capability area; the fact follows their change |
| RW-HEADLIT, RW-HEADNPA, RW-HEADASL (RA) | Read only; approve nothing here |
| PT-AGENCY, PT-LAWFIRM, PT-VALUER, PT-AUCTION, PT-BUYER, PT-RAMC (Partner portal RU) | Return a result on their own firm's instruction; the fact is written inward |
| RW-AUDIT, RW-COE, RW-CONDUCT (R) | Read the instruction, the result and the fact it produced |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Works the `.dlt` task of a fact the consumer refused; reads the payload only |
| SY-PARTNER, service identity (login `rwb_partner`) | Writes the outbox row in its own schema; holds no grant on another schema and no `v_ace_*` grant |
| Role without Partner portal R or C | Refused with MSG-P4-002 before a row is read |

The rights are the rows of TSD S9 T6.1 and T-A.1 and are not widened. No delegation of authority applies: a fact records a change, it decides nothing about the customer. No personal name appears in this story, a test or a log.

Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 and TSD S9 T3.1. **No business column, table or constraint is added**: the ledger attributes are derived from rows the instruction and result steps already write, and the one migration adds a read-only view and its index in `rwb_partner` (DP-15; ASM-5538). No personal data is written, and the payload carries no contact value.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The service's six operations are baselined and built by their own stories (API-S9-001 to API-S9-006; TSD S9 T-A.1), and this story adds no path, no request property and no answer property to any of them. The base stays `/api/recovery/partner/v1` (DP-13) and the partner gateway and the composite route are unchanged (DP-19); what changes is the payload the two facts carry.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | The reference-data read of the `RWB-P3-E1043-CON` contract (path Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3149; ASM-5533)) | P3 rwb-case | LOV-LEDGER-EVENT, LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-DIRECTION and LOV-SOURCE at the version in force (DP-07) |
| GET | The parameter read of the `RWB-P3-E1042-CON` contract (path Not specified in the source documents (GAP-3149; ASM-5535)) | P3 rwb-case | The retry bound after which a fact goes to the `.dlt` (DP-06) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The right, the scope and the holder reference of the caller, cached per session by the guard library; the sibling operation makes the call and this story reads its answer (DP-08) |

Each row is one hop with a 2 s client budget and a breaker (ADR-020; DP-11). The three are class C in fact and none is in the Work Package's C row, which holds `RWB-P2-E2034-CON`; they arrive with the platform libraries of the service template (GAP-3149; ASM-5532).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Schema | Topic | Key | Payload carries | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` (EV-20) | `rwb_partner_instruction_issued` | `rwb.partner.events.v1`, with its retry and `.dlt` topics | `caseId` | instruction, case and partner references, partner code, instruction type, `dueAt`; `eventCode` `HANDOVER`, `channel` `PORTAL`, `direction` `OUTBOUND`, `source` `WORKBENCH`, `occurredAt`, `fromHolderRef`, `toHolderRef` | Announces the hand-over of the case to the firm for the ledger entry and the case |
| `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1` (EV-21) | `rwb_partner_partner_result_submitted` | `rwb.partner.events.v1`, with its retry and `.dlt` topics | `caseId` | instruction, case and partner references, partner code, result code, document references; `eventCode` `PARTNER_RESULT`, `channel` `PORTAL`, `direction` `INBOUND`, `source` `WORKBENCH`, `occurredAt`, `toHolderRef` | Announces the partner's result for the ledger entry and the case |

| Envelope element | Value |
|---|---|
| Mode | CloudEvents 1.0, binary |
| ce_type | `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` or `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1` |
| ce_source | rwb-partner |
| ce_subject and key | The case ID of the instruction |
| ce_id and traceparent | The event identifier and the W3C trace context of the call |
| Payload | Identifiers, codes, dates and document references; no personal data, no contact value, no amount, no free text |

The two events are the service's own pair (context pack events EV-20 and EV-21; TSD S9 T5.3) and their emitters are the instruction stories and the result story; this story fixes the ledger attributes they carry and adds no third event, no second topic and no second outbox. The seven attributes are additive and are named by no source document, so the names are this story's design choice and are fixed with the contract owner (GAP-3149; ASM-5531). The outbox row is written in the change's transaction and relayed after the commit.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The fact is built from the service's own rows; the ledger's read and the composed timeline are consumed by the screen through the composite route and by `RWB-P2-E2034-CON`, not by this story. No inbox row, no consumer group and no subscription is added.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `InstructionWorkflow` | Workflow, one execution per instruction; the one workflow the S9 ownership row carries | `rwb-partner`, namespace `rwb-recovery` | The change's stage; this story adds no signal and no stage |
| `writeLedgerFact` (name is this story's design choice) | Activity | `rwb-partner` | Builds the fact and writes the outbox row inside the change's transaction (BR7) |
| The outbox relay | Library component, not an activity of this service | — | Publishes the row after the commit; a refusal retries, then the `.dlt` (BR6) |

The activity name and the payload element names are fixed by no source (GAP-3149; ASM-5531); a replay reuses the recorded outcome and writes no second fact.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The legacy EFS read step was a step of JOB-02 inside the monolith; in the target the EFS product is read by rwb-source-data and its step is that service's, so this service owns no job (ownership rows: Jobs 0) and adds no Temporal Schedule. The instruction clock is a durable timer of `InstructionWorkflow`, not a Schedule.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | This story |

| `partner_instruction` | `rwb_partner` | S9 | Read only, through the view; the row is written by the instruction and result steps |
| `partner` | `rwb_partner` | S9 | Read only, the firm and its code |
| `v_partner_ledger_fact` | `rwb_partner` | S9 | Created by this story's migration: the fact rows of the two events with their holders and dates |

Not owned and never read as a table: `interaction` (P1), `recovery_case`, `task` and `timer` (P3), `decision_log_entry` and `rule_row` (P7), the document tables (P5), the notice tables (P6) and the `v_ace_*` views (P1 only). `case_id` is a reference and not a key across schemas, and no foreign key leaves `rwb_partner` (DP-01).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.partner`, module `ledgerfact`. No front-end file: the entry is shown by the timeline the ledger owner serves.

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `LedgerFactReader` | Repository | Reads `v_partner_ledger_fact` in `rwb_partner`, and nothing else |
| `LedgerAttributeResolver` | Service | Reads the four lists at the version in force and resolves the event code, the channel, the direction and the source (BR1, BR2, BR3, BR9) |
| `LedgerFactAssembler` | Service | Builds the payload: the attributes, `occurredAt`, `fromHolderRef` from the decision, `toHolderRef` as `PARTNER:<code>`, the identifiers; no contact value (BR4, BR10) |
| `LedgerFactOutbox` | Library adapter | Writes the outbox row of the fact in the change's transaction; one row per key (BR5, BR7) |
| `HolderRefResolver` | Service | Takes the holder reference from the cached access decision and refuses a body-supplied holder (BR2, AC6) |
| `ReferenceDataClient`, `ParameterClient`, `DecisionClient` | Client | The three consumed contracts, one hop, 2 s, breaker, cached per request |
| `writeLedgerFact` | Activity | The step of `InstructionWorkflow` that runs the four components inside the transaction |

**Database.** One step in the per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_partner` (DP-15): `V2034_1__partner_ledger_fact.sql`, which creates the read-only view `v_partner_ledger_fact` over `partner_instruction` joined to `partner` — the instruction, the case, the partner and its code, the type, `instructed_at`, `due_at`, the status and `result_code`, with the standard columns — and one index on `(case_id, instructed_at)`. No business table, column or constraint is added, and no migration of this service touches another schema. The view and index names are a design choice fixed by no source (ASM-5538).

**Configuration and reference data.** The four lists are read at the version in force (DP-07); the retry bound is a parameter row, 3 in the legacy retry, with no published parameter name (DP-06; ASM-5535); the 2 s budget, the single hop and the breaker are ADR-020. The flag `rwb.partner.ledger-fact` is a flag of the platform library: off means the change commits without an outbox row and no fact is published, while no ledger entry is created downstream, and the timeline shows the case entries only (BR8).

**Build steps**

1. The view and its index in the service's Flyway sequence, applied on an empty and on a loaded `rwb_partner` (AC1, DP-15).
2. `LedgerFactReader` and its two projections, for an issued instruction and for a result (AC1, AC2).
3. `LedgerAttributeResolver` over the reference-data fake, with the two event codes, the two directions and a member the version does not carry (AC1, AC2, AC3, X6).
4. `LedgerFactAssembler` with the property test that a synthetic contact value, address and name never reach the payload, the row or a log (AC2, BR10).
5. `HolderRefResolver` and the refusal of a holder supplied by the body; the right and the scope cases (AC6, X5).
6. `LedgerFactOutbox` inside the transaction of the sibling operation, with the rollback case and the repeat case (AC4, AC5, X1, X2).
7. The `.dlt` path and its task for RW-PLATADM past the retry bound (AC4, X3).
8. The contract test against the `RWB-P2-E2034-CON` consumer element and the composed timeline (AC3, BR1).

This is a secondary slice: the metadata H row stays `None` and the C row stays `RWB-P2-E2034-CON` exactly as the Work Package fixes them, so the ten platform contracts the DP table names arrive with the service template and are not written into either row (GAP-3149; ASM-5532). **DP-09** is the core of the story: the fact row and the CloudEvents envelope in the change's transaction. **DP-18** is why no ledger table appears in 12.7: the entry, its retention class and its order are rwb-source-data's by the default ruling. **DP-05** is met by omission: no view and no ACE grant in this service, because the contact reference is resolved by the ledger owner. **DP-03** puts the record and the fact in one transaction, **DP-07** and **DP-06** are the lists and the retry bound, and **DP-08** is the holder reference. **DP-10** replaces the legacy JOB-02 step with the event-started instruction workflow and adds no Schedule. **DP-11** is the contract-with-mock rule the consumer test uses, **DP-13** and **DP-19** leave the base and the route unchanged, and **DP-15** is the view. The wave is the Work Package's 2, the W-MAP wave of EP02, earlier than the service's wave 4 and kept per §R5.6.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, `INS-SYN-0301` produces one `HANDOVER` fact with `USER:U-2002` and `PARTNER:LF-SYN-01`, a result produces one `INBOUND` `PARTNER_RESULT` fact with no contact value, a refused outbox insert leaves no instruction column, no record and no fact, a repeat writes one row, the consumer element of `RWB-P2-E2034-CON` is satisfied for both facts, and no statement outside `rwb_partner` exists in the build.

No screen is built here. The partner half of an entry is this story's payload: the channel "Portal", the direction, the firm reference, the holder before and after, the time and the source. SCR-34 Partner list and SCR-35 Placement and allocation are the instruction and result stories' and are untouched: this story adds no column and no action to them.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the event codes, the channel, the directions, the source and the retry bound are rows read at the version in force, and a build check fails on any of them in source or configuration (BR9).
- No personal data in the payload, an outbox row, a workflow input, a log or a span: identifiers, codes, dates and document references only; the contact key is not copied (BR4, BR10).
- No read of another service's tables and no cross-schema join: `interaction` (P1), `recovery_case` (P3), the decision ledger (P7), the document tables (P5) and the notice tables (P6) are reached only through their owners (DP-01).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or a `v_ace_*` view: this service holds no `v_ace_*` grant and reads no ACE table; the contact reference is rwb-source-data's (DP-05, DP-18).
- The record, the change and the fact are one transaction; a refusal of any of them writes nothing (BR7, AC4).
- One fact per key and one entry per fact: the write key, the `Idempotency-Key` and the consumer's key carry the rule (BR5, AC5).
- An applied migration is never edited: the view and the index are a new version in the service's own sequence (DP-15).
- No retired element is reintroduced: no Quartz job, no JOB-02 step, no shared ledger table in this schema, no monolith base and no `recovery_svc` login.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-034 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **the timeline of my case to return one time-ordered list of the case events of rwb-case and the ledger entries of rwb-source-data, each item naming its source, channel, entry type and occurred time, paged and stable when two items share a time, with the empty state and the scope refusal of the legacy story, and a call I record on the case written once through rwb-source-data's append under its idempotency key**, so that **a contact, a letter, a hand-over, an offer and a payment are read where I already look and are not found and then lost again, without rwb-case holding or reading the interaction table**.

This is the case-timeline slice of legacy RWB-E2-034, in `rwb-case`: schema `rwb_case`, base `/api/recovery/case/v1` (DP-13), topic `rwb.case.events.v1` with names `rwb.case.<Event>.v1`, queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, one schema and login per service (DP-01, DP-02).

- **Provided:** `GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline` on that base, the case timeline operation the Ownership Map keeps with P3, returning the case events of this service plus the ledger entries of `rwb-source-data` read one hop away through the P1 contract.
- **Consumed:** the case-scoped ledger read and the ledger append on `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`; the append is called once per Workbench-raised interaction with an `Idempotency-Key`.
- **Not this slice:** the ledger row, the EFS intake rule, the dedupe and the exception queue (rwb-source-data's under the R-PREC ruling and DP-18); the channel consumer, retry and exception queue (RWB-P2-E2034-APP); the letter, payment and offer objects; roles, scope and masking rows (DP-08); the full seven-type timeline and item-type rights filter (RWB-P3-E2016-APP). `interaction` is not a table of `rwb_case`.

The ruling is one sentence: the ledger and its intake rule are rwb-source-data's, the case timeline and the case-scoped interaction read stay with rwb-case, and every ledger read and write crosses one published contract, one hop, inside 2 s.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contact outcomes from collections, letters sent through WIN and work held by partners sit in different systems today, so a case owner who picks up a case does not know which number answered or who held it last. The measure is unchanged: the share of open cases whose last right-party contact is visible on the case, today zero for cases that came from EFS. REQ-ILG-012 asks for the ledger as an ordered timeline on the case record and REQ-ILG-006 for it to read back as one filtered sequence; this slice answers both on the case screen, serves REQ-ILG-009 to REQ-ILG-011 by reading the entries their channels produce, REQ-ILG-014 by showing a masked reference and REQ-ILG-013 by leaving the retention class to the entry's owner. REQ-ILG-007 and REQ-ILG-008 are cited for the one behaviour this slice owns: a call is written once under its key, and a refused write leaves no half item.

The realignment keeps the measure and moves the seam: one append-only ledger has one writer, so the case service asks its owner to write an entry instead of writing one itself, and the timeline is composed at the read rather than projected into `rwb_case`. Six moves carry the rule across that seam:

1. The legacy `interaction` table in the recovery schema becomes rwb-source-data's table in its own schema (DP-01, DP-18); the case service holds no column of it and reads what it shows through the P1 contract, turning the legacy in-process call into one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker (DP-11).
2. The legacy base `/api/recovery/v1` becomes `/api/recovery/case/v1` for the timeline and `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` for the ledger (DP-13).
3. Page size and source timeout become parameter rows (DP-06), and channel, source and entry-type values come from the reference-data contract with the version in force (DP-07): no code holds a LOV value.
4. `RecoveryAccessGuard` becomes the authorise contract of rwb-access with the guard library (DP-08), so the right, the scope and the mask are answered by their owner.
5. The case screen is composed at the edge by gateway-bff (DP-19): one composite route, never an owner service from the browser.
6. The order is the one value the sources do not settle: the timeline contract serves its page newest first, while the legacy story, its AC3 and AC9 and REQ-ILG-006 read the ledger in occurred-time order with case sequence on a tie. This slice fixes the sequence of the merged items and the tie-break and keeps the page order of the timeline contract (GAP-2226; ASM-3668).

##### 3. Preconditions

| Precondition | What it gives this story |
|---|---|
| RWB-P2-E2034-CON is baselined | The append as consumed: one entry per call, create-only, idempotent on the key, the same reference on a repeat, 409 for a held key, 503 when the store is down; the case-scoped read; the fakes. Element names of the append command, the case-scoped read and the intake result are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2225; ASM-3667) |
| The rwb-source-data stories of this key are published | The ledger table, its append-only trigger, the append, the case-scoped read, the EFS outcome list and the retention classes: consumed, never restated (DP-18) |
| The rwb-case baseline and the timeline contract of RWB-P3-E2016-CON | `rwb_case`, the base with `GET /cases/{caseId}`, the `rwb-case` queue and login (DP-02); the `TimelinePage` and `TimelineItem` shapes, the item types including `INTERACTION`, the paging parameters, the page order and the item-type rights filter |
| The parameters, reference-data and access contracts | Page default and maximum and the source timeout as parameter rows (DP-06); LOV-SOURCE, LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-LEDGER-EVENT and type labels with versions (DP-07); authorise and masking policies (DP-08) |
| The gateway-bff route and SIT data | The DP-19 route that merges the case answer and the timeline answer; case "RW-2026-000301" in team "MTG-BKK" with the transfer of 16 December 2026 11:00; case "RW-2026-000302" with no entry; the users of section 10 |

Business preconditions carried from the legacy story: the case is open and the reader holds Case record R with the case in scope; action code "PTP" carries channel CALL and every event code carries retention class "ILG-STD" until Compliance sets the periods, both as rwb-source-data reference rows read there and never here; the contact point travels as a reference such as "PHONE:CP-SYN-0301-M"; a case with no ledger entry is normal and shows the empty state.

##### 4. Flow

1. The case owner opens SCR-04, or the ledger section of SCR-03; the browser calls the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).
2. gateway-bff calls `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timeline` with the `type`, `channel`, `from`, `to`, `page` and `size` of the screen, one hop inside the 2 s budget (DP-11).
3. rwb-case asks rwb-access `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` for `CASE_RECORD` right `R` with the case as object reference and receives the decision, the scope and the masking policy. Missing right is 403; a case outside scope is 404.
4. rwb-case reads `recovery_case` and its own case events from `assignment` with `queue_code`: allocation, assignment and transfer, with holder before and after, reason and rule ID.
5. rwb-case reads `timeline.ledger-timeout-ms` and the page default and maximum through the parameters contract (DP-06); no budget or bound is a constant.
6. rwb-case calls `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` with the date range, channel and actor filters, `page` and `size`, under the parameter timeout and a breaker, and receives `occurredAt`, `channel`, `eventCode`, `sourceSystem`, `direction`, `contactResult`, `contactKey`, `caseSeq` and the entry ID.
7. rwb-case maps each ledger entry to one `TimelineItem` of type `INTERACTION` and each case event to one item of its type, with source marker, channel, entry type and occurred time; the text is built from codes and reference labels, never from another service's free text (BR1, BR5).
8. rwb-case orders the merged items by occurred time then `caseSeq` (BR2), masks the contact reference through the ACE common masking path with the policy from rwb-access (BR6), pages the list and returns `items[]`, `page`, `size` and `total`; a page past the last returns an empty `items[]` with the same total.
9. The owner filters by channel, source and date range; a `to` before a `from`, a `size` outside its bounds or an unknown type is refused before any source is called.
10. The owner records a call: the front end sends the `Idempotency-Key`, rwb-case calls the P1 append once with the entry command and that key, keeps no copy, and stores the answer of its own call in `idempotency_key`, so a repeat returns the first answer without a second append (BR4).
11. The owner reopens the timeline: the new entry shows as one `INTERACTION` item, source WORKBENCH, channel CALL, in its occurred-time place, because the list is composed at the read.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Role without Case record R | Refused with 403 before the case facts are read; nothing returned, nothing written | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-034-12 |
| X2 | Case outside the reader's scope | Refused with 404; no item, case number or contact reference returned | MSG-P4-003 | AC5 |
| X3 | Case with no ledger entry | Empty `items[]`, total 0; the ledger section shows the empty state | MSG-P3-024 | AC4 |
| X4 | Date `to` before date `from` | Refused before any source is called; nothing read, nothing written | MSG-GEN-003 | AC2 |
| X5 | `size` outside its bounds, or a type outside the seven | Refused before any source is called, naming the field and its bounds | MSG-GEN-002 | AC2 |
| X6 | Ledger read slow past the parameter timeout, or breaker open | The case events return with 200 and the missing source is named by the timeline contract; the read does not fail | MSG-GEN-006 | AC1 |
| X7 | Append answers 409 for a held key | The first answer is returned as success: the entry exists once and the call is a repeat | None | AC7 |
| X8 | Append answers 503 or times out | No item is added and nothing is half written in `rwb_case`; a repeat with the same key appends once when the store is back | None | AC7 |
| X9 | Intake result cannot be read | The items still show with 200 and the note says the intake result is unavailable; no count is invented | None | AC8 |
| X10 | Two entries at the same occurred-at time | The lower `caseSeq` reads first on every page and on a repeated query | None | AC3 |

The read never returns another case's item: the scope is answered by rwb-access before the case facts are read and the ledger read is case-scoped.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against `RWB-P2-E2034-CON` and the published rwb-source-data operations with their fakes; case facts come from its own schema |
| Negotiable | Page bounds, source timeout and labels are parameter and reference rows; sequence, refusal and empty state are fixed |
| Valuable | The owner reads the one history of the case without asking another team, and no second writer of the append-only ledger exists |
| Estimable | One provided operation, two consumed ledger paths, one rights call, one masking read, three components and one page section |
| Small | Fits one iteration; the ledger, the intake, the exception queue and the screen's other sections are other stories' |
| Testable | Every criterion of section 7 is one test of section 16, against a contract fake or a seeded `rwb_case` row; no test reaches another schema |

This secondary slice owns no legacy AC. AC1 to AC11 of RWB-E2-034 are carried by rwb-integration (RWB-P2-E2034-APP, RWB-P2-E2034-CON) and by the rwb-source-data stories of this key; the eight criteria above carry this slice's assertions with the legacy values unchanged. Behind them: the ledger is read one hop away, never from an `interaction` table in `rwb_case` (DP-18); every criterion that needs another service carries its contract mock; the Workbench entry is written by the ledger's owner, which is what makes "nothing is written twice" provable across two services; order is occurred time then case sequence, with the screen's page order left to the timeline contract; and the element names of the item, the append command and the intake result are assumed and renamed at contract review if the published contract differs (GAP-2225; ASM-3667).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The timeline is one list of the case events of `rwb_case` and the ledger entries of rwb-source-data read through the P1 contract; each item names its source marker, channel, entry type and occurred-at time | REQ-ILG-006; REQ-ILG-012 |
| BR2 | Items are ordered by occurred time and, at the same instant, by `caseSeq`, so order is stable across pages; the screen's page order stays the timeline contract's | Legacy BR9, AC3, AC9; REQ-ILG-006 |
| BR3 | `interaction` is not a table of `rwb_case`: no entry, field or summary is copied into this schema and no ACE view is read here | DP-01; DP-18; ownership ruling |
| BR4 | A Workbench-raised interaction is written by one append call under the request's `Idempotency-Key`; a repeat returns the first answer and is counted; a 409 is a repeat, not a failure | Legacy BR7; R-UNI-40; REQ-ILG-007 |
| BR5 | Source marker, channel and entry type are the values the ledger holds, from LOV-SOURCE, LOV-CHANNEL and LOV-LEDGER-EVENT with the version in force; no code holds one | DP-07; legacy BR4; TSD P3 v3 T3.2 |
| BR6 | The contact point is a reference: the item carries the contact key and the caller's mask, never a number, an address or an unmasked value | REQ-ILG-014; CTL-11; DP-08 |
| BR7 | The retention class belongs to the entry and its owner; this slice neither shows a class of its own nor recomputes one | REQ-ILG-013; DP-18 |
| BR8 | Paging is part of the operation: `page` starts at 0, `size` starts at the parameter default, its maximum is the parameter value, and an out-of-bounds size or a `to` before a `from` is refused before any source is called | DP-06; legacy contract |
| BR9 | Right and scope are answered by rwb-access: 403 without Case record R, 404 outside scope, both before any case fact or ledger item is read | DP-08; legacy AC11; CTL-09 |
| BR10 | The intake result is read through the P1 contract and named as received; this service writes no EFS row, applies no outcome list and keeps no summary | Legacy AC6; DP-18; REQ-ILG-009 |
| BR11 | The read writes nothing: no row, decision record, event or workflow state, and a refusal writes nothing either | Legacy section 9; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR12 | A ledger that does not answer inside the parameter timeout does not fail the read: the case events return with 200 and the missing source is named by the timeline contract | NFR-008; legacy AC6 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status and moves no case; the one write it causes is a ledger entry created by rwb-source-data, which moves none either. The ledger is append-only and has no state; the delivery states PENDING, RETRYING, DELIVERED and EXCEPTION belong to the integration slice and are not read here.

| Observed fact | Written by | Appears as |
|---|---|---|
| Case allocated to a queue | rwb-case allocation (RWB-P3-E1020-APP) | One case event with queue and owner |
| Case transferred with a reason code | rwb-case transfer (RWB-P3-E1021-APP) | One case event from "U-2001" to "U-2002" |
| A call recorded on the case | rwb-source-data through its append, on this slice's request | One `INTERACTION` item, source WORKBENCH, channel CALL |
| A letter, partner result, offer or payment recorded | rwb-comms, rwb-partner, rwb-treatment, rwb-payment through the intake of RWB-P2-E2034-APP | One `INTERACTION` item of its entry type |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the timeline of a case in scope (Case record R); records a call on a case they hold (Case record U; the entry is created by rwb-source-data) |
| RW-TEAMMGR; RW-CONDUCT; RW-AUDIT | Read the timeline of a case in scope (Case record R), the contact reference masked by role; change nothing |
| SY-CASEWF, the rwb-case service identity | Applies the access check, reads `recovery_case` and `assignment`, calls the P1 read, the P1 append and the masking read, one hop each; writes no ledger row |
| rwb-source-data contract | Owns the ledger, the append, the case-scoped read, the entry codes, the retention class and the intake rule; refuses a repeated key and answers the same reference |
| rwb-access contract | Answers the right, the scope and the masking policy of the caller's roles |
| RW-REFADM and every role without Case record R | Refused on the operation with MSG-P4-002 |
| No approval applies | The story takes no business decision and records none |

The reader's right is `CASE_RECORD` right `R` with the scope of the caller's team; no role name and no scope value sits in code. The service runs as the rwb-case login (DP-02), which no source names.

| DF-CAS-009, DF-CAS-011, DF-CAS-022 | recovery_case | owner_user_id, team_code, closed_date | Read |

| (idempotency) | idempotency_key in `rwb_case` | the stored answer of the append call under its key | Write |

Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. Every `interaction` row keeps its legacy field IDs and belongs to rwb-source-data (DP-18), so all of them are read through the P1 contract and none is a column of `rwb_case`; the physical names, lengths and required flags of the item, the append command and the intake result are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2225; ASM-3667). The contact reference is masked before it leaves the service (BR6), and item text is built from codes and labels, never from another service's free text.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/case/v1`; owner rwb-case (P3).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/timeline` | One page of the case timeline: `items[]`, `page`, `size`, `total`; each item carries `at`, `type`, `source`, `channel`, `entryType`, `summary`, `by`, `reference`; query `caseId` (path), `type` (`INTERACTION` selects the ledger items), `channel`, `from`, `to`, `page` (default 0), `size` (default and maximum from the parameters) | Case record R, scope applied by rwb-access, contact reference masked by role | Not applicable: the read writes nothing |

`TimelinePage` and `TimelineItem` are the shapes of the case timeline contract of RWB-P3-E2016-CON; this slice adds no field and removes none, and fills four of them for an interaction item: `source`, `channel`, `entryType`, `at`. Errors: 401 (MSG-P4-001); 403 (MSG-P4-002); 404 unknown case or outside scope (MSG-P4-003); 422 a `to` before a `from` (MSG-GEN-003), a `size` out of bounds or a type outside the seven (MSG-GEN-002); 503 the case store down. A slow ledger is not a 5xx here: the case events return with 200 and the missing source is named by the timeline contract (BR12). The operation is the Ownership Map's `GET /cases/{caseId}/timeline` (owner P3) on the rwb-case base, the re-based form of API-P3-003 of TSD P3 v3 T-A.1; the interaction read and the append are rwb-source-data's and appear in 12.2 as consumed.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; the parameter timeout `timeline.ledger-timeout-ms` and a breaker per downstream apply to every row.

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` | rwb-source-data (P1) | The case's entries for the date range, channel and actor filters: `occurredAt`, `channel`, `eventCode`, `sourceSystem`, `direction`, `contactResult`, `contactKey`, `caseSeq`, entry ID | One hop, parameter timeout, breaker |
| POST | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` | rwb-source-data (P1) | The append of one Workbench-raised interaction, create-only and idempotent on `Idempotency-Key`: 201 with a reference, the same reference on a repeat, 409 for a held key, 503 when the store is down | One hop, parameter timeout, no retry on a 4xx |
| GET | The ledger intake-result read of the rwb-source-data contract, for a business date | rwb-source-data (P1) | The intake result: `businessDate`, `rowsRead`, `written`, `excluded`, `notOnCase`; the path and element names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2225; ASM-3667) | One hop, parameter timeout, breaker |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | rwb-access (P4) | Case record R, the scope and the masking policy of the caller's roles, cached by the guard library (DP-08) | One hop, 2 s, cached |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/masking-policies` | rwb-access (P4) | The mask the ACE common masking path applies to a contact reference by role (CTL-11) | One hop, 2 s, cached |

The two ledger operations are the re-based forms of API-P3-014 and API-P3-015 of TSD P3 v3 T-A.1 on the rwb-source-data base, which the Ownership Map records as P1's. RWB-P2-E2034-CON restates the append as consumed with its command, its four answers and the rule that the append is called before the caller marks anything; this story consumes that restatement and defines no part of it.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The timeline is a read and the append is a synchronously owned write, so this slice has no outbox row and no topic of its own; the case events it shows are rows written by the allocation, transfer and timer stories. A decision record of a case action is written by the library of the story that takes the action (DP-03), never here.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. Entries reach rwb-source-data through its intake and its EFS step and this slice reads them when the case is opened, so it holds no projection and no inbox: a late or corrected entry reads correctly at the next open and no stale ledger copy exists in `rwb_case`.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The timeline is served inside the request and the append is one synchronous call under its key. The case workflow of RWB-P3-E2043-APP owns the case lifecycle and is not touched.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Schedule and no Quartz row: the read has no clock and the append is started by a person.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| recovery_case | P3 (`rwb_case`) | The case facts of the item and the access object: ID, case number, owner, team, entry date, closed date |
| assignment | P3 (`rwb_case`) | The case events of the timeline: allocation, assignment and transfer with owner, queue, reason, rule ID |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in `rwb_case` | The stored answer of the append call under the request's key |
| outbox_event, processed_event | PLT library, created in `rwb_case` | Present in the schema; this slice reads and writes none of them |

`interaction` is not a table of this contract: rwb-source-data owns it (DP-18) and it is read and written only through 12.2. `efs_ledger_outcome`, the retention classes and the intake summary are rwb-source-data's too. No table of another service is read and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01).

| Fake | Serves | Stubs used by this story |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-source-data WireMock, ledger read | The P1 case-scoped read | The 3 entries of 14, 15 and 18 December 2026; two entries at 17 December 2026 14:00 with case sequence 7 and 8; an empty answer for "RW-2026-000302"; one delayed answer beyond the parameter timeout |
| rwb-source-data WireMock, append | The P1 append | 201 with a reference; the same reference on a repeat with the same key; 409 for a held key; 503 and a slow answer for the retry path of AC7 |
| rwb-source-data WireMock, intake result | The P1 intake-result read | 3 read, 1 written, 1 excluded and 1 not on a case for 14 December 2026; one unavailable answer |
| rwb-access WireMock | The P4 contract | Allow `RW-CASEOWN` in team "MTG-BKK" with Case record R; refuse `RW-REFADM` with MSG-P4-002; refuse "U-3001" over team "MTG-BKK" with MSG-P4-003; the caller's masking policy |
| gateway-bff route WireMock | The DP-19 composite route of SCR-04 | The merged case and timeline answer, and the refusal that must not read as an empty timeline |
| `rwb_case` fixture | This story's own test data | Case "RW-2026-000301" held by "U-2001" in team "MTG-BKK" with the transfer of 16 December 2026 11:00; case "RW-2026-000302" with no entry |

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |

| REST | 1 provided, 5 consumed | The timeline operation provided; the P1 case-scoped read, append and intake-result read, and the P4 authorise and masking read consumed; one hop, parameter timeout, breaker |
| Kafka | None | No event published or consumed (12.3, 12.4) |
| Temporal | None | No workflow and no activity added; the read is served inside the request |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `timeline`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.timeline`, extending the timeline module of RWB-P3-E2016-APP; front end folder `src/modules/recovery/case/timeline` with the ledger section of the timeline page and the log-interaction panel of the case record page.

**Pattern application.** DP-01: `recovery_case` and `assignment` in `rwb_case` only, `interaction` absent. DP-03: no instance, a read writes no decision record (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON). DP-05: no instance, no view is read here. DP-06: the timeout and page default and maximum rows (H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON). DP-07: LOV-SOURCE, LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-LEDGER-EVENT and type labels (H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON). DP-08: right, scope and contact mask (H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON). DP-09: the `idempotency_key` row of the append call only (H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON). DP-10: no instance, no workflow and no Schedule (H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON). DP-11: the two ledger operations with their fakes (none; C from the legacy dependency). DP-13: both bases. DP-15: no instance, no table and no column added (H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON). DP-18: the read and the append of 12.2. DP-19: the route of SCR-03 and SCR-04 (H RWB-PLT-N001-CON). Metadata H is None and correct: those platform contracts are pulled by the rwb-case baseline stories and the timeline contract, so this slice is Day 1 and builds against the published `RWB-P2-E2034-CON` and the P1, P4 and gateway-bff fakes.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| TimelineController | REST controller | The operation, query and page validation, problem responses with their message IDs |
| TimelineService | Service | Merges case events and ledger items, applies the sequence of BR2, pages and returns the total |
| CaseEventReadRepository | Repository | Reads `recovery_case` and `assignment` with `queue_code` for a case and a date range |
| LedgerReadClient, LedgerAppendClient, IntakeResultClient | Clients | The P1 read under the timeout and breaker (BR1); the command sent once under the key with a 409 read as a repeat (BR4); the intake result named as received (BR10) |
| TimelineItemMapper, ContactMaskAdapter | Service, library adapter | The item from codes and reference labels; the contact reference masked through the ACE common masking path (BR6) |
| LedgerSection, LogInteractionPanel | React component | The ledger section of SCR-04 and SCR-03, the Loading, Filtered, Empty and Degraded states, the filters and the save panel |

**Database and migrations.** Reads `recovery_case` and `assignment` in `rwb_case` and writes one `idempotency_key` row per append call; no new table, no new column, no migration of this story. The indexes used, `ix_assignment_case_assigned_at` and `ix_timer_case_started_at`, come from `V2016_1__timeline_indexes.sql` of RWB-P3-E2016-APP in the same Flyway sequence (DP-15). The `interaction` table, its trigger and its indexes are rwb-source-data's migration and are never created, altered or indexed here (DP-18).

**Configuration and reference data.** Parameter rows through the parameters contract (DP-06): `timeline.ledger-timeout-ms`, `timeline.page-size-default`, `timeline.page-size-max`; breaker and bulkhead settings are the resilience library's defaults and no number is fixed here. Reference rows (DP-07): LOV-SOURCE, LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-LEDGER-EVENT and the seven item type labels with the version in force; the type list is a list value, not a Java enum. The mask of a role is read from rwb-access and applied by the ACE common masking path.

**Build steps**

1. `CaseEventReadRepository` over `recovery_case` and `assignment`, with one test per case event and the transfer of AC1.
2. `LedgerReadClient` against the P1 fake with the parameter timeout, the breaker and the delayed answer (AC1, X6).
3. `TimelineItemMapper` with source marker, channel and entry type from reference rows and the masked contact reference (AC1).
4. The sequence of BR2 and the paging of BR8, with the bounds and date refusals (AC2, AC3).
5. `TimelineController` with the 403, the 404, the empty state and the total (AC4, AC5, TC-E2-034-12).
6. `LedgerAppendClient` and the save panel: the key, the stored answer, the repeat and the 409 (AC7); then `IntakeResultClient` and the note (AC8).
7. The contract-fake run of every consumed answer in isolation, then the composite-route test with gateway-bff; and the read test on a case whose ledger holds 500 entries, first page inside 2 s (NFR-070), case indexes only.

**Feature switch.** None of its own: a case timeline must read and the operation has no off state. The save path is offered only where the append is reachable; elsewhere the timeline still reads and the save panel is not shown. The legacy flag `rwb.integration.ledger-channels` stays the integration slice's.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass; a case whose ledger holds 500 entries returns its first page inside 2 s at the parameter page size; a save with one key writes one entry and a repeat writes none; a case outside scope answers 404 with MSG-P4-003 and a case with no entry answers total 0 with MSG-P3-024; no statement of the service reads `interaction`, an EFS list or an ACE view.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-024 | The case has no ledger entry | No interactions are recorded on this case yet. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Case record R opens the timeline | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the reader's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | The page size is out of bounds, or the type is outside the seven | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | The date `to` is before the date `from` | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The ledger source does not answer inside the parameter timeout | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. |

For MSG-GEN-006 {system} is "Interaction ledger", the display name the timeline contract gives rwb-source-data; for MSG-GEN-003 the fields are "to" and "from"; for MSG-GEN-002 the field is "size" or "type" with the parameter bounds; for MSG-P4-002 {action} is "read the timeline of this case" or "record an interaction on this case". MSG-P3-024 is new in the legacy story and keeps its text; the other texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story and the message catalogue. Thai text for each follows DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

The ledger section of SCR-04 Case timeline and of SCR-03 Case record, served by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19) and built on the timeline page of RWB-P3-E2016-APP; the field list, layout and field-level masking are that contract's and change not here.

| Screen | State | What the user does |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-04 Case timeline | Loading | Sees skeleton rows while the composite route answers |
| SCR-04 Case timeline | Filtered | Filters by channel, source and date range, pages a long history, reads each item's source, channel, entry type and time |
| SCR-04 Case timeline | Empty | Reads MSG-P3-024 when the case has no entry, filters still shown and no error |
| SCR-04 Case timeline | Degraded | Reads the case events with the notice naming "Interaction ledger" when the ledger does not answer (BR12) |
| SCR-03 Case record | Read only, and Saving a call | Opens the timeline, records a call with its contact reference, channel and result, and sees it saved once; a repeat returns the first answer |

No screen shows a retention class, a decision log entry or another service's free text, and none shows a contact number or an address: the contact point is the masked reference.

The full test, with its Given, When and Then, is in Recovery Workbench Test Cases v7.xlsx, tab Story test cases, under the same ID.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: source, channel and entry-type values, type labels, page bounds and source timeout are reference and parameter rows read through their contracts (BR5, BR8).
- No personal data in logs, tests or prompts: an item carries identifiers, codes and a contact key, never a number, an address or another party's amount; the contact reference is masked by role before it leaves the service and is never logged; all test data is synthetic.
- No read of another service's tables: the ledger, the EFS list, the retention classes and the intake summary come only through the P1 contract, and `interaction` is not a table of `rwb_case` (BR3, DP-01, DP-18). No ACE view is read here: only rwb-source-data reads the `recovery.v_ace_*` views.
- One hop, no chaining: the timeline never calls a downstream of a downstream; breaker and bulkhead are per downstream (DP-11).
- The entry is never written twice and never rewritten: the append is create-only, keyed by the request's `Idempotency-Key`, and a 409 is a repeat (BR4). The timeline writes no ledger row, copy, projection or event; its only row is the stored answer of its own append call (BR11).
- A refusal returns no data: no item, case number or contact reference, with the catalogue message ID and an RFC 9457 problem body; the case number on screen comes from the case contract, never from a copy.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-034 for rwb-access. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner, a team manager, a specialist or an auditor who reads the interaction ledger of a case — and as an agent that reads it on their behalf**, I want **one access answer for that ledger: whether my role may read it, which scope admits the case, and which fields of an entry come back masked — the same on every channel the entry came from and on every screen that shows it — with each ledger read written into the access log**, so that **the ledger is read where the case is read, the contact point of an entry is never shown to a role that may not see it, and any audit question about who read which ledger can be answered from one log**.

Inside `rwb-access` this is the access-side slice of legacy RWB-E2-034: service `rwb-access`, schema `rwb_access`, REST base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, service topic `rwb.access.events.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`, one schema and one login per service (DP-01, DP-02, DP-13).

- **The answer this story builds:** for one case and the field IDs of its ledger entries, the area `CASE_RECORD` right `R`, the scope that admits the case (OWN, TEAM, REGION or ALL), and a `masked` or `clear` marker per field ID under the masking version in force. The answer carries markers and identifiers, never a value.
- **Owned here:** the mask of an entry's personal fields by role, the right and scope refusal of the ledger read, and the access-log entry of every ledger read and every refusal (FEAT-ACA-05, FEAT-ACA-07, FEAT-ACA-08, FEAT-ACA-16).
- **Not this slice:** the ledger table, the append, the case-scoped interaction read, the EFS intake rule, the outcome list and the retention class are `rwb-source-data`'s (DP-18, R-PREC default ruling on `interaction`); the channel consumer and the exception queue are `RWB-P2-E2034-APP`; the timeline and the case record section are `RWB-P3-E2034-APP`; the partner portal is the S9 slice. This story builds no screen, no consumer, no workflow and no ledger table.
- **Unchanged from the legacy story:** the 404 `MSG-P4-003` of a case outside the reader's scope (legacy AC11), the 403 `MSG-P4-002` of a role without Case record R (legacy exception X8), the contact point kept as a reference and masked by role (BR5, REQ-ILG-014), the mask holding whatever the screen (FEAT-ACA-05), and the access log written as a decision record (FEAT-ACA-07, FEAT-ACA-08).
- **Data, not code:** the roles, the permission matrix, the masking rows and the role conflicts are rows of `rwb_access`; LOV-SCOPE and LOV-CAPABILITY come through the reference-data contract (DP-07). No role code, scope name, capability area, field ID or version string is a constant.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contact outcomes from collections, letters sent through WIN and work held by partners sit in different systems today, so a case owner who picks up a case does not know which number answered or who held it last; the measure of the whole legacy key is the share of open cases whose last right-party contact is visible on the case, today zero for cases that came from EFS. The ledger and its channels answer the "what happened" half of that measure. This story answers the half that decides whether the ledger may be read at all and in what form: the right, the scope and the mask (REQ-ILG-012, REQ-ILG-014), and the record of who read it (FEAT-ACA-07, FEAT-ACA-08).

The risk it removes is concrete. A ledger entry carries a contact point — the reference behind which a phone number or an address sits — and CTL-11 and REQ-ILG-014 require that reference and never the value, masked by role. Without one owner of that decision, each screen that shows the ledger masks by its own rule, an export masks nothing, an agent reads whatever its prompt happens to include, and no log can say who looked at which entry: NFR-039 and NFR-040 ask for masking at rest and in use and for the minimum data per screen and per agent, NFR-042 for every read to be logged, and NFR-051 for an agent to pass the same role checks as a person.

The measure is the one the module reports — rule and limit changes made without a code release, at 100 percent, because the roles, the matrix version and the masking rows are data — plus two facts an audit can check: every ledger read is answered with a mask the policy in force names, and every read of it leaves one `AC-READ` entry naming the case and the masked field IDs.

This story implements the decision behind the element for the ledger and adds no operation |

This is the only cross-service shape the answer is asked about |
