Business preconditions carried from the legacy story:

- Permission matrix version `PM-2026.12` is in force and gives CASE_RECORD right R to RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-CONDUCT and RW-AUDIT, and no CASE_RECORD right to RW-REFADM (FSD P4 A2.4; TSD P4 T6.1). The default scope of each role is the `role.default_scope` row in force.
- Masking version `MASK-SIT-01` is in force. That this label is the masking version of SIT is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2321; ASM-3856).
- The personal fields of a ledger entry that the mask covers are `DF-INT-011` summary and `DF-INT-022` contact point, with `DF-ACE-076` and `DF-ACE-077` behind them. Which field IDs of the entry the policy covers is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2321; ASM-3857).
- The ledger of the case holds its entries (rwb-source-data); a case with no entry is normal and shows the empty state of RWB-P3-E2034-APP, not an error here.
- The caller signed in through Entra ID with multi-factor authentication and holds at least one Recovery role; with no role the answer is 401 `MSG-P4-001` (FSD P4 A2.1, A2.2).
- The database login is the rwb-access login (DP-02); its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2321; ASM-3861).
- The platform contracts named above are pulled by the wave-1 access stories, so this secondary slice adds no build dependency of its own (metadata H = None) and builds on Day 1 against `RWB-P2-E2034-CON` and the fixtures of section 12.8.

##### 4. Flow

1. Caller: a person opens SCR-03 Case record or SCR-04 Case timeline; gateway-bff resolves the session and `rwb-case` asks `rwb-access` for the ledger of the case, naming the case, the area `CASE_RECORD`, the right `R` and the field IDs of the entries on the page.
2. `rwb-access`: resolves the caller's roles from the session and the rights from `permission` for the matrix version in force, `PM-2026.12`; reads `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule` and `role_conflict` from `rwb_access` only (BR9).
3. `rwb-access`, right check: no CASE_RECORD R for any role of the caller gives 403 with `MSG-P4-002` naming the action and no case data (BR1), and one `AC-DENY` entry.
4. `rwb-access`, scope check: the case is admitted when its attributes satisfy the caller's `default_scope` in force read through DP-07 — OWN for a case the caller owns, TEAM for a case of the caller's team, REGION for its region, ALL for any case (BR2). A case outside it is answered 404 with `MSG-P4-003` and no case data, so the answer never confirms that the case exists, and one `AC-DENY` entry is written.
5. `rwb-access`, mask: for each field ID asked, the profile is read from `masking_rule` for the roles the caller holds and the masking version in force; with no covering row the field is `masked` (BR4). The channel of the entry is not an input: an entry from EFS, from the Workbench and from the partner portal is answered with the same markers (BR3).
6. `rwb-access`: writes one `AC-READ` decision record through the library of DP-03 with the case ID, the field IDs asked and their markers under the version used, then returns the answer — granted, with the scope and the version — inside the 2 s budget of DP-11 (BR5). Nothing is returned before the record commits; a failure answers 503 `MSG-P7-003` and raises an incident.
7. Caller: `rwb-case` applies the markers to each entry of the page and renders it; a field marked `masked` is rendered masked whatever the screen, the export or the agent call (BR3).
8. Agent: a service identity reads the same ledger for the same case and is answered by the same decision under its own roles; the `AC-READ` entry carries the agent's actor reference (BR8).
9. Repeat: the same ask under the same policy versions is answered from the cached decision, and that read still writes its own `AC-READ` entry (BR7).
10. Policy change: a new matrix or masking version is approved on the load path, the rows are written by that path, and the cache is dropped on the commit that writes them; the next ask is answered under the new version with no deployment (BR7).
11. Audit: `RW-PLATADM` calls `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` with the user, the event `AC-READ`, from and to, and reads one row per ledger read with the case ID, the field IDs and their markers (BR6).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The case is outside the caller's scope | 404 with no case data; one `AC-DENY` entry naming the area and the right and no case ID | MSG-P4-003 | AC4, TC-E2-034-11 |
| X2 | No role of the caller holds Case record R | Refused before any case fact is read: 403, no field marker | MSG-P4-002 | AC5, TC-E2-034-12 |
| X3 | No masking row covers a field ID | The field is marked `masked` with the default marker; the read is otherwise granted | None | AC1, AC3 |
| X4 | The reference list of scope or capability is not available | No answer rather than a guessed one: 503; the refusal is recorded | MSG-GEN-006 | BR8 |
| X5 | The decision record cannot be written | Nothing is returned: 503 with no case data, and an incident is raised to the platform administrator queue | MSG-P7-003 | AC8, TC-E2-034-07 |
| X6 | The token carries no Recovery role, or no second factor | No answer is given: 401 before the policy is read; one refusal entry with the reason | MSG-P4-001 | BR1, AC7 |
| X7 | Two roles of the caller conflict, for example RW-SECADM with a business role | The session is refused at sign-in from the `role_conflict` rows; no ledger ask is made | MSG-P4-006 | BR8 |
| X8 | An agent or service identity holds no role | Refused 401; no ledger data and no marker | MSG-P4-001 | AC7 |
| X9 | The page size of the access-log read is out of bounded range | 422 naming the field and its bounds, before any row is read | MSG-GEN-002 | BR6 |

A masking version that changes mid-day for the same case, and the version the answer then names, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2321; ASM-3856); until they are, the answer uses the version whose `valid_from` is the latest on or before the business date and names it, so a caller can never mistake a stale marker for a current one.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds and tests against `RWB-P2-E2034-CON` and the wave-1 access contract; reads its own schema only and calls no other service at run time |
| Negotiable | The policy pack — roles, matrix version, masking rows and their versions — is data; the story fixes the shape of the answer and the refusal behaviour only |
| Valuable | The ledger is readable by the roles entitled to it, masked by role on every channel and every screen, and every read is in the access log |
| Estimable | One decision behind an existing operation, one cache, one decision-record path, one admin read and one index |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests; no screen, no consumer, no ledger table and no workflow |
| Testable | Every owned criterion has a test case in section 16; the entry shape is a published fake |

AC1 to AC9 are the criteria this story owns; it owns no legacy criterion. The legacy AC1 to AC11 and the access row TC-E2-034-12 are carried by the slices named in section 19, and AC11 — a case outside the reader's scope is refused with `MSG-P4-003` — is stated here as AC4 with the legacy values unchanged, because the scope answer of the ledger read is this slice's. In AC1 and AC2 the assertions that belong to this service are the markers and the version they come from; the entries, their order and their text are P1's and P3's. AC2 proves that neither the channel nor the source of an entry is an input to the mask: the role is. AC3 proves that a covering row is what makes a field clear, not the screen. AC4 and AC5 prove the two refusals of the legacy story, each also as the entry the audit reads. AC6 turns the access log into an answer, which is what makes FEAT-ACA-16 real for this key. AC7 proves NFR-051 for the ledger, AC8 that a read is never unlogged, and AC9 that the mask follows the version in force without a release.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The right comes from the permission matrix version in force; a caller whose roles hold no Case record R is refused 403 `MSG-P4-002` with no case data and one `AC-DENY` entry | FSD P4 A2.4 VR-P4-004-1; TSD P4 T6.1; FEAT-ACA-04 |
| BR2 | A case is admitted when its attributes satisfy the caller's `default_scope` in force — OWN, TEAM, REGION or ALL; a case outside it is answered 404 `MSG-P4-003` with no case data and one `AC-DENY` entry | FSD P4 A2.14; LOV-SCOPE; legacy AC11 |
| BR3 | The mask depends on the role, the field ID and the masking version only: the channel, the source and the screen of an entry change no marker, so the same field is masked on SCR-03, SCR-04, an export and an agent call | FEAT-ACA-05; NFR-040; legacy BR5 |
| BR4 | A field is marked `masked` unless a `masking_rule` row for a role the caller holds and that field says unmasked true for the masking version in force; with no covering row the field is masked | FSD P4 A2.5 AC-EXC-P4-004-05; NFR-039; legacy BR6 |
| BR5 | Every granted ledger read writes one `AC-READ` decision record with the case ID, the field IDs and their markers under the version used, before the answer is returned; one read is one entry (GAP-2321; ASM-3858) | FSD P4 A2.7 AC-P4-007-01; FEAT-ACA-07; FEAT-ACA-08 |
| BR6 | Every refusal writes one `AC-DENY` decision record with the area and the right and no case ID, and the access-log read returns both codes to a role holding Platform administration R, within its page bounds | FSD P4 A2.7 AC-EXC-P4-007-04, A2.16; FEAT-ACA-16 |
| BR7 | The answer is cached per policy version and the cache is dropped on the commit that writes a new matrix or masking version, so a policy change takes effect with no deployment; the answer names the version it used, so a stale marker is detectable | FSD P4 AC-P4-004-01; DP-11; TSD P4 T3.2 |
| BR8 | Role codes, scope values, capability areas, field IDs and every version are data read from `rwb_access` and the reference lists; an agent or service identity is decided by the same checks as a person and its read is logged with its actor reference (GAP-2321; ASM-3862) | FSD P4 BR-P4-004, BR-P4-005; NFR-051; principle 1 |
| BR9 | The answer is built from the request and from `rwb_access`: no `interaction`, `recovery_case`, notice, instruction, treatment or proceeds row and no `v_ace_*` view is read, and the entry's values never enter this service | DP-01; DP-05; DP-18 |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-access`:

- BR1 is a read of `permission` for the caller's roles and the `matrix_version` in force; the letters C, R, U, D and A are the five-character field of TSD P4 T3.1, and the answer names the version it used.
- BR2 is `ScopeRule`, comparing the attributes of the request with the `default_scope` value read through DP-07; the four scope names are list values, never Java constants, and the attribute set of the request is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2321; ASM-3859).
- BR3 is the reason the request carries no channel and no source as decision inputs: they travel with the entry for display, and a marker that differed by channel would be a defect of this answer, not of the screen.
- BR4 is a read of `masking_rule` by `field_id`, `role_code` and `masking_version`; the answer carries markers, never values, so no personal data crosses the boundary in either direction (NFR-039).
- BR5 and BR6 are one transaction as the answer: the record is written first, the answer is returned after it commits, and a failure answers 503 with `MSG-P7-003` and changes nothing.
- BR7 is a cache keyed by the matrix and masking versions; the load path writes the new rows and drops it, and no answer is served under a version it does not name.
- BR8 is visible in the code review: no role code, scope name, capability area, field ID or version string appears in a constant.
- BR9 is the reason there is no ledger repository here: the service holds `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict`, the decision record and the outbox, and nothing else.

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status and no ledger entry: the ledger is append-only and belongs to `rwb-source-data`, the timeline and the case are `rwb-case`'s, and the story runs no workflow of its own. The only states it has are the states of its answer:

| Answer state | When | What the caller gets | Record written |
|---|---|---|---|
| Granted | The caller holds Case record R and the case is in scope | The scope, the masking version and a `masked` or `clear` marker per field ID | `AC-READ` |
| Refused, no right | No role of the caller holds Case record R | 403 `MSG-P4-002`, no case data | `AC-DENY` |
| Not found | The caller holds the right and the case is outside the scope | 404 `MSG-P4-003`, no case data | `AC-DENY` |
| Not answered | The record cannot be written, or a list the answer needs is unavailable | 503, no case data | None; the failure is raised as an incident |

The policy versions are not states of this story: a version is loaded, approved and put in force by the load path, and this story only reads the version in force.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Case record R with default scope OWN: reads the ledger of a case it owns, with the personal fields masked |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Case record R with default scope TEAM: reads the ledger of a case of its team |
| RW-CONDUCT, conduct and QA officer | Case record R with the role default scope: reads the ledger within that scope |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Case record R with default scope ALL: reads any ledger; a field is clear only where a masking row says so |
| RW-REFADM and every role with no Case record R | Refused with `MSG-P4-002`; no entry and no marker is returned |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Reads the access log through `GET /admin/access-log` with Platform administration R, scope applied |
| RW-SECADM, security administrator | Approves the permission matrix and masking versions through the load path stories; this story reads the versions in force |
| RW-COMPLY, Compliance and PDPA officer | Reads which masking version is in force and which fields it covers; this story writes no value on their behalf |
| SY-AGENT and the other service identities | Ask the same question for their own reads; the roles of a service identity are checked as a person's are and its read is logged |

Reading is the whole of this story: it grants or refuses a read and writes the record of it. It changes no case, no entry and no policy row; a policy row changes only through the load path stories of this service, and the break-glass grant, its incident reference and its four-hour ceiling stay with the wave-1 stories of the access service.

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Table in rwb_access | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039 | `role` | id, role_code, role_name, role_class, default_scope, entra_group | Read |
| DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044 | `permission` | id, role_id, capability_area, letters, matrix_version | Read |
| DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204 | `masking_rule` | id, role_code, field_id, unmasked, masking_version, valid_from, valid_to | Read |
| DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211 | `role_conflict` | id, role_code, conflicts_with, reason, conflict_version, valid_from, valid_to | Read (the sign-in check, X7) |
| DF-REF-027 to DF-REF-033 | `lov_value` | LOV-SCOPE and LOV-CAPABILITY values, read through the reference-data contract of DP-07 | Read through the contract; the table is P3's |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (local library, DP-03) | the `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entries: code, actor, area, right, case ID, actions, decided at | Write |
| (outbox) | outbox table in `rwb_access` | the decision-record row of the answer | Write |
| (inbox) | `processed_event` | present in the schema; this story consumes no event and writes none | Not used |

The field IDs the answer marks — `DF-INT-011` summary and `DF-INT-022` contact point, with `DF-ACE-076` and `DF-ACE-077` behind them — appear in `masking_rule.field_id` and in the answer as identifiers only. The entry itself, its contact key, its summary, its holder references and the values of the ACE views stay with their owners and are never copied, read or logged here: the answer is markers, identifiers and version labels (NFR-039, NFR-040, DP-18). Field IDs are those of the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.

Which field IDs of an entry the policy covers, and whether the mask applies to the summary as it does to the contact point, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2321; ASM-3857).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None new in this story. The operations are those of the service contract in force from wave 1 (RWB-P4-E1037-CON) on base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, owner rwb-access (P4), unchanged in path, request, response and error shape:

| Method | Path | What this story decides or serves | Access |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | The right, the scope and the `masked`/`clear` marker per field ID for the ledger of one case; 401 (MSG-P4-001), 403 (MSG-P4-002), 404 (MSG-P4-003), 503 (MSG-P7-003) | The session's roles; the answer is the check |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` | The `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` rows of ledger reads by user, event, from, to, page and size | Platform administration R, scope applied |

The Ownership Map rows of this service are the four administration operations — `GET /admin/access-log`, `GET /admin/roles`, `GET /me/session` and `POST /admin/break-glass-grants`; the authorise element is the guard contract of RWB-P4-E1037-CON on the same base and the sibling stories of this run consume it at the path above (GAP-2321; ASM-3859). `GET /admin/roles`, `GET /me/session` and `POST /admin/break-glass-grants` are other stories' and are not used here.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The entry shape arrives in the request — the field IDs, the case and the identifiers — so this story calls no service at run time and holds no ledger read. The shape it expects is the one `RWB-P2-E2034-CON` declares; that contract is used as a fake in the tests (12.8) and as the alignment reference in the build.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library; consumed by P7 | case ID where there is one, else the actor reference | the hash-chained `AC-READ` or `AC-DENY` record: code, actor, area, right, case ID, field IDs with markers, decided at |

CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, published by the library of DP-03 in the transaction of the answer. The payload carries no personal value: the `AC-READ` record carries field IDs and markers, the `AC-DENY` record the area and the right only. No event is published on `rwb.access.events.v1`: the ownership row of this service lists no event of its own, so the policy change is a commit in this service and not an event of this slice.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The policy versions are written by this service's load path and read from `rwb_access`; the story holds no inbox row and subscribes to no topic.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The answer is served inside the request and the record is written in the same transaction; this story registers no workflow and no activity on `rwb-access`.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Schedule and no Quartz row. JOB-18, the six-monthly access review list, is a Temporal Schedule of this service and its story is RWB-P4-AD008-APP.

`interaction`, its append-only trigger and its indexes are `rwb-source-data`'s and appear nowhere as an object of this contract (DP-18); `recovery_case`, `notice`, `instruction`, `treatment` and `proceeds` are never read (DP-01), and no foreign key crosses a schema.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`, module `access/ledgeraccess`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.ledgeraccess`, extending the authorise module behind RWB-P4-E1037-CON.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | ACE data through rwb-source-data or the owner's views; this slice reads neither and answers with markers | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library — this service is its owner | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library, CloudEvents, the owner's topic | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/access/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in `rwb_access` | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data; the answer is asked about its entry shape | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 is the shape of the answer: `interaction` and every case, notice, instruction, treatment and proceeds row belong to their owners, so the decision is built from identifiers in the request and from `rwb_access`, never from a joined query. DP-03 is the access log: an `AC-READ` and an `AC-DENY` are decision records on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, so an access question and a decision question are answered from one log. DP-05 is a statement: the contact value and the ACE view behind it stay with `rwb-source-data`, so this service answers with field IDs and markers. DP-06 supplies the page bounds of the access-log read and the batch limit of field IDs, whose names are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2321; ASM-3860); DP-07 supplies LOV-SCOPE and LOV-CAPABILITY with the version in force, because `lov_value` stays with P3. DP-08 is the contract this story implements: the guard library of the callers and the decision of this service are one contract, so a caller and an owner cannot disagree about a marker. DP-09 is the outbox row of the access event and nothing else, since the ownership row of this service lists no event; DP-10 is a statement that no job of this key runs from a shared Quartz table and JOB-18 is RWB-P4-AD008-APP. DP-11 is the caller-facing boundary — one hop, 2 s, cached — and DP-13, DP-15 and DP-18 are the naming, migration and ownership conventions of the service. DP-19 is the route the screens arrive through; the screens are P3's.

The platform contracts the DP rows name are preconditions of the service lane already in place behind RWB-P4-E1037-CON in wave 1, so metadata H is None and this secondary slice is Day 1 (ASM-3859).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| LedgerAccessController | Controller | The authorise element and the access-log read on the existing base; validation and problem responses |
| LedgerAccessDecisionService | Service | Right, scope and marker per field, in that order; one answer, one record |
| PermissionResolver | Service | Reads `permission` for the caller's roles and the `matrix_version` in force |
| ScopeRule | Service | Compares the case attributes of the request with the `default_scope` in force |
| LedgerMaskService | Service | The `masked` or `clear` marker per field ID for the caller's roles and the masking version in force; default masked |
| AccessRecordWriter | Service | The `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entries through DP-03, written before the answer commits |
| AccessLogQuery | Service | The paged `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` rows by user, event, from and to, bounded by the parameter rows |
| PolicyCache | Service | The cached answer per policy version, dropped on the commit that writes a new version |
| AccessRepository | Repository | `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict` and the outbox in `rwb_access`; no foreign table |

**Database and migrations.** No new table: `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule` and `role_conflict` exist from the wave-1 stories behind RWB-P4-E1037-CON, and the policy rows are loaded by the load path. One migration in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15: `V2034_1__ledger_access_read_path.sql` adds `ix_masking_rule_role_field` on `masking_rule (role_code, field_id, masking_version)` and `ix_permission_role_area` on `permission (role_id, capability_area, matrix_version)`, so the two reads of an answer are index reads inside the 2 s budget. No ledger table, column or index is created here (DP-18).

**Configuration and reference data.** The matrix version and the masking version in force are data: the latest `valid_from` on or before the business date. The access-log page default and maximum and the batch limit of field IDs per answer are parameter rows through DP-06 (GAP-2321; ASM-3860). LOV-SCOPE and LOV-CAPABILITY come through DP-07. No role code, scope name, capability area, field ID, version string or timeout constant sits in code; the 2 s is the platform standard of the guard client.

**Build steps**

1. `PermissionResolver` and `ScopeRule` over `permission`, `role` and the reference lists, with the matrix version named in the answer; tests for AC1, AC4 and AC5.
2. `LedgerMaskService` with the covering-row lookup, the default masked and the channel-independent answer; tests for AC1, AC2 and AC3.
3. `AccessRecordWriter` with the `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entries written before the answer, and the forced failure of X5; tests for AC4, AC5 and AC8.
4. `AccessLogQuery` and the admin read with the page bounds and the refusal of X9; tests for AC6.
5. The agent and service-identity path with its own actor reference and the 401 of X8; test AC7.
6. `PolicyCache` and the drop on the commit that writes a new version; test AC9 against the MASK-SIT-02 fixture.
7. The migration of the two indexes, and a timing test that one answer stays inside the 2 s budget on a policy pack of the loaded size.
8. The contract-fake run of the whole capability against the `RWB-P2-E2034-CON` entry shape and the decision-record fake, so the story builds before the ledger side exists in the environment.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.p4.ledger-access`, read from the platform feature-flag library under the R-PREC default ruling. Off: the ledger read is answered by the case record answer alone (the matrix right, the scope and the mask of the case fields), the ledger field IDs are answered `masked` for every role and the access-log write is unchanged — so nothing becomes readable that a policy did not already allow, and the story's other behaviour is untouched. The switch needs no schema rollback.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; a case owned by the caller is answered with its field markers and the version used; a case outside the scope is answered 404 with no case data; a role without Case record R is answered 403; an entry from EFS, from the Workbench and from the portal gets the same markers; a field with no covering row comes back masked; every granted and every refused read leaves its record; the access log answers who read which ledger; and a newly approved masking version changes the answer with no deployment.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | The token carries no Recovery role, or no second factor | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. | The access check before this story's answer (X6, X8) |
| MSG-P4-002 | No role of the caller holds the right in the capability area | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, on the refusal of BR1 and on the access-log read of BR6 (X2, AC6) |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. | This story, on the refusal of BR2 (X1) |
| MSG-P4-006 | Two roles of the caller conflict | {role} may not be held together with {role}. | The access check, from this service's `role_conflict` rows (X7) |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on every answer (X5) |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A list the answer needs is not available | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. | This story, on a reference-list failure (X4) |
| MSG-GEN-002 | The page size of the access-log read is out of bounds | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. | This story, on the admin read (X9) |

For `MSG-P4-002` the {action} value is the action the caller attempted, for example "read the ledger of this case" or "read the access log"; for `MSG-P4-003` no case fact is echoed, because the message must not confirm that a case exists. Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId`, the text with its placeholders filled and the instance of the request; the Thai text follows DL10. `MSG-P3-024`, the empty state of the ledger, is the screen's and is carried by RWB-P3-E2034-APP.

##### 15. Screens and states

This story builds no screen. SCR-03 Case record and SCR-04 Case timeline, with their ledger section, filters and empty state, are RWB-P3-E2034-APP's through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19; the access-log read serves the platform administration view of RWB-P4-E1039-APP, whose fields and layout are that story's.

What this story decides for those screens is what each state may show:

| Screen | State | What the answer decides |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-03 Case record, SCR-04 Case timeline | Granted | The ledger entries of the page are rendered; a field this story marks `masked` is rendered masked and a field marked `clear` is the only one shown in full, whatever the screen |
| SCR-03, SCR-04 | Entry from EFS, WORKBENCH or PORTAL | The same markers: the channel and the source of an entry change nothing on the screen |
| SCR-03, SCR-04 | Refused | The page shows `MSG-P4-002` and no entry and no case fact, and one `AC-DENY` entry exists |
| SCR-03, SCR-04 | Not found | The page shows `MSG-P4-003` and no entry and no case fact, and one `AC-DENY` entry exists |
| SCR-03, SCR-04 | Not available | The page shows `MSG-P7-003` where the record could not be written, and no entry |

A screen that renders a field clear because a client cached it is a defect of the screen, not of the answer: the answer always names the masking version it used, and a field is clear only where a row of that version says so.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: role codes, scope values, capability areas, field IDs, the matrix version, the masking version and the page bounds are data rows in `rwb_access` and list values read through DP-07; the switch is a platform flag (BR8).
- No personal data in logs, events, the record or the tests: the answer carries markers, the `AC-READ` entry carries field IDs and markers, the `AC-DENY` entry carries the area and the right, and the event carries version labels; test data is synthetic and staff appear as user references.
- ACE data only through its owner: the contact value and the `v_ace_*` views stay with `rwb-source-data`, and this service stores and returns no customer value (DP-05, DP-18, NFR-039, NFR-040).
- No cross-schema read (DP-01): `interaction`, `recovery_case`, `notice`, `instruction`, `treatment`, `proceeds` and the ACE views are never queried; the case arrives as attributes of the request and the policy is the service's own.
- The record is written before the answer: a failure answers 503 with no case data and raises an incident, so no ledger read is unlogged (BR5, BR6).
- One writer for the policy: only the load path stories of this service write a role, a permission or a masking row; this story reads them, so an answer and the policy it names cannot disagree.
- The answer is idempotent for a policy version and the mask never widens with the channel: the same question under the same versions returns the same markers, and the cache is dropped on the commit that writes a new version.
- The feature switch changes one rule and no schema, and it never widens a mask: off answers the ledger field IDs masked for every role and leaves every other decision as it was.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-034 for rwb-source-data. The legacy story appended channel entries in process to the shared `interaction` table, resolved the retention class with a local table read and showed the ledger as a timeline in the same module; in the target the ledger and the shape of one entry stay with rwb-source-data (DP-01, DP-18 and the R-PREC default ruling that the ledger belongs to rwb-source-data), the six columns the legacy story added become one version on this service's own Flyway sequence with the index `ix_interaction_retention_class` (DP-15), the append and the case read keep the two case-scoped operations the Ownership Map gives this service and gain the six fields on base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` (DP-11, DP-13), the retention class is a reference-data read through the client library and never a constant in code (DP-07), a decision record is written by the local library (DP-03), a redelivered append is absorbed by the inbox of the platform library (DP-09), no workflow and no Schedule sits in this story (DP-10), and the screens arrive through gateway-bff (DP-19); the event consumer and the event-to-entry mapping go to RWB-P2-E2034-APP, the partner result to the S9 slice of this key, the timeline to RWB-P3-E2034-APP, the scope to the P4 slice and the EFS history read to RWB-P1-E2001-APP. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **every channel entry of a case to be appended to one ledger with the contact point it reached, the holder who held the case before and after a move, the treatment or the proceeds it refers to and the retention class of its event code, and the case ledger to give those entries back in the order they occurred**, so that **a contact, a letter, a hand-over, an offer and a payment are recorded once and read once, and no service has to read another service's row to show them on the case**.

This is the rwb-source-data slice of legacy RWB-E2-034, and it owns **the ledger store and the shape of one entry**, not the channels that fill it. Under D-RCV-60 the one legacy story is five owners: the six channel events and their mapping are rwb-integration's (RWB-P2-E2034-APP), the partner result and the partner portal are rwb-partner's (the S9 slice), the timeline and the case record section are rwb-case's (RWB-P3-E2034-APP), the scope and the masking rule are rwb-access's (the P4 slice), and the EFS contact and promise history read is RWB-P1-E2001-APP's. This story delivers what is left, on the two case-scoped operations the Ownership Map already gives this service:

- **the migration.** One version on this service's own Flyway sequence adds to `interaction`, in schema `rwb_source_data`, `contact_key varchar(255)`, `from_holder_ref varchar(60)`, `to_holder_ref varchar(60)`, `treatment_id uuid`, `proceeds_id uuid` and `retention_class varchar(20)`, and creates the index `ix_interaction_retention_class`. The keys, the append-only trigger and the indexes of RWB-P1-E1066-APP and RWB-P1-E1068-APP are kept unchanged.
- **`POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions`.** The append of one channel entry, extended with the six fields. A `CASE_ALLOCATED` or `CASE_TRANSFERRED` entry carries the holder before and after the move; a `CONTACT`, `LETTER`, `HANDOVER`, `PARTNER_RESULT`, `OFFER` or `PAYMENT` entry carries the contact key token and, where it has one, the treatment or the proceeds link **as a reference** and never the amount of another service's record. Every entry carries the retention class resolved from its event code.
- **`GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions`.** The case read, extended with the six fields and ordered by occurred time and then by case sequence, so that a late EFS row reads before the call that was saved earlier (legacy BR9).
- **`RetentionClassResolver`.** The class of an event code is reference data, read through the reference-data client library with the version in force; a code with no class row is refused and nothing is written. Every event code carries `ILG-STD` until Compliance sets the periods (legacy assumption, DL26), and that value is a fixture value, never a value in the code.

**It owns no legacy acceptance criterion.** Legacy RWB-E2-034 wrote eleven criteria and an access row, and each one tests a slice that is not this one: **AC1** and **AC4** (an interaction, a letter, an offer and a payment are recorded) with RWB-P2-E2034-APP; **AC2** (a hand-over) with RWB-P2-E2034-APP and the S9 slice; **AC3** (the ledger is one place) and **AC9**, **AC10** with RWB-P3-E2034-APP; **AC5** (nothing written twice) with RWB-P2-E2034-APP's consumer and the writer criterion of RWB-P1-E1066-APP; **AC6** with RWB-P2-E2034-APP and RWB-P1-E2001-APP; **AC7** and **AC8** with RWB-P2-E2034-APP; **AC11** with the P4 slice. The cross-service proof is **RWB-ITG-E2034-ITG**. This story is therefore written with six new criteria tagged D-RCV-60, and each one tests only the store, the two operations and the retention resolution.

**What it reads and what it does not.** The story reads two values through library clients and neither is a record of another service: the **event-code list LOV-LEDGER-EVENT** and the **retention class of an event code**, through the reference-data client library of DP-07; and the **Case record C or R answer** of the two operations, through the guard library of DP-08. It reads no case row, no notice, no partner, no instruction, no treatment, no proceeds and no ACE view: the case check is the writer's (RWB-P1-E1066-APP), the holder values and the two links arrive from the caller as references, and the contact point is a token. The shape the consumer fills is declared by **RWB-P2-E2034-CON**, whose fake this story builds against from Day 1.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contactability that is found and then lost again is the failure legacy RWB-E2-034 exists to remove. A case owner who picks up a case must see which number answered, who held the case last and which offer or payment the contact produced, without asking EFS, WIN or a partner. One append-only ledger per case holds all of it, and every one of those facts arrives from a different service: the owner of the store guarantees that the six values of an entry are stored once and read back unchanged, and the channels guarantee that the entry is the fact they themselves observed.

In the monolith the six columns were an internal addition to a local table and the retention class was a local table read, so nothing had to be agreed. In the target three things change at once. `interaction` is P1's own table in `rwb_source_data`, and the other eighteen services reach it only over this contract (DP-01, DP-18; Architecture v5 slide 4). The append and the read are REST operations with one hop and a 2 s budget, called by the integration consumer and by the screens through gateway-bff (DP-11, DP-13, DP-19; Architecture v5 slide 11). And the values in the six fields are **references to records of other owners**: a contact key of the ACE contact view, a user or partner reference of the holder, the identifier of a treatment of rwb-treatment and of a proceeds record of rwb-payment. A reference can be stored; another service's amount, name or address cannot be copied, because the copy is wrong the next morning and puts personal data in a second place.

The retention class is the second reason the store needs its own rule. Compliance sets a class per record type and a period per class (DL26), and every entry must carry its own class independently of the decision log (REQ-ILG-013). The class therefore cannot be a constant in the writer and cannot be guessed when the row is missing: it is data, it is read when the entry is appended, and a code with no class row is refused rather than defaulted, because a default files a record under a period nobody agreed to.

**What D-RCV-60 changes.** Not one legacy value. The case, the account, the contact key, the transfer time, the partner, the notice, the barcode, the treatment, the proceeds, the promise and the event ID keep their meaning and their spelling. What changes is where the fact is stored and who guarantees it: the six columns move onto this service's own migration sequence, the append and the case read become the two operations of one resource family, and the class becomes a reference-data read.

##### 3. Preconditions

Nothing in this list is a build dependency: the story is Day 1 and builds against the published baseline, the published operations of RWB-P1-E1066-APP and RWB-P1-E1068-APP, and the fake of RWB-P2-E2034-CON, which is why the build dependency list is empty (Template and Rules §R5.7).

- RWB-P1-E1001-APP has run: schema `rwb_source_data` holds the base `interaction` table and the dictionary rows of P1.
- RWB-P1-E1066-APP and RWB-P1-E1068-APP are done: the ledger columns, the case-sequence allocator, the unique keys, the append-only trigger `tr_interaction_append_only` and the indexes exist, and `POST` and `GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions` are published on base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`. Both are adopted as published artefacts of this service, not as build dependencies.
- RWB-P2-E2034-CON is published with its fake: the append command as the integration consumer fills it, the answer it expects, the repeated-key answer and the 2 s budget (C).
- The reference-data client library (DP-07) and the authorise guard library (DP-08) are on the classpath as platform artefacts, and the event-code list and the class rows are served through the former. Their contracts are not in this Work Package's list, so both are fixture reads until those contracts are published (GAP-2184; ASM-3546).
- The local decision-record library (DP-03) and the outbox, inbox and idempotency library (DP-09) are in place in `rwb_source_data`, so an append records its own decision record and a repeated key is answered from the stored response.
- The login and role of `rwb_source_data` exist in DEV and SIT, and the credential is held by the platform and never written in code, a test or a runbook (DP-02).
- The event codes that reach this store are the values of **LOV-LEDGER-EVENT**, with the two values the legacy story adds, `PARTNER_RESULT` and `OFFER` (GAP-2184; ASM-3543).
- The retention class list and the periods behind it are not published; until Compliance sets them every event code takes `ILG-STD` (GAP-2184; ASM-3543).
- The ownership of `interaction` is a plan ruling and not a source statement: the default ruling of R-PREC and DP-18 give the ledger to rwb-source-data (ASM-3542).

##### 4. Flow

1. The consumer of rwb-integration, or a recording screen of rwb-case through gateway-bff, calls `POST /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` with the entry body and an `Idempotency-Key` (DP-11, DP-13, DP-19).
2. `InteractionController` binds the body against the `InteractionRequest` schema of RWB-P1-E1066-APP extended by the six fields; a body that fails schema validation is refused with 400 and nothing is written.
3. `ChannelEntryValidator` checks the **event code** against **LOV-LEDGER-EVENT** read through the reference-data client library, so no code value stands in the code (DP-07).
4. `ChannelEntryValidator` checks the **holder pair**: a `CASE_ALLOCATED` or `CASE_TRANSFERRED` entry carries both `fromHolderRef` and `toHolderRef`, and any other event code carries neither. The values are the references the caller supplies (`USER:<user id>` or `PARTNER:<partner code>`) and are never resolved into a name.
5. `ChannelEntryValidator` checks the **link rule**: an `OFFER` entry carries `treatmentId`, a `PAYMENT` entry carries `proceedsId`, neither carries the amount of the record it refers to, and a `CONTACT`, `LETTER` or `HANDOVER` entry carries the contact key token and no link.
6. `RetentionClassResolver` reads the class of the event code against the version in force; the class is written on the entry, a code with no class row is refused, and a class supplied by the caller is refused.
7. The write service of RWB-P1-E1066-APP runs its own checks (the case exists, the occurred time, the actor and the source, the key), allocates the next case sequence inside one transaction on this service's table, and the unique key `(case_id, case_seq)` decides a race.
8. `InteractionRepository` inserts the entry with the six values beside the fields the writer already stores; no update and no delete method exists on it (BR7).
9. The transaction commits, the local decision-record library records the ledger event, and the controller answers **201** with the stored entry, read back through the case read of this story inside the same call (DP-03).
10. A repeat of the same `Idempotency-Key` with the same body answers the stored entry with the same case sequence and adds no row, and the hit count of the key becomes 2 (DP-09; R-UNI-40).
11. `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` answers the entries of the case with the six fields, filtered by channel, actor and date range and paged, ordered by occurred time and then by case sequence (BR9); the authorise answer of DP-08 decides the read.
12. A database failure rolls the transaction back and answers 503; the incident hook of RWB-P1-E1066-APP fires with the case ID and the error class and no personal data.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A required value of the entry is missing or malformed, or a link is carried on an event code that has none | 422; nothing written; the field is named | MSG-GEN-001 | AC1 |
| X2 | The event code has no retention class row | 422; nothing written; the class is never defaulted | MSG-GEN-001 | AC2 |
| X3 | The event code is not a value of LOV-LEDGER-EVENT | 422; nothing written; the field is named | MSG-GEN-001 | AC2 |
| X4 | A `CASE_ALLOCATED` or `CASE_TRANSFERRED` entry carries no holder before or no holder after | 422; nothing written | MSG-GEN-001 | AC3 |
| X5 | The same `Idempotency-Key` arrives with a different body | 409; the stored entry is not replaced and no second row is written | None | AC6 |
| X6 | The case does not exist, or is outside the caller's scope | 404; nothing written and nothing returned | MSG-P4-003 | AC1, AC6 |
| X7 | The caller holds no Case record C on the append or no R on the read | 403; nothing written and nothing returned | MSG-P4-002 | AC1, AC4 |
| X8 | The reference-data or authorise library does not answer inside 2 s, or answers an error | 503; nothing written, because a class that cannot be read is never guessed | MSG-GEN-006 | AC2 |
| X9 | The entry cannot be inserted | 503 with the rollback; the incident hook fires; nothing is discarded silently | MSG-P1-022 | Section 12.1 |

X1 to X4 are the validation paths the six fields add to the append of RWB-P1-E1066-APP. X5 and X6 are the writer's own paths, kept unchanged because this story extends the same operation. X7 is the access path of both operations, answered through the guard library of DP-08. X8 is the path that a class read across a boundary adds: in the monolith the class was a local table read that could not time out. X9 is the writer's failure path, carried unchanged.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the published table and operations of RWB-P1-E1066-APP and RWB-P1-E1068-APP and the RWB-P2-E2034-CON fake from Day 1; the reference-data and authorise reads are library reads with fixtures, so no other service has to exist |
| Negotiable | The order of the checks, the class split of the validator and the read-back call are the squad's choice behind the operations; the six columns, their types, the index, the keys and the trigger are fixed |
| Valuable | One store where the contact point, the holder change, the treatment or proceeds link and the retention class of an entry are held once and read back unchanged, in time order |
| Estimable | One migration, two extended operations, one validator, one resolver, one repository method, two library reads and one fixture set |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests, as the store slice of the legacy key |
| Testable | Every criterion in section 7 is one call, one refused call or one statement against the ledger fixture |
| Day 1 | No build dependency; the store, the operations and the fake are published artefacts, so the tests run on the first day of wave 2 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Interaction ledger on the case and from every channel

  Background:
    Given open case "RW-2026-000301" with account "ACC-SYN-0301" and owner "U-2001"
    Given the retention class list holds class "ILG-STD" for every event code
    Given the rwb-integration contract mock returns an accepted append for instruction "INS-SYN-0301" of case "RW-2026-000301" with partner "LF-SYN-01"

  Scenario: AC1 A channel entry stores its six values and the case read gives them back (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a CONTACT entry of 14 December 2026 10:15 with event code "CONTACT", channel CALL, result RIGHT_PARTY, promise 12,500.00 for 20 December 2026 and contact key "PHONE:CP-SYN-0301-M"
    Given a LETTER entry for notice "NT-SYN-0301" dispatched on 19 December 2026 with external reference "EV000000001TH"
    Given an OFFER entry linked to treatment "TRT-SYN-0301" and a PAYMENT entry linked to proceeds "PRC-SYN-0301" of 5,000.00
    When each entry is appended through POST /cases/{caseId}/interactions and the case is read through GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions
    Then each append answers 201 and the read returns the four entries with their contact key, holder references, treatment link, proceeds link and retention class "ILG-STD"
    Then the OFFER entry carries no offer amount and the PAYMENT entry no proceeds amount, so 5,000.00 stays in "PRC-SYN-0301" of rwb-payment
    Then no entry, answer or log holds a phone number, a postal address, a person name or an account number

  Scenario: AC2 The retention class comes from the event code and a code with no row writes nothing (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the retention class list holds class "ILG-STD" for event code "LETTER" and no row for event code "PARTNER_RESULT"
    When the caller appends a LETTER entry for notice "NT-SYN-0301" and then a PARTNER_RESULT entry
    Then the LETTER entry carries retention_class "ILG-STD"
    Then the PARTNER_RESULT append is refused with 422 and MSG-GEN-001 for "event code"
    Then the ledger holds no PARTNER_RESULT entry and the case stays at its last case sequence
    Then no class value stands in the code and the list is read through the reference-data client library

  Scenario: AC3 A move stores the holder before and after on the entry of the move (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RW-2026-000301" is transferred from "U-2001" to "U-2002" on 16 December 2026 11:00
    When the CASE_TRANSFERRED entry of 16 December 2026 11:00 is appended
    Then the entry carries event code "CASE_TRANSFERRED", from_holder_ref "USER:U-2001" and to_holder_ref "USER:U-2002"
    Then the entry carries no channel and no direction
    Then an entry of the same event code with no from_holder_ref is refused with 422 and MSG-GEN-001 for "from holder"
    Then the case read returns both holder references unchanged

  Scenario: AC4 The contact point is a token and never a number or an address (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case owner "U-2001" records a call on 15 December 2026 09:30 to contact key "PHONE:CP-SYN-0301-M" with result NO_ANSWER
    When the CONTACT entry is appended and the case is read
    Then the entry stores "PHONE:CP-SYN-0301-M" as contact_key and the read returns the same token
    Then the row, the 201 answer and the read hold no phone number, no postal address and no electronic mail address
    Then the contact value is resolved only from the owner of the ACE contact view when a screen displays it

  Scenario: AC5 A late entry reads in occurred-time order (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the ledger holds the Workbench call of 15 December 2026 09:30 at case sequence 1
    When the EFS entry with contact time 14 December 2026 10:15 and key "EFS:EFS-SYN-0301-01" is appended on 15 December 2026 10:00
    Then the EFS entry takes occurred_at 14 December 2026 10:15 and its own later case sequence
    Then GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions returns the EFS entry before the call
    Then two entries with the same occurred time read in case sequence order

  Scenario: AC6 A repeated append key writes one entry and the read returns one (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given event "EVT-SYN-0001" has been appended once as a LETTER entry for notice "NT-SYN-0301"
    When the same append is posted again with Idempotency-Key "EVT-SYN-0001" and the same body
    Then the ledger holds one entry for "EVT-SYN-0001" and the answer is the stored entry with the same case sequence
    Then the repeat count for that key is 2
    Then the case read returns one entry for the notice and the case sequence series has no gap and no repeat
```

**Target reading.** Every assertion above is new, because this story owns no legacy criterion; each one tests only the store, the two operations and the retention resolution. What the legacy story asserted of the channels is proved in the slice that owns it: the consumer and the mapping in RWB-P2-E2034-APP, the partner result in the S9 slice, the timeline in RWB-P3-E2034-APP, the scope and masking in the P4 slice, the EFS history in RWB-P1-E2001-APP, and the whole key against live contracts in RWB-ITG-E2034-ITG. The legacy values are kept: case `RW-2026-000301`, account `ACC-SYN-0301`, owner `U-2001` and `U-2002`, contact key `PHONE:CP-SYN-0301-M`, action code `PTP`, result `RIGHT_PARTY` and `NO_ANSWER`, promise 12,500.00 for 20 December 2026, notice `NT-SYN-0301`, barcode `EV000000001TH`, treatment `TRT-SYN-0301`, proceeds `PRC-SYN-0301` of 5,000.00, event ID `EVT-SYN-0001`, instruction `INS-SYN-0301`, partner `LF-SYN-01`, the transfer of 16 December 2026 11:00 and the class `ILG-STD`. The `Given` of the contract mock in the Background is the fake of the C dependency RWB-P2-E2034-CON, which is how the consumer's write arrives (DP-11). AC5 proves the legacy ordering rule of BR9 on this store: the entry keeps the occurred time it is given, the case sequence is allocated at insert, and the read sorts on the time and not on the sequence. AC6 proves the repeat of an append key on the store, because this story extends the body the key is stored with; the repeat of a redelivered *event* is legacy AC5 and is proved in RWB-P2-E2034-APP.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One ledger holds every interaction on a case, and this service owns the store and the shape of an entry | REQ-ILG-012; DP-18; R-PREC default ruling |
| BR2 | A hand-over between bank owners is the entry of the move, enriched with the holder before and after; the two references sit on that entry and carry no channel | REQ-ILG-011; legacy BR2 |
| BR3 | An offer or a payment is recorded as a reference to the treatment or the proceeds, never as its amount | legacy BR1, BR3; REQ-ILG-010 |
| BR4 | Every entry carries the retention class of its event code, set independently of the decision log; a code with no class row is refused | REQ-ILG-013; NFR-075; DL26; legacy BR6 |
| BR5 | The contact point is stored as a reference to the ACE contact key; the number or the address is never copied into the entry | REQ-ILG-014; CTL-11; legacy BR5 |
| BR6 | One entry per idempotency key; a repeat answers the stored entry and is counted | R-UNI-40; REQ-ILG-007; legacy BR7 |
| BR7 | Entries are append only; a correction is a new entry naming the original, with its own case sequence | legacy BR7; tr_interaction_append_only |
| BR8 | A ledger write that fails rolls back and raises an incident; no entry is discarded and no value is guessed | REQ-ILG-008; NFR-077; legacy BR8 |
| BR9 | The case read returns entries by occurred time and then by case sequence | REQ-ILG-006; legacy BR9 |

**Where each rule lives in the target.** BR1 is a schema rule as well: `interaction` exists once, in `rwb_source_data`, and the other eighteen services reach it only over this contract (DP-01, DP-18). BR2 is the holder pair of steps 4 and 8: two `varchar(60)` business references with no foreign key, supplied by the caller because rwb-case knows who holds the case and this service does not (DP-11). BR3 is the link rule of step 5: `treatment_id` and `proceeds_id` hold a reference and no amount of the linked record; the one amount the ledger itself keeps is the promise a contact produced, which is the interaction's own fact (legacy BR3). BR4 is `RetentionClassResolver`, and it is where the target changes the legacy mechanism: the class is not a local table read but a reference-data read with its version in force (DP-07), and a code with no row is refused rather than defaulted (X2, X8). BR5 is enforced twice: the request carries a key and the schema has no column for a number, an address or a name, so the copy is impossible rather than forbidden. BR6 keeps the legacy shape and moves the counter onto the platform library: the unique key on `idempotency_key` refuses the second insert and the stored response answers the repeat (DP-09; R-UNI-40). BR7 is the trigger kept unchanged plus the absence of any update or delete method on the repository. BR8 becomes 503 with MSG-P1-022 and the incident hook, with no discard. BR9 is the read order of the case read: `occurred_at`, then `case_seq`.

##### 9. State transitions

None in the business sense. This story changes no case status, and an entry has no status and is never changed. The only states it moves are the entry's existence and the schema version it lives on.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| a case at case sequence n | a valid append | The event code is in the list, its class resolves, the holder pair and the link rule hold | One entry exists at case sequence n+1 with its six values |
| a case at case sequence n | a refused append | A value is missing, the code has no class row, or the holder pair is incomplete | The case is still at case sequence n and no entry exists |
| a stored entry at case sequence n | a repeated `Idempotency-Key` with the same body | The stored response is the authority | One entry exists at case sequence n and the hit count of the key is 2 |
| a stored entry at case sequence n | a repeated `Idempotency-Key` with a different body | The key is already used with another body | No entry is written and the answer is 409 |
| a stored entry at case sequence n | an update or a delete statement | The append-only trigger is in place | The statement is refused and the entry keeps its six values |
| an applied migration version | a correction to the columns or the index | A fix is needed | A new Flyway version is merged; the applied version is never edited |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The consumer identity of rwb-integration, with a workload identity token | Appends channel entries through the append and reads the case ledger back with its six values (Case record C then R) |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Appends entries for case actions it records, with the holder references of a move |
| SY-DATALOAD, data load | Appends entries from the EFS history read of RWB-P1-E2001-APP under the stable key that read supplies |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Records a contact on own cases through the recording screens of rwb-case and gateway-bff, and reads the ledger of cases in scope (Case record C then R) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, RW-CONDUCT and other roles with Case record R | Read the ledger of cases in scope; they append nothing here |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads LOV-LEDGER-EVENT and the retention class rows with their versions (Reference data C) |
| RW-COMPLY, Compliance and PDPA officer | Sets the class and the period of a record type (Reference data U); DL26 is theirs and open |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Receives the write-failure incident of a refused insert and reads the append series of the deployment |
| rwb-case (P3) | Owns the case, the case record and the timeline; answers the case check the append takes (C RWB-P3-E1018-CON) |
| rwb-access (P4) | Owns the roles, the scope and the masking policy; answers the authorise question of both operations (DP-08) |
| No approval level from the delegation of authority applies | The story takes no business decision |

The operations run as the service identity of rwb-source-data (DP-02), and the caller's identity travels in the token, so the case check and the authorise answer are made for the caller and not for the service. The holder references, the contact key and the two links are references to records of other owners; this story resolves none of them into a name, a number, an address or an amount.

**Which side is this story's.** `DF-INT-022` to `DF-INT-027` are this story's: the migration adds the six columns, the append writes them and the case read returns them. `DF-INT-001` to `DF-INT-018` are the writer's and stay as RWB-P1-E1066-APP created them; this story adds no column beside the six and changes no key. `DF-INT-028` `delivery_status` and `DF-INT-029` `external_ref` are not this story's columns: they stay with the comms slices of this key, which write them through this append (ASM-3547). `DF-CAS-001` is rwb-case's key, answered by the contract and never joined locally (DP-01).

**Legacy read fields and their home in the target.**

| Legacy field | Entity | Home in the target |
|---|---|---|
| DF-ACE-075, DF-ACE-076, DF-ACE-077 | v_ace_contact | The contact-fact read of this service's contract, consumed by RWB-P2-E2034-APP; this story stores the token only |

| DF-CAS-009, DF-CAS-022, DF-CAS-025, DF-CAS-026, DF-ACE-002 | recovery_case, case_account, v_ace_account | The case contract of P3 and the EFS read of RWB-P1-E2001-APP; never a local read here |

| DF-PRT-002, DF-TRT-001, DF-FIN-001 | partner, treatment, proceeds | The rwb-partner, rwb-treatment and rwb-payment contracts, consumed by RWB-P2-E2034-APP; this store keeps the reference only |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. No row of another service's table is read, and no value of one is copied into an entry.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner rwb-source-data (P1); base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1` (DP-13). Two operations, both case-scoped, and both already published by RWB-P1-E1066-APP and RWB-P1-E1068-APP; this story extends them with the six fields and adds no operation and no resource. The case-scoped form is the one the Ownership Map lists and the one the consumer contract fakes, and the flat append row of RWB-P1-E1066-APP is realigned to it rather than published a second time here (GAP-2185; ASM-3542).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/interactions` | Appends one channel entry to a case with its contact key, its holder pair, its treatment or proceeds link and its retention class, and answers 201 with the stored entry | An authenticated caller with Case record C on the case: the consumer identity of rwb-integration, the identities of rwb-case, and the recording screens through gateway-bff (DP-08) | `Idempotency-Key` required; the same key with the same body answers the stored entry and the same case sequence; the same key with a different body is refused with 409 |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/interactions` | Reads the ledger of a case with the six values, filtered by `channel`, `actor`, `from` and `to` and paged, ordered by occurred time and then by case sequence | Case record R on the case, answered through the guard library (DP-08) | Read only; changes nothing |

The request body is the `InteractionRequest` of RWB-P1-E1066-APP extended with `contactKey`, `fromHolderRef`, `toHolderRef`, `treatmentId`, `proceedsId`; the response is `Interaction` and `InteractionPage` extended with the same six. `retentionClass` is answered by the service for every entry and is not accepted from the caller, because the class is data of the event code and never a value of the caller (ASM-3541). `treatmentId` and `proceedsId` hold the identifier of the treatment and of the proceeds record and carry no foreign key; the type of the two cross-service references is not stated in the source documents (GAP-2184; ASM-3541), and this story fixes them as the `uuid` columns the legacy migration gives them.

Errors are the RFC 9457 problem body: 400 for a body that fails schema validation, 401 without a session (MSG-P4-001), 403 without Case record C or R (MSG-P4-002), 404 for a case that does not exist or is outside the caller's scope (MSG-P4-003), 409 for an `Idempotency-Key` already used with a different body, 422 for a missing or invalid field, an event code outside the list or a code with no class row, with MSG-GEN-001 naming the field, and 503 when the entry cannot be written (MSG-P1-022) or a library does not answer inside 2 s (MSG-GEN-006). The order and the paging of the read are those of the read this story extends: occurred time, then case sequence, with the size and the maximum that read takes from the rwb-case parameters contract (ASM-3545). The status of an append whose event code has no class row is not stated in the source documents (GAP-2184; ASM-3541); this story fixes it as 422 and writes nothing, because a class that cannot be resolved is never defaulted.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. This story calls no operation of another service with a client of its own; its C dependency is the contract story of its own key, RWB-P2-E2034-CON, which declares the append as the integration consumer fills it and is faked for this story's tests.

Two values reach the story as library reads rather than as calls of its own, and both are named because the criteria of section 7 depend on them.

| Value | Owner | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| The event-code list LOV-LEDGER-EVENT and the retention class rows, with the version in force, read once per append and once per read | P3 rwb-case, reference data (DP-07) | Client library read; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON, whose contract is outside this Work Package's list, so a fixture until it is published (GAP-2184; ASM-3546) |
| The Case record C or R answer for the caller on the case | P4 rwb-access (DP-08) | Guard library read; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON, a fixture until published (ASM-3546) |

###### 12.3 Events published

None of its own. The topic of the service is `rwb.source-data.events.v1` with event names `rwb.source-data.<Event>.v1` (DP-14), and its two events `AceDataReady` and `AceDataLate` belong to RWB-P1-E1015-APP. The local decision-record library publishes `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the outbox when an entry is recorded (DP-03, DP-09); that is the library's event, and this story adds no message schema.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The consumer of the six channel events (`rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1`, `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1`, `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1`, `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1`, `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1`, `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1`) is P2's consumer `ledger-channels` on the owners' topics (RWB-P2-E2034-APP). This story subscribes to nothing: it is reached over REST and writes what it is given.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The append and the read are synchronous REST steps that write or read rows in one transaction; this story starts no workflow and no activity. The task queue of the service is `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and the workflows `AceIngestCheck` and `reconciliation` and the activities `listEligibleAccounts` and `snapshot(page)` belong to other P1 stories (DP-10).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Temporal Schedule and no Quartz job sits in this story: an entry is written when the caller appends it, and no part of this store is swept on a timer (DP-10).

| `interaction` | `rwb_source_data` | P1 rwb-source-data (DP-01, DP-18) | The ledger table: the migration adds the six columns and `ix_interaction_retention_class`, and keeps the unique keys, the append-only trigger `tr_interaction_append_only` and the indexes of RWB-P1-E1066-APP and RWB-P1-E1068-APP; the append writes and the case read reads, with no update and no delete method |
| `processed_event` | `rwb_source_data` | Platform library, created in this schema (DP-09) | The inbox, read and written by the library and not by this story |

| `outbox_event` | `rwb_source_data` | Platform library, created in this schema (DP-09) | The outbox the decision-record library writes through; this story adds no row of its own |

No table of another service is read and no foreign key crosses a schema (DP-01): `recovery_case` stays in `rwb_case`, `notice` in `rwb_comms`, `partner` in `rwb_partner`, `treatment` in `rwb_treatment` and `proceeds` in `rwb_payment`.

| Ledger fixture | `rwb_source_data` | A container at the baseline plus the migrations of RWB-P1-E1066-APP, RWB-P1-E1068-APP and this story, with the six columns, the keys, the trigger and the new index, so the append-only test and the repeat test run on the real constraints |

The four fakes are local: no live rwb-integration, rwb-case, rwb-access, rwb-treatment or rwb-payment is needed for the tests of section 16, and no production ledger row, contact value or personal data is copied into a fixture.
