##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata`, module `ledger`, with the published types in `...sourcedata.ledger.api`. Service base `/api/recovery/source-data/v1`, schema `rwb_source_data`, topic `rwb.source-data.events.v1` (not published here), task queue `rwb-source-data` in namespace `rwb-recovery` (not used here).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The platform contracts of the table are pulled by the baseline stories of this service (RWB-P1-E1066-APP, RWB-P1-E1068-APP), so the build dependency list of this story stays empty and the story is Day 1. DP-01 is the shape of the story: `interaction` is P1's own table and no other service reads it. DP-03 and DP-09 are statements with one consequence: the local library records the entry and publishes the decision record through the outbox, and the inbox and the stored response absorb a repeat; this story writes no rule, no version and no outbox row of its own. DP-05 is a statement: no ACE value is read here. DP-06 is a statement: the page size and its maximum are read as data by the case read of RWB-P1-E1068-APP and are not redefined here. DP-07 is the retention class and the event-code list, and DP-08 is the authorise answer of both operations; both are library reads with a fixture. DP-10 is a statement: no workflow, activity or Schedule. DP-11 and DP-13 are the two case-scoped operations on the service base. DP-15 is the migration. DP-18 is the ownership ruling. DP-19 is the edge route the responding screens arrive through.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `V<next>__rwb_e2_034_interaction_channel_columns.sql` (next version on the service sequence) | Migration | The six columns and `ix_interaction_retention_class` in `rwb_source_data`; keeps the keys, the trigger and the two existing indexes |
| `InteractionController` | Controller | The two operations of 12.1, extended with the six fields; RFC 9457 details; `Idempotency-Key` handling |
| `ChannelEntryValidator` | Service | The event code against LOV-LEDGER-EVENT, the holder pair, the link rule and the contact key form; MSG-GEN-001 naming the field |
| `RetentionClassResolver` | Service | The class of an event code from reference data; refuses a code with no row; never defaults |
| `InteractionLinkValidator` | Service | The treatment and proceeds rule: a reference on the event code that has one, no amount of the linked record, no foreign key |
| `InteractionRepository` | Repository | One insert with the six values and one paged read by case, ordered by occurred time then case sequence; no update and no delete method |
| `Interaction`, `InteractionRequest`, `InteractionPage` | Published types | The schemas of 12.1 extended with `contactKey`, `fromHolderRef`, `toHolderRef`, `treatmentId`, `proceedsId` and `retentionClass` |
| `ReferenceDataClient` | Client library use | LOV-LEDGER-EVENT and the class rows as data, with the version in force (DP-07) |
| `AuthoriseClient` | Guard library use | The Case record C and R answers of both operations (DP-08) |

**Migration and sequence (DP-15).** One version on this service's own Flyway sequence, after the writer's columns and after the actor index of RWB-P1-E1068-APP. It adds `contact_key varchar(255)`, `from_holder_ref varchar(60)`, `to_holder_ref varchar(60)`, `treatment_id uuid`, `proceeds_id uuid` and `retention_class varchar(20)` to `interaction` in `rwb_source_data`, creates `ix_interaction_retention_class`, and leaves `tr_interaction_append_only`, both unique keys and both existing indexes exactly as they are. A repeated run changes nothing; the version number is assigned by the sequence owner at build time; no monolith version number is reused and an applied version is never edited.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The class of an event code is reference data of rwb-case under DP-07, read through the client library; the list and the periods behind it are Compliance's under DL26, and until they are set every event code takes `ILG-STD`, the legacy assumption, which the fixture carries and the code does not (GAP-2184; ASM-3543).
- The list LOV-LEDGER-EVENT with its values and Thai labels is read through the same library; the two values `PARTNER_RESULT` and `OFFER` are the legacy additions and are carried on that read (ASM-3543).
- The holder reference form (`USER:<user id>` or `PARTNER:<partner code>`) and the contact key form (`<contact type>:<contact key>`) are the forms the legacy criteria use; the append validates the form and never resolves the reference into a name (ASM-3544).
- The 2 s budget and the breaker of the two library reads are client configuration (DP-11); a class read that does not answer inside 2 s refuses the append and writes nothing.
- The flag `rwb.source-data.ledger-channels` gates the two operations at deployment.

**Build steps**

1. The migration for the six columns and `ix_interaction_retention_class`, with a repeated run that changes nothing and the trigger, the keys and the two indexes untouched (DP-15).
2. The three published types extended with the six fields and published with the service baseline (C).
3. `ChannelEntryValidator`: the event code against LOV-LEDGER-EVENT, the holder pair, the link rule and the contact key form, each with MSG-GEN-001 naming the field and no insert on a refusal (AC1, AC3, AC4).
4. `RetentionClassResolver` against the reference-data client library and its fixture, called before the insert for every entry, with a code that has no row refused and a timeout refused (AC2, X2, X8).
5. `InteractionRepository`: the insert of the six values and the paged read of a case ordered by occurred time then case sequence, with no update and no delete method (AC1, AC5).
6. The 201 read-back through the case read, so the answer of an append is what was stored (AC1).
7. The repeat path through the platform library: the same key and body answers the stored entry with the same case sequence and the hit count 2, and the same key with a different body answers 409 (AC6, X5).
8. `AuthoriseClient` through the guard library: Case record C on the append and R on the read, refused with MSG-P4-002, plus the timeout path (X7).
9. An architecture test that no class outside the `ledger` module uses `InteractionRepository`, that the repository has no update and no delete method, and that no class of this story names a table of another service (DP-01).

**Feature flag.** `rwb.source-data.ledger-channels`. Off, both operations are refused at the edge of this service and no entry is written; the consumer of rwb-integration sees the refusal as an error, parks the delivery and retries, and the ledger is unchanged.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the six columns and the index are applied on the service sequence with the trigger and the keys still in place, an append answers 201 with the six values read back through the case read, an event code with no class row is refused with nothing written, a `CASE_TRANSFERRED` entry carries both holder references, a late entry reads in occurred-time order, a repeated `Idempotency-Key` answers one entry with a hit count of 2, and no entry of the fixture holds a number, an address, a name or another service's amount.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required value is missing or malformed, an event code is outside the list, its class has no row, a class is supplied by the caller, or a holder pair is incomplete | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-P1-022 | The entry could not be written | The entry was not saved because the interaction ledger could not be written. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-001 | No session on either operation | Your session has ended. Sign in again. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller holds no Case record C on the append or no R on the read | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is unknown or outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The reference-data or authorise library does not answer inside 2 s | The request could not be completed because {system} is not available. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P3-024 | The case has no ledger entry (the timeline's empty state, owned by RWB-P3-E2034-APP) | No interactions are recorded on this case yet. |

Thai text for each message follows decision DL10. MSG-GEN-001 names the field and is never filled with a data value; MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 and MSG-P3-024 are raised by the access, case and screen slices and are carried here unchanged; MSG-GEN-006 names the failed system and never a key value. No message carries a number, an address, a name or a case summary.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story and no route of its own. The case owner records a contact through the recording screens of rwb-case and reads the ledger in SCR-03 Case record and SCR-04 Case timeline, both of which arrive through the gateway-bff composite route and belong to the screen owners (DP-19; RWB-PLT-N001-CON); the timeline is RWB-P3-E2034-APP's. The states shown there - Loading, Empty with MSG-P3-024, and Error - belong to those screens. This story serves the store behind the recording screen and the case read, and on a refused append the caller sees MSG-GEN-001 or MSG-P1-022 in the Error state of the recording screen; this story renders none of it.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the event codes are list values of LOV-LEDGER-EVENT, the retention classes are reference rows, and the holder and contact key forms are validated formats and not codes (DP-07).
- No personal data in logs, tests, events or prompts: the six fields are references, the entry summary is the one personal field and is masked at the read by the policy of rwb-access, and a contact number, an address, a name and an account number are never read, logged or returned by this store (BR5).
- No read of another service's tables: the case is answered by the case contract, the authorise answer by the guard library, and the six fields hold references to records of rwb-case, rwb-comms, rwb-partner, rwb-treatment and rwb-payment reached over their contracts only (DP-01, DP-08, DP-11).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views: this story reads no ACE data; the contact key is a token the caller supplies (DP-05).
- No entry is ever updated or deleted by application code: the trigger refuses the statement, it keeps its behaviour unchanged on this story's migration, and the repository has no such method (BR7).
- The idempotency, inbox and outbox tables stay the library's: they are created in this schema and are never redefined here (DP-09).
- One login, one schema and one sequence: the release carries the `rwb_source_data` login, migrates `rwb_source_data` only, and an applied version is never edited (DP-02, DP-15).
- Both operations are one hop with a 2 s budget and a breaker per library; a class read that does not answer refuses the append and writes nothing (DP-11, X8).
- No screen is served here: the recording screens, the case record and the timeline arrive through the gateway-bff composite route and are the screen owners' (DP-19).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-034 for rwb-integration. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **the rwb-integration ledger intake worker deployed on task queue `rwb-integration` with its consumer groups on the four owner topics, the retry scan and the outbox relay, the EFS read trigger as an event-started workflow, the exception queue alert, the five dashboard series and the runbook entries**, so that **an operator can see a channel event that stopped moving, resend it, and prove that nothing was lost between a channel and the ledger without reading code**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story assumed a consumer named "ledger-channels" inside one module: the outbox, the consumer offset, the exception queue and the ledger were in one process, so a stuck delivery showed up as a failed row and an operator had the database in front of them. In the target the consumer is a deployment of its own. Its progress is a Kafka offset, its failures are delivery rows in `rwb_integration`, its writes go to another service, and its busiest hour is the morning run and the 16:00 letter window (Arch v5 slide 33). Without this story the app story can pass its unit tests while a consumer group is unassigned, a partition lags for a day, the exception queue grows silently and the EFS read step never runs — and the business measure, that a contact is visible on the case, falls with no alert.

Deployment is also where the split is enforced operationally. The release carries the rwb-integration login only, subscribes to the owners' topics only, and applies the `rwb_integration` migration only; it never touches the ledger schema, the case schema or an ACE view (DP-01, DP-02, DP-18). The observability follows ADR-023 per service: five series (consumer lag, deliveries in RETRYING, deliveries in EXCEPTION, append answers by class, EFS read summary counts), three alerts and three runbook entries, each alert carrying a message ID and one runbook entry.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The rwb-integration baseline chart and login are deployed by RWB-P2-E1007-APP, with the REST base `/api/recovery/integration/v1` and the relay of `rwb_integration` (DP-02, DP-13).
- The Kafka event platform provides the four owner topics with their retry and `.dlt` topics and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and the ACLs of this service's principals (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON).
- The Temporal workflow kit and the `rwb-recovery` namespace exist, with worker versioning, the build ID provider and the payload codec (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON).
- The platform error envelope and the message catalogue are in force, so an alert can carry a message ID.
- The three environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist and the production namespace exists for the release date; the flag `rwb.integration.ledger-channels` exists in the flag library.
- The gateway-bff composite route for SCR-09 is published (RWB-PLT-N001-CON, DP-19).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds the service image and the contract jar, runs the unit, component and contract tests, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes one chart version.
2. The chart deploys the API deployment, the ledger intake worker and the outbox relay with the rwb-integration login, the namespace `rwb-recovery`, the task queue `rwb-integration`, the payload codec and the build ID of the release.
3. The consumer group step creates the two groups of the deployment on the four owner topics, with the offset reset policy, the maximum poll and the `.dlt` routing, and records the starting offsets of each partition.
4. The flag step sets `rwb.integration.ledger-channels` from the values of the environment.
5. The migration step applies the `rwb_integration` sequence of this release and refuses to run when the target schema is not `rwb_integration`.
6. The trigger step confirms that the EFS read step is started by `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` and registers no Schedule for it.
7. The retry scan step starts the delivery retry scan on its interval and confirms the attempt limit of three.
8. The dashboards are published with the five series and the environment, release and build ID as dimensions.
9. The three alerts are wired to their message identifiers and to their runbook entries: MSG-P2-001 for the exception queue, and for the lag alert and the EFS trigger alert the identifier that the Error and Message Standard has yet to name, carried as Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0666; ASM-1175).
10. A smoke step publishes one synthetic `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` for a synthetic case in DEV, follows it to DELIVERED against the P1 fake, and then parks one delivery in EXCEPTION and resends it through the admin operation.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The chart render or the migration job fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic and no offset is committed | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A consumer group is assigned no partition, or a partition lags past its threshold | The lag series rises and the lag alert fires; the runbook entry names the check | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0666; ASM-1175) | AC2, AC5 |
| X3 | The flag is off in an environment | The worker is not deployed, the consumer groups hold no member, the relay is idle and the deliveries stay PENDING | None | AC1 |
| X4 | A delivery reaches its third failure | The delivery is EXCEPTION with the last error code and a task for RW-PLATADM; the exception alert fires | MSG-P2-001 | AC3 |
| X5 | AceDataReady arrives and the EFS read step does not start | The EFS trigger check fails the smoke run and the runbook entry names the event and the group | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0666; ASM-1175) | AC4 |
| X6 | A dashboard series is missing, or an alert carries no message ID or no runbook link | The observability check fails the release | None | AC5, AC6 |
| X7 | The P1 append is unavailable at release time | The deliveries accumulate in RETRYING, the append-answer series shows the 5xx class and the alert fires; nothing is lost and nothing is parked before the third attempt | MSG-P2-001 | AC3, AC5 |
| X8 | A new build is promoted while deliveries are in RETRYING | The workflow of each delivery replays on the new build from its history; the dashboards show both build IDs | None | AC1, AC5 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the workflow kit, the topic provisioning and the flag library; no application code is built here |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, lag thresholds, alert thresholds and scan intervals are environment values |
| Valuable | Makes the intake observable, resendable and provable on the morning run and the 16:00 window before the release date |
| Estimable | One chart, two consumer groups, one retry scan, one event trigger, five series, three alerts and three runbook entries |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the groups hold offsets, an alert fires on a synthetic metric, the trigger starts a workflow, the runbook is reviewed |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One login, one task queue and one schema per service: the release carries the rwb-integration login, polls `rwb-integration` only and migrates `rwb_integration` only | Arch v5 slide 41; DP-02; DP-15 |
| BR2 | The deployment subscribes to the owners' topics only, one group for the six business events and one for AceDataReady, and to no topic of this service | Arch v5 slides 42 and 43; DP-09; DP-14 |
| BR3 | The attempt limit is three and an exhausted delivery is EXCEPTION with a task for RW-PLATADM; no delivery is ever deleted | Legacy AC7 and AC8; BR6 of the app story |
| BR4 | The EFS read step is started by AceDataReady and owns no Schedule; the only periodic element is the relay and the retry scan, which are platform intervals | Legacy section 12; Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-02 and JOB-04 |
| BR5 | Every worker carries the build ID of its release and worker versioning is enabled, so a new build takes new workflows while the old build drains | Temporal and Drools design slide 11; RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| BR6 | Every alert carries a message ID and the agreed text and links one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR7 | No environment value is hard-coded: replicas, resources, lag thresholds, alert thresholds, scan intervals and the flag come from values files and parameters | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR8 | Dashboard series, alert payloads and the runbook carry counts, ids, codes, event types and build IDs only, never a contact point, an amount or a decoded payload | Temporal and Drools design slide 11 (PDPA); ADR-023 |
| BR9 | The release writes no ledger row and reads no ledger table: the append goes to the P1 contract and the migration touches `rwb_integration` only | DP-01; DP-18 |
| BR10 | A failing release never replaces a working one: the previous build stays in force until the new build passes its tests and its smoke run | DP-10 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the contract tests pass | Deploying |
| Deploying | Worker registered and probes healthy | The worker polls `rwb-integration` only and the two groups hold an assignment | Ready |
| Ready | Release superseded | A new chart version passes its tests | Rolling |
| Rolling | All workers on the new build | The old build drains its open workflows | Ready |
| Ready | Flag off | `rwb.integration.ledger-channels` is turned off in the environment | Not deployed |
| Ready | Smoke run failed | The trigger, the append or the resend step of the smoke run fails | Blocked |
| Blocked | Previous build restored | The smoke run passes on a later build, or the previous chart is redeployed | Ready |

The delivery states PENDING, RETRYING, DELIVERED and EXCEPTION are the app story's runtime and are not states of this deployment.

| Who | What they may do in this story |

| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the consumer group step, the dashboards and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the topic ACLs, the consumer quotas, the flag library and the exception queue resend |
| Platform event owner | Owns the four topics, their retry and `.dlt` topics, the schema registry and the `.dlt` retention |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact and may block it on a failing smoke run |
| On-call operator | Runs the three runbook entries and opens an incident when a lag or a parked delivery persists |
| RW-AUDIT | Reads the deliveries, the resend record and the run summaries |

The worker runs as the rwb-integration service identity (DP-02), carried by the chart as a secret reference and never as a literal name. The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0666; ASM-1175).

##### 11. Data

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Deployment values | Image digest, chart version, replica counts, resource requests and limits, probe paths and timings, log level, namespace, task queue, build ID, feature switch |
| Task queue | `rwb-integration` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, polled by the rwb-integration worker only |
| Consumer groups | The ledger intake group on `rwb.treatment.events.v1`, `rwb.comms.events.v1`, `rwb.partner.events.v1` and `rwb.payment.events.v1`; the EFS read group on `rwb.source-data.events.v1` |
| Topics | The five consumed topics with their retry and `.dlt` topics; `rwb.decision-record.v1` published by the local library; `rwb.integration.events.v1` untouched by this slice |
| Schema | `rwb_integration`, migrated by its own per-service Flyway sequence; this release applies the intake migration |
| Dashboard series | Consumer lag by group and partition, deliveries in RETRYING, deliveries in EXCEPTION, append answers by class, EFS read summary counts; dimensions environment, release, build ID |
| Runbook entries | Lagging consumer group, parked delivery, missing EFS run; each with the check, the owner role and the recovery step |
| Alerts | Three rules and one runbook entry each: MSG-P2-001 for the exception queue, and the identifier placeholder of GAP-0666 for the lag alert and the EFS trigger alert |
| Secrets | The rwb-integration login secret, the Kafka client credential and the Temporal mTLS material, all from the platform secret store |
| Test data | One synthetic `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` for case "RW-2026-000301", one synthetic AceDataReady for the EFS source and one synthetic delivery to park and resend; the fixture owner is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0666; ASM-1175) |

The deployment topology (cluster names, node pools, replica counts, resource sizes, zone spread, ingress class and the exact probe timings) belongs to each environment and is set by the platform team in its values file; the chart exposes every one of them as a value and this story fixes only their names and the rule that they are never hard-coded.

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only after the worker has polled `rwb-integration` once, the two consumer groups hold an assignment and the relay has read its first delivery; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database or commits an offset, and a failing dependency is reported as not ready, never as live-and-broken. The paths and timings are values of the environment.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None from this story. The two admin operations of the slice — `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbox/deliveries` and `POST /api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbox/deliveries/{deliveryId}/resend` — are declared by RWB-P2-E2034-CON and implemented by RWB-P2-E2034-APP; this deployment exposes them through the chart and its ingress and declares no path of its own. The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None from the deployment. The worker calls the P1 append and the fact contracts at run time as the app story's client; the chart carries no REST client of its own, no composite route and no outbound call at start-up beyond the Temporal frontend and the Kafka brokers.

###### 12.3 Events published

None of its own. `rwb.integration.events.v1` carries FileDelivered and FileFailed from the outbound file side and this slice publishes neither; `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` is published by the local decision-record library through the relay when a resend or an exception is recorded (DP-03, DP-09).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event type | Topic | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|
| `rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1` | `rwb.treatment.events.v1` | Ledger intake group, with the inbox, the retry topic and the `.dlt` routing |
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | Same group |
| `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` | `rwb.comms.events.v1` | Same group |
| `rwb.partner.InstructionIssued.v1` | `rwb.partner.events.v1` | Same group |
| `rwb.partner.PartnerResultSubmitted.v1` | `rwb.partner.events.v1` | Same group |
| `rwb.payment.ProceedsMatched.v1` | `rwb.payment.events.v1` | Same group |
| `rwb.source-data.AceDataReady.v1` | `rwb.source-data.events.v1` | EFS read group, starting EfsLedgerReadWorkflow; not an outbox delivery |

The five topics, their retry and `.dlt` topics and the seven types are provisioned and owned by the platform event epic and by the owners' contracts; this deployment configures the two consumer groups, the inbox, the offsets and the relay that turns a delivery into a workflow start.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|---|
| LedgerChannelIntakeWorkflow | Workflow, one execution per consumed event, workflow ID = the CloudEvents id | `rwb-integration` | Registered by the worker of this release, with the build ID and worker versioning |
| EfsLedgerReadWorkflow | Workflow, started by AceDataReady for the EFS source | `rwb-integration` | Registered by the same worker; no Schedule |
| mapChannelEvent, resolveChannelFacts, appendLedgerEntry, parkDeliveryInException | Activities | `rwb-integration` | Registered by the same worker with the kit's retry policy of 1 s, back-off 2, 3 attempts |
| readEfsOutcomes, appendEfsEntries, writeEfsReadSummary | Activities | `rwb-integration` | Registered with the same policy; idempotent by the event key and the EFS key |
| LedgerChannelListener and the delivery retry scan | Outbox consumer and scan | not a worker | Deployed in the same release; start the workflow per event and move a delivery on its next attempt |

**Build ID and versioning.** The build ID is the one supplied by the workflow kit for the release commit; worker versioning is enabled and a new build takes new workflows while the old build drains. The build ID format and the versioning policy are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0666; ASM-1176).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The deployment registers no Schedule: the intake is event-started from the seven consumed types and the EFS read step is started by AceDataReady. The relay and the retry scan run on platform intervals of the outbox library, not on a Schedule of this service (BR4).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|
| outbound_item | P2 (rwb_integration) | Read by the exception queue screen only; the release adds no column |
| outbox_delivery | PLT library, created in rwb_integration | The delivery trail, its attempt count and its task; read by the retry scan |
| processed_event | PLT library, created in rwb_integration | The inbox; read and written by the listener |
| idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_integration | The stored response of the two admin operations |
| decision_record | PLT library, created in rwb_integration | The record of a resend and of an exception, published by the library |

The release applies the intake migration of the app story and no other: no ledger table, no EFS reference table and no case table is created, altered or read (DP-01, DP-15, DP-18).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. No fake is deployed. The workflow tests run on the platform's test environment in the pipeline and the contract mocks of the P1 append and of the five fact contracts are in-process test doubles of the app story. The smoke run of DEV calls the P1 fake of the service environment, never a fake shipped by this release.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 0 consumed by the deployment | The two admin operations are the app story's; the probes are cluster-internal |
| Kafka | 0 published, 7 types consumed through 2 groups | Four owner topics with the intake group, `rwb.source-data.events.v1` with the EFS read group; retry and `.dlt` on every one |
| Temporal | 2 workflows, 7 activities, 0 Schedules | Worker on `rwb-integration` with a pinned build ID and worker versioning |
| File | None | No file is read or written by the deployment |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | The release migrates `rwb_integration` only and reads no other schema | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | The local record library is deployed with the relay and publishes to `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | No ACE read in this release; the EFS rows come through the P1 contract at run time | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | The rwb-case parameters contract is a run-time dependency of the worker, with its client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | The rwb-case reference-data contract is a run-time dependency of the worker | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | The rwb-access authorise contract is a run-time dependency of the two admin operations | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | The two consumer groups with the inbox, the retry topic and the `.dlt` topic; the relay on its one-minute interval | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | The worker, the task queue and the namespace come from the workflow kit; no Schedule is registered | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | The release declares no REST path and no client of its own; the worker calls the contracts as the app story's client | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | The ingress serves `/api/recovery/integration/v1` and no other base | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | The per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_integration`; the migration step refuses another schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | No ledger object is deployed, migrated or read; the append goes to rwb-source-data | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff serves SCR-09; the deployment registers the route and no screen of its own | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-integration/` overlay | API deployment, ledger intake worker, outbox relay, retry scan, config map, secret references, probes, task queue, namespace, build ID and flag |
| `helm/rwb-integration/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, flag value, build ID, consumer group names, intervals (ASM-1175) |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit and contract tests, image and dependency scan, chart publish, migration step, smoke run, promotion |
| Consumer group step | The two groups on the five topics, with the offset reset policy, the maximum poll, the retry and `.dlt` routing and the starting offsets |
| Migration step | The `rwb_integration` migration of this release; a target schema other than `rwb_integration` is refused |
| Trigger step | Confirms the EFS read step starts from AceDataReady and registers no Schedule |
| Dashboards | The five series of section 11 with the three dimensions |
| Alerts | Three rules, each with a message identifier or its placeholder and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Three entries: lagging consumer group, parked delivery, missing EFS run |

**Alert mapping**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P2-001 | A delivery is in EXCEPTION, or the P1 append is failing | Exception queue alert naming the consumer, the event type and the build ID, with the count and the oldest attempt time | Platform on-call, page |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0666; ASM-1175) | Consumer lag of either group is past its threshold | Lag alert naming the group, the topic, the partition and the lag | Platform on-call, page in the morning run and the 16:00 window, else ticket |
| Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0666; ASM-1175) | AceDataReady was consumed and no EfsLedgerReadWorkflow started | EFS trigger alert naming the business date, the source and the group | Platform on-call and the business on-call, ticket |

**Retry and offsets.** The retry scan reads `outbox_delivery` where the status is PENDING or RETRYING and the next attempt is due, and moves the delivery on the interval of the environment; the attempt limit is three (BR3). Offsets are committed after the inbox row is marked, so a crash replays the append and the P1 writer returns the same entry — the at-least-once rule of DP-09 with the dedupe of the app story. The interval values and the lag thresholds are environment values (ASM-1175).

**Rollback.** A release that fails the smoke run is not promoted. A release already promoted is rolled back by redeploying the previous chart version with its own build ID, which keeps the old build serving its open workflows until they finish; the deliveries in RETRYING are replayed from their history and the inbox makes the replay harmless. No data repair is needed, because the intake writes no ledger row of its own.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.integration.ledger-channels`. On: the worker and the two groups are deployed, the intake and the EFS read step run. Off: no worker and no group member, the relay is idle, and deliveries stay PENDING without being dated or parked.

**Done when.** The chart renders for DEV, SIT and UAT with a pinned digest and the build ID, the two groups hold their assignments and report offsets, the migration step refuses a foreign schema, the smoke run follows one notice to DELIVERED and one delivery to EXCEPTION and back through the resend, the five series and the three alerts are published with their identifiers or placeholders and their runbook links, and the three runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P2-001 | A delivery is in the exception queue, or the P1 append is failing | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0666; ASM-1175) |
| Identifier pending | Consumer lag of one group is past its threshold | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0666; ASM-1175) |
| Identifier pending | AceDataReady was consumed and no EFS read run started | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0666; ASM-1175) |
| MSG-GEN-005 | A resend is accepted in the smoke run | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0666; ASM-1175) |

MSG-P2-001 and MSG-GEN-005 are named by the FSD and by the legacy exception flows, and their texts are not in the source set. The lag alert and the EFS trigger alert have no message identifier in the source set at all, so their identifier and their text are carried as the placeholder until the Error and Message Standard names both. An alert payload names counts, event types, group names, business dates and the build ID only, never a case identifier, a contact point or an amount.

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment has no screen of its own. Its operator-facing surfaces are the pipeline run view, the release view, the dashboard, SCR-09 Exception queue through gateway-bff, and the runbook. SCR-09 is served by the app story and the composite route of RWB-PLT-N001-CON; the deployment only registers the route. The Temporal Web UI stays behind Entra ID: RW-PLATADM operates and RW-AUDIT reads, and payloads are decoded only through the codec server under break-glass. SCR-44 Interface and job monitor is not used for the intake, because the deployment registers no job of its own and the relay is a platform interval.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the event codes, the channels, the attempt limit and the case states are reference data and application behaviour, never a deployment value.
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads, the runbook or the workflow history: counts, ids, codes, event types, business dates and build IDs only, and payloads stay encrypted.
- One login per service, one task queue per service and one schema per service: the release carries the rwb-integration login, polls `rwb-integration` and migrates `rwb_integration` only (DP-02, DP-15).
- The release deploys no ledger object and reads no ledger table; the append goes to the rwb-source-data contract (DP-01, DP-18).
- The two consumer groups subscribe to the five owner topics only and have a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic before they start (DP-09).
- No delivery is ever deleted: an exhausted delivery is EXCEPTION with a task, and a resend sets PENDING with attempt count 0 (BR3).
- The release pins the image digest, the chart version and the build ID; a rebuild between environments is not allowed, and a failing smoke run never replaces a working build.
- No secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; all secrets come from the platform secret store.

- The real cross-service proof of the append, the dedup and the exception rule against the live owners (the integration story of this key).
- The exact cluster topology, node pools, replica counts, lag thresholds and probe timings; they are set per environment by the platform team.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-034 for the wave 2 integration harness. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **member of the integration and QA team**, I want **a repeatable cross-service harness that drives the interaction ledger from the case, from the EFS history ACE holds and from the partner portal through gateway-bff, rwb-source-data, rwb-integration, rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-partner and writes one evidence report per run**, so that **a contact, a letter, a delivery, an offer, a payment and a hand-over are proved to land in one ledger, to be read as one ordered timeline, to be written once, and to be refused or excluded as the legacy story defined — across services, on Day 1 and on every release after**.

This story is the wave 2 integration harness for the legacy key. It builds no production screen, endpoint, table, workflow or schedule and it owns no table. The ledger itself, the channel listener, the mapper, the EFS read step and the timeline are owned by the app stories of this legacy key: RWB-P1-E2034-APP (the ledger store and the ledger read), RWB-P2-E2034-APP (the channel listener, the mapper and the EFS intake rule), RWB-P3-E2034-APP (the timeline on the case record), RWB-P4-E2034-APP (the rights and scope check) and RWB-S9-E2034-APP (the partner result). The harness builds the runner, the fakes, the seeds and the evidence, and it owns the ten acceptance criteria listed in section 7. The criteria of AC8 stay with RWB-P2-E2034-APP.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contact outcomes from collections, letters sent through WIN and work held by partners are recorded in different systems today, so a case owner who picks up a case does not know which number answered or who held the case last. The legacy story brought each of these into the one ledger built in Epic 1, read the EFS history from the ACE views instead of a Workbench load, added who held the case before and after each hand-over, gave each entry a retention class and showed the ledger as an ordered timeline on the case. In the target architecture that one journey is served by five services: rwb-source-data owns the ledger and reads ACE; rwb-integration owns the channel listener and the intake rule; rwb-case owns the case facts and the timeline; rwb-access answers the rights and scope check; rwb-partner holds the hand-over and the partner result. A defect at any seam — an event mapped to the wrong event code, an EFS row outside the outcome list, a duplicated delivery, a retention class taken from the decision log, a refusal that returns data — would only appear with a live case, unless the journey is exercised across the services as one flow.

This story is that exercise. It runs the ledger journey from gateway-bff through the fakes and then through the real services as their app stories land, reproduces every exclusion and refusal the legacy story defined in the same run, and attaches one evidence report per run keyed by story and business date, so the ledger can be shown to hold before the wave is accepted and after every change. It meets REQ-ILG-006, REQ-ILG-007, REQ-ILG-008, REQ-ILG-009, REQ-ILG-010, REQ-ILG-011, REQ-ILG-012, REQ-ILG-013 and REQ-ILG-014 at the integration level, and it leaves every business rule, every screen behaviour and every table with the owning stories.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The nine I stories are published and deployed in the SIT environment as they land: RWB-P1-E2034-APP (the ledger store, the append and the ledger read), RWB-P1-E1066-APP (the ledger writer and its command), RWB-P1-E1067-APP (the Workbench events and the holder fields), RWB-P1-E1069-APP (the read-only ACE view contract), RWB-P2-E2034-APP (the channel listener, the mapper and the EFS intake rule), RWB-P3-E2034-APP (the timeline and the case-record section), RWB-P3-E2016-APP (the case record and its facts), RWB-P4-E2034-APP (the rights and scope check) and RWB-S9-E2034-APP (the partner result).
- gateway-bff is deployed with the composite case-record route of DP-19 available, so the ledger section is read as one gateway answer and not by the browser calling each service. The composite route path and its merge order, the harness environment, its seeding and its evidence format and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0416; ASM-0591).
- The contract fakes of §12.8 are published from the owning services' OpenAPI documents, so the harness runs green from Day 1 before any I story lands.
- The synthetic seeds of the legacy story exist: open case "RW-2026-000301" with account "ACC-SYN-0301" and owner "U-2001"; the EFS ledger outcome list holds action code "PTP" with channel CALL; the retention class for every event code is "ILG-STD"; the EFS batch for business date 14 December 2026 holds an action row for "ACC-SYN-0301" with action code "PTP", call result RIGHT_PARTY, contact time 14 December 2026 10:15, promise amount 12,500.00 and promise date 20 December 2026.
- The reference rows and parameters the journey reads are loaded by their owners through their contracts: LOV-LEDGER-EVENT with PARTNER_RESULT and OFFER, LOV-CHANNEL, LOV-DIRECTION, LOV-SOURCE, the EFS ledger outcome list and the retention classes; the harness holds no copy of any of them.
- The partner "LF-SYN-01", the notice "NT-SYN-0301" with barcode "EV000000001TH", the treatment "TRT-SYN-0301" and the proceeds "PRC-SYN-0301" of 5,000.00 are seeded through the S9, P6, S2 and P8 contracts or their fakes, and the case "RW-2026-000302" with no ledger entry and the case of team "MTG-BKK" owned by "U-2002" exist for the empty and out-of-scope cases.
- Feature `rwb.integration.ledger-channels` is on in the harness environment, so the listener and the EFS read step write; the harness reads the flag through the platform library and asserts the off state does not write.
- No build dependency: the harness starts on Day 1 against the fakes, and each fake is replaced by the real service as its I story lands.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: starts a run for the story and the business date, takes the run lock, and records the build under test, the pack version and the fake or real mode of each of the owning services it touches.
2. Harness: seeds the run through the contract of each owning service, or through the fake in fake mode — the case "RW-2026-000301" with "ACC-SYN-0301" and owner "U-2001", the reference rows of the outcome list and the retention classes, the EFS batch rows of 14 December 2026, the partner "LF-SYN-01", the notice "NT-SYN-0301", the treatment "TRT-SYN-0301" and the proceeds "PRC-SYN-0301".
3. Harness: asserts the business date is ready through `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness` and drives the Workbench call of 15 December 2026 09:30 to contact key "PHONE:CP-SYN-0301-M" with result NO_ANSWER through the append on the ledger, then reads the ledger through `GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/cases/{caseId}/interactions` and asserts the two CONTACT entries of AC1 with their source, channel, occurred time, result, promise amount and date, and retention class "ILG-STD".
4. Harness: drives the transfer of "RW-2026-000301" from "U-2001" to "U-2002" on 16 December 2026 11:00 and the instruction "INS-SYN-0301" issued to "LF-SYN-01" on 17 December 2026 14:00, then asserts the holder before and after on the CASE_TRANSFERRED entry and the HANDOVER entry with channel PORTAL and direction OUTBOUND.
5. Harness: enters the partner result of "LF-SYN-01" in the partner portal on 18 December 2026 16:00 through the S9 contract and asserts the three entries in the order 14, 15 and 18 December 2026, each naming its source.
6. Harness: drives the four notice, treatment and payment events of 19 to 24 December 2026 through their owning contracts and asserts the LETTER entries with delivery status SENT and external reference "EV000000001TH" and DELIVERED on 22 December 2026, the OFFER entry linked to "TRT-SYN-0301" and the PAYMENT entry linked to "PRC-SYN-0301".
7. Harness: replays the event NoticeDispatched with event ID "EVT-SYN-0001" into the channel listener and asserts one entry for "EVT-SYN-0001" and a hit count of 2 for that key.
8. Harness: seeds the three EFS rows of 14 December 2026 — "PTP" for "ACC-SYN-0301", "SYS" not in the outcome list and "PTP" for "ACC-SYN-0999" on no open case — and asserts one new EFS entry and the read summary of 3 read, 1 written, 1 excluded by the outcome list and 1 not on a case.
9. Harness: makes the ledger store unavailable through the fake, delivers NoticeDispatched for "NT-SYN-0301", asserts no entry, the delivery in RETRYING and the incident, then returns the store and asserts one LETTER entry for "NT-SYN-0301" after the retry.
10. Harness: replays the late EFS row of contact time 14 December 2026 10:15 after the Workbench call and asserts the timeline order, opens the timeline of "RW-2026-000302" with no entry and asserts MSG-P3-024, and reads the ledger of the case owned by "U-2002" in team "MTG-BKK" as "U-3001" of team "HP-NE" with Own scope and asserts 404 with MSG-P4-003.
11. Harness: drives the exception of AC8 inside the same run — an InstructionIssued naming an instruction whose case does not exist, retried three times — and records it as cited, not as a criterion of this story.
12. Harness: publishes the evidence report keyed by story id and business date with one row per criterion, the seam each row exercised, the service or fake that answered, the entry or summary observed and the pass or fail result; the evidence format and its retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0416; ASM-0591).
13. Harness: releases the run lock and, on any failed criterion, fails the run and names the criterion, the seam and the observed value.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What the harness asserts | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The same event arrives twice with the same key | One entry exists; the repeat is counted as a hit | None | AC5 |
| X2 | An EFS row has an action code that is not in the outcome list | No entry; counted as excluded in the read summary | None | AC6 |
| X3 | An EFS row is for an account on no open case | No entry; counted as not on a case | None | AC6 |
| X4 | The ledger store cannot be written | No entry; the delivery stays RETRYING; an incident is raised; the retry writes one entry | None | AC7 |
| X5 | An event names a case that does not exist | No entry; after the retry limit the delivery is in the exception queue with a task for role RW-PLATADM | None | AC8 |
| X6 | An EFS row arrives after a later Workbench entry for the same case | The entry takes its own occurred time; the timeline orders by occurred time | None | AC9 |
| X7 | The case has no entry yet | Empty state on the timeline | MSG-P3-024 | AC10 |
| X8 | The reader's role does not hold Case record R | Refused; no entry returned | MSG-P4-002 | AC11; TC-E2-034-12-ITG |
| X9 | The case is outside the reader's scope | Refused with 404; no entry returned | MSG-P4-003 | AC11 |

X5 is driven inside the same run but AC8 is owned by RWB-P2-E2034-APP; the harness asserts the same seam and does not claim the criterion.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs on its own once the nine I stories are deployed; until then it runs against the §12.8 fakes, with no work order inside another team's lane |
| Negotiable | The seeds, the fakes and the assertions are configuration and data; the criteria are the legacy ones |
| Valuable | The ledger is proved to be one place across five services and the EFS history, with the exclusions and refusals the business asked for |
| Estimable | One runner, one fake pack, one seed set, one evidence publisher and one gate |
| Small | Fits in one iteration with the owning stories' contract tests |
| Testable | Each of the twelve `-ITG` test cases of section 16 is one run of the harness and one row of the evidence report |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Interaction ledger on the case and from every channel

  Background:
    Given open case "RW-2026-000301" with account "ACC-SYN-0301" and owner "U-2001"
    Given the EFS ledger outcome list holds action code "PTP" with channel CALL
    Given the retention class for every event code is "ILG-STD"

  Scenario: AC1 An interaction is recorded (legacy RWB-E2-034 AC1)
    Given the ACE batch for EFS with business date 14 December 2026 holds an action row for account "ACC-SYN-0301" with action code "PTP", call result RIGHT_PARTY, contact time 14 December 2026 10:15, promise amount 12,500.00 and promise date 20 December 2026
    Given case owner "U-2001" records a call on 15 December 2026 09:30 to contact key "PHONE:CP-SYN-0301-M" with result NO_ANSWER
    When the EFS batch is complete and the call is saved
    Then the ledger holds a CONTACT entry with source EFS, channel CALL, occurred 14 December 2026 10:15, result RIGHT_PARTY, promise 12,500.00 for 20 December 2026 and retention class "ILG-STD"
    Then the ledger holds a CONTACT entry with source WORKBENCH, channel CALL, occurred 15 December 2026 09:30, contact key "PHONE:CP-SYN-0301-M" and result NO_ANSWER

  Scenario: AC2 A hand-over is recorded (legacy RWB-E2-034 AC2)
    Given case "RW-2026-000301" is transferred from "U-2001" to "U-2002" on 16 December 2026 11:00
    Given instruction "INS-SYN-0301" is issued to partner "LF-SYN-01" on 17 December 2026 14:00
    When both moves complete
    Then the CASE_TRANSFERRED entry of 16 December 2026 11:00 holds from "USER:U-2001" and to "USER:U-2002"
    Then the ledger holds a HANDOVER entry with channel PORTAL, direction OUTBOUND, from "USER:U-2002", to "PARTNER:LF-SYN-01", occurred 17 December 2026 14:00

  Scenario: AC3 The ledger is one place (legacy RWB-E2-034 AC3)
    Given the EFS entry of 14 December 2026, the Workbench call of 15 December 2026 and a partner result from "LF-SYN-01" entered in the partner portal on 18 December 2026 16:00
    When the case is read
    Then GET /cases/{caseId}/interactions returns the 3 entries in the order 14, 15 and 18 December 2026
    Then each entry names its source: EFS, WORKBENCH, and WORKBENCH with channel PORTAL and event code PARTNER_RESULT

  Scenario: AC4 Letter, delivery, offer and payment are recorded (legacy RWB-E2-034 AC4)
    Given notice "NT-SYN-0301" is dispatched on 19 December 2026 with barcode "EV000000001TH"
    Given WIN returns delivered for it on 22 December 2026
    Given treatment "TRT-SYN-0301" is approved on 23 December 2026
    Given proceeds "PRC-SYN-0301" of 5,000.00 are matched to the case on 24 December 2026
    When the four events are processed
    Then the ledger holds a LETTER entry with delivery status SENT and external reference "EV000000001TH"
    Then a LETTER entry with delivery status DELIVERED on 22 December 2026
    Then an OFFER entry linked to "TRT-SYN-0301" and a PAYMENT entry linked to "PRC-SYN-0301"

  Scenario: AC5 Nothing is written twice (legacy RWB-E2-034 AC5)
    Given event NoticeDispatched with event ID "EVT-SYN-0001" has been processed by "ledger-channels"
    When the same event is delivered again
    Then the ledger holds one entry for "EVT-SYN-0001"
    Then the hit count for that key becomes 2

  Scenario: AC6 EFS rows outside the list or outside a case are not written (legacy RWB-E2-034 AC6)
    Given the EFS rows for 14 December 2026 hold 3 rows: action code "PTP" for "ACC-SYN-0301", action code "SYS" not in the outcome list for "ACC-SYN-0301", and action code "PTP" for account "ACC-SYN-0999" on no open case
    When the EFS batch is complete
    Then the ledger holds 1 new EFS entry
    Then the read summary shows 3 read, 1 written, 1 excluded by the outcome list and 1 not on a case

  Scenario: AC7 A ledger write failure loses nothing (legacy RWB-E2-034 AC7)
    Given the ledger store is unavailable
    When event NoticeDispatched for "NT-SYN-0301" is delivered
    Then the system writes no entry and the delivery stays in the outbox with status RETRYING
    Then an incident is raised
    Then when the store is available the retry delivers the event and the ledger holds one LETTER entry for "NT-SYN-0301"

  Scenario: AC9 A late EFS row reads in time order (legacy RWB-E2-034 AC9)
    Given the ledger holds the Workbench call of 15 December 2026 09:30
    When the EFS row with contact time 14 December 2026 10:15 is processed on 15 December 2026 at 10:00
    Then the timeline shows the EFS entry before the call

  Scenario: AC10 A case with no entry (legacy RWB-E2-034 AC10)
    Given open case "RW-2026-000302" with no ledger entry
    When the case owner opens the timeline
    Then the timeline shows the empty state with message MSG-P3-024

  Scenario: AC11 A case outside the reader's scope is refused (legacy RWB-E2-034 AC11)
    Given case "RW-2026-000301" is owned by "U-2002" in team "MTG-BKK"
    When case owner "U-3001" of team "HP-NE" with Own scope reads its ledger
    Then the response is 404 with message MSG-P4-003
```

AC1 to AC7 and AC9 to AC11 are the legacy criteria owned by this story and are copied word for word from RWB-E2-034 with the origin tag on the scenario line. AC8 stays with RWB-P2-E2034-APP and is not restated.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Event to ledger event code: InstructionIssued to HANDOVER; PartnerResultSubmitted to PARTNER_RESULT; NoticeDispatched and NoticeDelivered to LETTER; TreatmentApproved to OFFER; ProceedsMatched to PAYMENT; an EFS action row to CONTACT | events.txt EV-10, EV-14, EV-15, EV-20, EV-21, EV-25, EV-26; LOV-LEDGER-EVENT |
| BR2 | A hand-over between bank owners is the CASE_ALLOCATED or CASE_TRANSFERRED entry of RWB-E1-067, with no channel, enriched with the holder before and after; a hand-over to a partner has channel PORTAL and direction OUTBOUND; a partner result has channel PORTAL and direction INBOUND | REQ-ILG-011; LOV-CHANNEL; LOV-DIRECTION |
| BR3 | An EFS row enters the ledger only when its action code is in efs_ledger_outcome, and only for an account linked to an open case | DL29; INT-07 |
| BR4 | Entries from EFS carry source_system EFS; every other entry carries WORKBENCH, including partner portal entries, which are entered on Workbench screens | LOV-SOURCE; INT-24 |
| BR5 | The contact point is stored as a reference to v_ace_contact.contact_key; the number or address is never copied into the entry | REQ-ILG-014; CTL-11 |
| BR6 | Each entry carries the retention class of its event code from the Retention classes reference table, set independently of the decision log | REQ-ILG-013; NFR-075; DL26 |
| BR7 | One entry per idempotency key; a repeat is ignored and counted | R-UNI-40; REQ-ILG-007 |
| BR8 | A failed ledger write raises an incident and the delivery is retried; no entry is discarded | REQ-ILG-008; NFR-077 |
| BR9 | The timeline orders entries by occurred time, then by case sequence | REQ-ILG-006 |

The harness asserts these nine rules against the owning services and the published contracts; it does not re-implement them, and no BR row is changed by this story.

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status and no case state; it reads and drives records only, and the harness adds no transition of its own. The facts below are caused by the owning services and are observed and asserted by the harness.

| Observed fact | Caused by | Asserted as |
|---|---|---|
| EFS contact row written to the ledger | rwb-source-data EFS contact read step after AceDataReady | A CONTACT entry with source EFS and retention class "ILG-STD" (TC-E2-034-01-ITG) |
| Workbench call written to the ledger | rwb-source-data ledger append through the P1 and P2 contracts | A CONTACT entry with source WORKBENCH (TC-E2-034-01-ITG) |
| Case transferred between bank owners | rwb-case transfer | The CASE_TRANSFERRED entry with the holder before and after (TC-E2-034-02-ITG) |
| Instruction issued to a partner | rwb-partner instruction workflow | A HANDOVER entry with channel PORTAL (TC-E2-034-02-ITG) |
| Partner result submitted | rwb-partner result endpoint | A PARTNER_RESULT entry with channel PORTAL and direction INBOUND (TC-E2-034-03-ITG) |
| Notice dispatched and delivered | rwb-comms notice workflow | LETTER entries with SENT and DELIVERED (TC-E2-034-04-ITG) |
| Treatment approved | rwb-treatment approval | An OFFER entry linked to the treatment (TC-E2-034-04-ITG) |
| Proceeds matched | rwb-payment matching | A PAYMENT entry linked to the proceeds (TC-E2-034-04-ITG) |
| Delivery stuck in RETRYING | The outbox library | No entry, then one entry after the retry (TC-E2-034-07-ITG) |

None. The harness run is started by the test pipeline, not by a Temporal Schedule and not by Airflow, and it creates no Schedule.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-18 | Interaction ledger | Ledger owned by rwb-source-data (default ruling) | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The platform H dependencies named in the table (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1037-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are delivered by the platform waves and are not repeated in the metadata H column; DP-15 resolves to "no migration", because the harness owns no schema. DP-18 is the ruling this harness proves: the ledger and the EFS intake rule are rwb-source-data's, the timeline is rwb-case's, and every read crosses one contract. The blocking dependencies of this story are the nine I stories, which replace the fakes with the real behaviour; they gate the done state, not the Day-1 start.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| LedgerJourneyRunner | Test harness | Runs the twelve `-ITG` cases of §16 in one run per business date, in fake or real mode per service, and stops at the first failed assertion with the trace |
| LedgerClient | Harness adapter | Calls the ten consumed operations of §12.2 through one hop with the channel, actor, date, page and size parameters, and records the answer |
| LedgerEventReplayer | Harness adapter | Replays the nine business events of §12.4 into the channel listener, including the duplicate of "EVT-SYN-0001", and reads the record on `rwb.decision-record.v1` |
| FakePack | WireMock project | Serves the owning services and the gateway-bff route of §12.8 from the published OpenAPI documents |
| LedgerSeedLoader | Service | Seeds the case, the EFS batch rows, the reference rows and the partner, notice, treatment and proceeds fixtures through the owner's contract or the fake |
| EntryAsserter | Assertion | Asserts each entry's event code, channel, direction, occurred time, source, contact key, holder references, links, delivery status, external reference and retention class |
| SummaryAsserter | Assertion | Asserts the read summary of AC6 — 3 read, 1 written, 1 excluded by the outcome list and 1 not on a case |
| RefusalAsserter | Assertion | Asserts the status and the message of each refusal and the empty state: 404 with MSG-P4-003, and MSG-P3-024 with no items |
| SchemaBoundaryCheck | Assertion | Fails the run on any cross-schema reference in the trace, so only rwb-source-data reads the ACE views |
| RunLock | Service | One run at a time in the harness environment |
| EvidenceReportPublisher | Reporter | Writes the per-run evidence report keyed by story id and business date and attaches it to the release record |
| JourneyGate | Assertion | Passes the run only when every owned criterion passes; fails and names the criterion, the seam and the observed value otherwise |

**Database.** None. The harness owns no schema, runs no Flyway migration and holds no table; seeds and assertions go through the contracts (DP-01, DP-15).

**Environment and test data.** SIT for the run of record and UAT for the acceptance run, with `rwb.integration.ledger-channels` on in both. The data are the synthetic seeds of the legacy story: case "RW-2026-000301" with account "ACC-SYN-0301" and owner "U-2001"; the EFS batch for 14 December 2026 with the "PTP", "SYS" and "ACC-SYN-0999" rows; the case "RW-2026-000302" with no entry; partner "LF-SYN-01" with instruction "INS-SYN-0301"; notice "NT-SYN-0301" with barcode "EV000000001TH"; treatment "TRT-SYN-0301"; proceeds "PRC-SYN-0301" of 5,000.00; users "U-2001", "U-2002" and "U-3001" with their teams and scopes; the business date 20 December 2026 for the run key. Each run starts from the seeded state, so a repeated run is deterministic. The harness environment, its seeding and its evidence format and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0416; ASM-0591).

**Build steps**

1. Build LedgerJourneyRunner and LedgerClient against the published OpenAPI documents of the owning services and the gateway-bff route.
2. Publish FakePack for the owning services and the composite route from the same documents, and prove the harness runs green from Day 1 on the fakes.
3. Write LedgerSeedLoader and the seed files, with the run lock and the fake or real mode per service.
4. Write EntryAsserter and SummaryAsserter for AC1 to AC6 and AC9, with a unit test on fixtures for every entry field and for the read summary.
5. Write RefusalAsserter and SchemaBoundaryCheck for AC10, AC11 and the access case.
6. Write LedgerEventReplayer for the duplicate delivery of AC5 and the failed-store run of AC7, including the incident assertion.
7. Replace each fake with the real service as its I story lands, in the order rwb-source-data, rwb-integration, rwb-case, rwb-access, rwb-partner, and rerun in UAT.
8. Write JourneyGate and EvidenceReportPublisher, and attach the report to the release record for the build under test.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.integration.ledger-channels`, the legacy switch of this story: on in SIT and UAT. The harness asserts the off state on the fakes — the listener acknowledges the six events without writing, the EFS read step does not run and the holder fields stay empty — and asserts that the Epic 1 ledger is unchanged in that state.

**Done when.** The twelve `-ITG` test cases of section 16 pass in SIT and UAT with the nine I stories in place and not only against the fakes; the evidence report for the run is attached to the release record with the ten owned criteria green; and the access case and the empty state are green with the messages of section 14.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |

| MSG-P3-024 | The case has no ledger entry | No interactions are recorded on this case yet. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role lacks Case record R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the reader's scope | This case is not in your scope. |

The harness asserts the message id and the rendered text of each row and never rewrites the text. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

| SCR-03 Case record | On hold | The same ledger section is returned and no edit is possible; the harness writes nothing |

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the EFS outcome list, the event codes, the channels, the directions, the sources and the retention classes are reference data held by the owning services; the harness reads them and never holds a copy.
- No personal data in logs, tests, traces or reports: the contact point is a reference, the summary is masked by role, and the harness stores IDs, event codes, statuses and counts only.
- No read of another service's schema: every read goes through the owner's contract, the SchemaBoundaryCheck fails the run on a cross-schema reference, and only rwb-source-data reads the ACE views through its own interfaces (DP-05).
- No production data and no outside system: the harness calls only the owning services and their fakes, never an outside gateway or a production endpoint.
- One hop only: the harness fails a run when the trace shows a call chain deeper than the gateway and one owner.
- The ledger is append only: the harness asserts that a repeated delivery, a refusal and a successful read leave every entry unchanged and never update or delete one.
- The harness owns no table, no endpoint, no screen, no workflow and no schedule (DP-01, DP-18); it is test and evidence only.
