**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-035 for rwb-integration. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the rwb-integration side of the next action fixed as a contract: the three operations with their paths, shapes, rights and errors; the consumed contracts of rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision with their two shapes of read; the split between the compute here and the write there; the `NextActionCheckWorkflow` and its activities; the `next-action-check` Schedule; the `job_catalog` row and the `decision_record` library table; and the contract fakes**, so that **the app and operations stories of this key, the case transition of `RWB-P3-E2035-APP` and the integration harness build on Day 1 against one agreed, testable shape**.

The legacy story held the resolution, the field writes, the read endpoint and the JOB-05 step in one module and placed the read at `GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action` in the P3 backlog of the API Specification. Under D-RCV-60 the resolution is a service of rwb-integration and the case row stays with rwb-case. This contract fixes the seam between them: the resolve is side-effect free and returns the four values, the fill writes them through the rwb-case contract, and the case transition of `RWB-P3-E2035-APP` consumes the resolve inside its own transaction boundary while rwb-case keeps the write, the optimistic lock and the task lifecycle.

The Ownership Map keeps `GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action` with P3 while this work package assigns the story to rwb-integration. This document reconciles the two: the path is served by rwb-integration under its own base `/api/recovery/integration/v1` (DP-13), rwb-case keeps the case record and the write, and the conflict is carried in GAP-0668 and ASM-1178 rather than resolved silently.

The contract also states what this service does not own: the RESTRUCTURE registry rows and the catalog rows are rwb-decision's behind the `RuleCatalog.row` operation published in `RWB-P3-E2042-CON`; the evaluation of the package is the case workflow's `EvaluateRules` activity; the role rows, the service levels and timers rows and the calendar rows are rwb-case's reference data; the decision ledger is rwb-decision's; and the case row is rwb-case's. This service uses the embedded kit types `RuleResult` and `NoPackageInForce` and runs no second rule engine (DP-04).

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST and one hop with a 2 s timeout is the decoupling rule (DP-11, ADR-020), and the case record is rwb-case's while the rule catalog is rwb-decision's (Arch v5 slide 41; ASM-0069). Both only work if the seam is written down once. The seam here is small and load-bearing: an operation that turns a fired rule into an action, an owner and a due date without writing anything; a fill that writes those values through the owner of the case; a read the case record screen can consume; and a Schedule that sweeps the cases the transition never filled.

Four teams move at once if the shape is agreed and faked on Day 1. The app story builds the three operations against the fakes of rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision; the operations story deploys the worker, the Schedule, the flag and the runbook against the names this document fixes; the case transition story `RWB-P3-E2035-APP` builds its call and its write against the resolve shape; and the integration harness of `RWB-ITG-E2035-ITG` reads the same answer through the owning services. Without the contract, the action text, the owner role and the timer would be resolved in two places and the measure the legacy story sets — the count of active cases with no next action, with a target of zero — would have no single owner.

The contract is also where the legacy split is made explicit. Four statements of the legacy criteria belong to the case side and are proved in `RWB-P3-E2035-APP`: the write in the same transaction as the move, the cancel of the `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` task on closure, the optimistic lock and the refusal of the move when no package version is in force. This document fixes what the case side may rely on when it does them: the resolve answer, its refusal outcomes, the idempotency of a repeat and the one-task rule of the fill.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON), so the base, the task queue, the Schedule name and the event names follow the platform rule (DP-13, DP-14).
- The CloudEvents 1.0 envelope, the RFC 9457 problem-details body and the platform message catalogue are the platform baseline; this document narrows them where it must and says so.
- The embedded Drools kit contract is available (RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, DP-04): the `RuleResult` and `NoPackageInForce` types, the first-match semantics, the cache bound and the checksum rule are its elements, and this document reuses them rather than redefining them.
- The workflow kit and its Schedule conventions are available (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-WF): the task queue `rwb-integration`, the namespace `rwb-recovery`, the overlap policy, the catch-up window and the retry policy are the kit's elements.
- The rwb-case operations exist as published by the rwb-case contract stories: the case record read and write of RWB-P3-E1018-CON and RWB-P3-E2035-APP, the case list row read of RWB-P3-E1031-CON, the reference-data and parameter reads of RWB-P3-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1042-CON, and the `RuleCatalog.row` operation of RWB-P3-E2042-CON. This document consumes them and fakes them; it defines none of them.
- The rwb-access authorise contract (RWB-P4-E1037-CON) and the rwb-decision decision-log contract (RWB-P7-E1027-CON) are published, or are faked to the shapes this document declares.
- The three legacy values are the agreed values of this key: package code RESTRUCTURE, package version "RES-2026.12", and the rows R-RES-04, R-SET-13, R-RES-03, R-DEV-05 and R-RES-07 with their action, owner role and timer.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the three provided operations: `POST /next-actions:resolve`, `GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action` and `POST /cases/{caseId}/next-action`, with their paths, rights, inputs, answers, errors and idempotency.
2. Publish the consumed shapes: the case facts read and the next-action write of rwb-case, the case list row, the catalog row of `RuleCatalog.row`, the role class, the service level and the calendar reads, the decision-log read and the authorise call, each with the 2 s client budget.
3. State the split between the compute and the write, and reconcile the Ownership Map conflict of the read path.
4. Publish the `NextActionCheckWorkflow` contract: the input, the three activities, the output counts, the at-most-one-task rule and the non-retryable `NoPackageInForce` outcome.
5. Publish the `next-action-check` Schedule contract: the schedule ID, the cadence, the overlap policy, the catch-up window and the pause, resume and backfill operations of the kit.
6. Publish the table section: the `job_catalog` row this service owns and the `decision_record` library table, with the statement that no case, role or rule row is copied into `rwb_integration`.
7. Publish the error mapping of the five messages over the three operations and the fill.
8. Build the contract fakes of rwb-case, the catalog, the reference data, rwb-decision, rwb-access and the gateway route.
9. Add the contract tests: the operation shapes, the consumed shapes, the Schedule fields, the table section and the drift test between each fake and this document; tag the baseline and hand it to the app and operations stories.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | An operation, a consumed shape or the Schedule contradicts this document | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC1, AC2, AC3, AC4 |
| X2 | A fake drifts from this document, or answers a shape this document does not declare | The drift test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC6 |
| X3 | The resolve is called without a rule ID, a package version or a business date | The call is refused with the field named and nothing is resolved | MSG-GEN-001 | AC5 |
| X4 | The resolve is called for a business date with no package version in force | The answer is `NoPackageInForce` and it is non-retryable for the caller; the move is refused and nothing is written | MSG-P3-027 | AC5 |
| X5 | The caller's role does not hold Case record R or U, or the case is outside the scope | The call is refused before any consumed contract is reached, and no data is returned | MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 | AC5 |
| X6 | A field-level detail of a consumed operation is missing from the source material | The element is marked with the placeholder, one gap row and one assumption row are carried, and the fake is written to the assumed shape | None | AC2, AC6 |
| X7 | A document declares the case write, the catalog registry or a second rule engine as this service's own | The review refuses the document, because the case row is rwb-case's, the registry is rwb-decision's and the evaluation is the case workflow's | None | AC3 |

| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes and the published rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision contracts and fakes them |
| Negotiable | The field-level detail of the consumed operations is settled with their owners; the three operation names, the Schedule name and the split are fixed by this realignment |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app story, the operations story, the case transition of RWB-P3-E2035-APP and the integration harness of this legacy key |

| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact — the schema, the fake, the table section — and never against a business outcome |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Two operations serve the resolution and one writes it: the resolve is side-effect free, the read composes it, and the fill writes it through the owner of the case | Arch v5 slide 41; DP-01; RWB-P3-E2035-APP |
| BR2 | rwb-case is the only writer of `recovery_case`: this service writes no case column, no task row and no lock | Arch v5 slide 41; DP-01 |
| BR3 | One REST base and one task queue per service: this contract declares `/api/recovery/integration/v1` and `rwb-integration`, consumes the other bases and never declares another service's path as provided | DP-13; DP-14; Ownership Map |
| BR4 | The rule catalog is read only through `RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion)` as published in RWB-P3-E2042-CON; no workbook, no generated DRL and no rule table is read | D-RCV-36 T3, T5, T6; DP-04 |
| BR5 | The embedded kit supplies the `RuleResult` and `NoPackageInForce` types and the version-in-force check; no second rule engine runs in this service, because the evaluation is the case workflow's activity | D-RCV-36 T5, T7; DP-04; ASM-1185 |
| BR6 | Everything a business person may change is a data row: action text, owner role, timer, role class, service level and calendar are read through their owners' contracts and written in no code path | FSD P2 Integration v3 BR-P2-001; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR7 | The resolve answer is a pure function of the case facts, the catalog row, the reference rows and the business date: the same input answers the same output, which is what makes a repeated transition and a repeated fill safe | Legacy RWB-E2-035 AC9 and AC11 |
| BR8 | A fill raises at most one open `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` task per case, and the Schedule carries the overlap policy SKIP and a catch-up window so a missed run is caught by the next one | Legacy RWB-E2-035 BR7 and JOB-05 misfire rule |
| BR9 | No personal data appears in an event, an activity input, an example or a fake: case IDs, role codes, rule IDs, version labels and dates only | Arch v5 slide 42; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR10 | A consumed field, path or error that no source fixes is written with the placeholder and carried in one gap row plus its assumption rows, never invented | Template and Rules §R9 |
| BR11 | The legacy flag `rwb.casewf.next-action` is kept as the reference of the switch, and the switch is a feature flag of the platform flag library, never a column of a service table | R-PREC default ruling; Ownership Map `feature_flag` (PLT) |
| BR12 | The legacy values of the key are carried unchanged: package version "RES-2026.12" and the rows R-RES-04, R-SET-13, R-RES-03, R-DEV-05 and R-RES-07 with their action, owner role and timer | Legacy RWB-E2-035 section 7; RWB-E2-042 |

##### 11. Data

The contract declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Resolve input | caseId, ruleId, packageVersion, businessDate |
| Resolve answer | text, ownerRole, ownerName, ownerUserId (when BR9 names the case owner), dueDate, waiting, missing, ruleId, ruleVersion |
| Read answer | The resolve answer plus overdue, and the case state and closed flag it is computed against |
| Fill answer | The case ID, the outcome filled, unchanged, missing or skipped, the task reference when one is raised, and the decision-record reference |
| Case facts read | state, status, ownerUserId, queueId, queue role code, team code, closedDate |
| Catalog row | ruleId, packageVersion, drools_rule_name, action_text, owner_role, timer_spec, target_queue_code, outputs |
| Role row, service level row, calendar row | roleCode, roleName, roleClass; state, working days; calendar date and label |
| Decision-log read | ruleId, ruleVersion, entryId, decidedAt of the latest state change |
| Workflow input and output | business date and run window in; counts of filled, unchanged, missing and failed out |
| Schedule row | job_id, job_name, owner_role, schedule_text, runbook_path, expected_minutes, alert_after_minutes |

The field-level detail of the case facts read, the catalog row, the reference rows, the decision-log read and the next-action write — property types, lengths, required flags and the query parameters — is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0668; ASM-1179); this document fixes the element names above and leaves the types to the review with each owner. The values of the rule rows are the legacy values of this key and are carried unchanged (BR12).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/integration/v1`; owner rwb-integration (P2).

| Method | Path | Documented shape | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/next-actions:resolve` | Input caseId, ruleId, packageVersion, businessDate; answer text, ownerRole, ownerName, ownerUserId, dueDate, waiting, missing, ruleId, ruleVersion; 401, 403, 404, 409 (MSG-P3-027, MSG-GEN-004), 422 (MSG-GEN-001), 503 (MSG-GEN-006) | Case record R, scope applied | Side-effect free: the same input answers the same output |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/next-action` | Answer text, ownerRole, ownerName, ownerUserId, dueDate, waiting, overdue, missing, ruleId, ruleVersion; 401, 403, 404, 503 | Case record R, scope applied | Read only |
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/next-action` | The fill: answer case ID, outcome filled, unchanged, missing or skipped, task reference, decision-record reference; 200 for a case already filled, 409 (MSG-GEN-004), 422, 503 | Case record U for the service identity, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key`; at most one open NEXT_ACTION_MISSING task per case |

The `:resolve` suffix is the operation name this contract fixes for a resolution and not a resource: the legacy story called the component `NextActionAssigner` and its interface `NextActionAssigner.assign(...)`, and no source fixes an HTTP name for it (GAP-0668; ASM-1183). The read path is the Ownership Map row that the map keeps with P3; this contract serves it from rwb-integration under its own base and records the conflict (GAP-0668; ASM-1178).

Two responses of `RWB-P2-E2033-APP` change and are documented here as a change, not as a new operation: each Case item of `GET /cases` and each row of `GET /cases/export` gains `nextAction`, `nextActionOwner`, `nextActionDueDate` and `nextActionOverdue`, resolved by this service, with that story's authorization and errors unchanged.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11).

| Method | Path or operation | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case facts of the resolve and the read |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases` | P3 rwb-case | The active cases with no next action and the case list rows that carry the four columns |
| POST | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0668; ASM-1179) | P3 rwb-case | The write of the four next-action fields and the raise or cancel of the NEXT_ACTION_MISSING task, called by the fill |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion=`, the `RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion)` operation | P7 rwb-decision, published in RWB-P3-E2042-CON | action_text, owner_role, timer_spec and outputs of the firing rule |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/reference-data/role-classes/{roleCode}` | P3 rwb-case | role_name and role_class of the owner role |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/reference-data/service-levels/{toState}` | P3 rwb-case | The service levels and timers row of the to_state |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/parameters/rwb.calendar.bank-holidays` | P3 rwb-case | The bank holiday list of BR8 of the app story |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId=&latestStateChange=true` | P7 rwb-decision | The latest state change of a case: rule ID and rule version |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Case record R or U and the case scope, cached per session |

The reference-data and parameter paths are named by the reference tables and the configuration key of the legacy story; no source fixes them and they are taken from the P3 contract baseline when it is published (GAP-0668; ASM-1179). The catalog operation is the one `RWB-P3-E2042-CON` publishes over the rwb-decision catalog, so this service holds no registry row and reads no rule table (BR4).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This story declares no event type and publishes on no topic of its own. The fill writes through the rwb-case contract, and the event of the record is the shared ledger event: the local decision-record library of DP-03 publishes `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` from the same transaction as the record it writes, and this contract only names that event and its key (the decision-record reference). The move's own record is written by rwb-case's library call in `RWB-P3-E2035-APP`.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. Every call of this story is call-driven: the resolve is called by the case transition, the read by the case record screen through gateway-bff, and the fill by the `next-action-check` Schedule. The latest state change is read from the decision-log contract at the time of the fill, so the service subscribes to no topic, holds no inbox and keeps no projection.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| NextActionCheckWorkflow | Workflow | `rwb-integration` | Input: business date, run window. Output: counts of filled, unchanged, missing and failed cases, and the run reference |
| findCasesWithoutNextAction | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: business date. Output: the active cases with no next action from the rwb-case contract |
| resolveNextAction | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: caseId, ruleId, packageVersion, business date. Output: the resolve answer; raises `NoPackageInForce`, which is non-retryable |
| fillNextAction | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: caseId and the resolve answer. Output: filled, unchanged, missing or skipped; one rwb-case call, at most one task per case, idempotent by case ID and task code |

The activities carry the kit's retry policy; the workflow carries the Schedule's overlap policy and never runs two executions for the same fire window.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Cadence | Documented fields | Legacy reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `next-action-check` | Every 5 minutes | Schedule ID `next-action-check`; workflow `NextActionCheckWorkflow`; task queue `rwb-integration`; overlap policy SKIP; catch-up window; input business date and run window; pause, resume and backfill as kit operations | JOB-05 Timer check, the next action step |

The five minutes are the legacy cadence of JOB-05. The catch-up window, the overlap window and the backfill limit are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0668; ASM-1184) and are fixed as values of the deployment in RWB-P2-E2035-OPS. The timer vocabulary of the legacy story is JOB-05; in the target JOB-05 is retired (Arch v5 slide 44; the Ownership Map ruling on `timer`) and this Schedule is the mechanism that does the fill (ASM-1180).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|---|
| job_catalog | rwb_integration | P2 (Ownership Map; TSD P2 v3 T3.1) | One row for `next-action-check`: job_id, job_name, owner_role, schedule_text, runbook_path, expected_minutes, alert_after_minutes, first_release |
| decision_record | rwb_integration | PLT library, created in rwb_integration (DP-03) | The local decision record of a fill, written by the library in the same transaction as the record |

No case table, no task table, no role table and no rule table is owned, read or copied: the case facts, the case write, the role rows, the service levels, the calendar and the rule row come through their owners' contracts (DP-01, BR2). The Ownership Map ruling on `job_catalog` stands: each service's Schedules are not rows of a shared table, so this row exists for the job catalogue of the deployment and for the alerts, not to drive the Schedule.

**Deliverables.** `contract/next-action-openapi.yaml` (the three operations and the two changed case list responses), `contract/next-action-consumed.yaml` (the nine consumed paths and operations with the 2 s budget), `contract/next-action-split.md` (the compute-and-write split and the ownership reconciliation), `contract/next-action-workflow.yaml` (the workflow input, the three activities and their outputs), `contract/next-action-schedule.yaml` (the Schedule fields and the kit operations), and six WireMock mapping sets.

**Pattern application**

| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | The Schedule and the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |

**Build steps**

1. Write the OpenAPI document of the three operations, with the input, the answer, the errors and the idempotency of each; AC1, AC5.
2. Write the consumed document: nine paths and operations, their owner, their use and the 2 s budget; AC2.
3. Write the split note: the compute here, the write there, the four case-side statements and the ownership reconciliation; AC3.
4. Write the workflow contract and the Schedule contract, with the overlap policy, the catch-up window and the one-task rule; AC4.
5. Write the table section: the `job_catalog` row and the `decision_record` library table, with the absence rule for the case, role and rule tables; AC6.
6. Build the six fake sets and their fixtures.
7. Add the contract tests, including the drift test between each fake and this document, and the check that the legacy monolith base appears nowhere.
8. Tag the baseline and collect the sign-off of the app story, the operations story, the case transition story and the harness.

**Done when.** The six contract files validate in the pipeline, the contract tests pass, the six fakes answer every consumed path and operation, and the app, operations, case transition and harness stories of this legacy key have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P2-023 | The case has no next action or no due date | This case has no next action. It is on the exception list for {team}. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No RESTRUCTURE version is in force on the business date | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A case changed between the read and the write, or a fill repeats a case already filled | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Case record R or U calls an operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. |

The texts are the agreed texts of the legacy story and of the platform catalogue; this contract adds no message. For MSG-P3-027 the `{check}` value is "package in force" and the `{detail}` names the package code and the business date only. The operation that carries each message is named in section 12.1; MSG-P2-023 is carried by the case record and never returned as a problem body.

##### 15. Screens and states

None in this story. The contract serves the SCR-03 next action header through the gateway-bff composite route and the SCR-02 columns through the case list of RWB-P2-E2033-APP, and it renders no page and holds no screen state. The Schedule states are operator states of the deployment and are carried by RWB-P2-E2035-OPS as metrics and as a run view, not as a screen of this story.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: action text, owner role, timer, role class, service level, calendar and route state are data rows of their owners.
- No personal data in an answer, an event, an activity input, an example or a fake: case IDs, role codes, rule IDs, version labels and dates only.
- The contract names only rwb-integration operations as provided; the case facts, the case write, the catalog row, the reference rows, the decision-log read and the authorise call are consumed and never restated as this service's (DP-01, DP-13).
- One base, one queue and one namespace: a document that names another service's base as provided, or a topic outside `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- The rule row is read only through `RuleCatalog.row`; a workbook, a generated DRL or a rule table in a shape of this contract fails the review (BR4).
- No second rule engine: the kit's types and the version-in-force check are used and the evaluation stays with the case workflow's activity (BR5).
- The legacy flag name is kept as a reference only, and the switch is the platform flag library's (BR11).
- Every example and fixture is synthetic; no production payload, case number or rule row is copied into a schema or a fake.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-035 for rwb-integration. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **every active case to show one next action, its owner and its due date, resolved from the rule package that moved the case into its current state and served by one operation of the integration service**, so that **I never open a case and have to work out what it needs**.

The legacy story put the assigner, the field writes, the read endpoint and the JOB-05 check in one module. Under D-RCV-60 the work splits by owner. rwb-case owns the case record, the CMMN state, the queues, the tasks and the timers (Arch v5 slide 41), so rwb-case writes `recovery_case.next_action_*` in the same transaction as the move, cancels the exception task and holds the optimistic lock; that side is `RWB-P3-E2035-APP`, which consumes the resolve operation published here. rwb-integration owns the resolution itself: `POST /api/recovery/integration/v1/next-actions:resolve` is the side-effect-free operation that turns the rule that fired into the action text, the owner, the due date, the waiting flag and the missing flag; `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/cases/{caseId}/next-action` is the read the case record screen consumes; `POST /api/recovery/integration/v1/cases/{caseId}/next-action` is the JOB-05 fill, which resolves and then writes through the rwb-case contract; and the `next-action-check` Schedule finds active cases with no next action and fills them or raises one `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` task.

The Ownership Map keeps `GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action` with P3 (API Specification v4, x-module P3; Arch v5 slide 41), while this work package assigns the story to rwb-integration. The two are reconciled explicitly: rwb-integration serves the path under its own base `/api/recovery/integration/v1` (DP-13), and rwb-case keeps the case row, the four columns and the write. The operation is therefore served here and owned there, and the conflict is carried in GAP-0667 and ASM-1178 rather than left implicit.

What this story does not do is decide. The evaluation of the RESTRUCTURE package stays with the case workflow's `EvaluateRules` activity, which returns `RuleResult(packageCode, packageVersion, ruleId, outputs)` and raises `NoPackageInForce`; this service receives the fired rule ID and package version, reads the catalog row through `RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion)` as published in `RWB-P3-E2042-CON`, and holds no second rule engine. It reads no workbook, no generated DRL and no rule table (D-RCV-36 T3, T5, T6; DP-04).

##### 2. Business rationale

A case owner today reads the case history to decide what is owed next, and a case can wait for weeks with nobody owing anything on it. The route-set rules already hold the action, the owner of the next state and the timer for every move, as rows of the RESTRUCTURE rule package. The Workbench copies these onto the case at each move and shows them on the case and in the case list. A case with no next action is raised to the team manager as an exception. The measure is the count of active cases with no next action, with a target of zero, and it meets REQ-WKM-012, REQ-WKM-013 and REQ-WKM-016.

In the target the data stays where it is and the calls change. The rule rows are registry rows of rwb-decision (Ownership Map: `rule_row`, `rule_package_version` are P7; ASM-0069), and the catalog operation that answers action_text, owner_role and timer_spec is the one published in `RWB-P3-E2042-CON`, which reads rwb-decision. The role name and the role class, the service levels and timers rows and the calendar rows are reference data of rwb-case (Ownership Map: `reference_row`, `reference_version` are P3; DP-07). The case facts are case facts of rwb-case (DP-01). The decision log is the central ledger of rwb-decision (DP-03). The authorise check is the contract of rwb-access (DP-08 is not in the pattern list of this legacy key, and the check is therefore carried as the `RWB-P4-E1037-CON` contract dependency of the resolve read).

Two legacy components move for good reason. `RuleEvaluator` was called from the same transaction as the write; in the target the evaluation is the case workflow's activity and the resolution is a separate, side-effect-free call, so the case transaction stays short and the same resolve answer can serve the case screen, the fill step and the case list columns. `NextActionCheckStep` was a step inside JOB-05 Timer check; in the target JOB-05 is retired (Arch v5 slide 44 lists it as durable timers, and the Ownership Map ruling on `timer` retires `TimerDue`), so the fill becomes the Temporal Schedule `next-action-check` on the queue of this service, every five minutes. The legacy flag `rwb.casewf.next-action` is kept as the reference of the switch, and the switch itself is a feature flag of the platform flag library (R-PREC default ruling).

The authorise check is the contract of rwb-access. DP-08 is not among the patterns applied to this legacy key and the contract-dependency row of the work package does not list `RWB-P4-E1037-CON`, so the check is named in section 12.2 and the omission is carried in the gap row rather than hidden.

##### 3. Preconditions

- `RWB-P2-E2035-CON` is published: the three operations, the consumed shapes, the schedule, the error mapping and the contract fakes of this key. It is a same-service contract story and therefore a build dependency (Template and Rules §R5.7 rule 3).
- `RWB-P2-E2033-APP` is done: the case list and the case export of this service exist, and their responses are the ones the four next-action columns are added to.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-E1072-CON is published: the embedded Drools kit, with the `RuleResult` and `NoPackageInForce` types and the version-in-force check (DP-04).
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1042-CON are published: the parameters contract of rwb-case, which carries the calendar key `rwb.calendar.bank-holidays` (DP-06).
- RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are published: the reference-data contract of rwb-case, which carries the role name and role class, the service levels and timers rows and the route-state list with the version in force (DP-07).
- RWB-PLT-E1071-CON is published: the Temporal workflow kit, the `rwb-recovery` namespace and the Schedule conventions of the platform (DP-10).
- RWB-PLT-E1047-CON is published: the naming library, so the Schedule, the task queue and the topic names follow the platform rule (DP-14).
- RWB-PLT-E1044-CON is published: the per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_integration`, which carries the `job_catalog` row of the new Schedule and the `decision_record` library table (DP-15).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route that serves the SCR-03 Case record next action header (DP-19).
- `RWB-P3-E2042-CON` is published with the `RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion)` operation, and package version "RES-2026.12" of code RESTRUCTURE is in force from 2026-12-01 with rule R-RES-04 and rule R-SET-13 (RWB-E2-042; RWB-E1-073).
- `RWB-P3-E1018-CON` and `RWB-P3-E1031-CON` are published: the case facts read and the case list row read that the composition and the four columns use.
- `RWB-P3-E1043-CON` carries the service levels and timers rows (seeded with 5 working days for each state of the route sets in force until the DL22 values are loaded) and the calendar key `rwb.calendar.bank-holidays` with 31 December 2026 and 1 January 2027.
- `RWB-P4-E1037-CON` is published: the authorise contract the read and the fill check the Case record right and the case scope with.
- `RWB-P3-E2035-APP` is the case-side story of this key: it writes the four columns, cancels the exception task on closure and holds the optimistic lock. This story builds against the published rwb-case contract and its fake, so that story does not block (class C).
- The login is the rwb-integration login (DP-02): Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0667; ASM-1177).

##### 4. Flow

1. rwb-case: event CASE_PICKED_UP arrives on the case workflow, `EvaluateRules` returns `RuleResult` with rule ID R-RES-04 and package version "RES-2026.12", and the transition calls `POST /api/recovery/integration/v1/next-actions:resolve` with caseId, ruleId, packageVersion and businessDate.
2. rwb-integration: checks that the case exists and is in scope through the rwb-case contract, reads the case facts (state, status, owner, queue, team, closed date), and reads `RuleCatalog.row("R-RES-04", "RES-2026.12")` through the rwb-case catalog contract (DP-04, C dependency).
3. rwb-integration: `TimerSpecResolver` turns the catalog row's `timer_spec` into a due date (BR3); when the spec is "None" or has no fixed duration, it reads the service levels and timers row of the to_state through the reference-data contract (BR4), and skips Saturday, Sunday and the calendar rows (BR8).
4. rwb-integration: `OwnerResolver` sets the owner role from the catalog row, sets `ownerName` and `ownerUserId` when the owner role is the role of the case's queue (BR9), and sets `waiting` when the role class is Customer party or Partner user (BR5).
5. rwb-integration: returns the resolve answer — text, ownerRole, ownerName, ownerUserId, dueDate, waiting, missing, ruleId, ruleVersion — and writes nothing. A missing due date sets `missing` true and leaves the due date empty (BR7).
6. rwb-case: writes `recovery_case.next_action_text`, `next_action_owner_role`, `next_action_due_date`, `next_action_rule_id` and `next_action_waiting` in the same transaction as the move and raises one `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` task when `missing` is true (`RWB-P3-E2035-APP`).
7. rwb-integration: the `next-action-check` Schedule fires every five minutes and starts `NextActionCheckWorkflow`, which reads the active cases with no next action through the rwb-case contract, reads the latest state change of each case through the decision-log contract of rwb-decision, resolves each case, and calls `POST /api/recovery/integration/v1/cases/{caseId}/next-action` to fill it or raise the same task once.
8. Case owner: opens the case record (SCR-03); the front end calls `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/cases/{caseId}/next-action` through gateway-bff and shows the action, the owner and the due date, or the waiting text, or the missing message.
9. Team manager: opens the case list (SCR-02) and the case export; the four next-action columns are on each row and an overdue action is marked (BR6).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The rule's timer_spec is None or has no fixed duration | Due date taken from the service levels and timers row of the to_state through the reference-data contract | None | AC5 |
| X2 | No due date can be found from the rule or the table | The resolve answer sets `missing` true with no due date; rwb-case writes the action and raises one task for the team manager | MSG-P2-023 | AC6 |
| X3 | The due date falls on a weekend or a bank holiday | Working days skip Saturday, Sunday and the calendar rows of `rwb.calendar.bank-holidays` | None | AC7 |
| X4 | The case closes | The resolve answer carries no action and no due date; the cancel of the task is rwb-case's (`RWB-P3-E2035-APP`) | None | AC8 |
| X5 | The same transition is resolved twice | The resolve answer is identical and the fill writes once; no second task | None | AC9 |
| X6 | Two transitions on one case commit at the same time | The optimistic lock is the case row's (`RWB-P3-E2035-APP`); the resolve of the committed rule is the one that stays | MSG-GEN-004 | AC10 |
| X7 | An active case from before the flag was switched on has no next action | The `next-action-check` Schedule fills it from the latest state change in the decision log | None | AC11 |
| X8 | The rule's timer is "same day" | Due date is the business date of the move | None | AC12 |
| X9 | The reader's role does not hold Case record R | Refused with 403 before any contract call | MSG-P4-002 | AC13 |
| X10 | No RESTRUCTURE package version is in force on the business date, or the case is outside the reader's scope | The resolve answers `NoPackageInForce` and the fill writes nothing; an out-of-scope case is a 404 | MSG-P3-027, MSG-P4-003 | AC14 |
| X11 | The rwb-case, rwb-access, rwb-decision or reference-data contract does not answer inside the budget | One hop, 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream; the resolve fails and nothing is written, the read answers 503 and the fill skips the case until the next run | MSG-GEN-006 | AC1, AC11 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds after RWB-P2-E2033-APP against the published contracts of this service and the rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision fakes; the case-side write is another story's and does not block |
| Negotiable | Action text, owner, timer, role class, service level and calendar are data rows; the story fixes only the behaviour and the answer shape |
| Valuable | Every active case states what is owed, by whom and by when, and the measure of cases with no next action is driven to zero |
| Estimable | Three operations, one resolver, one timer resolver, one owner resolver, one read composition, one workflow with three activities and one Schedule |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion below has one test with fixed catalog rows, roles and dates, run against the contract fakes |

The fourteen criteria are the legacy criteria of RWB-E2-035, copied with their values and their dates. The legacy path of AC13 becomes `GET /api/recovery/integration/v1/cases/{caseId}/next-action` under DP-13: the monolith base of the legacy story is replaced by the base of this service, and no other value of the criterion changes. The mock Givens name the contract that answers where a legacy statement crossed a module boundary: the case facts come from the rwb-case fake, the catalog row from the catalog fake, the role class, service level and calendar rows from the reference-data fake, the state change from the decision-log fake and the role check from the rwb-access fake.

Four statements of the legacy criteria are the case side's, not this story's, and they are proved in `RWB-P3-E2035-APP`: the write of the four fields in the same transaction as the move (AC2), the cancel of the `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` task on closure (AC8), the optimistic lock and its retry (AC10) and the refusal of the move when no version is in force (AC14). What this story proves is the resolve answer and the same rwb-case contract call in each of those four: the answer carries the rule, the version, the owner and the due date; the answer of a closed case carries no action; the resolve of the committed rule is the one that stays; and the resolve refuses with `NoPackageInForce` and MSG-P3-027. AC11 is named by its legacy job name JOB-05; in the target the fill is the `next-action-check` Schedule of section 12.6, which runs every five minutes and does the same work (see ASM-1180).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | On every move, the next action text, the owner role and the rule ID come from the catalog row of the firing rule: `RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion)` returns action_text, owner_role and timer_spec, and the row is read through the operation published in RWB-P3-E2042-CON | FEAT-CWC-28; REQ-WKM-013; D-RCV-36 T6 |
| BR2 | The next action is never entered by a person | REQ-WKM-013 |
| BR3 | timer_spec "n working days" adds n working days; "n days" with any label before it adds n calendar days; "same day", "Same day" and "immediate" give the date of the move; "next working day" adds 1 working day | rule_row.timer_spec through RuleCatalog |
| BR4 | Any other timer_spec, including "None", takes the time for the to_state from the service levels and timers rows through the reference-data contract | DL22; DP-07 |
| BR5 | The next action is a wait when the owner role is of class Customer party or Partner user; the text starts "Waiting for {owner}:" | role.role_class through the reference-data contract |
| BR6 | A next action is overdue when its due date is earlier than today and the case is not closed | REQ-WKM-012 |
| BR7 | An active case with no due date or no next action raises one NEXT_ACTION_MISSING task to the team manager; the fill raises it once, and the task is written through the rwb-case contract | REQ-WKM-016 |
| BR8 | Working days are Monday to Friday, excluding the dates of the calendar key rwb.calendar.bank-holidays, read through the parameters contract | Configuration key rwb.calendar.bank-holidays; DP-06 |
| BR9 | When the owner role is the role of the case's queue, the owner shown is the case owner; otherwise the role name | queue.role_code of the case, through the rwb-case contract |
| BR10 | The rule version is the package version label of the `RuleResult`, and the next action records the version of the move that set it; a later version does not rewrite an action already set | D-RCV-36 T5, T7; R-UNI-38 |
| BR11 | No RESTRUCTURE version in force is a refusal (`NoPackageInForce` from the embedded kit), never a default move and never an empty next action | D-RCV-36 T3; R-UNI-41 |
| BR12 | rwb-case is the only writer of `recovery_case`; this service resolves and serves and never writes a case column, and the resolve operation is side-effect free | Arch v5 slide 41; DP-01; RWB-P3-E2035-APP |
| BR13 | The rule catalog is read only through `RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion)`; no workbook, no generated DRL and no rule table is read, and no second rule engine runs | D-RCV-36 T3, T5, T6; DP-04 |

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status and writes no case row: it resolves the next action, serves it and fills it through the rwb-case contract. The case status, the four next-action columns and the `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` task status (OPEN to CANCELED) are rwb-case's writes in `RWB-P3-E2035-APP`, in the same transaction as the move.

The only record lifecycles this story holds are its own: the `next-action-check` Schedule run (IDLE to RUNNING to COMPLETE or FAILED), and the resolve answer, which is stateless and stored nowhere.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-RULES, the rule evaluation activity of rwb-case | Returns the `RuleResult` (rule ID and package version) that this service resolves; it never resolves the action itself |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Writes the next action fields and the exception task through the rwb-case contract (Case record U, Queue and allocation C) and owns the transaction |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the next action of cases in scope (Case record R) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads the list and works NEXT_ACTION_MISSING tasks on the exception queue |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Owns the action, owner and timer columns of the rule rows (Rules and parameters CRUD) |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads the service levels and timers rows and the calendar rows of `rwb.calendar.bank-holidays` |
| No approval applies | The story takes no decision |

The service runs as the rwb-integration login (DP-02). The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0667; ASM-1177).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/integration/v1`; owner rwb-integration (P2).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/next-actions:resolve` | Side-effect-free resolution: input caseId, ruleId, packageVersion, businessDate; answer text, ownerRole, ownerName, ownerUserId (when BR9 names the case owner), dueDate, waiting, missing, ruleId, ruleVersion. Consumed by the case transition of `RWB-P3-E2035-APP` | Case record R, scope applied, through the rwb-access authorise contract | Not applicable: the call writes nothing, and the same input answers the same output |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/next-action` | The next action of a case for SCR-03: text, ownerRole, ownerName, ownerUserId, dueDate, waiting, overdue, missing, ruleId, ruleVersion. Composed from the case facts, the latest state change, the catalog row, the role class, the service level and the calendar rows | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable: read only |
| POST | `/cases/{caseId}/next-action` | The fill of the `next-action-check` Schedule: resolves the case and writes the four values through the rwb-case contract, or raises one `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` task; records its own decision record first | Case record U for the service identity, scope applied | `Idempotency-Key` on the POST; a case that already holds a next action is left unchanged and answers 200 with what it holds |

The Ownership Map keeps `GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action` with P3, and this story serves it from rwb-integration under its own base (DP-13); the reconciliation and the conflict are carried in GAP-0667 and ASM-1178.

Two responses of `RWB-P2-E2033-APP` change: each Case item of `GET /cases` and each row of `GET /cases/export` gains `nextAction`, `nextActionOwner`, `nextActionDueDate` and `nextActionOverdue`, resolved by this story from the same four fields, with the authorization and the errors left as that story set them. The response field names of the three operations and of the two changed responses are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0667; ASM-1182).

Errors: 401 no session (MSG-P4-001); 403 no Case record R (MSG-P4-002); 404 unknown case or case outside the scope (MSG-P4-003); 409 no package version in force (MSG-P3-027) or a case changed by someone else (MSG-GEN-004); 422 a missing required input (MSG-GEN-001); 503 a consumed contract does not answer inside the budget (MSG-GEN-006).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; 2 s timeout and a breaker per downstream (DP-11).

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | rwb-case (P3) | The case facts: state, status, owner, queue, queue role, team, closed date | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases` | rwb-case (P3) | The active cases with no next action and the case list rows that carry the four columns | One hop, 2 s, breaker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion=` | rwb-decision (P7), through the `RuleCatalog.row` operation published in RWB-P3-E2042-CON | action_text, owner_role, timer_spec and outputs of one rule row | One hop, 2 s, cached |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/reference-data/role-classes/{roleCode}` | rwb-case (P3) | role_name and role_class of the owner role (BR5, BR9) | One hop, 2 s, cached |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/reference-data/service-levels/{toState}` | rwb-case (P3) | The service levels and timers row of the to_state (BR4) | One hop, 2 s, cached |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/parameters/rwb.calendar.bank-holidays` | rwb-case (P3) | The bank holiday list (BR8) | One hop, 2 s, cached |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId=&latestStateChange=true` | rwb-decision (P7) | The latest state change of a case: rule ID and rule version, for the fill (AC9, AC11) | One hop, 2 s |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | rwb-access (P4) | Case record R or U and the scope of the case, cached per session by the guard library | One hop, 2 s, cached |
| POST | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0667; ASM-1179) | rwb-case (P3) | The write of the four next-action fields and the raise or cancel of the `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` task, called by the fill | One hop, 2 s |

The catalog path is the one the rwb-decision contract publishes and the operation name is `RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion)` as published in RWB-P3-E2042-CON. The reference-data and parameter paths are named by the reference tables and the configuration key of the legacy story, not by a path in a source: the operation shapes are the P3 contract's to fix, and the paths above are the ones this story builds against until that baseline is published. The write path of the fill is the rwb-case case-record contract of `RWB-P3-E2035-APP`, and its exact path and payload are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0667; ASM-1179).

###### 12.3 Events published

None of its own. This story declares no event type and publishes on no topic of its own: `rwb.integration.events.v1` carries FileDelivered and FileFailed, which belong to the file stories of this service. The fill writes its own decision record through the local decision-record library (DP-03), and the library publishes `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` from the same transaction; the record of the move itself is rwb-case's, written by its own library call in `RWB-P3-E2035-APP`.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The resolve is call-driven: the case transition calls it inside its own request, the read is called by the case record screen through gateway-bff, and the fill is started by the Schedule. The latest state change is read from the decision-log contract at the time of the fill, so the service subscribes to no topic and holds no inbox.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| NextActionCheckWorkflow | Workflow, started by the `next-action-check` Schedule | `rwb-integration` | Input: business date, run window. Output: counts of filled, unchanged, missing and failed cases |
| findCasesWithoutNextAction | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: business date. Output: the active cases with no next action, read through the rwb-case contract |
| resolveNextAction | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: caseId, ruleId, packageVersion, business date. Output: the resolve answer; the workflow-kit types `RuleResult` and `NoPackageInForce` are used and no rule engine is run |
| fillNextAction | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Input: caseId and the resolve answer. Output: filled, unchanged or missing; calls the rwb-case contract in one call and raises at most one task per case |

The three activities carry the retry policy of the workflow kit, and `NoPackageInForce` is a non-retryable outcome of `resolveNextAction`.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Cadence | Documented fields | Legacy reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| `next-action-check` | Every 5 minutes | Schedule ID `next-action-check`, overlap policy SKIP, catch-up window, business date and run window input, the workflow `NextActionCheckWorkflow` | JOB-05 Timer check, the next action step |

The cadence of 5 minutes is the legacy cadence; the catch-up window and the overlap window are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0667; ASM-1184) and are values of the deployment (`RWB-P2-E2035-OPS`).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| job_catalog | rwb_integration | P2 (Ownership Map; TSD P2 v3 T3.1) | One row for the `next-action-check` Schedule: job_id, job_name, owner_role, schedule_text, runbook_path, expected_minutes, alert_after_minutes |
| decision_record | rwb_integration | PLT library, created in rwb_integration (DP-03) | The local decision record of a fill, written by the library in the same transaction as the record |

No case table, no task table, no role table and no rule table is owned or read directly: the case facts, the task write, the role rows and the rule row come through their owners' contracts (DP-01, BR12). The service holds no ACE view and no copy of a case field.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| REST | 3 provided, 8 named paths consumed | Resolve, read and fill provided; the case facts, the case list, the catalog row, the role class, the service level, the calendar, the latest state change, the authorise check and the case write consumed; one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream |
| Kafka | None declared; 1 published by the decision-record library | `rwb.decision-record.v1` carries DecisionRecorded on the service's behalf on a fill (DP-03) |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.integration`, module `nextaction`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.integration.nextaction`; front end `src/modules/recovery/caserecord/NextActionPanel.tsx`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables; the case facts and the task write come through the rwb-case contract | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`; here the record of a fill is the service's own and the record of a move is rwb-case's | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit types and the catalog read through rwb-decision's registry; the evaluation itself stays with the case workflow, so no second rule engine runs | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | No ACE read in this story: the case facts come from rwb-case and no view is read | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case for the calendar key | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case for the role class, the service level and the calendar rows | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule `next-action-check` and the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/integration/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.integration.events.v1`; the naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in `rwb_integration`: the `job_catalog` row and the library table | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route for the SCR-03 header | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-04 applies as a prohibition as well as a rule: the kit's `RuleResult` and `NoPackageInForce` types and the version-in-force check are used, and the package is never evaluated a second time in this service (ASM-1185). DP-03 applies on both sides of the seam: this service writes the record of its fill, and rwb-case writes the record of the move.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| NextActionController | Controller | The three operations; input validation; the problem mapping of section 14 |
| NextActionResolveService | Service | BR1, BR5, BR7, BR9 and BR10: reads the catalog row, resolves the owner and the waiting flag, and assembles the resolve answer without writing |
| TimerSpecResolver | Service | BR3, BR4 and BR8: pure functions over the timer spec, the service level and the calendar rows |
| OwnerResolver | Service | BR5 and BR9: the owner role, the owner name and the owner user from the case queue role and the role class |
| NextActionReadService | Service | The read of SCR-03: case facts, latest state change, catalog row, role rows and the overdue marker |
| NextActionFillService | Service | The fill: finds the cases, resolves each one, records the decision, calls the rwb-case write, raises at most one task |
| RuleCatalogClient | Client | Calls `RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion)` and caches a row per rule and version (DP-04) |
| CaseClient | Client | Calls the rwb-case contract for the case facts, the case list and the next-action write |
| ReferenceDataClient | Client | Calls the reference-data and parameter contract for the role class, the service level and the calendar rows (DP-07, DP-06) |
| DecisionLogClient | Client | Calls the decision-log contract for the latest state change of a case (DP-03) |
| AccessCheckClient | Client | Calls the rwb-access authorise contract for Case record R or U and the scope, cached by the guard library |
| DecisionRecordWriter | Library client | Writes the local decision record of a fill and lets the library publish DecisionRecorded; a failure fails the fill and nothing is written |
| ScheduleRunRepository | Repository | Reads and writes the `job_catalog` row and the run outcome of the Schedule |
| NextActionPanel | React component | SCR-03's header: the action, the owner, the due date, the rule and version, the waiting text, the overdue marker and the missing message |

**Database and migrations**

- One migration in the `rwb_integration` sequence adds the `job_catalog` row of `next-action-check` and the library table `decision_record` (DP-15).
- No case column, no case table and no copy of a case, role or rule row lives in `rwb_integration` (DP-01, BR12).
- The service connects with its own login holding grants on `rwb_integration` only, and no grant on `recovery` or on another `rwb_*` schema (DP-02). The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0667; ASM-1177).

**Configuration and reference data**

- Package version "RES-2026.12" and the rows R-RES-04, R-SET-13, R-RES-03, R-DEV-05 and R-RES-07 are the legacy values of this story and are carried unchanged; they are rows of the RESTRUCTURE registry in rwb-decision and are loaded by RWB-E2-042 and RWB-P7-E2035-APP (ASM-1181).
- The service levels and timers rows are seeded with 5 working days per state until the DL22 values are loaded, and the calendar rows 2026-12-31 and 2027-01-01 are loaded under `rwb.calendar.bank-holidays` (RW-REFADM).
- The role names and classes are rwb-access and rwb-case reference rows; no role code and no class value is written in code (DP-07).
- The legacy flag `rwb.casewf.next-action` is kept as the legacy reference of the switch; the switch itself is a feature flag of the platform flag library (ASM-1186).

**Build steps**

1. Publish the resolve operation with the timer resolver and the owner resolver, against the catalog, reference-data and case fakes; AC1, AC2, AC3, AC5, AC7, AC12.
2. Add the missing path: the flag, the task raise and the answer that carries no due date; AC6.
3. Add the read operation and its composition, with the overdue marker and the closed-case answer; AC1, AC4, AC8.
4. Add the four columns to the case list and the export responses of RWB-P2-E2033-APP; AC4.
5. Write NextActionCheckWorkflow and its three activities, with the idempotent fill and the one-task rule; AC9, AC11.
6. Register the `next-action-check` Schedule with its `job_catalog` row and its overlap and catch-up values.
7. Add the access test, the no-version test and the contract test of the three operations; AC13, AC14.
8. Run the contract-fake suite of section 12.8 so the story builds before rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision land.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.casewf.next-action`. Off: the resolve answers 404 with MSG-GEN-006 for a caller outside the release, the fill does not run, the four columns are hidden and the panel is not served. The flag value comes from the platform flag library and is never a value of this service.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass and the report of active cases with no next action reads zero on the SIT data set after the `next-action-check` Schedule has run.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P2-023 | The case has no next action or no due date | This case has no next action. It is on the exception list for {team}. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No RESTRUCTURE version is in force | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A case changed between the read and the write, or a fill repeats a case already filled | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role lacks Case record R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the reader's scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required input of an operation is missing | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A consumed contract does not answer inside the budget, or the flag is off | The service is not available. Try again in a few minutes. |

For MSG-P3-027 in this story {check} is "package in force" and {detail} names the package code RESTRUCTURE and the business date only. The texts of MSG-P2-023, MSG-P3-027, MSG-GEN-004, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 are the legacy texts of RWB-E2-035 and are copied unchanged; MSG-GEN-001 and MSG-GEN-006 are the platform texts and are not restated here. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-03 Case record, states Read only, Editable and On hold: the header shows the next action, its owner, its due date and the rule ID with its version; a wait shows "Waiting for {owner}" and the wait end date; an overdue action carries the text "Overdue"; a missing action shows MSG-P2-023. The header is served by the gateway-bff composite route, which calls this service once and merges the answer into the case screen model (DP-19).

SCR-02 Case list: the next action, next action owner and due date columns with the overdue marker, on the rows of the case list of RWB-P2-E2033-APP. SCR-09 Exception queue: the team manager sees the `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` tasks rwb-case raised. The field-level layout, the masking and the composite route of the header are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0667; ASM-1182).

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: action text, owner role, timer, role class, service levels, calendar and route states are data rows of the catalog, the reference tables and the parameters.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or prompts: the next action holds rule text and role codes only, and the case is carried by its case ID.
- No read of another service's tables and no ACE view: the case facts, the task write and the catalog row come only through the rwb-case contract, the role and service level rows only through the reference-data contract, the calendar only through the parameters contract and the state change only through the decision-log contract (DP-01, DP-05).
- The parser recognizes timer patterns; it never holds a duration for a named state.
- The rule row is read only through `RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion)`; no workbook, no drl_source and no rule table is read by this story (BR13).
- One evaluator: the move is evaluated by the case workflow's `EvaluateRules` activity, and this service resolves the fired rule without running a second rule engine.
- rwb-case is the only writer of the case row and of the exception task; the resolve operation writes nothing (BR12).
- The Schedule carries the overlap policy SKIP and raises at most one open `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` task per case.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-035 for rwb-access. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner, a team manager or an internal auditor who reads the next action of a case**, I want **the access service to answer whether my role may read that case's next action, which scope admits the case, and what the role named as the owner is called and of which class it is**, so that **the next action reaches only the people entitled to it and always names its owner in the words the role catalogue holds**.

Inside `rwb-access` this is the access-side capability of legacy RWB-E2-035:

- Service `rwb-access`, schema `rwb_access`, REST base `/api/recovery/access/v1`, topic `rwb.access.events.v1` with event names `rwb.access.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-access` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`.
- The capability answers two questions behind the service contract of wave 1: does the caller hold Case record right R on this case, and does the scope in force admit it (`POST /authorise`); and what are the name, the class and the default scope of the role code the next action names (`GET /role-catalogue/{roleCode}`).
- The next action itself — the action text, the owner role code, the due date, `next_action_waiting`, the rule ID and its version, the `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` task and its cancellation, the JOB-05 check, the read endpoint and the case list and export columns — is the primary slice `RWB-P2-E2035-CON` and `RWB-P2-E2035-APP`, with the case fields at P3 and the rule row, the package version and the decision-log query at P7. This story builds no screen, starts no timer and runs no workflow.
- The case facts the decision needs — the case ID, its owner, its team and the queue role of the case — arrive in the authorise request. `recovery_case`, `queue` and `task` are P3's, so this story reads no case table (DP-01).
- The policy the answers come from is data in `rwb_access`: `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule` and `role_conflict`, with the matrix version in force (`PM-2026.12`). Loading and approving a policy pack is the load path of RWB-P4-AD002-APP and RWB-P4-AD004-APP.
- The access log is a decision-record entry on `rwb.decision-record.v1` written through the local library of DP-03: `AC-READ` for a granted read of the next action, `AC-DENY` for a refusal that carries no case data (FEAT-ACA-07, FEAT-ACA-08).

The legacy behaviour carried into the access service is unchanged: a reader whose roles hold no Case record R is refused with MSG-P4-002 and sees no next action (legacy AC13), a case outside the reader's scope is answered as not found, the owner shown for a role whose name and class are data is the role's name, and a role of a customer-party class is the case for the waiting text of BR5 of the legacy key.

##### 2. Business rationale

A case owner today reads the case history to work out what is owed next, and a case can wait for weeks with nobody owing anything on it. The rule package that moves the case already holds the action, the owner role and the timer, and the Workbench copies them onto the case; two parts of that copy belong to this service. The owner is a role code, so the words the case owner reads — "Restructuring officer (FCR)", "Waiting for Customer (borrower):" — come from the role catalogue, and if they are written in code a new role or a renamed role needs a release. The next action is also case data, so who may read it is an access decision rather than a screen decision: today any role that reaches the case list sees it, and NFR-042 requires every read of the case store to be logged.

This story supplies the access answer and the role catalogue behind the next action. It meets REQ-WKM-012 on the owner, REQ-WKM-014 on visibility, REQ-WKM-015 and REQ-WKM-016 on the case that has no next action or is overdue, and supports REQ-WKM-013 without reading the rule row. The measures are the FSD one, rule and limit changes made without a code release at 100 percent, because roles and the matrix are versioned data, and the legacy one, the count of active cases with no next action at zero, which this slice supports by keeping the exception task readable to the team manager it is raised for. Under Architecture v5 the access decision is a cached answer of `rwb-access`, each service authorises its own object against it within the 2 s budget, and the answer is one hop (slide 10 note; DP-11).

This story implements the answer behind the authorise operation for the next-action read and adds the role-catalogue operation |
| RWB-P2-E2035-CON | The next-action facts the request and the tests are built from: the case, the action text, the owner role code, the due date, `next_action_waiting`, the rule ID and the rule version, as the primary slice publishes them. Which of them an authorise request carries is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2322; ASM-3863) |
| RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03), written in the same transaction as the answer |
| RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The reference-data client library and contract that carry LOV-SCOPE, LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-ROLE-CLASS with the version in force (DP-07); the list table stays P3's and no scope name, capability area or role class is written in code |
| RWB-PLT-E1047-CON | The naming library behind the topic and event names of DP-14 |

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E2-035, owned by other services where they say so:

- Permission matrix version `PM-2026.12` is in force and gives CASE_RECORD right R to the reader roles of the background below. The TSD RBAC matrix tabulates three capability areas only, so those letters are read from the pack as data (GAP-2324; ASM-3865).
- Masking version `MASK-SIT-01` is in force (FSD A2.5). The next-action fields themselves are not personal, so no masking row covers them and they come back clear.
- The roles `RW-RESTRUCT`, `CU-BORROW` and `SY-CASEWF` exist in the role catalogue with the names of the background; `CU-BORROW` is of a customer-party class, which the list of role classes does not carry (GAP-2323; ASM-3864).
- The next-action read, its columns in the case list and the export, and the `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` task exist (RWB-P2-E2035-APP; RWB-P3-E2035-APP).
- The caller signed in through Entra ID with multi-factor authentication and holds at least one Recovery role; with no role the answer is 401 with MSG-P4-001 (FSD P4 A2.1).
- The database login is the rwb-access login (DP-02). Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2322; ASM-3863); the story says "the rwb-access login (DP-02)" and never the shared monolith login.

##### 4. Flow

1. Caller: a person opens SCR-03 Case record, or reads the next-action columns of the case list. gateway-bff resolves the session and calls the service that owns the next action; that service builds the authorise request from its own rows and the rule package facts.
2. Caller: the request names the area `CASE_RECORD`, the right `R`, the case ID, the case owner, the team code and the queue role of the case, and the field IDs the screen shows — DF-CAS-049 to DF-CAS-053. The full attribute set is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2322; ASM-3863).
3. `rwb-access`: resolves the caller's roles from the session the ACE common module resolved at sign-in, and the rights from `permission` for the matrix version in force, `PM-2026.12`. `role`, `permission` and their versions are read from `rwb_access` only.
4. `rwb-access`, right check: no CASE_RECORD R for any role the caller holds gives a refusal, 403 with MSG-P4-002 naming the action, and no next-action fact in the answer (BR1). The refusal is written as an `AC-DENY` entry (BR7).
5. `rwb-access`, scope check: the case is in scope when its attributes satisfy the caller's `default_scope` in force, read from LOV-SCOPE through the reference-data contract of DP-07 — OWN for a case the caller owns, TEAM for a case of the caller's team, REGION for a case of the caller's region, ALL for any case (BR2). A case outside it is answered 404 with MSG-P4-003 and no case data, so the answer never confirms that a case exists (BR2).
6. `rwb-access`, markers: each field ID is answered `masked` or `clear` from `masking_rule` for the masking version in force and the caller's roles; a field with no covering row is masked (BR3). The next-action field IDs are not personal and come back clear.
7. `rwb-access`: writes one `AC-READ` decision record through the library of DP-03 with the case ID and the field IDs and their markers, and returns the answer inside the 2 s timeout of DP-11 (BR6, BR7).
8. Caller, role labels: for the owner role code of the next action it calls `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/role-catalogue/{roleCode}` and gets the role name, the role class and the default scope under the matrix version in force, so it can show "Restructuring officer (FCR)" and produce the waiting text of the legacy BR5 for a party class (BR4, BR5).
9. `rwb-access`: caches the authorise answer and the role rows for the matrix version in force; a caller that asks again under the same version is answered from the cache and reads no matrix row twice, and the read still writes its own `AC-READ` entry (BR8).
10. Policy change: a new matrix version or a role change is approved through the load path, `rwb-access` writes the rows and publishes `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` in the same transaction. Every caller and the local cache drop the earlier answer and the next request is served under the new version, with no deployment (BR8).

Every answer, granted or refused, is written before it is returned; when the record cannot be written nothing is returned, the call answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 and an incident is raised, so no read of a next action is ever unlogged (BR7).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The case is outside the caller's scope | Not found: 404 with no case data; one `AC-DENY` entry | MSG-P4-003 | AC3 |
| X2 | The caller holds no role with Case record R | Refused before any case fact is read: 403, no case data, no next-action fact | MSG-P4-002 | AC2 |
| X3 | The decision record cannot be written | Nothing is returned: 503 with no case data, and an incident is raised to the platform administrator queue | MSG-P7-003 | AC9 |
| X4 | The token carries no Recovery role, or no second factor | No answer is given: 401 before the policy is read | MSG-P4-001 | BR1 |
| X5 | The role code has no row in force, or is inactive | 404 and no role name; the caller shows the role code as it stands and never a guessed name; the message is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2322; ASM-3863) | Placeholder | BR5 |
| X6 | Two roles of the caller conflict, for example RW-SECADM with a business role | The sign-in access check refuses the session from the `role_conflict` rows this service holds; no authorise request is made | MSG-P4-006 | BR9 |
| X7 | A cached answer outlives a policy change | The version-keyed entry is dropped on `AccessPolicyChanged` and the next ask is answered under the new version; no stale grant is served | None | AC7 |
| X8 | The caller is an agent or a service identity | The same checks run under the service identity's roles; a service identity with no role is refused 401, and a role of the non-human class gives no waiting text | MSG-P4-001 | AC6 |
| X9 | A reference list the answer needs is not available | No answer is given rather than a guessed one: 503, and the refusal is recorded | MSG-GEN-006 | BR2 |

A read that carries both an escalation grant and the caller's own scope is not a case of this story: the escalation scope of RWB-E2-015 is RWB-P4-E2015-APP's.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds and tests against RWB-P2-E2035-CON and its fake; reads its own schema only and calls no other service at run time |
| Negotiable | The policy pack — roles, names, classes, scopes and their versions — is data; the story fixes the shape of the two answers and the refusal behaviour only |
| Valuable | The right people see the next action, nobody else is told the case exists, and the owner is named and classed from data so a new role needs no release |
| Estimable | One answer behind an existing operation, one new read operation, one cache, one decision-record path and two indexes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests; no screen, no timer, no workflow and no case field |
| Testable | Every criterion below has a test case in section 16; the next-action side is a published fake |
