AC1 to AC9 are the criteria this story owns; the fourteen criteria of the legacy key (AC1 to AC14) are owned by RWB-P2-E2035-APP and are proved against this story's answers. In AC1 to AC3 the two assertions that belong to this service are the decision it names, the scope it used and the markers on the field IDs; the next action itself is the fake's. AC4 to AC6 prove that the owner label and its class are data rows with a version, not constants, which is what makes a renamed role or a new role need no release. AC7 and AC8 prove the cache behaves on the policy event rather than on a clock, and that a grant and a refusal are both recorded. AC9 proves the log-first rule: no unlogged read is ever returned. In every case the request and the answer carry identifiers and markers, never a personal value.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The right comes from the permission matrix version in force; a caller whose roles hold no Case record R is refused with MSG-P4-002 and no next-action fact | Legacy AC13 and X9; FSD P4 A2.4 VR-P4-004-1; TSD P4 T6.2 |
| BR2 | A case is in scope when its attributes satisfy the caller's `default_scope` in force: OWN, TEAM, REGION or ALL. A case outside it is answered 404 with MSG-P4-003 and no case data | FSD P4 A2.14 VR-P4-014-1; TSD P4 T3.2 LOV-SCOPE |
| BR3 | A field ID is answered `masked` unless a `masking_rule` row for a role the caller holds and that field says unmasked for the masking version in force; with no covering row it is masked | FSD P4 A2.5; NFR-039; NFR-040 |
| BR4 | The role catalogue answers the role name, the role class and the default scope of a role code under the matrix version in force, and names that version; it holds no permission row and no personal value | Legacy section 12 (`ReferenceData.role(roleCode)` returning roleName and roleClass); TSD P4 T3.1 `role`; FSD P4 A2.3 |
| BR5 | A role code with no row in force, or an inactive row, is answered 404 with no name and no class; the caller shows the role code and never a guessed name | Legacy BR9; TSD P4 T3.1 `is_active` |
| BR6 | The owner shown for a next action whose owner role is the role of the case's queue is the case owner, otherwise the role name; the role name and class are this story's, the queue role is P3's | Legacy BR9; `queue.role_code`; ASM-3863 |
| BR7 | Every granted read writes one `AC-READ` entry with the case ID and the field IDs with their markers before the answer is returned, and every refusal writes one `AC-DENY` entry with the area and the right and no case data | FSD P4 A2.7 AC-P4-007-01 and AC-EXC-P4-007-04; FEAT-ACA-07; FEAT-ACA-08 |
| BR8 | An answer is cached for the matrix version in force and dropped when `AccessPolicyChanged` arrives, so a policy or role change takes effect with no deployment and no stale grant is served | FSD P4 AC-P4-004-01; Architecture v5 slide 43; DP-11 |
| BR9 | Role codes, role names, role classes, scope values, capability areas, field IDs and every version are data; no business value is written in code | FSD P4 BR-P4-004, BR-P4-005, BR-P4-014; TSD P4 T3.2 |
| BR10 | The case facts used by a decision arrive in the request; no table of `rwb_case`, `rwb_decision` or `rwb_source_data` is read | DP-01; ownership map |

Target-service statements that make the rules hold in `rwb-access`:

- BR1 is a read of `permission` for the caller's roles and the `matrix_version` in force; the letters C, R, U, D and A are the five-character field of TSD P4 T3.1 and the answer names the version it used.
- BR2 is the scope rule of `ScopeRule`, comparing the attributes of the request with the `default_scope` read through DP-07; OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL are list values, never Java constants, and the attribute names of a request are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2322; ASM-3863).
- BR3 is a read of `masking_rule` by `field_id`, `role_code` and `masking_version`; the answer carries markers, never values.
- BR4 and BR5 are one indexed read of `role` by `role_code` under the matrix version in force; the version named in the answer is the one the role rows were loaded with (GAP-2325; ASM-3866).
- BR6 is the reason the request carries the queue role: this story supplies the role name and class and the caller applies the substitution, so the service needs no case row.
- BR7 is one `RecordAndApply` transaction: the record is written first, the answer is returned after it commits, and a failure answers 503 with MSG-P7-003 and changes nothing (X3).
- BR8 is a cache keyed by the matrix version; the `AccessPolicyChanged` entry is published by the same transaction that writes the new rows.
- BR9 is visible in the code review: no role code, role name, role class, scope name, capability area, field ID or version string appears in a constant.
- BR10 is the reason there is no case repository: the service holds `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict`, the decision record and the outbox, and nothing else.

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status, writes no next-action field and creates or cancels no task: those are the primary slice's. It owns no workflow and no Schedule.

The only states this story has are the states of its two answers:

| Answer state | When | What the caller gets | Record written |
|---|---|---|---|
| Granted | The caller holds Case record R and the case is in scope | The decision, the scope it used, the matrix version and the field markers | `AC-READ` |
| Refused, no right | No role of the caller holds Case record R | 403 MSG-P4-002, no case data | `AC-DENY` |
| Not found | The caller holds the right and the case is outside the scope | 404 MSG-P4-003, no case data | `AC-DENY` |
| Not answered | The record cannot be written, or the policy cannot be read | 503, no case data | None; the failure is raised as an incident |
| Role resolved | The role code has a row in force | Name, class, default scope and matrix version | None; the catalogue is a read |
| Role not resolved | No row in force, or an inactive row | 404, no name and no class | None |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Case record R with default scope OWN: reads the next action of a case it owns |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Case record R with default scope TEAM: reads the next action of a case of its team, including the case that carries `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` |
| RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL, RW-COMPLAIN, RW-FRAUD, RW-LEGAL | Case record R with the role default scope: read the next action of a case within it |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Case record R with default scope ALL: reads any next action |
| RW-REFADM and every role with no Case record R | Refused with MSG-P4-002; no next-action fact is returned |
| SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES, systems and agents | Ask the same questions for their own service under their own roles; a non-human role brings no waiting text |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Owns the action, owner and timer columns of the rule rows and loads them through the rule package store; this story reads none of them |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads the service levels, the timers and the holiday list of the primary slice; this story reads no such row |
| RW-SECADM, security administrator | Approves the matrix and the role rows through the load path stories; this story reads the versions in force and publishes the change |

Reading is the whole of this story: it grants or refuses a read, names a role and writes the record of it. It changes no case, no role row and no policy row; a policy row changes only through the load path of RWB-P4-AD002-APP and RWB-P4-AD004-APP, and break-glass access stays with the wave-1 stories of the service.

The database login is per service (DP-02). Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2322; ASM-3863); the story refers to "the rwb-access login (DP-02)".

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Table in rwb_access | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-REF-034 to DF-REF-039 | `role` | id, role_code, role_name, role_class, default_scope, entra_group | Read |
| DF-REF-040 to DF-REF-044 | `permission` | id, role_id, capability_area, letters, matrix_version | Read |
| DF-REF-198 to DF-REF-204 | `masking_rule` | id, role_code, field_id, unmasked, masking_version, valid_from, valid_to | Read |
| DF-REF-205 to DF-REF-211 | `role_conflict` | id, role_code, conflicts_with, reason, conflict_version, valid_from, valid_to | Read (the sign-in check, X6) |
| DF-REF-027 to DF-REF-033 | `lov_value` | LOV-SCOPE, LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-ROLE-CLASS, read through the reference-data contract of DP-07 | Read through the contract; the table is P3's |
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision record (local library, DP-03) | the `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entries: code, actor, area, right, case ID, actions, decided at | Write |
| (outbox) | outbox library table in `rwb_access` | the `AccessPolicyChanged` row | Write |
| (inbox) | `processed_event` | event_id, consumer, processed_at; used by the policy listener | Write |

The field IDs the answer marks — DF-CAS-049 `next_action_text`, DF-CAS-050 `next_action_owner_role`, DF-CAS-051 `next_action_due_date`, DF-CAS-052 `next_action_rule_id` and DF-CAS-053 `next_action_waiting` — appear in the answer as identifiers with a marker only, and their values are the primary slice's. None of them is personal data, so no `masking_rule` row covers them and they come back clear (BR3).

The case facts of a request — the case ID, its owner, its team and the queue role — are read from the request and never from a table: `recovery_case`, `queue` and `task` are P3's, and no foreign key and no query crosses a schema (DP-01, BR10). Which attributes a request must carry is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2322; ASM-3863). Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Operation | Path | Status | What this story decides behind it |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | Existing from wave 1 in RWB-P4-E1037-CON | The right, the scope and the field markers for one area, right, case and field list. Errors 401 (MSG-P4-001), 403 (MSG-P4-002), 404 (MSG-P4-003), 503 (MSG-P7-003) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/role-catalogue/{roleCode}` | New in this story | The role name, class, default scope and matrix version of one role code; 200, 401, 404 (BR5), 503 |

`GET /me/permissions` and `GET /masking-policies` are the same service's operations and are used by the screens; they are unchanged here. `GET /admin/roles` (API-P4-007) is the Platform administration list and is not used on this path, because a service identity holds no letter there. `GET /doa-limits` belongs to the delegation slice.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The case facts arrive in the authorise request, built by the caller from its own rows; this story calls no service at run time. The shape it expects is the one RWB-P2-E2035-CON publishes for the next action, and that contract is used as a fake in the tests (12.8) and as the alignment reference in the build. That the authorise request carries those facts rather than an object reference is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2322; ASM-3863).

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` | `rwb.access.events.v1` | P4 | policy kind and version | the policy kind (permission matrix, roles, masking), the version label, the valid-from date and the change reference |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | PLT library; consumed by P7 | caseId where there is one, else the actor reference | the hash-chained `AC-READ` or `AC-DENY` record |

CloudEvents 1.0 envelope. Neither payload carries a personal value: the `AC-READ` record carries field IDs and markers, the `AC-DENY` record carries the area and the right only, and the policy event carries version labels.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. A role or matrix change is written and published by the same service, so the cache is dropped on the commit that publishes `AccessPolicyChanged`; the topic exists for the other services' caches (Architecture v5 slide 43: every holder of permission data consumes it for cache refresh).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. This story runs no Temporal workflow and registers no activity on `rwb-access`.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The JOB-05 next-action check is the primary slice's and becomes a Temporal Schedule on `rwb-integration`; the six-monthly access review list (JOB-18) is RWB-P4-AD008-APP. This story starts no Schedule.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access`, module `access/nextaction`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.access.nextaction`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 is the reason the request carries the case facts: `recovery_case`, `queue` and `task` are P3's, so the answer is built from identifiers and never from a joined query. DP-03 is the access log: an `AC-READ` and an `AC-DENY` are decision records on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, so an access question and a decision question are answered from one log. DP-04 is recorded because the legacy key carries the RESTRUCTURE rule row and its package version, which the primary slice reads through the rule catalogue of P7; this slice reads no Drools object and needs no KieBase. DP-05 is recorded because the case the next action belongs to shows customer fields; this answer carries the field IDs and the markers and no value, so no `v_ace_*` view is queried here. DP-06 is recorded because the legacy key carries a feature flag and the timers of JOB-05; this slice reads one flag and no parameter value. DP-07 supplies the three lists with the version in force, because `lov_value` stays with P3 under the ownership map and no scope name, capability area or role class is a Java constant. DP-10 is recorded because the legacy key carries JOB-05; in the target that check is a Temporal Schedule of the primary slice, so this story adds no job. DP-11 is the boundary: one hop, 2 s timeout, cached, and both answers must hold inside it. DP-13, DP-14 and DP-15 are the naming and migration conventions. DP-19 is the route that renders the answers; the screen itself is the case service's.

The platform contracts the DP rows name are preconditions of the service lane already in place behind RWB-P4-E1037-CON in wave 1; this secondary slice adds no new build dependency of its own (metadata H = None; ASM-1664).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| AuthoriseController | Controller | The existing authorise operation on `/api/recovery/access/v1`; validation and problem responses |
| AccessDecisionService | Service | Right, scope and markers for one request, in that order; one answer, one record |
| PermissionResolver | Service | Reads `permission` for the caller's roles and the `matrix_version` in force; resolves the five letters |
| ScopeRule | Service | Compares the attributes of the request with the `default_scope` value in force |
| RoleCatalogueController | Controller | `GET /role-catalogue/{roleCode}` |
| RoleCatalogueService | Service | The role name, class, default scope and matrix version of one role code; no row in force is a 404 (BR5) |
| AccessRecordWriter | Service | The `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entries through the library of DP-03, and the `AccessPolicyChanged` outbox row |
| PolicyCache | Service | The cached answer and role rows per matrix version, dropped on the policy change |
| PolicyChangeListener | Service | Applies a new matrix or role version and publishes `rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1` in the same transaction |
| AccessRepository | Repository | `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule`, `role_conflict`, inbox and outbox in `rwb_access`; no foreign table |

**Database and migrations**

- No new table: `role`, `permission`, `masking_rule` and `role_conflict` exist from the wave-1 stories of the service behind RWB-P4-E1037-CON, and their rows are loaded by the load path stories.
- One migration in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15: `V2035_1__nextaction_access_read_path.sql` adds `ix_role_code_active` on `role (role_code) WHERE is_active` and `ix_permission_role_area_matrix` on `permission (role_id, capability_area, matrix_version)`, so both reads of an answer are index reads inside the 2 s budget of DP-11.
- The rows are versioned by `matrix_version`, `masking_version` and their `valid_from`; this story writes none of them, and a version is never edited in place.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The matrix version and the masking version in force are data: the latest `valid_from` on or before the business date, read from `permission.matrix_version` and `masking_rule.masking_version`. The masking version of SIT is assumed to be MASK-SIT-01 (ASM-3866).
- LOV-SCOPE, LOV-CAPABILITY and LOV-ROLE-CLASS through the reference-data contract of DP-07 (RWB-P3-E1043-CON). The class `CUSTOMER_PARTY` the party roles carry is not in the list of TSD P4 T3.2 (GAP-2323; ASM-3864).
- No parameter row, no timeout constant and no role code in code: the 2 s is the platform standard of the service client, and the cache lives for the matrix version in force (BR8).
- The database login is the rwb-access login (DP-02): Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2322; ASM-3863).

**Build steps**

1. `PermissionResolver` and `ScopeRule` over `permission`, `role` and the reference lists, with the matrix version named in the answer; tests for AC1 to AC3 and a test that a new scope value is accepted as data.
2. `RoleCatalogueService` and its controller over `role` under the matrix version in force, with the 404 of X5; tests for AC4, AC5 and AC6.
3. `AccessRecordWriter` with the `AC-READ` and `AC-DENY` entries written before the answer, and the forced failure of X3; test AC9.
4. The denial path with the refusal shape and no case data; tests for AC2 and AC8.
5. `PolicyCache` and `PolicyChangeListener` with the publish and the drop; test AC7 against the PM-2026.13 fixture.
6. The migration of the two indexes, and a timing test that one answer stays inside the 2 s budget on a policy pack of the loaded size.
7. The contract-fake run of both answers against RWB-P2-E2035-CON and the decision-record fake, so the story builds before the next action exists in the environment.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.access.nextaction.role-labels`, read from the platform feature-flag library under the R-PREC default ruling. Off: the role-catalogue operation answers 404 and the next action shows the role code with no name and no waiting text, so a role label can never be guessed; the access decision, the markers and the access log are unchanged. The switch changes no schema and never widens a scope.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; a caller holding Case record R is granted the next action of a case it may read, a case outside the scope is answered 404 with no case data, a role without the right is refused with no case data, the owner role is returned with its name and class from a versioned row, a role with no row in force is answered 404, a policy change replaces a cached refusal with no deployment, every answer leaves its record, and nothing is returned when the record cannot be written.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | The token carries no Recovery role, or no second factor | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. | The access check before this story's answer (X4) |
| MSG-P4-002 | No role of the caller holds the right in the capability area | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, on the refusal of BR1 |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the caller's scope | This case is not in your scope. | This story, on the refusal of BR2 |
| MSG-P4-006 | Two roles of the caller conflict | {role} may not be held together with {role}. | The access check, from this service's `role_conflict` rows (X6) |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on every answer (X3) |
| MSG-GEN-006 | A list the answer needs is not available | {system} is not available. Your request is queued and will be retried. | This story, on a reference-list failure (X9) |

For MSG-P4-002 the {action} value is the action the caller attempted, for example "read the next action"; for MSG-P4-003 no case fact is echoed, because the message must not confirm that a case exists. An unknown or inactive role code carries no message of its own in the sources (GAP-2322; ASM-3863); the answer is 404 with an RFC 9457 problem response and no name. Every error is a problem response with `messageId`, the text with its placeholders filled and the instance of the request; the Thai text follows DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

This story builds no screen. SCR-03 Case record, SCR-02 Case list and SCR-09 Exception queue are the case service's through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19 (RWB-PLT-N001-CON), and the next action panel and columns are the primary slice's.

What this story decides for those screens is what each state may show:

| Screen | State | What the answer decides |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-03 Case record | Read only, granted | The next action, its owner name from the role catalogue, its due date and the rule ID with its version are rendered; the screen holds no access rule of its own |
| SCR-03 Case record | Waiting | The owner class is a party class, so the caller renders "Waiting for {owner}" with the name from the catalogue; the waiting end date is the primary slice's |
| SCR-03 Case record | Overdue | The overdue marker is the primary slice's; the reader is the one this answer granted, and the read is logged |
| SCR-03 Case record | Refused | The page shows MSG-P4-002 and no case fact, and one `AC-DENY` entry exists |
| SCR-03 Case record | Not found | The page shows MSG-P4-003 and no case fact, and one `AC-DENY` entry exists |
| SCR-03 Case record | Not available | The page shows MSG-P7-003 where the record could not be written, and no case fact |
| SCR-02 Case list | Columns shown | The next action, owner and due date columns are rendered only for the readers this answer grants, row by row |
| SCR-09 Exception queue | Task open | The team manager reads the case behind `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` under the same grant; the task itself is P3's |

A screen that names a role from a constant, or that shows a next action to a reader this service refused, is a defect of the screen: the answer always names the matrix version it used and the catalogue always names the version its rows came from.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: role codes, role names, role classes, scope values, capability areas, field IDs and the matrix version are data rows and list values; the only switch is a platform flag (BR9).
- No personal data in logs, events, the record or the tests. The answer carries identifiers and markers, the `AC-READ` entry carries the case ID and field IDs, the `AC-DENY` entry carries the area and the right, and test data is synthetic with staff as user references.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views: this service stores no customer value and queries no ACE view on this path (DP-05).
- No cross-schema read (DP-01): `recovery_case`, `queue`, `task`, `decision_log_entry` and the `v_ace_*` views are never queried; the case facts arrive in the request and the policy is the service's own.
- One writer for the policy: only the load path stories write a role, a permission or a masking row; this story reads them and publishes the change, so an answer and the policy it names cannot disagree.
- The record is written before the answer: a failure answers 503 with no case data and raises an incident, so no read of a next action is unlogged (BR7).
- The answers are idempotent for a matrix version: the same question under the same version returns the same answer, and the cache is dropped on the policy event rather than on a clock (BR8).
- The feature switch changes one behaviour and no schema, and it never invents a label: off shows the role code and no waiting text.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-035 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **case owner (RW-CASEOWN)**, I want **every active case in rwb-case to carry one next action, its owner and its due date, written in the same transaction as the rule move that put the case into its current state and read from the rule catalogue row that fired**, so that **I never open a case and have to work out what it needs, and a case never waits for weeks with nobody owing anything on it**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A case owner today reads the case history to decide what is owed next, and a case can wait for weeks with nobody owing anything on it. The route-set rules already hold the action, the owner of the next state and the timer for every move, as rows of the RESTRUCTURE rule package. The legacy story copied these onto the case at each move, showed them on the case record and in the case list, and raised a case with no next action to the team manager as an exception.

In the target the case of record and its rule move live in rwb-case. Every move is made by CaseWorkflow: EvaluateRules asks the embedded Drools kit for package RESTRUCTURE on the facts and the business date, the answer names the fired rule and the package version, and RecordAndApply writes the state change, the task, the queue placement, the local decision record and the outbox row in one `rwb_case` transaction. This story adds the next action to that same transaction: NextActionAssigner reads the catalogue row of the firing rule inside the embedded kit by rule ID and package version (DP-04), copies `action_text`, `owner_role` and the rule ID onto `recovery_case`, and TimerSpecResolver turns `timer_spec` into a due date on the working-day calendar with the bank holiday list (DP-06). Because the values are written with the move and never recomputed by a reader, the next action always names the rule and the version that set it, and a later package version never rewrites an action already set.

The split is the realignment work. The legacy `RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion)` read of the monolith, the legacy `RuleEvaluator` call and the legacy `JOB-05` five-minute Quartz check are replaced by the catalogue of the embedded Drools kit with packages from rwb-decision (DP-04), by the platform workflow kit (DP-10) and by the decision-record library and shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03). The legacy operation on the monolith base with path `/cases/{caseId}/next-action` becomes `GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action` on `/api/recovery/case/v1` (DP-13), the four `nextAction` columns of the case list and the export are served from the same five fields, and the panel is composed at the edge by gateway-bff (DP-19). JOB-05 is retired: the fill for cases opened before the switch-on runs as a step of DailyCaseRun under a Temporal Schedule, so no Quartz row and no five-minute timer check survives.

It meets REQ-WKM-012, REQ-WKM-013 and REQ-WKM-016 for the case side and it carries the legacy measure: the count of active cases with no next action, with a target of zero. It owns no legacy acceptance criterion; the fourteen criteria of RWB-E2-035 are exercised across services by RWB-ITG-E2035-ITG and by the other slices of the key, and the fifteen criteria in section 7 are new for this service change.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P2-E2035-CON is published: the `NextAction` resource shape (`text`, `ownerRole`, `ownerName`, `ownerUserId`, `dueDate`, `waiting`, `overdue`, `missing`, `ruleId`, `ruleVersion`) and the consumer stub of the contract. This story builds against that contract and its fake; there is no run-time call to rwb-integration.
- The `rwb_case` schema baseline and the case of record exist from the Epic 1 case story (RWB-P3-E1018-APP): `recovery_case`, `task`, `queue`, `timer` and the outbox table.
- Package RESTRUCTURE version "RES-2026.12" is in force for the business date, with rows R-RES-04, R-RES-03, R-SET-13, R-DEV-05 and R-RES-07, each carrying `action_text`, `owner_role` and `timer_spec`; the rows are loaded through RWB-P3-E2042-APP and read only through the catalogue of the embedded Drools kit.
- The embedded Drools kit is published by RWB-PLT-E1072-CON with the rule packages of RWB-P7-E1073-CON, the workflow kit by RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, the decision-record library and shared topic by RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, and the platform guard library by RWB-PLT-E1037-CON. These platform dependencies are held by the platform stories and are not repeated in the metadata rows (GAP-0734; ASM-1301).
- The service levels and timers rows hold a time per state (DL22). Until the business values are loaded the table is seeded with 5 working days for each state of the route sets in force, as the legacy story assumed; a state left out of the seed has no row (GAP-0734; ASM-1304).
- The bank holiday list is loaded as the parameter `rwb.calendar.bank-holidays` (RW-REFADM) and read through the parameters contract of rwb-case, never from code.
- Roles, role names and role classes are data in rwb-access; the role name and the role class of an owner role are read through the rwb-access contract.
- The reader holds a role with Case record R; the move runs under the rwb-case service identity (DP-02) with the Case record write right.
- The feature switch `rwb.casewf.next-action` is a parameter row and is on.

##### 4. Flow

1. An event for the case, for example CASE_PICKED_UP, reaches rwb-case through the case router; the router dedupes it on `processed_event` and signals or starts CaseWorkflow (workflow ID = case ID) on task queue `rwb-case`.
2. CaseWorkflow passes the event to the running stage child, which asks the rules: the EvaluateRules activity calls the embedded Drools kit for package RESTRUCTURE on the facts of the case (route state, status, owner, queue, team) and the business date. The package model and its checksum are fetched from rwb-decision and the KieBase is swapped only after the checksum is verified (DP-04); `NoPackageInForce` is a refusal, never a default.
3. The answer names the package version, the fired rule ID and the outputs, including `to_state`.
4. RecordAndApply, in the same activity and in one `rwb_case` transaction, moves the case, writes the task row and the queue placement, writes the local decision record through the decision-record library and inserts its outbox row, and calls NextActionAssigner with the rule ID and the package version. A failed write rolls the whole move back, so nothing moves and no next action is set.
5. NextActionAssigner reads the catalogue row of that rule by rule ID and package version from the catalogue of the embedded kit — `action_text`, `owner_role`, `timer_spec` — and copies `action_text`, `owner_role` and the rule ID onto the case as `next_action_text`, `next_action_owner_role` and `next_action_rule_id`. The workbook, the generated DRL source and the `rwb_decision` rule tables are never read.
6. TimerSpecResolver turns `timer_spec` into `next_action_due_date`: "n working days" adds n working days, "n days" with any label before it adds n calendar days, "same day", "Same day" and "immediate" give the business date of the move, "next working day" adds one working day. Working days are Monday to Friday, excluding the dates of the bank holiday list.
7. Any other `timer_spec`, including "None", takes the time of `to_state` from the service levels and timers rows; a rule with no timer never leaves the due date empty by accident.
8. NextActionAssigner sets `next_action_waiting` when the owner role is of class Customer party or Partner user, and the rendered text starts "Waiting for {owner}: ". The role name and the role class are read through the rwb-access contract.
9. When the owner role is the role of the case's queue, the owner shown is the case owner named on the case; otherwise the owner shown is the role name.
10. When no due date can be found from the rule or the table, `next_action_due_date` stays empty and one task NEXT_ACTION_MISSING is raised on the exception queue for RW-TEAMMGR of the case's team, with the warning MSG-P2-023 on the case. The task is raised once: the idempotency key is the case ID and the task code, so at most one open task exists per case.
11. CaseWorkflow holds the due date of the task as a durable timer of the workflow kit (DP-10); no Quartz row and no five-minute timer check is involved.
12. On a case that closes, the next action fields are cleared and an open NEXT_ACTION_MISSING task is canceled in the same transaction as the closure.
13. A case opened before the switch-on is filled by the next-action check step of DailyCaseRun, fired by the DailyCaseRun Temporal Schedule (DP-10). The step finds active cases with `next_action_rule_id` empty or `next_action_due_date` empty, resolves the rule ID and the rule version from the latest state change in the local decision record, fills the action from the catalogue row, or raises the same task once. JOB-05 is retired and no Quartz job is scheduled.
14. Case owner: the case record is served by the gateway-bff composite route, which calls rwb-case `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/next-action` and merges the two answers (DP-19); the panel shows the action, the owner, the due date, the rule with its version, the waiting text and the overdue marker.
15. Team manager: the case list and the export carry `nextAction`, `nextActionOwner`, `nextActionDueDate` and `nextActionOverdue`, read from the same fields; `overdue` is computed at read time from `next_action_due_date`, the business date and the closure of the case, and is never stored.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The rule's `timer_spec` is None or has no fixed duration | The due date is taken from the service levels and timers rows for `to_state` | None | AC4 |
| X2 | No due date can be found from the rule or the table | The due date stays empty; one task NEXT_ACTION_MISSING is raised for the team manager and the warning shows on the case | MSG-P2-023 | AC5 |
| X3 | The due date falls on a weekend or a bank holiday | Working days skip Saturday, Sunday and the bank holiday list | None | AC6 |
| X4 | The case closes | The next action fields are cleared and the open task is canceled in the same transaction | None | AC7 |
| X5 | The same transition is delivered twice | The inbox drops it on `processed_event`; the next action and the due date are unchanged; no second task and no second decision record | None | AC8 |
| X6 | Two transitions on one case commit at the same time | The optimistic lock refuses the second; it is retried against the next version and the next action is that of the rule committed last | MSG-GEN-004 | AC9 |
| X7 | An active case from before the switch-on has no next action | The next-action check step of DailyCaseRun sets it from the latest state change in the local decision record | None | AC10 |
| X8 | The rule's timer is "same day" | The due date is the business date of the move | None | AC11 |
| X9 | The read is called by a role without Case record R, or for a case outside the caller's scope | Refused with 403 for the right and 404 for the scope; nothing is returned and nothing is written | MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 | AC13 |
| X10 | No RESTRUCTURE package version is in force on the business date | `NoPackageInForce`; the move is refused and no next action is written; the case keeps its state and queue | MSG-P3-027 | AC12 |
| X11 | The local decision-record write fails during the move | The transaction rolls back: the state and the next action do not move, the step fails and the move is retried | MSG-P7-003 | AC1 |

The exception of X5 is the inbox of the platform event library, recorded in `processed_event` with the idempotency key of the event; X6 is the optimistic lock on the case version, so a retried move always reads the version it commits against.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds on Day 1 against the RWB-P2-E2035-CON fake and the platform kits of DP-03, DP-04, DP-10, DP-11 and DP-19; no work order sits inside another team's lane |
| Negotiable | The action text, the owner role, the timer spec, the service levels and the holiday list are rows and parameters; the story fixes the behaviour |
| Valuable | Every active case states what is owed, by whom and by when, and the answer names the rule and the version that set it |
| Estimable | One assigner, one timer resolver, one step of the daily workflow, one read operation, two extended read operations, one cancel, one panel |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each of the fifteen criteria of section 7 is one automated test with fixed catalogue rows and dates |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | On every move, the next action text, the owner role and the rule ID come from the catalogue row of the firing rule, read by rule ID and package version inside the embedded Drools kit: `action_text`, `owner_role`, `timer_spec` | FEAT-CWC-28; REQ-WKM-013; D-RCV-36 T6; DP-04 |
| BR2 | The next action is never entered by a person | REQ-WKM-013 |
| BR3 | `timer_spec` "n working days" adds n working days; "n days" with any label before it adds n calendar days; "same day", "Same day" and "immediate" give the date of the move; "next working day" adds 1 working day | catalogue row `timer_spec` |
| BR4 | Any other `timer_spec`, including "None", takes the time of the target state from the service levels and timers rows | DL22 |
| BR5 | The next action is a wait when the owner role is of class Customer party or Partner user; the text starts "Waiting for {owner}:"; the role name and the role class are read through the rwb-access contract | role class; rwb-access contract |
| BR6 | A next action is overdue when its due date is earlier than today and the case is not closed; the flag is computed at read time and never stored | REQ-WKM-012; DF-CAS-051 |
| BR7 | An active case with no due date or no next action raises one NEXT_ACTION_MISSING task to the team manager; at most one open task per case, keyed on the case ID and the task code | REQ-WKM-016 |
| BR8 | Working days are Monday to Friday, excluding the dates of the bank holiday list held under the parameter `rwb.calendar.bank-holidays` | parameters contract (DP-06) |
| BR9 | When the owner role is the role of the case's queue, the owner shown is the case owner; otherwise the role name | `queue.role_code`; rwb-access contract |
| BR10 | The rule version is the package version label of the evaluation, and the next action records the version of the move that set it; a later version does not rewrite an action already set | D-RCV-36 T5, T7; R-UNI-38 |
| BR11 | No RESTRUCTURE version in force is a refusal (`NoPackageInForce`), never a default move and never an empty next action | D-RCV-36 T3; R-UNI-41 |
| BR12 | `next_action_text`, `next_action_owner_role`, `next_action_due_date`, `next_action_rule_id` and `next_action_waiting` are written together with the move or not at all: the state change, the next action, the task, the decision record and the outbox row are one `rwb_case` transaction | DF-CAS-049 to DF-CAS-053; Principle 5; DP-03 |
| BR13 | The catalogue row and the timer spec come from the embedded Drools kit's catalogue with the packages of rwb-decision; the workbook, the generated DRL source and the `rwb_decision` rule tables are never read | D-RCV-36 T3, T6; DP-04; DP-01 |
| BR14 | The next-action check for cases opened before the switch-on is a step of DailyCaseRun under a Temporal Schedule; JOB-05 is retired and no Quartz job, trigger or five-minute check remains | DP-10; D-RCV-36 T2 |
| BR15 | The read operations write nothing and raise no event | REQ-WKM-014 |

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case status: this story does not change a case status. It writes the five next-action fields on `recovery_case` in the same transaction as each move made by CaseWorkflow, clears them on closure, and creates or cancels the NEXT_ACTION_MISSING task.

| Object | From | Trigger | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| task (NEXT_ACTION_MISSING) | OPEN | The case closes with closure reason SETTLED | CANCELED |
| recovery_case (version) | n | A move commits with its next action | n+1 |
| next_action text, owner role, rule ID, due date and waiting flag | Any value | A move commits | The values of the firing catalogue row, or empty when no due date is found |

The case version is the optimistic lock of `recovery_case`; a refused commit is retried against the current version and never writes a second next action from the same event.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| rwb-case service identity (the rwb-case login, DP-02) | Runs the move and the next-action check step; writes the next-action fields, the task, the placement, the timer and the decision record |
| Drools evaluator (SY-RULES identity) | Evaluates package RESTRUCTURE through the embedded kit and returns the rule ID, the package version and the outputs (Rules and parameters R) |
| NextActionAssigner | Reads the catalogue row by rule ID and package version and writes the five fields inside the move's transaction |
| TimerSpecResolver | Turns `timer_spec` into a due date on the working-day calendar; holds no duration for a named state |
| CaseWorkflow | Holds the due date of the task as a durable timer and drives the RecordAndApply transaction; moves no state by itself |
| Decision-record library identity | Writes the local decision record and its outbox row in the same transaction (Decision log C) |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Reads the next action of cases in scope and receives the task of the move (Case record R) |
| RW-RESTRUCT, restructuring officer | Reads the next action of cases in scope (Case record R) |
| RW-LEGAL, legal officer | Reads the next action of cases in scope and works the DEV_WITH_OWNER task (Case record R) |
| CU-BORROW, customer party | Is a wait owner; holds no Workbench right and never reads the case (no Case record right) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads the list and works NEXT_ACTION_MISSING tasks on the exception queue |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Owns the action text, owner role and timer spec columns of the rule rows (Rules and parameters CRUD) |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads the service levels and timers rows and the bank holiday list; holds no Case record right and is refused on the read with MSG-P4-002 |
| No approval applies | The story takes no decision |

| DF-DEC-004, DF-DEC-005 | decision record (local library) | rule_id, rule_version | Write locally in the move's transaction |
| Not a field: the service levels and timers rows and the bank holiday list | reference rows and parameter of rwb-case | the time per state and the holiday dates | Read |

The catalogue row is read only inside the embedded kit by rule ID and package version; this story reads no workbook, no `drl_source` and no `rwb_decision` table (DP-04, DP-01). The field of the rwb-access answer that carries the role class is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0734; ASM-1303); until the field is agreed the story reads the role name and the role class through the platform guard library and its response model. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/case/v1`; owner rwb-case (P3).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/next-action` | The next action of the case: `text`, `ownerRole`, `ownerUserId`, `dueDate`, `waiting`, `overdue`, `missing`, `ruleId`, `ruleVersion` (the `NextAction` resource shape of RWB-P2-E2035-CON); a new operation recorded in the additions file of the contract story | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable: the call writes nothing |
| GET | `/cases` | The case list, extended with `nextAction`, `nextActionOwner`, `nextActionDueDate` and `nextActionOverdue` on each case item (a backward-compatible addition, no field removed) | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable |
| GET | `/cases/export` | The case export, extended with the same four columns (a backward-compatible addition, no column removed) | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable |

Errors: 401 no session (MSG-P4-001), 403 no Case record R (MSG-P4-002), 404 not found or out of scope (MSG-P4-003), 503 store down. `overdue` and `missing` are computed on the read: `overdue` is true when `next_action_due_date` is earlier than the business date and the case is not closed; `missing` is true when `next_action_rule_id` is empty.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | rwb-access (P4), through the platform guard library RWB-PLT-E1037-CON (DP-11) | The Case record right and the scope before a read, and the role name and role class for BR5 and BR9; cached per request | One hop, 2 s |

This story calls no other service at run time. The `NextAction` resource shape and the consumer stub come from RWB-P2-E2035-CON, which is built against and tested with its fake; there is no run-time call to rwb-integration in this story.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 owns the type and the central ledger; every service writes its own record (DP-03) | caseId | decision record reference, rule ID (for example R-RES-04), package version, business date |

The record and its outbox row are written in the same `rwb_case` transaction as the state change and the next action, and relayed with the CloudEvents envelope; no personal data and no account number is carried. This story adds no `rwb.case` event: the case events of the move belong to the stories that own each move.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The next action is set inside the transaction of a move that another story triggers; this story adds no consumer and no handler.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| CaseWorkflow | Workflow (parent, one per case, workflow ID = case ID) | `rwb-case` | Drives the move; the assigner runs inside the RecordAndApply transaction it starts, and the task due date is a durable timer |
| RecordAndApply | Activity (workflow kit) | `rwb-case` | Moves the case, writes the task, the placement and the local decision record, and calls NextActionAssigner to write the five fields in the same transaction |
| DailyCaseRun | Workflow (Schedule and event-started from AceDataReady) | `rwb-case` | Runs the next-action check step, replacing JOB-05 |
| NextActionCheckStep | Step of DailyCaseRun | `rwb-case` | Fills the next action of active cases that have none, or raises one NEXT_ACTION_MISSING task |

No new activity beyond RecordAndApply and the step of DailyCaseRun: the evaluate, the record and the apply are the ones the case workflow already has.

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Workflow | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| DailyCaseRun Temporal Schedule (DP-10) | DailyCaseRun | Fires the daily case run whose next-action check step fills the cases opened before the switch-on |

Nothing else is scheduled: JOB-05 is retired, no Quartz job, trigger or five-minute timer check is created, and the story adds no second Schedule. The time of day of the DailyCaseRun Schedule is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0734; ASM-1302).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| recovery_case | P3 (rwb_case) | The story adds `next_action_text` varchar(1000), `next_action_owner_role` varchar(20), `next_action_due_date` date, `next_action_rule_id` varchar(20) and `next_action_waiting` boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false (DF-CAS-049 to DF-CAS-053), and writes and clears them |
| task | P3 (rwb_case) | The NEXT_ACTION_MISSING task with its `due_at` and its CANCELED status |
| queue | P3 (rwb_case) | `role_code`, read for BR9 |
| timer | P3 (rwb_case) | The screen projection of the due date; the clock itself is the durable timer of CaseWorkflow |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_case | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects of the move and of the decision-record event |
| decision_record | Local table of the RWB-PLT-E1027-CON library, created in rwb_case | The local decision record of the move, with its rule ID and package version (DP-03) |

rwb-case reads no table of another service and holds no foreign key across services (DP-01). The catalogue row of the rule is read inside the embedded kit and no `rwb_decision` table is read or written by this story.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `nextaction`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.nextaction`; front end `src/modules/recovery/case/NextActionPanel.tsx`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The H and C dependencies this table adds are held by the platform and service contract stories and are not repeated in the metadata rows, which carry only the contract dependency of the legacy key: RWB-P2-E2035-CON (GAP-0734; ASM-1301). DP-05 resolves to no ACE view and no rwb-source-data call: the next action needs the rule row and the case row only, so rwb-case reads no `v_ace_*` view. DP-14 resolves to no new topic of its own, because this story publishes only on the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1` and adds no case event; the naming library still supplies the envelope. DP-15 resolves to one migration in `rwb_case`.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| NextActionAssigner | Service | BR1, BR5, BR7, BR9, BR10 and BR12; reads the catalogue row by rule ID and package version and writes the five fields inside the move's transaction |
| TimerSpecResolver | Service | BR3, BR4 and BR8; pure functions with the service levels and the holiday list as inputs, with no duration for a named state |
| NextActionCheckStep | Step of DailyCaseRun | The retired JOB-05 step: fills active cases that have no next action or no due date, or raises the task once (BR7, BR14) |
| NextActionRepository | Repository | Reads and writes the five fields on `recovery_case` in `rwb_case` only |
| NextActionController | Controller | `GET /cases/{caseId}/next-action` and the four fields of the case list and the export |
| ClosureListener | Service adapter | Clears the fields and cancels the open task in the closure transaction |
| NextActionPanel | React component | The next action on the SCR-03 header with the waiting text, the rule and its version, the overdue marker and the MSG-P2-023 warning |

**Database and migrations**

- Migration `V2035_1__next_action.sql` adds to `recovery_case`: `next_action_text` varchar(1000), `next_action_owner_role` varchar(20), `next_action_due_date` date, `next_action_rule_id` varchar(20) and `next_action_waiting` boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false (DF-CAS-049 to DF-CAS-053).
- `next_action_owner_role` is validated against the role list by the service, with no database check constraint on the list value.
- One index for the check step: `ix_case_next_action_missing ON recovery_case (team_code) WHERE closed_date IS NULL AND next_action_due_date IS NULL`, so the page of active cases with no due date is read without a scan.
- No new table: the task, the queue, the timer, the outbox and the local decision record already exist in `rwb_case` from the Epic 1 story and the platform libraries.
- The migration runs in the rwb-case Flyway sequence of the service's own schema (DP-15); no other schema is touched.

**Configuration and reference data**

- Package RESTRUCTURE version "RES-2026.12" with rows R-RES-04, R-RES-03, R-SET-13, R-DEV-05 and R-RES-07, each with its action text, owner role and timer spec (RW-COE, through RWB-P3-E2042-APP). The version in force per environment is read from the rwb-decision registry on every evaluation; there is no lock file.
- The service levels and timers rows (DL22, RW-REFADM): until the business values are loaded the table is seeded with 5 working days for each state of the route sets in force, as the legacy story assumed, so a state left out of the seed has no row (GAP-0734; ASM-1304).
- Parameter `rwb.calendar.bank-holidays` with the holiday dates (RW-REFADM), read through the parameters contract of rwb-case (DP-06).
- Roles, role names and role classes in rwb-access; the role name and the role class are read through the contract (GAP-0734; ASM-1303).
- Feature switch `rwb.casewf.next-action` as a parameter row: off means the assigner is not called, the check step does not run, and the panel and the four columns are hidden.

**Build steps**

1. Add the migration and the five fields to `recovery_case`, and extend the generated types with the `NextAction` schema of RWB-P2-E2035-CON.
2. Write TimerSpecResolver with a table of `timer_spec` cases taken from the route-set rows and the service level lookup, and unit tests for AC4, AC6 and AC11.
3. Write NextActionAssigner against the catalogue of the embedded kit and call it from RecordAndApply in the same transaction; tests for AC1, AC2 and AC3.
4. Add the NEXT_ACTION_MISSING task, its idempotency key and its cancel on closure; tests for AC5 and AC7.
5. Add the inbox dedupe and the optimistic lock paths around the assigner; tests for AC8 and AC9.
6. Add NextActionCheckStep to DailyCaseRun under its Schedule and retire JOB-05; test for AC10.
7. Write NextActionController with the access check, the scope, the overdue flag and the four fields of the list and the export; tests for AC13 and AC14, and the contract test for AC12.
8. Write NextActionPanel and the composite-route contract test; test for AC15.
9. Contract-fake run of every consumed answer in isolation, so the story builds before rwb-integration and rwb-access land.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the report of active cases with no next action reads zero on the SIT data set after the DailyCaseRun step has run, and every next action names its rule ID and package version.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P2-023 | The case has no next action or no due date (new) | This case has no next action. It is on the exception list for {team}. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No RESTRUCTURE version is in force | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A transition commits against a changed version | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The local decision-record write fails during the move | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role lacks Case record R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case is outside the reader's scope | This case is not in your scope. |

For MSG-P3-027 in this story {check} is "package in force" and {detail} names the package code RESTRUCTURE and the business date only, never a case fact. For MSG-P2-023 {team} is the team code of the case and nothing else. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-03 Case record, states read only, editable and on hold: the header shows the next action, its owner, its due date and the rule ID with its version; a wait shows "Waiting for {owner}" and the wait end date; an overdue action carries the text "Overdue"; a missing action shows MSG-P2-023. SCR-02 Case list: the next action, next action owner and due date columns with the overdue marker. SCR-09 Exception queue: the team manager sees the NEXT_ACTION_MISSING tasks.

All three are served by the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19), which calls rwb-case, one hop, and merges the answers into the screen model: the browser calls one composite route and no owner service directly. The full read-only case record view, the timer section and the deviation flag remain with RWB-P3-E1023-APP; the queue-view next action column remains with RWB-E2-011.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the action text, the owner role, the timer spec, the service levels and the holiday dates are rows or parameters.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or prompts: the next action holds rule text only, and logs carry case IDs and rule IDs, never account numbers, names or identity numbers; the workflow payloads pass the payload codec.
- No read of another service's tables: the catalogue row is read inside the embedded kit, the role name and role class through the rwb-access contract; `rwb_case` holds no foreign key into another schema (DP-01).
- One evaluator: the move calls the embedded Drools kit on the package version of rwb-decision, and no second rule engine decides the target state (DP-04).
- The workbook, the generated DRL source and the `rwb_decision` rule tables are never read by this story; the catalogue is the only source of an action text, an owner role and a timer spec.
- The parser recognises timer patterns; it never holds a duration for a named state.
- A read of the next action writes nothing and raises no event.
- The next action is written before the transaction commits and in the same transaction as the state change, the task and the decision record; a failed write rolls the whole move back (R-UNI-39, DP-03).
- NoPackageInForce is never caught and turned into a default move or an empty next action.
- The decision-record event is written to the outbox in the same transaction and carries IDs and facts only.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-035 for rwb-decision, the registry side of the next action. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As **the case workflow's rule evaluation and the case owner, team manager and internal auditor who read a next action**, I want **the decision service to answer three questions from its own registry — what the row of the rule that moved a case says (action text, owner role, timer spec, to-state), which version of the package is in force, and which rule and rule version set the latest state change of a case in the ledger — without reading a workbook, a generated DRL, a case table or another service's schema**, so that **every next action in the target names the rule and the package version that produced it, and a re-read of an old case gets the row that moved it and never the row of a later version**.

Inside `rwb-decision` this is the registry slice of legacy RWB-E2-035:

- Service `rwb-decision`, schema `rwb_decision`, REST base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, topic `rwb.decision.events.v1` with event names `rwb.decision.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`.
- Behind `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion=`, the operation `RWB-P3-E2042-CON` publishes and `RWB-P2-E2035-CON` consumes as `RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion)`: the row of one rule in one package version — DF-REF-008 `action_text`, DF-REF-010 `owner_role`, DF-REF-011 `timer_spec`, DF-REF-009 `to_state`, DF-REF-003 `rule_version`, DF-REF-297 `drools_rule_name` and DF-REF-298 `outputs`.
- Behind `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId=&latestStateChange=true`, the read the fill uses when a case has no next action: the latest state change of the case, with DF-DEC-004 `rule_id`, DF-DEC-005 `rule_version`, the entry ID and DF-DEC-016 `decided_at`, in `chain_seq` order.
- The version facts both answers carry, read from `rule_package` and `rule_package_version`: the package code, the version label, the version state and whether that version is in force. The version in force per environment is what the callers' embedded kit checks before it evaluates, and no lock file exists.
- Rows are immutable once stored: a row of a SUPERSEDED or ROLLED_BACK version is still answered, which is what makes a re-read of an old case return the action that was set (legacy BR10, legacy AC11).

Not this story, and stated again in section 6 and section 19:

- The five case fields, the `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` task and its cancel, the JOB-05 check, the read endpoint and the case list and export columns are **RWB-P3-E2035-APP**; the resolve, the read and the fill are **RWB-P2-E2035-APP** and **RWB-P2-E2035-CON**.
- The role name and class, the authorise answer, the service levels and timers rows and the calendar are **RWB-P4-E2035-APP**, **RWB-P4-E1037-CON** and **RWB-P3-E1043-CON**. This story returns the owner role as a code and computes no due date.
- The registry load, the six checks, the four-eyes approval, the promotion and the rollback are **RWB-P7-E1073-APP** and **RWB-P7-E2042-APP**. This story reads their rows and writes none of them.
- The cross-service proof is **RWB-ITG-E2035-ITG**; every criterion of this story is proved against the registry alone or through a contract fake.

The database login is the per-service login of DP-02, written only as "the rwb-decision login (DP-02)". Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2411; ASM-4010), and the shared monolith login appears nowhere in this story.

##### 2. Business rationale

A case owner today reads the case history to work out what is owed next, and a case can wait with nobody owing anything on it. The rule package that moves the case already holds the action, the owner and the timer, and the next action copies them onto the case — but only because a caller can ask what a rule row says. In the monolith that question was answered in process by `RuleCatalog.row`, over a table shared by every module; in the target the table is `rwb_decision`'s and every other service reaches it over one contract (DP-01, DP-04, DP-11). Two facts travel with it: the version the row belongs to, and the version that set the last state change of the case, which is where the fill starts when a case has no next action at all.

This story is the rwb-decision half of the RWB-E2-035 split. It supplies the row, the version state and the ledger lookup, and it supplies them read-only: a catalogue row and a ledger entry are evidence, and evidence that can be edited at a read is worthless in audit (NFR-033, NFR-034). It meets REQ-WKM-013 on the rule that set the action, REQ-WKM-012 on every case carrying one, REQ-WKM-016 on the case with none, REQ-WKM-014 on what is shown and REQ-WKM-015 on the version an overdue action is escalated under.

The realignment changes the mechanism, not the business rule:

1. The `rule_row`, `rule_package_version` and `decision_log_entry` rows move into `rwb_decision`, and no other service reads them (DP-01); the DF-REF and DF-DEC field IDs are unchanged.
2. `RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion)` becomes one REST read under `/api/recovery/decision/v1` (DP-13) with a 2 s budget and a cache, instead of an in-process call (DP-11).
3. The decision-log query of the latest state change becomes a filter on the decision-log read of the service, not a second store (DP-03).
4. The rule row, the package version and the ledger entry are read through the service's own schema and its own Flyway sequence (DP-15); the topic and event names of the service are the per-service ones (DP-14).
5. Nothing a business person may change is written in code: the action text, the owner role, the timer spec, the version labels and the version states are rows (DP-06, DP-07).

The measure is the legacy one, the count of active cases with no next action, at zero, plus the registry measure this slice adds: every next action on a case names a rule ID and a package version that the registry can answer for that version, and no answer is served from a superseded row in place of the row that moved the case.

The DP-added H and C dependencies above — H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON, and C RWB-P2-E2035-CON, RWB-P3-E2042-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON — are platform contracts of wave 0 and published contracts an APP story builds against as fakes, so none blocks this story and Ready to start stays Day 1 (GAP-2410; ASM-4009). The registry rows this story reads are the same service's and are in place from the wave-1 stories named above.

Business preconditions carried from RWB-E2-035:

- Package RESTRUCTURE version "RES-2026.12" holds R-RES-04, R-RES-03, R-SET-13, R-DEV-05 and R-RES-07 with the action text, owner role and timer spec of the background below. The valid-from date of that version is GAP-2406: the registry stories carry 2026-12-15 and the legacy tests of this key read it as in force on 11 December 2026; ASM-4005 pins the fixture until it is reconciled.
- The version states are LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK and REFUSED (Temporal and Drools design, adopted by RWB-P7-E1073-APP).
- No RESTRUCTURE version is in state IN_FORCE on 2027-01-04, which is the fixture of legacy AC14.
- Roles and rights: RW-COE holds Rules and parameters R, RW-AUDIT holds Rules and parameters R and Decision log R, and the service identities SY-RULES and SY-CASEWF hold the read letters of their own service. No role holds a write letter on this path.
- Synthetic data only: package codes, version labels, rule IDs, dates, role codes and entry IDs of the legacy story. No real account, customer, party or case appears in a read, a test or a fixture.

##### 4. Flow

1. Caller: the case workflow's `EvaluateRules` activity, holding the `RuleResult` of a fired rule, calls `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion={label}` with the rule ID and the version label the evaluation returned.
2. `RuleCatalogController`: authenticates the session or the service identity, checks Rules and parameters R through the authorise contract of rwb-access, and validates the two parameters. A blank or malformed parameter is 422 with MSG-GEN-001 naming the field (BR7).
3. `VersionStateResolver`: reads the `rule_package` row and the `rule_package_version` row of the label, and the version state and valid-from and valid-to it holds. A label the package does not hold is 404 with MSG-P3-027 for the version check.
4. `RuleCatalogService`: reads one `rule_row` by `rule_id` and `rule_version` through the catalogue index, and builds the answer: action text, owner role, timer spec, to-state, rule version, Drools rule name, the outputs map, the package code, the package version and its state (BR1, BR2).
5. The answer is returned as stored, character for character: the timer spec is a string and the outputs a map, and the service computes no due date, no working-day count and no calendar (BR3). The vocabulary of a timer spec has no list in any source (GAP-2408; ASM-4007).
6. Caller: the fill of a case with no next action calls `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId={caseId}&latestStateChange=true`. `DecisionLogQueryService` reads the `decision_log_entry` rows of the case in `chain_seq` order, takes the newest entry that carries a rule ID and a rule version, and answers the rule ID, the rule version, the entry ID and the decided-at time (BR5).
7. A case with no such entry is answered 200 with an empty result and `missing` true, not an error; a case with one entry answers that entry even when it is old (BR5, BR6).
8. No step of either read writes anything: no rule row, no version row, no ledger entry, no decision record and no outbox row. The read is idempotent for its inputs, and the cache is keyed by package version and dropped when this service promotes or rolls back a version (BR8, BR9).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A call carries no `packageVersion`, a blank `ruleId` or a malformed `caseId` | 422 before any row is read; the field is named and nothing is answered | MSG-GEN-001 | AC4 |
| X2 | The package version label exists but holds no row for the rule ID | 404; no default row, no last row and no row of another version is substituted | MSG-P3-027 | AC4 |
| X3 | The package code or the version label is unknown to the registry | 404 with the version check named; the registry is never asked to guess a version | MSG-P3-027 | AC4 |
| X4 | No version of the package is in force on the business date | The version list names no IN_FORCE row, the answer carries `inForce` false, and the caller's kit raises `NoPackageInForce`; this service invents no default | MSG-P3-027 | AC5 |
| X5 | The case has no state change in the ledger | 200 with an empty result and `missing` true; the fill raises its own task; the read is not an error | None | AC7 |
| X6 | The same decision record is delivered twice with one idempotency key | One entry, the first; both reads answer the same entry and the repeat is counted by the wave-1 ingest | None | AC7 |
| X7 | The caller's role holds no read letter | 403 before a row is read; no rule text, owner role, version label or entry ID is returned | MSG-P4-002 | AC9 |
| X8 | The registry or the ledger cannot be read | 503, nothing is answered, the caller retries inside its budget and an incident is raised | MSG-GEN-006 | AC8 |
| X9 | The row is read with a case fact in the answer or through a workbook, a DRL or another schema | Refused at review and failed by the build check: this service answers rows, never case values | None | AC10 |

X1 to X3 are the lookup refusals of the legacy `RuleCatalog.row` carried onto this service; X4 is legacy AC14 on the registry side; X5 to X6 are legacy AC9, AC10 and AC11 on the ledger side; X7 to X9 are the target's own boundaries. Whether an absent `packageVersion` may be answered with the row of the version in force is GAP-2409; ASM-4008 fixes the refusal of X1.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reads `rwb_decision` only and builds against the RWB-P2-E2035-CON, RWB-P3-E2042-CON and RWB-P4-E1037-CON fakes; calls no other service at run time |
| Negotiable | Nothing business is fixed here: the action text, the owner role, the timer spec, the version labels and the states are rows and list values |
| Valuable | The next action can always name the rule and the version that set it, and an old case is never re-read against a newer version |
| Estimable | Two read operations, one version-state resolver, two repositories, one cache and one index |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests; no screen, no workflow, no Schedule and no write path |
| Testable | Every criterion below has a test case in section 16, on registry and ledger fixtures |
