The legacy criteria stay with the primary slices: the case fields, the task and the check step with RWB-P3-E2035-APP at AC2, AC6, AC8, AC10 and AC11; the resolve, the read and the fill with RWB-P2-E2035-APP at AC1, AC3 to AC7 and AC9 to AC14; the refusal of a role without Case record R with RWB-P4-E2035-APP at AC13. What this story proves is that the two answers exist, name their versions and cannot be edited from outside.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The row of a firing rule is read only through `RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion)`, and it returns action_text, owner_role, timer_spec, to_state, rule_version, drools_rule_name and outputs | Legacy BR1 and section 12; D-RCV-36 T6 |
| BR2 | The answer is keyed by the rule ID and the package version label the caller names; a version label is never resolved to another version and a row is never rewritten | Legacy AC2 and section 12; D-RCV-36 T5, T7 |
| BR3 | The timer spec is answered as stored. The service computes no due date, no working-day count and no calendar, and holds no duration for a named state | Legacy BR3 and BR4 on the caller's side; legacy section 17 |
| BR4 | The next action is never entered by a person: no operation of this story writes a row of the registry or of the ledger | Legacy BR2; RWB-P3-E2035-APP |
| BR5 | The latest state change of a case is the newest ledger entry of that case, in `chain_seq` order, that carries a rule ID and a rule version; it answers the rule ID, the rule version, the entry ID and the decided-at time | Legacy AC11 flow step 7 and legacy section 12 `DecisionLogQuery.latestStateChange` |
| BR6 | A case with no such entry is answered 200 with an empty result and missing true; it is not an error and it creates no task, because the task is the fill's | Legacy AC8; RWB-P2-E2035-APP |
| BR7 | A missing or malformed parameter is refused before a row is read: 422 with MSG-GEN-001 for a field, 404 with MSG-P3-027 for an unknown row or version, 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a missing right | RWB-P2-E2035-CON X3 and X4; RWB-P7-E1073-APP |
| BR8 | A version is in force only while its state is IN_FORCE, which the 00:01 promotion sets and the rollback withdraws; no version in force is a fact of the registry, and `NoPackageInForce` is raised by the caller's kit | Legacy AC14; D-RCV-36 T3, T9; RWB-P7-E1073-APP |
| BR9 | Both reads are side-effect free and idempotent for their inputs: no row, no entry and no decision record is written, and the answer for a version state is the same whatever the business date | NFR-033, NFR-034; RWB-P7-E1008-APP |
| BR10 | A row is read only from `rwb_decision`; the workbook, the generated DRL, the `recovery.*` tables, `recovery_case` and the other services' schemas are never read and never joined | DP-01; ownership map |
| BR11 | No business value is written in code: action text, owner role, timer spec, to-state, version labels, version states and package codes are rows and list values | BR-P7-001, BR-P7-003 and BR-P7-007; DP-06, DP-07 |

How the rules hold in `rwb-decision`:

- BR1 to BR3 are one indexed read of `rule_row` by `rule_id` and `rule_version` plus one read of `rule_package_version` by `version_label`; the answer is a projection of those rows and holds no arithmetic.
- BR4 and BR9 are visible in the code review and in the fake run: the module has no write method on either repository and no outbox writer.
- BR5 is one ordered read of `decision_log_entry` by `case_id` with `chain_seq` descending; the filter is over the entries that carry DF-DEC-004 and DF-DEC-005, and the index of section 13 serves it. Which entries count as a state change is not enumerated in any source (GAP-2407; ASM-4006).
- BR6 is the empty answer: `missing` is a field of the answer, not an error code.
- BR7 is the envelope of the service's reads: 401 without a session, 403 without the right, 404 for an unknown row, 422 for a parameter and 503 when the store cannot be read.
- BR8 is a state read, not a date computation: the promotion story sets IN_FORCE at 00:01 on the valid-from date and the rollback withdraws it, so this story never compares a date to decide what is in force.
- BR10 is the reason there is no case repository and no ACE view grant of this service.

##### 9. State transitions

None. This story changes no case status, no next-action field, no rule row and no ledger entry, and it starts no task. The registry states it reads are set by RWB-P7-E1073-APP; the only state this story has is the state of an answer:

| Answer state | When | What the caller gets |
|---|---|---|
| Row answered | The version label exists and holds the rule ID | The row, the outputs, the package version, the version state and the in-force flag |
| Row not found | The version holds no row for the rule ID, or the version is unknown | 404 with MSG-P3-027; no substitute row |
| Not in force | No version of the package is IN_FORCE | `inForce` false on every answer; the kit raises `NoPackageInForce` |
| Latest change answered | The case has a ledger entry with a rule ID and a rule version | Rule ID, rule version, entry ID and decided-at |
| No change | The case has no such entry | 200, empty result, `missing` true |
| Refused | No session, no read letter or a malformed parameter | 401, 403 or 422, and nothing is read |
| Not served | The registry or the ledger cannot be read | 503 with MSG-GEN-006 |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-RULES, the embedded rules kit in the owning service | Reads the row of a fired rule and the version state under its service identity (Rules and parameters R) |
| SY-CASEWF, the case workflow's `EvaluateRules` activity | Reads the row of a fired rule for the facts of a case; it holds the case, not this service |
| rwb-integration, the resolve and the fill | Reads the row and the latest state change of a case under its service identity (Rules and parameters R, Decision log R) |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Owns the action text, the owner role and the timer spec of the rows and reads them here; the writes are RWB-P7-E1073-APP's |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads a row, its version state and the latest state change of any case in scope (Rules and parameters R, Decision log R) |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Operates the promotion and rollback of RWB-P7-E1073-APP; this story reads only the state those set |
| Any other role | Refused 403 with MSG-P4-002 where it holds no letter; no row is read |

Reading is the whole of this story. It holds no write operation, no approval and no break-glass path, and it delegates every write of a rule row, a version or an entry to the stories named above.

| DF-REF-008, DF-REF-009, DF-REF-010, DF-REF-011 | `rule_row` | action_text, to_state, owner_role, timer_spec | Read |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary. The row is answered from `rwb_decision` only; the workbook, the generated DRL, `recovery.*` and the case tables are not read (BR10). Which of the row's remaining columns an answer may carry is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2405; ASM-4004).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

| Operation | Path | Status | What this story decides behind it |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion=` | New in this story; the shape is published in `RWB-P3-E2042-CON` and consumed in `RWB-P2-E2035-CON` | The row of one rule in one package version: actionText, ownerRole, timerSpec, toState, ruleId, ruleVersion, droolsRuleName, outputs, packageCode, packageVersion, versionState, inForce. 401 MSG-P4-001, 403 MSG-P4-002, 404 MSG-P3-027, 422 MSG-GEN-001, 503 MSG-GEN-006 |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log?caseId=&latestStateChange=true` | Existing operation `API-P7-006`; the `latestStateChange` filter is new in this story | The latest state change of one case: entryId, ruleId, ruleVersion, decidedAt, missing. Same errors; 200 with `missing` true when the case has none |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` | Existing, from RWB-P7-E1073-APP | Read unchanged; this story asserts in AC5 that the version list names no IN_FORCE row when none is in force |

`GET /decision-log/{entryId}`, `GET /admin/rule-packages`, `GET /admin/rule-versions` and the approval operations are the same service's and are unchanged by this story.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None at run time. The two shapes this story provides are the ones `RWB-P2-E2035-CON` and `RWB-P3-E2042-CON` declare, and both are used as fakes in the tests (12.8) and as the alignment reference in the build. The case facts a read needs are parameters of the call, never a call back to the case service.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. A read is a read: no event, no `RulePackageInForce` and no decision record leaves this story. The service topic `rwb.decision.events.v1`, its retry topic and its `.dlt` carry the registry and approval events of RWB-P7-E1073-APP, and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` carries the records the callers write.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The cache of section 13 is keyed by package version, and the promotion and the rollback that change a version's state are written and published by this same service, so the cache is dropped on the commit that publishes `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` rather than on a subscription.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. This story registers no workflow and no activity on the `rwb-decision` queue. The `EvaluateRules` activity that asks for a row runs on the case service's queue, and the fill runs on `rwb-integration`; both call the REST operations of 12.1.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The JOB-20 rule-promote Schedule at 00:01 is RWB-P7-E1073-APP's, and the JOB-05 next-action check is RWB-P2-E2035-APP's. This story starts no Schedule and holds no timer.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, module `decision/catalogue`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision.catalogue`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-01 is the reason the answer is built from `rwb_decision` rows and holds no case value. DP-03 is recorded because the entry the fill reads is a decision record written by the owning service on `rwb.decision-record.v1` and stored here; this slice reads the store and writes no record. DP-04 is the split of the legacy rule component: the registry and the catalogue are this service's, the KieBase and the 300 ms evaluation stay in the owning service, and the row is fetched over the contract instead of the classpath. DP-05 is recorded and used for nothing on this path: no ACE view is granted to `rwb_decision`. DP-06 and DP-07 supply the business date, the version-state list and the DF-SYS field names as data, because the legacy key reads a configuration key and a holiday list and this story must not turn either into a constant. DP-10 is recorded because the legacy key carries JOB-05: in the target that check is the `rwb-integration` Schedule and the promotion is the JOB-20 Schedule, so this story adds no job. DP-11 is the boundary: two reads, one hop, 2 s, cached. DP-13, DP-14 and DP-15 are the naming and migration conventions. DP-19 is the route the case screens read through; this story serves no screen.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| RuleCatalogController | Controller | The catalogue operation; validation and the problem envelope of BR7 |
| RuleCatalogService | Service | Builds the answer of BR1 to BR3 from the row and the version row; no arithmetic |
| VersionStateResolver | Service | The package code, the version label, the version state and the in-force flag; 404 for an unknown label |
| DecisionLogQueryController | Controller | The decision-log read with the `latestStateChange` filter |
| LatestStateChangeService | Service | BR5: the newest entry of a case that carries a rule ID and a rule version, or the empty answer of BR6 |
| RuleRowRepository | Repository | `rule_row`, `rule_package` and `rule_package_version` in `rwb_decision`; read methods only |
| DecisionEntryRepository | Repository | `decision_log_entry` by case in `chain_seq` order; read methods only |
| CatalogCache | Service | The answer per package version, dropped on the commit that promotes or rolls back a version (BR9) |

**Database and migrations.** No new table: the four tables exist from RWB-P7-E1001-APP and RWB-P7-E1008-APP, and the catalogue index of `rule_row (rule_id, rule_version)` is created with them. One migration in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15, `V2_035_1__latest_state_change_index.sql`, adds `ix_declog_case_latest` on `decision_log_entry (case_id, chain_seq DESC) WHERE case_id IS NOT NULL`, so the latest state change is an index read inside the 2 s budget of DP-11. The story writes no row of either table.

**Configuration and reference data.** The version-state list and the business date are read through DP-07 and DP-06. The timer specs, the action texts, the owner roles and the version labels are rows of the package versions. No parameter, no timeout constant, no rule ID and no role code appears in code (BR11). The database login is the rwb-decision login (DP-02): Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2411; ASM-4010).

**Build steps**

1. `RuleRowRepository` and `VersionStateResolver` over the three registry tables, with the 404 of X2 and X3; tests for AC1, AC2 and AC4.
2. `RuleCatalogService` with the projection of BR1 to BR3, and a test that a timer spec is returned byte for byte for the five shapes of AC3.
3. `DecisionEntryRepository` and `LatestStateChangeService` with the ordered read and the empty answer; tests for AC6 and AC7.
4. `CatalogCache` keyed by package version and dropped on the promotion and the rollback commits; test AC8, including the 503 path.
5. The access check on both operations and the refusal of AC9 through the RWB-P4-E1037-CON fake.
6. The migration of the index, and a timing test that both reads stay inside the 2 s budget on a package of 38 rows and a case of 400 entries.
7. The fake run of both operations against the RWB-P2-E2035-CON and RWB-P3-E2042-CON fakes, so the story builds before the registry is loaded in the environment.

**Feature switch.** None. A switch here would let a next action be resolved from a row the registry cannot name for that version, which is the failure this story exists to prevent; the states of a version are data and the promotion is the only way a version becomes servable.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass; the row of a fired rule is answered for the version the caller names whatever its state; a timer spec is returned as stored; an unknown row is refused without a substitute; a package with no version in force is named in force nowhere; the latest state change of a case is answered from the ledger or answered empty; and neither read writes a row, an entry or a decision record.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-001 | No valid session or service identity | You have no Recovery Workbench role. Ask your team manager to request one. | The access check before this story's answers |
| MSG-P4-002 | The caller holds no Rules and parameters R, or no Decision log R, on the operation asked | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, on the refusal of BR7 |
| MSG-P3-027 | The rule row, the package code or the version label is not found, or no version is in force | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. | This story, for the rule row, the version and the package in force checks |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A parameter is missing or malformed | Enter {field}. | This story, before a row is read (X1) |
| MSG-GEN-006 | The registry or the ledger cannot be read | {system} is not available. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on X8 and on a read beyond the budget |

For MSG-P3-027 the {check} values of this story are "rule row", "version" and "package in force"; {detail} names the rule ID, the package code, the version label and the business date only, never a case fact, a customer value or an actor. Every error is a problem response with `messageId`, the text with its placeholders filled and the instance of the request; the Thai text follows DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

This story builds no screen. SCR-03 Case record, SCR-02 Case list, SCR-09 Exception queue and SCR-38 Decision log query are P3's and P4's through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19, and the next-action panel and columns are RWB-P3-E2035-APP's.

What this story decides for those screens is what the two answers may show:

| Screen | State | What the answer decides |
|---|---|---|
| SCR-03 Case record | Read only | The next action names the rule ID and its version, and both come from the row and the entry answered here |
| SCR-03 Case record | Waiting | The owner role of the row is the code the caller turns into the waiting text with the role name of RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| SCR-03 Case record | Overdue | The overdue marker is the case side's; the version shown is the one the answer names, so an escalation can cite it |
| SCR-02 Case list | Columns shown | The rule ID and version behind each row are the ones this story answers for that case |
| SCR-38 Decision log query | Entry opened | The latest state change read here is the same entry the query returns; no second ordering exists |

A screen that shows a next action with no rule ID and no version, or with a version the registry does not hold, is a defect of the screen: both answers always name what they answered for.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: action text, owner role, timer spec, to-state, package codes, version labels, version states and role codes are rows and list values (BR11).
- No personal data in a log, an answer, an event or a test: the two answers carry rule identifiers, version labels, dates and entry IDs, and test data is synthetic with parties as role codes.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views (DP-05): this service holds no customer value, is granted no ACE view and answers no case value.
- No cross-schema read (DP-01, BR10): `recovery_case`, `queue`, `task`, `role`, `lov_value` and `recovery.*` are never queried; the case ID is a parameter.
- One writer per row: this story holds no write method on either repository, so a rule row, a version and a ledger entry change only through RWB-P7-E1073-APP and RWB-P7-E1008-APP.
- The row is read only through `RuleCatalog.row`; the workbook, the generated DRL and the `rule_row` table of a retired schema appear in no code path (legacy section 17).
- One evaluation: the kit evaluates in the owning service and this service answers facts, so no second rule engine decides a to-state.
- A read is idempotent and side-effect free: the same question under the same version state answers the same bytes and writes nothing (BR9).

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **the next action operations of rwb-integration and the `next-action-check` Schedule deployed on the service's own worker and task queue, behind the platform flag, with a backfill and rerun path, five dashboard series, three alerts and a runbook with its entries**, so that **the measure the legacy story sets — no active case without a next action — is observable and operable by a rota from the first release**.

The legacy story assumed that a Quartz job would find the cases with no next action and that someone would read a job monitor when it failed. In the target the fill is a Temporal Schedule on the queue of this service (DP-10), the legacy JOB-05 is retired (Arch v5 slide 44; the Ownership Map ruling on `timer`), and the deployment is where the Schedule becomes real: its cadence, its overlap policy, its catch-up window, its `job_catalog` row, its run view and its alerts.

This story deploys and proves the deployment only. It builds no resolver, no read and no fill: those are the app story of this key, and the contract they answer to is `RWB-P2-E2035-CON`. It writes no case row: the fill writes through the rwb-case contract, and the case row stays rwb-case's. What it owns is the release: the chart, the worker, the Schedule, the flag values, the backfill operation, the five series and the three runbook entries.

##### 2. Business rationale

The next action is the measure of the case: the legacy story sets the count of active cases with no next action at a target of zero, and a case can wait for weeks when nobody owns the sweep. Three operational facts make the deployment a story of its own. The resolve is called inside the case transition, so a resolve that fails holds the move; the fill runs unattended every five minutes, so a stalled worker or a paused Schedule leaves cases with no action and no message; and the rule catalog is read on every resolution, so a version that is not in force is a refusal that must be visible rather than a silent empty action.

The deployment therefore carries the state of the sweep as data. Five series answer the questions a rota asks: how many cases were resolved, how many active cases have no next action, how many fills ended with no due date and raised a task, whether the Schedule ran and how long it took, and how many consumed calls failed or answered `NoPackageInForce`. Three alerts carry a message ID and one runbook entry each, so an operator acts without reading code (ADR-023; MSG-P2-023, MSG-P3-027, MSG-GEN-004).

The release also makes the flag real. `rwb.casewf.next-action` is kept as the legacy reference of the switch, and the switch itself is a feature flag of the platform flag library (R-PREC default ruling). Off, the Schedule is paused, the fill writes nothing and the operations answer the feature-off message; on, the sweep runs and the case record header and the case list columns are served. No environment value is hard-coded: the replica counts, the resource sizes, the thresholds, the catch-up window and the backfill limit are values files, as DP-06 requires.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The Temporal workflow kit, the `rwb-recovery` namespace, worker versioning and the build ID provider exist (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON).
- The platform flag library is available and the flag `rwb.casewf.next-action` is registered for this service (RWB-PLT-E1047-CON; R-PREC default ruling on feature flags).
- The `rwb_integration` schema and its Flyway sequence exist, with the `job_catalog` row of section 12.7 and the `decision_record` library table (RWB-PLT-E1044-CON; RWB-P2-E2035-CON).
- The platform error envelope and the message catalogue are in force, so an alert can carry a message ID.
- The three operations of `RWB-P2-E2035-CON` are published, with their paths, rights, answers and errors, and their contract fakes answer every consumed path.
- The environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist; the wave 2 release deploys to DEV, SIT and UAT, and the production values are a later promotion of the same artefacts.
- The topics of this service already exist: `rwb.integration.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics and the shared `rwb.decision-record.v1` (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON). This release adds no topic and registers no consumer group.
- The payload codec and the codec server of the namespace are in force (RWB-PLT-WF).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds the service image and the contract jar, runs the unit, component and contract tests of `RWB-P2-E2035-CON`, scans the image and the dependencies, and publishes one chart version.
2. The chart deploys the rwb-integration worker with its own login, the namespace `rwb-recovery`, the task queue `rwb-integration`, the payload codec and the build ID of the release.
3. The worker registration step confirms that the worker polls `rwb-integration` only, that `NextActionCheckWorkflow` and its three activities are registered, and that no second task queue is polled.
4. The API step confirms that the three operations answer on `/api/recovery/integration/v1` behind gateway-bff, with the authorise check of rwb-access reachable and the contract fakes replaced by the real services where they are deployed.
5. The Schedule step creates `next-action-check` with the cadence of 5 minutes, the overlap policy SKIP, the catch-up window of the environment and the workflow input, and writes or updates its `job_catalog` row.
6. The flag step sets `rwb.casewf.next-action` from the values of the environment and confirms that the Schedule state and the API answer follow it.
7. The backfill step runs the same workflow for a stated business date, fills only the cases with no next action, reports the counts, and refuses a window that already completed.
8. The dashboards are published with the five series and the environment, the release and the build ID as dimensions.
9. The three alerts are wired to MSG-P2-023, MSG-P3-027 and MSG-GEN-004 and to their runbook entries.
10. A smoke step fills one synthetic case in DEV through the backfill and checks that the answer of the read operation carries the action, the owner, the due date and the rule with its version, and that no second task is raised on a repeat.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The chart render, the image pull or the migration job fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic to the new version and no Schedule is created | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The worker polls a task queue other than `rwb-integration`, or the workflow is not registered | The registration check fails the release | None | AC2 |
| X3 | The Schedule cannot be created, or a second Schedule with the same ID exists | The Schedule step fails the release and names the Schedule ID; no partial Schedule is left behind | None | AC3 |
| X4 | The flag is off in an environment and the Schedule still runs, or the fill still writes | The flag step fails the release, because a paused switch must pause the sweep | None | AC4 |
| X5 | A backfill is asked for a window that already completed | The backfill is refused and nothing is filled again | MSG-GEN-004 | AC5 |
| X6 | A fill ends with no due date | One `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` task is raised through the rwb-case contract, once per case, and the case shows the missing message | MSG-P2-023 | AC6 |
| X7 | No package version is in force for the business date | The resolve answers `NoPackageInForce`, the fill skips the case, and the count and the alert rise for role RW-COE | MSG-P3-027 | AC6 |
| X8 | A consumed contract or the Temporal frontend does not answer inside the budget | The fill skips the case and the next run picks it up; the failure series and the backlog alert fire | MSG-GEN-004, MSG-P3-027 | AC5, AC6 |
| X9 | The worker stops while a run is in flight | The task stays on the queue, the worker returns and the run resumes from history; the stuck-run entry names the check | None | AC2, AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the workflow kit, the flag library and the published contract; no application code is built here |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, thresholds, the catch-up window, the backfill limit and the scan intervals are environment values |
| Valuable | Makes the sweep observable and operable before the release, so the target of zero cases with no next action can be read from a dashboard |
| Estimable | One chart, one registration check, one API check, one Schedule step, one flag step, one backfill, five series, three alerts and three runbook entries |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the worker registers, the Schedule runs and is paused, the backfill is idempotent, the alerts fire on a synthetic metric |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One service, one task queue, one login: the worker polls `rwb-integration` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and carries the rwb-integration login only | Arch v5 slides 24 and 41; DP-02; DP-10 |
| BR2 | Every worker carries the build ID of its release and worker versioning is enabled, so a new build takes new runs while the old build drains | Temporal and Drools design slide 27; RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| BR3 | The `next-action-check` Schedule is the only sweep: one Schedule ID, the cadence of 5 minutes, the overlap policy SKIP and a catch-up window, and no second job fills the same field | Legacy JOB-05; Arch v5 slide 44; DP-10 |
| BR4 | The fill writes only through the rwb-case contract; the release writes no case row and holds no grant on another schema | DP-01; DP-15 |
| BR5 | The flag is the platform flag library's, and its legacy name is kept as the reference of the switch; off means a paused Schedule and no write | R-PREC default ruling; BR11 of RWB-P2-E2035-CON |
| BR6 | The backfill and the rerun are idempotent: at most one open `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` task per case and at most one fill per case and business date | Legacy BR7; AC9 and AC11 of RWB-E2-035 |
| BR7 | Every alert carries a message ID and the agreed text and links one runbook entry | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR8 | No environment value is hard-coded: replicas, resources, thresholds, catch-up window, backfill limit and the flag come from values files and the flag library | DP-06 principle; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR9 | Dashboard series, alert payloads and the runbook carry counts, case IDs, role codes, rule IDs, version labels and build IDs only, never personal data and never a decoded payload | Arch v5 slide 42 (PDPA) |
| BR10 | A failing release never replaces a working one, and a paused Schedule is never left running by a partial deploy | Temporal and Drools design slide 27; DP-10 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the contract tests pass | Deploying |
| Deploying | Worker registered and probes healthy | The worker polls `rwb-integration` only and the four registrations exist | Ready |
| Ready | Schedule created | The Schedule step writes `next-action-check` and its `job_catalog` row | Sweeping |
| Sweeping | Flag off | `rwb.casewf.next-action` is off in the environment | Paused |
| Paused | Flag on | The flag is on and the Schedule resumes | Sweeping |
| Sweeping | Release superseded | A new chart version passes the tests | Rolling |
| Rolling | All workers on the new build | The old build drains its open runs | Sweeping |
| Sweeping | Consumed contract or Temporal frontend unavailable | The series and the backlog alert rise; the next run picks the cases up | Sweeping (degraded) |
| Any | A failing release or a failed Schedule step | The previous release stays in force and the pipeline stops | Previous state |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the registration check, the Schedule step, the backfill, the dashboards and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the worker versioning policy, the Schedule operations and the flag library registration |
| Platform workflow kit owner | Owns the Schedule conventions, the catch-up window semantics and the codec server |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact and may block it on a failed check |
| On-call operator | Runs the three runbook entries and opens an incident when the sweep stalls or `NoPackageInForce` persists |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Receives the no-version alert, because the package rows are its to load and to approve |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Works the `NEXT_ACTION_MISSING` tasks the sweep raises |
| RW-PLATADM | Reads the run, the Schedule and the job catalogue in the operator view, not in the cluster |

The worker runs as the rwb-integration service identity (DP-02), carried by the chart as a secret reference and never as a literal name. The identity name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0669; ASM-1187).

##### 11. Data

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Deployment values | Image digest, chart version, replica counts, resource requests and limits, probe paths and timings, log level, namespace, task queue, build ID, flag values, Schedule cadence and catch-up window, backfill limit |
| Task queue | `rwb-integration` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, polled by the rwb-integration worker only |
| Schedule | `next-action-check`, every 5 minutes, overlap policy SKIP, catch-up window of the environment, business date and run window input |
| Job catalogue row | `job_catalog` of `rwb_integration`: job_id, job_name, owner_role, schedule_text, runbook_path, expected_minutes, alert_after_minutes |
| Dashboard series | Cases resolved per run; active cases with no next action; fills with no due date and tasks raised; Schedule run outcomes and durations; consumed-call failures and the `NoPackageInForce` count |
| Alerts | Three rules, each with a message ID and one runbook entry |
| Runbook entries | Sweep stalled; missing-action backlog and no-due-date fills; no package version in force and consumed-call failure |
| Secrets | The rwb-integration login secret, the Kafka client credential and the Temporal mTLS material, all from the platform secret store |
| Test data | The synthetic cases `RW-2026-000401`, `RW-2026-000402` and `RW-2026-000403` in DEV and SIT only; the fixture owner is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0669; ASM-1189) |

The deployment topology (cluster names, node pools, replica counts, resource sizes, zone spread and ingress class) belongs to each environment and is set by the platform team in its values file; the chart exposes every one of them as a value, and this story fixes only their names and the rule that they are never hard-coded.

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only after the worker has polled `rwb-integration` once, the codec is attached and one authorise call has succeeded; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database, and a failing dependency is reported as not ready, never as live-and-broken. The paths and timings are values of the environment.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The three operations of this key — the resolve, the read and the fill — are provided by `RWB-P2-E2035-APP` and documented in `RWB-P2-E2035-CON`; this story deploys them and declares no path of its own. The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The deployment needs no REST client of its own: the worker calls the contracts of rwb-case, rwb-access and rwb-decision inside the activities, and the pipeline calls the platform registry and the secret store only.

###### 12.3 Events published

None of its own. The release publishes no event type: `rwb.integration.events.v1` carries FileDelivered and FileFailed, which belong to the file stories of this service, and the ledger event `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` is published by the decision-record library inside the fill.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The release registers no consumer group and subscribes to no topic; the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` and the service topic exist before the release and are used by other stories of the service.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|---|
| NextActionCheckWorkflow | Workflow, workflow ID prefix `next-action-check-` | `rwb-integration` | Registered by the worker of this release, with the build ID and worker versioning; started by the Schedule and by the backfill |
| findCasesWithoutNextAction | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Registered with the retry policy of the kit |
| resolveNextAction | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Registered with the same policy; the `NoPackageInForce` outcome is non-retryable and countable |
| fillNextAction | Activity | `rwb-integration` | Registered with the same policy; one rwb-case call, idempotent by case ID and task code |

**Build ID and versioning.** The build ID is the one the workflow kit supplies for the release commit; worker versioning is enabled and a new build takes new runs while the old build drains. The build ID format and the versioning policy are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0669; ASM-1187).

###### 12.6 Schedules

| Schedule | Cadence | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|
| `next-action-check` | Every 5 minutes | Created by the Schedule step with the workflow `NextActionCheckWorkflow`, the task queue `rwb-integration`, the overlap policy SKIP, the catch-up window of the environment and the business date input; paused and resumed by the flag; backfilled by the backfill step |

The cadence of 5 minutes is the legacy cadence of JOB-05 and is not an environment value. The catch-up window, the overlap window and the backfill limit are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0669; ASM-1188) and are fixed as values of the environment.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| job_catalog | rwb_integration | P2 (Ownership Map; TSD P2 v3 T3.1) | The row of `next-action-check` is written or updated by the release: job_id, job_name, owner_role, schedule_text, runbook_path, expected_minutes, alert_after_minutes |

The release applies no other migration and adds no other table. The `decision_record` library table, the outbox, the inbox and the idempotency objects are created in `rwb_integration` by the service baseline and by the DB story of the service (DP-15), and the case row is written only through the rwb-case contract (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. No fake is deployed: the workflow tests run on `TestWorkflowEnvironment` in the pipeline, and the contract mocks of the consumed services are in-process test doubles of the app and contract stories. No WireMock workload is part of this release.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 0 consumed | The three operations are deployed, not declared here; probes are cluster-internal |
| Kafka | 0 published, 0 consumed | No topic and no consumer group is created by this release |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 3 activities, 1 Schedule | Worker on `rwb-integration` with a pinned build ID and worker versioning; `next-action-check` every 5 minutes |
| File | None | The values files and the recorded histories are pipeline inputs, not runtime data |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | The release writes `rwb_integration` only and reaches the case through the rwb-case contract | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | The decision-record library is deployed with the worker and publishes to `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the outbox | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | The embedded kit is part of the worker image; the catalog row is fetched inside the activity and no second engine runs | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | No ACE read in this release and no view grant | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | The parameters and reference rows are read through the rwb-case contracts; the environment values are values files | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | The reference-data contract of rwb-case is a runtime dependency of the resolve activity | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | The worker, the task queue, the namespace and the `next-action-check` Schedule come from the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | The activities call the consumed contracts with the 2 s budget; the deployment adds no REST path | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | The deployed base is `/api/recovery/integration/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | The release uses the existing service topic and adds none | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | The per-service Flyway sequence is applied by the baseline; this release adds the `job_catalog` row only | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff serves the runtime path; the deployment registers no route of its own | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-integration/` overlay | Worker deployment, config map, secret references, probes, task queue and namespace, flag reference, build ID, Schedule values |
| `helm/rwb-integration/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, flag value, catch-up window, backfill limit, build ID, environment |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit, component and contract tests, image and dependency scan, chart publish, promotion |
| Registration check | Worker polls `rwb-integration` only; the workflow and three activities are registered; the codec is attached |
| API check | The three operations answer through gateway-bff and the authorise call succeeds |
| Schedule step | Creates or updates `next-action-check` and its `job_catalog` row; pause, resume and backfill through the kit |
| Flag step | Sets `rwb.casewf.next-action` from the environment and confirms that the Schedule state follows it |
| Backfill step | Runs the workflow for one business date and reports the counts of filled, unchanged, missing and failed |
| Dashboards | The five series of section 11 |
| Alerts | Three rules, each with a message ID and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Three entries: sweep stalled, missing-action backlog and no-due-date fills, no package version in force and consumed-call failure |

**Alert mapping**

| Message ID | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P2-023 | The active cases with no next action rise above the threshold, or one run raises missing-action tasks for more than the threshold of cases | Missing-action backlog alert with the count, the team codes and the run reference | Team manager of the team and platform on-call, page |
| MSG-P3-027 | The `NoPackageInForce` count is above zero for a business date | No-version alert naming the package code RESTRUCTURE and the business date | Business on-call (RW-COE), page |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The Schedule has not completed a run inside twice its cadence, or a consumed-call failure rate is above the threshold | Sweep-stalled alert with the last run, its outcome and the oldest unfilled case count | Platform on-call, page |

**Backfill and rerun.** The backfill step runs `NextActionCheckWorkflow` for a stated business date with the same input as the Schedule. It fills only the cases with no next action, is idempotent by case ID and task code, and reports the counts. A window that already completed is refused with MSG-GEN-004 and fills nothing; a case that failed on a consumed contract is picked up by the next run, so no repair script exists. The backfill limit per run is a value of the environment (ASM-1188).

**Rollback.** A release that fails a check is not promoted. A release already promoted is rolled back by redeploying the previous chart version with its own build ID, which keeps the old build serving its open runs until they finish; the Schedule is paused during the rollback so that the two builds never fill the same case, and it is resumed once one build serves the queue. The fill is idempotent, so no data repair is needed; a case filled twice is answered 200 unchanged by the rwb-case contract.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.casewf.next-action`, kept as the legacy reference of the switch and read from the platform flag library. On: the Schedule runs, the three operations answer and the case record header and the case list columns are served. Off: the Schedule is paused, the fill writes nothing and the operations answer the feature-off message. The flag is never a value of a service table, and its value is read at the start of every run so that a change needs no redeploy.

**Done when.** The chart renders for DEV, SIT and UAT, the registration check passes, the three operations answer through gateway-bff, the Schedule runs and is paused by the flag, the backfill fills only the missing cases and is refused on a completed window, the five series and the three alerts are published, the three runbook entries are reviewed by the on-call rota, and the smoke run of one synthetic case ends with the action, the owner, the due date and the rule version on the case and no second task on a repeat.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P2-023 | The active cases with no next action cross the threshold, or a run raises missing-action tasks | This case has no next action. It is on the exception list for {team}. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No RESTRUCTURE version is in force for a business date | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A backfill is asked for a completed window, or a consumed contract answers a conflict | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right calls a Schedule operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The run reads a case outside its scope | This case is not in your scope. |

The business texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story and the platform catalogue; the deployment adds the alert routing and the runbook link, never a new wording. For MSG-P3-027 the `{check}` is "package in force" and the `{detail}` names the package code and the business date only. An alert carries the message ID, the counts, the case IDs and the run reference, never a name and never a decoded payload.

##### 15. Screens and states

The deployment has no screen of its own. Its operator-facing surfaces are the pipeline run view, the release view, the dashboard of the five series, the Schedule view of the workflow kit, the scheduled-jobs read of the service baseline and the runbook. The operator view is behind Entra ID: RW-PLATADM operates and RW-AUDIT reads. SCR-44 Interface and job monitor is not used as a new screen: the `job_catalog` row is read through the existing job catalogue operation of this service.

| TC-P2-E2035-OPS-02 | AC2 | NFR | A worker polls `rwb-integration` only; the workflow and three activities are registered; the codec is attached; a non-retryable failure is counted |
| TC-P2-E2035-OPS-03 | AC3 | NFR | `next-action-check` created with 5 minutes, SKIP and the catch-up window; its job_catalog row; pause, resume, backfill; a completed window refused |
| TC-P2-E2035-OPS-04 | AC4 | NFR | The flag on and off per environment; the Schedule state and the operation answer follow it; nothing is written when it is off |
| TC-P2-E2035-OPS-05 | AC5 | NFR | Three cases with no next action filled once; the same backfill reporting three unchanged; a completed window refused with MSG-GEN-004 |
| TC-P2-E2035-OPS-06 | AC6 | NFR | Four synthetic conditions raise the five series and the three alerts with one runbook entry each |

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the package code, the rule IDs, the route states and the action text are data of the registry and the reference tables, never a deployment value.
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads, the runbook or the recorded runs: counts, case IDs, role codes, rule IDs, version labels and build IDs only.
- One login per service and one task queue per service: the release carries the rwb-integration login and polls `rwb-integration` only (DP-02, DP-10).
- The release writes `rwb_integration` only and holds no grant on `recovery` or on another `rwb_*` schema; the case row is written through the rwb-case contract (DP-01, DP-15).
- No secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; all secrets come from the platform secret store.
- The release pins the image digest, the chart version and the build ID; a rebuild between environments is not allowed, and a failing check never replaces a working release.
- One Schedule ID, one cadence: a second job or a second Schedule that fills the same field fails the review (BR3).
- The flag is the platform library's and its value is read at the start of every run; a paused switch pauses the sweep and the write.

##### 1. Story

As a **member of the integration and QA team**, I want **a repeatable cross-service journey harness that reads the next action of a case, its owner, its due date and the rule package version that set it through gateway-bff and the owning services**, so that **the wave 2 next action journey is proven end to end, with evidence, before the release is accepted**.

This story builds the harness and the evidence only. It builds no production screen, endpoint, table, workflow or schedule, it serves no operation, it owns no table and it starts no workflow. The real behaviour is owned by the I stories RWB-P3-E2035-APP (the next action fields, the timer resolver, the check and the panel of the case), RWB-P2-E2035-APP (the next action assigner and the case list export the legacy story carried in the P2 backlog), RWB-P7-E2035-APP (the RESTRUCTURE package registry, the rule catalog rows and the decision log), RWB-P4-E2035-APP (the role name and role class of the next action owner) and RWB-P3-E1018-APP, RWB-P3-E1031-APP and RWB-P3-E2042-APP (the case transitions, the case list and the RESTRUCTURE rows in force), and those seven stories block the ITG run.

The fourteen acceptance criteria of the legacy story stay with the APP stories that own them; this story owns none of them and restates none of them.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy RWB-E2-035 journey crosses more than one service: rwb-case holds the case, its state, its owner, its queue, the next action fields and the case list; rwb-decision holds the RESTRUCTURE rule package, the rule catalog row and the central decision ledger; rwb-access holds the Recovery roles as data, with the name and the class of the role that owns the next action; and rwb-integration holds the file runs and outbound items through which the case list export leaves the bank. Until the real services are exercised together through the gateway, the program cannot show that no case waits with nobody owing anything on it, which is the measure the legacy story sets: the count of active cases with no next action, with a target of zero.

The harness gives one repeatable run per business date that proves the composite route composes the next action from those owners one hop at a time inside the 2 s budget, that the action text, the owner role and the timer of the firing rule R-RES-04 of package version "RES-2026.12" are read from the catalog row and not held by the harness, that a wait for CU-BORROW on rule R-SET-13 is a valid next action, that the case list carries the next action, its owner and its due date with the overdue marker on 16 December 2026, that a case with no due date raises the warning MSG-P2-023 and one exception task, that NoPackageInForce is a refusal and never an empty next action, and that a repeated transition changes nothing. It meets REQ-WKM-012, REQ-WKM-013, REQ-WKM-016, REQ-WKM-014 and REQ-WKM-015 at the integration level and leaves every business rule, every message and every screen behaviour where the owning stories put them.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The seven I stories are published and deployed in the SIT environment: RWB-P3-E1018-APP (case transitions), RWB-P3-E1031-APP (case list), RWB-P3-E2042-APP (the RESTRUCTURE route-set rows in force), RWB-P2-E2035-APP (next action assigner and the case list export), RWB-P4-E2035-APP (role name and role class), RWB-P3-E2035-APP (next action fields, timer resolver, check and panel) and RWB-P7-E2035-APP (rule package registry, rule catalog row and decision log).
- gateway-bff is deployed with the composite route of DP-19 available. The gateway-bff composite next-action route path, its merge order and its call list: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0418; ASM-0593).
- The contract fakes of §12.8 are published from the owning services' OpenAPI documents, so the harness can run green from Day 1 before the I stories land.
- Package version "RES-2026.12" of code RESTRUCTURE is in force from 2026-12-01 and holds rule R-RES-04, which moves IN_FCR_QUEUE on CASE_PICKED_UP to WITH_FCR_OFFICER with action "Assign the case to a restructuring officer and start the offer clock", owner role RW-RESTRUCT and timer "2 working days", and rule R-SET-13, which moves WITH_OPS_SETTLEMENT on SETTLEMENT_BOOKED to AWAITING_PAYMENT with action "Set the payment due date and wait for the money", owner role CU-BORROW and timer "payment due 30 days" (RWB-E2-042; RWB-E1-073).
- The service levels and timers table holds 5 working days for each state of the route sets in force until the DL22 values are loaded, and the bank holiday list holds 31 December 2026 and 1 January 2027 (configuration key rwb.calendar.bank-holidays, loaded by RWB-E1-042).
- The roles RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-COE, RW-REFADM and RW-RESTRUCT are loaded with their class by RWB-P4-E2035-APP; the harness reads them and holds no copy.
- The harness repository and environment, its test-data seeding, and its evidence format and retention: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0418; ASM-0593).

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: seeds the cases, the queues, the roles, the service levels and timers rows, the bank holiday list and package version "RES-2026.12" through the owning contracts or the published fakes, and reads each object back to assert the seeded state.
2. Harness: calls the gateway-bff composite next-action route for case RW-2026-000401 and asserts the answer is composed from rwb-case, rwb-decision, rwb-access and rwb-integration, one hop per source inside the 2 s budget, with one trace in the run report.
3. Harness: drives the move of RW-2026-000402 through the case contract on business date 2026-12-11, asserts that rule R-RES-04 of version "RES-2026.12" fired and that the case holds its action text, owner role RW-RESTRUCT, rule ID and version and due date 15 December 2026, written in the same transaction as the move to WITH_FCR_OFFICER.
4. Harness: reads the catalog row of R-RES-04 through the rwb-decision contract and asserts the action text, the owner role and the timer it returns are the ones on the case, so the harness holds no copy of any business value.
5. Harness: opens the waiting case RW-2026-000403 moved by R-SET-13 on 14 December 2026 and asserts the waiting text with owner CU-BORROW, the wait end and the waiting flag.
6. Harness: reads the case list on 16 December 2026 and asserts the next action, next action owner and due date columns, that RW-2026-000401 is marked Overdue and RW-2026-000403 is not, and that RW-2026-000404 carries the missing-action warning MSG-P2-023 with one NEXT_ACTION_MISSING task on the exception queue.
7. Harness: reads the case list export as an outbound item of rwb-integration and asserts the four next action columns on the export row.
8. Harness: forces each failure of §5 through the fakes, asserts the message and that nothing was written, then returns the fake to its healthy answer.
9. Harness: drives the no-version case on 2027-01-04 and asserts NoPackageInForce with MSG-P3-027 and no next action from that move; repeats the transition with decision log entry DLE-SYN-0402 and asserts the next action and the due date are unchanged with no second task.
10. Harness: writes one run report per business date, keyed by story and business date; the report format and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0418; ASM-0593).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What the harness asserts | Message | ITG test case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The timer spec of the firing rule is "None" or has no fixed duration | The due date is taken from the service levels and timers row of the to_state (5 working days in the seeded table), and the owner shown is the case owner when the role is the role of the case queue | None | TC-E2-035-05-ITG |
| X2 | No due date can be found from the rule or the table | The case keeps the action and the owner of R-DEV-05 with no due date, one NEXT_ACTION_MISSING task is raised for role RW-TEAMMGR of the case team, and the case record shows the warning | MSG-P2-023 | TC-E2-035-06-ITG |
| X3 | The due date falls on a weekend or on a bank holiday | Working days skip Saturday, Sunday and the holiday list, so the move of 30 December 2026 gives the due date of 5 January 2027 | None | TC-E2-035-07-ITG |
| X4 | The case closes | The next action fields are empty, the open NEXT_ACTION_MISSING task is cancelled, and the case leaves the list of active cases with no next action | None | TC-E2-035-08-ITG |
| X5 | The same transition is delivered twice with decision log entry DLE-SYN-0402 | The next action and the due date are unchanged and no second task exists; the repeated read returns the same answer with one trace | None | TC-E2-035-09-ITG |
| X6 | Two transitions of one case commit against version 7 at the same time | One commits and the other is refused and retried against version 8, and the next action is that of the rule committed last | MSG-GEN-004 | TC-E2-035-10-ITG |
| X7 | A case opened before the switch-on has no next action | The check fills the three cases of the seed from the latest state change in the decision log, with the text read from the catalog row of R-RES-04 of version "RES-2026.12" | None | TC-E2-035-11-ITG |
| X8 | The timer of the rule is "same day" | The due date is the business date of the move | None | TC-E2-035-12-ITG |
| X9 | The reader holds RW-REFADM and no role with Case record R | The direct call answers 403 and no next action data is returned; the composite route does not return the action either | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-035-13-ITG |
| X10 | No RESTRUCTURE package version is in force on the business date 2027-01-04 | The answer is NoPackageInForce for the package in force check, the move is refused, and the case keeps its state and holds no next action from that move | MSG-P3-027 | TC-E2-035-14-ITG |
| X11 | The case is outside the reader's scope | The case is not in the case list rows and the direct call answers 404 with no next action data | MSG-P4-003 | TC-E2-035-04-ITG |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs on its own once the seven I stories are deployed; until then it runs against the §12.8 fakes |
| Negotiable | The harness pack, the data seeding and the evidence format are agreed with QA; no business value is fixed by the harness |
| Valuable | The next action, its owner, its due date and the package version that set it are evidenced across services rather than per service |
| Estimable | One harness project, one journey specification, one fake pack and one run report |
| Small | Fits in one iteration with the owning stories' contract tests |
| Testable | Each scenario of §7 is one automated journey with synthetic data and a machine-checkable result |

These four criteria are new for the ITG harness and do not restate the app criteria owned by the I stories; legacy AC1 to AC14 of RWB-E2-035 stay with RWB-P2-E2035-APP and the secondary APP stories of the same legacy key.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | On every move, the next action text, the owner role and the rule ID come from the catalog row of the firing rule: the catalog read returns action_text, owner_role and timer_spec for the rule ID and the package version | FEAT-CWC-28; REQ-WKM-013; D-RCV-36 T6 |
| BR2 | The next action is never entered by a person | REQ-WKM-013 |
| BR3 | timer_spec "n working days" adds n working days; "n days" with any label before it adds n calendar days; "same day", "Same day" and "immediate" give the date of the move; "next working day" adds 1 working day | rule_row.timer_spec through the rwb-decision contract |
| BR4 | Any other timer_spec, including "None", takes the time for the to_state from the service levels and timers table | DL22 |
| BR5 | The next action is a wait when the owner role is of class Customer party or Partner user; the text starts "Waiting for {owner}:" | role.role_class |
| BR6 | A next action is overdue when its due date is earlier than today and the case is not closed | REQ-WKM-012 |
| BR7 | An active case with no due date or no next action raises one NEXT_ACTION_MISSING task to the team manager | REQ-WKM-016 |
| BR8 | Working days are Monday to Friday, excluding the dates in the bank holiday list | Configuration key rwb.calendar.bank-holidays |
| BR9 | When the owner role is the role of the case's queue, the owner shown is the case owner; otherwise the role name | queue.role_code |
| BR10 | The rule version is the package version label of the rule result, and the next action records the version of the move that set it; a later version does not rewrite an action already set | D-RCV-36 T5, T7; R-UNI-38 |
| BR11 | No RESTRUCTURE version in force is a refusal (NoPackageInForce), never a default move and never an empty next action | D-RCV-36 T3; R-UNI-41 |

The harness asserts these eleven rules against the owning services and re-implements none of them, so no BR row is changed by this story.

##### 9. State transitions

None. The harness changes no case status, route state or stage clock, and it writes no next action field, no task and no decision record itself. The table is what it observes on the case after a call to the owning service.

| Observed on the case | Before the call | After a successful move | After a refusal |
|---|---|---|---|
| next action text, owner role, due date, rule ID, package version | the values of the previous move | the values of R-RES-04 of package version "RES-2026.12" | unchanged |
| next action waiting | false | true when the owner role is CU-BORROW under R-SET-13 | unchanged |
| exception task | none | one NEXT_ACTION_MISSING for role RW-TEAMMGR when no due date exists | none |
| status, route state, queue, owner | IN_PROGRESS, IN_FCR_QUEUE, and the queue and owner of the case | the to_state and the transition of the owning rule, with the next action in the same transaction | unchanged |

A failed or refused call leaves every row exactly as it was before the call.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | The synthetic user the harness drives: reads the next action of cases in scope (Case record R) |
| RW-TEAMMGR, team manager | Reads the case list and works NEXT_ACTION_MISSING tasks on the exception queue (Case record R; Queue and allocation RU) |
| RW-COE, centre of excellence analyst | Owns the action, owner and timer columns of the rule rows (Rules and parameters CRUD); the harness reads the rows it set and changes none |
| RW-REFADM, reference data administrator | Loads the service levels and timers table and the bank holiday list; the user U-REF-01 of the access case holds RW-REFADM and no role with Case record R |
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow module | Writes the next action fields and the exception task (Case record U; Queue and allocation C); the harness asserts its result, it does not act for it |
| SY-RULES, Drools evaluator | Evaluates the RESTRUCTURE package and serves the catalog row of the firing rule |
| No approval applies | The journey takes no decision |

Authorisation is answered by rwb-access through the role data read of §12.2, and the refusal of a role without Case record R is asserted by the harness on the owning service's answer.

| DF-REF-010 | rule_row | owner_role | Read through rwb-decision contract |
| DF-REF-011 | rule_row | timer_spec | Read through rwb-decision contract |
| DF-REF-281 | rule_package_version | version_label | Read through rwb-decision contract |
| DF-REF-282 | rule_package_version | status | Read through rwb-decision contract |
| DF-REF-036 | role | role_name | Read through rwb-access contract |
| DF-REF-037 | role | role_class | Read through rwb-access contract |
