The rule row and the package version are read only through the rwb-decision contract; the harness reads no workbook, no drl_source and no rule_row row directly. The role name and class are read only through the rwb-access contract. Test data is synthetic. No production case, party or task is used, and no personal data is written to a run report.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness calls the owning services; it serves no operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; the 2 s timeout and the circuit breaker per downstream of DP-11 apply to every row.

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/next-action` | P3 rwb-case | The next action text, owner, due date, waiting flag, overdue and missing flags, rule ID and package version |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The case status, route state, owner, queue, team and closure date after the move |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases` | P3 rwb-case | The case list rows with the next action, next action owner, due date and overdue marker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | P7 rwb-decision | The latest state change of a case with its rule ID and rule version |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` | P7 rwb-decision | The RESTRUCTURE version in force on the business date and its status |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-versions` | P7 rwb-decision | The catalog row of the firing rule: action text, owner role and timer spec (D-RCV-36 T6) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/roles` | P4 rwb-access | The name and the class of the owner role, used for the waiting text and the owner shown |
| GET | `/api/recovery/integration/v1/admin/outbound-items` | P2 rwb-integration | The case list export file run and its outbound item, which carry the four next action columns |

The composite screen route itself is gateway-bff (DP-19), owned by the platform edge story RWB-PLT-N001-CON. Its path, merge order and call list are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0418; ASM-0593).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness produces no event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | What the harness asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1 | rwb.case.events.v1 | P3 rwb-case | One event per move, keyed by caseId, in the same transaction as the next action fields |
| rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1 | rwb.decision.events.v1 | P7 rwb-decision | Package version "RES-2026.12" is announced in force for the business date 2026-12-11, and no version is in force on 2027-01-04 |
| rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 | rwb.decision-record.v1 | P7 rwb-decision (ledger); every service publishes its own record | The record of the move names rule R-RES-04 and package version "RES-2026.12" and reaches the central ledger within 5 minutes |
| rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1 | rwb.integration.events.v1 | P2 rwb-integration | The case list export file carrying the next action columns is delivered once for the business date |

The events are consumed for assertion only; order per case is guaranteed by the case key on the topic, and the harness reads the case, the ledger and the outbound item through the owning contracts rather than from a topic.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness starts no workflow and adds no activity; it drives REST only and observes the transition of the case through the case contract. The check that the legacy story ran as JOB-05 is a durable timer inside the case workflow in the target design, and the harness asserts its result on the case, not the timer itself.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The harness run is started by the test pipeline, not by a Temporal Schedule and not by Airflow.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Stubbed answers |
|---|---|---|
| rwb-case | cases/{caseId}/next-action, cases/{caseId}, cases | RW-2026-000401 IN_PROGRESS moved by R-RES-04 on 2026-12-11 with due date 15 December 2026; RW-2026-000403 moved by R-SET-13 on 14 December 2026 with the waiting text and wait end 13 January 2027; RW-2026-000404 with no due date and one NEXT_ACTION_MISSING task for RW-TEAMMGR; RW-2026-000407 with no move on 2027-01-04; a case of another team for the scope case; 403 with MSG-P4-002 for a role without Case record R; 404 with MSG-P4-003 for a case outside scope |
| rwb-decision | decision-log, admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions, admin/rule-versions | RESTRUCTURE version "RES-2026.12" in force from 2026-12-01 with rows R-RES-04 and R-SET-13 and their action text, owner role and timer; R-RES-03 with timer "None"; R-RES-07 with timer "same day"; R-DEV-05 with timer "deadline driven"; decision log entry DLE-SYN-0402; no version in force on 2027-01-04; a forced failure for the failure isolation case |
| rwb-access | admin/roles | Role name "Restructuring officer (FCR)" and class for RW-RESTRUCT; role class Customer party for CU-BORROW; the roles of RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-COE and RW-REFADM; a slow answer beyond 2 s for the failure isolation case |
| rwb-integration | admin/outbound-items | The case list export file run of the business date with one outbound item carrying the next action, next action owner, due date and overdue columns; a cleared answer for every other case |

The fakes are published from the owning services' OpenAPI documents and are replaced by the real service as each I story lands, contract by contract. The harness repository and its environment: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0418; ASM-0593).

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Used | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | Yes | Eight consumed operations of §12.2 through gateway-bff and the owning services; one hop, 2 s timeout, breaker per downstream |
| Kafka | Yes | Consumes rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1, rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1, rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 and rwb.integration.FileDelivered.v1; publishes nothing |
| Temporal | No | Starts no workflow and adds no activity or Nexus operation; it observes the case transition and the durable timer of the case workflow |
| File | No | The case list export is asserted as an outbound item through the rwb-integration contract; the harness reads and writes no file itself |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The platform H dependencies named by this table are delivered by the platform wave and are not repeated in the metadata H list. The blocking dependencies of this story are the seven I stories.

DP-10 applies because the legacy check ran as JOB-05 on Quartz; in the target design the check is a durable timer inside the case workflow and the shared Quartz and job tables are no longer used. DP-14 applies because the legacy topics were named after the monolith module; the events the harness reads are on the owner's topic. DP-05 applies to the case and the account facts the case list carries; the harness reads them through the rwb-case contract and no service reads an ACE view for this journey except rwb-source-data.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Test harness | Runs one journey per business date, keyed by story and business date, and stops at the first failed assertion with the trace |
| NextActionClient | Harness adapter | Calls the composite next-action route and the eight consumed operations of §12.2 through gateway-bff |
| FakePack | WireMock project | Serves rwb-case, rwb-decision, rwb-access and rwb-integration from the published OpenAPI documents of §12.8 |
| SchemaBoundaryCheck | Assertion | Fails the run on any cross-schema reference found in the trace, so a service never reads another service's tables |
| CatalogFidelityCheck | Assertion | Compares the action text, the owner role, the timer, the rule ID and the package version on the case with the catalog row read through the rwb-decision contract, and fails the run on a difference |
| DueDateCheck | Assertion | Recomputes the working-day arithmetic from the timer spec, the service levels row and the holiday list, and fails the run when the due date on the case differs |
| IsolationCheck | Assertion | Fails the run when one slow or failed source stops another case of the same run, or when a failed call wrote anything |
| RunReportWriter | Reporter | Writes one run report with the trace and the per-assertion result; format and retention Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0418; ASM-0593) |

**Environment and test data**

- Environment: SIT, one namespace, the seven I stories deployed from their wave 2 builds or replaced by the §12.8 fakes. Harness repository, environment and data seeding: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0418; ASM-0593).
- Data: synthetic cases RW-2026-000401, RW-2026-000402, RW-2026-000403, RW-2026-000404 and RW-2026-000407; package version "RES-2026.12" with rows R-RES-04, R-SET-13, R-RES-03, R-RES-07 and R-DEV-05; owner roles RW-RESTRUCT, CU-BORROW, RW-CASEOWN, RW-TEAMMGR, RW-COE and RW-REFADM; the service levels row of 5 working days; the holiday list of 31 December 2026 and 1 January 2027; the business dates 2026-12-11, 2026-12-15, 2026-12-16 and 2027-01-04; decision log entry DLE-SYN-0402. No production record is copied.
- Reset: each run starts from the seeded state, so a repeated run is deterministic and the same report is produced.

**Build steps**

1. Build JourneyRunner and NextActionClient against the published OpenAPI documents of the owning services.
2. Publish FakePack for the four owning services from the same documents, and prove the harness runs green from Day 1 on the fakes.
3. Add the composite route assertion of AC1, including the four sources, the one-hop check, the 2 s per-call budget, the single trace and the SchemaBoundaryCheck.
4. Add the rule-set journey of AC2 with CatalogFidelityCheck and DueDateCheck: the action, the owner, the due date and the package version of R-RES-04, and the waiting case of R-SET-13.
5. Add the list assertion of AC3: the columns, the overdue marker, the waiting text, the missing-action warning with its task, the export outbound item and the scope refusal.
6. Add the failure isolation, the no-version refusal and the idempotent repeat of AC4, then replace each fake with the real service as its I story lands and publish the run report per business date; the gate definition: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0418; ASM-0593).

**Feature switch:** the harness has no production feature flag and runs in the test environment only. The production switch it exercises is `rwb.casewf.next-action` from the legacy solution plan, with `rwb.p3.drools` on the evaluation path; with the next-action flag off the assigner is not called, the check does not run and the panel and the columns are hidden, and with `rwb.p3.drools` off every move is refused with MSG-P3-027. The harness asserts the disabled and the enabled state of both.

**Done when:** the journey runs green against the seven deployed I stories in SIT, the run report for the business date holds every assertion of §7 and §16 with its trace, the next action of every case in the run matches the catalog row and its package version, and the pass/fail gate agreed with QA is met for one full business date.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P2-023 | The case has no next action or no due date | This case has no next action. It is on the exception list for {team}. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No RESTRUCTURE version is in force | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A transition commits against a changed version | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role lacks Case record R | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside the reader's scope | This case is not in your scope. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values; it does not own the message text. For MSG-P3-027 in this journey {check} is "package in force" and {detail} names the package code RESTRUCTURE and the business date only. For MSG-P2-023 {team} is the team code of the case. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the action text, the owner role, the timer spec, the service levels row and the holiday list are data held by the owning services; the harness reads them and never holds a copy.
- No personal data in logs, tests, traces or reports: the next action holds rule text only, the owner is a role code, the case list read is limited to the next action columns, and the harness uses synthetic cases and parties.
- No read of another service's schema: every read goes through the owner's contract, the SchemaBoundaryCheck fails the run on a cross-schema reference, and only rwb-source-data reads the ACE views.
- No production data and no outside system: the harness calls only the owning services and their fakes, never an outside gateway or a production endpoint, and the outbound item it reads is the seeded one.
- The rule row is read only through the rwb-decision contract: the harness reads no workbook, no drl_source and no rule_row row, and CatalogFidelityCheck fails the run when the case and the catalog disagree.
- No second rule engine: the harness asserts the rule ID and the package version returned by the owning service and never evaluates a rule itself.
- One hop only: the harness fails a run when the trace shows a call chain deeper than the gateway and one owner.
- The journey never writes: the harness asserts that a refusal, a no-version answer and a repeated transition leave every source unchanged.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-036 for rwb-integration. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract of the rwb-integration queue-write adapter: the placement operation on the integration base with its request and response shape, its error mapping and its idempotent replay, the three contracts it consumes and never restates, the admission decision record of the local decision-record library, the two library tables it owns and the contract fakes for rwb-case and rwb-access**, so that **the app, operations and integration-harness stories of this legacy key build on Day 1 against one agreed, testable shape, without waiting for rwb-case or rwb-access to be built and without a second owner for the placement operation**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Contract-first REST, one hop and a 2 s timeout is the decoupling rule (DP-11, ADR-020), and one REST base and one topic per service is the naming rule (DP-13, DP-14; Arch v5 slide 41). A non-engine caller that reaches into the case service directly would break both: it would need the case base, the case schema's semantics and the case team's release cycle, and the case team would inherit a caller it never agreed to serve. The adapter is the seam that keeps the caller on a base of its own while the case owner keeps the business rules.

The seam is load-bearing in three places and this document fixes all three. First, the **operation identity**: the Ownership Map keeps `POST /queues/{queueId}/placements` with P3 rwb-case, and the realignment also gives this legacy key a P2 story, so the contract must say which path is whose. The answer is that the case base keeps the placement and owns its behaviour, and the integration base serves a distinct admission and forwarding operation at the same suffix; the conflict and its reconciliation are recorded as GAP-0671. Second, the **admission rules** the adapter applies before it forwards anything: the feature flag, the Queue and allocation C right, the four field checks and the approved callers list, each with the message the legacy story already fixes. Third, the **replay**: an `Idempotency-Key` on every POST is the platform rule (Arch v5 slide 11), and an adapter that forwards a placement must be able to answer a retry without producing a second placement, a second admission record or a second decision entry.

If the shape is agreed and faked on Day 1, three teams move at once. The app story builds the admission, the record and the forward against the rwb-case and rwb-access fakes; the operations story wires the flag, the alerts and the runbook against the same contract; the wave 2 integration harness drives the journey through the owning services with the fake pack from the same documents. Without it, every caller invents its own body, the placement is owned twice, and the replay window and the admission record become a local choice per environment.

The contract also states what rwb-integration does not own: the queue, the allocation method, the cap, the overflow queue, the assignment, the placement decision entry and the CaseAllocated and CaseTransferred events are rwb-case's (Arch v5 slide 41; ownership map), and the role, scope and right answer is rwb-access's (Arch v5 slide 14). This story therefore defines the provided operation and the consumed side, and never restates another service's operation as its own (DP-01, DP-13).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service naming rule and the platform envelopes are in force: schema `rwb_integration`, REST base `/api/recovery/integration/v1`, topic `rwb.integration.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-integration` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.integration`, OpenAPI 3.1, RFC 9457 problem details and the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope (DP-13, DP-14; RWB-PLT-E1047-CON).
- The local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` are published, so the contract can state who publishes DecisionRecorded (DP-03; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON).
- The idempotency, outbox and inbox library is published, with the stored-response table, its 24-hour retention and the `Idempotency-Key` convention (DP-09; RWB-PLT-TE006-CON).
- The reference-data client library (DP-07; RWB-PLT-E1043-CON) and the rwb-access guard library (DP-08; RWB-PLT-E1037-CON) are published; the contract narrows their use and redefines neither.
- The rwb-case placement contract and the rwb-case reference-data and parameter contract are published by their stories (RWB-P3-E1019-CON, RWB-P3-E1020-CON, RWB-P3-E1043-CON), and the rwb-access authorise contract by RWB-P4-E1037-CON. This document consumes them, fakes them and defines none of them.
- The legacy values the contract reuses are the legacy values: the path suffix `queues/{queueId}/placements`, the four request fields `caseId`, `reason`, `modelOrAgent` and `version`, the configuration key `rwb.casewf.placement.approved-callers`, the caller types MODEL and AGENT and the messages MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002, MSG-P2-020, MSG-P2-021, MSG-P2-024, MSG-P2-025, MSG-P3-005, MSG-GEN-004, MSG-P4-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P4-003 and MSG-P7-003.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7 rule 1), and it sits in contract group CG-W2.

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the provided operation: the path on the integration base, the required `Idempotency-Key`, the request body, the path parameter and the access expectation, and state that the Ownership Map keeps the same suffix on the case base with P3.
2. Fix the request and response shape, with the placement result returned exactly as rwb-case returns it, and mark every element that neither the legacy story nor a technical specification names with the placeholder.
3. Fix the error mapping: which status and which message comes from the adapter's own checks and which is returned unchanged from rwb-case or rwb-access.
4. Fix the idempotent replay: the key, the endpoint, the request hash, the stored status and body, the 24-hour window, the replay answer and the expiry behaviour.
5. Fix the approved callers source: the rwb-case parameter and reference-data row under the legacy key, the row fields, the caller types, the empty list at go-live and the rule that rwb-integration holds no copy.
6. State the admission decision record: the decision code D6, the caller identity and type, the version, the reason, the target queue and the answer, written before the forward and completed with it.
7. Publish the three consumed contracts as consumed, with their owners and the 2 s client budget, and state that none is restated as provided.
8. Publish the nine contract tables of section 12, the two library tables and the P3 and P4 fakes.
9. Add the contract tests: the completeness of 12.1 to 12.9, the request and response shape, the error mapping, the replay, the approved callers source and a drift test between each fake and this document.
10. Tag the baseline and hand it to the app story, the operations story and the wave 2 integration harness of this legacy key.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A sub-table of section 12 is missing or names an owner that is not in the Ownership Map | The contract review fails and the baseline is not tagged | None | AC1 |
| X2 | The operation is declared on the case base, or the case placement is declared as provided here | The review fails: the case placement is P3's and is consumed by this service | None | AC1, AC2 |
| X3 | The request or response shape carries an element no source names, and the placeholder is missing | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC2 |
| X4 | A status or a message in the error mapping differs from the legacy story or from the owning service's text | The contract test fails on the drift | None | AC3 |
| X5 | A repeat with the same `Idempotency-Key` inside 24 hours produces a second forward or a second admission record | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC4 |
| X6 | The approved callers list is copied into `rwb_integration`, or read from anywhere but the rwb-case contract | The review fails; the list has one source and one owner | None | AC5 |
| X7 | A fake drifts from this document, or answers a path this document does not declare | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes and the four platform and service contracts as published, and fakes the two consuming ones |
| Negotiable | Field-level detail of the consumed contracts is settled with their owners; the provided operation, the replay and the admission record are fixed by this realignment |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app, operations and integration-harness stories of this legacy key on Day 1 and keeps one owner for the placement |
| Estimable | One provided operation, three consumed contracts, two library tables, nine contract tables and four fakes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact — the document, the OpenAPI file, the fake — and never against a business outcome |

```gherkin
    Given the error table of 12.1
    When each status is read
    Then 404 with MSG-P2-025 is returned by the flag check before any read or write
    Then 403 with MSG-P4-002 is returned when the identity lacks Queue and allocation C
    Then 422 with MSG-GEN-001 or MSG-GEN-002 is returned for an empty field or a length out of range, and 422 with MSG-P2-020 for a caller that is not approved
    Then 409 with MSG-P2-024, MSG-P3-005, MSG-P2-021 or MSG-GEN-004, 404 with MSG-P4-003, 401 with MSG-P4-001 and 503 with MSG-GEN-006 are returned unchanged from rwb-case or rwb-access
    Then 503 with MSG-P7-003 is returned when the admission record cannot be written, and nothing is forwarded
    Then the adapter adds no message of its own to a forwarded refusal

  Scenario: AC4 The idempotent replay is fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the replay rule of 12.1 and 12.7
    When a request is admitted and its answer stored
    Then one row exists in idempotency_key for the endpoint and the Idempotency-Key, with the request hash, the stored status and the stored body
    Then a repeat with the same key and the same request hash inside 24 hours returns the stored status and body, with no second admission record and no second forward
    Then a repeat after 24 hours is treated as a new request and rwb-case's own one-open-assignment rule decides the answer
    Then a key reused with a different request hash is refused with 409 and nothing changes
    Then a refusal produced by the adapter's own checks is stored as well, so its retry replays the refusal

  Scenario: AC5 The approved callers list has one source (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the approved callers rule of this document
    When the source of the list is read
    Then the list is the rwb-case reference-data and parameter row under the key rwb.casewf.placement.approved-callers, read through the rwb-case contract with the version in force
    Then the row carries the caller code, the caller type MODEL or AGENT, the service identity and the approval state
    Then the row field names carry the placeholder of this document and no invented name
    Then rwb-integration holds no copy of the list and no table for it
    Then the list is empty at go-live and an entry is requested by RW-COE and approved by RW-RISK before it is loaded

  Scenario: AC6 The P3 and P4 fakes match this document (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the fakes of 12.8
    When each fake is compared with the tables of section 12
    Then the rwb-case placement fake answers the 201 with an owner, the 201 with the overflow queue, the four 409s, the 404 and the 503 of this document
    Then the rwb-case reference-data fake answers the approved callers list and the empty list
    Then the rwb-access fake answers the granted and the refused Queue and allocation C
    Then the decision-record stub answers one successful write and one forced failure
    Then a drift between a fake and this document fails the contract test and blocks the merge
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One REST base per service: this contract declares `/api/recovery/integration/v1` for the provided operation and consumes the rwb-case and rwb-access bases; it never declares another service's path as provided | DP-13; Arch v5 slide 41 |
| BR2 | The placement on the case base belongs to rwb-case; the Ownership Map keeps `POST /queues/{queueId}/placements` with P3, and the integration operation is a distinct admission and forwarding operation on the integration base | Ownership map (`POST /queues/{queueId}/placements` is P3); GAP-0671 |
| BR3 | Every POST carries an `Idempotency-Key`, and the stored answer is replayed for 24 hours against the same endpoint and request hash | Arch v5 slide 11 (Idempotency-Key on every POST, stored response); DP-09; TSD P2 v3 T3.1 |
| BR4 | The adapter's own checks run in one order: the flag, the right, the fields, the approved callers list; a failure at any step writes nothing except the stored refusal | Legacy RWB-E2-036 flow steps 2 to 4 and DS exception paths X1 to X3 |
| BR5 | The approved callers list has one source and one owner: the rwb-case reference-data and parameter row under the legacy key, read with the version in force; no copy exists in `rwb_integration` | Legacy BR1 and precondition; DP-07; R-PREC default ruling |
| BR6 | The access check is the same for a model, an agent and a person: Queue and allocation right C from the rwb-access authorise contract, with no bypass for a non-engine caller | REQ-ACA-010; CTL-09; NFR-051; DP-08 |
| BR7 | The admission decision record is written through the local decision-record library before the forward, with decision code D6, the caller identity and type, the version, the reason, the target queue and the answer; a failure blocks the forward | Legacy AC3 and BR5; DP-03; R-UNI-39 |
| BR8 | The adapter returns the rwb-case answer unchanged and adds no message, no field and no second effect of its own | Legacy AC1 and section 12; DP-11 |
| BR9 | The adapter writes no case, queue or assignment row and publishes no CaseAllocated or CaseTransferred; the case events belong to rwb-case | Arch v5 slide 41; DP-01 |
| BR10 | No business value in the contract: caller codes, caller types, caps, methods, overflow queues and the decision code are data of their owners, not literals of this document | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |

##### 11. Data

The contract declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Placement request | `caseId` (uuid), `reason` (text, 1 to 1,000 characters), `modelOrAgent` (a caller code in the approved list), `version` (1 to 40 characters); `Idempotency-Key` in the header |
| Placement response, 201 | The placement result as rwb-case returns it: the case, the queue, the owner and the assignment when an owner was chosen, or the overflow queue with no owner; the decision entry reference and the status after the placement |
| Problem response | RFC 9457 problem details with the status, the message identifier and the field or the caller it names; no personal value |
| Admission record | Decision code D6, the caller identity and type, the caller code, the model or agent version, the reason, the target queue, the answer and the freshness of the list version used |
| Replay row | The endpoint, the `Idempotency-Key`, the request hash, the stored status and body, the created time and the expiry at 24 hours |
| Approved callers row | The caller code, the caller type MODEL or AGENT, the service identity and the approval state, read through the rwb-case contract with the version in force |

The exact JSON field names of the placement request, the placement response and the three consumed contracts are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0671; ASM-1199); the row fields of the approved callers list are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0671; ASM-1200); the column names of the `decision_record` library table beyond the standard columns are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0671; ASM-1201). This document fixes the element names above and leaves the property types and lengths to the review with the owners of those contracts. The `idempotency_key` column set is the one of TSD P2 v3 T3.1.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/integration/v1`; owner rwb-integration (P2); OpenAPI 3.1, `placements.yaml`.

| Method | Path | Request | Responses | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/queues/{queueId}/placements` | Path `queueId` (uuid); body `caseId` (uuid, required), `reason` (text, required, 1 to 1,000 characters), `modelOrAgent` (required, a caller code in the approved list), `version` (required, 1 to 40 characters); `Idempotency-Key` required | 201 Placement; 401 MSG-P4-001; 403 MSG-P4-002; 404 MSG-P2-025 or MSG-P4-003; 409 MSG-P2-024, MSG-P3-005, MSG-P2-021 or MSG-GEN-004; 422 MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-002 or MSG-P2-020; 503 MSG-P7-003 or MSG-GEN-006 | P2 rwb-integration |

The check order is the contract: the feature flag, the replay lookup, the Queue and allocation C right, the field validation and the approved callers check, then the admission record and the forward. A refusal produced by the adapter is stored against the `Idempotency-Key`, so a retry replays it. The ownership note is part of this table: the same path suffix appears on the case base as `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/placements`, which the Ownership Map keeps with P3 and which this service consumes (12.2); the two are different operations and neither is a wrapper of the other's contract (GAP-0671; ASM-1197). The exact JSON element names of the request and of the returned result are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0671; ASM-1199).

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/placements` | P3 rwb-case | The placement: the queue, the allocation method, the cap, the overflow queue, the access rule, the assignment, the placement decision entry and the CaseAllocated and CaseTransferred events. Faked with 201 and an owner, 201 with the overflow queue, four 409s, 404 and 503 |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | The approved callers list under the key `rwb.casewf.placement.approved-callers`, with the version in force. Faked with the list and with the empty list |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | Queue and allocation right C for the caller's service identity, with the matrix version that answered. Faked with a grant and a refusal |

Every operation is one hop with a 2 s client budget and a breaker per downstream (DP-11, ADR-020). None is declared as provided by this service. The rwb-case reference-data and parameter contract that answers the second row is RWB-P3-E1043-CON; the exact JSON field names of the three rows are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0671; ASM-1199).

###### 12.3 Events published

None of its own. The local decision-record library publishes `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) on `rwb.decision-record.v1` when the admission record is written, with decision code D6, the caller identity and type, the caller code, the version, the reason, the target queue and the answer; its schema is unchanged by this story and is the one declared in RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (DP-03).

`rwb.integration.events.v1` carries FileDelivered and FileFailed for the outbound files (Arch v5 slides 16 and 43); this slice publishes neither, because a placement is not a file. CaseAllocated and CaseTransferred are rwb-case's on `rwb.case.events.v1` and are never declared here (DP-01, DP-14).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The adapter is called synchronously and subscribes to no topic; it consumes no case event and therefore needs no inbox row for this slice.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. The adapter is a synchronous admission and forward of one REST request; it declares no workflow, no activity and no signal, and the placement starts no Temporal execution of its own. The `rwb-integration` task queue in namespace `rwb-recovery` belongs to the file and integration work of the other P2 stories.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The adapter is caller-driven; no Temporal Schedule, no cron expression and no timer is declared by this contract.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Schema | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|---|
| idempotency_key | rwb_integration | PLT library, created in rwb_integration by the rwb-integration DB story | One stored answer per endpoint and `Idempotency-Key`, with the request hash, the status, the body, the created time and the 24-hour expiry (DP-09) |
| decision_record | rwb_integration | PLT library, created in rwb_integration by the rwb-integration DB story | The admission record of decision code D6, written before the forward and completed with the answer (DP-03) |

`processed_event` is declared in the baseline of every service schema, but this slice does not use it: the adapter consumes no event, so the contract names it only to say that no inbox row is written here. No business table is named: `recovery_case`, `queue` and `assignment` are P3's and are never read directly (DP-01). The column set of `idempotency_key` is the one of TSD P2 v3 T3.1 (id, idempotency_key, endpoint, request_hash, response, with the standard record columns); the further column names of `decision_record` are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0671; ASM-1201).

| rwb-case placement WireMock | 201 with owner "U-5002" in queue "MTG-BKK-PRI"; 201 with queue "MTG-BKK-OVF" and no owner; 409 with MSG-P2-024, MSG-P3-005, MSG-P2-021 and MSG-GEN-004; 404 with MSG-P4-003; 503 with MSG-P7-003 | App story, contract tests, integration harness |
| rwb-case reference-data WireMock | The approved callers list holding MDL-SYN-PRIORITY of type MODEL for SY-AGENT, the list without MDL-SYN-UNLISTED, the empty list at go-live and a stale version answer | App story, contract tests |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `contract/placements.yaml` (the OpenAPI 3.1 document of the provided operation, with the request, the response, the error table and the `Idempotency-Key` header), `contract/placement-consumed.yaml` (the three consumed operations with their owners and the 2 s budget), `contract/placement-idempotency.md` (the key, the request hash, the stored answer and the 24-hour window), `contract/placement-approved-callers.md` (the one source and the row fields of the list), and the four WireMock mappings with their fixtures.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-08 | RecoveryAccessGuard | Authorise contract of rwb-access and the guard library | H RWB-PLT-E1037-CON; C RWB-P4-E1037-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The contract story is Day 1 with no build dependency, so these platform contracts are listed as the patterns that shape it, not as build prerequisites (Template and Rules §R5.7 rule 1).

**Build steps**

1. Write `placements.yaml`: the path, the path parameter, the four body fields with their lengths, the required `Idempotency-Key`, the 201 shape and the problem responses.
2. Write the error mapping table and check every status and message against the legacy story and against the owning services' texts.
3. Write the replay contract: the key and endpoint pair, the request hash, the stored status and body, the 24-hour window, the replay answer, the expiry and the key-reuse refusal.
4. Write the approved callers contract: the key, the row fields, the two types, the empty list at go-live and the single-source rule.
5. Write the admission record contract against the decision-record library: decision code D6, the carried fields and the transaction boundary.
6. Write `placement-consumed.yaml` from the rwb-case and rwb-access documents, with the owners and the 2 s budget.
7. Build the four WireMock mappings and their fixtures from the shapes of this document.
8. Add the six contract tests, including the drift test between each fake and this document.
9. Tag the baseline and collect the sign-off of the app, operations and integration-harness stories.

**Done when.** The four contract files and the OpenAPI document validate in the pipeline, the six contract tests pass, the four fakes answer every declared path and status, and the app, operations and integration-harness stories of this legacy key have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P2-025 | The feature flag is off | Queue placement by models and agents is switched off. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Identity lacks Queue and allocation C | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | A required field is empty | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-002 | reason or version outside its length | {field} must be between {min} and {max}. |
| MSG-P2-020 | The caller is not in the approved callers list | {caller} is not approved to place cases on queues. |
| MSG-P4-001 | No valid session or workload token | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0671; ASM-1198). |
| MSG-P2-024 | The case is already in the target queue | This case is already in {queue}. |
| MSG-P3-005 | The case is closed | This case cannot move to {state} from {current}. |
| MSG-P2-021 | The case has an open deviation | This case has an open deviation and stays with the deviation handler. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The case changed during the placement | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Queue or case not found | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Admission record write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |

MSG-GEN-006 is the platform message for a consumed service that does not answer inside the 2 s budget; its text is the platform catalogue text and is not restated here. The texts above are the legacy texts of RWB-E2-036, unchanged; this contract adds no message. A status that this service returns unchanged from rwb-case or rwb-access carries that service's text, and the contract test compares it, so the two never drift.

##### 15. Screens and states

None in this story. The caller is a job or an agent, not a person; the placed case appears in its queue on the screens of the case service (SCR-07 Team queues and SCR-02 Case list), and the admission record is read by the platform team on the operation log, not on a business screen. The replay state is a row and a metric of the adapter, with no screen state.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: caller codes, caller types, caps, methods, overflow queues and the decision code stay data of their owners.
- No personal data in the request, the response, the admission record, the replay row or a fake: identifiers, a caller code and a reason phrase only.
- The contract names only the integration base as provided and only the rwb-case and rwb-access bases as consumed; a document that names another service's path as provided fails the review (DP-13).
- The placement on the case base stays P3's; this document consumes it and never declares it, and the review fails a contract that inverts the two (BR2).
- No business table is named and no cross-schema reference is declared; the case, queue and assignment facts are read only through their owner's contract (DP-01).
- The envelope, the problem detail format, the naming rule, the idempotency library and the decision-record library come from the platform; this story narrows them but never redefines them.
- Every example and fixture is synthetic; no production caller, case number or payload is copied into a schema or a fake.

- The role, scope and right answer and the matrix versions (RWB-P4-E1037-CON and the rwb-access stories).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-036 for rwb-integration. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **an integration adapter through which an approved model or agent places a case on a queue under its own service identity, with the feature flag checked first, the caller checked against the approved callers list, the four request fields validated, the request replayed from the adapter's own idempotency table and the placement forwarded to rwb-case as one hop**, so that **analytical output reaches a person the next working day instead of through a weekly manual file, while the queue's own allocation method, caseload cap and access rules keep deciding the owner**.

The legacy story held the whole journey in one P2 Integration service: the endpoint, the queue and case tables, the allocation engine, the assignment, the decision log entry and the two events. Under D-RCV-60 the journey crosses three services. **rwb-integration** owns the model and agent queue-write adapter: the caller-facing operation, the feature flag, the caller admission check, the field validation, the admission decision record, the idempotent replay and the forwarding. **rwb-case** owns the queue, the allocation engine, the caseload cap, the overflow queue, the assignment, the placement decision entry and the CaseAllocated and CaseTransferred events (Arch v5 slide 41: rwb-case owns case, CMMN state, queues, tasks, allocation, timers). **rwb-access** owns the role, scope and right answer that the caller's service identity passes (Arch v5 slide 14: rwb-access IN `POST /authorise`).

The Ownership Map keeps `POST /queues/{queueId}/placements` with P3 rwb-case, and this realignment also gives the legacy key a P2 story. The two are reconciled rather than duplicated: rwb-case serves and keeps `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/placements`, which is the placement contract this adapter calls; rwb-integration serves the caller-facing admission and forwarding operation `POST /api/recovery/integration/v1/queues/{queueId}/placements`, which is a different operation on a different base, owned by rwb-integration and named in RWB-P2-E2036-CON. The adapter writes no `recovery_case`, no `assignment` and no `queue` row and publishes neither CaseAllocated nor CaseTransferred, because those belong to the case owner (DP-01). The reconciliation and its evidence are recorded as GAP-0670.

The adapter is a decoupling device, not a second business rule engine. It applies four checks only: the feature flag, the caller admission, the field validation and the idempotent replay. Every business rule of the placement (the queue's method, the cap, the overflow queue, the closed case, the open deviation, the one-open-assignment constraint, the decision entry and the events) stays with the placement contract and the case, exactly as the legacy story had them, and is proved in RWB-P3-E2036-APP. The local decision record (DP-03) is written before the forward, so a caller that is admitted and then refused still leaves the record of its admission and of the answer.

##### 2. Business rationale

Model scores and agent findings reach the queues today through a weekly file that a person loads by hand, so a case flagged on Monday is worked the following week (legacy RWB-E2-036). The interface lets an approved caller place a case on a queue the day the decision is made, while the queue's allocation method, caseload cap and the role to permission matrix apply as they do to any case, and every placement is written to the decision record with the caller and its version. It meets REQ-CWC-017, REQ-CWC-018 and REQ-CWC-019; the business measure is the time from a model decision to the case reaching a queue, from up to 7 days today to the same day.

The target adds a second reason. The Workbench is no longer one deployable with one schema: nineteen services each own their tables and publish their contracts, and no service reads another service's tables (Arch v5 slides 20 and 41; DP-01). A model job or an agent is a non-engine caller with a service identity, and it must not be handed a path into the case schema. It calls one stable, versioned operation, on a base of its own (`/api/recovery/integration/v1`, DP-13), with an `Idempotency-Key` (Arch v5 slide 11) and a recorded answer, and the service that owns the case decides the placement. That is what makes the interface safe to switch on for an outside caller: the caller cannot reach the queue, the case or the assignment, only the adapter.

The adapter also carries the audit half of the legacy BR5. The legacy wrote one decision log entry with the caller, the reason and the model or agent version. In the target two records exist and both are needed: rwb-case writes the placement entry with final call "PLACED {queue}" in the same transaction as the case change, the assignment and the outbox rows (proved in RWB-P3-E2036-APP), and rwb-integration writes its own admission record through the local decision-record library of DP-03, with the caller identity, the caller type, the reason, the model or agent version, the target queue and the answer it returned. A decision that cannot be recorded does not proceed (R-UNI-39; Principle 5).

It applies REQ-ACA-010 as well: a model or agent passes the same role, scope and right checks as a person, through the rwb-access authorise contract and its guard library, with no bypass for a non-engine caller (CTL-09; NFR-051).

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P2-E2036-CON is published: the contract of this adapter, with the placement operation on the integration base, the three consumed contracts, the idempotent replay and the fakes. It is a same-service contract story and is therefore a build dependency.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03). The library writes the record and publishes `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) on the service's behalf.
- RWB-PLT-E1043-CON is published: the reference-data client library that reads a row by key with the version in force (DP-07), used for the approved callers list.
- RWB-PLT-E1037-CON is published: the rwb-access guard library that performs the authorise call and caches the answer per session and per workload identity (DP-08).
- RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is published: the idempotency, outbox and inbox library, with the stored-response table and the 24-hour retention rule (DP-09).
- RWB-PLT-E1047-CON is published: the naming library that fixes the base, the topic and the event names (DP-14), and RWB-PLT-E1044-CON the per-service Flyway sequence and migration conventions of `rwb_integration` (DP-15).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff route that lets an approved caller reach the integration base, and that serves the reading screens the placed case appears on (DP-19).
- The `rwb_integration` library tables `idempotency_key` and `decision_record` exist from the rwb-integration baseline, created by the DB story of this epic on the per-service Flyway sequence.
- The caller is listed in the approved callers list (legacy configuration key `rwb.casewf.placement.approved-callers`) with its caller code, its type MODEL or AGENT and its service identity. The list is empty at go-live (assumed in the legacy story); RW-COE requests an entry and RW-RISK approves it.
- The permission matrix in force gives the caller's service identity Queue and allocation C through the rwb-access authorise contract. The matrix today gives SY-AGENT R only, so a matrix version change by RW-SECADM is needed before the first caller is switched on.
- The target queue exists with its assignment method, caseload cap and overflow queue (DL23; caseload cap 150, assumed), and the case exists with a status and no open deviation. Both facts are read by rwb-case, never by this service.
- Feature flag `rwb.casewf.queue-placement` is off in every environment except DEV and SIT test runs. The flag value is read from the platform flag library (Template and Rules §R3 default ruling); off returns 404 with MSG-P2-025 and touches nothing.
- The service runs as its own login on the ACE database (DP-02). The login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0670; ASM-1190).

##### 4. Flow

1. Caller (model job or agent, under its service identity): sends `POST /api/recovery/integration/v1/queues/{queueId}/placements` with `caseId`, `reason`, `modelOrAgent` and `version`, an `Idempotency-Key` and its workload token.
2. gateway-bff: routes the call to rwb-integration on the integration base; it composes nothing for this path, because the caller is not a screen (DP-19).
3. PlacementAdapterController: resolves the caller identity from the workload token and reads the feature flag `rwb.casewf.queue-placement` from the platform flag library. Off returns 404 with MSG-P2-025 and touches nothing.
4. PlacementAdapterController: checks for a stored answer with the same `Idempotency-Key` for this endpoint in `idempotency_key`; a hit within 24 hours returns the stored status and body unchanged, and no second forward is made.
5. AccessCheckClient: checks Queue and allocation right C for the caller's service identity through the rwb-access authorise contract, cached per workload identity with the matrix version that answered (DP-08).
6. PlacementAdapterController: validates the four fields (presence, type, `reason` 1 to 1,000 characters, `version` 1 to 40 characters) and returns 422 naming the field and the rule, with MSG-GEN-001 or MSG-GEN-002.
7. ApprovedCallerCatalog: reads the approved callers list from the rwb-case reference-data contract under the key `rwb.casewf.placement.approved-callers`, with the version in force (DP-07), and checks that `modelOrAgent` is listed for this caller's service identity with its type. An unlisted caller returns 422 with MSG-P2-020.
8. PlacementAdmissionService: derives the request hash from the method, the path and the canonical body and writes the admission record through the local decision-record library (DP-03): decision code D6, the caller identity and type, the caller code, the version, the reason, the target queue and the outcome that will be recorded.
9. CasePlacementClient: forwards the placement to the rwb-case contract `POST /api/recovery/case/v1/queues/{queueId}/placements` with the same body plus the caller service identity, in one hop with a 2 s timeout and a circuit breaker (DP-11).
10. rwb-case: applies the queue, the allocation method, the cap, the overflow queue, the access rule of the case and the case state; this front end writes nothing of that (proved in RWB-P3-E2036-APP).
11. PlacementAdmissionService: records the answer in the admission record and stores the status and the response body against the `Idempotency-Key` in `idempotency_key` for 24 hours, so a repeat replays it.
12. PlacementAdapterController: returns the rwb-case answer unchanged: 201 with the placement result, or 403, 404, 409, 422 or 503 with the rwb-case problem. This adapter adds no message of its own to a forwarded refusal.
13. Repeat of the same request with the same `Idempotency-Key` inside 24 hours: the stored answer is returned with no second admission record, no second forward and no second effect.
14. A request refused by the adapter's own checks (flag, right, fields, approved callers, local record) is stored too, so the caller's retry replays the refusal instead of producing a second decision record.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | Feature flag off | 404; nothing changes, nothing is recorded | MSG-P2-025 | AC4 |
| X2 | Caller is not in the approved callers list for its service identity | 422; nothing is forwarded | MSG-P2-020 | AC5 |
| X3 | `caseId`, `reason`, `modelOrAgent` or `version` empty | 422 naming the field; nothing is forwarded | MSG-GEN-001 | AC6 |
| X4 | `reason` or `version` outside its length range | 422 naming the field and the range | MSG-GEN-002 | AC6 |
| X5 | The case is already in the target queue, including a repeated call without an `Idempotency-Key` | 409 from rwb-case, returned unchanged; no second entry, no second assignment | MSG-P2-024 | AC7 |
| X6 | The case is closed | 409 from rwb-case, returned unchanged | MSG-P3-005 | AC8 |
| X7 | The case has an open deviation | 409 from rwb-case; the case stays with the deviation handler | MSG-P2-021 | AC9 |
| X8 | The queue or the case does not exist | 404 from rwb-case or from the authorise call, returned unchanged | MSG-P4-003 | AC10 |
| X9 | Every owner in the queue is at the caseload cap | 201 with the overflow queue and no owner; this adapter returns the answer unchanged | None | AC2 |
| X10 | Two placements of the same case commit at the same time | One commits with 201; the other gets 409, returned unchanged | MSG-GEN-004 | AC11 |
| X11 | The caller's identity lacks Queue and allocation C | 403 before any forward; nothing is recorded as placed | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-036-13 |
| X12 | The admission record cannot be written | 503; nothing is forwarded and nothing changes; an incident is raised (R-UNI-39) | MSG-P7-003 | TC-E2-036-14 |
| X13 | rwb-case, rwb-access or the rwb-case reference-data contract does not answer inside the REST budget | One hop, 2 s timeout and breaker; 503 and nothing forwarded | MSG-GEN-006 | AC1 |
| X14 | The same request arrives twice with the same `Idempotency-Key` inside 24 hours | The stored answer is replayed; no second admission record, no second forward | None | AC1 |
| X15 | The same request arrives with the same `Idempotency-Key` after 24 hours | Treated as a new request; rwb-case's own one-open-assignment rule decides, and a repeat inside the queue is refused with 409 | MSG-P2-024 | AC7 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against the published contracts: its own contract story, the decision-record library, the reference-data and authorise libraries, the idempotency library, the naming rule, the migrations and the edge route. The rwb-case and rwb-access answers come from their contract fakes, so no case service is needed to build or test this service |
| Negotiable | Which callers are approved is configuration; the caps, methods and overflow queues are queue data of rwb-case; the adapter fixes only the flag, the admission, the validation, the replay and the forward |
| Valuable | A daily model or agent decision reaches a person the same day without giving a non-engine caller a path into the case schema |
| Estimable | One endpoint, one admission service, three consumed contracts, two library tables, one flag and one fake pack |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each owned criterion has one test with a synthetic caller; every cross-service answer is stubbed in the contract fake |
