**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-038 for the workflow platform epic; the codec protocol, the authorizer audit call, the entry contract and the error codes are published on Day 1 with three fakes. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **consumer of the codec and admin-audit contract** (the Temporal Web UI, the authorizer plugin, the security administrator and the audit team), I want **the codec protocol models, the authorizer audit call contract, the decision entry contract and the error codes published on Day 1 with fakes**, so that **the codec server, the plugin and the audit reconciliation are built and tested against one frozen set**.

This is the contract story of legacy key RWB-E2-038 under epic RWB-PLT-WF. It publishes, as a platform contract of the Temporal layer:

- The codec server protocol document: `POST /decode` and `POST /encode`, the request and response models of the Temporal codec server protocol, the payload metadata rule and the 401, 403, 413, 422 and 503 errors.
- The authorizer audit call contract: the operation, namespace, workflow ID, run ID, actor reference, grant, reason and request ID the frontend plugin sends, the 201 entry identifier it must receive, and the rule that any non-201 answer denies the call.
- The decision entry contract: the AC-READ, AC-DENY and PLATFORM_ADMIN codes and the field list of the entry, with no payload and no personal data.
- The idempotency contract: one entry per operation on one run, from the Web UI request ID and from the frontend request ID.
- Three fakes — a codec server, an audit receiver and an authorizer — and a contract test, so the plugin, the Web UI and the reconciliation can be built and tested with no Key Vault and no cluster.

The codec server and the audit path are shared platform, not one of the 19 services: Template and Rules §R4 has no platform row, so this document declares no `rwb_*` schema, no `rwb.<short>.events.v1` topic and no `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` base. The codec server publishes the Temporal codec server protocol behind the platform internal ingress, and the authorizer audit call is an mTLS call with no HTTP path of the Workbench API. The contract is published at status Draft (realignment v1) and is frozen when its consumers pass their contract tests.

##### 2. Business rationale

The decode path is the one place a clear payload leaves the engine, and the authorizer path is the one place an administrative action becomes recordable. Both must be frozen before any code, because they are consumed from three sides at once: the Temporal Web UI sets a codec endpoint per environment, the Temporal frontend loads a plugin that must agree on the audit call, and the reconciliation and the audit team read the same entry fields. If the three are written to three private readings, the first integration test in SIT discovers it, and by then the plugin configuration, the key resolver and the reconciliation are all built on the wrong shape.

ADR-020 makes the contract the first artefact: an OpenAPI-style protocol document for the two codec operations, a typed call contract for the audit path, a field contract for the entry and one error table, published with fakes. The fake is the second reason: the plugin and the Web UI integration can then be tested with no Key Vault and no cluster, so a decode test does not need a key and an audit test does not need a namespace. That is what keeps REQ-DRI-001, REQ-DRI-005 and NFR-045 testable on Day 1 rather than at the end of the wave, and it is what lets RWB-PLT-E2038-APP start on the same day as this story.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-PLT-E1070-CON is published: the namespace `rwb-recovery`, the mTLS identities, the Web UI codec endpoint setting and the frontend authorizer plugin slot from the values file.
- RWB-PLT-E1071-CON is published: the codec contract of the worker and SDK side, so the payload metadata this document declares is the metadata the codec writes.
- RWB-P4-E1039-CON is published: the ACTIVE break-glass grant, the AC-BGON entry, `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` and the LOV-DECISION codes AC-READ and AC-DENY.
- RWB-P7-E1027-CON is published: the decision-record contract behind DecisionLogApi, so the entry this document declares is the entry that library writes.
- The Temporal codec server protocol is the protocol of the platform's Temporal version 1.30 or later (Architecture v5 slide 23); this contract republishes it and adds no field of its own to the request or the response.
- The values 100 payloads and 1 MB per request, the 02:00 reconciliation and the key versions 1, 2 and 3 are carried from the legacy story; the key rotation period, the archive retention and the platform identity that runs the codec server are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1441; ASM-2536) and are published as the working read of that assumption.
- The contract is Draft until its consumers pass: RWB-PLT-E2038-APP, the Web UI integration and the reconciliation test. No approval is required to publish a Draft contract.

##### 4. Flow

1. The contract author writes the codec protocol document: `POST /decode` and `POST /encode`, the request model (namespace, workflowId, runId, requestId, payloads), the response model (payloads and entryId) and the error table.
2. The author writes the payload metadata rule: every payload carries `metadata.encoding` and `metadata.keyVersion`, and a payload without metadata is refused whole, with no key guessed and no clear fallback.
3. The author writes the authorizer audit call: operation, namespace, workflowId, runId, actorRef, grantId (nullable), reason and requestId, answered with a 201 and an entryId, with any other answer denying the call.
4. The author writes the decision entry contract: the three codes AC-READ, AC-DENY and PLATFORM_ADMIN and the field list of the entry, with no payload and no personal data.
5. The author writes the error contract and the idempotency contract: 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 413, 422 and 503, and one entry per operation on one run for a repeated requestId.
6. The fake codec, the fake audit receiver and the fake authorizer are generated from the documents, with the 201 and 503 answers and the refusal examples.
7. The contract test runs the fakes against the documents on every change: a field, a code or a status that drifts fails the build.
8. The documents and the fakes are published at v1 to the contract registry; RWB-PLT-E2038-APP, the Web UI integration and the reconciliation test pin v1, and the contract is frozen when all three pass.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message |
|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A payload in a document example carries no codec metadata | The lint step fails the build; the metadata rule is mandatory in every request model and in every example | Lint finding, no message id |
| X2 | A document lets a role other than RW-SECADM decode | The lint step fails the build; the authorization clause names RW-SECADM and the break-glass grant, and the 403 example uses MSG-P4-002 | Lint finding, no message id |
| X3 | A document or a fake treats an ended grant as a valid one | The lint step fails the build; the grant states are ACTIVE and ENDED, and only ACTIVE passes the check in every example | Lint finding, no message id |
| X4 | The decision log is unavailable in the audit-call contract or in the fake | The contract declares 503 and the deny rule; the fake answers 503 and the authorizer refuses; the workflow stays unchanged in the example | None (503 refusal text) |
| X5 | A breaking change is made to a published field, code or error | v1 is not edited; the change raises v2 and deprecates v1, and no consumer sees a changed v1 | Lint finding, no message id |
| X6 | A value the consumers need is named by no source: the platform identity that runs the codec server, its internal base, the key rotation period and the archive retention the version list depends on | The value is published as the working read of the assumption, with the placeholder where it is still open, and the gap stays open | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1441; ASM-2536) |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Publishes documents and three fakes; builds nothing, reads no business data, depends on nothing |
| Negotiable | Field order inside the models, the example values and the fake's transport are open until the version is frozen; the codes, the 201 rule and the write-before-act rule are fixed |
| Valuable | The codec server, the plugin, the Web UI integration and the reconciliation start on Day 1 against one frozen set and three fakes |
| Estimable | Two protocol operations, one audit call, one entry contract, one error table, three fakes, one contract test |
| Small | One sprint for the documents, the fakes and the lint rules |
| Testable | Each criterion in section 7 is a schema, lint or fake assertion in section 16 |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Temporal security, codec server and admin audit contract

  Background:
    Given the codec server answers the Temporal codec server protocol on the platform internal ingress
    Given the platform publishes no schema, no topic and no /api/recovery base of its own

  Scenario: AC1 The codec protocol document is published (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the codec server protocol document
    When it is validated and linted
    Then it declares POST /decode and POST /encode with the request model namespace, workflowId, runId, requestId and payloads
    Then it declares the response model payloads in the same order plus entryId
    Then it declares 401 no session, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 413 above 100 payloads or 1 MB, 422 without codec metadata or with a key version that is not enabled, and 503 with no payload returned
    Then it declares the authorization as Platform administration R plus an ACTIVE break-glass grant for area PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION

  Scenario: AC2 The payload metadata rule is mandatory (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a payload object of the request model
    When the schema is validated
    Then every payload declares metadata with encoding and keyVersion, and data as base64
    Then a request holding one payload without metadata is refused with 422 as a whole, and no payload of that request is answered
    Then no example and no fake answers a payload the metadata cannot attribute to a version

  Scenario: AC3 The authorizer audit call is published (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the audit record the Temporal frontend plugin sends over mTLS
    When the call contract is reviewed
    Then it declares operation as TERMINATE, RESET or SIGNAL, and namespace, workflowId, runId, actorRef, grantId, reason and requestId
    Then grantId is nullable, because an administrative call may carry a grant and a decode always does
    Then a 201 answer returns entryId and any non-201 answer denies the call with PERMISSION_DENIED, leaving the workflow unchanged

  Scenario: AC4 The entry contract is published (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the decision entry a decode, a refusal and an administrative call each write
    When the entry contract is reviewed
    Then it declares the codes AC-READ, AC-DENY and PLATFORM_ADMIN
    Then it declares the operation, namespace, workflow ID, run ID, actor, grant, incident and reason fields
    Then it declares that no payload, no history event and no clear personal data field is part of an entry
    Then a decode is AC-READ, a refusal is AC-DENY and a terminate, reset or signal is PLATFORM_ADMIN

  Scenario: AC5 The idempotency contract is published (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a decode and an administrative call repeated with the same requestId
    When the contract and the fake are read together
    Then the codec takes requestId from the Web UI and a repeat returns the same payloads and entryId and writes no second entry
    Then the audit call takes requestId from the frontend request and one operation on one run writes one entry
    Then a second entry for the same requestId is refused and logged, and no duplicate entry reaches the decision log

  Scenario: AC6 The fakes answer every contract test and a breaking change raises v2 (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the fake codec, the fake audit receiver and the fake authorizer, generated from the documents
    When the contract test runs
    Then the fake codec answers both operations, every error example and the payload without metadata
    Then the fake audit receiver answers the 201 entryId and the 503 failure, and the fake authorizer denies on any non-201 answer
    Then a breaking change raises v2 and marks v1 deprecated, and no consumer sees an edited v1
```

These criteria are new and test only the contract baseline: no legacy criterion is repeated here, and every value in the examples comes from RWB-E2-038, character for character.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The codec server is the only path to a clear payload and the protocol is the Temporal codec server protocol; this contract adds no field and no operation of its own | Architecture v5 slide 24; legacy RWB-E2-038 section 12 |
| BR2 | Every payload carries encoding and keyVersion in its metadata; a request with one payload without metadata is refused whole and no key is guessed | NFR-045; legacy BR8 |
| BR3 | A decode needs RW-SECADM with an ACTIVE break-glass grant for area PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION and right R; no standing right and no other role is declared | RWB-P4-E1039-CON; legacy BR1 |
| BR4 | The entry is written before the payload is returned, and before the frontend executes an administrative call; a failed write answers no payload and denies the call | REQ-DRI-005; legacy BR3, BR4 |
| BR5 | Every entry names the operation, namespace, workflow ID, run ID, actor, reason and, where one applies, the grant and the incident | REQ-DRI-001; legacy BR5 |
| BR6 | An entry carries no payload, no history event and no clear personal data field, and the codes are AC-READ, AC-DENY and PLATFORM_ADMIN from LOV-DECISION | LOV-DECISION; NFR-045; legacy BR6 |
| BR7 | One entry per operation on one run: the codec and the audit call are idempotent on requestId and a duplicate writes nothing | Legacy section 12 |
| BR8 | A breaking change raises a new version and deprecates v1; v1 is never edited in place | Template and Rules §R7.2; ADR-020 |

##### 9. State transitions

| Object | State | Meaning in this contract |
|---|---|---|
| Contract document | DRAFT | Published (realignment v1) and open to comment |
| Contract document | PUBLISHED | v1 in the contract registry, the fakes generated from it, consumers pinning it |
| Contract document | FROZEN | The app story, the Web UI integration and the reconciliation test have passed; a change now raises v2 |
| Contract document | DEPRECATED | A v2 exists; v1 is read-only and still served by its fake |
| Break-glass grant | ACTIVE | The only state in which the codec answers a decode |
| Break-glass grant | ENDED | The grant's end time was reached or it was revoked; the decode is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002 |
| Fake audit receiver | 201 | The entry was written; the authorizer allows the frontend call |
| Fake audit receiver | 503 | The entry could not be written; the authorizer denies the call and the workflow is unchanged |

The grant states are the P4 contract's and the fake answers are the fake's; this contract owns only the document states and the answer vocabulary.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| The contract author (any team, per U3) | Writes and versions the documents, the error table and the fakes |
| Security architecture | Confirms the decode rule, the grant area and right, and the no-standing-right clause |
| The platform owner of the Temporal platform | Approves a breaking change and a version freeze, and owns the values file that loads the plugin |
| Internal audit | Confirms the entry field list, the three codes and the no-payload rule |
| The rwb-access owner (P4) | Confirms the grant states and the access log read the document names |
| The rwb-decision owner (P7) | Confirms the entry fields and the code list it writes and seals |
| RW-SECADM, RW-PLATADM, RW-AUDIT | Read the contract; raise a change request rather than a private variant |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A codec and audit contract is a technical artefact, not a credit decision |

No personal name, no email address and no credential appears in a document, a schema, an example or a fake. Where a caller must be named, the example uses a user identifier or a role code only.

##### 11. Data

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Business data published | None. The documents publish operation names, model shapes, field names, codes and status codes; no customer, account, case or document value appears |
| Payload content in an example | Encoded base64 data of a synthetic payload with `metadata.encoding` and `metadata.keyVersion`; no clear value is published, and the response example shows the shape with a synthetic body |
| Workflow identifiers in examples | Synthetic: case-RW-2026-000301 to case-RW-2026-000307, and the run identifiers that go with them |
| Personal data | None. No name, no email address, no account number, no national identifier and no document content in a schema, an example or a fake |
| Entry fields | The field names and shapes of `decision_log_entry`, owned by rwb-decision (P7) and fixed by RWB-P7-E1027-CON: the operation, namespace, workflow ID, run ID, actor, grant, incident, reason, code and timestamps |
| Tables published | None. This document declares no table and no migration; the entry table is P7's and the frontend audit log is the Temporal namespace's |
| Retention | None at the contract: a document keeps no data, and the fakes hold only the examples they publish |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

The codec server speaks the Temporal codec server protocol on the platform internal ingress. It has no `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` base, no gateway route and no place in the Workbench API Specification.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Responses |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/decode` | Returns the clear payloads of one history request | 200 payloads and entryId; 401; 403; 413; 422; 503 |
| POST | `/encode` | Returns the encoded form of payloads written by an authorised client | 200 payloads and entryId; 401; 403; 413; 422; 503 |

| Model | Fields |
|---|---|
| Request | namespace, workflowId, runId, requestId, payloads: an array of { metadata: { encoding, keyVersion }, data: base64 } |
| Response 200 | payloads: an array of { metadata, data: base64 } in the same order, and entryId |
| Error | status, code or message identifier where one exists (MSG-P4-002 on 403), and a detail that names the payload index and the missing metadata on 422, never the payload |

The internal ingress base per environment is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1441; ASM-2536); the two operations and the models above are the published surface, and the base is environment configuration of the Web UI.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The contract publishes two operations and consumes none: the grant read and the entry write belong to the consumers, through RWB-P4-E1039-CON and DecisionLogApi.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The platform owns no topic, and the entry event `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` is the decision-record library's (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The reconciliation reads the frontend audit log and the access log; it subscribes to no topic.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

The authorizer audit call and the reconciliation contract, both without an HTTP path:

| Model | Fields |
|---|---|
| Audit call request | operation (TERMINATE, RESET or SIGNAL), namespace, workflowId, runId, actorRef, grantId (nullable), reason, requestId |
| Audit call response | 201 with entryId; any other status denies the call with PERMISSION_DENIED, and the workflow is unchanged |
| Audit call transport | mTLS from the Temporal frontend pods only, with the frontend's client certificate; no gateway, no Workbench route |
| Audit call idempotency | requestId from the frontend request; one entry per operation on one run |
| Reconciliation contract | The 02:00 run on task queue `rwb-platform` reads the frontend audit log and the AC-READ, AC-DENY and PLATFORM_ADMIN entries, reports each unmatched terminate, reset or signal with its workflow ID, operation and time, and writes no entry of its own |

The reconciliation is a Temporal Schedule in namespace `rwb-recovery` (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON); this contract fixes what the run compares and what it reports, not the workflow's internals.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None owned by this contract. The 02:00 reconciliation Schedule is the app story's (RWB-PLT-E2038-APP section 12.6); this contract fixes the cadence and the report only.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. `decision_log_entry` is rwb-decision's (P7) and the frontend audit log belongs to the Temporal namespace; this document declares no table, no column and no migration.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Fake codec server (this story) | `POST /decode` and `POST /encode` with the request and response models, the 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 413, 422 and 503 examples, a payload without metadata and a key version that is not enabled | RWB-PLT-E2038-APP, the Web UI integration |
| Fake audit receiver (this story) | The audit call with the 201 entryId and the 503 failure | The plugin configuration test, RWB-PLT-E2038-APP AC6 |
| Fake authorizer (this story) | The allow-on-201 and deny-on-any-other-answer rule, for the Web UI and CLI path | The plugin test and the denial example |
| rwb-access break-glass fake (RWB-P4-E1039-CON) | The grant read, the AC-BGON entry, the access log read and the LOV-DECISION codes, with ACTIVE, ENDED and wrong-area variants | The role, grant and area examples |
| Decision-record fake (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON) | The DecisionLogApi write, the entry fields and the write failure | The entry contract examples and the 503 path |

The three fakes answer from the two owner fakes rather than from copied payloads, so a change to the grant contract or the entry contract shows up as a contract-test failure here.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary (REST, Kafka, Temporal, File)

| Call type | Provided | Consumed | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| REST | 2 codec operations on the internal ingress, with no service base | 0 | Temporal codec server protocol, 401, 403, 413, 422 and 503 |
| Kafka | 0 | 0 | No topic of its own |
| Temporal | 1 audit call contract (mTLS, 201 or deny) and the 02:00 reconciliation contract | 0 | Namespace `rwb-recovery`, task queue `rwb-platform` |
| File | 0 | 0 | No file is read or written |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.**

- `codec-server.yaml`: the two operations, the request and response models, the payload metadata rule and the error table.
- `authorizer-audit.yaml`: the audit call request and response, the mTLS clause, the 201 rule and the deny rule.
- `decision-entry.yaml`: the three codes, the entry field list and the no-payload rule.
- The error and idempotency sections of this document, generated into the three artefacts.
- The fake codec server, the fake audit receiver and the fake authorizer, generated from the artefacts.
- The lint rules and the contract test.

**Pattern application**

| DP code | legacy marker | microservice pattern | dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | the entry contract this story publishes is DP-03 applied: H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON for its consumer |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none: the access log read is a C row of the app story |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

These are the Template and Rules §R5.5 rows that apply to this contract. The story documents them and adds no build dependency of its own: it is a CON story, starts on Day 1 and is frozen when its consumers pass. DP-03 and DP-11 are the two rows the document is about: DP-03 because every decode, refusal and administrative call is a decision record through the local library, and DP-11 because the access log is read as a REST contract, one hop, instead of the monolith's in-process call. DP-13 is why the legacy module path for the access log is never repeated here: the read is `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log`, and the codec server, which never sat under the monolith base, publishes no base of its own.

**Build steps**

1. Write `codec-server.yaml` with the two operations, the request and response models and the payload metadata rule.
2. Write the error table: 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 413 at 100 payloads or 1 MB, 422 without metadata or with a key version that is not enabled, 503 with no payload returned.
3. Write `authorizer-audit.yaml` with the call fields, the nullable grant, the 201 entryId and the deny rule.
4. Write `decision-entry.yaml` with the three codes, the entry fields and the no-payload rule.
5. Add the lint rules: no service base in the codec paths, metadata mandatory, RW-SECADM and the ACTIVE grant in the authorization clause, a message identifier on the 403, a personal-data scan over every example, and one entry per requestId.
6. Generate the three fakes over the P4 break-glass fake and the P7 decision-record fake, write the contract test, and publish v1 to the contract registry with the version the consumers pin.

**Done when.** The three artefacts and the schemas validate, every lint rule passes, the three fakes answer every example including the payload without metadata and the 503 denial, the contract test is green on the build of this story, and RWB-PLT-E2038-APP, the Web UI integration and the reconciliation test have pinned v1.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Published as |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | The role is not RW-SECADM, the grant is missing, ended or for another area, or the caller is not the platform identity on the internal endpoint | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | 403, reused unchanged, with {action} set to "decode this workflow payload" or "record this workflow action" |
| PLT-CODEC-401 | No session, or the session has expired | The standard no-session text; the title and detail are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1441; ASM-2536) | 401 |
| PLT-CODEC-413 | More than 100 payloads or more than 1 MB in one request | The request is refused before any key is resolved; the text names the count or the size only | 413 |
| PLT-CODEC-422 | A payload without codec metadata, or a key version that is not enabled | The request is refused whole; the text names the payload index and the missing metadata, never the payload | 422 |
| PLT-CODEC-503 | Key Vault is unavailable, or the entry could not be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded; no payload is returned and the workflow is unchanged | 503, and the deny answer of the audit call |

MSG-P4-002 is reused unchanged and is the only message identifier the documents borrow from a service. The three PLT-CODEC identifiers are reserved for this contract; when the message catalogue gains platform codec entries they replace the placeholder text and no other value changes.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story, and the contract declares none. The codec server has no user interface: the Temporal Web UI's payload panel is its only surface, and the panel shows encoded, decoding, decoded and refused with MSG-P4-002. The audit path has no screen either; the entries appear on the access log read and on SCR-38 Decision log query. This contract fixes the document states of section 9 so that the app story, the plugin test and the audit team share one vocabulary.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No service base and no gateway route in the codec contract: the protocol is the Temporal codec server protocol on the internal ingress, and the lint step fails the build if a `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` path appears.
- The metadata rule is mandatory: a payload without encoding and keyVersion is refused whole and is never resolved with a guessed key.
- Decode is never a standing right: the authorization clause names RW-SECADM, the ACTIVE grant, the area and right R, and the 403 example carries MSG-P4-002.
- No entry, no action: the contract declares the 201 rule and the deny rule, and no example shows an action taken after a failed write.
- No personal data in a schema, an example, a fake or a log: identifiers, codes and status values only, and the scan fails the build otherwise.
- No payload and no clear field in an entry: the entry contract lists the operation, namespace, workflow ID, run ID, actor, grant, incident, reason, code and timestamps, and nothing else.
- No table and no migration in this contract: the entry table is P7's and the frontend audit log is the namespace's.
- The contract is versioned: a breaking change raises v2 and deprecates v1 in place of editing v1.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-038 for the workflow platform epic; the codec server, the authorizer audit path and the daily reconciliation become platform work built against RWB-PLT-E2038-CON, and the seven legacy criteria are carried whole. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **security administrator (RW-SECADM)**, I want **decode of workflow payloads limited to an open break-glass grant and every decode, terminate, reset and signal written to the decision log**, so that **workflow history cannot leak personal data and no administrative action on a case workflow is unrecorded**.

This is the split (rework) slice of legacy key RWB-E2-038 under epic RWB-PLT-WF (Template and Rules §R6). No legacy section is copied word for word and no delta copy of an as-built story is made: section 7 carries the seven legacy criteria with every value kept, and the microservice change for the legacy key is described here. The change from the legacy story:

- **Placement.** The codec server stops being a servlet inside the monolith's access module and becomes the codec server of the shared Temporal platform, owned once and used by every workbench namespace (Architecture v5 slide 23; Temporal and Drools design slide 12). The platform team owns it, as it owns the cluster, the namespaces and the codec keys; the Workbench API Specification carries none of its paths.
- **Contract first.** The codec protocol, the authorizer audit call, the entry field contract and the error codes are published on Day 1 by RWB-PLT-E2038-CON with fakes, before any code (ADR-020). This story builds against that contract and its fake.
- **The entry.** The AC-READ, AC-DENY and PLATFORM_ADMIN entries are decision records, written through the DecisionLogApi of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON in the caller's transaction (DP-03); the table `decision_log_entry` stays with rwb-decision (P7) and this story owns no table (DP-01).
- **The read.** The access log is no longer a monolith path but the P4 REST contract `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log`, read one hop from the owner (DP-11, DP-13); the break-glass grant is read through the P4 break-glass contract, which is a C row.
- **The reconciliation.** The 02:00 job stops being Quartz (retired with RWB-TE-007 by Template and Rules §R6) and becomes a Temporal Schedule on the platform task queue that starts `TemporalAdminAuditListener` (DP-10 pattern, through RWB-PLT-E1071-CON).
- **The values.** `PLATFORM_ADMIN` stays a LOV-DECISION data row loaded through RWB-E1-043, now the reference-data contract RWB-PLT-E1043-CON (DP-07); the payload limits, the reconciliation time and the key version list stay configuration (DP-06); the flag `rwb.p3.temporal` stays a parameter read.

The codec server and the audit path are shared platform, not one of the 19 services: Template and Rules §R4 has no platform row, so this story writes no `rwb_*` schema, publishes no `rwb.<short>.events.v1` topic and owns no `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` base. What it does own is the codec server protocol behind the internal ingress, the audit receiver the Temporal frontend calls over mTLS, and the reconciliation Schedule on task queue `rwb-platform` in namespace `rwb-recovery`.

##### 2. Business rationale

The history is encrypted by the payload codec, which protects it at rest, but the Temporal Web UI needs a codec server to show a payload. A codec server that answers any Workbench session turns the encryption into a display setting: every history the user can open becomes clear personal data, and no log names the reader. At the same time terminate, reset and signal change the path of a live case, and the only record today is the frontend audit log inside the Temporal namespace, which a Workbench audit query by case cannot read.

This story puts both behind one rule: a decode is allowed only for RW-SECADM with an open break-glass grant against an incident, and every administrative call writes a decision log entry before the frontend executes it. It meets REQ-DRI-001 (one record per decision) and REQ-DRI-005 (no action without its entry), and it supports NFR-045, because a synthetic history is the only thing a test may carry and a clear payload is never a screen default. The measure is that no clear payload leaves the codec server without an AC-READ entry naming the grant, and that the daily reconciliation finds no administrative action without an entry.

After the split the two paths are also the platform's, and that is the point of moving them into this epic. The codec server sits in the layer the platform team owns once (Architecture v5 slide 23), so a second workbench inherits the rule instead of writing its own; the authorizer plugin is configuration of the same frontend the platform team operates; and the reconciliation becomes a Temporal Schedule instead of a Quartz trigger, so it lives where every other Recovery timer lives. The alternative — a codec server per service and a Quartz job per module — would give the bank one place per workbench where a clear payload can be read and no single place where an administrative action is proven recorded.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-PLT-E2038-CON is published: the codec protocol models, the payload metadata rule, the authorizer audit call, the entry field contract, the error codes and the three fakes.
- The nine platform contracts are published: RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (the local decision-record library and the DecisionLogApi), RWB-PLT-E1042-CON (parameters), RWB-PLT-E1043-CON (reference data, the LOV-DECISION row), RWB-PLT-E1047-CON (naming), RWB-PLT-E1044-CON (per-service Flyway baseline), RWB-PLT-N001-CON (the gateway route the access log read passes through, DP-19), RWB-PLT-E1070-CON (the cluster, namespace `rwb-recovery`, mTLS, the Web UI values file and the authorizer plugin slot) and RWB-PLT-E1071-CON (the workflow kit and the Schedule template, DP-10).
- The three owner contracts are consumed as C rows through their fakes: RWB-P3-E1042-CON (parameters), RWB-P3-E1043-CON (reference data) and RWB-P4-E1039-CON (the break-glass grant, the AC-BGON entry, `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` and the LOV-DECISION codes AC-READ and AC-DENY).
- `PLATFORM_ADMIN` is added as a LOV-DECISION value as a system event code through the versioned reference load of RWB-E1-043, loaded by the data steward role; the addition is recorded in the additions file.
- The codec server runs behind the internal ingress and the Web UI codec endpoint setting names it per environment; no key and no codec runs on a workstation.
- Key Vault holds the codec key with versions 1, 2 and 3, version 2 current at the start of the test and version 3 after the rotation drill; SY-CASEWF holds unwrap on every enabled version.
- The Temporal frontend loads the authorizer plugin from the values file of RWB-PLT-E1070-CON and reaches the audit receiver over mTLS.
- The platform login that runs the codec server, the audit receiver and the reconciliation Schedule, and the internal ingress base of the codec server, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1441; ASM-2536).
- The feature flag `rwb.p3.temporal` is on in SIT, read through the parameters contract rather than from a code constant.
- No approval is required to start: the story is Draft (realignment v1) and builds against the published contracts and their fakes.

##### 4. Flow

1. RW-SECADM: raises a break-glass request in the bank IAM against an open incident for area PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION and right R; the IAM approves it, and the account joins the break-glass group until the window ends (RWB-P4-E1039-CON, legacy RWB-E1-039).
2. RW-SECADM: calls `POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/break-glass-grants` with the incident reference, the IAM request ID, area PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION, right R, the scope and the reason; the grant is ACTIVE with an end time.
3. RW-SECADM: opens a workflow in the Temporal Web UI and asks for a payload; the Web UI calls the codec server `POST /decode`, the Temporal codec server protocol, with the namespace, workflow ID, run ID, request ID and the encoded payloads.
4. BreakGlassGrantChecker: checks the session, the role RW-SECADM, the ACTIVE grant, its area and its right; a missing, ended or wrong-area grant is a refusal.
5. PayloadGuard: checks the payload count and size, 100 payloads and 1 MB per request, and that every payload carries codec metadata with a key version; a payload without metadata is refused whole.
6. CodecKeyResolver: resolves the key version from the metadata and unwraps it in Key Vault; it never guesses a version and never falls back to a clear read.
7. TemporalAdminAuditWriter: writes the AC-READ entry with the actor, operation DECODE, workflow ID, run ID, payload count, grant and incident through DecisionLogApi; CodecServerController returns the clear payloads only after the entry commits.
8. RW-PLATADM: terminates, resets or signals a workflow from the Web UI or the CLI; TemporalAuthorizerPlugin passes the operation, workflow ID, run ID, actor, grant or reason and the frontend request ID to TemporalAdminAuditReceiver over mTLS.
9. TemporalAdminAuditWriter: writes the PLATFORM_ADMIN entry and returns its ID; the authorizer allows the frontend call only on 201, and a 503 denies it with PERMISSION_DENIED, so the workflow is unchanged.
10. TemporalAdminAuditListener: every day at 02:00 the Temporal Schedule on task queue `rwb-platform` starts the listener, which reads the frontend audit log, matches each terminate, reset and signal to an entry, and raises an incident for any gap without writing an entry of its own. This is the DP-10 pattern in place of the retired Quartz job: the target has no Quartz.
11. RW-AUDIT: reads the AC-READ, AC-DENY and PLATFORM_ADMIN entries through `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` and holds no decode right.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A history payload carries no codec metadata, because a test or a job wrote it without the codec | The whole request is refused; no payload is returned; one AC-DENY entry records the payload index and the reason; an incident reaches RW-SECADM and RW-PLATADM; no key is guessed | None (422 refusal text) | AC5 |
| X2 | The decision log store is unavailable when an administrative call arrives | The authorizer receives 503 and denies the call with PERMISSION_DENIED; the workflow is unchanged and no entry exists | None (503 refusal text) | AC6 |
| X3 | The frontend audit log holds a terminate, reset or signal with no decision log entry | The reconciliation reports the gap and raises an incident; no entry is invented | None (incident only) | AC7 |
| X4 | A value the story needs is named by no source: the platform login and the internal ingress base of the codec server, the key rotation period and the archive retention the version list depends on | The value is published as the working read of the assumption, with the placeholder where it is still open, and the gap stays open; no code constant is written for it | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1441; ASM-2536) | Section 13 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against nine platform contracts and three owner contracts and their fakes; reads no business table and waits for no other story in the lane |
| Negotiable | Payload limits, the reconciliation time, the key version list and the refusal texts are configuration; the role rule and the write-before-act rule are fixed |
| Valuable | A clear payload is one grant and one log entry away, and no administrative action on a case workflow is invisible to audit |
| Estimable | One controller, one grant check, one key resolver, one authorizer plugin, one audit writer and one receiver, one reconciliation workflow |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion in section 7 is one test in section 16 on fixed grants, key versions and workflows |

The seven criteria above are copied from RWB-E2-038 with every value kept: BG-2026-0042, INC0004521, U-88, U-53, U-62, U-70, key versions 1, 2 and 3, 100 payloads, 1 MB, 422, 403, MSG-P4-002, 13:00, 13:02, 02:00 on 17 November 2026 and case-RW-2026-000301 to -000307. ##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Decode is allowed only for RW-SECADM with an ACTIVE break-glass grant for area PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION and right R; there is no standing decode right | RWB-P4-E1039-CON; REQ-DRI-001 |
| BR2 | The codec server is the only path to a clear payload; the Web UI names it per environment, and no key and no codec runs on a workstation | Architecture v5 slide 24; this contract |
| BR3 | The AC-READ entry is written before the clear payload is returned; a failed write returns no payload | REQ-DRI-005 |
| BR4 | Terminate, reset and signal are recorded by TemporalAuthorizerPlugin before the frontend executes them; a failed write denies the call and leaves the workflow unchanged | REQ-DRI-005 |
| BR5 | Every entry carries the operation, namespace, workflow ID, run ID, actor, reason and, where one applies, the grant and the incident | REQ-DRI-001 |
| BR6 | A decode is recorded with AC-READ and an administrative call with PLATFORM_ADMIN; no entry carries a payload or a personal data field | LOV-DECISION; NFR-045 |
| BR7 | CodecKeyResolver resolves the key version from the payload metadata; a rotation keeps every earlier version enabled for the retention and the archive period, so old histories stay decodable | KeyRotationRunBook; AC4 |
| BR8 | A payload without codec metadata is refused and raises an incident; the codec never guesses a key and never returns a payload it cannot attribute to a version | NFR-045 |
| BR9 | The daily reconciliation compares the frontend audit log with decision_log_entry and raises an incident on any gap; it never writes a missing entry | REQ-DRI-001 |
| BR10 | RW-AUDIT reads the entries through `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` and has no decode right | RWB-P4-E1039-CON |

##### 9. State transitions

None for a case. A break-glass grant and a workflow execution change state, and the story records the change.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| ACTIVE (grant) | End time reached, or the grant is revoked in the bank IAM | - | ENDED |
| RUNNING (workflow) | TerminateWorkflowExecution | The PLATFORM_ADMIN entry is committed | TERMINATED |
| RUNNING (workflow) | ResetWorkflowExecution | The PLATFORM_ADMIN entry is committed | The current run closes and a new run starts at the reset point |
| RUNNING (workflow) | SignalWorkflowExecution | The PLATFORM_ADMIN entry is committed | RUNNING, with the signal handled |
| RUNNING (workflow) | TerminateWorkflowExecution with the decision log unavailable | The entry cannot be written | RUNNING, unchanged; the call is denied |

A refused call writes AC-DENY and changes no workflow state. The grant states are the P4 contract's; this story reads the grant and never writes it.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-SECADM | Requests break-glass in the bank IAM; decodes a payload under an ACTIVE grant; reads the access log (Platform administration, R) |
| RW-PLATADM | Terminates, resets and signals a workflow (Platform administration, U); reads the entries; receives the reconciliation incident |
| RW-AUDIT | Reads the AC-READ, AC-DENY and PLATFORM_ADMIN entries; holds no decode right (Platform administration and Decision log, R) |
| RW-TRIBE | Maintains the authorizer plugin configuration and the key rotation run book; may not decode |
| RW-CASEOWN and the other case roles | No decode right and no administrative call on a workflow |
| SY-CASEWF | Holds unwrap on every enabled key version; in SIT it runs the codec server and the audit writer and connects to the frontend with its certificate (Decision log C) |
| SY-RULES | No part in this story; a call to the codec server or the audit receiver with its certificate is refused |
| The platform identity that runs the codec server, the audit receiver and the reconciliation Schedule | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1441; ASM-2536) |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A decode or an administrative call is not a credit decision |

Separation of duty: the security administrator who decodes is not the author of the case decision the payload supports, and no person reviews their own break-glass use (RWB-P4-E1039-CON).

##### 11. Data

| BR Field ID | Entity | Field | Read or write |
|---|---|---|---|
| DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 | decision_log_entry | all fields | Write (one entry per decode, refusal and administrative call) |
| DF-DEC-002 | decision_log_entry | case_id | Write; empty for an access event, as RWB-P4-E1039-CON sets it, with the workflow ID in the actions field |
| DF-DEC-003 | decision_log_entry | decision_code | Write, read |
| DF-DEC-014 | decision_log_entry | actions | Write (operation, workflow ID, run ID, payload count, grant, incident) |
| DF-DEC-016 | decision_log_entry | decided_at | Write, read |
| DF-DEC-030 | decision_log_entry | actor_user_id | Write, read |
| DF-DEC-031 | decision_log_entry | idempotency_key | Write, read |

No field is added. `decision_log_entry` is owned by rwb-decision (P7) under the Ownership Map ruling; this story writes it through DecisionLogApi and reads it through the P4 access log contract. The PLATFORM_ADMIN value is a LOV-DECISION data row loaded through RWB-E1-043, now the reference-data contract of rwb-case, and recorded in the additions file. No payload, no history event and no clear personal data field is written to the decision log. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

The codec server speaks the Temporal codec server protocol on the platform internal ingress. It is not part of the Workbench API Specification: it has no `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` base and no gateway route, and only the Temporal Web UI and the internal network reach it.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/decode` | Returns the clear payloads of one history request | Platform administration R, plus an ACTIVE break-glass grant for area PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION | `requestId` from the Web UI |
| POST | `/encode` | Returns the encoded form of payloads written by an authorised client | Platform administration R, plus an ACTIVE break-glass grant for area PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION | `requestId` from the Web UI |

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Request | namespace, workflowId, runId, requestId, payloads: an array of { metadata: { encoding, keyVersion }, data: base64 } |
| Response 200 | payloads: an array of { metadata, data: base64 } in the same order, and entryId |
| Errors | 401 no session; 403 role, grant or area (MSG-P4-002); 413 more than 100 payloads or 1 MB; 422 a payload without codec metadata or a key version that is not enabled; 503 Key Vault unavailable or the entry could not be written (no payload returned) |
| Authorization | Platform administration, right R, plus an ACTIVE break-glass grant for area PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION |
| Idempotency | `requestId` from the Web UI; a repeat with the same requestId returns the same payloads and entryId and writes no second entry |
| Base | The internal ingress base per environment is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1441; ASM-2536); the operations above are the published surface |

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Operation | Provider | Used for | Pattern |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log | rwb-access (P4) | The entries with event codes AC-READ, AC-DENY and PLATFORM_ADMIN, for RW-AUDIT and for the reconciliation read (authorization and errors unchanged) | DP-11, DP-13 |

The active grant is read through the published break-glass interface of RWB-P4-E1039-CON; this story adds no method to it. The DecisionLogApi of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is called in process as a library, not over REST, so it is not a consumption row.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The platform owns no topic: the entries travel through the decision-record library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, which publishes `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` from the caller's transaction, and that event is the library's, not this story's.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The reconciliation reads the frontend audit log through the Temporal frontend API and the entries through the access log read of 12.2; it subscribes to no topic.

| BreakGlassGrantChecker | Service | The codec server process | Reads the ACTIVE grant through the P4 contract and checks role, area and right (BR1) |
| PayloadGuard | Service | The codec server process | Payload count and size limits, codec metadata and key version check (BR8) |

No other workflow is started, and no activity of this story runs on a service task queue.

The Schedule is created from the workflow kit template of RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, in namespace `rwb-recovery`, with the tenant and retention of the platform namespace. Its catch-up window and overlap policy are configuration.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. `decision_log_entry` is owned by rwb-decision (P7) under the Ownership Map ruling and is written through DecisionLogApi only; the frontend audit log belongs to the Temporal namespace and is read, never written. This story owns no `rwb_*` schema, no table and no migration, and it reads no table of another service (DP-01).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** The codec server, the grant check, the guard, the key resolver, the audit writer and the receiver in the platform workflow module (Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.workflow.security`); the authorizer plugin configuration in `deploy/temporal/plugins/`; the reconciliation workflow in the same module; the key rotation run book in `docs/operations/runbooks/`. The final Java package inside the plugin repository, and the deployment names of the two services, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1441; ASM-2536) and follow the platform template of RWB-PLT-TPL rather than this story.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| CodecServerController | Controller | `POST /decode` and `POST /encode` on the codec server with the access check and the response after the entry (BR2, BR3) |
| BreakGlassGrantChecker | Service | Reads the ACTIVE grant and checks role, area and right (BR1) |
| PayloadGuard | Service | Payload count and size limits; codec metadata and key version check (BR8) |
| CodecKeyResolver | Service | Resolves the key version from the metadata and unwraps it in Key Vault (BR7) |
| TemporalAdminAuditWriter | Service | Builds and writes the AC-READ, AC-DENY and PLATFORM_ADMIN entries through DecisionLogApi (BR5, BR6) |
| TemporalAuthorizerPlugin | Configuration | The Temporal frontend Authorizer and ClaimMapper: calls the receiver and denies on any non-201 response (BR4) |
| TemporalAdminAuditReceiver | Service | Receives the authorizer audit record over mTLS and writes it through TemporalAdminAuditWriter (BR4) |
| TemporalAdminAuditListener | Workflow | Daily reconciliation of the frontend audit log against decision_log_entry, started by the 02:00 Schedule (BR9) |
| KeyRotationRunBook | Document | The rotation steps, the version list and the version retention rule (BR7, AC4) |

**Database.** No migration. The entries go to `decision_log_entry` through the existing writer in the caller's transaction, and the owner of that table is rwb-decision (P7). LOV-DECISION gains PLATFORM_ADMIN as a data row through RWB-E1-043; no table and no column is added, and the Flyway baseline of RWB-PLT-E1044-CON is unchanged by this story.

**Configuration and reference data**

- Codec endpoint URL per environment in the Web UI; the codec server is reachable only from the Web UI ingress and the internal network.
- Limits: 100 payloads and 1 MB per request; the reconciliation runs daily at 02:00. Both are read as parameters through RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and are never code constants (DP-06).
- Key versions: every version named by a history inside the retention (30 days) or the archive of legacy RWB-E2-039 stays enabled. The archive retention, the key rotation period and the retention that keeps a version enabled are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1441; ASM-2536); the working read is section 3 of the assumption, and the run book carries the version list as release evidence.
- The LOV value PLATFORM_ADMIN is a data row in LOV-DECISION loaded through RWB-E1-043 (DP-07), recorded in the additions file.
- Feature flag `rwb.p3.temporal` through the parameters contract. Off: the codec endpoint returns 404, the authorizer plugin is not configured and the reconciliation Schedule is paused; the cluster and the Web UI are unchanged.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

These are the Template and Rules §R5.5 rows the legacy markers call for. **DP-03** is the centre of the story: every decode, refusal and administrative call is a decision record, written through the local decision-record library with the seven field groups, hash-linked into the central ledger and published as `DecisionRecorded`; the story owns no ledger and no table, it fills DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-018 in the caller's transaction. **DP-11** replaces the monolith's in-process call to the access log with one REST hop to `GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log`, with a 2 s timeout and a breaker, and the audit and the reconciliation both read it there; no path is copied into this story. **DP-13** is why the legacy module path for the access log is not republished: the read becomes `/api/recovery/access/v1/admin/access-log` and the codec server, which never sat under the monolith base, publishes no base of its own. DP-05 applies negatively — the story reads no ACE view and no extension table — and DP-15 applies as "no migration", because the only table touched is another owner's. DP-14 applies to the entry event the library publishes, not to a topic of this story. DP-19 is the gateway route the access log read passes through for the audit role. DP-10 is the pattern the 02:00 reconciliation follows; it adds no new dependency because the workflow kit contract is already an H row of this story.

**Build steps**

1. Add the PLATFORM_ADMIN LOV value through the versioned reference load and confirm the decision log writer accepts it as a system event (DP-07).
2. Build PayloadGuard and CodecKeyResolver with the version from the metadata; test AC4 with versions 1 and 2 and a rotation to 3.
3. Build BreakGlassGrantChecker and CodecServerController with the write-before-return order; tests AC1, AC3 and AC5.
4. Build TemporalAdminAuditWriter and TemporalAdminAuditReceiver; test AC2 for the four operations and the 201 rule.
5. Configure TemporalAuthorizerPlugin from the values file of RWB-PLT-E1070-CON to call the receiver and deny on 503; test AC6 with the decision log stopped.
6. Build TemporalAdminAuditListener and its 02:00 Schedule on task queue `rwb-platform`, with the incident; test AC7 with a planted frontend audit entry.
7. Run the two access tests, the key rotation drill in SIT, and record the version list and the run book in the release evidence.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the rotation drill decodes a history written under an earlier key version, the reconciliation finds no gap over seven days, and the access log shows every decode with its grant and incident.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P4-002 | The role is not RW-SECADM, the grant is missing, ended or for another area, or the caller is not the platform identity on the internal endpoint | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

A 401 returns the standard no-session text. A 413 names the payload count or the request size only. A 422 names the payload index and the missing codec metadata, but never the payload. A 503 says the action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. None of these adds a message ID. MSG-P4-002 exists and is reused unchanged, with {action} set to "decode this workflow payload" or "record this workflow action". The codec server publishes no message of its own, because it is not on the Workbench API.

##### 15. Screens and states

No new Workbench screen. The decode result appears in the payload panel of the Temporal Web UI, which shows the states encoded, decoding and decoded for a user with a grant, and refused with MSG-P4-002 for every other user. The entries appear on the access log read of RWB-P4-E1039-CON and on SCR-38 Decision log query (legacy RWB-E2-005) with the operation in the actions field. SCR-43 Roles and access in Epic 8 shows the grant rule; this story adds no panel to it.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the payload limits, the reconciliation time, the key version list and the refusal texts are configuration read through the parameters contract.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history or prompts: the test payloads are synthetic, and no payload or clear field is written to the decision log or a log line.
- No read of another service's tables and no ACE view: the entries are written through DecisionLogApi and read through the P4 access log contract (DP-01, DP-03, DP-11).
- Decode is never a standing right: no grant, no clear payload, and every decode names its grant and incident.
- No entry, no action: a terminate, reset or signal the authorizer cannot record is denied, not retried after the fact.
- The codec never guesses a key version and never falls back to a clear read.
- No key version is disabled while a history inside the retention or the archive names it.
- The reconciliation never writes a missing entry: it reports the gap and leaves the record to the security administrator.
- The platform publishes no `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` base, no `rwb_*` schema and no topic of its own; the codec server is reached on the internal ingress only (DP-13, §R4).

##### 1. Story

As a **member of the integration and QA team**, I want **a repeatable cross-service journey harness that decodes a workflow payload under an open break-glass grant and records every decode, terminate, reset and signal in the decision log before the frontend acts**, so that **the wave 2 workflow security and administrative audit journey is proven end to end, with evidence, before the release is accepted**.

This story builds the harness and the evidence only. It builds no production endpoint, table, workflow or schedule, it serves no operation and it owns no table. The real behaviour is owned by the two I stories: RWB-P4-E1039-APP (the break-glass grant, the AC-BGON entry, the grant end time and the access log read) and RWB-PLT-E2038-APP (the codec server, the payload guard, the key resolver, the Temporal authorizer audit writer and the daily reconciliation), and those two stories block the ITG run.

The journey also reads the P7 decision log through its contract, because every AC-READ, AC-DENY and PLATFORM_ADMIN row is a decision log entry and the harness asserts the entry before it asserts the payload or the workflow state. That read is asserted through the published contract and the §12.8 fakes; it is not claimed as work of this story.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy RWB-E2-038 journey crosses more than one service: rwb-access holds the break-glass grant, its end time and the access log read; rwb-decision holds the decision log writer and the entries themselves; the platform workflow service holds the codec server that turns an encrypted history into a readable payload and the Temporal authorizer audit that stands between a terminate, reset or signal and the workflow; and gateway-bff composes the access log for the screen. Until the real services are exercised together, the program cannot show that a clear payload costs one grant and one entry, and that no administrative action on a live case is unrecorded.

The harness gives one repeatable run per business date that proves a decode answers only for RW-SECADM with an ACTIVE grant and writes its AC-READ entry before the payload leaves, that a terminate, reset and signal each write a PLATFORM_ADMIN entry before the frontend acts, that other roles are refused with one AC-DENY entry per refusal, that a key rotation keeps an earlier history decodable while a payload without codec metadata is refused whole, and that a failed audit write denies the call and leaves the workflow RUNNING while the daily reconciliation reports a gap without inventing an entry. It meets REQ-DRI-001 and REQ-DRI-005 at the integration level and leaves every business rule, every message and every screen behaviour where the owning stories put them.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The two I stories are published and deployed in the SIT environment: RWB-P4-E1039-APP (break-glass grants, the AC-BGON entry, the grant end time and the access log read) and RWB-PLT-E2038-APP (the codec server, the authorizer audit writer and the reconciliation).
- The Temporal Web UI of the cluster names the codec server of the platform workflow service as its codec endpoint, per environment.
- Key Vault holds the codec key with versions 1, 2 and 3, version 2 current at the start of the run and version 3 after the rotation step; the unwrap right on every enabled version is held by the workflow service account named in the legacy story.
- LOV-DECISION carries PLATFORM_ADMIN as a system event code, loaded through the versioned reference load by the owning stories; AC-READ, AC-DENY and AC-BGON are already present.
- gateway-bff is deployed with the composite route of DP-19 available for the access log screen.
- The contract fakes of §12.8 are published from the owning services' OpenAPI documents and the codec server protocol stub, so the harness runs from Day 1 before the I stories land.
- The harness environment, its test-data seeding, its evidence format and retention, and the test certificate details: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0417; ASM-0592).

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: seeds the grant, the users, the seven workflows and the key versions through the owning contracts or the published fakes, and reads the grant back to assert it is ACTIVE with its end time.
2. Harness: decodes the payload of "case-RW-2026-000301" through the codec server at 11:40 as "U-88" with the ACTIVE grant "BG-2026-0042", asserts 200, the clear payload and the entryId.
3. Harness: reads the AC-READ entry through the rwb-decision contract and asserts decision code, actor, operation DECODE, grant, incident "INC0004521" and that the entry time precedes the response time.
4. Harness: repeats the decode at 12:05 after the grant ended, asserts 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no payload.
5. Harness: terminates "case-RW-2026-000302", resets "case-RW-2026-000303" to event 12 and signals CaseEvent to "case-RW-2026-000304" as "U-70"; asserts four entries, the three PLATFORM_ADMIN entries committed before the frontend reports the result, and no payload or personal data field on any row.
6. Harness: drives the decode as "U-53" with RW-AUDIT and as "U-62" with RW-CASEOWN, asserts 403 with MSG-P4-002 on each and one AC-DENY entry per refusal.
7. Harness: rotates the key to version 3 with versions 1 and 2 enabled, decodes the history written under version 1 and the history under version 2, and asserts the version used from the payload metadata; then starts a workflow and asserts its payloads carry version 3.
8. Harness: decodes the history of "case-RW-2026-000305" written with the codec off, asserts 422, no payload, one AC-DENY entry with the payload index and the reason, and no key guess.
9. Harness: stops the decision log answer, terminates "case-RW-2026-000306" as "U-70", asserts 503 read as PERMISSION_DENIED by the authorizer, the workflow still RUNNING and no TERMINATE entry; then plants a signal on "case-RW-2026-000307" in the frontend audit log with no entry, runs the reconciliation at 02:00 and asserts one reported gap and no invented entry.
10. Harness: writes one run report per business date, keyed by story and business date; the report format and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0417; ASM-0592).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What the harness asserts | Message | ITG test case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The grant is missing, ended, or for another area or right | 403 from the codec server; no payload; nothing reaches the workflow | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-038-01-ITG |
| X2 | The caller holds RW-PLATADM, RW-AUDIT or RW-CASEOWN | 403 from the codec server; no payload; one AC-DENY entry per refusal | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-038-03-ITG, TC-E2-038-09-ITG |
| X3 | A payload carries no codec metadata | 422 for the whole request; no payload index answers; one AC-DENY entry with the payload index and the reason; no key is guessed | None (422 refusal text) | TC-E2-038-05-ITG |
| X4 | More than 100 payloads, or more than 1 MB in one request | 413; no payload returned; no AC-READ entry | None (413 refusal text) | TC-E2-038-01-ITG |
| X5 | A payload names a key version that is not enabled | 422; no payload returned; one AC-DENY entry; no fallback to a clear read | None (422 refusal text) | TC-E2-038-04-ITG |
| X6 | The decision log store is unavailable when an administrative call arrives | 503 to the authorizer, read as PERMISSION_DENIED; the workflow is unchanged and no entry exists | None (503 refusal text) | TC-E2-038-06-ITG |
| X7 | The frontend audit log holds a terminate, reset or signal with no entry | The reconciliation reports the gap with workflow ID, operation and time; no entry is written by the job | None (incident only) | TC-E2-038-07-ITG |
| X8 | A caller presents a certificate that is not the workflow service's, or the frontend's on the audit endpoint | 403 with MSG-P4-002 on the codec path; a refused mTLS handshake on the audit endpoint; no entry | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-038-09-ITG |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs on its own once the two I stories are deployed; until then it runs against the §12.8 fakes and the codec protocol stub |
| Negotiable | The harness pack, the seeding, the evidence format and the certificate set are agreed with QA; no business value is fixed by the harness |
| Valuable | The decode and the administrative audit are evidenced across services rather than per service, with the entry order on the same trace |
| Estimable | One harness project, one journey specification, one fake pack, one rotation drill and one run report |
| Small | Fits in one iteration with the owning stories' contract tests |
| Testable | Each scenario of §7 is one automated journey with synthetic data and a machine-checkable result |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Temporal security, codec server and admin audit - wave 2 integration harness

  Background:
    Given the Temporal Web UI uses the codec server of the platform workflow service as its codec endpoint
    Given the codec key has versions 1 and 2 enabled, and version 2 is current
    Given the codec server accepts at most 100 payloads and 1 MB per request
    Given workflow "case-RW-2026-000301" holds a salary slip payload encrypted with key version 2
    Given the workflows "case-RW-2026-000302", "case-RW-2026-000303", "case-RW-2026-000304" and "case-RW-2026-000306" are RUNNING

  Scenario: AC1 A decode needs RW-SECADM with an open grant, and the entry is committed first (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given user "U-88" holds RW-SECADM and the ACTIVE break-glass grant "BG-2026-0042" for area PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION, right R, ending at 12:00 on 16 November 2026
    When the harness decodes the payload of "case-RW-2026-000301" through the codec server at 11:40
    Then the codec server answers 200 with the clear payload and an entryId
    And one decision log entry exists with decision code AC-READ, actor "U-88", operation DECODE, grant "BG-2026-0042" and incident "INC0004521"
    And that entry is committed before the response carries the payload

    And no service reads another service's schema and no entry holds a payload
    When the harness decodes again at 12:05, after the grant ended
    Then the answer is 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no payload is returned

  Scenario: AC2 Terminate, reset and signal each write PLATFORM_ADMIN before the frontend acts, and other roles are refused (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given user "U-70" holds RW-PLATADM and no break-glass grant
    Given user "U-88" holds RW-SECADM with grant "BG-2026-0042"
    When the harness decodes a payload of "case-RW-2026-000301"
    When the harness terminates "case-RW-2026-000302" with reason "stuck on a bad activity"
    When the harness resets "case-RW-2026-000303" to event 12
    When the harness sends signal CaseEvent to "case-RW-2026-000304"
    Then four decision log entries exist: AC-READ for the decode and PLATFORM_ADMIN for TERMINATE, RESET and SIGNAL
    And each entry carries namespace rwb-recovery, the workflow ID, the run ID, the actor and the reason, and the grant where one applies
    And the TERMINATE entry is committed before the frontend reports "case-RW-2026-000302" TERMINATED
    And the RESET entry is committed before the current run closes, and the SIGNAL entry before the signal is handled
    And no entry holds a payload or a clear personal data field
    Given user "U-53" holds RW-AUDIT with an active grant for area PLATFORM_ADMINISTRATION, right R
    Given user "U-62" holds RW-CASEOWN and no grant
    When "U-53" asks the codec server to decode "case-RW-2026-000301"
    Then the answer is 403 with MSG-P4-002 because RW-AUDIT reads the log and does not decode
    When "U-62" asks the codec server to decode
    Then the answer is 403 with MSG-P4-002 and no payload is returned
    And one AC-DENY entry records each refusal with the actor and the area, and no payload

  Scenario: AC3 A key rotation keeps an older history decodable, and a payload without codec metadata is refused whole (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given "case-RW-2026-000301" was written when key version 1 was current and "case-RW-2026-000304" was written when key version 2 is current
    When the key is rotated to version 3 and versions 1 and 2 stay enabled
    Then a decode of "case-RW-2026-000301" with an active grant returns the clear payload using version 1
    And a decode of "case-RW-2026-000304" uses version 2
    And a workflow started after the rotation writes payloads with version 3
    And every version named by a history inside the retention stays enabled
    Given "case-RW-2026-000305" was written with the codec off, so its payload carries no codec metadata
    When "U-88" decodes that payload with an active grant
    Then the answer is 422 and no payload is returned
    And one AC-DENY entry records the payload index and the reason
    And the codec does not guess a key and does not fall back to a clear read

  Scenario: AC4 A failed audit write denies the call, and the reconciliation reports a gap without inventing an entry (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the decision log store is unavailable at 13:00 on 16 November 2026
    When "U-70" terminates "case-RW-2026-000306" from the Web UI
    Then the authorizer receives 503 from the audit writer and denies the call with PERMISSION_DENIED
    And "case-RW-2026-000306" stays RUNNING and no TERMINATE entry exists
    When the frontend audit log holds a signal on "case-RW-2026-000307" at 13:02 with no decision log entry
    And the reconciliation runs at 02:00 on 17 November 2026
    Then it reports one gap with the workflow ID, the operation and the time
```
