##### 11. Data

The contract declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Workbook Rows tab | RuleSet = package code; NAME = rule ID; the condition columns of the package; the output columns action_text, owner_role, timer_spec, target_queue_code and outputs (DF-REF-008, DF-REF-010, DF-REF-011, DF-REF-052 to DF-REF-054, DF-REF-298); default row last |
| Workbook Tests tab | test_case_id, route_set, rule_version, rule_id, from_state, event_code, facts, expected_to_state, expected_owner_role, expected_timer_spec, result, result_detail (DF-REF-186 to DF-REF-197) |
| Blob object metadata | package code, version label, SHA-256 of the workbook, author role, authored date, environment |
| Model resource | packageCode, versionLabel, checksum (SHA-256), the model content and its compiler version, the valid-from date |
| Catalog resource | ruleId, packageVersion, drools_rule_name, action_text, owner_role, timer_spec, target_queue_code, outputs |
| Event payload | package code, version label, checksum, valid-from date, published at; identifiers and business facts only |
| Activity input and output | package code, facts reference, business date in; packageCode, packageVersion, ruleId, outputs out |

The field-level detail of the model and catalog resources — property types, lengths, required flags and the compiler-version element — is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0722; ASM-1269); this story fixes the element names above and leaves the types to the review with the rwb-decision owner. The Blob retention and immutability period are likewise Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0723; ASM-1270) and are fixed in RWB-P3-E2042-INF.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The rwb-case side of the three Epic 2 packages serves no new business operation. The model cache is internal, the packages are read from rwb-decision, and the case reads that carry a rule outcome are the operations of their own stories (`GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` and the case read surface of RWB-P3-E1023-CON). This baseline declares no cache read: a cache inspection path would be an operator concern and is carried by RWB-P3-E2042-OPS as a metric, not as an operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in the baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}` | P7 rwb-decision | The compiled model, its version label and its SHA-256; faked with one correct checksum and one wrong checksum |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion=` | P7 rwb-decision | action_text, owner_role, timer_spec and outputs of one rule row; faked for R-RES-04 and the route-set rows |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` | P7 rwb-decision | The version list, the status of each version and the checksum of the one in force; faked |
| POST | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` | P7 rwb-decision | The multipart load of a workbook with validFrom; faked with 201, 409 and 422 |
| POST | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/approve` | P7 rwb-decision | The four-eyes approval; faked with 200, 403 and 409 |

Every operation is one hop with a 2 s client budget (DP-11, ADR-020). The load and approve operations are called by the center of excellence analyst and the risk officer through the Workbench; rwb-case never calls them from a workflow.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. This contract publishes no event type. The shared ledger event `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` is published by the local decision-record library of DP-03 when a decision is taken in rwb-case; its schema is unchanged by this story and is the one declared in RWB-P3-E1018-CON.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Consumer contract |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | P7 | CloudEvents 1.0; key = package code; payload = package code, version label, checksum, valid-from date, published at; inbox dedupe; starts one model swap and nothing else |

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| RuleModelSwap | Workflow started by RulePackageInForce | `rwb-case` | Input: package code, version label, checksum, valid-from date. One execution per package code and version label |
| swapRuleModel | Activity | `rwb-case` | Input: package code, version label, checksum. Output: the cached version, the built KieBase reference and the outcome loaded, unchanged or refused |
| EvaluateRules | Activity (workflow kit) | `rwb-case` | Input: package code, facts, business date. Output: `RuleResult(packageCode, packageVersion, ruleId, outputs)`; raises `NoPackageInForce`, which is non-retryable |
| RecordAndApply | Activity (workflow kit) | `rwb-case` | Input: the decision record, the state change and the outbox rows; one transaction, and no partial write |

The swap contract is the only one this story adds: the evaluation contract is the kit's and is restated here so that the catalogue read and the evaluation name the same package version.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The 00:01 promotion is the Temporal Schedule JOB-20 in rwb-decision, owned there and announced as RulePackageInForce (Arch v5 slide 44). rwb-case registers no Schedule for a rule package.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Contracted use |
|---|---|---|
| recovery_case | P3 (rwb_case) | The case facts an evaluation reads; no column added |
| timer | P3 (rwb_case) | The due date a route-set row sets; no column added |
| queue | P3 (rwb_case) | The target queue a rule row names; no column added |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_case | The outbox, inbox and idempotency envelope of the consumer (DP-09) |

No other table is named in the contract. The four registry tables are rwb-decision's and are never read directly (ASM-0069; DP-01). `payment_match_rule` does not exist.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `contract/rule-package-workbook-schema.yaml` (the Rows and Tests schema of a workbook, with the package code as RuleSet and the rule ID in NAME), `contract/rule-package-blob.md` (the object naming and the metadata keys), `contract/rule-model-consumed.yaml` (the five consumed rwb-decision operations), `contract/rule-package-in-force.md` (the event contract), `contract/evaluate-rules.yaml` (the activity input, `RuleResult` and `NoPackageInForce`), and the three WireMock mappings.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Build steps**

1. Write the workbook schema: the Rows tab with RuleSet and NAME, the condition and output columns per package, the default row last, and the Tests tab with the twelve rule_test_case columns; add a schema lint to the pipeline.
2. Write the Blob contract: the `<PACKAGE_CODE>/<VERSION_LABEL>.xlsx` path, the write-once rule and the metadata keys, and hand it to RWB-P3-E2042-INF.
3. Document the five consumed operations from the rwb-decision documents, with the 2 s budget and the error codes; the model and catalog elements are agreed under GAP-0722.
4. Write the RulePackageInForce contract: envelope, key, payload, dedupe and the `.dlt` rule.
5. Write the activity contract: the input, `RuleResult`, `NoPackageInForce`, the cache bound, the atomic swap and the last-good-model rule.
6. Build the four WireMock mappings and their fixtures.
7. Add the six contract tests, including the drift test between each fake and this document.
8. Tag the baseline and collect the sign-off of the app, infrastructure, operations and test stories.

**Done when.** The five contract files validate in the pipeline, the six contract tests pass, the four fakes answer every consumed path and payload, and the app, infrastructure, operations and test stories of this legacy key have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-027 | A workbook fails the authoring schema or the tests-tab schema | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P7-002 | The approver is the author | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | An empty workbook or an empty required cell | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Valid from before today | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The version label is already loaded | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Rules and parameters calls a package operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The texts are the agreed texts of the legacy story and of the platform catalogue; this contract adds no message. The `{check}` value is compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row or scenario, and the `{detail}` names rows, cells, rule IDs, package codes and version labels only.

##### 15. Screens and states

None in this story. The contract serves the version list that SCR-39 Rules and parameters shows in Epic 8 and the package columns of the case screens only indirectly, through the rule outcome a decision carries. The cache states are internal to rwb-case and are exposed as the readiness signal and the metrics of RWB-P3-E2042-OPS, not as a screen.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: rows, tolerances, windows, action text, owner roles, timers and queue codes stay data of the workbooks and the registry.
- No personal data in an event, an activity input, an example or a fake: identifiers and business facts only.
- The contract names only rwb-case tables and only rwb-case operations as provided; the five rwb-decision operations are consumed and never restated as this service's (DP-01, DP-13).
- One REST base and one topic per service; a document that names another service's base as provided, or a topic outside `rwb.<short>.events.v1`, fails the review (DP-13, DP-14).
- `payment_match_rule` and DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 appear nowhere as an element of the contract.
- Every example and fixture is synthetic; no production workbook, payload or checksum is copied into a schema or a fake.
- The envelope, the naming rule and the embedded Drools kit elements come from the platform library; this story narrows them but never redefines them.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-042 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **center of excellence analyst (RW-COE)**, I want **the RESTRUCTURE, PAYMENT_MATCH and BOOKING_MATCH workbooks and their Tests tabs authored as write-once configuration artefacts in the `rule-packages` Blob container, and each version in force fetched from rwb-decision's `GET /rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}`, verified against its SHA-256, built into one KieBase per version (cache max 20) and swapped in atomically inside the EvaluateRules activity of rwb-case**, so that **every Epic 2 decision this service takes is made by an approved, dated package version that rwb-case holds only as an evaluated copy, and no workbook, DRL source or rule table is ever read by service code**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Epic 2 rules lived in three places in the monolith: reference rule rows, the `payment_match_rule` table and the `BookingMatchRules` class. D-RCV-36 T10 retires the table, and D-RCV-36 T3 to T6 move authoring, testing and effective dating into one governance path. In the target that governance is central in rwb-decision (P7): the three package codes, their versions, their rule rows and their test cases are registry rows there, published as a model over REST and announced by RulePackageInForce (Arch v5 slides 27, 41 and 44; Temporal and Drools slides 15 and 16). Evaluation stays local to the owning service (Arch v5 slide 27), so rwb-case keeps only the evaluated copy: it authors the workbooks, fetches the model, verifies the checksum and swaps it in (DP-04).

This story is the rwb-case half of that split. It fixes the three authoring artefacts (38 rows and 62 scenarios for RESTRUCTURE, 3 rows and 58 scenarios for PAYMENT_MATCH, 21 rows and 54 scenarios for BOOKING_MATCH — 174 scenarios in all, every package at or above `rules.testcases.min` = 50), the model cache and its swap rule, the catalog read, and the schema assertion that `rwb_case` has no `payment_match_rule` table and no column of DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273. It meets REQ-CWC-013 and REQ-CWC-014 and gives RWB-E2-002, RWB-E2-004, RWB-E2-007, RWB-E2-008, RWB-E2-027 and RWB-E2-035 one catalog row set to read, by rule ID and package version.

The measure is that the three versions are fetched, verified and in force as evaluated copies, 174 scenarios pass in every build, and a migrated database holds 93 tables with no `payment_match_rule`.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P3-E2042-CON is published: the authoring contract of the Rows and Tests tabs, the Blob naming and metadata contract, the five consumed rwb-decision operations, the RulePackageInForce consumption contract, the EvaluateRules activity contract and the contract fakes.
- RWB-P7-E2042-APP is done: `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` in schema `rwb_decision`, the three package codes RESTRUCTURE, PAYMENT_MATCH and BOOKING_MATCH seeded with owner role RW-COE, and the admin operations that load, list, approve and roll back a version (ASM-0069).
- RWB-PLT-E1072-CON is published: the embedded Drools kit, with one KieBase per package version, first-match semantics, a cache of at most 20 versions, the checksum check and the `NoPackageInForce` outcome (DP-04).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03).
- RWB-PLT-E1071-CON is published: the Temporal workflow kit in namespace `rwb-recovery`, with the event-started workflow and the activity contracts of the kit (DP-10).
- RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-P3-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are published: the parameters contract and the reference-data contract of rwb-case, with the client library (DP-06, DP-07).
- RWB-PLT-E1047-CON and RWB-PLT-E1044-CON are published: the naming library and the per-service Flyway sequence (DP-14, DP-15). RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route (DP-19).
- RWB-P3-E1073-APP is done: the rwb-case rule authoring pipeline — workbook template, compile, the load checks, the scenario runner, `RuleScenarioBuildGate` and the one-call rollback path.
- The three version labels are agreed on 16 November 2026: "RES-2026.12", "PMT-2026.12" and "BKG-2026.12", all valid from 2026-12-15 (the valid-from date is the legacy assumption and is copied unchanged). The scenario counts are agreed: 62, 58 and 54, all at or above `rules.testcases.min` = 50.
- The Blob container `rule-packages` exists, write-once, with the rwb-case workload identity holding read on that container only (RWB-P3-E2042-INF).
- The rwb-case login (DP-02) and the rwb-decision mTLS certificate are in the platform secret store; the per-service login name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0722; ASM-1269).

##### 4. Flow

1. Center of excellence analyst: reads the current Epic 2 rules from the rwb-decision catalog, the retired `payment_match_rule` rows of the monolith and the `BookingMatchRules` behaviour, and writes one workbook per package in the Drools XLS decision-table template.
2. Center of excellence analyst: fills the Rows tab (RuleSet = package code, NAME = rule ID, default row last) and the Tests tab with 62, 58 and 54 scenarios; stores the workbook under `RESTRUCTURE/RES-2026.12.xlsx`, `PAYMENT_MATCH/PMT-2026.12.xlsx` and `BOOKING_MATCH/BKG-2026.12.xlsx` in the write-once container, with the SHA-256 in the object metadata.
3. Center of excellence analyst: loads each workbook through the rwb-decision admin operation `POST /admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` with valid from 2026-12-15; rwb-decision runs the compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row and at least 50 scenario checks and its dry run.
4. Risk officer: approves each version through `POST /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/approve`; the author cannot approve.
5. rwb-decision: the promotion Schedule JOB-20 runs at 00:01, moves each APPROVED version to IN_FORCE, and publishes `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` on `rwb.decision.events.v1` with the package code, the version label, the checksum and the valid-from date.
6. rwb-case: the case router consumes the event through its inbox (one action per event) and starts `RuleModelSwap` on task queue `rwb-case` for the package code and version label.
7. RulePackageClient: calls `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}` inside the `swapRuleModel` activity, compares the returned SHA-256 with the checksum in the event and with the metadata of the Blob object, and hands the model to the cache only on a match.
8. ModelCache: builds one KieBase for the package version, stores it against the package code, and swaps the pointer atomically so a running evaluation keeps the KieBase it started with; a version not in force is evicted least-recently-used when the cache is at its maximum of 20.
9. EvaluateRules activity: evaluates a package code on the facts and the business date and returns `RuleResult(packageCode, packageVersion, ruleId, outputs)`; the package version is the one in force on the business date, or the one the case was decided under (R-UNI-38).
10. RuleCatalogClient: answers the catalog read through `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion=` for action_text, owner_role, timer_spec and outputs; rwb-case reads no rule row from a table.
11. Build: `RuleScenarioBuildGate` runs the 174 scenarios of the three in-force versions, and `PaymentMatchRuleAbsentCheck` asserts on a Testcontainers database that the migrated schema holds 93 tables, that no table named `payment_match_rule` exists, and that no column of DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 exists.
12. Any release migration that creates `payment_match_rule` fails the build; the migration script that drops a table left by an earlier DEV or SIT build runs before the gate.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The SHA-256 of the fetched model differs from the checksum in the event | The KieBase is not built and the pointer is not swapped; the model in force stays; the checksum mismatch is counted and alerted | None | AC1, AC6 |
| X2 | The model operation does not answer inside the 2 s budget, or answers 404 for the announced version | The swap retries on the activity retry policy; after the last attempt the model in force stays and the swap is alerted as failed | None | AC2, AC6 |
| X3 | No version is in force for a package on the business date | `NoPackageInForce` is raised; the activity fails without a retry and the caller reports MSG-P3-027; no default decision is taken | MSG-P3-027 | AC4, AC5 |
| X4 | The cache holds 20 versions and a further version is requested | The least recently used version that is not in force is evicted; a version in force is never evicted | None | AC1 |
| X5 | The same RulePackageInForce event arrives twice | The inbox drops the second event; no second fetch, no second swap and no second KieBase | None | AC3 |
| X6 | A release migration creates `payment_match_rule` | The schema gate fails and the build is blocked before the artefact is published | None | AC6 |
| X7 | Service code reads a workbook, a DRL source or a rule table directly | The architecture boundary test fails the build; the only reads allowed are the model operation, the catalog operation and the version list | None | AC5 |
| X8 | A catalog read names a rule ID or package version that is not held | The read answers 404 from rwb-decision; the caller records the missing rule ID for the package and takes no decision from a partial row | MSG-P3-027 | AC5 |
| X9 | A workbook holds fewer than 50 scenarios, or a scenario fails at load | The load is refused by rwb-decision with the failing scenario IDs named; no version is created and the version in force keeps running | MSG-P3-027 | AC1 |
| X10 | The Blob object is overwritten or its metadata checksum is missing | The write-once policy refuses the overwrite; a missing checksum stops the verification step and the swap is refused | None | AC1 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P3-E2042-CON, the platform contract stories and RWB-P3-E1073-APP. The rwb-decision answers come from its contract fake; the registry itself is RWB-P7-E2042-APP |
| Negotiable | Rows, scenarios, package codes, version labels and the cache bound are data and configuration; the checksum rule, the atomic swap and the schema assertion are fixed |
| Valuable | Every Epic 2 rule this service evaluates comes from one approved, dated, checksum-verified package version, and `payment_match_rule` can never come back |
| Estimable | Three workbooks and their Tests tabs, one client, one cache, one swap workflow, one catalog client, one schema gate and one seed-free migration |
| Small | Fits two weeks with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion is a cache test, a checksum test, a catalog test, a schema test on a Testcontainers database or a scenario run in the build |

    Then the rows are tried in the order EXACT priority 1, WINDOW priority 2, PARTIAL priority 3
    Then payment "PAY-91008" of 12,500.00 THB that both EXACT and WINDOW match is decided by EXACT
    Then payment "PAY-91002" of 11,875.00 THB is decided by PARTIAL with a shortfall of 625.00 THB
    Then the decision log entry names rule "R-RES-26" and rule version "PMT-2026.12"
    Then the order matches RWB-E2-027 BR1 and its "PM-2026.12" row order

  Scenario: AC5 RESTRUCTURE rows feed RWB-E2-035 (legacy RWB-E2-042 AC5)
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns package code "RESTRUCTURE" version "RES-2026.12" in force on 2026-12-15, and rule row "R-RES-04" with action_text "Assign the case to a restructuring officer and start the offer clock", owner_role "RW-RESTRUCT" and timer_spec "2 working days"
    Given RESTRUCTURE version "RES-2026.12" is in force on 2026-12-15
    When SY-RULES evaluates R-RES-04 for case "RW-2026-000777"
    Then RuleCatalog.row("R-RES-04", "RES-2026.12") returns action_text "Assign the case to a restructuring officer and start the offer clock", owner_role "RW-RESTRUCT" and timer_spec "2 working days"
    Then every route-set row that RWB-E2-035 reads carries the three fields
    Then RWB-E2-035 sets the next action, the owner and the due date from these values

  Scenario: AC6 payment_match_rule is not created (legacy RWB-E2-042 AC6)
    Given a database migrated from empty with the release migrations on 2026-12-10
    When the schema check runs
    Then no table named payment_match_rule exists
    Then no column of DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 exists
    Then the table count is 93
    Then the build fails if any migration in the release creates payment_match_rule
```

The six criteria above are the legacy criteria of RWB-E2-042 and they carry their values unchanged. The split is this: the three packages are governed and stored in rwb-decision, which owns `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row`, `rule_test_case`, the load and approve operations and the 00:01 promotion (ASM-0069; Arch v5 slides 41 and 44; Temporal and Drools slides 15 and 16). rwb-case authors the three workbooks and their Tests tabs, fetches the model over `GET /rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}`, verifies the SHA-256, builds and swaps one KieBase per version and reads `rule_row` only through the catalog. Every statement above about a registry row, an approval or a version in force is therefore proved against the rwb-decision contract mock in this story, and re-proved against the real service by RWB-ITG-E2042-ITG. What this story owns and proves on its own artefacts is the write-once workbook, the checksum-verified model cache with its atomic swap and last-good-model rule, the catalog read, and the schema assertion that `rwb_case` never holds `payment_match_rule`.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Each Epic 2 package is authored in the Drools XLS decision-table template; the workbook is stored write-once in Blob `rule-packages`, and governance — load, checks, scenarios, approval, effective dating — is rwb-decision's only | D-RCV-36 T3, T4; ASM-0069 |
| BR2 | Each package version carries at least `rules.testcases.min` (50) scenarios, and every scenario passes before the version may be approved | REQ-CWC-014; D-RCV-36 T4 |
| BR3 | PAYMENT_MATCH has one row per match type, and the row order is EXACT then WINDOW then PARTIAL, as in RWB-E2-027 | R-RES-26; D-RCV-36 T10 |
| BR4 | RESTRUCTURE route-set rows carry action_text, owner_role and timer_spec; RWB-E2-035 reads them only from the catalog, by rule ID and package version | D-RCV-36 T6; FEAT-CWC-28 |
| BR5 | `payment_match_rule` is not created in `rwb_case`, and DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 stay retired; no code, rule row, migration or test reads or writes them | D-RCV-36 T10 |
| BR6 | The package code is the RuleSet of the workbook; the version labels are RES-, PMT- and BKG-yyyy.MM | D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR7 | First match wins: exactly one row decides, and the default row is last | D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR8 | An open case keeps the package version it was decided under when a newer version reaches its valid-from date | R-UNI-38 |
| BR9 | `RuleScenarioBuildGate` runs every in-force package's scenarios in every build | REQ-CWC-014; D-RCV-36 T4 |
| BR10 | rwb-case holds only an evaluated copy: one KieBase per package version, at most 20 in the cache, never recompiled per call and never edited in place | Arch v5 slide 27; DP-04; Temporal and Drools slide 16 |
| BR11 | The SHA-256 of the fetched model is verified against the announced checksum before the KieBase is used; on a mismatch or a failed build the last good model stays in force and the package is alerted | Arch v5 slides 11 and 27; DP-04 |
| BR12 | rwb-case reads no workbook, DRL source or rule table: the only reads are the model operation, the catalog operation and the version list | D-RCV-36 T3, T6; DP-04 |
| BR13 | No code in rwb-case writes `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` or `rule_test_case`; those rows are written by rwb-decision only | ASM-0069; DP-01 |

##### 9. State transitions

This story changes no case status. It adds the model-cache states that rwb-case observes for a package version.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not cached | RulePackageInForce, or the first evaluation of a package | The checksum verifies and the KieBase builds | In force (cached) |
| In force (cached) | RulePackageInForce for a newer version | The checksum verifies and the swap succeeds | New version in force (cached); the earlier version is kept until it is evicted or superseded |
| In force (cached) | RulePackageInForce for a newer version | The checksum does not verify, the model is not served, or the KieBase does not build | The earlier version stays in force; the failure is counted and alerted |
| In force (cached) | No version in force on the business date | The evaluation raises `NoPackageInForce` once | Unchanged; the caller reports MSG-P3-027 |
| In force (cached) | The cache is at its maximum of 20 | A version that is not in force is the least recently used | Evicted; a later event or evaluation caches it again |
| In force (cached) | A newer version becomes the one in force | The swap has succeeded | Superseded in the cache; still held while the cases decided under it are open |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Authors the three workbooks and their Tests tabs, and loads them through the rwb-decision admin operation |
| RW-RISK, risk and model risk officer | Approves a package version in rwb-decision; may not hold RW-COE, and the author cannot approve |
| The rwb-case service identity | Fetches the model, verifies the checksum, builds and swaps the KieBase, reads the catalog and evicts an unused version |
| SY-RULES, Drools evaluator | Evaluates the packages inside the EvaluateRules activity only |
| The build pipeline, no user role | Runs `RuleScenarioBuildGate` and `PaymentMatchRuleAbsentCheck` against a Testcontainers database; no SIT, UAT or PROD data |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the version list, the rule rows and the scenario results through the rwb-decision operations |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A rule package version is not a credit decision |

The four registry tables are rwb-decision's and this story writes none of their rows (ASM-0069; DP-01). No new field ID is added for the cache, which is in memory and holds no case data. `payment_match_rule` and DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 are retired and appear in this story only as the assertion that they do not exist. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This story serves no new business operation. The three package codes and their versions are read through rwb-decision's operations, and the model cache is internal to rwb-case; no cache read is published.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Service | Used for | Timeout |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}` | rwb-decision (P7) | The compiled model, its version label and its SHA-256, on the swap and on a first evaluation (DP-04) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion=` | rwb-decision (P7) | action_text, owner_role, timer_spec and outputs of one rule row by rule ID and package version (AC5) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` | rwb-decision (P7) | The version list and the checksum of the version in force | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` | rwb-decision (P7) | The multipart load of a workbook with validFrom; rwb-decision owns the operation, this story calls it (AC1 to AC3) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/approve` | rwb-decision (P7) | The four-eyes approval of a loaded version (AC1 to AC3) | One hop, 2 s (DP-11) |

The five operations are rwb-decision's; this story consumes them and never defines them. A checksum mismatch is carried in the model response and compared locally.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The model swap records no decision and publishes no event. The local decision-record library of DP-03 is part of the build and publishes `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` when a decision is taken in rwb-case; this story adds no event type to it.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Handler |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` (EV-30) | `rwb.decision.events.v1` | P7 | Case router, inbox dedupe, `signalWithStart` of `RuleModelSwap` for the package code and version label; the swap fetches, verifies and swaps the model |

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| RuleModelSwap | Workflow started by RulePackageInForce, workflow ID = `rule-model-swap-{packageCode}-{version}` | `rwb-case` | One swap per package code and version label: fetch, verify, build, swap, record the outcome |
| swapRuleModel | Activity | `rwb-case` | Calls the model operation, verifies the SHA-256, builds the KieBase and swaps the pointer atomically; keeps the last good model on failure |
| EvaluateRules | Activity (workflow kit) | `rwb-case` | Calls the embedded Drools kit with a package code, the facts and the business date; the only place a rule is evaluated (DP-04) |
| RecordAndApply | Activity (workflow kit) | `rwb-case` | Writes the decision record, the state change and the outbox rows in one transaction (DP-03) |

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The 00:01 promotion is the Temporal Schedule JOB-20 in rwb-decision and is out of scope here (Arch v5 slide 44; the OPS story of this key). The swap is event-started, not scheduled.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Note |
|---|---|---|
| recovery_case | P3 (rwb_case) | Read by the evaluation for the facts of the case; no column added |
| timer | P3 (rwb_case) | Read for the due dates a route-set row sets; no column added |
| queue | P3 (rwb_case) | Read for the target queue a rule row names; no column added |
| outbox_event, processed_event, idempotency_key | PLT library, created in rwb_case | Outbox, inbox and idempotency objects of the event consumer (DP-09) |

No table is created and no column is added by this story. `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` are rwb-decision's and are never read directly (ASM-0069; DP-01). `payment_match_rule` does not exist.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `rules`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.rules.epic2`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Epic2PackageWorkbooks | Configuration | The three xlsx workbooks and their Tests tabs, owned by RW-COE, stored write-once with the SHA-256 in the object metadata |
| RulePackageClient | Client | Calls the model operation and the version list; compares the returned SHA-256 with the event checksum and the Blob metadata; never retries a checksum mismatch |
| ModelCache | Service | One KieBase per package version, at most 20 versions, least-recently-used eviction that never evicts a version in force, atomic pointer swap |
| RuleModelSwap | Workflow | One swap per package code and version label, started by RulePackageInForce through the inbox |
| SwapRuleModelActivity | Activity | Runs the fetch, the checksum check, the build and the swap, and records the outcome in logs and metrics |
| RuleCatalogClient | Client | Calls the catalog operation for action_text, owner_role, timer_spec and outputs by rule ID and package version |
| Epic2Evaluator | Service | The only caller of the embedded Drools kit inside the EvaluateRules activity; returns `RuleResult(packageCode, packageVersion, ruleId, outputs)` |
| PaymentMatchOrderCheck | Validator extension | BR3: one row per match type and the order EXACT, WINDOW, PARTIAL, checked at load in rwb-decision through the authoring pipeline of RWB-P3-E1073-APP |
| RestructureCatalogCheck | Validator extension | BR4: action_text, owner_role and timer_spec present on every route-set row, checked at load through the same pipeline |
| PaymentMatchRuleAbsentCheck | Schema gate | Fails the build when `payment_match_rule`, or any column of DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273, exists in a migrated database |
| RuleScenarioBuildGate | Build gate (existing) | Runs the 174 scenarios of the three in-force versions |
| Epic2LoadRunbook | Run book | The load order, the approver, the valid-from date and the rollback for each package |

**Blob and migrations**

- Blob paths `RESTRUCTURE/RES-2026.12.xlsx`, `PAYMENT_MATCH/PMT-2026.12.xlsx` and `BOOKING_MATCH/BKG-2026.12.xlsx`; write-once, the SHA-256 in the object metadata, no public access (RWB-P3-E2042-INF).
- No migration creates `payment_match_rule`. One migration runs `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS payment_match_rule` with its indexes, for DEV and SIT databases created before D-RCV-36 T10, after the load runbook has archived the rows to a CSV. No migration in the release creates the table.
- No seed migration: the three package codes are rwb-decision rows, seeded by RWB-P7-E2042-APP (ASM-0069).
- The schema gate asserts 93 tables on a Testcontainers database migrated from empty.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The three workbooks and their Tests tabs (RW-COE), with version labels and the valid-from date 2026-12-15 copied from the legacy story.
- `rules.testcases.min` = 50 through the parameters contract of rwb-case (DP-06).
- The cache bound of 20 versions through the embedded Drools kit configuration (DP-04); the stories of this key never hard-code it.

**Build steps**

1. Author the three workbooks and the 174 scenarios; store them write-once in Blob and record the SHA-256 in the metadata (AC1 to AC3, X9, X10).
2. RulePackageClient over the model and version operations, with the checksum comparison and the 404 answer; unit tests for X1, X2 and X8.
3. ModelCache with one KieBase per version, the bound of 20, the least-recently-used eviction and the atomic swap; tests for X1, X2 and X4.
4. RuleModelSwap and SwapRuleModelActivity, started by RulePackageInForce through the inbox with dedupe; tests for X3, X5 and X2.
5. RuleCatalogClient with the 2 s budget and the missing-row answer; tests for AC5 and X8.
6. Epic2Evaluator inside the EvaluateRules activity, returning the rule ID and the package version of the version in force and honouring R-UNI-38; tests for AC4 and AC5.
7. PaymentMatchOrderCheck and RestructureCatalogCheck wired into the authoring pipeline of RWB-P3-E1073-APP; tests for AC2, AC4 and AC5.
8. PaymentMatchRuleAbsentCheck and the table count assertion on a Testcontainers database; test for AC6.
9. Run `RuleScenarioBuildGate` over the three versions and add the lock manifest entries; test for AC1 to AC3.
10. Write the load runbook with the rollback step for each package.

**Feature switch.** The legacy flag name `rwb.p3.drools` is kept as the legacy reference; in the target the switch is a parameter read through the parameters contract. Off: the model cache loads nothing, the swap workflow does not start, and every evaluation returns `NoPackageInForce` with MSG-P3-027; nothing else changes.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the three versions are fetched, verified and cached in SIT with 174 passing scenarios, a swap on a checksum mismatch leaves the model in force untouched, and the migrated schema holds 93 tables with no `payment_match_rule`.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-027 | A workbook check fails, or no version is in force for a package | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P7-002 | The approver is the author | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The version label is already loaded | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | An empty workbook | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Valid from before today | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right calls a package operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

For MSG-P3-027 the {check} value is compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row or scenario; the match order and the catalog completeness are part of the schema check, and the {detail} names row IDs, cells, rule IDs, package codes and version labels only, never a case fact or a person. This story adds no message and changes no text. A checksum mismatch, a failed build and a refused overwrite are operator conditions: they carry the package code, the version label and the expected and computed checksum to the log and the dashboard of RWB-P3-E2042-OPS, and produce no user-facing message.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this story. The three versions are read through rwb-decision's version list, and SCR-39 Rules and parameters shows the same versions in Epic 8. The states LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED and REFUSED are rwb-decision's and are read from the version list; the model-cache states of section 9 are internal to rwb-case and are exposed only as the readiness signal and the metrics of RWB-P3-E2042-OPS.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code. Rows, conditions, match types, tolerances, windows, action text, owner roles and timers are data in the workbooks and the registry; the cache bound and the timeouts are configuration.
- No personal data in logs, metrics, tests, workflow history or prompts. Scenarios use synthetic case facts and payment codes; the swap log carries package codes, version labels and checksums only.
- No read of another service's tables: `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row` and `rule_test_case` are read only through the rwb-decision operations, and `rwb_case` holds no foreign key into `rwb_decision` (DP-01).
- One evaluator: the three packages are evaluated only through the embedded Drools kit inside an activity, on the version in force fetched from rwb-decision; no code reads a workbook, a DRL source or a rule table (D-RCV-36 T3, T6; DP-04).
- Every fetched model is checksum-verified before use, and a version is never edited in place: a change is a new version and a rollback moves the pointer in rwb-decision.
- `payment_match_rule` is never created, and DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 are never referenced, by a migration, a test, a query or a document in the service.
- The build gate reads a release manifest and a Testcontainers database; it never connects to SIT, UAT or PROD.
- No secret in a workbook, a value file or a runbook: the Blob identity and the rwb-decision certificate come from the platform secret store.

- The remaining 448 routing rules and the UNIVERSAL package (Epic 3; DL24).
- The rules and parameters screen (SCR-39, Epic 8).
- The Blob container, the identity, the certificate and the sizing (RWB-P3-E2042-INF); the Helm values, the consumer group, the dashboards, the alerts and the runbook (RWB-P3-E2042-OPS).
- The real cross-service proof of the load, the approval, the promotion and the swap (RWB-ITG-E2042-ITG).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: secondary slice of RWB-E2-042 for rwb-comms. The three package codes, their workbook, the load checks, the 50-scenario gate, four-eyes approval, effective dating, one-call rollback and the registry are rwb-decision's (`RWB-P7-E2042-APP`); the workbook authoring, the write-once Blob store, the model cache and the build gate are rwb-case's (`RWB-P3-E2042-APP`); the local copy, the checksum, the KieBase registry and the evaluation inside this service are `RWB-P6-E1073-APP`. This story carries what is left on the notice side: the Epic 2 versions and their counts as this service resolves them, the route-set fields of a rule row, the package code, version and checksum on the notice decision, and the proof that a load, an approval, a promotion at 00:01 or a rollback raises no notice, no message and no dispatch. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **litigation officer (RW-LITOFF) who owns a demand or recall notice, and the rwb-comms service identity that generates it**, I want **every notice decision that reads one of the three Epic 2 packages to carry the package code, the version label and the checksum that decided it, the route-set fields of a rule row to be copied verbatim from the registry by rule ID and version, and the whole notice path — the notice row, the template, the merge-field catalog, the outbox, the ACE notification path, the dispatch item and the WIN file — to stay untouched by a load, an approval, a promotion at 00:01 or a one-call rollback of RESTRUCTURE, PAYMENT_MATCH or BOOKING_MATCH**, so that **a rule change reaches the desk as tested, approved, dated data and never as correspondence to a customer, and any notice can still name the version that decided it months later**.

Inside `rwb-comms` this is the notice-side slice of legacy RWB-E2-042. The service facts are schema `rwb_comms`, REST base `/api/recovery/comms/v1`, topic `rwb.comms.events.v1` with `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1` (EV-13), `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` (EV-14) and `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` (EV-15), queue `rwb-comms` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms`, and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` on which the library writes the record of a notice (DP-03). The slice:

- The three versions of 16 November 2026 — RESTRUCTURE "RES-2026.12" with 38 rows and 62 scenarios, PAYMENT_MATCH "PMT-2026.12" with 3 rows and 58 scenarios, BOOKING_MATCH "BKG-2026.12" with 21 rows and 54 scenarios, all valid from 2026-12-15 and each at or above `rules.testcases.min` = 50 — resolved only through the operations of RWB-P3-E2042-CON.
- The route-set fields `action_text` (DF-REF-008), `owner_role` (DF-REF-010) and `timer_spec` (DF-REF-011) of R-RES-04, copied into the next action, the owner and the due date of the notice instead of compiled into code.
- The seed, the load, the approve, the dry run, the promotion and the rollback: read as states and counts, never performed here.
- The assertion the set relies on: a governance action on the three packages writes no `notice`, no `template` and no `merge_field` row, puts nothing on `rwb.comms.events.v1`, sends nothing through the ACE notification path, adds no dispatch item, raises no task, and leaves the 16:00 run of JOB-10 (DP-10) with the notices it had before.
- The negative schema assertion: `payment_match_rule` and DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 exist nowhere in `rwb_comms`, and no rule row, DRL or test of this service names them.

Not this story, and stated again in section 6 and section 19:

- The local copy, the model fetch, the SHA-256 verification, the KieBase registry of 20 versions, the scenario re-run, the atomic swap, the `EvaluateRules` and `RecordAndApply` activities and the consumption of `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` are **RWB-P6-E1073-APP**. This story uses them as published and adds no loader, no cache and no activity.
- The workbook, the Rows and Tests tabs, the write-once Blob object, the model cache and `RuleScenarioBuildGate` are **RWB-P3-E2042-APP**; the package rows, the checks, the four-eyes approval, the dry run, the promotion and the rollback are **RWB-P7-E2042-APP**; the rights, roles and screens are **RWB-P4-E2042-APP**; the cross-service proof of a load, an approval, a promotion, a swap and a record is **RWB-ITG-E2042-ITG**. Every criterion of this story is proved against this service alone or through a contract fake.
- The notice generation, the dispatch loop and the proof-of-delivery capture are `RWB-P6-E1052-APP`, `RWB-P6-E2021-APP` and `RWB-P6-E1055-APP`; the template lifecycle is `RWB-P6-AD017-APP`. This story changes none of their operations.

Which of the three packages a notice of this service actually reads is named in no source, and neither is the package code that `RWB-P6-E1073-APP` assigns to rwb-comms: the three Epic 2 packages serve the case engines of RWB-E2-002, RWB-E2-004, RWB-E2-007, RWB-E2-008, RWB-E2-027 and RWB-E2-035, and the legacy story attaches no notice to any of them. The resolution is carried as GAP-2395 with ASM-3979 and is not settled silently here.

##### 2. Business rationale

A rule change is a data change: authored in a workbook, compiled, tested against a scenario set, approved by a second person, dated and rolled back in one call (D-RCV-36 T3 to T6). The control exists because recovery decisions are taken under a procedure a supervisor has read, and audit found the procedure not followed because the rules were not in the system (CTL-08). Nothing in that control is safe if changing a rule also contacts a customer: a demand, recall or statutory notice starts a legal clock from the date of delivery, and a notice raised by a release cannot be unsent, unseen or re-dated.

That is the subject of this story. The legacy key puts three packages in one governance path and retires `payment_match_rule`; on this side the requirement is the one the integration story names as the harness assertion — *the notice path stays silent* (RWB-ITG-E2042-ITG, section 2) — and the one the registry story defers here: *the notices a rule change must not raise are RWB-P6-E2042-APP* (RWB-P7-E2042-APP, section 19). It meets REQ-CWC-013 and REQ-CWC-014 from the consumer side.

The measure is shaped like the notice path: three versions resolve by package code, rule ID and label with no value held in this service's code; the three route-set fields appear verbatim on the notice; every notice decision record names one package version and one checksum; and a load, an approval, a promotion and a rollback together add zero notice rows, zero template rows, zero outbox rows on `rwb.comms.events.v1`, zero dispatch items, zero tasks and zero messages to NSS or LINE OA. The 16:00 run of JOB-10 on the promotion date carries exactly the notices it carried before, and `rwb_comms` holds no `payment_match_rule` and no column of DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273.

The realignment changes the mechanism, not the business control:

1. The single recovery schema becomes `rwb_comms` for the notice facts and the lapse of the decision record, with `rwb_decision` read only through its contract (DP-01, DP-15).
2. The monolith's in-process rule read becomes the published contract of RWB-P3-E2042-CON: the catalog read of a rule row, the model read with its checksum, the version list, the parameters and the reference data (DP-04, DP-06, DP-07).
3. The evaluation itself stays inside the service, in the embedded Drools kit on task queue `rwb-comms` (DP-04, DP-10), and the mechanism is `RWB-P6-E1073-APP`'s; this story pins its result.
4. The version is no longer read from a properties file: it is a resolved value of the contract, recorded on the local decision record written through the library on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03).
5. The API base becomes `/api/recovery/comms/v1` and the notice read keeps its shape (DP-13, DP-19); this story adds no path.
6. The event names of the service and of the shared record topic follow the naming rule (DP-14), and no new event is created for a rule change — the absence of that event is the requirement.
7. `payment_match_rule` is never created in `rwb_comms`, and the thirteen retired field IDs are referenced by no row, DRL or test.

The business outcome is the one a supervisor can check on a notice: the letter that went out names the version that decided it, and no letter went out because a version changed.

##### 4. Flow

1. A capability of rwb-comms that generates a notice (`RWB-P6-E1052-APP`, `RWB-P6-E2021-APP`) calls `EvaluateRules` on queue `rwb-comms` with the package code, the facts of the case and the business date; Drools is never called in workflow code (DP-04, DP-10).
2. `NoticeRuleVersionResolver` resolves the package code the notice is assigned, the version in force for the business date and that version's checksum through the version list of RWB-P3-E2042-CON; no label, checksum or threshold is read from code or configuration (DP-04, DP-06).
3. The answer is `RuleResult` from `RWB-P6-E1073-APP`: package code, version label, rule ID and outputs. When no version is in force the answer is `NoPackageInForce`, which is non-retryable and creates no notice (X1).
4. For a rule that carries a route set, `RouteSetFieldReader` reads `action_text` (DF-REF-008), `owner_role` (DF-REF-010) and `timer_spec` (DF-REF-011) through the catalog read by rule ID and version and copies the three values verbatim into the next action, the owner and the due date. A blank field refuses the read and no notice is created.
5. `RecordAndApply` writes, in one transaction in `rwb_comms`: the `notice` row, the local decision record naming the package code, version label, checksum and rule ID, and the outbox row of `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1` (DP-01, DP-03, DP-09). The library publishes `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1`.
6. Elsewhere, and at no request of this service, a version of RESTRUCTURE, PAYMENT_MATCH or BOOKING_MATCH is loaded, approved and promoted at 00:01 on its valid-from date, or rolled back in one call. On the notice path that is an observation and nothing else: no controller, listener, workflow, Schedule or activity of `rwb-comms` reacts to a package state, a load, an approval, a promotion or a rollback.
7. A new or restored version reaches this service through the local copy of `RWB-P6-E1073-APP`; the next notice decided after the swap names the new version, and a notice already decided keeps the version on its record (R-UNI-38). No `notice`, `template` or `merge_field` row changes because a version moved.
8. The 16:00 dispatch run of JOB-10 pins the version it started with for the whole run and writes the WIN file of INT-14 through the hand-off of `RWB-P6-E1007-APP`; a version promoted at 00:01 changes neither the file nor its contents.
9. Internal audit reads the decision records of the notices of a case and proves which version decided each one, without reading a registry row and without touching a notice.
10. Nothing in this flow sends an SMS or a LINE message: the conduct check, the contact stop and the send of `RWB-P6-E2021-APP` are untouched by a rule change, and steps 6 to 8 create no dispatch item, task or notification.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The version list answers no version in force for the package a notice is assigned | `RuleResult` is `NoPackageInForce`, the notice is not created, nothing is written and nothing is dispatched; the caller sees the message and no notice exists | MSG-GEN-006 | AC5 |
| X2 | A route-set row of the version carries an empty `action_text`, `owner_role` or `timer_spec` | The catalog read is refused, the check names the rule ID and the column, and the notice is not created | MSG-P3-027 | AC5 |
| X3 | The catalog read, the model read or the version list answers 503 or times out beyond the 2 s client budget | The notice is not created; the previous version stays in force; the failure is in the local run record and the call is retried once with jitter on a GET | MSG-GEN-006 | AC5 |
| X4 | A governance action on any of the three packages runs (load, approve, promote, roll back) | No notice, no message, no dispatch item, no task and no event of this service; the notice rows and the dispatch file are what they were | None | AC2, AC3, AC4 |
| X5 | A notice was decided under a version that is later rolled back | The decision record keeps the rolled-back version; no notice row is rewritten and no second notice is generated | None | AC5 |
| X6 | The notice path would need to learn of a change from `rwb.decision.events.v1` | It does not: no listener of this service subscribes for the notice path, so a promotion cannot raise a notice; the architecture test fails the build if one is added | None | AC4 |
| X7 | The local decision record of a notice cannot be written | Nothing is applied: no notice row and no outbox row; an incident is raised under R-UNI-39 | MSG-P7-003 | AC5 |
| X8 | A caller without the right asks for a notice or asks for a rule version of this service | Refused at the edge and by the guard of the P4 story; nothing is read or written | MSG-P4-002 | AC1 |
| X9 | A migration of `rwb_comms` creates `payment_match_rule` or a column of DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 | The service's schema check fails the build before the artefact is published | None | AC6 |

A refused decision leaves every row exactly as it was before the call, and the notice path has no compensating action: a notice is either created with its version and its record, or it does not exist. The state a request rests in when no version is in force is named by no source; the refusal of X1 is the reading carried as GAP-2399 with ASM-3983, and no hold reason of this service is invented for it.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Builds against RWB-P3-E2042-CON, the platform contracts of its DP table and the local copy of `RWB-P6-E1073-APP`; no registry operation, no loader and no cache is implemented here |
| Negotiable | The package assignment, the version labels, the row and scenario counts, the route-set values and the message texts are data or registry rows; the silence of the notice path, the pinning of the version and the absence of the retired table are fixed |
| Valuable | A rule change cannot reach a customer, and every notice still names the approved version that decided it |
| Estimable | One version resolver, one catalog reader, one dispatch pin, one architecture test, one schema check and one probe of the notice path |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests. It builds no workbook, no loader, no cache, no registry operation, no screen and no event |
| Testable | Each criterion is a component, contract or end-to-end test on this service with fixed fixtures and a recorded result; the cross-service journey itself is RWB-ITG-E2042-ITG's |

```

The six criteria are new under D-RCV-60 and each tests only a deliverable of this story. No legacy criterion is restated: AC1 to AC6 of RWB-E2-042 belong to RWB-P3-E2042-APP, and the load and approve path belongs to RWB-P7-E2042-APP. The values inside the criteria are the legacy values — the package codes, the labels, the row and scenario counts, the valid-from date, the rule IDs, the three route-set values and the two payment fixtures — so this side is proved against the same data the legacy story used.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A rule change never raises a notice: a load, an approval, a promotion or a rollback of any package writes no `notice`, `template` or `merge_field` row, sends nothing on any channel and raises no task | RWB-ITG-E2042-ITG section 2; RWB-P7-E2042-APP section 19; legacy section 8 BR1 |
| BR2 | Every notice decision names the package code, the version label, the checksum and the rule ID that decided it, written on the local decision record in the same transaction as the notice row | R-UNI-38; DP-03; Temporal and Drools design slide 16 |
| BR3 | A notice keeps the version it was decided under; a promotion or a rollback changes the next decision and never rewrites a past one | R-UNI-38; legacy BR8 |
| BR4 | The values of a package are data of rwb-decision: no package code, label, row, threshold, match type, tolerance or window is held in this service's code or configuration | D-RCV-36 T3 to T6; DP-04; template §R7.2 s17 |
| BR5 | The route-set fields `action_text`, `owner_role` and `timer_spec` are read by rule ID and package version and copied verbatim; a blank field refuses the read and the notice is not created. Where the three fields set the next action of a case, the behaviour stays with RWB-E2-035 (GAP-2400; ASM-3984) | D-RCV-36 T6; FEAT-CWC-28; legacy BR4 |
| BR6 | The rows of a package are tried in the order the registry holds, first match, exactly one row decides and the default row is last; this service re-sorts nothing | D-RCV-36 T5; legacy BR7 |
| BR7 | A package version is used only when it is in force and its checksum is verified; when no version is in force the answer is `NoPackageInForce`, the notice is not created and nothing is dispatched | RWB-P3-E2042-CON AC5; RWB-P6-E1073-APP AC1 |
| BR8 | The version in force is resolved through the contract on each decision and the scenario count is read against `rules.testcases.min` = 50 through the parameters contract; neither is a constant | REQ-CWC-014; DP-06 |
| BR9 | The dispatch run of JOB-10 pins one version for the whole run, so one file never mixes two versions of the same package | DP-10; Arch v5 slide 44; this story |
| BR10 | The notice path learns of a version through the local copy of `RWB-P6-E1073-APP` and never through a listener added for it; the architecture test fails the build when one is added | Arch v5 slides 17, 20 and 42; this story |
| BR11 | `payment_match_rule` is never created in `rwb_comms`, and DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 stay retired and are referenced by no row, DRL, test or query | D-RCV-36 T10; legacy BR5 |
| BR12 | Every notice operation declares its capability area and right and a caller without it is refused; no role row is held in `rwb_comms` | TSD P6 v2 T6.1; RWB-P4-E2042-APP |

##### 9. State transitions

This story adds no state to the notice and removes none. It records the package version that a notice was decided under and proves that the package lifecycle does not move a notice.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | A notice is requested and a version is in force | The decision names one version and its checksum and the record is written | "Approved" (or "Held" where the template rule of RWB-P6-E2021-APP holds it) |
| (none) | A notice is requested and no version is in force | `NoPackageInForce` is answered | No `notice` row exists; nothing is dispatched |
| (none) | A route-set field of the decided rule is blank | The catalog read is refused | No `notice` row exists; MSG-P3-027 |
| Any notice state | A load, an approval, a promotion or a rollback of any package | None | Unchanged: no notice moves and no row is rewritten |
| Any notice state | The version it was decided under is rolled back | R-UNI-38 applies | Unchanged: the decision record keeps the rolled-back version |

The case transitions of RWB-E2-002, RWB-E2-004, RWB-E2-007, RWB-E2-008, RWB-E2-027 and RWB-E2-035 are those stories' and are neither raised nor observed here.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-LITOFF, litigation officer | Requests and reads a notice under Litigation C and R; sees the next action, the owner and the due date the route set gives, and no rule value |
| RW-ENFORCE, enforcement owner and RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Request and read a notice under Litigation C and R for a case in their scope |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Loads and rolls back a package version in rwb-decision under Rules and parameters C and U; here the actor is a registry role and not a user of this service |
| RW-RISK, risk and model risk officer | Approves a version in rwb-decision under Rules and parameters A; is never the author |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the decision records of the notices of a case and the version each one names, under Litigation R; changes nothing |
| SY-RULES, Drools evaluator | Returns `RuleResult` with the package code, the version, the rule ID and the outputs, or `NoPackageInForce` inside the activity |
| The rwb-comms service identity | Resolves the version, reads the route set, writes the notice, the record and the outbox row, and pins the version for a dispatch run; it performs no governance action on a package |
| The build pipeline, no user role | Runs the architecture test of BR10 and the schema check of AC6 on a Testcontainers database; never connects to SIT, UAT or PROD |
| No delegation of authority level applies | A rule package version is not a credit decision and a notice is not an approval item |

No person is named anywhere in this story: the actors are roles and service identities. The rights are answered by the guard of RWB-P4-E1037-CON and the matrix of RWB-P4-E2042-APP; this story names them and holds no role row. The database login is the per-service login of DP-02, written only as "the rwb-comms login (DP-02)".

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This story adds no REST operation, no path and no field: the notice operations it works with are `POST /api/recovery/comms/v1/cases/{caseId}/notices` (API-P6-001) and `GET /api/recovery/comms/v1/notices/{noticeId}` (API-P6-002), owned by `RWB-P6-E2021-APP`, and their answers are unchanged — a rule version is evidence on the decision record and not a field of the notice answer.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-catalog/{ruleId}?packageVersion=` | P7 rwb-decision | `action_text`, `owner_role`, `timer_spec` and the outputs of one rule row by rule ID and version; faked for R-RES-04 and the route-set rows |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/rule-models/{packageCode}/{version}` | P7 rwb-decision | The compiled model, its version label and its SHA-256, which is the checksum the decision record names; faked with one correct and one wrong checksum |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` | P7 rwb-decision | The version in force, its status, its valid-from date and its row and scenario counts; faked for the three packages |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case | `rules.testcases.min` (50) and `drools.kiebase.cache.max` (20) on the business date, as parameters and never as code (DP-06) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | LOV-NOTICE with DEMAND as a statutory notice, LOV-DELIVERY and the notice-state vocabulary (DP-07) |

Each call is one hop with a 2 s client budget, a GET retries once with jitter and each downstream has its own circuit breaker (DP-11, ADR-020). No call changes a registry row and no call is made from workflow code.

###### 12.3 Events published

None by this story. `rwb.comms.events.v1` carries `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1` (EV-13), `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` (EV-14) and `rwb.comms.NoticeDelivered.v1` (EV-15), published by the notice stories of this service; this story writes only the `DecisionRecorded` row that the local library publishes on `rwb.decision-record.v1` in the same transaction as the notice (DP-03). No event announces a rule version, and the absence is the requirement (BR1).

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. This story consumes no event on any topic. The consumption of `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` from `rwb.decision.events.v1` is `RWB-P6-E1073-APP`'s and feeds the local copy; the notice path of this story reacts to nothing, and AC4 fails the build if a listener is added for it. The consumed events of the service remain those of the notice, dispatch and proof-of-delivery stories. Architecture v5 slide 13 gives the P6 to P7 pair a Temporal cell and no event cell while the published contract and the local-copy story require the subscription; the difference is carried as GAP-2396 with ASM-3980, and this story declares no consumed event under either reading.

| Name | Type | Queue | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NoticeDispatchWorkflow` | Workflow (kit Notify template, existing) | `rwb-comms` | Carries the notice decision and the dispatch run; this story adds no step to it |
| `EvaluateRules` | Activity (existing) | `rwb-comms` | Input package code, facts and business date; output `RuleResult` or `NoPackageInForce`; returns the version the decision names |
| `RecordAndApply` | Activity (existing) | `rwb-comms` | Writes the notice row, the decision record with the package code, version and checksum, and the outbox row in one transaction |

The two activities and the KieBase they use are `RWB-P6-E1073-APP`'s; this story fixes only what they return and what is recorded from it.

None. This story registers no Temporal Schedule and no Quartz row. The 16:00 dispatch run of JOB-10 on queue `rwb-comms` belongs to `RWB-P6-E2021-APP` and `RWB-P6-E1007-APP` and is unchanged; the 00:01 promotion is JOB-20 in rwb-decision (DP-10).

No `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row`, `rule_test_case`, `recovery_case` or `payment_match_rule` row is owned or read: the first four are rwb-decision's and are read through 12.2, the case is rwb-case's, and the last is retired.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.comms.rules` for the resolver and the catalog reader; the architecture test in the service's test tree alongside the schema check.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `NoticeRuleVersionResolver` | Service | Resolves the package code, the version in force and its checksum for the business date; holds no label in code (BR4, BR8) |
| `RouteSetFieldReader` | Service | Reads `action_text`, `owner_role` and `timer_spec` by rule ID and version; refuses a blank field (BR5) |
| `NoticeDecisionRecorder` | Service | Puts the package code, version and checksum on the record written by `RecordAndApply`, in the same transaction as the notice and the outbox row (BR2) |
| `DispatchVersionPin` | Configuration of the dispatch run | Pins the version the run started with for every notice of the file, so one file never mixes versions (BR9) |
| `NoticePathSilenceProbe` | Test support | Asserts that a governance action on any package writes no notice, template, merge_field or outbox row, sends nothing and raises no task (AC2, AC3) |
| `NoticePathListenerTest` | Architecture test | Fails the build when a class of the notice path subscribes to `rwb.decision.events.v1` or reacts to a package state (BR10) |
| `PaymentMatchRuleAbsentCheck` | Schema test | Fails the build when `payment_match_rule` or a column of DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 exists in `rwb_comms` (AC6) |
| `Epic2NoticeRunbook` | Run book | The order of the four governance actions, the version evidence to collect per notice, and the check that the 16:00 file is unchanged |

**Database and Blob.** No migration and no Blob object. The package code, version and checksum sit on `decision_log_entry` of DP-03; the local copy and its rows are `RWB-P6-E1073-APP`'s. The retired table and its thirteen field IDs are absent by construction and asserted by AC6.

**Configuration and reference data.** `rules.testcases.min` = 50 and `drools.kiebase.cache.max` = 20 through the parameters contract; LOV-NOTICE and the notice-state vocabulary through the reference-data contract; the three version labels and the valid-from date 2026-12-15 as registry data.

**Build steps**

1. Build `NoticeRuleVersionResolver` against the fakes of 12.8; test AC1 and the empty answer of X1.
2. Build `RouteSetFieldReader` and copy the three values into the notice; test AC5 and the blank field of X2.
3. Put the package code, the version and the checksum on the record through `NoticeDecisionRecorder`; test the pinning and the rolled-back version of AC5.
4. Build `NoticePathSilenceProbe` and run the four governance actions against the fakes; test AC2, AC3 and AC4.
5. Add `DispatchVersionPin` and prove that one file never mixes two versions; test AC4 and the repeated run.
6. Add `NoticePathListenerTest` and `PaymentMatchRuleAbsentCheck`; test AC6 and X9.
7. Write the run book and hand the fixtures to `RWB-ITG-E2042-ITG`.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass; the three versions resolve with their counts; the four governance actions add no row, no message and no dispatch item; and the migrated `rwb_comms` holds no `payment_match_rule` and no retired column.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-GEN-006 | A downstream read is unavailable beyond the retry, or no version is in force | The service is unavailable. Try again later. |
| MSG-P3-027 | A rule row is incomplete at the catalog read | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P6-003 | The template behind the notice was withdrawn | The {template} template has been withdrawn. The notice is on hold until Legal approves a new version. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written | The decision could not be recorded. Nothing has changed. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right calls a notice or a version read | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

This story adds no message. For MSG-P3-027 the {check} value is catalog and the {detail} names the rule ID and the field, never a case fact or a person. The wording of MSG-GEN-006 for the empty-version case is the platform message and its text is the platform library's, not a value of this story.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built in this story and nothing is rendered. The notice panel, its states and its field list are `RWB-P6-E2021-APP`'s and are served through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19; SCR-33 Template approval and SCR-39 Rules and parameters are unchanged. What becomes visible to a reader of the notice and its audit trail is the evidence: the notice shows the next action, the owner and the due date from the route set, and the audit view of the decision record shows the package code, the version label and the checksum. No screen shows a package version it did not read from the record.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the package codes, the version labels, the row and scenario counts, the match types, the tolerances, the windows, the route-set values and `rules.testcases.min` are registry rows or parameters, read through DP-04, DP-06 and DP-07.
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs, logs, tests or prompts: the facts handed to the kit are the case reference, the notice type, the template code and version and the business date; the party, the address and the contact values never leave the notice row, and the payload check fails the build when one appears.
- No cross-schema read and no cross-service write: `notice`, `template`, `merge_field` and the record are `rwb_comms`; the rule facts come from the published operations of 12.2 and no statement names `rwb_decision`, `rwb_case` or another schema (DP-01).
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or the owner's `v_ace_*` views: this story reads no ACE view; the contact and address facts belong to `RWB-P6-E2021-APP` and to rwb-source-data (DP-05).
- A rule change never reaches a customer: no listener, controller, Schedule or activity of the notice path reacts to a package state, and the architecture test fails the build if one is added.
- `payment_match_rule` is never created and DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 are never referenced; the schema check reads only `rwb_comms`.
- The build gate and the schema check read a release manifest and a Testcontainers database; they never connect to SIT, UAT or PROD.
