##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, module `rules/registry`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision.rules.registry`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

How this story applies each row. **DP-01**: the four registry tables and `decision_log_entry` sit in `rwb_decision`; the story reads no schema of another service and no other service reads its tables — the rows travel as the model, the catalog and the event. **DP-03**: the load, the approval, the promotion and the rollback each write one local decision record and its outbox row in the same transaction; a record that cannot be written stops the action (BR11). **DP-04**: the load and the promotion use the embedded kit for the compile, the checksum and first-match semantics, and the registry supplies the package to the consuming services; the kit is a platform library and this story embeds it, while the consuming service's cache and swap are RWB-P3-E2042-APP's and are not rebuilt here. **DP-05**: no ACE view is read; the registry sees no customer, account or payment fact, and the dry-run counts carry no case identifier. **DP-06**: `rules.testcases.min` = 50 is read as a parameter and is never a constant, and the flag `rwb.p3.drools` is read the same way. **DP-07**: LOV-DECISION and the version-state list are read as reference data with the version in force; the match types, the row order, the thresholds and the three route-set fields stay row columns and are never reference data (BR13). **DP-10**: the promotion is the JOB-20 Temporal Schedule at 00:01, and this story implements its handler and registers no workflow of its own. **DP-13**: every path of section 12 uses `/api/recovery/decision/v1`; the monolith base appears nowhere. **DP-14**: the topic is `rwb.decision.events.v1`, the event is `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1`, and the queue is `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`. **DP-15**: the `rwb_decision` baseline, `V2_042_1__epic2_rule_packages.sql` and `V2_042_2__registry_constraints.sql` sit in this service's own Flyway sequence. **DP-19**: no screen is served here; SCR-39 reads the registry through gateway-bff in Epic 8, and the record of the route is the platform contract, not code of this story.

The platform H dependencies of the table — H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON, RWB-PLT-E1044-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON — and the C dependencies C RWB-P7-E1073-CON, C RWB-P3-E1042-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON are the DP-added dependencies that are **not** in the metadata rows, which name None and RWB-P3-E2042-CON. They are recorded in GAP-1296 and ASM-2306: they are platform contracts of wave 0 and published contracts of rwb-case and of this service, none of them blocks the build, and an APP story builds against the published set and its fake. **Ready to start therefore stays Day 1**: no DP-added H dependency is a same-lane story behind this one, and the only C dependency of the metadata is a published contract with a fake (R5.7 rule 2).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| RulePackageController | Controller | `GET /admin/rule-packages`: the guard, the scope, the package list and the problem mapping |
| RuleVersionController | Controller | The multipart load, the version list, the dry-run read, the approve and the rollback, with the Idempotency-Key and the 201, 200, 400, 404, 409 and 422 answers |
| RuleVersionService | Service | Orders the load in one transaction: parse, check, dry run, version row, rule rows, test cases, decision record |
| WorkbookParser | Service | Reads the Rows tab into `rule_row` candidates (RuleSet = package code, NAME = rule ID, default row last) and the Tests tab into `rule_test_case` candidates; rejects an empty or malformed workbook with MSG-GEN-001 |
| RuleCheckPipeline | Service | Compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row and scenario checks in order; refuses the whole load with MSG-P3-027 and names the check, the row, the column and the failing test-case IDs |
| PaymentMatchOrderCheck | Validator extension | BR4: one row per match type and the order EXACT 1, WINDOW 2, PARTIAL 3; called from the schema check, not from a separate path |
| RestructureCatalogCheck | Validator extension | BR5: a non-empty `action_text`, `owner_role` and `timer_spec` on every RESTRUCTURE route-set row; called from the schema check |
| TestCaseRunner | Service | Runs the Tests tab against the compiled model, counts total, passed and failed, and records the expected and actual result of every case |
| DryRunService | Service | Runs the dry run on the business date, stores the counts in `dry_run_counts` and serves the per-case result of the dry-run read |
| ApprovalService | Service | Refuses the author with MSG-P7-002, moves LOADED to APPROVED with the approver and the time, writes the record |
| PromotionService | Schedule handler | On the JOB-20 run, promotes every APPROVED version whose valid-from date has arrived, supersedes its predecessor, writes the record and publishes `RulePackageInForce` |
| RollbackService | Service | Moves the pointer to the previous version in one call, marks the rolled-back version ROLLED_BACK, refuses a version with no predecessor with MSG-P3-015, writes the record |
| RuleRegistryRepository | Repository | The four tables in `rwb_decision`, the optimistic lock and the four unique keys of the migrations |
| DecisionLogController | Controller | `GET /decision-log` and `GET /decision-log/{entryId}` with the decision-log read, the scope and the hashes |
| DecisionRecordWriter | Service | The local record and its outbox row in the same transaction as the action (DP-03) |
| RegistrySchemaCheck | Schema gate | BR14: fails the build when `payment_match_rule`, or a column of DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273, exists in the migrated `rwb_decision` |
| ParameterClient, ReferenceDataClient | Clients | The two consumed operations of 12.2, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `rule_package`, `rule_package_version`, `rule_row`, `rule_test_case`, `decision_log_entry` and the library objects, all in schema `rwb_decision`; reads no other schema.
- `V2_042_1__epic2_rule_packages.sql` inserts the three `rule_package` rows (DF-REF-274 to DF-REF-278) with owner role RW-COE and hit policy FIRST. It is idempotent on `package_code` and writes no version, rule row or test case.
- `V2_042_2__registry_constraints.sql` adds the unique keys `ux_rule_package_code` (`package_code`), `ux_rule_package_version_label` (`package_id`, `version_label`), `ux_rule_row_version_order` (`package_version_id`, `row_order`) and `ux_rule_test_case_version` (`package_version_id`, `test_case_id`), so a repeated label, a duplicate row order and a duplicate test case are refused by the database as well as by the checks. It adds no column and writes no seed row.
- No migration of `rwb_decision` creates `payment_match_rule` and none adds a column of DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273. There is no DROP of the table here: it never existed in this schema, and the drop of the monolith table is the schema owner's story, not this service's.
- An update of a version uses `WHERE id = ? AND version = ?`; zero rows updated is MSG-GEN-004 and the action is retried, never applied twice.

**Configuration and reference data**

- `rules.testcases.min` = 50 through the parameters contract of DP-06; the three Tests tabs hold 62, 58 and 54 cases, so each check passes with 12, 8 and 4 to spare.
- The three version labels, the row counts, the scenario counts and the valid-from date are the legacy values: "RES-2026.12" with 38 rows and 62 scenarios, "PMT-2026.12" with 3 rows and 58 scenarios and "BKG-2026.12" with 21 rows and 54 scenarios, all valid from 2026-12-15. RWB-E2-027 and its P7 story hold the same PAYMENT_MATCH package under "PM-2026.12" from 2026-12-01; the conflict is GAP-1297, and ASM-2307 pins this key to the legacy label and requires one reconciled version row before SIT.
- LOV-DECISION and the version-state list are read through DP-07 with the version in force; no decision code and no state is a constant in code. The decision code of a governance entry is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1298; ASM-2308).
- The owner role RW-COE and the approver role RW-RISK are rows of the access model; the author and the approver must be distinct user references (BR7). The title of each package is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1302; ASM-2312); the seed writes the package code as the title until RW-COE supplies one.
- The dry-run counts are stored and served, but their breakdown is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1302; ASM-2312); the tests assert presence and stability, not a business number.
- The login phrase is "the rwb-decision login (DP-02)"; the name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1299; ASM-2309).

**Build steps**

1. `RuleRegistryRepository`, the schema baseline and the two migrations; test the four unique keys and the idempotent seed (AC1).
2. `WorkbookParser` and `TestCaseRunner` over the Rows and Tests tabs; tests for the malformed and empty workbook of X1, the default row of X4 and the 49-case variant of AC4.
3. `RuleCheckPipeline` with the six checks; tests for the compile, overlap and unreachable-row refusals of X4 and for the default-row refusal.
4. `PaymentMatchOrderCheck` and `RestructureCatalogCheck` wired into the schema check; tests for AC2's blank `timer_spec` and AC3's wrong order and unknown match type.
5. `DryRunService` and the scenario gate over `rules.testcases.min` read through DP-06; tests for AC4 and for a changed parameter value.
6. `RuleVersionService` with the single transaction and `DecisionRecordWriter`; tests for the load of AC2, AC3 and AC4 and for the fail-closed 503 of X12.
7. `ApprovalService` with the four-eyes rule and the LOADED to APPROVED transition; tests for AC5 and X10.
8. `PromotionService` on the JOB-20 run, with effective dating, the supersede step and the `RulePackageInForce` outbox row; tests for AC6, including a run before the date.
9. `RollbackService` with the one-call rollback, the previous-version pointer and the MSG-P3-015 refusal; tests for AC7.
10. `DecisionLogController` and the two reads; test for AC8 and for the record of every action.
11. `RegistrySchemaCheck` on a Testcontainers database migrated from empty; test for AC9, including a deliberately bad migration that creates the table and one that adds a retired column.
12. The privacy test: the workbooks, the rows, the test cases, the records and the two event payloads hold package codes, version labels, rule IDs, thresholds, dates and payment codes only, and no name, e-mail address, mobile number, national identity number or account number.

**Feature switch.** The legacy flag `rwb.p3.drools` is kept as the legacy reference and is read in the target as a parameter through DP-06. Off: the load, the approve and the rollback operations answer as unavailable, no version reaches IN_FORCE, and the registry and the decision log stay readable so the version already in force keeps running. The exact answer with the switch off is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1302; ASM-2312).

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass; a SIT environment shows the three package rows with owner role RW-COE and hit policy FIRST; "RES-2026.12", "PMT-2026.12" and "BKG-2026.12" LOADED with 62, 58 and 54 passing scenarios; one refusal in full for a wrong match order and for a blank route-set field; the author's approve refused with MSG-P7-002 and RW-RISK's approve recorded; the three versions IN_FORCE from 2026-12-15 with one `RulePackageInForce` event each; one rollback that restores the previous version and leaves earlier decisions on the version they were taken under; and a migrated `rwb_decision` with no `payment_match_rule` table and no column of DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-027 | A workbook check fails, including the match order and the catalog completeness | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. | This story, on the load and the version list |
| MSG-P7-002 | The author of a version calls approve | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. | This story, on the approve |
| MSG-P3-015 | A rollback is called for a version with no predecessor | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1302; ASM-2312) | This story, on the rollback |
| MSG-GEN-001 | An empty workbook, or a missing `validFrom` or required part | Enter {field}. | This story, on the load |
| MSG-GEN-003 | `validFrom` is before the business date | {field} cannot be before {other}. | This story, on the load |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The version label is already loaded, or the version changed at commit | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. | This story, on the load and the update |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record of an action cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on every governance action |
| MSG-P4-002 | The role holds no right for the operation, or the version is outside its scope | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, through the guard of the P4 story |

For MSG-P3-027 the `{check}` value is compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row or scenario; the match order and the catalog completeness are part of the schema check. The `{detail}` names row IDs, cells, rule IDs, package codes, version labels and test-case IDs only, never a case fact or a person. The exact wording of the detail for the two Epic 2 checks is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1300; ASM-2310): this story fixes the naming rule above and confirms the text with the business analyst before SIT. MSG-P3-015 is named by FSD P7 v3 A2.7 AC-EXC-P7-007-05 and its text is not written out in a source this story may read (GAP-1302; ASM-2312). Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen is built in this story. The registry is read through the operations of section 12.1; SCR-39 Rules and parameters (Epic 8) shows the same packages and versions through the gateway-bff composite route of DP-19, and this story feeds the states and the counts that screen consumes. The workbench screens of the load and the approval are the Epic 8 administration story's, and the rights behind them are RWB-P4-E2042-APP's.

| Where | State | What the caller sees |
|---|---|---|
| The package list | Seeded | RESTRUCTURE, PAYMENT_MATCH and BOOKING_MATCH with owner role RW-COE and hit policy FIRST |
| The version list | LOADED | The version, its author, the checksum, the test result and the dry-run counts; not in force |
| The version list | APPROVED | The version and its approver; waiting for its valid-from date |
| The version list | IN_FORCE | The version, its valid-from date and its checksum, and the version it superseded |
| The version list | SUPERSEDED, ROLLED_BACK | The version, the date it stopped being in force and, for a rollback, the reason on the record |
| The version list | REFUSED, or no row | The refusal with MSG-P3-027 and the check that failed; the version in force is unchanged |
| The dry-run read | Counts | The dry-run counts and the per-test-case result of the version |
| The decision-log read | Record | The governance record with its inputs reference, rule ID, rule version, actor, final call, decided time and hashes |
| SCR-39 Rules and parameters (Epic 8) | List and detail | The same packages, versions and states; the screen is built by the Epic 8 story, not here |

##### 16. Test cases

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |

The legacy level System maps to Component and the legacy Schema case to Contract; the registry half of each legacy case is proved here, and the `-ITG` copies of all six cases belong to RWB-ITG-E2042-ITG. ##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the package rows, the labels, the valid-from dates, the row order, the match types, the thresholds, `action_text`, `owner_role`, `timer_spec` and `rules.testcases.min` are rows and parameters; only the check names and the version-state vocabulary are fixed by design.
- No personal data in logs, events, workflow history, tests or prompts: the rows, the test cases and the records hold package codes, version labels, rule IDs, thresholds, dates and synthetic payment codes only.
- No read of another service's tables, and no other service reads `rwb_decision` (DP-01): the parameters and the reference lists arrive on their operations, a case fact never enters the registry, and the dry-run counts carry no case identifier.
- The decision record is written before the action commits; no version exists, no version is approved, promoted or rolled back without its record (BR11).
- One registry, one evaluator: this story governs and stores; the consuming service evaluates through its own embedded Drools kit (DP-04). This story never evaluates a package for a business decision and never caches a KieBase.
- A version is never edited in place: a change is a new version, the workbook and the DRL are stored by reference and checksum, and a rollback moves the pointer.
- The version states are the six of BR10 and the check names are the seven of BR3; no other value is written and none is a constant of the code beyond the state machine.
- `payment_match_rule` is never created and DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 are never referenced by a migration, a test, a query or a document of this service; the schema check fails the build on any attempt.
- The build gate reads a release manifest and a Testcontainers database; it never connects to SIT, UAT or PROD, and the schema check reads only `rwb_decision`.
- No secret in a workbook, a record or the run material: the rwb-decision login (DP-02) and the certificate come from the platform secret store, and the test data is synthetic.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-042 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As an **infrastructure engineer**, I want **the write-once Blob container `rule-packages` with its checksum metadata and private access, the Key Vault secret and certificate that let rwb-case authenticate to rwb-decision and read that container, the compute and memory to hold 20 KieBases per pod, the one-hop network path to rwb-decision and to the schema registry, and the isolated Testcontainers PostgreSQL that the schema gate migrates**, so that **the three Epic 2 workbooks are stored immutably, the fetched model is provably the approved one, and the service can hold and swap rule models without touching a table, a topic or another service's data**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The Epic 2 packages are the only place where a business person changes how this service decides, and the target moves their governance to rwb-decision while keeping the evaluated copy local (Arch v5 slide 27; D-RCV-36 T3 to T6; DP-04). That split needs three pieces of infrastructure that the legacy monolith did not have: an immutable store for the workbook that is the authored artefact, an identity that can read that store and call rwb-decision over mTLS, and enough memory on each pod to keep up to 20 compiled models so that an evaluation never compiles a table (Temporal and Drools slide 16).

Without the immutable store, a workbook can be edited silently and the SHA-256, which is the only proof that a decision came from the approved version, proves nothing. Without the identity and the certificate, the model cannot be fetched at all. Without the memory, the cache of 20 versions either thrashes or the pod is killed under load, and a killed pod during a swap is exactly the case the last-good-model rule exists for.

This story creates no `rwb_*` table, no topic, no queue and no business value. It provisions and configures; the app story builds the cache and the swap, and the operations story owns the consumer group, the readiness signal, the dashboards and the alerts.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The platform Blob account and the platform Key Vault are available with the workload identity mechanism of the platform (RWB-PLT-LIB), so no credential sits in a file, a chart or a repository.
- The rwb-decision service is reachable through the platform service mesh with mTLS, and its front end presents a certificate the platform certificate authority issued (Arch v5 slides 11 and 20).
- The schema registry of RWB-PLT-N008-INF exists, because a service validates a produced payload against its subject before the outbox relay publishes it (DP-09, DP-14).
- The three package codes and the three version labels are agreed: RESTRUCTURE "RES-2026.12", PAYMENT_MATCH "PMT-2026.12" and BOOKING_MATCH "BKG-2026.12", all valid from 2026-12-15 (the valid-from date is the legacy assumption and is copied unchanged).
- The embedded Drools kit contract is available (RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, DP-04): the cache bound of 20 versions, the checksum check and the atomic swap are its elements.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Provision the Blob container `rule-packages` in the platform storage account for each environment, with a write-once (immutability) policy, a private access level and no public endpoint.
2. Set the object layout and the metadata contract: `<PACKAGE_CODE>/<VERSION_LABEL>.xlsx`, with the package code, the version label, the SHA-256 of the workbook and the author role in the object metadata.
3. Create the workload identity of rwb-case, grant it read on that container only, and grant it no list, no write and no delete outside the object read it needs.
4. Provision the Key Vault entries: the rwb-case mTLS client certificate and its secret reference for the rwb-decision front end, and the storage reference the workload identity uses for the container; no literal value reaches a values file, a chart template or a log.
5. Size the pod for the model cache: the heap request and limit that hold 20 KieBases of the three packages plus their working set, recorded as reviewed values and validated by a load test.
6. Open the one-hop network path from the rwb-case pods to rwb-decision and to the schema registry, with no broader egress, and record the allowed destinations as a reviewed list.
7. Provision an isolated PostgreSQL for the build's Testcontainers run of the schema gate: a database that is migrated from empty, holds no SIT, UAT or PROD data, and dies with the pipeline job.
8. Hand the naming, the metadata keys and the identity to RWB-P3-E2042-APP and the destinations and metrics to RWB-P3-E2042-OPS.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A write is attempted on an existing object path | The immutability policy refuses the overwrite; the old object and its checksum stay | None | AC2 |
| X2 | An object is stored without the checksum metadata | The verification step of the swap refuses the model; the object is flagged for the platform administrator | None | AC2 |
| X3 | The container policy allows public access, or the identity holds a broader grant | The provisioning check fails and the environment is not marked ready | None | AC1 |
| X4 | The mTLS certificate is missing, expired or not issued by the platform certificate authority | The call to rwb-decision fails the handshake; the swap is alerted and the model in force stays | None | AC3 |
| X5 | The pod is sized below the memory the cache needs | The load test shows an out-of-memory restart during a swap; the sizing is reviewed and the release is blocked | None | AC4 |
| X6 | A destination outside the one-hop list is called | The network policy drops the call; the attempt is counted and alerted | None | AC5 |
| X7 | A build job points the schema gate at a shared or non-test database | The pipeline refuses to run the gate; no migration touches a shared database | None | AC6 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Provisions storage, identity, certificate, sizing, network and a test database; no application code is built here |
| Negotiable | The retention period, the heap values and the port numbers are environment values settled with the platform team, not story decisions |
| Valuable | Makes the immutable workbook, the checksum-verified fetch and the cached model possible at all, and unblocks the app story on Day 1 |
| Estimable | One container with its policy, one identity and its grants, two Key Vault entries, one sizing decision, one network path set and one test database |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the provisioning checks |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the container policy, a refused overwrite, a handshake, a load test, a dropped call and a gate run |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Infrastructure for the Epic 2 rule packages in rwb-case

  Background:
    Given the platform storage account, Key Vault and service mesh are in force
    Given the three package codes are RESTRUCTURE, PAYMENT_MATCH and BOOKING_MATCH

  Scenario: AC1 The container rule-packages exists with private access and a read-only identity (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the container rule-packages in each environment
    When its access level and the grants of the rwb-case workload identity are inspected
    Then the container has no anonymous or public access
    Then the rwb-case workload identity holds read on that container only
    Then it holds no write, no delete and no list outside the object read it needs
    Then no other service's identity holds a grant on the container
    Then the provisioning check fails the environment when any of the four conditions is not met

  Scenario: AC2 The container is write-once and every object carries its checksum (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given an object stored at RESTRUCTURE/RES-2026.12.xlsx
    When a second write is attempted on the same path
    Then the immutability policy refuses the overwrite and the stored object is unchanged
    Then the object metadata carries the package code, the version label, the SHA-256 of the workbook and the author role
    Then an object without the checksum metadata is flagged and refused by the model verification step
    Then the retention and immutability period is the reviewed value recorded for the environment

  Scenario: AC3 The rwb-case identity and certificate reach rwb-decision over mTLS (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the Key Vault entries of the environment
    When rwb-case calls the rwb-decision front end
    Then the client certificate and its secret are read from Key Vault by the workload identity and never from a file or a chart value
    Then the handshake succeeds only with a certificate the platform certificate authority issued, and fails when it is expired or unissued
    Then no secret, no key and no certificate body appears in a values file, a log, a dashboard or a chart template
    Then the rotation of the certificate is a Key Vault operation with no rebuild of the service

  Scenario: AC4 The compute and memory hold 20 KieBases per pod (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the reviewed heap request and limit of the rwb-case pod
    When a load test caches 20 package versions and evaluates under load
    Then no out-of-memory restart occurs and no eviction touches a version in force
    Then the sizing is recorded as reviewed values per environment and is not hard-coded in a template
    Then the sizing figure itself is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0723; ASM-1270)

  Scenario: AC5 The network path to rwb-decision and the schema registry is one hop (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the network policy of the rwb-case pods
    When the allowed destinations are inspected
    Then rwb-decision and the schema registry are allowed, one hop each, on the reviewed ports
    Then no other destination outside the reviewed list is reachable
    Then a call to an unlisted destination is dropped, counted and alerted
    Then the Blob endpoint of the rule-packages container is allowed and no other storage endpoint is

  Scenario: AC6 The schema gate runs on an isolated Testcontainers PostgreSQL (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the pipeline job that runs PaymentMatchRuleAbsentCheck
    When the gate runs
    Then it migrates a Testcontainers PostgreSQL from empty with the release migrations and then drops it
    Then it reads no SIT, UAT or PROD database and holds no production data
    Then it asserts 93 tables, no table named payment_match_rule and no column of DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273
    Then a job pointed at a shared database is refused before any migration runs
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One container per environment, named `rule-packages`, with no public access and a write-once policy | Arch v5 slide 27 (a version is dated and never edited); DP-04 |
| BR2 | The object path is `<PACKAGE_CODE>/<VERSION_LABEL>.xlsx`, and the object metadata carries the package code, the version label, the SHA-256 and the author role | The authoring contract of RWB-P3-E2042-CON |
| BR3 | The rwb-case workload identity holds read on that container only; no service writes a workbook through the application | DP-02; DP-04 |
| BR4 | Every secret and every certificate comes from Key Vault through the workload identity; none appears in a file, a chart, a log or a dashboard | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR5 | The pod is sized to hold 20 KieBases plus the working set, and the figure is a reviewed value per environment, never a template constant | DP-04; Temporal and Drools slide 16 |
| BR6 | The service reaches rwb-decision and the schema registry one hop, on the reviewed ports, and nothing else outside the reviewed list | DP-11; ADR-020 |
| BR7 | The schema gate runs on a Testcontainers PostgreSQL migrated from empty and never on a shared database | RWB-PLT-E1044-CON; DP-15 |
| BR8 | This story creates no `rwb_*` table, no topic, no queue and no Schedule; storage and identity are the whole deliverable | Template and Rules §R7.2 s12 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not provisioned | Container created | The immutability policy, the private access level and the identity grant are in place | Provisioned |
| Provisioned | First workbook stored | The object carries the four metadata keys and the checksum matches the loaded version | Active |
| Active | New version stored | A new object under the same package code with a new version label | Active (two objects) |
| Active | Overwrite attempted | The path already exists | Unchanged; the write is refused |
| Active | Certificate rotated | The Key Vault entry is updated and the workload identity reloads it | Active (new certificate) |
| Active | A policy check fails after a platform change | The private access level or the grant drifts | Degraded; the environment is not marked ready |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. This story exposes no API, no cache read and no operator endpoint. The readiness and liveness endpoints are cluster-internal and are owned by RWB-P3-E2042-OPS.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None as a business operation. The network path to rwb-decision and to the schema registry is a platform route configured here; the operations that run on it are consumed by RWB-P3-E2042-APP and declared in RWB-P3-E2042-CON. This story adds no call of its own.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The story provisions no topic and publishes no event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. The RulePackageInForce consumer group is RWB-P3-E2042-OPS; this story only ensures the network path and no message is read here.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None. No Temporal workflow, activity or task queue is created by this story; the model swap workflow belongs to RWB-P3-E2042-APP.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The 00:01 promotion is JOB-20 in rwb-decision and this story registers no Schedule.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. This story creates no `rwb_*` table, no column and no index; the storage is a Blob container and the secrets are Key Vault entries, neither of which is an ACE DB table.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. The fakes run in the pipeline and in SIT and belong to RWB-P3-E2042-CON and RWB-P3-E2042-OPS; no fake is deployed or configured here.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | None | No operation is provided or consumed by this story; the routes it opens carry the app story's calls |
| Kafka | None | No topic, no producer, no consumer |
| Temporal | None | No workflow, activity or task queue |
| File | 1 storage path | The write-once container `rule-packages` with its three object paths and their metadata |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `infra/storage/rule-packages.json` (the container, its immutability policy, its access level and the object metadata rules), `infra/identity/rwb-case-workload.json` (the identity and its read grant), `infra/keyvault/entries.md` (the certificate and the storage reference), `infra/network/egress.yaml` (the one-hop allow list), `infra/sizing/rule-cache.yaml` (the heap values per environment) and `infra/testcontainers/schema-gate.yaml` (the isolated gate database).

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-04 is the pattern this story serves: the local evaluated copy needs an immutable source, an identity to fetch it and memory to hold it. DP-15 is served by the isolated gate database, which migrates the service's own schema and nothing else. No other pattern adds work here; the table, topic, queue and Schedule rows of the other stories are untouched.

**Build steps**

1. Create the container with the immutability policy, the private access level and no public endpoint; add the provisioning check that verifies all three (AC1, AC2, X3).
2. Define the object layout and the four metadata keys; store the three workbooks as the first objects and verify each checksum (AC2).
3. Create the workload identity and the read grant on the container only; verify that write, delete and list are refused (AC1, X1).
4. Create the Key Vault certificate and secret reference for the rwb-decision front end; test the handshake with a valid, an expired and an unissued certificate (AC3, X4).
5. Size the pod: run the load test that caches 20 versions and evaluates under load, and record the heap values per environment (AC4, X5).
6. Write the one-hop egress list and the drop rule; test a call to an unlisted destination (AC5, X6).
7. Provision the Testcontainers PostgreSQL for the gate, isolate it from every shared database, and run `PaymentMatchRuleAbsentCheck` once against it (AC6, X7).
8. Hand the container name, the metadata keys and the identity reference to the app story, and the allowed destinations and the sizing to the operations story.

**Done when.** The container is private and write-once in all three environments, a second write to an existing path is refused, every object carries its checksum, the mTLS handshake succeeds with the issued certificate only, the load test caches 20 versions without an out-of-memory restart, the egress list is one hop, and the gate runs on a private test database.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| None | A policy, identity or certificate check fails | No business message is produced. The provisioning check fails the environment with the resource name and the violated rule, and the platform administrator acts on it. |

This story adds no message ID. The business messages of the capability keep their identifiers and texts from the legacy story and from the message catalogue: MSG-P3-027 (a rule version refused or no version in force), MSG-P7-002 (the author cannot approve), MSG-GEN-001, MSG-GEN-003 and MSG-GEN-004 (workbook and date checks) and MSG-P4-002 (a role without the right). The infrastructure reports a condition to the operator, never to a workbench user.

##### 15. Screens and states

None. There is no screen in this story. The operator-facing surfaces are the environment's provisioning check, the container policy view and the load-test report; the model-cache readiness signal and the dashboards are RWB-P3-E2042-OPS.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a policy or a values file: rows, tolerances, windows, action text, owner roles and timers stay in the workbooks and the registry.
- No personal data in the container, in an object path, in an object metadata key or in a log: the container holds workbooks and identifiers only.
- One container, one identity, one read grant; no service writes a workbook through the application and no identity outside rwb-case holds a grant (DP-02).
- No secret, key or certificate body in a file, a chart value, a dashboard or a log; everything comes from Key Vault through the workload identity.
- The service reaches rwb-decision, the schema registry and its own storage endpoint and nothing else (DP-11).
- The immutability period is never shortened without the audit owner's approval, and an overwrite is never allowed as a convenience.
- The gate database is a private test database migrated from empty; no SIT, UAT or PROD data is read or copied into it.
- No `rwb_*` table, topic, queue or Schedule is created here; a change that needs one belongs to its own story.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-042 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **rwb-case deployed with Helm values for the model cache bound and the model warm-up, a RulePackageInForce consumer group on `rwb.decision.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics, a readiness signal that reports whether the model in force is loaded, four dashboards and three alerts on the package state and the evaluation latency, a runbook whose rollback is one call in rwb-decision followed by the swap back in this service, and a pipeline step that runs `RuleScenarioBuildGate` and `PaymentMatchRuleAbsentCheck` on every build**, so that **an operator can see which package version is deciding, catch a cold cache or a checksum mismatch before a case is affected, and return to the previous version without a release**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A rule package is data, so the only thing that can go wrong at run time is the state of the copy this service holds: it can be cold, it can be a version behind, it can fail its checksum, or no version can be in force at all — and each of those looks from the outside like "the service is up". The legacy story relied on a build gate and a manual check of the version list; the target adds an event that announces a new version and a local cache that must be warm for the service to decide (Arch v5 slide 27; Temporal and Drools slides 15, 16 and 28).

Deployment is therefore part of the capability. The cache bound and the warm-up must be values, not constants, because the same image runs in three environments. The consumer group needs a retry path and a `.dlt`, because a lost RulePackageInForce is a service that silently decides on yesterday's rules. Readiness must tell an operator whether the model in force is loaded, and the dashboards must show the version in force per package, the load failures, the checksum mismatches, the `NoPackageInForce` count and the evaluation latency against the 300 ms target. Only then can the on-call rota act before a decision is taken on the wrong table.

The 00:01 promotion Schedule is rwb-decision's: this story consumes its event and never registers, retimes or duplicates it.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB).
- The Temporal workflow kit and the `rwb-recovery` namespace are available (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), because the model swap is an event-started workflow on task queue `rwb-case` (DP-10).
- The Kafka event platform provisions topics with a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic and applies topic ACLs (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON).
- The container `rule-packages`, the workload identity and the rwb-decision certificate exist (RWB-P3-E2042-INF).
- The rwb-decision service publishes `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` on `rwb.decision.events.v1` (EV-30) and owns the 00:01 promotion (JOB-20; Arch v5 slide 44).
- The three package codes and version labels are agreed: RESTRUCTURE "RES-2026.12", PAYMENT_MATCH "PMT-2026.12", BOOKING_MATCH "BKG-2026.12".
- The platform error envelope and the message catalogue are in force, so an alert can carry a message ID where a message exists.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds the service image, runs the unit, component and contract tests, and runs the two rule gates before it publishes the chart.
2. `RuleScenarioBuildGate` runs the 174 scenarios of the three in-force versions from the release manifest; `PaymentMatchRuleAbsentCheck` runs on a Testcontainers database and asserts 93 tables, no `payment_match_rule` and no column of DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273.
3. The chart deploys the service with its own login, its migration job, its probes and the three rule-package values: the cache bound of 20, the warm-up list and the warm-up timeout.
4. The warm-up step asks the version list once at start-up and fetches the model in force of each package in the warm-up list, so the first case of the morning does not pay the fetch.
5. The provisioning step creates the consumer group of rwb-case on `rwb.decision.events.v1` with the retry topic and the `.dlt` topic, and registers task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`.
6. The readiness signal reports the schema version, the worker polling state and the model state of each package in the warm-up list.
7. The dashboards are published: version in force per package, model load failures, checksum mismatches, `NoPackageInForce` count and evaluation latency against the 300 ms target.
8. The three alerts are wired to the runbook entries: cache cold, checksum mismatch and package not in force.
9. A smoke step asserts in a test namespace that a synthetic RulePackageInForce event swaps the model and that readiness and the dashboards reflect it.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The model in force is not loaded when the pod starts | Readiness reports the package as not warmed; the alert "cache cold" fires after the warm-up window | None | AC3, AC5 |
| X2 | A RulePackageInForce event fails the swap | The activity retries on the kit policy; after the last attempt the event goes to the retry topic and then to `.dlt` with an alert, and the model in force stays | None | AC2, AC5 |
| X3 | A fetched model fails its checksum | No swap; the mismatch is counted with the package code and both checksums, and the "checksum mismatch" alert fires | None | AC4, AC5 |
| X4 | No version is in force for a package | `NoPackageInForce` is counted per package and the "package not in force" alert fires once per package per window; the message text is MSG-P3-027 | MSG-P3-027 | AC4, AC5 |
| X5 | The build gate fails on a scenario or on a table | The pipeline stops before the chart is published; nothing is deployed | None | AC6 |
| X6 | The 00:01 promotion does not run in rwb-decision | No event arrives; the version in force on the dashboard does not change and the "package not in force" path is the visible symptom, owned with rwb-decision | MSG-P3-027 | AC2, AC5 |
| X7 | A rollback is called in rwb-decision | rwb-decision announces the earlier version and the consumer swaps back to it; no release of this service is needed | None | AC5 |
| X8 | The evaluation latency exceeds the 300 ms target | The latency panel shows the breach and the package code; the card is reviewed with the rule owner, and nothing is restarted | None | AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the platform topic provisioning, the workflow kit and the two gates; no application code is built here |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, the warm-up list, the alert windows and the resource sizes are environment values, not story decisions |
| Valuable | Makes the package state, the swap and the evaluation latency visible and operable, and makes a rollback a call rather than a release |
| Estimable | One chart with three values, one warm-up step, one consumer group with retry and `.dlt`, four dashboards panels, three alerts, four runbook entries and one pipeline step |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: a rendered chart, a provisioned group, a readiness answer, a synthetic metric and a gate result |

```gherkin

  Background:

  Scenario: AC1 The chart carries the cache bound and the warm-up as values (new, D-RCV-60)

    Then neither probe writes to a database and no probe calls rwb-decision on every check

  Scenario: AC4 Four dashboard panels report the package state and the latency (new, D-RCV-60)

  Scenario: AC5 Three alerts and four runbook entries cover the package state (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published alerts and the runbook
    When a synthetic state is replayed for a cold cache, a checksum mismatch and a package not in force
    Then each condition raises its alert with the package code and the version label
    Then the package-not-in-force alert carries the message text of MSG-P3-027 and links the runbook entry of its owner role
    Then the rollback runbook entry is one call in rwb-decision, followed by the swap back in this service, with no release
    Then the cache-purge entry empties the model cache and warms the versions in force again
    Then every alert links exactly one runbook entry with the check, the owner role and the recovery step

  Scenario: AC6 The pipeline runs the two rule gates on every build (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a commit on the main line
    When the pipeline runs
    Then it runs RuleScenarioBuildGate over the three versions in the release manifest and fails on a failing scenario
    Then it runs PaymentMatchRuleAbsentCheck on a Testcontainers database and fails when payment_match_rule or any column of DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 exists
    Then it promotes the same image and chart artefact through DEV, SIT and UAT without a rebuild
    Then a red gate blocks the merge and the promotion
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The cache bound, the warm-up list and the warm-up timeout are values per environment; no template or code constant carries them | DP-04; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR2 | Every topic has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and a consumer never acknowledges an event it could not process | DP-09; Arch v5 slide 22 notes |
| BR3 | The model swap is an event-started workflow on task queue `rwb-case`; the 00:01 promotion Schedule belongs to rwb-decision and is not registered here | DP-10; Arch v5 slide 44 |
| BR4 | Readiness answers healthy only when the schema is at the expected version, the worker polls and the model in force of the warm-up list is loaded; a package with no version in force is a degraded signal, not a failed pod | Arch v5 slide 27; Temporal and Drools slide 28 |
| BR5 | Every alert carries the package code and the version label, and links one runbook entry with the owner role; where a message exists its text is the agreed text | Template and Rules §R7.2 s14 |
| BR6 | A rollback is one call in rwb-decision; this service swaps back on the event and is never redeployed to change a rule | Arch v5 slide 27; Temporal and Drools slide 15 |
| BR7 | The two rule gates run in every build and a red gate blocks the merge and the promotion | REQ-CWC-014; D-RCV-36 T4, T10 |
| BR8 | Nothing on a dashboard, an alert or a runbook carries a case fact or a personal datum | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR9 | No secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or a runbook; all come from the platform secret store | RWB-P3-E2042-INF |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart, the two rule gates and the migration job pass | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration complete and probes healthy | The schema is at the expected version and both probes answer | Ready |
| Ready | Warm-up complete | The model in force of each package in the warm-up list is cached | Warm |
| Warm | RulePackageInForce arrives | The checksum verifies and the swap succeeds | Warm (new version) |
| Warm | Checksum mismatch or swap failure | The last good model stays and the alert fires | Warm (unchanged; alerting) |
| Warm | Rollback called in rwb-decision | The earlier version is announced and swapped back | Warm (earlier version) |
| Warm | Release superseded | A new chart version is promoted | Rolling |
| Rolling | All pods on the new version | The old ReplicaSet drains and each pod is Warm | Warm |
| Any | The gate is red | A scenario fails or the schema assertion fails | Failed; nothing is published |

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None provided by this story. The deployment exposes the case read operations of the service through gateway-bff, and they are declared in their own contract story. The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` | P7 rwb-decision | The warm-up resolves the version in force per package |

None. This story publishes no event; the model swap records nothing on a topic.

| EvaluateRules, RecordAndApply | Activities (workflow kit) | `rwb-case` | Registered by the same worker |

None. The 00:01 promotion is the Temporal Schedule JOB-20 in rwb-decision and is out of scope; this release registers no Schedule for a rule package (Arch v5 slide 44).

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-case/` | Chart with deployment, service, migration job, config map, secret references, probes and the warm-up hook |
| `helm/rwb-case/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, feature switches, the model cache bound, the warm-up list, the warm-up timeout |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit, component and contract tests, the two rule gates, image and dependency scan, chart publish, promote the same artefact |
| Provisioning step | Consumer group of rwb-case on `rwb.decision.events.v1` with the retry topic and the `.dlt` topic; task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery` |
| Warm-up hook | One version list read and one model fetch per package in the warm-up list, with the timeout from the values |
| Dashboards | Four panels: version in force, load failures and checksum mismatches, NoPackageInForce count, evaluation latency against 300 ms |
| Alerts | Three rules, each with the package code, the version label and one runbook entry |
| Runbook | Four entries: cache cold and warm-up, checksum mismatch, package not in force with the rollback call, cache purge |

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only when the migration is at the expected schema version, the outbox relay is running, the Temporal worker has polled, and the model in force of each package in the warm-up list is cached. A package with no version in force is reported as a degraded dependency with its `NoPackageInForce` count and does not fail the pod. Liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database, and neither calls rwb-decision on every check; the warm-up is a start-up step and the refresh is the event.

**Alert mapping.**

| Condition | Alert | Payload | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| The model in force is not cached after the warm-up window | Cache cold, with the package code and the version label | Package code, version label, warm-up duration | Platform on-call, ticket |
| A fetched model fails its SHA-256 check | Checksum mismatch, with the package code, the version label and both checksums | Package code, version label, expected and computed checksum | Platform on-call and the rwb-decision owner, page |
| No version is in force for a package | Package not in force, with the package code and the text of MSG-P3-027 | Package code, first and last occurrence in the window | Business on-call (RW-COE), page |
| Evaluation latency above 300 ms | Latency breach on the latency panel and the dashboard card | Package code, version label, p95 and p99 | Dashboard, no page |

**Rollback runbook.** The rollback is one call in rwb-decision (`POST /admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/rollback`, owned there). rwb-decision announces the earlier version in force, and the consumer of this service swaps back on that event; no release of rwb-case is needed and no cache is edited by hand. The cache-purge entry exists only for the case where an operator must rebuild the cache from scratch: it empties the model cache, the warm-up runs again, and the versions in force are fetched and verified before readiness reports Warm.

**Done when.** The chart renders in all three environments with the cache bound and the warm-up as values, the consumer group and its retry and `.dlt` topics are verified by a test, readiness reports the version loaded per package, the four panels and the three alerts fire on synthetic metrics, the rollback and cache-purge entries are rehearsed by the on-call rota, and the two gates run in the pipeline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-027 | No version is in force for a package | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P7-002 | The approver is the author | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The version label is already loaded | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-GEN-001 | An empty workbook | Enter {field}. |
| MSG-GEN-003 | Valid from before today | {field} cannot be before {other}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A role without Rules and parameters calls a package operation | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The texts are copied unchanged from the legacy story and the message catalogue; the deployment adds the alert routing and the runbook link, never a new wording. The checksum mismatch and the cache-cold condition carry the package code, the version label and the two checksums or the warm-up duration to the alert, and produce no business message.

##### 15. Screens and states

The operator-facing surfaces of this story are the pipeline run view, the release view, the dashboard and the runbook. The version list a person reads to see the states LOADED, APPROVED, IN_FORCE, SUPERSEDED and REFUSED is rwb-decision's, shown by SCR-39 Rules and parameters in Epic 8; this story only carries the version in force per package onto its own dashboard. The deployment serves no new screen.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: rows, tolerances, windows, action text, owner roles and timers stay in the workbooks and the registry; the cache bound and the warm-up are configuration, not rule content.
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads or the runbook: package codes, version labels, checksums, counts and durations only.
- One topic and one consumer group per service; the 00:01 promotion Schedule is never registered, retimed or duplicated in this release (DP-10, DP-14).
- The service writes only schema rwb_case and reads no registry table; the packages come over the rwb-decision operations (DP-01, DP-04).
- Every topic has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and the consumer dedupes through the inbox (DP-09).
- The release pins the image digest and the chart version; a rebuild between environments is not allowed, and no rule version is ever shipped in the image.
- No secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; all come from the platform secret store.
- A red gate blocks the merge and the promotion; `PaymentMatchRuleAbsentCheck` is never waived for a release.

##### 1. Story

As a **member of the integration and QA team**, I want **a repeatable cross-service journey harness that loads the three Epic 2 packages, approves each version as a second user, promotes them at 00:01 and then reads what each owning service decided from the version in force**, so that **the wave 2 rule package journey is proven end to end, with evidence, before the release is accepted**.

This story builds the harness and the evidence only. It builds no production operation, table, workflow, schedule or screen, it serves no operation and it owns no table. The real behaviour is owned by the four I stories: RWB-P7-E2042-APP (the three package rows, the load, approve, dry-run and registry reads, the rule rows and the 00:01 promotion in rwb-decision), RWB-P3-E2042-APP (`rules.testcases.min` and the match-type and route-set reference rows), RWB-P6-E2042-APP (the notice path, which the harness asserts stays silent) and RWB-P4-E2042-APP (the Rules and parameters right answered on every call), and those four stories block the ITG run.

The packages themselves are evaluated locally by the one service that owns each model, from the version in force, inside an activity (DP-04, ADR-017). The harness asserts the decision records those services wrote; it never evaluates a package, never recomputes a match and holds no copy of a rule row.

##### 2. Business rationale

In v5 governance is central in P7 rwb-decision: the workbook is authored in the Drools template, compiled and checked against at least 50 scenarios, approved four-eyes, dated, and every version is audited. Evaluation is local: each model has exactly one owning service, which loads the approved version, verifies its checksum, swaps it in atomically and keeps the last good model, all inside an activity and under 300 ms. There is no shared rule server on the hot path, so a rule change is data rather than code, it is dated, and the version is stamped on every answer.

The legacy RWB-E2-042 left Epic 2 rules in three places: reference rule rows, the `payment_match_rule` table and the BookingMatchRules class. The harness proves the loop that replaced them: a load and a four-eyes approval in rwb-decision, a promotion at 00:01 with `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1`, a local swap in each owning service, a decision record naming the rule ID and the rule version, the first-match order of PAYMENT_MATCH proven from the records rather than recomputed, and no customer-facing notice raised by any of it. That is the outcome REQ-CWC-013 and REQ-CWC-014 describe, shown at the integration level rather than per service.

A run gives one evidence report per business date that proves the 50-scenario gate holds for all three packages, that the three package codes and their row counts are the ones in force, that R-RES-04 carries the three fields the route service reads, that the row order decides the two payments the same way the ledger says, and that every refusal writes nothing.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The four I stories are published and deployed in the SIT environment: RWB-P7-E2042-APP (the package rows, the load and approve paths, the registry and decision log reads and the promotion), RWB-P3-E2042-APP (`rules.testcases.min` and the reference rows), RWB-P6-E2042-APP (notices and their events) and RWB-P4-E2042-APP (the Rules and parameters right on the authorise operation).
- The contract fakes of §12.8 are published from the owning services' OpenAPI documents, so the harness runs green from Day 1 before the I stories land.
- The three package codes RESTRUCTURE, PAYMENT_MATCH and BOOKING_MATCH are seeded with owner role RW-COE, and the three versions are "RES-2026.12" with 38 rows and 62 scenarios, "PMT-2026.12" with 3 rows and 58 scenarios and "BKG-2026.12" with 21 rows and 54 scenarios, all valid from 2026-12-15.
- The business date is 2026-12-10; the loader is "U-41" (RW-COE) and the approver is "U-51" (RW-RISK), and they are separate users; `rules.testcases.min` is 50.
- Rule R-RES-26 carries the match types EXACT, WINDOW and PARTIAL; payment "PAY-91008" of 12,500.00 THB is matched by both EXACT and WINDOW and is decided by EXACT, and payment "PAY-91002" of 11,875.00 THB is decided by PARTIAL with a shortfall of 625.00 THB. Rule R-RES-04 carries action text "Assign the case to a restructuring officer and start the offer clock", owner role "RW-RESTRUCT" and timer "2 working days", and case "RW-2026-000777" is open.
- The production switch `rwb.p3.drools` is on in the harness environment; with it off the three package endpoints and the row reads answer 404 or NoPackageInForce and nothing else changes.
- The harness repository, the SIT environment, the seeding set for the three versions and the two payment cases, the evidence format and retention, the pass or fail gate and the exact response values of the §12.8 fakes: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0421; ASM-0596).

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: seeds the three package versions with the two users and their roles through the owning contracts or the published fakes, and reads each version back to assert status LOADED, the row count 38, 3 and 21 and the scenario count 62, 58 and 54.
2. Harness: loads each version through POST `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` as "U-41" with valid from 2026-12-15, and asserts 201, status LOADED, the checksum and the test result "62 of 62", "58 of 58" and "54 of 54 scenarios passed".
3. Harness: asserts the compile, schema, overlap, unreachable row, default row, scenario and dry run checks pass on each version, that the dry run covers the open cases and the payments of the business date, and that each version carries at least `rules.testcases.min` scenarios, read through GET `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters`.
4. Harness: reads GET `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages` and asserts exactly the three package codes with owner role RW-COE and no fourth Epic 2 package, then GET `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` and asserts 38 rows under "RES-2026.12" including R-RES-25, R-RES-27, R-RES-29, R-RES-30, R-RES-31 and R-LIT-02, the rows EXACT, WINDOW and PARTIAL under "PMT-2026.12" and 21 rows under "BKG-2026.12".
5. Harness: approves each version as "U-51" on 2026-12-14 through POST `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/approve`, asserts status APPROVED with author "U-41" and approver "U-51", and asserts that the same call as "U-41" is refused with MSG-P7-002.
6. Harness: promotes each approved version at 00:01 on 2026-12-15 through the `rulePackagePromote` Schedule in rwb-decision, and asserts status IN_FORCE with the earlier version SUPERSEDED and exactly one `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` per package on `rwb.decision.events.v1`, naming the package, the version and its checksum.
7. Harness: asserts the version in force in each owning service is the promoted version and the row counts are 38, 3 and 21 through the registry contract, then asserts the priority order EXACT then WINDOW then PARTIAL and the two payment outcomes from the decision records read through GET `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log`, with rule "R-RES-26" and rule version "PMT-2026.12" on each record; it never recomputes a match.
8. Harness: asserts R-RES-04 as the row the route service reads, with action text "Assign the case to a restructuring officer and start the offer clock", owner role "RW-RESTRUCT" and timer "2 working days", and that every route-set row of the version carries the three fields, read through the registry contract and the route-set reference rows of GET `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}`.
9. Harness: asserts that every call is one hop on `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with the 2 s budget and a breaker per downstream, that the Rules and parameters right is answered by POST `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` on every call, that no service reads another service's schema, and that the deploy-time check rwb-decision publishes for its own schema reports no `payment_match_rule` table and no column of DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273.
10. Harness: asserts that no `rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1` and no `rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1` appears on `rwb.comms.events.v1` during the load, the approval and the promotion, so a rule change raises no customer-facing notice.
11. Harness: forces each refusal and failure of §5 through the fakes, asserts the message and that nothing was written, then returns the fake to its healthy answer.
12. Harness: writes one evidence report per business date, keyed by story and business date, with the trace of every call; the report format and retention are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0421; ASM-0596).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What the harness asserts | Message | ITG test case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A compile or schema check fails: a PAYMENT_MATCH row carries match type "FUZZY" | The load is refused with 422, the row and the cell are named, and no version row and no rule row is written | MSG-P3-027 | TC-E2-042-02-ITG |
| X2 | A RESTRUCTURE version carries 49 scenarios, below `rules.testcases.min` = 50 | The load is refused with 422, the scenario check and the shortfall are named, and status stays absent | MSG-P3-027 | TC-E2-042-01-ITG |
| X3 | The PAYMENT_MATCH row order puts PARTIAL before WINDOW | The load is refused at the schema check with 422, the priority cells are named, and nothing is written | MSG-P3-027 | TC-E2-042-04-ITG |
| X4 | A RESTRUCTURE route-set row has an empty action text, owner role or timer | The load is refused with 422 and the row and column are named | MSG-P3-027 | TC-E2-042-05-ITG |
| X5 | "U-41" approves a version they loaded | The approval is refused and the version stays LOADED; no approver and no approved time is written | MSG-P7-002 | TC-E2-042-01-ITG |
| X6 | The same version label is loaded twice, or an empty workbook is loaded | 409 for the duplicate label and 422 for the empty workbook; the version in force is unchanged | MSG-GEN-004; MSG-GEN-001 | TC-E2-042-01-ITG |
| X7 | The valid from date is before the business date (2026-12-09 with the run on 2026-12-10) | 422 and no version row; the version label is not consumed | MSG-GEN-003 | TC-E2-042-02-ITG |
| X8 | A role with no Rules and parameters right calls a package path, or the decision log does not answer | 403 on the direct call with the refusal and not an empty list; 503 on the read with no record written and no record invented | MSG-P4-002; None (503 refusal text) | TC-E2-042-06-ITG |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Runs on its own once the four I stories are deployed; until then it runs against the §12.8 fakes |
| Negotiable | The harness pack, the seeding, the evidence format and the gate are agreed with QA; no business value is fixed by the harness |
| Valuable | The author, test, four-eyes, promotion, local swap and decision-record loop is evidenced across services rather than per service |
| Estimable | One harness project, one journey specification, one fake pack and one evidence report per business date |
| Small | Fits in one iteration with the owning stories' contract tests |
| Testable | Each scenario of §7 is one automated journey with synthetic data and a machine-checkable result |

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Each Epic 2 package is authored in the Drools XLS template and loaded only through rwb-decision; no direct SQL and no second load path | D-RCV-36 T3, T4 |
| BR2 | Each package version carries at least `rules.testcases.min` (50) scenarios, and every scenario passes before approval | REQ-CWC-014; D-RCV-36 T4 |
| BR3 | PAYMENT_MATCH has one row per match type, and the row order is EXACT then WINDOW then PARTIAL | R-RES-26; D-RCV-36 T10 |
| BR4 | RESTRUCTURE route-set rows carry action text, owner role and timer, and the route service reads them only from the catalog | D-RCV-36 T6; FEAT-CWC-28 |
| BR5 | `payment_match_rule` is never created and DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 are never referenced; no code, rule row or test reads or writes them | D-RCV-36 T10 |
| BR6 | The package code is the RuleSet and the version labels are RES-, PMT- and BKG-yyyy.MM | D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR7 | First match wins, exactly one row decides, and the default row is last | D-RCV-36 T5 |
| BR8 | Open cases keep the package version they were decided under | R-UNI-38 |
| BR9 | The build gate runs every in-force package's scenarios in every build | REQ-CWC-014; D-RCV-36 T4 |

The harness asserts these nine rules against the owning services and re-implements none of them, so no BR row is changed by this story.

##### 9. State transitions

None. The harness sets no package version state and changes no case status; it calls the owning service and reads the result. The table is what it observes on a package version, and it reads the state, it never sets it.

| Observed state | What it means in the run | Where the harness reads it |
|---|---|---|
| LOADED | The workbook compiled, the checks passed and at least 50 scenarios passed, so the version is stored but not approved | The load answer and the version list of rwb-decision |
| APPROVED | A second user approved the version; the author "U-41" never approves | The approve answer and the version list of rwb-decision |
| IN_FORCE | The 00:01 promotion reached the valid from date, the previous version became SUPERSEDED and the owning service swapped the version in | The version list, `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1` and the decision records of the date |
| SUPERSEDED | An earlier version was replaced by the promoted one and stays readable for the cases decided under it | The version list of rwb-decision |
| REFUSED | A load or an approval was refused, and no version row, rule row or test case was written | The refusal answer and the version list before and after it |

A refused load or approval leaves every row exactly as it was before the call, and a version in force changes only through the promotion the owning service starts and announces.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | The synthetic user the harness drives to load a version (Rules and parameters CRUD) |
| RW-RISK, risk and model risk officer | Approves each package version (Rules and parameters A); the harness asserts that the approver is not the author |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the versions, the rows, the scenarios and the dry run counts (Rules and parameters R); changes nothing |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Reads the same answers (Rules and parameters R); used by the access case only |
| RW-CASEOWN, case owner | Holds no Rules and parameters right; the access case proves the refusal with MSG-P4-002 |
| SY-RULES, Drools evaluator | Evaluates the version in force inside the owning service and writes the rule ID and version to the decision record; the harness asserts its result, it does not act for it |

No delegation of authority level applies: a package version is not a credit decision. Authorisation is answered by rwb-access through the authorise operation of §12.2.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness calls the owning services; it serves no operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

One hop per call, no chaining; the 2 s timeout and the circuit breaker per downstream of Architecture v5 slide 11 apply to every row.

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` | P7 rwb-decision | The load of each of the three versions with its workbook and valid from 2026-12-15 (Architecture v5 slide 27: author and test) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages/{packageCode}/versions` | P7 rwb-decision | The version in force, its status, its row count and the rule rows that R-RES-04, R-RES-26 and the route-set rows are asserted from |
| POST | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/approve` | P7 rwb-decision | The four-eyes approval by "U-51" and the refusal when the author approves (Architecture v5 slide 27: four-eyes sign-off) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-package-versions/{versionId}/dry-run` | P7 rwb-decision | The dry run counts over the cases and payments of the business date, before approval |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/rule-packages` | P7 rwb-decision | The three package codes with owner role RW-COE, and the absence of a fourth Epic 2 package |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | P7 rwb-decision | The decision records the rule ID, the rule version and the two payment outcomes are asserted from (Architecture v5 slide 14: central decision ledger) |
