| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case | The match types EXACT, WINDOW and PARTIAL and the route-set reference rows (DP-07) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/{productCode}/records` | P1 rwb-source-data | The case facts and the two payments the dry run and the decisions cover (DP-05) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The Rules and parameters right checked on every call (Architecture v5 slide 14: rwb-access IN POST /authorise) |

The composite screen route is gateway-bff (DP-19), owned by the platform edge story RWB-PLT-N001-CON. Its path and merge order, and any gateway call this run makes, are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0421; ASM-0596).

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness produces no event.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | What the harness asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1 | rwb.decision.events.v1 | P7 rwb-decision | One event per package at 00:01 on 2026-12-15, naming the package, the version and its checksum, and each owning service holds the new version only after it |
| rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1 | rwb.decision-record.v1 | P7 rwb-decision (ledger); every service publishes its own record | Every payment and route decision of the business date reaches the ledger with its rule ID and rule version, and the decision log count matches |
| rwb.comms.NoticeGenerated.v1 | rwb.comms.events.v1 | P6 rwb-comms | Asserted absent: no notice is generated by a load, an approval or a promotion |
| rwb.comms.NoticeDispatched.v1 | rwb.comms.events.v1 | P6 rwb-comms | Asserted absent: no notice reaches a delivery channel for a rule change |

The events are consumed for assertion only; the harness reads the ledger through the P7 contract rather than from a topic.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None added. The harness starts no workflow and adds no activity; it drives REST only. The `rulePackagePromote` Schedule and the promotion it starts in rwb-decision, and the build gate that runs every in-force package's scenarios, are owned and started by the owning services; the harness observes their result.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None added. The harness run is started by the test pipeline, not by a Temporal Schedule and not by Airflow. The 00:01 promotion Schedule `rulePackagePromote` (JOB-20, queue rwb-decision) is exercised as an observer of the run: the harness waits for its window and asserts `rwb.decision.RulePackageInForce.v1`.

None.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_<name>`; never read another service's tables | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit; rule packages from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON; C RWB-P7-E1073-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | `rwb.<short>.events.v1`; naming library | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The platform H dependencies named by this table are delivered by the platform wave and are not repeated in the metadata H list. The blocking dependencies of this story are the four I stories.

The legacy P3 module that held the rule packages, the loader and the effective-date job splits in two: governance (authoring, tests, four-eyes approval, effective dating and the version audit) moves to P7 rwb-decision, and evaluation moves into the one service that owns each model, as an embedded Drools kit inside an activity (DP-04, ADR-017). The Quartz effective-date job becomes the 00:01 Temporal Schedule `rulePackagePromote` in rwb-decision (DP-10). The single recovery schema becomes the per-service `rwb_<name>` schemas with their own Flyway sequences (DP-01, DP-15), the `rwb.p3.` topic names become `rwb.<short>.events.v1` (DP-14), `rules.testcases.min` and the reference rows are read through rwb-case (DP-06, DP-07), the payment and case facts through rwb-source-data (DP-05), the monolith base becomes `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` (DP-13) and the screen answer is composed by the gateway-bff route (DP-19).

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Test harness | Runs one journey per business date, keyed by story and business date, and stops at the first failed assertion with the trace |
| PackageClient | Harness adapter | Calls the ten consumed operations of §12.2 for the load, the approval, the dry run, the package and version reads, the registry read, the decision log and the authorise call |
| FakePack | WireMock project | Serves rwb-decision, rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-access and rwb-comms from the published OpenAPI documents of §12.8 |
| ScenarioGateCheck | Assertion | Fails the run when a version carries fewer than 50 scenarios, when a scenario fails, or when the three package codes and the row counts 38, 3 and 21 are not the ones in force |
| FourEyesCheck | Assertion | Fails the run when the approver equals the author, or when a refused approval writes an approver or an approved time |
| DecisionRecordReconciler | Assertion | Compares every decision record of the date with the rule ID and the rule version it must name, and the two payment outcomes with the ledger, and fails the run on any difference; it recomputes nothing |
| SchemaBoundaryCheck | Assertion | Fails the run on any cross-schema reference in the trace, and asserts the deploy-time schema check rwb-decision publishes for its own schema, without reading a catalogue of another service |
| NoticeSilenceCheck | Assertion | Fails the run when a `NoticeGenerated` or `NoticeDispatched` event appears for a load, an approval or a promotion |
| RunReportWriter | Reporter | Writes one evidence report with the trace and the per-assertion result; format and retention Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0421; ASM-0596) |

**Environment and test data**

- Environment: SIT, one namespace, the four I stories deployed from their wave 2 builds or replaced by the §12.8 fakes. Harness repository, environment and data seeding: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0421; ASM-0596).
- Data: the three package codes and versions "RES-2026.12" with 38 rows and 62 scenarios, "PMT-2026.12" with 3 rows and 58 scenarios and "BKG-2026.12" with 21 rows and 54 scenarios, all valid from 2026-12-15; users "U-41" and "U-51"; `rules.testcases.min` = 50; rule R-RES-26 with EXACT, WINDOW and PARTIAL; rules R-RES-04 and R-RES-25, R-RES-27, R-RES-29, R-RES-30, R-RES-31 and R-LIT-02; payments "PAY-91008" of 12,500.00 THB and "PAY-91002" of 11,875.00 THB; case "RW-2026-000777"; the business date 2026-12-10 and the promotion date 2026-12-15.
- Reset: each run starts from the seeded state, so a repeated run is deterministic and the same evidence report is produced. The seeding order and the seeding script: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0421; ASM-0596).

**Build steps**

1. Build JourneyRunner and PackageClient against the published OpenAPI documents of the owning services.
2. Publish FakePack for the five services from the same documents, and prove the harness runs green from Day 1 on the fakes.
3. Add the load, the checks, the 50-scenario gate and the four-eyes approval of AC1 and AC3 with ScenarioGateCheck and FourEyesCheck.
4. Add the 00:01 promotion, the `RulePackageInForce` wait and the local swap assertion of AC1.
5. Add the first-match order, the two payment outcomes and the ledger reconciliation of AC2 with DecisionRecordReconciler, and the R-RES-04 route-set assertion of AC3.
6. Add the refusals of AC4 for a wrong match type, 49 scenarios, a wrong row order, a blank catalog field, a duplicate label, an empty workbook, a valid from before the date and a role without the right, and assert that nothing was written.
7. Add the notice silence assertion and the decision log failure of X8, replace each fake with the real service as its I story lands, then publish the evidence report per business date and the pass or fail gate; the gate definition: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0421; ASM-0596).

**Feature switch:** the harness has no production feature flag and runs in the test environment only. The production switch it exercises is `rwb.p3.drools` from the legacy solution plan; with the flag off the three package endpoints and the row reads answer 404 or NoPackageInForce and nothing else changes, and the harness asserts the disabled and the enabled state.

**Done when:** the journey runs green against the four deployed I stories in SIT, the evidence report for the business date holds every assertion of §7 and §16 with its trace, the three versions are in force from 2026-12-15 with 174 passing scenarios, the two payment outcomes reconcile with the ledger, and the pass or fail gate agreed with QA is met for one full business date.

| MSG-P7-002 | The approver is the author | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The version label is already loaded | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |

| MSG-P4-002 | A role without the right calls a package endpoint | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The harness asserts the message ID and the substituted values, including "compile", "schema" and "scenario" for {check} and the row and cell for {detail}, and the version label and the two dates in MSG-GEN-003; it does not own the message text. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the rows, match types, tolerances, windows, action text, owner roles, timers and package rows are data held by rwb-decision; the harness reads them and never holds a copy.
- No personal data in logs, tests, traces or evidence: the report carries staff user IDs and synthetic payment and case codes, and no customer, account or case data.
- No read of another service's schema: every read goes through the owner's contract, the SchemaBoundaryCheck fails the run on a cross-schema reference, and only rwb-source-data reads the ACE views.
- No production data and no outside system: the harness calls only the owning services and their fakes, never a production endpoint.
- The approver is never the author; FourEyesCheck fails the run when they are equal or when a refused approval writes an approver.
- No second rule engine and no recomputation: the version in force, the row counts, the dry run counts and the decisions are read through the rwb-decision contract, and no caller reads the workbook, the generated DRL or a rule row directly.
- `payment_match_rule` is never created and DF-REF-261 to DF-REF-273 are never referenced; the schema assertion is the deploy-time check of the owner's own schema, not a cross-schema read.
- A refused call writes nothing: the harness asserts every row before and after each refusal and fails the run on any change.
- One hop only: the harness fails a run when the trace shows a call chain deeper than one owner.
- A rule change raises no customer-facing notice: NoticeSilenceCheck fails the run when a notice event appears.

- The authoring, approval and rollback mechanics of a package version and the rule package rows themselves (RWB-E1-073 lineage); the harness asserts their result and builds none of it.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-043 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the published contract of the reference case workflow for rwb-case: the workflow interface with its input and signal records, the two activity interfaces, the retry policy, the determinism and versioning declarations, the contract tables of section 12 and the replay fixture**, so that **the app story, the operations story and every Epic 3 squad can build against a fixed, testable workflow contract on Day 1 without waiting for the worker to be deployed**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A Temporal contract is not a REST document: it is a typed workflow interface, a typed activity interface and a set of serialisable records that are published as a contract jar, so a caller imports only the interface and calls the owner's task queue (Arch v5 slide 11). Get it wrong and two costs follow immediately: a workflow that cannot be replayed after a deploy, because the activity contract or the record shape changed under a running history, and a second squad inventing a different order of steps for its own case.

This baseline fixes both in one place. It names the workflow, its input record and its signal record; it names the two activities, with the rule answer in one and the decision record plus the state change in the other; it fixes the retry policy and the one non-retryable outcome; and it declares the determinism rule and the versioning rule that the replay gate of RWB-E2-040 enforces on every build (Temporal and Drools design slides 14 and 27).

The baseline has no REST path, no event of its own and no table. The skeleton is test-only, so the contract states that scope explicitly: the workflow ID prefix is `ref-case-`, the input carries `synthetic`, and the task queue is `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery` because the queue belongs to the owning service (Arch v5 slides 24 and 41). The legacy queue `rwb-platform` is not part of this contract.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service naming rule of the platform library is in force: schema `rwb_case`, REST base `/api/recovery/case/v1`, topic `rwb.case.events.v1`, task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case` (DP-14, RWB-PLT-E1047-CON).
- The workflow kit is available as a published library, with the contract-jar convention, the payload codec and the build ID provider (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, DP-10).
- The outbox and inbox library is available as the reference for the `OutboxConsumer` interface the relay implements, and for the delivery states PENDING, RETRYING and DELIVERED (RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, DP-09).
- The local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` are published, so the contract can state who publishes DecisionRecorded (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, DP-03).
- The embedded Drools kit is published, so the activity contract can name `RuleResult` and `NoPackageInForce` without redefining them (RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, DP-04).
- The operations and their owners are taken from the Ownership Map only; the contract documents no operation owned by another service.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (Template and Rules §R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the workflow interface: one workflow method, one signal method, and nothing else public.
2. Draft the two records: `ReferenceCaseInput` for the start and `CaseEventSignal` for the signal, with the field list and the `synthetic` flag fixed.
3. Draft the two activity interfaces against the rule evaluator and the case state service, and state the idempotency key and the transaction boundary in the contract text.
4. Declare the retry policy as configuration with its four values and the non-retryable outcome.
5. Declare the determinism rule and the versioning rule: build ID per worker, `getVersion` for an in-place change, the replay gate on every build.
6. State the scope: test-only, workflow ID prefix `ref-case-`, no REST path, no topic, no table, no Schedule.
7. Publish the nine contract tables of section 12, each with its owner from the Ownership Map, and state that no fake is required.
8. Add the contract tests: interface shape, signal schema, activity signatures, retry values, determinism boundary, and a recorded history that replays.
9. Tag the baseline and hand it to the app story, the operations story and every Epic 3 squad.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The workflow interface declares a second workflow method or a query that returns a mutable type | The contract check fails and the baseline is not tagged | None | AC1 |
| X2 | A signal record carries a personal-data field | The review refuses the record and no baseline is published | None | AC2 |
| X3 | An activity signature changes a parameter type or its order | The compatibility check fails; a breaking change needs a new contract version | None | AC3 |
| X4 | A workflow class places an I/O call or a Drools call inside workflow code | The boundary test fails the build | None | AC5 |
| X5 | A recorded history no longer replays against the build | The replay gate fails the release and the contract is not declared compatible | MSG-P3-038 | AC6 |
| X6 | The contract declares a REST path, a topic or a table of its own | The review fails the baseline, because the skeleton owns none of the three | None | AC6 |
| X7 | The retry values differ between the contract text and the worker configuration | The contract test fails on the drift | None | AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the workflow kit, the record library and the naming rule only |
| Negotiable | Field-level detail of the records is settled with the consumers; the two-activity form, the retry values and the determinism rule are fixed by the target design |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app, operations and test work of this legacy key on Day 1 and gives every Epic 3 squad the same order of steps |
| Estimable | One interface, two records, two activity interfaces, one retry policy, nine contract tables and six contract tests |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests and the replay fixture |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact, not against a business outcome |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Workflow and activity contract for the reference case workflow of rwb-case

  Background:
    Given the service naming rule of the platform library is in force
    Given the namespace is rwb-recovery and the task queue of rwb-case is rwb-case
    Given the workflow kit publishes its interfaces as a contract jar per service

  Scenario: AC1 The workflow interface is one method, one signal and nothing else (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the published contract of ReferenceCaseWorkflow
    When it is validated against the workflow kit contract rules
    Then it declares exactly one workflow method run(ReferenceCaseInput)
    Then it declares exactly one signal method onCaseEvent(CaseEventSignal)
    Then it declares no other public method, no query and no update handler
    Then the contract states the task queue rwb-case in namespace rwb-recovery and the workflow ID prefix ref-case-
    Then the contract jar is published with a version and the consumer imports only the interface

  Scenario: AC2 The CaseEvent signal schema is fixed and carries no personal data (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the CaseEventSignal record of the contract
    When its fields are read
    Then it carries eventId, caseId, eventType, occurredAt, idempotencyKey and synthetic, and no other field
    Then it carries no name, address, identity number or contact point
    Then synthetic is required and is true for every reference run
    When a payload omits idempotencyKey or carries an unknown field
    Then the contract test refuses the payload and the signal is not accepted

  Scenario: AC3 The two activity contracts replace the legacy three (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the activity interfaces of the contract
    When they are read
    Then EvaluateRulesActivity declares evaluate(packageCode, facts, onDate) and returns packageCode, packageVersion, ruleId and outputs
    Then RecordAndApplyActivity declares apply(request) with the event idempotency key in the request
    Then the contract states that the record write and the state change are one transaction and a retry returns the first result
    Then no WriteDecisionLog or ApplyState activity is declared for the target
    Then a changed parameter type or order fails the compatibility check and needs a new contract version

  Scenario: AC4 The retry policy is declared and matches the worker configuration (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the retry policy of the contract
    When its values are compared with the worker configuration
    Then the initial interval is 1 second, the back-off coefficient is 2 and the maximum attempts is 10
    Then NoPackageInForce is listed as non-retryable for both activities
    Then the policy applies to EvaluateRulesActivity and RecordAndApplyActivity only
    When a value in the configuration differs from the contract text
    Then the contract test fails on the drift

  Scenario: AC5 The deterministic build and the versioning declarations are enforced (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the workflow package of the contract
    When the boundary test and the determinism check run
    Then no workflow class reads a clock, a random source, a database or the network
    Then no workflow class calls Drools or the case state service outside an activity
    Then the contract declares the build ID of the worker and the getVersion change identity for an in-place change
    Then a workflow class placed outside the workflow package fails the boundary test

  Scenario: AC6 A recorded history replays and the nine contract tables are complete (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the recorded reference history of the contract fixture
    When it is replayed against the build
    Then the replay reaches the same activity path and reads the recorded activity result
    Then the replay calls no rule evaluator and no case state service
    Then the replay result is reported to the gate of RWB-E2-040 with the build ID
    Then each of 12.1 to 12.9 is present and names its owner from the Ownership Map
    Then the contract declares no REST path, no topic of its own, no table and no Schedule
```

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | A workflow and its activities are published as a typed contract jar; a caller imports only the interface and calls the owner's task queue | Arch v5 slide 11 (Temporal contract row); Design slide 12 |
| BR2 | One workflow interface has one workflow method and one signal method for this skeleton; a second public method is a new contract version | Design slide 13; RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| BR3 | The task queue is `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`; the legacy queue `rwb-platform` is not declared | Arch v5 slides 24 and 41; DP-10 |
| BR4 | The workflow ID of the skeleton starts `ref-case-` and never `case-`, and the input carries `synthetic`; the skeleton is test-only | Legacy RWB-E2-043 BR7; ASM-1272 |
| BR5 | The signal record carries identifiers, a type, a timestamp, a key and the synthetic flag only; no personal data | Design slide 27 (PDPA); Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR6 | The record write and the state change are one transaction in one activity; the legacy separate WriteDecisionLog and ApplyState activities are not declared | Design slide 14; DP-03; R-UNI-39 |
| BR7 | The retry policy is data: initial 1 s, back-off 2, maximum 10 attempts, NoPackageInForce non-retryable; the contract text and the configuration are checked for drift | Design slides 14 and 28 |
| BR8 | Workflow code is deterministic and all I/O is in an activity; the boundary test fails any class outside the workflow package | Design slide 27; ADR-011 |
| BR9 | A breaking change to an activity or a record needs a new contract version; a compatible addition is allowed within the current one | Arch v5 slide 11 (contract per service) |
| BR10 | The contract declares no REST path, no event of its own, no table and no Schedule, because the skeleton owns none of them | Section 12 of this story; DP-11; DP-19 note |

##### 10. Authority

| Solution architect | Approves a breaking change and a new contract version |

The worker runs as the rwb-case service identity (DP-02), carried by the chart as a secret reference; the contract fixes no literal login name.

##### 11. Data

The contract declares shapes, not business values.

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| `ReferenceCaseInput` | caseId, packageCode, businessDate, synthetic; no other field |
| `CaseEventSignal` | eventId, caseId, eventType, occurredAt, idempotencyKey, synthetic |
| `RuleResult` | packageCode, packageVersion, ruleId, outputs, as published by the embedded Drools kit |
| `RecordAndApplyRequest` | the event idempotency key, the rule result, the state change and the business date |
| `RecordAndApplyResult` | the record reference, the state reference and whether the call created the row or found it |
| Search attributes | CaseId, Stage, ProductGroup, QueueCode only; no personal data |
| History | references, codes, IDs, dates and amounts only; payloads pass through the payload codec |

The exact field-level detail of `RecordAndApplyRequest` and of the outputs map (types, cardinality, which rule output is mandatory per package) is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0727; ASM-1275); this story fixes the field names above and leaves the detail to the baseline review.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The skeleton has no REST path, no admin operation and no health contract beyond the platform probes of RWB-P3-E2043-OPS; it is started by the reference harness in DEV and SIT only.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The only remote call is `WorkflowGateway` to the Temporal frontend, which is a gRPC contract of the workflow kit (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON), and the in-process calls to the rule evaluator, the local decision-record library and the case state service.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The skeleton publishes nothing. The outbox deliveries it reads belong to RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, and the only event written on its path is DecisionRecorded on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, published by the local decision-record library (DP-03) and owned by P7.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event type | Topic | Owner of the type | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | CaseEventSignal, eventType CaseCreated |
| `rwb.case.CaseAllocated.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | CaseEventSignal, eventType CaseAllocated |
| `rwb.case.CaseAllocationFailed.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | CaseEventSignal, eventType CaseAllocationFailed |
| `rwb.case.CaseTransferred.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | CaseEventSignal, eventType CaseTransferred |
| `rwb.case.CaseStateChanged.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | CaseEventSignal, eventType CaseStateChanged |
| `rwb.case.TimerBreached.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 | CaseEventSignal, eventType TimerBreached |

The relay implements the `OutboxConsumer` interface of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, reads the delivery of one of these types and calls `WorkflowGateway.signal(workflowId, "CaseEvent", payload)`. The topic and the six event types are the property of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON and of the case event contract; this story only fixes how each type maps onto the signal. A failed call leaves the delivery PENDING or RETRYING with its next attempt time.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| ReferenceCaseWorkflow | Workflow, test-only scope, workflow ID prefix `ref-case-` | `rwb-case` | `run(ReferenceCaseInput)`, `onCaseEvent(CaseEventSignal)` |
| EvaluateRulesActivity | Activity | `rwb-case` | Package code, facts and date in; package code, package version, rule ID and outputs out |
| RecordAndApplyActivity | Activity | `rwb-case` | Event key, rule result and state change in; record reference, state reference and created-or-found out |
| CaseEventSignalRelay | Outbox consumer | not a worker | Delivery reference in; the signal call and the delivery status out |

```java
@WorkflowInterface
public interface ReferenceCaseWorkflow {
    @WorkflowMethod void run(ReferenceCaseInput input);
    @SignalMethod void onCaseEvent(CaseEventSignal event);
}
// ReferenceCaseInput: caseId, packageCode, businessDate, synthetic (true only)
// CaseEventSignal: eventId, caseId, eventType, occurredAt, idempotencyKey, synthetic
```

```java
RuleResult EvaluateRulesActivity.evaluate(String packageCode, CaseFacts facts, LocalDate onDate);
RecordAndApplyResult RecordAndApplyActivity.apply(RecordAndApplyRequest request); // record + state + outbox, one transaction
```

**Retry policy**

| Item | Value | Declared as |
|---|---|---|
| Initial interval | 1 second | Configuration, checked against the contract text |
| Back-off coefficient | 2 | Configuration |
| Maximum attempts | 10 | Configuration |
| Non-retryable | NoPackageInForce | Contract text and activity configuration |
| Applies to | EvaluateRulesActivity, RecordAndApplyActivity | Contract text |

**Versioning and replay.** Each worker carries the build ID of its build; an in-place code change uses `Workflow.getVersion(changeId, DEFAULT_VERSION, 1)`; the replay gate of RWB-E2-040 replays the recorded histories against every new build before release. The build ID format and the versioning policy are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0725; ASM-1273); the size of the replay corpus and the text of MSG-P3-038 are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0726; ASM-1274).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The reference workflow is started by the harness and is never started by a Schedule; the Schedules of rwb-case are declared by their own stories.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The contract names no table as its own: the local decision record, the outbox, the inbox and the idempotency objects are library objects created in schema rwb_case by its own DB story, and the case row is written by the P3 case state service. No table of another service is read or written (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. There is no WireMock mapping and no HTTP stub: the workflow tests run on TestWorkflowEnvironment with time skipping, and the rule evaluator, the decision-record library and the case state service are replaced by in-process test doubles of their published interfaces. The package facts of the reference (RESTRUCTURE "RES-2026.12", rule R-RES-04) come from the contract mock of rwb-decision named in the app story.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 0 consumed | No path, no admin operation and no client |
| Kafka | 0 published, 6 types consumed through the relay | The six `rwb.case.*` types of `rwb.case.events.v1` map onto CaseEventSignal; the topic belongs to RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 2 activities, 0 Schedules | ReferenceCaseWorkflow, EvaluateRulesActivity, RecordAndApplyActivity on `rwb-case` |
| File | None | The recorded history used by the replay test is a test resource, not runtime data |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Deliverables.** `contract/rwb-case-reference-workflow-v1.jar` with the workflow interface, the two activity interfaces and the records; `contract/reference-workflow.md` with the determinism, versioning and retry rules; `contract/replay/` with the recorded reference history; the six contract tests.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_case`; the contract names no table and reads no other service's table | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | The record and the state change in one transaction, plus `rwb.decision-record.v1`; two activities replace the legacy three | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | The activity contract names `RuleResult` and `NoPackageInForce` from the embedded kit; the package model comes from rwb-decision | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON (registry side is RWB-P7-E1073) |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | The contract carries no ACE field; an Epic 3 copy reads ACE data through the rwb-source-data contract | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | The reference data of the case status and route lists is read through the rwb-case contract inside RecordAndApply | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | The relay implements the `OutboxConsumer` of the outbox library; CloudEvents envelope and delivery states | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | The workflow kit provides the queue, the codec, the build ID and the versioning; no Schedule is declared | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | No REST hop is declared at all; the workflow reaches the rules and the state through activities | none |
| DP-14 | `rwb.p<n>.` or `rwb.casewf.` topic names | The contract reuses `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.case.<Event>.v1` through the naming library and adds no topic | H RWB-PLT-E1047-CON |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | No migration in this contract; the library objects arrive with the rwb_case baseline | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff is not used by this contract: no route, no screen and no endpoint are declared | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

**Build steps**

1. Publish the workflow interface and the two records with the field list of section 11; test the interface shape (AC1, AC2).
2. Publish the two activity interfaces against `RuleResult` and the case state service; test the compatibility rule (AC3).
3. Write the retry policy as a configuration fragment and state the non-retryable outcome; test the drift check (AC4).
4. Add the determinism boundary test and the package rule, and declare the build ID and `getVersion` identity (AC5).
5. Record the reference history and add the replay test with a later package version (AC6).
6. State the scope rule of BR10 and assert in the review that no REST path, topic, table or Schedule is declared (AC6).
7. Tag the baseline and circulate it to the app, operations and Epic 3 consumers.

**Done when.** The contract jar builds, the six contract tests pass, the recorded history replays with no rule evaluation, and the app and operations stories have accepted the baseline.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P3-036 | The Temporal frontend is unreachable when the relay signals | The workflow service is not available. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P3-027 | No package version is in force at evaluation time | The rule version was refused at the {check} check: {detail}. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record write fails inside the activity | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P3-038 | A recorded history does not replay against this build | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0726; ASM-1274) |

The business message IDs keep the text of the legacy story and of the message catalogue; this contract only states where each one is produced on the workflow path. The text of MSG-P3-038 and the size of the replay corpus are not fixed by any source read for this story.

##### 15. Screens and states

No screen in this contract. The contract serves the Temporal Web UI view of the reference run: the workflow state, the activity attempt count, the build ID of the worker and the search attributes CaseId, Stage and QueueCode, read by RW-PLATADM and RW-AUDIT. Payloads are decoded only through the codec server (RWB-E2-038). SCR-44 Interface and job monitor is not used, because the skeleton owns no job and no queue of its own.

##### 16. Test cases

| TC ID | Covers | Level | Data |
|---|---|---|---|
| TC-P3-E2043-CON-01 | AC1 | Contract | The contract jar declares one workflow method, one signal method and no other public member |
| TC-P3-E2043-CON-02 | AC2 | Contract | The six-field CaseEventSignal validates; a payload without the key or with an unknown field is refused |
| TC-P3-E2043-CON-03 | AC3 | Contract | The two activity signatures and the one-transaction statement; a changed parameter order fails the compatibility check |
| TC-P3-E2043-CON-04 | AC4 | Contract | Retry values 1 s, back-off 2, 10 attempts and NoPackageInForce non-retryable; a drift fails the test |
| TC-P3-E2043-CON-05 | AC5 | Component | The boundary and determinism checks; a workflow class outside the package and a clock or Drools call inside workflow code both fail |
| TC-P3-E2043-CON-06 | AC6 | Component | A recorded history replays against the build; the nine contract tables are complete and declare no REST path, topic, table or Schedule |

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the package code, the rule ID and the state values used by the reference are data in the rule packages and the reference tables, never constants in the interface.
- No personal data in a record, an example, a search attribute or the recorded history: identifiers, codes, dates and amounts only, and payloads pass through the payload codec.
- One task queue, one namespace and one Java package per service; the contract names only `rwb-case` and `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case` (DP-10, DP-14).
- The contract declares no operation, topic or table owned by another service, and the six event types are used through the ownership of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON (DP-01, DP-09).
- Every example and the recorded history are synthetic; no production payload is copied into a record or a fixture.
- A breaking change to a record or an activity is a new contract version, so a running history is never invalidated in place.
- The retry policy is declared once and checked for drift, so the contract text can never disagree with the worker.

##### 18. Traceability

| Requirement ID | Requirement (short) | Contract element | Test cases |
|---|---|---|---|
| REQ-DRI-001 | Every decision is recorded with the rule and version that made it | EvaluateRulesActivity result and the record written by RecordAndApplyActivity | TC-P3-E2043-CON-03, TC-P3-E2043-CON-06 |
| REQ-DRI-005 | No action proceeds if its decision record cannot be written | One transaction in RecordAndApplyActivity; the created-or-found result | TC-P3-E2043-CON-03 |
| REQ-CWC-016 | Rules are evaluated by Drools from a versioned package | packageCode and packageVersion in the activity result and the record | TC-P3-E2043-CON-06 |
| REQ-DRI-007 | An outbound step retries on a defined schedule and leaves a visible exception when it fails | Retry policy, the non-retryable outcome and the delivery states of the relay | TC-P3-E2043-CON-04 |
| D-RCV-60 | The pattern runs on the owning service's queue with two activities and one transaction | Task queue `rwb-case`, workflow ID prefix and the two activity interfaces | TC-P3-E2043-CON-01, TC-P3-E2043-CON-03 |

##### 19. Out of scope

- The implementation of the workflow, the two activities and the relay (RWB-P3-E2043-APP).
- The deployment of the worker, the flag, the replay gate step and the dashboards (RWB-P3-E2043-OPS).
- The replay gate as a platform capability and its release step (RWB-E2-040, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON); this contract only states that a build passes it.
- The outbox, inbox and CloudEvents library and the six case event schemas, which are owned by RWB-PLT-TE006-CON.
- The local decision-record library and the central ledger (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-P7-E2043-APP).
- The rule package governance and the registry contract (RWB-P7-E1073); the Epic 2 package content (RWB-P3-E2042-APP).
- The remaining case workflows of Epic 3 and their own contracts.
- The real cross-service proof of the pattern (RWB-ITG-E2043-ITG).
- gateway-bff, the composite route and every screen; the contract declares none of them.
- The field-level detail of the request record and of the rule outputs map (GAP-0727).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-043 for rwb-case. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **developer**, I want **a test-only reference case workflow that runs on task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and shows signal handling, rule evaluation inside one activity, the decision record and the state change written together by a second activity, and outbound work through the outbox**, so that **Epic 3 builds every case workflow the same way**.

##### 2. Business rationale

Epic 3 adds a workflow per case, and each squad would otherwise invent its own order of steps. A workflow that applies a state change before its decision record breaks the decision-first principle (R-UNI-39), and a workflow that calls Drools outside an activity breaks replay. This story fixes both in one small skeleton: the signal arrives through the outbox consumer, the rule is evaluated in an activity, the decision record and the state change are written together by a second activity, and a failure at either step stops the next. It is test-only and runs with no live case, so Epic 3 can copy it without a production risk. It meets REQ-DRI-001, REQ-DRI-005, REQ-CWC-016 and REQ-DRI-007.

In the target the two concerns are the local decision record and the central ledger (DP-03): the owning service writes the record in its own schema in the same transaction as the state change and publishes DecisionRecorded on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, and rwb-decision collects it into the central ledger within five minutes (Arch v5 slide 28). The Temporal and Drools design merges the legacy WriteDecisionLog and ApplyState steps into one RecordAndApply activity for exactly that reason (design slide 14), so this skeleton has two activities where the legacy story had three, and the order evaluate, record, apply is unchanged.

The skeleton is also the carrier of the platform rules that make a workflow safe to replay: deterministic workflow code, worker versioning with `getVersion` for an in-place change, encrypted payloads through PdpaPayloadCodec, and the replay gate of RWB-E2-040 that replays recorded histories against every new build (design slide 27). The measure is that every Epic 3 workflow is a copy of the skeleton and passes that gate.

The skeleton has no screen, no endpoint and no composite route, so gateway-bff (DP-19) is not used by it; the dependency on RWB-PLT-N001-CON is carried only because the service template registers the route of rwb-case.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P3-E2043-CON is published: the workflow interface, the two activity interfaces, the CaseEvent signal schema, the ReferenceCaseInput record and the retry policy of this legacy key.
- RWB-PLT-E1071-CON is published: the Temporal workflow kit in namespace `rwb-recovery`, with the task queue `rwb-case`, the worker configuration and the build ID provider.
- RWB-PLT-E1072-CON is published: the embedded Drools kit with one KieBase per package version, first-match semantics and the `NoPackageInForce` outcome (DP-04).
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the local decision-record library and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03). The central ledger behind it belongs to rwb-decision (P7) and is not written by this story.
- RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is published: the outbox and inbox library with the CloudEvents envelope and the `OutboxConsumer` interface the relay implements (DP-09).
- RWB-PLT-E1043-CON and RWB-P3-E1043-CON are published: the reference-data contract of rwb-case, with the client library (DP-07). RWB-PLT-E1047-CON is published: the topic and event naming library (DP-14). RWB-PLT-E1044-CON is published: the per-service Flyway sequence and migration conventions (DP-15).
- RWB-PLT-N001-CON is published: the gateway-bff composite route of the service template. This skeleton declares no route on it.
- Package RESTRUCTURE version "RES-2026.12" is in force from 2026-12-01, with rule R-RES-04 moving IN_FCR_QUEUE on CASE_PICKED_UP to WITH_FCR_OFFICER; the package is governed and served by rwb-decision and is answered in this story by the rwb-decision contract mock.
- The synthetic case "RW-2026-000777" exists in the DEV and SIT test data and is marked synthetic; no live case is used. The fixture that seeds and removes it is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0724; ASM-1272).
- The Temporal server and Java SDK versions approved by SCB IT are pinned by the platform, not by this story (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON).
- Feature switch `rwb.p3.temporal` is on in DEV and SIT; `rwb.p3.drools` is on. The switch is read through the platform parameters contract, never from code.

##### 4. Flow

1. Reference harness: starts ReferenceCaseWorkflow with workflow ID "ref-case-RW-2026-000777" on task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, with the synthetic case, the reference package code and the business date, and with synthetic true.
2. Workflow: waits for the CaseEvent signal; no activity runs before it.
3. CaseEventSignalRelay: reads the outbox delivery "EV-CASE-0777-01" of type CASE_PICKED_UP and calls `WorkflowGateway.signal(workflowId, "CaseEvent", payload)`; a failed call leaves the delivery PENDING or RETRYING for the next attempt (DP-09).
4. Workflow: calls EvaluateRulesActivity with the package code, the case facts and the business date; the activity calls `RuleEvaluator.evaluate` and returns `RuleResult` with the package code, the package version, the rule ID and the outputs.
5. Workflow: calls RecordAndApplyActivity with the event key; the activity writes, in one transaction in schema rwb_case, the decision record through the local decision-record library and the state change through the P3 case state service, plus the outbox row of DecisionRecorded.
6. Workflow: completes. A failed write leaves the state untouched because nothing committed, fails the workflow with MSG-P7-003 after its retries and raises an incident; the stuck-workflow scan of the platform (JOB-21) reports a workflow that waits on a non-retryable failure.
7. Workflow: a second CaseEvent that arrives while the first is processing is buffered by Temporal and handled in signal order.
8. Platform administrator: reads the run in the Temporal Web UI; internal audit reads the same history and sees encrypted payloads and references only.
9. Epic 3 squad: copies the workflow, the two activity interfaces and the retry policy, replaces the synthetic fixture with the real case, and keeps the order.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The decision record write fails | The state change does not commit either, because both are one transaction; the workflow fails after its retries and an incident is raised | MSG-P7-003 | AC2 |
| X2 | Temporal is unavailable when the signal is sent | The signal fails; the outbox event and its delivery stay for the next attempt | MSG-P3-036 | AC5 |
| X3 | The RecordAndApply activity commits and then times out before it returns | The retry uses the same idempotency key and finds the first record and the first state row | None | AC3 |
| X4 | A new package version is in force while the workflow waits | The recorded activity result keeps the version chosen at evaluation time; replay takes the same path | None | AC4 |
| X5 | `rwb.p3.temporal` is off | No worker on `rwb-case`, no reference workflow deployed and the relay idle; outbox deliveries stay PENDING | None | AC6 |
| X6 | A second CaseEvent arrives while the first is processing | Temporal buffers it and the first path completes in signal order | None | AC1 |
| X7 | No package version is in force at evaluation time | EvaluateRulesActivity fails with NoPackageInForce; the policy does not retry and the workflow fails at once | MSG-P3-027 | AC4 |
| X8 | A non-synthetic case ID is passed as the workflow input | The workflow refuses to run and fails before any activity; nothing is read or written | None | AC6 |
| X9 | The reference data read of the case status list fails | RecordAndApplyActivity is not called; the workflow retries the evaluation step only, never a partial record | MSG-P3-027 | AC1, AC4 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the workflow kit of RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, the evaluator of RWB-PLT-E1072-CON, the record library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and the outbox of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON; it adds one test-only workflow, two activities and one relay |
| Negotiable | Retry values are configuration; the order of the two steps is fixed |
| Valuable | Epic 3 copies one proven order instead of inventing one per workflow |
| Estimable | One workflow, two activities, one signal record, one input record, one relay, one retry policy |
| Small | Fits one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each criterion runs with TestWorkflowEnvironment time skipping and the synthetic case; no WireMock is needed because no REST call is made |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Temporal and Drools integration pattern and reference case workflow

  Background:
    Given the environment is SIT with synthetic data and no live case

    Given RESTRUCTURE version "RES-2026.12" is in force from 2026-12-01
    Given rule R-RES-04 moves IN_FCR_QUEUE on CASE_PICKED_UP to WITH_FCR_OFFICER
    Given the synthetic case "RW-2026-000777" has status IN_PROGRESS and route state IN_FCR_QUEUE

  Scenario: AC1 The four steps run in order (legacy RWB-E2-043 AC1)
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns package "RESTRUCTURE" version "RES-2026.12" and rule "R-RES-04"
    Given the reference workflow "ref-case-RW-2026-000777" is running and waits for a CaseEvent
    Given outbox event "EV-CASE-0777-01" of type CASE_PICKED_UP
    When CaseEventSignalRelay calls WorkflowGateway.signal with "CaseEvent" and the event payload
    Then the workflow history shows EvaluateRulesActivity, then WriteDecisionLogActivity, then ApplyStateActivity
    Then EvaluateRulesActivity returns rule "R-RES-04" and package version "RES-2026.12"
    Then WriteDecisionLogActivity writes one entry with rule "R-RES-04" and rule version "RES-2026.12"
    Then ApplyStateActivity moves the route state to "WITH_FCR_OFFICER"
    Then no case row is written before the decision log entry

  Scenario: AC2 A failed decision log write stops the state change (legacy RWB-E2-043 AC2)
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns package "RESTRUCTURE" version "RES-2026.12" and rule "R-RES-04"
    Given the decision log store is unavailable
    When the CaseEvent "EV-CASE-0777-02" is processed
    Then WriteDecisionLogActivity throws DecisionLogUnavailableException
    Then the workflow does not call ApplyStateActivity
    Then the route state of "RW-2026-000777" stays "IN_FCR_QUEUE"
    Then the workflow fails with MSG-P7-003 after its retries and an incident is raised

  Scenario: AC3 Activity retries are idempotent (legacy RWB-E2-043 AC3)
    Given ApplyStateActivity commits the state row and then times out before it returns
    When Temporal retries the activity with idempotency key "CASE_EVENT:EV-CASE-0777-03"
    Then the second attempt returns the first result and changes nothing
    Then one case state row exists for "EV-CASE-0777-03"
    Then WriteDecisionLogActivity ran once and one decision_log_entry row exists with that key
    Then the workflow completes once

  Scenario: AC4 The rule version is pinned in the result and replay is stable (legacy RWB-E2-043 AC4)
    Given EvaluateRulesActivity returned package version "RES-2026.12" and rule "R-RES-04" for "EV-CASE-0777-04"
    Given the rwb-decision contract mock returns package "RESTRUCTURE" version "RES-2027.01"
    Given package version "RES-2027.01" is in force from 2027-01-01 while the workflow waits for the next event
    When the workflow is replayed from its recorded history on 2027-01-05
    Then the recorded result still carries "RES-2026.12" and "R-RES-04"
    Then the replay reads the recorded activity result and never calls RuleEvaluator again
    Then the replay reaches the same activity path and the same state move

  Scenario: AC5 Temporal unavailable keeps the case event in the outbox (legacy RWB-E2-043 AC5)
    Given the Temporal frontend is unreachable
    When the outbox sender delivers "EV-CASE-0777-05"
    Then WorkflowGateway.signal fails with MSG-P3-036
    Then outbox event "EV-CASE-0777-05" stays in the outbox and its delivery is RETRYING with the next attempt time
    Then the sender retries on its schedule
    When Temporal is available at the next attempt
    Then the signal is delivered and the delivery is DELIVERED

  Scenario: AC6 The skeleton runs behind the flag with no live case (legacy RWB-E2-043 AC6)
    Given rwb.p3.temporal is off in DEV
    When the application starts
    Then no worker is registered on "rwb-case" and ReferenceCaseWorkflow is not deployed
    When the flag is on and the reference harness starts "ref-case-RW-2026-000777" with synthetic "true"

```

AC1 records the three legacy steps; in the target the same order is carried by two activities — EvaluateRulesActivity, then RecordAndApplyActivity, which writes the decision record and the state change in one transaction (Temporal and Drools design slide 14, DP-03) — so the recorded three steps are read as evaluate, record, apply. The target task queue is `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, because the queue belongs to the owning service (Arch v5 slides 24 and 41); the legacy queue `rwb-platform` is retired for this skeleton. A Given naming a package, a rule or a version in force is preceded by the parallel rwb-decision contract mock Given, because the registry is owned by rwb-decision and is answered by its fake in this story.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Workflow code is deterministic: no clock, random or I/O; Drools is called only inside EvaluateRulesActivity | Design slide 27; ADR-011; DP-04 |
| BR2 | The order is signal, evaluate, record and apply; no state row is written without its decision record, because both are one transaction | REQ-DRI-005; R-UNI-39; design slide 14; DP-03 |
| BR3 | Every activity is idempotent by the event idempotency key; a retry gives one record and one state row | REQ-DRI-005; R-UNI-40 |
| BR4 | The package version is chosen at evaluation time, pinned in RuleResult and written to the decision record; replay uses the recorded result | Design slides 15 and 27; R-UNI-38 |
| BR5 | Payloads are encrypted by PdpaPayloadCodec; history, search attributes and logs hold references and codes only | Design slide 27; NFR-034 |
| BR6 | When Temporal is unavailable the signal fails with MSG-P3-036 and the outbox event stays for retry | REQ-DRI-007; DP-09; RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| BR7 | The reference skeleton is test-only: it runs only under `rwb.p3.temporal` and only with a synthetic case, and its workflow ID starts `ref-case-` | Legacy RWB-E2-043 BR7; ASM-1272 |
| BR8 | Retry policy: initial interval 1 s, back-off 2, maximum 10 attempts; NoPackageInForce is non-retryable | Design slides 14 and 28 |
| BR9 | The state change goes through the P3 case state service inside RecordAndApplyActivity; the workflow writes no table and calls no repository | REQ-DRI-005; DP-01; design slide 11 |
| BR10 | The build passes the replay gate of RWB-E2-040 and the worker is versioned: a new build takes new workflows while the old build drains, and an in-place change uses `Workflow.getVersion` | Design slide 27; RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| BR11 | A reference-data or parameter value is read through the rwb-case contract with the version in force; no status, route or timer value is written in code | DP-07; Template and Rules §R7.2 s17 |
| BR12 | The skeleton calls no REST operation and declares no route on gateway-bff; its only remote call is WorkflowGateway to the Temporal frontend | DP-11; DP-19 note in section 2 |

##### 9. State transitions

This story changes no live case. It writes the route state of the synthetic fixture through the P3 case state service and moves the workflow through its own states.

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| RUNNING | CaseEvent | Evaluate and record-and-apply both succeed | COMPLETED |
| RUNNING | CaseEvent | The record and the state change fail after 10 attempts | FAILED |
| RUNNING | CaseEvent | NoPackageInForce | FAILED, no retry |
| RUNNING | CaseEvent | The input is not synthetic | FAILED, no activity run |
| IN_FCR_QUEUE | CASE_PICKED_UP | R-RES-04 fires | WITH_FCR_OFFICER |

A FAILED workflow is reported by the stuck-workflow scan of the platform (JOB-21) and is visible in the Temporal Web UI; it is never retried by a later signal, because the signal has already been consumed.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| SY-CASEWF, case workflow identity | Runs ReferenceCaseWorkflow on `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and registers its two activities |
| SY-RULES, Drools evaluator identity | Evaluates the package inside EvaluateRulesActivity (Rules and parameters R) |
| Decision-record library identity | Writes the local record and its outbox row in the same transaction as the state change (Decision log C) |
| RW-PLATADM, platform administrator | Runs the worker and reads the Temporal Web UI (Platform administration CRUD) |
| RW-AUDIT, internal audit | Reads the recorded history with encrypted payloads and references only (Platform administration R) |
| RW-COE, center of excellence analyst | Owns the RESTRUCTURE version used by the reference |
| No delegation of authority level applies | The skeleton takes no credit decision |

The worker runs as the rwb-case service identity (DP-02) and the chart carries it as a secret reference; the story fixes no literal login name.

| DF-DEC-030 | Local decision record | actor_user_id | Write, the service identity only |

Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8. The skeleton writes no table of its own and no new field: the local decision record, the outbox, the inbox and the idempotency objects are library objects created in schema rwb_case by its own DB story (DP-09, DP-15). No row of `rwb_decision` and no central ledger row is written by this story; the central ledger is filled by rwb-decision from `rwb.decision-record.v1` and is the subject of RWB-P7-E2043-APP. The fixture row is inserted and removed by the harness in DEV and SIT only; the seed file and its owner are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0724; ASM-1272).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The skeleton is started by the reference harness in DEV and SIT only; it declares no path under `/api/recovery/case/v1`, no admin operation and no health contract beyond the platform probes.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

None. The only remote call of the skeleton is `WorkflowGateway` to the Temporal frontend, which is a gRPC contract of the workflow kit (RWB-PLT-E1071-CON) and not a REST operation. The rule package and the reference data are read in-process through their published Java interfaces and the contract mocks of this story.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The skeleton publishes no event of its own; DecisionRecorded on `rwb.decision-record.v1` is published by the local decision-record library through the outbox in the same transaction as the record and the state change (DP-03), and that event type belongs to P7.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None at the Kafka level. The case event types of `rwb.case.events.v1` are read from the outbox delivery by `CaseEventSignalRelay`, which implements the `OutboxConsumer` interface of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON and turns each delivery into a CaseEvent signal; the event types and the ownership of the type stay with that contract, and this story consumes no topic of its own.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ReferenceCaseWorkflow | Workflow, test-only scope, workflow ID prefix `ref-case-` | `rwb-case` | Waits for the CaseEvent signal, calls EvaluateRules then RecordAndApply, completes |
| EvaluateRulesActivity | Activity | `rwb-case` | Calls `RuleEvaluator.evaluate(packageCode, facts, onDate)`, returns RuleResult |
| RecordAndApplyActivity | Activity | `rwb-case` | Writes the decision record and the state change in one transaction, idempotent by the event key |
| CaseEventSignalRelay | Outbox consumer | not a worker | Signals the workflow; a failed call leaves the delivery PENDING or RETRYING |

```java
@WorkflowInterface
public interface ReferenceCaseWorkflow {
    @WorkflowMethod void run(ReferenceCaseInput input);
    @SignalMethod void onCaseEvent(CaseEventSignal event);
}
// ReferenceCaseInput: caseId, packageCode, businessDate, synthetic (true only)
// CaseEventSignal: eventId, caseId, eventType, occurredAt, idempotencyKey, synthetic
```

```java
RuleResult EvaluateRulesActivity.evaluate(String packageCode, CaseFacts facts, LocalDate onDate);
RecordAndApplyResult RecordAndApplyActivity.apply(RecordAndApplyRequest request); // record + state + outbox, one transaction
```

**Retry policy**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Initial interval | 1 second |
| Back-off coefficient | 2 |
| Maximum attempts | 10 |
| Non-retryable | NoPackageInForce |
| Applies to | EvaluateRulesActivity, RecordAndApplyActivity |

**Versioning.** Each worker carries the build ID of its build, so a new build takes new workflows while the old build drains; an in-place code change uses `Workflow.getVersion(changeId, DEFAULT_VERSION, 1)`; every build replays the recorded histories under the replay gate of RWB-E2-040 before release. The build ID format and the versioning policy are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0725; ASM-1273).

**Called in-process, not over REST**

```java
RuleResult RuleEvaluator.evaluate(String packageCode, Object facts, LocalDate onDate);   // rwb-case, embedded kit
void WorkflowGateway.signal(String workflowId, String signal, Object payload);            // rwb-case, workflow kit
```

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The reference workflow is started by the harness, never by a Schedule; the Schedules of rwb-case belong to their own stories (DP-10).

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The skeleton owns no table: it writes through the local decision-record library and the P3 case state service, both of which write schema rwb_case, and the outbox, inbox and idempotency objects are library objects of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON created in rwb_case. No table of another service is read or written (DP-01).

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

None. The workflow test uses TestWorkflowEnvironment with time skipping and the in-process contract mocks of the published interfaces; there is no WireMock mapping, because the skeleton calls no REST operation. The rwb-decision mock answers the package and rule facts named in the acceptance criteria.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 0 consumed | No path and no client; the harness starts the workflow |
| Kafka | 0 published by the workflow, 0 consumed | DecisionRecorded is published by the local library; case events arrive as a signal through the outbox relay |
| Temporal | 1 workflow, 2 activities, 0 Schedules | ReferenceCaseWorkflow, EvaluateRulesActivity, RecordAndApplyActivity on `rwb-case` |
| File | None | The synthetic fixture is a build input, not runtime data |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case`, module `workflow.reference`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.workflow.reference` and `.activities`; the relay in `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.case.outbox.reference`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | `recovery.<table>` or "recovery schema" | Owner's schema `rwb_case`; the skeleton writes through the case state service and the record library, never another service's table | none |
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library in the same transaction, plus `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the two legacy activities merge into RecordAndApply | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-04 | RuleEvaluator, Drools | Embedded Drools kit inside EvaluateRulesActivity; the package comes from rwb-decision as a model | H RWB-PLT-E1072-CON (the registry side is RWB-P7-E1073) |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | No ACE read in the skeleton: the facts come from the synthetic fixture; an Epic 3 copy reads ACE data through the rwb-source-data contract, never a view | none |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case for the case status and route lists with their versions | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library, CloudEvents envelope, the relay as an `OutboxConsumer` | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ReferenceCaseWorkflow | Workflow (test-only scope) | Waits for CaseEvent, calls the two activities in order, completes; deterministic code only |
| EvaluateRulesActivity | Activity | Calls `RuleEvaluator.evaluate` and returns RuleResult; reads no case row and writes none |
| RecordAndApplyActivity | Activity | The local decision-record library and the P3 case state service in one transaction, plus the DecisionRecorded outbox row |
| CaseEventSignal | Record | eventId, caseId, eventType, occurredAt, idempotencyKey, synthetic |
| ReferenceCaseInput | Record | caseId, packageCode, businessDate, synthetic |
| CaseEventSignalRelay | Outbox consumer | Reads the delivery, calls `WorkflowGateway.signal`, leaves the event for the next attempt on failure |
| SyntheticCaseGuard | Service | Refuses a workflow input that is not marked synthetic, before any activity |
| ActivityRetryPolicies | Configuration | Initial 1 s, back-off 2, maximum 10 attempts, non-retryable NoPackageInForce |
| ReferenceCaseFixture | Test fixture | Synthetic case row and RESTRUCTURE version for DEV and SIT (GAP-0724) |
| ReferenceCaseWorkflowTest | Test | Time skipping, signal order, idempotency, failure, replay and flag tests |
| No controller | - | The skeleton has no endpoint and no route on gateway-bff |

**Database and migrations.** No migration and no new table. The skeleton writes the local decision record through RWB-PLT-E1027-CON and the case route state through the P3 case state service, both inside schema rwb_case. The fixture is a JSON seed in the test resources, inserted and removed by the harness; it is never part of a release.

**Configuration and reference data**

- Task queue `rwb-case` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, and workflow ID prefix `ref-case-` for the skeleton; Epic 3 case workflows use `case-{caseId}` on the same queue.
- Retry values of section 12.5 as configuration, not code.
- Feature switches `rwb.p3.temporal` and `rwb.p3.drools`, read through the platform parameters contract.
- The RESTRUCTURE version and rule R-RES-04 are owned by RW-COE and governed in rwb-decision; the skeleton references them, never edits them.
- Reference lists LOV-CASE-STATUS and LOV-ROUTE through the reference-data contract of rwb-case.

**Build steps**

1. Define ReferenceCaseWorkflow, ReferenceCaseInput and CaseEventSignal; test that no activity runs before the signal (AC1).
2. Build EvaluateRulesActivity against the embedded kit; test the rule ID, the package version and the NoPackageInForce path (AC1, AC4).
3. Build RecordAndApplyActivity with the idempotency key; test the rollback when the record write fails and the retry after a commit-then-timeout (AC2, AC3).
4. Add ActivityRetryPolicies and the NoPackageInForce do-not-retry rule (AC2, AC4).
5. Build CaseEventSignalRelay and test the Temporal-unavailable path with the outbox delivery, including the PENDING to RETRYING to DELIVERED sequence (AC5).
6. Add SyntheticCaseGuard and the flag checks; test AC6 and the workflow ID prefix.
7. Add the replay test with a recorded history and a later package version, and the `getVersion` change case (AC4).
8. Run the contract-fake profile so the story builds before rwb-decision and the platform stories are in SIT.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.p3.temporal`. Off: no worker on `rwb-case`, ReferenceCaseWorkflow is not deployed and the relay does not run; outbox deliveries stay PENDING. Nothing else changes; the switch does not affect any other workflow of the service.

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, a recorded reference history replays with the same path and no rule evaluation, the workflow ID prefix is enforced, and SIT shows no live case read or written by the skeleton.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code. Action text, owner role and timer come from rule packages; retry values are configuration.
- No personal data in logs, tests, workflow history, search attributes or prompts. Payloads are encrypted by PdpaPayloadCodec and the reference case is synthetic.
- No read of another service's tables and no ACE view: the facts of the reference come from the synthetic fixture, and an Epic 3 copy reads ACE data only through the rwb-source-data contract (DP-01, DP-05).
- Workflow code is deterministic: no clock, random or I/O; every call to Drools, the record library or the case state service is in an activity.
- The decision record and the state change are one transaction; no state row exists without its record, and a failed record leaves nothing moved.
- Every activity is idempotent by the event key; a retry never writes a second record or a second state row.
- The skeleton is test-only: it never runs against a live case, never writes a non-synthetic case row, and its workflow ID never starts `case-`.
- The skeleton declares no REST path and no gateway-bff route; it writes no topic of its own and publishes no event of its own.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-043 for rwb-decision — the collection of `DecisionRecorded` into the central decision ledger, the daily chain check and the two decision-log reads. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **developer of `rwb-decision` and the internal auditor (RW-AUDIT) who has to prove the order of a reference-case step**, I want **the central decision ledger of `rwb-decision` to collect every `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` fact of `rwb.decision-record.v1` into `decision_log_entry` — one entry per reference-case step, append only and hash chained, deduplicated by event ID and idempotency key, keeping the rule ID and the rule version exactly as the owning service pinned them — inside the five-minute collection target, with JOB-14 checking the chain every day at 02:00 and reporting a break to Compliance the same day, and with the two reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` and `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log/{entryId}`**, so that **the pattern "evaluate in an activity, record, then act" is provable from the ledger alone, and no decision of the reference run is a claim without a record**.

Inside `rwb-decision` this is the ledger half of the legacy story RWB-E2-043:

- Service `rwb-decision`, schema `rwb_decision`, REST base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, topic `rwb.decision.events.v1` with event names `rwb.decision.<Event>.v1`, Temporal task queue `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` through the decision-record library of DP-03.
- One deliverable and nothing else: (a) the ingest of `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` into `decision_log_entry`, the continuous consumption Arch v5 slide 44 calls JOB-13; (b) the inbox dedupe by event ID and by idempotency key, with the repeat counted for R-UNI-40; (c) the hash chain — `chain_seq`, `prev_hash` and `entry_hash` over the canonical form, a first `prev_hash` of 64 zeros, append only; (d) the rule ID and rule version held exactly as the fact carried them, with no lookup of the version in force; (e) the five-minute collection target of Arch v5 slide 28 and the completeness gap report; (f) JOB-14 at 02:00 on the `rwb-decision` queue, with a break reported to Compliance the same day (NFR-035); (g) the two reads API-P7-006 and API-P7-007; and (h) one entry per decision step of the reference run `ref-case-RW-2026-000777`.
- **Not this story:** the Temporal worker, `ReferenceCaseWorkflow`, `EvaluateRulesActivity`, `RecordAndApplyActivity`, the `CaseEventSignalRelay`, the synthetic case fixture and the replay gate — RWB-P3-E2043-APP and RWB-P3-E2043-OPS, with the replay gate of RWB-E2-040. This story names them only to say who writes the facts it collects, and it registers no worker, no workflow and no activity of the reference run.
- **Not this story:** the embedded Drools kit, which is RWB-PLT-E1072-CON's (DP-04). The story reads the `ruleId` and the `packageVersion` a fact carries and evaluates no package.
- **Not this story:** the cross-service proof. RWB-ITG-E2043-ITG publishes the case event, follows it into the workflow and reads this ledger beside the workflow history.
- The package RESTRUCTURE version "RES-2026.12" and rule R-RES-04 are the registry's (RWB-P7-E2042-APP), under the contract C RWB-P7-E1073-CON; this story records their identifiers and changes neither.
- The strict-mode acknowledgement before a point of no return and the daily seal of the ledger hash to write-once storage are named by Arch v5 slides 14 and 28 and sit outside this story, on the ledger built here (GAP-1310; ASM-2320).
- The decision code, the final call values and the approval level are reference data of `rwb-case` read through DP-07; the value set of LOV-DECISION is not enumerated by any source (GAP-1306; ASM-2316).
- The database login is the per-service login of DP-02. Its name is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1307; ASM-2317); this story uses the phrase "the rwb-decision login (DP-02)" and never the shared monolith login.

The values carried from the legacy story are unchanged: the synthetic case `RW-2026-000777` with status IN_PROGRESS and route state IN_FCR_QUEUE, the reference workflow ID `ref-case-RW-2026-000777`, the case events `EV-CASE-0777-01` to `EV-CASE-0777-05`, the event keys `CASE_EVENT:EV-CASE-0777-01` to `CASE_EVENT:EV-CASE-0777-05`, package RESTRUCTURE version "RES-2026.12" in force from 2026-12-01 and "RES-2027.01" from 2027-01-01, rule R-RES-04 moving IN_FCR_QUEUE on CASE_PICKED_UP to WITH_FCR_OFFICER, the retry policy of 1 s, back-off 2 and 10 attempts, and the messages MSG-P7-003, MSG-P7-009 and MSG-P4-002. The ledger's own two values are the five-minute collection target of Arch v5 slide 28 and the 02:00 chain check of JOB-14 (Arch v5 slide 44). The chain facts are the ones FSD P7 v3 A2.1 writes for the decision log: the append-only trigger `tr_declog_append_only`, the missing `UPDATE` and `DELETE` grant for the service login, `entry_hash` as the SHA-256 of the entry's canonical form, the first `prev_hash` of 64 zeros, and a check that holds count 100 and last `chain_seq` 100 on a chain of 100 entries.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy skeleton showed the order inside one module: the signalling relay, the evaluator, the decision-log writer and the case state service were called in process, against one schema and one transaction manager. Architecture v5 keeps the order and moves the record: each of the 19 services writes its own decision record in its own schema, in the same transaction as the state change, hash-linked to the record before it, and publishes `DecisionRecorded` on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (Arch v5 slides 20 and 28). `rwb-decision` consumes that topic into the central decision ledger. The order is therefore only provable if the collection is right: one entry per step, the rule and version untouched, no duplicate, no silent gap, and a chain a daily check can defend in an audit.

This story is that collection. It carries ADR-022 (a local decision record plus a central ledger) and the part of ADR-009 the target changes, and it makes the measure of RWB-E2-043 true: the pattern is one order, and the ledger shows it. Without the ledger, three of the legacy criteria degrade into statements about a workflow history that retention eventually removes — that the rule version was pinned at evaluation time, that the record exists before the state move, and that a retry wrote one decision and not two. With the ledger they are statements about an append-only, hash-chained row an auditor reaches through an operation of this service.

The realignment changes the mechanism, not the business rule:

1. The in-process `DecisionLogWriter` of the monolith becomes the decision-record library and its topic (DP-03): the owning service writes its record in its own transaction and publishes `DecisionRecorded`, and this story appends it to the central ledger with the append-only rule and the chain of FSD P7 v3 A2.1 (Arch v5 slide 28).
2. The order inside the workflow becomes an order in the ledger: the fact carries the rule and the version chosen at evaluation time, so a late collection still shows the version that decided and a later promotion cannot rewrite an earlier entry (R-UNI-38; design slides 6, 15 and 27).
3. The nightly copy of the log to a data lake is gone with the data lake (DP-17); the collection is continuous Kafka keyed by the case, with the five-minute target of Arch v5 slide 28 (JOB-13), and the daily anchor of the ledger hash to write-once storage is the separate step of that slide.
4. The Quartz job that walked the log becomes JOB-14, a Temporal Schedule at 02:00 on the `rwb-decision` queue with the overlap policy SKIP and the catch-up window of the job map (DP-10; Arch v5 slide 44).
5. The one decision-log path of the monolith becomes two operations on the service base (DP-13), reached through the gateway-bff composite route the decision-log screen uses (DP-19) and guarded by the decision-log baseline's authorise path (DP-11).
6. The rule ID and the rule version are no longer read from a catalogue at display time: they are columns of the entry written from the fact, so an entry explains itself even when the package has since been superseded (DP-04, without an evaluation).

This story meets REQ-DRI-001 and REQ-CWC-016 on the collection side, REQ-DRI-005 as the reason both the owning service's transaction and the append fail closed, and REQ-DRI-007 through the retry and exception behaviour of the outbox consumer. It carries NFR-033, NFR-035 and the principle that no action stands without its record (R-UNI-39).
