No row of `agent_run`, `agent_feedback`, `agent_policy` or `agent_prompt` is copied into `rwb_decision`: the run facts arrive on the P10 contract and the feedback row is `rwb-agent`'s, which stores this story's record reference in its own column. No row of `recovery_case`, `task`, `timer` or `queue` is written, and no role, scope or masking row is read from `rwb_access`. Field IDs are those in the Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Owner `rwb-decision` (P7); base `/api/recovery/decision/v1`. The two reads are API-P7-006 and API-P7-007 of TSD P7 v2 T-A.1; the append on the same collection is the write path DP-03 needs and is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1294; ASM-2298). The request and answer field set of the three operations is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1294; ASM-2298).

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/decision-log` | Append one decision record for one verdict of an agent output: validate, chain and write, then answer 201 with the record; a repeated key answers 200 with the first record | Service identity only, SY-AGENT and SY-DECLOG (TSD P7 v2 T6.1, right C); one hop from `rwb-agent` with a 2 s timeout | Idempotency-Key header, the run reference and the item key, kept on the ledger row |
| GET | `/decision-log` | API-P7-006: search the ledger by case, decision, rule, approver and date, one page at a time | Decision log, right R, scope applied through the authorise answer and the case read of P3 | Not applicable, read only |
| GET | `/decision-log/{entryId}` | API-P7-007: read one record with its inputs, its versions, its final call, its reason and its two hashes | Decision log, right R, scope applied | Not applicable, read only |

The append request this story assumes carries `caseId`, `runId`, `itemKey` ("SUMMARY"), `verdict`, `reason`, `idempotencyKey` and `decidedAt`; the agent code, the agent and prompt version, the model version and the data date are read from the run and not from the request. The DecisionRecord answer carries `id`, `caseId`, `decisionCode`, `agentVersion`, `modelVersion`, `inputsRef`, `recommendation`, `finalCall`, `overrideReason`, `approverUserId`, `decidedAt`, `chainSeq`, `prevHash` and `entryHash`. Both sets are the placeholder until the contract baseline is agreed (GAP-1294; ASM-2298).

Errors: 401 no session; 403 the role holds no Decision log right (MSG-P4-002); 404 the record or the case is absent or out of scope (MSG-P4-003); 409 the append repeats a key with a different body (MSG-GEN-004); 422 a reason is missing (MSG-P7-005) or a code, a final call or a version is not a value of its list (MSG-P7-009); 503 the record was not written (MSG-P7-003). Every error is an RFC 9457 problem response with `messageId` set.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs/{runId}` | P10 rwb-agent, on RWB-P10-E2028-CON | The run facts the record names: agent code, agent and prompt version, model version, autonomy mode, status, confidence and data as of; faked, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | The owner, team, region and product group the scope filter of the ledger read is applied to; faked, one hop |
| POST | `/api/recovery/access/v1/authorise` | P4 rwb-access | The cached decision of the Decision log right R and the scope of the reader behind the two reads; faked |

The three operations are the P10, P3 and P4 rows of the Ownership Map and of Architecture v5 slides 14, 16 and 41. Their request and answer shape is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1294; ASM-2298). The two reads declare the Decision log right R on the operation, take the right and the scope from the authorise answer and apply the scope filter to the case read, as ASM-2303 reads it. DP-08, which would add the guard library and the authorise contract as named dependencies, is not among the patterns of this key, so the authorise answer is consumed against its published contract or its fake and the dependency is carried in GAP-1295.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` (EV-08) | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7, published by this service | entryId | record ID, case ID, decision code D6, agent version, model version, inputs reference, final call, decided at, chain sequence, entry hash |

The event is written to the outbox in the same transaction as the record and relayed with the CloudEvents 1.0 envelope by the outbox relay of the platform (DP-09); the shared topic carries its own name, so the event of the catalogue is published there and not on the service topic. `rwb-decision` itself and `rwb-reporting` consume it, as event 08 of Architecture v5 slide 42 names them. No event carries a name, an e-mail address, a mobile number, an account number or the summary text.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. This story consumes no event: the verdict arrives on the append request and the run facts on the run read. The inbox objects of DP-09 are created in the schema by the service baseline and this story writes none.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

None of this story's own. The append is one synchronous service operation inside the caller's unit of work, not a workflow, and the ledger read is a query. `rwb-decision` holds `ApprovalWorkflow` of the workflow kit and its Schedules for other slices of the service; this story starts no workflow, signals none, and registers no activity and no Schedule on the `rwb-decision` queue. The chain check JOB-14 at 02:00 is the decision-log store's and the metrics run JOB-15 is `rwb-reporting`'s (Architecture v5 slide 44).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The metrics run JOB-15 at 01:30 is the reporting extract of `rwb-reporting` and runs on its own trigger; the chain check JOB-14 at 02:00 belongs to the decision-log store slice of this service; this story adds neither and polls nothing.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

| Table | Owner | Use in this story |
|---|---|---|
| `decision_log_entry` | P7 (`rwb_decision`) | The record of the verdict: the code, the versions, the inputs reference, the recommendation, the final call, the reason, the hashes and the chain sequence; written once and read |
| outbox library table | PLT library, created in `rwb_decision` | The `DecisionRecorded` row (DP-09) |
| `idempotency_key` | PLT library, created in `rwb_decision` | The stored answer of a repeated append (DP-09) |

Not owned and never read by this story: `agent_run`, `agent_policy`, `agent_prompt`, `agent_feedback` and `agent_evaluation` (P10), `recovery_case` (P3), `delegation_limit`, `role`, `permission` and `masking_rule` (P4). The run arrives on its contract, the case on its read, and the authorise answer on its own; no foreign key crosses a schema and no row of another service is copied (DP-01). The `approval` and `rule_package` tables are this service's but another story's, and this story writes neither.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, module `ledger/agentverdict`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision.agentverdict`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the core of the slice: the legacy `DecisionLogWriter` of the monolith becomes the local decision-record library of this service, which writes the record, the hash link and the outbox row in one transaction and publishes on the shared topic, so every verdict of an agent output has one record in the ledger that this service owns. DP-07 is where the decision code and the verdict list live: LOV-DECISION and the verdict list are read through the reference-data contract of `rwb-case` with the version in force, and neither is a constant here. DP-09 is the outbox and the CloudEvents envelope of the one published fact; the inbox objects are part of the service baseline and this story consumes no event. DP-10 is carried and not used: the metrics run JOB-15 at 01:30 belongs to `rwb-reporting` and the chain check JOB-14 at 02:00 to the decision-log store slice, so the Schedule stays with the service that owns it and this story registers no workflow and no Schedule. DP-13 puts the three operations on `/api/recovery/decision/v1`; DP-15 puts the migration in the per-service Flyway sequence of `rwb_decision`; DP-19 is the composite route through which the two ledger reads are reached by the decision-log query screen of the service, and this story adds no route and serves no screen of its own.

The platform H dependencies of the table (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, H RWB-PLT-N001-CON) and the C dependency that DP-07 brings with it (C RWB-P3-E1043-CON) are not in the metadata rows of this story, which name None and RWB-P10-E2028-CON; they are the dependencies the DP table adds and they are recorded in GAP-1295 and ASM-2304. The same row carries the two consumed operations that no pattern names: the P3 case read and the P4 authorise call. None of them blocks the build beyond Day 1: they are platform contracts of waves 0 and 1 and published contracts of other services. The agent contract arrives as the C dependency RWB-P10-E2028-CON, and DP-20, which would name an agent contract of its own, is not among the patterns of the key.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| VerdictRecordController | Controller | `POST /decision-log` with the shape and idempotency validation, the 201 and 200 answers, and the problem mapping for 401, 409, 422 and 503 |
| DecisionRecordController | Controller | `GET /decision-log` and `GET /decision-log/{entryId}` with the guard, the scope, the page and the problem mapping for 401, 403, 404 and 503 |
| VerdictValidationService | Service | Reads LOV-DECISION and the verdict list with the version in force, and refuses a code or a final call that is not a value of its list with MSG-P7-009 |
| AgentFactClient | Adapter | The run read of RWB-P10-E2028-CON, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker; takes the agent and prompt version from the owner of the run |
| ChainWriter | Service | Reads the head of the chain under the append lock, computes the entry hash over the canonical form and builds the previous hash and the sequence number |
| DecisionRecordAppendService | Service | One `RecordAndApply` transaction: the record, the chain link and the outbox row, or nothing; maps the failure to 503 with MSG-P7-003 |
| DecisionRecordRepository | Repository | `decision_log_entry` in `rwb_decision`, with the unique key of the chain sequence and of the idempotency key |
| DecisionRecordQueryService | Service | The ledger page and the single record, with the scope filter applied to the case read |
| AccessCheckClient | Client | The authorise answer behind the two reads, with the cached decision of the right |
| CaseScopeClient | Client | The P3 case read that gives the owner, team, region and product group of the scope filter |
| DecisionRecordOutbox | Library use | The outbox row of `DecisionRecorded` in the same transaction as the record (DP-09) |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `decision_log_entry` and the outbox and idempotency objects of the library, all in schema `rwb_decision`; reads no other schema.
- The `decision_log_entry` baseline, its append-only trigger and its grants belong to the decision-log store slice of this service (legacy RWB-E1-008) and are not rebuilt here.
- Migration in this story, in the per-service Flyway sequence of DP-15: `V2028_1__decision_agent_verdict.sql` adds the unique key `ux_declog_chain_seq ON decision_log_entry (chain_seq)`, the unique key `ux_declog_idem ON decision_log_entry (idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL`, the index `ix_declog_case_decided ON decision_log_entry (case_id, decided_at DESC)` for the ledger read of one case, and the foreign key of `corrects_entry_id` to `decision_log_entry (id)`.
- No row is updated and no row is deleted by this story; the update path of the store does not exist and the delete path does not exist.

**Configuration and reference data**

- LOV-DECISION and the verdict list ACCEPTED, CORRECTED and REJECTED are read through the reference-data contract of DP-07 with the version in force; the code D6 and the three final calls are values of those lists and never constants in code (ASM-2299).
- The reason codes of a correction and of a rejection are reference data; the list and its values are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1294; ASM-2300), so the story validates the presence and the length of the reason and not a set of codes it does not have.
- The reason length, 1,000 characters, is the column length of `override_reason` and of the legacy request (DF-DEC-013).
- The feature switch of the legacy capability, `rwb.agent.intake-l1`, stays with RWB-P10-E2028-APP and is not read here: a record that could be switched off would break R-UNI-39, so the append is never gated by a flag (ASM-2305).
- The `rwb-decision` login of DP-02, the flyway user and the outbox relay identity are environment configuration and not values of this story.

**Build steps**

1. The migration `V2028_1__decision_agent_verdict.sql` with the two unique keys, the index and the foreign key; test that a repeated chain sequence and a repeated idempotency key are refused by the constraints (BR8, BR10, X9).
2. `ChainWriter` with the head read, the canonical form and the entry hash; test the seeded chain of 100 records and the first record with the previous hash of 64 zeros (AC1, AC3).
3. `VerdictValidationService` with the two lists of DP-07 and the reason rule; tests for AC4, X1 and X6.
4. `DecisionRecordAppendService` and the fail-closed transaction; tests for AC1, AC5 and TC-E2-028-11.
5. `AgentFactClient` over the run read with the timeout and the breaker, and the contract-fake run of the whole fact before `rwb-agent` is live (AC1, AC2).
6. `DecisionRecordController` and `DecisionRecordQueryService` with the authorise answer, the scope filter and the page; tests for AC7 and TC-E2-028-10.
7. The idempotency path: a repeated append returns the first record and the chain gains no link; tests for AC6.
8. The privacy test: the record, the event payload and the log entries carry no name, e-mail address, mobile number, national identity number or account number (AC1, AC2).

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P10-E2028-CON stay green, and a SIT day shows one D6 record per verdict of the intake summary with the agent version "INTAKE@P2/PR3", a chain that verifies from its first entry, one `DecisionRecorded` event per record, no record and no feedback row when the record cannot be written, one record for a repeated verdict, and no personal data in any record, event or log.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message | Where it is produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-005 | A correction or a rejection carries no reason | Enter the reason you are not following the recommendation. | This story, on the append |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on the append transaction |
| MSG-P7-009 | The decision code, the final call or a required version is not a value it must have | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-1294; ASM-2298) | This story, on the validation; the FSD names only the identifier and the field |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The same verdict arrives again for the run and item, or the record changed | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. | `rwb-agent`, on the feedback; this story returns the first record |
| MSG-P4-002 | The reader holds no Decision log right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, through the authorise answer |
| MSG-P4-003 | The record or the case is outside the reader's scope | This case is not in your scope. | This story, through the authorise answer and the case read |
| MSG-P1-001 | The summary was built on data older than the business date | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. | `rwb-agent`, on the panel; this story records the data date and produces no message |

MSG-P7-005, MSG-P7-003 and MSG-P1-001 are copied unchanged from the legacy story RWB-E2-028 section 14; MSG-GEN-004, MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 are the platform messages the feedback operation and the authorise contract carry; MSG-P7-009 is named by FSD P7 v3 A2.2.4.3 and its text is not written out in any source this story may read, so the placeholder stands. Thai text for each message follows decision DL10.

No screen is built in this story. The record is read through the two operations of section 12.1 and shown by SCR-38 Decision log query, which is the decision-log query slice of this service and not this story; the composite route of DP-19 is used and not extended.

| `POST /decision-log` | 200 Already recorded | The first record of the same run and item, with its own reference; nothing new is written |
| `POST /decision-log` | 422 No reason, or a value out of its list | MSG-P7-005 or MSG-P7-009, naming the field, and nothing written |
| `POST /decision-log` | 503 Record not written | MSG-P7-003 and nothing written; the caller's feedback is rolled back |
| `GET /decision-log` | One page | The records of a case in scope with code D6, agent version, final call and decided time |
| `GET /decision-log/{entryId}` | One record | Code D6, agent version "INTAKE@P2/PR3", final call, reason, approver, decided time, previous hash and entry hash |
| `GET /decision-log`, `GET /decision-log/{entryId}` | 403 or 404 | MSG-P4-002 for a role without the right, MSG-P4-003 for a case out of scope |

The screen field list, the composite route specification and the field-level masking belong to RWB-PLT-N001-CON and to the stories that own each screen.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the decision code, the verdict list, the reason codes, the message texts and the data date are reference-data rows, message-standard rows or facts of the run; nothing of them is a constant here.
- No personal data in the record, the event payload, the trail, the tests or the prompts: case and run identifiers, a decision code, a version, a final call, a reason, a user reference and dates only; the summary text and its masking tokens never enter this service.
- No read of another service's tables (DP-01): the run arrives on its contract, the case on its read and the authorise answer on its own; no `agent_run`, `agent_feedback`, `recovery_case`, `delegation_limit`, `role` or `permission` row is copied into `rwb_decision`.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views: this story reads no ACE data at all.
- One recorder and no mover: this story changes no case status, no task, no timer, no run and no summary, so a record can never move a case.
- No record without its event and no event without its record: the record, the chain link and the outbox row commit in one transaction, and a failure changes nothing and leaves the caller's feedback unwritten (R-UNI-39).
- Append only and hash chained: no update path and no delete path exist, the sequence number is never reused, and a wrong record is corrected by a new record naming the one it corrects (REQ-DRI-002).
- One record per run and item: the idempotency key and the unique key make a second record impossible, and a repeated call returns the first record.
- One base, one topic, one queue: `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, `rwb.decision.events.v1` and `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, with the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` for the record event; no story in this key declares another service's base or topic as its own (DP-13).
- One hop and 2 s on every call, with a breaker per downstream; a missing answer never produces a record from a guessed version or a guessed code.
- The record path is never gated by a feature flag and never skipped for speed: a verdict without its record is a defect, not a degraded mode.

##### 19. Out of scope

- The agent policy, the prompt and its version, the agent run, the stored summary and the gap flags, the guardrails, the masked model call, the autonomy mode and its change, the panel "Agent summary" and its six states, the feedback row, the metrics job JOB-15 and SCR-46 Agent monitor: RWB-P10-E2028-APP, with the contract, the event schemas and the fakes in RWB-P10-E2028-CON.
- The case record, the case status, the case list, the stale warning on the panel and the case scope decision: RWB-P3-E1035-APP and `rwb-case`; the panel states are `rwb-agent`'s and the scope answer is `rwb-access`'s.
- The role model, the scope, the masking policy and the authorise answer: `rwb-access` (P4); this story consumes the answer and holds no rule of it.
- The decision-log store of this service — the append-only trigger, the grants, the chain verifier and the daily chain check JOB-14 at 02:00: the decision-log store slice (legacy RWB-E1-008) and the service baseline.
- The approval routing, the `ApprovalWorkflow`, the decision center screens SCR-10, SCR-11 and SCR-38 and the rule package registry: the other slices of `rwb-decision`.
- The acceptance and correction measure by segment and its extract: JOB-15 of `rwb-reporting` and the measure of RWB-P10-E2028-APP.
- The daily ledger seal to immutable storage and the lake copy: the seal is another slice's and the lake is removed (DP-17).
- The integration harness and the `-ITG` copies of the test cases: RWB-ITG-E2028-ITG.
- The ACE DB story, the infrastructure story and the deployment story of this legacy key: their own DB, INF and OPS stories; the Helm chart, the Kafka subscription values, the metrics, the alerts and the runbook of this capability are the OPS story's.

The names of the level holders and substitutes and the parameter values of the DoA are data of their owners, and no date is changed by this story: the release 31 January 2027 is copied unchanged and stays tentative.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: deployment slice of RWB-E2-028 for rwb-agent, split from the legacy key. This story deploys the L1 intake capability and builds no behaviour: the `rwb-agent` api deployment and worker deployment from one chart with one values file per environment, the pre-deploy migration job of `V10_008__agent_feedback.sql` in the service's own Flyway sequence on the `rwb_agent` login and schema (DP-15), the Temporal worker on the task queue `rwb-agent` in namespace `rwb-recovery` with the release build ID on the version set, the registration of the event-started `AgentRunWorkflow` with no Schedule for a cadence (DP-10), the topic `rwb.agent.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics and the consumer groups of its consumers (DP-09), the rights of the `rwb.decision-record.v1` record (DP-03), the reference-data and freshness reads wired by contract (DP-07), the feature switch of the legacy `rwb.agent.intake-l1` flag, the secrets and the egress, the probes and the KEDA scaling, the dashboards and the alerts for the L1 acceptance and override rates, the publication of the two operations behind the gateway-bff route (DP-19), the runbook, the rollback and the capacity plan. It deploys no Schedule and no job table, because the run is event-started. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **platform engineer**, I want **rwb-agent deployed from the service template with its api and worker deployments, its `agent_feedback` migration job on the `rwb_agent` login and schema, its probes, its Temporal worker and KEDA scaling on the `rwb-agent` task queue in namespace `rwb-recovery`, the event-started `AgentRunWorkflow` registered with no Schedule for a cadence, the topic `rwb.agent.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics and its consumer groups, the rights of the decision-record feed, the reference-data and freshness reads wired by contract, the feature switch, the secrets and egress, the dashboards and alerts that carry the L1 acceptance and override rates, the publication of the two operations behind the gateway-bff route, the runbook, the rollback and the capacity plan**, so that **the L1 intake capability is produced, watched and repeatable in every environment, and an operator can see and act on a fallen acceptance rate, a rising override rate, a `.dlt` message, a worker backlog and a failed migration without reading code**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy story depends on a scheduler chain, a shared job table, an in-process mode loader and a panel that called the service directly. In the target a service is a Helm release built by one pipeline with its own schema, login, topic and queue (DP-02, DP-09, DP-10, DP-15), the panel is reached only through the gateway-bff route (DP-19), and the decision record leaves through the local library and the shared record topic (DP-03). Deployment is therefore part of the capability:

- Without the migration job on the `rwb_agent` login there is no `agent_feedback` table, and a verdict has nowhere to be stored or counted.
- Without the worker on `rwb-agent` in namespace `rwb-recovery` and without the event-started registration, a new case starts no run and the panel has nothing to show.
- Without the topic, its retry and `.dlt` topics and the rights of its consumers, the monitor and the reporting projections have no feed and the acceptance rate of a segment lags a day behind.
- Without the alerts on the acceptance and override rates, a segment that should drop back to shadow keeps being served at L1 and nobody sees it.
- Without the route publication, the two operations exist but no screen can reach them.

This story makes the capability observable and repeatable so the app story can be proven in SIT and the on-call rota can operate it. It deploys and watches; it changes no business behaviour and holds no business value.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template, the chart skeleton and the pipeline are available (RWB-PLT-TPL, RWB-PLT-LIB), and the Temporal workflow kit with namespace `rwb-recovery` is in place (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON).
- The Kafka event platform provisions topics with a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic (RWB-PLT-EVT, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON).
- The ACE database administrator has created schema `rwb_agent` and its login, with rights on `rwb_agent` only and no grant on any other schema (DP-02).
- The platform error envelope, the message catalogue and the alert routing are in force, so an alert carries a message ID where one exists.
- The contract baseline of RWB-P10-E2028-CON is published: the two operations, the answer and request members, the eligibility answer, the record mapping, the two events, the registration and the four fakes.
- The reference-data contract of RWB-P3-E1043-CON, the case record contract of RWB-P3-E1035-CON, the decision-log entry read of RWB-P7-E1027-CON and the freshness read of rwb-source-data are published, so the release can start against their contracts and their fakes.
- The monitor read of RWB-P10-E2031-APP is known, because it counts the acceptance and override rates this release alerts on.
- The three environments DEV, SIT and UAT exist with the parameter scope of LOV-ENVIRONMENT.
- The per-service login name the chart references is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0624; ASM-0916); the chart references it through a secret and never a literal.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (§R5.7).

##### 4. Flow

1. The pipeline builds one image and one chart version from one commit, runs the unit, component and contract tests, scans the image and its dependencies, and publishes the chart.
2. The chart deploys the api deployment and the worker deployment with the `rwb_agent` login reference and the platform secret references, and the pre-deploy migration job that runs the per-service Flyway sequence and applies `V10_008__agent_feedback.sql` before the rollout is marked ready (DP-15; AC1, AC2).
3. The provisioning step registers the Temporal task queue `rwb-agent` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, checks that the worker polls only that queue with the release build ID on the version set, and sets the KEDA minimum and maximum from the values file (DP-10; AC3).
4. The registration step registers the event-started `AgentRunWorkflow` with `ResolveIntakeMode` and `RecordIntakeFeedback`, subscribes it to `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` through the service's own consumer group, and asserts that no Schedule exists for the capability, because a run starts from an event and a verdict from a person (DP-10; AC4).
5. The provisioning step creates or verifies the topic `rwb.agent.events.v1` with its retry topic and its `.dlt` topic, the publish right of rwb-agent, the publish right of the decision-record library on `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the consume right of rwb-agent on `rwb.case.events.v1`, and the consume rights of the four consumers of the agent topic on it, each of which belongs to its own release (DP-03, DP-09; AC5).
6. The configuration step wires the seven lists through the reference-data contract and the business date through the freshness read; no list value and no policy value is written into a values file (DP-07; AC6).
7. The secret and egress step binds the database credential, the Kafka client credential and the Temporal mTLS material from the platform secret store, and opens egress only to the database, the Kafka brokers, the Temporal frontend, the gateway-bff route and the model endpoint the agent platform calls (AC6).
8. The feature switch of the legacy `rwb.agent.intake-l1` flag is wired to the platform flag library: off by default in DEV and outside the L1 segment, on in SIT and UAT only after the smoke read answers (§R3 default ruling: feature flags to the platform library; BR12).
9. The dashboards are published: runs started, completed and failed by mode, L1 acceptance rate and override rate by segment and business date, fallback rate, tool read failures, `.dlt` messages, feed lag, worker backlog, refused reads and the migration state (AC8).
10. The alerts are wired to the acceptance rate below its floor, the override rate above its ceiling, the `.dlt` route, the worker backlog, the failed migration and the stale business date, each linked to one runbook entry (AC8).
11. The route publication step registers the two operations behind the gateway-bff pass-through route, one hop, and checks the health of the route target (DP-19; AC9).
12. A smoke step starts one run for a synthetic case in a test namespace against the four fakes, reads the answer through the route, records a verdict, and checks the feedback row, the record, the two events at the outbox, the dashboards and the probes (AC7, AC8).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The migration job of `V10_008__agent_feedback.sql` fails | The deployment stays unready and the pipeline stops; no traffic to the new version | None | AC2 |
| X2 | The readiness probe fails after the start-up window | The pod is removed from the service and the pipeline marks the release failed | None | AC7 |
| X3 | The task queue is not registered, or the worker build ID is not on the version set | The release fails; otherwise a new case would start no run | None | AC3 |
| X4 | A Schedule for the capability is found in the namespace | The pipeline fails the release, because the run is event-started and no cadence belongs to it | None | AC4 |
| X5 | The topic or one of its retry and `.dlt` topics is missing, or a consumer right is absent | The release fails on the provisioning check; a missing `.dlt` is escalated before the first run | None | AC5 |
| X6 | The `rwb_agent` login holds a grant on another schema | The release fails the grant check | None | AC2, AC6 |
| X7 | The acceptance rate of an L1 segment falls below its floor, or the override rate rises above its ceiling | The acceptance or override alert carries the segment, the business date, the rate and the review action | None | AC8 |
| X8 | A message lands in the `.dlt` topic of the agent topic | The `.dlt` alert carries the message type and its registry subject, and one runbook entry opens | None | AC5, AC8 |
| X9 | The business date is stale against the runs of the day | The stale-date alert carries the business date and the data date, and the panel shows MSG-P1-001 | MSG-P1-001 | AC8 |
| X10 | The route publication fails or the route target is not healthy | The release fails and the panel stays unreachable; no partial route is left | None | AC9 |
| X11 | A secret value is found in a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook | The pipeline fails the release on the secret scan | None | AC6 |
| X12 | A role without the Case record right opens the panel | The refused-read count rises on the dashboard with MSG-P4-002 and never pages the on-call rota | MSG-P4-002 | AC8 |

X1 to X12 are the deployment failures of this capability; none is a legacy exception path, because the legacy story carried no chart, no queue, no topic and no alert rule of its own. The legacy business refusals of RWB-E2-028 are the app story's and are not re-tested here.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Uses the chart skeleton, the platform topic provisioning, the workflow kit and the published contracts; no application code is built here |
| Negotiable | Replica counts, resource sizes, alert thresholds, topic partitions and retention and the cluster topology are environment values, not story decisions |
| Valuable | Makes the L1 capability deployable, observable and repeatable, and gives the on-call rota a signal when a segment must drop back to shadow |
| Estimable | One chart, one pipeline stage, one migration job, two deployments, two probes, two provisioning steps, one registration step, one route publication, eight dashboard panels, six alert rules and six runbook entries |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the runbook and the capacity plan |
| Testable | Every criterion tests an artefact: the chart renders, the probes answer, the queue is registered, the registration answers an event, the topic and its rights exist, the alerts fire on a synthetic metric, the route answers within 2 s |


##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | One service, one schema, one login: the release uses the `rwb_agent` login reference and no other service's credential, and the login holds rights on `rwb_agent` only | DP-02; Arch v5 slide 16 |
| BR2 | The migration of `agent_feedback` is a per-service Flyway sequence in schema `rwb_agent` and runs before the rollout is ready | DP-15; RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| BR3 | Every topic has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and the outbox relay publishes within its interval | DP-09; Arch v5 slide 11 |
| BR4 | The intake run is an event-started workflow on the queue `rwb-agent` in namespace `rwb-recovery`; the release registers no Schedule for a cadence | DP-10; Arch v5 slides 16, 31 and 44 |
| BR5 | No environment value is hard-coded: replica counts, resource sizes, probe timings, alert thresholds, the KEDA minimum and maximum and the switch state come from values files and from contracts | DP-07; §R7.2 s17 |
| BR6 | An alert carries a message ID where one exists and links one runbook entry | §R7.2 s14 |
| BR7 | A refused read is counted on the dashboard and never pages the on-call rota | MSG-P4-002 |
| BR8 | The release writes only schema `rwb_agent` and reads other services only through their contracts, one hop and 2 s each | DP-01 |
| BR9 | The decision record leaves through the local library on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; the release provisions the right and no copy, no lake write and no daily file | DP-03 |
| BR10 | The two operations are published only behind the gateway-bff pass-through route, and a screen never reaches the service | DP-19; ADR-019 |
| BR11 | The release carries no Schedule, no job table and no Quartz artefact of any kind | DP-10; Arch v5 slide 44 |
| BR12 | The feature switch `rwb.agent.intake-l1` is a data row of the platform flag library: off, the read answers an empty list and the panel is hidden | §R3 default ruling (feature flags to the platform library) |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Not deployed | Chart published | The image, the chart and the migration job pass the pipeline | Deploying |
| Deploying | Migration job complete and probes healthy | The schema is at the expected version, the worker has polled and both probes answer | Ready |
| Ready | Workflows registered | The registration accepts `AgentRunWorkflow` and a synthetic event starts one run | Ready with the L1 path live |
| Ready | Release superseded | A new chart version is promoted | Rolling |
| Rolling | All pods on the new version | The old ReplicaSet drains and the worker build ID is on the version set | Ready |
| Ready | Migration failed, a probe failed, the registration rejected or a Schedule found | The schema is not at the expected version, a probe is unready, the namespace refused the registration or a cadence Schedule exists | Failed |
| Failed | Rollback | The previous chart version is redeployed and the workflows are re-registered from the previous release | Ready |

The states of a run (ANSWERED, TIMED_OUT, GUARDRAIL_FAILED and the rest of LOV-AGENT-RUN) and the states of a verdict (ACCEPTED, CORRECTED, REJECTED) are the app story's and are only watched here.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| DevOps engineer | Owns the chart, the values files, the pipeline stages, the provisioning and registration steps, the route publication, the dashboards, the alerts and the runbook |
| Platform administrator | Owns the `rwb-recovery` namespace, the topic provisioning and the registration rights |
| ACE database administrator | Owns the `rwb_agent` schema, its login, its grants and the migration job approval |
| Release manager | Approves the promotion of one artefact through the environments |
| On-call operator | Runs the six runbook entries and opens an incident when an acceptance alert, a `.dlt` alert, a backlog alert or a failed migration persists |
| RW-PLATADM | Reads the runs and the metrics in the running service, not in the cluster |
| RW-COE, RW-RISK | Read the acceptance and override rates the alerts speak of |

The per-service login name used by the chart is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0624; ASM-0916); the chart references it through a secret reference and never a literal password.

##### 11. Data

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Deployment values | Image digest, chart version, replica counts, resource requests and limits, probe paths and timings, log level, feature switches, environment name |
| Schema and login | `rwb_agent` and its login, migrated by the per-service Flyway sequence; `agent_feedback` from this release and the library tables |
| Topics | `rwb.agent.events.v1` published with its retry and `.dlt` topics; `rwb.decision-record.v1` for the record; `rwb.case.events.v1` consumed through the service's own group |
| Queue | Temporal task queue `rwb-agent` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, event-started |
| Workflow registration | `AgentRunWorkflow` with `ResolveIntakeMode` and `RecordIntakeFeedback`; no Schedule |
| Parameters and reference data | LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-REGION, LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-FEEDBACK, LOV-DECISION, LOV-AGENT and LOV-AGENT-RUN through the reference-data contract, never held as deployment values |
| Dashboard series | Runs by mode, L1 acceptance rate, override rate, fallback rate, tool read failures, `.dlt` messages, feed lag, worker backlog, refused reads, migration state |
| Runbook entries | Acceptance below floor, override above ceiling, `.dlt` message, worker backlog, failed migration, route unavailable |
| Secrets | The `rwb_agent` login secret, the Kafka client credential and the Temporal mTLS material, all from the platform secret store |

The deployment topology detail (cluster names, node pools, replica counts, resource sizes, zone spread, ingress class, exact probe timings), the alert thresholds, the topic partition count, replication factor and retention, the dashboard series retention, the host, the SKU and the budget of the release are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0624; ASM-0926; ASM-0927; ASM-0928); the chart exposes them as values and this story fixes only their names and the rule that they are not hard-coded.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

The release publishes the two L1 operations behind the gateway-bff pass-through route, one hop: `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` and `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs/{runId}/feedback`, owner rwb-agent (P10), with the rights, the headers and the refusal codes fixed by RWB-P10-E2028-CON. The probes are cluster-internal and are not part of the API surface.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Item | Owner | Deployment need |
|---|---|---|
| `rwb_agent` schema and its login, with the grant list of the service only | ACE database team, on the P10 ownership of the eight agent tables and `agent_feedback` | The migration job, the read, the verdict and the relay run as this identity; no grant on another schema (DP-02, DP-15) |
| ACE PostgreSQL connection and its pool | ACE database team | One connection pool per deployment; the cap is a value of the environment (DP-01) |
| Kafka cluster and topic provisioning, with the retry and `.dlt` convention | Platform event team (RWB-PLT-EVT) | `rwb.agent.events.v1`, its retry and `.dlt` topics, `rwb.decision-record.v1` and `rwb.case.events.v1` (DP-03, DP-09) |
| Temporal cluster, namespace `rwb-recovery` and the task queue `rwb-agent` | Platform workflow team (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON) | The worker, the event-started registration and the worker version set (DP-10) |
| Platform secret store | Platform library (RWB-PLT-LIB) | The database, Kafka and Temporal material, referenced and never inlined |
| Platform feature-flag library | Platform library (§R3 default ruling) | The `rwb.agent.intake-l1` switch as a data row (BR12) |
| gateway-bff route | Edge team (RWB-PLT-N001-CON) | The pass-through route in front of the two operations (DP-19) |
| rwb-case reference-data contract | P3 rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | The seven lists at run time (DP-07) |
| rwb-case case record contract | P3 rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1035-CON) | The case facts, the scope and the case-decision proposal |
| rwb-decision decision-log entry read | P7 rwb-decision (RWB-P7-E1027-CON) | The entry of a verdict, read back for the monitor |
| rwb-source-data freshness read | P1 rwb-source-data | The business date the stale check compares (the `GET /freshness` of Arch v5 slide 15) |
| Model endpoint INT-23 of the agent platform | Enterprise AI interface, through the agent platform of the earlier P10 stories | The egress rule the run needs; no credential of it is held by this release |

Every operation is one hop with a 2 s client budget. No lake credential, no extract file, no data-set job and no job table is consumed or created.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Provisioning |
|---|---|---|
| `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28) and `rwb.agent.AgentFeedbackRecorded.v1` | `rwb.agent.events.v1` | The topic, its retry topic and its `.dlt` topic, the publish right of rwb-agent and the relay interval of the outbox are provisioned and verified by this release; the events belong to the run path and the verdict path of RWB-P10-E2028-APP |
| DecisionRecorded, the decision-record type of the library | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | The topic, its retry and `.dlt` topics and the publish right of the library are verified by this release; the record belongs to the same verdict path (DP-03) |

No daily copy, no extract and no lake write exists: the feed is these topics only.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Consumer group | Provisioning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` (EV-01) | `rwb.case.events.v1` | The consumer group of rwb-agent, created by this release | The consume right, the group and the inbox table of the service; dedupe on the event ID |

The consumer groups of `rwb.agent.events.v1` belong to rwb-decision, rwb-document, rwb-deviation and rwb-reporting (Arch v5 slide 43) and are created by their own releases; this story verifies that each consume right exists and puts the feed lag of the topic on the dashboard, and creates none of them inside rwb-agent (GAP-0624; ASM-0926).

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Deployment element |
|---|---|---|---|
| AgentRunWorkflow | Workflow, event-started, one execution per case and event (no Schedule) | `rwb-agent` in namespace `rwb-recovery` | Worker deployment with the release build ID on the version set; registered by the registration step |
| ResolveIntakeMode | Activity | `rwb-agent` | Registered by the same worker; reads the policy and the case contract |
| RecordIntakeFeedback | Activity (workflow kit, one transaction) | `rwb-agent` | Registered by the same worker; writes the record, the feedback and the outbox row |
| KEDA scaling | Worker scaler | `rwb-agent` | Scales on the task-queue backlog between the minimum and the maximum of the values file |

The release carries no Temporal Schedule: a run starts from `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` and a verdict comes from a person (BR4, BR11).

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The release registers no Temporal Schedule, and a Schedule found in namespace `rwb-recovery` for this capability fails the release: the intake run is event-started and no cadence belongs to it (DP-10; BR4, BR11). The legacy Quartz entry of the intake job is retired with the stage and no job table is deployed or read.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

The four H rows of the platform and the C row of rwb-case are the ones the release consumes as published artefacts; the metadata rows of this story declare no build dependency, because a CON dependency never blocks and a deployment story is Day 1 by rule (§R5.7). DP-09 and DP-10 carry the topic and the queue; DP-15 carries the migration job; DP-19 carries the route; DP-13 fixes the base the route publishes.

**Artefacts**

| Artefact | Content |
|---|---|
| `helm/rwb-agent/` | Chart with the api deployment, the worker deployment, the service, the migration job, the config map, the secret references, the probes and the workflow registration hook |
| `helm/rwb-agent/values-dev.yaml`, `values-sit.yaml`, `values-uat.yaml` | Image digest, replicas, resources, probe timings, log level, feature switches, environment name |
| Pipeline stage | Build, unit and contract tests, image and dependency scan, chart publish, promote the same artefact |
| Provisioning step | `rwb.agent.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics and the publish right; `rwb.decision-record.v1` verified; `rwb.case.events.v1` consume right and group; task queue `rwb-agent` in namespace `rwb-recovery` |
| Registration step | `AgentRunWorkflow` event-started with its two activities; the assertion that no Schedule exists |
| Route publication | The two operations registered behind the gateway-bff pass-through route, one hop |
| KEDA scaling | Worker scaled on the task-queue backlog with a minimum and a maximum from the values file |
| Dashboards | Eight panels: runs by mode, L1 acceptance rate, override rate, fallback rate, tool read failures, `.dlt` messages, feed lag, worker backlog and refused reads |
| Alerts | Six rules: acceptance below floor, override above ceiling, `.dlt` message, worker backlog, failed migration, stale business date |
| Runbook | Six entries: acceptance below floor, override above ceiling, `.dlt` message, worker backlog, failed migration, route unavailable |

**Probes.** Readiness answers healthy only when the migration is at the expected schema version, the worker has polled, the relay is running and the last reference-data read answered; liveness answers healthy when the process is up and its internal loop is responsive. Neither probe writes to the database. Exact paths and timings are values.

**Migration job.** Runs the per-service Flyway sequence for schema `rwb_agent` with the service login as a pre-deploy job with a backoff limit; `V10_008__agent_feedback.sql` applies in order with the earlier P10 migrations, a failed job blocks the rollout and the release, and the sequence is forward only (DP-15; GAP-0624; ASM-0921).

**Alert mapping.**

| Check | Condition | Alert | Route |
|---|---|---|---|
| Acceptance below floor | The L1 acceptance rate of a segment and business date falls below its floor | Acceptance alert with the agent, the segment, the date and the rate, and the review action | RW-COE and RW-RISK, ticket |
| Override above ceiling | The correction plus rejection rate of the segment rises above its ceiling | Override alert with the segment, the date and the rate | RW-COE and RW-RISK, ticket |
| `.dlt` | A message lands in the `.dlt` topic of the agent topic | `.dlt` alert with the message type and its registry subject | Platform on-call, page |
| Backlog | The task-queue backlog passes its window | Backlog alert with the queue and the age of the oldest task | Platform on-call, ticket |
| Failed migration | The migration job fails | Release alert with the schema version reached | Platform on-call, page |
| Stale business date | The business date of the runs is older than the day | Stale-date alert with the business date and the data date, and MSG-P1-001 on the panel | Data steward, ticket |
| MSG-P4-002 | A read without the Case record right | Refused-read count on the dashboard | No page |

The floors and ceilings of the acceptance and override alerts are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0624; ASM-0927) and are reviewed values per environment.

**Capacity.** The plan states, per environment, the runs of a peak business date, the pages served to the panel, the worker minimum and maximum, the connection cap of the login and the relay interval. The target is the legacy measure: the panel answers a case within the 2 s budget of NFR-009 and a verdict is stored before the owner leaves the screen.

**Rollback.** The previous chart version is redeployed and the workflows are re-registered from the previous release; the Flyway sequence is forward only, so `agent_feedback` stays and no down-migration is run; the topic, its retry and `.dlt` topics and the publish right stay in place, because removing them would break the feed of the monitor and of the projections; a rollback is rehearsed in SIT before UAT.

**Done when.** The chart renders in all three environments, the pipeline promotes one artefact, the probes answer, the queue, the topic and the rights are verified by a test, the event-started registration answers one run per case and event and no Schedule exists, the six alerts fire on synthetic conditions, the route answers within 2 s, the capacity plan is reviewed, the rollback is rehearsed and the six runbook entries are accepted by the on-call rota.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P1-001 | The business date of the runs is stale | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P4-002 | A read without the Case record right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P10-005 | The panel shows no summary because the run failed | The agent summary is not available for this case. Work from the case record. |

The three texts appear in the sources of this key and keep their wording character for character; the deployment adds the alert routing and the runbook link, never a new wording. The acceptance, override, `.dlt`, backlog and migration alerts have no message ID in the legacy story and keep none.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in a values file: the lists, the mode, the segment, the confidence floor, the decision code and the acceptance floors are contract and registration values, never deployment values (DP-07, BR5).
- No personal data in logs, dashboard series, alert payloads or the runbook: counts, identifiers, dates and durations only.
- No other service's table is read and no grant crosses a schema: the login holds rights on `rwb_agent` only (DP-01, DP-02).
- Every topic has a retry topic and a `.dlt` topic, and the relay publishes within its interval (DP-09).
- The release pins the image digest and the chart version; a rebuild between environments is not allowed.
- No secret is written into a values file, a chart template, a dashboard or the runbook; all secrets come from the platform secret store.
- The release registers no Schedule and carries no job table; a cadence Schedule fails the release (DP-10, BR11).
- The two operations are published only behind the gateway-bff route, one hop, and a screen never reaches the service (DP-19, BR10).
- Every fixture is synthetic; no production case, summary, verdict or record is copied into a schema, a payload or a fake.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-028 for the wave 2 integration harness. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **a repeatable cross-service journey harness for the case intake agent at L1 — a `CaseCreated` event that starts a run on rwb-agent, the stored summary read through the P10 agent-output operation, the owner's verdict and its D6 decision record, the acceptance measure and the fallback — with the evidence pack attached to the wave 2 release**, so that **the intake-agent journey is proven end to end across rwb-agent, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access before RWB-P10-E2028-APP, RWB-P3-E1035-APP and RWB-P7-E2028-APP claim Done**.

This story builds the harness, its contract fakes, its seed pack, its evidence pack and its pass or fail gate. It builds no production endpoint, no screen, no table and no migration. Nothing it writes is deployed to a service.

No single app story can prove the journey. RWB-P3-E1035-APP can prove that a case is created and that `CaseCreated` leaves rwb-case. RWB-P10-E2028-APP can prove that a run is started, that the model is called through the Enterprise AI private endpoint, that the summary and gap flags are stored and that a verdict is accepted. RWB-P7-E2028-APP can prove that a decision record is written and that the ledger read returns it. The agreement between the four of them — one event starting one L1 run whose stored output, verdict, decision record and acceptance measure all describe the same case on the same business date — is this story, and only this story.

##### 2. Business rationale

RWB-E2-028 split into three app stories and this integration story. The app stories build the agent runtime, the agent-output read, the feedback write, the decision-log mapping and the panel inside their own services. What no app story can prove on its own is the chain the business actually relies on: a new case raises `CaseCreated` on the case topic, rwb-agent consumes it under the policy in force for the segment, runs the model, stores a summary and the gap flags, publishes `AgentRunCompleted`, rwb-agent serves that stored output back to the case without waiting on the model, the case owner gives a verdict, rwb-decision holds one D6 entry that names the agent and prompt versions, and the acceptance and correction rates for the segment move by exactly that feedback. That proof is this story.

The journey carries two requirements. Every decision records the agent and prompt versions (REQ-DRI-001): the harness asserts that the decision record names version "INTAKE@P2/PR3" and that the D6 code is the one the feedback wrote, so a reader of the ledger can tell which model and which prompt produced the recommendation that was followed or overruled. Personal data stays masked by role on every screen and in every agent call (REQ-ACA-005): the harness asserts that the summary it reads back carries masking tokens and that neither the events, the workflow inputs, the logs nor the evidence pack carry a direct identifier.

The D6 decision is the anchor. Legacy section 12 gives the mapping: case, decision code "D6", agent version "INTAKE@P2/PR3", the model version, the run reference as the inputs reference, the recommendation, the final call from the verdict and the reason as the override reason. The harness exercises that mapping across rwb-agent and rwb-decision, so a change to the mapping on either side is caught before the owner sees a verdict that no ledger entry supports.

Architecture v5 changes the path, not the business. In the monolith the agent client, the feedback table, the scope check and the decision log all sat in one deployment and one schema. In the target:

- the local decision record and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` carry the entry, with rwb-decision holding the ledger (DP-03);
- the mode per segment, the verdict list and the panel labels are reference data served by rwb-case's contract, never values in code (DP-07);
- the events are CloudEvents on the owner's topic, with an outbox on the producer and an inbox on the consumer, so a duplicate never counts twice (DP-09);
- the run is an `AgentRunWorkflow` on queue `rwb-agent` with a 60 s limit and the rule result after it, which is the fallback of R-UNI-32 (DP-10);
- every path is on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` (DP-13);
- each service migrates its own schema through its own Flyway sequence (DP-15);
- the panel reaches the model through the gateway-bff composite route, so the harness drives the same route the screens use (DP-19).

The measure is the journey evidence: for each owned criterion, one pass or fail with the event, the run, the output, the verdict, the decision record, the measure and the fallback flag captured in one report that can be re-run for any build.

##### 3. Preconditions

- The wave 2 harness environment (SIT) is available with the gateway route for `/api/recovery/*`, the topics `rwb.case.events.v1`, `rwb.agent.events.v1` and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the Temporal namespace `rwb-recovery` with the queues `rwb-agent` and `rwb-case`, and the Enterprise AI private endpoint test profile (INT-23). Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0410; ASM-0585): the harness environment, its seed pack and its evidence format.
- The three integration dependencies have published their contracts, or their contract fakes stand in for them: RWB-P10-E2028-APP (rwb-agent, the agent-output read and the feedback write), RWB-P3-E1035-APP (rwb-case, the case record and `CaseCreated`) and RWB-P7-E2028-APP (rwb-decision, the D6 mapping and the ledger read).
- Policy "INTAKE" version "P2" with mode "L1" and prompt "PR3" is in force from 2027-01-25, and the policy fixture carries mode "SHADOW" for segment UNSECURED (legacy sections 3 and 7).
- Case "RW-2027-000501" is owned by "owner.user07", who holds RW-CASEOWN with Case record CRU and the case in that user's scope, and the case carries the gap flags MISSING_DOCUMENT and NO_VALID_APPRAISAL (legacy sections 3 and 7).
- January 2027 for segment MORTGAGE and region BKK holds 300 runs with feedback: 240 accepted, 45 corrected and 15 rejected, which is acceptance 0.8000 and correction 0.1500 (legacy AC2).
- The seeded states the scenarios name are present: case "RW-2027-000502" with a run that reached the 60 s limit, case "RW-2027-000503" whose run used data as of 2027-01-26 against business date 2027-01-28, case "RW-2027-000601" in team "HP-NE" outside the owner's scope, unsecured case "RW-2027-000701" with segment UNSECURED in SHADOW, and a test user of role RW-PHONECOL holding Case record R only.
- The feature switch `rwb.agent.intake-l1` is on in the harness profile (legacy section 13).
- Synthetic cases, synthetic owners and masking tokens only: no customer name, account number, national identifier or contact detail enters the harness, the seed pack or the evidence pack (legacy section 17).
- No build dependency. Day 1.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: takes the run lock for the environment and records the build ID, the business date and the versions of the six contracts it is about to exercise.
2. Harness: seeds cases "RW-2027-000501", "RW-2027-000502", "RW-2027-000503", "RW-2027-000601" and "RW-2027-000701", owner "owner.user07", team "HP-NE", the segments and scopes, the RW-PHONECOL test user and the policy fixture (INTAKE P2, mode L1 per segment, SHADOW for UNSECURED, prompt PR3).
3. Harness: calls the P4 session operation against the rwb-access fake and records the role, the scope and the Case record right the journey runs under.
4. Harness: reads the case through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` and records the owner, the team, the region, the product group and the two gap flags the journey starts from.
5. Harness: subscribes to `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.agent.events.v1` with its own consumer group before the case is created, so the run window starts before the event.
6. Harness: publishes `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1` for case "RW-2027-000501", or lets rwb-case create the case through its own operation where RWB-P3-E1035-APP has landed, and records which of the two paths was used.
7. Harness: waits for `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` on `rwb.agent.events.v1` inside the run window and records the run ID, the time to completion and the fallback flag.
8. Harness: reads the run through `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs` and records status, autonomy mode, agent code, agent version, data as of and the fallback flag.
9. Harness: calls `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` and asserts the summary, the two gap flags with reasons, agent "INTAKE", version "INTAKE@P2/PR3", the marker "Agent output" and the absence of feedback.
10. Harness: posts the feedback through `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs/{runId}/feedback` with an If-Match of the run row version, then reads `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` and asserts one D6 entry with agent version "INTAKE@P2/PR3" and the final call that matches the verdict, before the agent_feedback row is asserted.
11. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-metrics` and asserts acceptance 0.8000 and correction 0.1500 for INTAKE on MORTGAGE/BKK; asserts the SHADOW case returns an empty list with no decision record, the stale case carries MSG-P1-001 with 2027-01-26, the out-of-scope case answers 404 and the timed out case answers with no summary and fallback true.
12. Harness: writes the per-scenario evidence into one run report keyed by story key and business date, evaluates the gate, attaches the report to the wave 2 release record, releases the lock and restores the seed.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The agent timed out or failed a guardrail for the case | The run holds status "TIMED_OUT" with fallback true and no summary is returned; the scenario passes only when both are true | MSG-P10-005 | AC4 |
| X2 | The owner corrects or rejects without a reason | The feedback answers 422; no decision record and no agent_feedback row is written | MSG-P7-005 | AC5 |
| X3 | The decision log write fails on feedback | The feedback answers 503 and no agent_feedback row is written; the run is still readable with no verdict, and the incident is raised under R-UNI-39 by the service, not by the harness | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X4 | Feedback already given for the run and item, or two requests arrive at once | The second request answers 409; exactly one decision record exists | MSG-GEN-004 | AC7 |
| X5 | The case is outside the user's scope | The agent-outputs read answers 404 | MSG-P4-003 | AC8 |
| X6 | The agent's mode is SHADOW for the case segment | The agent-outputs operation returns an empty list and no decision record is written for the case | None to a user | AC9 |
| X7 | The run used data older than the business date | The output carries MSG-P1-001 with the data date 2027-01-26 above the summary; the scenario passes only when both the message and the date are present | MSG-P1-001 | AC1 |
| X8 | A user without Case record U sends feedback | The feedback answers 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-028-10-ITG |
| X9 | The seed pack cannot be loaded (case not owned, policy version absent, segment missing, counts off) | The run refuses to start and names the missing seed item; no scenario is reported | None | All |
| X10 | The evidence pack cannot be attached to the release record | The run is marked failed; the local evidence file is kept for rerun | None | All |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the three published contracts or their fakes, the policy fixture and the Enterprise AI test profile; it builds no service feature and has no build dependency |
| Negotiable | The scenarios, the seeded values, the verdict list, the mode per segment and the fixture counts are data files, never code |
| Valuable | The intake-agent journey is proven once across three services, with the D6 record and the acceptance measure in the same evidence as the summary |
| Estimable | One journey runner, one fake set, one fixture pack, three assertion helpers, one evidence collector, one gate |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each owned criterion has a fixed Given, When and Then and a recorded pass or fail in the report |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Case intake agent live at L1 [E3a]

  Background:
    Given policy "INTAKE" version "P2" with mode "L1" and prompt "PR3" is in force from 2027-01-25
    Given case "RW-2027-000501" is owned by "owner.user07" with RW-CASEOWN and is in that user's scope

  Scenario: AC1 L1 summary journey from CaseCreated to the stored output (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the harness subscribes to `rwb.case.events.v1` and `rwb.agent.events.v1` before the case is created
    Given case "RW-2027-000501" has an ANSWERED intake run with gap flags MISSING_DOCUMENT and NO_VALID_APPRAISAL
    When rwb-case publishes `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` for the case and rwb-agent completes the run
    Then the run read through `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs` shows agent "INTAKE" and version "INTAKE@P2/PR3"
    Then `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` returns the summary, the two gap flags with reasons, agent "INTAKE", version "INTAKE@P2/PR3" and the marker "Agent output"
    Then the evidence records that the run was started by `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1`
    Then the agent-outputs read answers inside the 2 s timeout of one hop

  Scenario: AC2 Feedback writes the decision record before it is stored (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the run of case "RW-2027-000501" has no feedback
    When "owner.user07" sends POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs/{runId}/feedback with verdict "ACCEPTED" and an If-Match of the run row version
    Then one decision record exists with decision code "D6", agent version "INTAKE@P2/PR3" and final call "ACCEPTED"
    Then exactly one agent_feedback row exists for the run and item "SUMMARY"
    Then the next agent-outputs read returns the verdict "ACCEPTED" on that run
    Then the evidence records that the decision record was written before the feedback row

  Scenario: AC3 Acceptance measured for the January 2027 MORTGAGE/BKK cohort (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given January 2027 for segment MORTGAGE and region BKK holds 300 runs with feedback, 240 accepted, 45 corrected and 15 rejected
    When the harness reads GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-metrics for "INTAKE"
    Then the answer holds acceptance rate 0.8000 and correction rate 0.1500 for MORTGAGE/BKK
    Then each of the 300 feedback rows has one decision record with decision "D6" and agent version "INTAKE@P2/PR3"

  Scenario: AC4 Rule fallback on a timed out run (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RW-2027-000502" has a run that reached the 60 s limit of AgentRunWorkflow
    When the harness reads the run and the agent outputs for the case
    Then the run holds status "TIMED_OUT" and fallback true
    Then `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` returns no summary for the case

  Scenario: AC5 Correction without a reason (new, D-RCV-60)
    When "owner.user07" sends POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs/{runId}/feedback with verdict "CORRECTED" and an empty reason
    Then the answer is 422 with MSG-P7-005
    Then no decision record and no agent_feedback row exist for the run

  Scenario: AC6 The decision cannot be recorded (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-decision decision log answers unavailable
    When "owner.user07" sends POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs/{runId}/feedback with verdict "ACCEPTED"
    Then the answer is 503 with MSG-P7-003
    Then no agent_feedback row exists for the run
    Then the next agent-outputs read still returns the run with no verdict

  Scenario: AC7 Feedback given twice (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given "owner.user07" accepted the summary of case "RW-2027-000501" and the run holds one decision record
    When a second feedback request arrives for the same run and item "SUMMARY"
    Then the answer is 409 with MSG-GEN-004
    Then one decision record exists for the run

  Scenario: AC8 A case outside the user's scope (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given case "RW-2027-000601" belongs to team "HP-NE" outside the scope of "owner.user07"
    When "owner.user07" requests GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs for it
    Then the answer is 404 with MSG-P4-003

  Scenario: AC9 A segment still in shadow (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the INTAKE policy for segment UNSECURED is mode "SHADOW"
    When the harness requests the agent outputs for unsecured case "RW-2027-000701"
    Then `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` returns an empty list
    Then no decision record is written for the case
```

No legacy acceptance criterion is owned by this story: the nine above are new and test only the integration deliverable, using the legacy values of RWB-E2-028 and no other. The stale-input assertion of legacy AC9 is carried inside AC1's evidence, because a harness has no panel to warn.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Only runs in mode L1 for the case segment are returned to a user; shadow output is never returned | agent_policy.autonomy_mode, segment fields (New); AC9 |
| BR2 | Agent output is marked "Agent output" with the agent name and version | REQ-DRI-001; labels "Agent version" |
| BR3 | Feedback writes one decision log entry before it is stored: decision D6 (LOV-DECISION, assumed code), agent version, recommendation reference, final call, reason | Principle 5; R-UNI-39; CTL-06 |
| BR4 | A correction or a rejection needs a reason | CTL-07; MSG-P7-005 |
| BR5 | One feedback per run and item; the intake summary is item "SUMMARY" | agent_feedback unique key (New) |
| BR6 | The case record never waits for the model; the panel reads stored output | NFR-009; R-UNI-32 |
| BR7 | The summary holds masking tokens only | CTL-11 |

The rules are unchanged by the split. The harness asserts them across the service boundaries and restates none of them in code: the mode per segment, the verdict list and the item key are seeded data.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case. This story changes no case status; the harness asserts that no status, task or field moves because of an agent run or a verdict.

The agent run carries the status rwb-agent gives it, and the harness asserts only the two the legacy story names: "ANSWERED" for a completed run and "TIMED_OUT" with fallback true for a run that reached the 60 s limit. The feedback carries one verdict: ACCEPTED, CORRECTED or REJECTED, written once per run and item.

The harness adds a run state of its own only: Not started, Running, Passed, Failed, with the latest run for a build deciding the gate.

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CASEOWN, test user "owner.user07" | Reads the agent output for cases in scope (Case record R) and gives one verdict per run (Case record U) |
| RW-TEAMMGR | Reads the agent output for team cases (Case record R); gives no verdict |
| SY-AGENT | Runs the agent and stores the output (read only to the harness) |
| SY-DECLOG | Writes the D6 entry the harness asserts, through rwb-decision's contract only |
| RW-COE | Reads acceptance and correction by segment (Platform administration R) |
| Integration lead | Agrees the fake set, the Enterprise AI test profile and the run window with the three service owners |
| QA lead | Owns the seed pack, the evidence format and the pass or fail gate |
| No approval level from the delegation of authority applies | The story takes no business decision |
