##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test asset in the integration pipeline and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` | P10 rwb-agent | Reads the stored L1 output: summary, gap flags with reasons, agent, agent version, marker and verdict (AC1, AC2, AC4, AC6, AC8, AC9) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs/{runId}/feedback` | P10 rwb-agent | Records one verdict with an If-Match of the run row version; the D6 record is written first (AC2, AC5, AC6, AC7) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-metrics` | P10 rwb-agent | Reads acceptance and correction by segment for INTAKE (AC3) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs` | P10 rwb-agent | Reads the run: status, autonomy mode, agent and agent version, data as of, fallback flag (AC1, AC4) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | Reads the case, its owner, team, region and product group the journey starts from (AC1, AC8) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | P7 rwb-decision | Asserts the D6 entry, its agent version and its final call (AC2, AC3, AC5, AC6, AC7, AC9) |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with the 2 s timeout, and every POST carries an If-Match and a key per scenario. The scope and owner check that rwb-agent makes inside its own process is not a path in the Ownership Map, so the harness seeds it through the role and scope of the rwb-access fake (12.8) and reads the resulting answer through the P10 operation instead of calling an access path.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event on a production topic; the one `CaseCreated` it sends is a seed message on the test topic, and the evidence goes to the release record through the pipeline.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | Asserts that the run of case "RW-2027-000501" was started by the case event inside the run window (DP-09) |
| `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` | `rwb.agent.events.v1` | P10 rwb-agent | Closes the run window and gives the run ID, the status and the fallback flag before the output read (DP-09, DP-10) |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | Asserts that the D6 entry reached the shared topic inside the run window, alongside the ledger read of 12.2 (DP-03, DP-09) |

The harness consumes with its own consumer group and never reads a producer's outbox, inbox or schema.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

`AgentRunWorkflow` on queue `rwb-agent` is exercised, not built: the run has a 60 s limit and then the rule result (R-UNI-32), and the harness asserts which of the two the run ended on through the status and the fallback flag (AC1, AC4). JOB-11 Outbox sender is observed on its every-minute window, so the harness knows when a seed message or a produced event should have crossed the topic.

The harness starts no workflow, adds no activity and writes no schedule. The agent call to the Enterprise AI private endpoint (INT-23), the guardrail check and the storage of the output belong to RWB-P10-E2028-APP.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The harness adds no workflow and no schedule; the 60 s limit is inside `AgentRunWorkflow` and JOB-11's every-minute window is the platform's, both only observed.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no table in any schema and no schema of its own; it reads and writes through the operations of 12.2 only.

###### 12.8 Contract fakes

| Fake | Serves | Contract | What it answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| WireMock rwb-agent | The four P10 operations of 12.2 | OpenAPI of P10 | The output with summary and gaps, the empty list for SHADOW, the run with status "TIMED_OUT" and fallback true, 200 with the verdict on feedback, 422 MSG-P7-005, 409 MSG-GEN-004, 403 MSG-P4-002, 503 MSG-P7-003, and the metrics answer 0.8000 and 0.1500; keeps the request journal for the If-Match and ordering assertions |
| WireMock rwb-case | `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | OpenAPI of P3 | The case, its owner, team, region and product group, and the ANSWERED case with the two gap flags |
| WireMock rwb-decision | `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | OpenAPI of P7 | The D6 entry with agent version "INTAKE@P2/PR3" and the final call; 503 for AC6 |
| WireMock rwb-access | The P4 session operation | OpenAPI of P4 | The role, the scope and the Case record right of "owner.user07", the RW-PHONECOL user with Case record R only (MSG-P4-002) and case "RW-2027-000601" outside scope (MSG-P4-003) |
| Enterprise AI private endpoint test profile | The model call rwb-agent makes | The INT-23 contract, not in this workspace | A completion and a guardrail pass per scenario, and a timeout for AC4, with masking tokens in place of identifiers |

Each fake is replaced by the real service as its integration dependency lands, without a change to the scenarios. Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0410; ASM-0585): the fake set, the concrete fixture values, the test profile of the private endpoint, the harness environment and the evidence format.

###### 12.9 Call-type summary

| Call type | In this story |
|---|---|
| REST | 0 provided, 6 consumed, one hop on the owner's base with the 2 s timeout; the P4 session operation is called against the fake only and is not a production path of this story |
| Kafka | 3 events consumed on `rwb.case.events.v1`, `rwb.agent.events.v1` and `rwb.decision-record.v1`; none published on a production topic |
| Temporal | Observed only: `AgentRunWorkflow` on queue `rwb-agent` with the 60 s limit, and JOB-11 Outbox sender; no workflow, activity or schedule added |
| File | None |

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `integration/recovery-agent-intake` in the ACE repository, package `<ACE base package>.recovery.integration.agentintake`. Not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added | How this harness applies it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The D6 entry is read through rwb-decision and the `DecisionRecorded` event is read on the shared topic; the harness never reads a decision table |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The mode per segment, the verdict list and the item key are seeded reference data, never values in the harness code |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON | The harness subscribes with its own consumer group and asserts the three events, never a producer's table |
| DP-10 | Quartz, JOB-nn | Temporal Schedule or event-started workflow through the workflow kit | H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON | `AgentRunWorkflow` is observed on queue `rwb-agent`, including the 60 s limit and the rule result behind it; the harness adds no workflow and no schedule |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none | Every path of 12.2 uses the owner's base, so the harness never calls a monolith base |
| DP-15 | V0001 baseline, migration | Per-service Flyway sequence in the service's own schema | H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON | The harness runs no migration and reads no schema; it asserts the seeded state through the contracts, so each service migrates on its own |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The journey runs through the gateway route the real case record uses, on the same bases |

The platform H dependencies in the table (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1071-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1044-CON, H RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are delivered by the platform waves and are not repeated in the metadata: the harness converges on them and has no build dependency of its own. The blocking dependencies of this story are the three I stories, which replace the fakes with real services one at a time.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Job | Runs the twelve flow steps for one scenario and one business date and holds the run lock |
| FakeRegistry | Configuration | WireMock mappings for rwb-agent, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access, one set per contract version, plus the Enterprise AI test profile selection |
| AgentFixturePack | Data | Cases, owners, segments, scopes, the policy fixture, the five seeded cases and the January 2027 counts, per scenario |
| OutputAssertion | Service | Compares the summary, the gap flags and reasons, the agent, the version and the marker against the fixture, and the empty list for SHADOW |
| FeedbackAssertion | Service | Posts the verdict, then checks the D6 entry, its agent version, its final call, the single agent_feedback row and the message of each refusal |
| MetricAssertion | Service | Reads the metrics operation and compares acceptance 0.8000 and correction 0.1500 for INTAKE on MORTGAGE/BKK |
| EvidenceCollector | Service | Writes one report keyed by story key and business date, with the event, the run, the output, the verdict, the decision record, the measure and the fallback flag |
| GateEvaluator | Service | Passes the run when every owned scenario passes and the evidence pack is attached |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, the wave 2 harness profile, one business date, synthetic cases and synthetic owners only. The seeded values are the legacy section 7 Background, the five cases of section 3 and the January 2027 counts; no other value is added. Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0410; ASM-0585): the environment, the seed pack and the evidence format.

**Build steps**

1. Write the AgentFixturePack with the Background, the five cases, the policy fixture and the January 2027 counts; test that a bad seed stops the run (X9).
2. Write the FakeRegistry with the four WireMock mapping sets and the Enterprise AI test profile selection, with the policy and verdict data loaded from files.
3. Write JourneyRunner for AC1: publish `CaseCreated`, wait for `AgentRunCompleted`, read the run and assert the stored output and the `CaseCreated` link.
4. Add AC2 and AC7 with the feedback write, the If-Match, the decision-record-first ordering and the duplicate refusal.
5. Add AC5 and AC6 with the 422 and the 503, asserting that neither writes a feedback row.
6. Add AC3 with the metrics read and the one-D6-entry-per-feedback sweep, and AC4 with the 60 s limit, the TIMED_OUT status and the fallback flag.
7. Add AC8 and AC9 with the out-of-scope case and the SHADOW segment, then write EvidenceCollector and GateEvaluator, attach the report to the wave 2 release record and rerun the nine scenarios on the release build.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.agent.intake-l1` is on in the harness profile, as the legacy story sets it. Off, the agent-outputs operation returns an empty list and the harness reports the journey as not applicable rather than as passed. The harness itself is a pipeline stage selected by the run profile, not by a business flag.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the run report is attached to the wave 2 release record with all nine owned scenarios, and each fake has been replaced by the real service where its I story has landed in SIT. The fixture pack and the evidence sign-off wait for the values of the gap and assumption rows cited in sections 3, 12.8 and 13.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P10-005 | No L1 summary for the case because the run failed | The agent summary is not available for this case. Work from the case record. |
| MSG-P7-005 | Correct or Reject with no reason | Enter the reason you are not following the recommendation. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Feedback already given or row changed | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P4-003 | Case outside scope | This case is not in your scope. |
| MSG-P1-001 | Summary built on stale data | {product} is from {date}. Today's load has not arrived. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The harness asserts these messages and never rewrites them. Its own report text is for the release team and is not part of the message standard.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-03 Case record gains the panel "Agent summary": loading (skeleton), empty (no panel when no L1 output), unavailable (MSG-P10-005), stale (MSG-P1-001 above the summary with the data date), ready (summary, gap flags, Accept, Correct, Reject) and recorded (verdict and date, no controls). In the read only state of SCR-03 the controls are hidden. SCR-46 Agent monitor (state live) shows acceptance and correction by segment.

No screen is built by this story. The harness drives the operations behind those states and asserts the same six states through the contracts: the output present, absent, stale, filtered by mode and carrying a verdict. The panel and its states belong to RWB-P10-E2028-APP.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the mode per segment, the verdict list, the item key, the policy version and the prompt version are data in the seed pack, never values in the harness.
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs, logs, evidence or agent calls. The summary carries masking tokens and the seed holds synthetic cases and synthetic owners only.
- No read of another service's tables and no schema of the harness's own: every read and write goes through the operations of 12.2, and the harness runs no migration.
- Agent output never changes the case: the harness asserts that no status, task or field moves because of a run or a verdict.
- Each fake is replaced by the real service as its I story lands; a fake that outlives its service is a defect, not a configuration.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and a value that must change changes in the seed pack through a reviewed change, never by an exception in a scenario.

##### 19. Out of scope

- Agent actions taken without the owner (autonomy L2 and above, Epic 8).
- Editing the summary text in the Workbench; a correction records the reason only.
- Intake document classification (P5 stories).
- Production code of any service in the journey: the operations of rwb-agent, rwb-case, rwb-decision and rwb-access, their schemas and their screens belong to their own stories.

The harness, the fakes and the evidence pack cover the four items above only as a caller or a consumer would see them; building any of them is out of scope for this story.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract slice of RWB-E2-029 for rwb-agent. It fixes the screening narrowing of the evaluation start and the evaluation report on `/api/recovery/agent/v1` (DP-13, restated from RWB-P10-E1061-CON and never redefined), the segment-eligibility and L1 decision request and outcome with the two segment members and the approval, the score row shape per code with the counts, precision and recall, the decision-record mapping and the idempotency of one feedback per run and item (DP-03), the event contracts on `rwb.agent.events.v1` and on `rwb.decision-record.v1` with their retry and `.dlt` topics (DP-09), the parameters and lists of rwb-case (DP-06, DP-07), the ledger and ACE facts reached through rwb-source-data (DP-05), the one-hop reads with the 2 s budget (DP-11), the gateway-bff route (DP-19) and the fakes. Because there is no data lake, the contract declares no lake table, no extract, no lake credential, no INT-19 or INT-20 path and no daily agent table. It builds no business behaviour and adds no migration. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the rwb-agent side of the screening key fixed as a contract on Day 1: the evaluation start and the report narrowed to agent "SCREENING" on sample "SCREEN-S2" version 1, the policy payload with mode L1, segment MORTGAGE and region BKK and its approval, the score row shape per code X1 to X7, the mapping of a confirmation and a rejection to one decision record with their idempotency, the event contracts of the run completion and of the decision record with the retry and `.dlt` topics, the gateway-bff route, the error taxonomy and the fakes**, so that **the app story, the S8 and P7 slices of this key and the integration copy build against one agreed, testable shape without waiting for the evaluation to run, and no reader is offered a lake artefact or a daily agent table that does not exist**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy key was written against objects inside one deployment: the evaluation wrote `agent_evaluation` rows beside the policy row, the panel filtered proposals in process, the decision log writer of the same deployment wrote the rejection, the deviation interface was a Java call, and the case and the ledger were read from the same schema. In the target each of those is a boundary:

- The evaluation harness and the score rows are rwb-agent's own tables, and the operations that start and report an evaluation are already baselined by RWB-P10-E1061-CON; this key narrows them and adds no member (DP-01, DP-11).
- The segment and the autonomy mode are columns of the approved policy row, so the L1 decision is a configuration version and its approval, not code (DP-06).
- The case, the deviation and the ledger are P3, S8 and P1; the record type and the central ledger are P7's, and each service writes its own record through the local library on `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03, DP-05).
- The run and score facts leave as CloudEvents on `rwb.agent.events.v1` with the platform retry and `.dlt` topics (DP-09).
- The data lake is removed by Architecture v5 (ADR-018), so the contract names no lake table, no extract and no daily agent aggregate; the aggregate of the monitoring story is a read of its own.

Contract-first only works if the seam is written once. Here it is small and load-bearing: one evaluation request and one report whose row carries the legacy figures, one policy payload that names the segment and one read that answers it, one feedback write whose record and idempotency are fixed, two event payloads, one route, one error taxonomy and one fake set. With that agreed on Day 1, the app story builds the evaluator, the resolver, the filter and the handler against the fakes; the S8 slice takes the raise with `raisedBy` "SCREENING_AGENT" and the refusal of a second confirmation; the P7 slice takes the record this key maps; and RWB-ITG-W2 proves the same behaviour across the real services. Without it, each caller invents its own score row, the report and the panel drift apart, and a confirmed deviation loses its record.

This story defines the provided side on the agent base and the consumed side of the key, and never restates what another owner holds: the evaluation operations are RWB-P10-E1061-CON's, the run and proposal shapes are RWB-P10-E1062-CON's, the panel and feedback operations are RWB-P10-E2028-CON's, the configuration operations are RWB-P10-E1058-CON's, and the parameters and lists are rwb-case's (DP-01).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL), so the base, the topic and the event names follow the platform rule and not a local choice (§R4; DP-13, DP-14).
- The CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the platform problem response are the baseline; this document narrows them where it must and says so.
- RWB-P10-E1058-CON is in force: the policy and prompt resources, the configuration operations, the approval and the run resource; this story narrows the policy payload with the two segment members rather than redefining it.
- RWB-P10-E1061-CON is in force: the evaluation start, the list and the report, their statuses and their messages; this story restates them with the screening narrowing and adds no operation.
- RWB-P10-E1062-CON is in force: the run and proposal shapes and the agent topic with its retry and `.dlt` topics. RWB-P10-E2028-CON is in force: the case agent-outputs read, the feedback operation and the `agent_feedback` resource.
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is published: the decision-record library and the shared topic, with the record fields, the hash chain and the idempotent write (DP-03). RWB-PLT-TE006-CON is published: the envelope, the relay, the retry topics and the `.dlt` rule. RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-PLT-E1043-CON publish the parameters and reference-data client libraries, and RWB-PLT-N001-CON the route contract and its stub.
- The rwb-case contracts are published: `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` (RWB-P3-E2015-CON), the parameters (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) and the lists (RWB-P3-E1043-CON).
- The rwb-deviation raise and open-deviation reads are published shapes; the raise returns the deviation ID and the entry ID the feedback maps (ASM-0931).
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (§R5.7) and sits in contract group CG-W2.

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the evaluation start and report as this key narrows them: agent "SCREENING", sample "SCREEN-S2" version 1, the statuses RUNNING, DONE and FAILED, the refusal codes and the report members.
2. Fix the score row shape: one row per code X1 to X7 with the label key, sample size 500, the true positives, false positives and false negatives, precision and recall at four decimals, and the legacy X1 figures 41, 4 and 5 giving 0.9111 and 0.8913.
3. Fix the segment-eligibility and L1 decision request: `autonomyMode` "L1", `segmentProductGroup` MORTGAGE, `segmentRegionCode` BKK, the prompt version, the evaluation run ID and the promotion conditions, its LOADED outcome, the approval with MSG-P7-002 and the read that answers the segment of a case.
4. Fix the decision-record mapping: an accepted confirmation stores the entry ID the raise returns; a rejection writes one record through the library with decision "X6", agent version "SCREENING@P2/PR2", final call REJECTED and the reason, and only then the feedback; the one-feedback rule and its key are declared.
5. Declare the two events: `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28) on `rwb.agent.events.v1` with the retry and `.dlt` topics and the run facts including the two segment members, and DecisionRecorded on `rwb.decision-record.v1` with the record fields of the library.
6. Fix the route, the parameter and list reads and the boundary of 12.2, one hop and a 2 s budget each, and name the values the contract expects.
7. Write the five fakes: rwb-case, rwb-deviation, the decision-record library, the model gateway and the route, each with the answers, errors and timings this key's tests need.
8. State the absence rule: no lake table, no extract, no lake credential, no INT-19 or INT-20 path and no daily agent table.
9. Publish the nine sub-tables and the contract tests, and tag the baseline for the app story, the S8 and P7 slices and the integration copy.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A member of the report, the score row or the policy payload drifts from this document: a renamed member, a dropped count, a retyped figure | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC1, AC2, AC3 |
| X2 | A caller sends a request the contract does not allow: an empty reason on a rejection, a sample with no labelled row, a second evaluation of the same version | The operation refuses with 422 or 409 and names the member or the state; nothing is written | MSG-P7-005, MSG-P10-002, MSG-P10-003 | AC1, AC4 |
| X3 | The contract declares a lake table, an extract, a lake credential, an INT-19 or INT-20 path, or a daily agent table | The review refuses the document: no lake exists and the aggregate belongs to another story | None | AC7 |
| X4 | A payload gains a personal field or fails its registry subject | The data-steward review and the contract test refuse it; a produced message that fails is routed to `.dlt` with an alert | None | AC5 |
| X5 | A restated operation drifts from its baseline | The contract test fails and this document is aligned, because the baseline is the owner | None | AC1, AC3, AC4 |
| X6 | The record cannot be written on a rejection, or the route refuses the read | The operation answers 503 and nothing is stored; the refusal is passed through the route unchanged | MSG-P7-003 | AC4, AC6 |
| X7 | A field-level detail of a consumed operation, a payload member or the route is missing from the source material | The element carries the placeholder, one gap row and one assumption row, and the fake is written to the assumed shape | None | AC2, AC6, AC7 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes, the agent runtime, evaluation, run and panel baselines, the record library, the outbox library and the rwb-case and rwb-deviation contracts as published |
| Negotiable | Field-level detail of the consumed operations, the page size of the evaluation list and the member types are settled with their owners; the narrowing, the score row, the segment payload, the record mapping, the payloads and the route are fixed here |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app, S8, P7 and integration slices of this key on Day 1 and gives every reader of a screening score one shape |
| Estimable | Two provided operations restated, two configuration operations narrowed, two panel operations restated, two events, two consumed boundaries and five fakes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact - the contract file, the payload, the fake, the document - and never against a business outcome |

**Target reading.** This contract adds no behaviour and no business value. Agent "SCREENING", the policy versions "P1" and "P2" with prompt "PR2", the segment MORTGAGE and BKK, the floor 0.80, sample "SCREEN-S2" version 1, the 500 cases, the codes X1 to X7, the X1 counts 41, 4 and 5, the precision 0.9111 and recall 0.8913, the recall 0.6000, the condition "recall at least 0.75 for every code", the case "RW-2027-000801" and the date 2027-01-26 are the legacy values of RWB-E2-029, copied character for character, and the score-row keys are the field names of TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 (DF-AGT-089 to DF-AGT-096). Four elements are settled here and marked where they appear: the five score-row members beyond the baseline `AgentEvaluation` (ASM-0941); the two segment members and the run facts on the completion payload (ASM-0940); the decision-record mapping and the one-feedback pair (ASM-0942); and the route in front of the operations (GAP-0626; ASM-0937).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The evaluation is two operations restated from their baseline - start and report - with the screening narrowing, and no caller embeds the harness or reads `rwb_agent` | DP-11; DP-13; RWB-P10-E1061-CON; legacy section 12 |
| BR2 | The report carries one score row per code X1 to X7 with the sample size, the counts, precision and recall at four decimals, and a row that does not reproduce its ratios is refused | Legacy AC1; TSD P10 T3.1 DF-AGT-090 to DF-AGT-096 |
| BR3 | The L1 decision is a policy version with `autonomyMode` "L1" and the two segment members, loaded LOADED and approved with a valid-from date by a person other than the loader | Legacy AC1, section 10; MSG-P7-002; LOV-CONFIG-STATUS |
| BR4 | Segment eligibility is answered from the approved row and the case facts read through the rwb-case contract; a case outside the segment is SHADOW and no row of another service is read | Legacy BR1; DP-01; DP-06 |
| BR5 | A confirmation stores the entry ID the rwb-deviation contract returns, and a rejection writes one record through the library before its feedback, so record and feedback are one transaction or neither | Legacy AC2, AC4, AC9; R-UNI-39; DP-03 |
| BR6 | One feedback exists per run and item, and a second verdict is refused with 409 and MSG-GEN-004 | Legacy section 12; legacy AC8 |
| BR7 | Every message is a CloudEvents 1.0 message on the owner's topic, keyed by the case ID, validated against its registry subject before the relay and routed to `.dlt` on failure | DP-09; DP-14 |
| BR8 | The contract declares no data lake and no daily agent table: the aggregate belongs to RWB-P10-E2031-CON and no lake table, extract, credential or path is named | ADR-018; DP-17 ruling |
| BR9 | The parameters, the eight lists and the segment values are read from rwb-case at run time with their version and never written in the contract as values | DP-06; DP-07 |
| BR10 | Every consumed call and every provided operation is one hop with a 2 s client budget on the base of its owner | DP-11; DP-13; ADR-020 |
| BR11 | A restated operation is never redefined: a drift is corrected in its baseline, and this document only narrows | DP-01; §R3 precedence |
| BR12 | The panel read and the verdict are reached through the gateway-bff route, which passes requests and refusals through unchanged | DP-19; ADR-019 |

##### 9. State transitions

The policy version, which carries the L1 decision:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| None | RW-COE loads the version | The file passes every check, including the condition on the named evaluation | LOADED |
| LOADED | RW-RISK approves it | The approver is not the loader | APPROVED, with approvedBy and validFrom |
| LOADED | A later version is approved | The new version takes effect on its valid-from date | RETIRED |
| LOADED | The condition fails on the named evaluation | AC10 of the app story | Refused; the version in force is unchanged and no row exists |

The evaluation run: RUNNING on the start, DONE when every labelled row is scored, FAILED when the harness stops; a report is answered only for DONE (409 MSG-P10-008 otherwise). The feedback row: none before the verdict; ACCEPTED with the entry ID the raise returns; REJECTED with the entry ID the library returns, written after the record; no row when the record cannot be written (503 MSG-P7-003) or the reason is empty (422 MSG-P7-005).

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| Tech lead of rwb-agent | Owns this contract, its nine sub-tables and its fakes, and publishes them on Day 1 |
| RW-COE | Loads a policy version, a prompt version and a sample, and starts an evaluation (Rules and parameters C) |
| RW-RISK | Approves a loaded version (Rules and parameters A) and may not approve its own load |
| RW-CONDUCT | Reads scores and reports (Rules and parameters R) |
| The case owner | Sends a verdict through the feedback operation (Case record U) |
| rwb-deviation (S8) | Owns the raise, the deviation and its entry; this key fixes only the members it consumes |
| rwb-decision (P7) | Owns the central ledger, the sealing and the record fields of the library |
| rwb-case (P3) | Owns the case, the owner check, the parameters and the lists |
| rwb-source-data (P1) | Owns the interaction ledger and the ACE views |
| No role | Redefines a restated operation, names a lake artefact or a daily agent table, or declares a migration here |

The login and the agent identity behind the run are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0626; ASM-0930). The separation of duty between loader and approver is the one fixed by RWB-P10-E1061-CON and is not restated as a rule of its own.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`; owner rwb-agent (P10). Two operations are restated from their baselines for the screening slice, and two are narrowed configuration operations. None is new here.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/admin/agent-evaluations` | Start the evaluation of agent "SCREENING" on "SCREEN-S2" version 1; 202 AgentEvaluationRun in RUNNING; 422 MSG-P10-002 on a sample with no labelled row; 409 MSG-P10-003 while one is RUNNING | Rules and parameters C | Idempotency-Key header |
| GET | `/admin/agent-evaluations/{evaluationId}/report` | Read the report: sampleSize 500, agreementByLabel[], failureCounts, cost, latency, the three versions; 409 MSG-P10-008 when not DONE | Rules and parameters R | Not applicable |
| POST | `/admin/agent-configs` | Load policy "SCREENING" version "P2" with `autonomyMode` "L1", `segmentProductGroup` MORTGAGE, `segmentRegionCode` BKK, prompt "PR2", the evaluation run and the promotion conditions; 201 LOADED; 422 MSG-P10-001 on a failed check | Rules and parameters C | Idempotency-Key header |
| POST | `/admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve` | Approve the loaded version; 200 APPROVED with approvedBy and validFrom; 409 MSG-P7-002 when the approver loaded it | Rules and parameters A | Idempotency-Key header |
| GET | `/admin/agent-configs` | Read the versions with their segment, so eligibility is answered from the approved row | Rules and parameters R | Not applicable |
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` | The screening narrowing of the panel read of RWB-P10-E2028-CON: `proposals[]` with code, reasons, sources, the preceding contact, confidence, lowConfidence and feedback; no screening output for a case with no L1 run | Case record R | Not applicable |
| POST | `/agent-runs/{runId}/feedback` | The verdict on one item, with itemKey the code, verdict ACCEPTED or REJECTED and a reason required for REJECTED; 422 MSG-P7-005, 409 MSG-GEN-004, 503 MSG-P7-003 | Case record U | Idempotency-Key header; one feedback per run and item |

Errors are the platform problem response: 401 no session, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404 an unknown case, run or version, 409 with MSG-GEN-004, MSG-P7-002 or MSG-P10-003, 422 with MSG-P7-005, MSG-P10-001 or MSG-P10-002, 503 with MSG-P7-003. No operation adds a code outside this set.

Both payloads are CloudEvents 1.0 with the attributes id, source, type, specversion, time, subject and datacontenttype; a payload that fails its registry subject is refused before the relay and routed to `.dlt` with an alert, and neither carries a personal field.

None. No Temporal Schedule belongs to this key: the evaluation is started by a person, a run starts from an event, and a verdict comes from a person. The legacy Quartz scheduler is retired and DP-10 is not a pattern of this key.

**Package and artefacts.** The contract lives with rwb-agent, `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.agent.contract`, as the OpenAPI and AsyncAPI fragments of the agent base, the JSON Schemas of the two payloads and the fake set of 12.8.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | Local decision-record library and the shared topic | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON (of the app story) |
| DP-05 | ACE data through rwb-source-data's contract or the own view | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Outbox and inbox library; owner topic; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/agent/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

This story is Day 1 and has no build dependency: the platform rows are the app story's H dependencies, and the rwb-case rows are its C dependencies, consumed here only as published shapes.

**Work items**

| Item | Deliverable |
|---|---|
| Evaluation narrowing | The OpenAPI fragment of the start and the report, the AgentEvaluationRun and AgentEvaluationReport schemas, the statuses and the three messages |
| Score row | The schema of `agent_evaluation` per code with the counts, precision and recall at four decimals, and the ratio check of the contract test |
| Segment and L1 decision | The policy payload with the two segment members, its LOADED and APPROVED outcomes, the separations of duty and the eligibility read |
| Record mapping | The mapping of ACCEPTED to the raise entry ID and of REJECTED to a library record written first, with the unique pair (agent_run_id, item_key) |
| Events | The AsyncAPI of `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics and of DecisionRecorded, with the registry subjects |
| Boundaries | The seven consumed shapes, the route, the error taxonomy and the absence rule |
| Fakes | The seven fakes of 12.8, with the answers, errors and timings the app, S8, P7 and integration tests need |

**Build steps**

1. Draft the two evaluation operations and the score row, with the X1 figures 41, 4 and 5 and the ratios 0.9111 and 0.8913 as contract examples (AC1, AC2).
2. Draft the policy payload with the segment members and the approval outcome, and the eligibility read (AC3).
3. Draft the feedback mapping and the idempotency pair against the record library (AC4).
4. Draft the two event schemas with their topics, retry and `.dlt` rules and registry subjects (AC5).
5. Write the error taxonomy, the route and the seven fakes (AC6).
6. Review against the Ownership Map and the no-lake rule, and remove every lake artefact and daily aggregate (AC7).
7. Publish, tag the baseline and hand the fakes to the app, S8, P7 and integration stories.

**Done when.** The seven contract tests of section 16 pass, the fakes answer every consumed path, the two event schemas carry their retry and `.dlt` topics, the X1 figures and the ratios appear exactly as in the legacy story, no lake artefact or daily aggregate is named, and the app story can start against the fakes on Day 1.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-002 | The approver loaded the version | You loaded this version, so you cannot approve it. |
| MSG-P7-003 | The record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-P7-005 | Reject without a reason | Enter the reason you are not following the recommendation. |
| MSG-P10-001 | A configuration file fails a check | The {kind} file for {agent} was refused: {check}. The version in force is unchanged. |
| MSG-P10-002 | The sample has no labelled row | The sample {sample} has no labelled row for {agent}. |
| MSG-P10-003 | A second evaluation is started while one runs | An evaluation of {agent} on {sample} is already running. |
| MSG-P10-008 | The report is read on a run that is not DONE | The report is not ready: the evaluation is {status}. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | A second verdict on the same item | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The message IDs and their texts are copied from the legacy story and the P10 FSD where they exist; this contract invents no text and adds no code. MSG-P7-002, MSG-P10-002, MSG-P10-003 and MSG-P10-008 are the messages of the baselines this document restates and are named so a reader of the key finds the whole refusal set; the wording stays with its owner.

None. This story delivers no screen: the panel "Proposed deviations" on SCR-03, its four states and the gateway-bff route in front of it are the app story's (section 15 of RWB-P10-E2029-APP), and this document fixes only the operations the panel and the verdict use.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in the contract: the segment, the floor and the condition appear only as examples copied from the legacy story and as rows read at run time (BR9).
- No personal data in a payload, a fixture or a log; every fixture is synthetic and no customer identifier appears in a schema.
- No lake artefact and no daily agent table: the absence rule is a review gate and a contract test (BR8).
- A restated operation is narrowed, never redefined; a drift is corrected in its baseline (BR11).
- Each call is one hop on the owner's base with a 2 s client budget, and no schema of another service is named (BR10).
- The record and the feedback are one transaction or neither, and the pair (agent_run_id, item_key) is the only idempotency key of a verdict (BR5, BR6).

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: app slice of RWB-E2-029 for rwb-agent. The business behaviour of the legacy story is kept whole - the evaluation of the screening agent on sample "SCREEN-S2" version 1 over 500 cases, the L1 proposal for segment MORTGAGE and region BKK, the mode per segment, the panel "Proposed deviations", the confirm path through the S8 deviation service under R-DEV-01, the reject path with its reason and its decision record, the confidence floor 0.80, the codes X1 to X7, the ten criteria and the twelve test cases. Only the seams move: the two E3 operations are served on the base `/api/recovery/agent/v1` (DP-13) with the shape baselined in RWB-P10-E1058-CON and published for E3 by RWB-P10-E2028-CON; the sample, the runs, the scores, the policy rows and the feedback stay in schema `rwb_agent`; the decision log becomes the local decision-record library on the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` (DP-03); the ACE collateral input of X7 is read through rwb-source-data or the service's own read-only view (DP-05); the floor, the segment values and the promotion condition are read from the rwb-case parameters and reference data (DP-06, DP-07); the outbox follows the platform envelope (DP-09); the legacy in-process `DeviationService.raise`, the case read, the owner check and the ledger become REST contracts with a mock, one hop and a 2 s budget (DP-11); and the panel is reached through the gateway-bff route (DP-19). Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **conduct and QA officer (RW-CONDUCT)**, I want **the deviation screening agent scored on 500 shadow cases and switched to L1 for Mortgage cases in Bangkok, with its proposed X flags shown on the panel "Proposed deviations" of SCR-03 Case record to the case owner to confirm or reject, each confirmation raised as a deviation through the rwb-deviation service under R-DEV-01 and each rejection written as a decision record before the feedback is stored**, so that **deviations on that segment are flagged from the first day a sign appears and the error rate per flag is known**.

##### 2. Business rationale

A deviation found weeks late means contact that should have stopped and clocks that should have paused. The shadow results of RWB-E1-062 give a measured precision and recall per code. This story scores a larger shadow run, records the proposal to go to L1 on one segment, and then shows the agent's proposals to the owner of each Mortgage case in Bangkok, who confirms or rejects each one. A confirmed proposal raises the deviation through the S8 deviation service, so the flag shows on the case and in every queue (REQ-DVH-006), and detection draws on case data, call notes and documents (REQ-DVH-001). Every other segment stays in shadow.

The legacy key was written inside one deployment; the target moves four seams and changes no business value:

- The runs, the scores, the policy versions and the feedback are P10 rows of `rwb_agent`, created by the earlier P10 stories; this story adds no table and no migration.
- The decision record of a rejection is written by the local library of DP-03 and published on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; rwb-decision owns the central ledger and seals the entry.
- The deviation service, the case of record, the owner check and the interaction ledger are other services; rwb-agent reaches each by one REST hop against its published contract and its fake, inside the 2 s client budget.
- The floor, the segment values, the condition and the seven codes are rows of the policy, the parameters and the reference data of rwb-case, read at run time and written nowhere in code.

The cross-service behaviour of this key - that a confirmation really raises one deviation and really moves the case to "On hold" under R-DEV-01, that the record is sealed in rwb-decision, and that the panel really reads the case facts - is proved by the wave 2 integration work of RWB-ITG-W2, which is why the story carries no integration dependency.

##### 3. Preconditions

- RWB-P10-E1062-APP is done: agent "SCREENING" runs in shadow from EV-01 CaseCreated and EV-16 DocumentStored, and stores one run per case and event with its proposed codes, their reasons, their source references, the preceding contact reference and their confidence.
- RWB-P10-E2029-CON is published: the screening narrowing of the evaluation start and the report, the score row shape per code, the policy payload with the two segment members and its approval, the decision-record mapping, the two event contracts, the error taxonomy and the fakes.
- RWB-P10-E2028-CON is published: the E3 operations `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` with its `proposals[]` member and `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs/{runId}/feedback`. This story restates them and adds no member.
- RWB-P10-E1061-CON is published: the evaluation start, the list and the report, and the L1 proposal payload with its condition check and its approval, reused here for agent "SCREENING" and policy "SCREENING" version "P2".
- RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON are published: the decision-record library and shared topic, the parameters and reference-data client libraries, the outbox and inbox library with the CloudEvents envelope, and the gateway-bff route contract with its stub.
- The rwb-case contracts are published: `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` (RWB-P3-E2015-CON), the parameters (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) and the lists (RWB-P3-E1043-CON).
- The rwb-deviation raise and open-deviation reads are consumed as REST contracts with a mock, one hop and the 2 s budget (DP-11); the story of the S8 slice that publishes the raise is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0625; ASM-0931).
- The L1 proposal checks exist in the policy loader of RWB-P10-E1061-CON, reused with the screening agent and its evaluation run.
- Sample "SCREEN-S2" version 1 holds the business analysts' review of 500 shadow cases, loaded through `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-samples` of RWB-P10-E1058-APP.
- The case owner holds RW-CASEOWN (Case record CRU) and the case is in scope.
- The per-service login of rwb-agent under DP-02 is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0625; ASM-0930); the story names it "the rwb-agent login (DP-02)" until it is agreed, and SY-AGENT stays the actor name of the run.
- The release date 31 January 2027 is tentative and is copied unchanged.

##### 4. Flow

1. RW-COE starts the evaluation of "SCREENING" on "SCREEN-S2" version 1 through `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations` of RWB-P10-E1061-CON (AC1).
2. The harness scores the 500 shadow cases and the service stores one `agent_evaluation` row per code X1 to X7 with the sample size, the true positives, the false positives, the false negatives, precision and recall (AC1; BR7).
3. `ScreeningEvaluationReporter` reads the run row and its score rows and confirms the counts: X1 with 41 true positives, 4 false positives and 5 false negatives gives precision 0.9111 and recall 0.8913 (AC1).
4. RW-COE loads policy "SCREENING" version "P2" with prompt "PR2", mode L1 for segment MORTGAGE and region BKK, the evaluation run, the promotion condition, the fallback rule and the watch measures through `POST /admin/agent-configs`; the promotion check reads the parameters and the lists of rwb-case at run time and refuses the load on a failed condition (DP-06, DP-07; AC1, AC10).
5. RW-RISK approves it through `POST /admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve`; the row stays LOADED until then and the version in force keeps serving (AC1).
6. `ScreeningModeListener` consumes EV-01 CaseCreated from `rwb.case.events.v1` and EV-16 DocumentStored from `rwb.document.events.v1`, dedupes on the event ID in the inbox, and `ResolveScreeningMode` reads `agent_policy.segment_product_group` and `agent_policy.segment_region_code` of the approved row: a Mortgage case in region BKK runs in L1, every other segment in shadow (BR1; AC2, AC3).
7. The run path of RWB-P10-E1062-APP assembles the masked inputs - the case facts, the open deviations, the ledger entries of the window and the documents with their masked fields - calls the model and stores one `agent_run` row with its proposals, their reasons, their sources, the preceding contact reference and their confidence (AC2, AC3, AC6, AC7).
8. The case owner opens SCR-03 through the gateway-bff route; `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` answers `AgentOutput[]` and the panel lists each proposed code with its reasons, its sources, its confidence and the marker "Agent output" (DP-19; AC2).
9. `ScreeningOutputFilter` drops a proposal whose code is already open on the case, read through the rwb-deviation contract, and sets the marker "Low confidence" on a proposal below the floor 0.80 of the policy in force (AC6, AC7).
10. The owner confirms a proposal: `ScreeningFeedbackHandler` calls the raise of rwb-deviation with the case ID, the code, the reason, the document IDs of the sources, `raisedBy` "SCREENING_AGENT" and the run ID, receives the deviation ID and the decision log entry ID, and stores `agent_feedback` with verdict ACCEPTED, item key the code and that entry ID (AC2; BR2, BR3).
11. The owner rejects a proposal with a reason: the handler writes the decision record first - decision the code, agent version "SCREENING@P2/PR2", final call REJECTED and the reason - through the library of DP-03 in the same transaction as the feedback, and only then stores `agent_feedback` with verdict REJECTED and the entry ID (BR4; AC4, AC5, AC9).
12. A rejection without a reason is refused with 422 and MSG-P7-005 before anything is written; a second confirmation of the same proposal is refused with 409 and MSG-GEN-004 and leaves one deviation; a decision record that cannot be written refuses the action with 503 and MSG-P7-003 and stores no feedback row (AC5, AC8, AC9).
13. Every read of another service is one hop on that service's base inside the 2 s budget; the model call keeps its own 60-second budget inside the run of RWB-P10-E1062-APP (DP-05, DP-11).

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The case is not Mortgage in region BKK | The run is in shadow; nothing is shown | None to a user | AC3 |
| X2 | Reject with no reason | Refused with 422 | MSG-P7-005 | AC5 |
| X3 | A proposal is below the confidence floor 0.80 | Shown with the marker "Low confidence" | None to a user | AC6 |
| X4 | The proposed code is already open on the case | The proposal is not shown | None to a user | AC7 |
| X5 | Two confirmations of the same proposal at once | One deviation; the second is refused with 409 | MSG-GEN-004 | AC8 |
| X6 | The decision log write fails on a rejection | Nothing stored; incident raised (R-UNI-39) | MSG-P7-003 | AC9 |
| X7 | The L1 proposal names scores below a stated condition | Policy load refused | MSG-P10-001 | AC10 |
| X8 | A role without Case record U confirms or rejects | Refused with 403 | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-029-11 |
| X9 | The parameters or the list read of rwb-case does not answer inside 2 s, or answers without the floor or the promotion condition | The load or the run is refused with 422 and MSG-P10-001 naming the missing parameter; no default and no code value is used and the version in force keeps serving | MSG-P10-001 | AC10 |
| X10 | The raise of rwb-deviation answers 503 or does not answer inside 2 s on a confirmation | The confirmation is refused with 503, no `agent_feedback` row is stored and the owner retries; rwb-agent raises no deviation of its own | None to a user | AC2 |
| X11 | The feature flag `rwb.agent.screening-l1` is off | Every segment runs in shadow and the panel is hidden, whatever the policy row says | None to a user | AC3 |

X1 to X8 are the legacy exception paths carried onto the service, with their legacy trigger, message and criterion unchanged. X9 to X11 are the failures that appear when the parameters and the lists become contracts, when the raise becomes a REST hop, and when the flag is read through the platform library instead of a local property.

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Reuses the screening run path (RWB-P10-E1062-APP), the evaluation contract (RWB-P10-E1061-CON), the E3 operations of RWB-P10-E2028-CON, the decision-record and outbox libraries and the three rwb-case contracts; it is the only in-lane story after RWB-P10-E1062-APP |
| Negotiable | The segment, the floor and the condition are rows of the policy and the parameters; the package, the component names and the panel layout are design |
| Valuable | Flags deviations on Mortgage cases in Bangkok when the sign appears, with a person deciding each one |
| Estimable | One evaluation report read, one mode resolver, one output filter, one feedback handler with two verdicts, one decision record, one panel, against four contract clients |
| Small | Two developers for two weeks, the legacy estimate, unchanged |
| Testable | Each of the ten criteria is one automated test on an observable: a score row, a policy row, a run row, a panel element, a deviation, a feedback row, a decision record or a refusal code |

```gherkin

    Given case owner "owner.user07" holds RW-CASEOWN

  Scenario: AC1 Evaluation (legacy RWB-E2-029 AC1)

  Scenario: AC2 L1 on one segment (legacy RWB-E2-029 AC2)

  Scenario: AC3 Other segments (legacy RWB-E2-029 AC3)
    Given the rwb-case contract mock returns case "RW-2027-000802" with product group HIRE_PURCHASE and region BKK
    Given hire purchase case "RW-2027-000802" in region BKK
    When the agent runs
    Then the result stays in shadow and GET /cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs returns no screening output

  Scenario: AC4 The owner rejects a proposal (legacy RWB-E2-029 AC4)

    When both requests arrive
    Then one deviation X1 exists and the second request is refused with 409 and MSG-GEN-004

```

**Target reading.** The segment MORTGAGE and region BKK, policy "SCREENING" version "P2", prompt "PR2", sample "SCREEN-S2" version 1, the 500 cases, the counts 41, 4 and 5, the scores 0.9111 and 0.8913, the cases "RW-2027-000801" to "RW-2027-000804", the complaint note of 2027-01-26, the rejection reason, the confidence 0.72, the floor 0.80, the recall 0.6000 against the condition 0.75, the statuses "LOADED", "On hold", "ACCEPTED" and "REJECTED", the agent version "SCREENING@P2/PR2", the codes X1 to X7, R-DEV-01, R-UNI-39 and the messages MSG-P7-005, MSG-P7-003, MSG-GEN-004, MSG-P10-001 and MSG-P4-002 are the legacy values of RWB-E2-029, copied character for character. The ten scenario titles and every legacy Given, When and Then are kept, and each carries the origin tag of its legacy criterion.

Each scenario whose content crosses a service boundary gained one or more inserted Givens of the form `Given the <service> contract mock returns <x>`, and nothing the service owns is mocked. AC1 and AC10 read the promotion checks through the rwb-case parameters contract. AC2 reads the case facts and the status through the P3 contract, the preceding contact through the rwb-source-data contract (DP-05) and the raised deviation with its entry ID through the rwb-deviation contract. AC3 and AC6 read the case facts through the P3 contract. AC4 reads the recorded entry back from rwb-decision, which seals what the local library writes. AC7 and AC8 read the open deviations and the raise outcome through the rwb-deviation contract. AC5 and AC9 cross no boundary: the reason check and the record write are the service's own. The window of the screening read is the one fixed by RWB-P10-E1062-APP and read through the parameters; the legacy criteria name no window and this story sets none.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Mode L1 applies only where the case product group and region match the policy segment; elsewhere the mode is SHADOW | agent_policy.segment_product_group, segment_region_code (DF-AGT-009, DF-AGT-010); legacy BR1 |
| BR2 | The agent raises nothing itself; a deviation is raised only when a person confirms the proposal | Agent catalog, screening agent "May decide alone: Nothing"; SY-AGENT has no Case record U; legacy BR2 |
| BR3 | A confirmed proposal is raised through S8 with raised_by SCREENING_AGENT, and R-DEV-01 pauses the stage clock and routes the case | R-DEV-01; LOV-RAISED-BY; legacy BR3 |
| BR4 | A rejection needs a reason and writes a decision record before the feedback is stored | CTL-07; Principle 5; R-UNI-39; legacy BR4 |
| BR5 | A proposal for a code already open is not shown | deviation.deviation_code (DF-CAS-038); legacy BR5 |
| BR6 | A proposal below the floor 0.80 is shown with the marker "Low confidence" | agent_policy.confidence_floor (DF-AGT-011); FEAT-DVH-08; legacy BR6 |
| BR7 | An L1 proposal must meet its stated conditions on the named evaluation | Principle 1; CTL-08; legacy BR7 |
| BR8 | The mode of a run is resolved from the approved policy row of `rwb_agent` and the case facts read through the rwb-case contract; no other service decides the mode | DP-01; DP-11; ownership of `agent_policy` |
| BR9 | The decision record of a rejection is written by the local library in the same transaction as the feedback and published on `rwb.decision-record.v1`; rwb-decision owns the central ledger and seals the entry | DP-03; ADR-022; R-UNI-39 |
| BR10 | ACE facts - the collateral appraisal date of an X7 proposal - are read through the rwb-source-data contract or the service's own read-only `v_ace_*` view, never from an ACE table and never from another service's row | DP-05; §R7.2 s17; ownership of `valuation_ext` |
| BR11 | The floor, the promotion condition and the segment values are parameters and reference data of rwb-case, read at run time with their version and never written in code | DP-06; DP-07; BR-P10-008; FSD P10 A2.8.3 |
| BR12 | Every read of another service is one hop on that service's base with a 2 s client budget; the model call keeps its own 60-second budget inside the run | DP-11; ADR-020; NFR-010 |
| BR13 | The panel is reached through the gateway-bff route and the two E3 operations are served on `/api/recovery/agent/v1`; no screen calls the service directly and no monolith base is served | DP-13; DP-19; ADR-019 |

##### 9. State transitions

The case state of a confirmed proposal, applied by S8 under R-DEV-01 and not by rwb-agent:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| ANY_STATE | DEVIATION_FLAGGED | The owner confirms a proposal; deviation_code in X1 to X7 (R-DEV-01, applied by S8) | DEV_FLAGGED |
| New, Assigned, In progress, any Waiting | Deviation flagged | As above | On hold |

A rejected proposal changes no case status. The state of one proposal of a run and of its feedback row:

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Proposed | The panel loads | The code is already open on the case | Not shown; no feedback row |
| Proposed | The panel loads | The confidence is below the floor of the policy in force | Shown with the marker "Low confidence" |
| Proposed | The owner confirms | The raise succeeds | Deviation raised; `agent_feedback` ACCEPTED with the entry ID |
| Proposed | The owner confirms | The raise answers 409 | One deviation; 409 MSG-GEN-004; no second feedback row |
| Proposed | The owner confirms | The raise answers 503 or times out | No feedback row; the owner retries |
| Proposed | The owner rejects with a reason | The record is written | Decision record REJECTED, then `agent_feedback` REJECTED |
| Proposed | The owner rejects without a reason | The reason is empty | No write; 422 MSG-P7-005 |
| Proposed | The owner rejects with a reason | The record cannot be written | No write; 503 MSG-P7-003; incident under R-UNI-39 |

##### 10. Authority

| Who | What they may do in this story |
|---|---|
| RW-CASEOWN | Reads proposals for cases in scope (Case record R); confirms or rejects (Case record U) |
| SY-AGENT | Runs the agent (read only) |
| S8 deviation service, under the owner's identity | Raises the deviation and writes its decision log entry |
| RW-COE | Runs the evaluation and loads the L1 proposal (Rules and parameters C) |
| RW-RISK | Approves the L1 proposal (Rules and parameters A) |
| RW-CONDUCT | Reads scores (Rules and parameters R) |
| The rwb-agent login (DP-02) | Resolves the mode, filters the proposals, writes `agent_feedback` and the record in `rwb_agent`, and calls the P3, P1, S8 and P7 contracts |
| rwb-deviation (S8) | Owns the deviation, applies R-DEV-01 and publishes EV-06 |
| rwb-decision (P7) | Owns the central ledger, `decision_log_entry` and the sealing of a record |
| rwb-source-data (P1) | Owns the interaction ledger, the ACE view contract and the extension tables |
| rwb-case (P3) | Owns the case of record, the owner check, the parameters and the reference lists |
| No role | Reads `rwb_case`, `rwb_deviation`, `rwb_decision` or another service's schema as a table, or raises a deviation without a person's confirmation |

The login of the service is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0625; ASM-0930). No delegation of authority level applies; the approval of the L1 proposal is the Rules and parameters A right of RW-RISK and the separation of duty between loader and approver is the one fixed by RWB-P10-E1061-CON.

No field of another service's table is written here: the deviation, the case status and the entry are written by their owners on a call of this story. The policy write is the configuration operation of RWB-P10-E1058-APP used to load version "P2"; the sample is loaded through the sample operation of the same story.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`; owner rwb-agent (P10). Neither operation is new here: both are baselined in RWB-P10-E1058-CON and published for E3 by RWB-P10-E2028-CON, and this story supplies their screening behaviour and adds no member.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Access | Idempotency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` | Read the L1 outputs of a case for the panel: `AgentOutput[]` with `proposals[{code, reasons, sourceRefs, precedingContactId, confidence, lowConfidence, feedback}]`; a case with no L1 run answers no screening output; errors 401, 403, 404 (MSG-P4-003), 503 | Case record R, scope applied | Not applicable: the call writes nothing |
| POST | `/agent-runs/{runId}/feedback` | Record the owner's verdict on one proposal: AgentFeedbackRequest with itemKey = the code ("X1" … "X7"), verdict ACCEPTED or REJECTED and reason, required for REJECTED; 200 AgentOutput; errors 401, 403, 404, 409 (MSG-GEN-004), 422 (MSG-P7-005), 503 (MSG-P7-003) | Case record U, scope applied | Idempotency-Key header; one feedback per run and item |

Errors: 401 no session, 403 no Case record right (MSG-P4-002), 404 an unknown case or run (MSG-P4-003), 409 a second verdict on the same item (MSG-GEN-004), 422 an empty reason (MSG-P7-005), 503 the store, the library or a consumed contract unavailable (MSG-P7-003). The configuration operations `POST /admin/agent-configs`, `POST /admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve` and `POST /admin/agent-samples` of RWB-P10-E1058-CON and the evaluation operations with the report read of RWB-P10-E1061-CON are used here and are not re-declared.

| Method | Path | Owner | Use | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case (RWB-P3-E2015-CON) | AC2, AC3, AC6: the case facts and the status - product group MORTGAGE, region BKK, "In progress", then "On hold" after R-DEV-01 | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) | AC1, AC6, AC10: the floor 0.80, the segment values and the promotion condition in force | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | AC1, AC2, AC8: LOV-DEVIATION (X1 to X7), LOV-AGENT, LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-CONFIG-STATUS, LOV-FEEDBACK, LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-REGION, LOV-RAISED-BY | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1/deviations?caseId=` | S8 rwb-deviation | AC7: the open deviations of the case, so a code already open is not shown | One hop, 2 s |
| POST | the raise of rwb-deviation: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0625; ASM-0931) | S8 rwb-deviation | AC2, AC8: the legacy `DeviationService.raise(caseId, deviationCode, reason, documentIds, raisedBy, agentRunId)`, answered with the deviation ID and the entry ID | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | the interaction-ledger read of rwb-source-data for the entries of a case in a window: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0625; ASM-0936) | P1 rwb-source-data | AC2: the preceding contact of an X1 proposal, and the ACE facts of X7 through the contract or the service's own `v_ace_*` view (DP-05) | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | the sealed entry read of rwb-decision: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0625; ASM-0933) | P7 rwb-decision | AC4, AC9: the sealed entry of the record the local library wrote, so `agent_feedback.decision_log_id` names it | One hop, 2 s |

Every call is one hop to the owning service on its own base (DP-13) with the 2 s client budget (DP-11); rwb-agent calls no service through another service and holds no schema client of another service. The ACE read of X7 adds no dependency (DP-05).

###### 12.3 Events published

| DecisionRecorded, the record type of the library | `rwb.decision-record.v1`, shared, with its retry and `.dlt` topics (DP-03) | P7 rwb-decision owns the ledger; the library of RWB-PLT-E1027-CON owns the envelope | the case ID | the record of a rejection: decision the code, agent version "SCREENING@P2/PR2", final call REJECTED, the reason, the run ID and the entry ID |

The record is inserted by the library in the same transaction as the `agent_feedback` row and published by the outbox relay of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON; the payload carries no personal data (section 17). This story publishes no agent event of its own: `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28) on `rwb.agent.events.v1` comes from the run path of RWB-P10-E1062-APP, and EV-06 DeviationRaised on `rwb.deviation.events.v1` is published by S8 on a confirmation.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| AgentRunWorkflow | Workflow, one per case and triggering event (of RWB-P10-E1062-APP, restated) | `rwb-agent` | Input: agent "SCREENING", case ID, subject ID, trigger event, event ID, idempotency key and the resolved mode. One execution per key, the 60-second policy budget, then the rule result (R-UNI-32) |
| ResolveScreeningMode | Activity, added by this story | `rwb-agent` | Reads the approved policy row of `rwb_agent` and the case facts of the P3 contract; output: mode L1 or SHADOW, the policy version and the segment it matched, or the refusal of X9 |

The confirmation and the rejection are synchronous inside the feedback request: the handler calls the S8 raise, writes the record, stores the feedback and answers 200, so no workflow is added beyond the relay of the record.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Temporal Schedule belongs to this story: the evaluation is started by RW-COE, a run starts from EV-01 or EV-16, and a verdict comes from a person. The legacy Quartz scheduler is retired and DP-10 is not a pattern of this key.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.agent.screening` inside rwb-agent; the front end module of the panel lives with the SCR-03 composition and is reached through the gateway-bff route.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | ACE data through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/agent/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-05 and DP-11 add no dependency of their own: the ACE facts arrive through the owner's contract or the service's own view, and the legacy in-process calls are the C contracts of the key and their fakes. The S8 raise is consumed with a mock because no source names the story that publishes it (GAP-0625; ASM-0931).

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| ScreeningModeListener, ResolveScreeningMode | Listener and activity | BR1, BR8: the mode per segment from the approved policy row, with the product group and the region checked through the rwb-case lists |
| ScreeningEvaluationReporter | Service | BR7: reads the run and its score rows, keeps precision and recall per code at four decimals, confirms the sample size 500 |
| ScreeningProposalReadService | Service | Serves the panel read from `agent_run` and `agent_feedback` of `rwb_agent` only |
| ScreeningOutputFilter | Service | BR5, BR6: drops a code already open and sets the marker "Low confidence" below the floor in force |
| ScreeningFeedbackHandler | Service | Both verdicts: ACCEPTED calls the raise and stores the feedback with the entry ID; REJECTED writes the record first, then the feedback |
| DecisionRecordWriter | Client of the platform library | BR4, BR9: inserts the record and the outbox row in the feedback transaction and reads the entry ID back |
| ProposedDeviationsPanel | React component | The panel on SCR-03: code, reasons, sources, confidence, the marker, Confirm, and Reject with a reason |
| AgentFeedbackService | Service | Extended with the item keys X1 to X7 and the one-verdict rule |
| CaseFactReader, ParameterValueReader, ReferenceDataReader | Clients | The P3 case read, the parameters and the lists (DP-06, DP-07, DP-11) |
| DeviationRaiseClient, OpenDeviationReader | Clients | The S8 raise and the open deviations of the case (DP-11) |
| LedgerReader, AceFactReader | Clients | The preceding contact of X1 and the appraisal date of X7 through P1 or the own view (DP-05) |

**Database and migrations.** No new table and no new column: `agent_feedback`, `agent_policy`, `agent_evaluation`, `agent_evaluation_run`, `agent_run`, `agent_sample` and `agent_prompt` exist from the earlier P10 stories (GAP-0625; ASM-0938). The indexes the panel and the evaluation need - on `agent_feedback (agent_run_id, item_key)` and on `agent_evaluation (evaluation_run_id, label_key)` - are created by the earlier migrations if not already present. No other schema is touched (DP-01).

**Configuration and reference data.** Policy "SCREENING" version "P2" with prompt "PR2", mode L1 for MORTGAGE and BKK, shadow elsewhere, the evaluation run of "SCREEN-S2" version 1, the condition "recall at least 0.75 for every code", the fallback rule and the watch measures, loaded by RW-COE and approved by RW-RISK. Sample "SCREEN-S2" version 1, the analysts' review of 500 cases. The floor 0.80, the segment values and the condition as parameters of rwb-case (DP-06) and the eight lists as its reference data (DP-07); the parameter keys are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0625; ASM-0934). The flag `rwb.agent.screening-l1` is kept as a legacy reference and read through the platform flag library: off, every segment runs in shadow and the panel is hidden (ASM-0939).

**Build steps**

1. Run the evaluation on "SCREEN-S2" version 1 and load the L1 proposal in SIT, against the parameters and lists fakes (AC1, AC10).
2. Extend the listener for the mode per segment with ResolveScreeningMode and the P3 case read (AC2, AC3).
3. Build ScreeningOutputFilter with the open-deviation read and the floor in force (AC6, AC7).
4. Build ScreeningFeedbackHandler for both verdicts, with the raise on ACCEPTED and the record first on REJECTED (AC2, AC4, AC5, AC9).
5. Add the parallel-confirmation test against the S8 fake, the 409 and the one-deviation outcome (AC8).
6. Build ProposedDeviationsPanel with its four states and the route in front of the panel read (AC2, AC6).
7. Pipeline scans: no business value of the segment, the floor or the condition in the source; no monolith base path; no other service's table name; no ACE table name outside the owner's view.
8. Contract tests of the two E3 operations against their baselines, so a drift is corrected in RWB-P10-E2028-CON and never here.

**Done when.** The twelve test cases of section 16 pass, the evaluation stores seven score rows with sample size 500 and X1 at 0.9111 and 0.8913, policy "P2" is LOADED with MORTGAGE and BKK and is refused when a condition fails, a Mortgage case in Bangkok shows its proposals and a hire purchase case shows none, a confirmation raises one deviation with its entry ID and an ACCEPTED row, a rejection writes one record and a REJECTED row, the refusals answer 422, 409 and 503 with their messages, and the scans find no code value and no monolith base.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-005 | Reject without a reason | Enter the reason you are not following the recommendation. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Second confirmation of the same proposal | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P10-001 | L1 proposal fails a check | The {kind} file for {agent} was refused: {check}. The version in force is unchanged. |
| MSG-S8-001 | Deviation raised after confirmation | {deviation} was raised. The case is with {handler}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |
| MSG-P4-003 | The case or the run is unknown | That record is not available to you. |

The six texts of the legacy table are copied unchanged and this story adds no message ID; MSG-P4-003 is the access message the legacy section 12 names for an unknown case or run, kept here so the refusal set of the key is complete. In AC5 the empty reason is refused before anything is written; in AC8 the {action} of MSG-GEN-004 is the second confirmation and the first one stands; in AC9 no feedback row exists; in AC10 {kind} is the policy file, {agent} is "SCREENING" and {check} is "X4 recall 0.6000 below 0.75"; in the access test {action} is "confirm or reject a proposed deviation".

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-03 Case record gains the panel "Proposed deviations" with states: empty (no panel), ready (proposals with Confirm and Reject), low confidence (marker on the proposal), recorded (verdict and date). After a confirmation SCR-03 shows the on hold banner of the deviation and SCR-08 Deviation queue lists it for the named handler; SCR-46 Agent monitor shows SCREENING as live for MORTGAGE/BKK and shadow elsewhere.

In the target the panel is composed by the gateway-bff route (DP-19) and reads `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs`; the verdict goes to `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs/{runId}/feedback`. The four states are unchanged, and a proposal is hidden when its code is already open or when the flag is off. The route name and path are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0625; ASM-0937); the route passes the read and the refusal through unchanged.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the segment, the floor and the condition are rows of the policy, the parameters and the reference data, read with their version (BR11).
- No personal data in logs, tests, events or prompts; reasons on the panel hold masking tokens.
- No read of another service's table: the case, the deviation, the ledger and the entry come through their owners' contracts, and ACE facts only through rwb-source-data or the service's own read-only `v_ace_*` view (BR10).
- The agent never raises a deviation without a person's confirmation, and no rejection reaches the feedback row before its record is written (BR2, BR4, BR9).
- Every consumed call is one hop with a 2 s client budget; the model call keeps its own 60-second budget inside the run (BR12).
- The panel is reached through the gateway-bff route and never from a screen to the service (BR13).
- The feedback is idempotent on the run, the item key and the verdict, and one deviation exists per confirmed proposal (AC8).
