##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision`, module `promotion/screening`, Java package `th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.decision.promotion`.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added |
|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON |

DP-03 is the core: the legacy `DecisionLogWriter` becomes the local decision-record library, which writes the record, the chain link, the approval status and the outbox row in one transaction. DP-06 and DP-07 carry every business value of the key — the condition set, the floor 0.80, the segment pair, the codes, the statuses and the approval level — with their versions, so a threshold or a limit is a row and not a release. DP-11 is the one hop to `rwb-agent` for the evaluation and the run, against the published contract and its fake. DP-05 gives the freshness of the ACE input without a read of an ACE table. DP-09 is the outbox and the CloudEvents envelope of the two published facts. DP-13 puts the eight operations on `/api/recovery/decision/v1` and DP-19 is the composite route through which the approval and ledger reads are reached; this story adds no route and serves no screen of its own.

The platform H dependencies of the table (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, H RWB-PLT-N001-CON) and the two C dependencies that DP-06 and DP-07 bring (C RWB-P3-E1042-CON, C RWB-P3-E1043-CON) are not in the metadata rows of this story, which name None and RWB-P10-E2029-CON; they are the dependencies the DP table adds and they are recorded in GAP-2402 and ASM-3995. None of them blocks the build beyond Day 1: they are platform contracts of wave 0 and published contracts of another service.

**Components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| PromotionRecordController | Controller | The append on `POST /decision-log` with the shape and idempotency validation, and the 201 and 200 answers |
| ApprovalController | Controller | `GET /approvals`, `GET /approvals/{approvalId}`, `POST …/approve`, `…/return`, `…/refuse` with the guard and the problem mapping |
| DecisionRecordController | Controller | `GET /decision-log` and `GET /decision-log/{entryId}` with the guard, the scope and the page |
| PromotionGate | Service | Reads the condition set and the floor of DP-06 and the evaluation of the P10 contract, and refuses a promotion that misses a condition with MSG-P10-001 |
| ApprovalService | Service | Writes the item with its level, its preparer, its status and its source reference; moves it through LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS; refuses a self-approval with MSG-P7-002 and holds a level above the limit with MSG-P7-001 |
| ProposalRecordService | Service | Validates the reason of a rejection, reads the run for the agent version and the data date, and builds the record |
| ChainWriter | Service | Reads the head of the chain under the append lock, computes the entry hash over the canonical form and builds the previous hash and the sequence number |
| DecisionRecordAppendService | Service | One `RecordAndApply` transaction: the record, the chain link, the approval status and the outbox row, or nothing; maps a failure to 503 with MSG-P7-003 |
| DecisionRecordQueryService | Service | The ledger page and the single record with the scope filter applied to the case read |
| AgentContractClient | Adapter | The evaluation and run reads of RWB-P10-E2029-CON, one hop with a 2 s timeout and a breaker |
| ParameterClient, ReferenceDataClient | Client | The DP-06 and DP-07 reads with the version in force |
| AccessCheckClient, CaseScopeClient | Client | The authorise answer behind every read and the P3 case read of the scope filter |

**Database and migrations**

- Writes `decision_log_entry`, `approval` and the outbox and idempotency objects of the library, all in schema `rwb_decision`; reads no other schema.
- The `decision_log_entry` baseline, its append-only trigger and its grants belong to the decision-log store slice of this service (legacy RWB-E1-008), and the `approval` baseline to the approval routing slice; this story widens neither.
- Migration in this story, in the per-service Flyway sequence: adds the unique key of `decision_log_entry (chain_seq)`, the unique key of the idempotency key, the index of the ledger read by case and decided time, the unique key that holds one record per approval on `approval (source_type, source_ref, status)` where the status is APPROVED, and the foreign key of `approval.decision_log_id` to `decision_log_entry (id)`.
- No row is updated except the status and the decision log reference of `approval`; no record row is ever updated or deleted.

**Configuration and reference data**

- The condition set "recall at least 0.75 for every code" and the confidence floor 0.80 are parameter values read through DP-06 with the version in force; the segment pair MORTGAGE and BKK, the codes X1 to X7 and the statuses are reference-data values through DP-07.
- The approval level and its limit come from the delegation of authority read with its version at the moment of the decision, and the version used is written on the record (BR5).
- The promotion decision code is a value of LOV-DECISION and its value is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2402; ASM-3990); the story validates against the list and never hard-codes the code.
- The feature switch of the legacy capability, `rwb.agent.screening-l1`, stays with RWB-P10-E2029-APP and is not read here: a record that could be switched off would break R-UNI-39 (ASM-3996).
- The `rwb-decision` login of DP-02, the Flyway user and the outbox relay identity are environment configuration and not values of this story.

**Build steps**

1. The migration with the two unique keys of the ledger and the one record per approval; test that a repeated chain sequence, a repeated idempotency key and a second approval are refused by the constraints (BR10, BR12, X8).
2. `PromotionGate` with the DP-06 conditions and the P10 evaluation read, and the refusal naming code, value and threshold; tests for AC2 and TC-E2-029-10.
3. `ApprovalService` with the item, the level, the preparer and the status machine; tests for AC1, AC4 and TC-E2-029-01.
4. `ChainWriter` with the head read, the canonical form and the entry hash; test the seeded chain and the first record with the previous hash of 64 zeros (AC1, AC5).
5. `ProposalRecordService` and `DecisionRecordAppendService` with the reason rule and the fail-closed transaction; tests for AC5, AC6, AC7, TC-E2-029-04, TC-E2-029-05, TC-E2-029-09 and TC-E2-029-12.
6. The parallel approval path and its 409; tests for AC8 and TC-E2-029-08.
7. `DecisionRecordController` and `DecisionRecordQueryService` with the authorise answer, the scope filter and the page; tests for AC9 and TC-E2-029-11.
8. The freshness read of DP-05 and the data date on the inputs reference; test for AC5.
9. The privacy test: no record, event payload or log carries a name, an e-mail address, a mobile number, a national identity number or an account number (AC1, AC5).

**Done when.** The tests in section 16 pass, the contract tests of RWB-P10-E2029-CON stay green, and a SIT day shows one dated promotion record for MORTGAGE and BKK with its evaluation run and condition set, a promotion refused when a code misses a condition, one record per rejected proposal with the reason and the agent version "SCREENING@P2/PR2", a chain that verifies from its first entry, one event per record and per approval request, no record and no feedback row when the record cannot be written, and no personal data in any record, event or log.

##### 14. Validation and messages

|---|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-005 | A rejection carries no reason | Enter the reason you are not following the recommendation. | This story, on the append |
| MSG-P7-003 | The decision record cannot be written | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. | This story, on the append transaction |
| MSG-P10-001 | A promotion misses a stated condition | The {kind} file for {agent} was refused: {check}. The version in force is unchanged. | This story, on the gate; the message id is the agent's and the check is the condition set |
| MSG-P7-002 | The preparer approves what the preparer prepared | You prepared this decision, so you cannot approve it. | This story, on the approval |
| MSG-P7-001 | The approval needs a level above the caller's limit | This needs approval at level {level}. It has been sent to {approver}. | This story, on the approval; the level and the approver are reference-data values |
| MSG-P7-009 | A code, a final call or a required version is not a value it must have | Not specified in the source documents (GAP-2402; ASM-3990) | This story, on the validation; the FSD names only the identifier and the field |
| MSG-GEN-004 | The item already moved, or a second approval arrives | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. | This story, on the approval |
| MSG-P4-002 | The reader holds no Decision log right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. | This story, through the authorise answer |
| MSG-S8-001 | A deviation is raised after a confirmation | {deviation} was raised. The case is with {handler}. | `rwb-deviation`, on the confirmation; this story produces no message |

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the condition set, the confidence floor, the segment pair, the codes, the statuses, the approval level and the message texts are parameter, reference-data or message-standard rows; nothing of them is a constant here.
- No personal data in the record, the event payload, the trail, the tests or the prompts: case and run identifiers, codes, versions, scores, a condition set, a reason, user references and dates only.
- No read of another service's tables (DP-01): the evaluation and the run arrive on the P10 contract, the case, the parameters and the lists on the P3 contracts, and the right on the authorise answer; no `agent_*`, `recovery_case`, `deviation` or `delegation_limit` row is copied into `rwb_decision`.
- ACE data only through the owner's contract or `v_ace_*` views: this story reads one appraisal date on the `rwb-source-data` contract or its own `v_ace_valuation` view and no ACE table (DP-05).
- One recorder and no mover: this story raises no deviation, pauses no clock, changes no case status and stores no feedback, so a record can never move a case.
- No record without its event and no event without its record: the record, the chain link, the approval status and the outbox row commit in one transaction, and a failure changes nothing and leaves the writer's feedback unwritten (R-UNI-39).
- Append only and hash chained: no update path and no delete path exist on a record, the sequence number is never reused, and a wrong record is corrected by a new record naming the one it corrects.
- A person decides a promotion: the agent may propose, and no path lets the agent, a job or a retry approve a promotion, move an item to APPROVED or write a rejection on its own behalf.
- One base, one topic, one queue: `/api/recovery/decision/v1`, `rwb.decision.events.v1` and `rwb-decision` in namespace `rwb-recovery`, with the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` for the record event.
- One hop and 2 s on every call, with a breaker per downstream; a missing answer never produces a record from a guessed version, code or score.
- The record path is never gated by a feature flag and never skipped for speed: an approval or a rejection without its record is a defect, not a degraded mode.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: split from RWB-E2-029 for the wave 2 integration harness. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **squad member (RW-TRIBE)**, I want **a repeatable cross-service harness for the deviation screening agent — the SCREEN-S2 evaluation with precision and recall per code, the L1 proposal and its approval for MORTGAGE in BKK, the proposals a run stores, the owner's confirmation that raises X1 through rwb-deviation under R-DEV-01 and pauses the stage clock, the rejection that writes its decision record first, and the measure the evaluation carries — with the evidence pack attached to the wave 2 release**, so that **the deviation-screening journey is proven end to end across rwb-agent, rwb-case, rwb-deviation and rwb-decision before RWB-P3-E2015-APP, RWB-P10-E2029-APP, RWB-S8-E2029-APP and RWB-P7-E2029-APP claim Done**.

This story builds the harness, its contract fakes, its seed pack, its evidence pack and its pass or fail gate. It builds no production endpoint, no screen, no table and no migration. Nothing it writes is deployed to a service.

No single app story can prove the journey. RWB-P3-E2015-APP can prove that the case record carries the product group and region, that the timers are stored and that the case turns "On hold" when a deviation clears it. RWB-P10-E2029-APP can prove that the evaluation is scored per code on a sample, that the L1 proposal is loaded and approved, that a run in mode L1 stores proposals and that a verdict is accepted or refused. RWB-S8-E2029-APP can prove that a raise with `raised_by` "SCREENING_AGENT" creates one deviation under R-DEV-01. RWB-P7-E2029-APP can prove that a rejection writes one decision record with the agent version and the reason, and that the ledger read returns it. The agreement of all four — one evaluation of 500 cases whose precision 0.9111 and recall 0.8913 for X1 are the numbers the L1 proposal names, one run whose proposals the owner decides, one confirmation that raises exactly one deviation and pauses exactly one clock while the prescription clock keeps running, one rejection that leaves one decision record and no deviation — is this story, and only this story.

##### 2. Business rationale

RWB-E2-029 split into four app stories and this integration story. The app stories build the evaluation and the policy load, the output read and the feedback write, the deviation raise with its decision log entry, the decision-record mapping and the timer pause and resume inside their own services. What no app story can prove on its own is the chain the business actually relies on: SCREENING is evaluated on sample "SCREEN-S2" version 1 and the score per code is stored; the L1 proposal for segment MORTGAGE and region BKK is loaded with that evaluation run and its conditions, and approved; a run on a Mortgage case in Bangkok stores proposals, and the case record shows them; the owner confirms one, rwb-deviation raises that deviation with `raised_by` "SCREENING_AGENT" and applies R-DEV-01, which pauses the stage clock and leaves the prescription clock running, and the case goes "On hold"; the owner rejects another, and the decision record is written before the feedback row and no deviation exists; and the measure the evaluation stored is the measure the proposal and the reader see. That proof is this story.

The journey carries two requirements. Deviations X1 to X7 are detected from case data, call notes, documents and external flags (REQ-DVH-001): the harness asserts that the run of case "RW-2027-000801" was started on `CaseCreated` and drew on the complaint note stored on 2027-01-26 through `DocumentStored`, and that the proposals it reads back carry their reasons and sources. A deviation flag is visible on the case record and in every queue (REQ-DVH-006): the harness asserts that the case reads back "On hold" through rwb-case and that the same X1 the confirmation raised is the deviation `DeviationRaised` announces on the deviation topic, which is what every queue projects.

Architecture v5 changes the path, not the business. In the monolith the agent client, the policy row, the feedback table, the deviation raise, the timers and the decision log all sat in one deployment and one schema. In the target:

- the local decision record and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` carry every entry, with rwb-decision holding the ledger (DP-03);
- the ACE data behind the X7 collateral inputs is read only by rwb-source-data through the `v_ace_*` views, and every other service asks its contract, so the harness reads the appraisal date through the owner's answer and never a view (DP-05);
- the policy version, the segment and the parameters behind it are configuration data served by the owning service, never values in code (DP-06);
- the deviation codes X1 to X7, the `raised_by` value "SCREENING_AGENT" and the verdict list are reference data of the owning contract, not literals in a scenario (DP-07);
- the events are CloudEvents on the owner's topic, with an outbox on the producer and an inbox on the consumer, so a replay never counts a case twice (DP-09);
- the in-process `DeviationService.raise` of the monolith is a REST contract with a mock, one hop and the 2 s timeout, and the answer carries the deviation ID and the decision log entry ID (DP-11);
- every path is on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` (DP-13);
- the proposal panel is composed by gateway-bff from the P10 output and the P3 case, so the harness drives the same route the case record uses (DP-19).

The measure is the journey evidence: for each owned criterion, one pass or fail with the evaluation rows, the policy version, the run, the proposals, the confirmation, the deviation, the case state, the two clocks, the rejection record and the measure captured in one report that can be re-run for any build.

##### 3. Preconditions

- Policy "SCREENING" version "P2" with prompt "PR2" is in force with mode "L1" for segment MORTGAGE and region BKK and mode "SHADOW" for every other segment, and carries the confidence floor 0.80 (legacy sections 3, 7 and 8).
- Sample "SCREEN-S2" version 1 holds the analysts' review of 500 shadow cases, with the X1 counts 41 true positives, 4 false positives and 5 false negatives, which is precision 0.9111 and recall 0.8913, and X4 at recall 0.6000 against the condition "recall at least 0.75 for every code" (legacy AC1 and AC10).
- Cases "RW-2027-000801" (Mortgage, region BKK, complaint note 2027-01-26, and a proposal for X6), "RW-2027-000802" (hire purchase, region BKK), "RW-2027-000803" (X2 at confidence 0.72) and "RW-2027-000804" (X1 confirmed twice at once) are seeded, owned by "owner.user07" with RW-CASEOWN and Case record CRU, and in that user's scope; a test user of role RW-PHONECOL holds Case record R only (legacy sections 3 and 7, TC-E2-029-11).
- The four integration dependencies have published their contracts, or their contract fakes stand in for them: RWB-P3-E2015-APP (rwb-case, the case record and the two clocks), RWB-P10-E2029-APP (rwb-agent, the evaluation, the policy load, the output read and the feedback write), RWB-S8-E2029-APP (rwb-deviation, the raise and R-DEV-01) and RWB-P7-E2029-APP (rwb-decision, the decision record and the ledger read).
- The wave 2 harness environment (SIT) is available with the gateway route for `/api/recovery/*`, the topics `rwb.case.events.v1`, `rwb.document.events.v1`, `rwb.agent.events.v1`, `rwb.deviation.events.v1` and the shared topic `rwb.decision-record.v1`, the Temporal namespace `rwb-recovery` with the queues `rwb-agent` and `rwb-deviation`, and the Enterprise AI private endpoint test profile (INT-23). Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0411; ASM-0586): the harness environment and its seeding, the SCREEN-S2 fixture pack with its 500 labels, the Enterprise AI test profile and the evidence format.
- The feature switch `rwb.agent.screening-l1` is on in the harness profile (legacy section 13).
- Synthetic cases, synthetic owners and masking tokens only: no customer name, account number, national identifier or contact detail enters the harness, the seed pack or the evidence pack; the reason on a proposal holds masking tokens (legacy sections 14 and 17).
- No build dependency. Day 1.

##### 4. Flow

1. Harness: takes the run lock for the environment and records the build ID, the business date and the versions of the four contracts it is about to exercise.
2. Harness: seeds the policy fixture (SCREENING P2 PR2, mode L1 for MORTGAGE in BKK and SHADOW elsewhere, floor 0.80), the sample SCREEN-S2 version 1 with its 500 cases and the X1 and X4 counts, cases "RW-2027-000801" to "RW-2027-000804", owner "owner.user07", the RW-PHONECOL test user and the segments.
3. Harness: calls the P4 session operation against the rwb-access fake and records the role, the scope and the Case record right the journey runs under.
4. Harness: subscribes to the five topics with its own consumer group before the run starts, so the window opens before the first event.
5. Harness: drives the evaluation through `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations` on sample "SCREEN-S2" version 1 and reads it back through `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations`, asserting sample size 500, precision 0.9111 and recall 0.8913 for X1 and recall 0.6000 for X4.
6. Harness: drives the L1 proposal through `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs` for policy "SCREENING" version "P2" with segment MORTGAGE and BKK and the evaluation run ID, and approves it through `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve` as RW-RISK; it then asserts through `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-runs` that the runs of the segment carry mode L1 and the runs outside it carry SHADOW.
7. Harness: drives the case event — `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` on `rwb.case.events.v1` for case "RW-2027-000801", and `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` on `rwb.document.events.v1` for the complaint note of 2027-01-26 — and waits for `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` on `rwb.agent.events.v1` inside the run window.
8. Harness: reads `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` and asserts the X1 proposal with its reasons, its sources, the preceding contact and the marker "Agent output"; it asserts X2 at confidence 0.72 with the marker "Low confidence" on case "RW-2027-000803" and an empty list for the hire purchase case "RW-2027-000802".
9. Harness: confirms X1 on case "RW-2027-000801" through `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs/{runId}/feedback` with verdict "ACCEPTED" and an If-Match, and rejects X6 on the same case with verdict "REJECTED" and the reason "Customer answered on 2027-01-25".
10. Harness: reads the deviation the confirmation raised through `POST /api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations` and, where the row must be touched, `PATCH /api/recovery/deviation/v1/deviations/{deviationId}`; then reads the case state through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` and the two clocks through `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers`.
11. Harness: reads the evaluation rows through `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations` and the decision records through `GET /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log`, asserting the one "X6" entry with agent version "SCREENING@P2/PR2" and final call "REJECTED", and the entry S8 wrote for the X1 confirmation.
12. Harness: writes the per-scenario evidence into one run report keyed by story key and business date, applies the gate, attaches the report to the wave 2 release record, releases the lock and restores the seed.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | The case is not Mortgage in region BKK | The run stays in shadow; the outputs read returns nothing and no decision record is written | None to a user | AC3 |
| X2 | Reject with no reason | Refused with 422; no decision record and no feedback row | MSG-P7-005 | AC5 |
| X3 | A proposal is below the confidence floor 0.80 | Shown with the marker "Low confidence" and passed only when the marker and the confidence are both present | None to a user | AC8 |
| X4 | The proposed code is already open on the case | The proposal is not shown, so the harness confirms nothing and raises nothing | None to a user | TC-E2-029-07-ITG |
| X5 | Two confirmations of the same proposal at once | One deviation exists, the confirmation that loses answers 409, and no second feedback row is stored | MSG-GEN-004 | AC7 |
| X6 | The decision record cannot be written on a rejection | The rejection answers 503, no feedback row exists, and the incident is raised by the service under R-UNI-39, not by the harness | MSG-P7-003 | AC6 |
| X7 | The L1 proposal names a score below a stated condition | The load answers 422 and names the failing code and value; the version in force is unchanged | MSG-P10-001 | AC9 |
| X8 | A role without Case record U confirms or rejects | The request answers 403 and no feedback row is stored | MSG-P4-002 | TC-E2-029-11-ITG |
| X9 | The seed pack cannot be loaded (policy version absent, sample size not 500, counts off, contract version missing) | The run refuses to start and names the missing seed item; no scenario is reported | None | AC1 |
| X10 | The evidence pack cannot be attached to the release record | The run is marked failed and the local evidence file is kept for a rerun | None | TC-E2-029-12-ITG |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | Needs the four published contracts or their fakes, the policy and sample fixtures and the Enterprise AI test profile; it builds no service feature and has no build dependency |
| Negotiable | The scenarios, the seeded cases, the policy segment and floor, the 500 labels and the evidence format are data files, never code |
| Valuable | The deviation-screening journey is proven once across four services, with the evaluation score, the raised deviation, the two clocks and the rejection record in the same evidence as the proposals |
| Estimable | One journey runner, one fake set, one fixture pack, three assertion helpers, one evidence collector, one gate |
| Small | Fits in one sprint with its tests |
| Testable | Each owned criterion has a fixed Given, When and Then and a recorded pass or fail in the report |

##### 7. Acceptance criteria

```gherkin
Feature: Deviation screening agent evaluation and L1 on one segment [E3b]

  Background:
    Given policy "SCREENING" version "P2" with prompt "PR2" has mode "L1" for segment MORTGAGE and BKK and mode "SHADOW" for every other segment
    Given case owner "owner.user07" holds RW-CASEOWN and the cases are in that user's scope

  Scenario: AC1 The evaluation scores every code and the L1 proposal names it (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the shadow run on 500 cases in sample "SCREEN-S2" version 1
    When the harness posts the evaluation through `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations` and reads it back through `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations`
    Then precision and recall per code X1 to X7 are stored with sample size 500
    Then for X1 with 41 true positives, 4 false positives and 5 false negatives precision is 0.9111 and recall is 0.8913
    Then the L1 proposal is recorded as policy "SCREENING" version "P2" with status "LOADED", segment MORTGAGE and BKK and the evaluation run ID
    Then the approval through `POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve` is accepted and the L1 proposal is the policy the next run carries

  Scenario: AC2 The L1 journey from the proposal to the raised deviation and the paused clock (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given Mortgage case "RW-2027-000801" in region BKK and a complaint note on 2027-01-26
    When the case event and the document event arrive and the agent runs in mode L1
    Then `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` returns X1 with its reasons, the preceding contact and the marker "Agent output"
    Then when "owner.user07" confirms X1 the S8 service raises deviation X1 with raised_by "SCREENING_AGENT" under rule R-DEV-01 and answers the deviation ID and the decision log entry ID
    Then `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` shows case status "On hold"
    Then `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` shows the stage clock paused and the prescription clock running
    Then agent_feedback holds verdict "ACCEPTED" for item "X1" with the S8 decision log entry ID
    Then `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` on `rwb.deviation.events.v1` announces the same deviation inside the run window

  Scenario: AC3 Other segments stay in shadow (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given hire purchase case "RW-2027-000802" in region BKK with mode "SHADOW"
    When the agent runs for the case
    Then the run stays in shadow and `GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` returns nothing
    Then no deviation is raised and no decision record is written for the case

  Scenario: AC4 A rejection writes its decision record before the feedback row (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the agent proposes X6 on case "RW-2027-000801"
    When "owner.user07" rejects X6 with the reason "Customer answered on 2027-01-25"
    Then one decision record holds decision "X6", agent version "SCREENING@P2/PR2", final call "REJECTED" and the reason
    Then the decision record exists before the agent_feedback row and agent_feedback holds "REJECTED" for item "X6"
    Then no deviation is raised for the case by the rejection

  Scenario: AC5 Reject without a reason (new, D-RCV-60)
    When "owner.user07" rejects X6 with an empty reason
    Then the answer is 422 with MSG-P7-005
    Then no decision record and no agent_feedback row exist for the rejection

  Scenario: AC6 The rejection cannot be recorded (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the rwb-decision decision log answers unavailable
    When "owner.user07" rejects X6 with a reason
    Then the answer is 503 with MSG-P7-003
    Then no agent_feedback row exists and no deviation is raised

  Scenario: AC7 Two confirmations at once (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given two sessions of "owner.user07" confirm X1 on case "RW-2027-000804" at the same time
    When both requests arrive
    Then one deviation X1 exists and the second request answers 409 with MSG-GEN-004
    Then exactly one agent_feedback row holds "ACCEPTED" for item "X1"

  Scenario: AC8 A low-confidence proposal (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the agent proposes X2 with confidence 0.72 on case "RW-2027-000803"
    When the harness reads the outputs for the case
    Then X2 is returned with the marker "Low confidence" and confidence 0.72

  Scenario: AC9 A proposal with scores below its condition (new, D-RCV-60)

    Then the version in force is unchanged
```

No legacy acceptance criterion is owned by this story: the `acs` list is empty and the nine above are new. They test only the integration deliverable, using the legacy values of RWB-E2-029 and inventing none.

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | Mode L1 applies only where the case product group and region match the policy segment; elsewhere the mode is SHADOW and nothing is returned to a user | agent_policy.segment_product_group, segment_region_code (New); AC3, AC1 |
| BR2 | The agent raises nothing itself; a deviation exists only when a person confirms the proposal | Agent catalog, screening agent "May decide alone: Nothing"; role SY-AGENT has no Case record U; AC2, AC7 |
| BR3 | A confirmed proposal is raised through S8 with raised_by "SCREENING_AGENT", and R-DEV-01 pauses the stage clock, keeps the prescription clock running and routes the case | R-DEV-01; LOV-RAISED-BY; AC2 |
| BR4 | A rejection needs a reason and writes its decision record before the feedback row; a failure to record leaves nothing behind | CTL-07; Principle 5; R-UNI-39; AC4, AC5, AC6 |
| BR5 | A proposal for a code already open on the case is not shown | deviation.deviation_code; TC-E2-029-07-ITG |
| BR6 | A proposal below the confidence floor 0.80 is shown with the marker "Low confidence" | agent_policy.confidence_floor (New); FEAT-DVH-08; AC8 |
| BR7 | An L1 proposal must meet its stated conditions on the named evaluation, and a failed check leaves the version in force unchanged | Principle 1; CTL-08; AC9 |

The rules are unchanged by the split. The harness asserts them across the service boundaries and restates none of them in code: the segment, the floor 0.80, the condition "recall at least 0.75 for every code" and the verdict list are seeded data.

##### 9. State transitions

None for the case itself: the harness holds no case record and moves no state of its own. What it asserts is that the owning services move the case exactly as the legacy story says — "On hold" on a confirmation (R-DEV-01 applied by S8), and no case status change at all on a rejection.

The run carries the autonomy mode the policy sets for its segment, and the harness asserts the two the legacy story names: L1 for MORTGAGE in BKK and SHADOW everywhere else, on the run row as well as on the policy row. The evaluation carries the sample size 500 and one precision and one recall per code. The feedback carries one verdict per run and item: ACCEPTED for item "X1" with the S8 decision log entry ID on the confirm path, REJECTED with the reason on the reject path.

The harness adds a run state of its own only: Not started, Running, Passed, Failed, with the latest run for a build deciding the gate.

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

None. The harness is a test asset in the integration pipeline and provides no REST operation.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case | Reads the case, its product group, region and status: the segment match before the run and "On hold" after the confirmation (AC2, AC3) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}/timers` | P3 rwb-case | Asserts the paused stage clock and the running prescription clock after R-DEV-01 is applied (AC2) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/cases/{caseId}/agent-outputs` | P10 rwb-agent | Reads the stored proposals with reasons, sources, preceding contact, confidence, the marker "Agent output", the marker "Low confidence" and the verdict (AC2, AC3, AC4, AC8) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs/{runId}/feedback` | P10 rwb-agent | Records one verdict per run and item with an If-Match of the run row version; the decision record is written first on a rejection (AC2, AC4, AC5, AC6, AC7) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations` | P10 rwb-agent | Runs the evaluation of "SCREENING" on sample "SCREEN-S2" version 1 and stores precision and recall per code with sample size 500 (AC1, AC9) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations` | P10 rwb-agent | Reads the evaluation rows back: 500, 0.9111 and 0.8913 for X1, 0.6000 for X4 (AC1, AC9) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs` | P10 rwb-agent | Loads the L1 proposal as policy "SCREENING" version "P2" with segment MORTGAGE and BKK, the evaluation run ID and the conditions (AC1, AC9) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve` | P10 rwb-agent | Approves the proposal as RW-RISK, and answers 409 with MSG-P7-002 when the loader tries to approve what it loaded (AC1, AC9) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-runs` | P10 rwb-agent | Reads the runs of a segment to assert mode L1 for MORTGAGE in BKK and SHADOW elsewhere (AC1, AC2, AC3) |
| POST | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1/cases/{caseId}/deviations` | S8 rwb-deviation | The only way a deviation is raised (DP-01): code "X1", `raised_by` "SCREENING_AGENT", R-DEV-01 applied, answering the deviation ID and the decision log entry ID (AC2, AC7) |
| PATCH | `/api/recovery/deviation/v1/deviations/{deviationId}` | S8 rwb-deviation | The other deviation row in the Ownership Map; the harness asserts what it needs from the raise answer and the `DeviationRaised` event and touches this path only where a scenario must update the row it created (AC2, AC7) |
| GET | `/api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log` | P7 rwb-decision | Asserts the one "X6" entry with agent version "SCREENING@P2/PR2" and final call "REJECTED", the S8 entry of the confirmation, and that a shadow case wrote none (AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC6) |

Every call is one hop on the owner's base `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` with the 2 s timeout, and every POST carries an If-Match and a key per scenario. The scope and owner check that rwb-agent and rwb-deviation make inside their own process is not a path in the Ownership Map, so the harness seeds it through the role and scope of the rwb-access fake (12.8) and reads the resulting answer through the owner's operation.

###### 12.3 Events published

None. The harness publishes no Kafka event on a production topic; the `CaseCreated` and `DocumentStored` it sends are seed messages on the test topic, and the evidence goes to the release record through the pipeline.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

| Event | Topic | Owner | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.case.CaseCreated.v1` | `rwb.case.events.v1` | P3 rwb-case | Asserts that the run of case "RW-2027-000801" was started by the case event inside the run window (DP-09) |
| `rwb.document.DocumentStored.v1` | `rwb.document.events.v1` | P5 rwb-document | The document side of REQ-DVH-001: the complaint note of 2027-01-26 is the source the X1 proposal names (DP-09) |
| `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` | `rwb.agent.events.v1` | P10 rwb-agent | Closes the run window and gives the run ID and the mode before the output read (DP-09) |
| `rwb.deviation.DeviationRaised.v1` | `rwb.deviation.events.v1` | S8 rwb-deviation | Closes the confirm window and proves that the flag every queue projects is the deviation the confirmation raised (REQ-DVH-006, DP-09) |
| `rwb.decision-record.DecisionRecorded.v1` | `rwb.decision-record.v1` | P7 rwb-decision | Asserts that the "X6" record and the S8 record reached the shared topic inside the run window, alongside the ledger read of 12.2 (DP-03, DP-09) |

The harness consumes with its own consumer group and never reads a producer's outbox, inbox or schema.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

`AgentRunWorkflow` on queue `rwb-agent` is observed, not built: the run has a 60 s limit and then the rule result (R-UNI-32), and the harness asserts which of the two the run ended on from the run it reads back (AC2, AC3). `DeviationWorkflow`, the child workflow of the case on queue `rwb-deviation`, is observed after the raise, and the harness reads the result of the pause from the two clocks (AC2).

The harness starts no workflow, adds no activity and writes no schedule. The agent call to the Enterprise AI private endpoint (INT-23), the guardrail check and the storage of the proposals belong to RWB-P10-E2029-APP; the raise, the pause of the stage clock and the routing belong to RWB-S8-E2029-APP and RWB-P3-E2015-APP.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. The harness adds no workflow and no schedule; the 60 s limit is inside `AgentRunWorkflow` and the every-minute outbox relay is the platform's, both only observed.

###### 12.7 Tables owned

None. The harness owns no table in any schema and no schema of its own; it reads and writes through the operations of 12.2 only.

##### 13. Solution plan

**Package.** Folder `integration/recovery-agent-deviation` in the ACE repository, package `<ACE base package>.recovery.integration.agentdeviation`. Not part of any deployed service.

**Pattern application**

| DP | Legacy marker | Microservice pattern | Dependency added | How this harness applies it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-03 | DecisionLogWriter, decision log | Local decision-record library and topic `rwb.decision-record.v1` | H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON | The "X6" rejection record and the record S8 writes are read through rwb-decision, and `DecisionRecorded` is read on the shared topic; the harness never reads a decision table |
| DP-05 | AceSourceQuery, `v_ace_*`, account_ext | Read through rwb-source-data's contract or the service's own ACE views | none | The X7 collateral input is the appraisal date DF-ACE-193, which only P1 reads from the view; the harness asserts it through the P10 output and reads no view and seeds no ACE data |
| DP-06 | Parameters, casewf.config | Parameters contract of rwb-case and the client library | H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON; C RWB-P3-E1042-CON | The policy version, the segment, the floor 0.80 and the condition "recall at least 0.75 for every code" are configuration values supplied through the owning service's admin operation, never constants in the harness |
| DP-07 | Reference data, LOV | Reference-data contract of rwb-case | H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON; C RWB-P3-E1043-CON | The codes X1 to X7, the `raised_by` value "SCREENING_AGENT" and the verdict list are reference data read from the owner's contract, not literals in the scenarios |
| DP-09 | Application event, EV-nn, outbox | Outbox and inbox library; Kafka topic of the owner; CloudEvents | H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON | The harness subscribes with its own consumer group to the five topics and asserts the five events; it never reads a producer's outbox or inbox |
| DP-11 | In-process call, published interface | REST contract with mock; one hop; 2 s timeout | none (C from the legacy dependency) | The in-process `DeviationService.raise` of the monolith is the S8 POST on the owner's base with the 2 s timeout; the harness asserts the deviation ID and the decision log entry ID it answers |
| DP-13 | `/api/recovery/v1` | `/api/recovery/<short>/v1` | none | Every path of 12.2 uses the owner's base, so no scenario can call a monolith path |
| DP-19 | Screen, ace-web | gateway-bff composite route | H RWB-PLT-N001-CON | The panel "Proposed deviations" is composed by gateway-bff from the P10 output and the P3 case; the harness drives the same route the case record uses, on the same bases |

The platform H dependencies in the table (H RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, H RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, H RWB-PLT-TE006-CON, H RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are delivered by the platform waves and are not repeated in the metadata: the harness converges on them and has no build dependency of its own. The blocking dependencies of this story are the four I stories, which replace the fakes with real services one at a time.

**Harness components**

| Component | Type | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| JourneyRunner | Job | Runs the twelve flow steps for one scenario and one business date and holds the run lock |
| FakeRegistry | Configuration | WireMock mappings for rwb-agent, rwb-case, rwb-deviation, rwb-decision and rwb-access, one set per contract version, plus the Enterprise AI test profile selection |
| ScreeningFixturePack | Data | Policy SCREENING P2 PR2, sample SCREEN-S2 version 1 with the 500 labels, cases "RW-2027-000801" to "RW-2027-000804", the RW-PHONECOL test user, the segment and the counts, per scenario |
| ProposalAssertion | Service | Compares the proposals, their reasons and sources, the preceding contact, the marker "Agent output", the marker "Low confidence", the confidence 0.72 and the empty list for SHADOW |
| DeviationAssertion | Service | Confirms and rejects through the feedback operation, then checks the raised deviation, `raised_by` "SCREENING_AGENT", R-DEV-01, the case status, the two clocks and the message of each refusal |
| MetricAssertion | Service | Reads the evaluation rows and compares sample size 500, precision 0.9111 and recall 0.8913 for X1, recall 0.6000 for X4, and the condition that refuses the load |
| EvidenceCollector | Service | Writes one report keyed by story key and business date, with the evaluation, the policy version, the run, the proposals, the confirmation, the deviation, the case state, the two clocks, the rejection record and the measure |
| GateEvaluator | Service | Passes the run when every owned scenario passes and the evidence pack is attached to the release record |

**Environment and test data.** SIT, the wave 2 harness profile, one business date, synthetic cases and synthetic owners only. The seeded values are the legacy section 7 Background, the policy and sample fixtures of section 3, the four cases of section 3 and the counts 41, 4, 5 and 0.6000; no other value is added. Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0411; ASM-0586): the environment and its seeding, the SCREEN-S2 fixture pack, the Enterprise AI test profile, the forced failures and the evidence format.

**Build steps**

1. Write the ScreeningFixturePack with the Background, the policy fixture, sample "SCREEN-S2" version 1 with its 500 labels, the four cases and the counts; test that a bad seed stops the run (X9).
2. Write the FakeRegistry with the five WireMock mapping sets and the Enterprise AI test profile selection, with the policy, the condition and the verdict list loaded from files.
3. Write JourneyRunner for AC1: post the evaluation, read it back, load the L1 proposal, approve it, and assert the numbers and the evaluation run ID on the proposal.
4. Add AC2 with the case and document events, the outputs read, the confirmation, the deviation raise, the case status, the two clocks, the feedback row and the `DeviationRaised` window.
5. Add AC3 and AC8 with the SHADOW case and the low-confidence proposal, then AC4 and AC7 with the rejection record first, the duplicate refusal and its 409.
6. Add AC5 and AC6 with the 422 and the 503, asserting that neither writes a feedback row, then AC9 with the condition that refuses the load.
7. Write EvidenceCollector and GateEvaluator, attach the report to the wave 2 release record and rerun the nine scenarios on the release build.

**Feature switch.** `rwb.agent.screening-l1` is on in the harness profile, as the legacy story sets it. Off, every segment runs in shadow and the outputs read returns nothing, so the harness reports the journey as not applicable rather than as passed. The harness itself is a pipeline stage selected by the run profile, not by a business flag.

**Done when.** The tests of section 16 pass, the run report is attached to the wave 2 release record with all nine owned scenarios, and each fake has been replaced by the real service where its I story has landed in SIT. The fixture pack and the evidence sign-off wait for the values of the gap and assumption rows cited in sections 3, 12.8 and 13.

##### 14. Validation and messages

| ID | When | Message |
|---|---|---|
| MSG-P7-005 | Reject without a reason | Enter the reason you are not following the recommendation. |
| MSG-P7-003 | Decision log write failed | The action was not taken because the decision could not be recorded. Try again in a few minutes. |
| MSG-GEN-004 | Second confirmation of the same proposal | Someone else changed this record. Reload it to see their change. |
| MSG-P10-001 | L1 proposal fails a check | The {kind} file for {agent} was refused: {check}. The version in force is unchanged. |
| MSG-S8-001 | Deviation raised after confirmation | {deviation} was raised. The case is with {handler}. |
| MSG-P4-002 | Role without the right | You cannot {action} here. Your role does not include it. |

The harness asserts these messages and never rewrites them. Its own report text is for the release team and is not part of the message standard.

##### 15. Screens and states

SCR-03 Case record gains the panel "Proposed deviations" with states: empty (no panel), ready (proposals with reasons, sources, confidence and Confirm and Reject), low confidence (the marker on the proposal), and recorded (the verdict and the date). After a confirmation SCR-03 shows the on hold banner of the deviation and the paused stage clock, with the prescription clock still running. SCR-08 Deviation queue lists the flagged case for the named handler. SCR-46 Agent monitor shows SCREENING as live for MORTGAGE in BKK and Shadow elsewhere.

No screen is built by this story. The harness drives the operations behind those states and asserts the same states through the contracts; the panel, the queue and the monitor belong to their own app stories. The screen fixtures that reproduce these states are in no source read. Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0411; ASM-0586).

Each `-ITG` case is the journey copy of the legacy case: the Given, When and Then are those of the legacy case of the same number, run across the four contracts and the Enterprise AI test profile, with the cross-service assertion added — the deviation, the case state, the two clocks or the decision record that a single service cannot show. The app stories keep the unit and component copies of the same cases.

##### 17. Guardrails

- No business value in code: the segment, the floor 0.80, the condition, the sample size 500 and the verdict list are data in the seed pack, never values in the harness.
- No personal data in events, workflow inputs, logs, evidence or agent calls: the reasons carry masking tokens and the seed holds synthetic cases and synthetic owners only.
- No read of another service's tables and no schema of the harness's own: every read and write goes through the operations of 12.2, no `v_ace_*` view is read, and only S8 raises a deviation.
- Agent output never changes the case: the harness asserts that no status, task or field moves because of a run or a verdict, and that only the confirmation moves the case.
- Each fake is replaced by the real service as its I story lands; a fake that outlives its service is a defect, not a configuration.
- The harness never runs against UAT or production, and a value that must change changes in the seed pack through a reviewed change, never by an exception in a scenario.

##### 19. Out of scope

- L1 on further segments: a later policy version, outside this journey.
- The deviation flows after the flag in S8: routing, contact stop, handling and return belong to RWB-S8-E2029-APP.
- The agent handling X6 and X7 within policy, which the S8 flows own.
- Production code of any service in the journey: the operations of rwb-agent, rwb-case, rwb-deviation and rwb-decision, their schemas and their screens belong to their own stories.

The harness, the fakes and the evidence pack cover the four items above only as a caller or a consumer would see them; building any of them is out of scope for this story.

**Change log.** D-RCV-60, 22 November 2026: contract slice of RWB-E2-030 for rwb-agent, written on Day 1. It fixes the seam the app story builds against: the run start and run read on `/api/recovery/agent/v1` (DP-13), the `legal-pack-v1` output with its completeness list, the consumed boundary of rwb-document (RWB-P5-E2025-CON), rwb-litigation and rwb-case, the policy payload narrowed with the review date and the evaluation run ID (DP-06), the restated evaluation and score shapes of RWB-P10-E1061-CON, the event contract of `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28) on `rwb.agent.events.v1` with its retry and `.dlt` topics (DP-09), the lists of rwb-case (DP-07), the gateway-bff route (DP-19) and the five fakes. It adds no business behaviour, no table and no migration. Tool: T3 Code / OpenCode / DeepSeek v4.1 Flash.

##### 1. Story

As a **tech lead**, I want **the rwb-agent side of the legal document key fixed as a contract on Day 1 - the run start and run read of agent "LEGAL_DOC" on `/api/recovery/agent/v1`, the `legal-pack-v1` output and its completeness list, the three document reads of RWB-P5-E2025-CON with the by-case legal-action and case reads, the policy payload with mode SHADOW, review date, evaluation run ID, allowed tools and schema reference, the restated evaluation and score shapes, the EV-28 event on `rwb.agent.events.v1`, the gateway-bff route, the error taxonomy and five fakes**, so that **the app story, the Epic 5 pack story and every reader of a legal-pack score build against one agreed, testable shape without waiting for the model, and no reader is offered a pack from a monolith table, a lake artefact or a schedule that does not exist**.

##### 2. Business rationale

The legacy key RWB-E2-030 was written against objects inside the monolith: the run wrote `agent_run` and `agent_evaluation` rows beside the policy row, the documents, their fields and the checklist came from `DocumentQueryService` in process, the open legal action from `LegalActionQueryService` in process, and the whole path was served on the legacy monolith base (legacy sections 4, 11, 12 and 13). In the target every one of those is a boundary:

- The run, the sample, the evaluation run, the score rows, the prompt and the policy version are rwb-agent's own tables in `rwb_agent`; the operations that start and report an evaluation already belong to RWB-P10-E1061-CON and the configuration and sample operations to RWB-P10-E1058-CON, so this key narrows them and adds no member of its own (DP-01).
- The documents, their checked fields and the case-type checklist are P5 rwb-document, read through RWB-P5-E2025-CON one hop with the 2 s budget (DP-11).
- The case and the legal action are P3 rwb-case and S4 rwb-litigation and are read through their contracts; no service opens another service's table (DP-01).
- The minimum sample of 50 and the promotion check list are parameter and policy values read at load time, never code (DP-06); the lists come from the reference-data contract (DP-07).
- The run facts leave as CloudEvents on `rwb.agent.events.v1` with the platform's retry and `.dlt` topics (DP-09, DP-14).
- The base and the route are the platform's: `/api/recovery/agent/v1` behind gateway-bff (DP-13, DP-19).

Contract-first only works if the seam is written down once. The seam here is small and load-bearing: one run start and one run read whose answer carries the pack, one output schema with its completeness list, three boundary reads with their failure mapping, one policy payload with the review date, two restated evaluation shapes whose score row carries 0.9200 on 46 of 50, one event, one route, one error taxonomy and one fake set that makes the app story testable on Day 1.

If the shape is agreed and faked on Day 1, two teams move at once: RWB-P10-E2030-APP builds the assembler, the checks, the scorer and the validator against these fakes, and the Epic 5 pack story of S4 consumes the same output schema and score row. Without it, each caller invents its own pack member, the panel and the evaluation report drift apart, and a promotion is decided on a number nobody can reproduce.

This document defines the provided side on the agent base and the consumed side of the key, and never restates what another owner holds: the configuration and sample operations are RWB-P10-E1058-CON's, the evaluation operations are RWB-P10-E1061-CON's, the parameters and lists are rwb-case's, the documents and the checklist are rwb-document's, and the legal action is rwb-litigation's (DP-01).

##### 3. Preconditions

- The service template and the naming library are available (RWB-PLT-TPL), so the REST base, the topic and the event names follow the platform rule and not a local choice (§R4; DP-13, DP-14).
- The CloudEvents 1.0 envelope and the platform problem response are the platform baseline; this document narrows them where it must and says so.
- The agent runtime baseline of RWB-P10-E1058-CON is in force: the policy, prompt and sample resources, the configuration operations, the approval and the admin run read are its elements, and this story narrows the policy payload with the review date, the evaluation run ID, the allowed tools and the schema reference rather than redefining it.
- The evaluation baseline of RWB-P10-E1061-CON is in force: the start, the list and the report operations, their statuses and their messages; this story restates them with the legal narrowing and adds no operation.
- The rwb-document contract RWB-P5-E2025-CON is in force for the documents of a case, the checked fields of a document and the checklist of a case type. The three paths this key consumes below the P5 base are named by no source and are fixed here against the fake (GAP-0628; ASM-0944).
- The rwb-case contracts are published: `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` (RWB-P3-E2015-CON), `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) and `GET /api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` (RWB-P3-E1043-CON).
- The rwb-litigation by-case legal-action read is published before this lane starts; its path is named by no source and is consumed and faked here with no C row of its own (GAP-0628; ASM-0944).
- The outbox and inbox library of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON publishes the envelope, the relay, the retry topics and the `.dlt` rule. The gateway-bff route contract and its stub are published by RWB-PLT-N001-CON.
- No build dependency: this story is Day 1 by rule (§R5.7) and sits in contract group CG-W2.

##### 4. Flow

1. Draft the run start and the run read on `/api/recovery/agent/v1` with their input, their answer and the run statuses of LOV-AGENT-RUN.
2. Fix the `legal-pack-v1` output and the completeness list: one item per checklist code with its status, its document IDs and its defect reason, plus the confidence.
3. Fix the consumed boundary: the three document reads, the by-case legal-action read and the case read, each one hop with the 2 s budget, and the mapping of a failed read to TOOL_UNAVAILABLE with the reason naming the read.
4. Fix the policy payload and the promote-or-keep outcome: mode SHADOW with the review date, mode L1 with the conditions, the evaluation run ID, the allowed tools, the schema reference and the 60-second timeout, loaded and then approved by a person other than the loader.
5. Restate the evaluation start, list and report with the legal narrowing, and fix the score row: one row per checklist code with the sample size, the agreement rate at four decimals and the not-run cases counted.
6. Declare the event: `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28) on `rwb.agent.events.v1` with the retry and `.dlt` topics, the run facts of this document and no pack member.
7. Fix the route, the parameter and list reads, and the boundary of section 12.2.
8. Write the five fakes: rwb-document, rwb-litigation, rwb-case, the model gateway and the gateway-bff route.
9. State the absence rules: no new table, no migration, no Schedule, no lake artefact and no pack on a topic.
10. Publish the nine sub-tables and the seven contract tests, and tag the baseline for the app story and the Epic 5 pack story.

##### 5. Exception paths

| ID | Trigger | What happens | Message | Covered by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| X1 | A member of the pack, of the score row or of the policy payload drifts from this document: a renamed item member, a dropped status, a retyped figure | The contract test fails and the merge is blocked | None | AC1, AC2, AC5 |
| X2 | A caller sends a request the contract does not allow: a policy file that fails a check, a sample with no labelled row, a second evaluation of the same sample | The operation refuses with 422 or 409 and names the check or the state; nothing is written | MSG-P10-001, MSG-P10-002, MSG-P10-003 | AC4, AC5 |
| X3 | The contract declares a table of another service, a lake artefact, a Schedule or a pack on a topic | The review refuses the document, because none of those exists in the target | None | AC6 |
| X4 | A payload gains a personal field or fails its registry subject | The data-steward review and the contract test refuse the payload; a produced message that fails is routed to `.dlt` with an alert | None | AC6 |
| X5 | A consumed read slows beyond 2 s or fails | The run is answered TOOL_UNAVAILABLE with fallback true and the read named, and the case is scored as not run | None to a user | AC3 |
| X6 | A restated operation drifts from its baseline of RWB-P10-E1058-CON or RWB-P10-E1061-CON | The contract test fails and this document is aligned, because the baseline is the owner | None | AC1, AC4, AC5 |
| X7 | A field-level detail of a consumed read, a pack member or the route is missing from the source material | The element carries the placeholder, the combined gap row and one assumption row, and the fake is written to the assumed shape | None | AC2, AC3, AC7 |

##### 6. INVEST check

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Independent | No build dependency; reads the platform envelopes and route stub, the agent runtime and evaluation baselines and the rwb-case, rwb-document and rwb-litigation contracts as published |
| Negotiable | The types of the pack members, the exact consumed paths and the route name are settled with their owners; the pack shape, the policy payload, the score row, the event and the fakes are fixed by this realignment |
| Valuable | Unblocks the app story on Day 1 and gives the Epic 5 pack story one output schema and one score row |
| Estimable | Two provided operations, two narrowed configuration payloads, three restated evaluation operations, three boundary reads, one event and five fakes |
| Small | Fits one sprint with the contract tests |
| Testable | Every criterion is tested against the artefact - the contract file, the payload, the fake - and never against a model outcome |

```gherkin
    Then POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve answers 200 with status "APPROVED", approvedBy and validFrom, 404 for an unknown version and 409 with MSG-P7-002 when the approver loaded the version
    Then a load with mode "SHADOW" and no review date is refused with 422 and MSG-P10-001 naming check "review date present", and a load with mode "L1" is accepted only when every stated condition is met by the evaluation, otherwise refused with 422 and MSG-P10-001 naming check "sample size at least 50"
    Then the six members beyond the baseline are additive and no member of the baseline is removed (ASM-0956)

  Scenario: AC5 The evaluation operations and the score row of this key are fixed (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the evaluation operations of RWB-P10-E1061-CON and sample "LEGAL-S1" version 1 on 50 cases
    When the evaluation of agent "LEGAL_DOC" on "LEGAL-S1" version 1 is started and reported
    Then POST /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations takes agent, sampleCode, sampleVersion and approaches and answers 202 with an AgentEvaluationRun in status "RUNNING", 422 with MSG-P10-002 for a sample with no labelled row and 409 with MSG-P10-003 for a second evaluation while one is RUNNING
    Then GET /api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations/{evaluationId}/report answers sampleSize 50, the three versions, one score row per checklist item, the not-run cases with their failure type, the cost and the latency
    Then the score row for "DEMAND_NOTICE_PROOF" with 46 agreeing cases answers agreementRate 0.9200 and the evaluation with one case not run answers sampleSize 49, and the rate is the value DF-AGT-094 at four decimals
    Then this document restates the operations and adds no member; the narrowing to "LEGAL_DOC" and the not-run count are its only content (ASM-0957)

  Scenario: AC6 The event contract is declared and no pack, table, migration or Schedule is added (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given a completed shadow run of agent "LEGAL_DOC" for case "RW-2026-000901"
    When the outbox row is relayed
    Then rwb.agent.events.v1 carries rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1 (EV-28), keyed by the case ID, with the retry topic and the .dlt topic, and its envelope carries id, source, type, specversion, time, subject and datacontenttype, with the run ID as its subject
    Then the payload carries run ID, agent_code, agent_version, prompt_version, case_id, autonomy_mode, trigger_event, status, fallback, confidence, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_thb and run_at, and no item, no document ID, no defect reason and no personal field
    Then this document publishes no second event, declares no pack topic, no new table, no migration, no Temporal Schedule and no lake table, extract or credential, because DP-15 and DP-10 are not patterns of this key and no data lake exists
    Then a payload that fails its registry subject is refused before the relay and routed to .dlt with an alert

  Scenario: AC7 The route, the fakes and the error taxonomy are complete (new, D-RCV-60)
    Given the nine sub-tables of section 12 and the gateway-bff route stub of RWB-PLT-N001-CON
    When the document and the five fakes are reviewed
    Then each of 12.1 to 12.9 is present, names its owner from the Ownership Map and writes None where it is empty
    Then the route is a pass-through of one hop in front of the operations and preserves the JSON and CSV media types, and its name and path are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0628; ASM-0950)
    Then the error taxonomy is the platform problem response with 401, 403 with MSG-P4-002, 404, 409 with MSG-P7-002 or MSG-P10-003, 422 with MSG-P10-001 or MSG-P10-002 and 503, and no operation adds a code outside it
    Then the fakes rwb-document, rwb-litigation, rwb-case, the model gateway and the route answer every consumed path and payload of this document, every fixture is synthetic, and a drift between a fake and this document fails the contract test
```

**Target reading.** This contract adds no behaviour and no business value. Agent "LEGAL_DOC", the policy versions "P1" and "P2", prompt "PR1", case type "MORTGAGE_CIVIL" with its 9 items, sample "LEGAL-S1" version 1, the 50 and 49 scored cases, the 46 agreeing cases and agreement 0.9200, the review date 2027-03-15, the 60-second timeout, the case "RW-2026-000901" with 14 documents and the refusal codes are the legacy values of RWB-E2-030, copied character for character; the member names are those of TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 and the API specification v4. Four elements are settled here and marked where they appear: the run start path, which no source names (ASM-0947); the consumed paths and field names of the boundary (ASM-0944); the six policy members beyond the baseline (ASM-0956); and the route (ASM-0950).

##### 8. Business rules

| ID | Rule | Source |
|---|---|---|
| BR1 | The run start and the run read are the agent runtime's and this key adds no operation of its own; the configuration and evaluation operations are restated from RWB-P10-E1058-CON and RWB-P10-E1061-CON and never redefined | DP-11; DP-13; ASM-0947 |
| BR2 | The `legal-pack-v1` answer carries one item per checklist code with a status, its document IDs and a required defect reason, and only documents the rwb-document contract returned for the same case | Legacy AC1, AC4, AC5; CTL-19; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 DF-AGT-049 |
| BR3 | The documents, their fields and the checklist are consumed from RWB-P5-E2025-CON one hop with the 2 s budget; no table of `rwb_document` is an answer source | DP-01; DP-11; ASM-0944 |
| BR4 | A failed or slow consumed read answers run status TOOL_UNAVAILABLE with fallback true and the reason naming the read, and the case is scored as not run | Legacy AC6; R-UNI-33 |
| BR5 | The mode, the review date, the evaluation run ID, the promotion conditions, the allowed tools and the schema reference are policy data with a version, loaded and then approved by a person other than the loader | Legacy AC3, AC8, AC9; MSG-P7-002; DP-06 |
| BR6 | The score row is the baseline `AgentEvaluation` with the checklist code as its label key, the sample size and the agreement rate at four decimals; a row that does not reproduce its rate is refused | Legacy AC2, BR5; DF-AGT-089, DF-AGT-090, DF-AGT-094 |
| BR7 | Every message is a CloudEvents 1.0 message on `rwb.agent.events.v1`, keyed by the case, validated against its registry subject before the relay and routed to `.dlt` on failure; the pack is never published | DP-09; DP-14; EV-28 |
| BR8 | The contract declares no new table, no migration, no Schedule and no lake artefact, because DP-15 and DP-10 are not patterns of this key and no data lake exists | ADR-018; Owned tables of P10 |
| BR9 | No business value in the contract: the 9 items, the 50 cases, the 0.9200, the date and the timeout are policy and reference rows, and the contract only names them | Template and Rules §R7.2 s17; DP-06; DP-07 |
| BR10 | One base and one topic per service: this contract declares `/api/recovery/agent/v1` and `rwb.agent.events.v1` for rwb-agent and never another service's path or topic as its own | DP-13; DP-14 |

##### 9. State transitions

| From | Event | Condition | To |
|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Review opened | The run start, the pack, the boundary reads, the policy payload, the score row, the event, the route and the fakes are described | In review |
| In review | Consumer sign-off | The app story and the Epic 5 pack story accept the document and the fakes | Baselined |
| Baselined | Additive change | A member, a query parameter or a payload field is added without removing one | Baselined |
| Baselined | Breaking change | A member of the pack, of the score row, of the policy payload or of the event is removed, renamed or retyped | In review, with the owner of the affected contract |
| Baselined | Drift in a fake or against a baseline | A contract test fails | In review |

These are the states of this document. The states of the run (LOV-AGENT-RUN), of the evaluation (RUNNING, DONE, FAILED) and of the policy version (LOADED, APPROVED, RETIRED) are values of their lists and belong to RWB-P10-E2030-APP.

The identity that reads the consumed contracts is the rwb-agent service identity; its name is fixed with the deployment story (DP-02 is not a pattern of this key).

The contract declares shapes, not business values.

| Pack | items[] with itemCode (the 9 codes of "MORTGAGE_CIVIL"), status PRESENT, MISSING or DEFECT, documentIds[], defectReason when DEFECT; confidence at four decimals |
| Documents read | id, caseId, documentType, writeOnce; the 14 documents of "RW-2026-000901" |
| Fields read | fieldName, fieldValue masked; DF-DOC-014 and DF-DOC-015 |
| Checklist read | the 9 itemCodes of the case type including "LOAN_CONTRACT", "MORTGAGE_DEED" and "DEMAND_NOTICE_PROOF" |
| Legal action read | id, actionType, status; one open action on "RW-2026-000901" |
| Policy request | kind POLICY, agent "LEGAL_DOC", policyVersion "P2", autonomyMode "SHADOW", reviewDate 2027-03-15, evaluationRunId, promotionConditions, allowedTools, outputSchemaRef "legal-pack-v1", timeoutSeconds 60 |
| Policy answer | the version resource of the baseline with status LOADED or APPROVED, approvedBy, validFrom and the review date |
| Score row | labelKey the checklist code, sampleSize 50 or 49, agreementRate 0.9200 for "DEMAND_NOTICE_PROOF"; DF-AGT-089, DF-AGT-090, DF-AGT-094 |

| Consumed values | the minimum sample 50 and the promotion check list through the parameters contract; LOV-AGENT, LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-CONFIG-STATUS, LOV-EVAL-STATUS, LOV-AGENT-RUN and LOV-SUBJECT-TYPE through the reference-data contract; the case facts through the case read |

The member types beyond the names the legacy story and TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 give - the type of `documentIds`, the member name of the defect reason, the exact type of `confidence` and `agreementRate` beyond four decimals - are Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0628; ASM-0944, ASM-0957). No table of another schema is an answer source: the answer comes from `rwb_agent` and the boundary reads (DP-01).

##### 12. Contract

###### 12.1 REST operations provided

Base `/api/recovery/agent/v1`; owner rwb-agent (P10). This key adds no operation: the seven operations below are the baselines of RWB-P10-E1058-CON and RWB-P10-E1061-CON restated with the legal narrowing.

| Method | Path | Purpose | Rights | Errors |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs` | Start one shadow run of "LEGAL_DOC" for a sampled case at the path fixed here; 202 AgentRun | Case record C, scope applied | 401, 403, 404, 409, 422, 503 |
| GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/agent-runs/{runId}` | Read the run with its outcome, guardrail result, pack and completeness list (Arch v5 slide 16) | Platform administration R, scope applied | 401, 403, 404, 503 |
| POST | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-samples` | Load sample "LEGAL-S1" version 1; 201 AgentSample with rows 50 | Rules and parameters C | 401, 403, 422, 503 |
| POST | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations` | Start the evaluation of "LEGAL_DOC" on "LEGAL-S1" version 1; 202 AgentEvaluationRun in status RUNNING | Rules and parameters C | 401, 403, 409 MSG-P10-003, 422 MSG-P10-002, 503 |
| GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations` | List the evaluation runs with their scores and proposals, JSON or CSV | Rules and parameters R | 401, 403, 503 |
| GET | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-evaluations/{evaluationId}/report` | Read the report: sampleSize, agreement per item, the not-run cases, cost, latency | Rules and parameters R | 401, 403, 404, 409 MSG-P10-008, 503 |
| POST | `/api/recovery/agent/v1/admin/agent-configs` and `/admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve` | Load and approve policy version "P2" with its mode, review date, evaluation run ID, tools and schema reference | Rules and parameters C and A | 401, 403, 404, 409 MSG-P7-002, 422 MSG-P10-001, 503 |

The path of the run start below the base is Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0628; ASM-0947): the sources name the read `GET /agent-runs/{id}` on Arch v5 slide 16 and no start operation, so this document fixes the pair instead of inventing a business value. Errors: 401 no session, 403 no right (MSG-P4-002), 404 an unknown run, version or evaluation, 409 a self-approval or a second evaluation, 422 a failed check or an empty sample, 503 a store or a consumed contract unavailable.

###### 12.2 REST operations consumed

| Method | Path | Owner | Use in this contract | Budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/documents` | P5 rwb-document (RWB-P5-E2025-CON; ASM-0944) | The documents of a case with their type and write-once flag | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/documents/{documentId}/fields` | P5 rwb-document (RWB-P5-E2025-CON; ASM-0944) | The checked field names and their masked values | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/document/v1/cases/{caseId}/document-checklist` | P5 rwb-document (RWB-P5-E2025-CON; ASM-0944) | The 9 itemCodes of case type "MORTGAGE_CIVIL" | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | the by-case legal-action read of rwb-litigation: Not specified in the source documents (GAP-0628; ASM-0944) | S4 rwb-litigation | The open legal action of the case and its type | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/cases/{caseId}` | P3 rwb-case (RWB-P3-E2015-CON) | The case facts of DF-CAS-001, DF-CAS-003 and DF-CAS-017 | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/parameters` | P3 rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1042-CON) | The minimum scored sample of 50 and the promotion check list in force, with their version (DP-06) | One hop, 2 s |
| GET | `/api/recovery/case/v1/admin/lists/{listCode}` | P3 rwb-case (RWB-P3-E1043-CON) | LOV-AGENT, LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-CONFIG-STATUS, LOV-EVAL-STATUS, LOV-AGENT-RUN and LOV-SUBJECT-TYPE (DP-07) | One hop, 2 s |

Every call is one hop to the owning service on its own base (DP-13) with the 2 s client budget (DP-11, ADR-020). A failure or a slow answer maps to TOOL_UNAVAILABLE on the run (BR4). No lake operation and no INT-19 or INT-20 path is consumed; the model endpoint INT-23 is called inside the run, not from this boundary.

###### 12.3 Events published

| Event | Topic | Owner of the type | Key | Payload (IDs and facts only) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rwb.agent.AgentRunCompleted.v1` (EV-28) | `rwb.agent.events.v1` with the retry topic and the `.dlt` topic | P10 | the case ID | run ID, agent_code, agent_version, prompt_version, case_id, autonomy_mode, trigger_event, status, fallback, confidence, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_thb, run_at |

The event is inserted in the outbox in the same transaction as the run row and relayed by the library of RWB-PLT-TE006-CON; it is validated against its registry subject before the relay and a refusal is routed to `.dlt` with an alert. It carries no item, no document ID, no defect reason and no personal field: the pack stays in `agent_run.output` (BR7; ASM-0954). This contract publishes no second event and declares no pack topic.

###### 12.4 Events consumed

None. A run of this key is started by the harness of the evaluation and not by a topic, so no event is consumed. The event-triggered run paths of rwb-agent (`CaseCreated`, `DocumentStored`) belong to RWB-P10-E1059-CON and RWB-P10-E1062-CON and are declared there.

###### 12.5 Workflows and activities

| Name | Type | Task queue | Contract element |
|---|---|---|---|
| AgentRunWorkflow | Workflow, one execution per case and evaluation run | `rwb-agent` | Input: agent "LEGAL_DOC", case ID, evaluation run ID, policy version, idempotency key. Output: the run with its mode, its pack, its completeness list and its status; the 60-second policy budget then the rule result (R-UNI-32) |
| AssembleLegalPackInputs | Activity | `rwb-agent` | Input: the case, the legal action, the documents with their masked fields and the checklist. Output: the masked model input and the item list, or the refusal naming the failed read (BR3, BR4) |
| ScoreLegalPack | Activity | `rwb-agent` | Input: the run and the officers' rows of `agent_sample`. Output: one `agent_evaluation` row per item with the sample size and the rate at four decimals (BR6) |

The workflow identity, the queue and the 60-second budget are those of Arch v5 slide 16; the activity names and their members are this contract's and are accepted by RWB-P10-E2030-APP.

###### 12.6 Schedules

None. No Temporal Schedule belongs to this contract: the evaluation is started by RW-COE and a run is started by the harness, never on a cadence, and DP-10 is not a pattern of this key. The retired Quartz scheduler is not replaced by a schedule here.

No table of another service is declared and no foreign key crosses a schema: `recovery_case`, `legal_action`, `document`, `document_field`, `document_checklist_item`, `parameter_catalog`, `parameter_value`, `reference_row` and `reference_version` are P3, S4 and P5 and are reached through their contracts (DP-01). No lake table is declared, because no data lake exists.
